name: Abies Canadensis References
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - abies-c. Abies canadensis. Hemlock Spruce. Canada pitch. Picea alba. Pinus Canadensis.
Tsuga canadensis. N. O. Coniferae. Pinaceae. Tincture of fresh bark and young buds. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphthous, ulcers. Burns. Chills. Cholera. Colds. Constipation. Croup. Coughs. Diarrhea.
Flatulence. Gangrene. Gonorrhea. Indigestion. Leucorrhea. Liver, disorders. Night-sweat. Prolapsed, anus.
Prolapsed, uterus. Rheumatism. Stomach, disorders. Uterine, displacements. Vertigo. Vomiting.
HERBAL - A strong decoction of the bark of this tree is beneficial in leucorrhea, prolapsed uterus, prolapsed
anus, diarrhea, etc., administered internally, and used in enema.
It is of service as a local application in gangrene, and in aphthous, and other oral ulcerations.
The essence (oil) of hemlock is diuretic and highly stimulant. As a liniment this oil has been used in croup,
rheumatism, and other affections requiring a stimulating local application.
Dr. W. K. Everson states it to be a superior remedy in gastric irritation to allay vomiting in cholera morbus, etc.
The dose is 5 or 10 drops in water, every 10 or 20 minutes, until relief is afforded.
It is likewise of value in passive hemorrhages, and is useful topically in scalds and burns. General asthenic
state, with feeble digestion, vascular weakness, and pale mucus membranes. Broncho-pulmonary irritation,
with profuse secretions. Coughs and colds. Renal torpor. Pyrosis and gastric irritation with vomiting and
diarrhea. Never to be used in inflammatory or sthenic conditions.
HOMEOPATHIC - Marked symptoms in mucus membranes and stomach, a catarrhal condition of the stomach
 is produced. Characteristic cravings and chilly sensations. Useful for women with uterine displacements,
probably due to defective nutrition with debility and lack of tone.
The skin is cold and clammy, hands cold, very faint. Respiration and heart action are labored. The right lung
and liver feel small and hard. Great appetite, tendency to overeat. Gnawing, hungry, faint feeling in
epigastrium. Wants to lie down all the time.
MIND - Easily fretful or quiet and careless. Patient wants to lie down all the time on account of nervous
weakness and feels faint. Abdomen - Flatulence disturbs the heart's action. Sick feeling in the bowels.
Burning and distention in abdomen with palpitations. Rumbling in the bowels after eating, with great appetite.
Back - Pain behind the right shoulder blade. Weak feeling in sacral region. Feeling as of cold water between
the shoulders.
Eyes - Sensation as of a stye in outer canthus of left eye.
Female - Uterine displacements. Sore feeling at fundus of uterus, relieved by pressure. Prostration, wants to
lie down all the time. Sensation as if the uterus is soft and feeble.
Food - Great appetite. Tendency to eat far beyond capacity for digestion. Craving for meat, pickles,
radishes, turnips, and artichokes. Craving for coarse food, such as pickles, radishes, turnips, etc. Canine
hunger with torpid liver.
Head - Feels light-headed, tipsy.
Heart - Action of the heart labored. Increased action of the heart with distention of the stomach.
Limbs - Hands cold, shrunken. Lies with the legs drawn up. Very faint, as if top of head were congested.
Twitching of the muscles.
Liver - Sensation as if the liver were small and hard, as if bile were deficient.
Lungs - Breathing labored. Sensation as if the right lung were small and hard.
Kidneys - Urinates frequently day and night. Straw colored urine.
Mouth - Dryness of the mouth.
Rectum - Burning in rectum. Constipation.
Sensations - A feeling as if the right lung and liver were small and hard, pain beneath right scapula. The
patient lies with the legs drawn up. Shivering as if the blood turned to cold water. Uterus feels soft.
Skin - Clammy and sticky.
Stomach - Catarrhal condition in the stomach, increases the patient's hunger. Gnawing, hungry, and faint
feeling in the epigastrium. Distention of the stomach and epigastrium, burning.
Temperature - Cold chills, as if blood were ice water (Aeon.). Chills run down back Cold-water feeling between
shoulders (Am-m.). Skin clammy and sticky. Nigh sweat (Chin.).
Vertigo - Tipsy feeling, a swimming of ths head, light-headed.
COMMENTS - According to Hale, Abie: c. cured a light-headed feeling, attendee with a gnawing, hungry and
faint feelinj at epigastrium. A craving hunger which, i gratified, was followed by distention of th
stomach and hard beating of the heart.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aeon. Chin. Am-m.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Abies Nigra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - abies-n. Abies nigra. Black Spruce. Double Spruce. Picea mariana. Picea nigra. N. O.
Coniferae. Pinaceae. North America. Tincture of gum. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL- Backaches. Belching. Bone aches. Chills. Constipation. Coughs. Depression. Dyspepsia.
Fevers. Heartbum. Hemorrhages. Hypochondriasis. Indigestion. Intermittent fever. Malaria. Menses, delayed.
Rheumatic pains. Stomach, disorders. Stomach, pain. Tachycardia. Water brash.
HOMEOPATHIC - Abies-n has been used in many diseases, when they are associated with stomach
symptoms. The dyspepsia caused by abuse of tea or tobacco has been cured by it.
Characteristic sensation in the cardiac end of the stomach or in the esophagus, “as if a hard body, as a hard-
boiled egg had lodged there.” Where this symptom is present, whether in dyspepsia or lung disease with or
without hemoptysis, constipation, Abies- n. will be the most likely remedy. Patients describe this sensation, as
if a hard lump is felt in the pit of the stomach or in the lung, which he wants to cough out.
Wakeful at night with hunger. Rheumatic pains and aching in bones. Abies-n in dyspeptic troubles of the
elderly with functional heart symptoms, also after tea or tobacco. Distress in the head with flushed cheeks
often accompanies the dyspeptic symptoms of this remedy.
“Pain in the stomach always comes after eating,” said Guernsey. Constipation. Worse after eating. In
lung disease when the sensation is as if there was a hard substance to be coughed up. Feeling in the
 epigastrium as if food were lying there (Puls., Bry.).
MIND - Very low spirited, unable to think or study. Hypochondriasis.
Back - Pain in small of back. Rheumatic pains and aching in bones.
Causations - Useful in indigestion in those who abuse tea drinking, tobacco smoking or tobacco chewing.
Chest - Painful sensation, as if something were lodged in the chest and had to be coughed up. Lungs feel
compressed, cannot be fully expanded. Worse from coughing. Water brash succeeds cough. Choking
sensation in throat.
Ears - Pain in left external meatus.
Female - Menstruation delayed for three months.
Food - Exceedingly hungry and wakeful at night. Great cravingforfoodat noon and night. Total loss of
appetite in morning.
Head - Hot with flushed cheeks. Low-spirited. Dull during the day, wakeful at night. Unable to think.
Heart - Heavy, slow beating of heart. Sharp, cutting pain in heart. Tachycardia and bradycardia.
Limbs - Rheumatic pains and aching in the bones.
Lungs - Easily gets out of breath. Difficult breathing, worse lying down.
Modalities - Worse after eating.
Mouth - Offensive breath.
Rectum - Constipation.
Sleep - Sleepy during the day. Wakeful and restless at night with hunger. Very bad dreams.
Stomach - Indigestion. Belchings. Pain in stomach always comes on after eating. Sensation of a lump that
hurts. As if a hard-boiled egg had lodged in the cardiac end of stomach. Distressing constriction just above
the pit of the stomach, as if everything were knotted up.
Temperature - Alternate heat and cold. Chronic intermittent fever with pain in stomach.
Throat - Choking sensation in throat. Sensation of something sticking in esophagus toward its lower end.
COMMENTS - Clarke after giving Abies nigra to one patient, he noted that the coldness around the stomach
was removed and general chilliness greatly lessened.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Lump in stomach. Chin.. Bry. Puls. (2) Nux-v. Kali-c. Chin., has the lump under
the sternum, but higher up. (3) AlsootherConifers - Thuj., Sabina, Cupressus - painful indigestion.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Abroma Augusta Radix
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - abrom-aug. Abroma augusta ' radix. Olat kambal. Perennial Indian hemp. Devil'sCotton.
Abrome. N. O. Sterculiaceae. Tincture of leaves, roots. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aching, pains. Amenorrhea. Colicky, pains. Constipation. Cough. Debility. Dysmenorrhea.
Dysentery. Edema. Emaciation. Headaches. Hoarseness. Insomnia. Itching. Leucorrhea. Malaise.
Menstrual, colic. Menorrhagia. Throbbing, pains. Vertigo.
HERBAL - Abroma augusta, indigenous tó India, is an evergreen large shrub or a small tree with drooping
branches. It grows wild in India's warmer regions, but is also cultivated in gardens for its beautiful deep scarlet
flowers. The roots and bark are used as an emmenagogue.
HOMEOPATHIC - The proving, carried out from 1970-1973 by the Central Council for Research in
Homoeopathy, consisted of 40 provers and 20 controls. Dr. D. N. Ray. of Calcutta, made a short proving in
1919 and Kishore made one in 1972, all provings are included in the drug picture.
General debility. Feeling of weakness after stool. Tingling and numbness, feeling of warmth and burning.
Trembling, lethargy, weakness, uneasiness, drowsiness and . heaviness in the whole body.
Body aches particularly in the joints, aggravated by rest, during movement. Malaise, with feverishness, cough.
Emaciation and weight loss with general debility. Edema and puffiness in the whole body, first appeared in
face and eyes with eruption, aggravated from heat or motion, ameliorated by cold, rest.
MIND - Peevishness. Anxiety. Restless with dislike for everything. Quarrelsome. Easily
excited and easily angered. Contradiction is unbearable. Irritability, moroseness. Indifference, vacantness.
Sadness of mind. Feeling of joy. Immoderate laughing from trifles.
Abdomen - Griping pain in the abdomen with dysentery, aggravated in the evening. Colicky pains. Dislikes
a tight band around the abdomen, brings on suffocative attack, with soreness near right hypochondrium.
Rumbling and ineffectual urging for stool. Flatulent distension of upper abdomen with moderate urging
before stool. Feeling of warmth in upper abdomen.
Back - Aching, lameness and sharp pains in lumbar region. Bubbling sensation in left lumbar region. Sore,
bruised pain in lumbar region, worse morning on rising, better motion. Aching or tingling in the nape of the
 neck. Pressure and constriction in the nape of neck.
Chest - Aching pain in the whole chest. Burning in chest. Sharp pain in left infra-clavicular region with catching
of breath. Stinging pain in left side of the chest. Aching pain in the left intercostal muscles. Catching pain in
the right lower chest with weakness and tiredness, worse movement.
Ears - Pain and soreness with stitching sensation inside the right ear, worse evening, better during the day.
Eyes - Redness of eyes without pain or discharge, ameliorated from cold application. Itching in the right eye
with redness, better rubbing the eyes. As if foreign body is lodged in the eyes. Heaviness of upper eyelids.
Watery exudation with redness of left eyeball. Burning in eyeballs with vertigo. Sore pain, aggravated by
sunlight, ameliorated by closing the eyes. Aching pain in right eyelid. Agglutination, redness and swelling of
eyelids.
Female - Amenorrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Menses scanty or copious. Menstrual colic and heavy bleeding.
Pain in the lower abdomen, with delayed and scanty menstrual flow. Menses with dark colored clots.
Leucorrhea with pain in the back and lower abdomen. Yellowish, white offensive leucorrhea. Leucorrhea,
thin,
acrid, whitish discharge. Pain in right ovarian region, better hot applications. Thin, profuse leucorrhea in
emaciated young girls.
Food - Voracious appetite. Loss of appetite. Dislike for food with heaviness of abdomen. Increased thirst for
cold water with dry mouth. Thirstlessness. Aversion to smoking. Aversion to starchy food. Desire for fish, juicy
things. Desire for sweets, Desires coffee and tea. Desires salty foods, sour foods.
Head - Headaches with heaviness and dull aching pains. Aching and throbbing pains. Burning sensation,
better application of cold water. Tingling pain. Heaviness in forehead. Sharp pain in forehead, ameliorated by
pressure. Bursting pain. Dullness, dizziness, and heaviness in forehead, ameliorated by bathing. Throbbing
pain in temples. Heaviness, aching pains. Dull pain in vertex, warmth in vertex. Sensation as if being pressed
with a blunt object over the supraorbital region.
Heart - Heart, palpitations with undesirable feeling of distress inside the chest, better lying quiet.
Kidneys - Urination followed by weakness and exhaustion. Fishy odor of urine.
Limbs -Aching in the limbs with weakness. Aching pain in shoulder joints. Tenderness in flexor, pronator
group of muscles of forearm. Trembling, burning pain in left hand. Paresis, numbness and tingling in right lower
extremely with anxiety, insomnia and restlessness. Heaviness of limbs. Tiredness in thighs. Aching pain in
the knee joints. Lameness and stitching pain. Drawing pain in calf muscles.
Lungs - Shortness of breath with sense of suffocation, with fever, worse during inspiration, lying down on left
side. Dry and barking cough. Suffocative cough. Cough with expectoration, whitish or yellowish, salty, mucoid,
sticky, thin orthick. Lumpy sputum resembling boiled starch, easily hawked up, worse at night. Must support
the chest during cough. Sensation as if the respiratory tract would be torn out.
Male - Lack of sexual desire in males.
Mouth - Dryness of tongue and lips. Sore pain due to the ulceration of the corners of the mouth. Tenderness
and swelling of gums, worse chewing, better cold application. Aching pain with swelling of the gums, worse
when eating or from any attempt to move the jaw. Stitching pain in gums on right side.
Nose - Sneezing with weakness. Burning in the nose with fever and coryza. Profuse coryza, thin, watery,
bland discharge with sneezing. Sensation of obstruction of nostrils at night. Thick, yellow, mucopurulent
discharge with weakness.
Rectum - Inactivity of rectum. Obstinate constipation. Constipation and headache. Ineffectual desire for stool
and rumbling inside abdomen. No desire for stool with pain in abdomen. Hard nodular stool. Weakness after
stool. Unfinished sensation after each stool. Constipation with hard, scanty stools. Insufficient, and straining
with stools. Stools hard balls like sheep dung.
Skin - Intense itching all over the body, with pimple-like eruption. Dryness and burning sensation of skin,
worse washing in hot water. Dry small vesicular and papular eruptions (resembling prickly heat) with black
discoloration on different parts of the body. Itching without eruptions on the whole body, particularly thighs,
during undressing, night, better open air.
Sleep - Insomnia. Sleepiness. Sleep in short naps. Restless tossing in bed with sensation of warmth,
ameliorated by hard fanning. Sleep disturbed by dreams. Vivid dreams about accidents. Dreams ofrobbers
and dreadful incidents. Dreams of extreme thirst. Dreams as if somebody is calling him by his name.
Stomach - Eructations, ameliorated by passing flatus. Heaviness in epigastrium with disgust for food and
headache. Feeling of emptiness. Sharp pain in epigastrium. Colicky pain in the epigastrium with fullness of
stomach. Nausea while taking food with watery stool, aggravated while eating.
Temperature - Heat all over the body at night with constant chilliness, body aches and sweat, aggravated at
night. Temperature ranges between 99° to 100° F. Thirst at night, with fever.
 Throat - Dryness at night, with great thirst. Hoarseness of voice. Soreness with tickling sensation and dry
cough. Stinging pain in the left side of throat with headache. Stitching pain on right side of the throat with sore
pain. Burning in throat with tickling cough aggravated in the evening.
Tongue - Bitter taste. Stinging pain in tongue, worse at midnight, from warm application. Heaviness and
soreness of tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo and giddiness with headache, worse lying down. Vertigo with nausea.
Vision - Blurred vision with aching pain in lids, aggravated by sunlight and bright light.
COMMENTS - In the female pro vers Abroma showed a capacity to relieve menstrual pains and to reduce the
tendency to heavy bleeding. None of these provers had a history of leucorrhea but during the proving yellowish
white leucorrhoea with offensive odour and pain in the lower abdomen was recorded.
In menstrual disorders it can be compared with Pulsatilla and Viburnum. Pulsatilla patients are generally mild
and weep easily, whereas in Abroma the patient is bad-tempered and easily angered.
RELATIONS - Compare: Puls., Vip., Bry. Mag-p. Ph-ac. Lac-ac. Uran-n. Syzygium.
REFERENCES - Kishore. Ray.

name: Abrotanum Artemisia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - abrot. Abrotanum artemisia. Southernwood. Lady's Love. Artemisia abrotanum. N. O.
Composite. Southern Europe. Tincture of fresh leaves and stems. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Angioma. Arthritis. Ascarides. Brain, congestion. Chlorosis. Contractions. Dyspepsia.
Emaciation. Epilepsy. Gastralgia. Gout. Hydrocele. Indigestion. Influenza. Malnutrition. Marasmus.
Nervousness. Nosebleeds. Otorrhea. Peritonitis. Pleurisy. Restlessness. Rheumatism. Sleeplessness.
Spinal congestion. Typhoid. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - The most prominent symptom of Abrot. is the emaciation in lower limbs. It has also an
intense indigestion and morbid appetite. There are burning, gnawing, constricting pains and sometimes
vomiting of offensive matters.
Marasmus, especially of lower limbs only, yet with good appetite. Marasmus of children. Malnutrition with a
failure to thrive.
The face is wrinkled, pale, old looking, feels cold, blue rings around eyes. Oozing of blood and moisture from
navel of newborn. Nosebleed and hydrocele in boys. Chlorosis.
Phagedenic diseases. Contractions of limbs from cramps or following colic. Sudden aching pain in back better
by motion. Symptoms are worse at night and in cold air.
A peculiar sensation is as if the stomach were hanging or swimming in water. Weak, sickly feeling, when
excited, trembling. Great weakness after influenza (Gels.. Kali- p.). A pressing sensation remaining after
surgery upon the chest for hydrothorax or empyema (Calen.).
Ill effects of suppressed conditions, especially in gout. Tuberculous peritonitis. Exudative pleurisy and other
exudative processes.
Metastasis of states and symptoms. Metastasis of rheumatism from joints to heart, to spine.
Rheumatism from suddenly checked diarrhea. cannot move her head, arms or limbs and suffers much pain,
no swelling.
After suppressed gout. Gout, painful and inflamed wrists and ankle joints. Joints stiff with pricking sensation.
Painful inflammatory rheumatism before swelling. Aggravation of hemorrhoids, when rheumatism improves.
MIND - Feebleness and dullness of the mind. Easily fatigued by conversation ormental effort. No capacity for
thinking, as if all bodily and mental power were gone. Thinks brain is softening. Indolence, aversion to physical
exercise. Gloomy, desponding.
Exceedingly peevish. Ill-natured, irritable and violent. Cross, anxious and depressed. Excited, loquacious, feels
like shouting. Taciturnity. Feels she would like to do something cruel, no humanity.
Abdomen - Weak, sinking feeling in bowels.
Hard lumps are felt in different parts of abdomen. Bloated and distended. Tuberculosis peritonitis. Blood and
moisture oozing from navel of newborn.
Back - Sudden aching pain in the back, worse night, better motion. Pain in lumbar region extending along
spermatic cord. Pain in sacrum with hemorrhoids. Back weak with ovarian pain.
Chest - Pain across chest, sharp and severe in region of heart, rheumatism. Pleurisy, when a pressing
sensation remains in affected side, which impedes free breathing (Aeon., Bry.).
Constitutions - Suited to disorders of newborn children, especially boys. Children with emaciation, especially
of legs. Marasmus. Digestive weaknesses in the elderly.
Eyes - Blue rings around dull-looking eyes. Hollow eyed, sunken features.
 Face - Dry, cold, wrinkled skin, as if old, with marasmus. Angioma of the face. Acne, comedones with
emaciation. Pale, hollow-eyed appearance.
Female - Menses suppressed. Darting pain in left ovary. Back weak with ovarian pain. Twitching in both
ovarian regions, seems to extend to back.
Food - Gnawing hunger and whining. Craving for bread boiled in milk. The appetite is great, ravenous while
emaciating. Emaciation progresses with good appetite. Marasmus. Loss of appetite. Food passes
undigested.
Head - Cannot hold the head up on account of weakness of neck. Brain feels tired after conversation or mental
effort. Veins distended on forehead. Scalp sore, especially left side, itching.
Heart - Metastasis of rheumatism to heart. Pulse weak and small.
Limbs - Lame and sore all over. Inability to move the limbs, due to rheumatism. Pain in shoulders, arms,
wrists and ankles. Joints stiff and lame. Marasmus of lower limbs only. Legs are emaciated. Contraction of
limbs from cramps or following colic. Painful contraction of limbs (Am-m.). Chilblains itch, frostbitten limbs.
Cold, prickling, numb, fingers and toes. Gout in wrists and ankles.
Lungs - Raw feeling. Impeded respiration. Dry cough following diarrhea. Cold air causes a raw feeling in
respiratory tract.
Male - Hydrocele of boys.
Modalities - Better from loose stools. Better motion. Worse in cold air. Worse at night. Worse foggy weather.
Worse wet weather. Worse from checked secretions, especially diarrhea.
Mouth - Slimy taste, acidic.
Nose - Nosebleeds. Dryness of nose.
Rectum - Alternating diarrhea with constipation. Food passes undigested? Rheumatism after suddenly
checked diarrhea. Destroys worms, especially ascarides (Ciña). Protruding hemorrhoids with burning from
touch. Hemorrhoids appeared and became worse as rheumatic pains abated. Frequent urging, bloody stools,
worse as rheumatic pains abate.
Skin - Flabby and loose skin. Furuncles. Falling out of hair. Skin becomes purplish after suppression of
eruptions. Itching chilblains.
Sleep - Restless, frightful dreams.
Stomach - Cutting, gnawing, burning pains, worse at night. Gastralgia. As if stomach is swimming in cold
water. Indigestion with vomiting of large quantities of offensive fluid.
Temperature - High fever, rheumatism. Hectic fever with chilliness, very weakening, and marasmus.
COMMENTS - Characteristic metastasis and marasmus. “Metastasis” is an idea in homeopathy that's not
limited to cancer. Metastasis means something disappeared and reappeared. Rheumatic fever followed by
sore throat is also known as metastasis. If the throat cleared up but was followed by joint problems, that's a
case of metastasis.
Keynote metastasis (Plat.), with a mental state alternating with a physical one. Metastasis in homeopathy is
synonymous with “suppression” if there was outside interference. It's perceiving the alternation of states in the
person. All the rubrics that say “alternation with...” are metastasis rubrics.
Useful for suppression, can correct the . suppression in some cases. Indicated when a disorder has moved
from one area and then to another.
Disorders often go to the intestines. Alternation of constipation and diarrhea. Crohn's disease, colitis, and
irritable bowel syndrome.
A very powerful children’s remedy for malnutrition, malassimilation, failure to thrive, marasmus (Aeth.), colitis
and rheumatism. May have a big appetite and still lose weight. Can be emaciated with poor food assimilation
(lod., Cina). Especially useful when failure to thrive is accompanied with muscular weakness.
Loss of muscular strength, of muscle tone. Flaccid. Difficulty holding up head, in older children.
Metastasis of mumps with a large swollen parotid gland, often metastasizes to the testicles or the breasts
(Puls., Carb-v.).
Clarke cured with Abrot. indigestion with vomiting of large quantities of offensive fluid (in a middle-aged
woman).
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Scroph., Bry., Stell. (2) Benz-ac in gout. (3) lod., Nat-m. in marasmus. (4) Agar,
Chin, Led, Nux-v. Follows well: Aeon and Bry in pleurisy.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Abrus Precatorius
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - abr. Abrus precatorius. Crab's eye vine. Jequirity. Indian liquorice. N. O. Leguminosae.
 Papilionoideae. India. Tincture of trituration of the seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cancer. Conjunctivitis. Epithelioma. Fever. Granular lids. Keratitis. Lupus. Malaise. Ophthalmia.
Ulcers. Tumors.
HERBAL - Abrus precatorius is a climbing plant, a native of India, but has been introduced to the Western
tropics. It was discovered by the natives of Brazil, who gave it the name Jequirity.
The Treasury of Botany notes that Abrus has small nearly globose seeds, which are of a brilliant scarlet color
with a black scar indicating where they were attached to the pods. The seeds are used for necklaces and as
a standard of weight under the name of Raté.
Abrus was the plant employed by Professor Nowack to determine weather and telluric forecasts owing to the
extreme sensitiveness of its leaves to atmospheric disturbances.
HOMEOPATHIC - Abr. acts chiefly on the eyes, skin and mucus membranes. The general effects are
headache, pain in the limbs, fever, and high pulse. Malaise. The roots are used in the same manner as licorice
roots. Eyes - Epithelioma, lupus, ulcers. Granular lids. Purulent conjunctivitis inflammation spreads to face and
neck. Granular ophthalmia. Keratitis.
Head - Headache.
Limbs - Pain in limbs.
Skin - Erysipelatous inflammation of skin. Lupus. Indolent ulcers.
Temprature - High temperature and high pulse.
COMMENTS - Shoemaker, of Philadelphia, gave a series of striking cures with the remedy. He showed it to
be useful for disorders of the skin showing great cell growth, lupoid conditions, epithelioma and sloughing
ulcers.
In a case of ulcerative lupus of both sides of the nose, which was cured by five applications, the first was
followed by an enormous amount of inflammation, accompanied by malaise, high fever, which lasted until the
crust began to dry.
The preparation he used was made by decorticating two hundred grains of the beans by slightly bruising and
crushing them in a mortar, the red hulls were carefully picked from the cotyledons.
The latter were putina bottle and covered with distilled water. They were macerated for twenty-four hours, then
transferred to a mortar and thoroughly triturated to a smooth paste.
Sufficient water was then added to make the whole weight 800 grains. Prepared in this way it was like an
emulsion and was applied to the surface to be treated with a large camel hair pencil or mop.
The application of this emulsion to ulcerated surfaces was almost painless, but soon (often within an hour)
there was much irritation and inflammation, the edges became red and infiltrated, surrounding tissues
edematous and shining.
In the course of from six to twelve hours a desiccated curass-like crust formed which the cracked in twenty-
four hours more and the discharge escaped freely. This went on for five or six days, the quantity of discharge
diminishing. The crust then separated or was removed by water dressing and disclosed healthy granulations.
If any unhealthy granulations were left, the application was repeated.
Shoemaker wrote, “This treatment exercises a destructive action on unhealthy granulated conditions followed
by a constructive change. Also promoting under the protective cover of the exudation which it causes, a rapid
development if healthy shin and tissue.”
But it must be used with caution, for he noted, “It may give rise to erysipelatous inflammation and if used on
weak and irritable patients cause great constitutional disturbances.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Jequiritol in cases of trachoma and pannus to engraft a new purulent
inflammation. The poisons contained in Jequirity seeds are almost identical in their physiological and toxic
properties with the similar principles found in snake venoms.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Absinthium Artemisia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - absin. Absinthium artemisia. Common Wormwood. N. O. Compositae. Europe (Not to be
confounded with Artemisia vulgaris, which is also called wormwood). Tincture of fresh young leaves and
flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Brain, congestion. Chlorosis. Chorea. Convulsions. Delirium. Dyspepsia. Epilepsy. Facial,
twitching. Headaches. Hysteria. Insanity. Insomnia. Impotency. Kleptomania. Mushrooms, poisoning. Ner-
vousness. Opisthotonos. Otorrhea. Paralysis. Restlessness. Spinal congestion. Tremors. Typhoid.
HOMEOPATHIC - Absinthium has been proved, but a number of the symptoms were taken from observations
made on absinthe drinkers. It causes hyperemia of brain, medulla and spine, more intense when combined
 with alcohol. Those who take absinthe are liable to hysterical manifestations.
This drug produces a perfect picture of epileptiform seizure. Convulsions are preceded by trembling, the
patient makes grimaces, bites tongue, foams. Marked tremors of nerves, tongue and heart.
The giddiness and epileptiform attacks are the most important of the symptoms. Sudden and severe,
giddiness, epileptiform seizures. Delirium with hallucinations and loss of consciousness. “A peculiar vertigo
on rising with a tendency to fall backward.”
Attacks occur in rapid succession.
Useful remedy for nervousness, restlessness, excitement and sleeplessness in children. Cerebral irritation,
hysterical and infantile spasms come within range of this remedy.
This remedy has been used for mushroom poisonings. Opisthotonos. Intoxication. Chorea. Paralysis of
inner organs.
MIND - Loss of memory. Forgets what has recently happened after and before convulsion. Wants nothing to
do with anybody. Foolish look on face. Hallucinations. Frightful visions. Kleptomania. Insanity. Patient walks
about in distress, seeing all sorts of demons. There is exhilaration followed by horrible delirium (Bell.), patient
obliged to walk about (Art-v., Cham, and Cina. are better moving about).
Abdomen - Nausea, apparently in region of gallbladder. Bloated around waist and in abdomen, as after ague.
Immense accumulation of flatulence in abdomen, wind colic. Liver feels swollen. Pain in spleen, it feels swollen.
Chest - Sensation of weight on chest. Irregular, tumultuous action of heart can be heard in back.
Constitutions - Younger and elderly patients. Chlorosis.
Ears - Discharge from ears after headaches. Otorrhea, especially after hemicrania.
Eyes - Pupils dilated unequally. Injected conjunctiva. Pain in eyes. Itching. Heavy lids.
Face - Foolish look. Rush of blood to the face. Spasmodic facial twitching. Makes grimaces and foams at
the mouth in epilepsy. Face blue.
Female - Darting pain in right ovary. Premature menopause. Pains in uterus. Chlorosis. Promotes menses.
Food - Loss of appetite, loathing of food.
Head - Confusion in head. Dull occipital headaches (Gels. Pic-ac.). Wants to lie with the head low. Congestion
of the brain and spinal cord.
Heart - Tumultuous action, heartbeats can be heard in back. Tremors of the heart felt toward the back.
Kidneys - Constant desire to urinate. Very strong odor, like horse's urine, deep yellow orange color (Kali-p.).
Limbs - Spasms of the body and limbs. Pain in limbs. Paralytic symptoms. Feet very cold.
Lungs - Cough with liver complaints.
Male - Spermatorrhea with relaxed, enfeebled parts. Impotency.
Mouth - Jaws firmly fixed. Bites his tongue in epilepsy. Tongue trembles, feels as if swollen and too large.
Tongue thick, protruding, can scarcely talk. Tongue trembling, feels paralyzed.
Nerves - Falling down, as in epilepsy. Unconsciousness with distortion of the features, followed by spasms of
the body and limbs. Bloody foam at mouth and biting of the tongue. Stupidity and the loss of memory
afterwards. Opisthotonos, with grinding teeth, followed by stupor. Paralysis of inner organs.
Sleep - Sleeplessness, typhoid with congestion of base of brain. Nervous excitement and sleeplessness in
children.
Stomach - Uncomfortable, irritated feeling of stomach. Food lies heavy. Stomach feels cold and oppressed.
Nausea, retching, eructation.
Throat - Scalded feeling in the thrpat. Sensation as if a lump.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising, with the tendency to fall backward.
COMMENTS - Clarke wrote about a case of epileptic vertigo with signs of constant cerebral and spinal
congestion, nausea and tendency to frequent vomiting, persistent tremors, epileptic attacks of hysterical
character and opisthotonos. Absinth, first in the tincture and later in 3c, completely cured.
Halbert regarded Absin. as of special service in cases of epilepsy where consciousness is not entirely lost.
The characteristic symptoms include a sudden and severe giddiness, epileptiform seizures, delirium with
delusions and loss of consciousness. For some time after the attack there is a loss of memory.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Alcohol, Agar., Artemisia, Hydrocy. acid. Ciña, Cicuta.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Acalypha Indica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - acai. Acalypha indica. Indian Nettle. Cupameni. Indian acalypha. N. O. Euphorbiacae. East
Indies. Tincture of fresh plant. The fresh plant is macerated with two parts by weight of alcohol. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
 CLINICAL - Bloody expectorations. Chest, pain. Coughs. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Flatulence. Hemoptysis.
Hemorrhages. Jaundice. Lung, cancer. Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Acai, is a remedy having a marked action on the alimentary canal and respiratory organs.
The herbal tincture of the Acai, is a specific in hemorrhage from the lungs. Hemoptysis. Acai, is indicated in
incipient tuberculosis with hard, racking cough, bloody expectoration, arterial hemorrhage, but no febrile
disturbance.
All hemorrhages are aggravated in the morning. Very weak in the morning, gains strength during the day.
Progressive emaciation, sense of weight in the stomach with sense of burning, flatulence and sputtering
diarrhea.
Abdomen - Burning in the intestines. Sputtering diarrhea with forcible expulsion of noisy flatus. Bearing
down pains and tenesmus. Rumbling distention and griping pain in abdomen. Rectal hemorrhage, worse in
morning.
Chest - Dullness of chest on percussion, constant severe pain in chest.
Constitutions - Tubercular constitution. Hemorrhagic diathesis.
Heart - Pulse soft and compressible.
Lungs - Dry, hard coughs, followed by hemoptysis, worse in morning and at night. Expectorates pure
blood in the morning and dark clotted blood in the evening. Cough most violent at night. Lung cancer with
violent coughs followed by bloody expectoration or pure blood.
Modalities - Worse in mornings. Cough is aggravated at night.
Rectum - Diarrhea. Flatulence and sputtering diarrhea.
Skin - Jaundice. Itching and circumscribed furuncle-like swellings.
Stomach - Burning, sense of a weight in the stomach.
COMMENTS - Dr. Tonnere of Calcutta, India, seems to have been the first to call attention to this plant as a
remedy. It first appears in a small work. Additions to the Homeopathic Materia Medica, collected and arranged
by Henry Thomas, M. D. and published in London in the year 1858:
Thomas employed a 6x dilution in three cases of tuberculosis. In one case, there was a tuberculous affection
of the upper portion of the left lung of two years' standing. Hemoptysis had been going on for three months,
the expectoration had been pure blood in the morning, dark lumps of clotted blood in the evening, and the fits
of coughing were very violent at night.
In this case, all homeopathic remedies had been tried unsuccessfully, then Thomas accidentally discovered
the virtues of the Acalypha Indica, that remedy having been given him by a native for jaundice.
Henry Thomas said, “I prepared the mother tincture upon the homeopathic principle and" took 10 drops, which
brought on a severe fit of dry cough, followed by spitting of blood. After having noted all the symptoms
experienced by myself and finding that they were nearly all similar to those of my patients.”
Thomas gave six drops of the 6x dilution in half a tumbler of water. A spoonful was to be taken every half hour,
beginning immediately at 9 a.m. At 6 p.m., the blood had stopped. He continued this for eight days and the
blood never reappeared. The patient improved and auscultation proved the disease decreased. Thomas was
hopeful to effect a cure.
In one case of passive hemorrhage from the lungs, after Arnica was used with little benefit, Acai, benefited
and then failed, after which the use of Arnica entirely stopped the hemorrhagic flow.
Grimmer stated that “Lung cancer with a violent cough which followed by bloody expectoration or of pure blood,
bright in the morning, dark and clotted in the evening. Dullness of chest on percussion, constant severe pain
in chest. Progressive emaciation with a sense of weight in the stomach with burning. Flatulence with a
sputtering diarrhea.”
RELATIONS - Calc, is an antidote to the Acalypha. Compare: (1) Mill., Phos.. Acet-ac., Kali-n. (2) Also,
compare Meri., Mane, and other Euphorbians. (3) Ham., ip.. Aeon.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Thomas.

name: Accutane
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - accu. Accutane. Isotretinoin. Allopathic drug for acne. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Acne. Allergies. Anemia. Birth, defects. Bleeding. Bruises. Chest pain. Colitis. Conjunctivitis.
Cysts. Depression. Diarrhea. Dry, skin. Edema. Emaciation. Eye, disorders. Fatigue. Hair, problems.
Headaches. Hematuria. Hepatitis. Herpes. Incoordination. Itching. Joint, pains. Liver, disorders. Nausea. Night
blindness. Nosebleeds. Palpitations. Photophobia. Rashes. Skin, disorders. Suicidal. Sun. sensitivity.
Sunbums. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Accutane, a chemical cousin of vitamin A, is prescribed for the treatment of severe,
 disfiguring cystic acne that has not cleared up in response to other drugs such as antibiotics. It works on the
oil glands within the skin, shrinking them and diminishing their output.
Accutane can cause severe birth defects, including mental retardation and physical malformations. Some
people taking Accutane have experienced headaches, nausea, and visual disturbances caused by increased
pressure within the skull. Swelling of the optic nerve.
Abnormal hair growth or loss. Allergic reactions. Chest pain. Delay in wound
healing. Dry nose. Fatigue. Flushing. Liver disorders. Pinkeye.
Stomach and intestinal discomfort. Suppression of growth. Swelling due to fluid retention. Weakness. Weight
loss.
Abdominal pain. Dizziness. Dry or cracked lips. Facial flushing. Incoordination and clumsiness. Headache,
vomiting. Bleeding from the rectum. Severe diarrhea. Inflammatory disease of the bowels.
MIND - Accutane may cause depression or other mental problems. Nervousness. Emotional instability.
Depression. Obsessive and compulsive disorders. Mental retardation. Self mutilation. Aggressive and violent
behaviors.
In some cases, it has prompted thoughts of suicide. Suicidal depression. Some patients taking Accutane
have had thoughts about hurting themselves or putting an end to their own lives. Some people tried to end
their own lives.
Abdomen - Colitis. Bowel inflammation and pain. Pancreatitis.
Blood - Anemia. Bleeding from, gums, rectum, and nose. Changes in blood sugar or cholesterol levels.
Ears - Hearing problems.
Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Night blindness. Photophobia. Vision problems. Decreased night vision. Decreased
tolerance to contact lenses. Swelling of the optic nerve.
Face - Facial flushing.
Female - Menstrual changes.
Head - Headaches.
Heart - Stroke. Irregular heartbeats. Sudden drop in blood pressure (causing unconsciousness).
Kidneys - Blood in urine. Urinary discomfort.
Limbs - Joint pains. Calcification of tissues. Tendon and ligament problems. Peeling palms or soles. Nail
disorders.
Liver - Liver disorders. Hepatitis.
Mouth - Dry, mouth. Cracked and bleeding lips. Bleeding gums.
Nose - Dry, nose. Nosebleeds.
Perspiration - Profuse sweating.
Rectum - Bleeding. Diarrhea.
Skin - Dry. fragile skin. Severe cystic acne.
Rashes. Skin infections. Sun sensitivity.
Sunburn sensitive skin. Delay in wound healing. Abnormal hair growth. Bruises easily. Herpes. Itching.
Changes in skin pigmentation.
Sleep - Drowsiness. Difficulty sleeping.
Stomach - Nausea. Vomiting.
Temperature - Flushing.
Vertigo - Dizziness.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aur.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Acetanilidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - Acetan. Acetanilidum. Antifebrinum. Formed from aniline. Exalgine is a derivative from this
Methylacetanilid and has almost identical action. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Asthma. Collapse. Cyanosis. Edema. Fainting. Palpitations. Thrombosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Acetan, was used as a sedative and antipyretic for various forms of headache and neuralgia
in doses of one to three grains.
Acetan, depresses the heart, respiration, blood pressure and lowers the temperature. Destroys red blood
corpuscles, pallor. Cyanosis and collapse. Increased susceptibility to cold. Albuminuria with edema of the feet
and ankles.
Several cases of thrombosis of the lower limbs from heart weakness have followed its use. Antifebrinum and
Exalgine have produced symptoms of collapse and cyanosis, in some instances fatal, with great rapidity. One
 patient experienced, after taking Exalgine, a sensation that his head was so large that it seemed to occupy the
whole room.
Eyes - Pallor of optic discs, contracted visual field and shrinking retinal vessel, mydriasis.
Head - Enlarged sensation. Fainting. Moral depravity. Given for migraines and in order to reduce fever.
Heart - Weak heart, irregular heartbeat with blue mucus membranes.
Lungs - Difficult respiration, as in a bad attack of asthma. As if the diaphragm ceased working.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Antipyrin., Anilinum, Glon.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Aceticum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - acet-ac. Aceticum acidum. Acetic acid. Vinegar. Glacial Acetic Acid. Dilutions. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ascites. Anemia. Anesthetics, poisoning. Anxiety. Ascarides. Birthmarks. Burns. Corns. Croup.
Debility. Delirium. Diabetes. Diphtheria. Dropsy. Edema. Ebullitions. Emaciation. Fevers. Hydrophobia.
Nevi. Narcotics, poisoning. Sausage, poisoning. Scalds. Scurvy. Skin, cancer. Stings. Stomach, cancer.
Tuberculosis. Varicose, veins. Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Antidotes the effects of anesthesia (Phos.). For dullness or grogginess since anesthesia,
with memory problems or chronic fatigue (Phos., Chlf.,. Nitro-o.).
Keynote waxy pale skin, anemia and severe water brash. The water brash is of a sour regurgitation during
pregnancy (Carbo- v., Nat-p.). Intense thirst, burning in throat, nausea, retching and sour rising as met with in
cases of cancer and debility. Used in the past as a tonic and to increase digestion.
Profound anemia with some dropsical edema symptoms. Great debility, frequent fainting, dyspnea, weak
heart, vomiting, profuse urination and sweat. Hemorrhage from any part. Varicose swellings. Emaciation and
debility. Especially indicated in pale, lean persons with lax, flabby muscles. Dropsy of abdomen and legs,
anasarca, great thirst, pale, waxen skin. Edema, peripheral edema associated with anemia or protein loss
through the urine.
Acetic acid has the power to liquefy albuminous and fibrinous deposits. Dissolves cancer cells.
W. Owens noted that it was useful for epithelial cancer internally and locally. Sycosis with nodules and
formations in the joints. Hard chancre, the lx solution will soften it and cause the formation of pus.
Changes gangrenous ulcers, hospital gangrene, prevents decomposition of animal matter.
There are gnawing, ulcerative pains in stomach, pain and burning in abdomen. Profuse, exhausting diarrhea.
Ebullitions. Diabetes. Scurvy. Putrid and hectic fevers with night sweats.
MIND - Irritable. Very dull and low-spirited. Grieves much, sighs often. Horrible attacks of anxiety with difficult
breathing. Borrows trouble, worried about business affairs. Grieves about his sickness and the children. Does
not know her own children. Forgets what has recently happened. Confusion of ideas. Alternate stupor and
delirium.
Abdomen - Distention of the abdomen, colicky pains. Inflammation of bowels during dentition. Abdomen feels
as if sunken in when lying on his back. Frequent watery stools, worse in morning. Tympanitic. Ascites.
Hemorrhage from bowels.
Back - Myelitis, with profuse urine, the pain in the back relieved only by lying on the abdomen.
Blood - Hemorrhages from nose, lungs, stomach, bowels, and uterus. Passive hemorrhages. Blood
coagulated in veins. Blood vessels contracted. Varicose swellings. Chlorosis, anemia.
Constitutions - Suited to children and old people. For lax, pale, lean anemic persons.
Face - Pale, waxen, emaciated. Expression wild, pupils dilated. Bright red flush on both cheeks. Left cheek
red during fever. Sweat on forehead in spots.
Female - Excessive menses. Hemorrhages after labor. Nauseaofpregnancy. Metrorrhagia with great thirst
after childbirth. Breasts painfully enlarged, distended with milk. Threatening abscess of the breast. Anemia of
nursing mothers. Breast milk impoverished, bluish, sour, child droops, lose flesh, gets marasmus.
Food - Greatest burning thirst, with diabetes or dropsy. Insatiable even by taking large quantities. Thirsty with
dry lips, which peel off in flakes. No thirst with fever. Cold drinks disagree. Loss of appetite. Disgust for salted
things and cold victuals. Bread and butter disagree. Vegetables, except potatoes, disagree.
Head - Blood rushes to head with delirium. Temporal vessels distended. Child does not let its head be touched.
Heaviness and dull pains in forehead and vertex. Headache from abuse of tobacco, opium, coffee, or alcohol.
Kidneys - Large quantities of pale urine. Diabetes with great thirst and debility (Ph-ac.).
Limbs - Emaciation. Edema of feet and legs with diarrhea. Varicose swellings.
Lungs - Hoarse, hissing respiration. Difficult breathing, cough when inhaling. Croup. Membranous croup.
 Irritation of trachea and bronchial tubes. False membrane in throat. Profuse bronchorrhea. Putrid sore throat
(gargle). Hurried and laborious breathing. Rattling in chest.
Male - Weakening emissions, semen passes at stool. Prepuce thickened, fissured, can't be retracted and
itches fearfully. Sexual passion, but feeble erection.
Mouth - Teeth feel dull, breath foul. Scorbutic ulcers, toothache. Sour taste. Epithelium of mouth quite white.
Tongue pale and flabby.
Nose - Nosebleed especially from a fall or blow. Liable to frequent catarrhal attacks.
Rectum - Hemorrhages from bowels. Constipation, with great thirst and excess of pale urine. Chronic diarrhea
of emaciated children. Diarrhea with great thirst and swelling of legs and feet. Diarrhea with colic pains.
Ascarides.
Skin - Pale, cold, waxen, and edematous. Burning, dry, hot skin or bathed in profuse sweat. Diminished
sensibility of the surface of body. Varicose swellings. Scurvy, anasarca. Bruises, sprains. Stings, bites, etc.
Tetter-like eruptions. Nevi, warts, corns.
Sleep - Sleepless.
Stomach - Burning water brash and profuse salivation. Fermentation in stomach. Vomits afterevery kind of
food. Epigastric tenderness. Sour belching and vomiting. Violent burning pain in stomach and chest, as of
an ulcer, followed by coldness of skin and cold sweat on forehead. Stomach feels as if had taken a lot of
vinegar. Scirrhus of pylorus. Indurations in stomach. Cancer of stomach.
Temperature - Hectic with drenching night sweats. Red spot on left cheek. No thirst in fever. Ebullitions.
Sweat profuse, cold. Low fever with night sweats. Putrid and typhous fevers.
Throat - False membranes in throat. Hoarse with laryngeal irritation. Children thirsty, but swallow with difficulty.
Diphtheria. Hissing respiration, with rattling in the throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo with feebleness and fainting.
COMMENTS - A plump and blooming young woman took a small glass of vinegar daily to reduce size. She
soon lost flesh and color. In a month, cough set in with white concocted phlegm, fever. Dyspnea, night sweats,
anorexia, dropsy, diarrhea and death. The lungs after death were found stuffed with non-suppurating tubercles.
A Oeiman, after working twelve months in a vinegar factory, had to leave from indigestion, dyspnea and ready
fatigue.
Equal parts of vinegar and hot water make a refreshing sponge-down for many conditions of fever with or
without perspiration. Acetic acid is often given in drop doses: five drops in four ounces of water, take two or
three times a day. It was also used in the past as a tonic and to increase digestion. Acet-ac. is useful
homeopathically for anemia.
RELATIONS - Acetic acid is antidotal to all anesthetic vapors. Counteracts sausage poisoning. Follows China
off. after hemorrhages. Compare: (1) Am-a. - profuse saccharine urine, patient is bathed in sweat. (2) Benzoin
oderiferum - night sweats. (3) Ars., Chin., Dig. (4) Liatris - anasarca in heart and kidney disease, dropsy and
chronic diarrhea.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Acetonum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-aceton. Acetonum. Acetone. It is also called dimethyl ketone, 2-propanone, and beta-
ketopropane. Dilutions. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL- Birth, defects. Coma. Confusion. Headaches. Menstrual, disorders. Nausea. Unconsciousness.
Vertigo. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Acetone is used to make plastic, fibers, drugs, and other chemicals, as well as to dissolve
other substances. Exposure to moderate to high amounts of acetone can irritate your eyes and respiratory
system, causing dizziness. Headaches. Light-headedness. Confusion. Increased pulse rate. Effects on blood.
Nausea and vomiting. Shortening of the menstrual cycle in women.
Very high exposure may cause loss of consciousness and coma. Swallowing very high levels of acetone can
result in uncon sciousness and damage to the skin in your mouth. Skin contact can result in irritation and
damage to the skin. Dizzy. Light-headedness. Tobacco smoke, smell of nail polish remover aggravates.
Health effects from long-term exposures are known mostly from animal studies, they include kidney, liver, and
nerve damage, increased birth defects, and lowered ability to reproduce (males only). It is not known if these
same effects occur in humans.
COMMENTS - Acetone is used to make plastic, fibers, drugs, and other chemicals. It is also used to dissolve
other substances.
It occurs naturally in plants, trees, volcanic gases, forest fires, and as a product of the breakdown of body fat.
 It is present in vehicle exhaust, nail polish, tobacco smoke, and landfill sites. Industrial processes contribute
more acetone to the environment than natural processes.
REFERENCES Murphy.

name: Achyranthes Calea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - achy. Achyranthes calea. Herb of fever. Herba du Tabardilla de Puebla. N. O. Amaranthaceae.
Mexico. Tincture of the whole dried plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Chickenpox. Encephalitis. Glomerulonephritis. Infectious diseases. Kidney abscess. Measles.
Meningitis. Neuritis. Psittacosis. Pyelonephritis. Rubella. Scarlet fever. Septicemia. Typhoid fever.
HERBAL - In herbal medicine, the plant is used as a diaphoretic and a febrifuge. The mother tincture is
prepared by using the whole, fresh plant, dried.
HOMEOPATHIC - The homeopathic proving is the work of Dr. De Legarreta, on himself and volunteers. Similar
to Aconite in fevers, but of a larger range, also adapted to typhoid states and intermittents. Fever with dry skin.
Temperature between 38°C and 40°C. Feeling of heat, which increases when resting.
Muscular pains in the long muscles. Fatigue with need for rest. Sensitive to change in barometric pressure.
Face red, swollen as after long exposure to the sun. Muscular rheumatism. Muscular stiffness.
Acute congestive states, feverish with torpor and indifference towards the environment. Congestive, throbbing
headache. Dryness and burning of the mucus membranes and of the skin. Acute osteomyelitis in adolescents.
MIND - Desire to be alone in a state of calm, answers in monosyllables. Apathy and indifference towards the
environment. Torpor with sudden starting from sleep to return again to a state of torpor. Mental effort tires him
and he puts it off until later. Chi Idren have nightmares and awake panic-stricken.
Depression. Fearof suffering. Low morale with uneasiness, twinges of conscience, religious preoccupation.
Desire to set his conscience right, begs forgiveness and tends to excuse himself for his errors. Suffocates with
the intense heat, wants immediate relief. Needs to be well covered despite the feeling of heat of which he
complains. Annoyed by light, ameliorated in the dark with the presence of a third, silent person.
Abdomen - Acute epigastric pain from the cold. Acute hemorrhaging pancreatitis. Acute gastritis, colitis,
enterocolitis and cholecystitis. Experiences no need for defecation. Feeling of repletion.
Back - Feeling of aching, bruising heaviness of the back and the loins. Feet and hands burning. Acute pain in
the back and neck. Cold sweat on the back. Torticollis. Lumbago.
Breasts - Acute mastitis. The breasts are sensitive to the touch.
Chest - Oppression with the need for deep, repeated inhaling. Pain in the pectoral muscles, in the intercostal
spaces. Thoracic pain in the pre-sternal and precordial regions.
Ears - Itching, heat and dryness of the auditory canal. The auricle of the ear bright red and tense. Cannot bear
noise. Acute congestive otitis media. Acute mastoiditis.
Eyes - Bright, sensitive to light. Feeling of sand in the eyes. Impression of burning in the eyes, watering. Eyes
bloodshot, giving a terrifying appearance. Eyelids are hot, heavy, drooping, eyelashes turn upwards. Eyes
infected, yellow mucus secretion eased by cold compresses. Painful eyeballs, relieved by pressure of the
lingers on the eyeball. Dacryocystitis, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, keratitis and iritis.
Female - Dryness and burning in the vagina. External genital organs relaxed. Menses sometimes relieve the
general condition. Valvulitis, bartholinitis, vaginitis, metritis and salpingitis.
Food - Needs to drink to slake thirst. Thirst for cold water, which seems to taste bad. Indifference to food,
aversion to solid food.
Head - Severe congestive frontal headache. Beating in the temporal arteries. Strange noises in the head.
Headache worse when touched, eased by compression of the head or by placing a heavy pillow on the head.
Heart - Regular yet slow heartbeats, steady with a low, strong and full pulse. Dry pericarditis. Aortitis, syphilitic
or atheromatous. Aneurysm of the aorta. Temporal arteritis. Arteritis. Myocarditis. Cardiotonic.
Kidneys - Acute glomerulonephritis. Py- eloneph.itis. Kidney abscess. Bladder tenesmus, burning in the
urethra. Frequent, pressing emission of small quantities of hot, clear urine, which when still, takes on a reddish
tint. Urethritis.
Limbs - Acute joint rheumatism. Muscular rheumatism. Acute osteomyelitis in adolescents. Hands and feet
also perspire.
Lungs - Breathing is difficult, breaths short, noisy and fast. A light cough, catarrhal and very tiring.
Bronchopneumonia. Pneumonia. Pleurisy.
Male - Penis hot and flaccid. Scrotum congested with veins standing out. No sexual desire, aggravated by the
cold. Ejaculation rare, erection incomplete. Burning in the urethra after ejaculation. After acute testicular
surgery.
 Modalities - Better from strong pressure. Better calm, and rest. Worse from movement. Worse cold, damp.
Worse on the left, but not exclusively.
Mouth - Hot and dry. Dry, burning tongue. Aphthae, from exposure to the sun or indigestion. Muscular pains
in the masseter and zygomatic muscles, which force the mouth to remain open.
Nose - Nose dry, blocked and painful. Black secretion, relief from flowing. Nosebleed on the left side when
blowing the nose. Maxillary sinusitis. Frontal sinusitis. Ethmoiditis.
Skin - Skin dry, burning, impression of goose flesh when moving. Burning redness of the skin. Malignant lupus
erythematous. Painful dermatitis.
Temperature - Fever after sudden changes of temperature. Temperature level from 38°C to 40°C.
Throat - Dry, burning throat. Needs to swallow often in order to moisten the throat. Prickling in the throat after
a cold drink. Hoarseness, difficulty in speaking in cold weather.
COMMENTS - Achyranthes calea is found in Mexico. This herbaceous plant produces a round stem, which,
while young is green, but which takes on a bluish-red hue When fully grown. The stem is gnarled and rugged,
the leaves oval, spear-shaped and smooth. Small, hermaphrodite flowers with a fruit crowned by a pistil, the
pericarp is fine and membranous with reddish dots.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aeon. - Dry, burning skin, but anxious restlessness with a fear of death. (2) Bry
- Severe inflammation of the mucus membranes, acute prickling pains aggravated by the slightest movement,
ameliorated by pressure. (3) Rhus-t. - Generalized aching. Constant need to change place tongue with red
triangle at the tip, painful stiffness of limbs, skin red with vesicular itching eruptions. (4) Pyrog. - Prostration
and agitation. Dissociation between pulse and temperature. Cadaverous odor of perspiration and discharges.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Julian.

name: Aconitinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - aconin. Aconitinum. Aconitine. Alkaloid of Aconite. Aconitia. N. O. Ranun- culacee. An alkaloid
obtained from the roots and stems of Aconitum napellus. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Blindness. Chills. Convulsions. Deaf. Dyspnea. Ears, noises. Esophagus, spasms. Eyes, strained.
Hemicrania. Hydrophobia. Liver, disorders. Neuralgia. Paralysis. Spasms. Spleen, enlargement. Tetanus.
Tongue, disorders. Trismus. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The knowledge of this alkaloid is chiefly derived from cases of poisoning and over-dosing.
On local application, first there is a sensation of warmth, then burning with sharp pains and itching. Finally
there is numbness and anesthesia.
In one poisoning case, vomiting recurred every two or three minutes and was performed by a sudden jerking
action of abdominal muscles, accompanied by a loud shout, probably dependent on a sudden contraction of
the diaphragm.
Every attempt to swallow was followed by the spasms, like hydrophobia, but they were not renewed by the
sight of water. The slightest touch renewed the spasms.
The numbness, tingling, prickling and heat of the Aconite provings are produced by the alkaloid, but with
increased intensity. Tingling sensation. Tinnitus aurium. Heavy feeling as of lead, pains in supra-orbital nerve,
ice-cold sensations creep up, hydrophobia symptoms. Aconitine should be helpful in cases of hydrophobia
cases, whether of the convulsive or the paralytic kind.
The senses are disordered or lost, including the sight, hearing, and smell.
Symptoms set in with great rapidity and develop with extreme intensity. If recovery occurs it is rapid and
complete. There is relaxation of the limbs and every exertion aggravates the symptoms. Worse by mental
exertion, by agitation, or touch. Erect position causes nausea.
MIND - Anguish with the fear of death. Intellect perfect, even vivid. Flow of ideas sluggish, long reflection
impossible. Power of attention impaired. Feels like one sleeping and dreaming. Forgetfulness and trembling
of limbs.
Abdomen - Rumbling in bowels. Sudden contraction of diaphragm. Liver and spleen greatly enlarged.
Ears - Sense of pressure in ears. Roaring in ears. Complete deafness.
Eyes - Strained feeling in eyes. Pupils dilated (both from internal and external use). Complete blindness,
accompanying dilatation of pupils, sight returning when pupilscontract. Vision hazy with giddiness and nausea.
Pupils insensible to light.
Face - Fullness in cheeks and temples gradually changing to painful sense of tension, formication and prickling.
Face tense and swollen. Creeping sensation in face and forearms. Peculiar drawing, stretching, pressing
sensation in cheeks, upper jaws, forehead.
Head - Fullness in the head with noises in the ears. Head and face ache, often darting pains in face, sometimes
 accompanied by vomiting. Hemicrania has been cured. Weight about head, unable to hold it up.
Heart - On entering a warm room, pulse is more frequent, then sinks far below normal, small, weak intermittent.
Sounds of heart only heard at apex.
Kidneys - Copious diuresis. Difficulty in voiding urine. Dysuria and occasionally retention with hypogastric
pain.
Limbs - Weakness, trembling, burning, creeping, tingling, and numbness of limbs.
Liver - Liver and spleen greatly enlarged.
Lungs - Respiration difficult. Oppressive anguish in precordial region. Sighing breathing.
Mouth - Burning on tip of tongue and lips. Burning, constricting, acrid, dry sensation in mouth and fauces.
Tongue stiff. Taste disagreeable and disgustingly bitter or completely lost. Taste impaired. Teeth more
sensitive when biting. Salivation.
Skin - General formication.
Sleep - Somnolence. Sleep disturbed. Throws himself continually around in bed.
Stomach - Belchings immediately. Severe vomiting, recurring every two or three minutes, from a sudden
jerking action of abdominal muscles accompanied by a loud shout. Nausea induced by erect position. Vomiting
relieves all symptoms. Warmth most marked in region of stomach.
Temperature - Surface cold, sweating and quite pale. Intense coldness. Head and face became suddenly
warm, warmth extended over rest of body, was more intense in region of stomach and was accompanied by
sweat.
Throat - Burning anguish in throat. Constriction and burning from mouth to stomach. Every attempt to swallow
followed by spasms like hydrophobia but not renewed by sight of water. Difficulty of swallowing and a pain in
back of neck and behind jaws in parotid region. Burning in gullet as if a hot coal were there.
Vertigo - Vertigo and confusion with ringing in ears, falls almost immediately. With giddiness, dimness of vision
and muscular weakness.
COMMENTS - Found in all species of Aconite except Acon-1. German Aconitine is amorphous, French
Aconitine is crystalline and 170 times stronger than the German.
Morson's “English Aconitine” is a secret preparation believed to be made from Acon- f. The alkaloid in Acon-f.
differs somewhat from ordinary Aconitine chemically and is called pseudo-Aconitine. The Aconitine of T. H.
Smith of Edinburgh is probably identical with Morson's.
Symptoms often proceed from below upwards. “A tingling, prickling sensation, running up leg to spine and
head and tingling of fingers.” “Ice-cold sensation creeps up from his feet.” Fear of death, anguish intense
chilliness, feeling of sickness, constricting burning sensation, extending from mouth to stomach. Twitchings
and spasms over whole body, especially in face. All symptoms are better by vomiting.
In one poisoning case, the blindness was coincident with sudden dilatation of the pupils and sight partially
returned as the pupils contracted. A heavy feeling as of lead all over the body. All parts except head and
stomach feel as if filled with lead. Neuralgia of fifth cranial nerve. Creeping on face with feeling of swelling and
tension. Pains in supra-orbital nerve were especially prominent.
Postmortem examinations showed the spleen very much enlarged, posterior part of liver dark and almost black.
Kidneys hyperemic.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aeon. (2) Hydrophobia, (rabies) symptoms, Bell., Canth., Hyos., Lach., Fagu.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Aconitum Cammarum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - acon-c. Aconitum cammarum. Aconitum neomontanum. Aconitum intermedium. Aconitum
stoerckianum. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Apathy. Belching. Catalepsy. Eruptions. Headaches. Memory weak. Neuralgias. Paralysis.
Pollutions. Salivation. Subsultus tendinum. Tongue, paralysis. Twitching. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The main symptoms of Aconitine are reproduced in Acon-c. It has been used for headaches
with vertigo and tinnitus. Also cataleptic symptoms, formication of tongue, lips and face. Subsultus tendinum.
Twitching.
Aconitum cammarum has formication that begins on the tongue and lips and spreads to the face and finally
over the whole body, with this there is distortion of features and dry skin. Headache, worse from bending the
body forward. Face pain accompanied by tinnitus aurium and vertigo.
Walking causes weariness and, if continued, causes pains in elbows, knees and hips. Violent belchings,
inclination to vomit without vomiting, spasmodic contraction of stomach and abdominal muscles.
Great sensitiveness to light. Erections and pollutions without voluptuous dreams. Small papules and vesicles
on lower limbs, filled with serous fluid, very painful. Memory weakened, sense of touch diminished.
 MIND - Apathy and indifference. Thought and power of concentration disturbed. Memory weak. Rage. Fear.
Abdomen - Burning in abdomen and sensation of ants crawling around in it.
Face - Black and blue color of face, blue swollen lips. Most remarkable sensation contraction of face.
Heart - The pulse is frequent, afterwards depressed, slow, irregular and intermittent.
Mouth - Paralysis of tongue. Salivation. Fuzzy sensation where the crawling was. Taste and sensation
diminished.
Throat - Voice hoarse and rough. Respiration slow, difficult with sensation as if chest and throat constricted.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Aconitum Ferox
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - acon-f. Aconitum ferox. Himalayan Aconite. Indian Aconite. Aconitum heterophyllum. Bisch.
Bikh. Ativisha. N. O. Ranunculacee. Himalayas, most poisonous species. Tincture of root. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anxiety. Burning pains. Cheyne- Stokes. Chill. Dyspnea. Gastralgia. Neuralgia. Numbness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Aconitum ferox is the most poisonous species known, containing the greatest proportion of
Aconitine from the Himalayan Mountains. Rather more violent in its actions than Aeon, napellus.
Acon-f. was proved by Dworzack, who also proved Aconitine. The Ferox devel-. oped burning pains in greater
intensity than the alkaloid, more intense mental activity followed by greater depression. It is more diuretic and
less anti-pyretic (fever).
In Aconitum ferox, there was marked suffering. Anxiety and fear of suffocation from paralysis of respiratory
muscles, obliged to breathe half-sitting up with head resting on palms of hands. Rapid respiration. Cheyne-
Stokes breathing. Cardia dyspnea, neuralgia and acute gout. Dyspnea. Pain in occiput and neck.
MIND - Very active mind, sequence of ideas rapid, talked constantly, remembered easily. Incapable of any
mental work, even the simplest addition, comprehension and understanding became confused.
Abdomen - Rumbling in bowels, constant gurgling.
Kidneys - Frequent and very copious evacuations of urine
Limbs - Gait tottering, remarkable weakness in lower limbs, especially right.
Lungs - Dyspnea increased to such a degree that he was obliged to breathe half-sitting up with head resting
on palms of hands, constantly feared suffocation from respiratory paralysis.
Modalities - Better cold drinks. Better sitting up. Better warm food. Worse coffee.
Mouth - Tongue almost insensible, feels like a piece of raw leather in month. Tongue covered with a thick
yellowish-white fur. Violent burning in mouth (in two minutes), renewed by eating, better by drinking cold water.
Rectum - Two half-watery, dark, not copious stools.
Sleep - Sleeplessness. On waking, violent burning in mouth and throat, warmth in stomach, dull sensation in
head.
Stomach - Pressure in stomach with pain. Warmth in stomach. Violentdrawingpain in region of stomach and
sacral region, soon spreading over the abdomen, worse by pressure on epigastrium. On pressing in stomach,
an internal, dull pressing pain.
Temperature - Icy coldness of body, objective and subjective, no amount of wraps and external warmth
relieved. Desire to get warm drove him to get out of bed and sit near stove. Tottered to stove, warmth was
pleasant, but vertigo, trembling, oppression and nausea ensued and compelled him to return to bed. Fierce
heat on forehead, cheek and hands with sensation as if numerous glowing hot wires were stuck into him, better
by perspiration.
Throat - Violent burning in pharynx.
COMMENTS - The proving caused a formication that spread over whole body, least noticeable on parts that
had been cold. Worse or excited by, change of temperature or motion. It caused a painful unrest so that he
could not possibly lie quietly more than a few minutes.
Getting up set up all the train of symptoms, which were better immediately on lying down. Benumbed sensation,
as if he had on gloves, on pinching cheeks no pain felt, seemed to walk on woolen carpets.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Curare and Phos. have similar lung paralysis. (2) Achyranthes - Cheyne-Stokes
breathing. (3) Eranthis hym- nalis, Winter Aconite acts on solar plexus and works upwards causing dyspnea.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
