name: Coca Erythroxylon
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - coca. Cocaerythroxylon. Coca leaves. Erythroxylon coca. N. O. Linee, suborder Erythroxylee.
Tincture of leaves. Solution or trituration ofthe alkaloid, Cocaine. The alkaloid Cocaine is the well-known local
anesthetic. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Altitude sickness. Angina pectoris. Aphonia. Asthma. Bedwetting. Chorea. Colic. Constipation.
Cough. Deafness. Debility. Delirium tremens. Diabetes. Diplopia. Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Dyspnea.
Emaciation. Emphysema. Fainting. Fever. Flatulence. Headaches. Heart, disease. Hemorrhoids.
Hoarseness. Insomnia. Marasmus. Migraine. Mountain sickness. Neuritis. Nervousness. Nosebleed.
Numbness. Nymphomania. Palpitations. Photophobia. Rheumatism. Satyriasis. Scrofula. Scurvy.
Sleeplessness. Tinnitus. Trembling. Tuberculosis. Vertigo. Voice, weakness.
HERBAL - The Divine Plant of the Incas, Coca, has been used for centuries by natives of Western South
America as an intoxicant and also as a remedy for “veta,” the condition induced in persons on coming to five
in highlands that is characterized by faintness, throbbing heart and head, and dysentery. Coca is like tea and
coffee in arresting tissue-change and enabling those who take it to undergo unusual fatigues.
HOMEOPATHIC - Complaints related to mountain climbing. Altitude, mountain sickness. Palpitations,
dyspnea, anxiety and insomnia. Dizziness, dyspnea and exhaustion on going to high altitudes, mountain
climbing, airplane flying etc.
Exhaustion of the brain and nervous system from physical and mental strain. Muscle exhaustion. Ringing in
the ears, deafness and also fever (Chin.). Tooth decay. Voice loss. Nocturnal bedwetting.
Emphysema(Queb.). Characteristic sensation as if a worm or small foreign bodies were under the skin,
moving away when touched.
Cocaine poisoning causes a sensation as if small foreign bodies were under the skin, generally like grains
of sand or else as of a worm under the skin.
It is known as Magnan's Symptom, after the neurologist who first described it. His description is “a sensation
as if foreign bodies were under the skin, generally small round substances like grains of sand.”
Korkasoff reported a case of multiple neuritis in which this symptom was present. The patient was a woman
 who was being treated for a uterine affection by means of vaginal tampons containing cocaine. A
discontinuance of these caused the disappearance of the symptom.
MIND - Lively mood, inclination for mental work. Clearness of mind at night. Hurry in movements. Timidity.
Bashful, ill at ease in society. Craves solitude, obscurity and darkness. Irritability on waking in morning.
Confusion of mind. Personal appearance neglected. Deceitful. Sense of right and wrong abolished.
Melancholy from nervous exhaustion. Mental prostration alternating with exhilaration. Mental depression and
drowsiness. Muddled feeling in brain. Want of will power. Forsaken feeling. Loss of energy. Unpleasant feeling
about himself. Slow in finding words to express oneself.
Loquacious excitement with blissful visions. Great mental excitement. Exhilaration, before menses.
Wonderful visions. Hallucinations of hearing. Very changeable mood. Pleasant fancies. Loquacious excitement
with blissful visions. Sense of impending death. Overpowered by indescribable anxiety. Nervousness and
nightly restlessness of children during dentition. Fear of falling when walking.
Abdomen - Tympanitic distention of abdomen. Pressure and tension in hypochondria after meals. Violent
pains with bloated distention. Colic. Passage of much flatulence. Violent bellyache, better frequent discharges
of inodorous flatus.
Causations - Ascending, high altitudes.
Chest - Sudden attack of cramp in chest, became cold and unable to continue the ascent. Intense oppression
in chest. Rush of blood to chest with slight headache. Heaviness and oppression of chest. Pain under
clavicles, worse under left. Transient, shooting, in chest, between third and
sixth ribs, worse during deep inspiration. Constitutions - Suited to old people. Short- breathed people, weakly,
nervous, fat, plethoric people. Children with marasmus.
Ears - Tinnitus. Noises in ears. Ringing, buzzing, and humming in ears with fever. Acute and painful hearing.
Eyes - Pressure and pain in eyes. Aching pain behind eyes causing feeling as if squinting inwards. Diplopia.
Intolerance of light with dilated pupils. White, dark and fiery spots before the eyes. Flickering before the eyes.
Dark cloud before eyes. Indistinct vision soon followed by headache and nausea. Pupils dilated with great
photophobia. Heaviness of lids.
Female - Menses flow in gushes, awakening her from sound sleep. Nymphomania during menses and after
childbirth.
Food - Retards hunger and thirst. Very little need of nourishment, even during heavy work and remarkable
vigor. Great satiety for a long time. No appetite except for sweets. Aversion to solid food. Desires stimulants.
Craving for alcohol and tobacco. Ailments from salt food. Can't eat salty food. Great thirst. Bad effects of
stimulants, alcohol and tobacco.
Head - Fainting fit from climbing mountains. Headaches of high altitudes. Headache with vertigo, preceded
by flashes of light. Shocks coming from occiput with vertigo. Like a band across forehead. Migraine, worse
coughing, better eating, sunset. Pressive pain in occiput. Sensation as if brain was muddled. Fullness and
pressive pain in forehead. Occiput painful and tender to touch, worse coughing. Occipital headache with
chilliness. Violent headache, just over eyes with low ringing in ears.
Heart - Angina pectoris from climbing mountains or over-exertion. Violent and audible palpitations with
flushing. Violent palpitations from overexertion. Rapid pulse with violent sweating. Pulse extremely slow
and intermittent, loses one beat in four. Palpitations with weak heart and dyspnea. Pulse weak and
accelerated, increased arterial tension. Throbbing of
heart against ribs audible. Exhaustion of heart with irregular action.
Kidneys - bine stitches in female urethra before urinating. Frequent desire, with increase, flow. Film on urine.
Urine smells like sweat. Yellowish red flocculent deposits, oily scum on surface. Nocturnal bedwetting. Pains
in perineum at end of urination. Decrease of solids in urine. Urine turbid on standing and covered with a light
pellicle.
Limbs - Weakness of limbs. Feeling of internal cold with numbness of hands and feet. Crawling, numbness of
arms. When walking, takes involuntary quick steps, head inclined forward with vertigo. Rheumatism, coming
from slightest cold.
Lungs - Oppressed breathing at night. Altitudes sickness. Rapid breathing. Want of breath, worse
ascending, high altitudes. Cough from cold air or fast walking. Short of breath, especially in aged athletes.
Dyspnea of those who use tobacco or whiskey to excess. Emphysema. Asthma, spasmodic variety. Senile
asthma. Obstructed breathing and heaviness in chest oblige him to walk slowly. Incessant dyspnea, with
desire to take a deep breath. Hawking of small, transparent pieces of mucus. Expectoration of small limps like
boiled starch, after rising in morning. Hemoptysis. Upper portion of both lungs as if constricted, during whole
day.
Male - Diabetes with impotency (Ph-ac.). Sensation as if penis were absent. Emissions. Spermatorrhea and
 partial impotence. Nervous prostration from sexual excess. Satyriasis. Weakness, seminal emissions with
voluptuous dreams.
Modalities - Better from wine. Better after dinner. Better lying on face. Better quick motion. Better open air.
Better after sunset. Worse from cold air. Worse ascending, high altitudes. Worse climbingmountains.
Worse mental or physical exertion. Worse walking. Worse sitting. Worse salty food.
Mouth - Mouth dry, especially on waking. Peppery sensation in the mouth. Tongue furred. Tooth decay. Lips
blue, swollen, chapped. Lips and gums pale. Dryness
Coca erythroxylon of lips and mouth. Ulceration at corners of mouth. Taste salty, slimy, bitter. Taste lost in
morning. Fetid breath.
Nose - Sense of smell greatly diminished. Nosebleedfrom high altitudes. Nosebleed passing from right to
left. Sneezing, and running of clear water from nose. Heat and irritation in nostrils.
Rectum - Dysentery of high altitudes. Sphincters relaxed. Flatus from bowels, smells like burnt gunpowder.
Constipation from inactivity of rectum, stools dry, like walnuts. Hemorrhoids, painful on walking or sitting.
Urging to stool, followed by natural evacuation. Constipation. Constant desire to stool after gonorrhea.
Skin - Itching and prickling under the skin. Like a worm or insects crawling under the skin, moving away
when touched. Scarlatina-like rash over body. Increased heat of skin.
Sleep - Nervousness with nightly restlessness during teething. Chronic sleeplessness. Inclination to sleep,
but can find no rest. Great drowsiness. Awakens with a shock in brain. Can find no rest anywhere, but sleepy.
Awakes with a shock in brain when lying on back.
Stomach - Empty feeling or full feeling in stomach. Incarcerated flatus, rises with noise and violence, as if it
would split the esophagus. Dyspepsia, especially in hypochondriacs. Hiccough after supper. Active digestion.
Frequent eructations. Weak and difficult digestion.
Temperature - Sense of flushing, especially up the back with palpitations. Chilliness and headache in
afternoon. At night, heat and sleeplessness, with throbbing in arteries. Night sweats. Flushes of heat on the
back and burning in abdomen. Extreme weariness accompanies the fever.
Throat - Hoarseness, worse after talking. Voice loss. Weak vocal cords. Uvula feels swollen, swallowing
difficult. Dryness early in morning. Tuberculosis of larynx. Belchings, rise with noise and violence, as if it would
split the esophagus. Tickling in fauces and pharynx. Hawking of small, transparent lumps of mucus, chiefly in
morning.
Vertigo - Fainting fit from climbing mountains. Vertigo and fainting after exertion. Vertigo with shocks coming
from occiput. Vertigo with involuntary quick stepping when walking.
COMMENTS - Dr. J. W. Springthorpe described a variety of this symptoms experienced by himself and
recorded in a paper entitled “The Confessions of the Cocainist.” He called it “Hunting the Cocaine bug.” “You
imagine,” he says, “that in your skin are worms or similar things, moving along.
“If you touch them with wool and especially with absorbent wool, they run away and disappear, only to peep
cautiously out of some corner to see if there is any danger. These worms are projected only on the Cocainist's
own person or clothing. He sees them on his linen in his skin, creeping along his penholder, but not on other,
people or things and not on clothes brought clean from the laundry.”
Cooper cured a case of chronic rheumatism in an aged woman who had this symptom with the fraction of a
grain of cocaine given in single doses at long intervals.
In a case reported in Lancet, June, 1886, a man who had a 4 percent solution of cocaine applied to a tooth
swallowed twenty to thirty drops of the solution. Half an hour after, he was seized with a feeling of faintness
and giddiness followed by an attack of palpitation with a sense of flushing, especially up the back.
There was a marked diminution of smell, great difficulty in producing vomiting, a scarlatina-like rash over the
body, especially about the neck, dimness of vision, relaxation of sphincters and weakness of limbs. The mind
remained clear, but the pulse was fast, weak and intermittent.
A striking case was recorded in the British Medical Journal of December 13,1890. At a meeting of the Paris
Academie de Medecine on December 2nd, M. Hallopeau presented a communication after distinguishing two
forms of cocaine poisoning: the acute in which the symptoms are produced immediately after a dose and
speedily pass off, and the chronic in which they are due to the prolonged use of the drug.
He then related a case that in his opinion showed that the poisonous effects, while coming on acutely, might
last for a considerable time. On March 7, 1890, a man had about eight milligrams oí hydrochlorate of cocaine
injected into his gum as a preliminary to the extraction of a tooth. Toxic symptoms at once supervened.
There was intense precordial oppression with thready pulse and extreme excitement and loquacity. The patient
walked about the room, hitting out at random with his fists and crying out that he was dying. In ten minutes he
became quiet and the tooth was extracted after which he was able to walk home, but arrived there in a state
of extreme prostration.
 Then ensued a train of nervous symptoms, such as continual headache, intractable sleeplessness, a bad taste
in the mouth with attacks of excitement accompanied by giddiness, faintness, and a sense of impending death.
All brain work was impossible, the patient could not do the simplest sum in arithmetic and was in a state of
profound depression. A sense of formication and numbness in the hands and forearms was almost incessant.
This condition lasted four months. It was two months after the injection before the least improvement was
observed, and then progress towards recovery was very slow.
M. Hallopeau thought the symptoms indicated a poisonous action of cocaine on the nervous centers and
especially the brain. As it is impossible to suppose that so small a quantity of the drug should have remained
in the circulation, he was driven to conclude either that it was stored up in the cells of certain nervous centers
or that it produced in them persistent lesions.
Among other effects observed from its use in dentistry are “mental depression and drowsiness and intense
oppression in chest, dilatation of pupils, acceleration of pulse and breathing and mental excitement.”
W. J. Guernsey quoted in H. P., November, 1888 from Med. Register, August 11, 1888, the experience of J.
E. Shadle, who applied pledgets of a 4 percent solution of cocaine to the nasal cavities of a man of 35,
preparatory to operation.
On each occasion he complained of a “cold, gone, relaxed feeling about the external genitals and a sensation
as if he penis were absent. Towards the end of treatment he noticed a permanent weakness of the sexual
organs and finally seminal losses and impotence set in and continued until the Cocaine was entirely withheld.”
R. K. Ghosh noted experiences with Coca (which he finds in drop doses act better in such cases than in the
potencies) in palpitation and dyspnea on ascending, when arising from nervous causes, especially in
complaints from self-abuse generally.
After the invigorating effects of cocaine have passed off, including the sense of lightness and ability to climb a
mountain without fatigue, or when the intoxication has been carried to a further degree, there is a sense of
heaviness, numbness and drowsiness with a disinclination to move.
Extreme weariness, especially weakness of the legs. Extreme affects from altitude sickness. Fatigue.
Characteristic headache, headaches of high altitudes. Tight headache, as if a rubber band were stretched
across the forehead.
After affects from altitude sickness (Carb- V., Sil., Calc.). Can be used prophylactically if there's a history of
altitude sickness or lung weakness. Asthma aggravated by altitude. Effects of cold, cough from cold air, rheu-
matism from slightest cold.
Excessive secretion of urine with or without sugar. Nocturnal bedwetting. General affect of relaxing the
sphincters. Sensation as if the esophagus would be rent by force of rising flatus. Nymphomania after childbirth
during menses, from irritation of eczema or other disorders of the vulva in satyriasis.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Gundlach discovered the best antidote to be Gels. Compare: (1) Ars., Guar.,
Cypr., Cham. (2) Arn., Calc., Ars. - effects of climbing. (3) Stram. likes company and light, Coca likes solitude
and darkness. (4) Scutel., Valer., Cann-i., Thea, Coffea, Tab.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.Phatak.

name: Cocainum Hydrochloricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-cocain. Cocainum hydrochloricum. Cocaine. An Alkaloid from coca leaves. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Altitude sickness. Angina, pectoris. Asthma. Chorea. Constipation, chronic. Cough. Deafiness.
Debility. Deliriumtremens. Dyspnea. Fever. Glaucoma. Heart, disease. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids.
Mountain sickness. Parkinson’s disease. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Scrofula. Scurvy. Trembling. Voice,
weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms of Coca, and Cocain. are mostly similar. Besides the great usefulness of
cocaine as a local anesthetic, it has specific homeopathic uses, though the symptoms are mainly clinical.
Sensation as if smallforeign bodies or worms were under the skin. Chorea. Parkinson's disease. Delirium
tremens. Alcoholic or senile trembling. Glaucoma. Paralysis.
MIND - Cerebral activity. Talkative. Insomnia. Irrational jealousy. Moral sense blunted. Constant desire to
do something great to undertake vast feats of strength. Sees and feels bugs and worms. Frightful persecu-
tory hallucinations. Hallucinations of hearing. Thinks he hears unpleasant talk about himself. Personal
appearance neglected.
Eyes - Glaucoma, increased tension, decreased corneal sensibility. Eyes staring, expressionless.
Head - Throbbing and bursting sensation. Pupils dilated. Hearing greatly increased. Roaring and noises in
head.
 Nerves - Parkinson's disease, chorea, alcoholic tremors and senile trembling. Local sensory paralysis.
Formication and numbness in hands and forearms.
Sensations - As if a small foreign body or a worm under the skin, seeing and feeling of bugs on his own person
and on his clothes and as if parts of the body were absent (more pronounced in Cocain. than Coca.).
Sleep - Restless, cannot sleep for hours after retiring.
Stomach - Loss of appetite for solid food, likes sweets. Hemorrhages from bowels, stomach.
Temperature - Coldness with intense pallor. Throat - Dry, burning, tickling, constricted, paralysis of muscles
of deglutition. Speech difficult.
RELATIONS - Antidote to disagreeable effects occasionally resulting from injection of cocaine into skin or
gums, drop doses of nitro-glycer. 1% sol. Compare: (1) Coca. (2) Stovain - an analgesic, a vaso-motor dilator.
REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Coccinella Septempunctata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cocci-s. Coccinella septem- punctata. Lady bug. Coccinella. Ladybird. Sun-chafer. N. O.
Coleóptera. Tincture of freshly crushed beetles. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Dyspnea. Face, neuralgia. Headache. Heartburn. Hiccoughs. Hydrophobia. Neuralgia. Tic
douloureux. Toothaches.
HOMEOPATHIC - Neuralgias in teeth, gums, mouth. Uvula feels too long. Awakened by profuse accumulation
of saliva, vomits and complains of sore throat. Hydrophobia (Canth.). Worse by any bright object.
Back - Pain in region of kidneys and loins.
Eyes - Cannot open eyes during paroxysm.
Face - Rush of blood to face. Cheeks red, especially right. Face ache. Pressure and heaviness, especially
over right eye.
Food - Appetite lost.
Head - Dull headache, as from an enlargement of the brain towards the occiput. Tearing and shooting pains.
Pain in forehead over right eye, sensitive to touch from superior molars to forehead. Aching in temples and
occiput. Periodical attacks of frontal neuralgia. Pain worse from any bright object, better sleep.
Heart - Subdued, intermittent pulse, with remission of pain in face. Contracted pulse, during toothache.
Limbs - Icy cold limbs during neuralgia.
Lungs - Dyspnea. Oppressed breathing with disappearance of pain in face.
Modalities - Worse by any bright object.
Mouth - Cold sensation in teeth and mouth (Cist.). Tobacco aggravates the tongue severely. Swollen gums.
Sleep - Nocturnal attacks of pain entirely preventing sleep, but could not sleep even when pain did not appear.
Pain ends in a general heat and sleep of two or three hours, from which he wakes without any pain.
Stomach - Hiccough and burning in stomach.
Teeth - Chronic pain extending from superior molars to forehead. Throbbing toothache. Sensation of
coldness in all the teeth. Painful sensation in back teeth as if they were hollow and air were forced into them.
Pulsative jerking in back teeth.
Throat - Sensation in the throat as though the uvula was too long (Nux-v., when the uvula is bluish and
inflamed).
Vertigo - Vertigo after cessation of toothache.
COMMENTS - Most of the symptoms appear in the teeth and nerves of the face and mouth. Neuralgia, worse
at night, accompanied by icy cold limbs and cold, moist skin, the right side is most affected. Pains extend from
one part to another and may jump from side to side.
Attacks recur periodically, often of brief duration but quickly recurring. Attacks are generally worse at night, but
may be entirely absent in the night. Returning every eight, ten, twelve, fourteen or twenty days.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Canth., Mang. (2) in tic douloureux, Spig., Thuj.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Cocculus Indicus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cocc. Cocculus indicus. Indian cockle. Anamirta cocculus. Menisperma cocculus. N. O.
Menispermacae. A tincture is prepared from the powered seeds, which contain a crystallizable principle
picrotox- ine, a powerful poison. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anger, ill effects. Anorexia. Asthma. Bones, disorders. Bulimia. Cerebro-spinal,
meningitis. Chills. Choking. Chorea. Colic. Convulsions. Coryza. Cough. Cramps. Debility. Dysmenorrhea.
 Dyspnea. Faintness. Fatigue, chronic. Fevers. Grief. Hangovers. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hernia.
Hiccoughs. Influenza. Intermittent, fever. Insomnia. Jet, lag. Knee, weakness. Memory, weakness. Meniere's
disease. Meningitis. Mental, excitement. Menstrual, problems. Menstruation,painful.Mononucleosis. Morning
sickness. Motion sickness. Muscles, weak. Nausea. Night-watching. Numbness. Nursing, others.
Overexertion. Palpitations. Paralysis. Paralytic, pain. Parotiditis. Rheumatism. Seasickness. Sleep,
deprivation. Sleep, loss. Somnolence. Spasms. Spinal, irritation. Sympathetic. Tympany. Ulcers. Vertigo.
Vomiting.
HERBAL - Cocculus has been used from ancient times as a poison for stupefying fish and making them easy
to catch. It produces great disturbance of the sensorium and the symptoms of intoxication in human beings.
Commonly used as an adulteration of beer to heighten its intoxicating properties. A deCoction of cocculus is a
domestic remedy used locally for destroying head or body lice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Paralysis of face tongue, pharynx, paraplegia with numbness and tingling. Numbness.
Sensation of hollowness or emptiness, head, chest, abdomen. As if single parts had gone to sleep. Too
weak to hold up head, stand or even speak. Feels too weak to talk loud.
Symptoms are worse riding in a cars, airplanes, trains or on shipboard, hence its use in motion sickness,
seasickness. Sleep loss and fatigue from travels.
Vertigo and dizziness with nausea and vomiting. Ailments from loss of sleep or nursing of loved ones.
Speech difficult at beginning of attacks of vertigo, afterwards, difficulty in reading and thinking.
Alternating symptoms. Unilateral disorders. Sensitive to cold. Falls down to ground unconscious. Senses
acute. Slowness in moving, answering, wants plenty of time to do everything. Adenitis with cold, hard glandular
swellings. Valuable remedy in hernias, both umbilical and inguinal, is particularly indicated when abdominal
muscles are weak and it seems as if a hernia would easily take place.
Shuddering. Painful contracture of limbs and trunk, tetanus. Tremors of head, lower jaw from excitement,
exertion, pain. Intentional tremors. Twitching of isolated groups of muscles. Spasms, through the body like
electric shocks. Cramps in muscles, in masseters, in abdomen, dysmenorrhea in the heart. Convulsions from
non-appearance or suddenly checked menses.
MIND - Mind benumbed with vertigo, nausea. Mental fatigue from sleep deprivation. Heavy and stupid
feelings. Ailments from loss of sleep. Spacey. Dazed. Night-watching. Things seem unreal. Slowness of
comprehension, must read apassage over several times in order to understand it. Memories are bad or blank
out at times. Memory lost. Distracted easily forgets what he has just thought. When her mind is turned away
from herself her sufferings are forgotten.
Generally very sympathetic to others. Ailments from the nursing of loved ones. Thoughts fixed on one
unpleasant subject. Profound grief and sadness. Sadness as if from insult. Depression. Despair feels as if
incurable. Mild, indolent and despondent in the face of difficulties.
Sits as if absorbed in deep and sad thoughts and observes nothing about her. Indulges in sad reveries. Dwells
on past disagreeable occurrences. Answers slowly reflects long. Tearful chagrin about least trifle. Weeping
spells, especially if they can't function and do the things they want to.
Cocculus indicus
Mental confusion after drinking and eating. Very anxious about health of others, but little concerned as to
his own health. Sudden great anxiety. Anxiety before menses. Anxiety from night-watching. Anxiety during
sleep. Mind is worse from suppressed menses. Weeping during menses.
Fear of not getting proper amount of sleep. Fear of death. Fears the unknown, danger. Especially fear
surrounding health and illness of others. Fear of ghosts and specters. Excitement after hearing horrible things.
Frighten easily from noises. Fear of sudden noises.
Oversensitive to everything. Very sensitive to fear, anger, grief and all mental disturbances. Sensitive
moods, everything worries and offends. Startles very easily. Easily offended, cannot bear contradiction.
Sentimental. Sensitive to noise and touch. Intolerance of noise. Intolerance of any disturbing influence.
Sensitive to insults, slights and disappointment.
Capricious. Vacillatory, doesn't accomplish anything at her work. Excessive irritability, excited by loud talking
or least increase of temperature. Anger from any interruptions. Anger from contradiction. Enlargement of
liver after anger. Starting, with trembling all over body, from slight noise or slight unexpected touch.
Irresistible inclination to sing. Absorbed in reveries. Sensitive to all external impressions. Speaks hastily.
Talkative, witty, joking, dancing, gesticulating. Sees something alive on walls, floor, chair etc. Time passes
too quickly. Alcoholics, reeling, roaring, quarrelsome, singing. Loud cries of despair and irritation, alternating
with stupefaction of brain. Feeling as after committing a wicked deed, with desire to escape.
Abdomen - Bloated with intestinal gas.
Great rumbling in bowels. Colic, flatus, twisting pain with faintness and salivation. Flatulent colic in pregnancy.
 Cramps in epigastrium with difficulty in breathing. Cramps deep in abdomen, instead of menses. Abdominal
muscles weak, as if a hernia would take place. Inguinal hernia is apt to protrude and become incarcerated.
Umbilical hernia, with obstinate
constipation. Pain in abdominal ring, as if something were forced through. Pains in region of spleen. As if
full of sharp stones, on every movement. Emptiness and sensation of hollowness in abdomen. Sensation as
if bowels would fall out. Hypochondria as if beaten. Ulcerative colitis.
Back - Drawing, lacerating or boring pains. Pressure in scapula and nape. Pain in shoulder and arms as if
bruised. Stiffness on moving shoulders. Stiffness in cervical muscles, with great weakness. Paralytic pain in
small of the back. Paralysis from lumbar region downward. Spinal weakness in lumbar region, worse walking.
Weak neck, cannot hold up head. Trembling in back. Cracking or stiffness of vertebrae.
Breasts - Shivering over breasts.
Causations - Ill effects of anger, fright, grief, anxiety, disappointment. Sleep loss. Nursing loved ones. Ill
effects of nightwatching. Overstrain mental and physical, traveling. Motion sickness. Noise. Hot or cold air.
Sun. Tea-drinking.
Chest - Sensation of emptiness or of cramps in chest. Audible rumbling in chest (left side), as from emptiness,
worse walking. Hysterical cramps in chest with sighing and moaning. Cramping, in chest during menstrual
period. Pressure under ribs, better belching. Fine stitches in various parts of chest. Contractive tension of right
side of chest, taking away the breath. Oppression in chest, better after vomiting of green mucus.
Constitutions - Suited to light haired, timid, nervous, persons, bookworms, unmarried, childless women.
Sensitive, romantic girls. Light-haired females, especially during pregnancy, causing much nausea and
backache.
Cough - Cough from choking in throat. Fatiguing, from oppression of chest. Cough worse indulging disposition
to cough. Spasmodic cough, in anemic and hysterical women. Cough from choking in throat.
Ears - Sensitive to hearing, dreads sudden noise. Feel closed (right). Noises as from rushing water. Hardness
of hearing. Pain
as if ears torn out of head with headache. Meniere's disease, ringing in the ears, oozy and loss of balance.
Roaring or ringing in ears.
Eyes - Pain as if eyes torn out of head, during headache. Eyes open and immovable. Eyes dull and glassy.
Eyes closed with the balls constantly rolling about in spasms. Protruding eyes. Jerking of eyelids. Pressure as
from dust in eyes. Eyelids inflame4. Dryness of lids. Eyelids feel as if paralyzed. Bruised pain in eyes, with
inability to open lids at night. Sharp or shooting pains in eyes from within outward. Pupils, contracted or dilated.
Face - Bloated, distorted and cold to touch. Blue margins around eyes. Flushed hot face and head during
vertigo or unconsciousness. Countenance devoid of any signs of mental activity. Heat in face, and redness of
cheeks, even in a cold room. Earthy countenance, with painful expression. Paralysis of facial nerve of one
sided. Lines of face deepened, it seems drawn. Cramp-like pain in masseter muscle, worse opening the
mouth. Prosopalgia in afternoon with wide radiations of pain. Tearing pains. Swelling of parotid glands.
Swelling and induration of submaxillary glands.
Female - Amenorrhea causes mental alienation. Sudden cessation of menses. Menses, too early, profuse.
Menses too often. Menses gushes out in stream when rising on feet on tiptoe. Menses clotted, with spasmodic
colic. Cutting, cramping pain in region of uterus and ovaries, on appearance of menses. Weak during
menstruation, scarcely able to stand. Dysmenorrhea with profuse dark menses. As if uterus were distended,
during dysmenorrhea. Dysmenorrhea followed by hemorrhoids. Clutching in uterus. Purulent, gushing
leucorrhea between menses or in place of menses. Leucorrhea very weakening, can scarcely speak.
Leucorrhea gushing, when squatting and stooping during pregnancy with frequent urging to urinate. Discharge
of bloody mucus from uterus during pregnancy. Hour-glass contraction of uterus with ter
rible pain in lumbar region. Labor pains spasmodic and irregular.
Food - All symptoms and affections, worse eating or drinking. Loss of appetite. Loathing of food and drink.
Disgust for smell of food (Colch.). Nausea when merely looking at the food, at the thought or smell of
food. Aversion to beer, acids, sour things. Aversion tofood. A version to drink, tobacco. Desire for cold drinks,
but eating or drinking anything cold causes tearing in limbs. Desires beer. Worse from coffee. Thirst, without
desire to drink. Confusion and vertigo after drinking, eating. Will eat nothing but bread and water, at other
times eats ravenously. Bulimia. Food tastes as if salted too little, tobacco tastes bitter. Thirstless.
Head - Congestion of blood to head, with mental derangement. Sick headachefrom carriage riding, cannot
lie on back part of head. Pain in occiput and nape worse lying on it, better bending backwards, worse coffee.
Migrain headaches. Headaches unable to bear least light, noise causes nausea and vomiting. Headaches
from working in sun. Headache as if skull would burst. Headache returning at each menstrual period. Sensation
of emptiness or hollowness in head. Opening and shutting sensation, especially in occiput. Dullness and
 confusion of head, worse reading. Heavy head. Convulsive trembling of head from weakness of muscles of
neck. Cramps in left temporal muscles. Trembling of the head. Throbbing in forehead. Tossing of head and
incessant trembling of hands.
Heart - Palpitations, worse quick motion, mental excitement, with vertigo and faintness. Endocarditis. Nervous
palpitations. Palpitations after rheumatism. During an attack of palpitation has vertigo and sensation as if about
to faint. Pulse small, hard and frequent. Pulse often imperceptible, weak. Pulse seldom hard and somewhat
accelerated. Feels pulse beat through whole body during heat, at times palpitation.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate with small discharge in pregnant women. Watery urine. Tensive, aching
pain in orifice of
urethra, between acts of urination. Itching and stinging near fossa navicularis. Involuntary urination during
epileptic attack. Diuresis, during prosopalgia.
Limbs - Limbs go to sleep. Lower limbs are very weak, numb and unsteady. Lameness, worse by bending.
Paraplegia. One-sided paralysis, worse after sleep. Painful stiffness in all joints. Acute rheumatism, pain
springing from joint to joint, with redness, swelling and stiffness. Limbs straightened out, painful when flexed
or vice versa. Trembling and pain in limbs. Clumsy gait. Edema of feet with paralysis of lower limbs. Knees
crack on motion. Humerus feels broken. Soles numb, while sitting. Involuntary motion of right arm and right
leg, better during sleep. Alternation of pain between arms. Pain in shoulder and arms as if bruised. Hands,
numb or hot and cold alternately become numb on grasping objects, trembles while eating. Hands and feet
become cold after change of position. Violent spasms of armstand legs. Takes hold of things awkwardly
and drops them. Bones feel as if they were broken.
Liver - Liver more painful after anger, worse least jar. Enlargement of liver after anger. Sharp pains in liver
region. Pressive pain in hepatic region worse coughing and bending over.
Lungs - Dyspnea as from constriction of trachea, as if irritated by smoke. Choking constriction in upper part
of esophagus, oppressing breathing and inducing cough. Hysterical asthma. Dyspnea, oppressing breathing
and inducing cough. Shortness of breath, on account of tension in abdomen. Quick, anxious and oppressed
breathing. Slow, heavy and laborious breathing. Panting. Dyspnea from pain in bowels during diarrheic stool,
in amenorrhea.
Male - Drawing, sore pain in testes when touched. Genitals sensitive with desire for sex. Sexual desire
increased alternating with decreased. Seminal emissions at night. Itching of scrotum.
Modalities - Better from sitting. Better lying quiet, on side. Better in a warm room. Worse eating or drinking.
Worse
from motion of trains, boat, cars. Worse from motion. Worse exertion. Worse rising from bed. Worse bending
over or stooping. Worse kneeling, walking. Worse swimming. Worse swallowing saliva. Worse from loss of
sleep. Worse from touch, pressure. Worse jar, pain. Worse emotions, anxiety. Worse from nursing others.
Worse at menses. Worse eating. Worse noise. Worse sun, cold, open air. Worse evening, night. Worse
midnight and 1 a.m. Worse warmth of bed.
Mouth - Dryness and burning of mouth and throat. Dryness of mouth at night, without thirst. Metallic taste
with loss of appetite. Coppery, metallic, sour taste after coughing. Taste, sour, offensive. Taste like sulphur,
putrid, nauseous. Food tastes as if salted too little, tobacco tastes bitter. Tremor of lower jaw and chattering of
teeth, when attempting to speak. Foamy phlegm from mouth. Salivation during nausea and vertigo. Thick
saliva. Corner of mouth, wing of nose and tip of tongue distorted. Lips parched and dry. Corners of mouth sore.
Nose - Swelling of the nose. Coryza, with ulcerated nostrils. Very acute sense of smell. Worse from strong
odors. Sense of smell weak. Ulcerated nostrils. Discharge from nose bloody, pus-like.
Perspiration - Sweat from slight exertion, on affected part. Cold sweat now of one, now of the other hand.
Cold sweat only on face. Sweat stands out in drops on face, is now cold and then again hot. Exhausting sweat
over whole body. Sweat in morning, principally on chest. Sweat from pain in bowels. Sweat during diarrheic
stool.
Rectum - Burning pain in rectum with soft, loose stool, sometimes yellow. Diarrhea brought on by riding in
cars or carriage. Diarrhea is better lying on sides. Diarrhea with bilious vomiting. Constipation, with ineffectual
urging to stool on account of lack of peristaltic motion. Bleeding hemorrhoids. Prolapsed rectum after stool.
After stool, violent tenesmus, even unto fainting. Contraction of rectum, during too early menses.
Skin - Skin feels soft, is white and moist. Paleness of skin, wretched color. Itching of skin from warmth. Burning
and itching as from nettles. Great itching, especially in the evening, worse undressing, in a featherbed. Ulcers
very sensitive to touch. Red pimples, like grains of millet. Miliary eruptions or red spots, worse undressing.
Induration, cold swelling of the glands, with stinging pains. Red irregular spots on chest and behind ears.
Pimples filling with pus, and then drying up and disappearing.
Sleep - Loss of sleep, complaints from night-watching, nursing. Slightest loss of sleep aggravates. Coma
 vigil. Insomnia. Sleepless from mental orphysical exhaustion. Constant drowsiness, after loss of sleep, night-
watching, nursing. Sleep deprivation. Spasmodic yawning with hiccough. Sleepless from nursing ofothers.
Sleeplessness from business thoughts, from anxiety and restlessness. Anxious frightful dreams. Sleep
frequently interrupted by waking and starting. Sleep unrefreshing. Maniacal sleeplessness. Dreams are
anxious, frightful.
Stomach - Esophagus is dry, burning. Putrid eructations. Gastralgia from suppression of menses. Violent
cramp in stomach, griping, squeezing, lacerating sensation. Cramps in stomach with flatulence and much
saliva. Motion sickness. Seasickness. Sensation of hunger or emptiness, even to fainting. Nausea and
vomiting from riding in cars, boats or looking at boat in motion. Nausea with faintness and vomiting,
worse on becoming cold or taking cold. Nausea, rising to head or felt in head. Retching. Vomiting of sour
bitter. Bad odor, of vomit, with profuse flow of saliva. Vomiting with headache, pain in bowels. Vomiting on
taking cold, with syncope. Vomiting from cerebral tumors. Vomiting from loud talk. Cramp in stomach during
and after meal. Hiccough and spasmodic yawning. Chronic dyspepsia from prolong study. Morning sickness.
Stool - Small, frequent stools with flatus. Foul-smelling stool, during colic. Hard
stool every other day, expelled with great difficulty. Watery stools, none in night, but comes on directly after
rising from bed. Simultaneous with vomiting, sudden, thin, black, slimy, very fetid stool. Disposition to stool,
but peristaltic motion in upper intestines is wanting. Thin, whitish-yellow watery stool. Fetid or hot flatus,
emission of hot flatus before stool.
Teeth - Teeth feel chilly. Teeth as if long and loose. Pain in teeth, better when biting with empty mouth.
Toothache in hollow tooth, pains only when chewing, even soft food. Toothache in upper incisors. Toothache
with headache and ringing in ears. Drawing pain in dental nerves. Fine drawing pain in borders of teeth.
Temperature - Chills alternating with fever. Chills in evening and shivering. Chilliness with perspiration and
heat of skin. Chills with flatulent colic, nausea, vertigo, coldness of lower limbs and heat of head. Chills with
great disgust at even smell of food. Internal chill with great trembling of head. Upward and downward shaking
chills. Chills running down back, in evening. Nervous form of low fever from fits of anger. Dry heat, the
whole night through. Flushes of heat, with burning heat of cheeks and cold feet. Heat in head, chilliness in
body. Burning heat arid redness of cheeks.            ;
Throat - Constriction in throat, with difficult breathing and inclination to cough. Paralysis of the muscles
preventing swallowirig. Tickling in throat with lachrymation. Tightness in larynx. Voice whimpering and
tremulous. Speech difficult, during vertigo. Sensation of constriction. Pressive pain in tonsils, worse when
swallowirig saliva than when swallowing food.
Tongue - Bitter taste at root of tongue. Complains of dryness of tongue, which is moist and clean. Dry, rough
tongue. Dry tongue, with whitish-yellow coat, without thirst. Tongue coated white and dry upon edges. Pains
at base of tongue when stretching tongue out. Tongue, as if paralyzed, speech difficult or hasty, pains at the
base when protruded. Root of tongue as if swollen.
Vertigo - Vertigo, nausea when riding or sitting up. Seasickness and motion sickness (Tab.). Vertigo and
dizziness, with nausea and vomiting. Vertigo when riding in a car or train. Vertigo on sitting up. Vertigo
worse watching moving surroundings. Vertigo with palpitations, worse in morning, raising head, felt in
forehead. Vertigo from loss of sleep. Constant sensation as if about to faint. Vertigo as if intoxicated.
Vision - Dim vision with black spots before eyes. Dark spots before eyes, though objects appear clearly. While
reading, can only see left half of line of writing. Black spots seen after reading.
COMMENTS - Chiefly affects the right hypochondrium (especially liver), inner hypogastrium, inner forehead,
back, upper arm and the bones of the arm. Irritable weakness. Slowness and numbness over their body (Calc.,
Alum.).
Vertigo and dizziness, with nausea and vomiting. Attacks of vertigo with confusion as if they are lost.
Nauseated with whirling sensation. Sensation as if drunk because everything spins (Con., when turning in
bed). Seasickness and motion sickness (Tab.). Motion sickness brought on by trying to read while riding in a
car or train, or from looking out the window at things going by, from seeing a moving object. Jet lag.
Nerve exhaustion, weakness. Too tired to sleep. Chronic fatigue since loss of sleep or stress. Twilight sleepers,
chronic insomnia with no recollection of sleeping, although they sleep for small amounts. Wake unrefreshed.
excited nervous system (Coff.), worse coffee. All symptoms worse from loss of sleep. Conditions caused by
loss of sleep and night-watching. May be used prophylactically to prevent conditions arising from loss of sleep.
Stinging pains, stitches, constriction in the hands, a pithy feeling. Sensitive to touch. The least jar is unbearable.
Keynote empty, hollow feeling in the body, lungs, stomach, legs. Hollow weakness. Sensation of hollowness
or emptiness in the head or other parts. Sense of lightness of the body. Opening and shutting sensation,
especially
in the occiput. Sinking feeling.
 Paralytic pains or pains as of dislocation. Paralytic weakness, lax muscles. Weakness of neck muscles with
heaviness of head. Migratory numbness. Sensation as if single parts have gone to sleep. Neurological
problems, locomotor ataxia, incoordination, stumbling, lack of control, and the knees tend to give out.
Immovability of parts affected. Ataxia, staggering gait. Paralytic rigidity. Limbs become very painful to flex, but
they often continuously bend them to obtain relief. Rigid limbs, chorea, involuntary motions (Caust.). Cramp,
spasm, etc., coupled with electric-like shooting pain. Faintness from the pain. Joint rheumatism, ulcers,
neuralgic disorders of bones.
Esophageal spasms. In the elderly, spasms can cause food to get stuck, inability to swallow (Caust.).
Sensation of worms crawling in the stomach, pinches and scrapes in the stomach (Coloc.). Inguinal hernias
(Nux-v., Lyc.). Hemorrhoids during menses. Metallic, bitter taste in the mouth. Desires beer. Drunkenness and
hangovers (Nux-v.).
Meniere's disease, ringing in the ears, oozy and loss of balance. Poor vision with weak eye muscles. Dimness
of eyesight. Severe occipital headache, sense that head opens and closes. Flu or mononucleosis with loss of
sleep.
Morning sickness, when they can’t stand the sight, thought and smell of food, especially when they are in the
car (Colch.). Amenorrhea, may have vaginal discharge instead of period. Symptoms may be worse with
menses.
Cocc. cured a case of delirium at onset of menses during first and second days, the patient said, “I always see
something alive, on wall, floor, chairs or anywhere, always rolling and will roll on me.”
A case of “spasmodic, flatulent colic, about midnight, flatus passed without relief,” recurring several nights,
was cured by Cocc. 3x. Lippe cured a case of enlargement of the liver after childbirth, the indication being “the
liver was more painful after anger.”
RELATIONS -Antidotes: Coff., Nux-v. Compare: (1) Picrotoxin - alkaloid of Cocculus - epilepsy, attacks in
the morning on leaving horizontal position, hernia, locomotor ataxia, night-sweats. (2) Symphoricarpus -
morning sickness. (3) Petr., Calad., Puls.. Ign.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
keynote:

Menispermacae. A tincture is prepared from the powered seeds, which contain a crystallizable principle
picrotox- ine, a powerful poison. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anger, ill effects. Anorexia. Asthma. Bones, disorders. Bulimia. Cerebro-spinal,
meningitis. Chills. Choking. Chorea. Colic. Convulsions. Coryza. Cough. Cramps. Debility. Dysmenorrhea.
 Dyspnea. Faintness. Fatigu

name: Coccus Cacti
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - coc-c. Coccus cacti. Cochineal. Dactylopius coccus. N. O. Hemiptera. An insect infesting cactus
plants. The tincture is prepared from the dried bodies of the female insects. They also constitute a well-known
dye. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anasarca. Anuria. Ascites. Asthma. Backache. Dysuria. Catarrh. Coughs. Gonorrhea. Gravel.
Hemorrhages. Heart, disorders. Impotence. Irritation, nerves. Labia. inflammation. Menorrhagia. Nephritis.
Spasrps. Tinnitus. Tuberculosis. Uric acid, diathesis. Vomiting. Whooping, cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Coccus Cacti has sometimes been confounded with the Coccinella septempunctata, both
are insects known as “Cochenille” in French.
Coc-c. causes a catarrhal condition and irritation of the throat, respiratory and genito-urinary organs. Affects
the mucus membranes. Spasmodic morning cough. Whooping cough attacks end with vomiting of tough
mucus. Regular paroxysms or violent tickling, hacking cough ending in vomiting or raising much clear ropy
mucus, hanging from mouth.
General lassitude. The least exertion causes lassitude and tendency to perspire or cough, worse during
exercise. Pain in occiput is worse mental exertion. Intolerable internal itchings, burning like pepper. Pulsation
in different organs. Sensation as of a fluid forcing its way during pain. Spasms.
Spasmodic pains in kidneys with visceral tenesmus. Catarrhal conditions of the bladder. Anuria. Ascites.
Anasarca. Discharges are stringy, including hemorrhages, which are apt to be in large, black clots. Rising
up
causes hemorrhage with passage of large clots from uterus. Periodic symptoms.
MIND - Confusion, better open air. Apprehensive, irritable, fretful. Anxiety after eating. Anxiety from irregular
action of heart. Lively, talkative mood. Excitement after beer. Delusions of being enlarged. Sadness, early
morning on waking. Sadness afternoon 2 p.m. to 3 p.m.
Abdomen - Excruciating pain from left iliac region, extending to the groins half way down the thighs, as if fluid
were forcing its way there.
Back - Coldness in back.
Constitutions - Uric acid, gouty, rheumatic diathesis.
Cough - Cough from rawness in air-passages. Short paroxysms, followed by easy expectoration of globules
of mucus. Suffocative cough, worse first waking, with tough, white mucus, which strangles. Whooping cough
 attacks end with vomiting of tough mucus. Spasmodic cough in morning, worse 6 a.m. or 7 a.m. Spasmodic
cough on first rising. Regular attacks of violent, tickling, racking coughs ending in vomiting or raising
much clear ropy mucus. Periodical coughs, slowly increasing then gradually decreasing in its intensity, better
cold air or cold drinks. Cough worse warm room. Violent cough, caused by brushing teeth, by rinsing mouth,
by trying to clear throat of viscid mucus. Coughs of alcoholics.
Ears - Cracking in ears, when swallowing.
Eyes - Sensation as of a foreign body between the upper lid and the eyeball.
Face - Crawling sensation. Becomes purple, red worse coughing.
Female - Menses too early, profuse, black and thick, dark clots with dysuria. Large clots escape from the
vagina when passing urine, when quiet or when rising up. Intermittent menses, flow only in the evening or at
night. Inflamed labia. Vulva sensitive, worse when urinating.
Head - Throbbing pain with sensation as if fluid were forcing its way. Suboccipital soreness, worse after sleep
and exertion. Headache, worse from lying on back,
better with the head high. Dull pain over right eye in morning. Sensation of a foreign body between upper
lid and eyeball. Distress from cinders in eye.
Heart - Sensation as if everything were pressed toward the heart.
Kidneys - Region of kidneys painful to pressure. Constant urging to urinate, better after passing blood clots
from the vagina in females. Sticking pain along ureters. Lancinating, violent pain from kidneys to bladder with
dysuria. Urine, brick-red sediment, urinary stones, hematuria, urates and uric acid. Deep-colored, thick
urine. Nephritis. Nephritic colic.
Limbs - Sensation as if a fine splinter were under the fingernails.
Lungs - Fauces very sensitive. Walking against wind takes breath away. Shortness of breath. Chronic
bronchitis complicated with gravel, large quantities of albuminous, tenacious mucus, are expectorated.
Constant hawking from enlarged uvula, coryza with inflamed fauces.
Male - Pulsation in glans.
Modalities - Better from washing in cold water. Better cold drinks. Better walking. Worse left side. Worse after
sleep. Worse touch, pressure of clothing. Worse slightest exertion. Worse periodically, from heat, cold
exposure, lying down, night and early morning, awakening, brushing teeth, irritation of throat, rinsing mouth.
Cough worse on waking.
Mouth - Tip of tongue burns like pepper. Sweetish, metallic taste. Salivation, constant desire to spit. Loud
speaking or brushing of teeth causes cough.
Nose - Burning as of pepper in nostrils. Accumulation of thick viscid mucus in naso-pharynx.
Sensations - As if a ball or stone lying in stomach. Raging pain as though a fluid were injected into a small
blood vessel. As if something ascending towards stomach. As of mucus ascending and descending trachea,
as of a plug of mucus moving in chest. As if head would split.
Stomach - Irritation of throat, hawking, brushing of the teeth causes retching and vomiting. Thirst, drinks water
often and
in large quantities. _ . _ ---------- Temperature - Burning, as of pepper. Throat - Sensation as of a thread
hanging
down the back of the throat. Sensation as if uvula is elongated. Tickling in larynx. Any irritation in throat
causes cough, retching and vomiting. Constricted throat or as of a plug lodged in it. Profuse postnasal
discharge. Accumulation of much viscid mucus, hawking it, excites cough, retching and vomiting.
COMMENTS - Coc-c. acts especially on mucus membranes, kidneys (Canth.), and in causing hemorrhages
in disturbing the heart (Cact.). Hemorrhages are apt to be in large black clots, especially hemorrhages from
kidneys and uterus.
Sensation as if a hair or crumb were lodged behind the larynx and as if a thread were hanging down the back
of the throat causing a cough. “Cough, worse in morning, the child awakens and is immediately seized with a
paroxysm of coughing ending in vomiting clear, ropy mucus hanging in long string from the mouth.”
Rapid, spasmodic coughs in periodic attacks. Constant irritating cough. Sense of dry spot or tickle.
Hoarseness. Fatigue of vocal organs. Violent tickling in larynx. Stitching and ulcerating pains below clavicles,
especially left. Whooping cough (Dros., Cupr.), bronchitis.
Lancinating, stitching and pricking sensations. Itching, sticking and biting in various parts of the skin, red spots
and itching pimples. Sharp pains and itching of glans penis, symptoms of the passage of small stones.
General sensitiveness to touch and pressure, rinsing mouth or brushing teeth causes cough and vomiting.
Most symptoms worse from warmth, cough worse entering warm room, throat worse by warmth of bed. Tickling
in trachea and cough better open air. Teeth very sensitive to cold. Catarrh worse on slightest exposure. Catarrh
from autumn until warm weather.
 Berridge cured with Coc-c. a case of gonorrhea, guided by the symptom “excruciating pain in left iliac region
extending to groin and halfway down thigh, as if a fluid were forcing its way there.”
Kunkel recorded the case of a man, 75. who suffered from nocturnal bedwetting up to the age of seven. When
almost 20 he frequently passed large quantities of uric acid and at the same time he began to have symptoms
of chronic catarrh of the colon, frequent scanty stools, much mucus, cross humor, itching anus, threatening of
hemorrhoids but no bleeding.
Insomnia soon followed. Coc-c. 2c and 3c was given without benefit. Aqua calcis did some good, but not much.
In three successive years he was sent to Carlsbad with good results to the intestinal catarrh, the sleeplessness
was untouched.
Gradually all kinds of arthritic symptoms developed, especially in knees. There was occasionally a
considerable flow of urine and the more copious it was the better the patient slept and the less pain in the
joints. The same relief followed an attack of diarrhea.
Four weeks at Assmanhausen caused the excretion of large quantities of uric acid one year, but had no effect
the next and the knee got worse. Wiesbaden helped one year but not the next.
Half a tumbler of Kronenquelle water drunk every morning helped the knee and enabled him to walk better
than he had for a long time. In three or four years, the excretions of uric acid had ceased and the patient's
state grew worse, insomnia recurred, diarrhea became much more frequent.
A fortnight previous to such attack, the patient noticed he had great aversion to butcher's meat. Coc-c. 30c
morning and evening was given. Gradually sleep returned. There was almost daily excretion of uric acid,
sometimes in the form of large shot, the diarrhea ceased and the patient went about his work with pleasure.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Canth., Cact., Oci., Sars. (2) apices of lungs sore, tenacious mucus, Kali-bi. (3)
Many Cactus symptoms, like the pricking and sticking pains, heart disturbances, reappear in the pathogenesis
of this Cactus-fed insect.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Cochlearia Armoracia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - coch. Cochlearia armoracia. Horse radish. Armoracia sativa. Armoracia rusticana. N. O.
Crucifer. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Aphonia. Asthma. Backache .Cataract. Colic. Cornea, spots. Coryza. Eruptions.
Eyes, disorders. Flatulence. Gonorrhea. Gravel. Headaches. Impotency. Leucorrhea. Lungs, edema.
Rheumatism. Scurvy. Strangury. Toothache. Ulcers. Urinary, disorders.
HERBAL - Cochlearia and Cochlearia officinalis (Coch-o), are old-world anti-scorbutics, and the homeopathic
provings have confirmed the old experience. Coch, has the anti-scorbutic properties of the other Cruciferae
and is specially efficacious in scurvy from eating salt. The essential oil is said to be identical with that of Sinapis.
Coch, is useful as a condiment in enfeebled states of the stomach. Raises the vital forces. An infusion of the
root in cider, for dropsy, causes copious diuresis. Locally cures dandruff. Used as a gargle in scorbutic gums
and sore throat. Hoarseness and in relaxed conditions of the fauces.
HOMEOPATHIC - Affects the mucus membranes. Frontal bone and sinus, antrum and salivary glands are
specifically affected by this remedy. Mucus stools. Bloated sensation. Gonorrhea. Leucorrhea. Asthma and
tuberculosis.
The peculiar symptoms are in connection with the teeth. Some violent abdominal pains were experienced.
Colic with backache. Wandering chronic rheumatism. Tearing pains from the belly through to back, down the
back and settling in sacrum.
MIND - Anxiety, driven to despair by pain. Difficult thinking in evening. Irresolution. Melancholy alternating with
merriness. Worse from nervous excitement. Worse from vexation.
Abdomen - Spasms through to back and loins. Borborygmi in morning. Crampy, tensive pain above
epigastrium apparently in diaphragm, better by bending forward.
Back - Pain in back as from incarcerated flatulence from abdomen through to back and down into sacrum.
Causations - Checked foot sweat. Nervous excitement. Cold.
Chest - Chest painful to touch.
Eyes - Traumatic inflammation of eyes and cataract. Lachrymation. Swelling of eyes. Sore and scrofulous.
Spots on cornea. Copious running from eyes. Obscuration of sight for some minutes. Styes. Rheumatic
ophthalmia.
Face - Twitching of left corner of mouth, 4 a.m. Soreness of upper lip.
Female - Stringy black blood passes from the vagina when urinating, also during the night. Menses every ten
or fifteen days. Menses suppressed with chlorosis. Leucorrhea. Since menopause, cramp in stomach.
 Food - Unnatural craving for food with profuse, painless diarrhea.
Head - Pressing, boring pain as if frontal bone wouldfall out. Violent headache with vomiting. Headache, now
one side now the other, worse opening the eyes (wide), but not on reading or motion. Violent headache with
nausea, worse sitting up. Aching, boring pains in head, as if brain bursting. Impaired hearing.
Kidneys - Burning and cutting at glans penis before, during, and after urination. Frequent urination. Increased
desire and increased secretion. Urination difficult, causing burning, tenderness and inflammation of urethra as
in first stage of gonorrhea. Strangury. Gravel. Albuminuria. Uneasiness in region of kidneys.
Limbs - Twitching in limbs. Towards morning, pain in all joints when lying still, worse lying on side, better on
motion and when getting up. Suppressed foot sweat.
Lungs - Promotes expectoration and relieves cough, increases activity of respiratory organs. Dry, hacking,
laryngeal cough, also after influenza cough, dry or loose, worse lying down. Coryza with hoarseness. Mucus
asthma and tuberculosis. Edema of lungs. Throat feels rough and hoarse. Aphonia with blood-spitting, op-
pressed breathing.
Male - Burning or cutting at glans before, during or after urination. Gonorrhea. Impotence.
Modalities - Bending forward better. Touch or slight pressure aggravates many symptoms. Worse evening
and night.
Mouth - Paralysis of tongue. Biting sensation on tongue. Tongue furred white. Very offensive odor from mouth
and lungs.
Rectum - Tenesmus all night until morning, sometimes discharging a little blood. Profuse painless diarrhea
with craving for food. Diarrhea after great nervous excitement. Mucus stools. Involuntary passage of mucus
from anus. Itching and burning at anus.
Sleep - Very refreshing, awoke with clearer mind than usual.
Stomach - Belching and cramps. Belchings of sulphurous odor like garlic. Bilious regurgitations. Pain towards
back, worse pressure on dorsal vertebrae. Colic with backache. Violent cramp from stomach through both
sides around to back. Gripping around navel. Cramp in stomach, pain drives to despair.
Teeth - Dull sensation in teeth, as if they were soft and became bent and moved in their sockets on chewing.
Scurvy of salt-eaters. Dental fistula.
Throat - Dryness of pharynx, larynx and posterior sinuses. Scraping in throat with nausea. Hawking thick,
viscid mucus.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The Cruciferae generally. (2) Can th., Caps., Rhus-t, Sin-n. (2) Arg-n. - diarrhea
from nervous excitement.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Cocos Nucifera
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - coco-n. Cocos nucifera. Coconut. N. O. Palmae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Asthma. Baldness. Bronchitis. Bruises. Bums. Colds. Colitis. Constipation. Coughs.
Dermatitis. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Dysentery. Earache. Eczema. Fever. Gingivitis. Gonorrhea. '
tfluenza. Jaundice. Kidney, stones. Lice.
Malnutrition. Measles. Nausea. Parasites. Rash. Scabies. Scurvy. Skin, disorders. Sore throat. Stonuich,
disorders. Swelling. Syphilis. Toothache. Tuberculosis. Tumors. Typhoid. Ulcers. Weakness. Worms.
Wounds.
HERBAL - Early Spanish explorers called it coco, which means “monkey face” because the three indentations
(eyes) on the hairy nut resembles the head and face of a monkey. Nucífera means “nut-bearing.”
Coconut oil is of special interest because it possesses healing properties far beyond that of any other dietary
oil and is extensively used in traditional medicine among Asian and Pacific populations. Pacific islanders
consider coconut oil to be the cure for all illness.
Coconut oil does not form harmful byproducts when heated to normal cooking temperature like other vegetable
oils do. It has no harmful or discomforting side effects. It is non-toxic to humans.
Root - In Java, a concoction from the root is used to treat dysentery.
Leaves - In India, the hairs on the lower surface of the leaves are used to stop bleeding.
Bark - In Ghana, the bark is used as an antiseptic, to clean the teeth and the ashes are used to treat scabies.
Milk - In Mexico, the milk is considered to be diuretic and is used to combat intestinal worms.
Oil - The Tahitians use the oil of coconut with perfumed flowers to apply to their hair. It is also used to heal
wounds and sprains.
Husk - It is also said in Tahiti that for skull fractures, the husk was used to cover the head and it would fit nicely
and hold the head injury in place until complete healing had occurred. This way the patient was protected
 against any further shock to his head.
MIND - Feeling trapped. Feeling like she is losing her freedom.
Abdomen - Feel bloated.
Breast - Breast soreness. Feels like a pin being pushed through breast. Stabbing, burning pain.
Chest - Tightness of chest. Burning stabbing pain in the intercostal area.
Food - Malnutrition. Craving for sweet foods. Weakness.
Lungs - Gasping for air. Need for fresh air.
Modalities - Worse in cold weather. Worse after vaccinations. Worse after antibiotics.
Rectum - Severe constipation. Diarrhea, explosive. Yellow stools.
Skin - Skin very soft. Dermatitis. Eczema.
Jaundice. Rash. Wounds. Skin of fingers sore, burning and cracked.
Stomach - Nausea. Ulcers.
Throat - Dry throat. Feel like something is stuck in the throat, like a piece of shredded coconut. Croaky voice.
Vertigo - Dizziness before meal time. Vertigo in the morning, on waking. Vertigo after eating. Vertigo feeling
of swaying, feels like going to fall. Vertigo feel drunk.
Vertigo with no sense of balance, has to hold on. Vertigo, with nausea.
COMMENTS - Nutritional studies show that coconut and coconut oil, in one form or another, may provide a
wide range of health benefits.
Kills bacteria that cause ulcers, throat infections, urinary tract infections, gum disease and cavities, pneumonia,
and gon- onhea. Kills fungi and yeasts that cause candidiasis, ringworm, athlete's foot, thrush, diaper rash,
and other infections. Expels or kills tapeworms, lice, giardia, and other parasites.
Provides a nutritional source of quick energy. Boosts energy and endurance, enhancing physical and athletic
performance. Helps relieve symptoms associated with chronic fatigue syndrome.
Improves digestion and absorption of other nutrients including vitamins, minerals, and amino acids. Reduces
problems associated with malabsorption syndrome and cystic fibrosis. Improves calcium and magnesium
absorption and supports the development of strong bones and teeth. Helps protect against osteoporosis.
Supports thyroid function. Promotes loss of excess weight by increasing metabolic rate. Is utilized by the body
to produce energy in preference to being stored as body fat like
other dietary fats. Helps prevent obesity and overweight problems.
Improves insulin secretion and utilization of blood glucose. Relieves stress on pancreas and enzyme systems
of the body. Reduces symptoms associated with pancreatitis. Helps relieve symptoms and reduce health risks
associated with diabetes. Helps protect against kidney disease and bladder infections. Dissolves kidney
stones. Helps prevent liver disease.
Helps relieve symptoms associated with gallbladder disease. Relieves symptoms associated with Crohn's
disease, ulcerative colitis, and stomach ulcers. Improves digestion and bowel function. Relieves pain and
irritation caused by hemorrhoids.
Reduces inflammation. Supports tissue healing and repair. Supports and aids immune system function.
Functions as a protective antioxidant. Helps to protect the body from harmful free radicals that promote
premature aging and degenerative disease. Does not deplete the body's antioxidant reserves like other oils
do.
Helps protect the body from breast, colon, and other cancers. Relieves symptoms associated with benign
prostatic hyperplasia (prostate enlargement). Reduces epileptic seizures. Helps prevent periodontal disease
and tooth decay.
Applied topically helps to form a chemical barrier on the skin to ward of infection. Reduces symptoms
associated the psoriasis, eczema, and dermatitis. Supports the natural chemical balance of the skin. Softens
skin and helps relieve dryness and flaking. Prevents wrinkles, sagging skin, and age spots.
Promotes healthy looking hair and complexion. Provides protection form damaging effects of ultraviolet
radiation form the sun. Helps control dandruff.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aloe vera. Calen.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Codeinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cod. Codeinum. Codeine. Codeine purum. Codeine phosphoricum. Codeine sulphuricum.
AlkaloidfromOpium. Papaveraceae. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Blepharospasm. Chorea. Constipation. Cough. Diabetes. Eczema. Numbness. Pruritus.
Restlessness. Spasms. Stomach pain. Twitchings. Vomiting, pregnancy.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Codeine possesses many of the properties of opium, from which it is derived, but it is
sufficiently distinctive to entitle it to a separate description. Cod. seems to possess in great degree the
exhilarating properties some persons experience when taking opium, though it is not without strong soporific
effects as well.
Disorders of sensation, notably troublesome itching. Marked sensitiveness of surface. Itching with feeling of
warmth, numbness and prickling. Characteristic “Itching with warmth. Itching and heat of face and head. A
sensation of agreeable warmth.”
Trembling of whole body. Chorea. Involuntary twitching of muscles of arms and lower limbs. Convulsive
twitchings of muscles and limbs and especially of orbital muscles, are very marked. Twitchings prevent sleep
at night. Numbness and prickling.
Extreme restlessness. Symptoms are periodic, paroxysmal, at times sudden. Diabetes.
MIND - Great exhilaration of spirits. Depression with desire to sleep, frightful dreams and dull headache on
awaking. Increased or diminished power of fixing attention or applying mind. Confusion of the mind. Depression
with dull headache. Inability to apply mind. Lascivious thoughts. Bewildered on waking.
Back - Neuralgic pains from occiput to back of neck. Convulsions in muscles of back. Sharp pains extending
from stomach and chest through to back, between shoulders, worse on right side.
Bladder - Semi-paralysis of bladder. Quantity of urine increased. Sugar in urine.
Causations - Fatigue and excessive mental excitement causes headache.
Eyes - Involuntary twitching of eyelid (Agar.), sometimes better by rubbing. Pupils contracted. Sudden failure
of vision. On blowing nose sparks before eyes.
Food - Great thirst with desire for bitter substances.
Head - Pain from occiput to back of neck. Skin of face and scalp sore after neuralgia. Dull headache in morning,
gradually diminishes towards noon, when it disappears. Headache with dry lips and constant desire to moisten
them. Headache from fatigue and excessive mental excitement.
Heart - Uneasy feeling about heart. Fluttering and oppression, with great desire to walk in open air. Violent
pulsations of heart and carotids. Painful pulsation when attempting to study or write.
Limbs - Paralytic weakness in arms and legs. Spasmodic twitches in arms and legs. Numbness of hands and
feet, prickling and numb sensation in various parts of the body.
Lungs - Dry cough worse at night. Tickling in larynx and coughing. Short and irritating cough, worse at night.
Copious, purulent expectoration. Night cough of tuberculosis. Troublesome cough with copious mucus and
sometimes purulent, expectoration with nervous excitability.
Male - Sexual excitement during the night, leading to pollutions.
Modalities - Worse by motion and better by rest. Headaches are worse in morning. Restlessness and cough
worse at night.
Mouth - Mouth dry. Unable to articulate. Nose - Mucus discharge with irritation of the Schneiderian membrane.
Entire loss of smell for several days.
Rectum - Constipation with tenderness of bowels, especi ally transverse and descending colon, with some
flatulence.
Skin - Itchy, dry and prickling. Eczematous eruption with troublesome itching. Itching with feeling of warmth.
Sleep - Sleepy and drowsy. Cough disturbing sleep. Twitchings in sleep. Frightful dreams.
Stomach - Spasmodic pain at pit of stomach. Belchings. Empty belchings with acute pains in stomach. Nausea
and vomiting, sometimes preceded by an agreeable glow at epigastrium. Violent spasmodic pain at pit of
stomach (solar plexus).
Throat - Strong pulsations in both carotids Tickling sensation in throat in afternoons and evenings.
Vertigo - Dizziness on blowing nose. When closing eyes objects appear to turnaround.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Agar., Hyos., Am-be. (2) Op. in sickness, pains in stomach and region of solar
plexus, constipation, sexual excitement. (3) Agar. - twitching of eyelids. (4) Ars. - pains in legs, nightly
restlessness. (5) Hyos. - twitching of eyelids after reading. (6) Lach. - sensitiveness of surface. (7) Rhus-t.,
Sulph., Sul-ac. - trembling. (8) Culex - vertigo on blowing nose.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
