name: Cyclamen Europaeum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cycl. Cyclamen europaeum. Sow-bread. N. O. Primulacae. Tincture of the root gathered in
spring. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Bone, pain. Chlorosis. Coryza. Diplopia. Dyspepsia. Enteralgia. Eye, disorders.
Headaches. Heel. pain. Hiccoughs. Menstruation, disorders. Menopause. Pregnancy. Prostatitis.
Rheumatism. Sleepiness. Strabismus. Thirstless. Urethritis. Vertigo. Weaning, complaints. Writer's spasm.
HOMEOPATHIC - Cyclamen has a traditional reputation as a remedy for disorders of the uterus and
appendages. Later provings affirmed this reputation. Large doses produce violent purging and vomiting,
disturbed digestion with very salty saliva.
Cycl. is in many ways similar to Puls., from which it differs mainly in having no relief from open air and in hot
having thirstless- ness as so frequent an accompaniment of
other conditions.
Anemic and chlorotic conditions. Affections of uterus. Gastro-intestinal and genitourinary tracts affected
inducing secondary anemia and various reflexes. Cough, at night while asleep without waking, especially in
children (Cham., Nit-ac.). Sleepiness, morose and lassitude.
MIND - Dull, sleepy and morose. Depression, with weeping desire to be alone. Silent weeping. Grieves,
sadness as if he had committed a bad act or not done his duty. Self-reproaches. Terrors of conscience. Tearful
and broods over imaginary grief.
Ajoyous feeling alternating with irritability. Hallucinations as if two persons were lying in her bed. The room
seems too small. Thinks she is alone and persecuted.
Abdomen - Fullness and pressure. Uneasiness in the abdomen with nausea. Painful on the slightest touch.
Sudden attacks of griping, with pinching. Borborygmi in the abdomen, immediately after a meal. Running in
bowels as if something alive.
Back - Excoriation in the nape of the neck. Aching, with paralytic weakness, or traction in the nape of the neck
and in the neck. Dull stitches in the region of the kidney, worse when drawing a long breath.
Breasts - Air seems to stream from the nipples. Milk in virgin breast or nonpregnant women. Swelling of breast
with milky secretion after menses.
Causations - Ill effects of inward grief and terror of conscience.
Constitutions - Suited to the blonde leuco-phlegmatic subjects with chlorotic conditions, disinclined for labor
and easily fatigued. Special senses enfeebled or their functions suspended.
Ears - Itching in the ears with increased wax. Drawing in the ears. Diminution of hearing, as if the ears were
stopped.
Eyes - Disturbance of vision, associated with gastric disturbances. Dim vision with headache, worse on waking
with spots before eyes. Diplopia. Flickering of various colors. Hemiopia. Sees countless stars. Fluttering,
glittering orblack spots. Squint, especially connected with menstrual irregularities. Convergent squint
after convulsions, left eye drawn inwards. Face - Pale, anemic. Upper lip, as if numb or indurated.
Female - Menses changeable, profuse, black, membranous, clotted too early, with labor-like pains from
 back to pubes. The flow is less when moving about. Dysmenorrhea. Menstrual irregularities with megrim and
blindness or fiery spots before eyes. Suppression of menses after excessive dancing or being over heated.
Leucorrhea with retarded or scanty menses. Hiccough during pregnancy. Post-partum hemorrhage with
colicky bearing-down pains with relief after gush of blood.
Food - Desire for lemonade, sardines, inedible things. Aversion to bread, butter, fat, beer. Disgust for meat,
especially pork. Loss of appetite after taking beef tea or a cup of tea. No thirst all day.
Head - Prolonged migraine. One-sided headache. Headaches in morning with flickering before eyes, better
cold water. Pain in left temple. Brain as if wrapped up in a cloth. As if brain wobbled about while walking,
menses absent or scanty. Frequent sneezing with itching in ears.
Heart - Pressure on the heart, as from congestion of blood. Sensible palpitations of the heart, stitches in the
region of the heart. Frequent palpitations from suppressed menses.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate with abundant emission of whitish urine. Shootings in the urethra, followed
by a sudden discharge of a dark red urine. Urine profuse, watery and frequent.
Limbs - Pains in parts where bones lie near the surface. Pains in periosteum. Shooting pains in the loins.
Weakness of knees. Burning, sore heels, better walking, worse sitting, standing. Chilblains. Cramp-like slow
contractions of the right thumb and index finger, they have to be extended by force. Writer's spasms.
Lungs - Scraping and dryness in the pharynx, causing a suffocative cough. Coughing without waking.
Male - Prepuce and corona glandis feel sore after slight rubbing. Stitches and pressure in prostate with urging
to stool and urination.
Modalities - Better from moistening diseased parts, bathing. Better rubbing parts. Better moving about,
walking. Better warm room. Better during menstrual flow. Better weeping. Better lemonade. Worse cold, cold
water. Worse open air. Worse night, evenings. Worse eating at night. Worse standing. Worse sitting, rest.
Worse fats. Menstrual flow worse sitting. Worse drawing shoulders forward or backward.
Mouth - Taste lost or salty, which is communicated to all food. Saliva salty. Tongue loaded with a white coating.
Fine stitches on the surface of the tongue. Burning on the tip of the tongue. Dryness of the lips, without thirst.
Nose - Fluent coryza, with sneezing. Sneezing with itching in the ear. Loss of smell.
Rectum - Drawing pressure in the anus. Pain about anus and perineum, as if a spot were suppurating, when
walking or sitting. Pressure in the rectum. Discharge of blood from the rectum. Evacuations hard and frequent.
Diarrhea after every cup of coffee.
Skin - Gnawing itching in several parts of the skin. Itching, in the evening in bed. Acne in young women.
Pruritus better scratching and appearance of menses, worse at night in bed.
Sleep - Great inclination to lie down, and to sleep. Nightmares when falling to sleep. Unrefreshing sleep, with
terrible, frightful, lascivious dreams.
Stomach - Satiety after a few mouthfuls, loathing and nausea from the least food afterwards. Nausea felt in
throat. Salty taste, hiccough-like eructation, worse fat food. Hiccough, worse pregnancy, with yawning.
Vomiting of pregnancy.
Temperature - Attacks of chilliness in the morning or evening. During the evening, chill and great sensitiveness
to cold air or to being uncovered. Chilly all over, not better by covers. Febrile shivering and
cold, followed by heat. Offensive sweat. Throat - When reading aloud the voice is
weak. The tonsils and palate are shriveled and white. Dryness in the throat. Burning and scraping in throat.
Sensation of painful constriction in the throat. Nausea in throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo, objects turn in circles or look pale, worse open air, better in a room and sitting.
COMMENTS - Debility, torpidity of mind and body. Dullness of senses. Flickering before the eyes, squint,
especially in connection with menstrual irregularities or fevers. After convulsions, convergent squint, lefteye
drawn inwards. Amblyopia, diplopia, hemiopia.
Digestive disturbances. Saliva has a salty taste, which is communicated to all food eaten. After eating but little,
satiety, aversion to food with nausea in palate and thirst. Aversion to bread, butter, meat, fat, beer and ordinary
food. Craving for lemonade, sardines, inedible things. Frequent vomiting in morning.
Prostatic troubles with stitches and pressure, urging to stool and urination. Menstruation too early, with some
relief of melancholy mood and heaviness of feet. Scanty or suppressed menstruation with headache and
vertigo. During pregnancy, hiccough, loathing and nausea in mouth and throat, complaints after weaning.
Pressing, drawing or tearing pains at parts where bones lie near surface. Chilliness. Itching leaving a numb
sensation. Chilblains, itching and pricking, worse at night in bed.
Eidherr of Vienna gave the best account of this remedy. He noted the more copious menstruation, more
frequent, tooearly, with severe abdominal pains. Accompanied with labor-like pains, flow is excessive, black
and lumpy. Commencement of menses after protracted cessation.
Eidherr's clinical experience illustrates in a remarkable way Cycl.'s sphere of action. In one i nstance a higher
 potency of the same remedy antidoted this effect. He found the remedy especially suited to blonde leuco-
phlegmatic subjects.
The “Sleepiness, morose and lassitude.” and also the vertigo noted by Hahnemann, are prominent in many of
Eidherr's cases.
J. K., 24, blonde, pale delicate skin, pale lips and gums, had menstruated normally until 22, when she got wet
at a picnic just as menstruation was starting. It stopped at once and did not reappear until ten months later
after vigorous use of all kinds of domestic remedies.
The periods were then accompanied by terrible abdominal, labor-like pains, lasting eleven hours. Menses
recurred every two or four months, always with the pains, starting from sacrum, extending along both sides of
abdomen to pelvis.
They were periodical, every one, two or five minutes during which time there was no flow, the blood appearing
after these attacks was somewhat watery.
Other symptoms included slightly edematous eyelids, pressing pain in the forehead and vertigo frequently
changing into syncope. Chilliness of the whole body. Disturbed, unrefreshing sleep interspersed with terrible
dreams. Continued loathing for meat. Longing for salt fish. Frequent vomiting in morning. After partial relief
from Puls., Cycl. made a complete cure.
The ocular symptoms which developed were remarkable. The vertigo and headache were untouched by Puls.,
but quickly subsided under Cycl. 15x.
On their disappearance she saw fiery flames dancing before her eyes, on awakening at night and in the
morning she saw everything double. And she had the hallucination as if two persons lay in her bed and that
the body of the other overlapped hers by half.
Cycl. was discontinued and in two days her sight was normal.
Anna F., 20, blonde, menstruated since her tenth year. In her seventeenth year she suffered from chlorosis,
ever since, menstruation was regular, but lasting only one or two days in a moderate degree. Troubled at other
times by vertigo and pressing pain in forehead and temples, which attacks were ameliorated by foot baths with
ashes.
Appetite poor, little thirst, stool regular, sleeps too long, always sleepy, dejected mood, morose. All
movements, as well as speech, were languid, palpitation. Puls, made no change, Cycl. 3x quickly improved
the headache, vertigo and spirits. After three days, sight became obscured and there was glimmering before
eyes.
A case of hemicrania was cured with Cycl. Theresa F., 37., had menstruated sparingly and irregularly (often
at two or three months' intervals). For four years suffered from violent headache affecting right side of head
and face, coming every 8-14 days, spells lasting 12-36 hours.
During menstruation, the attacks were extra severe. Patient was emaciated, skin, gums and lips pale. Right
eye closed owing to cramps in eyelids. When forcibly opened, a stream of hot tears gushed out, otherwise the
eye was normal.
Under Cycl. 3c the symptoms diminished, but there appeared “glittering sparks before the eyes” and these
remained after all symptoms of headache had gone. Cycl. was given persistently, the periods became regular
and rather copious, and the headaches entirely ceased.
Another case (in a wet-nurse who had just weaned her baby) presented unceasing, violent, stitching pain in
temporal region extending to vertex. Throbbing temporal arteries. Bell, diminished the pain, but vertigo came
on.
Under Cycl. 3x, the headache and vertigo disappeared altogether, but the patient complained of her sight
having become so weak that she did not dare to walk alone. This passed off when the medicine was discon-
tinued and her headache did not recur.
Cycl. cured aboy of violent squinting. Six months before, he had a fall from a table, convulsion followed and
after the second attack the squinting came on. Am. was given and the convulsions did not recur, but the
squinting remained. Cycl. 15x was given and after a few weeks the squint entirely disappeared.
Wurmb cured a case of squint in a coachman with Cycl.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Coff., Puls. The modalities of Cycl. are in general opposite to those of
Puls., the menstrual flow of Cycl. is more profuse while at rest with Puls, the opposite is the case. Compare:
(1) Puls., Ign., Ambr. (2) Ferr. and Chin, resemble it in chlorosis. (3) Crocus and Thuj. in sensation of something
alive in abdomen. (4) Am-m. - menses worse at night. (5) Iris-v. and Kali-bi. (migraine with scintillations,
headache worse as sight returns, Kali-bi. (6) Coc-c. - leucorrhea worse sitting better walking, Cycl. menses
worse sitting better walking. (7)Rhus-t. (enter- algia). Gels, and Seneg. (diplopia), Am. (falls), Bar-c., Calc.,
Canth. (chilly and fever), Cocc. (8) In speedy satiety. Lyc., Nux-v., Sep. (9) In prostatitis and urethritis, Lith-c.,
Dig., Sei., Caust., Lyc., Apisin squint. Alum., sudden vanishing of sight with menses, Sep., Puls. (Puls, scanty,
 Cycl. profuse and dark). ( 10) nausea in throat, Sep. Berb.. pain in heels on standing. Desire for lemonade.
Bell., Sabin.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Cynodon Dactylon
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cyn-d. Cynodon dactylon. Doorba. Grantha doorba bhargavi. N. O. Graminaceae. A grass from
India. Tincture of the whole fresh plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Amenorrhea. Anasarca. Cholera. Conjunctivitis. Diarrhea, summer. Dysentery. Flatulence.
Headaches. Hematuria. Scabies. Ulcerative, colitis.
HERBAL - The Cynodon dactylon grows throughout India, and is used in some of the religious ceremonies of
the country. Popularly known as doorba, the Sanskrit name for this plant is grantha doorba bhargavi. It is an
elegant perennial plant that flowers throughout the whole year.
The freshly extracted juice of the grass is useful for hematuria, vomiting and as an application for conjunctivitis.
A decoction of the plant is used as a diuretic and can be useful for dropsy and anasarca. Chakradatta
mentioned it as being an excellent remedy for scabies and amenorrhea.
HOMEOPATHIC - Jugal Kishore carried out a homeopathic proving on three provers, two men and one
woman. The potencies used were the mother tincture, 6x and 200c. The stock of Cyn-d. was supplied by the
Hahnemann Publishing Co. of Calcutta.
General weakness, more marked in the hands, with difficulty in writing. General lassitude, laziness, aversion
to work. The least physical effort causes pain all over. Mental work causes frontal headaches. Aversion to
noise, but desires jolly company.
Elective action on the gastro-intestinal passages and urinary system. Flatulence and abdominal cramps. Stools
irritating with acrid odor and noisy expulsion. Urgent need to stool. Urethral pain after urination.
Pain in the upper or lower limbs, ameliorated by a tight bandage or by walking. Heat in the soles of the feet
with the need to take the feet out from beneath the covers.
MIND - Irritable, quarrelsome, flies into a rage. Angry without cause. Aversion to noise and does not want to
be spoken to. Desire jolly company.
Abdomen - Flatulence and abdominal distention after 4 p.m. Cramping abdominal pains, with an urge to go
to stool. Pain in the right hypochondrium, which disappears after resting. Heaviness around the umbilicus.
Impression of a ball below and around the umbilicus.
Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Conjunctiva are painfully sensitive. Swelling of the upper right eyelid, worse in the
morning. Eyelids stuck together in the morning. Pain in the eyes in morning after a bath or washing the face.
Food - Loss of appetite, which returns on eating.
Head - Forehead hot and heavy. Pain on the right side of the head and in very localized areas of the body.
Headache after mental exertion or anger.
Kidneys - Involuntary urination while sneezing. Frequent and copious urination. Urethral pain after urination
with feeling of not having finished.
Limbs - Sudden, shooting pain in the back of the left forearm Feeling of great weakness in the forearms and
hands. Aggravation
from typewriting. Pain in the upper part of the body, especially in the back. Pain and restlessness in the legs
when lying down at night, better by rising from the bed or by tight bandaging. Sensation of heat in the soles of
the feet, desire to put the feet outside the covers.
Modalities - Better from heat, eating. Worse in the afternoon, evening. Worse from physical or mental exertion.
Worse predominantly on the right side.
Mouth - Increased salivation with insipid taste. Loss of sense of taste. Dryness of the palate, cannot take sour
or spicy food, better by taking something cold. Red patch on the palate and small red granules in the pharynx.
Rectum - Urgent need to go to stool when rising with a feeling of colic. Urgent need to go to stool continues
during the day. Stools hard, difficult to evacuate. Stools semi-solid, then soft with irritating mucus. Stools,
irritating, yellow and soft. Offensive, acrid stools with noisy expulsion. Much gas passed with stools.
Sleep - Sleepiness after meals. Heavy sleep. Sleep disturbed by pains in the legs.
Stomach - Sensation of heaviness in the stomach after lunch.
Temperature - Feverish, needs to cover himself. Sensation of heat in tips of toes.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Podo. - Diarrhea in the morning, fetid stools, expelled in a rush, tenesmus general
weakness, rumbling and feeling of emptiness in the abdomen. (2) Verat. - Copious diarrhea, abdominal colic,
extreme weakness with cold sweating. (3) Aloe - Abdominal distention, hot stomach, heavy with expulsion of
burning irritating gases. Diarrhea after resting, urgent need to go to stool. Involuntary passing of stools when
 urinating or when expelling wind.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Cypripedium Pubescens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cypr. Cypripedium pubescens. Yellow lady's slipper. N. O. Orchidaceae. Tincture and infusions
of fresh root gathered in autumn. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Brain, disorders. Chorea. Con- vulsions. Debility. Delirium, tremens. Ecstasy. Epilepsy.
Insomnia. Mental, despondency. Nervous, debility. Nervousness. Neuralgias. Post-influenzal, debility. Rhus,
poisoning. Sleeplessness. Spermatorrhea. Styes.
HERBAL - Lady’s slipper has great repute as a “nervine” among eclectics and in domestic practice. It ranks
with Scut, and Valer. Hale noted a strong infusion causes exhilaration followed by calmness and is much
resorted to by women whose nerves are shattered by long illness or excessive indulgence in greentea or
coffee.
HOMEOPATHIC - Indicated in the brainhyperesthesia of children who wake in the night lively and full of play.
Epilepsy from reflex irritation. Trembling and twitching of limbs. Nervousness in children from teething and
intestinal troubles. Debility after gout. The skin symptoms correspond to those of Rhus-t. poisoning, for which
it has been found an efficient antidote.
MIND - Sleeplessness and agitation. Irascibility. Throws emotional fits. Hysterical symptoms. Ecstasy,
preliminary to incipient brain disorder. Indifference.
Constitutions - Suited to nervous disorders from mental over-excitement or reflex nervous excitement.
Nervous weakness after influenza.
Eyes - Stye on right lower lid.
Female - Amenorrhea with hysteria. Great nervous debility and despondency. Irritable vagina, hysterical
symptoms, sleeplessness and agitation.
Head - Child cries out at night, is wakeful and begins to laugh and play. Brain hypersensitivity in young children
often the result of over stimulation of brain. Hydrocephaloid symptoms, result of long, exhausting diarrhea,
sleeplessness.
Headaches of elderly people and during menopausal.
Male - Spermatorrhea with great nervous prostration and dejection of spirits.
Sleep - Sleeplessness with desire to talk. A constant crowding of pleasant ideas with restlessness of body.
Ecstasy, children awaken in night from sleep “wide-awake,” unnaturally playful, with no desire to go to sleep
again.
Vertigo - Vertigo followed by heaviness and dragging of left foot.
RELATIONS - Antidote to: Rhus poisoning. Compare: (1) Aven., Kali-br., Scut., Valer., Ign. (2) Skin relations:
Grind., Anae. (3) Ambra. Coca, Guar., Thea, Zinc. (4) In ecstasy, Coffea.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Cystisus Laburnum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - cyt-1. Cystisus laburnum. Laburnum anagyroides. Cystisus aubour. N. O. Leguminose. Tincture
or trituration of seeds. Tincture of fresh bark. The tincture is prepared from the essences ofthe flowers and
young leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abdominal typhus. Angina, pectoris. Convulsions. Cramps. Cyanosis. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Eyes,
disorders. Heart, anomalies. Heat-stroke. Hydrocephalus. Hypertension. Influenza. Meningitis. Migraines.
Morning sickness. Motion sickness. Nausea. Raynaud's disease. Spasms. Sunstroke. Thyroid disorders.
Typhoid. Vertigo. Vomiting, pregnancy. Writer's cramp.
HOMEOPATHIC - The proving was done by Joseph Schier in 1900-1901 on sixteen pro vers using the low
potencies and the mother tincture. J. Mezger made a clinical re-proving with it.
Cystisus Laburnum, or wild laburnum, is a member of the leguminosae family. Cystisus Aubour is a shrub or
small tree, growing naturally or cultivated as an ornamental plant with trifoliate leaves. It has pale, yellow
flowers which hang in clusters with long pods and which are hairy when yellow.
All parts of this well-known ornamental tree are poisonous, especially the flowers and seeds, owing to the
presence of cytisin. This oxygenated, unsaturated alkaloid is toxic to the glands, which it first arouses and then
paralyzes. It causes convulsions and can lead to death by asphyxia. The toxicity of cytisin is allied to that of
nicotine.
Knowledge of it is derived chiefly from the accidental poisoning of children who have eaten the pea-like seeds
 and pods.
A typical case can be seen in that of W. G., et. 10, who ate eight to ten seeds. Five or ten minutes later, began
to sweat, but soon became cold and shivering, skin pale, pulse scarcely perceptible, general collapse.
Pupils dilated. Drowsy and giddy, without pain. Emetics and brandy were given, but after an hour of this there
was no improvement. An enema of hot, strong coffee was then given, the patient was wrapped in blankets and
hot bottles applied. The collapse then gradually passed off.
Cyt-1. acts on the central and sympathetic nervous system causing cramping spasmodic conditions.
Hyperesthesia of the peripheral nerves. Cerebral shock. Epidemic cerebral and spinal meningitis. Migraine.
Nausea, pallor, cold sweating. Vertigo. Face pale. Dryness of the mouth tongue and throat. Sunstroke.
Heatstroke. Travel sickness (air, sea and car).
MIND - Intense uneasiness, anguish. Depressive and irritable condition. Maniacal depressive conditions.
Oppression. Insomnia. Sleepiness to the point of being in a stupor. Comatose condition.
Abdomen - Chronic gastro-duodenitis.
Spasmodic colon afflictions. Mesenteric irritation.
Back - Muscular cramps. Drawing pains starting at the nape of the neck, spreading towards the occiput.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Feeling of tightness in the chest.
Eyes - Pupils dilated.
Female - Dysmenorrhea. Menopausal complaints. Copious leucorrhea.
Head - Neuralgic pains in the head of a migraine type. Pulsating headaches. Pressing frontal pain. Pricking
pain in
the left temple.
Heart - Hypertensive attack with state of collapse, pale, livid face and cold sweating. Palpitations with
accelerated pulse. Arterial pulsation in all limbs. Rhythmic anomalies. Raynaud's disease.
Limbs - Weakness and numbness of the limbs. Sensation of breaking in all the limbs. Stiffness and drawing
pains in the limbs. Muscular cramps.
Lungs - Respiration rapid at first, then slower and difficult. Wheezing respiration. Whooping cough.
Male - Strong erections.
Modalities - Better after passing wind, after going to stool. Worse from the cold. Worse in the afternoon,
evening. Worse predominantly on the left side.
Mouth - Dryness of mouth, tongue and back of throat. Burning, mouth and pharynx.
Nose - Nosebleeds.
Rectum - Diarrhea with painful abdominal colic, intestinal rumbling and anal tenesmus. Cholera-type diarrhea.
Skin - Skin cold, cold sweating. Cyanosis. Pruritus. Vésicules around the cheek.
Sleep - Insomnia with delirium. Worrying dreams.
Stomach - Gastric heaviness, burning pains in the stomach. Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea with vertigo and
vomiting.
Temperature - Discomfort, accompanied by a feeling of coldness.
Throat - Feeling of constriction in the throat. Tickling sensation in the throat with the need to clear it.
Vertigo - Vertigo and absent feeling. Constant vertigo, even while lying, if she attempted to sit upright, she
immediately fell back again.
COMMENTS - In one case of poisoning by Cyt-1., the head was hot and rigidly thrown back. Muscular
twitchings about the face. Convulsions, insensibility, drowsiness and mental indifference.
Two boys who were poisoned by the root of an old tree had very strange waving motions of the arms and
convulsive drawing up of the legs, first one leg then the other. Pupils equally dilated.
A boy who ate the green twigs of Cyt-1. was seized with vomiting, pain in the stomach and collapse, there was
no diarrhea but tenesmus and erections. After a few hours he passed 300 grams of grass-green urine, after
which he felt better. Soon after passing, the urine assumed a natural color.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Coffee and stimulants, hot and cold douches to chest. Compare: (1) Nux-v. (2)
Gels. - better by copious urination. (3) Tab. - Prostration, nausea, vomiting, general coldness and cold
sweating, vertigo and pallor. (4) Verat. - State of discomfort, collapse, coldness of the limbs, cyanosis,
prostration, vomiting, cold sweating and tiring diarrhea. (5) Bapt. - Intense nervous depression, extreme
agitation, impression that the body is double, sensation of breaking in the bones, putrid breath, fetid diarrhea.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

name: Damiana Aphrodisiaca
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - dam. Damiana aphrodisiaca. Tumeraaphrodisiaca. N. O. Turneraceae. Tincture of fresh plant.
 Tincture of dried leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Chronic, fatigue. Dysmenorrhea. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Infertility. Impotence.
Incontinence. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Prostate, disorders. Sexual, weakness. Spinal, injury. Spermatorrhea.
Syphilis. Urinary, disorders.
HERBAL - Damiana is the local name of the herb Tumera aphrodisiaca. It has long been a domestic medicine
in Mexico, where it is used to “invigorate the system.”
Indians discovered that a decoction of it was a great invigorator after wearisome journeys and dispels fatigue.
They also found in it a remedy for the inability to exercise the reproductive functions in both sexes.
Back - Spinal injury.
Bladder - Urinary disorders. Incontinence.
Female - Dysmenorrhea. Amenorrhea. Leucorrhea. Sexual weakness. Infertility.
Head - Headaches, migraines.
Male - Prostate disorders. Spermatorrhea. Gonorrhea. Syphilis. Impotence. Sexual weakness.
COMMENTS - Hale collected a great deal of experience concerning this remedy from old-school sources,
showing its power over the genito-urinary system.
Douglass reported three cases of incontinence of urine, including the case of a man, age 63, who had dribbling
of urine day and night for four years. He was given Dam. 2x in water, four times a day, and was cured in two
months.
History of curing cases of severe migraines. One or two doses given within an hour would cause the headache
to cease and induced sleep, from which the patient woke free from headache and with good appetite.
Spinal injury from a fall. Sexual excess. Syphilis or gonorrhea. Amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea and leucorrhea.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Impotence, injuries, over-exertion, fatigue, Bell-p., Arn., Agn. (2) Prostatic
affections, Sabal., Solid. (3) Migraines, Bry., Epipheg.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy.

name: Daphne Indica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - daph. Daphne indica. Spurge laurel. Daphne odora. Sweet-scented spurge laurel. N. O.
Thymelaceae. Tincture of fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, esp. the first to sixth
potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Amblyopia. Constipation. Coughs. Exhaustion. Eyes disorders. Exostosis. Fever.
Gastralgia. Gonorrheal rheumatism. Gout. Halitosis. Leprosy. Mer- curio-syphilis. Prostatorrhea. Rheumatism.
Splenitis. Sleeplessness. Syphilis. Tobacco, craving. Toothache.
HOMEOPATHIC - Daphne indica was proved by G. Bute. It, like its relative Daph. mezereon, produces
disorders of the muscles, bones and skin, hence its relation to syphilis and the anti- syphilitic remedies Aur.,
Merc., and Staph. Clammy skin. Red rash in spots on legs in evening. Itching. Daph. oleoides is credited by
Hering with relieving leprosy.
Daph. acts on the tissues, muscles, bones and skin. Fetid breath, urine, sweat. Erratic and electric-like pains.
Sudden, lightning jerks in different parts of the body. Exostoses with stitching, pressing or dull pain, worse at
night. Bruised pain. Exhaustion. Parts of the body feel separated (Bapt.).
Burning in stomach. Gastric symptoms, worse from alcohol. For the craving for tobacco (Calad.). Prostate
discharges, worse from tobacco.
MIND - Despondent and sad. Mental dejection. Timidity. Exhaustion. Absent-minded. Indecisive, walks about
room and can't make up his mind to anything.
Agitated. Irritability. Over-excitement and trembling, during the pains.
Any effort at thinking causes pain or soreness in brain. Fearful and trembling, from pain about heart.
Abdomen - Colic with chilliness. Pain in the abdomen, with shiverings. Contraction of the abdomen. Shootings
and pains in the region of the spleen. Arthritic pains which pass rapidly from the limbs to the abdomen.
Trembling in abdominal muscles.
Back - Pain in the nape of the neck with headache. Screwing pain from the ear to the shoulder. Sensation as
though the cervical glands were much swollen. Sharp pain beneath left scapula. Burning itching in the back.
Painful pulling along the spinal marrow, worse by stooping.
Ears - Burning about ears and on vertex with constant inclination to yawn. Buzzing, roaring in ears. Roaring
and humming.
Eyes - Scraping in the eyes. Violent pains in the eyeballs, in the evening, with great nervous excitement.
Painful sensation as if the eyes were pushed outwards from the head. Sensation around the eyes and eyelids
 with dryness and heaviness of eyelids. Contraction of the pupils. Eyes inflamed, weak, dull, as it were swim-
ming in tears.
Face - Heat and burning sensation in the cheeks, around the ears, and in the vertex, sometimes with constant
inclination to yawn. Sensation of swelling. Stiffness and tension in the temporo-maxillary joint, with burning,
smarting in the skin.
Food - Loss of appetite, moderate thirst. Craving to smoke tobacco. Gouty pains ■worse aicohof.
Head - Headache, provoked by all kinds of intellectual labor. Bursting pain on rising in bed. Heat in head,
especially in vertex. Feels as if skull would burst. Sensation as if head were separated from body. Soft
nodular swellings on bones about vertex, pain worse at night and touch. Itching on scalp. Painful pulsation in
temples with soreness when touched.
Heart - Palpitations and starting of the heart, with inability to remain lying on the left side. Acute pains in the
region of the heart, with discouragement and trembling.
Kidneys - Frequent and abundant emission of urine. Pain, as from excoriation in the urethra, when
urinating. Urine fetid, turbid, thick, yellowish like rotten eggs. Reddish sediment, which adheres to the side
of the vessel. Frequent bedwetting at night.
Limbs - Shooting pains, shift rapidly, worse cold air. Pains shift upwards towards the abdomen and heart.
Bone-ache, piercing pains in the bones and acute shooting pains in the fingers. Excessive itching on the arms
and hands. Rheumatic pains in thighs and knees. Buttocks cold. Right toe swollen, painful.
Lungs - Cough, fatigues and hinders sleep. Thin, slimy, copious, and bloody expectoration. Cough, with
vomiting, and yellowish frothy expectoration, mixed sometimes with streaks of blood. Suffocative feeling with
throat complaints. Yellow, often frothy, blood-streaked expectoration. Copious, thin, slimy mucus.
Suffocating fits at night.
Male - Toothache with erections, after sex. Sweating of scrotum. Discharge of prostatic fluid, after making
water. Prostatic discharge worse smoking.
Modalities - Worse from cold air. Worse touch, pressure. Worse evening in bed. Worse at night. Worse waning
moon. Cold air aggravates wandering gout. Lying down aggravates gouty pains, backache. Pains are worse
from warmth of bed. Stooping or bending aggravates pains in spinal cord. Walking aggravates rheumatic pains
in thighs. Gastric symptoms worse akohoL Pains worse warmth of bed-
Mouth - Dryness of mouth as if burnt, after sleep. Tongue coated on one side only (Rhus-t.). Fetor of the
tongue. Dryness of the tongue after sleep, as if it had been burned. Saliva, hot. Foul smelling breath. Salivation,
with toothache.
Nose - Nose scurfy, with some heat.
Perspiration - Clammy, offensive sweat, with a putrid smell. Viscid sweat over the whole body.
Rectum - Stools scanty, bloody at end.
Constipation.
Sleep - Inclination to sleep with inability to accomplish it. Sleeplessness from aching in bones. Starting on
falling to sleep, with fright, with chilliness, shivering, clamminess and viscid sweat. Agitated, unrefreshing
sleep. Nightmares. Dreams of black cats. Dreams of fire.
Skin - Clammy skin. Red rash in spots on legs, in evening.
Stomach - Burning in stomach and sensation of soreness after each meal. Pressure in stomach after
drinking. Sensation of fullness and ebullition in the precordial region. Aching in the stomach after drinking.
Heartburn and sour vomiting. Frequent cramps in the stomach. After each meal, burning pain and sensation
of excoriation in the stomach, with frequent risings of flatus, the pains extend to left hypochondrium and to the
back. Nausea and vomiting after breakfast.
Teeth - Pulsation in the teeth and gums. Acute drawing pains in all the teeth. Toothache, with and without
salivation. Toothache with fits of shivering, or disposition to perspire. Toothache with erections, after sex.
Temperature - Chilliness with stretching and yawning. Fever, similar to typhus, with excessive shivering,
followed by continued heat, and complete loss of appetite. Fever with gastric and nervous suffering.
Throat - Soreness in left side of throat on pressure. Inflammation of throat and suppuration of tonsils. Feeble
voice.
Vision - Floating black spots. Weak sight, with confusion of the letters when reading. While reading, the letters
fade and appear as a black line. Diplopia.
COMMENTS - Tongue coated on one side only (Rhus-t.). Foul-smelling tongue. Ptyalism with hot saliva.
Fetidity is a marked feature of breath, urine, sweat. Sensation that parts of the body are separated from one
another.
Sudden pains, wander suddenly from limbs. Pain shoots into the region of the heart or abdomen. Sudden stitch
in region of spleen. Ball of right great toe swollen and very painful. Cold feeling on buttocks.
 Daphne indica
RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Bry., Dig., Rhus- t., Sil., Sep., Zinc. Antidote to: Chr-ac.. Merc. Compare: (1) Fl-
ac., Aur., Mez., Staph. (2) Thuj. - effects of suppressed gonorrhea. (3) Benz-ac. - fetid urine, Puls., Chin., (4)
Taxus - erratic pains, Verat. - lightning pains, Bapt. - limbs seem scattered about the bed, Ars. - body seems
divided at waist. (5) Dirca belongs to the same family.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Datura Arborea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - dat-a. Datura arbórea. Brug- mansiasuaveolens. Brugmansiacandida. N. O. Solanaceae.
Tincture ofthe dossiers. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Brain, disorders. Clairvoyance. Confusion. Spinal, irritation. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Froriep, the juice instilled into the eye causes amaurosis. The odor of the
flowers, left in a room for two days, caused many remarkable symptoms including spasms.
While cutting and handling the flowers, there was depletion of the nervous circulation in the medulla oblongata.
Cerebellum and a spinal irritation.
Sensation as if forehead were expanded. Headache. Heartburn. Burning sensation around cardiac end of
stomach, extending to esophagus, with sense of constriction. Heat and fullness over liver region.
MIND - Confusion of ideas with nervous irritation. Can't concentrate thoughts. Floating sensation as if ideas
were floating outside of brain. Brain floats in thousands of problems and grand ideas.
Strange feeling of pleasant and easy comfort, as if he scarcely touched earth with his feet and had to gather
ideas from afar. Sensation as if they were floating in the clouds. Involved in a most beautiful atmosphere, bright
and calm as the sunlight at noon.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Stram.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Datura Ferox
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - dat-f. Datura ferox. Chinese datura. N. O. Solanaceae. Trituration of seeds. Tincture of unripe
fruit. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Delirium. Mania.
HOMEOPATHIC - Poisoning with this drug causes raving madness.
A girl who ate half an unripe fruit was completely out of her mind in a quarter of an hour, dizzy. Sleepy, slept
with eyes open. If disturbed, she sprang up raving and uttered unintelligible words, if one sang she began to
dance in the Favanese fashion.
This symptom may prove a keynote in certain cases of mental alienation. Dryness of the mouth was also noted
in this case, as with Bell, and other Solanaceae.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Datura Metel
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - dat-m. Datura metel. Indian datura. N. O. Solanaceae. Trituration of seeds. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Delirium. Epilepsy. Eye disorders. Mania. Timidity.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dat-m. causes a sleepy condition and later delirium and spasms. The soporose state may
be absent. Delirium may be vociferous or merely garrulous. Patient usually manifests excessive timidity. Picks
at real or imaginary objects. Performs ridiculous antics.
Several movements appear due to perverted vision and inability tojudge distances. After the delirium, patient
remembers nothing of what has occurred. Extreme dilatation of pupils. Flickering before eyes with sensitive-
ness to light. Pulse and temperature undergo extremes of exaltation and depression.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Other Solanaceae.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Deoxyribonucleic Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - des-ac. Deoxyribonucleic acidum. DNA. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Amnesia. Cancer. Down's Syndrome. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Fatigue. Hypersensitivity.
Hyperthyroidism. Insomnia. Manic, depression. Neuralgia. Neurosis. Premature senility.
 HOMEOPATHIC - The proving of DNA. following the method indicated by Hahnemann, was conducted from
1970 to 1972 by O. A. Julian. Thirty people took part in this proving, four of whom were women, and all were
doctors. Using the single blind method, the 30c, 7c, and 3x potencies were used, along with a placebo.
The symptoms of that proving were incorporated with indications given by some Belgian homeopathic authors,
who carried out some clinical research using potencies of DNA.
Symptoms include a sense of general well being, more so in the morning. Difficulty in assembling thoughts,
poor powers of concentration. Does not want to be idle, need to work. Difficulty working, but better when body
fatigue wears off. General hypersensitivity, with asthenia. Tendency to hyperthyroidism.
MIND - Hot-tempered, nervous disposition. Bad-tempered. Extremely irritable, with general feeling of
discomfort in the morning. General feeling of uneasiness. Personality disorders, periods of dual personality.
Narcissistic neurosis. Neurosis from anguish. Manic depression psychosis.
General amnesia. Lack of willpower. Physical and psychological slowness, backwardness. Impossible for him
to work, cannot concentrate. Mental slowness from the after effects of poliomyelitis. Down's syndrome.
Abdomen - Pain in the epigastrium. Distention, not eased by food. Flatulence and rumbling. Disorders of the
liver, pancreas. Biliary sycosis.
Back - Pain in the left shoulder, in the acromion and the clavicular joints. Torticollis. Arthrosis of the neck and
back. Intercostal neuralgia.
Blood - Peripheral circulatory complaints: hands cold during the day, hot in the evening. Leucopenia.
Hemorrhage. Nightly acroparesthesia.
Constitutions - Psoric and allergic constitutions. Cancerous condition.
Eyes - Persistent bilateral conjunctivitis. Asthenopia. Extreme ocular fatigue, difficulty in seeing things in the
distance clearly. Myopia. Bright spots before the eyes, which disappear when closed, appearing around 10:30
a.m., and last for an hour.
Female - Anal and vulvar pruritus.
food-Increases the appetite. Hungerpangs between meals. Anorexia.
Head - Neuritis and neuralgia of the brain. Headache and nausea after drinking a little wine. Pulsating
headache over the whole head. Headache concomitant with need to go to stool, which does not provide relief.
Ophthalmic migraine.
Kidneys - Painful urination. Urinates, especially about half an hour after meals. Irregular diuresis, sometimes
copious, with yellow urine, sometimes copious and pale. Oliguria.
Limbs - White spot on the left index finger. Arm very painful, aggravated by pressure. Nightly recurring cramps
in the calves. Osteomyelitis. Fractures repair slowly. Peri-arthritis of the scapula and humerus. Arthrosis of
hips and shoulders. Patches of sclerosis.
Male - Sexual mania. Diminution of libido. Hypertrophy of the prostate. Eczema of the scrotum.
Modalities - Better from rest. Better lying in the dark. Better laterality left side. Worse from movement.
Mouth - White coating over the whole tongue reaching even the edges, not removed easily by brushing.
Burning sensation in mouth mucus membranes, with sensitive gums. Gingivitis. Angina. Gums bleed when
brushing the teeth.
Nose - Frontal sinusitis.
Rectum - Tendency to constipation, with dry, dark stools. Tendency to diarrhea after meals, with flatulence.
Anal eczema, with burning and oozing.
Skin - Burns. Psoriasis. Eczema. Marginal and eczematous rash, with burning and oozing. Reappearance of
an eczematous dermatitis. Inflammatory folliculitis of the thighs. Alopecia. Seborrhea.
Sleep - Twilight sleep. In the evening, irresistible desire to sleep, once in bed, no longer wants to sleep.
Insomnia. Disturbed sleep. Sleepwalking. Erotic dreams at the end of the night. Dreams of dead bodies.
Stomach - Acid dyspepsia. Burning in the stomach and esophagus. Chilliness after meals, with a cold feeling
between the shoulders and feeling of heat on the face, disappearing with movement.
Throat - Laryngitis. Splinter-like feeling in the throat in the morning on waking. Raw feeling in the throat. Feeling
of a foreign body, especially on the left side, ameliorated by cold water and by swallowing.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Plat., Nep., Arg-n.
REFERENCES-Julian.

name: Derris Pinnata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - der. Derris pinnata. N. O. Leguminosae. Papilionoideae. China. Tincture of plant. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Blepharospasm. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Eyes, inflammation. Locomotorataxia. Mania.
Ozaena. Smell, affected. Tic douloureux.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. X. Roussel is the authority for this plant. Peculiar symptoms include “He walks as if
stepping on down,” Painful and convulsive tic douloureux .Electric shocks and cramps.
Exalted sense of smell. “He perceives celestial odors,” also “intolerable smells after frequent sneezing.” Heat
helps toothache. Viscid urine and viscid saliva. Many symptoms, including diarrhea, come on at night. Worse
from touch.
Derris pinnata
MIND - Delusion that he is seasick. Fear of falling on turning head. Censorious with dearest friends. He is
afraid of killing some one with a knife. Singing alternating with weeping.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Anae. - sense of smell. (2) Stict. - levitation. (3) Ign. - ball in throat, hysteria.
REFERENCES Clarke.

stepping on down,” Painful and convulsive tic douloureux .Electric shocks and cramps.

name: Desmodium Gangeticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - desm-g. Desmodium gange- ticum. N. O. Leguminosae. India. Tincture of plant. Historieal
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Catarrhal. Cough. Dropsy. Fever. Headache. Heat, flushes. Intermittent, fever.
Meningitis. Neuralgia. Pleurodynia. Rheumatism. Typhoid, fever. Ulcers. Vomiting. Wry-neck.
HERBAL - It is a small tree growing in the forest and is found throughout the plains of India, also the lower
Himalayan regions.
The Hindu physicians have highly extolled it as an alternative, tonic, and bitter remedy. They have found it
efficacious in vomiting, fevers, dropsy, ulcers, cough, respiratory troubles and affections due to worms.
It is a bitter tonic and febrifuge. It is also digestive and anti-catarrhal. It is one of the principal ingredients of
Dashamula, an ayurvedic decoction of reputation successfully used in many diseases, namely typhoid fever,
cough, asthma, pleurodynia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Desmodium gangeticum can safely be used in typhoid fever and cere- bro-spinal meningitis
when the patient feels pain all over the body, there is sleepiness, or comatose sleep, headache is present, and
there is feeling as if the head is bound up with a tape or rope.
In intermittent or remittent fevers of children it can be used when there are sleepiness or drowsiness and pains
over the body. In this respect it bears a close resemblance to Gelsemium and in place of which it may be given.
It may be employed in remittent and typhoid fevers and cerebro-spinal meningitis associated with pains over
the whole body, specially over the spine, headache and sleepiness with a feeling as if a tape lay around the
head.
The fever comes on in the morning generally at 7 a.m. There is slight chilliness, lasting for 2 or 3 hours. From
the onset burning sensation is felt over the face and eyes and in the hands and feet. Flushes of heat come out
of the face.
There is remission of fever with perspiration over forehead and back part of the hands and in feet. The fever
indicating this drug is quotidian in character, regularly returning daily. The pains all over the body and headache
and other symptoms may also be present.
The above are the characteristic symptoms in which Desmodium gangeticum will be found an excellent remedy
in intermittent fevers. It is also a valuable remedy for wry-neck.
COMMENTS - The late Dr. Aghore Ch. Bhaduri. with his three pupils made a proving of this drug. The result
of the proving is given below.
He felt pains all over the body. Nervous pain, specially in the legs and neck. Burning sensation was felt in the
hands and feet. Sleepiness.
Pains like rheumatism and neuralgia were felt in hands, feet, legs and the rest of the body. Could not sit straight
on account of spinal pain. Burning sensation was felt in the eyes, face hands and feet and flushes of heat
ignited from the face.
Neuralgic pain was felt in the stomach. Pain was felt in knee joint. Headache associated with a sensation as if
all sides of the head are bound up with a tape. The above were the symptoms which were noticed by Dr.
Bhaduri during the course of the proving.
RELATIONS - Compare: In burning sensations, it can be compared with Azadirachta, Kalmegha, Rohitaka,
Sulphur, etc.
REFERENCES Ghose.

name: Dichapetalum Thunbergh
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - dicha. Dichapetalum thunbergh. Dichapetalaceae or Chailletiaceae family. The flowerinhabits
tropical the regions. Tincture of leaves and bark. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthrosis. Cellulitis. Duodenal, ulcer. Eczema. Hernia. Joint, pain. Lichen planus. Migraines.
 Neuralgias. Rhinitis. Sinusitis. Tonsillitis. Vertigo.
HERBAL - Dicha, is a dicotyledonous family with super-ovarized dialypetals, growing as trees or shrubs with
simple alternate leaves, flowers in clusters or corymbs. The fruit is a drupe with a pendant seed, which has no
albumen.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dicha, was brought to Europe by Dr. Willmar-Schwabe of Germany. The symptomatology
was established by G. Mating on a group of four women and three men. all doctors. Using adouble blind
method, the 3x, 4x, 6x, 15x, and 30x potencies were used, along with a placebo.
General fatigue of the body, despite a state of euphoria when working. Sudden lack of energy with fatigue and
a feeling of hunger, ameliorated by food and alcohol. Sullen mood. Inner trembling. Snuffles. Sensation of
trembling inside the entire body.
Stiffness at the nape of the neck, back, loins and sacrum. Occipital headaches. Migraines. Vertigo, buzzing in
the ears, visual and psychosomatic complaints. Radicular neuritis. Chronic infection of the mucus membranes.
Cervical and brachial neuralgia. Lichen planus.
MIND - Sullen moods. Mental fatigue. Disinterested, must make an effort to work.
Abdomen - Rumbling and pinching feeling in the abdomen, amelioratedby eating and expelling wind. Passage
through intestines accelerated with more frequent stools. Duodenal ulcer. Diaphragmatic hernia.
Back - Pain between the shoulders. Pain in the right shoulder, spreading towards the neck. Dorsal pain and
stiffness like ankylosis. Severe pain and stiffness in the lumbar region, when seated or when walking. Pain in
the lumbar region with drawing
pains around the thighs. Drawing pains in the sacrum, ameliorated by urinating or expelling wind, worse when
standing. Cellulitis of the nape of the neck.
Chest - A retro-sternal pain, worse when swallowing.
Female - Premature, too frequent menses. Amelioration of rheumatic pains at the beginning of menses.
Food - Low blood sugar. Fatigue is ameliorated by food and alcohol.
Head - Migraines. Occipital headaches. Pounding headache on all sides of the head, better by rest and fresh
air. Diffuse, dull head pain with numbness of the head. Pain and stiffness at the nape of the neck.
Heart - Pain in the precordial region with palpitations, followed by ascending hot flushes. Cardiac anguish with
feeling of uneasiness and difficulty in falling asleep.
Limbs - Fatigue and rheumatic pains in the limbs. Joint pain. Arthrosis. Legs feel like rubber. Heaviness in the
calves.
Modalities - Better from fresh air. Better resting. Better eating. Better from menses. Worse on right side. Worse
from standing. Worse walking.
Mouth - Dryness, formication and tension at the lips. Quick, short, drawing pains in the teeth of the lower jaw.
Nose - Itching of the nose and face. Feeling of having acold with blocked nose. Painful drawing sensation at
the root of the nose, especially when the eyes converge to read. Sinusitis. Rhinitis.
Rectum - Bleeding hemorrhoids.
Skin - Deep eczematic fissure on the palm of the hand, stretching along the ‘lifeline,' with scaly eruption at the
edges. Herpestype eruptions, which itch, on the inner side of the left ankle with burning and scratching. Lichen-
type eczema, in cement workers and bakers. Lichen planus.
Temperature - Shivering and sensation of cold, even when in a warm room. Rising heat, as if about to have
a fever.
Throat - Tonsillitis. Painful pulling on the right tonsil. Feeling of a grating lump in the throat. Fit of laryngeal
coughing. Aphonia, ameliorated after speaking for a
long time. Swallowing painful on the right side of the throat. Dysphagia.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Rhus-t. - Aching, stiffness, ameliorated by prolonged movement, vesicular
eruptions, burning and itching. (2) Tub. - Joint pains with stiffness, dragging, worse on waking and after meals.
(3) Zinc - Occipital pain with heavy feeling on the vertex or the root of the nose. Nose blocked, burning pains
in the back, fidgety feet.
REFERENCES-Julian.

name: Dictamnus Albus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - diet. Dictamnus albus. Fraxinella. Dictamnus fraxinella. N. O. Rutacae. Tincture of whole plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Constipation. Flatulence. Leucor- rhea. Metrorrhagia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dictamnus acts on the female organs. Increased secretions. Early menses, of black clots,
preceded by blindness. Profuse, corrosive leucorrhea with tenesmus. Bearing down with bilious vomiting,
 worse standing. Cramps from anterior thighs into the uterus before the menses.
Sensation of milk flowing into breasts. Increased flow of urine. Frequent emission of copious, offensive flatus.
Sensation of a lump rising in the throat. Worse from standing. Sleepwalking. Dreams of piecing bodies of her
children together.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Digitalinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - digin. Digitalinum. Active principle, glucoside of Digitalis purpurea. N. O. Scrophulariaceae.
Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Diarrhea. Emissions. Exophthalmus. Fainting. Heart disorders. Palpitations.
Spermatorrhea. Vertigo. Vision, hallucinations.
HOMEOPATHIC - Digin. is a poison of great activity. It produces a profound effect on muscular tissue, both
voluntary and involuntary, more especially on the heart. Irregular and intermittent action.
Digin. causes profound prostration, even to inability to move a muscle. The heart is slowed or else its action is
made rapid and feeble. Sensation as if the heart stood still. Paralytic weakness, numbness, tremulousness
of the limbs. Cold, clammy surface. Goose-flesh.
A sinking, faint sensation at the epigastrium. Shivering. Diarrhea, the stools are not characteristically white as
are those of the plant. Nausea and vomiting of egg yolk matter. Drinking causes nausea and vomiting.
Symptoms are better after dinner.
Sensitiveness of eyes to light and nose to odors. Disorders of vision and hearing. Confusion of the head, better
walking in open air. Chilliness and fever worse in afternoon and evening. Heart pains are worse lying on left
side. Pains in trunk worse during rest. Many symptoms appear on waking in the morning.
COMMENTS - According to Hale, Digin. is indicated in cases of “overburdened heart where it is constantly
laboring."
Digin. cured the case of Mrs. X, who had for over a year swelling ofherright hand and fingers, which she thought
to be rheumatic. Digitalis has the symptoms, “swelling of right hand and fingers,” and this would have been
given, but only Digin. was at hand. It was given in 4x potency. After the second dose the swelling began to
subside, and in two or three days was completely gone.
One prover noted “frontal headache, dazzlings, loss of appetite, sinking at epigastrium with intestinal
flatulence, borbo- rygmi, eructation. Slight abdominal pains, urine abundant, great fatigue, painful heat in
evening but no thirst.”
For a whole day pressure in supra orbital region towards frontal sinus and when walking a feeling as if the
ground gave way under his feet. Sexual weakness is shown in “Deep sleep in which an emission occurs without
waking him.” “Sexual power diminished or quite abolished temporarily.”
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Dam., Dig., Con., Grat., Tab., Gels., Sec.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Digitalis Purpurea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - dig. Digitalis purpurea. Foxglove. N. O. Scrofulariaceae. Tincture from the leaves of the second
year of the plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Angina pectoris. Aphthae. Ascites. Asthma. Balanitis. Bright'sdisease. Cataract.
Collapse. Congestive heart failure. Coryza. Cyanosis. Cystitis. Delirium tremens. Diplopia. Dropsy. Dyspnea.
Emphysema. Faintness. Fevers. Gonorrhea. Headache. Heart, disorders. Heart, weakness. Hepatitis. Hot,
flushes. Hydrocele. Hydrocephalus. Hydrothorax. Impotence. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Lungs, congestion.
Melancholy. Memory, lost. Meningitis. Mitral valve, disease. Nausea. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Noises, in head.
Pericarditis. Phimosis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Prostate, enlarged. Prostration. Pulmonary, edema. Pulse,
slow. Ptyalism. Spermatorrhea. Stomatitis. Toothache. Uremia. Urethritis. Urinary, disorders. Vertigo. Vision,
disorders. Vomiting. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Digitalis is a heart remedy, but also affects the liver, lungs, stomach and genito-urinary
organs. Dig. should be considered in all diseases where the heart is chiefly involved with abnormally slow,
irregular or intermittent pulse, along with indefinite and causeless symptoms.
Weakness and dilation of the myocardium. Indicated in failure of compensation. Auricular flutter
andfibrillation, especially when subsequent to rheumatic fever. Useful for people with side effects from the
digitalis drug.
Symptoms of organic heart disease, such as great weakness and sinking of strength, faintness, coldness of
skin and irregular respiration, cardiac irritability. Faint, as if dying. Bluish appearance of face. Cardiac
 muscular failure when systole is present. Stimulates the heart's muscles, increases force of systole, increases
length.
Heart blockage with a very slow pulse. The pulse is weak, irregular intermittent, abnormally slow and
dropsy of external
Digitalis purpurea and internal parts. Slow pulse in recumbent posture, but irregular and dicrotic on sitting
up. Irregular pulse. Pulse can be slow or it can be intermittent. Slow pulse with menopause, puberty, or after
sexual abuse.
Congestive heart failure, especially in elderly people with dizziness and ringing in the ears. Tightness of the
chest and weak heart. Constriction of the chest (Cact.). Weary feeling and their limbs feel heavy (Gels., Con.).
Fluttering of the heart (Nat-m.). High blood pressure, with kidney involvement or prostate problems.
Sense of suffocation, a fear of suffocation relating to a weak heart. Sinking feeling in the stomach with heart
palpitations. Faintness. Sensation as i fhe would die if he moves during the palpitations. Great weakness,
can hardly talk, sinking of strength. Collapse. Prostration from slight exertion.
As of an electric shock going through the body. Cyanosis. Must walk about, with precordial anxiety, with urging
to urinate. Dropsy with suppression of urine. Jaundice from induration and hypertrophy of the liver. Jaundice
with heart disease. Tongue is blue and clean, thick and flabby. Eye troubles after tobacco.
MIND - Great anxiety, as from troubled conscience. Reproaches himself. Great guilt, better weeping.
Anxious, low-spirited and tearful. Extreme anxiety related to the heart. Anxious about the future. Excitement,
stammers when talking to strangers. Excitement at night.
Suspicious. Fearful. Fear of suffocation at night. Fear of insanity. Fear from music. Fear of death while
walking. Feels as if he would fly to pieces. Every emotional shock strikes in epigastrium. Fear arising from
stomach. Hurried, abrupt speech.
Deep sighing and grief with heart problems (Ign., Calc-p.). Arrhythmias and palpitations that are worse since
grief (Nat- m). Despair. Despondent. Sadness from unhappy love. Sadness, great depression, with
sleeplessness. Weeping improves symptoms. Weeping from music. A broken heart with the sensation that
the heart will fly to pieces.
Melancholy, dull lethargic withslowpulse. Excessive desire to be alone. Tries to escape if others force
themselves on her. Stammers when talking to strangers. Converses with absent people. Unsympathetic.
Dullness of senses. Thinking difficult. Weak memory. Forgets everything immediately. Insane obstinacy and
disobedience, with desire to escape. Suspicious. Irritability after sex. Lascivious thoughts in old men with
enlarged prostate.
Abdomen - Ascites. Severe abdominal pains. Pain in left side apparently in descending colon and under false
ribs. Tenderness of epigastrium. Pulsation in the abdominal aorta and epigastric constriction. After a meal,
pressure and inflation of the abdomen and of the stomach. Sensation as if intestines were twisted. Gripingpain.
Incarcerated hernia. Bowel symptoms alternating with chest symptoms.
Back - Stiffness and tension of the muscles of the neck and of the nape of the neck. Drawing pains in the back
and in the loins, as after a chill. Bruise-like pains in the loins on blowing the nose. Tearing, sharp, aching and
cutting pains, in neck. Lacerating, and sharp pains in lumbar region.
Bladder - Cystitis, after passing a few drops the desire to urinate is increased and the patient walks about in
great distress. Urethritis, phimosis, strangury. Full feeling after urination. Urine, suppressed. Sharp cutting
or throbbing pain at neck of bladder. Difficult urination. Pain, as if a straw was being thrust back and forth,
worse at night. Constriction and burning, as if urethra was too small. Dragging in bladder as if distended, not
better frequent urination. Contractive pain in bladder, during urination. Urine more easily retained in recumbent
position. After urination pressure in bladder and burning in urethra.
Breasts - Shuddering at the breasts.
Causations - Ill effects of high living, sexual abuse or excessive alcohol intake.
Chest - Angiria pectoris. Great weakness in chest, can't bear to talk. Suffocative painful constriction
ofchest, as if internal parts were grown together. Creeping all
Digitalis purpurea over skin. Smarting in the chest. Tension in the chest with necessity to breathe deeply.
Contractive, pressing pain in the chest, when sitting with the body bent. Sensation of soreness. Congestion in
the chest. Raw, sore feeling in chest, with cough. Trembling in chest.
Constitutions - Nervous lymphatic constitutions. Children with very pale complexions, light hair, scrofulous.
Cough - Dry cough, on deep inspiration. Cough followed by great prostration. Cough after eating, with vomiting
of food. Cough causes pain in shoulders and arms or sore, raw feeling in the chest. Cough from suppressed
menses. Hemoptysis with weak heart or from chronic bronchitis, before menses. Hollow, deep, spasmodic
cough, excited by roughness and scratching in palate and in trachea.
Ears - Otalgia with contractive pains in the ears. Swelling of the parotids and behind the ear. Veins distended
 on ears. Single stitches behind the ears. Hissing before the ears like boiling water, with hardness of hearing.
Eyes - Yellowish, red eyes. Both the eyes turned to left. Burning in eyes and stitches darting through them.
Lachrymation, worse in bright light or cold air. Veins distended on eyes. Blueness of eyelids. Swelling of lower
lid. Mydriasis. Lid margins red, swollen. Agglutinated lids in morning. Catarrhal inflammation of eye. Meibomian
glands inflamed. Chronic conjunctivitis. Detachment of retina. Cataract. Painless obscuration of lens. Irregular
pupils. Pupils dilated and insensible.
Face - Paleness of the face. Cyanosis. Blue color of the lips and eyelids. Bluish swelling of the lips. Dryness
of the lips. Eruptions on the lips. Eruptions with gnawing itching in the cheeks and in the chin. Cramp-like and
drawing pains in the cheekbones. Distended veins. Pores of the face black and suppurating.
Female - Menses scanty and too late. Labor-like pains in abdomen and back before menses. Menorrhagia.
Uterine hemorrhage. Dropsy of uterus. Bleeding from lungs instead of menses. Menopausal
period, sudden flushes of heat followed by great debility, least motion causes palpitations. Leucorrhea.
Lascivious state of fancy day and night. Nymphomania.
Food - Want of appetite, sometimes even with a clean tongue. Smell of food causes violent nausea and
gagging. Desirefor bitter things. Desire for beer. Bread tastes bitter. Continuous thirst with dry lips. Thirst for
acid, sour, cold drinks. Cough worse cold drinks. Worse after meals. Worse cold food or drinks, alcohol. Worse
after drinking. Worse from spirituous liquors. After cold water or ice cream, sharp pain in forehead extending
to nose.
Head - Face bluish. Dullness of head as from intoxication, with increased mental activity. Heaviness of head
with sensation as if it would fall backward. Brain feels fatigued and weak, from weak action of heart.
Confusion, fullness and noises in head. Crashes, cracking in head, on dropping to sleep. Bores head in the
pillow. Pulls the hair. Violent, lancinating pains, in vertex and occiput. Spastic hemicrania. Throbbing, in
forehead. Sharp, shooting pains in forehead, after drinking cold water or eating ice cream. Pressure in
forehead when exerting mind or thinking of it. Sharp pains in temples, evening and night.
Heart - Sinking feeling at heart. Sudden sensation as if heart stood still. Sensation as if heart would cease
beating if he moves, must hold the breath and keep still (opposite of Gels.). Precordial anxiety, with sensation
of weakness in forearm. Audible throbbing of heart. Metallic sounding heart-beat. The least movement causes
violent palpitations. Palpitations with depression from grief. Angina pectoris. Attacks of angina, worse raising
arms with tingling in arm and fingers. Constant pain or anguish in region of heart. Frequent sharp pains in
heart. Irregular heartbeat especially with mitral valve disease. Cardiac failure following fevers. Heart tired
after sprains. Hypertrophy with dilatation. Cardiacfailurefollowing fevers. Cardiac dropsy. Pericarditis,
copious serous exudation. Rheumatism of heart with irregular pulse. Pulse weak and quickened by
least movement. Pulse small, weak and excessively slow, irregular, intermitting. Very slow pulse. Especially
slow when at rest, every other beat intermits, but accelerated by the slightest movement. Thready pulse.
Kidneys - Nephritis after scarlatina. Uremia. Contracted kidneys. Profuse and frequent emission of clear pale
urine. Frequent urination at night. Continued urging, urine in drops, dark, hot. burning. Suppressed urine.
Ammoniacal and turbid urine. Brick-dust sediment. Urine thick, turbid, yellowish-brown, blackish, acrid.
Diminished secretion alternating with copious secretion of watery urine.
Limbs - Rheumatic pain in joints. Swelling of the feet. Sensation as if a red-hot wire suddenly darted
through legs. Stinging pains in muscles of upper and lower limbs. Piercing pains in joints. Shining, white
swelling of joints. Muscular debility. Numbness, heaviness or paralytic weakness, worse left arm. Fingers
become numb easily and frequently. Coldness of hands and feet. One hand hot, the other cold. Nails blue.
Fingers swell at night.
Liver - Enlarged, sore, painful liver. Soreness over region of liver, with jaundice. Liver, hard and painful.
Jaundice from induration. Hypertrophy of the liver. Jaundice with heart disease.
Lungs - Cardiac asthma. Slow, asthmatic attack early in morning. Great weakness in the lungs. Lungs feel
compressed. Dyspnea, constant desire to breathe deeply. Breathing irregular, difficult. Deep sighing.
Breathing slow, worse talking, walking, drinking cold things. Cannot bear to talk (Stan.). Suffocates when
he drops to sleep, fearof suffocation at night. Can only breathe in gasps, each one seeming as if it would
be the last. Chronic bronchitis, passive congestion of the lungs, giving bloody sputum due to failing
myocardium. Expectoration, sweetish like boiled starch, mixed with bloody mucus. Yellow, jellylike mucus,
difficult expectoration. Cannot expectorate without vomiting. Moist rales, yet cough dry. Senile pneumonia.
Emphysema with heart disease. Edema
of lungs. Hydrothorax.
Male - Dropsical swelling of genitals (Sulph.). Prostate enlarged, in elderly men. Hydrocele (left), scrotum
looks like a bladder filled with water. Testicles swollen. Bruise-like pain in testes with swelling. Contusive pain
in right testicle. Balanitis with edema of prepuce. Gonorrhea (Med.). Profuse, thick, yellow-white gonorrheal
 discharge. As if something were running out in urethra after emission. Irritation of sexual organs, with painful
erections, night and day. Desire strongly excited, frequent erections and pollutions. Atonic nightly emissions
after sex. Spermatorrhea. Pollutions always with lewd dreams and subsequent pains in penis. Early morning
erections. Sexual desire without ability.
Modalities - Better when stomach is empty. Better from weeping. Better lying flat on back. Better sitting
erect. Better rest. Better in open air, cool air. Worse from lying on left side. Worse sitting erect. Worse being
raised up in bed. Worse touch, pressure. Worse motion. Worse exertion. Worse sexual abuse or excess.
Worse from food. Worse smell of food. Worse cold food or drinks, alcohol. Worse after meals. Worse music.
Worse from cold air, cold weather. Worse changes of weather. Worse heat. Worse night. Worse waking in the
morning.
Mouth - Soreness of mouth, gums and tongue. Aphthae. Stomatitis. Bitter taste. Taste flat, clammy, slimy.
Sweet taste, with constant salivation. Copious salivation. Salivation after smoking tobacco. Scraped feeling in
mouth. Severe toothache in a hollow tooth.
Nose - Coryza with hoarseness. Pain at the root of the nose, after vomiting. Nosebleeds.
Perspiration - Cold, clammy sweat. Copious sweat at night. Perspiration after the chill, no heat intervening.
Sweats on upper part of body, on face. Sweats during cough. Covered with copious perspiration, without relief
of heart symptoms. Cold sweat, on body, warm on palms of hands.
Rectum - Evacuation forcible. Constipation. White, chalk-like, ashy, pasty stool. Diarrhea during jaundice.
Watery diarrhea. Stool mixed with mucus. Frequent, distressing and exceedingly offensive stools. Stools,
perfectly flat and shaped like a boat. Renewed desire and urging in rectum after stool.
Sensations - As if the heart would stand still if he moved, must hold the breath and keep still (Gels, has “must
keep moving or the heart would stop”). As if heart had torn itself loose and were swaying to and fro by a thin
thread. As if the lungs were constricted and tied up in bundles. As if the stomach would sink into abdomen. As
if something were running out of urethra, as of a weight attached to stomach, as if the internal parts were
grown together. As if the brain were loose, as if something fell forward in the head on stooping, as if the brain
were made of fine glass and shattered at a blow.
Skin - Dry, arid heat of skin. Paleness of the skin. Cyanosis. Bluish skin particularly at the eyelids, lips tongue
and nails. Blue distended veins. Cold skin. Dropsy. Elastic white swelling of whole body. Itching and
jaundiced. Gnawing itching increasing to intolerable burning pricking. Corrosive itching. Erythema, deep red,
worse on back like measles. Measly eruptions on back. Sebaceous follicles ulcerate. Skin painful to touch.
Desquamation of the skin.
Sleep - Lethargy. Continuous sleepiness. Drowsy in the day. Unrefreshing, agitated sleep. Somnolency
interrupted by fits of convulsive vomiting. Uneasy sleep at night on account of constant desire to urinate.
Frequent waking, as from anxiety. Nightmares. Starts from sleep in alarm that he is falling from a height in a
dream. Dreams of falling from a height or into water. Dreams with jerking and electriclike sensations through
the body.
Stomach - Discomfort in stomach, even after a small quantity of food, or from mere sight or smell. Burning in
stomach and into esophagus. Faintness, great weakness in stomach. Extreme anxiety in pit causing
frequent deep sighs. Epi-
gastric region tender. Neuralgic pain in stomach. Stomach burning, extending to esophagus. Gulping up of
an acrid or tasteless fluid. Deathly nausea, with faint sinking in stomach. Persistent nausea and vomiting
with clean tongue (Ip.). Excessive nausea, not better vomiting. Nausea before and after urination. The mere
sight or smell of food excites nausea. Nausea early on rising, with thirst. Faintness and vomiting from motion.
Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy. Vomits easily, on taking anything into stomach. Vomiting, with extremely
feeble and irregular pulse. Vomiting of bile, mucus.
Temperature - Chills alternating with heat. Coldness in the hands and in the feet with cold perspiration.
Chilliness and shivering of the whole body. Chills with head and redness of the face. Internal chills with external
heat. Chilliness before stool. Frequent and sudden flushes of heat, followed by nervous weakness, at
menopausal period. Sudden hot flushes, with palpitation from least motion. Heat of body with cold sweat
of face. During cough. General violent heat, with swollen veins and rapid pulse. Fever with profuse sweat.
Heat of one hand and coldness of the other.
Throat - Scraped feeling in throat. Stinging in throat between acts of swallowing. Choking when he tries to
swallow. Spasm of glottis with diarrhea and thirst. Edema of larynx. Frequent painless hoarseness.
Hoarseness in early morning.
Tongue - Blue tongue and lips. Tongue blue, thick, flabby. Tongue clean with nausea and vomiting. Veins
distended on tongue. Tongue pale. Tongue coated white.
Vertigo - Constant dizziness with ringing in ears. Vertigo, when walking or riding. Vertigo with trembling.
 Vertigo on rising from sitting, with very slow pulse. Vertigo from cardiac or hepatic disorders. Vertigo with
anxiety and faintness. Vertigo as if faintness would occur.
Vision - Diplopia. Dim vision. Dark bodies like flies, before eyes. Change in acuteness of perception of
shades of green. Objects appear green and yellow. Sees
Digitalis purpurea hairs before his eyes. Loss of vision and many symptoms with anemia of retina and optic
nerve. Hemiopia, as if upper part of field of vision were covered by a dark cloud. Optical illusions in bright or
prismatic colors.
COMMENTS - Slow, weak, irregular and intermittent pulse. Acute cyanosis (Carb-v.). Palpitations, with hot
flashes. Prostration from slight exertion. Restlessness with a great nervous weakness. Lassitude, mental and
bodily. Faintness. Convulsions with retraction of head, syncope and collapse. History of helping reduce or
control aneurysm. Vertigo, dizziness as if intoxicated.
Pneumonia and pleurisy. Senile pneumonia. Asthmatic sufferings as from hydrothorax. Respiration is painfully
restricted at night, when lying down or in the day, when walking or seated. In the morning, suffocating
constriction of the chest, forcing the patient to rise up in the bed.
Delirium tremens in high livers, stomach and liver diseases with the mental state of the drug. Enlarged, sore,
and painful liver. Deathly sinking in the epigastrium. Every shock, like bad news, strikes her in the epigastrium.
Portal engorgement. White, pasty stools. Constant irritation or urge to urinate. Urine can be dark brown.
Dribbling of the urine.
Nausea and vomiting, worse from smell of food, not better by vomiting. Violent nausea with clean tongue. The
food eaten comes up by mouthfuls, cannot expectorate without vomiting. Terrible pain at root of nose after
vomiting. Thirst for water.
Enlarged prostate in elderly men, with lascivious thoughts. Prostate enlargement and weaknesses with
concomitant heart disease. Impotence. History of gonorrhea. Yellow-white urethral discharge. People with a
history of excess, particularly sex and alcohol, with weakened heart or liver.
Discharged blood coagulates slowly or not at all. Distended veins in eyes, ears, lips and tongue. Blue skin.
Absence of fever.
Teste classed Dig. with Bry. and Ign. He noted that there is an “anxious and concentrated sadness with
sleeplessness at night.
owing to pains at the heart: for instance from unhappy love, especially in women of brown complexions, firm
and obstinate dispositions. In such cases far preferable to Ignatia.”
Ross regarded the indications as being: “dry cough with mucus rales and no expectoration or only "prune juice'
expectoration, cyanosis, cold limbs, feeble intermittent pulse, deathly nausea or gone sensation at
epigastrium.”
Malcolm Macfarlan reported Dig. having produced severe urethritis, phimosis and strangury. He cured with it
many cases of gonorrhea.
Ballard cured a man of headache and dizziness, originating probably in gonorrhea suppressed several years
before. He complained of feeling bad about the head after drinking and this keynote symptom was elicited:
“after drinking cold water the pain would seat itself in the forehead and extend down the nose.”
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Camph., China. Compare: (1) Crat. - a true heart tonic. (2) Adon., Kalm., Spig.,
Liatris, Serum ang. (3) Nerium odorum - resembles in heart effects Digitalis, but also has an action like Stry.
on spinal cord. Spasms appear more in upper part of body. Palpitations, weak heart will be strengthened by it.
Lock-jaw. (4) Digitoxinum. Nit-s-dulc. increases actionofDig. (5)Conval- laria - heart disease with vertigo and
digestive disturbances. Compatible: Bell., Bry., Cham., Lyc., Nux-v. Incompatible: China.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
