name: Ephedra Vulgaris
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ephe. Ephedra vulgaris.Ma huang. Ephedra distachya. N. O. Gnetacee. Ephedraceae. Tincture
of branches and flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Exophthalmic goiter. Headaches.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ephedra has been proved in Russia by Dr. B. H. Mouravow. Ephedra produced symptoms
when twenty drops of a strong alcoholic extract were taken five times a day, fifteen drops four times a day
were taken without apparent effect.
General weakness from early morning, great fatigue. Extreme apathy. Asthma. Stiff-neck and backward pulling
of whole body on turning the head. Starting of the eyes from the orbits as if pushed out.
To Mouravow, these symptoms suggested exophthalmic goiter. He also considered that the remedy acted on
the ganglions of the sympathetic nerve and caused congestion of the spinal cord.
MIND - Extreme apathy and fatigue.
Abdomen - Dull pain in region of spleen (Cean.).
Back - Stiffness of neck with exophthalmos. Stiffness of neck and backward pulling of all the body on turning
head, with a dull pain in region of spleen.
Eyes - Heavy eyes. Pain in the eye. Starting from their orbits, as if pushed out.
Head - Violent headache, nausea, general weakness, with a slow pulse. Left side hemicrania with numbness
 of entire left arm.
Heart - Abatement of the pulse, increases rapidity of action of heart. Strong heartbeat with weakening of pulse,
respiration is accelerated.
Kidneys - Retention of the urine (fourth day).
Limbs - Heaviness in all the limbs, in evening. Numbness of entire left arm with left-side hemicrania.
Sleep - Longing for sleep.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ferr., lod., Lyco-
pus v„ Spong., (2) Thyroid. - exophthalmos.
REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Epigea Repens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - epig. Epigea repens. Gravel weed. Trailing arbutus. N. O. Ericaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves.
The fresh leaves are pounded to a pulp and macerated in two parts by weight of alcohol,Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, disorders. Cystitis. Dysuria. Gravel. Kidney, stones. Pyelitis. Stones, urinary. Strangury.
Uric acid.
HERBAL - Epigea has long had a reputation in urinary difficulties and even in calculous disorders. The
common appellation of “gravel root” shows that the popular belief points in the direction of its use.
Hale mentioned Epig. as having been a popular remedy in kidney stones throughout the United States ever
since the settlement. It has been successful in removing dysuria and strangury as well as urinary tenesmus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Chronic cystitis with dysuria. Pyelitis with incontinence of urine. Mucus, pus and uric acid
deposit, gravel, kidney stones. Fine sand in urine of a brown color. Burning in neck of bladder while urinating.
Tenesmus after urination. Croaking noise and rumbling in bowels.
COMMENTS - Hale gave ten drops of the tincture six times a day to a patient who had a bloody muco-purulent
sediment in the urine with intense dysuria. A copious deposit of fine brown sand was observed and all
symptoms were relieved.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Mitch., Chim., Cann-i., Calc, ren., Urt-u., Uric acid. (2) Uva, Lyc. Pareira. (3)
Epigea contains Arbutin, Formic acid. (4) Arbutus, Uva ursi.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke. Hale.

name: Epilobium Palustre
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-epil. Epilobium palustre. Willow herb. Epilobium linears. N. O. Onagraceae. Tincture of fresh
rhizome. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Dysphagia. Fever. Larynx, disorders. Ptyalism. Throat, sore.
HOMEOPATHIC - A boy poisoned with the flowers of Epil. hirsutum had strong epileptiform convulsions in
rapid succession. Epil. was proved by Dr. J. S. Wright using a tincture of the root.
Headache. Red face. Ptyalism, chokes on saliva. Feeling of throat filling up, could not swallow water. Larynx
sore to pressure, swollen on outside, with hard lumps on both sides of larynx. Cannot swallow liquids, can fly
out of nose. Loose stools, red urine.
Hard chill beginning at 11 a.m., lasting an hour. High fever, with aching all over and severe headache, lasting
through the night, could not sleep. Fever and headache passed off, but returns in the afternoon and evening
more severely, lasting all night. Dull and sleepy, but could not sleep.
REFERENCES - Allen. Clarke.

name: Epiphegus Virginiana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - epip. Epiphegus virgini- ana. Beech-drop. Epiphegus americana. Cancer root. Orobanche
virginiana. N. O. Orobanchaceae. Tincture of whole fresh plant in full flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Cancer. Diarrhea. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Neurasthenia. Palpitations. Salivation. Sub-
involution, uterus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Epip. is a remedy for sick, neurasthenic and nervous headaches, especially in women,
brought on or made worse by exertion, nervous strain, etc.
Headaches with pressive pain, as if fingertips were pressing into the temples inwards or compressive pain
going backwards, worse until 4 p.m., then better with spitting of viscid saliva and nausea.
 Neurasthenia. Languid feeling. Drowsy after meals. Tongue coated yellow, bitter taste. Loose stools. Sub-
involution of the uterus with painful menstruation and congestion.
MIND - Confusion of mind, makes wrong letters or words in writing. Fears death from heart palpitations, injury
to her health from the drug.
Causations - Physical or nervous overstrain. Any unusual exertion or excitement, as going on a visit or doing
a day's shopping.
Eyes - Smarting. Could not read because the words seemed to be blurred.
Female - Subinvolution of uterus, with painful menses and congestion.
Head - Nervous headaches. Pain, worse left side. Pressing pain in temples from without inwards.
Headaches from nervous strain caused by mental or physical exhaustion, preceded by hunger. Sick
headache coming on when deviating from ordinary pursuits, weekly sickheadaches. Viscid salivation,
constant inclination to spit.
Heart - Palpitations, causing weakness. Limbs - Pain in left shoulder, left knee.
Modalities - Betterfrom sleep. Worse from fatigue. Worse nervous strain. Worse eyestrain. Worse working in
open air. Worse rising up in bed.
Mouth - Tongue coated yellow, bitter taste. Saliva viscid, almost constant desire to spit. Sticky viscid, bitter
taste in mouth.
Rectum - Loose stools. Stool passed with difficulty, though feces soft.
Stomach - Nausea.
Teeth - Tartar on teeth.
COMMENTS - Grimmer noted skin cancers, palpitations with weakness, and a constant desire to spit viscid
saliva. Severe headache brought on by exertion, relieved by a good sleep. Symptoms travel right to left.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Iris, Meh., Sang. (2) Fagus - beech-nuts - headache and salivation, swelling on
mouth, dread of water. (3) It is allied to the Scrofulariaceae. (4) Phos. - in better from sleep, Lach., Sulph. and
Nat-m. have the opposite, worse from sleep in the most marked degree.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer.

name: Equisetum Hyemale
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - equis. Equisetum hyemale. Horse-tail. Scouring-rush. N. O. Equisetaceae. A rush growing in
damp soil in Europe and America. Tincture of fresh plant chopped and pounded to a pulp. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bedwetting. Bladder, disorders. Cystitis. Diabetes. Dropsy. Dysuria. Gleet.
Gonorrhea. Gravel. Hematuria. Involuntary, urination. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, weakness. Paralysis.
Polyuria. Urinary, retention.
HERBAL - Equisetum contains silica in an appreciable quantity. Horsetail tea is widely know as a kidney and
bladder tonic. It is a natural and soothing diuretic used for polyuria and urinary retention.
Teaspoonful doses of the decoction or the tincture in hot water is found useful to allay irritability of the urinary
tract, kidney stones, dysuria, pleuritis effusion and dropsy.
HOMEOPATHIC - Affinity for the urinary organs. Pain in the kidneys (especially right), in the bladder and
urinary passages. Irritation of the bladder and kidneys.
Urinary retention and dysuria, especially in women during pregnancy and after confinement. Constant desire
to urinate and passes large quantities of clear, lightcolored urine without relief.
Cystitis. Severe, dull pain that does not lessen after urination. Aching, full, tender bladder, not better after
urinating. Pain in bladder as from distention. Pricking, burning, cutting pain in urethra while urinating.
Dribbling urine in old women with involuntary stool. Much mucus in urine. Bedwetting (Lyc., Nat-m., Sil.. Sep.).
 Nocturnal bedwetting of children without causes except habit. Bedwetting when he dreams, he always sees
a crowd of people. Pain in sacroiliac joints.
MIND - Very irritable and easily fatigued.
Abdomen - Distended feeling. Sharp pains on either side of hypogastrium, extending to middle line. Dull,
heavy pains in either side of lower abdomen and bladder with frequent desire to urinate, not better by urinating.
Severe pain in lower abdomen with passage of fetid flatus.
Back - Pains in back, especially while sitting, better lying on back and walking. Right lumbar region painful.
Heavy sensation like a lump in right lumbar region. Severe rheumatic pains in region of sacral-lumbar joint and
through left hip joint extending down outer side of left leg, ending in front three inches above knee.
Bladder - Frequent, profuse urination of clear, watery urine. Urgent desire to urinate with prickling, biting,
itching, and soreness of meatus from contact and pressure, worse scratching. Retention of urine after
childbirth. Retention and dysuria during pregnancy. Pricking in urethra a short distance back from meatus.
Severe, dull pain in bladder. Feeling of fullness in bladder, not relieved by urinating. Profuse urination with
burning in urethra and sharp pain at root of penis. Sharp, burning, cutting pain in urethra
while urinating. Involuntary urination during daytime. Bedwetting, nocturnal and diurnal. Bedwetting in
children with dreams or nightmares when passing urine. Obliged to rise several times at night to urinate.
Incontinence in old women, with involuntary stools.
Breasts - Sharp stitch in left breast, one inch to left and over nipple.
Ears - Dull, transient pain and stiff feeling behind left mastoid. Confused feeling in ears. Confusion of sounds,
confused noises, fearful rumbling.
Eyes - Severe pain in roof of right orbit. Sharp pain in outer angle of right eye.
Face - Face flushed, feeling of heat. Disposed to frown. As if blood pressed into face. Heat and burning
without redness.
Head - Severe headache with intense pain in upper part of eyes or roof of orbit. Headache with heat of face
without redness. Constrictive feeling across forehead. Sticking and darting pains, changing locality.
Constriction of whole scalp, as if drawn tightly over whole skull. Feeling of skin continuing to contract, continual
desire to wrinkle up forehead.
Heart - Sharp pain in region of heart, worse by inspiration.
Kidneys - Nephritis. Diabetes insipidus. Weak and sensitive kidneys from abuse of diuretics. Slight pain
in right kidney, then in left, extending down left side of sacrum. Frequent urination at night. Deep pain in
region of right kidney, extending to lower abdomen with urgent desire to urinate. Polyuria associated with
diabetes. Frequent urging, with severe pain at the close of urination.
Limbs - Pain in upper part of shoulders and in region of vertebra prominence, worse by least motion or contact.
Pain in right shoulder to middle of upper arm. Pain in left shoulder with shi veringo vet body and great heat of
head. Pain in right hip joint and near knee joint. Knees very weak on least exertion. Dull, heavy pain under left
patella. On awakening, sharp pain inner side of left knee, better after moving about a short time.
Male - Violent erections in the afternoon. Soreness of testicles and cords, worse left.
Modalities - Better in afternoon. Better lying down. Better continued motion. Worse right side. Worse
movement. Worse touch. Worse pressure. Worse contact. Worse sitting down. Worse at close of urination.
Rectum - Smarting in anus during and after stool. Stool with aching in anus and feeling as if rectum would
protrude. Feeling as if some feces still remained. Sticking-like pains in anus (Ila. m.). Stool with great flatulence.
Sleep - Very sleepy, heavy eyelids. Sleep disturbed by tiresome dreams. Dreams of many persons, places
and things. Dreams of crowds of people. Nightmare when passing urine.
Stomach - Excessive hunger, appetite greatly increased.
Temperature - Creeping chills beginning below and creeping up back.
Throat - Sharp sticking in throat.
Urine - Copious amounts of watery urine. Urine flows only drop by drop. Profuse urination of clear, watery
urine. Passes large quantities of clear, light-colored urine withoutrelief. Albuminuria. Urine cloudy. Great
excess of mucus on standing.
COMMENTS - Equis, is a deep anti-sycotic. Pain in the kidneys, especially the right. Pain in the bladder and
urinary passages, as from distention. Retention and dysuria, especially in women during pregnancy and after
confinement.
Severe cystitis. Acute bladder infections, especially when passing large amounts of pale urine. Polyuria.
Frequent urination or lack of urination. Paralysis of the bladder, urinary retention (Aeon., Apis., Caust.).
Constant desire to urinate, passes large quantities of clear, light-colored urine without relief. Severe, dull pain
that does not lessen after urination, irritation of the bladder, especially in women. Burning pain at the end of
urination (Sars.).
 Diabetes with frequent urination. General paralysis with loss of control over bladder and rectum. Multiple
sclerosis cases with incontinence of the urine. For the side effects
of strong diuretics.
Loss of hair, and weak nails. Mending broken bones, can help retain calcium and prevent osteoporosis. Hot
flashes. The tincture is a natural diuretic and tonic for weak kidneys, and is also good for hemorrhoids.
Farrington noted the bedwetting with frequent painful urging to urinate, causing the patient to rise at night.
According to Grimmer, this remedy cured a case of uterine cancer.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Sars., Apis, Berb., Hydrang., Ferr-p., Linaria, Chim. (2) Cann-i., Puls., (3) Canth.
comes closest, there is less bleeding, tenesmus, scalding and fibrinous flakes than with Canth., but more
mucus.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Polyuria. Urinary, retention.
HERBAL - Equisetum contains silic

name: Erechthites Hieracifolia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - erech. Erechthites hieracifolia. Fireweed. Senecio hieracifolia. Erechthites praealta. N. O.
Composite. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Eczema. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhages. Herpes. Metrorrhagia. Nausea. Nosebleeds.
Psoriasis. Orchitis. Rhus poisoning. Ulcers.
HERBAL - Erechthites belongs to the composite and closely allied to erigeron and the groundsel family
(Senec.). “Fireweed” is so called because it grows abundantly in clearings which have been burnt out.
According to Hale, “Oil of Fireweed” is also extracted from erigeron and is said by alchemists to be similar to
turpentine. All three cause active and passive hemorrhages, the former being the primary and the latter the
secondary action.
HOMEOPATHIC - Erech. is indicated in hemorrhages of bright red blood from nose, mouth, bowels, kidneys,
uterus and especially the lungs. Hemorrhagefrom any part, always attended by excitement of the circulation.
Passive hemorrhages of dark fluid blood. Nosebleed of bright blood.
Metrorrhagia. Flashes of heat that suddenly give way to coldness. Scanty urine, edema of the limbs. Useful as
a local application in skin affections, herpes, eczema, psoriasis and indolent ulcers. Increased appetite.
Increased feeling of strength and desire for exercise.
Hale commended it in gonorrhea and orchitis.
Back - Stitches in middle of back. Aching across small of back.
Female - Premature and profuse menses. Metrorrhagia.
Head - Giddiness with nausea. Dull frontal headache. Throbbing of temporal arteries with flushes of heat
running across the back from one shoulder to the other. The sensation of heat suddenly gives way to that of
coldness.
Kidneys - Increased flow of urine. Slight burning at meatus during urination.
Limbs - Cold feeling in back of legs. Legs feel stiff and painful.
Male - Prolonged erections with dreams of nudity, towards morning. Orchitis from suppressed discharge.
Gonorrhea with scanty discharges and great pain.
Rectum - Griping followed by three copious discharges of semi-solid, yellow fecal matter.
Skin - Symptoms like rhus poisoning. Sleep - Dreams of nudity and shame.
Stomach - Enormous appetite. Feeling in stomach as if it would be dissolved after drinking coid water.
Belchings and heartburn after eating warm bread and coffee (cured).
Throat - Sore throat.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-t. Senec., Erigeron, Ham. Mill., Calc., Canth., Terebe., Puls., Clem.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Ergotinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ergot. Ergotinum. Ergotin. Alkaloids of Secale comutum. Trituration. His- torieal dose:
Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Alopecia. Anal, incontinence. Bedwetting. Dysmenorrhea. Faintness. Gangrene. Heart, paralysis.
Hemorrhages. Menorrhagia. Migraines. Miscarriage. Neurological, disorders. Pre-menstrual, migraines.
Sphincters, paralysis. Urticaria.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ergotinum is the total extract of the ergot Claviceps Purpurea. The ergot is the intermediary
stage through which this mushroom passes in order to complete its development. Claviceps Pupurea, other-
wise known as Secale Comutum, is widely used in homeopathic medicine, with its own indications.
This Ascomycetes Pyrenomycetes is a parasite on the ears of rye, as well as on other grain such as wheat or
 oats, and on other plants such as Cypetaceae and palm trees.
The toxicity of ergot has been known for a long time, manifested by the medieval epidemics of Saint Anthony's
Fire due to the consumption of contaminated flour. Its oxytocic and abortive powers are also well known.
The insoluble polypeptide alkaloids are stimulants of smooth tissues, especially uterine and vascular. Affects
the sympathetic system, counteracts the effects of adrenalin. Ergotinine, the extract of ergot of rye, is used in
allopathic medicine, as a constrictor of blood vessels to encourage hemostasis, as in uterine and pulmonary
hemorrhages.
Ergot, acts by causing contraction of the arterioles and its effect is produced most promptly when it is
administered by subcutaneous injection. Its homeopathic use are in the main identical with those of Sec., but
Ergot, will sometimes succeed when Sec. fails.
Ergot, is primarily a female remedy, functional complaints of the female genitalia. Pre-menstrual migraines.
Menstrual complaints. Vulvar itching.
General ill-defined discomforts, head feeling empty, misty vision, noise in the ears, vertigo, nausea, occasional
vomiting.
Nervous system disturbed, anxiety, faintness. Nerve attacks with sudden strokes, abrupt clouding of
consciousness, both psychological and physical. For cases with a loss of consciousness.
Certain forms of alopecia or allergy. Urticaria. Bedwetting in both sexes with no anatomical lesion or any urinary
infection, with an increase in the level of neurosis from anguish.
MIND - Anxious, hyper-emotiional state. Instability of the character. Slowing down of mental processes.
Chronic mental depression. Depressive state, particularly before menstruation. Sadness and weeping before
menses. Loss of consciousness.
Breasts - Premenstrual swelling of the breasts and abdomen.
Ears - Buzzing, intermittent deafness.
Eyes - Visual complaints such as mistiness, cloudy vision, luminous spots before the eyes. Black patches,
black or glinting spots across the field of vision.
Female-Pre-menstrual syndrome. Painful menstruation with no clinically discernible lesion. Dysmenorrhea
with red, non-clotting blood. Menorrhagia in young virgins from the beginning of menses in the young woman.
Vulvo-vaginal itching, congestion, redness, dryness of the mucus membranes. Hyper functioning of the
pituitary and ovaries.
Head - Migraines. Habitual headaches. Premenstrual migraines. Diffuse alopecia. Round patches of
alopecia.
Skin - Alopecia-type areas. Urticaria. Pruritus. Edema.
Sleep - Insomnia, especially in women.
Vertigo - Attacks of faintness.
COMMENTS - “Wide-open anus sensation” (Sec., Phos.). Koeck of Munich recorded a case of a patient who
suffered from diarrhea since the Franco-German war and latterly had lost all power of retention. The rectum
had lost all sensation, so that the patient had no warning and was never clean.
Old school treatment had failed to relieve him. He was about to be pensioned by his employers and had
thoughts of suicide. Sec. 3x ameliorated slightly, the 2x had the same result.
“Remembering Kafka's advice to use the alkaloid when the indicated drug did not seem to act, he prescribed
Ergotin 2x.” After taking this for four days the patient regained control.
Demange recorded the case of a young woman suffering from typhoid fever and threatened with heart
paralysis. Stimulating injections of ether and of rum and frictions completely failed to rally her.
Cyanosis increased rapidly and threatened the trunk. Fainting spells occurred in rapid succession, pulse
filiform. Ergot, was then injected and the pulse rose and the symptoms of collapse disappeared. Most of the
symptoms of this patient may be found under Sec.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sec. - Dysmenorrhea with blood clotting and black blood. (2) Folliculinum - Pre-
menstrual syndrome with swelling, headaches, hypermenorrhea. (3) Thyr. - Depressive condition, anxious with
hyperthyroid tendency, trembling and pigmentation, especially of the eyelids. (4) Ign. - Nervous, paradoxical
instability, anguish with feeling of constriction in the throat and the epigastrium. (5) Lil-t. - Complaints in the
uterus and ovarian region, heaviness of the lower abdomen.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian.

name: Erigeron Canadensis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -erig. Erigeron canadensis. Fleabane. Leptilon canadense. N. O. Compositae. Canada. Tincture
from the fresh plant when in bloom. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
 CLINICAL - Black, eye. Bruises. Coughs. Dysentery. Dysuria. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hematocele. Hemorrhages.
Hemorrhoids. Injuries. Leucorrhea. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Placenta, previa. Proctalgia. Spermatorrhea.
Tympanites. Uterus, weak. Wounds.
HERBAL - Native Americans used Erigeron as an application to wounds. It compares as a vulnerary with Arn.
Erig. is chiefly known as a remedy for hemorrhages and congestions in all parts of the bodÿ. Bnght red
hemorrhages.
HOMEOPATHIC - Erig. has been proved by Burt and others. Wilmot Moore gave it with success in three cases
of placenta previa. He gave the lx trituration (of what part of the plant is not mentioned) on the tongue.
Hemorrhagic remedy, especially when hemorrhages are profuse, bright red, gushing. Persistent hemorrhage
from the bladder. Uterine hemorrhage with painful urination. Pain in left ovary and hip. Chronic gonorrhea with
burning urination, continual dribbling. Gleet.
Burning congestions. Hard aching. Sensation as if something had lodged in upper part of esophagus.
Dysentery with soreness and burning in the bladder. Tympanites. Prominent pains in umbilical region. Feeling
as if anus had been torn. Urination is painful or suppressed, sharp stinging pains in region of left kidney.
MIND - Great despondency. Excessive fatigue in morning, all day with great depression. No ambition to move
in afternoon and evening. Sadness with feeling of great languor. Weeping during urination.
Abdomen - Abdomen distended. Frequent distress in umbilicus with hard, aching distress in whole dorsal
region. Frequent dull pain in umbilical region, can be severe, cutting, with a feeling in anus as if it had been
torn.
Back - Dull, aching distress in whole dorsal region. Dull pains in lumbar and sacral regions. Severe sticking,
stabbing pain in region of left kidney, passing to right kidney.
Bladder - Frequent desire. Dysuria of teething children. Urination painful or suppressed. Crying when
urinating. Urine profuse, with strong odor. External parts (female) inflamed or irritated with considerable mucus
discharge.
Ears - Loud singing in right ear.
Eyes - Smarting, burning, in afternoon or evening. Ecchymosis around from below. Slight agglutination of lids
in morning.
Face - Congested, red face.
Female - Miscarriage, because of exertion.
Pregnant women with a weak uterus. Bloody discharge on slight exertion. Metrorrhagia with violent irritation
of rectum and bladder and prolapse uterus. Metrorrhagia after miscarriage with diarrhea or dysentery after
least motion. Uterine hemorrhage, bright-red flow (Phos. ). Bloody lochia returns after least motion, comes
in gushes, between periods. Bleeding hemorrhoids, nosebleed instead of menses (Bry. ) Leucorrhea with
urinary irritation, profuse.
Head - Congestion of the head, red face, nosebleed, febrile action. Awakened with dull headache, with aching
distress in all the large joints. Dull frontal headache with smarting in eyes.
Heart - Palpitations.
Kidneys - Persistent hemorrhage from the bladder. Bladder, rectal tenesmus with metrorrhagia. Aching in
bladder. Retention of urine. Dysuria during dentition, crying when urinating.
Limbs - Aching dullness in all the joints and limbs. Hard aching in all the limbs.
Lungs - Cough, bloody expectoration. Incipient tuberculosis.
Male - Sticky sweat on genitals. Gonorrhea and gleet. Blue, black spots on genitals. Pain in right lumbar region
passing down to testicle.
Modalities - Worse from exertion. Worse rest. Worse left side. Worse rainy weather. Every movement
aggravates flow, causes bloody lochia to return.
Mouth - Bad taste in mouth.
Nose - Nosebleed of bright red blood. Increased secretion of mucus all forenoon. Nosebleed.
Rectum - Hemorrhages from the bowels. Burning in the bowels and rectum, hard lumps of feces mixed with
the discharges. Hemorrhoids, bleeding with ahard, lumpy stools, burning in the margin of anus, it feels as if
torn. Rheumatic pains in abdominal muscles. Stools small, streaked
with blood. Mushy stools.
Skin - Ecchymosis. Slightly elevated, sharply defined vesicles on skin.
Stomach - Sharp cutting pains in epigastric region every few minutes followed by dull pains. Burning in
stomach and abdomen. Belchings of air. Violent retching and burning in the stomach. Vomit or stool of pure
blood.
Throat - Increased secretion of mucus in nostrils all forenoon. Feeling of roughness of pharynx. Sensation as
if something had lodged in the upper part of the esophagus that caused frequent inclination to swallow.
 RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Ip., Phos., Ham., Arn., Canth., Cop., Sabin. (2) Terebinthina similar. (3) It is
related to Senec., Erech.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Eriodictyon Californicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-erio. Eriodictyon californicum. Yerba santa. Eriodyction glutinosum. N. O. Hydrophyllaceae.
Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Bronchitis. Catarrh. Coryza. Coughs. Influenza. Nausea. Nightsweats. Tuberculosis.
Wheezing.
IERBAL - Yerba Santa, the holy plant, is a popular expectorant remedy in Mexico and California. Allen said
“Eriodyction has a strong terebinthine taste and abounds in a resinous matter which sometimes exudes so
copiously that in drying, the specimens stick firmly together and to the paper.”
IOMEOPATHIC - Erio. is a remedy for asthmatic and bronchial disorders. Asthmatic breathing with
accumulation of mucus, relieved when the mucus is cleared. Coryza and catarrh. Coughs after influenza.
Whooping cough. Furthers absorption of effusion in pleural cavity.
Tubercular conditions, especially bronchial tuberculosis. Tuberculosis as the result of frequent bronchial
catarrhs. Impaired digestion, poor appetite, intolerance of food. Wasting, night-sweats.
Ears - Pain in ears. Sharp, shooting pain in right ear, at intervals or on suddenly changing position of head to
right or left, changing to just below external ear.
Head - Pressure outwards, worse occiput. Aching at base of cranium, 8 a.m. Sensation of pressure outwards
on all sides of head, greatest at cerebellum upwards. Intense, dull, heavy pain in back of head and over eyes.
Burning in occiput, heavy pain as if occiput was being pressed out.
Lungs - Asthma, coryza and mucus secretions. Wheezing. Chronic bronchitis, bronchial tuberculosis with
profuse, easily raised bronchial secretion, giving relief. Wheezing voice, at 5 p.m. Dull pain in right lung, front.
Male - Sore, dragging, tender feeling in testicles, worse left, could not bear any pressure, better gentle support.
Dreaded to move because of its tenderness. Slight fluttering at intervals at bottom of testicles.
Modalities - Worse in afternoon. Nausea, worse on running. Symptoms come at intervals or on any sudden
changes of position.
Mouth - Foul mouth in morning. Burning in fauces.
Nose - Coryza with dizziness and sneezing. Yellowish-green catarrh.
Stomach - Great appetite. Nausea. Deathly sickness, worse by running.
Temperature - Slight fever, cheeks flushed and burning.
Throat - Burning sensation in fauces and throat.
Vertigo - Dizziness and a sense of intoxication.
COMMENTS-G. M. Payne's proving brought out marked preference for the right lung. Foul mouth in the
morning on rising. J. Perry Seward gave it with great success in two cases of cough remaining after influenza.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Grind., Aral., Eucal., Ip. (2) Balsam of Peru, Pix liquida, Stann. (3) afternoon
aggravation. Lyc., Grind., Phos., Hep., Rumex, Caust., Dros.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Erodium Cicutarium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - erod. Erodium cicutarium. Hemlock Stork'sbill. N. O. Geraniaceae. Tincture of fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Decoction of half ounce of the herb to six ounces of water.
CLINICAL - Hemorrhages. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Uterine, polyps.
HOMEOPATHIC - Erodium is apopular hemostatic remedy in Russia, and is especially used for metrorrhagia
and menorrhagia. Uterine hemorrhage with polyps. Has controlled hemorrhage after Sec. failed.
Komorowitch cured with it numbers of cases in which Ergot. andHydr. had failed, including a case of cervical
polyps. After three day's use of the decoction, the polyps were found lying free in the vagina.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ger.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Eryngium Aquaticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ery-a. Eryngium aquaticum. Button snake-root. N. O. Umbelliferae. Tincture of fresh root.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
 CLINICAL - Anus, prolapse. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Cough. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Gleet. Gonorrhea.
Hemorrhoids. Influenza. Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Kidney,colic. Prostate, weakness. Sclerotitis. Sexual,
weakness. Strabismus. Spermatorrhea. Urine incontinence. Wounds.
HERBAL - Eryngium is a remedy for urinary disorders. The English Eryngo, the E. Maritinum, is noted as an
aphrodisiac and is very similar in appearance to the Eryngium aquaticum.
HOMEOPATHIC - Acts on the mucus membranes, producing thick yellow mucus discharges from eyes,
ears, nose, mouth, bowels, urethra and vagina. Cough with a sense of constriction. Hemorrhages from
stomach and bowels. Influenza.
It is a vulnerary, antidoting the effect of blows. Headaches, expanding sensation in forehead, dull, dragging
pain in occiput, neck and shoulders. Seminal and prostate weakness. For spermatorrhea properly so called
or emission of semen without erections. Strangury with nervous weakness. Sweat smells like urine, in evening.
MIND - Thoughts are confused. Verysoberand depressed in spirits. Very dull at night. Not able to think steadily
on any subject. Cannot concentrate on any subject, the effort causes heavy full, pain if persisted at.
Abdomen - Severe colicky or cramping pains in small intestines. Severe pain in left groin and testicle.
Back - When headache is less severe, it is worse in neck and shoulders. Weakness and heavy dragging pain
in lumbar region.
Chest - Oppression of chest, feeling of fulness, inability to take a full breath.
Ears - Bruised tearing pain, as if ears being torn off. Inflammation of Eustachian tube, left ear swollen in and
out, tender to pressure, constant aching, bleeding readily, thick white, bloody, foul-smelling pus. Continued
singing and ringing with creaking sound in left ear.
Eyes - Purulent inflammation of left eye, sticking discharge causing gumming of lids, conjunctiva granular and
rough. Muscles of eyes feel stiff, pain on moving them quickly. Burning, sensitive to light. Effects of exposure
to strong light, squinting, sclerotitis, watery or purulent discharges.
Female - Leucorrhea.
Head - Sharp, shooting pain over left eye, when sitting in stooping posture leaves eye, passes into neck and
along muscles of shoulder and beneath scapula. Shooting in coronary region and in right side of face from
eyes to teeth in morning. Dull, dragging pain in occiput, neck and shoulders, when less severe in head is worse
in shoulder. Scalp sore, combing hair causes pain (Cina.).
Kidneys - Congestion of kidneys with dull pain in back, running down the ureters and limbs. Pain behind
pubes. Kidney pain, colic (Berb., Pareir., Calc.). Spasmodic stricture. Tenesmus of bladder and urethra.
Difficult and frequent urination. Must urinate every five minutes, urine dropping away all the time and burning
like fire. Stinging, burning pain in urethra, behind glans during urination. Irritable bladder from enlarged prostate
gland or from pressure of uterus.
Lungs - Oppression of chest, feeling of fullness inability to take a long breath. Short, hacking cough. Cough
with sensation of constriction in throat. Smarting in throat and larynx.
Male - Discharge of prostatic fluid from slight causes. Desire suppressed, then excited with lewd dreams and
pollutions. Seminal emissions without erections, with lassitude (Dios., Phos-ac). Emissions without erections,
day and night, followed by great lassitude after injury to testicles. Gonorrhea with painful erections. Gleet.
Modalities - Better from heat. Worse from motion, mental exertion. Bending head forward aggravates head
symptoms. Turning eyes causes pain in them. Most symptoms occur on left side and extend or move from part
to part.
Mouth - Thick, tenacious, disagreeable mucus in mouth.
Nose - Profuse, thick, yellow mucus discharge.
Rectum - Constipation. Tenesmus at stool, with a sensation of cutting as they pass through anus. Stools dark
leaden color, dry and very hard. Mucus diarrhea of children. Hemorrhoids and prolapsed anus.
Stomach - Partial anorexia. Hollowness or emptiness in stomach with heavy, dragging pain. Nausea, followed
by acrid belchings. Spitting of bright arterial blood, mixed with black clots, with burning in epigastrium after a
blow on the stomach. Burning in stomach or esophagus after taking the drug.
Throat - Chronic laryngitis. Smarting, raw pain along left side of throat, dry tongue. Intense redness, slight
swelling without pain, profuse secretion of thick whitish mucus.
Vertigo - Vertigo with an expanding sensation in frontal region above eyes, worse stooping, causing dimness
of sight.
COMMENTS - Ery-a. has two remarkable cures, reported by Dr. Parks. In the first, a married man injured his
testicles by jumping upon a horse, this was followed by discharge of what was considered semen for fifteen
years during which time he was treated by allopaths and homeopaths.
The emissions were without erections, day or night, and followed by great lassitude. Dr. Parks tried a number
of the usual remedies without permanent benefit. He then gave a half grain dose, three times a day of the third
 decimal trituration of the “Eryngium aquaticum.” In five days the emissions were entirely suppressed and did
not return.
The second case concerned a married man who was not conscious of having sustained any injury, who was
troubled for eight to ten years with emissions at night with erections The semen also passed by day with urine.
The loss of semen was followed by great lassitude and depression, continuing from twelve to forty-eight hours.
There was also partial impotence. He had been treated al- lopathically.
Dr. Parks gave him Ph-ac. for two weeks without material benefit. He then the Ery- a., as above with the same
excellent and prompt result.
J. Whitfield cured three cases of kidney colic with stones (two left side, the other not stated) with Ery-a.
Hale found it useful in epidemic influenza when there was raw, smarting burning in throat and larynx, with
constant irritating cough and expectoration of yellow mucus. Loss of energy and nervous weakness.
W. K. Leonard reported the following case of a young Methodist minister, apparently healthy, who was just
over his twelfth attack of kidney colic.
The attacks had recurred at intervals of two to four weeks and lasted from one to three days. They were so
weakening as to keep him incapacitated in the intervals.
He had old-school treatment including morphine and quinine, without benefit. The attacks were accompanied
with severe nervous chills and it was for these that the quinine had been prescribed. Ery-a. tincture, five drops
three times a day, put an end to the trouble.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Con., Cann-i., Dios., Oci., Clem.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Eryngium Maritimum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ery-m. Eryngium maritimum. Sea holly. N. O. Umbelliferae. Tincture of whole plant including
root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cough. Debility. Fever. Herpes. Sexual weakness. Skin eruption.
HERBAL - The maritime Eryngium is a beautiful plant growing on sand-hills by the sea with holly-like leaves
of a pale blue color with metallic luster, in general appearance much more resembling a thistle than an
Umbelliferae.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ery-m. was proved by one pro ver only, E. B. Ivatts, but the symptoms showed considerable
resemblance to those of Ery-a.
Pains in the eyes, groins, larynx, nape of neck, sinking at epigastrium and weakness of the male sexual organs
appear in both. Ery-m. has its symptoms more prominently on the right side. Circulation deadened or as if
stagnated, but great determination of blood to surface.
MIND - Light and unusually cheerful. On awaking in the morning feeling so merry commences to sing in bed
(usually heavy and drowsy).
Abdomen - All viscera seemed prostrated and as heavy as lead. Dull, continuous pain in bowels. Pain in one
spot in right groin.
Back - Pain at nape, compelling the support of head on hand or against something. Occasional shooting pains
under left scapula.
Eyes - Pain at back of right eye, left eye feeling weak. Inclination to close eyes to shut out moving objects.
Fever - Chills commencing at nape, going down shoulders and back. Chills predominate, little fever heat
Limbs - Veins of hands at back appear contracted and depressed so as to be hardly visible, though generally
full and prominent. Sore pain in muscles inside right thigh just above knee.
Lungs - Occasional darting pains through lungs to back. Occasional stomach cough during the day, sending
a spasmodic pain to the head.
Male - Insensibility of corona glandis. Absence of desire (secondary action), power of erection quite gone.
Skin - Patch of eruption half the size of palm of hand came out in cluster where pain had been the day previous
like fine pin-heads, points feeling rough to fingers, died away next day leaving red areola.
Stomach - Loss of appetite. Sinking feeling at pit of stomach.
Throat - Voice low, larynx feels weak. Great dryness of throat, larynx and lips.
Urine - Increased flow of urine, very red, thick on standing.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phel., Con. and other Umbelliferae.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Erythrinus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - eryth. Erythrinus. Red mullet fish. N. O. Erythrininae. South America. Tincture of the whole fish.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Pityriasis rubra. Syphilis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Burnett is the authority for this medicine. He based his use of it on an account of its
effects on some sailors who ate the fish and came out with a peculiar red rash which became chronic and
which the doctors took for a form of syphilis.
COMMENTS - Burnett cured with it a case of pityriasis rubra appearing in a large patch on the chest, and
benefited other cases. He believed this form of skin affection to be a manifestation of syphilis in the second
generation, the father of the patient he cured having had syphilis.
RELATIONS - Aur-m. is the complementary remedy.
REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Eschscholtzia Californica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - esch. Eschscholtzia califor- nica. California poppy. N. O. Papaveraceae. Tincture of the whole
plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Insomnia. Paralysis.
HERBAL - A harmless soporific herbal remedy (Aven.), experiments showed it to act like morphine. It has
been used as a nerve sedative to help induce a peaceful sleep.
Esch, causes general weakness torpor, accelerated respiration, complete paralysis of the limbs. Slowing of
the circulation. Nervous and restless. Insomnia due to anxiety and worry.
REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Eserinum Physostigminum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - esin. Eserinum physostigminum. Eserine. Physostigmine. The alkaloid of Physostigma
venenosum, Calabar Bean. Trituration or solution. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Astigmatism. Blepharospasm. Ciliary, spasm. Glaucoma. Headaches. Heart, weakness. Pupil,
contracted. Salivation. Sweat, excessive. Vision, blurred. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Eserine, the alkaloid of physostigma, is best known as used by oculists to procure
contraction of the pupils in glaucoma. Esin, contracts the pupils dilated by atropine, but not those by Gels. It
slows the action of the heart and increases arterial tension.
Ciliary spasm and spasmodic astigmatism due to irregular action of ciliary muscles. Blepharospasms with
pupils contracted.
Twitching of lids, soreness of eyeballs. Blurred vision after using eyes. Pains around eyes and head.
Eyes - Contraction of pupils. Spasm of accommodation. Ciliary spasm. Blepharospasm. Pain and irritation of
eyes on continued reading. Used locally to contract the pupil.
Face - Pale color.
Head - Violent headache with repeated vomiting.
Heart - Signs of cardiac weakness increased, after repeated vomiting. Pulse small and thready.
Mouth - Saliva, first increased, later arrested.
Perspiration - Face and upper part of the body covered with profuse perspiration.
Stomach - Vomited profusely, with headache. Repeated vomiting with signs of cardiac weakness.
COMMENTS - A remark of Mittendorf that “spasm of the accommodation is also produced artificially by
Eserine,” led R. B. Leach to prescribe successfully the 6x trituration in cases of ciliary spasm and of
astigmatism due to irregular action of the ciliary muscles. Esin, has also produced blepharospasm.
A solution of one grain to the drachm (mixed in mistake for a grain to the ounce) was instilled into the eye of a
woman of 60 suffering from cataract. Sweating and lach rymation followed and, as these passed off in a quarter
of an hour “clonic spasm of the eyelids’’ set in, “the upper lid falling down on the lower every few seconds.”
Spasmodic feeling in lips and the same sensation under jaw of left side followed. Feeling of tremor and spasm
without retinal movement, followed in an hour. Pupils contracted to small point.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phys., Jab., Opium.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Estrogen
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - estro. Estrogen. A female hormone. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergic reaction. Amenorrhea. Blood, clots. Breast cancer. Breast, disorders. Candida.
 Depression. Dizziness. Dryness. Fibroid. Fluid retention. Gallbladder, disease. Gynecomastia. Hair loss.
Heart, disease. Hemorrhage. Hepatitis. High blood pressure. Hot, flashes. Migraine. Menopause. Nausea.
Pancreatitis. PMS. Rash. Strokes. Tumors. Twitching. Weight, loss. Vaginitis. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - More common side effects may include: Back pain, headache. Skin redness and irritation
at the site of the patch.
Less common or rare side effects may include: Abdominal cramps, bloating. Breakthrough bleeding. Breast
enlargement. Breast tenderness. Change in cervical secretions, Change in menstrual flow. Change in sex
drive. Change in weight. Darkening of skin.
Dizziness. Fluid retention. Growth of benign fibroid tumors in the uterus. Intolerance to contact lenses.
Migraine. Nausea. Rash. Severe allergic reaction. Vaginal bleeding.
Other side effects reported with estradiol include: Abnormal withdrawal bleeding. Certain cancers.
Cardiovascular disease. Excessive growth of hair. Gallbladder disease. Hair loss. High blood pressure.
Reddened skin. Twitching. Vaginal yeast infection
Menopausal symptoms. Atrophic vaginitis. Dizziness. Mild headaches. Myocardial infarction. Pulmonary
embolism. Thrombophlebitis.
MIND - Depression.
Abdomen - Pancreatitis. Abdominal cramping or bloating. Abdominal pain, tenderness, or swelling.
Breasts - Breast pain. Breast tenderness. Breast enlargement. Breast tumors. Breast lumps. Discharge from
breast.
Chest - Pain in your chest or calves.
Eyes - Vision changes. Yellowing of the eyes.
Female - Amenorrhea. Breakthrough bleeding. Heavier vaginal bleeding between regular menses.
Menopausal symptoms. Menorrhagia, prolonged or heavier menses. Vaginaldryness. Spotting, lighter
vaginal bleeding between regular menses. Endometrial atrophy. Libido decreased. Abnormal bleeding of the
vagina.
Food - Anorexia. Loss of appetite.
Head - Migraine headaches. Severe headache, dizziness, or faintness.
Limbs - Peripheral edema. Weakness or numbness of an arm or leg. Thrombophlebitis.
Liver - Gallbladder obstruction. Hepatitis.
Lungs - Sudden shortness of breath. Coughing up blood. Pulmonary embolism.
Male - Gynecomastia. Libido decreased.
Rectum - Diarrhea.
Skin - Dryness of skin. Skin irritation, redness, or rash. Darkening of skin. Yellowing of skin.
Stomach - Nausea. Vomiting.
Temperature - Hot flushes and sweats.
Throat - Difficulty with speech.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sep., Foil., Lach., Puls.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Eucalyptus Globulus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - eucal. Eucalyptus globulus. Blue gum-tree. Fever-tree. N. O. Myrtacae. Tincture of fresh leaves.
Essential oil, Eucalyptol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aneurysm. Aortitis. Asthma. Bladder, disorders. Bronchitis. Cachexia. Coryza. Diarrhea.
Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Dysuria. Fistulae. Gonorrhea. Gout. Influenza Intermittent, fever. Kidney, disease.
Migraines. Nephritis. Ophthalmia. Quinine, cachexia. Rheumatism. Spleen, affection. Strychnine, poisoning.
Syphilis. Toxemia. Tumors. Typhoid. Urethra, stricture. Urethral, caruncle. Varicose, ulcers. Worms.
HERBAL - Eucalyptus, the gum-tree, is a native of Australia. It was transplanted to marshy districts in mild
climates on account of its capability of absorbing water and its alleged power of destroying malarial poisons.
Eucal. became well-known during the influenza epidemic as a prophylactic and disinfectant. Eucalyptus is a
powerful antiseptic and disinfectant.
Merrel noted that the volatile oil possesses in common with other terpenes, the property of converting water in
the presence of air and sunlight into hydrogen peroxide or to convert oxygen into ozone.
Used locally in catarrhal affections, especially when of a suppurating or putrid nature. Enlarged, ulcerated
tonsils and inflamed throat. Use the tincture locally as a gargle.
HOMEOPATHIC - Eucal. affects the mucus membranes, producing profuse acrid and foul catarrhal
discharges, with aching, stiffness and weariness, as from taking cold. Marked effects on catarrhal processes,
 malaria and intestinal disturbances.
Relapsing or intermittent fevers. Typhoid fever. Malaria. Useful in convalescence from intermittents. Odorous
sweat. Influenza (Gels.), said to be a preventive for influenza. Coryza, headache of a dull, congestive
character, sore throat.
Hemorrhages internally and locally (Ham.). Exhausted with toxemia and hemorrhage. Sticking, jerking pains
at night. Remarkable bodily exhaustion, no desire for any motion, unable to do any real mental work, study,
etc. Rheumatism.
Atonic dyspepsia, gastric and intestinal catarrh. Indigestion with excessive development of fetid gas and fever.
Slow digestion. A gastro-intestinal irritant with pain in stomach and upper intestines several hours after eating.
Diuresis and increase of urea.
MIND- Mental exhilaration. Exhilaration with feeling of buoyancy and increased strength. Desire for exercise,
to move about. Intoxication followed by mental depression and exhaustion. Dull and drowsy.
Abdomen - Gastrointestinal derangements with sleeplessness and restlessness. Burning in epigastrium
and umbilical regions. As if a weight in bowels. Sharp aching in the hypogastrium, worse after dinner. Flatulent
distention. Spleen hard and contracted.
Breasts - Swellings in different parts of body, one below nipple in right side, size of filbert with stabbing, darting
pains.
Ears - Tinnitus. Ringing in ears.
Eyes - Eyes hot, burning, smarting. Eyes smart and burn. Catarrhal ophthalmia. Eyelids heavy. Gonorrheal
ophthalmia. Dim vision.
Face - Flushed, congested face.
Female - Acrid, fetid leucorrhea. Ulcer around orifice of urethra. Vasculartumors of urethra.
Food - Increased appetite, tormenting thirst.
Head - Cerebral congestion with much excitement. Dull and congestive headache. Migraine. Sick headache.
Nervous headache, and other pains in head, not exactly periodical. Headache in anemic persons. Eucal.
relieves the pain and causes sleep.
Heart - Painful palpitation. Strong beating of abdominal aorta. Aneurysms pressing on vagus nerve. Sudden
flushing of face with much flatulence, in women at menopause.
Kidneys - Suppurative inflammation of kidneys. A cute nephritis, complications from influenza. Urethral
caruncle. Bladder feels loss of expulsive force. Catarrh of bladder. Spasmodic stricture, gonorrhea. Burning
and tenesmus. Diuresis. Hematuria. Urine contains pus and is deficient in urea. Urine has the odor of violets.
Limbs - Rheumatic pains, worse at night, walking orcarrying anything. Stiff, weary sensation. Pricking
sensation, followed by painful aching. Nodular swellings over metacarpal and metatarsal joints.
Lungs - Asthma with great dyspnea and palpitations. Breathing is quickened. Cardiac asthma. Moist
asthma. Bronchial asthma. Bronchitis in elderly, feeble pesons. Bronchorrhea (Bals-p.). Fetid
form of bronchitis, bronchial dilatation and emphysema. Irritativecough. Coughs of influenza. Profuse
expectoration of offensive muco-pus. Expectoration is white, thick with frothy mucus. Whooping cough in
rickety children.
Male - Increased sexual appetite. Subacute and chronic gonorrhea. Recent chancres.
Modalities - Worse periodically. Worse night.
Mouth - Aphthae. Mouth burns. Mouth feels full. Relaxed aphthous condition. Excessive secretion of saliva.
Slightly burning taste extending into throat and esophagus with thirst. Tongue pasty.
Nose - Coryza, sore throat. Stuffed-up sensation . Thin, watery coryza, nose does not stop running. Chronic
catarrhal, purulent and fetid discharge. Ethmoid and frontal sinus involved. Tension across the nose,
tightness across the bridge.
Rectum - Dysentery with rectal heat, tenesmus, hemorrhage. Typhoid diarrhea. Aching pains in bowels with
feeling of impending diarrhea. Acute diarrhea. Chronic diarrhea, mucus and bloody. Stools thin, watery,
preceded by sharp pains. Fetor of stools and flatus. Condition of mucus membrane favoring worms.
Sensations - Burning pains and sensations predominate, but also pricking, stabbing, and sharp aching.
Skin - Glandular enlargements and nodular swelling over joints. Foul and indolent ulcers. Herpetic eruptions.
Stomach - Hot, burning sensation in stomach. Strong smelling, burning eructations. Slow difficult and painful
digestion with much fetid gas. Pain in epigastrium and upper abdomen ameliorated by food. Beating and
emptiness with pulsation in epigastric arteries. Throbbing in stomach. Fullness, pressure and weight in
stomach. Malignant disease of stomach with vomiting of blood and sour fluid. Cancer. Nausea and vomiting
with chill.
Temperature - Chill, then nausea and vomiting. Fever with aching. Continued and typhoid fevers. Scarlet
fever.
 Throat - Aphthous condition of throat with burning. Burns, feels full. Excessive secretions of saliva. Constant
sensation of phlegm in throat. Enlarged, ulcerated tonsils and inflamed throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo during all stages of intermittent fever.
COMMENTS - Vascular conditions including a distinct beating in stomach region, accompanying a sense of
emptiness, one prover referred this to the abdominal aorta. V ascular tumors of the female urethra. Glandular
enlargements and nodular swellings over joints.
Marked periodicity. Most pains occur at night. It has an intoxicating effect and produces adesire forexercise.
Discharges show a tendency to foulness, high temperature, accelerated but not strong pulse. Largely used for
bronchitis and bronchial asthma.
It cured a tumor, the size of a filbert with stabbing pains below left nipple.
C. E. Fischer cured many case of dysentery with it.
Dr. Arthur Dalzell related two striking cases of bronchial asthma promptly relieved with five-drop doses of Oil
of Eucalyptus given in a tablespoonful of water. The dose was given last thing at night. It also relieved the
dyspnea in a case of mitral insufficiency.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Eucalyptus tereti- coris - menstrual cough and prostration. (2) Eucalyptol -
depresses temperature of healthy body more than Quinine, acts on kidneys like Ter., Anae., Hydr., Kali-s.
Eucalyptus neutralizes ill effectsofStry. (3) Angophora, Red Gum - dysentery, pains, tenesmus, better lying flat
on face, obstinate constipation. Eucalyptus rostrata, Kino.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Eugenia Jambosa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - eug. Eugenia jambosa. Rose- apple. Jambosa vulgaris. Eugenia vulgaris. Malabar, Plum-tree.
N. O. Myrtacae. A tree native to the tropics, never without flower or fruit. Tincture of fresh seeds. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne rosacea. Catarrhal, fever. Catarrhs. Comedones. Constipation. Coryza. Cough. Cramps.
Diarrhea. Diplopia. Hernia. Hiccough. Impotence. Influenza. Nausea. Otitis. Pimples. Throat, sore.
HOMEOPATHIC - Eug. like Eucal., produces a state of intoxication similar to alcohol. Talkative, but indolent.
Excitement soon changing to depression. Characteristic better after urination,becomes more cheerful,
exhilarated, but passing into gloominess again soon after. Nausea, better from smoking.
Acne rosacea. Acne, simple and indurated. Comedones. The pimples are painful for Some distance around.
Sufferings occur especially in the evening and at night. An old wound from a thrust became painful again.
Rheumatic pain wanders from place to place with catarrh.
MIND - Quite talkative but indolent. Prefers to do nothing but smoke all day. Remarkably changed, mentally,
after urination. Sadness better urination, but soon everything became gloomy again.
Constant desire to sit alone and reflect. Everything seems wrong. Nothing seems right. Restlessness,
constantly changing positions. Forgets all his business. Delusion, all things seem beautiful after urination.
Abdomen - Flatulence, rumbling in bowels.
Colic, with labor-like pains, pressing downward, much urging to stool and to urinate. Burning pain in abdomen.
Drawing about navel. Inguinal hernia from a fall.
Back - Burning, itching in a small spot on back, worse after scratching. Sticking pains in back. Pain in small of
back and in calves. Aching in sacrum and knees.
Ears - Catarrhal otitis.
Eyes - Eyes look sleepy and drunken. Burning pain, in the afternoon. Suddenly biting in the eyes as from
pepper. Needle-like stitches in inner canthus right eye. Hot lachrymation. Lachrymation with burning and
gnawing pains. Whirling before right eye.
Face - Pimples on the face with painful sensibility of their circumferences.
Food - Appetite increased. Great thirst. Great desire to smoke tobacco (Calad., Daph.). Agreeable taste, of
tobacco, of food and drink when smoking.
Head - Headache as if a board were lying on right side. Dullness and slight sticking pain. Pressive, pinching
pain, in small spot deep in forehead. Pressive pinching pain, on vertex. Neuralgia in left forehead over eye.
Headache in evening nausea, vomiting. Nocturnal headache, with burning in eyes, great thirst and much
urination.
Kidneys - Burning during urination. Frequent urination at night. Shuddering or sudden increase of brightness
and of light before the eyes after urinating. Deepcolored urine.
Limbs - Nightly cramps in soles of feet (Calc., Cupr.. Mag-p.). Fissures between toes. Skin recedes from
the nails, forming pus. Cramp-like and paralytic pains in the tibia and in the heels. Hot hands.
 Lungs - Catarrh with much mucus and rheumatic pains. Rattling in lungs. Moist cough without yellowish,
bloody expectoration in the evening and at night.
Male - Impotence. Emission of semen too slow or entirely wanting during sex. Perspiration and thirst after sex.
Mouth - Abundant accumulation of frothy and viscid saliva in the mouth, especially before a meal and when
talking.
Nose - Mucus goes from nose into throat. Perspiration - Sweats when walking. Rectum - Cramp or pinching
pains in rectum. Constipation. Urging to stool and colic. Tenesmus, urging to stool. Loose evacuation, followed
by vomiting. Hemorrhoids bleed copiously for days with great relief of mind and body. Scanty evacuation
of stool, the consistence of pap and sandy, spurting and fetid. Very scanty,
pasty, gritty stool. Scanty, hard stool after much pressing, followed by spasmodic closure of anus.
Offensive, sputtering stool, without much urging.
Sensations - Headache as if a heavy board were lying on right side. As of cramp in orifice of stomach, as if a
ten-pound weight were hanging on rectum and as if everything below would fall out.
Skin - Acne rosacea. Acne, simple and indurated. Comedones. Desquamation and suppuration of the skin
around the nail of the thumb. Skin cracks about toes.
Sleep - Profound sleep. Stupefying sleep, even at noon with confused dreams. Yawning while walking in open
air. Difficult waking.
Stomach - Heartburn at night. Cramp in orifice of stomach, causing nausea. Contractive, pinching sensation
deep in stomach. Sensation as of cramp in orifice of stomach, which results in nausea. Nausea rising up from
end of esophagus.
Temperature - Shiverings run over him after urination. Coldness, as if the body were naked. Perspiration in
the morning with burning thirst. Hot hands. Fever, heat before midnight with little thirst and much sweat.
Throat - At night, violent thirst from dryness low down in throat, so that he did not feel the drink, which also did
not better the dryness. Pain in small spot in region of left corner of hyoid bone. Inflamed throat (in catarrhal
fever).
Vertigo - Whirling in head while sitting. Vertigo after rising from lying down. Vertigo caused by rush of blood
to head. Dizzy and nauseated, in evening.
COMMENTS - Effects the eyes and vision. Darkness and double vision, on looking intently double vision
disappears. Whirling before right eye as if it would become dark. Whirling in the head while sitting, houses at
a distance seem to turn bottom upwards.
Inflamed eyes. As though fire came out of eyes and tears ran out in streams in evening and night. Worse by
sun, causes eyes to fill with water. Burning worse by closing eyes, prevents sleeping at night. Burning not
better from cold water.
Pain in small of back and calves. Aching in sacrum and knees. Sticking pain in back as if something were
sticking in spine, better by bending back. Rheumatic pain wanders from place to place with catarrh.
An old wound from a thrust became painful again. Skin disease, worse during menses. Open air causes much
exhaustion, yawning while walking in morning.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Coffee, by smoking tobacco. Compare: (1) Myrtus chekan - chronic bronchitis.
(2) Ant-t., Berb-a. (3)Eucal. a myrtaceous tree in catarrhal conditions, Laur. and drugs containing Hydrocyanic
acid, Puls. - fugitive rheumatic pains.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Euonyminum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - euonin. Euonyminum. A concentrated extract, so-called active principle from the bark of
Euonymus Americana, E. atropurpúrea and other American species of Euonymus. Celastraceae. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bright's disease. Cholera. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Gallstones. Indigestion.
Liver, disorders. Nausea.
HOMEOPATHIC - Euonyminum is largely used by herbalists in cases of constipation, indigestion, and torpid
liver. It has not been proved, but Hale quoted the following account of its effects, which do not seem to differ
much from Euon.
“In very large doses, it proves a drastic cathartic, its operation being attended with a death-like nausea,
excessive tormina and cold sweats. The dejections from the bowels are profuse, violent and accompanied by
much flatus.”
COMMENTS - Lutze recorded a case of albuminuria of pregnancy with dropsy cured with the 1 x, and also a
case of albuminuria and dropsy in a young man of seventeen. This patient had eczema and was cured by
Lutze with Ars. 200c. Later he got a chill from standing in the water fishing. He suffered from malaise and
 finally dropsy developed.
Euonyminum
After a week of treatment, he was indifferent, drowsy, sleeping most of the day and night, sometimes with
heavy breathing. Anasarca general, chiefly in face and limbs. Pulse full, slow, 50 to 60.
Occasionally dull frontal or occipital headache, face sallow, sclerotics yellow, temperature 102 to 103. Urine
scanty, 1,017 (later 1,009), containing large quantities of albumen, epithelial casts and granular debris, no bile
or chlorides. Stool grayish. He had no pains or subjective symptoms.
There were all the evidences of a fully- developed case of acute Bright's disease. He was given Euonymus lx,
2 grains in half a tumbler of water, a spoonful every hour. In three days there was evident improvement. The
treatment was continued for a month, when he was nearly well, the cure being completed with Puls., Calc.,
Sulph. at long intervals.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Euonymus Atropurpurea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - euon-a. Euonymus atropurpúrea. Burning bush. Wahoo. N. O. Celastra- ceae. Tincture of fresh
bark and root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bilious fever. Biliousness. Cholera morbus. Constipation. Diarrhea. Gallstones. Gout.
Heart, weakness. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Levitation. Liver disorders. Rheumatism. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Euon-a„ like Euonin. and Euon., is a favorite liver remedy among herbalists. It has not been
proved, but clinical experience shows that its action is very like that of its botanical relatives.
Migraines. Headache, mental disturbances and much distress in hepatic and kidney region. Bilious headache,
coated tongue, bad taste, constipation.
Passive congestion and torpor of liver. Chronic catarrhal disorders of stomach and intestines. Profuse stools,
varying or of several colors. Albuminuria. Chronic rheumatism and gout. Weak heart.
MIND - Mental confusion. Loss of memory,
Euonymus atropurpúrea unable to recall familiar names. Despondent, irritable.
Abdomen - Flatus and pain. Pain about umbilical region, navel.
Back - Crawling in back. Dull pain between shoulders and about kidney and splenic region, pain in lumbar
region better lying down.
Constitutions - Brunettes more easily affected.
Head - Bilious headaches, pressure over brows, compressing eyes. Heavy frontal headache. Sore, tired
feeling, bruised feel ing of scalp. Pain overright eye extending back through the head.
Kidneys - Urine scanty, high-colored. Acid ity increased. Urine poured out rapidly.
Limbs - Aching in all joints, especially ankles. Feet feel swollen and tired.
Liver - Liver engorged. Gallstones.
Modalities - Better from cool air. Better pressure. Worse from eating. Worse evening.
Mouth - Dry, pasty taste.
Rectum - Anus very sore and burning. Constipation with hemorrhoids and severe backache. Diarrhea, stools
variable and profuse, bloody.
Stomach - Thirsty. Feels full and uncomfortable.
Vertigo - Vertigo, obscure vision and gastric derangement, associated with albuminuria. Vertigo in forehead,
as if drawn up and pitched forward.
COMMENTS - A woman who tasted the juice of the bark related her experience to Hale: “I felt immediately a
sick weakening feeling all through the nervous system, dull, heavy pain through upper portion of head together
with enlarged blurred feeling. I seemed so drawn up from the floor, that is seemed difficult to place my foot
down when walking with sufficient firmness to stand up, a tipping over sensation when sitting and walking.”
She also had a deathly sickness at her stomach with perspiration and heat in her face, in alternation with chills
in the back and back part of the arms. Some of the symptoms returned the next day, but were dissipated by
vinegar, which must be looked upon as its antidote.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Euonymus Euro- poea. Spindle-tree - liverdisorders, biliousness, lumbago,
gastric derangements with albuminuria. (2) Cutting pains in malar bones tongue, penis up to bladder, Podo.
(3) Am-pic., Chel., Euonymin lx trituration, albuminuria.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Euonymus Europaea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - euon. Euonymus europaea. Spindle-tree. N. O. Celastraceae. Trituration of dried seeds.
Tincture of fresh seeds. Historical dose: Trimration and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Albuminuria. Backaches.BiZioMS. Cholera. Collapse. Constipation. Convulsions. Diarrhea.
Gallstones. Gastric, derangements. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Liver, disorders. Lumbago. Pusmles. Vertigo.
HERBAL - The Celastraceae, to which Euonymus belongs, are closely related to the Rhamnacae which
include the well-known purgative Cascara sagrada.
HOMEOPATHIC - Euon. has been used successfully in cases of engorgement of the liver, biliousness,
headache, coated tongue, bad taste, and constipation. Passive constipation with hemorrhoids or severe pain
in back like lumbago.
Diarrhea, profuse stool, variable in color. Gastric derangements with albuminuria, headache, weakness,
vertigo and obscuration of sight. Liver disorders, biliousness, lumbago.
COMMENTS - Allen recalls the effects ofEuon- yminum in a case of poisoning with the seeds. “A man, forty-
three took eighteen seeds one morning and as many the following evening. He was seized with frightful
abdominal pain and profuse diarrhea, eventually bloody.
“He was not seen until the evening, when he was in a state of profound collapse with involuntary evacuations
of blood and mucus. On lifting him up tetanic convulsions were induced which immediately preceded death.”
In its proving, cutting, sticking and drawing pains predominated. The left side is more affected than the right.
Cutting pains in the
malar bones in the tongue. Cutting in the penis extends up to the bladder.
Pains compel lying down and are then relieved or reappear in other parts. Violent shivering chill over whole
body. Pains in chest, head and abdomen, worse after eating. Tingling in the skin which provokes scratching,
followed by a burning sensation. Eruption of small dry pustules.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Podo., Rham., Iris. Euon. atrop.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Eupatorium Aromaticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - eup-a. Eupatorium aromaticum. White snake-root. Eupatorium urticifolium. Deer-wort. Pool-
root. N. O. Composite. Found in low woods from Massachusetts to Louisiana. Flowers are white and aromatic.
Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ague. Aphthae. Chorea. Gravel. Hysteria. Neurasthenia. Sore, nipples. Stomatitis. Vomiting.
HERBAL - Eupatorium aromaticum, when chewed, produces in the mouth a warm, aromatic, pungent
sensation and is regarded as a “warm, stimulating tonic.”
Hale quoted herbal authorities as commending this plant in “aphthous stomatitis” in women and children. Also
for burning in the stomach with “nursing sore mouth,” before and after confinement. Locally it is useful as a
mouthwash.
Eup-a. is a “nervine,” like Scutellaria and Cypripedium for “restlessness and morbid watchfulness, morbid
irritability of the nervous system, tremors, chorea and hysteria.” Like Eup-pur., it has been used for gravel. The
Native Americans used it as a cure for ague.
HOMEOPATHIC - Eup-a. is doubly indicated where nervous weakness and aphthous disease are combined.
Nervous weakness, restlessness and morbid watchfulness.
Hysteria and chorea. Low fevers with extreme restlessness. Aphthous disease. Sore nipples. Sore mouth in
infants.
Vomiting of bile, pain in stomach, headache and fever.
COMMENTS - In a case of sore mouth in a man, 57, recorded by P. S. Duff, Eup-a. caused soon “a general
aggravation like a cold or catarrh, annoyed by pain in left shoulder, posterior scapular region, pulse 94
unnatural, tight in left bronchia, felt ill, dull and oppressed.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lapsana communis - useful in sore nipples andhemorrhoids. (2) Hyos., Passi.,
Hydrin-mur.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
