name: Ferrum Arsenicosum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr-ar. Ferrum arsenicosum. Iron arseniate. Tri-ferric diarsenate. Trituration. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Anemia. Bright's disease. Chilly. Chlorosis. Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea.
Eczema. Headache. Impetigo. Leucorrhea. Liver, enlargement. Psoriasis. Spleen, enlargement.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hale was the first to use Ferr-ar., giving the 2x with a promptly curative result to an anemic
girl who had been given iron and arsenic separately, under old-school treatment, in vain.
P. C. Majumdar put Ferr-ar. to excellent use in cases of enlarged liver and spleen with fever. When there is no
fever Ferr-i. is better.
Enlarged liver and spleen with high fever of a continued type. During fever the face is flushed and sweaty, but
during the intermission the face is pale. No thirst during any stage of the fever, heat intense and prolonged
with slight burning of the whole body, emaciation and debility.
Undigested stool. Constipation, sometimes, colliquative diarrhea, the stools consisting of undigested matter
and mucus. Albuminuria. Skin dry. Eczema, psoriasis, impetigo. Simple and pernicious anemia and chlorosis.
Disinclination to work, even to leave his bed.
MINDS - Conscientious about trifles. Restlessness at night, driving out of bed. Sensitive to noise. Fear in a
crowd. Fear of evil. Fear of people. Tossing about in bed.
COMMENTS - Majumdar reported two cases. The first, concerning a robust, healthy man, 25, who went into
a malaria district of Bengal and had his first attack of fever. He was given large does of quinine, which
suppressed the paroxysms for a time, but they continually recurred.
After four years he returned home achanged man: pale, jaundiced, emaciated, abdomen filled with enlarged
and indurated liver and spleen, slightly tender to pressure. His organs left no room for food. Obstinate
constipation. High fever generally appearing in afternoon, no chill or thirst, but copious sweat without much
relief to fever.
Ferr-ar. 6c, twice daily, made an improvement in three days. It was continued for a month and a half with
occasional stoppages and in six months he was completely restored to health.
The second case concerned a boy, 15, who suffered from fever and enlarged spleen. The liver was not
enlarged.
Voracious appetite, but no digestion, undigested diarrhea stools. Continued fever, 102 to 104, burning of body.
Some thirst. Great emaciation.
Ferr-ar. 6c was given night and morning. He was cured perfectly in a year.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ferr-i., Ferr., Ars., Calc-a., Chin.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
 ***FERRUM BROMATUM
(Iron Bromide)
PHARMACY - ferr-br. Femim bromatum. Iron bromide. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Diarrhea. Headaches. Leucorrhea. Numbness. Spermatorrhea. Uterus, prolapsed.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Sarah N. Smith of New York proved Ferr-br., using the sixth dilution, made by Boericke
andTafel. Ferr-br. Produced, in this order, were very distinct symptoms in the head and eyes, dry mouth and
nose, relieved by coryza, a feeling that she might die, diarrhea, burning in urethra when urinating, sticky,
excoriating leucorrhea, and weight and discomfort in uterus.
The symptoms that made the most impression on the prover were the “dead, numbness" feeling of the scalp,
the unconscious moaning after stool and the sticky, excoriating leucorrhea. Heaviness and discomfort in the
uterus was so severe that she declined to continue the proving as it interfered with her work.
COMMENTS - Hale mentioned this remedy as having been highly commended in cases of spermatorrhea with
anemia, debility and depression.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Heavy eyes. Con., Caust., Gels. (2) Smarting while urinating, Cann-s. - has
burning while urinating and after.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Ferrum Iodatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr-i. Ferrum iodatum. Iron iodide. Trituration of freshly prepared crystals. Solution. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Alcohol, effects. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Boils. Breast, tumors. Bronchorrhea. Cancer.
Catarrh. Coryza. Debility. Diabetes. Dyspepsia. Exophthalmic, goiter. Eyes, scrofulous. Glands, enlargement.
gonorrhea. Heartbum. Impetigo. Kidneys, disorders. Leucorrhea. Li ver, enlarged. Nephritis. Pneumonia.
Scoliosis. Scrofula. Spleen, enlarged. Tuberculosis. Uterus, prolapsed. Writer's cramp.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ferrum iodatum has been independently proved, and corresponds more particularly to
scrofulous affection, glandular enlargement and tumors.
Grimmer used Ferr-i. for breast tumors, cancer, exophthalmic goiter inflammation and enlargement of glands,
symptoms and conditions based on the tubercular diathesis. Berridge removed with Fen-i. “Morning catarrh,
hot and restless in bed, sweet smell of urine.”
“Food seems to push up to throat as if it has not been swallowed,” somewhat like the Ferr. symptom “as if
something rolled into ihroal and closed il like a valve. "Sharpor cutting pains in the eyes, ears and root of nose
to occiput. Sensation as if lying in a cramped position.
Anemia. Body emaciated. Debility following drain upon vital forces. Impetigo of the cheek. Crops of boils.
Acute nephritis following eruptive diseases. Exophthalmic goiter following suppression of menses. Uterine
displacements. Breast tumors, cancer and conditions based on the tubercular diathesis.
MIND - Dullness of mind and confusion in head worse when reading aloud. Anxiety. Aversion to company.
Conscientious about trifles.
Confusion worse putting hat on. Confusion while reading. Confusion after smoking. Confusion while writing.
Abdomen - Abdomen bloated after food or drink. Fullness, even after a little food, stuffed feeling, as if she
could not lean forward. Abdomen swollen. As if a cord were drawn connecting the navel and anus.
Back - Small of back as if broken. Pain as if lying in a cramped position. Neck sore when touched or on moving.
Dull pain in back. Stiffness on getting up from bed, better during day.
Chest - Oppression of chest with inclination to lie on back. Pressure beneath sternum.
Constitutions - Suited to scrofulous or mercurial diathesis to subjects of relaxed tissue (tuberculosis in the
third stage, bronchorrhea, pneumonia).
Cough - Hemoptysis. Short, hacking cough with yellowish-white, thick expectoration.
Ears - Roaring in ears.
Eyes - Eyes shut on account of pain. Lids swollen, discharging copious quantities of pus when forcibly
 opened. Exophthalmic goiter, after menses suppressed. Burning in eyelids. Photophobia. Trachoma. Bright
objects floating before eyes, like sparks of fire, after breakfast.
Face - Red, chlorotic look. Itching of right cheek, reddening when rubbed. Submaxillary and cervical glands
swollen and hard. Vesicles, when rubbed, become raw.
Female - Amenorrhea. Menses is absent with exophthalmic goiter. Menses suppressed or scanty. Constant
bearing down. When sitting, a feeling as if something pressed upward in vagina. Retroversion and prolapse
of uterus. Prolapsed uterus, difficult to retain the urine. Itching and soreness of vulva and vagina. Leucorrhea
like boiled starch.
Food - No appetite. Craving for sardines or salty fish. Great thirst.
Head - Headache with a confused sensation. Headache with feeling of heaviness and pressure. Sharp pain
from below eye up through head to vertex. Cutting pain from bridge of nose to occiput. Headache on going to
bed. Throbbing pain in head on right side and forehead. Headache worse smoking.
Heart - Palpitations at night. Heartbeats seems to go into stomach, and cause a nervous, trembling feeling.
Bloodvessels throb all over, even when quiet. Violent beating of heart on rising or when turning in bed.
Kidneys - Difficulty in retaining urine. Incontinence in anemic children. Crawling sensation in urethra and
rectum. Sensation as if urine were stopped at fossa navicularis. Urine, sweet smelling. Urine, dark colored.
Urine, depositing thick white sediment.
Limbs - Weak, trembling feeling in limbs on using hands and on walking. Paralyzed and bruised feeling in all
limbs, with great aversion to moving about.
Lungs - Bronchorrhea. Chronic pneumonia. Shortness of breath, obliged to take a deep breath. Greenish,
purulent, containing small, cheesy particles. Grayish-white, rather tenacious mucus drawn out in threads.
Male - Nocturnal emissions with violent pain and burning in urethra. Inability to urinate. Tenesmus of neck of
bladder Prickling itching in urethra, with frequent urging to urinate, but scanty flow. Gonorrhea.
Modalities - Better from open air. Worse from motion. Worse touch. Worse warmth. Worse at night and in the
morning.
Mouth - Salivation. Sudden bleeding of gums. Offensive taste. Metallic, bitter taste. Flat, insipid taste. Taste
of peppermint. Dryness of mouth and throat. Mucus membrane of mouth bright red or dotted with red.
Nose - Nose dry, stopped up. Blowing nose gives no relief. Coryza. Scrofulous swelling of nose, with ulcers
and crusts inside. Discharge of mucus from nose, trachea, and larynx. Discharge all day, with stuffed-up feeling
at night. Discharge thick, yellow or green.
Perspiration - Sweat at night is cold and copious, and comes from the least exertion.
Rectum - Crawling in rectum. Constriction in rectum and anus. Sensation as if worms were in it. Small, hard
stool, with sticking pain. Constipation then loose stools, preceded by griping pain.
Sensations - As if anus were compressed. As if worms were in anus. As if something twisted around about in
a circle, as if a cord were drawn connecting navel and anus, as if a screw were boring in anus.
Skin - Pale skin. Eczema. Lichen. Shortlasting skin eruptions. Eruptions like urticaria.
Sleep - Frequent starting in sleep and waking with feeling as if paralyzed. Restless sleep with frequent waking.
Dreams of long past events. Dreams of thieves. Dreams of fighting with them.
Stomach - Dyspepsia with nausea and headache. Impaired digestion. Food seems to push up in the throat,
as if it had not been swallowed. Violent eructations. Sour and bitter risings. Stomach full of gas.
Throat - Sore pain, as if of a splinter, shooting in different directions. Hoarse. Violent scraping and tickling in
throat and nose. Frequent rattling of mucus in throat.
Tongue - Burning on tongue. Tongue coated thickly yellow.
Vertigo - Dizziness worse moving.
COMMENTS - P. C. MajumdarusedFerr-i. with success in cases of enlarged liver and spleen when
unaccompanied by fever. When fever is present Ferr-ars. is the better remedy.
“Feels as if she has eaten too much, a
sort of upward pressure. Stuffed feeling in abdomen as if she could not lean forward, costiveness,” especially
incasesof enlarged spleen. “Sweet-smelling urine.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Alum. - anemia, leucorrhea, prolapse uterus. Alumn. - swollen vagina, prolapse
uterus. (2) Caul. - prolapse uterus and leucorrhea from atony, fitful, crampy pains. (3) Melon. - pruritus,
prolapse, leucorrhea. albuminuria. (4) Hydr. - debility and atony, tenacious, profuse leucorrhea, palpitations.
(5) Graph. - chlorosis, leucorrhea profuse, hot, watery. (6) lod. - red face, irritability, corroding leucorrhea,
emaciation marked. (7) Kali-bi. - has stringy, albuminous leucorrhea, stringy expectoration. (8) Thyr. -
palpitations, exophthalmic goiter. (9) Ferr-br. - leucorrhea, prolapsed uterus. (10) Ferr-a. - enlarged liver and
spleen.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
 ***FERRUM MAGNETICUM
Magnetic Ferric Oxide)
PHARMACY - ferr-ma. Ferrum magneticum. Magnetic ferric oxide. Loadstone. Iron ses- quioxide. A black
oxide of iron. Historical dose: All potencies.      /
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Diarrhea. Flatus. Ganglions. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Vision, disorders. Warts.
Weakness. Whitlow.
HOMEOPATHIC - Caspari is the authority for Ferr-ma. Teste, who put Ferr-ma. in the Arnica group along with
Led., Crot-t., Rhus- t. and Spig., had some experience with it. Indicated for the sycotic constitution. Small warts
on hands.
Ferr-ma. produces paralytic weaknesses like the other iron preparations, of which this; is the most peculiar:
after perspiring during a moderate walk, weakness and lassitude, which seem to proceed from the abdomen.
Difficulty of movement and relaxation of muscles.
Prickings, lancinations, tingling and itching in different parts. Pains and itchings, some of which reappear at
intervals of four weeks. Pain in nape of neck. Trembling in the legs and arms. Excessive lassitude. Fatigue on
taking the slightest exercise.
Worse during a meal, flatulency, grumblings, movements in abdomen with urgent diarrhea after a meal (Ferr.).
Abdominal sufferings are felt more on the left side. Very abundant and frequent emission of fetid wind.
MIND - Indecision and long reflection before undertaking anything. Indolence, slowness of movement. Air of
importance and self-sufficiency. Irascibility.
Abdomen - Movements and grumbling in abdomen. Loose evacuations with much flatulency, especially left
side, with pullings in legs. Abundant and frequent emission of fetid flatus.
Chest - Tearing and lancination in the left side of the chest, when breathing. Sensation of emptiness in the
chest.
Ears - Tingling in the ears. Itching, wringing and cold lancinations in the auditory duct. Pullings in the ears and
the pharynx when swallowing.
Eyes - Pricking itching in the canthi. Painful sensibility of the lachrymal sac with profuse lachrymation. Pressive
pain on the eyelid, which impedes the sight. Swelling of the lower lid, which makes the eye appear smaller.
Darkness before the right eye, causing it to wink.
Face - Face dejected with general heat, followed by redness of the face. Itching and tingling in the face and
on the lips. Eruptions on the forehead in the eyebrows, at the root of the nose, on the cheeks, the lips and the
chin.
Head - Pulsative headache, by fits. Circumscribed headache in the morning, generally on right side. Headache
on stooping, on moving the arms, and on going up stairs. Itching in the scalp. Small, painful eruption on the
scalp. Falling off of the hair.
Kidneys - Urine red and copious, which becomes the color of clay after having stood some time.
Limbs - Cramp-like, paralytic pullings or jerking pullings in the forearms and hands. Paralytic pulling in the
right arm. Pain, as from dislocation in the wrist. Dryness and tension in the hands. Small warts on the back of
the hands and on the wrist. Whitlow. Acute lancination in the
knee. Ganglion of the foot. Tingling and pricking in the heels. Starting in the soles of the feet. Painful little toe.
Lungs - Frequent hawking of mucus. Dry cough after dinner, proceeding from an irritation in the trachea, as if
one had swallowed dust.
Male - Itching and lancination in the scrotum and in the extremity of the glans. Increased sexual desire, with
and without erection, or absence of all sexual desire, yet without importance.
Mouth - Accumulation of water and saliva in the mouth. Itching sensation in the posterior part of the palate.
Neck - In the morning, pain in the nape of the neck, as if from having lain in an inconvenient position.
Nose - Sneezing, with stoppage of one nostril and catarrh.
Rectum - Urgent want to evacuate with expulsion of flatus only. Small, liquid evacuation when expelling flatus.
Itching and shooting in the anus. Tingling and itching in the rectum.
Skin - Itching and tingling in different parts, especially in the evening, mitigated by scratching, but appearing
in other parts. Red spots, sometimes of a bright red or bluish red. some disappear on being pressed. Small
warts on the hands.
Sleep - Violent and noisy yawnings with accumulation of water in the mouth. Drowsiness with prompt sleep
on lying do wn or even when seated. Absurd dreams at night. Dreams immediately after lying down, waking
with a start, coldness causing trembling. Inclination to remain in bed in the morning. After rising, weakness in
the knees.
Stomach - Flatulence during a meal, afterwards fatigue and burning pain in epigastrium, especially on
 breathing. Nausea. Abortive risings.
Teeth - Bleeding of the gums, when slightly pressed upon. Painful sensibility of the teeth during mastication.
Temperature - Shivering and cold in the side opposite to that on which the patient has lair Heat, as if a catarrh
were developing its. If with lassitude and downcast eyes.
Internal heat with perspiration and slow pulse after washing the body. The pulse is slow and small. Perspiration
on the slightest exercise. Sweat in the morning on the body and on the occiput. Sweat of an acid smell, as in
measles.
Throat - Bitter and rancid taste in the pharynx, on hawking. Sensation as if mucus were adhering to the uvula.
Lancinations in the throat. Pressure in the esophagus, as if too much had been swallowed at one time.
COMMENTS - Ferr-ma. relieved, after Spig. failed, in an old man suffering from chronic rheumatism of the
nape of the neck with irritable disposition.
Cured a case of compound capsular cataract in a gouty patient. A third patient had rheumatism of both thighs,
coming on after violent exercise. This patient was treated in two attacks. In the first attack he received Arn.
first and then Ferr-ma. In the second, Ferr-ma. was given at once and the effect was speedy and marked.
Teste noted the case of a patient who had a very unpleasant experience with the medicine. He suffered from
a mercurial neurosis and was very sensitive to medicines. Teste was led to give the medicine due to a painful
contraction of the posterior cervical muscles, against which no remedy he had tried had produced any effect.
Teste gave Ferr-ma., four globules in a tumbler of water, two tablespoonfuls every day. The first tablespoonful,
taken in the morning, seemed to produce a sensible improvement. A quarter of an hour after the second dose,
taken at 4 p.m., the sight became dim, a halo of fire, red and violet, was seen first in front of the right eye, and
afterwards in front of the left eye.
Soon after, this halo, which formed a circular zigzag-shaped line, became narrower and narrower. Finally
produced such a complete blindness, that the patient assured Teste he was unable to distinguish night from
daylight. This lasted one hour and did not pass off entirely until after a meal.
Much more distressing phenomena followed towards 8 p.m. The pain in the nape, which first was seated on
the left side, passed
Ferrum magneticum to the right invading the whole extent of the trapezoid muscle, where it became literally
frightful.
“For two days and nights the patient, who was a brave and strong man and whom I had seen bear the most
painful surgical operations without uttering a sound, suffered to such an extent that he uttered heart-rending
cries.”
Camph., Puls, and Bry failed to relieve, the first rather aggravated. Rhus-t. effected some relief. But it did not
prevent the recurrence, for eight days in succession of the visual phenomena, though with less intensity then
the first time, at irregular intervals, generally 6 or 7 a.m. and sometimes even at night in perfect darkness.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ferr., Elect., Galv., Magn. arct., Magn. aust.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

PHARMACY - ferr-i. Ferrum iodatum. Iron iodide. Trituration of freshly prepared crystals. Solution. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Alcohol, effects. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Boils. Breast, tumors. Bronchorrhea. Cancer.
Catarrh. Coryza. Debility. Diabetes. Dyspepsia. Exophthalmic, goiter. Eyes, scrofulous. Glands, enlargement.

name: Ferrum Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr. Ferrum metallicum. Iron metal (Fe, At. Wt. 56). Includes symptomsof the acetate and the
carbonate. Triturations of the pure metal and of the carbonate, solution of the acetate. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Aphonia. Asthma. Biliousness. Blood, disorders. Blood, loss. Bruises. Cachexia.
Catalepsy. Chlorosis. Chorea. Constipation. Cough. Cramps, Debility. Diarrhea. Bedwetting. Fever,
intermittent. Goiter, exophthalmic. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhages. Heart, disorders. Hectic, fever. Hydrocephalus.
Iron, poisoning. Jaundice. Kidneys, disorders. Lienteria. Morning, sickness. Menstruation. disorders.
Miscarriages. Nausea. Neuralgia. Paralysis, viscera. Pregnancy, disorders. Rectum, prolapsed. Rectum,
weak. Rheumatism. Shoulder, pains. Spasms. Syphilis. Toothache. Tuberculosis. Urinary, incontinence.
Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ferr. is one of the prominent constituents of the animal body, present in considerable
quantity in the blood. It is present in many articles of daily food and, when given in excess, its first effect is to
increase the amount of iron in the blood.
Ferr. is adapted to young, weakly persons, anemic and chlorotic with pseudo-plethora. Over-sensitive,
weakness, but looks strong. Delicate girls, constipated, with low spirits. Red-faced old men.
Iron poisoning, symptoms including nausea and vomiting, varicose veins (Sep.), easy bruising, nosebleeds
of pale blood, swelling of the limbs, anemia, and sensitivity to smell. Bad affects of iron pills, particularly during
pregnancy.
 Anemia with weakness. Anemia in those subject to irregular distributions of blood, particularly the young.
Flushed cheeks, pallor of lips and mucus membranes, fatigue and breathlessness, and any motion will set up
the symptoms. Useful in anemia of cancer and syphilis as a secondary remedy.
Hemorrhages, bright blood or with small clots. Veins dilate during neuralgia, menses orfever. Irregular
distribution of blood. Congestions, surgings of blood and pulsations. Orgasms of blood to face, chest, head
and lungs. Flushes easily, worse after any active effort. Chlorosis, worse in winter. Hemorrhagic tuberculosis,
but it may aggravate.
Dropsy or paralysis after loss of vital fluids, hemorrhages. Rapid emaciation. Cachexia. Pressure, on chest,
stomach etc. Cold limbs, muscles relaxed and flabby. Catalepsy. Red parts become pale. Cracking in joints.
Softening of bones. Nightly pains that compel motion of part.
Ferr. stimulates the appetite, augment the heart's beats and the bodily vigor. Dryness of mouth, vagina.
Exophthalmic goiter from suppressed menses. Spleen, digestion and left deltoid are also affected.
MIND - Mind confused. Can't collect his thoughts. Confusion better washing face. Brain-fag. Always in the
right. Proud and haughty. Excitement after menses.
Sensitive, excitable. Slight noises unbearable. Irritability from noise. Oversensitive to pain. Ailments from
anger. Irritable mind and body. Excited from slightest opposition. Anger from contradiction. Intolerant of
contradiction.
Changeable mood. Nervous, hysterical. Great alternations of mood, excessively
lively, then sad and melancholic. Weeps and laughs immoderately.
Restlessness, must walk about slowly. Anxiety from slight causes. Anxiety as after committing a crime.
Fear of having a stroke. Great anxiety about family. Restlessness, driving out of bed, wants to go from one
bed to another.
Despondent after menses. Desire for solitude. Aversion to friends. Sadness better exertion. Conversation
aggravates. Occupation relieves. Great indifference. Not inclined to talk or study, from nervous restlessness.
Constant thoughts of death. Abdomen - Colic with watery diarrhea.
Rumbling in bowels. Flatulent colic at night. Bowels feel sore to touch. Hard, distended, sore, bruised when
walking. Soreness of abdominal walls. Soreness all over abdomen, better warmth. Sharp pain in abdomen.
Sensation as if bowels were bruised, or weakened by cathartics. Shooting pain in left hypochondrium. Cramp-
like in region of spleen.
Back - Neck and shoulder painful. Rheumatism of the neck and shoulder. Neck sore and stiff. Lumbago all
night, goes off on rising. Lumbago, better slow walking. Stitch-like jerks in small of back when walking. Pain
between scapula.
Blood - Blood diseases, with exhaustion. Anemia with exhaustion. Anemia with pregnancy. Chlorosis.
Hemorrhages. Ailments from blood loss. Bleeding, pale or watery blood and weakness (Chin., Phos.). Weak
blood. Hemophilia. Throbbing pains, the blood vessels all over the body throb violently. Hemorrhages from
over-fullness of blood vessels Hemorrhages from vasomotor paralysis, Hemorrhages from delicacy of the
blood vessels themselves.
Chest - Anxiety in chest. Chest oppressed, breathing difficult. Constriction of chest, worse walking. Flying
stitches in the chest. Feeling of dryness in chest. Surging of blood to chest. Rush of blood to chest and head,
with cold hands and feet. Pressure under sternum, with catarrh and cough. Sharp pain in chest when coughing.
Burning pain in sternum after coughing.
Constitutions - Sanguine temperament. Adapted to young, anemic, pseudo-plethoric persons, who though
looking strong are so weak that they are unable even to speak or walk, want to lie down.
Coughs - Cough dry, spasmodic. Dry, tickling cough, worse moving, better lying down. Cough with pain
in the occiput. Breath fails at end of coughing fit. Cough, worse abuse of tea, quinine, brandy. Cough after
loss of fluids. Tickling cough in trachea, worse moving, better lying down. Cough from tobacco smoke.
Cough after eating. Cough, must sit up to raise sputum. Hemoptysis (Mill.). Dry, tickling cough with blood
spitting. Spasmodic whooping cough at once better eating a small quantity of food.
Ears - Sharp pain in ears in morning. Ulcerative pain of outer ear. Fetid discharge from left ear. Oversensitive
to noise. Noises in ears better leaning the head on table. Ringing in the ears, worse before menses. Ringing
in right ear. Singing, humming.
Eyes - Eyes cloudy, watery, dull with blue rings around them. Eyes red with burning pain. Swelling and redness
of the eyelids. Puffy eyelids. Pain over eyes (left). Exophthalmic goiter after suppression of menses.
Photophobia. Weakness of eyes with lachrymation. Pupils contracted. Suppurating stye on upper lid.
Face - False plethora. Face feels as if bloated. Blushes easily. Pale face and flushes red from least pain,
emotions or exertion. Florid. Lips pale. Face pale with red spots on each cheek. Neuralgia after cold washing
and overheating. Red parts become white, bloodless and puffy. Blue rings around eyes, which are dul I
 and lustreless. Distended veins. Easy flushing of face, after drinking wine. Face fiery red during vomiting.
Female - Women who are weak, delicate, chlorotic, yet have a fiery-red face. Amenorrhea. Suppression of
menses with extremenervousness. Menses, pale, watery. Passive flow, dark, clotted. Menses too early, too
profuse and protracted. During menses, must keep perfectly still, least
Ferrum metallicum movement greatly worse flow. Menses with labor-like pains. Menses remit a day or two
and then return. Dysmenorrhea with scanty discharge of pale blood with violent colic. Sticking, shooting pains
in uterus. Discharge of long pieces of mucus from uterus. Uterine hemorrhage with labor-like pain in abdomen
and small of back. Leucorrhea, milky, acrid, watery, at puberty. Leucorrhea resembling watery milk, smarting
and corroding when first appearing, not afterward. Itching of vulva. Sensitive vagina. Vagina too dry, pain as
if raw. Swellings and indurations in vagina. Vagina insensible during sex. Prolapse of vagina. Promotes
expulsion of moles. Sexual desire diminished. Sterility. Tendency to miscarriage. Uterine hemorrhage with
threatened premature labour, at end of eight month. Morning sickness, constipation, nausea, worse from
iron pills. Eruption on genitals or inflamed. Ascarides in vulva. Gonorrhea.
Food - Appetite good and bad alternately. Voracious appetite. Loss of appetite. All food tastes bitter.
Unquenchable thirst or thirstlessness. Aversion to eating and drinking during headache. Aversion to meat,
children accustomed to meat suddenly become disgusted with it. Aversion to beer. Aversion to sour things,
sour fruits. Aversion to accustomed tobacco. Desire for raw tomatoes. Desire for sweets. Desire for bread and
butter. Worse from eggs. Worse abuse of tea, quinine, brandy. Worse tobacco smoke. Intolerance of eggs.
Worse tomatoes. Worse hot things. Worse fat food. Worse drinking milk. Worse sourfruit. Worse after drinking
beer. Bread tastes dry and bitter. Wine agrees, if not acid. Meat and acids, sour fruit, as well as beer, causes
nausea.
Head - Head hot, feet cold. Rush of blood to head with flushes of heat in face. Congestion of head with
pale face. Headache after menses, with hot head and cold feet. Hammering, pulsating, congestive
headache, pain extends to teeth with cold limbs. Severe, frontal headache with cold feet. Pain in back of
head with roaring in neck. Sudden pain over left eye. Stinging
headache. Long continued headache, often lasting 2 to 3 days. Headache during coryza. Feeling of an
iron band around head, better external pressure, with red face. Writing causes headache to reappear. Scalp
and hair painful to touch. Must take down the hair. Falling out of hair. Hydrocephalus with open fontanels and
great anemia.
Heart - Anemic murmurs. Hypertrophy of heart. Fatty degeneration of heart. Endocarditis with chlorotic
symptoms. Sense of oppression. Throbbing in all blood vessels. Heart suddenly bleeds into the blood
vessels and as suddenly draws a reflux, leaving pallor of surface. Palpitations, worse least motion, better
walking slowly. Palpitations with fear, has to move about, can neither sit nor stand. Palpitations of
masturbators after loss of fluids. Constrictive pain in region of heart. Pulse full, but soft and yielding. Pulse
increased by exertion. Pulse small and weak.
Kidneys - Chronic nephritis. Albuminuria. Diabetes. Kidney pain with desire to urinate. Involuntary urination,
especially during the day, when standing, from sudden movement, walking in children. Copious urination with
nervousness. Tickling in urethra extending to bladder. Chronic catarrh of bladder and gleet. Burning in urethra
during urination, as if urine were hot. Urine hot with menorrhagia. Urine clear as water, in anemia.
Limbs - Dropsy after loss of vital fluids. Swollen hands and feet. Sudden cramps or tearing pains in the
limbs. Restlessness in limbs. Contraction of limbs. Cracking in joints. Pain in hip joint, tibia, soles and heel.
Heels pain, worse lying on back. Rheumatism of the shoulder. Rheumatism of the left deltoid muscle.
Tearing pains in deltoid, worse at night, driving him out of bed, and motion diminishes the pain. Difficulty raising
the arm. Deltoid muscle soreness and pain. Irresistible desire to bend the arm with intense pain. Hands
tremble when writing, better when writing fast.
Liver - Tightness and fullness in region of liver. Liver enlarged. Neonataljaudice in childfrom mother taking
iron pills during pregnancy. Liver sensitive to pressure.
Lungs - Asthma worse after 12 p.m., must sit up, worse sitting still, better walking slowly about. Catarrhal
asthma every morning from 10 a.m. to 11a.m. Dyspnea better walking slowly and talking. Dyspnea after
midnight, also when sitting up. Suffocative fits in evening in bed. Slowly increasing dyspnea, in pneumonia.
Shortness of breath from tension in abdomen. Difficult inspiration, as from heaviness of chest. Neglected
pleuro-pneumonia, absorbs exudation. Hemoptysis (Mill.). Spitting of blood in tuberculosis. Spitting of blood,
of masturbators. Pneumonia.
Male - Nightly emissions, with backache after over-exertion. Impotency. Increased sexual desire. Erections
night and day, Sterility, low sperm count. Discharge of mucus from urethra after a cold. Gleet, copious,
painless, milky.
Modalities - Better in summer. Better solitude. Better moving about slowly. Better from gentle motion. Better
 slight bleeding (Puls.). Better from leaning head on something. Better after rising. Worse at night, midnight.
Worse heat. Worse cold. Worse while sitting still. Worse after cold washing. Worse overheating. Worse from
sudden motion. Worse raising arms. Worse loss of vital fluids. Worse eating, drinking. Worse from
emotions, anger. Worse violent exertion. Worse while sweating. Worse during menses. Worse noise. Worse
conversation.
Mouth - Breath hot. Dry mouth in morning. Canker sores. Mouth dry, food seems too dry, all solid food tastes
dry and insipid. Sweet or bitter taste. Earthy, pasty taste, like rotten eggs. Taste of blood. Toothache from tea.
Toothache better icy cold water. Pain in teeth, relieved by icy-cold water. Numb, pithy feeling of tongue, as
if burned. Burnt sensation on back and middle portion of tongue. Tongue coated white.
Nose - Nostrils dilated during expiration. Nosebleed in anemic patients .Nosebleed alternating with
hemoptysis. Nosebleed in anemic children, with changing of color of face. Nosebleed in mornings when
stooping. Clots of blood constantly accumulate in nose, during coryza. Mucus membranes relaxed, boggy,
anemic, pale. Dripping of fluid from posterior nares or frontal sinuses, with headache. Bloody, purulent,
greenish, slimy, acrid discharges. Scabs come out of nose or are coughed up every few weeks.
Perspiration - Profuse, debilitating sweats. Profuse sweats at every motion. Anxious, cold sweat, during
cramps of different parts. Cold sweat during convulsions. Clammy, yellow, cold, acrid sweats. Worse while
sweating. Sweats often confined to lower part of body. Sweats preceded by headache. Nausea during sweat.
Sweats lessened while speaking. Fetid sweats on going to sleep. Sweat at night of a very strong odor.
Rectum - Chronic constipation with easily flushed head and face, cold hands and feet. Constipation from
taking iron pills. Constipation during pregnancy. Contractive pain in rectum. Cramping, in rectum, after stool.
Prolapsed rectum in children. Hemorrhoids, copious bleeding or ichorous oozing. Hemorrhoids with itching
and gnawing, tearing pains. Itching of anus due to ascarides or worms in children. Evacuation of mucus,
with worms. Attempts to eat bring on diarrhea. Diarrhea, painless, worse while eating. Summer diarrhea of
children with emaciation. Nightly, gushing and spluttering of undigested food, alternating with constipation,
worse if nervous or tired. Diarrhea during pregnancy. Frequent diarrhea, stools watery, with or without
tenesmus. Rice-water discharges. Stools, hard difficult, followed by backache or cramps in rectum, prolapsed
rectum. Acrid, watery diarrhea, excoriating anus.
Skin - Pale skin. Flushes easily. Skin pits on pressure. Skin withered, flabby. Dry skin in pneumonia.
Jaundice. Yellow-brown spots, sore to touch. Black or dark violet
spots. Burning, with pain as if excoriated when touched. Scarlatina during desquamation. Skin peels off on
shoulders and left hand. Ulcers pale, edematous. Warts on fingers and backs of hands.
Sleep - Falls asleep from debility, while sewing, sitting and studying. Must lie on back at night. Sleepy at
night with inability to sleep. Sleeplessness. Child doesn't sleep because of itching from worms. Restless sleep
at night. Anxious tossing in bed. Sleep disturbed by dreams; much weariness in morning. Vivid dreams.
Nightmares. Confused, unpleasant dreams. Dreams of being engaged in war. Dreams of falling into water.
Stomach - Stomach won't tolerate any food, causes distention and pressure. Heat and burning in stomach.
Spits up food by the mouthful (Phos.). Belchings of food. Bitter eructations after fat food. Flatulent dyspepsia.
Cramp-like pain in stomach. Hemorrhage from stomach. Nausea during headache. Nausea and vomiting
after eating. Vomits after eggs. Easy vomiting without nausea. Vomiting after midnight. Vomiting during
pregnancy. Vomiting in morning after breakfast. Vomiting of everything eaten without being digested. Vomiting
of food after exertion.
Temperature - Chill with red face and thirst. General coldness of limbs, head and face hot. Chilly every
evening. Frequent short attacks of chilly shivering. Chill at 4 a.m. Chills with great thirst, preceded and
succeeded by headache. Chills with trembling all over. Heat with distended veins. Heat in palms and soles.
Heat flushes over body as if sweat would break out. Hectic fever. Sensation of heat all over body, which is
cold to touch. Heat with very red face and inclination to uncover. Fever abating when moving about.
Intermittent fever.
Throat - Sore throat with burning pains. Burning in larynx and trachea after talking. Sensation as if a lump
(left side), worse swallowing empty .Asif something rolling in the throat and closing it like a valve. Sensation
as if something was in larynx, which he wished to remove by hawking
or coughing. Aching, pressing pain in throat while swallowing. Hoarseness, with sense of roughness in
larynx. Voice changeable. Complete aphonia, causes much anxiety. Speaking causes general weakness.
Exophthalmic goiter.
Vertigo - Vertigo on suddenly rising. Vertigo as if balancing to and fro. Vertigo on seeing flowing water. Vertigo
on crossing a bridge over water. Vertigo during headache. Vertigo during headache. Vertigo with nausea,
prostration, lethargy. Vertigo with disposition to fall forward. Vertigo on descending. Giddy as if drunk, when
walking.
 Vision - Letters run together when reading or writing. At night can see in the dark, hysteria. Darkness before
eyes, giddy. Darkness before eyes in evening, with aching pains and slight nosebleed. Attacks of blindness.
COMMENTS - Hahnemann described the effects of iron on persons who habitually drink chalybeate waters:
“In such localities there are few persons who can resist the noxious influence of the continued use of such
waters and remain quite well, each being affected according to his peculiar nature.”
“There we find more than anywhere else chronic disorders of great gravity and peculiar character, even when
the regimen is otherwise faultless.
“Weakness, almost amounting to paralysis of the whole body and of single parts. Some kinds of violent limb
pains. Abdominal disorders of various sorts, vomiting of food by day or by night. Tuberculosis. Tubercular
pulmonary ailments often with blood spitting, deficient vital warmth.
“Suppression of the menses, miscarriages, impotence, in both sexes infertility. Jaundice and many other rare
cachexias are common occurrences.”
Blood diseases, especially if with exhaustion. Anemia, hemophilia. Hemorrhages from over-fullness of blood
vessels, from vasomotor paralysis, or from delicacy of the vessels themselves. Throbbing pains, the blood
vessels all over the body throb violently.
Bleeding, pale or watery blood, (Phos.) and weakness (Chin.). Uterine hemorrhage. Weakness and tiredness
since hemorrhage (Chin.). Irregular distribution of blood in chlorotics.
Abnormally pale mucus membranes. Bruises easily, nosebleeds. Palpitations, worse least exertion,
excitement. Face flushes. Varicose veins. Legs swell and bruise easily. Hands and feet swell.
Anemia, chronic fatigue since blood loss, chemotherapy or radiation. Lack of stamina. Menses that cause
anemia and weakness. Paralytic weakness. Restlessness. Tremor. Rheumatic symptoms, especially of left
shoulder and deltoid.
Neuralgia, brought on by washing in cold water, especially after being over-heated. Hammering headache,
pain worse after midnight. Pain in os on lying down. Feeling of dryness in vagina.
Gastralgia, heavy pressure in the region of the stomach. Walls of abdomen are sore. A feeling as if something
rolled into the throat and closed it like a valve. Frequent spells of nausea, periodic vomiting. Intolerance of
eggs.
Marked cramps. Irritability of the bowels causing diarrhea while eating. Diarrhea coming on when the patient
beings to eat. Constipation. Irritability of the bladder, causing incontinence of urine when standing. The liver
and spleen are affected. Neonatal jaundice. Good for over-dosing from quinine.
Kunkel noted the case of a patient about forty-five, who had repeated attacks of joint rheumatism. Kunkel cured
the case based on the symptom “intolerance to eggs” after he had been dosed for three weeks with salicylate
of soda by allopaths.
RELATIONS-Antidotes: Ars., Hep. Compare: ( 1 ) All Ferrums. (2) Rumex - similar in respiratory and
digestive sphere and contains organic iron. (3) Graph., Mang., Cupr. Complementary: Chin., Alum., Ham.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Ferrum Muriaticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr-m. Ferrum muriaticum. Iron chloride. Sesquichloratum. Ferrous chloride. Ferrous dichloride.
Tincture consisting of 25 parts of crystals to 225 parts of alcohol. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Anorexia. Cramps. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Erysipelas. Hemoptysis. Insomnia. Afolaría.
Nephritis. Pyelitis. Shoulder, pain. Spleen, enlarged. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - This remedy has been employed in enlargement of the spleen due to malaria. There is
great pain in the left hypochondrium which is worse at night. The face is pale and anemic. Vertigo, anorexia,
sleeplessness and a sensation of coldness alternating with heat and lasting for several hours
It is also of service in chronic diarrhea, with loss of appetite, pain and tenesmus. The passages consist of
blood and membranous shreds.
Phlegmonous erysipelas. Pain in right shoulder, right elbow. Marked tendency to cramps. Round red spots
on cheeks. Hemoptysis of dark, blood clot.
Suppressed        menstruation.   Chronic      interstitialnephritis. Pyelitis.  Bright    crystals  in urine.
Copiousurinationatpuberty. Diphtheria. Very dark and watery stools. Painful sexual intercourse. Tendency to
seminal emissions.
COMMENTS - Useful for anemia, given in the 3x after meals. Forchronic interstitial nephritis, 1 to 5 drops of
the tincture, 3 times daily.
RELATIONS - Compare: Cean., Ferr.

name: Ferrum Phosphoricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr-p. Ferrum phosphoricum. Iron phosphate. Ferric phosphate. Ferroso- ferric phosphate.
White phosphate of iron (Schilssler's). This is said to be a true ferric phosphate as contrasted with the ordinary
phosphate of iron, which is a ferrous-hydric phosphate. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Anemia. Anus, prolapse. Bedwetting. Bladder, paralysis. Bronchitis. Bright’s disease. Bruises.
Chills. Colic. Colds. Conjunctivitis. Contusions. Coryza. Coughs. Croup. Cystitis. Debility. Delirium tremens.
Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysentery. Ear, disorders. Erysipelas. Fevers. Frostbite. Gastritis. Gonorrhea.
Hematemesis. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhages. Heart, palpitations. Hyperemia. Inflammation. Influenza. Injuries.
Iron, poisoning. Fevers. Kidneys, weak. Mastoiditis. Measles. Mumps. Nevus. Neuralgias. Nosebleeds.
Otitis, media. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Raynaud's disease. Rheumatism. Sprains. Styes. Tarsal, cysts. Throat,
sore. Tuberculosis. Urinary, incontinence. Veins, varicose. Vomiting. Weakness. Whooping cough. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Knowledge of Ferr-p. comes from Schilssler's work and the clinical experience of those who
have used it on his indications. It has also been proved by Dr. John Moffat.
Early stages of febrile conditions, it stands midway between the activity of Aeon, and Belk, and the
sluggishness and torpidity of Gels. Marked prostration, face more active
than Gels. The superficial redness never assumes the dusky hue of Gels. Pulse soft and flowing, no anxious
restlessness of Aeon.
Typically not full blooded and robust, but nervous, sensitive, anemic with false plethora and easy flushing
(Ferr.). Pale, anemic subjects with violent local congestions.
Anemia. Hemorrhages anddisordersof the veins. Passive congestions and hemoirhages due to hyperemia.
Bright hemorrhages from any orifice. Increases hemoglobin. Discharges are blood streaked or like meat-
water. Fresh wounds, pains, contusions, and sprains.
Inflammation, induration, and enlargement of blood vessels. First stage of all inflammatory disorders.
Inflammation of the soft parts. Acute inflammatory rheumatism, especially of the right shoulder (Ferr-m.).
Rheumatic paralysis. Bruised soreness on the chest, shoulders, muscles.
Emaciation. Great prostration, can hardly move about. Great physical and mental lassitude, indisposed to
physical exertion. Nervousness. Burning rawness. Generally right-sided.
Takes cold easily. Susceptibility to chest troubles. Bronchitis of young children. Acute exacerbation of
tuberculosis.
MIND - Anger and apathy. Keeps quiet. Averse to company. Fear of going into a crowd. Very talkative, hilarious
and excited. Transient mania from cerebral irritation. Indifferent to pleasurable things.
Abdomen - First stage of peritonitis. Distended intolerance of clothes. Colic before stool. Pain in abdomen
with watery diarrhea. Abdominal hernia in persons otherwise robust. Inflamed and incarcerated hernia.
Back - Crick in neck and back. Stiff neck.
Blood - Anemia. Blood disorders. Hemorrhages. Chlorosis. Iron poisoning. He- matochromotosis.
Hyperemia, congestion of blood. Hemorrhages, uterine hemorrhages, nosebleeds. Bright red blood (Phos.).
Ailments from loss of blood, debility. Ailments from blood transfusions (Ferr., Chin.).
Causations - III effects of checked sweat, blood loss, mechanical injuries.
Chest - Chest heavy, sore or congested. Pleurisy, stitching pain worse coughing and deep breathing.
Constitutions - Suited to nervous, sensitive, anemic persons. Sanguine constitutions. To the leuco-
phlegmatic temperament to young persons with varicose veins. The inflammatory, febrile, emaciating, wasting
tuberculosis. Corresponds to Grauvogl's oxygenoid constitution.
Cough - Short, painful, tickling cough. Hard, dry cough, with sore chest. Cough worse at night, with much
 rattling of mucus in chest. Hacking, tormenting, spasmodic cough, worse morning and evening. Cough worse
going into open air. Paroxysmal cough, mostly at night or during day when asleep. Whooping cough with
retching and vomiting. Tormenting cough, when bending head forward or touching larynx.
Ears - First stage of otitis. Ear canal inflammed, red, and swollen. Acute otitis media (Bell.). Throbbing
pains. Eardrum red and bulging. Otitis media, with muco-purulent discharge. Eustachian tubes inflamed.
Catarrhal affection of eustachian tube and ear. Prevents suppuration. Mastoid process swollen and sore.
Noises, tinnitus worse lying. Deafness from colds, worse during menses. Sensitive to noise. Roaring or buzzing
from rush of blood to head.
Eyes - Acute conjunctivitis without suppuration or discharge of mucus. Traumatic conjunctivitis (Aeon.).
Measles with conjunctivitis and photophobia. Red. inflamed with burning sensation. Feeling of a tiny particle
in upper eyelid. Feeling as of sand under lids. Ophthalmia, first stage, marked redness with great pain, and
without mucus or pus. Encysted tumors of the eyelids. Eyes suffused, cannot see on stooping. Eyes inflamed
during dentition. Hyperemia of optic disc and retina with blurred vision. Stye on lower lid.
Face - Paleness alternating with redness. Florid complexion. Face earthy, pale, sallow. Heat and redness
of face during pain. Flushed, cheeks sore and hot. Hot cheeks during toothache. Facial neural-
gia, with stinging, pressing or throbbing pains, worse shaking head, stooping and all motion. Facial
neuralgia, better cold applications. Painful red swelling of parotids.
Female - Menses, with bearing-down sensation and headche. Menses every three weeks. Dysmenorrhea,
with sacral pain, headache. Dysmenorrhea, frequent urging to urinate, pain in left ovary. Dysmenorrhea with
vomiting and indigestion. Bearing down pain in uterus. Constant dull pain in either ovarian region. V agina
sensitive, can't bear examination. Vaginismus, pain during sex. Vagina dry and hot.
Food - Loss of appetite. Chills while eating at table. Aversion to meat and milk. Desire for stimulants. Desire
for sour things. Better drinking tea. Worse by eating. Worse meat, herring, cake. Worse tea and coffee.
Head - Rush of blood to head. Soreness to touch, cold, noisejar. Headache, shooting, aching from vertex down
over the sides of the head with earache, better nosebleed, cold application. Headache with stinging,
pressing or throbbing pains, worse shaking head, stooping and all motion. Throbbing headache with
sensitive scalp. Headache better cold applications. Head often feels as if pushed forward while walking with
vertigo. Empty sensation in the head during menses. Vertex sensitive to cold air, noise and anyjar.
Congestion to head with epilepsy .Blind headache. Headache during pregnancy. Ill effects of heat of sun.
Heart - First stage of cardiac diseases. Palpitations from congestion. Pulse rapid. Short, quick, full, soft.
Flowing pulse.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate. Diurnal bedwetting, better lying down. Incontinence. Urine spurts with
every cough. Polyuria. Urinates after every drink. Irritation at neck of bladder. Urine retained in children during
fever.
Limbs - Fractures at beginning of injury to soft parts, adjacent parts red, hot and painful. Acute rheumatism.
Rheumatism attacking one joint after another, worse slightest motion. Rheumatic pain in
shoulder, pains extend to chest and wrist. Jerking in limbs. Sore, bruised pain in shoulders, extending to chest
and wrist. Sprains of the elbows. Wrists ache with loss of power to grasp. Hands swollen and painful. Fingers
contracted by acute articular rheumatism. Palms hot, in children. Whitlow. Varicose veins.
Lungs - First stage of all inflammatory affections. Acute bronchial catarrh affecting larger and smaller bronchi.
Bronchitis of young children. Congestions of lungs. Croup. Short, painful, tickling and hacking, tormenting,
spasmodic cough, worse morning and evening. Hard, dry cough with sore chest. Pneumonia, the first stage.
Hemoptysis of pure blood, in pneumonia, after concussion or fall (Mill.). Hemoptysis after concussion or fall.
Pleurisy, sharp pain, right side, worse coughing and deep breathing.
Male - Seminal emissions. Inflammatory stage of gonorrhea.
Modalities - Better cold applications. Better bleeding. Better lying down. Better from rest. Better from gentle
motion. Worse at night. Worse 4 a.m. to 6 a.m. Worse cold air. Worse open air. Worse checked sweat. Worse
right side. Worse touch. Worse jar. Worse motion. Worse noise. Worse cold drinks and sour food. Worse meat,
herring, coffee, and cake. Worse right side.
Mouth - Mouth hot, fauces red inflamed. Toothache, better cold. Ranula in vascular. Tongue swollen and dark
red. Inflammation of tongue, fauces and tonsils. Redness, pain without exudation.
Nose - Predisposition to colds and sore throats. Acute coryza and sore throat. First stage of colds,
influenza. Nosebleed in children. Nosebleed with blood-spitting. Nosebleeds, bright red blood (Phos.).
Controls soreness and bleeding after operations. Watery discharge with colds.
Perspiration - Night sweats of anemia or tuberculosis. Copious night sweats, does not relieve pains of
rheumatism. Sweats driving out of bed. Sweats between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. Sweats with increase of pains.
Rectum - Diarrhea worse midnight till morning. Habitual constipation. Constipation caused by atony of
 muscular fibres of intestines. First stage of dysentery with much blood in discharges. Hemorrhoids with
obstinate constipation. Hemorrhoids with catarrh of stomach and bowels. Summer diarrhea with red face and
soft pulse. Chronic diarrhea. Disposition to prolapse rectum. Stools of yellow water. Stools watery, bloody,
undigested.
Skin - Pale, flushed skin. Bleeds easily. Bruises easily. Acne. Measles with conjunctivitis and photophobia.
Measles in beginning. Acne. Capillary congestion with burning of skin, worse violent exertion or warm
room. Erysipelas with intense fever and inflammatory symptoms.
Sleep - Restless and sleepless. Drowsiness. Restless sleep followed by great depression in morning. Night
sweats of anemia or tuberculosis. Sleepless from severity of pains. Anxious dreams.
Stomach - Dyspepsia. Sour belchings. Chill while eating. Catarrh of stomach and bowels. Pain in stomach
worse after eating .Acute and chronic gastralgia worse eating and pressure on stomach. Gastralgia with
vomiting of food. Sudden attacks of deathly nausea. Persistent vomiting of food in morning, before eating.
Vomiting of undigested food. Vomiting green matter. V omiting of bright red blood. V omiting during pains.
Teeth - Toothache better cold. Toothache always appearing after eating food. Toothache worse warm drinks,
better cold drinks. Congestive or inflammatory toothache. Decayed teeth. Complaints during dentition.
Dentition with fever.
Temperature - Chill with desire to stretch, at 1 p.m. First stage of catarrhal antiinflammatoryfevers. Fevers
of unknown origin. Continued infectious fevers. Intermittent fevers. Fever and sore throat. Pneumonia fever.
Hemorrhagic fevers. Measles fever. Heat with sweaty hands.
Throat - Predisposition to colds and sore throats. Sore throat with colds, pain worse empty swallowing.
Fauces red, inflamed. Ulcerated sore throat. Tonsils
Ferrum phosphoricum red and swollen. Inflamed eustachian tubes. First stage of diphtheria. Hoarseness
from overstraining voice. Laryngitis with hoarseness of singers. Laryngitis with fauces inflamed and red.
Sore throat of singers. Ranula in vascular, sanguine constitutions. Much mucus in throat and rattling in
chest. After operations on throat and nose to control bleeding and relieve soreness. Feeling of nausea in
throat. Croup.
Vertigo - Vertigo with rush of blood to head. Fainting from the sight of blood. Vertigo from anemia,
weakness. Vertigo with constant feeling as if head were being suddenly pushed forward, with danger of falling.
Great dizziness, everything swims around him, muscles seemed so weak he could hardly move about. Vertigo
caused by congestion to various parts of brain or head.
COMMENTS - Hematochromotosis. Hyperemia, congestion of blood. Hemorrhages, uterine hemorrhages,
nosebleeds. Tendency to bleed. Bright red blood (Phos.), thicker than Ferr. Ailments from loss of blood,
debility. Ailments from blood transfusions (Ferr., Chin.). Fainting from the sight of blood or from weakness.
Coughing up of blood, in pneumonia cases. Vomiting blood. Blood in the stool, bleeding hemorrhoids, blood
in the urine, with no symptoms. Fainting spells, weak with circulatory problems. Great emaciation.
Fevers of unknown origin. Early stage of acute diseases. Nonspecific convalescent remedy. Nonspecific
inflammation.
Nondescript sore throats and colds. Flus. Bronchitis with a short, painful cough. Acute coryza (Ars., Aeon., All-
c.). Earaches, with redness. Otitis media with throbbing (Bell.). Mastoiditis (Caps., Bell.), with inflammation as
the only symptom. Eye infections, bloodshot and red eyes with no other symptoms. Conjunctivitis (Euph.).
Red face that feels cool, flushed but weak. Face goes red when child is picked up. Teething in children with a
fever and a hot, red face (Bell.). Toothaches or inflammation of gums. Toothache, better cold (Mag-p. better
heat).
Acute arthritis, hands swollen and red. Neck stiff from being out in the cold. Cold hands and feet. Chilly.
Sensitive to open or cold air. Results of checked perspiration on a warm summer day (peritonitis). Pains go
from below upward. Thirsty for ice cold drinks. Desires sour things.
Similar to Phos., where Ferr. is more similar to Puls.
In Schiissler's therapy Ferr-p. takes the place filled by Aeon., Bell., Gels., Verat-v., Arn. and other remedies
which correspond to disturbed states of circulation, irritation and relaxation of tissue.
Schiissler noted “The pains which correspond to iron are increased by motion, but relieved by cold in the
muscle-cells iron is found in the form of a phosphate, we should therefore in therapeutics use Ferrum
phosphoricum.”
Nimier and Parenteau cured several cases of right-supra-orbital neuralgia with morning aggravation with Ferr-
p. 6x. The morning aggravation appeared to be the distinctive indication.
Nash said the hemorrhages are bright red, but occur not in the plethoric subjects of Aeon., but rather in pale,
anemic subjects liable to sudden local congestions.
Cooper cured with Ferr-p. a case of tuberculosis in a patient “of the transparent-skin type, the hemoglobin
 shining through.”
According to Cooper, Ferr-p. antidoted “violent dysuria, night and day,” caused by Stront-br. “Painless irritability
of tissue” is Cooper's keynote, as exemplified in diurnal bedwetting.
Halbert cured a case of Raynaud's disease of the fingers and toes in which amputation seemed inevitable. He
affected a complete cure with Ferr-p. 6x trituration.
Ferr-p. can be used as a nutritional supplement for anemia in the 6x potency. Schiissler generally used the
12x trituration.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Oxygenoid constitution. (2) Aeon., Chin., Ars, Graph., Petr.
(3) Ferrum pyrophosph. - congestion of brain and headache following great loss of blood, tarsal cysts. (4)
Gels. - more flowing pulse. Caust. and Puls. - cough with spurting of urine.
(5)   Kali-m. - croup, pneumonia, palpitations, typhus, Kali-p. - colic, threatenedgangrene. (6) Calc-s. - hip joint
disease, Calc-p. - chlorosis, hemorrhoids, Calc-f. - hemorrhoids, Nat-s. - diabetes, Ant-t. - capillary bronchitis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Ferrum Picricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr-pic. Ferrum picricum. Iron picrate. Trituration. Tincture. Historicaldose: All potencies.
CLINICAL- Albuminuria. Bilious, disorders. Corns. Deafness. Dyspepsia. Ears, diseases. Fatigue. Gout.
Headache. Indigestion. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Lupoid, warts. Lupus. Nosebleeds. Polyuria. Prostate,
enlarged. Rheumatic, arthritis. Rodent, ulcer. Tinnitus. Vasculitis. Voice, loss. 'Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ferrum picricum is considered a great remedy to complete the action of other medicines.
Indicated by the functional failure of an organ under exertion.
This is an unproved medicine, but Dr. Cooper gave the leading indications for its use and these are so clear
that it has taken a definite position in the Materia Medica.
Ferr-pic. is a liver medicine and is particularly suited to persons with dark hair and eyes and bilious-looking
patients. A dirty appearance about the joints indicates it, the stain due to bile pigments.
Senile hypertrophy of the prostate gland, with frequent urination at night, with full feeling and pressure in
rectum. Smarting at neck of the bladder and penis. Meatus dry. Retention of urine.
Warts and epithelial growths, corns with yellowish discoloration. Nosebleeds. Chronic deafness and tinnitus
due to gout. Pseudo-leukemia. Failed voice after public speaking.
MIND - Prostration of mind. Irritable and sensitive.
Back - Pain in right side of neck and down right arm.
Causations - Overwork, exertion. Fatigue, overpowering effects of fatigue.
Constitutions - Suited to dark-haired, plethoric people.
Ears - Tinnitus. Humming in ears as from telegraph wires. Crackling in ears and low-pitched voice. Vascular
deafness. Deafness before menses. Dental neuralgia, radiating towards ears and eyes.
Face - Lupoid wart on face.
Food - Loss of appetite. Indigestion.
Head - Headache after meals, especially in bilious, dark-haired persons. Bilious headaches. Giddiness with
disturbance of cerebral circulation, pain in occiput, and inability to walk.
Kidneys - Frequent urination at night with full feeling. Retention of urine. Smarting at neck of bladder
andpenis (Baros.). Pain along entire urethra.
Limbs - Chronic gout. Dirty appearance about joints. Pain in right side of neck and down right arm. Locomotor
ataxia, ocular stage. Hands covered with warts.
Liver - Liver and bilious disorders. Jaundice. Liver weakness. Liver sensitive, some jaundice.
Male - Prostate gland enlarged. Modalities - Worse from fatigue.
Mouth - Dental neuralgia, radiating towards ears and eyes. Furred tongue.
Rectum - Pressure in the rectum. Constipation.
Skin - Warts, multiple, pedunculated. Sensation as if a wart were growing on thumb. Corns. Jaundice. Dirty
looking skin about joints.
Sleep - Restless sleep with unpleasant (often erotic) dreams.
Stomach - Dyspepsia.
COMMENTS - Acts best in plethoric people with sensitive livers. Burnett cured with it rheumatic arthritis in a
dark-haired subject.
Effects of fatigue (Pic-ac.), unusual fatigue. Cooper described it as the failure of an organ under exertion which
would not ordinarily strain it, e.g., failure of the voice in public speakers.
Noises in the ears. Nervous deafness, “diffused vasculitis.”
 Dr. Cooper was led to give Ferr-pic. in cases of warts by a symptom produced in a patient to whom he was
giving it for deafness, “sensation as if a wart were growing on the thumb.”
Cooper observed that warts, especially old pedunculated warts, frequently accompany chronic deafness. He
considered it especi ally indicated for multiple warts on the hand, and noted a case of lupoid warts cured by it.
P. C. Majumdar cured a student suffering from anemia and malarious fever off and on for a y ear. The student
had impaired hearing of both ears, buzzing, hissing, and vertigo. Indigestion, headache and tired feeling after
bodily or mental exertion. Majumdar considered Ferr-pic. suited to the results of malarious fever, sexual
excesses and blood loss.
It has a specific action in the prostate gland. Puller cured with it a case of albuminuria. Dudley Wright confirmed
Cooper's observation that it will frequently control senile prostate hypertrophy.
Dr. Mende considers Ferr-pic. almost specific in nosebleed.
Ferr-pic. is apt to aggravate if given too low.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Pic-ac., Nit- ac., Thuj. Am-pic., Calc-pic. (2) the Ferrum preparations. (3) Buchu,
Sulph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Cooper. Phatak.

name: Ferrum Sulphuricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ferr-s. Ferrum sulphuricum. Iron sulphate. Ferrous sulphate. Iron vitriol. Green vitriol. Copperas.
Trituration of the pure crystals. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphthae. Bulimia. Cardialgía. Chorea. Constipation. Diarrhea. Eczema. Gallbladder, pain.
Gastritis. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhages. Headache. Helminthiasis. Menorrhagia. Nettle rash. Scrofula. Spasms.
Toothache,
HOMEOPATHIC - Ferr-s. has the leading features of the other Ferrums, but many of the Sulphur characters
appear, especially in the modalities. There is worse from warmth or warm room, better from cold air, ice, or
fresh air.
Acidity and belchings of food in particles (Sulph.). Watery and painless stools. Sensation of fermentation or
purring in stomach. Pain in gallbladder. Toothache. Basedow's disease.
Passive hemorrhages. Pallor or flushing. Sensation as if all the blood were rushing into head and face.
Menorrhagia. Pressing, throbbing between periods with rush of blood to head.
Muscular pains or contractions. Weakness. Local atony, disposition to congestions. Nettle rash, aphthae,
eczema with sluggish liver. Feeling of general heat and disposition to sweat with sensation in skin of back as
if he wore a stout woolen shirt.
COMMENTS - This remedy has been employed in diarrhea when the stools are watery, reddish-brown. Stools,
odorless and painless. There is great pallor of the skin, emaciation, anemia. Edema of the lower limbs. Affects
the blood-vessels and heart. Anemic murmurs.
Also in menorrhagia, when the flow is of long duration and is profuse. There is a pressing, throbbing between
the periods, with ringing in the ears and a sensation as though the blood were rushing to the face. Face is
scarlet red. The bowels are constipated, and there is loss of appetite.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phos. - regurgitation of food in particles. (2) Cina - worms. (3) Bapt. - pain in
region of gallbladder. (4) Ferr., Meh.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Ficus Indica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - fic-i. Ficus indica. Banyan tree. Vata. N. O. Moraceae. India. Tincture of the bark. Tincture of
the hanging roots and buds.
CLINICAL-Colic. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysentery. Enteroptosis. Gonorrhea. Hematuria.
Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Leucorrhea. Nausea.
HOMEOPATHIC -The banyan tree is planted throughout India. It grows to a height of about a hundred feet
and is a common roadside tree.
Ficus Indica has being used successfully in all kinds of hemorrhages. Pure red blood. It possesses greater
anti-hemorrhagic properties than Ficus religiosa.
Hemorrhage from the throat or mouth. Dysentery and piles mixed with blood. Hemorrhage before evacuations.
Acute or chronic bloody dysentery associated with great urging, colic and tenesmus (Merc-c.).
Diarrhea, with nausea. Feels as if bowels were settled down in lower abdomen. Enteroptosis with loose
and frequent evacuations. Sick feeling in lower third of abdomen.
Copious hemorrhages during menses. Bloody leucorrhea. Nervous weakness due to seminal discharge.
Gonorrhea and diabetes associated with burning sensation during urination and in hematuria.
COMMENTS - Proving by Dr. O. N. Banerjee, Calcutta, India, in the Homoeopathic Recorder, July, 1891.
Dr. O. N. Banerjee wrote “In June, 1888, while visiting a patient in the country I saw in the garden a large tree
of the variety known as Ficus Indica. As the tree is considered sacred I regarded it and its branches, which
were ladened with ripe, yellow fruit, with the greatest interest, and plucking one of the fruits, ate it upon an
empty stomach.
“To my great astonishment there occurred one hour thereafter an unusual frequent desire to urinate, I did not
relish my breakfast, there was loss of appetite and sour belching; in the afternoon the urine became phosphatic
and I suffered from headache ; in the evening I felt an itching of the thighs, heaviness of the head, dullness of
the mind, and a burning heat over the body; there was but a scanty discharge of urine during the day.
“After gathering a large quantity of fruit I returned to Calcutta and made an alcoholic tincture thereof. This was
distributed among nine provers and two drops of the mother tincture were taken every morning before breakfast
for eight days.
“As a remedy it has been used successfully in every case presenting the following conditions: Frequent, at
times unsatisfactory discharge of amber-colored or phosphatic urine with discharge of seminal fluid. Headache,
heaviness of the head. Itching of the limbs. Thirst. Dyspepsia. Ill humor. Irregular stool. Disturbed sleep.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Merc, cor., Chin., Phos.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Ghose.

name: Ficus Religiosa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lie. Ficus religiosa. Ashwathya. Bo-tree. Pakur. N. O. Moraceae. India. Tincture of juice of fresh
leaves mixed with equal parts of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bloody, discharges. Dysentery. Hematemesis. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Menorrhagia.
Nosebleed. Typhoid. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Sarat Chandra Ghose of Midnapore made the first proving and thereby discovered its
power to cause and cure hemorrhages of many kinds. Ghose related some striking cases cured with the
remedy in cases of dysentery, hematemesis, hemorrhage of typhoid, bleeding hemorrhoids and nosebleed.
General hemorrhages. Vomiting of a bright red blood. Hemoptysis. Menorrhagia. Profuse discharge of bright
red blood, bearingdown pains in lower abdomen. Bloody urine. Very weak and restless. Headache, burning at
 the top of the head. Sight dim.
MIND - Quiet and disinclined to move. Sad and melancholic.
Abdomen - Bearing-down pains in lower part of abdomen.
Eyes - Sight dim.
Face - Face became yellow.
Female - Menorrhagia, bright red blood, bearing-down pains in lower abdomen.
Head - Burning at vertex, vertigo and slight headache.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate. Urine contains much blood.
Lungs - Difficult breathing, cough with vomiting of blood, pulse very weak.
Nose - Nosebleed.
Rectum - Dysentery with menorrhagia. Dysentery, bright red blood.
Stomach - Pain and sick feeling in stomach. Nausea, vomiting of bright red blood.
COMMENTS - Dr. Ghose participated in his own proving, along with his wife and a dog. The dog, which was
perfectly strong and healthy, received 40 drops of the tincture one morning. No result followed that day and
the dose was repeated the next morning.
The animal commenced and continued to vomit blood of a bright red color. It kept very quiet and was unwilling
to move. After three doses of five drops of the tincture given in quick succession, the vomiting ceased. The
same treatment (minute doses of the remedy) was effectual in arresting the effects of the drug throughout the
provings.
Mrs. Ghose took the tincture in 20-drop doses repeatedly throughout two days. On the third day dysentery and
menorrhagia set in simultaneously. The blood was bright red.
Other symptoms included a headache, very weak and restless, sight dim, burning at the top of the head. The
face became yellowish, breathing difficult. She became sad and melancholic. With the profuse discharge of
bright red blood there were bearing-down pains in the lower abdomen.
Dr. Ghose took 40 drops in one dose. The result was a frequent desire to pass water, which gradually became
bloody, containing much blood. Inclination to cough, causing him to spit blood. Slight headache, giddiness and
nausea. Sight dim. Very weak and restless. The tincture was taken three drops every two hours, and after the
third dose the symptoms vanished.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Acalypha, Ip., Am., Mill., Phos., Hirudo, Cact., Ferr. Thlaspi.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Filix Mas
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - fil. Filix mas. Male fern. Aspidium filix-mas. N. O. Filices. Dryopteri- daceae. Tincture of fresh
root or fresh root grated. Maceration of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abdomen, bloated. Abortion. Blindness. Infertility. Miscarriage. Tapeworm. Worms.
HERBAL - The male fem has been recognized as a vermifuge from the time of Galen. For worm symptoms,
especially with constipation. Dioscorides credits it with the power of causing infertility and abortion.
HOMEOPATHIC - A fragmentary proving in Allen's Appendix records a case in which 15 to 20 drops of the
tincture given three times a day to a woman suffering from bloated abdomen with more or less pain caused
diminution of the bloating. Also, severe prolapse of vagina. Pain and tenesmus of bladder with copious and
frequent emission of urine, with intense pain.
Filix was then discontinued and Chim. relieved the symptoms. They did not return afterwards, except after
much walking or standing.
The leading symptoms include a pale face with blue rings around the eyes, and blindness from atrophy of the
optic nerve. Torpid inflammations of lymphatic glands. Pulmonary tuberculosis in young patients, no fever
with limited, ulcerated lesions. Gnawing, boring pains in abdomen, worse after sweet things. Tapeworms.
Soporific conditions.
Abdomen - Bloated. Gnawing and boring in bowels, worse eating sweet things. Great pain in abdomen with
diarrhea and constant vomiting. Worm colic with itching of nose, pale face, blue rings around eyes. Painless
hiccough.
Eyes - Blindness, monocular amblyopia. Blindness, first mydriasis and amaurosis with normal fundus, eight
days later, atrophy of optic nerve. Immobility of pupil.
Face - Pale face, blue rings around eyes. Female - Menstruation stimulated. Prolapse
of vagina with pains and tenesmus of bladder and copious frequent emission of urine with internal pains.
Abortion. Sterility.
Limbs - Numbness of right wrist.
 Nose - Itching of nose.
Rectum - Violent vomiting and diarrhea. Ineffectual urging to stool. Pappy stools. Worm symptoms with
constipation. Worm colic.
Sleep - Soporific condition. Restless and sleepless at night.
Stomach - Nausea. Sick after taking food. Temperature - Violent rigor, fever, great pain in abdomen with
diarrhea and constant vomiting.
COMMENTS - C. S. Spencer recorded this effect from taking capsules each containing ten minims of the oil
of male fem for tapeworm:
“A feeling of nausea, abdomen became painfully distended with colicky pains. Menses returned after only one
week's absence and continued profusely for three weeks. Very sick after taking her food. The worm was got
rid of and the capsules stopped when these symptoms passed away.”
Hering said the best time to give the drug for expulsion of tapeworm is in the summer when the fresh root can
be obtained. If an ounce of the grated root is given in the forenoon, usually the tapeworm comes away in the
afternoon.
Teste used it successfully in a case of violent dyspnea without cough, with stitches in region of heart and
obscure symptoms of pericarditis. The patient was a young woman of lymphatico-nervous temperament and
was much weakened by long sickness.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aspidium alha- manticum. Panna - 3 doses, 2 grams each, all in half hour, fasting
in a glass of milk. Tasteless and will remove tapeworm. (2) Ciña, Gran., Kousso.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Flavus Bacillus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-flav. Flavus bacillus. Neisseria pharingis Hava. Neissericeae. Micrococ- cales. A non-pathogenic
bacterium found in the upper respiratory passages but was also found in cerebrospinal fluid during meningitis.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Arthrosis. Brachial, neuralgia. Coughs. Dysmenorrhea. Dysphagia. Dyspnea.
Endometriosis. Headaches. Intoxication. Otitis. Palpitations. Premenstrual syndrome. Rhinitis. Sciatica.
Sinusitis. Thyroid, problems.
HOMEOPATHIC - Flavusisabacteriumcalled Neisseria Phringis Flava, belonging to the Neisseriafamily of the
Micrococcales order. These microbes are in the shape of shells arranged in pairs like coffee beans. They are
Gram-positive. Neisseria Flava is an aerobic saprophyte found in the upper respiratory passages.
Flavus is not considered to be pathogenic. Nevertheless, it was isolated from the cerebrospinal fluid of several
children suffering from meningitis. It owes its name to the formation of a yellow pigment in the middle of the
culture colony.
Flav. shows signs of irritation in the eyes, nose and pharynx which can lead to spasmodic rhinitis. Sensation
of a lump in the throat. Feeling like feathers in the throat (Kali-bi.). Feeling of gravel in the larynx after speaking
for a long time. Thyroid problems.
Headaches. Peri-orbital headaches, localized on the right side (Sang.). Pain at the level of the frontal and
maxillary sinuses. Discharge from the eyes and nose. Tendency tocolds, coughs and expectorates. Slight
localized trembling, particularly in the fingers. Intoxication.
MIND - Low morale, exaggerates difficulties. Sensitive to others' emotions and being contradicted.
Back - Arthrosis of the cervical column with cracking. Neck pains. Cervical-brachial neuralgia. Pain in the back,
spreading to both arms.
Constitutions - Psoric, sycotic and tubercular constitutions.
Ears - Frequent attacks of otitis, recurring. Pain in the right ear.
Eyes - Per-orbital headache, localized on the right side. Eyes red in the evening, when tired. Eye fatigue. Eyes
swollen in the morning, on waking, eyelids heavy. Conjunctivitis.
Female - Menses irregular, too early, of varying quantities with pale blood. Menses too frequent. Menses late
with premenstrual syndrome. Loss of blood at ovulation. Dysmenorrhea. Endometriosis. Hot flushes, worse at
night.
Food - Complaints aggravated by wine (Zinc, Nux-v.).
Head - Peri-orbital headaches, localized on the right side (Sang.).
Heart - Palpitations at night with feeling of fever, worse after drinking wine.
Limbs - Arthrosis, rheumatic arthritis. Sciatica. Pain in the joints with cracking situated at the knees, wrists,
shoulders and fingers. Pain in the left hip, left arm. Slight localized trembling, particularly in the fingers.
Lungs - Dyspnea, worse at night, worse around 2 a.m., with waking and suffocation. Coughing in the morning
for 1 hour, on waking.
 Modalities - Better in the autumn. Better spring. Better from hot baths. Worse from cold. Worse heat. Worse
at night. Worse in the morning. Worse on the left side. Worse after drinking wine.
Mouth - Arthritis of the jaw with loose teeth.
Nose - Nose dry with dry scabs. Nasal discharge of greenish pus (Kali-bi.). Sinusitis. Sneezes easily.
Spasmodic coryza. Nasal congestion at night, one nostril becomes blocked. Bleeding from the nose in the
morning on waking.
Skin - Perspiration from the palms. Dry eczema of the palms. Ecchymosis occurring regularly from the slightest
shock.
Stomach - Digestion bad. Digestive complaints after moist food. Frequent nausea after meals.
Throat - Red, sore throat. Sore throat after having had wet feet. Throat dry with slight discomfort at night.
Throat inflamed. Fre
quent loss of voice. Dysphagia. Tickling sensation in the right side of the larynx. Dry cough, aggravated in the
morning. Feeling that the hard palate is touching the tongue.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali-bi. - Coryza and sinusitis with sensation of blocked nose and tickling in the
nostrils. Thick yellow or greenish discharge, viscous or running, forming greenish elastic lumps, sticky, which
leave the mucus membranes raw and burning. (2) Zinc - Also shows aggravation from wine, but the depressive
condition is infinitely more accentuated. General weakness. Cannot keep his legs still.
REFERENCES -Julian.
