name: Flor De Piedra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - flor-p. Flor de piedra. Lopho- phytum leandri. Balanophoraceae. South America. Tincture of
whole dried plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cholecystitis. Colic. Colitis. Diabetes. Dysthyroidism. Emaciation, Epilepsy. Exophthalmus. Goiter.
Headache. Hyperthyroidism. Hypothyroidism. Rickets. Vertigo.
HERBAL - Flor de Piedra grows in the tropical forests of Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil. This plant is used
by the natives for stomach and liver disturbances. In Pio Carrera's book on Brazilian phototherapy, rickets and
epilepsy are also indicated.
HOMEOPATHIC - W. Schwabe brought back the plant from Brazil. In collaboration with others, he carried out
a proving on sixteen provers (10 women and 6 men), using the 6x, 4x, 3x, and 2x potencies, on February 21.
1964.
J. R. Reside undertook another proving in 1966-67. Finally, Juliette Fourmon undertook an extremely thorough
clinical proving.
Emaciation from the pituitary or the thyroid gland. Neuro-endocrine complaints. Congestion of the thyroid with
vago-sym- pathetic disharmony. Pituitary diabetes. Cardiac complication of hyperthyroidism.
Pain in the heart and liver. General nausea. Distention and spasmodic diarrhea.
Constriction of the neck. Feeling of tightness around the neck. Headache, vertigo. Sudden tiredness, especially
in the morning.
MIND - Increase in general activity. Mentally alert, clear-headed. Bright, then slow. Confused, lacking focus.
Depressed.
Abdomen - Wakes at 2 a.m. with abdominal pains, ameliorated by going to stool. Heavy, full feeling and
abdominal distention. Pressure in the right iliac region. Cannot bear the pressure of underclothes.
Back - Pain in the right shoulder on lifting the right arm.
Blood - Disorders of the basal metabolism. Hypo-cholesterolemia.
Chest - Right subcostal pain. Feeling of oppression in the thorax, rather more to the right that the left side.
Thoracic pain, worse by movement and deep respiration.
Constitutions - Suited to tubercular, nervous, phosphoric or phospho-fluoric types.
Ears - Pruritus of the auditory canal.
Eyes - Eyes bloodshot. Stye on the lower right eyelid. Orbital pain of a pressing type, when reading. Diminution
in visual activity.
Female - Menses infrequent, abundant, but late by five days. Greenish vaginal discharge.
Food - Extreme thirst.
Head - Left frontal or temporal headache, ameliorated in the open air, increased in the evening. Headaches,
as though the brain would burst with visual disturbances and zigzags at the edge of the field of vision.
Heart - Palpitations.
Kidneys - Abundant urine.
Limbs - Painful drawing and pricking feeling in the left arm, elbow and hand, with formication in the left hand.
Drawing pain in the right thigh down to the calf and heel. Sharp, cutting pain in the left knee, worse when
 walking. Heaviness in the legs. Right foot slightly edematous and sensitive to pressure. Feet cold.
Lungs - Irritating, dry, hacking cough.
Modalities - Better from open air, Better heat. Worse in the evening. Worse from exertion.
Mouth - Mouth dry with difficulty in swallowing. Ulcers in the mouth and on the lips and tongue. Heartburn.
Diminution in sense of taste.
Nose - Dryness in the nose. Fits of sneezing.
Rectum - Tendency to diarrhea with grayish or pale yellow stools.
Skin - Generalized pruritus, but particularly the ears, scalp, arms and face, abdomen and anal region. Marks
on the thighs and lower limbs. Perspiration.
Sleep - Sleep disturbed. Fiery, hot feeling in bed.
Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea and epigastric discomfort.
Temperature - Profuse sweating and hot flushes.
Throat - Throat dry, empty swallowing to clear the throat. Feeling of a lump in the back of the throat. Stabbing
pain in the throat, worse during the morning.
Vertigo - Vertigo and tendency to fall to the left.
COMMENTS - Freiwald reported favorable results in thyroid infections, using the potencies 3x and 6x and in
infections of the liver and bladder, using 4x and 6x. Juliette Fourmon reported some clinical successes in goiter
cases, hyperthyroidism, and in a case of bilateral degenerative labyrinthitis.
M. Tetau made a general review of thyroid disorders and their homeopathic and biotherapeutic treatment,
noting the value of Lophophytum Leandri.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) lodum - Anxious, cannot stay still, emaciation, hoarseness, diarrhea. Precordial
anxiety with palpitation at the slightestexertion. (2) HederaHelix. (3)Nat-m. - Emaciation of the upper part of
the body, headache, dryness of the mouth and fissure on the middle of the lower lip. Abnormal desire for salt.
(4)Tuberculinum - Asthenia, emaciation, erratic pains, constant need to move, diarrhea in the morning,
sweating at the least physical or mental effort.
REFERENCES-Julian.

name: Fluoricum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - fl-ac. Fluoricum acidum. Fluoric acid. Hydrofluoric acid. Made by distilling pure fluorspar
(Calcium fluoride) in a state of fine powder with sulphuric acid. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Alcoholism. Alopecia. Bedsores. Birthmarks. Bone disorders. Brain, atrophy.
Coccyx.pain. Dental, fistula. Dropsy.Edema. Exostosis. Eyes, disorders. Felon. Fistula. Fluoride,
poisoning. Gleet. Goiter. Gonorrhea. Hair, loss. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hydrocele. Keloids. Liver,
induration. Locomotor ataxia. Nevi. Nose, inflammation. Nymphomania. Otorrhea. Peritonitis. Perspiration.
Pityriasis. Satyriasis. Scars. Spleen, pains. Strokes. Suppuration. Syphilis. Teeth, decayed. Toothaches.
Tongue, ulceration. Ulcers. Varicocele. Varicose, ulcers. Varicose, veins. Veins, diseased. Whitlow.
HOMEOPATHIC - Fl-ac. acts on the lowertis- sues of the body much like Sil., which it follows and precedes
well, although their modalities differ, Fl-ac. is better from cold applications. Useful after the abuse of Sil.
Slow, deeply destructive effects. Decay of long bones, ulcerations, bedsores, varicose veins. Necrosis of
the bones, favors the expulsion of the necrosed part. Acts especially upon lower tissues.
Teeth are deficient in enamel, black, rough, unsightly-looking. Early decay of teeth. Calcareous degeneration.
Nails grow rapidly. Felon. Nevus, flat.
Edema. Tissues are puffy indurated and fistulous. Dropsy with numbness or without. Old scars, scars become
redder and itch. Red blotches on body which tend to desquamate. Small red spots here and there, worse by
warmth, better in cool place. Discharges are thin, foul, acrid or salty, causing itching.
Increased sensitiveness of vision and hearing. Glabella region bloated. Numbness of the part not lain on in
brain diseases, spinal disorders. Goiter. Affinity for rectal, dental and lachrymal fistulas. Suffering if the call for
evacuation is not immediately attended to.
Old cases of nightly fevers, coming on periodically. Always feels too hot, wants to bathe in cold water. Patient
is compelled to move about energetically.
Hob-nailed liver of the alcoholics. Complaints of old age or the prematurely aged with weak, distended blood
vessels. Especially adapted to chronic diseases with syphilitic and mercurial history. Secondary syphilis.
MIND - Absent-mindedness. Forgetful in evening, better morning. Great loss of memory. Forgets almost
everything. Forgets dates. Mistakes right for left.
Opinionated, strong-minded. Domineering behavior. Irritability, sends the nurse home. Abuses and
reproaches others. Irritability with absent persons. Sensitive to noise. Conversation aggravates.
 Depression of mind. Aversion to his own family. Aversion to those loved best (Sep.). Sits silently, does not
utter a single word, nor answers anyone when questioned. Inability to realize responsibility. Shuns
responsibilities. Indifference to business affairs. Indifference to loved ones, to relations.
Anxious ideas. Apprehensive, causes sweat, better morning than evening. Fear of having a stroke. Sensation
as if danger menaced him, but without fear.
Impulse to walk fast, necessity to be always on the move. Becomes interested and converses pleasantly with
strangers. Buoyancy of mind. Mentally elated and excited. Fears nothing and is self-satisfied. Cheerful during
menses. Cheerful when walking in open air.
Delusion, marriage must be broken. Thinks he must drive children out of the house, must dissolve marriage.
Thinks he must get rid of servants. Stands on the street looking at women as they pass by, so great is his lust.
Nymphomania.
Abdomen - Ascites from hepatic disorders.
Induration, enlargement and portal congestion. Flatus and belchings. Sensation of emptiness at the region of
navel with a desire to draw a deep breath, better bandaging. Burning, pinching, about navel.
Back - Pain in third cervical vertebra. Coccyx pain worse motion and exercise. Bruised, in sacrum. Aching in
sacrum and lumbar region, better stretching and bending backwards, esp. by pressure. Stiffness of nape.
Lameness in back, hips and legs.
Breasts - Nipples sore, cracked, itching. Itching on left breast.
Chest - Oppression in chest, difficult breathing, great dyspnea, better bending backwards. Hydrothorax. Upper
part of chest seems most affected. Scaly eruption on chest and arms. Itching under ribs left side.
Constitutions - Suited to complaints of old age or the prematurely aged. Suited to the weakly constitutions,
sallow skin, emaciation. Pale, miserable, cachectic, flabby and broken down patients. Dropsy of limbs in old,
feeble constitutions.
Ears - Intolerable itching in ears. Itching momentarily better scratching, but followed by burning. Profuse
otorrhea. Otitis externa. Great sensitiveness in morning to little noises. Difficulty in hearing human voices, with
numbness of bones around ear. Deafness, better bending head back. Singing, ringing.
Eyes - Burning in eyes. Increased lachrymation. Chronic inflammation of lachrymal sac, worse cold air.
Lachrymal fistula, worse] cold air. Violent itching of inner canthus. As if sand in eyes. As if something in the
eyes, that could not be rubbed off, must wink. Sensation as of a cold wind blowing through the eyes. Left
eye smaller than right.
Face - Heat in face, wants to wash it in cold water. Pale. Exostoses of bones of face. Heat in face, wants to
wash it in cold water. Crusta lactea, dry, scaly, itches very much. Suppurating tubercles in skin of forehead
and face. Sweats on face. Right lower jaw swollen.
Female - Menses, blood thick and coagulated. Menses too early, copious, frequent, too long. Feels distressed
if the flow is slightly delayed. Metrorrhagia with difficulty of breathing. Copious and excoriating leucorrhea,
itching. Acrid leucorrhea.
causes itching. Ulceration of uterus and os. Nymphomania.
Food - Hungry. Averse to coffee. Desire for pungent, spicy, highly seasoned food. Desire for fancy dishes.
Craves refreshing drinks. Craving for cold things. Craves cold water. Warm drinks produce diarrhea. Desire
for wine. Worse from sweet things. Worse from coffee.
Head - Atrophy of brain. Stunning headache, better urinating. Pressure on sides of head from within outward.
Compressing pain in temples. Pressure in occiput. Pain along the sutures. Numb sensation in forehead. Puffy
glabella. Congestion of blood to head during pregnancy. Decay of ossicles and mastoid with copious
discharge, worse warmth (Sil.). Decay of skull bones. Exostosis. Decay of skin. Itching of head. Brittle hair.
New hair dry and breaks off. Falling out of hair after fevers. Alopecia areata. Baldness. Scaly eruptions on
head.
Heart - Sore pain in heart. Pulse somewhat accelerated, only during exercise. Small, frequent pulse.
Kidneys - Involuntary urination at night. Increases urine in dropsy, with great relief. Burning in urethra during
and after urination. Upward drawing in the urethra. Whitish or purple colored sediment. Urine pungent and
fetid. Urine alkaline. Urine, scanty, dark.
Limbs - Dropsy of limbs in old feeble constitutions. Limbs go to sleep. Osteitis. Decay and necrosis,
especially of long bones. Constant redness of the hands, especially the palms. Hot, sweaty palms.
Inflammation of joints of fingers. Feeling of hair on back of fingers. Soreness between toes. Nails distorted.
Nails crumble. Nails grow rapidly. Felon. As of a splinter under the nail. Nails corrugated lengthwise. Corns
are sore. Necrotic bones. Ulcer over tibia.
Liver - Ascites from hepatic disorders. Degeneration of liver in consequence of alcoholism. Soreness over
liver. Hepatic disorders with ascites.
 Lungs - Difficulty of breathing with, or alternating with, metrorrhagia. Great dyspnea, better bending
backwards. Wheezing. Difficult breathing, in afternoon and evening. Great dyspnea, has to be propped up in
bed.
Male - Burning in urethra. Oily pungent smelling sweat on genitals. Dropsical swelling on penis. Gleety
discharge at night, staining linen yellow. Varicocele. Swollen scrotum. Violent erections at night. Increased
sexual desire in old men. Overwhelming sexual desire, keeping him awake at night. Enjoyment excessive.
Gonorrhea. Sensation of fullness in spermatic cords. Sudden loss of sexual power. Impotence. Yellow drop
from urethra in morning.
Modalities - Better cold. Bending open air. Better cool bathing. Better walking. Better rapid motion. Better
bending head back. Better short sleep. Better sitting. Better eating. Worse heat of room. Worse night. Worse
morning. Worse warmth. Worse warm drinks. Worse alcohol, red wine. Worse sour foods. Worse rest. Worse
rising. Worse coffee. Worse standing.
Mouth - Mouth coated with mucus in morning. Painful ulcer in right angle of jaw. Affects teeth and bones of
upper jaw. Increased flow of saliva, with sneezing. Viscid, tasteless saliva in mouth. Syphilitic ulceration of
mouth, which is very sensitive to cold.
Nose - Red, swollen, inflamed nose. Fluent coryza during sleep. Sneezing with salivation. Chronic nasal
catarrh with ulceration of the septum. Sudden copious watery discharge from eyes, nose and mouth. Nose
obstructed and dull heavy pain in forehead. Itching on right side of nose. Cold water causes coryza. Posterior
nares feel expanded, during a walk.
Perspiration - Profuse and sour, offensive perspiration. Feels as if hot vapor were emitted from all the pores.
Acrid, eroding sweat, excites itching. Sweat on diseased part. Sweats on hands and feet. One-sided sweat
(left). Sweats in afternoon. Sweats during exercise. Sweat relieves. Excessive sweat on feet. Sweat promotes
excoriation
Fluoricum acidum and bedsores.
Rectum - Flatus and eructations with constriction of anus. Constipation. Itching and burning at anus. Bilious
diarrhea with aversion to coffee. Diarrhea worse on alternate days. Warm drinks and salmon produce diarrhea.
Itching in perineum. Very loose, bright yellow stools, with much mucus, preceded by considerable griping.
Stools frequent and hard. Stools pappy, yellowish brown, fetid, with tenesmus and prolapsed anus.
Sensations - Sensation as of a cold wind blowing under lids, even in warm room, as of air passing down from
shoulder joint to fingers. Numbness of limbs even when not lain on. Increased ability to exercise his muscles
without fatigue. Less affected by excessive heat in summer or cold in winter.
Skin - Dry, harsh, itching or cracked skin. Burning pains on small spots of skin. Itching, especially of the
orifices. Itching in spots, worse warmth. Itching of scars. Keloids. Scars, surrounded by pimples, become red
around the edges. Bedsores, worse warmth. Varicose veins. Atony of capillary and venous system. Tissues
bloated. Nevus or birthmarks on children. Nails grow rapidly. Ulcers, red edges and vesicles. Ulcers on
ankles. Syphilitic tubercles. Syphilitic rupia. Periosteal abscess. Hard, dry warts. Frequent small boils,
carbuncles.
Sleep - Sudden sleepiness. Drowsy and sleepy in early evening. Sleeplessness without inclination to sleep. A
short sleep suffices and refreshes him. Sleep disturbed by accumulation of mucus in fauces. Sensation as if
sleeping on side not lain on. Sleeplessness in evening from crowding of thoughts. Dreams towards morning.
Dreams of fire. Dreams with amaurosis.
Stomach - Frequent eructations and discharge of flatulence. Sour eructations. Stale eructations. Burning,
pinching pain in stomach, before stool. Heaviness and weight in stomach. Heat in stomach before meals.
Gnawing hunger, is always eating which temporarily relieves. Sour or stale
belchings. Bilious vomiting on slightest errors in diet. Stomach symptoms, better tight clothes.
Teeth - Affects teeth and bones of upper jaw. Great sensitiveness of teeth. Late dentition. Teeth, décay
rapidly, worse at roots. Thin enamel. Teeth feel warm, heavy, rough. Dental fistula with bloody, salty
discharge. Acrid, foul tasterfrom roots of teeth. Teeth coated with mucus in morning. Wisdom teeth come late.
Toothache worse cold drinks. Toothache better until water becomes warm in mouth.
Temperature - Nightly fevers coming on periodically. Ebullitions of heat with pain in bones. Feels as if burning
vapor were emitted from pores. General heat with nausea, with inclination to uncover. Face constantly hot,
wants to bathe it continually in cold water.
Throat - Excessive pain, when swallowing or talking. Sore throat, worse inspiring cold air. Throat sensitive
to cold, slightest exposure resulting in sore throat, with increase of pain and impeded swallowing. Constriction
in throat, with difficult swallowing. Hawking of phlegm, mixed with blood. Red blotches, over palate and
sides of cheek, bleeding easily. Throat intensely red and much swollen, with fetid breath, nasal voice.
Goitre. Trachea sore and raw. Weak voice. Dryness in larynx and trachea. Itching in larynx, causes hawking
 and swallowing. Soreness and increased irritability in larynx with impeded respiration and wheezing. Syphilitic
ulceration of throat.
Tongue - Tongue, fissured in all directions, painful when talking. Ulcer on and under tongue. Tongue as if stiff,
with restricted mobility. Tongue vivid red at tip and edges. Tongue coated yellow in centre. Tongue whitish and
dry. Numbness and tingling of tongue. Pricking sensation of tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea, must sit down. Feeling as if in an earthquake.
Vision - Amaurosis. Dark spot before eye, worse reading. Flashes like lightning. Red photopsia. due to retinal
excitement.
COMMENTS - Severe bone diseases and ulcers, where the bones decompose instead of healing. Necrosis of
the bones, bone abscesses. Bone pains (Merc.. Calc-f.). For syphilis, when it causes ulcers and goes to the
bones.
Tendency to form ulcers on the skin and in the mouth that do not heal well, particularly in the elderly. Ulcers
can have a red edge. Bedsores. Keloids that ulcerate or don't heal well (Sil.).
Varicose veins that swell and ulcerate with severe burning pain, worse heat (Sec., Lach.). Varicose veins with
itching, swelling and burning pains. Varicose veins or ulcers aggravated after each childbirth.
Hot blooded. Worse heat. Better from cold washing and walking in the open air (opposite Sil.). Constant desire
to walk in the open air, and does not fatigue. Hungry. Symptoms seem to move from below upward.
For children with weak tooth enamel (Sil., Calc-f.), or whose teeth erupt rotten and abscessed (Kreo., Calc-f.).
Generally a woman's remedy. Hate between spouses.
Guernsey noted that it tends to affect the right ear, the left teeth, left hypochondrium, left side of the abdomen,
right side and nape of the neck, and the right side of the back.
McLachlan added that the left hand is affected rather than the right, and the pus tends to point on the dorsum
of the finger. T. F. Allen noted its use for whitlow.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Thiosin. - action on scar tissues, adhesions, strictures, tumors. Calc-f., Sil. (2)
Coca - fatigue, Coffea - toothache. (3) Cit-ac. and Sep. - aversion to one's family. (4) Ox-ac. - diarrhea worse
from coffee. (5) Rhus-t. and Ruta - Coccyx, pain. (6) Sil. - fistula, onychia, bone diseases. Coccyx, pain. (7)
Brom.. lod., Spong, and Kali-c. - goiter. (8) Staph. - teeth. Complementary: Sil. Compatible: after Ars. in
ascites from gin-drinker's liver after Kali-c. in hip disease after Ph-ac. in diabetes. Followed well by: Sulph..
Nit-ac.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Fluoride
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - fluor. Fluoride. Historicaldose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Bone, disorders. Cancer. Collagen, diseases. Constipation. Decayed, teeth. Faintness.
Miscarriages. Nausea. Skin, rash. Stomach cramps. Rash. Teeth, disorders. Ulcers. Vomiting. Weight loss.
Wrinkles.
HOMEOPATHIC - In a number of small villages in Sicily, Turkey and India there is naturally occurring fluoride
in the water ranging from 0.7 to 5.4 ppm. Here the villagers and their livestock are chronically ill, while
neighboring villages with no fluoride have no such illnesses. Premature aging is the overall effect.
Children have brown decaying teeth; young adults often have none. Young men are bent over and crippled
with pain in their joints and hips. Their skin is wrinkled and they look 60 at age 30 to 40.
There is premature hardening of the arteries. Loss of appetite and sex drive by age 30. The rate of stillborn
miscarriages by 4 months is extremely high.
Fluoride damages enzymes which results in a wide range of chronic diseases. Fluoride causes breakdown of
collagen. It also leads to irregular formation of collagen which serves as a major structural component of skin,
ligaments, tendons, muscles, cartilage, bones and teeth.
Female - Miscarriages.
Limbs - Bone, disorders. Tremors. Aching bones. Stiffness.
Rectum - Constipation.
Skin - Skin rash. Wrinkled, skin. Ulcers.
Stomach - Stomach cramps. Nausea. Bloody vomit.
Teeth - Deformed teeth. Decayed teeth. Brown or black discoloration of the teeth.
Vertigo - Faintness.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Fl-ac., Calc-f.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Foeniculum Sativum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - foen. Foeniculum sativum. Fennel. Foeniculum vulgare. N. O. Umbel- liferae. Tincture of seed.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -
HERBAL -The fruit (seeds) are quite fragrant, and are among the most relaxing and least pungent of all the
aromatics. They are eminently carminative, and quite diffusive; and are usually better received by the stomach
than are cummin or dill seeds, being also more relaxing than these, but more stimulating than anise seed.
Their principal use is in combination with senna, rhubarb, juglans, rhamnus, and other cathartics. The oil may
be made into essence.
From a very early period of medical history, fennel seed has been credited with the power of increasing the
secretion of milk, (galactagogue.) Its use for this purpose is most extensive in Germany; but leading physicians
of many countries ascribe to it excellent power in this direction. The infusion of the seed may be used without
limitation.
Huefeland employed it in the following combination: Fennel seeds, one drachm; sweet orange-peel, half a
drachm; carbonate of magnesia, three drachms; sugar, two drachms. Mix the powders, and give a teaspoonful
three times a day. This preparation is greatly extolled through Germany. Others have given formulas combining
the fennel with anise seed, parsley root, licorice root, etc., and using an infusion freely.
HOMEOPATHIC
The whole plant has an aromatic odor and taste, owing to a volatile oil by which it is pervaded.lt is cultivated
largely in Italy and Sicily for the sake of the shoots, which are eaten raw, or in salad, or boiled as pot-herbs.
The odor of fennel-seed is fragrant, its taste warm, sweet and agreeably aromatic. It is among our most grateful
aromatics, and in this country much employed in the old school as a carminative and as corrigent
of other less pleasant medicines, especially senna and rhubarb. In infants it is employed as a tea, or injection,
to produce the expulsion of flatus.
In most of the ancient books on the practice of medicine we find it in common use as a modifier and corrective
of cathartic infusions, to prevent griping, and to obviate flatulence. As far back as Hippocrates can its
employment be traced.
Pressure in the left upper jawbone, which soon ceases. Pungent pain in the right elbow joint, it recurs often
during several days. Diarrhea. Increased secretion of urine. Excites the vascular system and the respiratory
organs.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Folliculinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - foil. Folliculinum. Ovarian follicle. Oestron. Estrone. Hormone secreted by the ovaries.
Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Backache. Cystitis. Headaches. Leucorrhea. Mastitis. Metrorrhagia.
Migraines. Palpitations. Premenstrual, syndrome. Seborrhea. Tachycardia. Vaginal, pruritus.
HOMEOPATHIC - A female remedy, affecting primarily the female hormonal system. Foil, in a homeopathic
dilution could be indicated in premenstrual syndrome, as well as for all the functional symptoms present in a
patient.
Premenstrual syndrome. Weight gain without excessive eating, worse before menses or during ovulation.
Premenstrual migraines. Congestive headaches, either with redness of the face or the opposite with pallor,
but still with the sensation of chilliness at the limbs.
Frequent ecchymosis, bruises very easily. Acne on the face and seborrhea of the nostrils. Hypersensitive to
heat, noise and contact.
Foil, in low potencies of 3x and 4c is an arouser to be given in cases of amenorrhea and insufficient
menstruation. In 7c, it is a regulator.
In 9c, it is a restrainer and a dose should be given either towards the tenth day of the cycle, when the pains
predominate on the 14th day or 5 days before the beginning of menstruation, when the discomforts are
predominant before the arrival of menses.
MIND - Alternation of excitability and depression, worse before menses. Irritable and sensitive before the
menses. Extreme instability with anguish, worse at nightfall. Sexual hyper-excitability. Fixed ideas of a sexual
nature.
Abdomen - Abdominal meteorism, worse three or four days before menses. Liver swollen, soft and
hypertrophic.
Back - Lumbar pains, worse during ovulation. Backache before menses.
 Bladder - Recurring cystitis in women.
Breasts - Breasts enormous, swollen, cannot bear being constricted or touched. The pain is ameliorated or
disappears with menses. Congestive mastitis.
Eyes - Swelling with edema of the conjunctiva tissue.
Face - Acne on the face and seborrhea of the nostrils.
Female - Congestion, uterine, and premenstrual pains. Vaginal, vulvar pruritus, worse before menses. Menses
prolonged, blood bright red with clotting. Menses painful for the first few days. Leucorrhea. Yellow or brownish
discharge, sometimes blood streaked, between menses, especially during ovulation. Small losses of blood
during ovulation. Uterus is fibrous with metrorrhagia.
Head - Alopecia in women.
Heart - Tachycardia. Palpitations with faintness. Sensation of constriction around the heart with feeling of a
bar in the precordial region, spreading to the left arm.
Lungs - Need for fresh air, takes large breaths of air and sighs deeply. Fitful cough, worse when in company,
with sensation of constriction around the heart.
Modalities - Better after the third day of menses. Better with movement. Better fresh air. Worse before menses.
Worse during ovulation. Worse from heat and resting.
Nose - Coryza with headache and profuse discharge. Hay fever.
Rectum - Feeling of heaviness in the rectum. Chronic constipation, sometimes alternation of constipation and
diarrhea.
Skin - Dry eczema, worse during ovulation, before menses. Dry eruption of the fingers with splitting and
chapping of the skin.
Stomach - Indigestion. Nausea with vomiting. Premenstrual pain in the right hypochondrium.
Throat- Swallowing of liquids very painful. Cannot bear pressure on the pharynx.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The closest remedy is Lach. Like this remedy, it has: Alternating excitability and
depression, extreme sensitivity to contact, amelioration by menstrual flow. But, unlike Lachesis, we do not find:
Laterality or aggravation from sleep, but, on the contrary, aggravation during ovulation. (2) Sepia, Lac-c., Puls.,
Kali-c.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Formalinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - formal. Formalinum. Formaldehyde. Formaldehydum solutum. Aqueous solution (35 percent)
of Formaldehyde gas. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anuria. Albuminuria. Catarrhal, disorders. Chills. Dyspnea. Eczema. Forgetfulness.
Laryngismus, stridulus. Ptyalism. Tuberculosis. Vertigo. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Formalinum is a powerful disinfectant and deodorant, as well as a potent poison. Prevents
growth and kills almost any pathogenic microorganism. It seems to have the peculiar property of eating into
malignant tumors, leaving the surrounding healthy tissue uncharred an unchanged.
MIND - Anxiety. Forgetfulness. Dullness of mind. Unconsciousness.
Head - Coryza, eyes water.
Kidneys - Anuria, albuminous urine. Lungs - Dyspnea. Whooping cough.
Mouth - Ptyalism, thick saliva. Loss of taste.
Rectum - Intense urging to stool, watery stools.
Skin - Puckers skin like leather, wrinkles, scales off. Eczema in neighborhood of wound. Damp sweat most
marked on right
upper extremity.
Stomach - Food feels as if it were a ball in stomach. Burning in mouth and stomach.
Temperature - Chills in forenoon, followed by long fever. Bones ache during whole paroxysm. During fever
forgets where he was.
Throat - Laryngismus stridulus.
Vertigo - Severe vertigo.
COMMENTS - A plug of cotton wool soaked in a 20 percent solution of formaldehyde and applied for a few
hours, will produce a necrotic slough, which must be scraped away before the next application, otherwise it
hardens.
Formal., in hot water as vapor, is a most valuable therapeutic agent in whooping cough, tuberculosis and in
catarrhal disorders of the upper air-passages.
RELATIONS - Antidote: Ammonia water. Compare: (1) Ammonium formaldehyde, known commercially as
 Cystogen. Dose, five to seven grains two to four times daily, dissolved in hot water after meals. Prevents the
decomposition of urine in the bladder, kidneys and ureters. Turbid urine rendered clear and non-irritating,
phosphatic deposits dissolved and growth of pyogenic bacteria arrested. (2) Also, Urotropin - A diuretic and
solvent of uric acid concretions, relieves cystitis associated with putrefaction. Three grains well diluted. When
administered it invariably appears in the cerebro-spinal fluid and therefore advised in threatened meningeal
infection.
 - Boericke.
FORMICA RUFA
(Red Ants)
PHARMACY - form. Formica rufa. Red ants. Myrmexine. Contains formic acid. N. O. Hymenoptera. Tincture
from crushed live ants. Contains formic acid. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Arthritis. Braindisorders. Bruises. Chorea. Cough, Diarrhea. Dislocations. Dropsies. Eyes
disorders. Facial, paralysis. Foot-sweat, checked. Gout. Hair, loss. Headaches. Nodes. Over-lifting, complaints
from. Paralysis. Polyps. Rheumatism. Spinal,
disorders. Spleen, pain. Stroke. Tapeworm. Throat, sore. Vision, disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - Formica rufa causes many rheumatic and gouty pains. Pains appear suddenly and dart
from place to place: left, then right, then left. Pains are worse from motion, better pressure.
Arthritis with sudden rheumatic or gouty pains. Chronic gout and stiffness in joints. Acute outbursts of gouty
poisons, especially when assuming the neuralgic forms. The spinal cord is affected, paralyzes and spasms
occurring. It affects the liver, kidneys and right side.
Influence on theformation of polyps. Tuberculosis. Carcinoma, cancer. Apoplectic diseases. Lupus. Chronic
nephritis. Atrophy of wounds. Takes cold easily. Clammy skin, disagreeable sweat during night, sweat without
relief. Chorea from checked foot sweat. Complaints from over lifting.
MIND - Indisposed, morose. Fearful, apprehensive. Exhilarated after pain. Remarkable and unexpected
activity of the mind during the day with absence of usual dullness and sleepiness. Forgetful in the evening.
Abdomen - Flatulence. Drawing pain around navel before stools. Dull pain in region of spleen. Hardening of
mesenteric glands.
Back - Soreness in neck and up into head. Severe pain in left side of neck while chewing. Severe pain across
sacrum and dorsum of each hand. Affection of spinal cord.
Breasts - Violent penetrating pain in region of right nipple. Lack of milk in nursing women.
Causations - Complaints from over-lifting. Checked foot-sweat. Wounds. Great liability to take cold,
consequences of cold and wet. cold bathing, damp weather.
Chests - Pleuritic pains.
Coughs - Cough tedious and long-lasting, worse at night and worse motion. Cough with aching in forehead
and constrictive pain in chest. Cough, mostly at night. Violent attacks of cough with vomiting, day and night.
Ears - Ringing and buzzing. Deafness. Cracking in left ear with headache. Polyps.
External sensitiveness of right ear and temple. Parts around ear feel swollen.
Eyes - Pain in the eyes on waking, better washing. Rheumatic iritis. Rheumatic ophthalmia. Macule and ulcers
on cornea. Dim sight. Flickering before eyes. Pterygium. Spasmodic twitching of upper eyelid.
Face - Entire left side of face and cheek feel as if paralyzed.
Female - Menses scanty and pale with bearing-down pain in back. Menses appear eight days too soon.
Ovarian cysts containing water or blood.
Head - Brain feels too heavy and large. As if bubbles bursting in forehead. Headache with cracking in left ear.
Headache better after combing hair. Vertigo.
Heart - Uneasy pain in region of heart. Fluttering palpitations.
Kidneys - Paralysis of bladder. Quantity of urine increased, urates. Urine like saffron, bright yellow, no
sediment, passed frequently. Bloody, albuminous urine with much urging.
Limbs - Rheumatic pains, stiff and contracted joints. Rheumatism comes on with suddenness and
restlessness. Muscles feel strained and torn from their attachment. Stiffness and contraction of joints. Hard
nodes around joints in and out. Weakness of lower limbs. Paraplegia. Pain in hips. Itching in armpits in
morning. Hands numb.
Lungs - Nervous asthma. Hoarseness with dry, sore throat, with aching in forehead and constrictive pain in
chest, pleuritic pains.
Male - Seminal emissions, weakness. Long- lasting erections after urinating in morning. Scanty ejaculation
with incomplete erection. “Slothful to venery.”
Modalities - Better warmth. Better pressure. Better rubbing. Better combing hair. Better after midnight. Worse
motion. Worse sitting. Worse dampness. Worse cold washing. Worse cold. Worse before snowstorms.
 Mouth - Water tastes sweetish.
Neck - Pain in neck when chewing, especially on closing jaws.
Nose - Nasal polyps. Coryza and stopped up feeling.
Rectum - Constriction in the anus. Drawing pain around navel before stool. Pain in bowels before stool with
shuddering chilliness. In the morning, difficult passages of small quantities of flatus, afterwards diarrhea-like
urging in the rectum. Light, foaming stools.
Skin - Red, itching and burning. Nettlerash. Hives in flat plaques. Nodes around joints. Wounds that atrophy.
Profuse sweat without relief.
Sleep - Could get to sleep if she could get the right position. All night dry throat, woke her out of sleep.
Disagreeable sweat during night, awoke with clammy skin. Wakes early and feels she has had sufficient sleep.
On awaking, headache, vomiting with headache, pain in eyes, stitches in ears.
Stomach - Constant pressure at the cardiac end of the stomach, with burning pain. Pains shifts from stomach
to vertex. Gas cannot be passed. Nausea with headache and vomiting of a yellowish bitter mucus.
Temperature - Profuse sweat without relief.
Throat - Sore throat in morning with much mucus, worse left side. Hoarseness with sore throat. Pain in neck
when hawking or gargling.
Vertigo - Vertigo, all things seem to move to and fro, reeling of body. Pain in left supra-orbital region when
going to bed with dizziness, blackness before eyes, better by sitting down.
COMMENTS - Sensation as if brain too heavy and large. Sensation as if a bubble burst in forehead. Hering
noted its use “in all kinds of apoplectic diseases. It strengthens the brain.” Cooper gave the 3x with success in
cases of weakness of the lower limbs.
J. W. Thomson reported the case of a man, aged 84, who had severe neuralgic pains between posterior of
right ear and center of occiput. He apparently recovered, but returned eighteen months later with a steady,
sore and burning pain in the same region, swollen and tender around, but especially
behind right ear.
He could only sleep in one comfortable position, which he could not describe, but only knew when he found it
and he must be covered up warmly behind right ear and between that and occiput and neck. All on the right
side. Better from taking right hand and rubbing gently behind right ear. Sweat afforded no relief, the whole
head seemed to sympathize with the distress. He had dribbling of urine.
Form, was given, six doses, one before each meal. On the second day towards evening, he felt worse, and on
the third day there were twinges and spasms of severe pain in addition to the sore pain that he had experienced
before. These gradually got better and on the fourth day even the soreness was much better.
The main thing, however, was that he felt mentally better, said his mind and head felt stronger and from feeling
depressed he had become cheerful and life did not seem the burden it had for some time past.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Formic acid, Ars., Bry. (2) Dulc. - Rheumatism. (3) Urt-u. - nettle-rash, gout,
rheumatism. (4) Frag-v. - lack of breast secretion. (5) Trom. - Diarrhea.
(6) Caps. - Burning pains worse by cold water. Compatible: after Cham.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Formicicum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - form-ac. Formicicum acidum. Formic acid. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Catarrh. Gout. Polyps. Tremors. Varicose veins. Vision, weak.
HOMEOPATHIC - Form-ac. is known to the homeopathic Materia Medica only in the preparation of Formica
rufa, a tincture made of ants that contain the acid. Apis and other insects contain formic acid, as well as Urtica
urens and many other plants.
Form-ac. in small doses increases muscular strength and resistance to fatigue. Feels stronger and more fit in
ordinary walking.
Chronic muscular pains and soreness.
Tremors. Gout and joint rheumatism, which appear suddenly. Pains usually worse on right side, motion and
better from pressure.
Chronic arthritis following an attack of acute rheumatic fever. Chronic arthritis in connection with gouty
diathesis. Marked diuretic effect, greater elimination of products of disassimilation, particularly urea. Failing
vision.
Hering gave as an indication for Form-ac.: “Burning pain, burning from washing, renewed burning from cold
washing.”
In prescribing it for varicose veins, polyps, catarrh, Clarke ordered an ounce or two of a solution of formic acid
 to the proportion of one part of the acid to eleven of distilled water. Of this, one teaspoonful is taken in a
tablespoonful of water after food once or twice daily.
COMMENTS - Mr. R. Wallace Ellison of Richmond, sent three letters to Anshutz concerning his experiences
with formic acid.
“About two years and nine months ago I added to my daily diet from one to two grains of Formic Acid with the
result that it has produced the following results in my body: Polyps and fibrous matter absorbed from my nose.
Nose tongue, lips and some other parts greatly reduced in thickness.
“Chronic catarrh of nose, throat and intestines practically cured. Stiff joints throughout the whole body have
become loose. Short sight diminished by fifty percent. Eyes have changed in color from light slate gray to a
darker shade.
“Varicose veins in left leg and others at base of neck now of no consequence. Facial and bodily appearance
so altered that even my mother is puzzled and I can meet and converse with people who formerly knew me
very intimately without my identity being discovered.
“I have also tried its effects upon a sickly and scabby pony and found it quickly restored the animal to health
as well as giving it a beautiful, healthy crop of hair. Anyone who cares can produce this result in the case of
an old pony. I hasten to add what I would have mentioned before, that the
quantity taken during the last two years was not much over 1 grains daily.
“I found that 2 grs. daily was too much for regular use, though it served the purpose. If my theory be correct,
perhaps 1 grains daily would be the proper thing and best to be taken in the form of honey, raw juice of sugar
cane, etc.
“When I first commenced I used to drink about a pint of water with it, but now I just put the teaspoonful of acid
into a very small quantity of water and drink it. It has a pleasant, 'fruity' sort of taste. I add a little citric acid and
sugar to it and I believe this improves the effect.
“Chronic arthritis of traumatic nature can be cured by formic acid. In the latter case Formic acid 6x showed
quicker and better results than 12x or 30x which are indicated in the previous cases. In general the
disappearance of the stiffness of the joint is the first sign of improvement. Then the pain and swelling cease
gradually in 1-6 months time.”
In the Homeopathic World of April, 1902, Dr. Dudgeon gave an account of the work of Dr. Edward Krull of
Gustrow, who was led to think of formic acid as a remedy from its constant occurrence in the internal organs
and soft parts of the body.
He found it constantly present in the sweat of healthy persons, but very much diminished in or entirely absent
from the sweat of persons affected with tuberculosis. He thought to supply the defect in tubercular subjects by
introducing it into the system in material doses.
He found no benefit when he gave considerable doses by the mouth, so he used hypodermic injections of the
watery solution. After two years of experiments he found to his surprise that the more dilute his injections were,
the more powerful the effects and he ended by giving injections of a dilution which corresponds to our 3c or 4c
and waiting five or six months before repeating the injection.
Dudgeon noted “He treated in this way with success externar and internal tuberculosis, chronic nephritis and
malignant tumors.
It was necessary for the success of the treatment that the nutrition of the body should be well maintained. In
cachectic states the treatment is not indicated. It will be remembered that Hering mentions the case of an
anemic woman who died from the effects of an ant-vapor bath.
“The general effects which were observed in all the cases treated by Krull's method were: Immediate increase
of nutrition, the appetite improved, the weight increased, all this without any material change in the diet.
“In all the patients during the first months, sometimes every two or three days, sometimes at an interval of
weeks, there occurred slight transient attacks of pain in the abdomen, on the right and left of the umbilicus,
sometimes accompanied by urging to stool.
“If several copious fecal evacuations occurred, this had no bad effect on the patient, they seemed to have a
critical character. After the injection the menses came on earlier and were more copious, all diseased organs
and parts showed greater activity.
“In the first and second stages of tuberculosis cure is the rule. In the third stage the treatment only does harm,
rapidly diminishing the strength.
“The action is most remarkable in lupus. During the first days after the injection the effected part commences
to grow vividly red, rises up somewhat and discharges moderately and is the seat of shooting pains
occasionally. Curative action usually begins in the third week.
“In carcinoma of the breast and stomach, the tumor first increases in size and becomes very sensitive and the
skin over it feels warmer. The shorter the term the tumor has existed and the stronger the constitution, the
 sooner does reaction occur and the consequent cure of the disease.”
In the concluding words of Dudgeon’s article, “Tuberculosis, chronic nephritis and carcinoma are not diseases
in which we can claim a great amount of success. So where other remedies fail or cannot be discovered we
may take Solomon's advice and ‘Go to the ant!'”
RELATIONS - Compare: Formica rufa., Apis., Urtica urens.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

In ancient medicine, Fragaria vesca was used in decoctions of leaves, roots or fruit, ripe or unripe, or
combinations of these. Fragaria vesca is commended by W. Salmon as a wash for sore-mouth, as a hemostatic
arresting the menses and stopping “bloody- flux,” swelling of the spleen, many forms of skin eruption and for

HOMEOPATHIC The allergic effects from those who are sensitive to strawberries have been utilized in
homeopathy. The well-known “strawberry tongue” is an indication for its use. Dr. Burnett gave it as “pippy
tongue.” Faintness, suffocation like a stroke, convulsions and death have resulted, general anasarca and
especially swollen tongue. Profuse viscid sweat.
Lippe mentioned “Tapeworm. Pain in chilblains in hot weather.” In two instances Clarke noted the indulgence
in strawberries to revive symptoms of gonorrhea in men who thought themselves cured. A number of cases of
sprue or pilosis have been cured by a diet of strawberries ad libitum.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hydr-ac., Apis, Ars. Crat.

name: Frankincense
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - Frankincense. Olibanum. Frankincense is an aromatic gum resin obtained from the trees:
Boswellia thurifera, Boswellia sacra, Boswellia carterii. N. O. Burseraceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Anxiety. Arthritis. Asthma. Bronchitis. Coughs. Dysentery. Fevers. Fungal, infections.
Joint, pain. Laryngitis. Leprosy. Scars. Skin, disorders. Stretch marks. Tumors. Ulcers. Vomiting. Wounds.
HERBAL - Frankincense remedies appear in the Syriac Book of Medicine, ancient Arabic texts, and in
Ayurveda and Chinese medical writings. Greek and Roman physicians used Frankincense in the treatment of
a great variety of diseases. It is stimulant, but seldom used now internally, though formerly was in great repute.
 Pliny mentions it as an antidote to hemlock.
The famous eleventh-century Arabian physician, Avicenna, recommended its cooling effects as a remedy for
infections and illnesses that increase the body's temperature. Avicenna used it fortumors, ulcers, vomiting,
dysentery and fevers. In China it is used for leprosy.
Recently, the Frankincense boswellic acids that are a part of the resin it produces have shown some promise
as a treatment for asthma and various inflamatory conditions. The inhalation of steam laden with the volatile
portion of the drug is said to relieve bronchitis and laryngitis.
The essential oil of Frankincense has been used for anxiety, stress, asthma, bronchitis, severe coughing, scars
and stretch marks. This oil is rejuvenating to the skin, treating acne, bacterial and fungal infections, and to treat
wounds and scars.
Thus, it is used in cosmetics, soaps, and perfumes. The anti-inflammatory properties of frankincense very
effective as a treatment for joint pain and arthritis.
COMMENTS - Frankincense is used in incense and perfumes. Its principal use now is in the manufacture of
incense and pastilles. It is used in plasters and might be substituted for Balsam of Peru or Balsam or Tolu.
It is also a natural insecticide and was used ‘ in ancient Egypt to fumigate wheat silos and repel wheat moths.
In Arabia, the smoke of burning frankincense resin is used to repel mosquitoes and sand flies.
Researchers have found that burning frankincense indoors improves the acoustic properties of the room. In
ancient Egypt the resin was a key ingredient for embalming the dead.
RELATIONS - Compare: Myrrh, Camphor.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Fraxinus Americana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - frax. Fraxinus americana. White ash. N. O. Oleaceae. Tincture of the bark. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cramps. Depression. Dysmenorrhea. Eczema. Fever, sores. Fibroids. Hot, flashes. Leucorrhea.
Menopause. Uterus, disorders. Uterus, prolapse. Uterus, tumors.
HOMEOPATHIC - Frax. had a fragmentary proving, but the chief clinical authority for its use is Dr. Burnett,
who regarded it as a uterine tonic in all heavy states of the uterus with prolapse, bearing-down and relaxed
ligaments. Burnett called it “the medicinal pessary.” Clarke repeatedly verified these indications.
It is an organ remedy of the first rank. A uterine tonic, especially useful for nervous females. Uterine tumors,
especially fibroids with bearing-down sensations. Uterine displacements. Enlargement of the uterus.
Subinvolution and prolapse. Fever sores on lips. Cramps in feet. Cold creeping and hot flashes. Infantile
eczema.
MIND - Depression with nervous restlessness and anxiety. Must talk.
Abdomen - Heavy bearing-down pain, extending to the thighs or falling out sensation with fibroids. Tenderness
in left inguinal region.
Female - Profuse menses. Dysmenorrhea. Profuse leucorrhea. Watery, non-irritating leucorrhea. Uterus is
enlarged, heavy and prolapsed. Uterine tumors. Subinvolution. Sensitive left ovary. Fibroids with bearing-
 down sensation, cramping in feet, worse in afternoon and night.
Head - Hot spot or dryness on vertex. Headache, with vertigo, followed by fever. Throbbing pain in back of
head and neck.
Kidneys - Urine scanty and brown. Limbs - Cramps in feet after midnight. Lungs - Pain through the lungs.
Modalities - Worse injury, sprains. Worse lifting.
Mouth - Fever sores on the lips.
Rectum - Bowels constipated.
Skin - Infantile eczema.
Sleep - Wakefulness the first part of the night. Dreamed that two rough men came into house, awoke breathing
quick, with a fearful feeling.
Temperature - Fevers. Cold creeping and hot flushes.
COMMENTS - Burnett writes: “A maiden lady, forty-three years of age, came under my observation on January
19th, 1892, telling me of her painful nerves and flushes that ave troubled her ever since she changed. She
gets gouty swellings of the feet, and has leucorrhea. Is much given to sleeping draughts. The womb is
somewhat large, the pain in the feet considerable, depriving her of sleep.”
“On condition that she abjures sleeping draughts once and for all, I undertake her case. This is an invariable
condition with me, as it is quite impossible to really cure people who take hypnotics.”
“I gave Fraxinus Americanus tincture. Ten drops in water at bedtime. March 3rd. Has done her much good,
womb is lighter, and she is better able to do her work. She sleeps now quite well without any sedative, a sure
proof that the neurasthenia was here primarily a womb ailing.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sep., Lil-t„ Sec. (2) Epiphegus, Nat-hyperchlor., Hydr. (3) Galega - Goat's Rue.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Fraxinus Excelsior
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - frax-e. Fraxinus excelsior. European ash. Common ash. N. O. Oleaceae. Tincture of the leaves.
The fresh leaves are pounded to a pulp and macerated with two parts by weight of alcohol. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Gout. Joint, disorders. Rheumatism.
HERBAL - Ash leaves were highly recommended by the medical alchemist Dr. Rademacher and were
extensively used in Germany on his suggestion. In the Union Medical for Nov. 27, 1852, two French physicians,
Drs. Pouget and Peyraud. detailed several case of gout and rheumatism cured by an infusion of ash-leaves in
boiling water. Dr. Peyraud himself was one of those relieved.
A commercial traveler, who had been gouty for twenty years and had saturated himself with the syrup of
Boubee and other
vaunted specifics, consulted Dr. Pouget. At this time he was almost constant prisoner in his room successive
attacks. After eleven days' use of the infusion he was able to walk two kilometers (one and a quarter miles), in
fifteen days he resumed his journeys and was able to travel without suffering from Bordeaux to Quimper.
Acute and chronice painful gout and rheumatism. Joint rheumatism in numerous instances.
COMMENTS - Anshutz recorded the case of Dr. Peyraud. In 1842, Peyraud had his first attack of gout, which
was severe and lasted for twenty-five days. During the three following years the attacks increased in frequency
and severity.
Having derived little benefit from the remedial means that he had resorted to, he listened to the suggestion of
one of his patients, an inhabitant of the department of Dordogne in France, who advised him to try an infusion
of ash leaves. Informing Peyraud, at the same time, that his forefathers had been cured by this prescription
and that many of the country people got rid of “their pains” by employing it.
Dr. Peyraud took the infusion of ash leaves and from 1845 to 1849 had no fit of gout. He then had an attack,
which yielded in five days to the infusion of ash leaves, used under the observation of Dr. Pouget.
Dr. Pouget recalled that when he was a physician at Soreze in 1824, the peasants of that place had spoken
to him of the great power which an infusion of ash leaves had in driving away pains. He afterwards discovered
that it had been used forty years ago as a gout specific by the peasants of Auvergne.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Colch., Rhus-t.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke.

name: Fucus Vesiculosus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lue. Fucus vesiculosus. Bladderwrack. Sea-wrack. Sea-kelp. Kelp-ware. N. O. Algae.
Phaeophyceae. Rich in iodine. Tincture and trituration of the dried plant. The fresh alga gathered in May or
June are pounded to a pulp and macerated in two parts by weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tritura- tion,
tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Constipation. Dyspepsia. Flatulence. Goiter. Obesity. Thyroid, enlargement.
HERBAL - In the American Eclectic Dispensatory, John King stated “Fucus vesiculosus, sea wrack or bladder-
wrack, has a peculiar odor and a nauseous saline taste. The charcoal of this plant has long had the reputation
of the deobstruent and been given in goiter and scrofulous swelling.
“The dose is a teaspoonful of the tincture twice or three times daily in a well-developed case. Half a teaspoonful
twice a day will answer in recent cases. Smaller doses seem not to produce any effect. The medicine is very
unpleasant to the taste, but causes no disturbance after it has been taken. It ought to be taken, each dose in
a few ounces of water and preferably between meals.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Fuc. is a tissue remedy of great power and must be compared with lod., of which it contains
a large proportion.
Digestion is improved and flatulence diminished. Obstinate constipation, forehead feels as if compressed by
an iron ring.
Very weak and restless. Thyroid enlargement in obese subjects. Obesity and nontoxic goiter, also
exophthalmic. Goiter has been cured with it in teaspoonful doses of the tincture given two or three times a day.
Abdomen - Flatulency diminished and then
disappears. Bearing-down pains in lower part of abdomen.
Eyes - Sight dim.
Face - Face became yellow.
Female - Menorrhagia, bright red blood, bearing-down pains in lower abdomen.
Head - Intolerable headache, forehead felt as if compressed by an iron ring. Headache with hemorrhages.
Burning at vertex. Nausea, vertigo, and slight headache.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate. Urine contains much blood.

Knapp to the Homeopathic Recorder, was publishedin 1896: ‘After treating many cases of exophthalmic goiter,
I have come to the conclusion that I have found a specific for that disease in Fucus vesiculosus, (sea-wrack).
I might record one case.
“ ‘Mrs. Mary B., age 24 years, German, came into my clinic at the Brooklyn E. D. Homeopathic Dispensary to
be treated for swelling of the neck of several years duration. I gave her the tincture of Fucus ves., thirty drops
three times a day. The treatment began December 1, 1895 and patient was discharged cured, on October 2,
1896. Would be pleased to hear from any others who have had any experience with Fucus vesiculosus.'
“So far as I now remember, this is the only hint I ever receive which led me to try in goiter. At the same time, I
do not feel sure of this. I had met in some medical journal
a statement respecting the relation of this drug to goiter, which fact led me to look it up in the ‘Eclectic
Dispensatory.' But if so, I cannot recall the authority.
“At all events, I was led to try the remedy in a pronounced case of goiter with such goods results that I have
never since given any other remedy for that disease either in the exophthalmic or in the uncomplicated form.
“What is more, I have never known it to fail to cure when the patient was under thirty years of age. After that
time of life or about that period, it seems to be no longer efficacious.
“I have now used it on more than twenty- four cases with the same unvarying result and never with any other
result-that is, no unpleasant consequences have ever accompanied or followed its use.
“I published this fact in the medical investigator after I had used it in a few case and again announced it in the
 Chicago Homeopathic Medical Society still later and again have frequently repeated it with growing confidence
and of greater numbers of cases in medical societies in colleges and in private conversation with physicians.
“And yet the fact is so utterly unknown that your journal published Dr. Knapp’s inquiry respecting it, which
shows how easily a good thing may be forgotten. Also how readily a genuine specific may be superseded by
a host of abortive procedures right under the eyes of the profession. It is most probable that more real good
remedies have been forgotten or cast aside in medicine.
“Respecting this Fucus vesiculosus and its use in goiter, I would like to add a few words. The drug is of variable
quality. If one specimen fails to give satisfaction it ought to be discarded and another tried. The pharmacist
must be importuned to make special efforts to give us an article that is not inert, but contains all the activity
that belongs to the drug.
“Time is required for effecting a cure. This varies according to the age and size of the goiter. Three months
may suffice for a small goiter of one year's growth. Six months may be required for one twice as
large and of longer standing. A year and a half is the longest period during which I have had to continue the
medicine. But during all that time the goiter was manifestly diminishing.”

name: Gaertner Bacillus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - gaert. Gaertner bacillus. Bacillus gaertner. Salmonella enteritidis. A bowel nosode of Bach.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Acidosis. Celiac, disease. Blisters. Cachexia. Colitis. Dentition. Emaciation. Eye, disorders.
Fibrositis. Gastro-enteritis. Growth, disorders. Hypersensitive. Indigestion. Ketosis. Malnutrition.
Marasmus. Neurasthenia. Otorrhea. Smallpox. Urticaria. Tabes mesenterica. Threadworms. Urticaria.
Vomiting. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - This organism was first isolated from a case of food poisoning and, when identified by
Gaertner, was given the title B. Enteritidis, the bacillus of the intestine.
The keynote is nutrition, and this nosode might suitably be named “the children nosode.” Clinically useful for
the nutritional disorders common to children.
 For children fed on artificial food who have poor digestion.
Affects the digestive tract. Inability to digest fat, celiac disease, ketosis intestinal infantilism. Malnutrition,
either from lack of adequate diet or failure to metabolize, e.g. in steatorrhea, celiac disease or following gastric
operations and in some cases of colitis.
Indicated by marked emaciation, marasmus, especially in children, the elderly, or with malignant disease.
Growth disorders. Poorly nourished bodies and poor muscular development, but with active minds. Restless,
lack of attention. Hypersensitive to physical or psychological impressions. Fear of the dark and of being alone.
Urticaria.
MIND - Hypersensitive to all impressions. Restless. Mental uneasiness. Pessimistic, lack of confidence. Fear
of heights, of the dark and of being alone.
Abdomen - Chronic gastro-enteritis, tabes mesenterica.
Back - Severe pain in hip and back.
Chest - Bronchial colds. Nocturnal coughs.

Pale, thin. Long, black eyelashes.

Pruritus vulvae.

meat, and fish.
Kidneys - Blood and mucus with urine.
Burning in urethra.

hands in winter. Bites nails. Pes planus. Soles of feet covered with blisters, itch and are worse at night.
Male - Hydrocele.
Mouth - Herpes. Dry, scaly eruption.
Salivation. Deep fissures in tongue. Teeth black.
Nose - Polyps. Catarrh.
Rectum - Constipation. Blood and mucus in stool. Diarrhea offensive, attacks every few weeks. Itching of
anus. Worms, threadworms (Cina).
Skin - Urticaria, heat spots. Circinate eruption on sternum. Eruption on back, head and neck. Boils on arms
and legs. Perspiration, worse at night.
Sleep - Desires light in room. Desires company, especially mother. Late in falling to sleep. Sleep walking.
Restless sleep, night terrors.
Stomach - Pain in stomach. Dilated stomach. Vomits everything, worse after sweets. Headache and
vomiting. Acidosis attacks.
COMMENTS - Ghosh noted “Gaertner in 30c potency may be used in extensive suppuration with intestinal
disorders in small-pox.”
E. Paterson thought that Gaert. may help in teething troubles where Cham, fails. Defective digestion of fat as
of Puls, has a worthy trial of this remedy. “In all varietiés of neurasthenia, I know of no single remedy to
compare with the Gaertner nosode.”
Wheeler noted: “For cases of children who get a discharging ear every time they cut a tooth, give one dose of
Gaertner 30, followed the next day by the dose of Silica 30c and repeat the Gaertner as soon as there is any
■'ign of a further out break of this ear discharge.”
Griggs indicated that “it is helpful to make a comparison and to remember the Dys-co. child whose nervous
tension expressed itself by an uneasiness of the muscular system. Although fidgety and uneasy, the shyness
of his temperament would prevent him from leaving his chair while you are taking the preliminary notes in your
consulting room.
“The Gaertner child has mental uneasiness. He must know the reason for everything you do and for what
purpose you use this or that article lying on you desk or somewhere in the room. Furthermore, he will proceed
to make close inspection of it, but you will notice that his attention is not held long on any subject.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The remedies most closely associated with this nosode are Dys-co., Phos., Sil.
and Merc.
REFERENCES - Bach. Boericke. Paterson.

tonic in cases of anemia and impaired nutrition. Backache and debility.

kidney though it is unaccompanied by any sign of kidney disease.
Carron de la Carriere tested its action on the milk glands of nursing women. He found it rapidly increased the
quantity and quality of the milk and increased the woman's appetite.

name: Gallicum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - gall-ac. Gallicum acidum. Gallic acid. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Constipation. Debility. Delirium. Heartburn. Hematuria. Hemophilia. Hemorrhages.
Kidneys, pain. Pulmonary, hemorrhage. Tuberculosis. Urticaria.
HOMEOPATHIC - Gallic acid is the well- known astringent, derivative of tannic acid, obtained from galls or
oak-apples. It is used in old-school practice as a local application to arrest hemorrhages and in popular practice
to check excessive menstruation.
A case is recorded in which the application of an ointment containing gallic acid or the insertion of a tannin
suppository for hemorrhoids caused an attack resembling hay asthma with an eruption of urticaria. The
experience was repeated several times before the cause was discovered.
 This is sufficient to show that Gall-ac. is homeopathic to pulmonary cases in which it has been largely used by
the old school as well as the new. Pulmonary hemorrhage, excessive expectoration, and the nightsweats of
tuberculosis.
Tuberculosis. Weakness with irritability. Excessive dryness of mouth and throat. Sense of contraction of anus.
Jerking of limbs. Itching of skin.
MIND - Wild delirium at night, very restless, jumps out of bed, sweats. Rude, abuses every one. Cursing.
Strange speech. Jealousy. Afraid to be alone.
Eyes - Photophobia with burning of lids. Head - Pain in back of head and neck.
Kidneys - Kidneys painful. Distress along ureters into bladder. Dull heavy pain in bladder, directly over pubis.
Urine loaded with thick, cream-colored mucus. Hematuria.
Lungs - Pain in lungs. Pulmonary hemorrhage. Excessive expectoration. Much mucus in throat in the
morning, dry at night.
Nose - Thick, stringy discharge from nose.
Rectum - Copious stool, anus feels constricted. Chronic mucus discharges. Faint feeling after stool.
Throat - Much mucus in throat in morning. Dry throat at night.

purulent expectoration, night-sweats, evening fever, pulse 130. Under the prolonged use of Gall-ac. lx she
recovered her normal health except that the left lung remained dull and she had great shortness of breath on
the slightest exertion. Her flesh, strength and general appearance were as when she was in perfect health.
Bayles said Gall-ac. rapidly checks secretions, give general tone to the stomach, increases appetite, and
removes constipation. Heartburn. Hematuria. Hemophilia. Passive hemorrhages when pulse is feeble and
capillaries relaxed, cold skin.
RELATIONS-Compare: ( l)Querc.,Tann-ac., Bac., Ars-i., (2) Phos. relieved pain in right lung. (3) Ars., lod.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Dysentery. Eyes, inflammation. Flatulence. Food, poisoning. Lienteria.
Rheumatic, pains. Sneezing. Sore, pains. Throat, sore. Typhlitis. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Affects the stomach and bowels, chiefly known as a remedy for a diarrhea similar to Crot-
t.
Burning in anus after stool, anus sore and excoriated. Profuse watery diarrhea, particularly with elderly
people. Stool preceded by excessive cutting about navel. Stool is expelled all at once after considerable urging
and is followed by a feeling of great relief. Stools are yellow, green, bloody, lienteric.
Frightful vomiting and purging with fainting. Burning in the liver. Pain in small of back, as if bruised or sprained.
Pain in sacrum, resulting from a blow. Gnawing pains in the coccyx. Burning pains. General soreness.
Rheumatic symptoms. Periodic symptoms.
MIND - Irritable in morning on waking. Despondency, sadness. Cheerful and talkative. Feeling of ease, great
lightness of all his motions.
Abdomen - Gurgling in abdomen, as of fluid running from a bottle. Rushing sounds in abdomen as from
motions of air. Tenderness in epigastrium. Pain and distention of abdomen from flatulence after stool.
Rumbling and rolling. Ileo-cecal region sensitive to pressure. Pinching pain in abdomen immediately after
eating.
Back - Pain in coccyx. Small of back as if bruised or sprained. Gnawing pain in coccyx. Pain and itching
between scapula. Cutting pain across top of sacrum and in left hip. Cutting pain in muscles just above sacroiliac
symphysis on left side.
Chest - Congestion of blood to chest. Chest, sore and raw. Pressure and weight in chest. Pressure pain in
middle of chest. Sharp pains in sternum. Sharp pains going from both sides of chest towards each other.
Cough - Dry, with hoarseness and hawking of mucus. Severe cough, at night, compelling him to sit up, with
easy expectoration of mucus. Cough better sitting up.
Ears - Ringing in left ear all the time. Lancination pain in ears.
Eyes - Burning in eyes. Itching and burning in eyes. Itching of eyelids, he rubs them.
Eyelids stick together with sneezing. Eyes as if sticky and dry. Nightly agglutination of lids, burning in
morning. Violent burning of eyes with photophobia. Smarting of eyes with lachrymation. Very severe pain in
eyeballs.
Face - Swelling of face. Swelling of eyelids, nose and lips. Upper lip swollen. Itching, smarting on right cheek,
chin and upper lip.
Female - Menses too early and too profuse. Menses long-lasting. Congestion to sexual organs. Leucorrhea.
Food - Aversion to food. Violent thirst in evening. Appetite good, but a little food satisfies. Thirst after dinner.
Thirst during chill. Great thirst, in chronic diarrhea. Worse after drinking ale.
Head - Gastric headaches. Head hot, face red, during attacks of diarrhea. Heat rises to head, with sweat.
Heavy sensation with inertia and drowsiness. Sensation of great coldness in left temple as from a wet cloth.
Vertex as if bruised, in forenoon, better open air. Oppressive pain with heaviness in forehead. Compressive
pain. Pain in coronal suture.
Kidneys - Sharp pain in left kidney. Infrequent urination. Increased secretion of urine. Urine smells like onions.
Urine diminished in dropsy.
Limbs - Stinging and numb feeling in ball of right thumb. Tearing pain in shoulders. Sharp pain, in upper limbs.
Itching blisters on both hands, at first pale, afterwards red. Severe aching deep in hip, and severe cutting pain
about trochanter major. Aching pain in knees. Cramp in calf with contraction of toes. Heaviness and languor
of feet.
Liver - Burning in liver.
Lungs - Expectoration of blood.
Male - Gleety discharge agglutinating orifice of urethra.
Modalities - Better by motion. Better in open air. Better after stools. Better sitting up. Worse evening and at
night. Worse motion. Worse in open air. Worse after stools. Most symptoms come on while sitting, and go off
during motion in open air.
Mouth - Aphthae. Deep ulcers in mouth, inner side of lips and cheeks. Bitter taste in mouth. Feeling of coldness
at the edge of teeth. Burning vesicles on inner side of lips. Dryness of mouth. Clammy, adhesive state of
mouth.
fióse-Violent chronic sneezing, in daytime only. Smarting as if a sore pimple existed immediately below right
 nostril. Dryness of right nostril. Much mucus in nose, smelling like pus. Tendency to hemorrhages from nose
and lungs.
Perspiration - Sweats all over, at night. Sweats on awaking at 4 a.m. Cold sweats on limbs, during stool.
Rectum - Burning and heat in anus during stool. Tenesmus after stool with burning in anus. Pinching,
gurgling in bowels, then sudden yellow or green. Diarrhea alternating with constipation. Hard, insufficient stool,
with strong urging. Dysentery, with retained stool, with pain in sacral region. Frequent emission of flatulence.
Thin stools coming out in prolonged gushes with burning at anus. Diarrhea with sudden and forcible
ejection of bilious stools. Diarrhea after drinking ale. Profuse, watery diarrhea in hot weather, particularly
old people. Yellow and green diarrheic stool, mixed with mucus. Stools of dark green mucus, offensive,
corrosive. Infantile diarrhea.
Skin - Violent itching in various parts of body, burning after scratching, worse evening and night. After
scratching, burning and ulcerative pain, with swelling and redness of parts, worse evening and night.
Biting as of ants over whole body, worse 1 evening and night. Itching on various parts of surface pleasantly
better gentle friction. Itching and formication here and there all night. Pemphigus.
Sleep - Sleepiness, great inclination to sleep. Sleeplessness from weight on chest. Anxious, vexatious dreams.
Dreams with broken sleep.
Stomach - Frequent violent empty eructations. Gulping up of sour water. Gnawing pain in stomach. Emptiness
in stomach and abdomen. Great irritability of the stomach. Pain in the stomach after food. Acute dart
ing, stitching pain in stomach. Nausea, inclination to vomit with accumulation of saliva in mouth. Frightful
vomiting and purging, with fainting. Ulcerative pain in stomach, better after eating. Vomiting and purging with
fainting.
Temperature - Violent chill, beginning in back. Chill with empty eructations. Internal and external coldness
from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. Violent shaking chill at 7 p.m., beginning in back. Sudden shaking chill at night, waking
him from sleep, and suddenly disappearing. Chill with chattering of teeth and violent thirst. Increased heat with
anxiety.
Throat - Swollen sensation. Violent stitches in right side of throat. Pain as from soreness in throat. Rawness
and burning in throat, causes constant hawking. Sore, in throat. Scratching sensation in larynx. Tickling in
larynx and trachea from epiglottis to pit of throat.
Tongue - Burning, smarting and dryness of tongue and throat. Burning of anterior half or only tip of tongue,
which feels hard. Raw, rough feeling in fauces and at root of tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo during rest or motion. Vertigo in morning. Vertigo on rising. Confusion of head with feeling of
reeling or motion from side to side.
COMMENTS - Gamb. painted on the chest in lung tuberculosis was considered by Abrams a specific. Also
incipient diarrhea cases were symptomatically cured in several weeks.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Coff., Coloc., Kali-c., Op. Compare: (1) Crot-t., Aloes, Podo., Puls. -
cough better sitting up, better open air. (2) Apoc. - stool expelled all one, but Gamb. has cutting before and
better after stool. (3) Crot-t. has stool in one gush, but Gamb. is not worse from least food or drink like Crot.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Gastein Aqua
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - gast. Gastein aqua. Gastein springs. The hot springs of Wildbad Gasterin in Salzburg, Austria.
Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Callosities. Colds. Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Gout.
Hemorrhoids. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Scars. Sexual, weakness. Stones. Strokes. Typhlitis. Varicose ulcers.
HOMEOPATHIC - The hot springs of Wildbad Gasterin in Salzburg. Austria, contain sodium sulphate
predominantly, but also silicic acid, potassium sulphate and carbonate, lithium chloride, magnesium carbonate,
ferrum carbonate, aluminium phosphate and traces of calcium fluoride, strontium, arsenicum, titanic acid,
rubidium, cesium, also free carbonic acid. Lapis albus is a kind of gneiss found in the spring. It is a silicofluoride
of calcium.
Constantin James described the effects of the baths as a “General unpleasant sensation. Instead of expanding
(as would be expected in a warm bath) the skin is drawn up upon itself as if by a tight astringent. There is slight
dyspnea, the abdominal walls draw together, the testicles rise to the inguinal rings.
“Soon an unusual warmth, accompanied by shocks and tremors, spreads throughout all the limbs. The pulse
becomes hard and vibrating, the face becomes suffused, there is humming in the ears. It is now time to leave
the bath to stay longer is attended with danger.
“Then after the seventh to the fourteenth bath the thermal influence tends to concentrate itself entirely on the
 nervous system. Thus it seems to the patient that an increase of vitality spreads through his whole being, he
feels more active then before, the longest walks cause hardly any fatigue and that is promptly repaired by
sleep.
“Among individual symptoms noted are diminished secretions. Activity of all the veins, excitement of the
circulation. Weakness and weariness with dragging sensation in the abdomen, as if it were too heavy.
Exhaustion and inclination to sleep.
“Takes cold very easily, which was caused then cured. Pulsation in the body, especially in the arms with
jumping in them. Contractive sensations predominate. Scar tissues and callosities are affected. Worse before
a storm.”
COMMENTS - The baths affect phlegmatic patients in an increase of force and tone, causing the
disappearance of involuntary losses of semen. In irritable temperaments it will provoke erotic dreams and
unwanted excitement, in such cases the waters are aphrodisiac.
Sensation of indescribable mental and physical comfort runs through all the tissues during the bath.
Predominantly influences the sexual system.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lap-a., Fl-ac. Sil., Canth., Phos.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
