name: Hedeoma Pulegioides
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - hedeo. Hedeoma pulegioides. Pennyroyal. American pennyroyal. N. O. Labiate. The British
Pennyroyal is Mentha pulegium. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Gastritis. Flatulent, colic. Leucorrhea. Miscarriages. Nausea. Poison
oak. Vertigo. Vomiting.
HERBAL - Hedeoma puleg. is also known as the common English Pennyroyal, the German Poley, the Arabic
Alnam, and the ancient Greek Glachon. Hedeoma belongs to that large class of mints and common herbs that
have been cast aside by the medical profession as worthless.
Hedeoma is one of the oldest remedies known, a common household herb long before the time of Hippocrates.
Hippocrates and the ancient physicians used it as a tea for increasing the flow of urine, for kidney stones, and
as a uterine stimulant. Popularly believed to be valuable for treating miscar 1 riage in weak, cachectic women.
HOMEOPATHIC - Marked female symptoms, often associated with nervous disturbances. Bearing-down
 pains, worse by any movement and accompanied by almost paralytic weakness of the legs.
Nervous symptoms, jerkings and twitch- ings. Weak, faint, better lying down, inability to sit up. Pains in
abdomen, worse after eating or drinking, touch and pressure. Flatulent colic. Pain along ureter. Red sand ih
urine. Antidotes effects of poison oak (Grin.). Abdomen - Distended, sore and sensitive.
Flatulent colic.
Female - Leucorrhea with itching and burning. Ovaries congested and painful, bearing-down spasmodic
contractions. Bearing-down pains with much backache, worse least movement.
Head - Dull, heavy feeling in morning. Sore pain, as from a cut. Weak, faint, better lying down.
Kidneys - Dragging pain from kidney to bladder. Dull burning pain over left kidney. Frequent urging, cutting
pains. Pain along left ureter. Burning irritation at neck of bladder causing frequent, intense desire to urinate
and inability to retain urine for more than a few minutes, better urinating.
Limbs - Pain, coldness and paretic conditions. Twitchings, jerkings, soreness. Pain in thumb joint. Achilles
tendon painful, as if sprained and swollen, walking painful. ,
Stomach - Gastritis. Everything taken into stomach causes pain. Tongue coated thin white. Nausea.
COMMENTS - Anshutz wrote “Hedeoma contains three bodies peculiar to the plant, three different oils, also
formic and acetic acid and likewise ischeptoic acid. There are on record seven cases of poisoning. Two
provings have been made by my self. Several of the poisoning
cases are very meagre and of little value.
“One teaspoonful of the oil, three drachms of the essence, seems to be almost a fatal dose in one case only
was abortion produced and that from one ounce of the oil, followed by collapse and death.
“The leading symptoms of the cases of poisoning are briefly: Vertigo. Dimness of vision. Dilated pupils. Nausea
and vomiting. Persistent severe bearing-down pains from the upper part of the sacrum and the region of the
kidney to the uterus like true laborpaints. Frequent painful, scanty, burning urination. Small, rapid pulse.
Nervous weakness. Cold clammy limbs.”
Dr. Toothaker reported a case in which the bearing-down labor-like pains and the scanty, painful urination
lasted for many days and were very severe.
Clarke prescribed this remedy in two cases. In the first, a woman of gouty, rheumatic tendency, who had
dragging burning pains in the left ureter going to the bladder and was passing quantities of “red sand.” The
pain lasted for ten days. Hedeo. 1c, on discs, was given, one disc every two hours. Complete relief was
obtained after two doses.
The second case concerned a man of 60, very fond of champagne, who was bothered by constant burning
irritation at the neck of the bladder, which caused frequent, intense desire to urinate and an inability to retain
his urine for more than a few minutes. He always had marked relief on urinating. Urine retained in the bladder
increased this irritation at the neck of the bladder and also caused an uneasy pain in the right testicle.
These symptoms had been more or less persistent for months and the attacks always lasted days at a time.
Complete relief was obtained after one or two doses of Hedeo. 1c.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Menth., Sep., Lil-t. (2) Oci. - uric acid diathesis, pain in ureters. (3) Hed.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Hedera Helix
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - hed. Hederá helix. Common ivy. Ground ivy. Glechoma hederacea. N. O. Araliacee. Tincture
of young shoots. Tincture of flowering twi¡is. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anxiety. Arterial sclerosis. Arthrosis deformans. Cataract. Cerebro-spinalis.
Cirrhosis. Convulsions. Cough. Delirium. Diarrhea. Emphysema. Gallstones. Gastritis. Hay fever. Hemor-
rhoids. Herpes. Hydrocephalus. Insomnia. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia. Myocarditis. Raynaud's syndrome.
Rhinorrhea. Rickets. Sinusitis. Tachycardia. Whooping cough.
HERBAL - Hederá helix, or Ivy, is a shrub that grows all over Europe. It is a creeper, which fixes itself by
clinging roots. The leaves are cadiform at the base and more separated in the higher parts of the plant.
The fruit is bluish-black in color, equal to a pea in size. Historically, the wood was used for coughs as an anti-
spasmodicl; the leaf was used internally as an emmenagogue and externally as a topical anti-neuralgic. The
fruit was used for intoxication, digestive and nervous complaints, delirium, and convulsions. The mother
tincture is used for coughs and is prepared from the flowering twigs.
HOMEOPATHIC-The symptomatology was established by Mezgerin 1932 on seventeen people, using the lx,
6x, and 15x potencies, for a period of twelve weeks. Easily tired, ameliorated by fresh air or noticeable increase
in physical ability.
Dr. Cooper's experience has shown it to have a relation to rickets and rickety conditions. Rhinorrhea cerebro-
 spinalis. Hed. has been used for “clearing the sight” and Cooper said it has cured cases of cataract.
Joint pains and circulatory complaints, especially in the middle of the night. Cardiac palpitations. Acts on blood
vessels, menorrhagia. Menses reduced, vesicular eruption on the face and body.
Swelling of the thyroid glands. Glándula sub-mentalis inflamed. Extreme anxiety with the feeling of constriction
of the throat. Cough with laryngeal and tracheal irritation. Morbid hunger, gastric cramps. Diarrhea. Anus feels
raw and sore. Hemorrhoids with rectal irritation and bleeding.
Delirium and convulsions. Chronic hydrocephalus, rhinorrhea, and cerebro-spinalis. General improvement in
fresh air. but extreme sensibility to catching cold and to chills. Symptoms start on the left side and spread
towards the right.
MIND - Constant state of unrest and worry. Anxiety, which grows all the more as he feels incapable of
mastering it. Insomnia. Psychological symptoms improve in fresh air.
Abdomen - Pancreatitis.
Constitutions - Tubercular conditions, especially in phosphoric types.
Ears - Pain and buzzing.
Eyes - Feeling of sand in the eyelids. Cataract. Muscae volitantes.
Female - Premenstrual leucorrhea. Acrid, scorching discharge. Menses late, shorter and less copious.
Infrequent menses. Feels better during menses. Amenorrhea in young girls. Pain in the Fallopian tubes and
left ovary. Sclera-cystic ovaritis, especially on the left side. Genital tuberculosis.
Food - Lack of appetite or strong hunger pangs.
Head - Catarrhal inflammation of the frontal sinuses with headache. Headache, especially in the left side of
the forehead and nape of the neck. Neuralgic pains in the head, ameliorated by fresh air.
Heart - Angina pectoris. Needle-like pains in the precordial region. Palpitations and anguish with swelling of
the thyroid gland. Myocarditis. Arterial sclerosis. Rhythmic anomaly, accompanied by tachycardia. Thyrotoxic
tachycardia. Extrasystole or paroxysmal tachycardia, in a young subject with a normal heart.
Kidneys - Frequent, abundant urination.
Limbs - Pain in the arms, legs, back and sacral region, sometimes ameliorated, sometimes aggravated by
movement. Muscular rheumatism. Joint rheuma
tism. Tubercular inflammatory dislocating rheumatism. Arthrosis deformans. Nocturnal paresthesia pains in
the arms. Raynaud's syndrome.
Liver - Inflammation of the gallbladder. Gallstones. Pain in the region of the gallbladder. Cirrhosis of the liver
with cardiac decompensation.
Lungs - Irritated cough with grayish or yellow sputum. Whooping cough. Bronchial asthma in children.
Emphysema.
Modalities - Better from fresh air. Better cold baths. Better in a room. Better movement. Better friction,
massage. Better in the afternoon and evening. Worse in the middle of the night. Worse 3 a.m.
Mouth - Transparent vesicles on the lips and on inside of cheeks in a group, circumscribed by ared ring.
Toothache from hot and cold. Dental neuralgia.
Nose - Hay fever. Acute and chronic rhinitis. Sinusitis (frontal, ethmoidal). Pharyngitis. Nasal discharge, worse
in a warm room. Pain in the ethmoid and frontal sinuses. Chronic tracheitis, caused by a lesion in the nasal
mucous membrane.
Rectum - Stools copious, either diarrhea or constipation.
Skin - Pruritus. Eruption of small pustules on the skin of the face and body. Prurigo. Urticaria. Labial and
genital herpes.
Sleep - Wakes around 3 a.m., falls asleep again after eating a little.
Stomach - Pain on empty stomach, ameliorated by eating. Nausea, gastric heaviness, stomach cramps.
Gastritis. Stomach and duodenal ulcers.
Temperature - Peripheral circulatory complaints. Feet and hands icy, red. Shivering and chilliness with bouts
of perspiration and palpitations. Shivering and nausea in the evening until 4 a.m.
Throat - Chronic tracheitis. Pain around the tonsils and throat on swallowing. Hoarseness and inflammation
of the larynx. Cough with a cold and inflammation of the pharynx, aggravated by heat and by speaking.
Vertigo - Vertigoon bending down and from rapid movement of the head.
COMMENTS - Cooper published case of a woman of twenty, who was cured of chronic hydrocephalus with a
single dose. When she was brought to Cooper, the circumference of her head was 27.5 inches, rendering her
an object of wonder and ridicule and reacting on her disposition and nervous state.
The condition had existed from childhood and was apparently growing much worse. There were two large
edematous swellings on the nape of the neck, one on either side and immediately below the occiput, evidently
the result of intra-hydrocephalic pressure.
 One drop of Hed. tincture was placed on her tongue. The next morning, clear fluid began dripping from the
nostrils, a “cerebrospinal rhinorrhea” in face.
This continued for three weeks, between twenty and thirty pocket-handkerchiefs were used in a day.
Simultaneously the swellings began to diminish and had completely disappeared when the discharge ceased.
Thirteen months later, when being measured for a hat, it was found that the size of the head was reduced to
25 inches and no longer occasioned remark.
When, later on, some symptoms of brain pressure seemed to threaten, a second dose of Hed. completely
dispelled them. The disposition of the patient was completely changed from being nervous, unhappy and
diffident, she became lively, cheerful and active.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aral-r., Gins., Sil., Nat-m. (2) lodum - is the remedy, whose symptomatology is
very similar. lodum shows more emaciation inflammation and hardening • of the lymphatic glands. Ovarian
pain on the right and menses more abundant. (3) Calc- fl - Fear that his way of life will collapse. Pains
aggravated by humid or cold weather. Menses copious. Hardening of the breasts, ovary or uterus. (4) Nat-m.
- Depressed and sad, prefers solitude. Emaciation. Fissure in the middle of the lower lip. Chronic, periodic
headaches with strong pulsating, as though the head would burst. Dryness of the mouth with extreme thirst.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.
keynote:
PHARMACY - hed. Hederá helix. Common ivy. Ground ivy. Glechoma hederacea. N. O. Araliacee. Tincture
of young shoots. Tincture of flowering twi¡is. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anxiety. Arterial sclerosis. Arthrosis deformans. Cataract. Cerebro-spinalis.
Cirrhosis. Convulsions. Cough. Delirium. Diarrhea. Emphysema. Gallstones. Gastritis. Hay fever. Hemor-
rhoids. Herpes. Hydrocephalus. Insomnia. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia. Myocarditis. Raynaud's syndrome.

name: Hedysarum Ildefonsianum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - hedy. Hedysarum ildefonsianum. Brazilian burdock. Hedysarum desmodium. Barba de Roy.
Carapicho. N. O. Leguminose. Papilionoideae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Gonorrhea. Ophthalmia. Penis, inflammation.
HERBAL - This plant is named by Mure, who gave an account of it in his book and described it as “The
brownish ligneous stem of this plant is about three feet high, it is ramose, pubescent, especially above. Leaves
alternate, pinnate, trifoliate, folioles oval and slightly tormentóse, on a hairy, bi stipulate petiole.
“The flowers, which are small and seated on filiform unifloral peduncles, form loose, terminal spikes. Fruit oval,
hairy, on bent peduncles and attaching itself very intimately to clothes and to hairy skin of animals.
“The chief effect of Hedysarum was inflammation of the penis and of the eyes, which should indicate it in some
cases of gonorrheal ophthalmia.”
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Helianthus Annuus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - helia. Helianthus annuus. Sunflower. N. O. Composite. Tincture of mature flower-heads.
Tincture of ripe seech. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Hemorrhoids. Intermittent fever. Nasal obstruction. Nausea.
Nosebleeds. Spleen, disorders. Throat, sore. Urticaria. Vomiting. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Helia. is a spleen remedy (Cean.). Spleen disorders. Chronic cases of intermittent fever.
Coryza, catarrh, nasal hemorrhage and thick scabs in nose. Rheumatic pain in left knee. Externally, used as
a vulnerary like Arn. and Calen.
In the pro vers there were marked effects on stomach, with nausea and vomiting. Congestion and dryness of
mouth and pharynx.
Dry mouth. Redness and heat of skin, worseexternal warmth. Black stools (Lept.), soft, with an emission of
semen; stools become black, hard, occurring every other day. Hemorrhoids.
Abdomen - Spleen enlarged and painful.
Eyes - Slight redness on margin of left upper lid with smarting in inner canthus. Eyes suffused. Weakness of
the eyes.
Face - Anxious, countenance. Face deeply flushed.
Food - Thirst, nausea.
Head - Headache.
Limbs - Rheumatic pain in left knee on descending stairs.
Lungs - Cough in forenoon with gelatinous expectoration streaked with blood. Breath rather difficult and
hurried.
Modalities - Better after vomiting. Worse from external heat, especially the skin.
Mouth - Tongue and fauces very red and inclined to dryness. Unusually hot taste when eating. Difficulty in
articulation. Sticking in upper back teeth.
Nose - Coryza, catarrh. Nosebleeds and thick scabs in nose.
 Rectum - Hemorrhoids. Stools soft, black, hard, every other day, with emission of semen.
Skin - Skin generally of scarlet redness and very hot. Tingling of skin. Many urticarialike pimples. Groups of
red pimples on inner side of knee with slight itching. Small red tetter to right of navel. Measles.
Stomach - Vomiting, increasing in severity-
Throat- Voice hoarse. Stiffness and dryness of the throat. Sensation of glowing in the throat and stomach.
Severe burning in fauces, esophagus and epigastrium.
COMMENTS - Dr. Cessoles proved the expressed juice of the flowers, some observations have also been
made on the effects of eating the seeds. In some parts of America the Native Americans use the seeds as an
article of food.
Hansen said it equals Arn. and Calen., also yellow-flowered composites, as an application to wounds. Burnett
regarded Helianthus as a great spleen remedy.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lept. - black stools. (2) Arn., Calen., Hyper. - wounds. (3) Cean. - spleen.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Heliotropinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - fielio. Heliotropinum pe-ruvianum. Heliotrope. Cherry pie. N. O. Boraginaceae. Tincture of whole
fresh plant when in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Backaches. Clergyman's, throat. Dysmenorrhea. Headache. Hoarseness. Leu- corrhea. Sore,
throat. Uterus, displacement.
HOMEOPATHIC - Helio, has been slightly proved. Cooper used this remedy clinically and considered
hoarseness and “thick voice” a great indication. He cured clergyman's sore throat with it.
Helio, has an action in uterine displacement, leucorrhea, backache. There is a bearing down from heavy,
waterlogged condition of the uterus. ,
Symptoms of pressure and tension were produced in many parts: pressure on the sternum impeding breathing,
pressure on the head, on mons veneries, pain as if beaten in leg muscles.
Chest - Pressure and oppression of external parts of chest, without affecting breathing.
Eyes - Feeling of tension in left inner canthus extending down into nasal bone. As if a swelling were there. Eye
seems drawn together and smaller.
Female - Membranous dysmenorrhea. Leucorrhea. Pressure on mons veneries only when sitting. Uterine
displacements with backache, especially if subject to loss of voice.
Head - Headache in forehead like a pressure and drawing pressing pain, better walking in open air.
Limbs - Pain, as if beaten above ankle, extending up the muscles, even when sitting. Itching on tibia, with
sensations as if there was an eruption.
Modalities - Head symptoms better on walking in the open air. Other symptoms were worse after resting.
Worse on inspiration.
Stomach - Pressure in pit of stomach, worse on inspiration. Epigastric region is sore to touch, most violent
after eating and in evening.
Throat - Voice thick, clergyman's sore throat.
COMMENTS - Cooper gave Helio, to a woman who had been advised by several surgeons to have various
organs either braced up surgically or removed. She described the effect as having made her “feel just as if
braced up” six hours after taking the dose.
Helio, is especially indicated if there is also a tendency to loss of voice. It has also cured membranous
dysmenorrhea.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bor. - membranous dysmenorrhea., (2) Symph. - bruised pain in leg.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Helix Tosta
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-helix.Helixtosta.Toastedsnail. N. O. Helicide. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Dyspnea. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhage. Hoarseness. Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Snails have a tradition for curing tuberculosis.
COMMENTS - W. H. Leonard reported two cases cured with Helix 100,000c. In the first, a man had frequent
hemoptysis. Continuous hoarseness with a dry tickling cough, worse at night, preventing sleep. Dyspnea,
worse from ascending stairs. He had already had all the usual remedies.
Helix 100,000c., three powders were given. There was no more hemorrhage. A few weeks later a return was
 feared and a few more doses were given. Four months later the patient was greatly improved in health and
remained well.
In the second case, a woman of tubercular diathesis developed the disease after confinement. Several well-
indicated remedies
failed to check its progress. At length, hemorrhage set in.
Helix was given, as in the other case, with prompt effect. Hemorrhage ceased, cough and expectoration
gradually improved, and in eight months the patient was well and remained so.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Helleborus Foetidus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - hell-f. Helleborus foetidus. Bears foot. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of the root. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Cholera. Hair, loss. Nails, brittle. Scarlatina. Skin, peeling. Stiff-neck.
HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of Hell-f. have been observed on several persons. It is a violent narcotic-acrid
poison and in fatal poisoning cases death has taken place in convulsions.
The vision is disordered, choleraic symptoms occur, skin, hair and nails exfoliate. “Profuse discharge from
ulcerated surfaces.” Anxiety, better after vomiting.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Verat. - copious liquid stools. (2) Hell., Hell-v., Colch.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Helleborus Niger
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - hell. Helleborus niger. Black hellebore. Snow-rose. Christmas rose. N. O. Ranunculacee.
Central Europe. Tincture of dry powdered root. Juice of fresh root mixed with equal parts of alcohol. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amenorrhea. Apathy. Aphthae. Ascites. Brain, disorders. Cholera. Coma.
Concussions. Convulsions. Cough. Cystitis. Depression. Diarrhea. Dropsical, swellings. Dullness. Epilepsy.
Fevers. Headaches. Head injury. Hernia. Homesickness. Hydrocele. Hydrocephalus. Hydrothorax. Hysteria.
Kidneys, congestion. Mania. Melancholy. Meningitis. Night -blindness. Post-partum, convulsions. Scarlatina.
Strokes. Stupor. Tetanus. Typhoid, fever. Ulcers. Uremia. Wounds.
HERBAL - “Black” hellebore receives its name from the external color of its root. It is commonly known as the
Christmas Rose or black hellebore. Black hellebore was one of the drugs used to produce the “Helleborism of
the ancients,” a subject of Hahnemann's famous writings.
HOMEOPATHIC -Low states of vitality and serious diseases, when everything around the patient looks dark
and dusky. Patient's face, lips, hands etc. become dark, nostrils sooty. Parts that are usually red can turn
white. Feeble and delicate.
Sensorial depression. Senses become blunt and responses are sluggish, sees, hears, and tastes imperfectly.
Mania of a melancholy type.
Muscles do not obey the will, can stagger, drops things etc. General muscular weakness, which may go on
to complete paralysis, accompanied by dropsical effusions Convulsions and twitching of muscles, automatic
acts, automatic motion of one arm and leg.
Epilepsy with consciousness, followed by deep sleep. Convulsions with extreme coldness in nursing children.
Noise arrests the paroxysms of convulsions. One side is paralyzed, the other keeps up automatic motions.
Sinking sensation. Gradual onset of the disease with progressive weakness. Lies on back with knees drawn
up or with legs spread apart. State of effusion in hydrocephalus. Serous effusions. Characteristic aggravation
from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. (Lyc.).
MIND - Dull, stupid, slow perception. Slow in answering. Answers confusedly as if thinking of something else.
Inattention. Sensorial apathy and constant thoughtless staring at one spot alternating with unintelligible mut-
tering. Gloomy, dismal, despair.
Irritable, worse consolation, does not want to be disturbed. Aversion to company, better when alone.
Indifference to loved ones, relations. Indifference to pleasures. Indifférance to everything. Indifférance to
sufferings. Envious seeing others happy.
Ailments from disappointed love. Homesickness. Worse or better from thinking of complaints.
Fixed ideas. Just sits and says nothing, does nothing. Hysterical mania from selfaccusation. Drops things when
attention is diverted, as when being spoken to. Things look new and different. Melancholy during puberty.
Sensitive to noise.
 Involuntary sighing. Picks at lips and clothes, ends of fingers. His mind seems to have lost all control over
his body. Stubborn silence. Would not eat or speak. Never expresses desire for anything. Idiocy after a stroke.
Complete unconsciousness. When aroused he talks about spirits and says he sees devils.
Fear of dying. Believes she is doing wrong. Thinks she is going to die on a certain day. Delusions, sees devils.
Delusions sees images in the dark. Delusions pursued by enemies. Fancies at talking with dead people.
Abdomen - Distended. Swollen, painful to touch. Coldness in abdomen. Inflation of the epigastrium with pain
of ulceration and impeded respiration. Ascites. Griping, pinching colic with weakness. Griping, pinching about
navel, in the abdomen, followed by gelatinous stools. Rumbling and borborygmi in the abdomen, gurgling, as
if bowels were full of water. Severe, hard pressure on middle of os pubis.
Back - Gnawing and obtuse lancinations of the spine. Pain, as from a bruise, between the shoulder blades.
Neck rigid (meningitis). Stiffness and painful sensibility of the neck and the nape of the neck during movement.
Swelling of the glands of the neck.
Bladder - Cystitis. Constant desire to urinate, causing spasms, passing very little. Urination suppressed. Child
can't urinate. Bladder overdistended. Bladder becomes paralyzed and greatly distended during pregnancy.
Uremia. Dropsy. Frequent urging, with scanty discharge. After great pressure he passes, with much pain, a
few drops of blood.
Breasts - Pain under left nipple, pains all over her, forced her menses on, had to get up at night to pass water.
Causations - Ill effects of checked exanthemata, blows, disappointed love.
Chest - Constriction of the throat, nose and chest. Heat in the chest. Tension in region of left short ribs during
cough. Sharp cutting pain in region of lower ribs across chest, from within outward, worse inspiration. Chest
constricted, gasps for breath with open mouth, propped up in bed.
Coughs - Short, dry cough, worse at night, smoking or suddenly appears while smoking. Dry cough with
gagging. Sudden cough, constant hacking.
Ears - Shootings in the ears, day and night with searching piercing. Roaring and ringing. Apparatus of hearing
intact, yet hears nothing distinctly nor comprehends.
Eyes - Eyeballs red, glassy. Eyeballs turn upwards, squinting, vacant look. Contraction alternating with
dilatation of pupil. Eyes wide open, sunken. ¡Blue edges. Stupid staring or tired look. Night blindness.
Photophobia without inflammation. Squinting of eyes with insensibility to light. Sensation as if eyelids were
pressed down, difficult to open them. Lids sticky, dry. Loss of hair from eyebrows.
Face - Face flushes red and then becomes pale. Pale, sunken, edematous, red hot or cold. Wrinkled. Neuralgia
on left side, parts so tender he cannot chew. Face distorted, yellowish. Constant chewing motion of the lower
jaw, hangs open. Cold sweat on face, icy-cold.
Female - Suppression of the menses. Amenorrhea from disappointed love, from damp feet and getting wet
through. Pains all over her body forces her menses on. Uterine dropsy with piercing pain in limbs. Puerperal
convulsions, arrested by sudden noise.
Food - Anorexia, with brain complaints. Speedy satiety with repugnance as to rest of meal. Organs of taste in
working order, yet finds not the proper taste in anything. Nausea, can't take food, though hungry. Aversion to
vegetables, meat, sauerkraut. Thirst absent in most complaints or thirst
with disgust for drinks. Violent thirst and usually canine hunger during fever. Greedily swallows the cold water,
then bites the spoon, while unconsciousness, with hydrocephalus. Children nurse greedily. Head - Concussion
of the brain from blow on the head (after Arn. has failed). Rolls the head constantly with moaning.
Hydrocephalus. Dropsy of brain. Bores into pillow. Meningitis. Strikes the head. Forehead wrinkled in folds
in brain disorders. Brain feels too large. Cold sweat. Stupefying headache, worse stooping. Headache ends
in vomiting. Shooting pains, causing sudden screams. Dull pain in occiput with sensation of water swashing
inside. Electric shock passes through brain before spasms. Heat deep within head. Pain in vertex as if a nail
were driven in. Humid scurf on scalp. Hair falls off with pricking on scalp.
Heart - Palpitations. Heart's action weak. Anxiousness about heart which prevents him resting anywhere.
Pulse, small, slow, soft, almost imperceptible. Slow, small, soft pulse, often slower than beating of heart. Pulse
intermittent in hydrocephalus.
Kidneys - Congestion of kidneys with extensive effusion of serum in abdominal cavity and tissue of lower
limbs. Nephritis causing dropsical symptoms. Uremia. Large quantity of pale, watery urine. Urine scanty, dark
with floating, dark specks. Coffee-ground sediment, especially during pregnancy. Passes blood and slime,
with burning and stinging.
Limbs - Limbs heavy and painful. Stretching of limbs. Edemaoflegs. Shiverings, alternating with shooting pains
in the limbs. Automatic motion of one arm and leg, except when asleep. Thumb drawn into palm (Cupr.).
Legs drawn up with every attempt to change the position. Contractive pain in the loins. Vesicular eruption
between fingers and toes.
 Lungs - Suffocating constriction in the lungs, throat and nose. Sighing respiration. Accelerated or deep and
slow respiration. Gasps for breath but can't inhale. Hydrothorax (Merc., Sulph.). Breathes
easier lying down.
Male - Hydrocele from suppressed eruption, on either side. Suppression of sexual desire with flaccidity of the
genital parts.
Modalities - Better when mind is diverted. Better in warm air. Better by wrapping up. Breathing easier when
lying down. Worse from cold air. Worse uncovering. Worse evening until morning. Worse 4 p.m. to 8 p.m.
Worse from puberty. Worse dentition. Worse suppressions. Worse exertion. Worse motion. Worse touch.
Worse stooping. Worse when thinking of ailment.
Mouth - Lips dry and cracked. Mouth dry, also palate, with cutting and scraping in palate on moving mouth to
swallow. Meaningless picking of lips. Chewing motion. Greedily swallows cold water, though unconscious.
Child nurses greedily with disgust for food. Horrible smell from mouth. Apthous, lienteria. Falling of lower
jaw. Ptyalism, with sore corners of mouth. Mouth, gums and tongue full of flat yellow ulcers, with elevated grey
edges, or red, swollen edges. Salivation. Will take no food except drink. Eruption of blisters around mouth.
Nose - Dirty, dry nostrils. Nostrils, sooty, dilated. Nose pointed. Fluent coryza with confusion of head, as if
bruised. Sneezing. Smell diminished. Rubs nose in hydrocephalus.
Perspiration - Nocturnal sweat towards the morning. Cold, clammy perspiration. Sweats temperature
unchanged. Sticky sweat. Sweat relieves. Sweats less after sleep.
Rectum - Constipation alternating with mucous diarrhea. Feeling as if intestines had no power to evacuate
feces, during soft stool. Diarrhea with pain in the abdomen and nausea. Diarrhea preceded by colic, which is
better after every stool. Diarrhea during acute hydrocephalus, dentition or pregnancy. Stools, involuntary,
loose, watery, like frog-spawn, of white jelly-like mucus. Watery and frequent evacuations. Burning, smarting,
at anus, after stools. Hemorrhoids.
Skin - Pale, dropsical, itching. Anasarca. Angio-neurotic edema. Sudden, watery, swelling of skin. Livid spots
on skin. Military eruptions. Falling off of hair and nails. General desquamation of the skin.
Sleep - Stuporous, cannot be fully aroused. Sleepiness with eyes half open and pupils turned upwards.
Confused, anxious dreams, the remembrance of which is not retained. Tossing in the bed. Sleeps with shrieks
and starts. Sudden screams in sleep. Muscles twitch during sleep. Cri encéphalique (Apis.).
Stomach - Heaviness, fullness of the stomach. Pit of stomach sunken. Burning and scraping in the stomach,
which extends to esophagus during pregnancy. Nausea, sometimes with excessive hunger, rising up from pit
of stomach. Nausea during pregnancy, before and during stool. Nausea and violent vomiting, with much heat
in stomach. Vomiting of greenish-black substance with colic. Anorexia with brain complaints.
Teeth - Grinds the teeth. Toothache at night with shooting and tearing pains, worse by cold and heat.
Temperature - Coldness of the body, especially the limbs. Chill spreads from arms. Goose bumps. Chill with
fever, sweat and aversion to uncover. Chilliness predominates during the day with heat of the face and
drowsiness. Heat followed by chill with colic.
Throat - Bitter taste in the throat, worse by eating. Water rattles down throat. Scraping feeling on back of
palate. Tiresome dryness on palate and cutting and scraping pain on moving the parts in swallowing. Aching,
sore throat on swallowing, feels excoriated.
Tongue - Tongue, numb, trembling, covered with yellow ulcers. Tongue red and dry, white in morning. Pimples
on tip. Bitter taste, worse eating.
Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea, watery vomit and loose bowels, worse stooping, better becoming erect.
Vision - Early stage of amaurosis. Nightblindness. Vision unimpaired, nevertheless sees imperfectly and
doesn't regard the objects he sees.
COMMENTS - Hahnemann wrote “I conclude from various observations that one of the first effects of Black
Hellebore is a kind of stupor, a dullness of the sensorium commune, a condition where with sight unimpaired,
nothing is seen very fully and the patient does not pay any attention to anything.
“The hearing is perfectly sound, but nothing is heard distinctly. With perfectly constituted gustatory organs,
everything seems to have lost its taste. Where the mind is often or always without ideas. Where the past is
forgotten or little remembered. Where nothing gives one any pleasure. Where one's sleep is very light and a
really sound, refreshing sleep is not to be had and where one desires to work without having the necessary
strength or attention required for it.”
Cooper, who studied the Hellebores very closely, noted that they produce the “sinking sensation” more
intensely than any other drugs. The winter aconite (Eranthis hyemalis), a close ally of Hell., “acts on the solar
plexus and works upwards, causing dyspnea.”
Cooper quoted from Flora Histórica an interesting account of how French prisoners of war at Norman-cross
were suffering from an epidemic of night-blindness (nyctalopia), when for lack of snuff they took to using
 powdered black hellebore with the result that they were cured of their blindness in a few days.
Teste grouped Hell, in the Chamomilla class with Grat, and Viol-t., all of which cause “a joint derangement of
the cerebral functions and even of the whole nervous system, a painful increase of the sentient action, followed
by a considerable depression of the vital forces and a certain disorder of the mental faculties.”
Impaired mental functioning. Functional shut-downs of various parts of the brain, particularly since fever,
trauma, drug overdoses. Fluid buildup in the brain. Loss of memory.
Stupor or coma since head injury (Arn., Nat-s.). Hydrocephalus. Strokes followed by idiocy. Brain symptoms
during dentition. May help for autism.
Lack of response to sensations, mumbling. Pupils are fixed and dilated, or fixed and contracted (Op.). Craves
cold water. Mouth chews, bites, while unconscious. Constantly picks the lips or bedding while unconscious.
Grinding teeth, the head bores into the pillow. Pulse is slow and feeble, the respiration is slow and the
temperature low. Torpidity and apathy (Op.).
From a purely nervous derangement, it can go on to inflammatory states of the brain and its meninges. Keynote
drowsiness, particularly in meningitis or fever. Effusion from the inflamed membranes. Dropsical conditions,
post-scarlatina dropsy.
The forehead is wrinkled, there are automatic movements of one arm and leg, while the other is paralyzed.
The head rolls from side of side with screams. Chewing motion of jaws. Greedy drinking of water.
Stupefying headaches, as though contents of head were bulging at forehead and eyes. Shocks pass through
the brain like electricity. Boring and shaking in forehead and occiput, bruised pain, heat in brain. Pains in
occiput and nape of neck.
In fever, sooty appearance of the nostrils, dry, yellow tongue with red edges, horribly offensive breath, drinks
roll audibly into stomach. Pale, cold face. Pulse is faint, imperceptible. Fever is worse 4 to 8 p.m.
Suppressed urine in high fevers (Apis). Scanty or entirely suppressed urine, sometimes with sediment like
coffee grounds. Urine symptoms in general conditions, will increase the flow. Vomiting and purging, the vomit
is apt to be green and the stools jelly-like.
Hydrocele from suppressed eruptions. Ulcers with dropsical conditions (Cooper treated with Hell, and Hell-v.
given internally). History of use as an application to drain the tissues of ulcers. Hell. fet. is noted for “profuse
discharge from ulcerated surface.”
Clarke frequently cured with Hell, a headache which the patient could only describe as a “stupid headache.”
Teste cured with Hell. a case of epilepsy in a little girl five weeks old after the failure of Cham. Cham, was
given to the nurse, Hell, directly to the patient.
History of a case of brain concussion resulting from a blow on the head (after Arn. failed). One pupil was larger
than the other, the patient was drowsy, answered questions slowly, one leg dragged on walking.
RELATIONS-Antidote: Camph., Chin. Compare: (1) Threatening effusion. Tub., Apis, Zinc., Op., Chin., Cic.,
lodof. (2) Hell-f. - Acts especially on spleen (Cean.), also rectum and sciatic nerve. Splenic pains extend to
scapula, neck and head, worse left side and evening, chronic ague cake, hypertrophied uterus, glandular
enlargements, hair and nails falling off, skin peeling.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Heloderma Suspectum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - helo. Heloderma suspectum. Gila monster. Heloderma horridus. N. O. Helodermide of the
Lacertilia. Trituration of sugar of milk saturated with the venom. Solution of the venom in alcohol. Historical
dose: All potencies, thirtieth potency.
CLINICAL - Brain, affected. Cerebrospinal meningitis. Coldness. Cyanosis. Depression. Headache. Heart
failure. Locomotor ataxia. Melancholy. Neuralgia. Numbness. Paralysis. Paralysis agitans. Parkinson's
disease.
HOMEOPATHIC - The first notice of the remedy is from Dr. Charles D. Belden, who supplied Boericke and
Tafel with a living specimen and poison he obtained.
Heloderma is sluggish and slow of movement when kept in the dark, but may develop great activity when
brought into the sunlight. The only vulnerable part seems to be at the junction of the head with the spine, a
blow on which will kill it.
Belden noted that this animal does not bite frequently, but when it does it is understood that the result is
abenumbing paralysis similar to Parkinson's disease or to locomotor ataxia. There is no tetanic phase, a
condition almost reverse in objective symptoms to Hydrocy. acid or Strychnia.
Helo, is indicated in many forms of disease characterized by great coldness, “an arctic” coldness as the
intense icy coldness is the most peculiar symptom of the poison. Cold waves from occiput to feet or
ascending, as if frozen from within outwards.
Breath and tongue are cold, cold feeling in lungs and chest, coldness across scapula, burning in the spine.
Cold, creeping ring around the body.
The eyeball becomes more prominent and the cornea shows opacities. Boyd noted that the exophthalmus
is due to the pressure of the blood behind the eyeball.
Steps high and puts heel down hard, sensation as if walking on a sponge or as if with swollen feet. Turns to
right when walking. Stitch pains going from left to right. Weak, giddy, making it difficult to stand. Unable to
balance himself. Patient staggers while walking. Movement does not increase the pain. Throbbing all over
body. Bone pains.
MIND - Melancholy with weeping. Depression. No inclination for exertion in any way. Passively indifferent.
Forgetfulness. Difficulty in remembering the spelling of simple words. Unable to confine mind to any object.
Startling easily with trembling, on slight noise. In spite of very severe symptoms, not alarmed.
Abdomen - Sensation of constriction about the whole abdomen. Throbbing, rumbling in bowels. Sharp,
shooting, stitching pain in bowels, more on left side. Pain across pubic bones, extending down into left testicle.
Back - Stiff neck, aching in bones of neck. Painfulness of upper neck. Chill in back from base of brain
downwards. Coldness across scapulae. Pain in back, pain in lumbar muscles awakening him. Burning along
spine.
Chest - Cold feeling in lungs and in heart. Sharp stitch through right nipple to inside of the right arms.
Ears - Pressure behind left ear, pressure in ear from within outward. Copious flow of wax. Ears dry and scurfy.
Ringing in ear like night-bell.
Eyes - Itching of eyelids, heavy, hard to keep open. Eyeballs become more prominent and the cornea shows
opacities. Lachrymation.
Face - Cold, crawling feeling, from temple down right cheek, as if facial muscles were drawn tight over the
bones. Stiffness of jaw. Dry lips. As if pricked with points of
ice. Sensation of heat. Flushes of heat.
Female - Burning and dryness of the vagina.
Food - Dislikes sweet things, worse from taking them.
Head - Cold pressure within the skull. Cold band around head. Heat on vertex. Benumbed feeling all over
head. Soreness and stiffness in occiput. Throbbing on vertex. Pain beginning in right ear, extending around
back of head to left ear. Sensation as if head would fall to right side. As if scalp were drawn tight over skull.
Bores head in pillow. Awakes suddenly with jerk in head.
Heart - Palpitations and dyspnea from slight exertion. Slow labored thumping of heart. Pressure at heart.
Tingling, trembling, oppression and coldness around heart. Sticking pains, shooting from left to right. Stitches
in heart. Soreness in heat, more under left nipple.
Kidneys - Aching, stitching in right kidney. Bladder irritable, frequent urging to pass urine. Tenderness in
urethra with sensation of discharge. Urine not as free as usual, muddy. Intermittent flow. Urine is greenish-
 yellow, fetid like decaying fruit. Burning in the urethra during and after urination.
Limbs - Stretching relives pains in muscles and limbs. Numbness and trembling. Coldness. Numbness of the
arms from the hands to the elbows. Cyanosis of hands. Tingling, creeping sensation on the legs as if from
insects. Leg is insensible to an electric battery. Leg is wasting away, skin very dry and inelastic. Ankle turn
easily when trying to walk. Sensation as if walking on sponge and as if feet were swollen. Staggering gait.
Cock's gait. When walking, lifts feet higher than usual and puts down heel hard. Feet cold as ice or burn.
Lungs - Slight, hacking cough with pain in the left scapulae. Fullness in chest, requiring an effort to inflate the
lungs. Oppressed for breath from least exertion.
Male - Cold penis and testicle with gluey discharge. Pain and enlargement of left testicle.
Modalities - Better from stretching. Better warmth. Worse when thinking of her ailments. Worse being cheered
by company. Worse from cold. Worse exposure to cold air. Worse stormy weather. Worse lying in bed at night.
Worse after sleep.
Mouth - Breath cold. Tongue dry and cracked in the morning. Tongue cold, tender and dry. Very thirsty.
Swallowing difficult. Dryness of lips. Soreness.
Nerves - Startled easily. Tired feeling, very weak and nervous. Trembling, of left side, hands shaky, can be
controlled with effort. Intense aching in bones and all parts of body.
Nose - Left nostril sore, ulcerated. Dry, itching scurfs in nostrils. Severe attack of sneezing. Fluent discharge.
Pulse - Full and jerky.
Rectum - Constipation from torpor of the rectum. Loose, copious stool, lumpy, mushy, preceded by stitches
in abdomen, with considerable flatus. Stool soft, dark, difficult to expel. Hemorrhoids, swollen, itch and bleed.
Itching of the anus.
Skin - Yellow skin. Itching, as from insects.
Sleep - Drowsiness, but inability to sleep. Restless sleep, awakens at 3 a.m. Awakened from sleep by jerking
in head, trembling of limbs, pain in lumbar muscles.
Stomach - Empty belchings, especially before breakfast. Empty, gone sensation in the stomach. Acid burning
in stomach.
Temperature - Internal coldness, as if frozen to death. Temperature subnormal (Camph.). Cold spots.
Cold rings around body. Arctic coldness. Severe chill ran down back. Cold waves (Abies-c., Aeon.), ascend
from feet or downward from base of brain. Hot flushes and burning in head and along spine.
Throat - Swallowing difficult. Dryness, parched sensation. Tingling. Soreness, tenderness to touch. Stinging,
sore feeling in right tonsil.
Vertigo - Sensation as if would fall to right side.
COMMENTS - The Gila monster is a native of Arizona, New Mexico and Texas. It is smaller than the Mexican
variety, called
Heloderma suspectum Heloderma horridum, the “Crust lizard” or the “Gila monster,” which is generally
regarded as harmless.
Belden described it as “an ugly, disagreeable-looking creature, the head long and blunt, eyes black and bead-
like, tail half the length of the body, thick-set and club-like. The entire body cased in a thinly coated armor,
marked curiously with yellow and black.” Its skin is studded with nail or tu- bercle-like heads.
The venom is alkaline in reaction. A number of cases of bites are on record. A dog bitten in the nose “uttered
fearful howls and when after great difficulty, he was released, had symptoms like ‘blind staggers,' began turning
around in a circle and died in twenty minutes.”
A young miner bitten in the leg, through in robust health at the time, at once began to lose flesh, became
melancholic and died in a few months like a person with rapid tuberculosis.
A Native American woman bitten in the leg survived, but the leg shriveled and she became a semi-idiot, though
she lived over thirty years after. The writer of an article quoted by the Recorder from the New York Sun related
her case, describing the effect as:
“Where the person survives an hour or two after the bite, the agony is described as awful to witness. The
poison goes through the human system with rapidity and causes unspeakable pain and excruciating agony
from head to foot.
Though paralyzed, every muscle, bone, sinew and nerve is keenly alive to intense pain. The sufferer's head
seems as if it would split open. Very few persons bitten can speak after the first fifteen minutes, but
unconsciousness seldom comes until a few minutes before death.”
Belden noted its reputation of being fatal to drinkers and to affect non-drinkers less severely. This is borne out
somewhat by the recovery of Mr. Vail of Tucson, a man of temperate habits, after a bite: and the death of a
man bitten while drunk, after lingering several months.
This lingering nature of the poison is markedly different from snake poisons, which generally kill quickly, if at
 all.
Mr. Vail said his suffering was intense, the pain proceeding from the wounded part to the head and back.
Immediately after receiving the wound, which was on his index finger, both wrist and finger were tightly
bandaged.
Two hours later, the wound was cleansed and dressed and the bandages reapplied. For three days those
intense pains would shoot toward the head and spine on loosening the bandages in the least degree.
After three months the only perceptible result was a swollen tongue that seemed then unwilling to resume its
proper size. The treatment he received was profuse sweating by administration of Jab.
This much was known when Dr. Robert Boocock made his proving. His first experience was with three or four
drops of a solution of the 6x trituration, one drachm in four ounces of alcohol.
He was seized with an internal coldness from the heart as if being frozen to death internally and had no way
of warming himself. “Coldness from within outward.” The coldness of this remedy is more intense than that of
any other. The prover called it “arctic coldness.”
The coldness was at times followed by sensations of heat and burning. Dr. Boocock's observation of the cold
sensations of Helo, was confirmed by a young clerk in the employment of Messrs. Boericke and Tafel, who
took six doses of Helo. 6c out of bravado.
The second night he awoke and felt a cold sensation creeping down his body and legs and was in a very cold
clammy sweat. This lasted all the rest of the night and he could get no more sleep. It began to pass off by
morning, and he felt no more of it.
Helo, produced the constricting sensations of the serpent venoms as well as the numbness, darting pains and
the sensitiveness to external pressure. Many of the symptoms came on in the night waking the pro ver from
sleep (Lach, is “worse from sleep”).
Tremors, spongy feeling of feet on walking. Pains in back and limbs. Belden recommended it for locomotor
ataxia and Parkinson's disease (Merc., Rhus-t., Ars., Zinc), particularly with depression. Raynaud's disease.
Polyneuritis, peripheral neuralgias. May be useful for hypothermia.
Dr. Boocock gave great relief with the medicine in a case of Parkinson's disease.
E. E. Case effected great improvement in a case of locomotor ataxia in an auburnhaired woman, 55. She had
the classical symptoms of the complaint and “tingling, creeping sensations in legs as if from insects. She was
worse lying in bed at night, worse from exposure from touch. Arms numb. Legs insensible to battery. Tongue
dry and cracked. Swallowing difficult.”
Under Helo. 900c and later, 45,000c after the appearance of an eruption, she recovered a fair degree of health
and usefulness.
C. E. Johnson reported to Dr. Boocock the relief of a woman who had many of the symptoms of the proving
(and had been pronounced incurable), complaining especially of the intense coldness. She received Helo.
200c and the coldness disappeared almost completely.
Boocock cured a case of “blue hands,” remaining long after diphtheria paralysis and he restored two patients
apparently moribund. In one case the breathing was slow, “tongue cold and slate-colored, breath cold.”
The other case was that of a woman, 65. In the act of dressing, strength suddenly left her, mouth fell open
tongue and breath cold and she was apparently dying and felt so. There was intense pain at the back of the
head. Helo. 200c was given, as in the other case, and she made a good recovery.
Dr. Boocock compared the weakness he experienced in the proving to that of Gels., only Gels, did not dry up
the mouth and secretions as Helo. did.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lacer. - skin eruptions. Vesicles under tongue. Increased mental acumen.
Difficult swallowing. Constant accumulation of saliva in the mouth. Nausea, violent pressure in stomach.
Camph., Lach.
(2)   Crot-h., Camph. - coldness. (3) Arg-n., Alum. - locomotor ataxia. (4) Ant-t. and Merc. - Parkinson's
disease, Gels., Con., Lyss.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Helonias Dioica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - helon. Helonias dioica. Uni- com-root. Helonias lútea. False unicorn. Devil's Bit. Blazing Star.
N. O. Melanthacee. Tincture of the root. Triturations of the resinoid Helonin. Historical dose: Trimration,
tincmre and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Atony, uterus. Backaches. Breast, disorders. Chlorosis.
Cramps. Debility. Depression. Diabetes. Dysmenorrhea. Impotency. Kidney, pains. Leucorrhea. Lochia,
prolonged. Menopausal, disorders. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Pruritus vulva. Rheumatism. Splenalgia.
 Infertility. Uterus, disorders.
HERBAL - Helonias has been called a uterine tonic.
HOMEOPATHIC - Helonias has an extensive range of action, as its provings show, but it predominantly affects
the uterus. One of the keynote indications for its use is a “consciousness of the womb.” Relaxation of the
uterine ligaments, misplacements and prolapse (Sep.). Exhaustion from the least mental or physical exertion.
Emaciation or chronic fatigue since childbirth (Sep., Caul.), or multiple abortions ormiscarriages. Tendency
toprolapse and other malposition of the womb, from uterineatony. Uterine reflexes. Dropsy after uterine
hemorrhage.
Toxemia of pregnancy with great fatigue. Premenstrual syndrome with fatigue, swollen breasts, and
metrorrhagia. Suppressed menses. Congested kidneys, as if the monthly congestion, instead of venting itself
through the uterine vessels, had extended to the kidneys.
Bearing down pain, and chronic vaginal infections since childbirth. Sensation of weakness, dragging in the
sacrum and pelvis with great languor and prostration.
Tired backaches in females. Constant aching and tenderness over kidneys. Muscles, heavy, sore, aching,
burning. Sleepless, with a worn out feeling. Diabetes mellitus and insipidus. Anemia.
MIND - Extreme depression, gloom. Profound melancholia. May have a preliminary feeling of wellness
depression. Irritable, cannot endure the least contradiction. Finds faults with everyone. Conversation
unpleasant, desires to be left alone. Better when busy. Patient must be doing something to engage mind.
Consciousness of the womb.
Abdomen - Burning in the lower third of abdomen. Pain in left side, as if in spleen, which feels as if distended,
causing a dull ache. Colic-like pains in hypogastric region off and on all day. Motion and rumbling in abdomen,
as if diarrhea would come on, cramps in the stomach.
Back - Pain and weight in back, tired and weak. Aching and burning across the lumbar region, can trace
outlines of kidneys by constant burning. Boring pain in lumbar region, extending down legs. Aching
between scapulae. Weakness, weight and dragging down in sacrum, down to buttocks. Great languor, better
exercising.
Bladder - Frequent desire and urging. Involuntary discharge of urine after the bladder feels empty. Profuse
urine, clear, albuminous, saccharine, phosphatic. Strangury. Burning, scalding when urinating. Diabetes
mellitus and insipidus.
Breasts - Breasts swollen, nipples painful and tender, worse pressure of clothes.
Chest - Chest sensitive to the air. Aching, as if the front of chest had been compressed in a vice, as if
squeezed.
Constitutions - Suited to nervous, run-down females, easily fatigued by any work, who complain of a tired
backache, a tired feeling extending into the limbs. Some of this passes off after commencing to work.
Face - Pale, earthy. Sallow, having an expression of suffering.
Female - Conscious of womb. Uterus, weak. heavy, sore, tender, ulcerated or prolapsed or other
malpositions. Weight and soreness in womb. Dragging in sacral region with prolapse, especially after a
miscarriage. Backache after miscarriage (Kali-c.). Heavy dragging in pelvis. Menses too frequent, too
profuse. Menses, suppressed, kidneys congested. Foul, lumpy orcurdled leucorrhea. Albuminuria during
pregnancy. Debility attending menopause. Hemorrhage from atony of dark, foul blood. Pruritus vulvae. Parts
hot, red, swollen, bum and itch terribly. Vulva, aphthous inflamed. Loss of sexual desire and power with or
without sterility.
Food - Loss of appetite, food tasteless. Belchings, cramps. Fullness and painful congestion ofthe stomach.
Bilious, sleepy during the day.
Head - Burning sensation on top. Heat or upward pressure in vertex, as if skull were too full. Headache, better
mental exertion.
Heart - Palpitations.
Kidneys - Burning sensation at the kidneys. Constant aching, extreme tenderness of kidneys. Dull ache and
heat in region of the kidneys instead of menses. Nephritis of pregnancy with obstinate vomiting.
Limbs - Severe pains in right hip joint, worse during motion. Sore pain in outer side of thighs. Sensation as if
cool wind streamed up calves. Feet feel numb, when sitting.
Male - Sexual desire and power increased. Erections unusually strong and frequent. Impotence.
Modalities - Better if busy. Better from diversion. Better holding abdomen. Worse from fatigue. Worse
pregnancy. Worse stooping. Worse motion. Worse touch, pressure of clothes. Worse pressure on breasts,
nipples or kidneys.
Mouth - Salivation of pregnant women and teething children. Aphthae during pregnancy. Bitter taste in early
a.m.
 Rectum - Stool loose, yellow in the morning, lumps of feces in the evening.
Skin - Pale, earthy, sallow. Epidermis of the labia peels off thin, transparent
exfoliation.
Sleep - Drowsy, heavy. Sleepy during the day.
Stomach - Cramp-like pain in the stomach. Burning in stomach, belchings. Irritable stomach with general
dropsy.
Temperature - Feels hot when tired. Flushes of heat pass over him with every movement while in a room.
Chills, seemingly radiating from solar plexus all over body, caused by motion of arms.
COMMENTS - Alternate sensations of heat and cold. Burning sensations, particularly at the epigastrium.
Useful for menopausal temperature disturbances.
Irritation in mucous membranes, sore mouth, irritable stomach, burning and scalding when urinating, irritated
vaginal mucous membrane.
Backache in the lumbar region, over the kidneys or in the sacrum. Pains are worse on commencing to work,
better after working a little (Rhus-t.). Pain from the kidneys, especially the right. Generally scanty urine.
Marvin A. Custis reported a case. “Mrs. L, 28, has two children, both living. Has prolapse of uterus, ulceration
of cervix, dark offensive leucorrhea. Her system is worn out and her expression one of great distress.
“Irritable, finds fault with every one and cannot bear contradiction. Restless, wants to move around, as she
feels better when mind and body are employed.
“She had a severe backache and a sore and heavy feeling in the womb, she said she was always ‘conscious
of her womb.'
“Helon. 30c every three hours for two days, and then every night, was prescribed with a warm water injection
night and morning. At the end of three weeks the leucorrhea had almost ceased, the womb was in the first
position and she ‘forgets that she has such an organ.'”
L. L. Danforth treated Mrs. W., who had intense pruritus, vulvar and vaginal, for several weeks. “She could
tear the flesh out” it was so intense. There was vulvovaginitis, the labia and adjoining skin were red, swollen
and covered with thin, white, curdy deposits.
Further examination showed a thin, albuminous leucorrhea pouring from a congested cervix, evidently the
cause of the pruritus. The leucorrhea coagulated on the vagina, forming small curds covering the mucous
membrane of vagina and vulva. Helon. tincture on tablets speedily relieved.
S. A. Jones found that Helon. turned an alkaline urine acid, and increased the amount of urea as well as the
amount of urine secreted. Jones considered this the result of a condition of debility, venous paresis, the result
of previous arterial tonic contraction.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Alet., Lil-t, Puls., Senec., Stann. (2) Agri. - painful kidneys, indigestion and
menstrual difficulties, bron- chorrhea and catarrh of bladder. Cough with profuse expectoration attended with
expulsion of urine. Tincture 1 to 10 drops.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Hepar Sulphuris Calcareum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - hep. Hepar sulphuris calcareum. Calcium sulphide. Calcarea sulphurata Hahnemanni. An
impure Sulphide of Calcium prepared by burning in a crucible the white interior of oyster shells with pure
flowers of sulphur. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Amaurosis. Angina, pectoris. Asthma. Axilla, abscess. Beard, eruptions. Blepharitis.
Bo/iv. Breast, disorders. Bronchitis. Bubo. Bums. Carbuncle. Decay. Chilblains. Chlorosis. Colds.
Constipation. Cornea, ulceration. Cornea, opacity. Coughs. Croup. Diaphragmitis. Diarrhea. Ear, infections.
Ears, polyps. Eczema. Emphysema. Erysipelas. Eyes, disorders. Glandular, swellings. Headaches. Hectic,
fever. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Hip joint disease. Hoarseness. Jaundice. Joints, disorders.
Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Lips, swollen. Liver, disorders. Lungs, disorders. Lupus. Marasmus. Menorrhagia.
Mouth, sore. Nipples, sore. Ovaries, disorders. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Pylorus, disorders. Quinsy. Rheumatism.
Scarlatina. Scrofula. Skin, disorders. Spinal, irritation. Syphilis.
Styes. Suppuration. Syphilis. Tenesmus. Throat, sore. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Urticaria. Wens. Whitlow.
Whooping, cough
HOMEOPATHIC - “Liver of Sulphur" is a name given by the old alchemists to several sulphur compounds
whose color was supposed to resemble that of the liver. Before Hahnemann's time, Hep., Sulfuret of lime, was
used as an external remedy for itch, rheumatism, gout, goiter and scrofulous swellings.
Hahnemann prepared Hep. with oyster shells instead of ordinary lime. As it is a chemical combination of Calc,
and Sulph., it has some of the properties of both, but is very different from either and though it is useful to
 compare them. Hep. must be studied as a separate entity.
Material doses were used in pellagra. The higher potencies may abort the suppuration, the lower promote it.
If it is necessary to hasten it, give 2x. Hep.; lx will often start secretions and profuse drainage in stuffy colds.
In 1794, Hahnemann proposed to use it internally to arrest mercurial salivation. A few years later it was tried
for asthma and pulmonary tuberculosis, with success.
It acts on the mucous membranes, causing croupy, catarrhal process with a tendency to hemorrhage and
ulceration. Tendency to suppuration. Lesions spread by the formation of small papules around the side of
the old lesions.
The catarrh may be in the throat, stomach, uterus, or urethra, and is characterized by thick, yellow, acrid,
ropy discharge. Mucus in the stools, the urine, and is hawked up. Easy perspiration with mucus. Infected
sinus with pus formation.
Great sensitiveness to all impressions. Hypersensitiveness. Chilliness. Sweating, but desire to pull blanket
around him. Feeling as if wind were blowing on some part. Splinter-like pains. The side of the body on
which he lies at night becomes gradually insufferably painful, he must turn. Craving for sour and strong things.
Syphilis after gross medication. For the abuse of mercury.
MIND - Mental dullness. Forgetful. Weak memory. Depression. Dejected and sad. Remorse. Bitter crying.
Dissatisfaction with one's self and others. Anguish in the evening and night with thoughts of suicide.
Delicate, oversensitive to impressions, people and places. Hypersensitive. Hasty speech and hasty drinking.
Restlessness, desires a constant change. Hurried. Child does not laugh, and is not inclined to play or to amuse
itself in any way. Children who lose their tempers and hit, kick and scream (Cham., Cina.).
Quarrelsome. Extreme irritability, peevishness. Abusive and vehement. Ferocious. Slightest upset
irritates him. Everybody disturbs him. Bad tempered. Angry because of pain, at the least trifle. Impulsive.
Impulse to do violence and to destroy, to start fires. Impulse to kill, to stab with a knife, especially if annoyed.
Insanity and mania.
Abdomen - Distended, tense, chronic abdominal disorders. Pain in the groins as if sprained. Atrophy, cancer
of liver.
Baek - Neuralgia of neck. Dull, dragging, heavy pain across lumbar region, uses arms to raise himself from a
seat.
Breasts - Pain in right breast on sneezing. Breasts cancer. Retracted, sore nipples, cracked in nursing women.
Causations - Cold, dry winds. Injuries. Suppressed eruptions. Abuse of mercury.
Chest - Constriction and tightness, oppression. Anxiety and heat in chest. Burning, sharp, sore, pressing pains,
worse motion. Weakness of the chest, preventing talking. Pleuritis. Empyema. Angina pectoris. Inflammation
of diaphragm. Axilla abscessed, offensive perspiration. Boils, eczema, herpes, pimples.
Constitutions - Slow, torpid constitutions with lax tissue and light hair, great sensitiveness to slightest contact
of ulcers, eruptions and affected parts. Suited to the psoric. scrofulous, diathesis. Debilitated subjects.
Tendency to suppurations. Cross children. Torpid, lymphatic constitutions, persons with light hair and
complexion, slow to act, muscles soft and flabby.
Cough - Loose cough, bloody or thick, yellow, tenacious sputum, raises much mucus. Cough from exposure
to cold, especially to dry, cold air, west or northwest winds. Dry, hoarse, rattling cough. Croupy, choking
cough. Croup with loose, rattling cough, worse in morning. Suffocative attacks, has to rise up and bend head
backwards. Cough worse whenever any part of the body gets cold or uncovered or from eating anything
cold. Loses voice and coughs when exposed to dry. cold wind. Cough troublesome when walking. Cough
ameliorated by wrapping up, keeping warm.
Ears - Otitis media, painful (Cham.). Ears are sensitive to touch, wind. Discharge of fetid pus from the
ears. Pustules in auditory canal and auricle. Scurfs on and behind the ears. Mastoiditis. Whizzing and throbbing
in ears with hardness of hearing. Roaring. Deafness from Eustachian catarrh after scarlet fever.
Eyes - Purulent conjunctivitis with chemosis, profuse discharge, great sensitiveness to touch and air. Iritis with
pus in anterior chamber. Ophthalmia, thick mucous discharge. Corneal ulcers. Eyes and lids red and inflamed.
Pain in the eyes, as if pulled back into the head. Boring pain in upper bones of the orbits. Eyeballs sore to
touch. Hypopion. Yellow. Photophobia. Vision obscured by reading, field reduced one- half. Bright circles
before eyes. Objects appear red and too large.
Face - Yellowish, sunken complexion. Vesicular erysipelas with pricking in parts. Cancer on lips. Middle of
lower lip cracked. Ulcers in corners of mouth. Shooting in jaw on opening mouth. Neuralgia of right side,
extending in streak into temple, ear, ale and lip. Pains in bones of face, especially when being touched.
Female - Menorrhagia and metrorrhagia with fibroids. Menses late and scanty. Pruritus vul vae with profuse
leucorrhea with sexual excitement. Thick, acrid, yellow, ropy leucorrhea. Leucorrhea smells like old cheese
(Sanie.). Vagina sore during sex, bleeding after. Itching of pudenda and nipples, worse during menses.
 Abscesses
of labia with great sensitiveness. Profuse perspiration at the menopause (Til., Jab.). Erosion of cervix.
Removes the tendency to habitual adherent placenta. Hot, watery, discharge from uterus.
Food - Desire for acids, pickles, vinegar, sour food. Desires wine, fruit, spicy and strong-tasting food, warm
drinks. Better from spicy foods. Aversion to fat food, butter, cheese, which aggravate. Worse from alcohol,
brandy, whiskey, tea, sweets, cold food, drinks and ice.
Head - Boring pain in the right temple and in root of nose every morning. Eczema on forehead along the line
of hair, worse after washing. Scalp sensitive and sore. Humid scald-head itching and burning. Cold sweat on
head.
Heart - Anxiety in heart. Enlarged heart. Murmurs. Violent palpitations, with anxiety, worse after fright, eating.
Palpitations from a slowly progressing weakness. Palpitations in the morning on waking. Angina pectoris.
Stenocardia. Pericarditis. Gouty heart.
Kidneys - Bladder difficulties of elderly men (Phos., Sulph., Cop.). Voided slowly without force, drops vertically,
weak bladder. Seems as if some urine always remained. Mucus, greasy pellicle on urine. Gleety discharge,
thick, yellow. Putrid odor of urine.
Limbs - Finger joints swollen, tendency to easy dislocation. Nail of great toe painful on slight pressure.
Liver - Jaundice. Hepatitis, hepatic abscess. Stitching in region of liver when walking, coughing, breathing or
touching it (Bry., Merc.). Cutting pain from liver to right scapula worse lying on back or right side.
Lungs - Bronchiectasis. Bronchitis of elderly, exhausted people. Emphysema. Pleuritis. Breathing difficult
worse lying on left side. Anxious, wheezing, moist breathing. Asthma worse in dry cold air, better in damp.
Pneumonia in suppurative stage with fever. Lobar pneumonia. Chronic pneumonia, with profuse purulent
expectoration. Empyema. Sputum varies from scanty to tenacious mucopurulent.
Hepar sulphuris calcareum First stage of pulmonary tuberculosis. Sputum pus-like, bloody tuberculous
masses, or small balls, when crushed, emit a carrion-like odor. Paralysis of lungs.
Male - Obstinate gonorrhea “does not get well.” Herpes, sensitive, bleed easily. Figwarts of offensive odor.
Ulcers externally on prepuce similar to chancre (Nit-ac.). Suppurating inguinal glands. Humid soreness on
genitals and between scrotum and thigh. Itching of glans, frenum and scrotum. Excitement and emission
without amorous fancies.
Modalities - Better in damp weather. Better warmth, wrapping head up. Better pressure, after eating. Worse
inhaling air. Worse cold air. dry winds. Worse slightest draft. Worse open air. Worse single parts of the body
getting cold. Worse from touch. Worse motion. Worse washing. Worse slight bleeding. Worse blowing the
nose. Worse on waking. Worse at night.
Mouth - Tongue, white, yellow, dirty, swollen, large, tabby, slimy, with imprints of teeth, feels as if scalded.
Bitter taste. Aphthae. Ptyalism. Gums and mouth painful to touch and bleed readily. Bleeding painful cancerous
growth on hard palate. Stomatitis of nursing mothers or weakly children.
Nose - Hay fever. Sinusitis after coryza. Sneezes every time he goes into a cold, dry wind with running from
nose, later, thick offensive discharge. Stopped up every time he goes out into cold air. Ozaena. Offensive
discharge, smells like old cheese. Post nasal dripping. Sore, bleeds, bloody crusts. Soreness of nostrils with
catarrhal troubles. Air feels cold in nose.
Perspiration - Clammy, cold sweat. Constant offensive exhalation from the body. Offensive sweats. Sour,
fetid, cheesy odors. Profuse sweat, sour, sticky, offensive, debilitating. Sweats day and night without relief,
better from warmth, covers, worse from eating, exertion, uncovering. Night-sweats with tuberculosis. Perspira-
tion with menopause
Rectum - Loss of power to expel even a soft stool. Clay-colored, soft, sour, white, undigested, fetid stools.
Lumpy stools, coated or mixed with mucus. Raw smarting in the rectum during stools, remaining long
afterwards. Obstinate constipation of pregnancy, after purgatives. Hemorrhoids, even slight bleeding exhausts.
Skin - Unhealthy skin, every little injury suppurates (Psor., Sil.). Boils and abscesses. Suppurating
glands. Chronic and recurring urticaria. Ulcers very sensitive to contact, burning, stinging, easily
bleeding. Cancerous ulcers. Atonic ulcers, following removal of tumors. Putrid ulcers, surrounded by little
pimples. Ulcers with bloody suppuration, smelling like old cheese. Papules, pimples prone to suppurate and
extend. Acne in youth, suppurate with prickly pain, bleeds easily. Cold-sores, very sensitive. Ringworm.
Smallpox. Chapped skin with deep cracks on hands andfeet. Great sensitiveness to slightest touch. Cannot
bear to be uncovered, wants to be wrapped up warmly. Sticking or pricking in afflicted parts. Angio-neurotic
edema.
Stomach - Stomach ulcers and cancer. Painful epigastric tumors with pulsations. Distention of stomach,
compelling one to loosen the clothing. Burning in stomach. Heaviness and pressure in stomach after a slight
meal. Gone feeling in stomach with loathing of food or as of a sharp lump in stomach. Weak digestion. Frequent
 belch- ings without taste or smell. Apt to vomit all food, retaining only milk or water, mixed. Cannot eat bread
or vegetables.
Temperature - Chilly in open air. Chilly from slightest draft. Chills and shi verings. Heat alternating with chill.
Hectic fever. Dry, burning heat at night. Intermittent fever. Malaria. Typhoid, yellow fever. Catarrhal fever.
Eruptive fever, measles, smallpox. Fever with teething.
Throat - Follicular pharyngitis. Hawks up yellow tenacious mucus. Quinsy with impending suppuration.
Stitches in throat extending to the ear when swallowing. When swallowing, sensation as if a plug. Sensation
of a splinter in throat. Hoarse-
Hepar sulphuris calcareum ness with loss of voice.
Vertigo - Vertigo, with headache, nausea, with a tendency to fall. Vertigo in mornings. Worse on rising, when
shaking the head, from motion.
COMMENTS - Guernsey noted the effects on the skin and touch, “any trouble occurring on the skin where
there is a great sensitiveness to the slightest touch, patient can't bear to have even the clothes touch the part
or have it touched in any way. Exanthema like nettle rash, sore to the slightest touch. Skin hard to heal,
inflammation, sensitive soreness of skin.”
Teste added that the sensitiveness is not confined to touch. There is excessive sensitiveness to the air, patient
can't bear the least draft and if a hand accidentally gets outside the bedclothes it brings on an aggravation.
Characteristic over-sensitiveness. Sensitivity to touch, to pain, can suffer intensely (Cham.). The slightest pain
causes fainting. Sensitive to the stimulation of light, noise and odors. Desires constant change, can't adjust to
find comfort.
Very chilly, particularly when sick. Very sensitive to drafts, even uncovering a hand or foot can bring on a
coughing spasm (Rumx., Rhus-t.). Worse from air conditioning, better warmth and heat. Sensitiveness to cold,
dry air (Aeon., Bry.).
Restlessness and anxiety (Ars.). Anxious about pain (Ign. ), and worse pain, can overreact and become
hysterical or violent (Nux-v., Cham.). Frenzy because of pain, impulsive. Very irritable, abusive. Can have an
impulse to kill or throw someone in a fire or out the window. Can have a desire to set fires, desire to kill her
child. Swears and curses, fears they may do something violent.
Painful, inflamed sores and wounds, slow to heal. Painful, hypersensitive boils (Bell., Tarent.), with sticking
pains. Tendency to boils, painful eruptions, ulcers, abscesses and pus. Suppuration, inflammation and severe
pain from foreign bodies under the skin or in eye (Sil.).
Sensation of foreign body under the skin or in the eye. Abscesses anywhere in the body, with sensitivity.
Throbbing, stabbing
pains, splinter-like sensations. Splinters under the nail that abscess (Sil., Myris.). Sticking pains in the nails.
Itching, particularly in affects the bends of the elbows and popliteal spaces. Itching in connection with jaundice.
Pruritus, especially when of mercurial origin. Inflammations, especially of respiratory organs, bowels and
kidneys and the skin.
Colds and flus from exposure to drafts or cold dry winds (Kali-c.). Chronic sinusitis or bronchitis from exposure
to cold winds, drafts or cold dry weather. Sinusitis with yellow, thick discharge (Puls.) with irritability. Coryza,
nose swollen and sore to the touch, especially inside the ale. Boring at root of nose with catarrhal symptoms
or headaches. Suffocative attacks in the respiratory organs. Asthma.
Whooping cough. Croup that's worse from dry cold (Aeon., Spong.). Yellow discharge. Dry, painful, hacking
cough, as though a feather were in the throat. Loose cough with wheezing and rattling, as if mucus would
come up but it does not. Choking cough. Cough, worse drafts, more often in the early morning (Aeon, in
evening).
Inflammation of the throat. Painful, swollen tonsils. Abscessed tonsillitis. Discharge from the tonsils. Quinsy,
with throbbing pains, where suppuration is imminent (Calc-s. after it breaks). Sore throats with pain on
swallowing, as though a splinter or fish bone were caught in the throat. Sticking pains. Hoarseness.
Earaches in children, with night sweats that don't relieve (Merc.). Tearing and pressure as though it would
burst. Pus. Side of face is sensitive, hypersensitive to noise. Sensitive to the least touch or draft (Caust.).
Abscess in the ear with bloody, yellow, or pus-like discharge from the ear. Ear canal is very painful. Sticking
pains in the ears. Eye disorders, likes to have eyes tightly covered.
Toothaches, especially if there is an abscess or boil. Very irritable because of the sharp, dental pain. Food or
drink aggravates. Drinking water goes to the bone. Desires acids and sour things.
Semi-paralytic condition of the rectum and bladder (Alum.). Stools are passed with great difficulty even when
clay-like and soft. Diarrhea with sour stools. Fetid stools with a sour body smell in children.
Impeded urination, obliged to wait before urine passes, then flows slowly for many days. Never able to finish
urinating, seems as if some always remains in bladder. Urine drops vertically down. Acrid urine. Complaints
 during urination and after.
Nocturnal emissions. Escape of prostatic fluid at any time and at stool. Affections of the sexual organs
occurring on the right side. Vaginitis with thick, cheesy, fetid discharge. with a bad odor like rotten cheese
(Kali-p., Kreos.).
Anti-psoric. Marked periodicity, every day, every fourweeks (attack ofparalysis). Every four months (scabby
eruptions on head). Whitlows every winter. Bilious attacks in the spring and autumn.
In Hahnemann's article, “Medicine of Experience,” he speaks of the itch-like eruptions caused by Hep. and its
corrective properties in wool-workers' itch.
Guernsey noted that there is respiration with mucous rattle, expiration in the morning, none in the evening,
cough with expectoration during the day, none in the night (in croup no expectoration at night but only in the
daytime with the suffocative coughing spells, low, weak voice).
P. Foster distinguished between Hep., Calc-s. and Kali-s. in their action on tissues. Kali-s. acts on the
epidermis, Hep. on lymphatic glandular system, skin and respiratory mucous membrane, Calc-s. acts much
as Hep., only more deeply. Hep. acts on abscesses before they open, Calc-s. after.
Foster cured a woman with Calc-s. of “several large ulcers in the gluteal region 3 inches in diameter and 3/4
inches deep, exposing the bone.” The pain ceased immediately and the cure was completed in two months.
The relation of Hepar to the suppuration process is very marked. It meets the hectic condition generally and
the process locally.
Clarke once cured with Hep. 6c a case of axillary abscess with a large collection of pus. The whole was
absorbed without breaking.
A case of pustular ophthalmia of the left eye was cured after Sulph. and Calc, had failed. It was better keeping
the eye closely covered with some soft fabric, worse mornings, better as the day advanced. Pimples
surrounded affected eye.
In a case of eczema pudendi in a young girl, 11, three months after puberty, the parts red and itching, Merc,
was given and the whole body became covered with the rash. Hep. was then given and removed all symptoms
immediately. “Sweats day and night without relief.”
It antidotes the sensitiveness of Merc, to atmospheric conditions. In the old days of mercurialization, one of
the chief things to be avoided by a patient under the “course” was exposure to chill.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Acet-ac., Bell., Cham., S'ñ. It antidotes: Metals and especially mercurial
preparations, Nit-ac., Calc., lod., Kali-i. Compare: (1) Croup - Aeon., Spong. (2) Sil., Calc-s., Calen., Sulph.,
Staph., Myris. (3) Hep. antidotes bad effects from mercury, iodine, potassium, (4) Cod-liver oil removes the
weakening effects of ether. Compatible with: Aeon., Am., Bell., Lach., Merc., Nit-ac., Sil., Spon., Zinc.
Complementary to: Calen, in injuries.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
