name: Jaborandi
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jab. Jaborandi. Pilocarpus jaborandi. Pilocarpus pennatifolius aut mi- crophyllus. The alkaloid
is pilocarpine. N. O. Rutaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves. Tincture of dried leaves and stems. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies, third potency.
CLINICAL - Alopecia. Asthenopia. Baldness. Bronchitis. Burns. Cataract. Ciliary, spasm. Diarrhea.
Dysmenorrhea. Erysipelas. Exophthalmic, goiter. Eye. disorders, Eye, surgery. Eye-strain. Gland,
disorders. Glaucoma. Hair, loss. Heart, disorders. Hot, flushings. Hypermetropia. Leucorrhea. Menopause.
Miliaria. Mumps. Nightsweats. Perspiration, excessive. Pregnancy, salivation. Salivation, excessive.
Scalds. Snakebites. Strabismus. Tuberculosis. Worms.
HERBAL-Jaborandi is a South American tree growing up to twenty feet high. It is used by South American
natives as an antidote to snakebites of the Trigonocephalus group.
HOMEOPATHIC - A few minutes after a dose of Jab., the face, ears and neck become deeply flushed and
drops of perspiration break out all over the body, the mouth waters and saliva pours out in an almost continuous
stream.
A single dose often produces enormous amounts of sweat and saliva, not infrequently half a pint. The
observation of its action on the skin and salivary glands led to extensive provings.
A powerful glandular stimulant, it produces hypersecretion from upper respiratory tract and salivary glands.
Increases lachrymal, nasal, bronchial and intestinal secretions to a lesser degree.
Abnormal sweats, perspiration, salivation . Heavy night sweats, hot flushes. Night sweats of tuberculosis
patients. Sweat only on the left side, dry on the right. Drawing pain in joints during perspiration.
 Exophthalmic goiter with increased heart’s action and pulsation of arteries, tremors and nervousness, heat
and sweating, bronchial irritation. Acts upon the thyroid and its sudorific action may be due to it.
Limits the duration of mumps. Mumps when metastasized to the testes, causing infertility, metastasized to
the breasts. Never well since mumps (Morbill., Parot.).
Pronounced action in the eyes, it has been found to be useful in many conditions of eye weakness, especially
hypermetropia, ciliary spasm, convergent strabismus and after operations for strabismus. Mydriatic properties.
Miosis. Glaucoma.
Headaches, more on the left side. Headaches worse at noon every day. Pains appear gradually and disappear
gradually. Symptoms are generally more on the left.
Kidney disease, especially with uremia, eliminating both water and urea. Nausea. Stomach distress, better
from eating. Scarlatinal dropsy. Contra-indicated in heart failure, in post-puerperal uremia, and in senile cases.
MIND - Mental confusion. Dullness of mind. Cheerfulness, gaiety. Very nervous and tremulous. Disinclination
to speak. Desire to kill loved ones. Fixed idea that she will murder all her family with a hatchet.
Abdomen - Empty, gone feeling. Cutting in lower abdomen. Severe pains over pubes with strong desire to
pass water, which relieved. Ailments of the pancreas.
Breasts - Milk absent or deficient. Milk increased, too profuse.
Chest - Sticking in chest. Pain in chest and around heart. Pressure on chest with anxiety, palpitation and pain
in region of heart. Anxiety in chest with oppression, preventing sleep.
Ears - Serous exudation into tympanic cavity. Tinnitus. Nervous deafness, better in noise. Noises and vertigo.
Eyes - Tension in eyes. Pupils contracted, do not react to light. Glaucoma. Atrophic choroiditis. Vitreous
opacities. Eyestrain from whatever cause (Ruta.). Eye pain from exertion of vision atfine work. Eyes easily
tire from slightest use. Sensation of heat and burning in eyes during exertion.
Smarting pain in eyes. Lachrymation during coryza, headache. Irritation from electric or other artificial light.
Staring eyes. Irritability of the ciliary muscle. Periodic strabismus. Spasms of the accommodation while
reading. Near-sighted. Hyperopia. Exophthalmos, protrusion of eyes. Squints, convergent after surgery. Lids
twitch.
Face - Redness of face and of ears. Pallor with heat of face and throbbing of temporal arteries. Mumps,
especially when metastasis to the testes. Inflammation of parotid gland.
Female - Menses, start with coldness, throbbing in head and pelvis, and backache. Menses scanty, congested
head, dry skin. Leucorrhea. Edema of pregnancy. Puerperal convulsions in a stupor, threatened suffocation
from inability to swallow excessive quantity of saliva. Heat and dryness of vagina during labor. Labor pains
ceasing or sluggish. Flushing at menopause.
Food - Good appetite. Hunger disappeared and he could not eat. Urgent thirst.
Head - Empty, hollow sensation in head. Headache every day about noon. Headache from straining eyes.
Headache with smarting and pain in eyeballs. Pulsating in temporal vessels, at vertex. Throbbing pain in vertex
and front of head. Pain in lower part of occiput. Light hair turns black. Baldness.
Heart - Pain in heart region. Oppression of chest. Nervous cardiac disorders. Violent ebullitions to heart and
chest. Palpitations, during perspiration. Pulse is irregular, dicrotic. Irregularity, weakness and rapidity of action.
Cyanosis, collapse.
Kidneys - Scanty, pain overpubes with much urging. Burning in urethra with urging to urinate. Urine dark.
Urine increased during the sweat.
Lungs - Edema of lungs. Breathing difficult, hurried. Slow, sighing respiration. Bronchial mucus membrane
inflamed. Loose cough. Much inclination to cough and difficult breathing. Frothy or profuse, thin, serous
expectoration.
Male - Orchitis from metastasis of mumps. Orchitis with incipient bronchial trouble.
Modalities - Worse left side, exertion of eyes, exhaustion, start of menses, cold. Nausea worse motion of
eyes.
Mouth - Tension in salivary glands. Profuse salivation with profuse sweating, with dry skin. Saliva viscid
like egg white, or stringy but not viscid. Constant spitting of alkaline saliva. Saliva contained a notable quantity
of urea. Salivation during pregnancy. Dryness of mouth.
Nose - Copious nasal discharge. Coryza and perspiration (Merc.).
Perspiration - Excessive perspiration from all parts of the body. Sweat on forehead, then over whole
body, then chiefly on face, legs and feet. Sweat breaks out on the face and upper part of the chest. Sweats
with palpitations, general pulsations and tremors. Copious sweating with chilliness, with salivation, with
diarrhea (Verat.). Nervous sweats. Semi-lateral or unilateral sweat. Night-sweats. Perspiration in bed. Hot
flushes and sweats. Perspiration during menopause. Sweat contains urea. Perspired easily before taking,
but did not sweat during the proving.
 Rectum - Constipation. Hard stools. Diarrhea with flushed face and profuse perspiration. Diarrhea during
daytime. Stools are watery, yellow. Frequent, undigested, gushing, weakening, papescent, and large and
painless stools. Passage of threadworms.
Skin - Redness of skin. Persistent dryness of skin. Dry eczema.
Sleep - Sleepiness. Profound sleep in daytime. Fell asleep while sitting reading. Night-sweats. Perspiration
in bed. Did not sleep well on account of restlessness, with pressure on chest and hurried breathing. Distressing
dreams towards morning. Dreams of accidents and fights, waking him twice a night.
Stomach - Thirst in morning on waking. Hiccough, before vomiting. Nausea, sudden and retching often with
hiccough Vomiting after supper. Nausea worse motion of eyes. Nausea on looking at objects
moving, vomiting, pressure and pain in stomach. Stubborn vomiting of pregnancy. Nausea during menopause.
Temperature - Chilly up and down back at 7 p.m. Shivering. Chilliness with sweat. Cold limbs. Heat flushes,
at menopause, with profuse sweat, nausea and vomiting.
Throat - Exophthalmic goiter with increased heart's action, pulsation in arteries, tremors and nervousness.
Swelling of submaxillary glands (Merc., Calc.). Dryness at back of throat. Soreness and smarting of throat.
Vertigo - Headache with vertigo. Vertigo with nausea after exertion of vision. Vertigo as if head were too light,
on moving or looking at objects.
Vision - White spots before eyes. Everything at a distance appears hazy. Vision becomes indistinct every
few moments. Focal distance changes while reading. Dim vision, better looking sideways (Chin-s.). Retinal
images retained long after using eyes.
COMMENTS - Sandesberg noticed that the internal use of Jab. and pilocarpine in cases of detached retina
and choroiditis seemed to occasion opacity of the crystalline lens. He treated a horse for iridochoroiditis and
large opacities of the vitreous with infusion of Jab. leaves and injections of Pilo. The disease was quickly
arrested, the vitreous cleared up completely, but during the first week the crystalline lens became opaque.
Jab. has been used as a remedy for baldness and it forms the principal ingredient in some of the popular hair
restorer tonics. In a number of patients taking it, white hair and blonde hair have been observed to turn black.
Jab. has a reputation for stimulating breast secretions. A case is quoted from the Lancet in which a woman
whose milk had ceased for a fortnight received ten drops of the fluid extract every four hours. The secretion of
milk was re-established, but the patient began to suffer from extreme nervous excitement accompanied by a
fixed idea that she should murder her family with a hatchet.
The drug was stopped and these symptoms disappeared, and with them, the activity of the breast glands.
Bell commended it in diarrhea with gushing. painless stools, flushed face, profuse salivation and sweat, and
intense thirst with dark urine that is scanty or profuse.
Cooper saw Jab. cause violent leucorrhea as well as a discharge of threadworms. He noted its use in relieving
“a feeling of coldness and faintness and neuralgic throbbings in head and pelvis with a backache” when the
period begins. He suggested treating with a drop or two of Jab. in hot water.
The Hom. News, February, 1900, quoted an incidental cure of dysmenorrhea in a woman, age 23, who
received five-drop does of Jab. for increased eye-tension which rapidly disappeared. The patient noticed that
she passed the next menstrual period without pain though she usually had to spend two to four days in bed.
The drug was continued in smaller doses and the improvement was maintained.
Hale commended its use in women or young girls who always have dry skin, scanty menses and a tendency
of blood to the head.
Duncan aborted erysipelas by painting the tincture on the part four to five times daily. A sharp smarting is the
first effect, followed by a more agreeable, soothing sensation. For burns, scalds and some forms of eczema
and psoriasis.
One patient, after having been injected with pilocarpine, complained of great sensitiveness to cold, constantly
taking cold and bronchitis, the skin became irritable.
Dudgeon recorded a case of a man, 45, who rose at an early hour and went to the other side of his bedroom
to get a dose of Nux-v. 3c for some fancied derangement of his stomach. On coming back to bed he was
seized with a sudden, violent, crimson flushing of the face followed almost immediately by profuse perspiration,
beginning in the face and head and extending all over the body.
This was followed by extreme coldness of the limbs and sickness terminating in the vomiting of sour mucus.
The attacks recurred every quarter of an hour throughout the day. Not only was he unable to get out of bed,
he could not raise himself up in bed or lie otherwise than on his right side without the most distressing giddiness
and a feeling “as if he should die.” Pulse 60, regular and strong, temperature below normal.
Ten drops of Jab. 1c were mixed in half a tumbler of water and a dessert spoonful given immediately and
repeated every half hour. After the second dose the attacks ceased and he was able to take bread and milk
without sickness. He had a good night's rest and was perfectly well the next day.
 RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Amyl-n., At- rop., Phys., Lyc, Ruta. (2) Piloc. - Meniere's disease, rapidly
progressive tuberculosis with free hemorrhages, profuse sweating, 2x trituration. (3) Atropine is the antagonist
to pilocarpine in dose of one one-hundredth grain for one-sixth of pilocarpine.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-

name: Jacaranda Caroba
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-jac-c. Jacarandacaroba. Brazilian caroba tree. Caroba tree. Jacaranda procera. Bignonia
caroba. Jacaranda Brasiliensis. N. O. Bignoniaceae. Jacarandae. Tincture of fresh flowers. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anal, itching. Balanorrhea. Chancre. Chordee. Coryza. Gonorrhea. Morning sickness. Muscular,
rheumatism. Phimosis. Rheumatism. Syphilis.
HERBAL - “There are several species of Jacaranda,” especially Jacaranda procera, “that have the reputation
of being curative in syphilis” notes the Treasury of Botany. Mure proved Jacaranda caroba, and the symptoms
of the proving certainly confirmed this.
HOMEOPATHIC - Jac-c. has a reputation in venereal diseases and rheumatism. The urinary and sexual
symptoms are important.
Rheumatic symptoms, pains in the limbs. Lancinations in the heart. Morning sickness. Itching at anus.
Hering confirmed symptoms including tearing pains affected the whole organism when urine contacts a
chancre. Prepuce much swollen, could not be drawn over glans, on attempting to do so, copious discharge of
yellowish green pus. Chordee in gonorrhea. Dull pain under sternum on raising head and drawing breath.
Abdomen - Painful stitch in the right and left side of navel. Acute pain at the hypo- gastrium when pressing
upon it. Swelling of the right groin, painful to touch.
Back - Pain in nape. Neck so painful that the head cannot be turned to right. Stiffness in loins.
Chest - Dull pain under the sternum on raising head and drawing breath. Prickling under the sternum.
Ears - Flapping in the ears, as of wings. Stoppage and heat in the left ear, with burning, digging pain extending
to the left nostril.
Eyes - Eyes pain, are inflamed and watery.
Food - Food tastes insipid, nausea while eating.
Head - Fullness in the head. Pain, as if a plug were pressing on the right side of the forehead. Dull pain
between the forehead and right temple. Coryza with heavy head.
Heart - Sensation as if the heartbeat was in the pit of the stomach. Sharp pain in region of heart. Painful stitch
at the heart, extending to the right side. Stitch at the heart, which seems to beat slowly.
Kidneys - Urethra inflamed, discharge of yellow matter.
Limbs - Morning soreness and stiffness of muscles. Weakness of lumbar region. Gonorrheal rheumatism.
Gonorrheal and syphilitic arthritis. Rheumatic pain in right knee. Itching pimples on hands.
Male - Heat and pain in penis. Painful erections. Chordee. Itching pimples on glans and prepuce. Discharge
of yellowish white liquid from the prepuce. Prepuce painful and swollen. The prepuce cannot be drawn
back. Phimosis. Suppuration between the glans and prepuce. Acute pain in the left testicle when walking. Heat
and swelling of the scrotum. Syphilis. Chancroid.
Mouth - Dry mouth in the morning in bed. Mouth dry and clammy. Raw pain at the left side of tongue. Food
tastes flat or acid.
Nose - Sneezing and fluent coryza. Coryza, with heaviness and weariness at the vertex, forehead, and eyes.
Rectum - Constipation. Acute pain with lancinations in the anus. Prickling around the anus. Itching at the anus
while sitting. Excrescence at the anus.
Sleep - Restless sleep with frightful dreams.
Stomach - Fullness at the pit of the stomach, with hurried breathing. Pressure at the pit of the stomach. Painful
stitch between the pit of the stomach and the umbilicus. Nausea when eating.
Temperature - Internal chill. Dry, prickling heat all over.
Throat - Sore and dry. Vesicles in pharynx. Sore throat with constrictions of the pharynx and difficult
swallowing. Constrictive sensation at the throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising with heavy forehead.
COMMENTS - Mahony confirmed symptoms including “Food tastes insipid, nausea during eating.” Motion
aggravates. Symptoms come on when walking, raising head, sitting.
J. S. Whittinghill cured several cases of muscular rheumatism characterized by a peculiar soreness and
stiffness of muscles in the morning.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Thuj. - gonorrhea, rheumatism. (2) Cor-r. - red and sensitive chancre and
 chancroids. (3) Jac-g.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Jacaranda Gualandai
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jac. Jacaranda gualandai. N. O. Bignoniaceae. The driedleaves are crushed and macerated in
five parts by weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Ophthalmia. Rheumatism. Syphilis. Ulcers. Vertigo.
HERBAL - Dr. J. S, Whittinghill contributed the following from the Eclectic Medical Journal concerning
Jacaranda: “Of this South American remedy the Dispensatory says it is used in Brazil and other South
American countries for syphilis, sometimes under the name Carroba.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Jac. has syphilitic symptoms, especially of the eyes and throat. Chancroids. Atonic ulcers.
Dark, painless diarrhea. Weakness of memory and inability to study.
Back - Weakness of the lumbar region.
Eyes - Pains and inflammation of the eye with redness, more marked in the left eye. Sensation of sand in the
eyes. Ophthalmia, which begins in the left eye with lachrymation and night agglutination of the eyelids.
Syphilitic-like ophthalmia. Weakness of sight.
Male - Pain in the penis. Increased secretion of urine. Gonorrhea with a discharge which stains the linen a
dirty yellow color. Chancroids.
Rectum - Diarrhea with dark mulberrycolored stools without pain or tenesmus, but with mucus.
Throat - Pain and burning of the larynx, when laughing or reading aloud. Small vesicles in the pharynx.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising after stooping, with momentary loss of sight and sensation of heaviness in the
forehead.
COMMENTS - Dr. J. F. Con vers, of Bogotá, found Jac. to be useful in certain kinds of rheumatism. He noted
the case of one patient who suffered from rheumatism for about 10 years, and never became serious.
Sometimes she was nearly relieved from it. She lost a good deal of sleep due to it.
Her wrist would become painful and very weak from ordinary labor. She complained of being stiff and had pain
from any motion, particularly in the morning. She needed assistance dressing. Upon sudden motion, she had
the sensation of the muscles tearing and being bruised, painful on pressure.
Convers gave her different remedies as they seemed to be indicated with no result. He thought there could be
nothing lost by trying Jac. and did so. In a few days, she was
entirely relieved of muscular pains.
Six weeks after, her symptoms returned, but a second dose again relieved and the pains did not return.
Con vers tried Jac. on three other patients with the same peculiar morning stiffness and soreness. All were
relie ved in a few day s and experienced no further muscular pains.
Convers used the mother tincture at 5 drops per dose and the 3x dilution of it in the treatment of gonorrhea
and chancroids with the great success.
Anshutz noted that it is a complementary and antidote to Merc.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

name: Jade
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jad. Jade. Nephrite. Jadeite. Jade is found in two varieties. Jadeite and Nephrite and comes in
a wide range of colors including white, lavender, red, brown, yellow, orange, blue, and green, each color said
to relate more specifically to certain ailments or organs. Historical dose: The gem mother tincture diluted can
be applied externally and given internally. Four to Eight drops of Jade Essence in a cup of pure water. Repeat
as needed.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Detoxification. Eye, disorders. Gastric,pains. Heartburn. Kidney, disorders. Kidney,
stones.
HOMEOPATHIC - The Portuguese, who brought home jade pieces from their settlement in Canton, China,
called jade piedre de ilharga, or stone of the loins, because they believed it to be strong medicine for kidney
ailments. Jade objects brought back to Spain from the new world were called by the Spanish version of this
phrase piedra de hijada. This became the French ejade and then, finally, jade. Jadeite is from the Spanish,
piedra de ijada, “stone of the side,” because its supposed to cure kidney ailments if applied to the side of the
body.
Suggested healing properties common to all colors of Jade include, ability to mellow one's existence, rid
negative thoughts and energy, soothe the mind. Thus making tasks
seem easier and less complicated. Strengthen the body’s filtration and cleansing systems. Develop a greater
 capacity for love, and assist in the removal of toxins. Also said to be a very protective stone.
Jade was known as the kidney stone, and it was widely employed as a remedy for renal disease. It was worn
over this organ to break up kidney stones. Powdered and mixed with gold and silver, jade strengthened the
lungs, the vocal organs, and the heart and prolonged life.
A potion of jade, rice, and dew was employed to harden bones, make muscles more supple, calm the mind,
and purify the blood. Taken regularly, this prescription eliminated hunger and thirst as well as sensations of
heat and cold.
Believed to protect the body from decay, jade was used for embalming. When worn around a child's neck jade
would guard against infantile disease. It also was worn to relieve gastric pains and heartburn, to calm asthma,
and to aid childbirth. Four grains, dissolved in wine, relieved bile.
Suggested healing properties common to all colors of Jade include, ability to mellow one's existence, rid
negative thoughts and energy, soothe the mind making tasks seem easier and less complicated, strengthen
the body's filtration and cleansing systems, develop a greater capacity for love, and assist in the removal of
toxins. Also said to be a very protective stone.
Health, wealth, longevity stone. Ancient Chinese used also for courage, wisdom, justice, mercy, emotional
balance, stamina, love, fidelity, humility, generosity, peace, harmony. Lungs, heart, thymus, immune, kidney
and blood detoxification, nervous system. A gentle, steady energy.
Increases fertility, longevity. Provides wisdom when evaluating issues or problems. Brings needed energy.
Improves concentration. Encourages education. Considered a “Dream Stone.” Benefits eye disorders, kidney
stones and female discomfort.
COMMENTS - The ancient jade carved in China was what we today call nephrite jade: an ar .phibolite mineral.
In the 19th Century
, it was discovered that the material from the new world was not the same mineral as the jade from China. The
mineral from Central America, a pyroxene, was called jadeite to distinguish it from the original nephrite.
Because of its smooth even texture, jade has long been a preferred material for carving. The most common
shape is the flat donut-shaped disc called a pi, which is commonly worn as a necklace. The Emerald Buddha,
the sacred image that is enshrined at Wat Phra Kaeo in Bangkok, Thailand, is actually beautiful green jadeite.
Good fortune, prosperity. A peaceful stone for centuries of primary importance to the people of the Orient
(where it is considered to be one of the most importance symbols of purity and serentiy). The Chinese referred
to jade as the musical stone, because of the melodic tones it makes when struck.
For centuries, jade was thought to be a single gemstone, but in 1863 two types were recognized: jadeite and
nephrite. Jade, Venus: Chinese Stone of Heaven. Since at least 2950 BC, jade has been treasured in China
as the royal gemstone, yu. The character for jade resembles a capital I with a line across the middle: the top
represents the heavens, the bottom the earth, and the center section, mankind.
The word yu is used in Chinese to call something precious, as in English we use gold. Jade was thought to
preserve the body after death and can be found in emperors' tombs from thousands of years ago. One tomb
contained an entire suit made out of jade, to assure the physical immortality of its owner. For thousands of
years, jade was a symbol of love and virtue as well as a status symbol.
RELATIONS - Compare: Aurum Met. Nat. Mur. Rose Quartz.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Jalapa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jal. Jalapa. Ipomoea jalapa. Ipomoea purga. Exogonium purga. Concol- vulus purga. N. O.
Convolvulacae. Mexico. Trituration of dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, soreness. Colic. Coryza. Diarrhea. Gout. Fainting. Restlessness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Jalapa, the well-known purgative of old school practice, had a short proving by Jeanes.
Allen cured a case of “coryza in an infant, violent attacks of crying and intense pain, quiet during the day, but
screaming all night.”
Colic and diarrhea. Severe abdominal pain, “as if the abdomen would be cut to pieces,” severe griping,
cutting pains. Pain is better by belchings of frothy matter and flatulence.
Cutting colic before and during the stool. Stools are watery, sour smelling and bloody. Stools, watery, muddy
or sour, bloody. Infantile diarrhea with general coldness, blueness of face. Pain in sigmoid flexure.
General coldness and blueness of the face. Restlessness and anxiety. Great weakness with fainting fits,
excessive uneasiness and tossing about of limbs. Symptoms are worse at night. A child may be quite quiet
all day, but screams and tossed about all night.
MIND - Great restlessness with anxiety. Fainting fits, weakness. Quiet all day, but screams and tossed about
 all night. Weeping in sleep, good during day. Screams and restless all night. Shrieking in children.
Abdomen - Abdomen distended. Pain in middle of abdomen and in region of left superior flexure of colon.
Pain in right hypochondrium. Pain in cecum. Colic, violent pain in small intestines, as if abdomen would be cut
to pieces. Inflammation of intestines. Severe griping, cutting pain in bowels, worse at night. Flatulent rumbling
in bowels. Flatulence and nausea.
Back - Severe pain about superior margin of left scapula.
Ears - Humming in ears.
Head - Violent headache. Pain in head, smarting in skin of forehead.
Kidneys - Pain and pressure in region of bladder.
Limbs - Excessive uneasiness and tossing about of limbs. Aching in arms and legs, mostly right side. Pain in
thighs. Pain in large joint of great toe. Smarting on inside edge and at root of left great toenail with heat, tearing
and pulsation. Burning of soles of feet.
Male - Thrilling sensation in urethra while urinating.
Modalities - Worse night, belchings.
Mouth - Dryness of lips. Tongue, smooth, glazed, dry, smarting and biting. Stinging on tongue and in fauces.
Perspiration - Great disposition to perspiration of head and superior parts of body.
Rectum - Pinching and griping. Severe cutting, griping pain in bowels. Cutting colic before and during stool.
Watery diarrhea, thin, muddy stools. Stools, violent, excessive, bloody, watery, with weak pulse, sour smelling,
with great restlessness and anxiety. Infantile diarrhea, general coldness, blueness of face. Pain in sigmoid
flexure of colon. Soreness of anus.
Stomach - Flatulent and frothy belchings with abatement of pain. Nausea.
Temperature - General coldness and blueness of face. Febrile attacks.
COMMENTS - Nash cured with Jal. 12c a desperate case of enterocolitis in which there was screaming all
day as well as all night. With the screaming there was constant body contortions, bending forward, backward
and sideways alternately.
RELATIONS-Antidotes: Elat., Cann-s. Compare: (1) Camph. - diarrhea with coldness. (2) Coloc. - colic. (3)
Iris-t. - pain in cecum.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Convolvulacae. Mexico. Trituration of dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, soreness. Colic. Coryza. Diarrhea. Gout. Fainting. Restlessness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Jalapa, the well-known purgative of old school practice, had a short proving by Jeanes.

name: Jasminum Officinale
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jasm. Jasminum officinale. White jessamine. N. O. Jasminaceae. Some botanists include
jasmine in the Oleaceae. Jasminum should not be confounded with Gelsemium, the “Yellow Jessamine,” or
“Carolina Jessamine,” which belongs to a different order of plants. Tincture of red berries. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Coma. Convulsions. Lockjaw. Tetanus. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - W. H. Hull recorded the case of a boy who ate the red berries, causing vomiting,
convulsions, tetanus and acomatose state. Symptoms went from above downwards and from left to right.
Muscular movements were observed first about the eyes and face, especially on the left side, towards which
eyes and facial muscles were directed. The movements became generally more severe, going from head to
left arm, then to left lower limbs, until finally the whole body was thrown into violent convulsions.
At one time the spasms were chiefly opisthotonos, when the whole surface was congested almost to a
blackened hue, most marked about the muscles of the head and throat, jaws locked, trismus complete, better
by a bath. The body was weak and almost helpless for a few days. Lay on the floor in a fainting fit. Perfect
insensibility. Surface cool.
MIND - Comatose condition. Perfect insensibility.
Eyes - Pupils immoderately dilated.
Face - Face pale. Muscular movement first above eyes and face, especially left side towards which eyes and
facial muscles were directed.
Lungs - Breathing somewhat bronchial but of unusual frequency.
Pulse - Slow and feeble.
Stomach - Vomiting. Slight emesis after first sleep.
COMMENTS - The Treasury of Botany stated that the bitter leaves of Jasminum floribundum are used in
Abyssinia against tapeworms. In India, the bitter root of Jasminum angustifolium, powdered and mixed with
the powdered root of Acorns calamus, is considered an excellent application in ringworm.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
 ***JATROPHA CURCAS
(Purging Nut)
PHARMACY - jatr. Jatropha curcas. Purging nut. Atrophacurcas. Physic nut. N. O. Euphor- biaceae. West
Indies.Tincture and triturationof seeds. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies, third to thirtieth
potency.
CLINICAL - Blepharospasm. Borborygmi. Cholera. Cholerine. Constipation. Cramps. Diarrhea. Eyelids,
inflamed. Food, poisoning. Heels, sensitive. Hiccough. Mouth, ulceration. Skin, disorders. Tympanites.
Vomiting. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Jatr. is one of the most active of the Euphorbians and strongly resembles Croto-t. in its
action, especially in the urgent gushing stools and the irritation and pimples of the skin. It is also an active
purgative, affecting the stomach and intestines.
Kent described the sphere of Jatr. in cholera, noting that “The characteristic is rice water discharge, it has
vomiting and purging, more or less sweat, more or less cramps. Suppression of urine, the great prostration,
syncope and rapid onset peculiar to cholera and it has this to differentiate it from all other remedies. The
vomiting and purging and evacuations are thick, albuminous, lumpy instead of thin and watery.”
Jatr. corresponds more to the earlier stage than to the collapse stage of cholera. Predominant cramps, gripping
cutting pains, sensation as if balls were rolling together in abdomen. Violent cramps that draw the muscles of
calf flat. The patient writhes about in bed with pain.
Sudden desire for stool and constant noise of liquids in abdomen, especially left side. Marked and peculiar
gurgling, like water. Much noise in the abdomen as if a bottle was being emptied, followed later by a thin
stool or by profuse gushing stools. Rice water stools.
Vomiting, easy, albuminous. Hiccough followed by copious vomiting. Unquenchable thirst. Food poisoning.
Icy coldness of the whole body, especially lower limbs.
MIND - Apathy. Indifference to pain. Anxiety and anguish, with burning in stomach and
coldness of body.
Abdomen - Abdomen swollen and sore to touch. Tympanites. Pain in hypochondria, deep in abdomen, behind
the navel. Griping, sticking, in abdomen. Lancinating, stinging pain with the colic. Colic with rumbling in
abdomen, better walking in open air. Distended with gurgling noises. Much noise in abdomen, as if a full
bottle was emptied, followed by thin stool. Noise like the gurgling of water during the fecal discharge.
Sensation as if balls were rolling together in abdomen.
Back - Stiffness of muscles of nape of neck and forehead. Bruised feeling muscles of back and chest. Stiffness
in lumbar region.
Chest - Constriction in chest with anxiety, preventing sleep. Violent aching pain in left clavicle. Sticking from
above downwards, deep in chest behind sternum. Pain in region of left third rib inside the nipple.
Ears - Burning hot ears with heat in the back part of the head.
Eyes - Itching and smarting of margins of lids. Twitching of left upper lid. Bright and dark spots before eyes.
Black points before eyes.
Face - Hot face and head, chilliness in the back. Pale face with blue margins around the eyes. Painful cracked
lips.
Female - Vomiting during pregnancy.
Food - Great thirst. Violent, unquenchable thirst, not satisfied by drinking water. Dreads to drink on account of
nausea. Food poisoning.
Head - Heat and heaviness of the head. Heat in head, face and ears. Stupefaction with yawning and nausea.
Headache with nausea and vomiting. Violentpressing pain in the temples, ceasing in open air and re- appeari
ng when entering aroom. Stiffness of muscles on forehead and neck.
Heart - Feeling of sinking and nausea in the precordial region, followed by soft stool. Violent palpitation,
shaking the chest, when moving slowly about the room. Pulse is irregular, small thready and intermittent,
greatly slowed. Almost pulseless.
Kidneys - Violent urging to urinate. Urine pale yellow, frothy.
Limbs - Muscles of limbs contracted by violent spasms. Pain in the limbs and joints. Cramps in muscles,
especially calves, legs and feet. Pain in ankles, feet and toes. Heels sensitive.
Liver - Pain in region of liver and under right scapula to shoulder.
Lungs - Painful pressure right side of larynx at night, waking him, not worse by touch. Respiration quick,
panting, difficult. Short, hacking, persistent cough. Hollow cough.
Male - Aching in genital as after excessive sexual intercourse. Drawing in genitals, extending along inner side
right thigh to navel.
Modalities - Better by placing hands in cold water. Worse summer, walking in open air, morning, pressure,
 touch, covering. Patient seeks to cool himself by throwing off covers and lying on ground. Headaches are
worse in a room.
Mouth - Metallic, bloody taste with much spitting of saliva. Increased accumulation of thin saliva. Long
continued pain and burning of the tongue. Numbness of tongue with heat and dryness of mouth. Mouth feels
as if scalded.
Nose - Ulcers in the nose and mouth. Itching of the nose while eating.
Rectum - Loud noise in abdomen like gurgling of water, associated with coldness, cramps, nausea and
vomiting. First stage of cholera, before collapse. Diarrhea, forced discharge. Sudden, profuse, watery, rice-
water stool, gushes from him like a torrent. Very copious, mushy stools with quantities of lumbrici and
threadworms. Constipation. Stitches in anus and rectum.
Skin - Pimples on wrist, back of hand, cheek, back of neck, bend of right thigh. Itching and slightest tension
around mouth. Itching between fingers in palms, between toes in bed at night, first worse then better by
rubbing.
Sleep - Excessive drowsiness. Restlessness at night on account of rush of thought and palpitations. Attacks
of anxiety at night,
not permitting sleep.
Stomach - Heat and burning in stomach with crampy, constrictive pain in the epigastrium. Food poisoning.
Belchings of air. Hiccough, followed by copious vomiting. Very easy vomiting, of a large mass of dark green
bile, with acrid feeling from throat. Nausea and vomiting, brought on by drinking water. Vomiting during
pregnancy.
Temperature - Chilliness and clammy perspiration. Coldness of the whole body, mottled blue. Chilliness in
the back, cold hands, blue nails, with heat in the mouth, throat, face and head.
Throat - Burning in the mouth and throat, followed by dryness. Spasmodic constriction in throat, ascending
from stomach.
Vertigo - Giddiness, followed by unconsciousness and delirium.
COMMENTS - Diarrhea associated with coldness, mottled blue surface, cold sweat. Sudden desire for stool.
Diarrhea accompanied by copious and easy vomiting of watery, albuminous, ropy liquid. Water is almost
immediately vomited. Cholera. Suddenly occurring summer diarrhea.
Mouth dry, itching between toes, at night. Profuse, watery diarrhea after midnight. In the morning, stools,
headache, are worse. Metallic bloody taste, much spitting of saliva. Farrington noted that it is useful in cases
of suppressed measles.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Camph., Verat., Gamb., Crot-t. (2) Jatr-u., Sponge nettle - edema and cardiac
paresis.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Jatropha Urens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jatr-u. Jatropha urens. Spurge nettle. Tread softly. N. O. Euphorbiaceae. Southern United
States. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cardiac, paresis. Edema.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Allen, this is the most poisonous plant known. He quoted, from the Kew
Gardens Quarterly, the experience of Mr. Smith, who touched his wrist against the fine bristly stings of the
plant while reaching over it. He experienced numbness and swelling of the lips. His circulation stopped and
Smith soon fell unconscious, the last thing he remembered were cries of “Run for the doctor!”
COMMENTS - Other Jatropha include Jatr. glauca, or Jatr. glandulifera, of the East Indies. It has a curious
nodulated, gouty looking stem. When crushed, the seeds yield an oil that is used as an external application
against rheumatism.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Joanesia Asoca
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - joan. Joanesia asoca. Ashoka bark. Jonosia asoca. Saraca indica. Bark of an IndianTree. N.
O. Caesalpinioideae. Tincture of bark or seeds. Dried bark. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Emaciation. Fibroids. Headache. Hemorrhoids.
Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Menopause. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Nausea. Palpitations. Uterine, disorders.
Vomiting.
HERBAL - Joanesia is a noted plant in India and its therapeutic properties in curing and alleviating all sorts of
 menstrual troubles and uterine disorders date back from antiquities. Long-lasting costiveness, occasional
headache and vertigo associated with uterine derangements are some of the marked symptoms of the drug.
Joanesiais a sovereign remedy for amenorrhea or scanty menses with intolerable pain
and burning sensation during the passage of urine. In dysmenorrhea its efficacy has been verified by several
homeopaths of our country.
The Ayurvedic physicians prize it as an uterine tonic. It imparts a healthy tone and an all round strength to the
uterus which has been weakened by long-lasting disorders of the uterus.
In the cure of leucorrhea its action can never be questioned and upon bloody leucorrhea, whether acute or
chronic, it exerts an exhilarating and permanent curative action which sometimes appears to be a miracle. It
removes weakness and physical emaciation to the females suffering from long - lasting uterine complaints, or
due to those causes.
It is generally considered to be an astringent medicine and uterine sedative. It is said to possess a stimulating
effect on the endometrium and on the ovarian tissue.
Joanesiais extensively employed in uterine ailments especially menorrhagia which is the outcome of uterine
fibroids and other causes.
In cases of bloody leucorrhea its efficacy is sure and pronounced. Menstrual flow appears too soon, is copious
and lasts long and this sort of flow makes the female very weak, anemic and bloodless, she experiences
burning sensation all over the face and eyes suffers from pain in the lumbar region and constipation.
Joanesia is considered by competent authorities to be an excellent remedy for the eradication of the above
complaints. Asoka will be found to be a grand medicine if the menstrual flow be stopped for any cause and for
which colicky abdominal pains supervene.
HOMEOPATHIC - Joanesia was introduced by Dr. N. D. Ray, of Calcutta. Extensive sphere of action on female
organs. Amenorrhea and metrorrhagia.
The remedy is principally used by the native physicians of India for menorrhagia, metrorrhagia, leucorrhea
from delayed menses or in the place of menses. Infantile leucorrhea, child getting thin and emaciated
in spite of getting usual nourishment.
Joanesia has been found to be an excellent medicine for the complaints appearing at the time of menopause.
For barrenness it is generally used with success.
In bleeding piles, its efficacy has been verified. In bleeding piles, the color of the blood is red. the patient
experiences severe pain and stiff feeling in the back and suffers from constipation, there is burning sensation
while passing urine, and there is also burning of the hands, feet and eyes in the evening.
MIND - The patients are generally affectionate, nervous, sentimental, gloomy and religious. Good-natured,
affectionate. Absentminded. Timid. Easily weeping, easily excitable, easily fatigued. Disinclination to work. Not
very imaginative.
Changeable thoughts. Satisfied with small things. Slow to understand. Disposition to take cold easily, feels
better in the open air. Impatient. Cannot bear sufferings. Hysterical exaggerates sufferings.
Abdomen - Hard distended abdomen, pain on pressure, passage of foul-smelling wind, eructation, flatulent
colic, worse in the evening, soreness in lower abdomen or pelvis.
Back - Coldness between shoulders. Pain along spine, radiating to abdomen and thighs. Pain at the ape of
the neck along the spine. Pain in sacrum and in back radiates on both sides of the abdomen and down the
thighs.
Bladder- Irritable bladder. Bladder irritable, desire for frequent passage of urine. Tenderness of bladder.
Chest - Tight feeling across the chest.
Ears - Pains in ear. Hardness of hearing especially after catarrhal or severe cold.
Eyes - Pain in the eyeballs. Redness of the conjunctiva. Burning and itching sensation. Styes on upper lids.
Profuse lachrymation. Short-sightedness. Great sensibility of eyes to light. Supra-orbital pains on one or both
sides. Great photophobia. Tired feeling in the eyes with least exertion, such as reading and staring at an object.
Face - Paleness of the face, alternately with heat and redness of the cheeks. Pimples on the face.
Female - Menses suppressed and irregular. Headache due to suppression of menses. Severe headache due
to scanty flow of menses with severe pain all over the lower parts of the abdomen, pain in back and thighs.
Menstrual colic. Delayed and irregular menses. Menstrual discharge scanty, pale and watery, sometimes bad
odor and blackish, slightly clotted and painful. Leucorrhea. Amenorrhea at puberty with headache, palpitation,
hysteria, loss of appetite, constipation. Pain in ovaries before the flow. Congestive feelings in pelvic organs as
before menses. Pain in both ovarian regions. Pain in the sacral region, better on the appearance of menses
with free flow. Menorrhagia.
Food - Want of appetite and dislike for food. No desire for food, eats little. Thirsty. Desire for sweets. Desire
for acid and sour things. Drinks large quantities of water. Disinclined to take milk, which when taken agrees
 well.
Head - Stupefying headache, frontal headache, worse sometimes on right temple and sometimes on the left.
Unilateral headache. Reflex uterine congestive headache. with scanty menstrual discharge relieved by free
flow, nausea, vertigo, disinclination for food or drink, periodical headache, better after bathing, sweat of
forehead, relieved of all symptoms in the open air, heaviness of the whole head. Congestive headache, better
open air and by free flow.
Heart - Palpitations. Pain in the region of the heart. Pulse quick, full and hard. Accentuated first sound.
Palpitations, worse on movement or walking or bending forward.
Kidneys - Urine scanty, bloody, passes frequently. Involuntary urination at night in bed. Profuse emission of
watery urine, pain in loin.
Limbs - Weakness in limbs. Shifting pain from place to place. Pains in small joints. Numbness of the limbs.
Pain along the thighs.
Lungs - Respiration hurried. Difficulty in breathing when walking, worse in the afternoon and evening. Hacking
throat cough.
Male - Testicles swollen, drawing pain in the spermatic cords, itching in the scrotum, discharge of prostatic
fluid, emission at night with or without dreams.
Mouth - Dryness of the mouth, excessive thirst, drinks large quantities of water at a time, tongue coated with
thick, white or brown coating, bleeding of the gums, toothache.
Nose - Nasal catarrh, sneezing, profuse watery discharge from the nose. Nostrils sore. Obstruction of the
nose. Loss of sense of smell. Ulceration of the nostrils. Profuse bleeding from the nose of red color.
Rectum - Hemorrhoids. Obstinate constipation. Feces are hard. Large stool and passed every third or fourth
day. Evacuation difficult, pain before stools. Stools are covered with slime or mucus. Pains on the back.
Soreness in anus. Blind or bleeding piles. Protrusion of hemorrhoids with itching, smarting and pain.
Sleep - Disturbed sleep. Sleeplessness. Fearful dreams. Dreams of traveling.
Stomach - Excessive nausea, sometimes vomiting. Vomiting of bile. Biliousness. Pain in epigastrium. Colicky
pain.
Temperature - Chilliness without thirst. Dry heat with restlessness. Redness of cheeks. Flushed face, running
from the nose, catarrhal symptoms.
Throat - Redness of the throat, tonsils and uvula, sore throat, easily takes cold, troublesome throat cough.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Ghose.

name: Juglans Cinerea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jug-c. Juglans cinerea. Butternut. Juglans cathartica. N. O. Juglandaceae. North America.
Tincture of bark of root. Triturations of the resinoid Juglandin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies,
tincture to third potency.
CLINICAL - Acne. Angina pectoris. Axilla, pain. Chest, pain. Gallstones. Coryza. Dropsy. Eczema. Erysipelas.
Erythema nodosum. Gallstones. Headaches. Herpes. Hydrothorax. Impetigo. Lichen. Migraines. Pemphigus.
Ringworm. Rodent ulcer. Scapula, pain. Scarlatina. Tetters. Vision, lost.
HOMEOPATHIC - The butternut and the black walnut (Juglans nigra) are the American repre- sentativesof the
walnut family. It has a reputation as a mild cathartic. Applied to the skin, the juice causes reddening and
blistering. It was successfully used in camp diarrhea and dysentery in the early American wars. The green
rind, rubbed on tetters and ringworm, has a reputation for curing them.
Jug-c. and Jug-r„ or Nux Juglans, have both been proved and studied. With both, the digestion is disordered,
accompanied with other acute symptoms, including headaches. These are followed by chronic skin disorders.
Sharp, occipital headache, usually associated with liver disturbance. Pain in chest, axilla and scapula with
suffocative sensation. Feeling as if all internal organs were too large, especially those of left side. Gallstones.
Faulty elimination that produces jaundice and various skin eruptions. Itching is worse when overheated from
exercise.
MIND - Absent-minded. Confusion. Difficulty concentrating. Dull feeling, cannot remember anything that was
read. Depression of spirits. Aversion to company. Want to do nothing but eat and sleep.
Abdomen - Soreness in region of liver.
Stitches in hepatic region, and under right scapula. Pain in the hypochondrium. Heavy pain in umbilical region.
Flatulent pain in different parts of abdomen. Burning in abdomen after stool.
Back - Muscles of neck rigid, lame. Pricking up and down spine. Pain in lumbar vertebrae. Pain between
scapula. Sticking under right scapula on stooping.
Chest - Pain in left chest. Retro-sternal pain. Angina pectoris. Oppression at chest, hindering long breathing
 with cutting pains in lungs. Tuberculosis with great emaciation. Dropsy of chest, of rheumatic origin.
Eyes - Eyes red and swollen. Inflammation, with pustules on lids and around eyes. Eyes burning in afternoon.
Feeling in eyes as if drawn together. Loss of vision on sudden motion, with faint-like giddiness.
Face - Pallor. Erythematous redness with dry, burning sensation.
Food - Ferocious appetite. Thirsty, wants to drink all the time.
Head - Dull, full head. Head feels enlarged. Dull headache, better when getting up. Sharp, occipital
headache. Severe headache, can hardly see. Eruption on scalp. Itching of scalp, intense, must scratch
constantly. Pustules on lids and around eyes.
Kidneys - Frequent and copious urination, with burning, smarting, with a headache.
Limbs - Aching pains in the limbs. Sharp, rheumatic pain in shoulders and wrists. Pain in right axilla in
afternoon. Pain in elbows and knees. Cramp-like pain in hip at night. Pain in thighs and left knee in forenoon.
Occasionally sharp pain in calves.
Lungs - Expectoration of very tenacious mucus, raising a quantity of dark blood.
Modalities - Better getting heated, exercise, scratching, rising in the morning. Worse walking, chest pains.
Going up hill causes retro-sternal pain. Stooping causes pain in scapula and back.
Mouth - Acrid feeling in mouth and throat. Coppery taste. Tongue coated white, yellow in the morning. Dryness
of root of tongue and fauces. Burning and pricking in mouth and throat. Swelling of submaxillary glands, worse
right. Soreness in region of tonsils, externally.
Nose - Tingling in nose, sneezing. Coryza, preceded by pain under sternum, with threatening suffocation.
Copious, bland, thick mucus discharge.
Rectum - Constipation, with griping in umbilical region. Constipation preceded by diarrhea. Diarrhea with
burning in anus before and after stool. Yellowish- green stools with tenesmus and burning at anus. A drastic
purge, producing irritation and inflammation of mucus membrane
of bowels. Bilious, copious, frequent, painless stools. Loose stool, smelling like onions. Camp diarrhea.
Skin - Jaundice with pain about liver and right scapula. Red-like flush of scarlatina. Erythema and erysipelatous
redness. Itching and prickling when heated. Eczema, especially on lower limbs, sacrum and hands.
Pustules.
Sleep - Constant yawning, without sleepiness. Sleepiness. Sleeplessness after 3 a.m. Sleep restless, light,
unrefreshing. Dreams are vivid, frightful.
Stomach - Burning in stomach. Sinking in stomach extends to abdomen, with headache. Atonic dyspepsia
with much belchings and flatulent distention. Nausea in morning. Nausea worse at night.
Temperature - Chilliness, alternating with flashes of heat. Chilliness along spine, beginning in back when near
the fire, without coldness of flesh.
Throat - Sore throat in forenoon with roughness on swallowing. Fauces dry. Pain in right side of fauces.
Burning in pharynx.
Vertigo - Vertigo with slight nausea. Slight vertigo with sinking faint feeling in stomach extending to abdomen.
COMMENTS - Scrofulous and scorbutic conditions. Rheumatic pains. Characteristic sharp shooting pain in
occiput. Headache, with frequent urination and burning. Morning headaches (Nux-v., Bry., Chef, Iris.).
Disturbance of the digestive organs (Iris.). Pains in liver and right scapula. Epigastric sinking, extending to the
abdomen, with a headache. Acute diarrhea.
Dark, clotted hemorrhage from the lungs (Jug-r., from the uterus). Acute pains and numbness in the axilla
(Jug-r. affects the skin and glands of the axilla).
Eruptions. Scarlatina. Rodent ulcer. One patient who was taking Jug-c. for acne developed all the symptoms
of angina pectoris.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Juglin. - duodenal catarrh, bilious diarrhea. (2) Chef, Bry., Iris.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Tincture of bark of root. Triturations of the resinoid Juglandin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies,
tincture to third potency.
CLINICAL - Acne. Angina pectoris. Axilla, pain. Chest, pain. Gallstones. Coryza. Dropsy. Eczema. Erysipelas.
Erythema nodosum. Gallstones. Headaches. Herpes. Hydrothorax. Impetigo. Lichen. Migraines. Pemphigus.
Ringworm. Rodent ulcer. Scapula, pain. Scarlatina.

name: Juglans Regia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - jug-r. Juglans regia. Walnut. Nux juglans. N. O. Juglandaceae. Tincture of leaves and of rind of
green fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Anus, burning. Axillary glands, suppuration. Chancre. Eruptions. Exhaustion. Eyes, pain.
Favus. Flatulence. Headaches. Herpes. Levitation, sensation. Menorrhagia. Purpura. Ringworm. Skin, dis-
orders. Scurvy. Spleen, pain. Styes. Syphilis.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany noted, “Its plantation should not be too near dwellings, as some persons
are affected by the powerful aroma of its foliage. It was said that in the golden age, when men lived upon
acorns, the gods lived upon Walnuts and hence the name of Juglans, Jovis glans or Jupiter's nuts”.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Excited, as if intoxicated in the evening in bed and a feeling as if the head were floating in
the air, or as if flying. Sharp pains in the forehead (Jug-c. in the occiput). Muscles relaxed. Prominent skin
eruptions. Exhaustion and disinclination for the usual business.
MIND - Mental indolence. Disinclined to talk or argue. Inattention when reading and disinclination to work.
Peevishness. Discontented in evening. Excited in evening in bed as if intoxicated. Feeling as if the head were
floating in the air.
Abdomen - Fullness, bloated, tension and heaviness in the abdomen. Pain in epigastric region with distention
of abdomen. Drawing with pressure in region of spleen. Pain above umbilicus.
Back - Stitches in sacral region. Violent stitches in the small of the back, causing one to tremble.
Chest - Oppression. Sticking in lungs not dependent on motion or respiration. Itching on the sternum.
Ears - Aching and fullness in right, then left ear, followed by a discharge of pus from both ears. Burning in left
ear, then redness and swelling. External ear inflamed, with painful sores. Eruption behind ears
of children.
Eyes - Burning in eyes. Pressive pain above eye (left) worse by motion. Styes. Feeling of coryza.
Face - Swelling of left cheek and upper lip.
Female - Menses preceded by pressive drawing pains in the abdomen, worse by motion, accompanied with
general exhaustion and loss of appetite. Menstruation early, too profuse, discharge of a large quantity of black,
pitch-like clots.
Food - Unusually great appetite without increase of thirst. Thirstlessness while eating and aversion to wine.
Appetite lost. Thirst increased. Aversion to tobacco smoking in the evening.
Head - Confused, feels as if head were floating in air. Occipital sharp pain.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to pass water from loss of tone of sphincter. Constant urging and involuntary
dribbling. Copious urine, but no thirst. Urine scanty, clear, dark red.
Limbs - Drawing pain, as if sprained. Paralyzed feeling in legs and knees with weakness. Sticking and itching
in right leg and right fingers.
Male - Frequent erections day and night. Burning in penis after sex.
Modalities - Worse by motion. Worse after fat food, evening, at 9 p.m. and after 9 p.m. Migraine worse by
speaking. Pain in abdomen worse by laughing. Warmth of bed aggravates toothache. Itching, worse at night.
Rash aggravated by undressing, washing.
Mouth - Tongue coated white in morning with bitter, slimy taste. Salivation. Tearing in hollow teeth, worse
warmth of bed.
Rectum - Stool twice a day, preceded or accompanied by pain in abdomen. Thin, soft, large, hard, difficult,
scanty stool. Large stool, then burning pain and pressure in anus. Stool delayed. Constipation. Itching at the
anus in the evening, with stitches, compelling one to walk about.
Skin - Comedones and acne of the face. Itching and eruptions of small red pustules. Pimples on face, red
pimples on face, neck, shoulders and back. Scalp red and
itches violently at night. Crusta lactea with soreness around ears. Chancre-like ulcer. Axillary glands suppurate.
Sleep - Yawning in afternoon with stretching. Sleepiness. Inability to sleep after dinner, though inclined to do
so earlier than usual. Restless sleep with frightful dreams.
Stomach - Fullness and bloated of the stomach. Burning in stomach. Hiccough more violent after eating.
Belchings are violent, frequent, loud, tasting as after eating fat. Nausea at 6 a.m. and after supper. Vomiting,
woke suddenly vomited food eaten four hours before, then slept without further trouble.
Throat - Aphonia or great hoarseness. Hawking of much mucus.
COMMENTS - Severe flatulence and bloating of the abdomen. Affects the spleen more than the liver (opposite
of Jug-c.). Diarrhea and many rectal and anal symptoms. Hemorrhagic, blackandclottedblood (Jug-c.,
Cary.),particularly uterine hemorrhages. Inflammation and ulceration in the male sexual organs.
Pronounced skin symptoms. Scrofula. Scabs on the arms and in axilla. Symptoms go from the right axilla to
the left.
Farrington said Jug-r. is one of the best remedies in “tinea favosa, especially in the scalp behind the ear, itching
is intense at night so that the patient has difficulty in sleeping.”
Clotar Miiller, who experienced the axillary skin symptoms in his own person, had never suffered from a skin
affection before. One of the provers was cured of an itching eruption of the legs from which he had suffered in
winter for four years, the itching commencing as soon as he began to undress.
Many of the symptoms closely resembled syphilis and the affection of the cheek in one of the provers was
actually diagnosed as syphilitic by a doctor who saw him in Miiller's absence. The left side of head, face and
abdomen were mostly affected. Axillary symptoms proceed from right to left.
In one case, a nurse poisoned her left arm some years before from septic and possibly syphilitic cause,
 inflammation of
Jugions regia the axillary glands ensued, first of the left then of the right, leaving an eczematous itching
condition. The glands of the groin also became affected.
Elaps. 200c relieved the bulk of the conditions, but there was still a little irritation occasionally in the axilla and
Jug-r. 2c three times a day was given.
Five days after beginning the Jug-r., an eruption of minute vesicles appeared on her back, itching a great deal.
It extended up the center of her back from sacrum to mid-dorsal region, spreading out below, tapering above.
She had scratched holes in two places.
The rash was worse after washing. All soreness and irritation had gone from the arms and axilla. The rash
was antidoted with Rhus-t. 2c. She had no more trouble with her glands.
Muller observed, “In the digestive organs it causes derangement and irritation, which simultaneously call forth
abnormal symptoms in other organs, especially in the head. After this action, which is brief, appear various
exanthematous symptoms, which appear late and run a chronic course.”
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Rhus-t. Compare: (1) Jug-c., Cary. (2) Rhus-t. - skin. (3) Graph. - tinea favosa
behind ears. (4) Rumex - rash worse undressing. (5) Mez., Merc. (6) Cean. - spleen. (7) Lyc. - flatulence.
Follows well: Elaps. - axillary affections, black hemorrhages. Sulph. - head hot, cold limbs. Grind. - pain over
left eye.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

***JUNCUS EFFUSUS (Soft Rush)
PHARMACY-june. Juncuseffusus. Softrush. Common rush. Juncus communis. N. O. Juncaceae. Tincture of
root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Backache. Calculus. Catarrh. Dropsy. Dysuria. Flatulence. Headache. Kidney, diseases.
Rheumatism. Scars disorders.
HERBAL - According to Nowack and Rinks, Juncus is a diuretic and has been used in dropsical, kidney stones
and kidney diseases. Hartmann used the tincture with success in dysuria, strangury and ischuria. In Livonia,
a decoction is used for stone and gravel.
HOMEOPATHIC Junc-e. was proved by Dr. Whale, producing a number of symptoms. The exact preparation
used in the proving was not recorded. Fresh plant tinctures should be used in any further experiments.
The most notable symptoms were bubbling sensations in various parts. A number of pressive and sticking
pains were noted in the chest. Pulling in cervical vertebrae in neck muscles. Rumbling of flatus in abdomen;
abdominal symptoms were markedly better when flatus was emitted.
Rheumatic pains worse by rest, on left side, appeared or were worse at night and came on again in morning
and evening. Worse flexing parts, bending sideways. Better stretching out arm. Chilliness worse on
uncovering. Better by motion.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-t. - worse rest and uncovering, better stretching. (2) Berb. - bubbling
sensations. (3) Sil. - scars.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke

name: Juniperus Communis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - juni-c. Juniperus communis. Juniper berries. N. O. Gymnosperm of the Conifer. Cupressaceae.
Juniperus. Tincture of fresh ripe berries. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Allergies. Cedar, fever. Coryza. Coughs. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Hay fever. Hemorrhages.
Nephritis. Pyelitis.
HERBAL - Gin owes its distinctive properties to the oil of juniper berries, perhaps explaining why the spirit is
in such popular repute as a remedy for dysmenorrhea. It has a very powerful action on the kidneys and has
cured cases of kidney dropsy.
HOMEOPATHIC-Juni-c. has notbeen proved, but sufficient is known of its action to warrant its inclusion and
to show the analogy between
its action and that of Sabina.
Hale commended it in certain coughs with scanty, loaded urine. He said German doctors used juniper in gastric
affections, abdominal flatulence and colic. Catarrhal inflammation of kidneys. Dropsy with suppression of urine.
Elderly persons with poor digestion and scanty secretion of urine. Chronic pyelitis.
Chest - Painful ribs and sternum from coughing attacks (Bry.).
Kidneys - Nephritis. Strangury, bloody, scanty urine, violet odor (Tereb.). Weight in kidney region. Pyelitis.
Kidney hyperemia (Eucal.).
 Lungs - Severe, painful coughs. Cough with scanty, loaded urine.
Male - Prostatic discharge.
Nose - Coryza. Hay fever. Allergies. Violent sneezing from cedar pollen.
Comments - Hale wrote, “I have known cases of dysmenorrhea and uterine hemorrhage cured by the common
Juniper, and I have treated some kidney and bladder difficulties with Juniper. The popularity of pure gin in
dysmenorrhea is owing to the effects of the oil of Juniper berries which it contains.
“In domestic practice, an infusion of Juniper leaves and berries is used successfully in amenorrhea and
dysmenorrhea, as well as retention, suppression, and other urinary troubles.
“In some cases of dropsy, a tincture of the berries, or the oil of Juniper, will act on the kidneys favorably after
the failure of other medicines.
“We ought to have provings of the common Juniper, and give it a place in our Materia Medica. I would also
suggest that the tincture be made from equal parts by weight of the fresh berries and green leaves. The Oil of
Juniper of commerce is made from the berries alone.
“German physicians make much use of Juniper in gastric complaints, in abdominal flatulence, colics, and even
in some hepatic affections. I know that the 3x of Oleum juniperus is useful in certain coughs, with scanty urine,
loaded with solid matters.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) All-c., Wye., Sabin., Tereb.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale. Murphy.

name: Juniperus Virginianus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - juni. Juniperus virginianus. Red cedar. N. O. Gymnosperm of the Conifer. Tincture of fresh
twigs. Tincture of twigs and berries. Tincture of the oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Chilliness. Comatose. Convulsions. Cystitis. Delirium. Dropsy. Dysuria. Eyes, twitching. Fever.
Nausea. Pyelitis. Strangury. Strokes. Tetanus. Uterine, hemorrhage. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of Juni. have been largely observed on women who have taken it to stimulate
the uterus or bring on the menses. A number of fatal cases have occurred from overdose of the herb.
The patients passing into violent convulsions, followed by an apoplectic or stroke condition, insensibility and
collapse. Hands at times clenched. Jaws firmly fixed. Staggering. Comatose sleep. Chilliness. Rigors followed
by fever. Considerable fever and pain, similar to labor pains. Sweats. Pulse very irregular.
Persistent dragging pain in back. Hyperemia of kidneys. Pyelitis and cystitis. Dropsy of the aged with
suppressed urine. Violent tenesmus of bladder. Constant urging to urinate. Dysuria, burning, cutting pain in
urethra when urinating. Uterine hemorrhage.
Mind - Emotional during the paroxysm of fever. Fright. Raved incoherently. Delirious. Insensible state.
Moaning.
Abdomen - Abdomen swollen and hot.
Complained of intensity of pain in abdomen. Pain in the bowels. Thirst.
Bladder - Cystitis. Violent tenesmus of bladder. Constant urging to urinate. Dysuria, burning, cutting pain in
urethra when urinating.
Eyes - Eyes bloodshot. Sclerotic congestion. Pupils dilated. Eyes glare and twitch. Eyes felt as if bursting from
their sockets.
Face - Very red, swollen and livid face. Veins of the face, head, and neck fully distended. Ecchymosis.
Female - Uterine hemorrhage.
Food - Great thirst.
Head - Head felt as if enclosed with an iron band.
Kidneys - Hyperemia of kidneys. Pyelitis. Great difficulty in passing urine.
Rectum - Violent purging. Bowels loose.
Skin - Skin dry and parched.
Sleep - Deep, comatose sleep.
Stomach - Considerable distension and tenderness at pit of stomach. Stomach pain. Sick and distressed in
stomach. Nausea and vomiting a black and then a greenish matter. Heartburn.
Throat - Fauces in spots denuded of their mucus covering.
REFERENCES - Allen. Clarke.

name: Justicia Adhatoda
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-just. Justiciaadhatoda. Malabar nut. Adhatoda vasica. Vasika. Singhee. An Indian Shrub.
 Acanthaceae. Tincture of the fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Allergies. Appetite, loss. Asthma. Blood, spitting, Bronchitis. Colds. Constipation. Coryza.
Coughs. Depression. Dyspnea. Fevers. Hay fever. Jaundice. Pneumonia. Sneezing. Thirst. Tuberculosis.
Vomiting. Whooping cough.
HERBAL - The Ayurvedic physicians of India prize justicia. They are so very sure of its efficacy that they call
it Vaidyamata, i.e. mother of physicians. They claim that no death can occur from cough of any kind if Vasika
can play its role and find time to display its healing virtues.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dry, spasmodic, constricted cough. Violent dyspnea associated with the cough.
Threatened suffocation. Whooping cough, with breath loss, pale, stiff and blue, and rigidity of the body. Cough
with tightness of chest, as if it would burst with bronchial rattle, obstruction of breath and sneezing.
Vomiting with the cough, no food or drink is retained. Dry mucus membranes, especially of the mouth and
throat, with thirst. Tough expectoration. Acute catarrhal conditions of the respiratory tract, particularly in the
beginning. Colds.
Coryza, fluent, acrid with violent sneezing, coughing or asthmatic attacks. Fits of sneezing with
lachrymation and loss of smell and taste. Allergies and hay fever. Bronchitis, pneumonia. First stages of
tuberculosis, with spitting of blood. Hoarseness.
Functional derangements of the liver. Jaundice. Thirst. Great loss of appetite. Obstinate constipation.
Stiffening out, trembling and convulsions with cough or fever. Puffy hands and feet in morning. Chilliness.
Fever. Marked oversensitiveness to external impressions.
MIND- Irritability, easily angered. Badhumor. Anxious and discouraged. Depression of spirits. Averse to
conversation. Sensitive to external impressions.
Chest - Tightness across chest, as if it would burst.
Coughs - Cough with sneezing. Dry cough from sternal region all over chest. Paroxysmal cough with
suffocative obstruction of respiration. Whooping cough.
Eyes - Lachrymation.
Head - Hot, full and heavy head.
Limbs - Puffy hands and feet in morning.
Liver - Jaundice. Liver weakness. Liver pains.
Lungs - Acute catarrhal conditions of the respiratory tract. Severe dyspnea with cough. Obstruction of breath
and sneezing. Asthmatic attacks, cannot endure a close, warm room. Bronchitis and pneumonia. Rattling in
bronchi. Tough mucus. Tuberculosis.
Modalities - Worse in a close room, from dust, noise, eating.
Mouth - Mouth is dry. Loss of taste.
Nose-Allergies and hayfever. Profuse, fluent coryza, with constant sneezing. Coryza with cough. Fits of
sneezing with lachrymation and loss of smell and taste.
Stomach - Nausea and vomiting.
Throat - Hoarseness, larynx painful. Dry and painful during empty swallowing. Tenacious mucus.
COMMENTS - Blackwood wrote, “This one of the most ancient drugs in India, the most highly valued by
Ayurveda. Its field of use is in colds, coryza, cough of any kind, vomiting, bronchitis, pneumonia, tuberculosis,
spitting of blood. Fevers, jaundice, loss of appetite, and constipation. These ailments are what the ancient
physicians use it for.”
It was proved by two men, twenty-seven and thirty-two years of age; their symptoms were later clinically
verified. Proving symptoms included catarrh, violent sneezing, watering eyes, profuse coryza, loss of appetite,
vomiting, liver pains, hoarseness and very painful suffocative cough with blood streaked mucus and high
temperature.
Ghose recorded a case of coryza. “My son had an attack of cold. He had fluent coryza, with constant sneezing;
there was hoarseness with swollen nose; there was stoppage of nose at night; there was also thirst; no appetite
existed; there were occasional coughing fits, but no expectoration ensued.
“I prescribed Justicia 1 x every three hours. After administration of the third dose he fell asleep. He came round
within three days. From the second day there was no hoarseness.”
Ghose also recorded another case of coryza. The son of Babu Bhupati Choudhuri, of Bhowanipore. suffered
from a severe attack of cold. Copious fluent coryza, accompanied by violent coughing, the eyes were
somewhat swollen and watered all the time; he was feverish. Ghose prescribed Just, lx every three hours, and
he was fully cured within two days.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Seems to come between All-c. and Euphr.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Blackwood. Boer- icke. Clarke. Ghose.
 ***KALI ACETICUM
(Potassium Acetate)
PHARMACY -kali-acet. Kali aceticum. Potassium acetate. Acetate of potash. Kali acetas. Solution in distilled
water. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Urine, alkaline.
HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-acet. is well known in allopathic practice as a diuretic and, to a lesser degree, as a
cathartic. Derivatives have been used in cases of dropsy, chiefly ascites and hydrothorax. The homeopathic
uses are chiefly in cases of over-secretion of urine and in diarrhea.
The provings have brought out a preponderance of abdominal and urinary symptoms. Great disturbance in the
circulation of fluids in the tissues (Acet-ac.). Griping diarrhea. Increased flow of urine, which was more watery
and alkaline. Bleeding of hemorrhoids.
Weakness, trembling, profuse perspiration, especially about the head. Trembling and anxiety in whole body of
transient duration. Symptoms generally worse in morning, but there was a headache, worse 4 p.m.
Abdomen - Unnatural distention of abdomen after dinner. Griping. An indefinite gnawing pain lasting an hour.
Gnawing sensation in abdomen which lasted until evening. Pains in region of umbilicus, lasting until going to
bed, when they suddenly disappeared.
Head - Dull headache in morning. Headache about 4 p.m. Much perspiration of head.
Kidneys - Urine very much increased in quantity and very watery. Urine strongly alkaline, sweetish odor,
yellow color, ammoniacal.
Limbs - Extreme weariness and trembling in all limbs in morning. Great weariness of all limbs, with some
headache, disappearing half an hour after an afternoon nap.
Rectum - Bleeding hemorrhoids, several times during day. Diarrhea. Two stools in evening.
Stomach - Constrictive, dull pain in stomach, extending to low down in abdomen, gradually disappearing after
two hours. Dull, pressive, pinching and constrictive pain in epigastric region, coming on a few minutes after
each dose and lasting an hour.
Temperature - Much perspiration on head, especially from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Profuse perspiration, very
offensive during exertion.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Acet-ac., Kali-c., Am-a. (2) Lyc. - worse at 4 p.m.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
