name: Kali Nitricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kali-n. Kali nitricum. Potassium nitrate. Saltpetre. Nitre. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose:
Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Bedwetting. Chest, pain. Colic. Debility. Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy. Dysentery.
Dysmenorrhea. Gastritis. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhages. Herpes. Meniere's disease.
Menorrhagia. Nephritis. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Polyps. Rheumatism. Tuberculosis.
Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - The Saltpetre of the Alchemists, Kali-n. is known in old-school practice principally as a
“refrigerant diuretic” and as the active agent in the well known “nitre papers,” which are burnt, producing fumes
 to allay attacks of asthma.
A solution of saltpetre as an application was an old remedy for inveterate mange in cats. Nitre with sulphur
and charcoal forms gunpowder. A teaspoonful of this in hot water was a favorite remedy for gonorrhea among
soldiers in the days when black powder was used.
Affects the respiratory organs, kidneys, heart and blood vessels. Secretions are increased into cavities.
Sudden dropsical swellings over the whole body. Pains are dull stitching, throbbing. Wooden, numbness.
Very weak.
Asthma and cardiac asthma. Relapsing tuberculosis. Hemorrhagic tendency. Rheumatism. Gastro-intestinal
inflammation with much debility and relapse in tuberculosis. Suppurative nephritis. Incontinence of urine in
children.
MIND - Peevish, fretful. Bored. Mental weariness from lack of occupation or interest. Discouragement.
Sadness when alone. Aversion to thinking in morning. Fear of death. Anxiety and congestion to chest. Anxiety
during headache.
Abdomen - Excessive distention of abdomen. Griping about umbilicus. Stitching and sticking pains. Violent
pain in right side after eating veal. Peritonitis. Incarceration of flatus, especially in afternoon
and evening. Very loud rumbling in abdomen.
Back - Aching in lumbar region. Pains in back on stooping. Shootings in and between scapula. Pains extend
into the chest. Shooting pains in sacral region. Violent pains in loins on waking. Feeling in back as if kidneys
engorged.
Chest - Chest feels constricted. Oppression on chest, when ascending. Contractive pain in chest. Sticking in
left side near sternum. Inflammation of lungs.
Constitutions - Suited to asthmatic constitutions and chest complaints.
Ears - Shooting in ears. Inflammation and swelling of lobe of right ear. Chronic deafness from paralysis of
auditory nerve. Vertigo and tinnitus. Tinkling and ringing in ears.
Eyes - Burning in eyes, with lachrymation and photophobia. External angle of right eye twitches, worse
chewing. Vision becomes clouded. Turbid corpus vitreum (Arn., Ham., Phos.). Transient blindness. Colored
circles before eyes. In evening, candles appear surrounded by a rainbowlike halo.
Female - Profuse menses, black like ink. Menses too early, profuse, preceded and with violent backache.
Burning pains in the ovarian region only during menses (Zinc, after menses). Leucorrhea.
Food - Better hot food. Aversion to beef, eggs, meat, veal. Worse from eating veal, causing headache,
diarrhea. Worse from cold food, fats, rich food, milk. Worse from beef, fish, lobster, oysters. Worse from beer,
wine, bread, coffee, rice, soup, watery fruits and vegetables.
Head - Headache with vertigo, as if falling to right side and backwards, worse stooping. Head pain, better
motion of carriage. Pains in occiput, better letting hair down. Scalp very sensitive.
Heart - Violent stitch in précordia and beating of heart. Palpitations, worse lying. Pulse is weak, small and
thready.
Kidneys - Diabetes insipidus. Dull kidney pains. Burning in urethra while urinating and greatly diminished
urine. Frequentand profuse emission of clear urine.
Limbs - Drawing in limbs with paralytic weakness. Rheumatic pains and stitches in limbs and joints. Stitches
between shoulder blades. Tearing and sticking in shoulders and joints. Hands and fingers seem swollen.
Lungs - Rapid gasping breathing, sits upright. Congestion of right lung. Dyspnea so great that breath cannot
be held long enough to drink, though thirsty. Asthma with excessive dyspnea, nausea, dull stitches and
burning in chest. Spasmodic croup, paroxysm of crowing. Bronchitis with sharp, short, dry, hacking cough.
Acute exacerbations in tuberculosis. Dry, morning cough with pain in the chest and bloody expectoration. Sour-
smelling expectoration. Expectoration of clotted blood after hawking mucus.
Modalities - Better lying down, lying on right side, uncovering head, gentle motion, drinking water in sips.
Worse cold, damp, taking cold, morning, afternoon. Worse lying with head low, walking, breathing, eating veal,
coffee, wine, beer.
Mouth - Tongue loaded with a white coating. Tongue red with burning pimples. Burning blister at tip of tongue.
Crawling on tongue. Taste disagreeable, nauseous, disgusting, sour. Fetid breath. Throat constricted and sore.
Nose - Violent coryza with obstruction of nose, and loss of smell. Sneezing. Swollen feeling, worse in the right
nostril. Burning in nose with digging and clawing pain. The nasal bones are painful, especially to the touch.
Swelling of interior of nose. Ulcers in the nostrils covered by a scurf. Nosebleed with acrid blood. Polyps (Thuj.,
Sang-n.). Point red and itching.
Perspiration - Profuse perspiration every alternate night (Nit-ac.).
Rectum - Frequent pressing in rectum. Urgent want to evacuate with tenesmus. Dysentery with much cutting
pain, great thirst and icy coldness of feet. Diarrhea from eating veal. Membranous shreds with tenesmus.
 Thin, watery dark, bloody stools. Feces difficult, and retarded, evacuated with much effort. Hard like sheep's
dung.
Skin - Lancinations in skin. Pricking like needles, followed by burning. Tubercles, size of a pea. Burning
vesicles filled with yellowish serum, which break when scratched. Sudden dropsical swelling.
Sleep - Drowsiness during day. Disturbed sleep at night, constant dreaming, with frequent awakening. Anxious
and uneasy dreams about dangerous situations. Nightmare. Coma.
Stomach - Faint-like weakness at stomach pit. Epigastric or sub-sternal pains go towards axilla. Gnawing,
spasmodic weakness, and pressure on epigastrium. Burning in stomach. Severe pain after every meal.
Nausea, as if about to vomit worse at night. Ineffectual retching. Vomiting of mucus, mixed with blood.
Teeth - Toothache, with sharp drawing, or tearing pains in teeth and head. Shooting in carious teeth, when
touched. Pulsative toothache, at night, worse by cold things. Swelling of gums, of an inflammatory or scorbutic
character, they bleed readily.
Temperature - External coldness, chin, skin. Extraordinary shiverings not better by hot drinks or coverings.
Coldness in afternoon with thirst, or coldness, preceded by headache. Quotidian fever, with drawing pains in
limbs. Profuse and colliquative sweat. Sweat in morning, especially on chest. Internal burning.
Throat - Laryngeal diphtheria. Sore throat with shooting pain. Nocturnal pain in throat, as if it were contracting.
Impeded swallowing from tension and cutting in the larynx. Hoarseness. Loss of speech.
Vertigo - Fainting fits with vertigo in morning, worse on standing, better sitting down. Vertigo and tinnitus.
COMMENTS - Kali-n. has been extensively proved by homeopaths and symptoms have been added from
cases of poisoning, so that its characteristics are well defined. It is almost equal to Kali-c. in producing stitching
pains and it is similar to it in having a cough at 3 a.m.
Severe stitching, cutting, lancinating, tearing and pressing pains. As with many other Kalis, there is external
sensitiveness of scalp, of abdomen, of testes.
Kali nitricum
Diabetes insipidus. Bedwetting. Painful colic. Diarrhea and dysentery. Sexual excitement. Pain in testes and
cords. Menorrhagia with flow of ink-like blackness.
“The pain-like contraction in the eyes, forehead and face concentrates in the tip of the nose. Swollen feeling
in right nostril, which is painful on pressure, sore pain in upper part of right nostril with external sensitiveness,”
these two last symptoms led to the cure of large nasal polyps in a girl.
In a poisoning case, during the recovery there was intense vertigo with tinnitus, which should indicate Kali-n.
in some cases of Meniere's disease. Easy intoxication by wine or beer was noted by several provers. A peculiar
symptom is a sour taste in the throat.
In the asthmatic state the breathlessness is so great that the patient, though thirsty, can only drink a sip at a
time between the breaths. Allen defined the asthma of Kali-n. as asthma with excessive dyspnea, faintness
and nausea with dull stitches or with burning pain in chest, rather free expectoration.
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Op., Nit-s-d. It antidotes opium or morphine poisoning, 8 to 10 grains to glass of
water. Compare: ( 1 ) Cann-s. which contains a large amount of Kali-n. (2) Lyc., Sang., All-s., Ant-i.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Kali Oxalicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kali-ox. Kali oxalicum. Potassium bioxalate. Kali oxalas. Salts of sorrel. Trituration. Solution.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Cramps. Eyes inflamed. Lumbago. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Only cases of poisoning have been observed with this salt. The main symptoms of Kali-ox.
are those of violent irritation. Convulsions. Violent and continuous vomiting. Throbbing in the head with great
thirst. Cramps. Severe pains in the back (Ox-ac., Rumx-a.). Coldness and collapse. One patient became
insane.
MIND - Extreme depression. Insanity.
Abdomen - Violent pains in abdomen and convulsions. Scalding sensation extended over abdomen with
tenderness on tolerably firm pressure.
Back - Pain in back. Severe lumbar pain.
Bladder - Urination accompanied by a sensation of scalding.
Eyes - Great soreness of eyes with dim vision. Conjunctive injected, pupils dilated.
Face - Countenance flushed. Face pale, anxious-looking and covered with a cold sweat. Face and lips pale
with continual riggers over whole body.
Food - Great thirst and throbbing pain in head.
 Head - Swimming in head, heaviness, throbbing pain and great thirst.
Kidneys - Urination accompanied by a sensation of scalding.
Limbs - Spasmodic contractions in hands. Great weakness in lower limbs. Cramps in legs. Muscular
weakness. Falls and utters loud cries. Tendency to faint. Lying on the floor quite faint. Nails and fingers blue.
Mouth - Tongue and fauces red and irritable. Very strong acid taste of poison lasting two days.
Skin - Cold and clammy.
Stomach - Vomiting and faintness. Vomiting, continuing at intervals of ten minutes to an hour for nearly a
week. Very severe burning pain in stomach and bowels. Excruciating pain, followed by violent convulsions and
death.
Temperature - Sensations of coldness, succeeded by burning heat in chest and stomach and general
muscular weakness. Continued rigors affecting whole body.
Throat - Scalding sensation in throat and stomach.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Cramps. Eyes inflamed. Lumbago. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Only cases of poisoning have been observed with this salt. The main symptoms of Kali-ox.
are those of violent irritation. Convulsions. Violent and continuous vomiting. Throbbing in the head with great
thirst. Cramps. Severe pains in the back (Ox-ac., Rumx-a.). Coldness and colla

name: Kali Permanganicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kali-perm. Kali permanganicum. Potassium permanganate. Permanganate of potash. Kali
manganicum. Kali hypermanganicum. Solution in distilled water. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bites. Cough. Diphtheria. Gastritis. Opium poisoning. Ozaena. Salivation. Snakebites. Throat,
sore. Uvula, swollen. Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-perm, is a well-known disinfectant and has been chiefly used in medicine as a local
application in diphtheria and other conditions where there are fetid discharges. Kali-perm, counteracts the
effects of alkaloids of many poisonous plants owing to its oxidizing powers, if given before the alkaloid has
been absorbed.
A case of opium poisoning is reported in which an ounce of laudanum had been swallowed by mistake. Kali-
perm, in dilute solution (2 grains to the pint) was given repeatedly and acted promptly. The next day, only
dryness of mouth and throat was felt. Intense irritation of nose, throat and larynx.
Kraft, who used it largely in diphtheria, dissolved a few grains in a tumbler of water, sufficient to make it very
red. A teaspoonful of this was put into another tumbler of water and a teaspoonful out of the second tumbler
was given every hour or two.
Various septic conditions, the tissues are infiltrated with tendency to sloughing. Bites of snakes and for other
animal poisons (Led.). Dysmenorrhea.
Diphtheria, with extreme fetor of the breath and bloody discharges from the nose and intense prostration.
Intense irritation of nose, throat and larynx with bloody and bloody discharges and constant inclination and
constant flow of ropy mucus from the stomach. The uvula was swollen and red. Back - Muscles of neck feel
sore.
Chest - Aching in region of cricoid cartilage, worse every attempt to swallow.
Ears - Sharp pricking pains extending from throat to left mastoid process, apparently along Eustachian tube.
Eyes - Profuse lachrymation.
Face - Face hot.
Food - Appetite lost. Thirst, inability to drink.
Head - Head feels full.
Kidneys - Compelled to urinate frequently.
Urine copious, clear, watery.
Limbs - Legs feel as though he could not move them, tremble on attempting to stand.
Lungs - Short, hacking cough, with a constant, painful urging to swallow, with blood-streaked sputa.
Mouth - Fetor of breath. Mouth and lips very dry, lips smart when exposed to cold air. Increased flow of saliva
runs constantly out of the mouth. Swollen uvula. Speech painful, difficult, hoarse.
Nose - Posterior sinuses painful. Nasal discharge smart and irritates. Bloody discharge, nose feels stuffed and
full as in catarrh. Profuse bleeding from nose.
Rectum - Obstinate constipation.
Skin - Profuse sweat.
Sleep - Restless at night. Sleepless.
Stomach - Hot, burning pain in stomach.
Sickening pain in stomach. Nausea and constant inclination to swallow. Nausea and vomiting.
Throat - Constrictive, smarting sensation in throat. Swollen and painful. Larynx feels raw. Everything hawked
 up streaked with blood. Constant inclination to swallow.
COMMENTS - Potassium permanganate is recognized as being the most effective chemical antidote in cases
of morphine or opium poisoning, acting directly on the morphine and oxidizing it to less toxic substances.
To be effective, the permanganate must come in direct contact with the opium or morphine in the stomach.
The treatment is administration of two to five grains of potassium permanganate in dilute aqueous solution as
soon as possible after the poison is taken, this amount to be increased if very large doses of the poison have
been taken.
Washing out the stomach with a quantity of 1 to 500 solution of permanganate is also recommended, using at
least a pint of this solution either by a stomach pump or by enforced vomiting.
RELATIONS - Kali-perm, antidotes opium. Compare: (1) Other oxidizing salts, especially Kah-bi., also Mang.,
Caust., Kali-c. (2) in edematous uvula, Mur-ac., Apis. (3) in diphtheria, Diph., Merc-cy., Arum-t., Kali-bi., Kali-
m., (4) in thick, ropy mucus, Kali-bi.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Kali Phosphoricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kali-p. Kali phosphoricum. Potassium phosphate. Trituration. Solution in distilled water.
Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Agoraphobia. Alopecia, areata. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Aphthae. Asthma. Atrophy. Bedwetting.
Brain, concussion. Brain-fag. Brain, softening. Cancrum oris. Carbuncle. Cerebral, anemia. Chilblains.
Cholera. Constipation. Coughs. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Emaciation. Enterocolitis.
Erysipelas. Face, neuralgia. Fatigue. Feet, fidgety. Gangrene. Hay fever. Headaches. Hernia.
Hypochondriasis. Hysteria. Impotency. Insomnia. Leucorrhea. Leukemia. Melancholia. Memory, weak.
Menstrual, disorders. Miscarriage. Nervous, prostration. Neurasthenia. Night-terrors. Noma. Nosebleeds.
Nymphomania. Ozaena. Palpitations. Paralysis. Pemphigus. Pneumonia. Ptosis. Puerperal fever. Puerperal
mania. Pulmonary, edema. Seasickness. Sciatica. Scurvy. Stomach, ulcer. Typhoid fever. Typhus fever.
Ulcers. Urticaria. Vertigo. Weakness. Whitlow. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Schiissler used this remedy for conditions arising from want of nerve power. According to
Schiissler, Kali-p. is contained in the cells of the brains, nerves, muscles, blood (corpuscles and plasma) and
intercellular fluids.
A disturbance in the motions of its molecules produces despondency, anxiety, fearfulness, fearfulness,
homesickness, suspiciousness, agoraphobia, and weak memory. There is
Kali phosphoricum at first a small and frequent pulse, later it is retarded.
Pain with sensation of paralysis in sensory nerves. Weakness of muscles and nerves even to paralysis.
Retarded nutrition, even total arrest in a limited area of cells and then a softening.
Cases in which there is increased sensitivity to all impressions from a weakness of the vital resistance or
control. In weakened states from mental or physical shock, from over strain or over drain of the system.
H. T. Doge noted that it is indicated for worn-out nursing mothers, tired to distraction by nervous babies. Wom-
out business and professional men or women, or students. Doge recommended the higher potencies where
indications are close.
Characteristic low, nervous condition. Generally nervous, sensitive, weak and easily fagged by slight
causes like pain, worry, mental fatigue etc. Conditions arising from lack of nerve power, neurasthenia, and
mental and physical depression. Nervous prostration. Weak and tired.
Marked disturbance of the sympathetic nervous system, usually from excitement, overwork and wony.
Convalescence after exhausting diseases. Muscular weakness after acute diseases. States of weakness and
decay, gangrenous conditions. Suspected malignant tumors. Delayed labor.
Putrid, carrion like odor of secretions, foul odor of the body. Foul breath, with brownish mustard-like coat on
the tongue. Secretions are golden yellow. Emaciation, wasting diseases. After surgery, when in the healing
process the skin is drawn tight over the wound, especially cancer.
Stitching pains. Dull, heavy ache between the shoulders. Paralytic weakness or pain with sensation of
paralysis. Paralysis infantile during dentition. Nervous, restless, fidgety feeling in feet, trembling sensation in
muscles of legs. Numb sensations.
Sexual excitement from indulgence or suppression. Irregular, menses, pulse, etc. Seasickness without nausea.
Especially adapted to the young.
MIND - Mental and physical prostration caused by a combination of overworking and psychological factors
like excitement, worry and vexation. Mental fatigue from over study or overwork. Brain fatigue. Mental
exertion aggravates.
 Ailments from strong emotions, fright, grief, care. Extreme lassitude and depression, lethargy, gloom. Morose.
Great despondency about business. Slightest labor seems a heavy task. Dullness of mind. Weak memory.
Forgetful, loss of memory.
Shyness, disinclined to converse. Indisposition to meet people or to talk with them. Sighing ormoaning.
Homesickness. Sadness on waking. Weariness of life and fear of death. Negative, dark forebodings.
Very nervous, starts easily. Anxiety and worry. Anxiety with nervous dread. Apprehensive about future. Fear
of being alone, open spaces, crowds. Fear about his health, of death.
Angry. Irritability when spoken to. Impatience about trifles. Gloomy moods. Dwelling upon grievances.
Suspicious. Obstinate. Perverted affections. Aversion to own family, cruel to husband, baby.
Easily frightened. Starting from noise, when touched. Sensitive to light and noise, especially during menses.
Disposition to feel bodily pains too acutely. Oversensitive children. Children cry and scream, fly into passion,
can hardly articulate. Night terrors. Shyness, excessive blushing, from undue sensitiveness.
Hysterical fits of laughter and crying. Weeping about trifles. Religious melancholy, believes she is eternally
and irretrievably damned. Continually weeping and crying. Wringing hands. Tears things. Pulling to pieces and
tearing her clothing, as well as bed covering. Doesn't recognize her surroundings.
Abdomen - Abdomen feels cold, better covering. Cutting pain in abdomen. Affections of spleen. Splenic
leukemia. Enterocolitis. Hernia. Flatulence with distress about heart.
Back - Stiffness of back after rest, better gentle motion. Paralytic lameness of back, must lean on a chair.
Rheumatic pains
and weakness. Spinal irritation. Creeping sensation and intense pain along spine, relieves the headache.
Constitutions - Weak nervous system and brain. Suited to pale, sensitive, irritable persons.
Causations - Ill effects of mechanical injuries, grief, or vexation. Mental overwork.
Chest - Pain in lower part of left chest, worse coughing. Axillary sweat smells of onions.
Ears - Ulceration of the eardrum and middle ear suppurations, with foul discharge. Sensitive hearing, cannot
endure noise. Noises in ears from nervous exhaustion. Noises in head on falling asleep. Humming and
buzzing in the ears. Deafness from atrophic condition of nerve.
Eyes - Burn, sting, with a lot of tears. Yellowgray milky secretion. Retinitis. Drooping of eyelids, especially the
left (Caust.). Squint after brain diseases. Weakness of vision. Loss of perceptive power, after diphtheria from
exhaustion. Black spots before eyes.
Face - Sad, careworn look. Livid and sunken with hollow eyes. Neuralgia of face followed by great weakness.
Right-sided neuralgia, relieved by cold applications. Sharp pains from riding in cold air. Brown stripe at the
edge of hair.
Female - Delayed menses with depression. Menses irregular. Menses too late or too scanty in pale, initable.
sensitive, lachrymose females. Menses, too profuse discharge. Menses, deep-red or black- red, thin and not
coagulating. Menses, sometimes with offensive odor. Horribly foul leucorrhea. Periodical discharge of
copious orange colored fluid from vagina and rectum. Intense sexual desire for days afterthe menses. Tired,
worn out, nervous women, subject to miscarriage. Feeble and ineffectual labor pains. Puerperal fever with
absurd notions or mania.
Food - Hungry soon after eating. Wants to eat almost every hour. No appetite except for sweets. Craves ice
cold water, cold drinks, vinegar, sweets. Aversion to food, bread and meat.
Head - Excruciating nervous headache with great sensitiveness to noise. Headache of students, worse
mental exertion. Occipital pain, better after rising. Pains and weight at back of head, with feeling of weariness
and exhaustion. Cerebral anemia. Headache with weary, empty, gone feeling at stomach (Ign., Sep.), with
hunger. Headaches worse before and during menses. Headache are relieved by gentle motion.
Heart - Sluggish circulation in sensitive, nervous subjects. Weak action of heart causes fainting. Palpitations
with shortness of breath, with nervousness, anxiety, sleeplessness Palpitations, worse slightest motion or
ascending stairs. Intermittent action of heart from violent emotions, fright, grief, care. Pulse irregular.
Kidneys - Nocturnal bedwetting, in nervous, excitable children and in old people. Incontinence of urine. Very
yellow urine, saffron yellow or milky. Bleeding from urethra. Urine comes in stops and starts.
Limbs - Paralytic lameness in back and limbs. Paralyzing pain in limbs, better motion and external warmth,
worse during rest. Exertion aggravates. Pains with depression and subsequent exhaustion. Prickling in hands
and feet. Numb fingertips. Feet fidgety. Chilblains. Foot feels frostbitten. Pains in soles.
Lungs - Nervous asthma, least food aggravates. Short breath, worse going upstairs. Cough with yellow
expectoration. Whooping cough in highly nervous patients with great exhaustion. Frothy, expectoration with
pulmonary edema.
Male - Nocturnal emissions. Sexual excitement. Impotency. Sexual power diminished. Prostration and weak
vision after sex or after nightly emissions (Kali-c.).
 Modalities - Better from warmth, rest, sleep, gentle motion, leaning against something. Better from
nourishment, eating, when menses comes. Worse mental and physical exertion, anxiety and worry. Worse
from slight causes. Worse from cold, dry air, cold drinks, eating. Worse puberty, sex, excitement, touch, pain,
early morning.
Mouth - Aphthae. Breath offensive, fetid. Palate feels greasy. Mouth excessively dry. in morning. Gums,
spongy, receding, with bright-red seam. Noma. Slow speech, becoming inarticulate. Nervous, chattering of
teeth.
Nose - Hay fever with nervous irritability. Hay fever, as a prophylactic. Itching in posterior sinuses. Violent
sneezing with symptoms of fresh cold, at 2 a.m. Ozaena. Nasal disease with offensive odor. Fetid discharge.
Nosebleeds.
Perspiration - Excessive, exhausting, strong-smelling sweats. Axillary sweat smells of onions.
Rectum - Diarrhea, foul, putrid odor. Diarrhea caused by fright. Diarrhea with depression and exhaustion.
Brain affection with diarrhea smelling like carrion. Diarrhea, at night and after eating. Dysentery, stools consist
of pure blood, patient becomes delirious, abdomen swells. Cholera, rice water stools (Verat., Ars., Jatr.). Hot,
golden yellow stools. Painless stools. Prolapse rectum (Ign., Podo.). Paretic condition of rectum and colon
after removal of hemorrhoids.
Sensations - As if tongue would cleave to root of mouth, as if a ball were rising in throat, as if a rocket had
passed through head.
Skin - Skin diseases with bad smelling discharge. Greasy, offensive smelling crusts or scales. Ulcers,
ichorous, bad smelling. Vesicles with bloody, ichorous contents. Pemphigus. Urticaria. Erysipelas bordering
on gangrene. Gangrene. Blue spots on skin. Skin inactive. Cold skin. Jaundiced.
Sleep - Drowsy. Yawning. Sleeplessness from worry, over study, business troubles. Sleeplessness from
overactive mind. Restlessness and heat during sleep. Sleepwalking. Sighing and moaning during sleep.
Amorous dreams. Night terrors. Awakening with fright and screaming. Loss of sleep.
Stomach - Indigestion with great nervous depression. Gastritis with failing strength. Nervous, gone sensation
at the pit of stomach, bettereating (Ign., Sep., Sulph.).
Hungry soon after eating. Feels seasick without nausea. Nausea, better belchings, worse coughing.
Teeth - Nervous chattering of teeth. Toothache, with easily-bleeding gums. Gums spongy andreceding (Caps.,
Ham., Lach.). Toothache of highly nervous, delicate, pale, irritable, sensitive persons.
Temperature - Subnormal temperature.
Yellow fever.
Throat - Aphonia. Paralysis of vocal cords. Hoarseness from overexertion of voice. Croup, last stage.
Sensation as if a ball rising in throat. Gangrenous sore throat.
Tongue - Tongue coated brownish, yellow like liquid mustard. Sensation as if tongue would adhere to roof of
mouth from dryness of mouth. Creeping paralysis of the tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo from fatigue, from lying down, when facing the sun, on standing up from sitting, when looking
upward (Gran.).
COMMENTS - Chronic fatigue from excessive mental work or over-exertion of the mind; the mind and nervous
system become weak. Mental fatigue. Headaches from over studying. Nervous insomnia (Aven.). Memory loss
and difficultly concentrating in the elderly. Pain in the back of neck and head. General irritability, great
despondency.
Depressed states of mind and body. Hypochondriasis, hysteria. Neurasthenia. Great lassitude, emaciation.
Nervous, hot, restless, easily startled. The least touch causes starting. Trembling of hands from nervousness.
Stitching pains. Numb fingertips.
Spasms of irritable weakness, paralysis. Progressive muscular atrophy, around ulcer of stomach. Typhoid,
typhus fever. Septic states, septic fevers and hemorrhages. Phagedenic chancre, carbuncles. Toothache
alternating with headache. Alopecia areata. Scurvy.
Menstrual headaches, backaches with menses. Severe vaginitis with yellow- brown, offensive discharge
(Kreos.). Worse after sex and sensitiveness to touch. Aching in sacrum. Frequent urination, passing large
quantities night and day, containing phosphates.
H. C. Allen noted the indications of waking in the early morning, the peculiar mouth and the severe action on
the skin. Characteristic golden or orange-yellow color. Urine is very yellow. Allen gave the remedy for
sleeplessness, and cured an old pelvic abscess with orange colored discharge.
W. T. Laird pointed out that Kali-p. cures a nervous dyspepsia almost identical with that of Anae. The Kali-p.
patient is more decidedly neurasthenic than the other and the relapses, which are frequent in both, are mostly
due to dietetic errors in Anae, cases and to excitement or worry in the Kali-p. cases.
H. M. Rean reported cures in cases of amenorrhea. One young woman, who was very nervous, pale blonde,
 skin rather waxy, cross and snappish, but cried easily, had a constant dull headache, yet was very drowsy all
day.
Fidgety, at times could not control herself, and called her mother to hold her hands. Menses did not appear
until eighteen and were scanty then and since. Kali-p. 3x four times daily caused great improvement at next
menstrual period. In three months the menses were regular and normal, and in five months the patient was
perfectly well.
J. C. Nottingham considered a leading indication of Kali-p. “nervousness arising from excessive sexual
excitement, whether indulged or suppressed.” He has cured impotence and seminal losses on these
indications.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Zinc., Gels., Cimic., Lach., Mur-ac. (2) Kali-hp. (3) Mac- roz.- extreme debility
after severe illness, collapse. Macroz., weariness from no assignable cause, no pains. Boring pain at vertex,
vomiting and retching all night, impossible to eyes, giddiness and cold. (4) Genist.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Kali Silicicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kali-sil. Kali silicicum. Potassium silicate. Silicate of potash. Historical dose: Trituration and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Backache. Chilly. Constipation. Diarrhea. Eczema. Emaciation. Flatulence. Headaches.
Leucorrhea. Nasal catarrh. Nausea. Photophobia. Vertigo. Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-sil. is a deep acting remedy. Marked lassitude. Desire to lie down all the time. Absent-
minded, anxious indolent, timid. Feeble will power. Emaciation. Head congested, blood surges from body to
head. Nasal catarrh, discharge bloody, excoriating offensive. Nose, swollen, ulcerated.
Stiffness over body and limbs. Creeping sensation over limbs. Twitching of muscles. Weak and weary. Weight
in stomach after eating, naùsea, pain, flatulence. Pain in liver region. Constipation. Construction of anus during
stool. Vertigo, coldness of head, photophobia.
MIND - Absent-minded. Confusion from mental exertion. Anxious. Indolent. Timid. Feeble willpower. Mental
troubles worse consolation. Irritability and irresolution, after sex.
Eyes - Eyes better from heat. Photophobia.
Female - Backache during menses. Leucorrhea, excoriating, yellow, worse after menses. Eruptions on vulva.
Itching of vulva.
Head - Head congested. Blood surges from body to head. Coldness of head. Headaches, worse from cold air.
Headaches worse after sex, mental exertion, stooping and exerting the eyes. Headaches better warmth and
wrapping head up.
Limbs - Creeping sensation over limbs. Stiffness of body and limbs. Twitching of muscles. Weak and weary
limbs. Gouty nodosities. Offensive sweat on feet and between toes.
Liver - Pains in liver region.
Modalities - Better heat, summer. Worse open air, drafts, cold, winter, uncovering, bathing. Worse exertion,
motion.
Nose - Nasal catarrh. Discharge bloody, excoriating, offensive. Nose swollen, ulcerated. Discharge and breath
offensive.
Rectum - Constipation. Diarrhea, after midnight and at night. Painful diarrhea, during menses. Stools
insufficient and difficult even though soft. Stools bloody, frequent, offensive, purulent and watery. Constriction
of anus during stool. Itching of anus after stool.
Skin - Injuries and small wounds that suppurate and refuse to heal. Eczema. Warts, painful, stinging,
suppurating, withering.
Stomach - Nausea, pain, flatulence. Weight in stomach after eating. Aversion to meat.
Temperature - Chilly, weak, wants to keep still and rest.
Vertigo - Vertigo while sitting and stooping.
REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Kali Sulphuricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-kali-s. Kali sulphuricum. Potassium sulphate. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritic nodes. Asthma. Bronchitis. Cataract. Catarrh. Chorea. Colds. Constipation. Dandruff.
Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Epithelioma. Eustachian catarrh. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Headache. Hemorrhoids.
 Intermittent fever. Leucorrhea. Metrorrhagia. Nails, diseased. Nasal, catarrh. Nettle-rash. Ophthalmia. Orchitis.
Otorrhea. Ozaena. Palpitations. Pneumonia. Polyps. Psoriasis. Rheumatism. Rhus poisoning. Scabies.
Scaldhead. Seborrhea. Sinusitis. Skin, disorders. Suppurations. Toothache. Vertigo. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-s., introduced by Schiissler, affects respiration, mucus membranes and skin where it
causes desquamation. Schiissler explains that Kali-s., in reciprocal action with iron, effects the transfer of the
inhaled oxygen to all the cells and is contained in all the cells containing iron.
When a sulphate and any oxide of iron come into contact with decomposing organic substances they surrender
their oxygen and form sulphate of iron. With more oxygen added, this may be further decomposed into
sulphuric acid and an oxide of iron.
A deficiency of Kali-s. causes a sensation of heaviness and weariness, vertigo, chilliness, palpitations of the
heart, anxiety, sadness, toothache, headache and pain in the limbs. Symptoms are worse in a warm room and
towards evening, better in open, cool air.
Catarrh of larynx, bronchi, nostrils, etc., with yellow discharges. Catarrh of the stomach where the tongue has
a yellowish mucus coating. Profuse and deep yellow discharges, thin or sticky.
Ailments accompanied by profuse desquamation. Suppurations. Yellow, mucus and serous discharges,
profuse and intermittent. Later stages of inflammation. Wandering pains, wandering rheumatism (Puls., Kali-
bi.). Stitching, tearing, festering pains that shift about.
Torpid processes. Lack of reaction. Warmblooded. Oxaluria. Facilitates the formation of new epithelium.
Epithelial cancer. Interrupted growth of nails. Gonorrhea and ophthalmia neonatorum (Puls.).
MIND-Alwayshurried. Irritable. Timid. Confusion and restlessness, worse in a warm room. Mental exertion
aggravates. Desires and then rejects things. Desire to lie down, but lying aggravates so must walk for relief.
. Anxiety, better in the open air. Anxiety in evening. Frightened at trifles. Fear of falling, of losing her reason.
Claustrophobia with fear of suffocation.
Abdomen - Colicky pains, abdomen feels cold to touch. Abdomen cold and distended after eating. Hard,
ascites, in whooping cough. Empty feeling in hypogastrium, better passing flatus.
Back - Pain in nape. Stiff neck, head inclined towards left. Rheumatic pains in back and limbs, worse in warm
room, better cool open air.
Causations - Ill effects of chill when over heated. Injuries.
Chest - Anxiety in chest.
Ears - Eustachian deafness. Stinking otorrhea. Bro wn offensive secretion from right ear. Offensive discharge
with polyps. Discharge of yellow matter (Hydr.). Watery, sticky, thin discharge.
Eyes - Purulent yellow mucus in eye diseases. Sticky, watery discharge from eyes. Thin, yellow crusts on
eyelids. Cataract. Ophthalmia neonatorum.
Face - Aches in heated room, better cool open air. Epithelioma.
Female - Menses too late, scanty. Menses with a feeling of weight in the abdomen. Metrorrhagia. Leucorrhea,
yellowish, watery.
Food - Burning thirst. Craves sweets, cold food, cold drinks. Dread of hot drinks. Averse to and worse from
eggs.
Head - Rheumatic headache, beginning in evening. Headaches worse warm room, better open air. Headache
during menses. Great pain on moving head from side to side or backwards. Dandruff yellow, moist and
sticky. Scaldhead. Bald spots, after gonorrhea.
Kidneys - Albuminuria after scarlatina. Oxaluria. Pyelitis.
Limbs - Rheumatism. Rheumatic pains, worse heat, evening, better cold weather or cold applications. Pain in
back and limbs, worse in a warm room. Shifting, wanderingpains. Arthritic nodes. Cold hands and feet. Scaly
eruption on arms, better hot water. Diseased condition of nails.
Lungs - Asthma with yellow, slimy expectoration, easily expelled. Coarse rales in lungs. Bronchitis, mucus is
distinctly yellow and slimy, thin, or watery matter and profuse. Rattling of mucus in lungs (Ant-t.). Post-
influenza cough, especially in children. Cough, worse in evening and in hot atmosphere. Croupy cough (Hep.,
Spong.). Pneumonia with wheezing. Yellow, loose rattling mucus is coughed up with difficulty. Sputum
consists of watery matter. Whooping cough.
Male - Gonorrhea, slimy, yellowish, green discharges. Gleet. Orchitis after suppressed gonorrhea.
Modalities - Better from walking, fasting, discharge of flatus, cool, open air. Worse in evening (Puls.), noise,
consolation. Cannot stand warm rooms or other forms of heat. Worse warm air, warm wraps, warm
weather, heated room.
Mouth - Mouth breathing, snoring. Insipid, pappy taste. Loss of taste and smell. Tongue coated yellow and
slimy. Yellow mucus coating on tongue. Painful gums. Toothache, worse warm room and toward evening,
better cool open air. Blistered lips and mouth. Lower lip swollen. Epithelioma on lip.
 Nose - Colds with ayellow,slimy discharge. Yellow, thick discharge, alternating with watery discharge.
Sinusitis with thick yellow, green discharges. Nose obstructed. Loss of smell and taste (Nat-m.). Swelling of
the nasal pharyngeal mucus membrane, remaining after removal of adenoids.
Perspiration - Profuse, easy sweat.
Rectum - Constipation with hemorrhoids (Sulph.). Stools large like sheep's dung. Black, thin, offensive
stools. Stools light-colored and bilious. Yellow, slimy diarrhea.
Skin - Dry skin. Itching, worse heat. Peeling, flaking of skin. Psoriasis (Ars., Thyr.). Intertrigo. Eczema,
burning, itching, papular eruption. Desquamation of skin. Promotes desquamation after erysipelas.
Accelerates removal of scabs in smallpox. Nettle rash. Yellow scales. Favus. Yellow skin jaundice. Skin
affections with yellow, slimy discharge. Ulcers, ooze thinyeZ/ow water. Polyps. Epithelioma. Suppressed rash
of measles or other eruptive diseases, with harsh and dry skin. Seborrhea. Scabs with yellow pus.
Ringworm of scalp or beard with abundant scales. Scabies. Rhus poisoning.
Sleep - Sleeplessness from heat, warm room. Vivid, terrifying dreams of ghosts, death, robbers, murder.
Dreams with violent struggling in their sleep.
Stomach - Burning thirst. Pressure and feeling of fullness in stomach. Sensation as if a heavy load on stomach.
Sensation of faintness in stomach with befogged
feeling in head. Catarrh of stomach and duodenum. Nausea, and vomiting.
Temperature - Chilliness. Cold hands and feet. Intermittent fever. Temperature rises at night.
Throat - Croupy hoarseness (Hep., Spong.). Constant scraping. Sore throat and hoarseness after catching a
cold. Every cold settles in larynx.
Vertigo - Dreadful vertigo on rising from lying, on standing from sitting. Vertigo when looking upwards. Vertigo
with a fear of falling.
COMMENTS - Useful for chronic Puls, conditions, recurring earaches, asthma, respiratory problems, when
Puls, doesn't cure completely. Yellow discharges, thick and bland, especially from the sinuses and lungs.
Rattling mucus (Ant-t.). Wandering arthritis, worse hot applications and hot baths.
Desquamation. Skin conditions with flaking and peeling. Psoriasis, eczema, dandruff. Scabs with yellow pus.
Ulcers ooze yellow, watery fluid. Skin cancer. Tongue can be yellow with a slimy coating. General
sluggishness.
Modalities similarto Puls. Worse in warm, stuffy rooms, at twilight, better fresh air. Thirstless. Better walking in
the fresh, open air. Mood changes and can weep easily. Claustrophobic with fear of suffocation.
M. E. Douglass reported an asthma case with a lot of thick, yellow expectoration. Much rattling in chest, with
labored breathing and talking almost impossible, this was cured with Kali-s. 3x, five grains every hour in the
attack.
Hansen cured with Kali-s. a case of psoriasis beginning on the right leg, later attacking the left elbow and left
leg. Eruption, papular, oval and annular with paler centers, covered with whitish scales, skin beneath red and
smooth. The guiding symptom was “great desquamation of the epidermis.”
RELATIONS - Antidote to: Rhus poisoning. Compare: (1) Kali-s., Puls., Kali-bi., Nairn. (2) Puls., Kali-bi. (3)
Hydr. - dyspepsia, epithelioma. (4) Chr-ac. 3x. - produces in the nasal passages very fine threads from the
septum to external wall, disorders of nasal fosse
and hay fever. Chronic colds. Sneezing, red, watery eyes, irritation of mucus membrane. Compatible: Acet-
ac. (itching and redness of skin), Calc., Hep., Puls., Rhus-t., Sep., Sil., Sulph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Kali Tartaricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kali-t. Kali tartaricum. Potassium tartrate. Cream of tartar. Tartrate of potash. Trituration.
Sohition. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Colitis. Debility. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Flatulence. Paraplegia. Vomiting. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - A few symptoms of this well-known substance are collected in Allen's works. Among them,
pain in loins and paraplegia are very noticeable. Emaciation. Extreme weakness, can scarcely walk. Vomiting
of black-green fluid. Feces look like coffee-grounds. Pain in umbilical region with great thirst.
Abdomen - Pain in umbilical region with thirst. Flatulence and griping. Pain in loins.
Limbs - Thighs and legs paralyzed. Mouth - Tongue brown and dry.
Pulse - Pulse feeble.
Rectum - Diarrhea and violent vomiting. Feces like coffee-grounds.
Stomach - Great thirst and pain in umbilical region. Inflammation of stomach and intestines. Violent vomiting
and diarrhea. Vomits a black-green fluid.
 REFERENCES - Clarke.

***KALI TELLURICUM (Potassium Tellurate) PHARMACY-kali-tel. Kali telluricum. Potassium tellurate.
Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Insomnia. Salivation. Tongue, swelling.
HOMEOPATHIC - A few symptoms of Kali-tel. have been observed, of which the garlicky odor of the breath
was the most noticeable and persistent. Offensive breath. Tongue coated white and swollen, with salivation.
Appetite increased at first, later diminished, finally lost.
Heart - Oppression in cardiac region.
Mouth - Tongue coated white and somewhat swollen. Offensive garlicky odor in mouth. Copious secretion of
saliva.
Sleep - Sleepiness during first days.
Stomach - Inclination to vomit.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tell., Phos. and Kali-p. - garlicky odor.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Kalmia Latifolia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kalm. Kalmia latifolia. Mountain laurel. Ledum floribus bullatis. American laurel. Calico bush.
Cistus chamerhododen- dros. N. O. Ericaceae. Rocky sterile hills, near water in New England States. Flowers
May and June. Tincture of fresh leaves when the plant is in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Albuminuria. Angina, pectoris. Arthritis. Blindness. Bright's disease. Coryza. Dropsy.
Dysmenorrhea. Gastralgia. Globus hystericus. Gout. Headache. Heart, disease. Hoarseness. Locomotor,
ataxia. Lumbago. Nausea. Neuralgias. Palpitations. Ptosis. Pregnancy, albuminuria. Rheumatic, fever.
Rheumatism. Retinitis. Scleroderma. Sunheadaches. Syphilitic, sore throat. Tachycardia. Tinnitus. Tobacco,
effects. Tobacco, heart. Vertigo. Vomiting.
HERBAL - Kalmia is the name of a genus of heath worts native to North America. Kalmia latifolia, which has
large and showy flowers, is found in the northern parts of the United States.
Its flowers yield a honey said to be deleterious, and its leaves and shoots certainly are so to cattle. Dr. Meadows
says cattle eat Kalmia in the latter part of the winter when they are in want of something green.
Kalmia latifolia
K. angustifolia, probably for the same reason, has the name of lamb-kill. The powdered leaves are used as a
local remedy in some skin diseases. The hard wood of K. latifolia is used in the manufacture of various articles.
The Treasury of Botany noted that the Canadian partridge is said to become poisonous to humans after feeding
on Kalmia berries.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hering introduced Kalm. into homeopathic practice, and he, and some friends, completed
the first proving. The head, including the eyes and face, shows the majority of its action, followed by the heart.
A number of skin symptoms confirm the popular use of the leaves, among them a stiffness of the skin,
especially of the eyelids.
A heart, nerve, circulation and rheumatic remedy. In small doses, it accelerates the heart’s action, in larger
doses, it moderates it greatly. Nausea and slow pulse frequently accompany conditions.
Neuralgic pains, shoot downwards with numbness, tingling, trembling or paralytic weakness. Neuralgia
after the disappearance of herpetic eruptions. Great weakness with neuralgia. Pains of locomotor ataxia.
Protracted and continuous fevers with tympanites. Albuminuria. Paralytic sensations, pains and achings in
the limbs.
Pains shift rapidly, shooting outward along the nerves with much nausea and slow pulse. Aching, bruised,
stiff feeling. Dull tearing, crushing pain, moving downwards. Pain alternating with cardiac symptoms or between
upper and lower limbs. Rheumatism, syphilitic. Motion brings on complaints.
MIND - Confusion of brain. Memory and mental faculties are perfect in a recumbent posture, but vertigo on
attempting to move. Anxiety and palpitations. Irritable, cross. Talk of others aggravates.
Abdomen - Incarcerated flatus with nausea.
Sensation of weakness in abdomen extending to throat, better by eructation. Sudden pains in paroxysms,
across abdomen, above umbilicus. Neuralgia of bowels.
Back - Pain from neck down arm, brachial- gia. Pain down back, as if it would break.
Kalmia latifolia Pain in localized regions of spine, through the shoulders. Sharp pain in lower part • of left
scapula. Lumbar pain of nervous origin, with heat and burning. Sensation of lameness in small of back.
Drawing or sharp pain in spine.
 Chest - Angina pectoris with dyspnea and pain. Feverish heat with great pain in chest, worse when breathing
and from slightest motion. Pain in chest as from a sprain. Sharp pain in lower chest. Shooting through chest
above heart into shoulder blade. Pain in left arm. False pleurisy of winter season. Rheumatism of muscles of
thorax and back, worse from every motion.
Ears - Sharp pain in and behind right ear, at night. Acute inflammation of meatus. Sound like blowing a horn
after cracking in head. Meniere's disease.
Eyes - Stiff drawing sensation when moving eyes. Pains increased by moving the eye. Pressure in and
above right eye. Paralysis of upper lids. Stiff eyelids. Retinitis, albuminuria especially during pregnancy.
Rheumatic iritis. Scleritis. Itching in eyes, stinging when rubbing them. Eye symptoms worse evening and in
open air.
Face - Anxious expression. Flushing with vertigo. Redness of face during throbbing headache. Neuralgia,
worse right side. Neuralgia from exposure to cold, better eating, worse from worry or mental exertion.
Trigeminal neuralgia. Facial neuralgia after herpes zoster. Sharp and tearing pains in bones of jaw and face.
Itching of face at night. Tired feeling in masseters. Cracked lips with dry skin.
Female - Menses too soon. Menses regular but painful. Suppressed menses, with severe neuralgic pains
throughout whole body, with pain in limbs, back and inside of thighs. Leucorrhea, one week after menses,
aggravating other symptoms.
Head - Cracking in head, sounds like a horn blowing in the ears, frightens him. Headache worse and better
with sun. Headache begins at sunrise, worse at noon and leaves at sunset. Headache worse bright
sunlight. Headache better profuse urina-
tion. Shooting pain from nape to vertex and face. Maddening supra-orbital pain (right). Pain in front and
temporal region from head, to nape, and to teeth, from cardiac origin. Aching in forehead.
Heart - Angina pectoris with empty eructations. Heart disease, after frequent attacks of rheumatism, or
alternating with it. Tumultuous action, rapid and visible. Paroxysms of anguish around heart. Fluttering of heart
with anxiety. Pains, sharp, burning shooting, stabbing, radiating to left scapula and arm. Sharp pains take
away the breath. Tachycardia with pains (Thyr.). Severe palpitations with constriction of throat, worse motion.
Palpitations, worse leaning forward, better sitting erect. Gouty and rheumatic metastasis of heart. Shooting
through chest above heart into shoulder blades. Tobacco heart. Hypertrophy, valvular insufficiency. Aortic
obstruction. Pulse slow, weak, tremulous (Dig., Apoc.). Frequent pulse.
Kidneys - Frequent urination of large quantity of yellow urine, with sharp pains in lumbar region. Frequent
urination of scanty, hot urine. Profuse urination, better headache. Post-scarlatinal nephritis. Albuminuria with
pains in lower limbs, dropsy. Albuminuria during pregnancy.
Limbs - Pains affects a large part of a limb or several joints and pass through quickly. Weakness, numbness,
pricking and sense of coldness in limbs. Joints red, hot, swollen. Pains from hips to knees and feet. Pains
along ulnar nerve, goes into third or fourth fingers. Tingling and numbness of left arm (heart pains). Deltoid
rheumatism, especially right.
Liver - Pains in region of liver.
Lungs - Dyspnea and pressure from epigastrium toward the heart. Short-breathed, must breathe quickly,
involuntary. Difficult and oppressed breathing, throat feels swollen, nausea, with palpitations and anxiety.
Noise as from spasm of glottis when breathing. Hoarseness with coryza. Tickling in trachea. Frequent cough
caused by dryness or scraping in the throat. Expectoration easy, smooth, gray, tasting putrid, salty.
Male - Frequent, spontaneous, lasting erections without desire. Pain in the right testicle in morning, in the left
testicle in afternoon.
Modalities - Better from eating cloudy weather, continued motion, sitting, or standing upright. Worse looking
down, turning eyes, stooping, bendingforward, motion, lying on left side. Worse from heat of sun, open air,
becoming cold, from sunrise to sunset. Worse during leucorrhea.
Mouth - Tingling in salivary gland. Sublingual salivary gland inflamed. Bitter taste with nausea, better eating.
Tongue white, dry. Sharp pain in tongue. Tongue, sore left side, hurts when talking. Teeth tender, during facial
neuralgia. Pressing in molars, late in evening. Tired feeling in chewing muscles. Lips, stiff, dry, swollen.
Nose - Coryza, with increased sense of smell. Coryza with sneezing, dullness, headache and hoarseness.
Tearing in root of nose and nasal bones, with nausea.
Perspiration - Cold sweat.
Rectum - Diarrhea with dullness, dizziness, weariness, nausea and bellyache. Stools like mush, easily
discharged. Stools as if glazed, followed by pressure on rectum.
Sensations - As if something loose in head diagonally across the top. As if the body was surcharged with
electricity, as shuddering without coldness. As if something was being pressed away from under sternum.
Skin - Stiff, dry skin. Sensation of rigidity. Pricking sensation in skin with moderate sweat. Erysipelatous on
 hand with oppressed breathing. Scabies-like eruptions. Red inflamed places here and there, exceedingly
painful, as if boils would form. Scleroderma.
Sleep - Sleepless. Restless sleep, turns often. Periosteal pains prevent sleep. While sleeping, stands up and
walks about. Talks in sleep. Fantastic dreams. Dreams of murder. Wakes very early in morning.
Stomach - Crampy pain with eructation of gas. Pain in pit of stomach, worse by bendingforward, relieved
by sitting erect. Sensation of something being pressed
under the epigastrium. Warm, glowing sensation in epigastrium. Gastralgia with empty eructations. Bilious
attacks with nausea, vertigo and headache. Nausea and vomiting. Wine relieves vomiting.
Temperature - Shivering and coldness. Shaking chill in cold air; chills run over back. Protracted and continued
fevers with tympanites. Fever with burning and pain in back and loins.
Throat - Throat feels swollen. Sensation as of a ball rising. Pressure in throat, stitches in eyes and nausea.
Dryness in throat with aching pains, causing cough, difficult swallowing and thirst. Chronic syphilitic sore throat.
Tickling in trachea. Noise as from spasm in glottis when breathing. Hoarseness during coryza.
Vertigo - Vertigo with headache, nausea, blindness, pains in the limbs and weariness. Vertigo worse from
motion (Bry.), worse stooping, looking down. Vertigo with blindness.
Vision - Impaired vision. Vision becomes black on looking downward. Diplopia, from paralysis of ocular
muscles. Glimmering vision, with dimness.
COMMENTS - For paralytic weakness and trembling. Neuralgias in almost all regions, generally on the right
side. Wandering arthritis, sharp, shooting pain jumps from joint to joint. Arthritis with heart conditions or
neuralgias. Wandering rheumatic pains that travel from above downwards. Rheumatic fever.
Pain, followed by numbness in the joints (Naphtin. with sciatica). Joints can swell, become red, hot and
throbbing (Bell. ). Pains worse sunrise to sunset (Nat-m., Spig.). Painful facial neuralgias (Spig., Mag-p.).
Neuralgic pains are better from food.
Pain in the back, shuns all exertion, can hardly go up stairs. Pains in the periosteum preventing sleep. Pain
between shoulders coming up over the head. Pain with nausea and slow pulse. Pain during the early part of
the night or soon after going to sleep. Pain from a sudden chill or exposure to a sudden wind.
Tumultuous action of the heart and slow pulse. Every heartbeat has a strumming as if it would burst, along
sternum to throat. Palpitations are better lying on back and breathing, worse on left side, from mental effort.
Generally acts on the right side of the head, the left side of the chest and the left arm. Vertigo from least motion,
worse from motion (Bry.), even motion of eyes and eyelids is painful. Vertigo is worse on stooping, on looking
down, on rising from a seat.
Headache comes on in the morning, worse again in evening. Headache, worse heat, better cold. Sun
headache, worse or better with the sun. Headache and eye symptoms are worse in evening, from open air.
Rubbing eyes causes stinging in them.
Scleroderma. Cheek roughness every summer. Much external sensitiveness, face, pit of stomach, muscles of
neck sore, worse by touch.
Dry throat. Feeling as if a ball was rising in the throat. Dry, stiff, swollen, cracked lips. Tingling in the salivary
glands immediately after eating. Stitches in the tongue.
Sensation of weakness in abdomen extending to throat. Vomiting with ruminating action, without the least
nausea, better with wine. Pressure on rectum after stool. Symptoms worse during leucorrhea.
Vonder Luhe cured with Kalm. 200c an intercostal neuralgia of the left side, so intense that the patient could
not lie down or sleep at night. The chief guiding symptom was a concomitant numb sensation of the whole left
arm.
Lambert recorded the case of a gatekeeper, age 54, who had smoked since he was seven years old. He
suffered from “tobacco heart” palpitations, occurring on the least exertion or fright and sometimes awakening
him in the night. Intermittent pulse, no valvular lesion, tingling in the left arm and leg and sensation as if the
blood did not circulate in them.
He could walk, but not far. The chief complaint was a sharp pain in the right temple like pins and needles, of
eighteen months' duration. It was induced by touch
and turning the head quickly. Kalm. 3x cured the temporal neuralgia and greatly alleviated all the other
symptoms.
Proell cured with Kalm. 1c, 2c and 3c headaches and weak memory in a boy of 13 that were preventing him
from continuing his studies. He also had insufficiency of the mitral value.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Aeon., Bell.Antidote to: Tab. Compare: (1) Kalm. contains Arbutin. (2) Der. of
great service in neuralgic headaches of rheumatic origin). (3) Spig., Puls. Complementary: Benz-ac. Follows
well: Nux-v., Thyr., Spig.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
 ***KAMALA
(Spoonwood)
PHARMACY - kam. Kamala. Spoon wood. Croton coccineus. Rottlera tinctoria. Mallotus philippinensis. N. O.
Euphorbiacae. India, South Arabia, Australia. A red mealy inflammable powder, obtained from the tri-lobed
capsules of the plant. Tincture. Solution in ether. Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Leprosy. Pustules. Skin, affections. Tapeworm. Worms.
HERBAL - Kamala is best known in medicine as a remedy for tapeworms. It is given in doses of half to two
drachms. The Treasury of Botany noted that “Among the Arabs of Aden it is given internally in leprosy, and
used in solution to remove freckles and pustules, while in this country it has been used successfully in treating
the eruption known as ‘wildfire’ (Strophulus volaticus) in children, by rubbing the powder over the affected part
with moist lint.“Kam. appears, however, to be most valued as an anthelmintic, and has been extensively used
with much success in India in cases of tapeworms, three drachms being sufficient for a robust person, and
half that quantity for one of feeble habit.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kam. shows by its clinical uses it relationship with Croton and the other
Euphorbians.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Karaka
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kara. Karaka. Kopi tree. Co- rynocarpus levigatus. N. O. Myrsinacee, Allen puts it in
Anacardiacae. New Zealand. Tincture or Trituration of fresh seeds. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Pains. Paralysis.
HOMEOPATHIC - The Treasury of Botany noted that karaka seeds contain a tasteless farinaceous substance
and are eaten in times of scarcity. The raw seeds are poisonous and produce spasmodic pains, giddiness and
partial paralysis. To render them edible, they are steamed for twenty-four hours and then either buried in the
ground or allowed to soak in water for some days.
G.      Bennett recorded a few symptoms observed in the case of a Maori chief poisoned with the seeds. Spasm
with pains. Violent pain lasting a week. Partial paralysis. Heat anesthesia, when warm water was applied he
did not feel any warmth from it. Violent spasms and convulsions of whole body, arms and legs stretched
violently and rigidly out. Permanent rigid distortion.
COMMENTS - C. F. Fischer proved Kara, and used it clinically in cases of convulsions. He recorded an account
of its effect from the proceedings of the New Zealand Institute.
“Violent spasms and convulsions of whole body, arms and legs stretched violently and rigidly out, great
flushings of heat, protrusion of eyes and tongue, gnashing of jaws. The poison proves rapidly fatal if the patient
is not attended to immediately and the limbs are permanently and rigidly distorted if they are not fixed in proper
positions until the crisis is passed.
“The general treatment is to bind the patient (generally a child) with the limbs in right positions, dig a pit and
place him in it, standing, buried up to the chin with a gag in his mouth.
“The writer described a youth, age 12, who had recovered after being poisoned, but whose limbs had not been
properly secured and were ever after absolutely useless.
“One leg was curved up behind his loins, the other bent up with the foot outwards. One arm inclined behind
his shoulder, the other slightly bent and extended forward and all, as to muscles inflexibly rigid. He could not
move himself or even drive away the flies.”
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Karwinskia Humboldtiana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - karw-h. Karwinskia humboldtiana. N. O. Rhamnacae. Foundin Mexico and Southern North
America. The seeds, crushed and macerated are used for the preparation of the tincture. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acute poliomyelitis. Acute bulbar paralysis. Amyotrophy. Bedsores. Dyspnea. Encephalitis.
Paralysis. Paresis.Poliomyelitis. Quadriplegia.
HERBAL - The plant Karwinskia belongs to the Rhamnacae family, it is found in the northern states of Mexico.
It is known locally under different names including Tullidora, the “little coyote,” “wild capuli,” “little black rod,”
and “cacachila.”
It is a small shrub, but can grow up to 9 meters in some places. The leaves are elliptical or oblong, rounded at
 the end, the flowers are small, yellow-green in color. The fruits are small in clusters from 6 to 9 mm in diameter,
dark violet in color, usually containing four seeds of which only two are reproductive.
The seeds are toxic, causing paralysis of the limbs, which becomes generalized and can terminate in death.
They contain a fatty acid, a yellow substance and a glucoside, which is the cause of the paralysis of the motor
nerves.
HOMEOPATHIC - The clinical observation of the mass intoxication of one hundred and six soldiers constitutes
the first Memoirs of Dr. Castillo Najeros, published in Mexico in 1918. A homeopathic proving of Karw-h. was
carried out by Luis de Legarreta and published in 1961 in his Materia Medica of Mexican Plants.
Karw-h. is a remedy with neurotrophic action, paralyzing the motor nerves. Flaccid paralysis, which increases,
ending in quadriplegia.
Ascending progressive paralysis, flaccid and painless, predominantly on the left side, with amyotrophy of the
lower limbs. Acute spinal paralysis, sub-acute atrophic spinal paralysis. Chronic anterior paralysis. Loss of
contractility and mobility of the leg muscles. Reduction of tendons reflexes and skin.
Paresis of paralysis, rising to the upper limbs and muscles of the thorax and diaphragm. Paralysis of the lips,
tongue and larynx. No diminution of reflexes of the bladder and intestines. Poliomyelitis. Acute and sub-acute,
polioencephalitis. Bedsores.
Abdomen - Lack of intestinal inactivity, partial obstruction.
Back - Cramping pains in the back.
Ears - Buzzing in both ears.
Head - Severe headache. Constant headache with feeling of heaviness.
Heart - Pulse slower with fever.
Limbs - Progressive paralysis. Cramping pains in the arms and legs. Loss of contractility and mobility of the
leg muscles.
Lungs - Dyspnea, which becomes worse and can end in respiratory paralysis. Bronchopneumonia, paralytic
alveolitis, which can cause fatal asphyxia. Difficult speech.
Rectum - Diarrhea in the first 48 hours, followed by intestinal paralysis with difficulty in evacuating.
Skin - Bedsores.
Stomach - Nausea with vomiting.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Lath. - Weakness, then paralysis of the lower limbs with exaggerated reflexes
and complaints of sensitivity. (2) Hydroph. - Paralysis with muscular dystrophy. (3) Plb. - Rapid emaciation,
progressive paralysis of the limbs with amyotrophy and starting in the extensor muscles.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Kerosolenum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - keroso. Kerosolenum. Kerosene. One of the lighter products, obtained by distillation from the
crude oil. Kerosolene being the trade name given by the “Downer Kerosene Oil Company,” nearly identical
with gasoline. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anesthesia. Asphyxia. Convulsions. Delirium. Ecstasy. Laughter.
HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of Keroso. have been observed on workmen, andexperi- ments have been
made with it for the purpose of testing its anesthetic properties.
Keroso. causes a pleasurable kind of intoxication, but too much muscular rigidity, asphyxia and intermittent
pulse to render it a safe anesthetic. Moderate convulsions.
Laughter was noticed in two cases and this should prove an indication in some kinds of delirium and insanity.
Partially or wholly insensible, but rapidly recovers when brought into open air. Insensibility complete, though
eyes not closed.
MIND - Sense of complete loneliness. Insensible, with inclination to laugh. Cannot keep still Chest - Breathing
checked during convulsions due to rigid contraction of chest muscles.
Eyes - Eyes a little unnaturally open and staring.
Face - Momentary dusky redness of face at each convulsion (as in epilepsy).
Head - Peculiar lightness of head. Slight headache.
Limbs - Weakness of the limbs. Modalities - Better in open air.
Pulse - Accelerated intermittent, volume diminished during insensibility.
Temperature - Some sweating.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Petr., Paraf., Benzin.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
 ***KISSINGEN AQUA
(Saline Springs)
PHARMACY - kiss. Kissingen aqua. Saline springs. Cold, chlorinated, gaseous, saline Springs of Kissingen
in Bavaria. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Constipation. Coms. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Gallbladder, disorders. Gout. Hemorrhoids.
Liver, disorders. Mesenteric glands, disorders. Noises, ears. Rectum, disorders. Spleen, disorders. Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Kissingen water has been proved by Carl Preu and observations have been made on its
general effects. Nat-m. is the leading solid ingredient, existing in the proportion of 5.82 out of a total of 8.55 in
the 1,000. It compares with Nauheim, Kreutznach and, to some extent, with Vichy.
Useful for abdominal affections, especially a catarrhal condition of intestinal atony. Convalescence from
typhoid and gallbladder affections. Disorders of the liver, spleen and intestinal glands.
Gout where the asthmatic principle appears to be repercussed upon the abdominal viscera, for then the waters
draw it out to the joints. The dosage must be managed with extreme prudence, too much can bring on a true
attack of gout.
Modalities - Worse in the forenoon, at night, on waking, while reading and writing. Vertigo worse while eating.
Toothache worse during menstruation.
COMMENTS - Constantin James, recorded in Allen, noted that the dose is from three to six glasses of the
water in the morning and two glasses at 4 p.m., but the general rule is that no more it to be drunk than the
stomach can digest without difficulty.
In the first days, appetite and force is increase, but as the water is absorbed the effects become general. Then
an elimina- tory “crisis” comes on. The stools become brownish, loose, bilious. The urine is turbid, depositing
a sediment which rapidly putrefies.
The secretion of the bronchial, genital, and ocular mucus membranes, as well as the skin, is increased and
changed in character. Moral and physical prostration, old and long-forgotten troubles reappear. This crisis,
which appears in the first or second week, soon disappears of itself and the cure proceeds.
In one case, a patient vomited blood after the disappearance of a hemorrhoidal flux. Kiss, restored the latter,
and the bloodvomiting ceased.
Trembling, pulsation of the whole body. Weariness. Stitches here and there. Muscle volitantes. Noises in the
ears. Chills, heat and perspiration. Tearful disposition, especially at 10 a.m. “If he only looks at any one he
must weep.”
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Nat-m. - weeping disposition, chill at 10 a.m., catarrh, constipation. (2) Ant-c. -
saburral condition. (3) Urt-u. - gout. (4) Ferr-pic. - warts and corns.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Kola Nut
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kola. Kola nut. Sterculia acuminata. Nux colae. Cola acuminata. Tincture of the ripe nuts without
their shell containing caffeine and theobromine. N.O. Sterculiaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Asthma. Diarrhea. Neurasthenia.
HERBAL - Kola regulates the circulation and the heart rhythm. Weak heart. Asthma. Neurasthenia. Promotes
the appetite and digestion. Diuretic and anti-diarrhea. Lessens the craving for alcohol.
Kola nuts give the power to endure prolonged physical exertion without taking food and without feeling fatigued.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Querc., Coca. (2) Alf. (3) Aven., Lach., Nux-v., Kudzu.

name: Kousso
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - kou. Kousso. Brayera anthelminthica. Hagenia abyssinica. Kuso. Cosso. N. O. Rosacee.
Abyssinia. Infusion of dried flowers. Tincture of flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Miscarriage. Tapeworm. Worms.
HERBAL - The flowers of Kousso are a favorite remedy for tapeworm with the natives of Abyssinia. The use
of them in European practice for that purpose has led to the observation of the few recorded symptoms, among
which thirst, nausea and vomiting are prominent. In one case miscarriage was caused.
To use as a vermifuge, take a quarter of an ounce of the dried flowers and boil in four ounces of distilled water.
Infuse for fifteen minutes without straining. The powder is to be taken with the infusion in the morning, fasting.
Two such drafts may be given. It is best to give a purgative before and an hour or two after the draft.
 Nausea and vomiting. Vertigo. Precordial anxiety, slowing and irregular pulse, delirium and collapse. Rapid
and extreme prostration.
HOMEOPATHIC - Alexander Milne remarked “Though Kousso leads to the expulsion of the worm, it seems
not to improve the morbid condition which favors its production.” The prostration caused by the treatment is so
great that Milne advises a course of Cinch, and Ferr. to follow.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cuc-c„ Gran., Fil. (2) Kam., an efficient remedy for tapeworm in 30-60 minims of
tincture taken in cinnamon water.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
