name: Lactuca Virosa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lact. Lactuca virosa. Acrid lettuce. Poison lettuce. Opium lettuce. “Lactucarium” or Lettuce
opium. N. O. Compositae. Genus, Cicoracee. Tincture of fresh flowering plant. Specimens of both Lactuca vir.
and Lactuca sat. might be included in the tincture. Tincture of impissated juice. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anus, disorders. Ascites. Asthma. Breast-feeding, disorders. Constipation.
Cough. Cramps. Diarrhea. Globus, hystericus. Gonorrhea. Headache. Heartburn. Hemiopia. Hysteria.
Insomnia. Levitation. Liver, disorders. Musca, volitantes. Noises, eats. Pylorus, pain. Sleep, excessive. Smell,
illusions. Spinal cord, pains. Spleen, disorders. Whooping cough. Yawning.
HERBAL - The leaves of garden lettuce, Lactuca sativa, when too old and going to seed, have a bitter taste
and the stalk contains a milky juice which is intensely bitter. This juice contains Lactucin and is common to all
lettuces, but is especially virulent in Lact. vir. from which (as well as well as from Lact. sat.) Lactucarium or
“Lettuce Opium,” is prepared.
HOMEOPATHIC - Brunton noted that Lact. has a soporific action and is used “instead of Opium to allay cough,
quiet nervousness and induce sleep in cases where from idiosyncrasy, Opium is not borne.” This use of
lettuces has been known from very remote times and has not been added to by old-school observers. The
sleep-provoking power of Lact. is recognizable in sensitive persons who eat ordinary garden lettuce in salad.
Boericke specified Lact. as a “true galact- agogue,” as it increases the milk in breasts. This remedy also acts
upon the brain and circulatory system. Delirium tremens with sleeplessness, coldness and tremor. Hydrothorax
and ascites.
Impotence. Sense of lightness and tightness affecting whole body, especially chest. Marked action on limbs.
MIND - Stupefaction of sense. Difficulty in thinking. Loss of memory. Anxiety and disturbed sleep. Great
restlessness. Fear driving him from place to place. Negative thinking. Contrary. Excessive ill humor, provoked
by slightest contradiction. Repulsive mood.
Prolonged emotional suffering, resulting in emotional deadness orcoldness. Forsaken feeling. Disposition
melancholy, fretful. Sadness with extravagant and exaggerated notions. Headache after grief.
Foolish behavior. Plays antics. Jumping. Singing or sighing. Delusions, sees soldiers on his bed. Delusions,
that he would be murdered. Vivid, exaggerated fancies.
Abdomen - Sensation of weight, fullness.
Movements in abdomen. Borborygmi, abundant emission of wind. Colic in early morning, tense abdomen,
relieved somewhat by evacuation and passing of wind. Cramping pain, better passing flatus. Dull shocks or
else lancinations in right hypochondrium. Contusive pain in liver region, in morning.
Back - Tension in muscles of neck or right side, sometimes spasmodic. Lancinations under right armpit. Pains
in spinal marrow, as far as the cauda equina and extending to sacrum. Contusive pain in lumbar region.
Drawing pains in loins towards the groins.
Breasts - Milk absent. Increase of milk in breasts (Asaf.).
Chest - Constriction. Sense of oppression of chest. Squeezing sensation in lower chest. Sensation of warmth.
Pain on bending forward. Shaking of chest during cough.
Cough - Cough as from dust. Must hold chest with both hands.
Ears - Drawing pains in ears, shootings followed by tension in left ear. Buzzing in ears, ringing sound before
ears, in evening, in bed.
Eyes - Biting in the eyes. Burning in eyes, especially in the lids. Redness of conjunctiva with increased mucus
 secretion in elderly persons. Pupils dilated. Cloudiness of vision, weakness of sight. Hemiopia. Flying
insects before eyes, on stooping after a meal. Itching above the eyebrows.
Face - Pale. Heat of face with trembling and sensation of swelling of lips. Quivering in lips. Tingling with a
feeling of tightness on face. Lancinations in chin at extremity of sub-maxillary nerve. Swelling of the lymphatic
glands.
Female - Promotes menses. Menses too early. Bearing down and weak feeling about pelvic organs and
general relaxed feeling. Painful gonorrhea.
Food - Want of appetite, food is repugnant, no appetite for bread and meat. Food tastes sickly, bitter. Appetite
and thirst increased. Desires milk, pickles, sour. Aversion to bread, meat, wine. Better from bread, coffee,
vegetable acids, worse from milk.
Head - Empty sensation. Sensation of looseness of brain. Dull, heavy, confused, dizzy. Heat of face and
headache with general coldness. Pain, stupefying headache, after grief. Headache with disorders of respira-
tory organs.
Kidneys - Dragging pressure in region of bladder, as from urgency to urinate. Burning in urethra. Urine smells
of violets. Urine clear as water, copious. Sensation as of a drop continuously passing along the urethra when
seated.
Limbs - Cramp-like pains. Rush of blood to lower limbs. Sensation as if circulation in legs were suspended.
Numbness while sitting. Coldness and numbness of feet and legs. Lame hip down left side, worse walking.
Cramps in shin bones, extending to toes and side of leg involving calves. Tension in hollow of knee on rising
from a seat, while walking. Tremor of hands and arms.
Lungs - Difficult breathing. Suffocative breathing from dropsy of the chest. Irritating, suffocating cough.
Constant tickling cough. Incessant, spasmodic cough, as if chest would fly to pieces.
Male - Drawing pains at root of penis, in right spermatic cord and along internal surface of thigh. Diminished
sexual appetite, chases away lasciviousness and voluptuous fancies. Painful erections during morning sleep.
Swelling of a lym-
phatic vessel in penis, following morning erections.
Modalities - Better in open air, bending, sitting up. Worse from touch, crossing legs, sneezing, in a warm
room. Yawning and stretching helps pressure in chest.
Mouth - Dry mouth, without thirst. White coating on tongue, thick mucus, sore, as if burned at tip. Contraction
under tongue. Sharp pain in molars on left side of lower jaw, as if they were being twisted. Soreness of gums,
on an empty socket on masticating.
Nose - Sensation as though end of nose were distended. Peculiar smell before nose and a similar taste in
mouth. Coryza, followed by excoriation and dryness in nose. Frequent sneezing.
Rectum - Constipation, no stool the first day or else a tardy and hard evacuation (habitual constipation
diminishes). Stool only after urgent calls and griping.
Sensations - As if chest would fly to pieces. As if circulation in legs was suspended. Coldness of stomach,
throat, chest, feet.
Skin - Subcutaneous lancinating and pinching in various places. Inflammation and eruptions.
Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness in daytime. Frequent yawning and stretching of limbs. Restless, impossible to
get to sleep. Insomnia. Disturbed sleep from anxiety, cough. Position, lying on back impossible. Sound,
refreshing sleep. Deep, comatose sleep.
Stomach - Sensation of icy coldness in stomach. Sensation of retraction. Pains in stomach with contraction of
pit of stomach, worse by pressure. After a meal, sensation of fullness in stomach with pressure downwards.
Pain better passing flatus. Loathing, nausea, vomiting, sometimes with uneasiness at pit of stomach.
Temperature - Slight shivering chill. Frequent coldness over back and head, with heat in face. Chilliness in a
warm room with coldness of hands and feet. Dry heat of upper part of body, with icy coldness of feet.
Throat - Slight burning in throat. Difficult swallowing with sensation as if uvula were raw with burning. Sensation
of coldness in esophagus from eructations. Accumulation of mucus in throat, viscid mucus in throat in morning.
Vertigo - Vertigo with heaviness of head and lower limbs. Vertigo with blackness before eyes. Vertigo with
sensation as if head were too large and expanded.
COMMENTS - There are several recorded instances of poisoning. A man, 25, ate Lact. in a salad, 7 p.m. and
went to bed at 9. He woke at 11 with sharp, colicky pains, soon followed by nausea and vomiting that lasted
all night. He fell asleep at 5 a.m., but in the morning was astonished to find himself unable to distinguish objects
clearly.
A boy of 10 who ate the same meal became affected with lively delirium at midnight that lasted until morning.
He jumped about on the bed, played all sorts of pranks and nobody could quiet him. He had no colic or vomiting.
His pupils were dilated until the iris was a mere rim. Trying to read he mistook M for P and O for V. In his
 delirium, he had hallucinations, saw on his bed a soldier, an inkstand, etc. Both these patients as well as
another had liquid stools. The dilated pupils persisted some time.
Keynote indescribable sensation of tightness, affecting the whole body, but especially the chest. Intolerance
to touch and pressure. Pain in spinal marrow even to cauda equina, streaming along coccyx. Right arm is
much affected.
Much yawning and stretching to relieve the squeezing of the lower chest. Squeezing in left breast. Feeling as
if a hundredweight on chest. Feeling of relaxation in the chest. Angina pectoris.
Asthma. Spasmodic cough in frequent paroxysms with feeling of suffocation. Attacks come suddenly without
any apparent cause, induced by a violent tickling in pharynx and roof of mouth. Whooping cough, paroxysms
preceded by anxiety. Antispasmodic. Chest symptoms are better sitting up.
Lactuca virosa
Tightness in the liver region. Enlargements of the liver with tightness. Stomach pain, better bending. Pinching
in umbilical region, better crossing the legs.
Constipation and diarrhea with many concomitant anal symptoms. Sensation as of a drop continually passing
along the urethra when seated. Urine smells like violets. Hering noted “painful gonorrhea in females.” Used as
a galactagogue (Aven.. Alf.).
Extraordinary lightness of body, more pronounced in open air. Feels as if swimming in bed. Dreams of
swimming in the air or of walking above the ground. The head feels light, empty. Sensation as if head too large,
as if brain loose. Sensation as if looking through gauze. Mild sedative.
Cured a case of hypertrophy of the ovaries in a woman of fifty as a consequence of a miscarriage twenty-five
years before. The tumor was excessively large and the patient could get no rest because of the pain from the
pressure. The rectum was contracted and feces evacuated with great pain.
“Fatigue during stool,” and also “sleepiness during stool” were peculiar and may prove characteristic.
Ebullitions rising up from abdomen suggest globus hystericus.
RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Vegetable acids and coffee. (In a proving of Lact., Acet-ac., aether and hoch.
were more effectual than coffee). Compare: (1) Drowsiness, dryness and constipation - Op., Nux-m. (2)
levitation, Stict. Puls., Ph-ac., Lac-c., Asar., Thuj., etc. (3) intolerance of anything tight around neck, Lach. (4)
gonorrhea, urine smells of violets, Terebe. (5) squeezing in left breast, Bor. (6) Bor. has empty feeling.
Coldness. (7) Helo., pain in soles as if he had jumped on a stone. (8) Bor., heart symptoms, Kali-c. and Kali-
i., cough Dros. (9) Nabal. (10) Lach., Kali-c., (11) Spira. - galactagogue.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Laetrile
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - laetr. Laetrile. Amygdalin. Pangamic acid. Vitamin B-17. Anti-cancer drug. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Cancer. Cyanosis. Dizziness. Fatigue. Hair, loss. Headache. Hypotension. Liver,
damage. Muscular, weakness. Nausea. Ptosis. Rheumatism. Tumors. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Laetrile formula is laevo- D-mandelonitrile-B-glucoronide. Laetrile is a decomposition
product resulting from the hydrolysis of amygdalin. This compound is chemically related to amygdalin, a
substance found naturally in the pits of apricots and various other fruits.
The term “laetrile” was first proposed by Ernest T. Krebs, Jr. in 1949. Most proponents of laetrile for the
treatment of cancer use the terms “laetrile” and “amygdalin” interchangeably. Amygdalin is one of the first and
best known cyanogenic glycosides. Neither amygdalin nor laetrile contain free cyanide.
Amygdalin is a herbal constituent derived from the kernels of various fruits of the Genus Prunus (synonym
amygdalus), which includes the plum, prune, cherry, peach and apricot. It is among the most ancient herbal
remedies used against cancer.
Apricot kernels have been in medical use since the days of Pen T'sao (an herbalist), in 2800 B.C., in China.
The great Persian master of pharmacy, medicine and natural sciences. Avicenna (980-1037), recommended
the use of apricot bitter oil in the treatment of tumors of the spleen, uterus, stomach and liver.
Some doctors believe that laetrile relieves the pain of cancer. Experimental results show effects of amygdalin
on breast tumors. Adenocarcinomas. Stoppage of growth of small tumors. Prevents the development of lung
cancer metastases. Other reported uses have been in the treatment of high blood pressure and rheumatism.
Toxicities are generally mild when patients adhered to treatment schedules. The side effects associated with
treatment mirror the symptoms of cyanide poisoning, including nausea, vomiting, and headache. Fatigue,
muscular weakness, pain. Respiratory difficulties. Decreased blood cell counts. Hair loss and mouth sores.
More severe side effects are experienced when laetrile is given by mouth than when it is given by injection,
 including mental confusion, dizziness. Cyanosis, anemia, hypotension. Liver damage. Ptosis.
Ataxic neuropathies, difficulty walking due to damaged nerves. Coma.
RELATIONS - Compare: Ars., Cadm-s., Hydr.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Lamium Album
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lam. Lamium album. White nettle. Lamium levigatum. Lamium macula- turn. Dead Nettle. N. 0.
Labiatae. Tincture of entire fresh plant while in flower and seed. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Blisters. Chills. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Hemoptysis. Hernia. Leucor- rhea. Menstruation,
early. Ulcers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lamium was proved by Hahnemann and others, including Stapf. Affinity for female and
urinary organs. Sensation in urethra as though a drop of water were flowing through it. Hemoptysis. Hemor-
rhoids and hard stool with blood.
Menses appeared too early and were scanty. Much leucorrhea with biting sensation or without sensation, white
mucus.
“Deep-in”headache (Bac.), tightness of scalp and a backward and forward motion of the head. Headache
with backward and forward motion of head.
Much uneasiness of mind and body, trembling of limbs, weakness during the chill. Tearing and drawing in the
limbs. Blisters on heel from slight rubbing. Ulcers on heel (All-c.).
MIND - Whining mood, inclination to weep, feels as if abandoned (Puls.). Great sadness with lachrymose
humor. Great agitation and anxiety, which permit no rest.
Modalities - Better on rising, sitting. Worse while lying down in bed, in morning, rising from stooping. Worse
in open air, drinking, eating.
COMMENTS - Farrington said, “Lamium has been recommended for external hemorrhoids. ‘Hardstool with
blood' is the nearest symptom bearing on this.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Puls., All-c. (2) Members of the Mint tribe - Hedeo., Oci., Orig., Menth. (3) “Deep-
in” headache, Bac. (4) Head moves backwards and forwards - Am., Cham., Lyc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Lapathum Acutum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lapa. Lapathum acutum. Common dock. Lapathum sylvestre. Rumex obtusifolius. N. O.
Polygonacae. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Headache. Kidneys, pain. Leucorrhea. Nosebleed. Uterus, atony. Weariness.
HERBAL - Lapathum is the old name of the docks, now generally named rumex. The word is of Greek origin
and signifies, according to Gerarde, “to soften, ease or purge the belly,” and the name was given to “herbs
used in pottage and medicine, very well known to have the power of cleansing.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Lapa, was proved by Widenhorn. It produced some rather severe headaches and
nosebleeds. Hansen said it is indicated in nosebleed following headache. Weight in stomach. Pain in kidneys
with pressure from without inwards. Weak feeling in genitals. Leucorrhea with uterine bearing down pain.
Weariness.
MIND - Sadness and morose, alternating with gaiety.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Rumx., Rheum., Phyt. (2) Sep., Lil-t. (3) Kidney pain, Santa.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Lapis Albus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-lap-a. Lapisalbus. White stone. Calcarea silico-fluorica. Trituration. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Anemia. Bronchocèle. Cancer. Cretinism. Dyspepsia. Dysmenorrhea. Epithelioma.
Fibroids. Fibroma. Glands, disorders. Goiter. Growths. Hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Lipoma. Otitis media.
Pruritus, vulva. Sarcoma. Scirrhous. Scrofula. Sores. Tuberculosis. Tumors. Ulcers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lapis albus is silico-fluo- ride of calcium. A kind of gneiss, it was found by Grauvogl in the
mineral springs of Gastein, Germany. These waters flow over gneiss formations into the valley of the Achen,
where goiter and cretinism abound. The mineral waters have a reputation for curing ulcers, cancers and
tumors.
 Grauvogl cured with it a case of carcinoma and he and others have cured cases of goiter and scrofulous
glands. Uterine cancer. Fibroid tumors with intense burning pains through the part with profuse
hemorrhage. Pre-ulcerative stage of carcinoma. Sarcoma. Lipoma. Growths.
Glandular disorders, glands are elastic and pliable (Calc-f. and Cist, have a stony hardness). Goiter. Especially
affects the connective tissue about the glands. Glandular swellings where no glands are usually found.
Scrofulous affections, except in malarial cases. Fat, anemic babies with a ravenous appetite.
Burning, shooting, stinging pains in the stomach, pylorus, in the breasts and uterus. Severe menstrual pains
causing weakness and swooning.
Chest - Persistent pains in breast region. Glandular hardening.
Ears - Suppurative otitis media.
Face - Opening in cheek as large as a silver dollar, in carcinoma. Epithelioma of lip, crusts coming off leave
raw surface. Tumor of lower lip with burning, stinging pains, that make him jump off his feet.
Female - Painful menses, suddenly taken with pain so severe that she swoons.
Lapis albus Severe pain preceding the flow. Pruritus vulva. Burning, shooting, stingingpains in breasts and

Pruritus. Enlargement and induration of glands, especially the cervical glands. Lipoma, sarcoma, carcinoma.

In one patient, the swelling was as large as a goose-egg in the right sternoclavicular region. This patient, a

Whiting recorded a fragmentary proving of Lap-a. Mrs. Smith., 40, fair, stout, no children, had a large
bronchocele. Averse to all animal food, craved sweets. Craved and drank much ice-water in all seasons since
a child. Feet and legs cold to knees.
Lap-a. 6x was given, 2 grains, powders, one four times a day. She reported in a month that the tumor was
rapidly diminishing in size, but she was having much pain in it. No further medicine was given.
Two months later, the tumor had diminished to one-half, and the patient stated that since taking the powders
she had had no pain at her menstrual period, no dyspepsia and no sick-headaches. She had experienced
severe dysmenorrhea since the menses first appeared. Since leaving off the medicine, the pain in the tumor
ceased and also the decrease in size.
Lap-a. 6x was again given and again the pain in the tumor came on and in addition, itching of the external
genitals. The 30c and 200c caused such intense itching that the patient refused to take any more medicine of
any kind.
Since then, Whiting cured many cases of pruritus and also of dysmenorrhea with Lap-a. The pains come on
before the flow and cause swooning.
One patient, 19, had dysmenorrhea from the first. Pain so severe she would fall unconscious wherever she
might happen to be, the swoon lasting half an hour at times. Better when flow established. Lap-a. 200c cured.
Miss X., 34, normal until she had measles at age 20; since then, pain at commencement of menstruation, so
severe as to cause fainting. “This severe pain would continue less for a day or until the flow was established.”
Lap-a. 200c cured in six months.
W. P. Wesselheft, discussing Whiting's paper, narrated the cure of a case of epithelioma of the lip in a man of
seventy with Lap-a. 12x in water.
Dr. Gregory cured a young man of a tumor of the lip with Lap-a. 30c. It recurred two years later with “burning,
stinging pain, which made him jump off his feet.” More Lap-a. 30c was given and cured in a year. There was
in further recurrence.
Bellows noted that where Sil. is indicated, progress is hastened by Lap-a.

name: Lapis Granites Murvey
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lap-gr-m. Lapis granites murvey. Granite rock. Murvey granite from near Barna. Co. Galway,
Ireland. Triturations. Historical dose: All potencies.
 CLINICAL - Chronic fatigue. Constipation. Dandruff. Diarrhea. Exhaustion. Fevers. Flatulence. Headache.
Influenza. Nausea. Rheumatism. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lap-gr-m. wasfirstused as a medicine by ancient Egyptian physicians and it is mention in
many of the medical scrolls. It has recently been proved in England by Nuala Eising.
Connemara granite of Ireland has one of the highest levels of radioactivity of the granites found in Britain and
Ireland. The pink granite has a particularly high level of radioactivity.
Granite in Ireland is considered responsible for a higher rate of cancer and Down's syndrome in that country.
Eising obtained a sample of the granite by breaking through a rock and taking a piece from the center which
was previously not exposed. This was sent to the Galen Pharmacy and was potentized to the 30c potency,
which was used by the provers.
Extreme exhaustion and weakness. Inability to move. Drags oneself around the place, having to lie down,
sleep often. No inclination to do anything, pleasurable. Profound introversion and withdrawal. Occasional
bursts of energy or nervous high energy.
Heavy and painful limbs. Rheumatic pains. Pressure, bruised and sore feeling. Headaches, frontal pain, or in
temples. Delirious fevers or milder, recurring fevers, with profuse sweating.
Marked effect on the liver and digestive system, with nausea. Yellow skin. Lost or diminished sexual energy.
Pain and discomfort in genital areas generally. Disturbed menstrual cycle and menstruation.
MIND - Apathy and weakness. Making decisions was a great effort. Spaced out all day and very giddy. Lack
of concentration, very forgetful. Deep feeling of sadness and worthlessness. Weepy. Self-pity. Vulnerable
feeling. Self-doubt, poor self-confidence.
Restlessness. Easily startled by sudden noises. Great fear for no apparent reason. Fear or panic attacks.
Claustrophobia. Feeling of anticipation. Uneasy feelings as if something were about to happen or as if she had
something to do and couldn't remember what.
Extremely introverted, detached and indifferent. Lonely.Introversion with arrogance. Believes that
others are trivial or petty. Aversion to company, to socializing. Contempt for others. Insolent and rude.
Suspicious of motives of others. Outbursts of anger. Irritability or anger at being invaded or disturbed by others.
Abdomen - Dull, heavy, dragging pain in lower abdomen, has to bend double. Pain radiates down thighs.
Tension in the solar
plexus. Spluttery and full of gas with cramps in abdomen.
Back - Neck felt tense and painful. Aching, dull, heavy pain in the lower back. Pain in kidney region.
Breasts - Breasts sore and swollen.
Ears - Ear infections. Ears itchy inside and a thick discharge following. Eruption like a cold sore appeared on
the left ear lobe, scabby, pus, itching. Ears felt like they were stuffed with cotton wool. Pressure and popping
in ears, affecting hearing. Difficult hearing, voices and sounds seemed distant.
Eyes - Eyes were stinging, burning and watering. Burning sensation and pressure behind eyes. Eyelids felt
heavy all day. Short-sighted.
Face - Pale. Face looks strained, frowns a lot.
Female - Disturbed menstrual cycle and menstruation, with pain and discomfort. Menses with severe pain in
lower abdomen and lower back. Sharp pain in right ovary. Sexual urge diminished or lost.
Food - Appetite lost, with nausea. Hungry but couldn't find any food that interested her. Nibbling at food all the
time out of boredom. Craving for sweets. Thirsty most of the time.
Head - Frontal pressure. Temples felt bruised and sore. Headache as if a tight band. Frontal headache, in
morning. Head hot, scalp and forehead very itchy. Dandruff. Scalp scaly, itching with hair falling out.
Kidneys - Sharp, stabbing pains over kidneys. Aching pain in back over kidneys. Pressure on bladder.
Frequent urination.
Limbs - Limbs sore and achy. Rheumatic pains, in right arm and left thigh at night. Sore, bruised type in left
shoulder, over left kidney and in left hip. Arms were very heavy, had no power in them, lifting things was very
difficult.
Lungs - Cough, like she was clearing her throat all the time. Short, phlegmy cough.
Male - Sexual energy lost or diminished.
Modalities - Better lying down, from alcohol. Worse from cold, even when hot.
Worse from tobacco, particularly the weakness and nausea.
Nose - Acute sense of smell.
Rectum - Constipation and diarrhea. Chalky colored diarrhea, in the morning. Diarrhea with pains like
premenstrual pains in her lower abdomen.
Skin - Very yellowish skin. Skin generally itchy, particularly the scalp. Pimples on neck and back. Eruptions,
red patches of dry skin, intensely itching and burning. Must scratch, scratching brings up little lumps.
 Sleep - Confused, exhausted on waking. Unrefreshing sleep. Dreams about the past, grandparents, mother,
elderly relatives dying. Very aggressive dreams, attaching people, being in a war, being raped dead babies.
Stomach - Nausea with lost of appetite.
Temperature - Fever with sweat. Hot anc feverish, sweating on palms and back Sweating in bed.
Throat - Throat sore and raw. Tickling it throat causing a cough.
Vertigo - Feels giddy and exhausted. COMMENTS - Occasional desire forthe com pany of one close friend,
where no social effor was necessary, marked during anxiety. Asser tive. Fear or panic attacks. Anxiety rising
suddenly without apparent cause. Restless ness, have to keep moving. Trembling al over, particularly hands.
Easily startled b; sudden noises or while driving.
Eruptions. Red patches on skin, dry itchin; with aggravations from dairy products. Ski and scalp symptoms.
Inner ear infection; with pressure and popping. Weakness an nausea aggravated by smoking.
One case concerned a man who had move to Galway two years earlier and was havin recurring panic attacks
since then. He wi very introverted, with profound feelings c loneliness and isolation. He was prone 1 outbursts
of anger. Granite 200c cured.
A second case concerned a woman wf suffered from severe headaches, pain fro her eyes. She had been
diagnosed as nea sighted and needed glasses. She was tin all the time and had difficulty getting out bed in
the morning.
Introverted, strong feelings of hatred and jealousy. Enjoyed trying to provoke her passive husband into fighting.
Granite 200c cured. She has hadhereyes tested again since the remedy and her sight became perfect.

m.

name: Lapis Lazuli
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lap-laz. Lapis lazuli. Gemstone. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Acne. Boils. Anal, itching. Conjunctivitis. Coryza. Diarrhea. Flatulence. Glands, swelling. Hair, loss.
Headaches. Heartburn. Hemorrhoids. Hoarseness. Itching. Lachrymation. Leucorrhea. Meniere's, disease.
Nausea. Night-sweats. Nosebleeds. Palpitations. Thyroid swollen. Tinnitus. Trembling. Vesicles. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - The name lapis lazuli originated from Arabic “lazaward,” meaning blue, and developed into
azul, meaning blue sky. It is a combination of natrium- alumina-silicea with the golden lines and spots of pyrite.
In folk medicine, lapis lazuli was used to treat cataract, headache, laryngitis, pharyngitis, and to regulate the
thyroid gland. Neuritis, neuralgic pains, cramping pains, joint pains, dysmenorrhea. Melancholy, fever,
apoplexy, epilepsy. Spleen diseases. Respiratory tract.
MIND - Absent-minded. Difficult concentration. Mistakes in speaking. Awkward, drops things. Weariness,
worse in morning. Apathy, with sleepiness.
Mind active. Fretful. Vexation. Anger, bad temper. Irritable. Offended easily, take s everything in a bad light.
Conscientious about trifles. Haughty. Indifferent. Averse to company, presence of other people aggravate
symptoms.
Tranquility, serenity, yielding disposition. Forsaken feeling. Sense of isolation. Despondent, depressed,
gloomy, melancholy. Causeless sadness. Taciturn, desire to be
silent. Cannot cry, though sad. Weeping suddenly.
Full of indefinite desires. Desire for retirement. Fear of rain, water. Fear of being hurt, of impending disease.
Anxiety from the pains in the heart. Presentiment of death. Delusions eyes are falling out, that she is pregnant.
Dreams of water, churches, witches. Prophetic dreams. Clairvoyance.
Abdomen - Distended. Flatulence, rumbling. Cutting, drawing and sharp pains.
Back - Backache in lumbar region. Lancinating, sharp, and pressing pains. Eruptions like flea bites. Itching.
Bladder - Urging to urinate. Burning pains.
Chest - Constriction, tension, tightness, on waking. Oppression of chest. Axillary glands swelling. Stitching
pain in axilla.
Ears - Heat sensation. Ear pain on blowing nose. Tinnitus. Noises in ears, rushing, whistling.
Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Itching. Lachrymation from eye pain. Dim vision. Tired expression and sensation.
Face - Acne rosacea. Pale or red color. Boils.
Crusty, scabby eruptions.
Female - Brown leucorrhea.
Food - Thirstless. Desires chocolate, alcohol.
Head - Hair, loss. Headaches. Itching of scalp.
 Heart - As if heart would cease to beat.
Pressing, stitching pain. Sore, bruised pain. Pain in heart, better walking. Palpitations with vertigo.
Kidneys - Drawing pains in kidneys.
Limbs - Numbness, upper limbs. Tottering gait. Cracking joints. Joint pains, burning, stitching. Trembling,
worse after anger. Weak knees. Felon, onychia, paronychia, panaritium.
Male - Increased sexual desire.
Mouth - Dryness. Cracked, dry lips.
Neck - Swelling glands.
Nose - Nasal obstruction. Coryza. Fluent discharges. Nosebleeds, during headache or vertigo, on blowing the
nose.
Rectum - Flatus, offensive like rotten eggs. Diarrhea. Stools, bloody, thin, liquid. Putrid odor of stool. Stools
like balls. Anal itching. Rectal bleeding. Hemorrhoids.
Skin - Acne rosacea. Dry and itching. Night-sweats. Boils. Eruptions, crusty, scabby. Vesicles.
Sleep - Disturbed, during the full moon. Wakes after midnight. Wakes from vertigo.
Stomach - Nausea. Heartburn.
Throat - Cold sensation. Sore throat. Burning in throat. Sharp pains, on empty swallowing. Hoarseness. Nasal
voice. Thyroid swollen.
Tongue - Burning sensation. Vesicles on tip. Metallic taste.
Vertigo - Vertigo in morning, on waking, with nosebleed, during headache. Vertigo and tinnitus like Meniere's
disease.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chin-s., Thios.
REFERENCES - Schadde.

name: Lappa Arctium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY- lappa. Lappa arctium. Burdock. Arctium lappa. Lappa major. Lappa officinalis. Arcion. Gobo.
Great dote burre. N. O. Composite. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Acne. Backache. Belching. Boils. Bunions. Diarrhea. Dupuytren's contraction. Dyspepsia. Eczema.
Eruptions. Flatus. Glands, disorders. Gonorrhea. Gout. Impotency. Infertility. Leucorrhea. Phosphaturia.
Prolapsed, uterus. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Scrofula. Sour, stomach. Styes. Ulcers. Uterus, prolapsed.
Vaginitis. Vertigo.
HERBAL - A writer in the Amer. Homeopath recommended the local use of the seedling roots in acne. The
roots are softened by soaking in water for two hours, then the blunt end is rubbed on each individual pimple.
It is not to be repeated more often than once a week.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lappa arctium has been extensively proved, notably by Dr. Jeanes and Dr. S. A. Jones.
The provings generally confirm older teachings.
Lappa chiefly affects the skin, liver joints and uterus. Historically, it was given for prolapsed uterus, infertility,
milky urine and sores about the joints. It was one of Culpepper's remedies for fetid sweat of axilla. Useful in
skin therapeutics.
A large number of symptoms were observed upon the skin and mucus membranes. Acne, eczema, especially
of the scalp, with discharge. Eruptions on the head, face and neck. In skin disorders, it has been used externally
as a glycerol, as well as internally.
Styes and ulcerations on the edge of the eyelids. Crops of boils and styes (Anthr.). Profuse and frequent
urination. Heavy, sore aching, as if lying uncomfortably. Numbness, lumbar region of aching calves.
Constriction.
Abdomen - Flatulent dyspepsia, belching inodorous gas.
Back - Pains in back about eighth dorsal vertebra.
Chest - Trembling in chest. Acute tingling, cutting pain under middle of sternum, extending across breast.
Eyes - Redness about eyes. Crops of styes. Feeling as if the eye was small and constricted.
Face - Inveterate acne, worse touch. Spreading vesicular eruption, great tearing and itching. Herpetic eruption
on right ala nasi.
Female - Uterine displacement, worse standing, walking, sudden jar. Bruised, sore, heavy feeling in uterus
with great relaxation of vaginal tissue. Prolapsed uterus with much bearing down pain. Leucorrhea.
Head - Weight on vertex. Pain in head.
Eczema of scalp.
Heart - Pain in heart with indescribable movement under sternum. Exceedingly rapid pulse with frequent
intermissions.
 Kidneys - Profuse and frequent urination. Milky phosphatic urine.
Limbs - Eruption on limbs. Soreness of muscles. Pain in all joints. Old sores about joints. Rheumatic and gouty
pains. Rheumatic pains entirely relieved by onset of diarrhea. Sharp, darting, fugitive pains in tendons.
Dupuytren's contraction. Front
of thigh weak. Pain in hands, knees and ankles extending downward to fingers and toes. Bunion.
Lungs - Tickling in glottidis, loose-sounding cough, no expectoration. Short breath on exertion.
Male - Cutting, squeezed pain in whole length of urethra, scalding on urination. Ringworm-like patch of eruption
on thigh beside testicles, groins raw. Loss of sexual desire.
Modalities - Better from cloudy weather. Worse cold, wet, shaking, violent exertion, lying on right side.
Nose - Red discoloration across the nose.
Rectum - Frequent yellow stools in forenoon, with some nausea. Diarrhea alternating with rheumatic
symptoms.
Skin - Eruptions, sticky on head, face. Many small painful boils. Moist, offensive eruptions, grayish white crusts,
especially when glands are swollen. Moist, foul eczema of infants. Old sores, about joints. Axillary sweat
cold, runs down chest, foul.
Stomach -Sour stomach, sour taste, all food turns sour, vomits it. Diarrhea alternating with rheumatic
symptoms.
Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea and vomiting.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) The composites, Am., Calen., Ciña. (2) Bry. - rheumatism. (3) Frax., Lil-t. and
Sep. - in uterine prolapse. (4) Calc-p. - phosphaturia. (5) Vine., Viol-t. - skin.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Lapsana Communis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - laps. Lapsana communis. Nipple-wort. N. O. Composite. Genus Cicora- cee. Tincture of
infusion of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Hemorrhoids. Nipples, sore.
HERBAL - As the common name of Lapsana would imply, it is a popular remedy for sore nipples, a decoction
of it being used as a lotion for that purpose. Cooper published documents in proof of its efficiency in
hemorrhoids.
Three ounces of the green plant (or four of the dry) are boiled in three pints of thin water gruel until it is reduced
to a pint and a half. The decoction is then strained. Half a pint is to be drunk on three mornings following,
fasting immediately on getting out of bed.
One patient who was cured in this way said he had no swallowed the draft more than a few minutes before he
felt his stomach as warm as if he had drunk hot brandy and water.
Only three doses were ordered and the patient was told, if not cured, to wait a fortnight before repeating the
treatment.
HOMEOPATHIC - Laps, is a remedy for sore nipples and hemorrhoids. Cooper confirmed the power of Laps,
over hemorrhoids, using single doses of the tincture.
RELATIONS - Compare: Calen.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Lathyrus S Ati Vus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lath. Lathyrus sativus. Wild vetch. Lathyrus cicera. Lesser chick-pea. “Jesse,” “Jarosse.” N. O.
Leguminose. Papil- ionoideae. Trituration of seeds. Tincture of the flower. Tincture of the green pods.
Trituration of the dried pea. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Athetosis. Beriberi. Constipation. Cramps. Depression. Diarrhea.
Dysentery. Emaciated, limbs. Emaciation. Heartburn. Impotence. Infantile, paralysis. Locomotor ataxia.
Lumbago. Multiple sclerosis. Nausea. Paralysis. Paralysis, spinal. Paraplegia. Parkinson's disease.
Poliomyelitis. Rheumatic, paralysis. Rheumatism. Roaring (in horses). Spinal, sclerosis. Urine, incontinence.
Vertigo. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lathyrus is a vetch, a member of the Leguminosae family that grows in India. Lathyrus
contains variable amounts of a toxin that, when ingested, may cause lathyrism, a paralytic affection. Produces
a perfect picture of certain spinal affections.
In Christison's Toxicology, it is stated that Lath, causes paraplegia, dragging gait, turning-in of the toes,
stiffness and semiflexion of the knee joints.
The clinical record of Lath, indicates that it may prove useful in numerous cases of bedridden paraplegias and
infantile spinal paralysis, as well as in certain forms of myelitis. In 1877, Clarke published cases relieved by
Lath., two of paralysis, one of multiple sclerosis, one of rheumatic paralysis with stiff knees.
Affects the anterior and lateral columns of the cord, causing paralytic disorders of lower limbs, spastic paralysis,
lateral sclerosis, beriberi. Infantile paralysis. Athetosis. Trembling of arms, worse on attempting to do
anything.
Increased reflexes. Lack of pain. Wasting, exhaustive diseases with weakness and heaviness, slow recovery
of nerve power. Sleepy, constant yawning.
MIND - Depressed, hypochondriacal. Lack of inner strength. Sense of being trapped by circumstances.
Suppressed emotions.
Abdomen - Colic. Sensation as if a damp cloth around waist.
Back - Lumbago. Pain in back so severe as to prevent movement, worse or excited by touch.
Bladder - Increased bladder reflexes. Frequent urge to urinate, must hurry, or else voided involuntarily.
Ears - Singing in ears.
Kidneys - Pressure on bladder, if not immediately satisfied, urine, rushes out with great force. Incontinence of
urine. Increased bladder reflex.
Limbs - Polio myelitis with marked spastic symptoms. Rheumatic paralysis. Excessive rigidity of legs,
spastic gait. Tremulous, tottering gait. Knees knock together when walking. Knee jerks exaggerated. Cannot
extend or cross legs when sitting. Sits bent forward, straightens up with difficulty. Stiffness and lameness of
the ankles and knees. Heels do not touch the ground when walking. Feet are dragged or put down suddenly
and forcibly while walking. While lying down legs can be moved from side to side but cannot be lifted. Legs
blue, swollen, if hanging down. Cramps in legs, worse cold and cold feet. Legs are cold during day. become
hot and burn at night better uncovering. Gluteal muscles and muscles of lower limbs are emaciated.
Male - Impotence. Occasional erections and pollutions.
Modalities - Better uncovering, lying down (lower limbs move freely). Worse from cold, damp weather, touch,
movement.
Mouth - Burning pain, tip of tongue. Tingling and numbness of tongue and lips, as if scalded.
Rectum - Diarrhea, with urgent pressure on intestines. Dysentery. Constipation.
Sensations - Sensation as of a damp cloth around the waist.
Sleep - Continuous yawning and sleepiness.
Stomach - Weight in stomach and indigestion. Heartburn. Nausea and vomiting. Vomiting of blood.
Vertigo - Vertigo when standing with eyes closed.
COMMENTS -The two varieties of Lathyrus that have occasioned poisonings are Lath, sativus and Lath,
cícera. The peas are very alike in appearance. Those of Lath, cicera are rather smaller than Lath, sativus,
more square, and are a lighter brown. Except for this brownish color they could easily be mistaken for ordinary
peas. Lath, cicera has red flowers. Lath, sativus, bluish. Both are cultivated for food and are sometimes cut
green for fodder.
In the British Journal of Homeopathy there is an account of a wheat famine in India, where the peas of the
plant were substituted for wheat and used as a food. Those who subsisted on it were taken, even during sleep,
with sudden paralysis of the lower limbs. This occurred without warning in young men more than in young
 women, and was never recovered from.
Another observer recorded fifty cases of people who had eaten the lathyrus bread and all stated that they
became paralytic during the wet season of the country. They went to bed quite well and woke with stiff legs,
unsteady gait and aching, but no severe pain. The upper limbs were free.
Another saw the disease in Algeria and described the symptoms in ten cases. Symptoms came on suddenly
in damp weather with some pains in the loins, trembling, motor paralysis and exaggerated reflexes. He
attributed these phenomena to an acute transverse myelitis with degenerative changes in the cord.
Polio (Gels.). Post-polio neuralgia syndrome (Rhus-t, Gels.). Guillain-Barre syndrome, ascending paralysis.
Multiple sclerosis. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Characteristic increased reflexes. Weak and lame joints.
Severe muscle cramps in the calves. Pain induced by touch. Emaciation of the paralyzed muscles (Plb.,
Caust.).
Burning pain on the tip of the tongue. Weak bladder with sudden urgencies to urinate.
Never well since an influenza or a virus. Symptoms may be brought on or be made worse by cold or damp
wind. Burning heat, better uncovering.
O'Connor found that marked benefit followed its use in old cases of myelitis with marked spastic symptoms.
Bartlett recommended Lath, for excessive kneejerk and rigidity.
Hart spoke of it as a remedy for locomotor ataxia, but the absence of sensory symptoms and the presence of
exaggerated reflexes would seem to contraindicate it in this disease. He also spoke of Lath, in spinal anemia,
giving as symptoms “numbness, followed by pain in the lower limbs, sensation of a band around the body,
unable to step or distinguish one limb from another.”
In a case related by Bojanus, the general symptoms were the same. Lath, was the cause of the trouble, arising
during the great Russian famine. Horses fed with Lath, along with oats manifested symptoms of paralysis of
the limbs and also of the throat and wind-pipe, setting up the condition called “roaring.” Some died of
suffocation.
Clarke relieved several cases of spastic paralysis, including Miss R., 25, who had been ill four years with the
usual symptoms of spastic paralysis. Excessive constipation and violent urging to pass water, if she attempted
to retain it, it passed of itself. The muscles were hard and unyielding.
She was heavily drugged under allopathic treatment before coming under his care. Hyper, was first given with
considerable benefit. As the improvement went no further, Lath. 1c and 30c were given and then the
improvement was much more marked.
W. A. Dewey recorded a cure with Lath. 3x in a case of spastic paralysis in a man of twenty-eight. The attack
had been coming on six months. The patient was a hunchback, having been deformed since the age of five,
but this had given no more than the usual inconvenience.
Lathyrus sativus
On admission to the hospital (December 1, 1898), he was unable to make the slightest movement of the lower
limbs, even of the toes.
The adductors were in a constant state of irritable contraction, so that the thighs were constantly crossed.
Reflexes greatly exaggerated. No pain. Spine not tender. General health was normal. The only other symptom
was a girdle sensation, as if he had a cold, damp cloth around his waist.
Three weeks after commencing Lath., there was slight lessening of rigidity. On April 5, 1899, he could raise
his limbs and move his toes. On July 2nd he walked out of the hospital without difficulty, the abnormal irritability
of the muscles having disappeared.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Oxyt., Sec. (2) Peti., a South American plant. - paralysis, paraplegia with
numbness. Sensation of internal coldness. (3) Agrostema githago - burning sensation in stomach, through
esophagus into throat in lower abdomen and anus, nausea, bittervomiting. impaired locomotion, difficulty in
remaining erect, vertigo and headache, burning from lower jaw to vertex.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

 Septicemia conditions, blood poisoning. Tinnitus. Roaring noises. Loss of memory. Vertigo, tendency to fall

name: Latrodectus Katipo
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lat-k. Latrodectus katipo. Red- back spider. N. O. Arachnida. New Zealand spider. Tincture of
living spider. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Chorea. Delirium. Depression. Edema. Faintness. Heart, slow. Lymphangitis. Nettle-rash.
Twitchings.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lat-k. is a venomous spider found in New Zealand and some parts of California. The
symptoms recorded are the effects of bites. The seat of a bite becomes immediately painful and swelling
occurs. In some cases, the swelling does not come on until some days after the bite.
In one case, five days after the bite, a scarlet papulous rash appeared on both limbs, burning like fire. The
symptoms were somewhat slow in evolution. In a fatal case, that of a girl bitten on the abdomen, death did not
occur until six weeks after the bite.
Lassitude, faintness, twitchings and trismus. Scarlet and burning eruptions. Lymphangitis with nervous
twitchings. Long suffering, wasting. Loss of energy. Faint and pale.
MIND - Delirium, half smothered by imperfect intoxication. Semi-intoxicated state. Nervous depression.
Abdomen - Very severe drawing or cramping sensation in abdomen.
Face - Anxious expression. Extreme pallor changing to blue tint of face and body. Jaws stiff, could not open
mouth to eat and could scarcely articulate.
Food - Loss of desire for food.
Heart - Almost pulseless. Pulse slow, scarcely more than twelve or fourteen beats to the minute.
Limbs - Severe shaking, burning pains ran from the bite on the foot up the limbs to back, with nervous twitching
all over body. Pain felt almost equally in both limbs and seemed to center about heel. Feet felt as if rudely
lacerated by dull instrument, walking him from sleep.
Lungs - Breathing almost ceased.
Skin - Small, red spot like flea-bite. Bitten surface raised, the raised part white with red halo with swelling and
pain. Swelling size and shape of hen's egg. The bite remained a small purple point for nine days, on the tenth
began to swell and turn white like a bee sting, pain and swelling rapidly increased, dorsurn of foot and ankle
like a puff-ball, red streak running up leg. A bright scarlet, papular eruption on both lower limbs, which stung
and burned like fire.
Temperature - Limbs cold and flaccid. Cold, clammy sweat covered left lower extremity in morning.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lat-m., Tarent., MygaL, Aran. (2) Apis, Vesp. and serpent poisons.
REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Latrodectus Mactans
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lat-m. Latrodectus mactans. Black widow spider. N. O. Arachnida. Southern North America,
South America. Tincture of living spider. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Chest, pains. Colic. Cramping, pain. Heart, attacks. Heart, disorders.
Hematuria. Hemorrhages. Idiopathic thrombocytopenia. Infectious, purpura. Proteinuria.
HOMEOPATHIC - S.A. Jones and A. J. Tafel introduced Lat-m. into the Materia Medica. The bite produces
tetanic effects that last several days. From the time a man was bitten he took 3 1/2 quart bottles of the best
rectified whisky without any sign of intoxication.
Affects the heart, producing angina pectoris. Heart attacks. The precordial region seems to be the center
of attack. Restless with heart pains and prostration. Constriction of chest muscles with radiation to shoulders
and back. Fear of suffocating or dying.
Blood becomes thin, watery. Lowered coagulability. Inflammation of the coronary arteries. Pain in the solar
plexus. Infectious purpura. Chronic hemorrhaging endothelial plasmatic condition. Chronic idiopathic
thrombocytopenia.
Itching and redness of the part bitten, at first without pain, but violent pain soon commenced there (back of left
hand), and extended in a short time up forearm and arm to shoulder and then to precordial region. Painful
sensations extended up arm to shoulder, along neck to back of head, later, pain in précordia and apnea,
screaming fearfully. Nervous tremors.
MIND - Speech hesitant with tears. Apparently moribund. Depression. Mental fatigue. Amnesia. Memory gives
 no answer to logical deduction. Reading impossible. Staring up at ceiling, vague, in a stupor. Emotional
disturbances. Very nervous.
Acute and enormous anxiety, with sensation of imminent death. Anxiety about the heart. Intense anguish
with the sensation of severe thoracic constriction. Screams fearfully with pain, exclaiming that she would lose
her breath and die. Thinks he will suffocate. Fear of dying. Lamenting helplessly. Wailing.
Agitation. Mental irritability and restlessness. Sensitive to noise. Writhing and rolling in pain. Extreme state of
nervous irritation with fear of going mad. Psychosis, becomes mad and psychotic, with hallucinations.
Abdomen - Severe abdominal pain with nausea and a sinking sensation at epigastrium. Colic and hardness
of the abdominal wall. Chronic cramp of the abdominal muscles without painful tenderness on palpation.
Back - Dorsal and lumbar cramps, going from the nape to the loins.
Chest-Angina pectoris. Violent, precordial pain extending to the axilla and down the arm and forearm to
fingers, with numbness of the extremity. Sinking sensation. Cramping pain from chest to abdomen.
Ears - Pain in the right middle ear.
Eyes - Constant pulsating pain in the eyes.
Face - Expression of deep anxiety.
Food - Extreme thirst, vomits what he drinks.
Head - Pain in neck to back of head. Occipital pain. Headache, aggravated between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m.
Heart - Precordial anxiety. Angina pectoris. Pain in précordia with a loss of breath, screaming fearfully,
exclaiming that she would lose her breath and die. Violent heart pains, sharp, extending to shoulders or
both arms to fingers with numbness. Restless with cardiac pain and prostration. Pulse feeble and rapid.
Limbs - Left arm partially paralyzed, or feels paralyzed, with pain. Hard, aching pain in axilla. Stinging in right
wrist with itching and redness of bitten spot. Paresthesia of lower limbs. Weakness of legs followed by cramps
in the abdominal muscles.
Kidneys - Burning pains on urinating in the urethra. Urine red, albuminous with casts. Proteinuria, hematuria,
glycosuria, diminution in the level of nitrogen eliminated through the urine.
Lungs - Bronchial rales. Cough with hawking, yellow, thick, acrid sputum. Pulmonary edema. Gasping for
breath. Extreme apnea. Respiration only occasional, gasping. Respiration very slow, thinks he will suffocate.
Fear of losing breath and dying.
Male - Frequent erections. Testicularpains, aggravated by movement. Very acute pains in the right testicle.
Perspiration in the genital regions. Itching of prepuce with a little redness of the part.
Modalities - Better by sitting quietly. Worse from the slightest movement, even of the hands, exertion.
Mouth - Labial fissure. Copious salivation. Trembling of the tongue. White coloring of the tongue. Hypertrophy
of the lingual papillae.
Nose - Nose blocked, thick, yellow discharge.
Pulse - Pulse, feeble and rapid. Pulse so frequent it could not be counted and so feeble it could scarcely be
felt. Left pulse extinct, right pulse doubtful.
Rectum - Constriction of the anus with tarry stools. Copious evacuations similar to the black vomit.
Skin - Skin cold like ice, marble-white. Blue coloring. Heavy, cold perspiration. Skin very painful at the slightest
touch. Burning of the soles of the feet. Eruption,
which itches. Formication and extreme sensitivity. Loss of hair.
Sleep - Insomnia. Sleep disturbed, anxious. Dreams of flying.
Stomach - Eructation and loss of appetite. Nausea, then abdominal pains. Vomiting of black blood, which
soothes the condition. Transfixation of pain or sinking at epigastrium. Feeling of weakness in epigastric region.
Throat - Throat red, dry. Tonsillitis with glairy deposit on tonsils. Pain on swallowing.
Vertigo - Vertigo and constrictive headache.
COMMENTS - Heart attack (Cact.), with sharp, shooting pains. Chest pain. Gasping for breath, difficulty
breathing with a fear of dying.
Semple recorded a case of a man bitten on the prepuce. At first there was itching, in less than half an hour
nausea, followed by severe abdominal pains. Soon after, violent precordial pains, extending to axilla and down
left arm and forearm to fingers with numbness of the limbs and apnea. Dry cupping was resorted to and the
blood that flowed was thin, florid and un-coagulable.
When Semple arrived, he found violent precordial pains, the left arm almost paralyzed, pulse 130, very feeble,
Skin cold as marble, countenance expressive of deep anxiety. At eight the next morning, in spite of stimulants,
the symptoms were worse and continued to increase until 2:30 p.m.
The pulse was uncountable and scarcely felt. Vomited black vomit, a quart or more. Soon after, reaction set in
and the man gradually recovered. He had two copious stools like the black matter vomited earlier, and after
that felt quite well.
 Jones noted that the precordial region is the chief locus of attack. He considered the order of the occurrence
of these symptoms of great importance.
Linnell recorded a case of angina pectoris, pain in precordial region and left arm, brought on by the slightest
exertion, that was cured with Lat-m. 3c.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lat-k. and other Arachnida. (2) Helo. - coldness. (3) Lach., Spig., Cimic., Cact.,
Kalm., Lycps. in angina pectoris. (4) Hir. - non-coagulating hemorrhages. (5) the Aran., Mygal., Ther., Lat-h.,
Lat-k. spider venoms. (6) Triât., Kissing bug - swelling with violent itching of fingers and toes. A smothering
sensation and difficult breathing succeeded by fainting and rapid pulse. (7) Helo. - Intense chill, going from the
inside to the outside. Vertigo with tendency to fall backwards. Numbness of the limbs. (8) Kalm. - Palpitations,
aggravated when lying on the left side, pulse slow. Lightning pains, suddenly changing place. (9) Cact. -
Feeling of constriction of the heart, as if a vice, spreading to the left arm, which feels numb. Hemorrhaging of
black blood. (10) Spig. - Violent contractions of the heart with oppression, anxiety. Feels soothed when lying
on the right side with head raised.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Julian. Mtuphy.

name: Laurocerasus Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - laur. Laurocerasus officinalis. Cherry laurel. Common laurel. Aqua lauroc- erasi. Cerasus
laurocerasus. Prunus laurocerasus. N. O. Rosacea. Tincture of young leaves. Dilutions of Aqua Laurocerasi.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Asphyxia, neonatorum. Asthma. Breathing, difficult. Cholera. Cholera infantum. Chorea.
Convulsions. Coughs. Cramps. Cyanosis. Debility. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Heart, disorders.
Hemorrhages. Liver disorders. Lock-jaw. Memory, lost. Menopause. Metrorrhagia. Palpitations. Pneumonia,
typhoid. Strokes. Tetanus. Tumors. Twitchings. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Laurocerasus, the so-called “Laurel” of our gardens, is not a member of the Lauracae,
though the Bay Laurel, Laurus nobilis, is. The Aqua Laurocerasi, prepared by distilling the fresh leaves,
contains hydrocyanic acid and is supposed to owe all its medicinal virtue to this fact.
Symptoms accompanied by sudden debility and lack of reaction, especially in chest and heart disorders.
Asphyxia neonatorum. Cyanosis, of heart disorders. Suffocating spells about heart compel him to lie down.
General coldness not ameliorated by warmth. Coldness and blueness with epileptiform convulsions.
Hemorrhages of thin, bright blood mixed with gelatinous clots. Dry, tickling cough. Cough with jelly-like
expectoration dotted with bloody points. Spasmodic tickling cough in cardiac patients.
Internal burning. Nervous collapse. Long lasting faints. Sensation of falling down in brain, in abdomen, in heart
etc. Bluntness of special senses.
Strokes. Spasm of facial muscles and esophagus. Epilepsy, clonic spasms of all limbs with paralytic weakness.
Chorea, emotional with constant jerks, cannot keep still. Twitchings. Gasping, before during and after spasms.
The speech indistinct after every excitement, gasping for breath. Drink rolls audibly through esophagus
and intestines. Weak sphincters. Violent pain in stomach with loss of speech.
MIND - Insensibility and complete loss of sensation. Loss of consciousness, with loss of speech and motion.
Sudden loss of memory from fright, pain etc. Forgetful on motion. Dullness of special senses.
Angry when not understood. Want of moral feeling. Feels unloved. Cries easily when criticized. Sadness with
impeded respiration.
Fear and anxiety about imaginary evils. Fear of insanity. Delusions, sees old men with long beards and
distorted faces. Thinks she is accused, that she is criticized. Sees distorted faces on lying down during day.
Visions of fire.
Abdomen - Falling down sensation of a lump in abdomen from above the navel to small of back, worse talking
or overexertion. Gurgling flatulence.
Back - Painful stiffness in left side of neck and nape. Compressed feeling in shoulders and nape.
Causations - Effects of fright.
Chest - Constriction of chest. Burning in chest on taking inspiration. Dyspnea with sensation that he is unable
to raise the chest walls, better lying down.
Ears - Hardness of hearing. Tingling, itching in ears.
Eyes - Dry eyes. Eyes widely open or halfclosed, convulsed, prominent and fixed. Burning pain in eyes. Pupils
dilated and immovable. Eyes distorted. Objects look larger. Darkness before the eyes, with obscuration of
sight.
Face - Blue with gasping. Lock-jaw. Twitching of the muscles of face. As if flies and spiders are crawling over
the skin.
 Female - Pain in uterus with cancer, with oozing of bright blood with gelatinous clots, better sleep. Faints with
coldness during menses. Burning and stinking in and below breasts.
Head - Head pain worse 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Nightly tearing in vertex. As if a cold wind were blowing on head.
As if brain were falling. Brain feels contracted and painful.
Heart - Clutching at heart, folds hands over the heart, as if there were some trouble there worse by any
exercise. Pains in the region of heart. Pulse, weak, variable, slow or irregular. Mitral regurgitation. Palpitations.
Kidneys - Urine, retained, suppressed, involuntary, with palpitations, suffocation and fainting.
Limbs - Skin blue. Veins of hands distended. Clubbing of fingers. Toes and fingernails become knotty. Cold
clammy feet up to the knees in chorea, heart disease. Feet numb on crossing the legs. Sprained pains in hips,
thighs and heels.
Liver - Pain in the liver as though abscess were forming. Liver indurated, atrophied.
Lungs - Shallow breathing. Gasping for breath, clutches at heart. Suffocation, gasps for breath, on sitting
up. Exercise causes pain around heart. Small and feeble pulse. Threatening paralysis of lungs. Asphyxia
neonatorum. Cyanosis neonatorum. Cough with valvular dis
ease. Tickling, dry cough. with a copious, jelly-like, bloody expectoration.
Modalities - Better sitting up. Better lying with head low. Better sleep. Better eating. Better open air. Worse
sitting up. Worse stooping. Worse exertion. Worse cold. Worse fright. Worse in the evening and night.
Mouth - Tongue, stiff, cold, burnt or numb. Speechlessness from pain in stomach. Foam at the mouth, with
convulsions.
Rectum - Paralysis of anal sphincter, involuntary stools. Rectal cancer, with bleeding of bright red blood.
Sensations - Coolness of forehead as from draft of air. Weight on top of head. As if brain loose and falling
into forehead when stooping. As if a veil before eyes. As if lungs could not be sufficiently expanded. As if lungs
pressed against spine. As if mucus membranes were dry. Stitches are very prominent, also stiffness and pres-
sure, especially pressure outward.
Skin - Cool, livid.
Sleep - Frequent yawning. Coma vigil. Sleeplessness from over-excitement and sudden heat. Fearful anxiety
and restless, cannot fall to sleep. Spells of deep sleep with snoring and stertorous breathing. Troublesome
and agitated dreams.
Stomach - Disgust for food during pregnancy. Drinks roll audibly through esophagus and intestines. Violent
pain in stomach with loss of speech. Stomach pains during urination. Persistent hiccough. Bitter belchings.
Nausea near a hot stove. Vomiting of food during cough.
Temperature - Coldness, chills and heat alternate. Shuddering, followed by burning heat. Heat running down
the back. Thirst with dry mouth in afternoon.
Throat - Spasmodic contraction of throat and esophagus. Larynx and trachea raw. Low voice.
Vertigo - Vertigo with sleepiness.
COMMENTS - Laur. has a peculiar “gasping,” gasping without really breathing. Blueness and twitching of the
muscles of the face. Cyanosis, particularly in newborns (Aeon., Carb-v.). Valvular problems, regurgitation,
weak hearts.
Suffocative spells about the heart, worse by sitting up, the patient is compelled to lie down (Psor.). Some heart
symptoms compel the patient to sit up. Blue around fingertips. Clubbing of fingers, common in cyanosis and
tuberculosis.
Guernsey gave these leading symptoms, “gasping for breath, the patient puts his hand to the heart as if there
was some trouble there, this may result from running a short distance, which puts him completely out of breath,
going upstairs, walking or any exercise may bring the gasping on.”
Cough with valvular heart disease, incessant cough, especially on lying down, fluttering in heart and gasping
with cough. Spasmodic cough of later stages of whooping cough, when patient is much prostrated and has
nervous spasmodic symptoms. Dry, harassing cough of tuberculosis. Alternation of chill, fever and sweat in
tuberculosis.
Long-lasting faints (Camph. has sudden fainting), seems to have no reactive power, face pale, blue, cold
surface. Prostrate before getting up in the morning with difficulty opening the eyes. Nervous disorders with
constant jerks, cannot keep still. Allen noted an extremely nervous, excitable condition accompanying ailments.
Attacks of indigestion and pains across lower abdomen that come suddenly in the morning and generally
disappear on getting up. Gnawing pain in lower abdomen, with occasional looseness of stool, particularly in
old men. Green mucus diarrhea, with suffocative spells about heart.
Fluids roll audibly into the stomach. Digestion is weak, bowels confined. Low- spirited with flatulence and
burning in chest after food. Audible and gurgling flatus, rolls about the upper abdomen. Constricted sensations
in gullet, in rectum. Symptoms worse before eating.
 Inclined to lose flesh and hemorrhages that are small in quantity and bright in color. Menorrhagia and
dysmenorrhea. Eruptions are livid after pressure with the finger, the skin is long in regaining its color.
Constant tired and sick feeling. Sleepless with a great desire for sleep.
Coldness, internal coldness and external heat. Cold tongue. Heat of single parts. Warmth on center of
forehead, then a coldness as from a draft of air lasting a long time. The left chest is most affected.
Pains start from the lower part of the spine and extend either around the pelvis or up to the head. Pains are
accompanied with a sense of suffocation, a sick feeling with drowsiness, and a great desire to sleep that
generally brings relief.
Cooper, in his work in Cancer and Cancer Symptoms, offered cases emphasizing the uterine symptoms. The
indications of Laur., according to Cooper, are a sense of fatigue that pervades the whole system with a very
painful condition of the hard and indurated tissue of the parts affected. Pain is much better by sleep.
Tendency to ooze blood, which is generally bright and mixed with gelatinous clots. This applies to the chest
as well as to uterine and rectal symptoms, only the blood comes painlessly into the mouth, but with great pain
in the vagina.
E. Wigg related the case of May S., 7, who had been troubled for some time with an almost incessant cough,
for which many remedies were given without benefit. At last Wigg came to the conclusion that Laur. was the
remedy and put ten drops of Laur. 200c into five tablespoonfuls of water ordering a teaspoonful of this to be
taken every two hours when the child was awake.
This was at 4 p.m. After the third dose she fell asleep. At 3 a.m. she awoke in a very excited condition. Her
mother asked her if she had not been dreaming, but her tongue was so stiff she could not answer. Suddenly
she began to tremble all over as if in a chill.
After ten minutes she began to twitch and jerk. Wigg was sent for and found her in this convulsed state. She
could not articulate for the thickness and heaviness of the tongue. The mind was clear. Recognizing the action
of Laur., Wigg antidoted it with camphor, and later a cup of coffee, and symptoms ceased in a few hours. She
had no more of the cough.
RELATIONS -Antidotes: the effects of digitalis given in crude doses. Antidoted by: Camph., Coff,Ip.,
Op.Compare: ( 1 ) Hydr-ac., Camph., Sec., Am-c., Ambr. (2) Amyg., Prun., Prun-v., and other Rosacea. (3)
In hunger after meals with feeling of emptiness, Calc., Chin., Cas-s., Chion., Grat. (4) after meals and after
stool, Petr. (5) in semi-lateral swelling of tongue, Calc., Sil., Thuj. Laur. has loss of speech with it. Compatible:
Bell. Phos., Puls., Verat.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Laurus Nobilis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - laur-n. Laurus nobilis. Bay leaf. Bay laurel. Sweet bay. Grecian laurel. Laurel tree. Bay tree. N.
O. Lauraceae. Tincture. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Arthritis. Bacterial, infections. Blood, sugar. Bronchitis. Bruises. Cancer. Colic.
Flatulence. Fungal, infections. Headaches. Indigestion. Influenza. Migraine. Rheumatism. Sprains. Stomach,
ulcers.
HERBAL - The bay tree is indigenous to Asia Minor, from where it spread to the Mediterranean and then to
other countries with similar climates. Bay leaves and berries have been used for their astringent, carminative,
diaphoretic, digestive, diuretic, emetic and stomachic properties.
It has a long history of folk use in the treatment of many ailments, particularly as an aid to digestion and in the
treatment of . bronchitis and influenza. It has been used to treat various types of cancer.
Bay leaf has been used as an herbal remedy for headaches. It contains compounds called parthenolides,
which have proven useful in the treatment of migraines. It has also been shown to help the body process
insulin more efficiently, leading to lower blood sugar levels. Reduces the effects of stomach ulcers.
Bay leaves also contain eugenol, which has anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties. They are also anti-
fungal and anti-bacterial. The leaves have been used to treat rheumatism, arthritic aches and pains.
Upper respiratory tract disorders. Hysteria. Amenorrhea. Flatulent colic.
Bay oil, Oleum Lauri, has been used in liniments for bruising and sprains. The essential oil has narcotic,
antibacterial and fungicidal properties. An infusion has been used to improve the appetite and as an em-
menagogue.
The fruit is antiseptic, aromatic, digestive, narcotic and a stimulant. It has been used in making carminative
medicines and was used in the past to promote digestion. It has a tonic effect, stimulating the appetite and the
secretion of digestive juices.
COMMENTS - Bay Laurel is the source of the bay leaves which are used for their flavor in cooking. It was also
 the source of the laurel victory wreath of ancient Greece, and therefore the origin of the expression of “resting
on one's laurels.”
According to legend, the Delphi oracle chewed bay leaves, or sniffed the smoke of burning leaves to promote
visionary trances. In the Middle Ages it was believed to have many magical qualities.
It has also been used to keep moths away; the leaves' lauric acid content gives it insecticidal properties.
RELATIONS - Compare: Cham., Catar., Mag-p.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Lavandula Vera
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lav-v. Lavandula vera. Lavender. Lavandula angustifolia. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of the
flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Backache. Belching. Bums. Constipation. Flatulence. Headaches. Indigestion. Insomnia. Lice.
Memory, weak. Nausea. Palpitations. Toothache. Wounds.
HERBAL - Although lavender is a native of southern European hillsides, where it thrives in the sparse soil and
burning sunshine, it has been grown in Britain for decades. The Romans would certainly have introduced a
herb they esteemed so highly, and possibly it had been introduced before their days.
Historically, lavender has been used not only for its fragrance but also as a disinfectant, vulnerance (useful for
healing wounds), sedative, stimulant, tonic and caiminative (a medicine that expels flatulence). The herbal
history of lavender can be traced back to ancient Greece.
Dioscorides (an army doctor) mentioned French lavender, which seems to have been used only medicinally
by the Greeks. He attributed to it certain laxative and invigorating qualities and recommended its use in a tea-
like infusion for chest complaints.
The Romans used lavender to perfume their public baths (its name derives from the Latin “lavare,” meaning
to wash). Roman soldiers carried their own first aid kits of herbs, and whenever the armies settled herbs would
be grown, including lavender.
The Romans were aware of lavender's healing, soothing and insect repellent properties, and used its oil in
massage. They also burnt lavender in honor of their gods. Galen (129-199 AD) added lavender to the time
honored antidotes, theriac and mithridate, and Nero's physician used it for anti-poison pills and in uterine
disorders.
Abbes Hildegarde (1098-1180) from a monastery in the diocese of Malinz in Saxony, made some of the earliest
mediaeval references to lavender in her writings. She realized its practical effect in getting rid of lice and
prescribed it for cleaning eyes. She also thought it could drive away evil spirits.
The first original work on gardening written in English, a treatise by Jon Gardener (1440), mentions “lavyndull”
growing in English gardens. From this date on, lavender is mentioned often in manuscripts and books, and it
is clear that it became a popular herb valued for its medicinal virtues and scent.
HOMEOPATHIC - Insomnia. Memory, weak.
MIND - Lack of focus. Disorientated. Distracted, restless. Overwhelmed by responsibilities. Anxious, better
alone. Worried feeling during the day. Active thoughts, prevents sleep.
Poor short term memory. Forgetful. Difficulty recalling events and conversations that occurred only days or
even hours before. Difficult concentrating. Particularly tired when trying to communicate. Muddled up words or
even forgot them altogether. Could not string a sentence together.
Disinclined to talk. Crossness and irritability. Jumpy, nerves on edge. Intolerant of others. Short tempered.
Irritated by noise. Woke up feeling slightly headache and cross without reason. Does not feel comfortable but
cannot say why.
Miserable and depressed. Negative outlook, fatalistic. Weeping. Felt insignificant and unlovable. Sensation
that every thing feels far away. Indifferent to loved ones. Bored with life.
Abdomen - Constant burning indigestion, mid-abdomen. Bloating in abdomen.
Arms - Right arm painful. Burning sensation under right arm. Left elbow, bone pain as if sitting in damp. Elbow
to hand felt numb, slight pins and needles. Right wrist, weak, difficulty in writing. Left hand, itchy at base of
fingers, especially center finger.
Back - Backache. Lower back pain, in lumbar region. Lower back pain almost unbearable, better stretching.
Dull aching pain over left kidney, right side of lumbar region. Pain better lying, worse sitting, bending down
drawing up the knees. Dull nagging lumbar pain, worse lying, better sitting. Sharp, pulling ache. Unbearable
pressing pain in lumbar region, feels as if internal organs are squeezed by hands, better bending down,
drawing knees up, rest, worse movement, moving causes clinching pain, tighter and tighter.
Bladder - Slow urination.
 Breasts - Sensitive breasts. Sharp tingling pain in right breast. Severely painful breasts.
Heart - Palpitations on climbing stairs.
Chest - Burning sensation in chest. Constant stinging pain in right breast. Tightness in chest muscles.
Ears - Severe stabbing pain in left ear. Loud sound like musical instrument in left ear.
Eyes - Heavy eyes through exhaustion, difficulty keeping the eyes open, the eyelids very heavy. Tiredness
between and behind eyes. Painful left eye, wakes at night.
Generals - Immune system feels weak.
Female - Feels physically lighter before period. Menstrual flow heavy, stops abruptly.
Food - Appetite and thirst diminished. Appetite increased, no desire to eat. Increased thirst, evening. Wakes
up with thirst. Thirsty with dry mouth. Desires for tea, orange juice. Desires green salad, fruit. Desires savory
food. Averse to bread.
Head - Headaches. Congested feeling. Head feels clogged up, thick. Brain feels loose, floating, soft, spongy.
Sensation of blood pulsating around brain. Dull headache on right side with stiff neck. Slight headache in
forehead, above eyes. Throbbing frontal headache with pressure above eyes, better drinking water. Throbbing
temples. Itching on right temple, red with white flakes.
Limbs - Uncoordinated movement. Constant dragging, painful ache in joints. Severe nagging aching in legs,
thighs. Tingling, cramping limp in left leg. Pulling pain in right thigh. Aching pain in left calf muscle. Feet cold.
Pain along side of big toenail on left foot.
Lungs - Breathing labored, better drinking
Mouth - Dry mouth with a slightly sensitive tongue, thirsty. Less saliva than usual. Increased saliva. Sticky
saliva not better by washing mouth, eating or drinking. Thick saliva, better drinking. Dull aching in bottom right
side of jaw. Toothache in carious teeth. Sharp pain upper incisor, better hot soup, worse cold butter.
Neck - Aching, painful neck.
Nose - Sense of smell increased. Slight running nose.
Rectum - Painless, sudden diarrhea. Constipation. Offensive stools. Sore rectum. Flatulent at night.
Shoulders - Stiff, aching pain in left shoulder. Painful right shoulder.
Skin - Dry skin, itching, worse scratching, after hot water, better in water, particularly
Lavandula vera on hands. Burns.
Sleep - Insomnia. Could not get to sleep even though tired. Restless, tossed around all over the place,
constantly changing position. Disturbed sleep. Once asleep awakes early and find it difficult to get back to
sleep. Heavy and unrefreshing sleep. Moaning in sleep.
Stomach - Stomach pains with hunger, even after eating. Stomach upset, burning indigestion. Indigestion,
better milk, small meals. Slight dull ache, covering size of frying pan. Cramping pains with bloating and
belching, better sitting up, worse lying down. Nausea. Upset stomach followed by constipation.
Throat - Sore, dry throats that persist, better drinking water, hot drinks. Sore throat only at night. Spasms,
better drinking.
Tongue - Taste diminished. Unpleasant taste in mouth. Burning sensation on the tongue, sensitive, sore. Tip
of tongue feels burnt, sore. Yellow coating on tongue.
Vertigo - Dizzy with flushed feeling, felt heat on top of head. Dizzy when turning suddenly, on driving car.
Vision - Diminished vision. Double vision, as if looking through frosted glass.
RELATIONS - Compare: Kali-p., Gink-b.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Lecithinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lec. Lecithinum. Lecithin.
Prepared from the egg yolk or soybeans. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Convalescence. Fatigue. Impotency. Insomnia. Malnutrition. Neurasthenia. Ovarian,
insufficiency. Tuberculosis. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lecithin is important in the vital processesof plant and animal organisms. It is prepared from
the yolk of egg, a phosphorus containing complex organic body. Causes an immediate decrease in the
excretion of phosphates.
Favorable influence upon the nutritive conditions and especially upon the blood. Marked improvement in
nutrition and general improvement in tuberculosis.
Galactagogue, it renders breast milk more nourishing.
General weakness. Anemia. Neurasthenia. Useful for convalescence. Tired, weak, short breath, loss of flesh.
Insomnia. Ovarian insufficiency. Sexually weak. Impotency.
 MIND - Mental exhaustion and impotency. Prostration of mind. Forgetful, dull, confused, worse mental
exertion. Concentration difficult. Confusion of mind, as if in a dream. Insomnia. Excitement in company.
Fear of impending disease.
Ears - Pulsating and ringing in ears.
Face - Pain in zygoma, face pale.
Head - Aching, especially in occiput-pulsating and ringing in ears. Pain in zygoma, face pale.
Kidneys - Scanty with phosphates, sugar or albumen.
Limbs - Soreness, aching, lack of energy. Tired and weak.
Sexual - Anaphrodisia and ovarian insufficiency. Male power lost or enfeebled. Impotency.
Stomach - Loss of appetite. Thirsty, craves wine and coffee. Bloated feeling. Sore pain in stomach rising
toward throat.
RELATIONS - Compare: Agn., Phos.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Phatak.
