name: Ledum Palustre
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - led. Ledum palustre. Wild rosemary. Marsh tea. Marsh cistus. Labrador tea. N. O. Ericaceae.
Tincture of dried small twigs and leaves collected after flowering begins. Tincture of whole fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincnire and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anal, fissure. Ascites. Asthma. Bedsores. Bites. Black-eye. Boils. Bruises.
Carbuncles. Colic. Deafness. Ear, inflammation. Eczema. Erythema nodosum. Face, pimples. Feet, pains.
Gout. Hemoptysis. Hands, pains. Joint, disorders. Lice. Meniere's disease. Priapism. Prickly, heat.
Punctured, wounds. Rheumatism. Rhus, poisoning. Skin, eruptions. Stings. Tetanus.
Tinnitus.Tuberculosis. Vaccinations. Varicella. Whitlow. Wounds.
HERBAL - Teste, who was one of the chief clinical authorities on Ledum, mentioned that it is native to damp
regions of the North of Europe, and that no animal except the goat eats it on account of the strong, resinous
smell of its leaves, which “keeps off lice and prevents flour from getting moldy.”
Merat said Ledum cures the itch and scald-head, which Teste explained by its parasiticide action. This anti-
parasitic action led Teste to think of Led. as a remedy for bites and punctured wounds, especially as certain
symptoms of the proving seemed to agree with it.
The success which has attended this use of Led. in mosquito bites, stings of bees and wasps, rat bites, and
needle pricks resulting in whitlows, confirmed the observation. Wesselheft noted that Led. aborted a felon in a
few days, “Redness, swelling and throbbing in point of index finger from prick of a needle.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Led. affects the fibrous tissue of joints, especially ankles, tendons, heels and skin, hence it
can be called a rheumatic remedy, where rheumatism begins in the feet and travels upwards. Affected parts
become purple puffy and then emaciate.
Punctured wounds, produced by sharp- pointed instruments or bites, particularly if the wounded parts are
cold. Insect stings, animal bites. Helps prevent tetanus (Hyper, if tetanus develops). Tetanus with twitching
of muscles near wound.
Rheumatic diathesis, functional pain, altered secretions, deposits of solid, earthy matter in the tissues.
Rheumatism begins in feet and travels upward. Painful, cold, edematous joints. Shifting, tearing pains.
Weakness and numbness of the affected parts. Dropsy.
Rushes of blood. Abscess and septic conditions, better by cold. Petechia. Cold all the time, in bed in the
house. General lack of body heat, heat of bed is intolerable. Pale, delicate persons. Alcoholism. Eruption,
like poison-oak and is antidotal to it.
MIND - Absent-minded. Mental dullness. Sluggishness. Difficult thinking and comprehending. Confusion of
mind, as if intoxicated, after eating. Anxiety. Timidity. Ennui, boredom.
Discontented in daytime. Morose and pee- vishhumor. Vehementangrymood.Tendency to anger and rage.
Violent. Misanthropy. Dissatisfied, hates his fellow beings. Hatred of men. Aversion tofriends, company.
Avoids the sight of people. Desire for solitude.
Frightened easily. Fear in a crowd. Fear he will die if he goes to sleep after nightmare. Delirium on closing
eyes. Ideas abundant on closing eyes. Dementia. Moaning, groaning. Suicidal disposition. Unconsciousness,
coma.
Abdomen - Pain in abdomen as if intestines were bruised. Sensation of fullness in upperpart of the abdomen.
Ascites. Drawing pain. Colic as if diarrhea would set in from umbilicus to anus. Dysenteric bellyache. Frequent
discharge of flatus.
Back - Lumbago. Stiffness, cramps in back, worse rising from sitting.
 Causations - Ill effects of punctured wounds, recent or chronic injuries, animal and insect bites, stings, bruises.
Ill effects of alcohol, hair cutting or suppressed discharges.
Chest - Oppressive constriction of chest. Chest hurts when touched. Pain along trachea.
Constitutions - Sanguine temperament. Adapted to full-blooded, plethoric, robust people. Suited to pale,
delicate persons. Complaints of people who always feel cold and chilly. Rheumatic, gouty diathesis,
constitutions abused by alcohol.
Ears - Hardness of hearing, as if the ears were stuffed up with cotton, worse cutting the hair, wetting the head.
Eyes - Bloodshot or bruised. Black eye from injury. Hemorrhage into the anterior chamber after an
iridectomy. Ptosis of eye (right) from injury. Contused wounds. Aching in eyes. Cataract with gout. Tears
acrid, make the lower lids and cheeks sore.
Face - Mottled. Facial eczema. Red pimples on forehead and cheeks, stinging when touched. Crusty
eruptions around the nose and mouth. Swollen submental glands.
Female - Bleeding fibroids. Great coldness during menses, yet desires cold air. Menses too early and too
copious, the blood is bright red. Leucorrhea.
Food - Violent thirst for cold water. Want of appetite and speedy satiety.
Head - Raging, pulsating headache, worse least covers. Blood boils on forehead. Itching as office. Misstep
causes concussion in the brain. Affected after getting wet.
Kidneys - Urine often stops during the flow. Copious, clear, colorless urine, deficient in salts. Much uric acid
and sand in urine.
Limbs - Gouty pains shoot all through the foot and limb and in joints, but especially in small joints. Gouty
nodosities. Cracking in joints, worse warmth of bed. Cramps over hip joint. Rheumatism begins in lower
limbs and ascends (Kalm., opposite.). Swollen blotchy ecchymotic legs and feet. Easily sprained ankles.
Ankles swollen. Soles painful, can hardly step on them. Heels sore. Feet itch by night and are stiff in
morning. Ball of great toe swollen (Both-1.). Feet held to earth as by a magnet, when attempting to move.
Trembling of hands when moving them or grasping anything. Throbbing in right shoulder, on raising arm.
Lungs - Dyspnea, chest feels constricted. Suffocative arrest of breathing. Bronchitis with emphysema of the
elderly. Whooping cough, spasmodic double inspiration with sobbing. Yellow, purulent, sputum. Cough with
bloody expectoration. Hemoptysis, alternating with rheumatism or coxalgia.
Male - Inflammatory swelling of penis, the urethra is almost closed. Increased sexual desire. Violent and
prolonged erections. Pollutions of bloody or serous semen.
Modalities - Better by application of ice water, bathing, cold, air, reposing. Worse in evening, night, heat of
bed, warmth of covers, stove, air. Worse injury, motion of joints, spitting, eggs, wine.
Mouth - Bitter taste in the mouth, moldy when coughing. Sudden flow of watery saliva during colic. Musty taste
with catarrhal affection.
Nose - Persistent nosebleed (Meli., Bry.). Soreness of the nose with violent burning.
Rectum - Anal fissure. Blind, smarting hemorrhoids.
Sensations - Pricking, biting sensations. Sensation of torpor of tissues, especially after suppressed discharge
from ears, eyes and nose. Sensation as if something was gnawing in temples, occiput and ears. As if sand in
eyes. As if eyeball would be forced out. Noises in ear as from ringing of bell or from a wind-storm, as if ear
was obstructed by cotton. Itching as from lice on chest, as of lump in throat. As of boiling in hip joint. As if
muscles of thigh in wrong position. As if knee beaten.
Skin - Puncture, stab wounds. Animal bites and insect stings. Ecchymosis. Long discoloration after
injuries, injections, vaccinations. Twitches, from bites, nails, stings, with foul pus. Red spots and rash.
Eruptions on only covered part. Acne on forehead, with sticking pain. Itching of feet and ankles, worse
scratching and warmth of bed. Carbuncles (Anthr., Tarent-c.). Antidote to rhuspoisoning (Grind., Cypr.,
Anae.). Bedsores. Edematous swelling.
Sleep - Great inclination to sleep during day, drowsiness with great wish to lie down. Sleeplessness with
restless tossing, jerking, fantastic visions and images on closing eyes. Agitated, anxious dreams. Uneasy
dreams in which he changes from place to place and from one subject to another. Lascivious dreams with
emission of semen.
Stomach - Nausea with the inclination to vomit, on expectorating. Dry, retching with eructation. Contractive
pain in sternum when eating quickly. Water brash with cramp-like pains in abdomen.
Temperature - Coldness, want of body heat. Coldness of parts, worse in limbs with the pain during fever, as
if in cold water. Sensation as of cold water over parts, general coldness with heat of face.
Foul sweat. Profuse night sweat.
Throat - Sore throat with shooting pain, during and after deglutition. Tormenting cough from tickling in larynx
with nosebleed, then sobbing respiration, worse receding eruptions. Sensation as if there were a plug in the
 throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo when walking, with tendency to fall to one side. Distress when head is covered.
COMMENTS - Puncture wounds, stab wounds, animal bites and insect stings (Hyper.), particularly if septic in
appearance. After affects of punctured wounds. Preventative for tetanus. Side effects of vaccinations.
Dental work with punctures (Hyper., Am.). Bedsores. Sore, achy and bruised injuries (Am.). Injured part feels
cold. Wounded area can emaciate. Wounds are better with cold applications.
Red, gushing hemorrhages. Hemoptysis alternating with attacks of rheumatism. Lengthy discoloration of
contused parts. Slight injuries cause ecchymoses. Ecchymosis from blood transfusions or IVs.
Marked eye symptoms. Nash says Led. 200c is unequaled as a remedy for “blackeye” from a blow (Symph.,
if there is pain in the eyeball). Ecchymoses of conjunctiva. Inflammation of ear with deafness from getting cold
(as having hair cut).
Sticking, tearing, throbbing pains. Pain in ankle as from sprain; limbs as if beaten and bmised. Hot, tense, hard
swellings. Hering noted that “Ledum has often been given to horses when they go lame and draw up their legs.
The pains move upward.”
Led. occupies the second place in Teste's Am. group, in which are also Crot-t., Ferr., Mang., Rhus-t., and Spig.
According to him, the sphere of Led. is frequently identical with that of Am.
However, Led. has a special action on the capillary system in parts where cellular tissue is wanting and where
a dry, resisting texture is present, as in the fingers and toes. “It is, perhaps for this reason that it acts better on
the small joints than on the large joints,” hence its appropriateness in gout.
Rheumatism and gout that migrates from joint to joint, generally from feet upward. Pains shoot upward (Kalm.,
downward). Symptoms are worse from warmth, better by sitting with feet and legs in cold water. The warmth
of the bed is intolerable, he must get up and walk about.
Teste describes the characteristic skin affection of Led. as a sort of bluish or violet-colored tuberosities,
especially on the forehead. Eczematous eruptions with a tingling itching, that spreads over the whole body,
penetrating into the mouth, probably also into the air-passages and occasions a spasmodic cough (Rhus-t.
and Crot-t.).
Teste reported “In a gouty subject I have seen cough precede by days the breaking out of vessel on the which
could not fail to suggest the use of Led. These vesicles, which had existed on the bronchial membrane, before
showing themselves in the face, on the shoulders, etc., became quite apparent on the tongue, where they
might be traced to its root.”
Eczema concentrated on one leg, less frequently on both at once. Ingalls commended a light paste of Led.
(equal parts of Led., alcohol and water) as an application for carbuncles, giving Led. lx internally at the same
time.)
For hangovers from drinking hard liquor (Nux-v. is for wine and beer). For rhus poisoning.
Teste related a case of a puncture wound in which a young woman fell with an embroidery needle in her hand
and the hand was pierced through, giving a serious wound. There was no hemorrhage, but Teste noticed the
intense cold that accompanies and characterizes Ledum fever. Within a week, Led. cured the patient.
Yingling recorded a parallel case, A. J. M., 38, drove a rusty spike through his left foot near the arch of the
instep, glancing to the inside of the foot without passing through the bone. This was at 5 p.m. At 8 p.m. a report
was brought to Yingling relating the events.
A few moments after the accident the patient felt stiffening pains in the foot, running up the leg and rapidly
increasing
in severity. Great chilliness with chattering of teeth followed. The lower jaw became somewhat stiff, general
shivering, the neck felt stiff.
The patient reported that he “can't endure it much longer.” Led. 3x was sent and rapid improvement took place
from the first dose. A compress of Calen. 3x. was also applied, an attack of tetanus being evidently aborted.
Teste recorded the case of an octogenarian who had rheumatism of his left arm, chiefly in the elbow and wrist,
coming on in the night or early morning. There was no more sleep for him unless he rose and took a cold bath
after which he could sleep. Cured with Led. 30c.
E. Carleton completed the cure of a case of primary syphilis in which Aur. had done well, where the feet were
held to the earth as by a magnet when attempting to move, when moving felt as if pricked with needles.
The pain rising gradually from feet to head, every joint and muscle of body and limbs stiff and sore, sore night-
sweats, great emaciation with loss of appetite. Led. 200c in water, cured completely and speedily.
Dr. R. Hilbert, a German physician, obtained very satisfactory results from the use of an infusion of the leaves
of Led. as an expectorant in bronchitis. He stated that the feeling of pain along the trachea, which is
characteristic of the early stages of acute bronchitis, disappeared after a few doses of the remedy.
The fever rapidly subsided, especially in the case of children. In chronic bronchitis, the infusion facilitates
 expectoration and lessens cough.
Particularly useful in bronchitis with emphysema of the aged, because of its action in rendering the bronchial
secretion less viscid in these cases. It lessens dyspnea and stimulates the circulation. Whooping cough.
Lembke offered the indication that before the paroxysms there is an arrest of breathing. During attacks, there
is nosebleed, a shattered feeling in head and chest, and rapid respiration. After, there is staggering, spasmodic
contraction of diaphragm, and sobbing respiration. Worse in the evening.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. according to Teste, Rhus-t. is the best antidote. It antidotes: Effects of
alcohol, Apis. Compare: (1) Led. and Hyper, antidote spider poisons. (2) Ruta, Ham., Bell-p., Arn. (3) Kalm. -
bot., Kalm. pains shoot down. Led. pains shoot up. (4) Arn. - trauma. Led. follows Arn. when it fails to relieve
soreness, punctured wounds. (5) Crot-t. - skin cold. (6) Ham. - traumatic ecchymosis, black-eye. (7) Ruta -
bruises, Ruta, especially of periosteum, Symph. of bone, Hyper, of nerve. (8) Apis - nightly itching of feet. (9)
Am-m., Nat-c. (blistered heels), Zinc.,Rhus-t.,Nux-v.,Sei., H-ac.,Ant-c.,Puls., Bov. ( 10) Sil. - worse from wine,
Sil. - chronic rheumatism, extending from feet upwards, Sil. better covering up, Led. better uncovering.
Compatible: Aeon., Arn., Bell., Bry., Nux-v., Puls., Rhus-t., Sulph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

***LEMNA MINOR (Duckweed) PHARMACY - lem-m. Lemna minor. Duckweed. N. O. Lemancee or Pistiacee.
The fresh plant is pounded to a pulp and macerated in two parts by weight of alcohol. Tincture of the whole
fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Atrophic rhinitis. Catarrh. Coryza. Diarrhea. Influenza. Nose, disorders. Ozaena.
Polyps. Rhinitis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lindley noted Dr. Robert Cooper's description in the Homeopathic Monthly, “The lowest
form of phenogamous vegetation. It consists of lenticular floating fronds, composed of stem and leaf together
and bearing the flowers in slits in the edge.”
It forms the green scum found on stagnant ponds and dikes. It is found in two varieties, Lemna minor and
Lemna gibba.
Nose blocked with polyps. Nasal polyps, swollen turbinates. Atrophic rhinitis, crusts and muco-purulent
discharge very abundant with fetor. Asthma from nasal obstruction, worse in wet weather. Excessive catarrh
with frequent sneezing attacks. Foul smell in nose or loss of smell.
Dr. Burnett noticed that Lem-m. patients have their nasal symptoms aggravated in damp and rainy weather.
Lem-m.'s symptoms aggravated in heavy rains, Calen., when heavy clouds are about, Rhod. in thunder storms,
and Dulc., in damp surroundings and in foggy weather.
Nasal polyps in aman, 60, that were markedly worse in wet weather took Lem-m. 3x at 5 drops three times a
day for a month, and said “That is the best tonic I have ever taken,” he could breathe quite comfortably.
Abdomen - Rumbling and disturbance in bowels. Twisting pains in bowels, followed by diarrhea.
Ears - Hearing impaired.
Face - Pale, dull, sickly look.
Head - Flitting pains about head and legs with pains in eyes during heavy rain. Drowsy by day, restless at
night.
Lungs - Asthma with nasal obstruction. Asthma, attacks coming on in rainy weather. Snoring inspiration.
Modalities - Worse in damp. Worse rainy weather. Worse heavy rains.
Mouth - Putrid taste on rising in the morning. Foulness of mouth, putrid teeth. Dry pharynx and larynx.
Nose - Polyps which swell in wet weather. Nostrils plugged by swollen turbinates. Nasal obstruction from an
edematous condition. Coryza and catarrh. Ozaena. Discharge profuse, thick, purulent, viscid, yellow, white.
Post-nasal dripping, ulceration. Crusts and muco-purulent discharge very abundant. Pain like a string from
nostrils to ear. Foul smell from the nose and foul taste in the morning on waking. Dryness of naso-
pharynx.
Rectum - Diarrhea, worse wet, damp weather. Disposition to noisy diarrhea. Diarrhea with pains across bowels
as from flatus, worse after eating with very putrid teeth. Bowels acted freely with much heat in anus. Morning
diarrhea.
Sleep - Snoring, cured after an aggravation of diarrhea.
Smell - Odors, imaginary and real. Putrid smell. Loss of smell.
Throat - Sensation of intense dryness in pharynx and larynx. Dryness with atrophic rhinitis. Dropping of foul
secretion from posterior sinuses.
COMMENTS - Nasal polyps (Sang., Thuj.), nostrils plugged by swollen turbinates and other causes. Chronic
atrophic rhinitis. Putrid smell in the nose, or loss of sense of smell. Nasal symptoms are worse in wet weather.
Putrid taste in the mouth, especially on rising in the morning with a general foulness of mouth, due to postnasal
 dripping. Disposition to “noisy diarrhea.”
Clarke recorded a case of a woman, 47, who had, two years previously, met with an accident, a sign board fell
on her head when she was out walking in the street. Seven days after, she was taken with sneezing attacks,
suffered from nasal catarrh with little intermission until March, 1893, when she came under his care.
Psor. 30c relieved her trouble, which had made her life almost unbearable, as she never dared make an
appointment for fear of an attack coming on, and she discontinued treatment. That winter, a sharp attack of
influenza brought back the catarrh and it proved less amenable to treatment.
Fears of polyps distressed the patient, though Clarke could not discover any. However, she again made
progress, when he thought of giving her Lem-m. on indications given by Dr. Cooper.
On February 15,1894, Clarke gave Lemna 3x, one tablet four times a day. February 22, she felt very much
better, freer in the head than at any time during the last ten years, spirits braced up. She steadily progressed
to cure, and by March 15 could endure the smell of strong scented flowers, which before was impossible.
Captain B., aged forty-four, consulted Clarke on February 29, 1894, for violent neuralgia on the right side of
the neck, the part being exquisitely sensitive to touch. He had a cough and cold for a month. On getting up in
the morning, he filled two pocket handkerchiefs with yellow effusion before he got his nose clear.
Clarke gave him Bell. 12c to take until the neuralgia was better and then told him to take Lem-m. 3x, three
times a day. On March 9 he reported that the Bell, speedily took away the neuralgia and that then the Lem-m.
cleared off the catarrh in a most astonishing fashion. He never had a medicine act so magically before.
A man of sixty years of age with nasal polyps only moderately developed, yet of many years duration, was
much troubled by the chronic nasal obstruction that was markedly worse in wet weather. Clarke gave him Lem-
m. 3x, five drops in water, night and morning.
Returning in a month, he exclaimed, “That is the best tonic I have ever taken, I have never taken any medicine
in my life that has done me so much good. I feel quite comfortable in my nose and can breathe through it quite
well.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1 ) Dulc. - damp surroundings and foggy weather. (2) Calc., Teucr., Calen., Nat-s.
(3) All-c., Agra., Chlor., etc., (4) in nasal catarrh, Teucr., Calc, and Thuj. in nasal polyps. (5) Psor., Cadm-s.,
Aur., Kali-bi. and Syph. in ozaena. (6) Anae, in bad smell in nose. Follows well: Calc., Merc., Psor.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Leonurus Cardiaca
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - león. Leonurus cardiaca. Motherwort. N. O. Labiate. Tincture or infusion of fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Dysentery. Hemorrhages. Miscarriages. Suppressed, lochia. Suppressed, menses. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The popular name of this plant sufficiently indicates its traditional virtues. The only
experience with it is an involuntary proving recorded by Clarence Bartlett.
A married woman, 40 took an infusion to produce miscarriage. Twenty-four hours later Bartlett saw her and
found her vomiting and retching, passing bloody stools, suffering severe abdominal pains.
The pains were provoked by drinking anything more than a small quantity of water, which she did to allay her
great thirst. Dry conjunctive, and a dry, cracked tongue were noted. The bowels symptoms were worse
midnight to 3 a.m. Ars. 3x relieved all symptoms. She did not miscarry.
Influences pelvic organs, allays spasm and nervous irritability. Promotes secretions and reduces febrile
excitement. Suppressed lochia and menses. Dysentery, with vomiting, frightful pains in abdomen and violent
thirst. Tongue dry and cracked.
Abdomen - Very severe abdominal pains with soreness to touch. When lying on side, better drawing up legs;
when on back, better with legs out straight.
Eyes - Conjunctive looked as if wiped dry.
Female - Suppressed lochia and menses. Tends to miscarriages.
Food - Intense thirst, yet drinking more than a very slight quantity of water, warm or cold, provokes epigastric
pains.
Mouth - Tongue dry, coated or brownish white, covered with cracks in arborescent arrangement, main crack
down center.
Rectum - During the night, frequent calls to stool. Stools dark brown, then bloody.
Stomach - Vomiting and retching.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Ars. Compare: Hedeo.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
 ***LEPIDIUM BONARIENSE
(Brazilian Cress)
PHARMACY - lepi. Lepidium bonariense. Brazilian cress. Lepidium mastruco. Senebiera pinnatifida. N. O.
Crucifere or Brassicacee. Tincture and trituration of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture, trituration and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Breasts disorders. Cough. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Indigestion. Rheumatism.
HERBAL - Lepidium is a Brazilian cress. Mure noted that “It is very common in the neighborhood of Rio, where
it is found along the roads and in stony regions.” It is a great remedy in domestic practice in Brazil and is
used for purposes similar to those for which Am. is used.
All the Lepidium are anti-scorbutic and Lepidium oleraceum, the New Zealand variety, was eagerly sought
after as a remedy for scurvy by the early voyagers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Disorders of breasts, heart. Heart symptoms with numbness and pain in left arm, sensation
of sinking in pit of stomach. Sensation of a tight girdle around chest, as of a knife piercing the heart.
Sharp pain in left side of head, face, chest, hip to knee. Pain in neck, back and limbs. A streak of pain from the
temple to the chin, as if the face were cut with a razor. Burning in the throat, roaring in ears.
MIND - Sad and quarrelsome. Inability to think. Imagined the floor sinking under her. Imagines herself pursued
by a phantom in a churchyard, cries with loss of voice next morning.
COMMENTS - Mure's proving of Lepi. brought out some distinctive symptoms on the left side of the head, in
the limbs, and especially in the heart.
Heart symptoms with numbness and pain in the left arm. Sinking feeling in the pit of the stomach indicating an
action in the solar plexus. Darting pains. Sharp, throbbing pains. Worse from stooping, turning head to the
right, when covered.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Am., Lach. (2) Brass., Cheir.. Thlaspi., Armor, sat., Raph., Sinap. (3) Spig.,
Kalm., Lycps. - heart problems.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Leprominium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lepro. Leprominium. Leprosy nosode. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne, vulgaris. Alopecia. Aphonia. Dermatitis. Edema. Erythema multiforme. Flatulence.
Gingivitis. Glaucoma. Immune, disorders. Iritis. Kaposi's, sarcoma. Leprosy. Leucoderma. Leukemia. Lichen,
planus. Lipoma. Lupus, erythematosus. Lupus, vulgaris. Lymphoma. Molluscum, contagiosum. Neuritis.
Neurofibromatosis. Numbness. Osteoarthritis. Pityriasis. Psora. Psoriasis. Rhinitis. Ringworm. Sarcoidosis.
Scleroderma. Skin, disorders. Tinea versicolor. Urticaria.
HOMEOPATHIC - Leprosy is a disfiguring, crippling disease prevalent in tropical countries. Dr. Vakil
introduced Leprominium, using signs and symptoms collected from 100 patients suffering from various types
of leprosy.
There are two preparations. The first, Leprominium H, was prepared from a leprous nodule from the ear of a
patient where the presence of lepra bacilli was microscopically demonstrated.
The second, Leprominium A, is used for ascertaining the reactivity of the patient, and was prepared from the
lepra bacilli cultured on the foot web of an armadillo.
MIND - Meticulous. Mild or irritable. Brooding. Weeping. Attributes disease to fate. Hopeful of recovery.
Fearless. Aversion to begging.
Feels rejected. Likes company. Desires sympathy, yet secludes self to hide early stages of disease. Religious
melancholy. Desire to put on white colored clothes, aversion to black colored clothes. Loathes life, but not
suicidal.
Abdomen - Flatulence in lower part of abdomen. Passing flatus ameliorates.
Cough - Chronic cough in some smokers with emphysematous changes.
Ears - Chronic otorrhea. Thickening and nodulation of the ear. Appearance as if had rat-bite.
Eyes - Swelling, puffy, baggy under eyes. Ectropion. Cannot close the eyes completely, sleeps with eyes half
open. Eyelashes drop off. Red, painless discoloration. Sensation of heat. Xerophthalmia. Dryness, with bland
or acrid lachrymation, worse from light, sun. Itching and agglutination. Photophobia. Squints. Conjunctivitis.
Scleritis. Interstitial keratitis. Iritis, iridocyclitis. Trachoma. Corneal opacity. Herpes simplex on cornea.
Glaucoma. Cataract formation, left to right. Blindness.
Face - Anesthesia of the face, anesthetic patches. Numbness and cobweb sensation. Deformed, leonine,
prematurely old appearance. Thickened skin of the face with permanent wrinkling. Nodules on the face,
nodulation and ulceration of nose and lips. Edema, angioneurotic. Palsy. Paralysis. Trigeminal neuralgia. Waxy
 or oily look. Outer one third of eyebrows lost. Eyelashes lost. Mustache hair lost in the middle.
Female - Menopause early. Sexual desire absent.
Fever - Scanty perspiration. Rigors with fever. Remittent or intermittent fever with infections. Malaria giving
rise to lepra reaction.
Food - Thirst increased. Desires green chilies, meat, fish, spicy, sour, ice cold water. Aversion to milk, sweets,
worse from sour food.
Head - Alopecia areata. Hair loss on hy- popigmented patches. Hair turns gray prematurely. Hemicrania.
Kidneys - Glomerulonephritis. Nephritic syndrome. Urination frequency increased in some patients.
Intermittent flow. Urination painful, from walking in sun.
Limbs - Anesthesia of hands, feet. Heat in palms, soles. Ascending coldness. Hands andfeet icy cold.
Sensation of ice in limbs, better warm clothes. Numbness and tingling. Ascending numbness. Peripheral
neuritis. Paralysis, paraplegia. Edema of the feet, worse evening, walking, hanging feet down. Wrist drop, foot
drop. Pain in limbs, massaging ameliorates. Pain in knee joints, worse initial motion, better
continued motion. Osteoarthritis. Nodules like neurofibromatosis. Deformities of limbs. Patches
hypopigmented, well defined, thickened, raised. Sensation loss on hypopigmented patches. Non-healing
ulcers. Gangrene. Maggots.
Lungs - Tendency to catch cold. Pulmonary tuberculosis. Difficulty breathing.
Male - Gynecomastia. Sexual desire absent. Desire increase, with nocturnal emissions. Enlarged testes.
Impotency. Aspermatogenesis. Oligospermia.
Mouth - Swelling lips. Flat-topped nodules on tongue, lips. Deep fissure in tongue. Glossitis. Adherent uvula
to soft palate. Uvula ulceration. Infiltration and nodules on uvula and soft palate. Small ulcers. Gums bleed
easily. Gingivitis. Turgid and swollen gums, shiny purplish in color.
Nose - Nasal obstruction. Clinkers and scabs. Offensive scabs from nose but patient cannot smell. Waxy
nose. Flattened tip. Collapse of the nose. Depressed nose. Atrophic rhinitis. Atrophy of the anterior and inferior
turbinate. Perforation of septum. Nosebleeds, worse cold, wet on head, washing face, or sneezing.
Rectum - Constipation. Semi-solid stools with mucous, without pain in abdomen.
Skin - Lupus vulgaris. Anesthesia, hy- poesthesia or thickened erythematous anesthetic patches.
Neurofibromatosis. Discoloration, dark pigmentation. Dryness of whole body, in many patients with scanty
perspiration. Cracks deep in palms and soles. Erythema multiforme, ulcerous lesions. Nodules, small, pe-
dunculated. Eruptions bullous, macules, flat, hypopigmented or erythematous. Pemphigoid scabs, dark brown
small, scaling, resembling exfoliative dermatitis. Ichthyosis. Psoriasis, itching all over. Ringworm. Urticaria.
Scabies. Pellagra. Skin sticking to the bones giving a shiny appearance like scleroderma.
Sleep - Eyes remain half open during sleep. Dreams frightful, unremembered. Dreams of dead people, dead
relatives. Refreshed on waking.
Teeth - Loose teeth, because of changes in the bones which secure the teeth. Upper
Leprominum central and lateral incisor dropping out.
Throat - Cicatrices, laryngeal and pharyngeal constriction. Sensation of something stuck in throat.
Hoarseness of voice. Loss of voice, complete aphonia.
Vertigo - Weak feeling, blackout. Vertigo with nausea, worse opening eyes, sun.
COMMENTS - Vakil concluded that Lepro. should prove to be a useful nosode on the basis of symptom
similarity and also as an intercurrent remedy to clear the miasmatic background.
He noted that leprosy resembles many skin conditions, including leucoderma, nutritional discolouration of the
skin, macular syphilides, tinea versiclour, lupus erythematosus, and lupus vulgaris. Neurofibromatosis,
cutaneous sarcoidosis, leukaemia cutis, Kaposi's sarcoma, subcutaneous phycomycosis, lymphoma.
Seborrheic dermatitis, erythema multiforme, alopecia areata. Ringworm of the skin, psoriasis, lichen planus,
pityriasis rosea, urticaria, scleroderma. Lipoma, acne vulgaris, molluscum contagiosum etc.
Leprosy can resemble progressive muscular atrophy, ainhum, gangrene, mango-toe, peripheral neuritis, Bell's
palsy, Dupuytren's contracture, nasal deformities, maralaga paresthetica, carpal tunnel syndrome,
syringomyelia, tabes dorsalis, and spina bifida. Leprosy also resembles syphilis to a great extent.
Leprosy affects the reticuloendothelial and immune system. The disease traumatizes the mind of the individual,
and gives rise to symptoms resembling anxiety neurosis, depression and melancholia.
As it resembles many diseases, some of them chronic and intractable, and as this disease was widespread in
many countries, “lepra” can be considered as a separate miasm. For complaints that develop slowly but give
rise to irreversible pathological changes.
Vakil suggested that as Bac. andTub. have separate spheres of action, Leprominium H and Leprominium A
should have separate spheres of action.
 Leprominum
Vakil noted the case of a female child, 6, came to the out-patient department of the Government Homeopathic
Hospital with a rough patch of skin just near the right cubital fossa since she was 2. It was roughly 2 inches by
4 inches and itched slightly. There was thick scab formation with a raw surface underneath.
Mez. 30c was prescribed on the symptoms chilliness, possible bad effects of vaccination, and itching from
touch. A small scab came off within a week, but there was no further improvement.
Vakil waited for 2 months, and was considering repeating the Mez. in a higher potency when he noticed an
anesthetic patch on the back of the woman who accompanied her, who turned out to be the girl’s neighbor.
Additional symptoms included a religious feeling, desire for white clothes, sympathetic and desiring sympathy
for herself, tendency to catch cold, desire for green chilies and an obstinate skin condition.
Vakil prescribed Lepro. A 30x, single dose. To the surprise of all, the scabs started coming off within a week.
By the end of the month she was 80% better. It was noticed that immediately after the administration of the
nosode she had semi-solid stools with mucus and running of the nose for a week.
RELATIONS - Compare: Psor., Sulph. Mez.
REFERENCES - Vakil.

name: Leptandra Virginica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lept. Leptandra virginica. Culver's root. Veronica virginica. Black root. Culver'sphysic. Tall
speedwell. N. O. Scrophu- lariaceae. Tincture of resinoid Leptandrin. Tincture of fresh root of second year.
Trituration of dried root. A fresh plant tincture should also be made and tested. Historical dose: Trituration,
tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ascites. Bilious, attack. Bilious, fever. Black, stools. Constipation. Diarrhea. Dysentery.
Dyspepsia. Headaches. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Remittent fever infantile. Typhoid, fevers. Yellow fever.
HOMEOPATHIC - Leptandra, in the form of the resinoid Leptandrin, was proved by Burt. As one of the grand
characteristics of it relative Digitalis is white stools, so the grand characteristic of Leptandra is black stools.
Great varieties of stool, in the later stages of the proving it became dysenteric and mixed with shreds.
Constipation with hard black stool, followed by softer stools.
Liver symptoms, with adull, heavy, frontal headache. These symptoms confirm the use of the drug by eclectics
as a kind of “vegetable calomel.” Sensation as if something was passing out of rectum.
Farrington noted the dull aching in the right hypochondrium, gallbladder and back of liver, accompanied by
soreness. Burning distress in and about liver after spreading to stomach and bowels, with drowsiness and
despondency. Bilious and typhoid fevers with black, tarry stools.
Eye symptoms (Euphr.). Generally rightside. Chilly sensation along the spine and down right arm. Pains in
right shoulder and arm. Symptoms are worse by motion, rising causes nausea and faintness. Weakness, so
great he is hardly able to stand.
MIND - Hopeless, despondent and drowsy. Sadness with liver troubles. Irritable. Anxiety in abdomen after
stool. Sensitive to penetrating noises. Weary, can hardly walk.
Abdomen - Sore or dull, burning ache over liver or near gall bladder, extending down over bowels to navel or
towards left scapula or along spine, which feels chilly. Constant dull aching in umbilical region. Great distress
in stomach and intestines with desire for stool.
Back - Chilly sensation in shoulders and down back. Sore, lame feeling in small of back. Constant distress
with very sharp pains by spells in lumbar region.
Eyes - Smarting and aching in eyes with dull pain in eyeballs. Profuse lachrymation. Lids agglutinated.
Female - Menses, suppressed or retarded with liver affection. Warm, watery leucorrhea, runs down the limbs,
from ulceration of the os.
Food - Canine hunger. Craving for cold food and drinks, raw food, salads. Worse fats, rich foods, meat and
vegetables.
Head - Dull pain, vertigo, drowsiness and depression. Dull frontal headache, with aching in navel. Smarting
and aching in eyes.
Heart - Soreness in heart. Pulse slow and full.
Kidneys - Red or orange colored urine with dull aching in lumbar region.
Limbs - Pain in sciatic nerve (left), worse on sitting. Nails very thin, soft and splitting.
Liver - Acute liver conditions. Dull, burning aching in liver, worse near gallbladder. Sore or dull pain, worse
from touch or pressure. Burning distress in back part of liver and spine. Liver swollen transversely. Periodical
liver derangement, every two or three months. Bilious states. Gallstones. Jaundice. Hepatitis. Portal vein
congestion.
 Modalities - Better from lying on abdomen, on side. Worse fromcolddrinks, exposure to wet weather, motion,
periodically.
Mouth - Tongue, yellow or black down center. Flat taste.
Rectum - Prolapse of rectum with hemorrhoids. Bleeding hemorrhoids. Rectal hemorrhage.
Skin - Jaundice. Dry, hot skin.
Sleep - Sleepiness with liver troubles. Sound sleep. Sleep restless after midnight, feels very ill next day.
Stomach - Craving for cold drinks, which aggravate burning and aching in stomach. Sinking at the pit of
stomach. Great distress in stomach and small intestines with immediate desire for stool. Nausea and deathly
faintness on rising. Bilious vomiting. Vomiting of bile, yellow tongue, shooting pains about liver, black stools.
Stools - Jaundice with clay-colored stools. Stools, muddy, watery, worse in morning. Stools, tarry or black,
foul with pain at umbilicus. Typhoid stools turn black and look like tar. Stingy, waxy or spurting stool in the
morning with pain at navel.
Temperature - Chilly along the spine and down the arm. Shivering or dry, hot skin,
limbs cold and numb tongue black down center. Bilious typhoid fever.
COMMENTS - Affects the right side and liver. Bilious states. Enfeebled portal circulation. Hemorrhages due to
liver disorders. Jaundice and black, tarry stools. Conditions with black, tarry stools. Melanotic stools. Hepatitis.
History of cirrhosis, hepatitisjaundice or colon cancer with dried blood in the stools. Colon cancer. Weakness,
hardly able to stand or walk. Typhoid. Malarial conditions. Useful as an herbal tonic for the liver.
Hale noted the order of the different kinds of stools in the proving. First there are black, thick, tar-like, fetid
stools. This is followed by thinner, brownish, often fetid stools. Then stools of mixed mucus, flocculent and
watery matter with yellow bile or blood. Finally, there is mucous, bloody stool mixed with shred-like substances,
often pure blood.
Hale said it is only in cases of dysentery that have developed in this way that Lept. is curative, not in cases
primarily dysenteric. Cases due to sudden climatic changes have been cured by it.
Neidhard observed a periodicity in cases cured by him. Periodical, occurring every two or three months, yellow-
coated tongue, constant nausea with vomiting of bile. Shooting or aching pains in region of liver, loss of
appetite, urine brownish or very dark, often pain in transverse colon, giddiness. Characteristic very dark, almost
black stools.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Podo.. Iris, Bry., Merc., Ptel., Myric. (2) Like Dig. and Tab. it has sinking at the
pit of the stomach.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Levico Aqua
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lev. Levico aqua. Tyrol mineral springs. An arsenical mineral waterof the South Tyrol.
Containing iron and copper with other elements. Dilutions. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Debility. Chorea. Skin, diseases.
HOMEOPATHIC - Levico has a high reputation among health resorts for nervous and skin cases, favoring
assimilation and increasing nutrition.
Burnett is the only homeopathic authority. He said “Levico in 5 to 10 drop doses is a valuable intercurrent to
help in grave cases where there is much debility. Notably after the searching remedies such as Bacillinum.”
Lev. is supplied in two strengths, the strong and the weak. Either may be used in the doses indicated by
Burnett, which is much smaller than that usually prescribed.
Chronic skin diseases. Chorea minor, spasms in scrofulous and anemic children. Debility. Favors assimilation
and increases nutrition.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Levomepromazine
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - levo. Levomepromazine. Allopathic drug. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Agoraphobia. Alcoholism. Allergies. Anorexia. Athetosis. Chorea. Epilepsy. Hypotension.
Hypothyroidism. Mental, disorders. Myoclonia. Parkinson's disease. Tachycardia. Wilson's Disease.
HOMEOPATHIC - Symptoms of the toxicologic iatrogenic effects of the drug. The salt, used therapeutically,
is the maleate.
Depressive action, anti-convulsive, sedative, anti-emetic, anti-histaminic. It is used in psychiatry for maniacal
cases, conditions of agitation, delirium and hallucination in the form of tablets of 5 mg and 25 mg.
Symptoms result from the toxicology of the product, the clinical case of a female patient in Brussels, from self-
observation by a pharmacist, and from the proving by O. A. Julian, on a group of sixteen provers, nine men
 and seven women during the winter of 1968-69, using the 3x, 7c, 9c, 15c, 30c potencies and placebo.
Mental complaints of a depressive and schizophrenic nature. General apathy with nausea. Mental laziness
with agitation. Morning lassitude. Fatigue, sleepiness around 5 p.m. with slow heartbeat.
Clear diminution in attention and ability to concentrate.
Hypotension and tachycardia. Multiple allergic sensitivities. Intestinal, hepatic and gastric malfunctioning.
Increase in weight.
MIND - Disinterested state. Anxiety from anticipation. Premonition of an indefinable imminent event. State of
panic with desire to cry out for help. Anguish, aggravated in a room with light and people. Neurosis from
anguish.
Instability. Desire to weep. Fear of going mad, nervy, on edge. Agoraphobia. Desire to harm someone.
Anorexia. Schizophrenia. Hallucinations in chronic alcoholics.
Abdomen - Distention after eating starchy food. Hypertrophic cirrhosis of the liver. Entero-hepatic syndrome.
Gastric and intestinal dyspepsia.
Back - Pains in the shoulder.
Blood - Rise in the sedimentation rate.
Chest - Oppression of chest.
Constitutions - Suited to phospho-fluoric or tubercular types with psychomotor depression, hypotension and
disinterest in the environment, listless with morning fatigue.
Ears - Diminished hearing.
Eyes - Feeling of eyes enlarged.
Food - Anorexia, alternating with bulimia and desire to eat anything. Progressive loss of appetite. Desire for
alcoholic drinks which are badly tolerated. Cannot digest milk, milk products, Crustacea.
Head - Diffuse, dull headache.
Heart - Acrocyanosis. Tachycardia neurosis, on exertion in anxious types. Postural hypotension. Heart
constricted with anguish in the morning. Palpitations at the slightest effort.
Kidneys - Oliguria.
Limbs - Twisting spasms. Cramps, in the toes. Arthritis of the scapula and humerus. Clumsiness, drops things.
Circulatory disorders at the periphery, the limbs of the limbs take on a purple color with mauve or white patches.
Lungs - Tachycardia with asthma. Dyspnea on effort. Dyspnea from anguish. Nervous asthma.
Male - Urinary retention. Diminished libido. Neurotic impotence.
Modalities - Better from gentle heat, coffee, tobacco. Worse from light, a crowd.
Mouth - Dryness in the mouth. Bitterness and bad breath. Tongue whitish-gray with absence of thirst.
Nose - Diminished sense of smell.
Rectum - Diarrhea with liquid stools around 8 p.m. with 4-5 successive stools. Constipation.
Skin - Pruritus sometimes accompanied by small urticaria patches. Prurigo strophulus. Painful skin hardening
without suppuration, following intra-muscular injections of Levomepromazine.
Sleep - Y awning with sleepiness after meals. Unpleasant, anguished dreams, about the death of dear people.
Stomach - Gastric and intestinal dyspepsia.
Vertigo - Feeling of faintness.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sep. - Apathy, sadness, headache with pressing pains. Feeling of emptiness in
the stomach. Yellowish mark across the nose. Desire to be alone. (2) Tub. - Weakness with constant need to
change place. Headache from mental exertion. Anxious, glum, melancholic. Morning diarrhea. (3) Chlorpr. -
Disorders of the body of the endocrine system and the thalamus of an introverted psychopathic nature. Halluci-
nation, genetic troubles. Thermal and hepatic disorders. General slowing down and dumbness. Catatonic
syndrome. Vesicular, bullous rashes and pigmentation disorders.
REFERENCES-Julian.

Hypothyroidism. Mental, disorders. Myoclonia. Parkinson's disease. Tachycardia. Wilson's Disease.
HOMEOPATHIC - Symptoms of the toxicologic iatrogenic effects of the drug. The salt, used therapeutically,
is the maleate.

name: Liatris Spicata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - liatr. Liatris spicata. Colic root. Liatris serratula. Dense button-snakeroot. Gay feather. Devil's
bit. N. O. Composite, tribe Cicoracee. Tincture of powdered fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Anasarca. Colic. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Headache. Indigestion. Kidney, dropsy. Ulcers.
HERBAL - Liatris is an old herbal remedy for indigestion and colic. T. C. Duncan explained
Liatris spicata that it is called “Devil's bit” as a piece is missing from each tube, as if it had been bitten out.
Liatris has the reputation of being “aromatic, stimulant, diaphoretic, diuretic, anodyne and carminative,”
particularly useful in colic, headache and flatulency.
 HOMEOPATHIC -Generalanasarca due to heart and kidney disease. Colic. Diarrhea with violent urging and
pain in lower part of back. Suppressed urine. Dropsy from liver or spleen diseases. Kidney dropsy.
Applied locally to ulcers and unhealthy wounds. A prompt diuretic. Vascular stimulant. Increases functional
activity of the skin, mucus membranes.
COMMENTS - Liatr. was introduced to homeopathic medicine because of its action in two cases of dropsy
under eclectic treatment. The first was a case of dropsy from material enlargement of liver and spleen, the
second was a case of dropsy with almost total suppression of urine. After other remedies had failed. Liatr. was
given and, on the second day. the patient passed a gallon and a half of urine.
A. E. White wrote that it has a popular repute as specific in chronic diarrhea following exposure in camp life,
and also as an application to non-granulating ulcers. For this purpose the root is to be chewed and then applied.
White was invited to chew a piece, which he did. In six or eight hours he had three successive calls to stool,
very urgent, a little griping in lower back and some straining at stool. He has confirmed its use in camp diarrhea,
but says it acts better if Sulph. or Merc-c. is given first.
White reported the case of Mr. X, 56, who had chronic diarrhea since the war. He had tried treatment of all
kinds, homeopathic included. He had twelve to sixteen stools a day and had loss much weight. He was run
down and had made up his mind he had only a short time to live.
He was given Sulph. 30x two doses, one each night, then Merc-c. 3x, a dose each night for five nights, then
Liatr. lx, four pellets each night for five weeks, by which time he was completely cured.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Lilium Tigrinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lil-t. Lilium tigrinum. Tiger lily. N. O. Liliaceae. Tincture of fresh stalk, leaves and flowers. Some
of the provings were made with tincture of the pollen alone. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Arthritis. Asthenopia. Astigmatism. Dementia. Depression. Diarrhea,
Dysentery. Eyes disorders. Fibroma. Heart,disorders. Hysteria. Ovarian disorders. Pruritus vulva. Sexual,
disorders. Spinal irritation. Urination, frequent. Uterus, disorders. Uterus, prolapsed.
HOMEOPATHIC - The tiger lily, which was introduced into the West from China and Japan, was first suggested
as a remedy by W. E. Payne. Carrol Dunham urged Payne to have it proved and assisted by having it proved
on a woman under his supervision. The account of this case is given in Dunham's Science of Therapeutics.
Some of the provings were made with the tincture of the pollen alone.
The provings showed symptoms of increased activity, things went more easily. Ill humor, drowsiness, sleep
but with unpleasant dreams. Sweetish nausea without inclination to vomit. Abnormal fullness worse after eating
ever so little. Bloating more pronounced and chiefly across hips, in uterine region.
Darting pains in head and lower abdomen, from ovaries down thighs. Knees ache. Pressure in vagina, pain at
of sacrum extending to hips. Increased sexual instinct. Crazy feeling with thoughts of suicide, head grows wild
after being quiet for a short time. Increased depressing weight, worse evening.
During the provings, Lil-t. was given for 10 days, then stopped, but the symptoms continued to develop and
increase in intensity for eight weeks longer, when it had to be put an end to by an antidote.
Lil-t. manifests its chief action upon the venous circulation, the heart and female organs, ovaries and uterus.
Useful for reflex conditions dependent on pathological conditions of these organs.
Lilium tigrinum
Uterine reflex states, dependent on pathology of uterus or ovaries. Utero-ovarian sagging. Symptoms of
sexual overexcitement. Women exhausted by sexual excess. Often indicated in unmarried women.
Pain in small spots (Ox-ac.). Rheumatic arthritis. Burning palms and soles accompany complaints. Full, heavy
orforced outfeeling in uterus, ovaries, heart etc. Wandering, flying, shooting pains or opening and shutting
pains, radiating from ovary to heart, to left breast, down the legs etc. Backward pains, about eyes to occiput,
from nipples through chest, from heart to left scapula.
Affects the bladder and rectum. Pulsations, ebullitions, gurglings and burnings. Nervous tremors in
hypogastrium in spine, knees etc. Venous congestion. Acrid discharges. Nervous, hysterical. Faints in warm
room or after standing for a long time. Rheumatism.
MIND - Mental and physical symptoms alternate. Mental and uterine symptoms alternate. Mental and heart
symptoms alternate. Hurried, wants to do several things at once, walks fast, does not know why.
Restlessness and nervousness. Must keep busy.
Haughty and proud. Capriciousnessi Abrupt. Snappish. Censorious, critical. Irritability and sensitivity.
Indifferent to anything done for her. Apathy, indifference to love ones. Averse to amusement. Very timid.
Prefers company.
 Anxiety with palpitations. Anxious, fears some organic and incurable disease. Delusions that she has an
incurable disease. Anxiety about business, the future, health. Dementia from business worries. Fear of going
insane, impending disease and suffering, being incurable. Fear of falling, from faintness, worse close warm
room. Fear of evil.
Discontented. Dissatisfied, envious of others. Sentimental. Sits alone and broods over imaginary troubles,
dwells on past. Grief, sighing. Constant inclination to weep. Grief, hunting for something to grieve oneself.
Profounddepression, worse consolation. Post-partum depression. Desires death. Suicidal disposition by
poison.
Disposed to curse, strike, think obscene things. Cursing, swearing, blasphemy, and profanity. Feels as if she
must scream out. Desire to pull the hair out. Hysteria. Wild, crazy feeling. Stupefaction, as if intoxicated.
Religious affections and sadness. Tormented about salvation. Delusions that she is doomed.
Strong sexual desire, lessened by keeping busy. Confusion of mind from sexual excitement. Sexual
excitement, alternating with apprehension of religious ideas, or despair. Nymphomania. Erotic, sexual
fantasies. Dementia from sexual excesses, uterine problems.
Abdomen - Abdomen sore, distended, can't bear weight or covers. Skin of abdomen feels stretched and stiff.
Abdomen sensitive to pressure or jarring. Trembling sensation in abdomen. Heavy dragging downfeeling of
whole abdominal contents with dysuria. Bearing down pain in lower part of abdomen, worse walking. Sharp
pains, better gentle rubbing with warm hand, doubling up.
Back - Neck pain and aches, worse if tired. Glands on left side of neck swollen and painful. Broken feeling
between scapula. Sensation of pulling upward from tip of coccyx. Spine sore, with stiffness, worse in loins.
Dull pain in sacrum. Cold feeling across loins and sacrum. Back as if drawn backwards, after heart attack.
Breasts - Cutting pain in left breast, with sighing and shortness of breath. Pains in left breast and left ovary.
Cramp like pain, in left breast, shoulder and fingers. Sensation as if a rivet or ball under left breast.
Causations - Ailments from being alone, celibacy, being unmarried. Ailments from sexual excesses, childbirth,
menopause.
Chest - Constricted feeling in left side of chest. Oppressive load on chest. Tight, hot, congested feeling. Sharp,
quick pains in left side of chest, with fluttering of heart. Chest feels as if too full of blood. As if a lump in the
center of chest moving up and down on empty swallowing.
Ears - Neuralgia in right ear. Rushing sounds in ears after going to bed.
Eyes - Wild look in eyes. Biting and burning sensation, worse reading. Pain, extending back into head,
lachrymation and impaired vision. Sensitive to light. Photophobia during pain in forehead. Hyperesthesia of
retina. Weakened ciliary muscle ( Arg-n.). Feel sprained.
Face - Heat and bloated feeling of face and head. Chilly feeling in face in afternoon.
Female - Amenorrhea with cardiac distress or burning stinging ovarian pains. Menses, early, scanty, dark,
clotted offensive. Flow only when moving about. Menses cease when resting (Bell., Lac-c., Sep.). Dys-
menorrhea with sensation of constriction from back around hips, ending in pubes. Offensive leucorrhea and
great weakness during menses. Acrid, brown, thin leucorrhea, stains brown, worse after menses. Smarting in
labia, worse after menses. Ovarian pains with palpitations, mental symptoms. Ovarian pain down thighs
or up below the left breast. Sharp pain in region of ovaries and in back. Pains in left ovary and left breast.
Stinging pain in left ovarian region. Bloated feeling in uterine region. Neuralgic pains in uterus, cannot bear
pressure of clothes. Bearingdown pains with urgent desire for stool. Sub-involution. Congestion of uterus.
Prolapse uterus. Anteversion and retroversion of uterus. Sensation as though all organs would escape
(Sep., Lac-c., Bell-p.), especially uterus. Constant desire to support parts externally, afraid to move.
Nymphomania. Sexual desire increased, obscene, must keep herself busy. Sexual excitement, ending in
orgasm. Voluptuous itching in vagina. Pruritus pudendi. Slow recovery after labor.
Food - Hungry, craving for meat, sour or sweet dainties. Aversion to coffee to bread. Thirsty, drinks often and
much, before severe symptoms.
Head - Hot, dull, heavy, with morning diarrhea. Faint in warm room. Wild feeling in head, as though she
would be crazy- Headache burning, dependent on uterine disorders, worse before and after menses, better
at sunset. Headache over left eye to
vertex with vertigo and visual effects. Sick headache every few days, much worse at menses. Drawing hot
pain through head and eyes, better frequent sneezing. Sharp neuralgic pains over eyes, worse motion and
evening. Stinging, burning pains in forehead.
Heart - Sensation as if heart were grasped in a vise (Cact.). Heart as if alternately grasped and relaxed. As
if heart is hanging by a thread. Heart feels full to bursting. Cold feeling about heart. Heaviness in region of
heart. Sensation as if heart stopped, followed by rush of blood to heart and palpitations. Palpitation from
excitement, worse lying on either side. Palpitations during pregnancy. Pain in cardiac region with feeling of
 a load on chest. Angina pectoris with pain in right arm. Pulse irregular, very rapid. Pulsations all over the body.
Kidneys - Frequent urging. Constant pressure on bladder with constant desire to urinate, with a sensation as
of a ball in rectum. Frequent urination, almost every fifteen minutes, with scanty discharges, followed by
irritation and smarting in urethra. Urine, milky and scanty, hot like boiling oil. If desire is not attended to,
feeling of congestion in chest.
Limbs - Pain in back and spine with trembling, often of a pressing-down character. Limbs feel cold, clammy,
worse when excited or nervous. As if acool wind blowing on legs. Staggering gait, cannot walk straight, or on
uneven ground. Pain from hip to hip. Joints feel dry. Trembling of knees. Legs ache, cannot keep them still.
Pain in right arm, hip, ankle joint. Burning in palms and soles. Paralytic stiffness of fingers. Pricking in fingers.
Lungs - Air hunger, takes long, deep breath. Suffocates in a warm or crowded room, theater or church.
Shortness of breath. Oppressed breathing with sighing. Sharp pain through right lung, worse in open air.
Male - Increased sexual desire. Lascivious dreams and emissions, followed by irritability, difficulty in fixing
one's mind, selecting wrong words.
Modalities - Better from pressure, support, rubbing, lying on left side, crossing legs. Better from cool, open,
fresh air, during the day, when busy. Worse from warmth of room, sunset, evening, night, afternoon, from 5
p.m. to 8 a.m.. Worse from motion, walking, standing, jarring, lying on left side, pressure of bed clothes,
rubbing. Worse after miscarriage. Worse from consolation. Diarrhea worse early morning.
Mouth - Sweet taste in back of mouth. Foul taste, better eating. Taste of blood, during congestion to chest.
Saliva abundant. Mouth and throat feel coated on waking in the night. Tongue, coated yellowish, white in
patches. Darting pain from teeth to ear.
Nose - Sneezing, better pain in head andeyes. Discharge thin, clear, yellow mucus. Nose stopped up.
Stoppage of right nostril with pain in right side of face. Rubbed her nose violently. Constant desire to pick nose.
Rectum - Constant desire to defecate from pressure in rectum, worse standing. Pressure downwards and
backwards against rectum and anus. Weak, tremulous feeling extending to anus. Diarrhea, directly after
dinner, sudden and peremptory. Early morning diarrhea after rising, urgent, cannot wait a moment. Sensation
as if diarrhea would come on, passing off by urinating. Dysentery, mucus and blood with tenesmus,
especially in plethoric and nervous women at menopause. Stool preceded by griping pains or great urging,
with pressure on rectum. Stools, small, frequent with tenesmus. Tenesmus of the rectum and bladder.
Hemorrhoids after childbirth.
Sensations - With nausea, a lump in center of chest which could be moved down by empty swallowing. As if
an electric current in fingers and hands. As if cool wind blowing on lower limbs.
Skin - Tingling, formication, burning in various parts. Irritation of upper chest and arms and a fine rash about
forehead and around borders of the hair with much itching. Skin of abdomen feels stiff and stretched.
Sleep - Yawning, stretching, drowsy. Unable to sleep on account of wild feeling in head. Slept soundly, but
suddenly waked by desire to evacuate bladder. Restless sleep, wild feeling in head, everything seems too hot.
Unrefreshing sleep with bad dreams, half-awaking, labored. Frightful, unpleasant dreams. Amorous, lewd,
voluptuous dreams.
Stomach - Hollow, empty sensation in stomach and bowels. As if a hard body rolling around, during day only.
Hunger, as if from spine. Flatulence. Nausea with sensation of lump in stomach. Nausea with pressure in
vagina and pain at top of sacrum. Nausea with morning diarrhea. Morning sickness with frequent, copious
urination. Retching, but no vomiting. Feels like vomiting when touching epigastrium. Vomiting from
displacement of uterus.
Temperature - Chilly in cool open air, otherwise better. Chilly sensation running down face, head and back.
Chills with violent beating of heart and constriction. Great heat and lassitude in afternoon with throbbing
throughout body.
Throat - Soreness and dryness. Hawking of mucus with constant nausea. Enlargement of right tonsil, with
exudation. Feeling of lump, with pulsations when lying.
Vertigo - Vertigo feeling as if intoxicated, head confused and heavy. Vertigo when walking, staggering forward.
Vertigo better in fresh open air, worse in close room.
Vision - Myopic astigmatism, has to turn head sideways to see clearly, with frontal headache.
Farsightedness. Presbyopia. Blurred vision with heat in eyes and lids. Blurred vision with prolapsed uterus.
Dim vision after seminal emissions. Muscae volitantes.
COMMENTS - Characteristic downward dragging from shoulders, from thorax, from left breast, from
epigastrium down to pelvis and out at the vagina as if everything would be forced through. Downward pressure
in the rectum, bladder and loins.
General pel vic distress, affecting the bladder, rectum and back. Increased sexual instinct, more intense affect
on female organs. High
 Lilium tigrinum sex drive with bearing down pains (Sep., Murx.), and sharp, stabbing pains in the uterus.
Consciousness of the ovaries as distinct, painful, burning spots with pains radiating from them down the thighs.
Pains in the uterus and ovaries as if they were squeezed.
Premenstrual syndrome, worse consolation, very irritable before menses. Hurried and restless before menses
(Arg-n., Sep.). Fatigue. Can have palpitations of tightness in the chest associated with menses or premenstrual
syndrome.
Severe menstrual cramps (Sep.), as if squeezed with sharp, stabbing pains. Regular menses, flows only as
long as she moves. Menses too soon, leucorrhea after menses. Intermittent, thin, brown leucorrhea, leaving a
brown stain.
C. Sigmund Raue observed excellent results from Lil-t. 3x and 30c in cases of uterine fibroid presenting the
characteristic symptoms of the remedy.
Another prover, a woman, 53, who had ceased to menstruate took a drop of Lil-t. 30c. She had a feeling of
exhaustion as if the blood were pushed outward and later a blinding headache “as if all the blood were pressing
outward through every aperture.” Felt hurried and driven, without knowing why.
Sudden fluttering sensation in the heart, better if busy, with faintness, as though she could make no exertion
but must sit still. Contractive pain in the heart, intermittent pressure. Alternate spasm and relaxation. Sharp
pain in apex of heart. Pain and numbness in the right arm along with the heart pain. Alternation of heart pain
with uterine or ovarian pains.
Intermittent action of the heart, every intermission is followed by a violent throb, causing an involuntary catching
of the breath. At the same time, the blood rushes up through the carotids to the head, producing great heat
and crowded feeling of head and face. Fever and sweat during the night.
Wandering pain, flying, shooting, squeezing and relaxing, opening and shutting, burning and radiating.
Lilium tigrinum
Pain radiates from ovary to heart, to left breast, down legs (especially left), across to opposite ovary, through
left breast, to back from ilium, across sacrum. Pulling up sensation from the tip of the coccyx. Convulsive
contractions of the muscles of the body. Backache. Generally left sided.
Intense restlessness, irritable nervous system, weak, trembling, aimless hurry, walks to and fro. Obscene
thoughts. Disposition to strike and swear. Feeling as if she would be crazy if she did not hold tightly upon
herself, feeling as if she must scream. Fear of dying.
One prover, who was astigmatic, had much suffering in the eyes during the proving, and found her astigmatism
gone when the proving was over.
S. Lilienthal had among his symptoms “a sensation as if a rubber band were stretched tightly from temple to
temple, as if a skullcap were crushing the head, as if the brain was being pushed through eyes and ears.”
A patient to whom Clarke gave Lil-t. 30c said it caused a sensation in the abdomen as if the contents were
“tied up in knots.”
H. C. Allen noted the symptom “cannot walk on uneven ground.”
Berridge cured a woman, 50, of heart pain, with a sensation as if the heart was grasped with a hand, with a
cold feeling from apex of heart to under left scapula, excited by worry, worse lying on right side, better lying on
left side and when busy at work.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Plat., Helon. (ante-version), Nux-v. (colic), Puls. Compare: (1) Cact., Helon.,
Murx., Sep., Plat.. Pall. (2) Sep. - very like in most respects, but Lil-t. better by diverting mind and busying
about, Sep. better by violent exertion, leucorrhea of Lil-t. is more excoriating, Lil-t. worse afternoon, Sep. better
afternoon, Lil-t. pressure in anus, Sep. weight like a heavy ball. (3) Puls. - worse in warm room, venous stasis
with taste of blood in mouth, weeping mood, Puls, quiet weeping. (4) Nat-m. - heart, uterus, coldness about
heart. (5) Helon. - profound melancholy with consciousness of womb. (6) Cact. - heart constricted by iron band,
constriction continuous, Lil-t. intermittent, uterine and ovarian pains. (7)
Sulph. - early morning diarrhea, burning palms and soles. (8) Zinc - heart symptoms better by lying on left side.
(9) Pall, over-sensitive Plat., hauteur. (10) Aur. - prolapse, Aur. from weight of organ, Lil-t. from relaxation of
ligaments. (11) Rhus-t. - pain and numbness of left arm with heart disease, Lil-t. more characteristic, right.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Limulus Cyclops
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lim. Limulus cyclops. King crab. Limulus polyphemus. Polyphemus occidentalis. Xiphosura.
Horse foot. Saucepan. N. O. Merostomata or the pecilopoda of the Crustacea. Coast of North America.
Triturations of the dried blood. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cholera. Colic. Constipation. Coryza. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Fever. Hemorrhoids. Sea-bathing,
 effects. Skin, affection. Strokes. Vesicles.
HOMEOPATHIC - Lim. was introduced by Hering, and partially proved by him and Lippe. Hering was surprised
to see that the blood of the King crab he dissected was blue, and on investigation was found to contain copper.
He thought it would prove to be another medicine for cholera.
The most notable symptoms include a rush of blood to the face with heat of the face and over whole body
(Aster.). Bodily and mental exhaustion. Painful fullness of whole right side of body. Gastro enteric symptoms.
Drowsiness after sea bathing.
MIND - Mental depression. Weak memory. Forgetful, difficult to remember names. Confusion with heat of face,
rush of blood to face, worse when meditating.
Abdomen - Abdomen hot and constricted.
Colic with heat. Cramp-like pain with watery stools.
Chest - Oppression of chest.
Eyes - Pain behind left eyeball.
Face - Flushing of face, worse in afternoon.
Rush of blood to face. Heat in face alternating with confusion in head.
Head - Headache from straining at stool.
Limbs - Crural neuralgia. Pain in right hip joint. Soles of feet ache, feel numb. Heels sore. Burning in palms.
Lungs - Husky voice. Dyspnea after drinking water. Oppression of chest.
Nose - Fluent coryza. Constant nasal dripping. Sneezing, worse drinking water. Pressure above nose and
behind eyes.
Rectum - Hemorrhoids, constriction of anus.
Skin - Itching spots and vesicles on face and hands.
Throat - Husky voice.
COMMENTS-Theonly italicized Lim. symptoms in Allen are “Frequent rush of blood to the face and painful
fullness of the whole right half of the body, especially here and there and in the lower limbs” and “heat, burning
and constriction in abdomen.”
Gastrointestinal disturbance, a choleric condition. Headache caused by straining at stool. Dyspnea, worse
drinking. Coryza worse drinking cold water. Flushing of the face, worse in afternoon. Heat in face alternated
with confusion in head.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aster., Hom., Cupr. (2) Fenr. - flushing. Ind. - pains in head from straining at
stool. Ars. - ill-effects of sea-bathing.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Linaria Vulgaris
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lina. Linaria vulgaris. Snap dragon. Toad-flax. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Apathy. Bedwetting. Diarrhea. Fainting. Hemorrhoids. Ophthalmia. Tongue, roughness. Tongue,
prickling.
HOMEOPATHIC - In domestic practice, Linaria has long been used as a lotion for inflamed eyes and as an
application for painful hemorrhoids. It is said to be purgative and diuretic. Lina, was proved by Muller, Raidi
and others.
Farrington commended it for cardiac fainting, “faints dead away without apparent cause” ; and also in
bedwetting, “bedwetting with frequent painful urging to urinate causing patient to rise at night.” Carleton saw it
produce “Fainting feeling three or four times a day, fainted away completely once.”
Marked enteric symptoms. Pressure on stomach. Jaundice, splenic and hepatic hypertrophy. Salivation.
Constriction of the throat. Thirst with rough tongue. Belchings. Nausea, vomiting. Bedwetting. Rectal
symptoms. Diarrhea, with profuse urination. Better by taking tea with milk.
Great tiredness. General prostration. Irresistible sleepiness. Fainting from heart weakness. Confusion in
the head. Coldness. Oppression of the breathing and stitches in the chest. Symptoms worse walking in open
air.
MIND - Peevish mind. Indifferent. Confusion, stupid feeling in the head.. Ill-humor with dull pain in forehead,
with fever, after the sleep, lasting until midnight.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby:Tea in milk. Compare: ( 1 ) Dig. - fainting and other Scrophularia. (2) Caust., Eup-
per., Equis. - bedwetting.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
 ***LINUM CATHARTICUM
(Purging Flax)
PHARMACY - linu-c. Linum catharticum. Purging flax. N. O. Linacee. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Bronchitis. Cough. Diarrhea. Hemorrhoids. Laryngitis. Rheumatism.
HOMEOPATHIC - Proved by Stokes and Gaston, Linu-c. has marked colic and diarrhea of loose, bright yellow
stools and also of slender stools.
Nasal and respiratory catarrh, stuffed-up condition of nose and chest. Troublesome cough and difficult
expectoration of frothy, yellow mucus. Menses omitted or delayed. Depressed sexual functions in men,
absence of desire in women.
MIND - Dullness and depression. Irritable.
Modalities - Cough, worse walking in open air. Headache, better in open air and from eating.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Sulph. (headache). Compare: Linu-u.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
keynote:
PHARMACY - lina. Linaria vulgaris. Snap dragon. Toad-flax. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Apathy. Bedwetting. Diarrhea. Fainting. Hemorrhoids. Ophthalmia. Tongue, roughness. Tongue,
prickling.
HOMEOPATHIC - In domestic practice, Linaria has long been used as a lotion for inflamed eyes and as an
application for painful hemorrhoids. It is said to be purgative and diuretic. Lina, was proved by Muller, Raidi
and others.
Farrin

name: Linum Usitatissimum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - linu-u. Linum usitatissimum. Flax-seed. Linseed. Common flax. Source of Linseed or Flax-seed.
N. O. Linacee. Trituration and tincture of seed, meal, oil or freshly made poultice. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Convulsions. Hay fever. Headaches. Tongue, paralysis. Trismus. Urticaria.
HERBAL - Linseed-tea and linseed poultices are among the most innocent of domestic remedies, but
occasionally the application of a linseed poultice has produced severe respiratory disturbances such as
asthma, hives, etc. It has been found to contain a small quantity of hydrocyanic acid, which may account for
this intensity.
The “soothing” effects of linseed-tea and linseed poultices are really of a specific and homeopathic nature.
A teaspoonful of whole linseed, steeped in warm water for half an hour and then taken, acts as a laxative.
HOMEOPATHIC - Linu-u. is marked by intense irritation. The decoction is of service in inflammation of the
urinary passages, cystitis, strangury, etc. Diseases of the intestinal tract. Trismus and paralysis of the tongue.
Asthma, hay fever and urticaria.
MIND - Perfectly conscious, but only able to express herself by signs.
Eyes - Unpleasant heat, burning, dryness. Intense conjunctivitis. Chemosis. Swelling of lids, completely closes
eye in one hour, edema persisted three days.
Face - Face red and slightly moist. Violent, dull pain in cheeks and temples. Jaws immovably clenched.
Head - Heavy frontal headache. Violent
pain in cheeks and temples. Rigid and prominent temporal muscles, jerk rapidly. Head shakes spasmodically
in measured time.
Limbs - Upper limbs shaken by spasms, but pliable and uncontracted.
Lungs - Bronchial asthma. Livid, struggles for breath.
Mouth - Tip of the tongue turned upwards and backwards so as to touch the velum palati. Tongue drawn down
into her throat. Complete paralysis of tongue. Could not articulate a syllable.
Nose - Irritation rapidly extended through lachrymal duct to nose. Heat, burning dryness with indescribably
scraping. Itching sensation, nearly driving him wild. Nasal passage completely closed, compelled to breathe
through mouth.
Skin - Herpes. Urticaria. One complete blotch from crown to toes, smarting, stinging, burning.
Stomach - Great weight in stomach. Fullnessin stomach and precordial uneasiness, followed by convulsions.
Severe colic. Vomiting with copious stools.
Throat - Irritation continued from eyes and nose down into throat. Throat filled with large white blisters.
COMMENTS - Clarke quoted the case of a woman in which the application of a linseed poultice to an ulcer
over the right shin-bone produced an attack of asthma which nearly proved fatal. It was not the first time this
had happened to her and she protested, but in vain, against the doctor's order. If a linseed poultice even come
near her she felt constriction of the chest.
The doctor who ordered the poultice and reported the case, was speedily summoned to witness the worst
attack of asthma he had ever seen. The patient was livid and struggling for breath. When the poultice was
removed the symptoms gradually subsided. A crop of herpes appeared where the poultice had been and an
eruption of urticaria over back, chest and arms.
Dr. A. G. Towner related his own experiences, noting that when he lived in New York state he could handle
 linseed in all forms freely, but after moving to Illinois, it
affected him powerfully.
Once he rubbed his eye while preparing a poultice; intense conjunctivitis came on at once, chemosis, and in
an hour the eye was closed and did not come right again for three days. The irritation passed along the
lachrymal duct and the same burning and irritation took place in the nose, nearly driving him wild.
The swelling closed the nostrils and he had to breathe through his mouth. The irritation still spread, affecting
the throat, which was covered with large white blisters and a desperate attack of bronchial asthma supervened,
slightly relieved by large doses of Ip.
In two hours, the skin became affected with an attack of “hives” (urticaria). “I was one complete blotch from
the crown of my head to the end of my toes, a complete bodily eruption, smart, sting, burn.” He had five of
these attacks.
The steam of a poultice would cause coryza, the dust would occasion a complete attack. One was caused by
inadvertently eating a lozenge containing linseed.
An entirely different set of symptoms was recorded by Allen in which a girl, 19, drank a cupful of milk into which
she had poured by mistake some spoonfuls of linseed oil. Immediately she felt a fullness in her stomach and
precordial uneasiness. She vomited profusely and had copious stools. She went to bed, where she was seized
with spasms.
Head shook spasmodically in measured time, the eyes and prominent temporal muscles jerked rapidly. Jaws
clenched. Tongue paralyzed and drawn down into throat. All the time the brain was quite clear.
A clyster of Asaf, gave temporary relief, but the symptoms recurred for a time with renewed violence. On the
third day she was quite recovered, but her health was not good for some time.
RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Ip., Asaf. Compare: ( 1 ) Linu-c. - in asthma and skin disorders. (2) Ars., Chloral.,
Apis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Lippia Mexicana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - lip. Lippia mexicana. N. O. Verbenacae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - The leading indication for Lip., as noted in the Chicago Medical Times, is a cough occurring
every winter, especially in women. Hoarse ringing or barking chest coughs, without expectoration.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
