name: Magnesia Sulphurica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mag-s. Magnesia sulphurica. Magnesium sulphate. Epsom salts. Magnesia sulphate.
Trituration. Historicaldose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acidity. Acne. Allergies. Backache. Bedwetting. Boils. Constipation. Coughs, spasms. Diabetes.
Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Eczema. Epithelioma. Erysipelas. Eye, pain. Female,
disorders. Gallbladder, pain. Gallstone, colic. Headache. Hernia. Intermenstrual, hemorrhage. Itching.
Leucorrhea. Liver, complaints. Lumbago. Menorrhagia. Mental, problems. Migraines. Miliary, eruptions.
Neuralgias. Pimples. Scabies. Skin, disorders. Tetany. Thyroid, weakness. Toothache. Urinary, disorders.
Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - The ancient reputation of Mag-s. as a “refrigerant cathartic” under the familiar name of
“Epsom Salts,” or “salts” par excellence, has overshadowed its homeopathic uses.
Recently old-school authorities have discovered in this “cathartic” a remedy for dysentery. It is the chief
ingredient in many laxative mineral waters and popular saline aperient mixtures.
Mag-s. is of diagnostic and therapeutic value in gallstone colic. The physiological dosage from 2 to 4
teaspoonfuls in glass hot water taken at onset of a colicky attack may abort or stop the colic.
Epsom salts is one of the most active saline cathartics, operating with little pain or nausea, especially if pure.
Its action causing a rush of fluid into the intestine, which by producing a distention of the bowel produces
evacuation.
It causes little or no irritation in the intestine. In common with the other salines, it is the classical évacuant to
be employed in connection with mercurials and anthelmintics and in cases of poisoning.
It usually acts within from one to two hours, more quickly if taken in hot water and in the morning before
breakfast.
The ordinary dose as a mild laxative is a heaping teaspoonful, as a cathartic, two to four teaspoonfuls. The
taste may be improved, if necessary, by the addition of a little lemon juice and sugar. Use on compresses
saturated with solution.
Besides Mag-s. chief use as a saline cathartic, magnesium sulphate is used to a considerable extent externally
in saturated solution as an antiphlogistic and anti-itching in erysipleas, poison ivy poisoning, cellulitis and other
local inflammations.
Percy Wilde noted that the purgative action of Mag-s. is not a quality of the drug, but a quality of its physical
state, which renders its absorption impossible. The properties inherent in the substance itself can only be
discovered by potency.
The skin, urinary and female symptoms are most marked. Greenish urine with red sediment. Profuse dark
intermittent menses. Thick leucorrhea as profuse as menses. As of a lump between shoulders. Back feels
broken. Left arm and foot numb. Crawling in fingertips. Small pimples all over the body which itch violently.
Warts, large, soft.
Mag-s. has a depressive condition with hypersensitivity. Dysthyroidism. Tendency to spasms in the hollow
organs. Liver weakness. Intermittent discomfort with prolonged periods of relief.
MIND - Apprehensive. Anxious, as though about to be struck by misfortune. Prostration from anxiety.
Foreboding anxiety, as if some accident would happen. Irritable with a fear of dying. Hypersensitive to pain
(Cham., Mag-p.).
Depression. Melancholy and disposition to weep and restlessness. Bad-tempered with nervous tension.
Tendency to fly into a passion, every thing is taken in bad part. Misunderstands everything. Errors of imagi-
nation. Sees people who are absent.
Abdomen - Sharp pains in left hypochondrium. Tension, hardness and fullness of abdomen after a meal.
Violent shooting pains in whole abdomen, around the navel. Painful drawing in abdomen. Rumbling in
abdomen with emission of flatulence. Itching of left inguinal region, not removed by scratching.
Back - Pains in the lumbar region. Lumbago. Violent pain in the small of the back, as if bruised and as before
menstruation. Bruised and ulcerative pain between the shoulders with a feeling as of a lump as large as the
fist, on which account she could not lie upon her back or side, relieved by rubbing.
Constitutions - Allergic, tubercular types with nervous hyper-excitability.
Ears - Noises, tinkling in ears. Shooting pains in ears.
Eyes - Burning in eyes. Shooting pains in eyes. Pains in eyes, as if protruding from orbits. Lachrymation with
photophobia. Dimness of eyes with frequent drowsiness. Supra-orbital neuralgia, left side.
Face - Face discolored, gray. Earthy color of face. Tearing in bones of face. Dryness and burning in lips, in
evening.
Female - Premenstrual nausea. Menses too early or late, scanty or heavy. Blood thick and black. Discomfort
during menses. Thick leucorrhea, as profuse as the menses with weary pain in the small of the back and
thighs, on moving about. Some blood from the vagina between the menses.
 Food - Intense thirst, morning and evening. Want of appetite and repugnance to all food, even when thinking
of it. Desire for fruits, green salad and refreshing dishes. Aversion to sausages, meat, fats and fatty foods.
Head - Headache with feeling of fullness in the head, blood in the head and a prickling, drawing, piercing
sensation.
Heart - Pricking pain in the heart, ame1 iorated by sitting and resting and aggravated by heat. Palpitations and
breathlessness from physical exercise. Wakes at night with palpitations, following sleep filled with nightmares.
Kidneys - Stream intermits and dribbles. The urine passed in the morning copious, bright yellow, soon
becomes turbid and deposits a copious red sediment. The urine is greenish as passed is of a clear color and
in a large quantity. Diabetes (Ph-ac„ Lac-ac.). Stitches and burning in the orifice of the urethra after urinating.
Limbs - Sciatic pains, aggravated at night and during rest, ameliorated by walking. Chronic, non-inflammatory
rheumatism of the hip. The left arm and foot fall asleep in bed in the morning after waking.
Liver - Pain in the liver region, especially on breathing. Painful sensitivity in the region of the gallbladder.
Nightly attacks on the liver and gallbladder.
Lungs - Respiration panting after exercise. Laryngeal cough on waking, sometimes spasmodic and dry,
sometimes with sputum. Dry and shaking cough after waking in morning, and which compels sitting up.
Expectoration of sour mucus.
Male - Urethritis. Prostatitis. Frequent stinging about penis when sitting or walking. Erections without amorous
fancies or sexual desire.
Modalities - Better from movement in the fresh air. Better from washing in cool water. Better from rubbing.
Better walking. Worse morning. Worse on awaking. Worse from traveling on a train. Worse in a closed vehicle.
Mouth - Dryness and sweetish bitterness of the mouth, especially in the morning. Dryness of mouth with
sensation of numbness. Roughness of tongue. Vesicles on edges of tongue with incisive pains. Toothache.
Nose - Congestive pain. Nasal discharge with painful ulceration inside the nose. Copious secretion of thick
and yellow mucus in nose. Fluent coryza with loss of smell. Nosebleed, at night. Rough voice and frequent
flow of water from nose.
Perspiration - Perspiration at night or in morning, accompanied by thirst. Hands moist from sweating.
Rectum - Neuralgia of rectum. Constipation. Feces at one time hard, at another soft. Liquid stools with
tenesmus. Soft stools early after rising. Loose evacuations with violent thirst. Stools like diarrhea, grayish in
color or constipation with gray stools covered with mucus. Diarrhea preceded by rumbling in abdomen.
Diarrhea with diuresis. Diarrhea after eating pancakes. Acid diarrhea of children. Ejection of ascarides during
every evacuation.
Skin - Generalized itching over the whole body, worse in bed. Eczema and vesicular eczemas. Miliary
eruptions with burning and itching. Small pimples over the whole body, that itch violently. Boils. Suppressed
scabies (Sulph.). Crawling in the tips of the fingers of the left hand, better on rubbing. Warts. Erysipelas.
Dropsy. Acne on the back. Epithelioma.
Sleep - Extreme sleepiness in the daytime. Sleepy, early in evening. Sleeplessness at night, caused by violent
pains in head, abdomen and loins. Wakes at 3 a. m. with difficulty in falling asleep again. Many dreams at
night, sometimes disagreeable and anxious. Sleep with worrying, with palpitations.
Stomach - Frequent belchings, tasting like bad eggs. Regurgitation of fluid, preceded by a quivering in
stomach. Disgust and nausea with accumulation of water in mouth. Vomiting, first of food, then of mucus.
Temperature - Chill from 9 a.m. to 10 a.m. Chilliness with thirst, early in morning after waking. Shaking chill
with violent headache in evening, succeeded by thirst. Shuddering in back, heat in one part and chill in another.
Cold feet all day, although otherwise he feels hot. Heat of head with coldness of rest of body. Alternation of
heat and shuddering, redness and paleness of face.
Throat - Deep, hollow, bass voice. Sore throat on swallowing and pricking pains spreading to the ear. Sore
throat, with shooting pains at night, worse by swallowing. Dryness and sensation of numbness in throat.
Accumulation of mucus in throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo, heaviness and numbness of the whole head. Vertigo during menses.
COMMENTS - Poisonings from Mag-s. have occurred from overdoses, death apparently occurring from
collapse. The provings of the salts produced many symptoms of utter prostration.
The provings bring out effects common to the other magnesia. Tearfulness, restless uneasiness, pains in facial
bones, sensitive-
Magnesia sulphurica ness to touch, better by walking. The diuretic action of the drug with great thirst has led
to its successful use in diabetes.
Diarrhea, accompanied with great thirst. Toothache, worse coming into a room out of cold air, worse by contact
with food, whether cold or warm, better in bed. Chill, accompanied or followed by thirst. Shuddering in back
from below upward.
 According to Med. Press in Sept. 9,1891, eight cases of new growth having all the outward characters of
epithelioma were cured by Graves with teaspoonful doses of a solution of three drachms to the pint.
Warts are allied to epithelioma, and H. T. Webster cured many cases in children, giving as much of the salts
as would lie on a dime three times a day. One boy was literally covered with warts, his face being much
disfigured. One girl of 16 was cured of large warts on her hands.
F. H. Pritchard gave his experience with Mag-s. (1/2 grains in a teaspoonful of water) in summer diarrhea with
vomiting of food, copious yellowish, slimy and stinking stools and later merely watery serum. The first sign of
improvement was that the stools became bile-tinged after which they soon became of thicker consistency. The
copious stools seemed to be the cardinal indication.
RELATIONS - It is claimed that the addition of a small amount of Mag-s. to the usual hypodermic of morphine
increases the value of the hypodermic from 50 to 100%. Compare: (1) Mag-c., Mag-m., Mag-p. (2) In diabetes,
Nat- s. (3) Sadness, weeping, foreboding anxiety, Cimic., Puls. (4) Stinging in fauces between acts of
deglutition, Ign. (5) Belchings, Hep. (6) Apprehension, Lyc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian.Phatak.

name: Magnetis Poli Ambo
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - m-ambo. (m-p-a.) Magnetis poli ambo. Magnet. Both poles of the magnet. Trituration of Sugar
of Milk after exposure of the influence of the both poles of the magnet. Dilution of distilled water similarly
exposed. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Colic. Coma. Constipation. Cough. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Fainting. Flatulence. Headaches.
Hemorrhage. Hemorrhoids. Orchitis. Pains. Paraphimosis. Prolapsed, anus. Rheumatism. Toothache. Ulcers.
Vertigo. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - General symptoms of the magnet produced by touching either magnetic pole
indiscriminately while handling the magnet or by laying the whole of the magnetic surface upon the body.
Marked sensations of coldness. The eyeball feels cold, as if it were a lump of ice in the socket. Sensation as
if the blood was rushing towards points. Burning sensation in the limbs and joints.
Burning lancinations across all parts of body in different directions. Pains as if broken in joints, when cartilages
of two bones touch. Wrenching pain in the limbs.
Shooting and jerkings. Shuddering, which traverses the whole body. Shaking in the body with fright or shocks,
which cause violent bending and straightening of the body, sometimes with the loss of consciousness.
Headaches as if a nail were driven in. Long-lasting swoons during which she feels her pains, but is not able to
speak or move. Tendency of old wounds to bleed afresh.
MIND - Irresolution. Inadvertence. Hurried, heedless and forgetful. Busy precipitation. Absence of mind. Talks
aloud to himself without being aware of it. Does things he doesn't intend to. Tendency to anger and rage.
Abdomen - Pressure and anxious fullness in abdomen, especially during mental exertion. Noisy, gas,
grumbling and borborygmi in abdomen. Flatulent colic. Production of much flatus. Expulsion of flatulence with
painful pressure.
Back - Jerking in the spine, as from something alive. Painful sensibility of the joint of the sacrum in morning in
bed, when lying on side or by day, when stooping.
Wrenching pain in shoulder joint or pain as from the starting of a tendon in wrist.
Chest - Burning insupportable lancinations in muscles of chest.
Ears - Humming in ears. Diminution of hearing.
Eyes - Itching in eyes, especially the lids. Pupils dilated. Scintillation of white light, beyond the range of vision
in the twilight. Sparks before the eyes.
Face - Perspiration on face without heat in morning. Jerking, tearing in upper jaw. Small pimples with pain like
that of a wound, on lips. Violent burning lancination in muscles of face in evening. Swelling of lips with salivation
in evening.
Female - Menses premature, profuse and of too long duration.
Food - Fetid breath. Metallic taste in mouth. Insipid taste of tobacco and beer. Many things have a moldy taste.
Speedy satiety. Good appetite in evening.
Head - Headache from over-strained memory and reflection. Digging, stupefying headache, which is
immediately dispersed by movements of flatus. Head pain, as if a nail were driven into the head, as if caused
by a wound, especially after a fit of anger. Jerking, tearing in head, appearing at intervals. Rushing or buzzing
noises in whole head. Pain, as of a bruise in head, on waking in morning.
Limbs - Drawing pains in joints and muscles of arms, often from head to fingers. Tearing, jerking in muscles
of arms after remaining some time in the cold. Red spots in palms like vesicles. Attacks of cramp in calves of
 legs and toes after waking in morning. Burning lancinations in heels and in corns on the feet.
Lungs - Paroxysms of dry cough at night. Spasmodic cough, especially after midnight, when awake or during
reflection. Nocturnal dyspnea, excited by mucus in trachea, which is easily detached in morning.
Male - Burning sensation in region of spermatic vesicles, which excites sexual desire. Dullness of sexual
feeling and aversion to sex. Erection without amorous thoughts. Retraction of prepuce behind the glans.
Swelling of epididymis with pain during movement and when touched.
Modalities - Worse by motion and on waking. Toothache is worse from cold
and on contact with anything cold. Touch aggravates pain in joints. Heat is better from uncovering.
Nose - Aberration of smell, a smoky or moldy scent is perceived.
Rectum - Constipation, as from contraction of rectum. Painless diarrhea with flatulence. Hemorrhoids,
smarting pain in anus after evacuation with constriction in rectum. Blind hemorrhoids. Prolapsed rectum.
Skin - Tendency of old wounds to bleed afresh. Ulcers painful, like new wounds. Small furunculi. Small
pustules with lancinating, drawing pain.
Sleep - Jerking of the body before going to sleep. Disturbed sleep with talking, snoring and continued
tossing.Wakingat3a.m. and falling into a drowsy lethargy towards sunrise. Lying on the back with the hand
under the head, the legs wide apart and the mouth half open with snoring respiration. Amorous, lascivious
dreams. After waking in morning, headache with pain, as of a fracture in all the joints, which forces constant
change in position of limbs. .
Stomach - Stomachache with cramp towards upper part, agitation, which allows no rest whatever, heaviness
of tongue, paleness of face and coldness of body. Abortive risings. Risings with smell and taste of horn
scrapings. Sour regurgitation, when stooping.
Teeth - Pressive, jerking toothache in isolated shocks. Toothache after drinking anything cold or from contact
with cold air. Toothache in carious teeth with swelling of gums.
Temperature - Dry heat with need to be uncovered, at night and in morning in bed.
Vertigo - Vertigo, especially in evening after lying down, as if about to fall or as from concussion in head.
Vertigo with staggering, when walking, objects seem to waver before eyes.
COMMENTS - The effect of the magnet as a whole and of each pole separately was tested by Hahnemann,
and the symptoms are mainly from his pathogenesis.
He said he did not expect “ordinary mechanical, materialistic and atomistic heads” to be able to regard diseases
as “immaterial alternations of the vitality or pure dynamic derangements of our state of health and medicinal
powers as merely virtual, almost spiritual, forces.”
Hahnemann asked how they can reconcile with their materialistic notions the fact that “a single imponderable
spark from a Leyden jar gives a shock to the strongest man and yet to ascertainable ponderable substance is
communicated to his body?”
Clarke’s experience with magnetism is confined to M-ambo. 2,000c, but that is sufficient to give him confidence
in prescribing potencies of these remedies when their indications arise, particularly burning lancinations
throughout the body, pains as if broken in joints, where cartilages of two bones touch, shootings and jerkings,
disturbed sleep, headache as if a nail were driven in.
Hahnemann said the symptoms “occurred from various powerful magnets brought in contact with various
sensitive individuals without distinction of the poles.
“They were observed in experiments conducted for half a year for the purpose of ascertaining the proper and
most efficacious mode of stroking the steel with magnets in which a horse-shoe magnet, capable of lifting a
weight of twelve pounds, was held in the hands, which were held in contact with both poles for an hour at a
time.” Additional symptoms came from Andry, Thouret, Unzer and De Harsu.
Hahnemann noted that “Although each of the poles presents something peculiar in its power of altering the
human health, yet each of them seems, when applied twice of oftener to produce alternating actions which
resemble those of the opposite pole.”
For curative purposes, Hahnemann recommended a much milder application of the magnet. The popular use
of magnetic rings for rheumatism is analogous to this. The method of attenuating media saturated with
emanations from the magnet does not seem to have occurred to Hahnemann.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Ign., Electr., Galv., Zinc. (imposition of Zinc plate). Compare: ( 1 ) M-arct., M-
aust„ Ferr-ma., Mang-o. (2) Burnt smell in nose, Anae. (3) Prolapsed anus, Podo., Caust., Ign. (4) Bell., Lyc.,
Nux-v., Petr., Puls., Stram., Sabin., Teucr.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Magnetis Polus Arcticus
author: Murphy
full:
(North Pole of Magnet) PHARMACY - m-arct. Magnetis polus arcti- cus. North pole of the magnet. Potencies
 of saccharum lactis or water charged with the influence of this pole. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Clairvoyance. Coma. Constipation. Cough. Flatulence. Headache. Heartburn.
Hernia. Menses, suppressed. Nosebleed. Panaritium. Salivation. Sleep, disturbed. Sleepwalking. Toothache.
Vertebra, cracking. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms of Mag-arct. were obtained by applying it in the region of the 4th to 6th
thoracic vertebra, at a distance of four or five finger's breadth from the body.
Over-excitement with trembling, uneasy restlessness in limbs and great nervous weakness. Great lassitude
and painful weariness of the whole body with dejection, especially in morning and in open air, as during sultry
weather.
Sharp shocks, throbbing, trembling, coldness and sensation as if the blood were driven toward parts. Drawing
sensation in periosteum of all bones, as at commencement of intermittent fever. Cracking in cervical vertebrae.
Marked affect in the teeth and jaws. Sensation of coldness with toothache. Increased flow of saliva. Swelling,
heat and redness of one cheek. Coldness of eyes as if a piece of ice lay in orbit. Disturbed sleep, sleep-
walking. Constipation, sopor, trembling. Abdominal flatulence.
MIND - Mildness, submission. Anxious hesitation and restlessness. Fickleness. Irresolution, followed by
prompt execution after a resolution has been once formed. Indolence when seated, as if power of mov-
ing were lost.
Peevishness. Sensitive to noises. Weakness of memory. Tendency to make mistakes when writing. Loss of
ideas. Loss of sense. Speaking loud while quite alone and engaged in business. Inclination to weep with
shivering.
Abdomen - Inflation of abdomen. Shocks in abdomen, as if something in it were falling or blows proceeding
from abdomen and passing upwards through chest, as far as the throat. Pressure and boring towards inguinal
ring, as if preparatory to a rupture with relaxation of the inguinal ring. Production and incarceration of much
flatus. Flatulent, pressive colic.
Back - Cracking in the cervical vertebra during movement. Pains in back, as if broken, on bending it backwards.
Ears - Murmuring in ears and internal heat, as from boiling water. Deafness, as if caused by a band over ears.
Eyes - Restless movements of eyes. Eyes prominent and fixed. Icy coldness of (weak) eye, as if a lump of ice
lay in orbit instead of the eye. Lancinations, itching and jerking drawing in eyelids with lachrymation. Painful
sensation of dryness in eyelids, on awaking in morning.
Face - Paleness in face. Tension in face. Painful squeezing in maxillary joint with sensation, while moving it,
as if it were dislocated. Swelling of one cheek only. Trismus.
Female - Menses too feeble. Menses suppressed.
Food - Voracity in evening. Loss of taste. Acid taste in the mouth. Tobacco has a bitter taste.
Head - Headache is worse lifting or moving arm.
Kidneys - Increased secretion of urine. Deep-colored urine.
Limbs - Inflammation of back of hand with pulsative pain. Heaviness in arms, hands and fingers. Great
lassitude in lower limbs, which feel as if they would break, when walking. Pains, as of a fracture in hip joints
and lower limbs. Pain, as from excoriation in toes and corns on the feet.
Lungs - Dry, asthmatic, suffocating cough.
worse by walking in open air. Constant want to cough in evening, which is removed only by restraining the
cough. Spasmodic, shaking cough in evening, on going to sleep, which hinders sleep. Spasmodic, suffocating
cough towards midnight, produced by irritation in bronchia. Cough shaking the head and whole body and
exciting heat until a general perspiration ensues with cessation of the cough.
Male - Excitement of sexual desire. Immoderate erections with frequent pollutions.
Modalities - Better from uncovering, worse on waking. Toothache, worse breathing through the mouth.
Mouth - At night, collection of saliva in mouth, so profuse that every time he wakes the pillow is quite wet.
Itching in point of tongue, compels him to scratch it.
Nose - Aberration of smell, smell of rotten eggs, fresh plaster or dust. Nosebleed, preceded by pressive head
pain in forehead. Redness and heat in point of nose, followed by red spots, hot and plainly circumscribed, on
cheeks.
Rectum - Obstinate constriction of abdomen and constipation. Hard feces of a large size, difficult to evacuate
often preceded by drawing, dysenteric pains in the hypogastrium.
Skin - Tingling and lancination itching in skin. Burning sensation or burning tearing in tetters. Panaritium.
Sleep - Violent, spasmodic yawning, with wrenching pain in maxillary joint. Strong disposition to sleep by day.
Coma. Profound sleep at night during which the patient generally ties on the back. Tossing during sleep, with
troublesome heat and urgent inclination to be uncovered without thirst. Waking in the evening after sleep, in
consequence of a violent shock in the head and muscles of the neck. Many vivid dreams, sometimes
 lascivious. Sings in her sleep, is wakened by it, falls asleep again, recommences to sing and again wakes up
from it. Imperfect waking in morning (2 a.m.), with perfect inner consciousness, vivid memory, great concourse
of ideas and reflections on some important
subject.
Stomach - Frequent empty risings. Continued heartburn, especially after supper.
Teeth - Toothache in carious teeth, at intervals, as if they were being extracted. Pains in carious teeth with
gums swollen and painful when touched, worse after a meal and by heat, better in open air and when walking.
Toothache with red, hot, swollen cheeks. Toothache with shocks, which traverse the periosteum of the jaw or
with drawing, pressive or else tearing, digging or burning sharp pains. Incisors set on edge, when breathing
through the mouth. Numbness and insensibility of the gums, on the cessation of the toothache.
Temperature - Sensation of coldness or of coolness over whole body. Chilliness. Cool hands with cool
perspiration upon them and over whole body. Cold sweat on hands and soles of feet. Shuddering, followed by
transient heat and swelling of veins of hands. Sensation of heat over whole body with coldness of hands and
lower limbs.
Vertigo - Vertigo, as from intoxication with staggering, when walking in open air and instability when standing.
COMMENTS - Swan reported a case cured by C. M. Conant in which Mrs. S., age 31, blonde, had pain in her
left lower jaw as if out of joint, worse morning, on moving it. Sensation as if head of bone were squeezed and
crowded into socket. Mag-arct. 1,000c cured.
One symptom of the proving, occurring in a half-waking state, suggests an approach to sleepwalking. He thinks
out a “difficult subject in the best form in a foreign language,” but when awake he cannot remember distinctly
the subject.
Several provers complained of faintness. One had “sensation of dryness and lightness in the body with want
of strength.” Sensation as if scalp adhered to skull.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: M-aust., Ign., Zinc. Compare: (1) M-ambo. M-aust. (2) Sensation as if teeth
being pulled out, Ip. (3) Worse raising arm, Bar-c.,Con., Cupr., Ferr. (4) One cheek red, Cham. (5) Coff., Cham.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Magnetis Polus Australis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - m-aust. Magnetis polus australis. South pole of the magnet. Potencies of alcohol saturated with
emanations of the south pole. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Borborygmi. Bulimia. Colds. Coryzas. Coughs. Dislocation, easy. Frostbite. Heart,
palpitations. Hernia. Ingrown, toenails. Lachrymation. Levitation. Menorrhagia. Pains. Palpitations.
Toothaches. Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Wisdom tooth.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann first noticed the symptoms that led to the use for ingrown toenails, including a
sore pain on the inner side of the nail of the big toe when walking. As if the nail had grown into the flesh on the
side, very painful on being slightly touched. The shoe presses on the toes and on the nail of the big toe when
walking, as from corns.
The accurate response of M-aust. to these symptoms proved to Clarke the possibility of attenuating and so
fixing this “energy” for use as an ordinary homeopathic remedy. Clarke cured so many cases of ingrown toenail
with M-aust. 2,000c., that he invariably gave it in the first place when there were no symptoms plainly indicating
another remedy.
Sharp, pulsative pains in roots of nails, as if about to suppurate. Easy dislocation of joints of foot, feet are
painful when letting them hang down. Aching in patella, shooting in soles.
Drawings in fingers, feet and ankles. Pains with pinching or burning, lancinations in different parts of the body.
Contusive pains in limbs and joints, as if the patient had been lying on flints.
Dryness of eyelids. Tendency of nose, ears, hands and feet to be frozen by a moderate degree of coldness.
Liability to suffer from achill. Sudden lassitude when walking with anxiety and heat or sudden inclination to
sleep. Lightness of whole body.
MIND - Mood is changeable, variable. Capriciousness. Abrupt. Irritability. Instability of ideas. Inconstancy.
Irresolution, indecision.
Confused, wandering thoughts. Absentminded. Indifference, apathy. Indolence, aversion to work.
Anxiety with fear. Frightened easily. Fear of people, anthropophobia. Timidity. Aversion to anyone who comes
near, even loved ones. Forsaken feeling. Weeping, tearful mood after anger, vexation. Guilt.
Morose and ill-humor, with aversion to conversation. Society is disagreeable, wants to be alone. Dislike to
society and to laughing faces. Wants to say something hateful. Sulky. Ill-humor, peevish.
Asserts himself with vehemence and despises others. Anger at trifles. Anger with trembling. Harshness, rough.
 Abusive, insulting. Quarrelsome, scolding. Reproaches others. Violence, vehemence. Wild, hasty, harsh,
violent in word and deed. Passion and rage.
Dreams of animals, fire. Nightmares. Amorous disposition. Stupefaction, as if intoxicated. Crawling around like
a animal. Abdomen - Noisy borborygmi and grum
bling in abdomen. Pressive, flatulent colic with pinchings and inflation of abdomen. Sensation, as if inguinal
ring were dilated, preparatory to the rupture with painful sensibility of that part, when coughing.
Back - Pressive, burning pain in loins during repose and movement. Pain, as of a fracture or wrenching pain
in joint of sacrum and lumbar vertebra.
Causations - Ailments from anger, vexation, emotional excitement.
Chest - Oppression of the chest, as if the respiration were tremulous and produced an impression of coolness.
Drawing pressure in both sides of sternum with anguish of conscience, which allows no rest.
Eyes - Dryness and smarting in eyelids, especially when moving them, worse morning and evening.
Lachrymation. Amblyopia.
Female - Menses premature and profuse. Metrorrhagia.
Head - Great rush of blood to brain early in morning in bed. Heaviness, tingling and digging in head. Shocks
in head, sometimes with tearing.
Heart - Violent palpitations of the heart with great heat in cardiac region. Palpitation of the heart during which
it seems that it is not the heart that palpitates.
Kidneys - Involuntary emission of urine from paralysis of bladder sphincter, especially at night. Frequent
emission of urine at night. Very feeble stream of urine. Emission of urine, drop by drop with torpor of urethra.
Lungs - Coughs and coryzas with expectoration of greenish mucus and shortness of breath. Paroxysms of
fetid cough at night, when sleeping. Want to take full, sighing inspirations, with involuntary deglutition.
Male - Strong disposition to emission. Emissions in a hemiplegia patient, paralysis worse after the emission.
Impotence with sudden cessation of all enjoyment in the moment of greatest excitement. Pain in penis, as if
some tissues were torn or plucked away. Painful retraction of testes at night. Swelling of testes with tearing
shocks and sensation of contraction.
Modalities - Worse when walking in open air, sitting, hanging limb down.
Mouth - Metallic taste, at one time sweetish, at another acidulous, on and under the tongue. Accumulation of
watery saliva in the mouth. Speech embarrassed, as by a swelling of the tongue.
Rectum - Stools, soft, loose, preceded by gripings. Evacuation of liquid feces with a sensation as if flatus were
about to be discharged. Contractions and painful constriction in rectum and anus, which hinder the expulsion
of wind.
Sleep - Urgent inclination to sleep, evening and morning. Closing the eyes without power to sleep.
Sleeplessness with overexcitement before midnight. Confused, frightful dreams. Prolonged dreams on the
same subject with fatigue. Dreams of incendiary fires. Lying on the back during the night. Slow, noisy, snoring
expiration. Congestion in head in morning, which compels lying with head high.
Stomach - All kinds of food appear insipid. Extreme indifference to food, drink and tobacco-smoke. Bulimia at
noon and
Magnetis polus australis evening, sometimes during the febrile shiverings. Aching in scrobiculus during
mental exertion.
Teeth - Tearing, jerking toothache, worse by hot things.
Temperature - Excessive dread of open air, which penetrates to the very marrow of the bones, even when
the weather is hot, with ill-humor and inclination to weep. Shuddering with cloudiness before eyes. Trembling
and tossing of limbs without shivering, followed by heat in head and face.
Throat - Burning sensation in gullet.
Vertigo - Vertigo, as from intoxication with staggering gait.
COMMENTS - Ingrown toenails, toothache, insomnia, and arthritis. Pinching, squeezing sensations and
bruised pains. Faintness, comes on when walking, worse when sitting. Great rush of blood to the brain early
in the morning in bed.
Berridge reported the case of Miss X, who had for three weeks aching in the middle of front of left lower leg,
where she had varicose veins for eight months, when standing or when the leg is hanging down. Aching pain
is removed by placing it horizontally.
Frequent feeling of hot water running down the affected part, but only when leg is down, at times throbbing
when leg hangs down. She was given M-aust. 100,000c, one dose. The hot-water feeling never returned and
the pain ceased in two days.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: M-arct., Ign., Zinc. Compare: (1) M-ambo., Galv., Electr. in fetid cough, Caps.
(2) Rush of blood to head, Aster. (3) Toenails, Graph., Sil., Nit- ac.,Thuj.
 REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Magnolia Glauca
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - magn-gl. Magnolia glauca. Sweet magnolia. Sweet bay. Beaver-tree. N. O. Magnoliacee.
Tincture of the flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Fainting. Gout.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany said “M. glauca is a low-growing, deciduous tree, called in America Swamp
Sassafras from the nature of the locality in which it grows and from the resemblance in its properties to Laurus
sassafras. It is also called Beavertree, because the root is eaten by beavers, which the animals also make use
of the wood in constructing their nests.”
HOMEOPATHIC - S.A. Jones and T. F. Allen observed the effects of the flowers on three persons. Symptoms
included a sense of great oppression about his chest, and a strong tendency to fainting.
A woman had oppression of chest, could not expand the lungs with a feeling as if she had swallowed food
without chewing and it distressed her stomach. In a doctor, it increased the pain of inflammatory gout and
evidently increased the paroxysm of a pain which came on every afternoon.
REFERENCES - Allen. Clarke.

name: Magnolia Grandiflora
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - magn-gr. Magnolia grandiflora. Talauma mexicana. Magnolia yolotxochitl. N. O. Magnoliacee.
Mexico. Tincture of the flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aneurysm. Angina pectoris. Constipation. Dyspnea. Endocarditis. Flatulence. Headaches. Heart,
disorders. Inter-menstrual flow. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Nausea. Pains. Pericarditis. Rheumatism. Stiffness.
Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Allen, in his Handbook, gives a full pathogenesis of Magn-gr. Rheumatism and heart lesions
are prominent features in the symptomatology of this drug.
Alternating pains between spleen and heart. Erratic shifting of pains. Pains rapidly change their place or
alternate. Rheumatic action, particularly manifested in the chest and heart. Stiffness and soreness. Bruised,
constrictive and rheumatic pains in various parts, particularly the joints.
Patient tired and stiff. Tiredness impeding motion. Soreness when quiet. Marked action was developed in the
female sexual sphere and an inter-menstrual flow was observed.
MIND - Confusion and dullness. Memory weak, lost. Repugnance to all occupation. Ill-humor with burning in
hands. Sadness. Nervous, easily frightened. Uneasiness. Apprehensive, thinks she will die. Illusions and
hallucinations of sight with sharp pains in eyes.
Abdomen - Rapid, pulsating pain with griping in intestines, extending to hypochondria, as from a blow. Burning
in left side of abdomen, extending to chest. Contusive pain in liver and spleen, extending to the stomach.
Flatulence. Lancinations in liver and spleen.
Back - Weight in neck with tiredness of spine. Stiffness, tiredness of neck and back. Contusive pain. Stitches
in right side of back.
Chest - Oppression of chest with inability to expand the lungs. Constriction as from a band just beneath axilla.
Tired feeling. Stiffness of sides of chest, as from exposure to a draft when over heated. Stitches in sides of
chest, in right side.
Ears - Lancinations in left ear, traveling to shoulder. Sharp pain in ears, in morning, traveling to throat.
Eyes - Sharp pain in eyes, from sunlight, with nervousness and visions. Vision weak, blurred. Lids heavy,
sensation in lids as after weeping.
Face - Lancinations in jaw joints. Pain in right side in joints, worse pressure, also impeding opening of mouth.
Sharp pain going to ear.
Female - Before menses, pain in small of back, hypogastrium and thighs with headache, flushes of heat to
face, nausea and chill. Menses delayed, pale and scanty of coagulated blood for two days, then normal, painful.
Bloody flow in interval between menses. Thick white or yellow leucorrhea, with constipation, straining when
urinating. Congestion of left ovary with pain extending to left thigh.
Food - Appetite lost after vertigo, with lassitude.
Head - Migraines. Congestive, throbbing headache with griping in abdomen, flushes of heat. Pain in temples
on bending forward, especially left temple. Pain in occiput and upper dorsal region. Pain
Magnolia grandiflora in occiput as from a blow. Weight in occiput.
Heart - Endocarditis and pericarditis. Tendency to faint. Pulse weak and frequent. Sensation as if heart had
stopped beating. Alternating pains between spleen and heart. Crampy pain in heart. Angina pectoris.
 Stitches, which waking him frequently. Pain around heart accompanied by itching of the feet. Soreness after
disappearance of pain.
Limbs - Stiffness and sharp erratic pains, worse in joints. Sprained pains in joints. Shooting in all limbs. Limbs
tired, stiff. Stiffness of lower limbs. Sharp, erratic or rheumatic pains. Rheumatic pain in clavicles. Rheumatic
pains in wrists. Numbness in left arm. Arms weak. Feet itch.
Lungs - Dyspnea. Suffocation, with desire for stretching and uneasiness in paroxysms, when walking fast,
when lying on left side after a meal. Hoarseness. Dry cough during the day, better at night.
Kidneys - Straining on passing water.
Modalities - Better dry weather, motion. Better inter-menstrual flow (Ham., Bov., Bell., Elaps.). Worse damp
air, in morning, lying on left side.
Mouth - Pain in mouth, better by tepid water.
Rectum - Constipation.
Skin - Itching feet, sometimes with uneasiness of legs.
Sleep - Yawning during the day with sleepiness. Sleepless early in morning. Extravagant dreams.
Stomach - Sensation as from hunger with acidity. Emptiness with general lassitude, vertigo and nausea.
Nausea in morning on rising, better by breakfast. Nausea as from tobacco. Feeling of a large bolus of food
which distressed the stomach.
Teeth - Shooting in teeth. Soreness of teeth, impeding mastication.
Temperature - Erratic chill. Chill in afternoon, then fever lasting into night. Heat with burning in throat and
headache, flushing with sweat of hands, hands and feet, upper limbs.
Throat - Red fauces. Burning and dryness with pain in pit of stomach and often
extending to abdomen, preventing sleep. Difficult swallowing saliva. Sensation of mucus with fruitless attempts
to remove it. Constriction, worse right side, worse bending forward. Pain in throat on turning head, waking him
frequently at night.
Vertigo - Vertigo in evening, better going to bed with an emptiness at stomach with flushing of face. Vertigo
with dislike for physical labor. Vertigo beginning with blurring of slight. Vertigo as from seasickness, causing
loss of appetite.
COMMENTS - Allen gave indications including rheumatic pain in clavicles. Crampy pain in heart, alternating
with lancinations. Pain in heart with suffocative constriction of throat. Aortic aneurysm. Nausea with vertigo
and angina pectoris.
Dry cough. Rheumatic pains in back, especially when alternating with similar pains in different parts. Muscular
rheumatism of left arm.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-t., Dulc., Aur. (2) Magn-gl., Anis. (3) In rheumatism, Kali-bi., Kalm. (4) Inter-
menstrual hemorrhage, Ham., Bov., Bell., Cham., Elaps.
REFERENCES - Allen. Boericke. Clarke.

name: Malandrinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - maland. Malandrinum. Grease of horses. Nosode of the disease in horses called “Grease.”
Trituration of Sugar of Milk saturated with the virus. Solution of the virus. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Boils. Eczema. Fistula. Impetigo. Knock-knee. Measles. Skin, unhealthy. Smallpox.
Typhoid fever. Vaccination, effects.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Jenner, the origin of cow-pox is infection of the udders of cows by contact with
grass on which a ’horse infected with “Grease” has trodden. This assertion is to some extent confirmed by the
experience of homeopaths, who have found in Maland, a very effectual protection against infection with
smallpox and against vaccination. Straube made provings of the 30c potency.
Clarke cured with it cases of unhealthy, dry, rough skin remaining for years after vaccination in smallpox,
measles and impetigo. Burnett cured with it a case of knock-knee in a child who was constantly handling his
penis.
Maland, has been used on inferential grounds with great success in ill effects of vaccination. Efficacious in
clearing of the remnants of cancerous deposits. Bone-like protuberances. Toes feel scalded and itch terribly.
MIND - Dullness of mind. Dizziness. Confusion and lassitude of the mental faculties with a dread of any mental
exertion. A lack of concentration.
Abdomen - Pains around umbilicus.
Back - Pain along back, as if beaten.
Causations - Ill effects of vaccinations (Thuj., Sil.).
Ears - Profuse, purulent, greenish-yellow discharge, mixed with blood.
 Eyes - Red stripes under eyes.
Face - Scab on upper lip, with stinging pain when torn off.
Female - Vagina closed with crusts, yellowish-greenish-brown in color.
Head - Aching in forehead. Frontal and occipital headache. Impetigo covering head from crown to neck and
extending behind ears. Thick, greenish crusts with pale, reddish scabs, itching worse in evening.
Limbs - Sore pains in limbs andjoints. Pains, especially in left tibia with petechia-like patches on anterior
aspect of left leg from knee to ankle. Petechia on both thighs, worse left. Knock-kneed. Impetiginous crusts on
extensor sides of forearms. Runaround on nails of hands and feet.
Male - Child constantly handles his penis. Mouth - Tongue is coated yellow with red streak down middle
(typhoid). Tongue cracked and ulcerating down middle, swollen.
Skin - Smallpox. Measles, also as a preventive. Small, dusky red spots on legs, not disappearing on pressure.
Petechial typhus. Impetigo covering back of head, extending over back to buttock and even into vagina,
covering labia. Impetigo on extensors of forearms. Eczema. Dry, scaly,
itching, cracks of hands and feet in cold weather andfrom washing. Boils. Malignant pustule. Bad effects
of vaccination (dry, harsh skin).
Sleep - Dreams of troubles. Dreams of quarrels.
Stomach - Vomiting of bilious matter, nausea.
Stool - Dark, cadaverous-smelling stool. Yellowish, foul-smelling diarrhea.
COMMENTS - Burnett's indications are “Lower half of body, greasy skin and greasy eruption. Slow
suppuration, never ending, as one heals another appears.” Impetigo, ecthyma, fat, greasy-looking pustular
eruptions are particularly acted on by this remedy.
A. L. Marcey related a striking experience with Maland. 30c. In the presence of a smallpox epidemic, he
vaccinated himself, taking at the same time Maland. 30c night and morning. The vaccination did not take. It
was twice repeated and still did not take, nor was smallpox contracted.
Called to vaccinate four children in a family whose parents were recovering from smallpox, he vaccinated all
and gave Maland. 30c to three of them at the same time, the remaining child was the only one whose
vaccination “took.”
This was so severe that Maland, had to be given to modify its intensity, which it did effectively. The other three
were re-vac- cinated but none “took.”
Of five children from six to seventeen years of age, only the eldest had been vaccinated and he had a good
scar. All except the eldest were given Maland, and were vaccinated and none of the four “took.” The eldest
took smallpox. Maland, was then given and in a few days he was convalescent.
In another case of smallpox, Maland, was given and the disease only lasted a few days, the eruption drying
up. In Straube's proving, the symptoms were worse in evening.
Burnett considers Maland, a very deeply acting remedy and one not to be repeated oftener than once a
fortnight. Clears the remnants of cancerous deposits.
Heath cured with Maland. 30c fistula in a pony's neck, following strangles.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) For the bad effects of vaccination, Vario., Vac., Thuj., Sabin., Ant- t., Apis, Sil.
(2) In general, children handling genitals, Med. (butMaland. has deeper action). (3) In pustular eruptions, Hep.,
Merc. (4) Casteq., Hippoz., Hipp.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Malaria Co. Nosode
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - malar-co. Malaria co. nosode. Combination of the nosodes from all four types of malaria.
(Plasmodium falciparum, Plasmodium malariae, Plasmodium vivax, and Plasmodium ovale). Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Ague. Bilious, fever. Cachexia. Chills. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Fatigue. Fever. Headaches.
Intermittent fever. Liver, disorders. Malaria. Nausea. Spleen, disorders. Sweats. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The first episode of symptoms usually occurs about 8 to 30 days after the mosquito bite.
Headache, fatigue, and nausea. Hard, shaking chills with fever for 12 to 24 hours. Rapid breathing. Heavy
sweating, accompanied by a drop in temperature.
Episodes may recur every 2 or 3 days until the disease is treated. Without treatment, the disease can continue
for years. Generally worse in crowded or unsanitary living conditions. Hot, humid climates. Malaria is endemic
in Latin America, Asia and Africa.
COMMENTS - Malaria is an infection caused by a single-cell parasite, which is transmitted by the bite of an
anopheles mosquito. Malaria affects the blood cells, blood vessels, liver, central nervous system.
 There are four types of malarial parasites, they are transferred from person to person by a mosquito bite. The
mosquito becomes infected with malaria after biting a person with the disease. The organism multiply in the
mosquito, then enter the bloodstream of the next person the mosquito bites.
Once in a person's bloodstream, the parasites travel to the liver, where they
thrive and multiply rapidly. After several days, thousands re-enter the bloodstream and destroy red-blood cells.
Some parasites remain in the liver, continue to multiply and are released again at intervals into the
bloodstream.
REFERENCES Murphy.

name: Malaria Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - malar. Malaria officinalis. Decomposed vegetable matter. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Ague. Bilious, fever. Cachexia. Camp fever. Colic. Constipation. Cramps. Diarrhea. Emaciation.
Fever. Gout. Hay fever. Headaches. Liver, disorders. Malaria. Nausea. Neuralgias. Rheumatism. Spleen,
disorders. Tuberculosis. Typhoid. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Malar, is made from vegetable matter decomposed in water in glass jars for one two and
three weeks.
Malarial cachexia. Malaria and rheumatism. Rheumatic paralysis and emaciation. General sense of weariness.
Sense of weariness from a very short walk. A kind of simmering all through the body.
Spleen disorders. Functional hepatic diseases. Typhoid, semi-paralytic condition. Right arm gets numb and
has to be rubbed. Cold limbs, poor appetite but food does not distress her.
Fearful headache, nausea, aversion to food, distress through hypochondriac region, first in the spleen, then
liver and stomach and chills. Bilious colic, nausea, cramps, diarrhea and headache. Urine red, scanty. Bowels
sluggish but stools natural. Menses regular, rather scanty.
Dull headaches, dizzy and drowsy at all times, worse mornings. Eyes weak, blurring, reading difficult.
Laryngeal irritation with cough and secretion of bloody mucus. Slow pulse.
MIND - Feels stupid and sleepy. Very forgetful. Dizzy and drowsy (Gels.).
COMMENTS - Yingling cured a Kansas volunteer with Malar. The volunteer, 28, after a week in camp in rainy,
chilly weather had
chill and fever, continuous nausea, vomiting bile, retching. Tongue white, thick coat. Mouth felt dry but was
moist. Thirst for large quantities.
Symptoms were moderated by Ip. and later Bry., but not removed. Skin, eyes and face very yellow. Malar. 1
m. Was given and improvement set in; in a week was in better health than usual.
Mrs. S. A. H., 63, had shooting pains all over muscles, bones ache. Diarrhea in morning, stools thin, yellow,
foul. Bitter taste, parched mouth tongue white. Stretching and gaping. Malar. 1000c. cured quickly.
RELATIONS - Malar, belongs to the same order of remedies as Pyrog. (product of decaying animal tissues).
Bowen found the best antidotes toMalar.:Nux-v.,Bry.,Ars.,Rhus-t..Eup-per. and Chin, gave negative results.
Compare: ( 1 ) Spleen, Cean. (2) Liver, Bry., Lyc., Chol.,Chel. (3) Pain under right scapula, Chel. (4) Effect of
damp and wetting, Lem-m., Dulc. (5) Half machine-gun cough, Cor-r., Cocc-c. (6) better after urinating, Lith.,
Ambr. (7) Intermittents, Ip., Cedr., Nat-m., Meny.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

name: Malathion
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - malat. Malathion. Pesticide. Ovide. A pesticide and topical drug for lice, scabies. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abdominal, cramps. Allergies. Aplastic, anemia. Asthma. Autoimmune, disorders. Birth, defects.
Conjunctivitis. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Eye, disorders. Immune, disorders. Impotency. Infertility.
Intestinal, disorders. Kidney, failure. Learning disabilities. Leukemia. Miscarriages. Rash. Rheumatoid,
arthritis. Stomach, cramps. Trembling. Twitching. Vertigo. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Malathion is an organophosphate parasympathomimetic which binds irreversibly to
cholinesterase. Malathion is an insecticide of relatively high human toxicity. It weakens the immune system.
Causes autoimmune disorders. Rheumatoid arthritis. Asthma and allergies. Leukemia. Aplastic anemia.
Kidney failure.
Drowsiness. Unusual weakness. Slow heartbeat. Dizziness. Convulsions, seizures. Trembling. Clumsiness or
unsteadiness. Difficult or labored breathing. Increased sweating. Increased watering of mouth or eyes.
Abdominal or stomach cramps. Diarrhea. Loss of bowel or bladder control. Intestinal disorders in children.
 Birth defects. Infertility or miscarriages. Lower sperm count. Slower sperm movement.
Muscle twitching of eyelids, face, and neck. Pinpoint pupils. Redness, pain, swelling of eye, eyelid, inner lining
of eyelid. Burning, dry or itching eyes. Conjunctivitis. Eye discharges, excessive tearing. Skin rash. Stinging or
irritation of scalp.
MIND- Anxiety and restlessness. Hyperactivity. Attention deficit disorder. Learning disabilities in math, reading,
etc. Language or speech delays. Mental retardation. Memory weakness, confusion. Depression. Irritability.
Aggressive behavior.
COMMENTS - Malathion breaks down into malaoxon, which is 60 times more toxic than malathion. For this
reason, if malathion is used or somehow enters an indoor environment, as it breaks down into malaoxon, it
can seriously and chronically poison the occupants living or working in this environment.
Malathion present in untreated water is converted to malaoxon during the chlorination phase of water
treatment, so malathion should not be used in waters that may be used as a source for drinking water, or any
upstream waters.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Mancinella Venenata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mane. Mancinella venenata. Manganeel apple. Hippomane mancinella. Manzanillo. N. O.
Euphorbiacae. Caribbean. Tincture of fruit, fiesh leaves and bark. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Blindness. Blisters. Borborygmus. Chills. Cholera infantum. Colic. Dermatitis.
Diphtheria. Erysipelas.
Erythema. Esophagus, stricture. Eyes, disorders. Fever. Fungoid, growths. Hair, loss. Headache. Herpes.
Melancholy. Menopause. Nausea. Nerve, disorders. Pemphigus. Photophobia. Puberty. Scarlatina. Skin,
disorders. Sore throat. Stomatitis. Tongue, patched. Typhoid fever. Vesicles. Vomiting. Wounds.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany noted that “Mancinella is a species of the Euphorbiacae and has all the
virulent properties of the family in a high degree. It is one of the trees around which the upas legends have
clustered. It is certain that the juice, which resembles pure white milk, does possess a considerable amount of
acridity and that some persons suffer great pain from incautiously handing it.
“Perhaps its most dangerous property is that of causing blindness, if by chance the least drop of the milk or
smoke of the burning wood, comes in contact with the eyes.
“Dr. Seeman states that at Veraguas some of the ship's carpenters were blinded for several days by the juice
getting into their eyes while cutting down Manchineel trees, while he himself suffered from temporary loss of
sight from merely gathering specimens. The same accident happened to a boat's crew from making a fire. Salt
water is said to be an efficacious remedy.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Marked skin symptoms. Dermatitis with excessive blistering, oozing of sticky serum, and
formation of crusts. Acridity. Burning, smarting in various parts. Favors rapid healing of wounds. Loss of
vision. Pain in the thumb.
Hering suggested it in mental depressed states at puberty and at menopause with an exalted sexuality.
MIND - Bashful and taciturn. Timid. Sympathetic. Weeps a great deal, especially when alone. Melancholy.
Homesickness. Silent mood, sadness. Depression with sexual weakness.
Wandering thoughts. Sudden vanishing of thoughts. Forgets what she wishes to do next. Forgets her
errands. Anger aggravates. Impatience during headache. Averse to work and answering questions.
Anxiety from becoming cold, during or after scarlatina, before menses.
Fear of becoming insane. Fear of evil spirits. Sometimes feels as light as if she could float or hover in the air.
Delusions that he will be taken by the devil.
Abdomen - Rumbling in abdomen renewed by every motion and when taking a deep inspiration. Colic, worse
cold drinks. Bowels sore and burn.
Back - Backache with nausea and tenesmus. Sharp pain in left scapula and left chest at intervals. Painful
stiffness of small of back, neck, after sleep, could scarcely move neck.
Chest - Oppression of chest, better expectoration. Aching pain behind sternum. Severe pain in middle of
sternum, worse pressure and breathing.
Ears - Ears feel as if closed. Redness and heat of ears.
Eyes - Lids, heavy and sore. Eyes smart or burn on closing them. Dull ache behind the eyes. Intense
inflammation with loss of vision (for some days). Photophobia.
Face - Swollen, spotted. Herpes on lips.
Food - Craves cold water. Aversion to meat, bread, wine.
Head - Pain in vertex, worse lying. Heat in head, better from rest. Congestion of head before menses. Scalp
 itches. Hair falls out after acute sickness.
Heart - Pressure in region of heart. Needle like stitches at heart. Palpitations in evening, on turning in bed, as
from eating. Palpitations with weakness. Pulse weak, very large and soft.
Limbs - Pain in thumb. Icy coldness of hands and feet. Biting vesicles on soles, desquamation and dryness
of soles.
Lungs - Rattling in left lung during breathing. Violent cough and painful stitches in trachea from slightest
exertion. Cough, worse cold drinks, at night.
Modalities - Worse from cold. Worse cold drinks. Worse cold feet. Worse dampness. Worse touch. Worse
puberty, menopause. Worse anger. Worse after eating.
Mouth - Feels peppery. Burning and pricking in the mouth, not better by cold water. Burning of fauces.
Dysphagia from constriction of throat and esophagus. Copious, offensive saliva. Profuse foul
yellow saliva. Taste of blood.
Nose - Illusions of smell of gunpowder, dung, etc. Pressure at root of nose.
Perspiration - Cold sweats. Acrid, sticky foot sweat.
Rectum - Sensation of fullness in rectum with hollow feeling in stomach. Sudden desire to go to stool in
morning. Profuse diarrhea with colic, vertigo, much discharge of flatus. Greenish stools. Burning pain during
diarrhea. Pulsation in anus. Discharge of fetid blood from hemorrhoids.
Sensations - Head feels as if bruised or as if it had been exposed to the sun. Head as if hollow, as if lying on
something hard. Ears as if closed. Electric thrusts in upper part of throat. As if flames rising from stomach. As
if stomach drew together in a lump and then suddenly opened. As if something alive in stomach.
Skin - Intense erythema. Dermatitis with extensive blisters, oozing of sticky serum and formation of crusts.
Heavy, brown crusts and scabs. Large blisters, as from scalds. Fungoid growths. Vesicles. Erysipelas.
Pemphigus.
Stomach - Swollen epigastrium. Continual choking sensation rising from stomach. Vomiting of food, followed
by severe colic and profuse diarrhea. Vomiting of ingesta, followed by griping and copious stools. Repeated
green vomit. Burning pains and black vomit. As of flame rising from stomach.
Temperature - Chills with icy cold hands and feet. Burning heat, with inclination to cover himself in bed.
Flushesof heat. Fever with tingling in skin, with thirst.
Throat - Cutting pains, worse cold drinks. Diphtheria. Tonsils swollen. Choking sensation rises in the throat
when speaking, preventing drinking though thirsty.
Vertigo - Vertigo, head feels light, empty, while walking about.
COMMENTS - Mane, was introduced into homeopathy by Bute, who proved it. It was also proved by Mure and
Ackermann. Marked affects on the head, eyes, throat, abdomen and rectum. The symptoms induced included
burning in all parts, vesication and ulceration
of the skin and mucus membranes.
Symptoms worse from drinking cold water, especially cough. Better from heat when lying down, but headache
is worse from the warmth of a stove and there is an inclination to uncover. Cough is worse at night.
Med. Cent, quoted the case of a woman who for several years was possessed with the fixed idea that she
would become insane. She had become a wife and mother, but still the ideas possessed her. Happening to
see in Puhlmann's Therapeutics that Mane, has “fear of going crazy,” she took Mane. 12c and was
permanently cured.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Crot., Jatr., Canth., Anae.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
