name: Mercurius Vivus
author: Murphy
full:
METHYLENUM COERULEUM
(Methylene blue)
PHARMACY -meth-b. methyl. Methylenum coeruleum. Methylene blue. Teleamethyl- thionine chloride. One
of the aniline dyes. A diphenyl amine compound, also classed as an aniline color. Trituration. Solution.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Arthritis. Cancer. Chorea. Coma. Cystitis. Epilepsy. Epithelioma. Gonorrhea.
Hemicrania. Kidneys, disorders. Malaria. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Neurasthenia. Pleurisy. Rheumatism.
Spasms. Spinal irritation. Suppuration. Tremors. Typhoid fever.
HOMEOPATHIC - Methylene blue consists of small, indigo-colored, scaly crystals with a bronze-like tinge, that
 are dark green in transverse fracture. Slightly soluble in water, forming a deep blue solution. It has been used
in old-school practice in doses of about three grains in capsules or pills for rheumatism of joints and muscles
and in rheumatoid arthritis.
The dyes are carcinogenic. Mose tig treated a man, 50, who suffered from cancer of the femur. Mosetig injected
into the groin a 1 percent solution of “Trichlorate of Aniline,” increasing the strength, until four grams were used
at one injection. Almost an hour after the first injection the patient became dark blue, the next morning the
discoloration was gone.
After the four-gram doses, poisoning symptoms appeared including unconsciousness, stertorous breathing,
feeble pulse, the whole body becoming dark blue. Artificial breathing and stimulants brought the patient around
in four hours. Smaller doses were
used after that. In eight weeks he went home, cured to follow his ordinary work. Methyl- violet 1 to 500 and 1
to 1,000 produced equally good results.
Methyl, is a remedy for neuralgia, neurasthenia. Malaria. Typhoid fever, delirium and fever.
Tendency to tremor, chorea and epilepsy. Later states of a stroke. Backache, sciatica. Gonorrheal rheumatism
and cystitis. Pus infection.
Nephritis (acute parenchymatous), scarlatinal nephritis. Urine acquires a green color. Bladder irritation from its
use is antidoted by a little nutmeg. Surgical kidney with large amount of pus in urine. Tympanites.
Cancerous ulcerations on the skin and mucus membrane and on internal organs such as uterus, lungs and
the gastrointestinal tract. Hemorrhages are mostly bright red with few clots. Cough with blood-streaked
expectoration and difficult breathing.
MIND - Neurasthenia. Unconsciousness.
Back - Backache with sciatica.
Bladder - Irritation of the bladder. Cystitis. Urine greenish. Gonorrhea.
Chest - Causes absorption of pleural effusion.
Head - Hemicrania. Habitual headache.
Limbs - Tremors. Spastic hysterical contractions.
Lungs - Stertorous breathing.
Skin - Turns the patient dark blue. Pus infection.
Temperature - Typhoid fever. Malarial fever. Fever from pus absorption.
COMMENTS - The kidneys have a distinct attraction for Methyl., as it appears in the urine within half an hour
of the dose and, if the kidneys have their normal permeability, the whole is eliminated in thirty-six hours. If
there is delay beyond this it indicates that the urea is not being perfectly eliminated and that a tendency to
uremia exists. The aniline products have been used as remedies for malignant growths.
Mosetig of Moorhof published a case treated with Trichlorate of Aniline, “an aniline dye.”
E. Thomson, stated that Methyl, in 1-5 grains doses, “with equal parts powdered nutmeg to prevent irritation
of the bladder” (a useful item in view of the homeopathic employment) is valuable in habitual headache and
hemicrania.
Cardamantes of Athens gave 10 to 12 grs. ten hours before an expected malarial attack. He said it is useful in
combination with quinine or when quinine had failed. Immunity from malaria seems to follow its continued use.
Apt to cause cystitis. A gentleman who suffered excruciating pains from calculus in the kidney, giving rise to
pyelitis and cystitis, derived no benefit from any treatment until his doctor gave him Methyl, with occasional
doses of eucalyptus.
L'Art Medical gave an account of the use of Methyl, injection in pleurisy with serous effusion. C. H. Lewis of
New York, first drew off by aspiration 100 cubic centimeters of the liquid, dissolved in this one grain of Methyl,
and reinjected it into the pleural cavity.
The patient soon began to pass greenish urine and then the exudation quickly disappeared, partly from the
diuretic effect of Methyl., partly from its stimulating action on the pleura. A watery solution is not borne, causing
pain and irritation of the pleura.
The most homeopathic experience is that of Halbert. Utilizing the affinity of Methyl, for nerve tissues and nerve
cells, Halbert gave it in 3x trituration with success in neuralgias of neurasthenia, tremor in neurasthenia,
spasticity of hysterical contraction, trophic disturbances, the result of nerveexhaustion, and spinal irritation.
Halbert confirmed its anti-malarial powers and commended it in typhoid as an intestinal anti-septic. An
apparently hopeless case of typhoid was signally benefited by it, the tympanites disappearing as if by magic.
Wherever there is pus infection it is indicated and it has “made a record” with him in gonorrhea and cystitis.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Anil., Pyrog..
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer.
 ***MEZEREUM
(Spurge Olive)
PHARMACY - mez. Mezereum. Spurge olive. Daphne mezereum. Chameleons germánica. Mezereon. N. O.
Thymelaceae. Hilly woods over nearly whole of Europe and Russian Asia. Tincture of fresh bark gathered just
before the plant flowers in February and March. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Anus prolapsed. Bones disorders. Ciliary, neuralgia. Coccyx, pain. Constipation.
Contraction, tendons. Convulsions. Crusta lactea. Ear, affections. Eczema. Eruptions. Erythema. Exostoses.
Eyes, disorders. Glands, enlarged. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hematuria. Hernia. Herpes, zoster. Impetigo. Itching.
Leucorrhea. Lice. Mercury, effects. Neuralgias. Osteoma. Periostitis. Pityriasis. Pruritus, senilis.
Rheumatism. Scrofula. Skin, disorders. Syphilis. Teeth, affection. Testicles, enlarged. Tinea, capitis. Tinea,
versicolor. Tongue, disorders. Twitch- ings. Ulcers. Vaccination.
HERBAL - The plant flowers in very early spring, even when snow is on the ground. Suited to complaints that
come on in the earliest months of the year.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann recorded the history of a robust man who took mezereum bark for some
ailment and continued it after the ailment disappeared. Soon, unbearable itching set in all over his body, and
he could not sleep a moment. Thirty-six hours after discontinuing it, the itching was still increasing. A few grains
of camphor removed it.
Mez. is the vegetable analog of Merc., it and Mez. antidote one another. The mind, skin, eyes, mucus
membranes and bones are affected in much the same way by both. They have the same sensitiveness to
damp, cold and warmth and the same nightly aggravations.
Mez. affects skin, bones, nerves and mucus membranes of the mouth and stomach. Affinity for skin symptoms
and disorders of bones and neuralgias, especially about the teeth and face.
Bruised, weary feeling in joints with drawing and stiffness. Pains of various kinds with chilliness and
sensitiveness to cold air. Sudden pains of various kinds followed by chilliness, numbness and soreness.
Pains shoot upward and seem to draw the patient up out of bed.
Irritation, burning itching or burning smarting on the skin. Violent, burning, darting like fire in the muscles.
Burning, darting sensation in the muscles, subsultus tendinum. Burning, boring pains in bones especially long
bones, with neuralgia of the teeth and face or after shingles. Decay, exostosis of bones. Periostitis. Bones
seem enlarged.
Internal burning with external violent itching in small areas or in single parts.Ac- rid secretions, pus, leucorrhea,
etc. Ulcers. Eruptions after vaccination. Cystic osteoma. Abscesses of fibrous parts or tendons. Body feels
light. Twitchings in the eyelids, on the right side of the face etc. Convulsions better by tight grasping.
Affected parts become cold or emaciate. One sided symptoms, whole or partial. Excessive sensitiveness to
air, even of a fan. As if a cool breeze blowing on the part. Affections go from above downward, from within
outward, and from right to left. Worse from cold, damp, cold winds, sudden changes of weather, heat, and
warm food.
Nash mentioned an exception to the worse by warmth modality. In a man whom he cured with Mez. of obstinate
facial neuralgia, the pains were brought on or greatly worsened by eating, and the only relief the man could
get was by holding the painful side close to a hot stove. Only radiated heat was of any use, hot cloths, wet or
dry, gave no relief whatever.
MIND - Forgetful. Vanishing of thoughts while speaking, unable to repeat what has been learned by heart.
Indifference to everything and everybody, looks through a window for hours without being conscious of objects
around. Dullness of mind after sound sleep.
Apprehensive at the pit of the stomach when expecting some very unpleasant news or shock. Irresolution.
Nervous, compelled to move and change positions. Aversion to talk, it seems to be hard work to utter a word.
Hypochondriac and despondent. Sadness about trifles, when alone. Religious or financial melancholy.
Despair of eternal salvation. Anger alternating with quick repentance. Vexed and angry at trifles. Censorious.
Reproaches or quarrels with others. Irritability during headache.
Abdomen - Burning and heat in abdomen. Swelling of glands with large abdomen in children. Contraction of
diaphragm. Pressure in inguinal ring. Dull or severe pain in region of spleen. Stitches in left hypochondrium.
Flatulent colic with shivering and difficult respiration.
Back - Pain in muscles of back. Pain in neck and back, worse motion and at night intolerant of all touch. Violent
itching rash on nape. Stiff pain in nape and muscles of sides, worse motion. Rheumatic pain in right scapula,
in morning after rising. Shuddering over back and limbs, when itching is most severe. Coccyx painful after a
fall.
Causations - Ill effects of suppressed eczema capitis, vaccination and mercury.
Chest - Stitches in chest. Sore pain in right axilla. Soreness and burning in bones of thorax. Constriction across
 chest. Contraction of diaphragm. Painful tension in intercostal muscles. Chest feels too tight on stooping.
Sensation as if ants were running over chest. Intercostal neuralgia following herpes zoster, worse at night and
in warmth of bed. Red spots like fleabites on chest.
Constitutions - Suited to light-haired persons, phlegmatic temperament, irresolute. Gouty, rheumatic,
syphilitic miasm.
Cough - Irritation in throat causes hacking cough. Dry tickling cough, into vomiting. Cough, worse eating, on
taking a warm drink. Cough from beer. Must cough till food is vomited.
Ears - Thickening of tympanum. Ears feel too open, as if tympanum was exposed to the cold air and it
blew into the ear. Chronic diffuse otitis. Oozing eruption behind ear. Itching behind ears, scratching
causes small elevations, when scratched off the spots feel sore. Desire to bore fingers into ears. Deafness
after suppression of head eruptions.
Eyes - Eyes feel strained. Dryness of the eyes, they feel too large. Pains radiate and shoot downward with
cold feeling and stiffness of bone. Pain outward along the brows. Smarting pain in eyes, with lachrymation.
Lachrymation with any pains. Ciliary neuralgia after operations. especially after removal of eyeball.
Inclination to wink, jerking of eyelids. Obstinate twitching of muscles of left upper lid. Eczema of lids.
Face - Red. Facial muscles drawn tight. Face swollen, burning pains, confluent vesicles. Boils on face.
Impetigo. Eruptions around the mouth with coryza. Cracks in corners of mouth. Scabs about mouth. Ulcers on
upper lip. Lips swollen, dry, scaly externally, painful, sore and burning. Chin covered with elevated, white
scabs. Violent neuralgia about face and teeth, running towards ear, at night, worse eating, better near hot
stove. Neuralgic pains come and go quickly and leave part numb. Sudden pains, wakes from sleep. Left-sided
prosopalgia. Twitching of muscles, right sided. Boring pains in bones of upper jaw. Violent itching of face and
scalp.
Female - Menses scanty with face ache. Menses too frequent, too soon, too profuse. Leucorrhea like albumen,
very corroding. Ulceration of vagina and cervix.
Food - Loss of appetite. Constant longing for food. Confusion after eating. Thirst during chill. Aversion to meat.
Craving for bacon, ham, fat, coffee, wine. Desire for acid drinks. Beer tastes bitter and causes vomiting. Worse
from wine. Itching temporarily better from wine and coffee.
Head - Violent headache on slightest touch, after vexation. Headache, worse from talking. Stupefying
headache in right side. Numbness of one side of scalp or top of head. Pressing pains as if skull would split.
Pains on slightest touch in temples and sides. Cranial bones painful. Boring pains in bones of occiput. Violent
congestion to head during menopause. Affections
of external head, scaly eruption, white scabs. Burning pain of scalp. Intolerable itching. Eczema capitis. Head
covered with thick, leathery crusts, under which pus collects. Milk crusts. Exostosis. Sore boils. White
scabs or scales. Hair falls in handfuls. Dandruff, white, dry.
Heart - Pulse full, hard, accelerated evenings. Pulse at times intermittent. Pulse frequent mornings, slow
evenings.
Kidneys - Red flakes float on top of urine. Hematuria, hot, preceded by cramps in bladder. After urinating, a
few drops of blood are passed. Biting, burning in forepart of urethra at the close of urination.
Limbs - Trembling of limbs. Limbs feel cold, as if shortened. Joints feel bruised and weary, as if they would
give way. Pain in hip and knee. Aching, itching in knee. Legs and feet go to sleep. Hands and feet cold, nails
blue. One hand hot. Paralysis of flexors of fingers, cannot hold anything. Long bones inflamed and swollen,
decay, exostosis. Pain, worse night touch, damp weather (Merc., Syph.). Burning in tibia and long bones.
Lungs - Dyspnea, as if from adhesions or contraction of lungs. Desire to take a long breath. Snoring in children.
Yellow, viscid, salty expectoration. Expectoration during day or tasting like an old catarrh.
Male - Testicles enlarged. Painless swelling of the penis and scrotum. Heat and swelling of penis. Itching
glans penis. Fine, pricking, stitches in penis and tip of glans. Urethra sore. Violent sexual desire. Gonorrhea
with hematuria, discharge of watery mucus.
Modalities - Better open air, wrapping up, eating. Facial pains better radiated heat of stove. Head pains better
wrapping up head. Headache better stooping. Worse at night, evening until midnight, touch, motion. Worse
warmth of bed, fire, warm food, cold, air, drafts, damp. Worse during menses, suppressions, vaccinations,
mercury.
Mouth - Salivation. Mouth waters. Taste bitter, sour, beer tastes bitter, which is vomited. Breath smells like
rotten cheese. Burning in mouth and throat, sometimes
better eating. Ranula, worse talking and chewing, ejects a watery fluid. Dry, dark red mouth. Flat, whitish ulcers
on inner side of lips and corners of mouth.
Nose - Sneezing, coryza. Frequent sneezing with pain of excoriation in chest. Visible twitching at the root of
nose. Interior of nose excoriated. Post nasal adenoids.
 Perspiration - During sleep, following chill. Skin drips with cold sweat.
Rectum - Itching in anus. Biting, sore pain in anus on walking. Constriction of anus, stitches and prolapse of
rectum. Burning in rectum. Much painless straining. Painful tenesmus. Constipation with hepatic and uterine
inertia. Constipation after confinement. Summer diarrhea of children. Diarrhea with small, white glistening
particles. Green discharges. Constant passing of flatus, but in a short and interrupted manner.
Sensations - Head as if drunk, as if everything in the head would press asunder. As if skull would split, as if
top of head gone, as if head bruised, as if head was in an ants' nest. Eyes as if too large, as if drawn back into
head. Throat as if narrowing. As if food remained long time in stomach. Stools feel as if they would split anus.
Limbs feel shortened. As if fire darting through muscles. Sensation of lightness of body. Bones are very sore
and feel distended. Diseased parts wither.
Skin - Skin wrinkled and in folds. Eruptions ulcerate and form thick scabs under which purulent matter exudes
(Chry s-ac.). Eruptions, ooze, acrid, gluey moisture, form thick crusts, scabs with pus beneath or chalky
white. Intolerable, itching, worse by warm bath, worse in bed. As if millions of insects were crawling on him.
Crusty eruptions, white scabs, bleeding when touched. Skin cold on places where itching is most intense.
Pruritus senilis. Itching changes place on scratching, coldness after. Itching without eruption. Itch-like
eruption, after vaccination, depriving child of sleep. Eczema. Psoriasis. Herpes zoster with burning pain.
Liver spots on chest and arms become dark and desquamate. Ulcers itch and burn, surrounded by
vesicles and shining, fiery-red areola. Deep, hard, painful ulcers worse touch and warmth. Old ulcers burn and
sting. Ulcers form over bony protuberances. Desquamation over whole body. Scurf like fish scales on back,
thighs, chest and scalp.
Sleep - Much yawning and stretching. Irresistible sleepiness during day. Sleepiness from debility.
Sleeplessness from itching. Sleeplessness from cramps in calves. Sleep disturbed by violent pain in face.
Nightmare at night, awakening after midnight.
Stomach - Chronic gastritis, burning, corroding pain. Constant, severe pain and pressure in stomach even
after light foods. Induration of stomach. Stomach ulcer with much burning. Burning and corroding pain in
stomach, better milk and eating. Constricting, pinching pain in stomach. Sensation of apprehension, fear,
faintness and goneness at stomach as if something was going to happen. Sensation as if food remained for a
long time undigested in stomach and caused pressure. Stomach pain culminates and ends with retching and
vomiting of all food taken. Vomiting of chocolate colored substance with nausea. Vomit bitter, sour, slimy, oily
or greasy. Water brash.
Stools - Stools preceded and followed by shivering. Stools, hard, large, as if they would split the anus. Stool
soft, brown, sour, fermented, undigested, offensive.
Temperature - Chill of single parts as if dashed with cold water. Chill alternating with flushes of heat. General
weakness. Great tendency to get remittent or typhoid fever. Ague.
Throat - Dark, red, burning, sore, worse winter. Burning in mouth and throat, sometimes better eating. Burning
in pharynx and esophagus. Throat as if dry. Sensation as if posterior part of throat were full of mucus.
Swallowing even of fluids difficult and painful, from severe burning and raw pain. Constriction of pharynx.
Sensation of narrowing in throat. Nausea felt in throat, better eating.
Teeth - Teeth feel dull and elongated. Teeth feel cold. Teeth painful on biting on them and from cold air.
Roughness from tartar on teeth. Roots of teeth decay. Rapid decay of hollow teeth. Toothache into temples,
better with mouth open and from drawing in air. Toothache in gums from cold air. Toothache from congestion
to head. Sensation as if tooth was being lifted out of socket.
Tongue - Burning in tongue with salivation. Tongue coated along one side only. Middle of the tongue fissured.
Thick, white coating on tongue with large, red, elevated papillae.
Vertigo - Vertigo with contracted pupils, faintness. Vertigo and flickering before eyes, inclination to fall to left
side.
COMMENTS - A case reported in Allen's Appendix recorded the history of apale girl, 14, having been advised
to use mezereum leaves to make her fat and rosy, went into the woods and used them freely on her cheeks
and surrounding parts.
Burning soon set in, the whole face swelled enormously, especially the nose, eyelids and hairy scalp. Severe
and painful sneezing, delirium, dull, unbearable, pressing pains in forehead, a nauseous dryness in throat and
constant irritation to dry cough. The face soon showed the appearance of erysipelas bullosum, nostrils closed,
she could only breathe through her mouth, febrile pulse, burning urine.
Oil and compresses were applied, and after the second day desquamation occurred in large areas. Health did
not return. Debility followed, with loss of vitality, mental depression bordering on idiocy. Then typhoid fever,
lasting fully for three months to which she finally succumbed.
Poisoning has also been observed from the effects of the berries, causing dryness and burning of throat and
 stomach, intense thirst, a narcotic state, coma, and convulsions of eyes and upper limbs.
In a child of four, poisoned with the berries, the lips swelled, the tongue was furred and swollen, protruding,
with difficult swallowing. The tongue remained quite raw when other symptoms had passed away.
Mez. is one of Hahnemann's anti-psoric remedies. Ulcers, with thick, yellowish, white scabs. Vesicles, itch and
burn. Lint dressings stick to them and when they are torn away, bleeding occurs. Burning vesicles on the sides
of the fingers and ulcers on finger joints.
Canker sores with a scab, pus (Rhus-t., Nat-m.). Herpes zoster, shingles itch and burn and form scabs. Herpes
zoster, during the eruption and for the neuralgia remaining after, especially if the pains are burning. Vaccination
eczemas. Psoriasis and eczema, itching, worse in bed and from touch. Intolerable itching, migratory itching.
Skin is scabby looking, with an itch underneath the scab that aggravates. Pimples on ankles and backs of feet,
horrid taste and clamminess of mouth in morning. Pimples better by hard scratching. Dry crust on the scalp
and falling out of hair, accompanied with short sight.
Bone pains, particularly of the long bones. The least touch is intolerable. Affinity for the facial bones and teeth
(Merc.). Decay attacks the roots or sides of the teeth, rather than the crowns (Merc.). Toothache is worse at
night, from touch, even with the tongue. Better by holding the mouth open and drawing in air.
Neuralgia about the eyes, the pains radiate and shoot downward. Sensation in the eye as if a cold wind were
blowing in it. Hypersensitiveness of the ear to air. Feeling as if air went through the ear to the throat.
Stitching, burning and itching in the rectum and anus. During stool, the rectum prolapsed and the sphincter
closes upon the protruded part. Sluggish bowels. Constipation after confinement.
Constricting tendency in the throat, stomach and tendons. Enlarged testicles (Clem.). The leg is shortened
with pain in the hip. Tension in muscles of the chest. Pain and stiffness in muscles of neck. Cramp-like
contraction over chest and back and across front of chest.
Cooper noted that green discharges were particularly characteristic.
Carroll Dunham recorded a notable case of
deafness, due to suppressed psora. A youth, age 17, deaf since four and incapacitated thereby, secluded
himself and brooded over his trouble. Membranes thickened.
At the age of three, he had an eruption of thick, whitish scabs, hard, almost horny, covering the whole scalp.
There were fissures through which exuded on pressure a thick, yellowish pus, often very offensive. There was
much itching and disposition to tear off the scabs with the fingernails, worse at night.
The allopathic treatment was vigorous, a tar cap was placed on the head and when firmly adherent to the
scabs was violently torn off, scabs and all, leaving the whole scalp raw. This was painted with a saturated
solution of Arg-n. The eruption did not reappear, but from that time the child was deaf. The eruption was the
very counterpart of an eruption observed in a proving by Wehle.
Mez. 30c, three globules in a powder of sugar of milk, was given on February 3, March 1, and September 28,
1857 and January 26, 1858. Improvement set in slowly after the first dose, which was only repeated when the
effect of each preceding dose seemed to be exhausted. Finally, the hearing was for all practical purposes
completely restored.
The action of Mez. in catarrhal cases is illustrated in the case of Miss M. R., 39, a brunette, who had chronic
catarrh. The left ear had long been deaf and the right had begun to fail. There were noises in the ears. Drum
membranes retracted and scarred.
The naso-pharynx mucus membrane was granular and irritable. There was excessive sensitiveness to the air,
even of a fan and occasionally a sensation as if air went through to the throat. A dose of Mez. given before
each meal entirely relieved the symptoms.
T. S. Hoyne collected many cases illustrating the action of the remedy including a case of a woman treated by
W. E. Payne. She had no rest when alone, wanted company. Ideas vanished while talking, could not repeat
what had been learned by heart. Looked through the window for hours without being conscious of objects
around.
Did not know what she was doing, forgot what she was about to utter, looked
ill-humored pale, wretched, fallen away. Apprehensiveness at pit of stomach, as when expecting some very
unpleasant intelligence. All symptoms relieved in a single night by Mez. 20c.
S. R. Geiser noted the case of a man, 28, who had a violent neuralgia, boring pain in left lower jaw bone,
extending to temple and ear. Pain was worse at night, better from pressure. Mez. 3c relieved in two hours.
J. W. Vance recorded the history of H. G., stout, healthy-looking, left supra-orbital neuralgia recurring daily at
9 a.m. increasing until noon, declining until 4 p.m., when it entirely departed leaving no soreness behind. Pain
caused flow of tears. Mez. 1c cured permanently after other remedies had failed.
Hempel noted the case of a toothache in the incisor of a woman. Tooth felt elongated, loose, excessively
sensitive with sensation as if being raised out of its socket. Upper part of tooth was excessively painful. Mez.
 200c cured in a few hours.
Oehme noted the case of Mrs. X., who had pain in her right eye tooth, daily increasing. Felt too long. Pains
much worse by pressure on crown and outside root. Mez. 2c cured.
Oehme also recorded a case in which the fastenings of a hammock broke and a woman on it fell, striking her
sacrum and coccyx on the stump of a tree. She suffered excruciating pain. Arn. was applied locally. In a few
weeks she came home and the coccyx was still so tender she could not sit, only lie or stand. Arn. internally
and externally for two weeks had no influence. Mez. 2c cured in five days.
Cooper noted the case of a woman, 48, who had rheumatism which came on ten years before in her hands
from wearing wet gloves and extended later to arms and knees. She had stiffness on walking with loss of
muscular power, worse in hot weather, “pins and needles” in fingers on elevating arms. Could not grasp things,
sometimes one hand burned when the other was cold, menopausal flushings. Great relief from Mez. tincture.
Cooper also noted that Daphne laureola, the British representative of the genus, cured
scald-head when Mez. failed to work.
The symptoms in this case were worse by day, whereas Mez. has worse at night. The pains of D. laureola
come on in the morning and affect the entire head or whole left side. Guai. pains are also worse by day and
better by warmth.
H. B. Esmond cured with Mez. 3x a youth, 17, who had been afflicted with “salt rheum” as long as he could
remember. It was absent in summer, but every autumn, as soon as cold weather came, his face, neck, hands
and forearms would break out and continue sore until warm weather returned.
Mez. cured a girl, 18, getting thin with headache across forehead, temples and eyes, a throbbing with sickness
of stomach and water brash, always worse by movement, bowels very confined, menses never appeared.
H. Noah Martin noted a patient that said “my stools are as hard as stone and as large a my arm. I feel as if
they would split me open. They come in sections like mouthfuls and I becomes much exhausted and tremble
with weakness. Every stool is immediately preceded by chills and followed by long stitches up rectum.” Mez.
12c produced a natural stool in twelve hours.
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Kali-hp., Merc. Compare: (1) Merc., Phyt., Rhus-t., Guai., Syph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
keynote:
METHYLENUM COERULEUM
(Methylene blue)
PHARMACY -meth-b. methyl. Methylenum coeruleum. Methylene blue. Teleamethyl- thionine chloride. One
of the aniline dyes. A diphenyl amine compound, also classed as an aniline color. Trituration. Solution.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Arthritis. Cancer. Chorea. Coma. Cystitis. Epilepsy. Epithelioma. Gonorrhea.
Hemicrania. Kidneys, disorders. Malaria. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Neurasthenia. Pleurisy. Rheumatism.
Spasms. Spinal irritatio

name: Micromeria Douglasii
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - micr. Micromeria douglasii. Yerba buena. California. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Colic. Flatulence. Nausea.
HERBAL - A California mint-like plant acting on stomach and bowels. It is a pleasant beverage and febrifuge,
blood purifier and tonic. Used as a tea for colic and to relieve flatulence. Nausea with pain in the stomach and
bowels.
REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Millefolium Achillea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mill. Millefolium achillea. Y arrow. Achillea millefolium. N. O. Composite. Asteraceae. Tincture
of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Ascites. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bleeding. Blows. Bruises. Cancer. Chlorosis. Colic.
Dentition. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Fistula lachrymalis. Hematemesis. Hematuria. Hemoptysis.
Hemorrhages. Hypochondriasis. Hysteria. Infertility. Injuries. Leucorrhea. Lochia, profuse. Lochia,
suppressed. Milk, absence. Nipples, sore. Nosebleeds. Puerperal convulsions. Puerperal fever. Rodent
ulcers. Sycosis. Tetanus. Trauma. Tuberculosis. Varicose, veins. Urine, bloody. Wounds.
HERBAL - Yarrow was named Achillea by Linneus because the plant is mentioned in the Iliad as having been
used by Achilles on the instruction of Chiron to heal the wounds of his soldiers.
Millefolium received its popular name, “nosebleed,” because nosebleed comes on if the leaves are inserted
into the nostrils. The other species of Achillea indigenous to Great Britain, Achillea ptarmic, is called “sneeze-
wort” from its allergic properties.
HOMEOPATHIC - Mill, affects the capillaries of lungs, nose and uterus. Suited to all wounds which
bleedprofusely, sprains and over-lifting. Profuse, painless, bright, red, fluid hemorrhages. Nosebleeds.
Hemoptysis. Oozing of blood from the edges of closed wounds from over exertion.
Spasms or convulsions especially after the suppression of hemorrhages, menses, lochia, milk etc. Varicose
veins in pregnancy. Bruised soreness and congestions. Sprains and over-lifting. Bad effects from fall from
 a height. Profuse mucus discharges. Piercing thrusts of pain. Incarcerated hernia. Smallpox with great pain in
pit of stomach. Continued high temperature.
MIND - Forgetfulness. Loss of memory. Difficulty thinking and comprehending. Confusion and dullness in
evening. Confusion after coffee, wine. Desires nothing.
Does not know what he is doing or wants to do. Aversion to mental work. Moaning, sighing and groaning of
children.
Anxiety in chest, heart. Anxiety, excitement from pains. Anxiety better on rising from a seat. Very excited with
pain in stomach. Sadness. Violent, irritable. Hysteria. Delusions, he has been poisoned. Hypochondriasis.
Delirium. Knocking his head against wall.
Abdomen - Ascites. Abdomen distended. Pain in region of the liver. Congestions to portal system. Wind colic.
Frequent emission of fetid flatulence. Colic during the menstruation. Violent colic with bloody diarrhea during
pregnancy. Dysentery. Hemorrhage from bowels. Incarcerated hernia.
Back - Piercing, drawing pains, under left scapula. Fine piercing pains in left scapula, when standing.
Breasts - Sore nipples. Agalactorrhea. Suppressed secretion of milk.
Causations - Ill effects from operations for kidney stones, gallstones. Bad ejfects from a fall or sprain,
injuries, over-lifting, over-exertion. Suppressed lochia, menses, milk.
Chest - Oppression of chest with bloody expectoration or palpitations. Bubbles in chest as if warm blood was
ascending.
Constitutions - Suited to the aged, atonic, anemic women and children.
Ears - Darting pain in left ear. Sense of cool air passing through the ears. Noise in left ear causes starting with
fright. Sensation of stoppage in ears, after dinner.
Eyes - Glistening, brilliant eyes. Piercing pain from eyes to root of nose. Sensation of too much blood in eyes.
Lachrymation and discharges from eyes. Fistula lachrymalis. Agglutination of eyes in morning. Spots on eyes.
Face - Sensation of heat, as if blood was rising to head. Redness of face without internal heat. Tearing pain
in face to temples.
Female - Menses early, profuse, protracted. Menses suppressed, with colicky pain in abdomen. Convulsions
and epilepsy from suppressed menses. Leucorrhea
from atony of vaginal mucus membrane. Leucorrhea of children. Infertility with too profuse menstruation or
tendency to miscarry. Cramps during pregnancy. Painful varicose veins during pregnancy. Uterine
hemorrhages, bright red, fluid, after great exertion. Hemorrhage after labor, abortion or miscarriage.
Prolonged bleeding during labor. Lochia too profuse. Suppressed lochia with violent fever. Curative of post-
partum hemorrhage. Severe after-pains.
Food - Want of appetite. Sluggish appetite from stagnation in liver. Thirst during fever. Mouth dry, with thirst.
Confusion after coffee, wine. Dullness after wine. Congestion to head from coffee. Symptoms worse coffee,
better wine.
Head - Confused, dull headache, in evening, worse after coffee. Head seems full of blood. Fullness in head
after siesta. Headache with twitching of eyelids and frontal muscles. Piercing thrusts of pain. Beats the head
against the wall. Headache worse stooping. Throbbing in arteries of head and face.
Heart - Inflammation with tearing and piercing pains. Pains in heart with anxiety. Ebullitions from coughing
blood. Violent palpitation with bloody sputum. Pulse accelerated and contracted.
Kidneys - Chilliness with pain in left kidney, followed by hematuria. Catarrh of bladder from atony. Stone in
bladder with retention of urine. Pus-like discharge after surgery. Urine bloody (Senec.). Involuntary urination
of children.
Limbs - Bad effects from falls and sprains. Convulsions, convulsive motion of all limbs and violent pain.
Paralysis and contraction of limbs. Violent pains on a level with crest of left ilium. Pricking numbness. Left arm
frequently feels as if going to sleep. Hot hands and feet. Right Achilles tendon pains as after a blow or sprain.
Painful varicose veins during pregnancy. Painless or bleeding varices in pregnant women.
Lungs - Shortness of breath. Very difficult breathing, with tetanic spasms. Asthmatic affections. Inflammation
of lungs. Exces
sive accumulation of mucus in bronchi. Hemoptysis with incipient tuberculosis. Hemoptysis after injury.
Expectoration of bright red blood, without much coughing, sometimes in consequence of violent exertions.
Cough with bloody sputum in suppressed menses or hemorrhoids. Lung disease with coughing blood.
Male - Wounds and injuries of penis. Swelling of the penis and testicles. Semen is not discharged during sex.
Spermatorrhea. Gonorrhea, gleet. Sycotic excrescences.
Modalities - Better from bleeding, re-establishment of discharges. Better during the day, from wine, violent
exercise. Violent exercise improves vertigo. Worse from violent exertion, injury, exertion, lifting, stooping,
doubling the body, lying down. Worse evening and night, coffee, hemoptysis, suppression of discharges.
 Mouth - Tongue swollen and coated. Thirst, mouth dry. Putrid sore mouth. Gumboils. Rheumatic pain with
diseased gums. Toothache from eating things. Useful given before tooth extraction.
Nose - Nosebleed (Erech.), with congestions to head and chest. Piercing pain from eyes to root of nose.
Stuffed nose.
Perspiration - Profuse sweats. Colliquative perspirations.
Rectum - Fetid flatus. Diarrhea, preceded by rattling of fluids in abdomen. Mucus diarrhea. Bloody dysentery.
Bloody diarrhea during pregnancy. Hemorrhages from bowels after much exertion. Bleeding hemorrhoids.
Pains from blind hemorrhoids. Profuse flow of blood from condylomata. Ascarides.
Sensations - As if he had forgotten something. As if all blood ascended to head. Right side of head as if
screwed together. As if too much blood in eyes. As if cold air passing out of ear. As of a liquid moving from
stomach to intestines. Pain as from a blow or sprain.
Skin - Bruises and bleeding from wounds. Wounds after operation for stone in the bladder. Painless
varicose veins of pregnant women. Exanthemata and delirium. Suppressed itch, causing fever. Fistulous
ulcers. Gangrenous ulcers. Ulceration
of internal organs. Cancerous ulcers. Condylomata.
Sleep - Violent yawning without being tired. Goes to sleep late and does not feel refreshed in morning.
Stomach - Stomachache. Painful gnawing and digging in stomach as from hunger. Burning pain in stomach,
extending to chest. Sensation of fullness in stomach. Pressure like a plug in stomach. Cramps in stomach with
sensation as of a liquid flowing in intestines to anus. Eructations. Hiccough. Vomiting when coughing. Nausea
with vertigo. Hematemesis.
Teeth - Toothache from eating things. Gumboil. Ulcers on gums. Rheumatic pain with diseased gums.
Temperature - Chilliness with pain in left kidney. Heat in hands and feet. Fever heat with thirst. Continuous
high fever. Fever from suppressed itch or suppressed lochia. Hectic fever with hemoptysis. Malignant fever
with tetanus. Intermittent fever. Quartan, tertian, irregular fever.
Throat - Rough feeling in throat. Rough voice. Elongation of palate. Uvularelaxed. Ulceration of throat, pain in
left side when swallowing. Dull piercing pain, right then left. Throat catarrh.
Vertigo - Vertigo when moving slowly. Vertigo, falls to right side and backward. Vertigo with nausea when
stooping, not when lying down. Violent exercise improves vertigo.
Vision - Vision nebulous with contortions of facial muscles. Clear, bright vision. Foggy vision, not near eyes,
but at a distance.
COMMENTS - Hemorrhages and wounds (Am.). Anti-convulsive. Convulsions occur, although not exclusively,
as a result of suppressed hemorrhages, particularly the menses, or other discharges or secretions.
Trauma (Am., Ham., and Phos.), with profuse bleeding. Hemorrhage with bright, red blood, florid hemorrhage.
Tubercular hemorrhage. Bleeding hemorrhoids, bloody urine or stool. Useful for reabsorbing blood clots.
Useful after surgeries (Phos.).
Copious mucus discharges, especially due to atony. Pronounced relation to pregnancy and the puerperal state.
Useful for varicose veins during pregnancy. Uterine tonic, particularly for profuse menses.
C. W. related an interesting case in which a man had severe diarrhea, with profuse dark, chocolate-colored
stools, verging on black and slightly tinged with blood. A club doctor had failed to relieve, but an old woman
cured the man with “yarrow tea.”
C. W. had a collie dog that, when excited, would pull up grass or weeds and swallow them. When it happened
to swallow Mill., this invariably caused a rattling of fluid in the bowels, followed by dark chocolate diarrhea,
changing to black, very offensive, finally blood-tinged.
This lasted a day or two. It was found that Ars-i. 3x in solution was a complete antidote. Given every ten
minutes, as soon as rattling came on, it effectually stopped it. The dog also had fissured pads. Ars-i. did nothing
for these, but Ars. 30c cured.
RELATIONS - Ant-t. relieves the vertigo to Mill., Ars-i. the diarrhea. Antidotes: Ars-i., Amm-m. Compare: (1)
Composite group generally, Am., Bell-p., Calen. (2) Fic-v., Pakur. - hemorrhage from bowels and lungs. (3)
Acai., Helix. - in hemoptysis, diseases of chest, tuberculosis. (4) Erech. - nosebleed and hemoptysis. (5)
Senec. - hematuria. (6) Ham. and Ip. - hemorrhages. (7) Mill, red, clotted, Plat, dark, clotted. (8) Bry., Ust. and
Ham. - hematemesis. (9) Aeon. - hemorrhages, profuse flow of bright red blood. (10) Aeon., anxiety, Mills.,
absence of anxiety. Incompatible: Coffee causes head congestion.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - mill. Millefolium achillea. Y arrow. Achillea millefolium. N. O. Composite. Asteraceae. Tincture
of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Ascites. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bleeding. Blows. Bruises. Cancer. Chlorosis. Colic.

name: Mimosa Humilis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY- mim-h. Mimosa humilis. Sensitive plant. N. O. Leguminose. Mimosoideae. Tincture of leaves.
 Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ankle swelling. Borborygmi. Colic. Conjunctivitis. Coryza. Flatulence. Goosebumps. Numbness.
Rheumatism. Sneezing. Trembling. Twitching.
HERBAL - Mimosa humilis is one of the remedies introduced and proved by Mure. The “sensitive plant” of
the hothouses is M. púdica, but the leaves of M. humilis, said Mure, “close at the least contact.”
HOMEOPATHIC - The most notable Mim-h. symptoms were lancinations in the back and limbs
andswellingand redness of left ankle with tension and lancination. Smarting pain in legs with paralysis of
knee. Stiffness of bends of knees. Pressure in nape and right temple. Prostration.
MIND - Indolent with indifference (Ph-ac.). Abdomen - Borborygmi. Flatulent colic. Back - Violent lancinations
in back.
Ears - Whizzing in ears.
Eyes - Inflammation of eyes of left eye. Itching. Vision dim, halo around candle.
Head - Sensation of heat in head, as if enlarged.
Limbs - Lancinations in legs and hands, now in arm, now in leg. Swelling of left ankle with redness, tension
and lancination. Trembling of legs. Twitching of arm, extending to chest. Numbness of arm and right hand,
ceasing on movement. Inflammatory swelling of left hand.
Lungs - Dry cough in morning. Difficult breathing.
Male - Inflammatory swelling of scrotum. Mouth - Bleeding of gums. Salivation. Nose - Sneezing and coryza.
Rectum - Diarrhea. Frequent stools, colic.
Skin - Pimples and pimply excrescences about legs and arms. Goosebumps.
Sleep - Yawning. Drowsy in evening with frequent waking at night.
Stomach - Stomach aches and pains.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Mimosa Pudica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mim-p. Mimosa púdica. N. O. Leguminosae. Mimosoideae. Brazil and India. Tincture is
prepared from the root and the flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Backache. Blepharitis. Colic. Conjunctivitis. Coryza. Cough. Diarrhea. Enterocolitis.
Fistulae. Headache.
Hemorrhoids. Hydrocele. Hypersensitivity. Influenza. Otitis. Pains. Photophobia. Salivation. Scorpion, bites.
Sinusitis.
HERBAL - Mimosa Púdica is ligneous with regular flowers in clusters with reduced corolla, meristenous
androecium and albuminous seeds. It is a tropical plant originating from Brazil and in the warm parts of India.
The root contains 10% tannin, and its common usage suggests that it is an aphrodisiac.
HOMEOPATHIC-The homeopathic proving is the work of Sankaran (Mumbai), who experimented with it on
six young provers, for three weeks, using the potencies 3x and 6x in 1968-69.
Sensitiveness and headache above the eyes, aggravated by movement, ameliorated by closing the eyes.
Irritation of the conjunctiva and nasal mucus membranes. Pains in the shoulders. Diarrhea with abdominal
colic and irritating stools. Feeling that the body is too big.
MIND - General irritability. Annoyed by the thought of taking medicine. Easily angered, it takes a long time to
forgive. Sensitivity, impression that the body is too large.
Abdomen - Pain in the epigastric region, worse when coughing.
Back - Backache. Dorsal pain. Sharp pain in both shoulders.
Chest - Thoracic pain, especially around the lower part of the large pectoral muscle. Better by a hot bath and
by abduction movement of the arm, worse fresh air.
Constitutions - Allergic and psoric constitutions. Tubercular, nervous types, predominantly phosphoric.
Ears - Sudden, acute stinging pain, especially in the right ear. Pain coming in the evening, lasting through the
night. Pain worse when lying on the right side with pressure and draft of air. Pain ameliorated by lightly covering
the ear. Buzzing in the ears. Hears less well against a noisy background.
Eyes - Burning in the eyes, worse from a draft of air. Blepharitis. Conjunctivitis. Photophobia with headaches,
aggravated by the sun. Vision slightly blurred. Eyelids secrete a yellowish pus, which forms in the corner of
the corner of the eye.
Eyelids stuck together in the morning on waking.
Head - Headache above the eyes, especially at the left eyebrow. Headache aggravated by straining the eyes,
or by quarreling. Headache, worse from movement, ameliorated by closing the eyes or by a tight bandage.
Lungs - Dry cough.
Male - Increase of sexual desire.
 Modalities - Better by friction, tight bandage, hot bath. Worse from a draft, movement, bright light.
Mouth - Abundant ptyalism throughout the body. Nocturnal salivation when lying on the right side. Loss of
sense of taste.
Nose - Irritation of the nasal mucus membranes. Coryza. Constant discharge of a watery secretion.
Rectum - Irritating stools with abdominal colic. Stools frequent, as often as ten times aday. Better after
evacuation. Ameliorated by rubbing the abdomen.
Throat - Pain and tickling in the throat, ameliorated by a hot drink, aggravated by speaking and by coughing.
COMMENTS - Mim-p. has been used as a decoction of the root ( 1:10), to be prescribed for gravel and all
urinary complaints. The infusion of the leaves has been used as a blood cleanser. Powder of the leaves and
root is for fistulae and hemorrhoids. The juice can be used as an application for insect and scorpion bites,
hemorrhoids and fistulae. A paste made from the leaves is an effective application for hydrocele. The leaves
can be used in the bath for cases of lumbar and hip pains.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Euphr. - Inflammation of the nose and eyes. Aggravated by light and air,
ameliorated in darkness when lying down. (2) Sabad. - Senses: irritation of the mucus membranes in the nose
and the throat. Ameliorated by hot drinks. (3) Psor. - Periodic migraines, worse from the slightest draft,
hypersensitive to the cold, sudden nocturnal diarrhea with a fetid odor.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Mimulus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mimul-b. Mimulus. Mimulus guttatus. Flowers are picked, placed in abowl of water and left to
the sun's action for several hours. The water imbued with healing power is then prepared as medicine.
Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into aone ounce dropper bottle, ( add brandy or alcohol,
if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth
or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Mimulus belongs to Bach's group “For Those who have Fear" along with the remedies of
Rck-r-b., Cher-p-b., Asp-b. andRd-ch-b. Anxiety disorders and phobias when there are concrete objects,
persons, or situations of fear (Rck-r-b.).
Nervousness, lowered stamina and decrease in vitality. Dread with internal agony or a slumping of vitality.
Hypochondriacal. Obsessive anxieties, intensifying minor symptoms. Excessive self-observation. Fear of
being rejected.
Frequent loose bowels and intestinal griping pains during acute states of anxiety. Chronic diarrhea. Heart
neurosis, with duodenal ulcers in the passive-dependent patient, emotional diarrhea, urticaria and atopic
dermatitis.
Useful during physical rehabilitation after accidents or surgery, or during sickness or old-age infirmities, when
every move frightens and small pains intimidate.
MIND - Constant fear. Dreaded things, persons, or events are seen as a hurdle, or as a dangerous deterrence.
Shyness and nervousness. Desire to hide shyness.
Anticipatory fears. Chronic phobias. Fixations or obsessions. Fear of death, accidents, poverty, loneliness,
misfortunes. Hypochondriasis (Chic-b., Heath-b.) and excessive self-observation (Cer-b., Lar-b.).
REFERENCES Bach.

name: Mitchella Repens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mit. Mitchellarepens. Partridge berry. Partridge-beans. N. O. Rubiacae. Tincture of whole plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Belchings. Bladder, irritation. Catarrh. Constipation. Depression. Dysmenorrhea.
Dysuria. Hemorrhages. Kidneys, pain. Menorrhagia. Menses delayed. Metritis. Uterine, hemorrhage.
HERBAL - Mitchella is a small, trailing evergreen bearing a scarlet bean and is common throughout the United
States. It belongs to the same order as Chin., Coff. and Ip. and shows its affinity with these in its power over
hemorrhages.
Indian women drink a decoction of it before confinements to make labor safe and easy. Herbalists use a
concentrated decoction as an application to sore nipple.
HOMEOPATHIC -Duncan induced pains and burning in the kidneys in his proving and Hale, who observed
the effect on a woman, recorded some characteristic symptoms in the urinary and uterine sphere.
Congestion of the uterus with bladder irritation. Irritation at neck of bladder with urging to urinate (Eup-pur.,
Apis.). Engorged uterus, hemorrhage, bright with dysuria. Lassitude. All muscles feel sore. Whole digestive
 tract feels cold, transverse colon tender to pressure.
MIND - Inability to concentrate mind. Depression, followed by buoyant spirits.
Abdomen - Griping. Distention with flatus.
Rumbling.
Back - Aching pains running down back. Dull pain between shoulders in kidney region.
Bladder - Uneasiness in neck of bladder, urging to urinate, burning, 11 a.m. Catarrh of bladder. Urethra and
neck of bladder swollen and irritated, especially in females).
Ears - Burning in left pinna. Dull aching in right ear.
Eyes - Eyes dull and heavy.
Female - Amenorrhea. Menses delayed. Menorrhagia. Dysmenorrhea and uterine hemorrhage, blood bnght
red. Uterus irritated, severe pain in it. Cervix engorged, dark red, swollen. False pains in last mouth of
pregnancy. Slow, feeble ineffective labor pains.
Food - Appetite impaired.
Head - Severe frontal headache on waking. Burning in vertex. Throbbing in occiput. Scalp sensitive to touch.
Heart - Burning pains, uneasy feeling as if its action was being interfered with. Beats irregular.
Kidneys - Heat in kidneys with dull pain. Dysuria, accompanying the uterine complaints. Increased quantity
of urine, acid. Urine high-colored, white sediment.
Limbs - Aching and burning sensation in right upper limbs. Walk unsteady, inclines to fall to right. Aching in
lower limbs in knee joint.
Lungs - Much mucus in bronchi. Dry, backing cough in morning. Breathing difficult, 11 a.m.
Male - Pain, drawing in right testicle. Mouth - Burring and prickling on tongue. Rectum - Tenesmus, urging.
Constipation, feces small, thin, difficult.
Sleep - Yawning, drowsy. Woke in a fright, frightful dreams.
Stomach - Burning in stomach extending whole length of esophagus. Acid belchings.
Temperature - Chill over whole body with flushes of heat, very sensitive to cold air.
Throat - Fauces dry. Pharynx feels constricted, impeding swallowing. Tonsils enlarged, painless, especially
the left. Some enlargement of left submaxillary gland.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chim., Senec., Uva., Ger., Goss. (2) In congested cervix associated with irritation
of neck of bladder, Sep. - Mitch has no general resemblance to Sep., (3) Eup-pur. - bladder irritation in women.
(4) Hydre. has in addition heat and itching in vagina. (5) Apis, Vesp. - has ulcer around os. (6) Caul., Chim.,
Cimic., Helon., Puls., Senec.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Momordica Balsamica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mom-b. Momordica balsamica. Balsam apple. Momordica balsamina. N.O. Cucurbitaceae.
Momordica. Tinctureof fresh ripe fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, externally used as a
liniment and poultice for bums, chapped hands, etc.
CLINICAL - Colic. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Flatus. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Mom-b. was introduced by Dr. Mercer, whose wife made the proving with twenty-four drops
of the tincture, producing some very well characterized symptoms.
Griping and colic (Coloc. and Elat.). Accumulation of flatus in splenic flexure of colon. Dropsy. Severe pains in
back and hypogastrium with painful and excessive menses. Sensation as if the whole contents of the head
had greatly diminished in weight.
Abdomen - Rumbling, griping, colicky pains, starting from back, spreading over abdomen.
Eyes - Mist before eyes.
Female - Painful and profuse menses, laborlike pains, followed by gushes of blood, pain at small of back
coming towards front of pelvis.
Vertigo - Dizzy, contents of head feel lighter.
COMMENTS - Farrington gave as a keynote “distention and rumbling in splenic flexure of colon,” which he
compared with the effects of Lyc.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Mom-ch., Lyc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Monosodium Glutamate
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mono-s-g. Monosodium glutamate. MSG. Sodium salt of glutamic acid.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Anaphylactic, shock. Asthma. Cramps. Flushings. Headaches. Hives. Insomnia.
Migraine. Nausea. Numbness. Palpitations. Rash.
HOMEOPATHIC - MSG is made by either a bacterial fermenting process, protein hydrolysis (a breaking of
protein into its constituent amino acids), or by synthesis. When a product is 99% pure MSG, the product is
called “monosodium glutamate” by the FDA and must be labeled as such. However, when a hydrolyzed protein
contains less than 99% MSG, the FDA does not require that the MSG be identified.
Many food products manufacturers advertise “No MSG” on their food packages, but MSG may be disguised
as “hydrolyzed vegetable protein,” “glutamic acid,” “enzyme modified,” “natural flavor,” “yeast extract,”
“maltodextrin,” or “autolyzed yeast.”
There have been reports of allergies and/or sensitivities to MSG, sometimes attributed to the free glutamic
acid component. It has been blamed for causing a wide variety of physical symptoms including migraines,
nausea, stomach cramps, bloating, irritable bowel syndrome. Extreme dryness of the mouth, mouth lesions.
Hives or rash.
Numbness to the tongue and face, burning sensation in the neck, facial pressure or tightness. Drowsiness,
insomnia, anxiety, panic attacks, mental confusion. Asthma, runny nose, sneezing. Flushing, heart palpitations,
and anaphylactic shock. “Chinese restaurant syndrome” is often used as an example of the symptoms
purported to be caused by MSG.
MSG has been shown to cause lesions on the brain, especially in children. These lesions cause cognitive,
endocrinological and emotional abnormalities.
Monosodium glutamate
In children, excess glutamate affects the growth cones on neurons. Growth cones are vital in laying down
chemical pathways in the brain to enable the brain to operate effectively. MSG could affect human children's
cognitive skills and cause learning difficulties.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Monotropa Uniflora
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - mono. Monotropa uniflora. Indian pipe. Ghost flower. Corpse plant. Convulsion weed. Fit root.
N. O. Monotropaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bunions. Colds. Convulsions. Epilepsy. Eye, disorders. Eye, inflammation. Fainting. Fevers.
Gonorrhea. Sores. Toothache. Ulcers. Warts.
HERBAL - The plant was used by some North American Indian tribes to treat eye problems, the stem was
bruised and the clear fluid of the stems applied to the eyes. An infusion of the root is antispasmodic, hypnotic,
nervine, sedative, tonic.
The flowers have been chewed in order to bring relief from toothache. Water extracts of the plant are
bactericidal. The crushed plant has been rubbed on bunions and warts in order to destroy them. A poultice of
the plant has been applied to sores that are difficult to heal.
The juice of the plant used alone or combined with water helps ophthalmic inflammation, ulcers, gonorrhea,
and inflammation and ulceration of the bladder. The juice from the stems has also been used to treat nervous
irritability, including fits and spasms.
It is a good remedy for spasms, fainting spells and various nervous conditions. It has been given to children
who suffer from fits, epilepsy and convulsions.
Because of the salicylic acid, the base of asprin, Monotropa unifora is considered a pain reliever. It has been
suggested in the past as a possible asprin or opium substitute.
An infusion of the leaves has been used to treat colds and fevers.
Monotropa uniflora
An infusion has been used for sore, tired swollen eyes. A tea is made from equal parts juice of Indian pipe and
fennel seed.
The infusion of Indian pipe to douche to help ease vaginal irritations. Safety is undetermined and it is possibly
 toxic at high doses as it contains several glycosides.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Morbillinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - morbill. Morbillinum. Measles nosode. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenitis. Catarrh. Conjunctivitis. Coryza. Coughs. Ear, disorders. Erythematous, lupus.
Exanthema. Eye, disorders. Lachrymation. Laryngitis. Measles. Optic neuritis. Otitis. Photophobia. Rash. Skin,
disorders. Splenomegaly. Spontaneous, abortion. Tachycardia.
HOMEOPATHIC - The well-known symptoms which characterize an attack of measles may all be taken as
guides for its homeopathic use. Its chief use has been as a prophylactic against infection and to clear up after-
effects of an attack.
Morbillinum is extremely useful for cases of debility, weak eyes, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, etc., left after severe
measles. Treated in fever hospitals, children who simply will not put on weight, are anemic, weary, and often
with some bronchitis, morbillinium will help to remove all these symptoms, prevent lung complications and help
them to assimilate their food well and to put on weight rapidly.
Affinity for the mucus passages, eyes, ears and the respiratory mucus membranes. Diffused bronchial rales.
Nasal voice, rough cough, lachrymation. Fevers, nasal and eye catarrh.
Koplik spots. Macular exanthema, begin- ing on the face and behind the ears. Fine scaly desquamation.
Aggravation of a first infection of measles. Troubles of the perception. General convulsions. Grumbling
children.
Mind - Mental dullness, sluggishness. Difficulty of thinking and comprehending. Moaning, groaning in children.
Fear of the sea.
Abdomen - Abdominal pain, localized at the appendix region. Acute mesenteric adenitis. Splenomegaly.
Swollen lymph glands.
Ears - Acute otitis.
Eyes - Optic neuritis. Lachrymation. Photophobia.
Female - Spontaneous abortion.
Heart - Tachycardia.
Lungs - Cough. Paroxysmal respiratory dyspnea. Purulent pleurisy.
Mouth - Koplik spots. Small white patches, surrounded by a red areola, slightly raised seen on the internal
walls of the cheeks and on the mucosa of the gums.
Nose - Flapping of the nasal wings, snoring. Catarrh of the nose.
Skin - Rosy maculae, round and oval, of different shapes separated by healthy skin disappearing by pressure.
Papulous eruption. Miliary, confluent, scarlatina-like eruptions. Ecchymotic spots.
Throat - Hypertrophy of the superficial glands of the neck. Throat red, irritated. Striduous laryngitis.
COMMENTS - This nosode was prepared by Gross, a contemporary of Hering. Gross used to soak some
globules in the blood of the patient suffering from measles, dynamised and used via olfaction.
According to another version, Gross gave some natural globules to the patient suffering from measles, who
kept them in his hands firmly closed, and afterwards Gross made dilutions from these globules.
Clarke would prescribe a dose of the Mor- bill. 30c 2 or 3 times daily as a prophylactic given to those who are
or may be exposed to infection. For an attack of the disease, he found nothing better than Morbill. 30c, eight
or ten globules in six ounces of water, a dessert spoonful every two hours.
Clarke noted that the effect of this is heightened by alternately giving Bell. 30c in the same way. These two
medicines will be sufficient to carry through any uncomplicated case and in his experience do even
Morbillinum better than Puls.
Dr. D. Sheppard case: Baby Jean, aged 13 months, who had done well on repeated doses of Silica, so that
she weighed 22 lb. and had 7 teeth without any disturbance, developed measles at the beginning of June,
1941. When seen again on June 19th, she was not her usual bright self, very quiet and miserable, had lost
about a pound in weight.
Morbillinum 100 given at once. The next week she was extremely lively and happy as always, and had gained
6 oz. Morbillinum was repeated weekly until July 10th, when she weighed 22 lb. 3 oz., a gain of nearly 20 oz.
in three weeks, plus the eruption of another tooth and four more nearly through; always cheerful and bright
now.
Dr. D. Sheppard writes: "Let me repeat once more: remember the measles serum, Morbillinum, in potency
during the convalescence period after measles. There will be no need to send the child to the seaside or give
innumerable doses of the nauseating cod - liver oil and malt mixture. This treatment is much simpler, less
 costly and more efficacious.”
“And if in an older child or even an adult you find that the individual had one or more attacks of measles, and
has not been doing too well since, interpose a dose or two of Morbillinum 30 or higher, and then go back to
the other constitutional remedies as may be necessary; and you will be surprised how quickly various states
of ill-health will clear up.”
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Puls., Hep., Merc., Sulph. Complementary: Bell.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.
