name: Nitromuriatic Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - nit-m-ac. Nitromuriatic acidum. Aqua regia. A mixture of chloro nitric acid, chloronitrous acid,
chlorine and water. Prepared by mixing 18 parts of nitric acid with 82 parts of muriatic acid. Dilutions. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, constricted. Bilious. Canker, sores. Catarrh. Cirrhosis. Constipation. Depression. Digestion,
slow. Dysphagia. Gravel. Headache. Hepatitis. Mouth, sore. Oxaluria. Palpitations. Ptyalism. Salivation.
Scurvy. Vertigo. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Aqua Regia, the royal water of the Alchemists, has been proved in the lower dilutions, in
the 30c.
 Some experiments were made by Dr. Scott, who acidulated his bath with the acid and sponged his body with
acidulated water. Sponging and bathing had the same effect. Scott noticed that the symptoms were more
marked as the proportion of muriatic acid was increased.
Salivation and sore mouth and throat with dysphagia were produced in Scott and the provers. Scott noticed
that the salivation was intermittent. Weakness. Headache with drowsiness. Slow digestion. Pricking pains.
Clinical reputation in oxaluria and gravel. Removes the distressing skin symptoms
resembling psoriasis. Weak, physically and mentally depressed. Constricted anus. Gravel. Bilious conditions
torpid liver, hepatitis and early cirrhosis of liver.
Hale noted that it is more adapted to liver torpor and gastric catarrh common in hot and damp climates and
aggravated by meat eating and alcohol.
MIND - Nervous irritation andrestlessness. Low spirits, depression.
Abdomen - On rising, sensation from left hypochondrium to rectum as of desire for stool. Slight colic in lower
abdomen.
Back - Catching pain in back muscles while taking a cold bath.
Food - Aggravated by meat and alcohol.
Head - Headache and great sleepiness, worse 3 p.m. Sensation in temples as if brain distended. Sudden
sticking ache in left temple while leaning to left side, preceded by twitching of anterior tissues of temporal
muscle.
Heart - Palpitations. Fluttering at heart, while eating or moving.
Kidneys - Urging in penis and bladder, aching in hips, thighs and small of back, after a short delay some pale
urine passed. Burning in urethra. Oxaluria. Cloudy.
Limbs - Heavy pain in loins. Sticking in various parts of limbs successively, while walking. Languid aching
through hips and front of thighs and small of back.
Liver - Bilious conditions, torpid liver, hepatitis and early cirrhosis of liver. More adapted to liver torpor and
gastric catarrh common in hot and damp climates. Sudden increase of secretion of bile.
Lungs - Inflammation of larynx and bronchi. Breathing easier than usual.
Modalities - Worse after eating and from exercise.
Mouth - Metallic taste (Cupr.). Ptyalism. Extreme salivation, could not spit it out fast enough. Constant
drooling at night (Merc.). Salivation intermittent, no fetor. Pain in palate or mouth. Small superficial ulceration
over inside of mouth and tongue, excoriation. Cankers. Large blister inside lower lip. Gums bleed easily.
Rectum - Sphincter constricted. Constipated with ineffectual urging. Constipation, desire for stool, but unable
to pass anything owing to constriction of anal sphincter. Anus moist and sore. Loose, yellowish, pappy stool
after breakfast.
Sleep - Sleepy with headache. Slept unusually well and felt better for it.
Stomach - Salivation, worse at night. Food takes longer to digest than usual. Sour belchings with empty
hungry feeling in stomach, not relieved by eating. Evacuation of flatus and belchings.
Temperature - Chill passing upward, while sitting near stove. Mild fever. Perspiration increased, often to a
great extent.
Throat - Pain on swallowing all down esophagus with burning there and in roof of mouth. Spasmodic,
tremulous contractions in pharynx near levator palati muscles, while writing at a very low table.
Vertigo - Frontal headache with dizziness. Sensation on rising from bed as if brain was all in occiput, making
it feel heavy.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak

***NUPHAR LUTEUM (Yellow Pond-lily)
PHARMACY - nuph. Nuphar luteum. Yellow pondlily. Nymphaealutea. N. O. Nympheacee. Tincture of fresh
root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cholerine. Colitis. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Entero-colitis. Exhaustion. Headaches. Impotence.
Psoriasis. Pityriasis, capitis. Rhus poisoning. Seminal emissions. Sexual, weakness. Typhoid fever.
HOMEOPATHIC - Nuph. was proved by Pitet, and many of his symptoms have been clinically confirmed.
Yellow diarrhea coming on in the early hours of the morning, with great exhaustion. Typhoid fever.
Produces nervous weakness with marked symptoms in the sexual sphere. Sexual weakness and pollutions.
Pityriasis capitis very much aggravated, with much itching and falling out of the hair.
MIND - Impatient of slightest contradiction. Ex- cessivemoral sensibility. Sympathetic. Acute pain in witnessing
sufferings of animals.
Abdomen - Colitis. Entero-colitis. Colicky
pains all around waist, worse 5 a.m. to 7 a.m.
 Back - Dull pain in left lower lumbar region. Sensitive in kidney region. When walking, painful stitch to flank,
better from pressure.
Chest - Pain behind sternum, when running, as though subjacent organs violently shaken.
Eyes - Sparks filled field of vision, converging from circumference to center, when standing.
Head - Heaviness of head. Bruised shaking in brain. Dull pains in front part of base of brain on level of orbits.
Lancination in right and left anterior lobes of brain. Headaches attending depressed states of generative
organs.
Limbs - Weakness and loss of power in limbs, worse evening.
Male - Pain in testicles and penis. Spermatorrhea. Weakening nocturnal omissions while convalescing from
typhoid. Impotency with involuntary emissions during stool, when urinating. Complete absence of sexual
desire, parts relaxed, penis retracted.
Modalities - Diarrhea worse 4 a.m. to 6 a.m., worse after the least excess of any kind. Weakness and itching
worse evening. Walking causes painful shocks in hams and pain in flank, better by pressure. Worse the day
after sex.
Mouth - Sweetish taste. Tongue white, mouth pasty.
Rectum - Stitches as from needles in rectum, above. Smarting and burning at anus after every stool. Much
exhaustion with stools, sense of exhaustion in epigastric region.
Skin - Violent itching. Red blotches, regular in outline, ovoid or circular, prominent and covered with little silvery
white scales. As eruption disappeared, scales ceased to be reproduced and the skin at place of each blotch
became pale red or yellowish.
Stomach - Painful sensation of weariness in stomach. Exhaustion in epigastrium. Digestion slow, wind colic
with liquid, sour-smelling stools.
Stool - Diarrhea during typhoid. Soft stools preceded by some colic for several days or painless diarrhea.
Yellow diarrhea, worse in the morning. Stools liquid, yellow, fetid.
Urine - Urine deposits copious reddish sand, hard, adheres to the vessel.
COMMENTS - A marked feature of the proving was the excessive depression of the male generative system.
Nuph. has done good work in analogous conditions and headaches associated therewith.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) in sexual weakness, Agn., Kali-br., Lyc., Sei., Yohim., Nym. (2) In diarrhea: Chel.,
Gamb., Sulph., (3) Early morning diarrhea: Sulph.. Nat-s., Rumx., Podo. (4) Sexual debility, Gels., Con., Dig.,
Nat-m„ Chin.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Nux Moschata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - nux-m. Nux moschata. Nutmeg. Myristicafragrans. Myristica officinalis. Myristica moschata. N.
O. Myristicacee. Tincture of powdered seeds deprived of the Mace. A fresh nut and fresh plant tincture should
be prepared and tested. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Asthma. Backache. Belch- ings. Brain, softening. Catalepsy. Chilblains. Clairaudience.
Clairvoyance. Colic. Convulsion. Cough. Debility. Drowsiness. Dryness. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Eyes,
disorders. Fainting. Fevers. Flatus. Freckles. Frostbite. Gastralgia. Hemorrhage. Headaches. Head,
movements. Hemorrhages. Hiccoughs. Hoarseness. Hysteria. Intermittent fever. Locomotor ataxia. Lumbago.
Mania. Marasmus. Menopausal disorders. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Narcolepsy. Pelvis,
congestion. Perspiration, bloody, hysterical. Pregnancy, complaints. Ptosis. Puerperal convulsions. Kidney
colic. Rheumatism. Sleep, overpowering. Speech, defective. Stammering. Strangury. Strokes. Toothache.
Turpentine, effects. Typhoid, hemorrhage. Uterus, prolapse. Vertigo. Worms.
HERBAL - Nux-m. is one of the many examples of poisonous and medicinal substances commonly used as
food. The use of nutmeg as a condiment doubtless originated because Nux-
Nux moschata m. is specifically related to weak digestion.
Ground nutmeg is popularly used in conditions of excessive flatulence and when the smallest excess in eating
or drinking sets up indigestion. Used for diarrhea and boils. Nutmeg has a reputation for putting off the
menstrual period or else for bringing it on.
Using nutmeg for these purposes has led to many cases of poisoning, supplying a large number of the
homeopathic symptoms.
HOMEOPATHIC - There is a characteristic “irregularity” in the remedy. It produces states of exaltation
resembling hysteria, as well as the mesmeric state with exalted senses and consciousness of double person-
ality. Profoundly disturbs the sensorium, mind and nerves.
Characteristic drowsiness, conditions accompanied by drowsiness, especially if there is also chilliness,
 coldness or thirstlessness. General inclination to become unconscious during acute attacks.
Marked tendency to fainting fits with heart failure, worse at stools, at menses, with slight pain, from sight of
blood, while standing (when dressing). Epilepsy with consciousness. Paralysis with spasms and trembling of
tongue, eyelids, esophagus. Catalepsy. Automatism. Mania. Hysteria. Mental depression from grief.
Feels as if drunk, staggers on trying to walk. Cold limbs. Humming, buzzing, funny feeling in body. Hard parts
feel soft. Fleeting pains. Parts lain on feel sore. Heaviness of eyes tongue etc. Sensation as of a hard lump in
stomach, liver, throat. Puffiness.
Extreme dryness of the mucus membranes and skin. Female organs are affected. Bearing-down pain, dark
blood. Dark hemorrhages. Uterine prolapse and displacements. Useful for threatened miscarriage. Affinity for
pregnancy, labor, and the puerperal state.
Disturbed digestion. Indicanuria. Spasms of children with diarrhea. Marasmus of children. Useful to scrawny,
delicate, hysterical women who have small breasts and who laugh or cry by turns. Clairvoyant.
MIND - Confused mind and impaired memory. Memory weakness, loss associated with dryness in the brain

HOMEOPATHIC - Strychnos nux vomica is a moderate-sized tree, native to the Coromandel Coast and Cochin
China. The fruit is like an orange in appearance and contains numerous seeds of flattened circular outline,
about the size of a half penny, ash-gray in color, covered with fine silky hairs.
The seeds are intensely bitter owing to the presence of strychnia and brucea that exist together with certain
peculiar acids, but the pulp is innocuous and is said to be eaten by birds. If nitric acid is added to the seeds a
deep orange-yellow color is produced. The wood of the tree is very bitter.
Nux-v. is used in India in cases of intermittent fever and snakebites. The Treasury of Botany noted that a

in connection with the same case.

Kidneys - Pressure, burning and heat in region of kidneys, in nephritis. Nephritis from abuse of liquors. Severe
sharp pains in region of left kidney, worse rising from seat and motion. Kidney colic (right), extending to genitals
and legs with dribbling urine. Spasmodic strangury, after beer. Painful ineffectual urging to urinate. Frequent
calls, urinates little and often. Tenacious mucus passes with the urine, without pain. Urine pale, later thick,
whitish, purulent, reddish, with brick-dust sediment. Hematuria from suppressed hemorrhoidal flow or menses
 (Ip., Ter.). Urine dribbles in old men with enlarged prostate or gonorrhea.
Limbs - Chorea. Convulsions from abuse of alcohol. Progressive locomotor ataxia from alcoholism.
Cramps and spasms of limbs. Cramps in calves and soles. Paresis of arms with shocks. Automatic motions
of hand towards mouth. Partial paralysis from overexertion of getting soaked (Rhus-t.). Crawling and formica-
tion in paralyzed parts. Legs numb, feel paralyzed. Sudden loss ofpower of arms and legs in the morning.
Aching, drawing or bruised pains in limbs, worse motion and at night. Limbs heavy as lead. Rheumatism
attacking mostly muscles of trunk and large joints. Legs stiff. Knee joints as if dry, cracking during motion.
Drags his feet while walking, legs tremble, unsteady gait. Shooting from toes to thighs, worse after stool. Heat
of hands, feet, yet they must be covered. Arms go to sleep, numb, stiff feeling. Varicose veins attributable to
high living.
Liver - Great soreness and tenderness in region of liver, with pain in right shoulder. Liver sore, enlarged,
sticking pain. Sharp pain in region of liver, worse from contact or motion. Pressure and stinging pains. Weak
liver from bad diet, meat, fats, spices, alcohol, etc. Gallstone colic. Throbbing pain as from hepatic abscess.
Hepatitis from bad food or water. Jaundice from anger. Jaundice from habitual use of alcohol. Cirrhosis from
alcohol abuse. Enlarged liver of alcoholics. Toxic liver from drugs, chemicals and alcohol.
Lungs - Shallow and oppressed breathing. Awakened every night by intolerable sense of suffocation.
Dyspnea in morning and evening. Loud, snoring, during sleep. Difficult breathing, from accumulation of gas.
Dyspnea during pregnancy. Asthma from disordered stomach. Asthma with fullness in stomach, worse in
mornings or after eating. Asthma with feeling as if clothing were too tight, better belching. Asthma from
spasmodic constriction. Yellow, grey, cold mucus. Sour or sweetish expectoration. Bright red blood. Hemop-
tysis from anger, suppressed hemorrhoidal flow. Pneumonia with catarrhal irritation. Pneumonia, after
suppression of hemorrhoidal flow, when hepatization occurs, from becoming chilled. Pneumonia of the elderly,
also of children. Pneumonia in sick people compelled to lie upon back.
Male - Drawing pain in testicles and spermatic cords. Testes hard and retracted. Constricting pain in testes.
Orchitis (Ham., Puls.). Sharp pain in testes. Heat in testicles. Hydrocele. Chronic prostatitis. Increase of
smegma. Gonorrhea, thin discharge, with burning on urinating and frequent urging to stool. Spermatorrhea
with dreams, backache, burning in spine, weakness and irritability. High sex drive. Cannot be in female society
without having emission. Premature ejaculation. Bad effects of onanism, sexual excess. Emissions from high
living. Impotency. Penis becomes relaxed during sex.
Modalities - Better from a nap, if allowed to finish it in evening. Better moist air, damp, wet weather (Caust.).
Better from free discharges. Better strong pressure, wrapping head, lying on sides, resting, frequent
stretching. Better hot drinks, milk, fats. Worsefrom overeating, coffee, condiments, liquor, stimulants.
Worse from high living, debauched, sedentary habits. Worse narcotics, drugs tobacco,
purgatives. Worse anger, mental exertion, vexation, mental shock, wounded honor, disappointment of
ambitions. Worse cold, open air, dry air, drafts, wind. Worse disturbed sleep, early morning. Worse noise,
music, odors, after eating, yawning. Worse pressure of clothes at waist, touch, uncovering.
Mouth - Dry mouth. Foul, sour breath. Offensive breath in morning. Sour, bitter, bad taste in morning.
Internal mouth, tongue and palate slimy, and feel raw and sore. Small aphthous ulcers in mouth and throat.
Bloody saliva runs out at night. Itching of palate, Eustachian tube. Gums, swollen, white and bleeding. Teeth
chatter. Toothache, worse cold, better warm drinks. Jaws contracted. Articulation and speech difficult.
Nose - Stuffy colds, snuffles after exposure to dry, cold atmosphere, worse in warm room. Snuffles in a
newborn. Stuffed up at night and outdoors or alternates between nostrils. Sudden fluent coryza after rising.
Coryza, fluent in daytime, worse warm room, better open air. Coryza with lachrymation. Acrid discharge, but
with stuffed-upfeeling. Violent sneezing, abortive, from intense crawling in nostrils (left). Bloody mucus in
nose. Nosebleeds in morning (Bry.). Nosebleeds during sleep, from suppressed flow of hemorrhoids, from
coughing. Oversensitive to strong odors, even fainting. Smell before nose like old cheese, burning sulphur.
Nose looks sharp and pointed. Picking at nose, worms.
Perspiration - Sour perspiration, on one side of body. Rather light sweat. Cold, clammy sweat on face. Odor
of sweat, musty straw. Sweats during sleep, disappears on waking. Sweats after midnight and in morning.
Rectum - Constriction of rectum. Constant uneasiness in rectum. Irregular, peristaltic action. Constipation
with frequent ineffectual urging or passing but small quantities at each attempt. Urging to stool felt
throughout abdomen. Constipation, the harder he strains the harder it is to pass stool. Feeling as if part of
stool remained. Sharp pain in rectum after stool. Frequent small evacuations. Dysentery, stools relieve
pains for a time. Alternate constipation and diarrhea after abuse of purgatives. Diarrhea after a debauch,
worse morning. Diarrhea after night watching, after overexertion of mind, after anger, after ginger or brandy.
Diarrhea with jaundice (Dig.). Itching, blind hemorrhoids with ineffectual urging to stool. Burning pain in
hemorrhoids, intolerable to least touch. Hemorrhoids very painful after drastic drugs. Hemorrhoids during
 pregnancy or after childbirth. Dragging pain at anus when not at stool. Prolapsed rectum.
Sensations - As if something heavy fell into head. As if his head were immensely larger than his body. As if
pressing a nail into brain into vertex, as if skull pressed asunder. Chest as if drawn together, as if something
torn loose in chest. As if blood would be jerked out of veins. Navel as if drawn in. As if hernia would occur, as
if everything in region of umbilicus were being shattered and torn. As of a band above knees, around body.
Skin - Pale or yellowish color of skin. Jaundice. Blue mottled skin. Skin red and blotchy. Skin as if numb.
Ecchymosis, blue spots. Goose bumps. Eruptions with burning, pricking, itching. Burning, pricking like
fleabites. Miliary and pimpled eruptions. White miliary eruption. Acne. Furunculi. Urticaria with gastric derange-
ment. Ulcers with elevated margins of a pale red color. Chilblains, burning itching. Tendency to boils.
Abscesses.
Sleep - Better after a nap, unless aroused. Y awning. Drowsy after meals and in early evening.
Sleeplessness from abuse of coffee, wine, liquor, opium or tobacco. Sleepless from rush of ideas.
Sleeplessnessfrom mental strain. Awakens in fright from least noise, as if someone were in room. Awakens
at 3 a.m., lies awake for hours, with a rush of thoughts. Cannot sleep after 3 a.m. until towards morning.
Weeping and talking during sleep. Amorous dreams. Dreams about exerting the mind. Anxious dreams.
Dreams full
of bustle and hurry, anxious. Dreams of being pursued by animals, dogs and cats. Dreams of quarrelling, of
mutilations, of fatal accidents. Nightmare after a heavy supper or alcoholic beverages. Wakes feeling
wretchedly.
Stomach - Weight and pain in stomach, worse eating. Severe pain in stomach from injury, worse least food.
Ravenous hunger, especially about a day before an attack of dyspepsia. Region of stomach very sensitive
to pressure (Bry., Ars.). Indigestion from alcohol. Disordered stomach from debauchery, from high living,
from drugs, from sedentary habits. Indigestion, after business anxiety, from sedentary habits, night watching.
Dyspepsia from drinking strong coffee. Cramps in stomach in morning and after eating. Sour taste and
nausea in the morning. Food lies like a heavy knot in stomach. Epigastrium bloated with pressure as of a
stone several hours after eating. Hiccough from overeating, from cold or hot drinks. Flatulence and
heartburn. Sour, bitter belchings. Difficult belching of gas. Nausea and vomiting every morning, with
depression of spirits. Nausea and vomiting with much retching. Nausea, better if he can vomit. Wants to
vomit, but cannot. Vomiting of sour mucus, oily, greasy or black substances. Vomiting of greenish matter,
undigested food, blood. Vomiting of bile with thirst, after anger. Motion sickness from riding in cars or
seasickness.
Stool - Stool is incomplete and unsatisfactory. First part of stool soft, last part hard. Scanty stool with
much urging. Black, dark or brown stool. Hard and knotty stool, consisting of little balls. Stool often mixed
with mucus and blood. Black, hard stool, often streaked with blood.
Teeth - Teeth seem too long. Sensation as if tooth were wrenched out. Tearing pain in teeth and jaws, worse
cold drinks, better warmth. Stinging pain in decayed teeth. Pain in hollow tooth. Sharp pain in teeth on drawing
in air or just after eating. Toothache, worse mental exertion, when reading or thinking. Toothache worse
from exercise, better external warmth. Toothache with swollen face. Chattering of teeth. Gums swollen, white,
and bleeding. Gumboils, which seem about to burst.
Temperature - Chilliness alternating with heat. Cold stage predominates. Chills with backache on slightest
motion. Chills on being uncovered, must be covered in every stage of fever. Chill with thirst, and heat without
thirst. Fever with internal chilliness. Fever with anxiety and restlessness. Body burning hot, especially the
face.yet cannot move or uncover without feeling chilly. Warm on uppermost side, on lying down. Dry heat
of the body. Paroxysms in morning. Excessive rigor with blueness of fingernails. Aching in limbs and back,
and gastric symptoms.
Throat - Sensation of roughness, tightness and tension. Stitches into ear. Pharynx constricted. Acute
catarrhal laryngitis. Spasmodic constriction of larynx with suffocating spells. Tickling in throat after waking in
morning. Sore rawness in throat. Catarrhal hoarseness with scraping in throat. Tenacious mucus in upper part
of trachea. Putrid taste in throat on coughing. Dark gray patches on right tonsil. Small ulcers in the throat, pain
worse during empty swallowing. Diphtheria. Elongation and swelling of uvula.
Tongue - First half of tongue clean, posterior covered with deep fur, white, yellow, cracked edges. Tongue
black and dark red, cracked on edges. Tongue red, sore and yellow at base. Needle-like stitches at edges of
tongue. Painful vesicles on tongue. Tongue seems heavy when talking.
Vertigo - Vertigo in morning, on empty stomach, after dinner. Intoxicated feeling, worse morning, mental
exertion, tobacco, alcohol, coffee, open air. Vertigo, brain and other objects turn in circle. Vertigo with black
spell. Vertigo with momentary loss of consciousness. Dizzy and faint in a crowd or where many lights are
burning. Vertigo from night watching and mental overexertion. Vertigo from opium, smell of flowers, gas, etheric
 oils, etc.
Vision - Weakened power of accommodation from overexerting eyes. Diplopia
from muscular asthenopia. Diplopia from paralytic strabismus. Blurred vision from overeating. Dim vision,
can see better on cloudy day. Obscuration of vision in morning. Printed matter is seen with difficulty. Sees
flashes from external canthi towards pupils, like a circle of fire, before headache. Sees streaks like lightning.
Glittering appearance just outside of distinct field of vision. Floating black and grey points.
COMMENTS - Clarke stated, under Brucea antidysenterica, how the bark of the tree was imported into Europe
in mistake for Angustura. The tree from which the ignatia “beans” are obtained is unknown, but it is not doubted
to be a strychnos, the seeds actually contain a larger proportion of strychnia than those of Nux-v.
In poisoning cases, the most marked feature is the spasms and convulsions which cause death by arresting
the respiratory movements. The general effect of the spasms was to cause opisthotonos and throwing the
head back. In some, the body was spasmodically drawn sideways.
Tetanus, differing from traumatic or idiopathic tetanus in that the spasms of the former are less continuous, do
not invariably begin with the muscles of the jaws, but preferably in the lower limbs and are not accompanied
by rise of temperature.
Characteristic spasms. Spasms affect all the muscles, including the esophagus, stomach, intestines, uterus,
bladder, rectum. Intestinal spasms after eating unripe fruit. Tetanic seizures with a drawn facial expression.
Respiratory spasms. Asthmatic states. Asthma, coryza from drafts or air conditioning. A dry, persistent
fatiguing cough that causes headache as if the skull would split. Cough, worse at night, after midnight. Clarke
cured with Nux-v. many cases of bronchitis with copious moist rales and expectoration. Acute flus. Flu with
muscle aches, toxic feeling. Gastric flus with cramps, spasms, irritability and nausea.
High blood pressures, heart attacks, often from severe exhaustion. Hepatitis, cirrhosis of the liver with
irritability.
Kidney conditions, liver weakness. Crave fats (Nit-ac.), sweets, salt, spicy foods, coffee, tobacco, stimulants.
Desires alcoholic drinks, but they aggravate.
Pressure two or three hours after eating (Nux-m. and Kali-bi., have it immediately after). Severe cramps and
spasms in the stomach and colon. Severe peristalsis. Colitis, ulcers, gas and bloating with irritability,
depression, and frustration. Colic with alternating diarrhea with mucus in the stool and constipation with severe
cramps and spasms.
Irritability of the bladder and rectum. Constant urging and desire, very little passed. Tenesmus. Incontinence
of urine or feces. Constipation with ineffectual urge. Alternate constipation and diarrhea. Sudden diarrhea,
drives the patient out of bed. Involuntary diarrhea, can come on after a meal. Straining ceases as soon as the
stool passes. Improvement for a short time after a stool.
Portal stasis. Prolapse of rectum with constipation. Lack of bowel tone. Itching and burning hemorrhoids
(Sulph.), worse from alcohol. Hernias in infants, or from lifting things. Incipient hernia. Inguinal and umbilical
hernias. Clarke saw a case of strangulated hernia resolved by Nux-v. while preparations for an operation were
in progress.
Tendency to faint after diarrhea stools or after vomiting. Fainting from odors in a warm room after eating, after
every labor pain. Epilepsy attacks during stool. Headaches with nondescript achiness, irritability, often
associated with dietary errors.
Hemorrhage. Metrorrhagia, menorrhagia. Uterine bearing down and prolapse, cramps at menstrual periods
and pressure on bladder and rectum. Menses too early and profuse, dark flow, faints easily, irregular, cease
flowing at nighttime. Cramping pains, cause nausea and fainting, twisting, moving about in abdomen, soreness
across pubes, cramps in bladder.
Nash gave a characteristic of the menses of Nux-v., “Menses a few days before the time and rather too copious
or keeping on several days longer with complaints at the onset which remain until it is over.”
Menses return at full moon.
Pregnancy with irritability, hiccough, morning sickness, varicose veins, hemorrhoids. False labor pains.
Irritability with labor pains (Cham.), with nausea or indigestion or vomiting (Sep.). Labor pains are violent and
causes fainting. Lochia scanty offensive. Nipples sore, with a white spot in center. Tensive pains when nursing.
Strong sexual desire in both sexes, even the slightest provocation excites sexual passion. May be impotent
from overuse of drugs or excessive sexual activity.
Keynote over sensitiveness. Morbid sensitiveness. Severe irritability. Languor, great nervous debility (as from
sexual or other excesses). Over stimulation, particularly in sedentary people. Trembling, excitement with
trembling. Locomotor ataxia. Hemiplegia. Paralysis, after a stroke, parts cold, numb, emaciated.
Sleeplessness, from excitement, anger or resentment. Wakes at 3 a.m. and lies awake for hours. Falls asleep
when it is time to rise and feels heavy and unrefreshed. Sleep is unattainable except from a stimulant.
 Symptoms are better after undisturbed sleep, worse when sleep is disturbed.
Chilliness. Cannot get warm in bed at night. Coldness of the whole body with blue hands and skin. Cold, moist
hands with cold tip of nose. Repugnance to cold or cold air. Chilly on least movement, from being uncovered,
must be covered in every stage of fever, chill, heat or sweat.
H. C. Allen noted that in the fever there is great heat, whole body burning hot, face red and hot, yet patient
cannot move or uncover without being chilly.
Boenninghausen’s keynote is “Feels worse in morning, soon after walking, also after mental exertion after
eating and in cold air.” Worse cold, dry weather. Worse from music.
General toxicity, usually from addictions to drugs, stimulants, and strong foods. Bilious affects, ailments due
to high living. Alcoholism. Rage when drunk. Drug withdrawal (with Aven.). Hangovers (Ran-b., Coff.). Toxic
drugged feeling, particularly
in the morning.
Ambitious personality, impatient, irritable. Craves stimulants. Very competitive from a young age, aggressive.
Hyper or over active children, but purposeful (unlike Med.). Robust, energetic, passion behind a quick intellect.
Often from an early sibling comparison (Lyc.).
Career and work oriented, can be workaholics. Not sentimental. Stress and tension lead to over sensitivity,
weakness. Anxious, overreact, never satisfied. Fear of failure, of not being successful. Worry. Suicidal
depression. Homicidal, suicidal impulse, insanity.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Wine, coffee, Aeon., Bell., Camph., Cham., Cocc., Op., Pal., Plat., Stram., Thuj.
(ineffectual desire to pass water). It antidotes: Narcotic, drastic and vegetable remedies. Bad effects of
anomalies on foods, e.g., ginger, nutmeg, pepper and so-called “hot ” medicines, alcohol, Merc, (tremors),
Mez. (neuralgia), ether, Thuj. (urination). Compare: (1) In tetanus, Piero., Verin., Thebin., Cic., Hy-ac., Bell.,
Aeon., Phys., Phyt., Cur., Camph. (2) Cerebrospinal affections, Pic-ac. (3) Fainting in nervous women, Ign.,
Nux-m., Mosch. (4) Gastric troubles, Bism., Ars., Kreos., Lyc., Puls., Carb-v. (Carb., v. often follows Nux- v. in
ill effects of debauchery). (5) Asthma, Zing., Carb-v., Lyc., Nat-s. (6) Paralysis of sphincters, Sep., Bell., Sulph.
(6) Bad temper before and during menses, Cham., Mag-m., Sep. (Lyc., before menses). (7) Wakes 3 a.m. and
cannot get to sleep, Kali-c., Ars., Calc., Sep. (8) Night watching effects, sensitiveness, effects of noise, traveling
by land or sea, umbilical hernia, Cocc. (9) Fear of losing senses, Calc., Lyc., Sulph. (10) Desire to kill love
ones, Hep., Ars. (11) Fainting or faints after every evacuation, Dig., Nux-m. (12) Hemorrhoids, Aesc., Ham.
(13) Leucorrhea staining yellow, Agn., Carb-an., Chel. (14) Impotence from abuse, Agn.. Calc., Sulph. (15)
Stricture of rectum, Nat-m., Op. Compatible after: Carb-v., Ars., Ip., Mag-m., Phos., Sep., Sulph. Compatible
before: Bry., Puls., Sulph. Incompatible: Zinc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

PHARMACY - nux-m. Nux moschata. Nutmeg. Myristicafragrans. Myristica officinalis. Myristica moschata. N.
O. Myristicacee. Tincture of powdered seeds deprived of the Mace. A fresh nut and fresh plant tincture should
be prepared and tested. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Asthma. Backache. Belch- ings. Brain, softening. Catalepsy. Chilblains. Clairaudience.

name: Nyctanthes Arbor Tristis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - nyct. Nyctanthes arbor tristis. Sad tree. Arbortristis. Paghala tree. Sephalika. Harsinghar. Night-
Jasmine of India. N. O. Jasminacee. Verbenaceae. Forests of Central India. Tincture of fresh leaves, collected
March to April. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Chills. Constipation. Fevers, bilious. Fevers, remittent. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Vomiting.
HERBAL - Nyctanthes is a small tree of the Jasmine family, having brilliant, highly fragrant flowers, white and
yellow, whichdonotexpand until evening and which fall off about sunrise. During the day the tree lose all its
brightness and hence is called “The Sad Tree.” “Nyctanthes” means “Night-flowering.”
S. C. Ghose gave an account of the medicinal properties of this plant. He used it extensively in cases of bilious
and remittent fevers, rheumatism and sciatica and the constipation of children.
Nyctanthes is “a bitter tonic and expectorant and a mild purgative.” In the fever there is thirst before and during
chills, and bitter vomiting at close of chill. Not much sweat.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ghose, who made a short proving of it, compared Nyct. with Eup-per. Bilious and obstinate
remittent fevers, sciatica, rheumatism. Constipation of children.
MIND - Anxious and restless. Depression.
Food - Insatiable thirst, before and during chill and fever.
Head - Dull headache.
Kidneys - High-colored urine.
Liver - Tenderness of liver. Stitches in liver region, which is very sensitive to touch.
Mouth - Tongue coated.
Rectum - Constipation. Profuse, bilious stool with nausea.
Stomach - Burning sensation, better cold application. Constant nausea may or may not be present. Bilious
 vomiting occurs every time he takes a drink.

Temperature - Thirst, before and during chill and heat. Bitter vomiting at close of chill. Sweat not generally
marked.
COMMENTS - Dr. Sarat Chandra Ghose of Calcutta, India recorded his observations of clinical experiences
and provings made about the years 1898-1903.
The first case noted a woman at the house of Babu I. C. Chakrabarti, B. A., Head Master. Town School,
Midnapore, was suffering from a complicated attack of intermittent fever. No medicine could give her any relief.
In another case, a boy, aged 7, was suffering from intermittent fever for some time. The fever came on every
evening at 7 p.m. Violent thirst during chill and fever. Bilious vomiting. Constipated bowels. Ghose prescribed
Nyct. tincture in five drop doses thrice daily. The boy was cured within three days.
The third case, a woman, aged 68, was suffering from remittent fever for ten days. Ghose took her under
treatment on the eleventh day.
The son of Babu Sarada Kanta Chatterjee was suffering from a malignant type of ague with great constipation.
He was treated by some allopaths and native Kabirajes for nearly five months, but no perceptible improvement
was wrought by the administration of their remedies. He was eventually placed under Ghose’s treatment.
The son of Mr. M. M. Ray. Deputy Magistrate and Collector of Midnapore, was suffering from remittent fever,
associated with bilious symptoms for five days. On the sixth day the boy was placed under Ghose’s treatment.
The son of Mr. G. C. Dutt, Deputy Magistrate of Midnapore, was suffering from an attack of intermittent fever
for some time. The fever came on every morning at about 7 a.m. Violent thirst was present during all the
stages. Bilious vomiting came on in the hot stage. Constipated bowels. Ghose prescribed Nyct. tincture in
three-drops doses. The boy was all right within three days.
Nyct. proved an excellent remedy for the symptoms and Ghose treated nearly 120
Nyctanthes arbor tristis cases with this medicine alone and an overwhelming majority of them were cured.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

name: Nymphaea Odorata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - nym. Nymphaea odorata. Sweet waterlily. N. O. Nympheacee. Tincture of the root. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Back, pain. Bronchorrhea. Coryza. Diarrhea. Leucorrhea. Throat, sore. Ulcers.
HERBAL - Hale mentioned this emblem of purity and its traditional reputation as a dis- sipater of venereal
desires. Like Nuph., it has early morning looseness of bowels.
HOMEOPATHIC - Nymph, has early morning diarrhea, and backache. Acrid leucorrhea. Offensive ulcers.
Bronchorrhea. Ulcerative sore throat.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Nystatin
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - nyst. Nystatin. Antibiotic drug. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Acne. Blisters. Dermatitis. Hair, disorders. Skin, disorders. Stretch marks.
HOMEOPATHIC - Blistering, burning, dryness of skin. Eruptions resembling acne. Excessive discoloring of
the skin. Skin irritation, itching, peeling, prickly heat. Reddish purple lines on skin. Secondary infections.
Severe inflammation of the skin. Softening of the skin. Stretch marks, stretching or thinning of the skin.
Excessive hair growth, especially on the face. Hair loss, especially on the scalp. Inflammation around the
mouth. Inflammation of hair follicles.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Oak
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oak-b. Oak. Quercus robur. Red female flowers are gathered and put in a bowl of sunlit water
for several hours. The water is strained and prepared as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the
stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks).
This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - The remedy Oak-b. belongs to Bach's group of Despondency and Despair, along with
Crb-a-b„ Will-b, Star- b-b., Sw-ch-b., Elm-b„ Pine-b. and Lar-b. States of stoic perseverance and willpower in
the face of hardship.
 Mental/emotional and physical weariness. Over-work and strength of will may lead to physical strain and undue
stress. Older people may become bent from over-exertion and one-sided activity.
Great determination to not succumb to invalidity. Avoids necessary rest and restful recreation, even though
both may be of vital need. Psychosomatic diseases from the continued rule of willpower over the need for
healthfill diversion and renewal (Cent-b.).
MIND - Self-discipline, seriousness of intention. Tendency to over-work. Loyalty. Focused on completing tasks.
Perseverance in duties, even though strength and vitality may be failing. Unceasing disappointments or lack
of rewards despite efforts made will increase resolve to struggle on with great strength of will and ever rene
wed hope. Inner weariness and lack of motivation.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Ocimum Canum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oci. Ocimum canum. Brazilian alfavaca. Hoary basil. Ocimum incanescens. Ocimum
fluminense. N. O. Labiate. Portuguese. Tincture of fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies. Arthritis. Belching. Breasts, painful. Bubo. Diarrhea. Edema. Gravel,
urinary. Headaches. Herpes. Hiccoughs. Kidney, diseases. Kidney, pain. Kidney, stones. Nausea.
Pyelonephritis. Salpingitis. Urine, abnormal. Vagina, prolapse. Vulvitis.
HERBAL - All the members of the Ocimum genus are aromatic. The Sweet or Common Basil, Ocimum
basilicum, is one of the best known. Mure reported that it is used in Brazil as a specific for diseases of the
kidneys, bladder and urethra.
P. C. Majumdar added that Ocimum sanctum is the sacred tulsi of India and that the Kabirajes use it in diseases
of the liver and bilious remittent fevers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Oci. is useful in diseases of kidneys, uterus, bladder and urethra. Kidney pain with violent
vomiting every fifteen minutes. Wrings one's hands and moans and cries all the time. Kidney colic, especrally
on the right side. Pronounced symptoms of kidney stones.
Uric acid diathesis. Red sand in the urine. Red urine with brick-dust sediment after the attack. The urine may
be saffron color or thick, purulent with an intolerable smell of musk.
Febrile condition, shivering, sweating and with congestive headache. Vomiting, cries tossing about and
wringing hands. Arthritis. Allergies.
Pain in the left testicle. Prolapsed vagina. Vulvarcongestion. Breast congestion. Swelling of inguinal glands
and breasts. Excessive sensitiveness of the breasts and pain on nursing.
MIND - Difficulty concentrating. Confused state. Anxiety.
Abdomen - Abdomen distended, painful on the right side during menses. Glands in the groin swollen. Edema
on the right side of the testes or labia.
Breasts - Constrictive tension in the breasts. Breasts feel full and tense, itching. Neuralgic pains in the breast.
Nipples painful and sensitive to the touch. Congestive pains in the breasts as after nursing. Puerperal mastitis.
Chest - Chest painful on right side. Dry cough in the evening and early morning. Copious sputum.
Constitutions - Allergic constitutions. Psoric constitutions. Neuro-arthritic temperament.
Ears - Boil on the meatus of the right ear. Noise heard painfully in the ears.
Eyes - Blurred vision.
Female - Menses late, short or abundant. Whitish-yellow leucorrhea. Vulvitis. Vulva swollen, darting pain in
labia majora. Vaginal prolapse. Salpingitis.
Food - Lack of appetite. Desire for cold drinks during fever.
Head - Stinging pain in the head. Pain in the head, as if a nail were being driven in, ameliorated by pressure.
Pulsating, throbbing headache. Headaches followed by shivering.
Kidneys - Pyelonephritis. Cramps in kidneys. Kidney colic on the right side with vomiting ever quarter of an
hour with calling out. Restlessness and groaning. Pronounced symptoms of kidney stones, especially of right
side. Stones in the bladder. Tenesmus of the bladder. Sore pain in ureters. Burning pain in the urethra during
urination. Urine abundant, burning.
Male - Pain in the testes. Tenderness, heat and swelling of the left testicle. Increase, then diminution of sexual
desire. Absence of erection.
Modalities - Better in a room, in rainy, humid weather. Worse in the morning, from cold, right side.
Mouth - Lips dry, face red. Tongue furred, yellow, yellowish-white with a brown spot in the center. Toothache
on the right, ame
liorated by pressing the teeth together. Nose - Nasal congestion.
Rectum - Constipation with dry, hard, evil-smelling, yellow or greenish stools. Diarrhea several times a day.
 Skin - Herpes. Eczematous eruptions. Stomach - Belching, hiccoughs. Nausea.
Temperature - Shivers, fever and lack of thirst. Profuse sweating with strong odor. Fever of the tertian or
quartan type.
Urine - High acidity, formation of spike crystals of uric acid. Brick-dust red or yellow sediment. Red sand in
saffron colored urine. \Jrinefoul-smelling with odor of musk. Turbid, thick, purulent, bloody urine. Urinary
complaints with proteinuria. Scanty urine, which aggravates.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising and on sitting down.
COMMENTS - Majumdar related the case of a medical man, 45. Majumdar was sent for at 4 a.m. one morning
and found the patient in great agony, pain in upper part of region of right kidney, extending downwards and
forwards to pubes.
Constant vomiting, bilious, acid tossing about without any relief. After Calc., Lyc., Sep., Sars. and Berb. had
been given in vain, Oci. 3x gave immediate relief and no other remedy was required.
Majumdar also noted the case of a man, 50, with excruciating pain in his left kidney, for which he had received
opium under allopathic treatment without relief. Majumdar saw the patient on the sixth day of the attack. The
suffering was extreme, vomiting of bile, constant nausea, bowels constipated.
Oci. 3x, one drop every three hours, speedily gave relief, and two days later two small uric acid stones were
passed. There was no recurrence.
Clarke published two cases. The first concerned a man, 27, who was seized with violent pains of a leaden
character in the right side of the abdomen, every three or four weeks. The pains commenced in morning, lasted
twelve to fifteen hours. For four hours from commencement of attack the pain steadily increased, culminating
in vomiting, first of sour fluid, then slime, then
a fluid like coffee.
After the vomiting there was some relief of pain. Urine contained no sediment. The attacks had lasted seven
years. At first they began in the evening. There was a history of epilepsy in the family, and as a child the patient
had three fits.
Oci. 200c, one dose, was given and there were no more attacks for about two years. On their recurrence Oci.
failed to control them, but Dios, tincture succeeded.
In the second case, a woman, 24, had severe pain in her right flank shooting around to her back. Frequent
urination, sometimes depositing clots. Terebe. 3c gave some relief, but it was not permanent. Oci. 200c, a few
globules in water, a teaspoonful every two days, rapidly relieved the symptoms and cleared up the case.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In kidney colic, Berb., Dios., Coloc., Calc., Lyc. (2) Berb.. Hedeo., Lyc., Urt-u. (3)
Pareir., Coloc., Tab. (4) In painful breasts, Lac-c., Bor. (5) Crot-h., Phel. (6) Prolapsed vagina, Staph. Followed
well by: Dios.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian. Phatak.

name: Ocimum Sanctum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-oci-s. Ocimum sanctum. Holy Basil. Tulsi. N. O. Labiate. Brazil. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphthae. Asthma. Bites. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Catarrh. Colds. Constipation. Cough.
Delirium. Diarrhea. Headache. Hiccoughs. Influenza. Intermittent fevers. Leucorrhea. Memory, weak.
Ophthalmia. Ozaena. Pneumonia. Ringworm. Ulcers. Urethritis.
HERBAL - Ayurvedic physicians like Cha- raka, Harita, Chakradatta, Bangasena, and others have found
Ocimum sanctum very efficacious in cough, cold, catarrh, nose affections, ozaena, scorpion bites, remittent
and intermittent fevers and constipation.
The medicated oil is used as drops, in the ears in earache and purulent discharges, and into the nose in
ozaena. The leaves, with lime juice, are rubbed over ringworm. The seeds are mucilaginous and used as a
diuretic in scanty urine and cough. The leaves are expectorant, and given, sweetened with honey, in chronic
cough, especially in children.
The expressed juice of the herb has traditionally been administered to children who are attacked with catarrh,
cough with fever and constipation, with very gratifying and beneficial results.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ocimum canum is a species of this shrub which grows abundantly in Brazil. Dr. Mure, who
proved and introduced it, noted that it is largely used in Brazil “as a specific for diseases of the kidneys,
bladder, and urethra.” He gave a short list of nineteen symptoms which are partly clinical and partly
pathogenetic.
Dr. Mure's experience was several times verified by several noted homeopaths. Drs. Pramada Prasanna
Biswas of Pabna, Bengal, N. Sinha and N. C. Ghosh have made provings of this drug.
 MIND - Memory weak. Forgetfulness. Mistakes in talking. Difficulty concentrating. Prostration and
drowsiness. Patient falls asleep while answering questions. Child is peevish and cries, does not like to lie in
bed. Irregular delirium, disturbed.
Abdomen - Abdomen distended. Heaviness in abdomen. Griping pain in the abdomen. Pain is felt over the
region of liver and spleen. Pain in the right iliac region. Hepatic pain. Gurgling sound can be felt on pressure.
Chest - Pains are felt on both sides of the chest, worse while coughing or sneezing. Pleuritic pains in the chest.
Pain is felt in the middle of sternum. Patient cannot lie quiet in bed.
Ears - Watery secretion from the ear. Offensive pus from the ears. Ears painful due to nasal catarrh. Hot
flushes come out from the ears. Noises in the ears, loud sound appears to be very painful. Shortness of
hearing.
Eyes - Eyes red. Pain in the eyes, lachrymation, eye complaints due to nasal catarrh. Ophthalmia. Foggy
vision. Mist before eyes, especially when fixing them on something.
Face - Face red or pale with reddish hue. Flushed and hot.
Female - Menses too late. Metrorrhagia. Leucorrhea alternating with bloody discharge. Leucorrhea offensive,
profuse, white, yellow. Metritis after childbirth. Profuse bloody discharges after delivery. Lochia offensive,
profuse, fetid, lasts for a long period. Sexual desire diminished or increased.
Head - Headache as from a nail. Heavy, throbbing pain as if thousand nails were being driven into it, relieved
by pressure. Giddiness of head, worse while walking, likes to keep quiet, relieved by wrapping up the head.
Heat on the vertex, relieved by pouring cold water on the head or by fanning.
Kidneys - Kidney colic. Urethritis. Desire to urinate off and on. Burning in the urethra while urinating. Yellow
like saffron, urine. Discharge of mucus with urine. Involuntary urination of the children.
Limbs - Aching pains, better from pressure.
Lungs - Asthmatic attack, wheezing and rattling sound felt in the chest. Asthma better from bending head
forward, rocking. Asthma of infants and children. Croupy cough. Hacking cough, profuse expectoration.
Male - Troublesome erections. Sexual desire increased or decreased. Impotency.
Mouth - Lips bright red. Lips dry and black as if burnt. Watery salivation or spitting from the mouth. Putrid and
bitter taste in mouth. Ulcer, aphthae in mouth. Ulcer in mouth and tongue of children. The tongue is bright red
or its edges and sides are red and the middle portion is deeply coated. Toothache, better pressing the gums
together, warmth, pressure.
Nose - Nasal obstruction. Nasal catarrh associated with frequent sneezing, white or yellow secretions. Coryza.
Watery discharge from the nose. Nostrils ulcer
ated. Nosebleeds.
Perspiration - Offensive sweats.
Rectum - Constipation. Incomplete stools. Diarrhea with high fever. Diarrhea during rainy season and
autumn. Stools liquid, copious, watery, very offensive. Yellowish or greenish liquid stools. Mucus or bloody or
streaked with blood. Involuntary stools during high fever.
Skin - Skin disease.
Stomach - Want of appetite. Thirstlessness during chill. Eructations, Hiccough.
Temperature - Chills and fever. Influenza. Remittent and intermittent fevers. Bilious, continued fever. Quartan
fever, tertian fevers. Typhus, typhoid fever.
Throat - Pain in the throat while walking or during cough. Pain and difficulty in swallowing. Redness, ulceration
of throat. Glairy phlegm. Enlargement of tonsils. Hoarseness. Voice gets changed.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising.
COMMENTS - Oci-s. has an assured place in the treatment of influenza and in common nasal catarrh.
Remittent fever associated with cough, cold or diarrhea, pneumonia, broncho-pneumonia, bronchitis and
asthma.
Typhoid fever or fever associated with delirium, comatose condition, prostration, and falls into slumber or
drowsiness while answering questions (Bapt.). Fever in influenza, associated with cough, acute pains in the
body, bone pains, soreness of the muscles, and terrible headache (Eup-per.).
Fevers associated with cough, cold and diarrhea, especially in children. Fevers prevalent in rainy season,
winter or spring. Intermittent fever. Fever with thirst or absence of thirst.
Fever comes on in the afternoon with extreme chilliness, with shivering. Chilliness, even when exposed to the
sun. Hands and the feet become cold and do not become warm easily. Numbness and tingling in hands and
feet.
Extreme heat and flushes of heat felt over the face and eyes during hot stage. Burning sensation in the palms
of hands and soles of feet, relieved by cold breeze or placing cold water on the head.
Sweat with heat. Heat, sweat, and chilliness may appear alternately. Sweat, delirium, drowsiness or comatose
 condition.
Remittent fevers of children, fever during dentition period, diarrhea and worm affections (Cina.).
Wormcomplaints of children, fretful and peevish, start from sleep, and do not allow the physician to examine
them. The children become awfully peevish, always cry, become quiet while they are being carried (Cham.).
Aching pains, in the feet and legs. Pains are felt all over the body. Offensive and filthy odor. Putrefaction.
Contagious and infectious diseases caused by bacteria or bacilli.
Terrible headache. Headache due to congestion, common cold, influenza or fever. Headache relieved by
application of cold water on the head or by fanning the head. Better from keeping quiet or wrapping the head
with a cloth, worse while walking or by motion.
Face is flushed and hot. lips are red and parched, eyes are drowsy. Pain in the throat, felt while swallowing,
coughing or sneezing. Redness inside the throat, both tonsils are enlarged.
Offensive smell comes out of the mouth, offensive salivation. Tongue is red or reddish and shining at the edges
with yellow or brown coating in the middle (Bapt.). Aphthae. Putrid ulcer in the mouth and teeth. Toothache,
with terrible pains, worse at night, from touch or cold.
Eyes congested, red, with lachrymation, especially in cases of the common cold. Watery discharges and sticky
discharges. Ophthalmia, ophthalmia neonatorum. Earache and purulent discharges from the ear. Shortness
of hearing.
Difficult respiration. Asthma, the patient cannot lie on the back. Bends forward and supports the head with the
hands, the elbows resting on the knees or leans forward and puts the head on the hands lain flat on such
support (Aral., Lob., Blatta.). Asthma of children.
Gastric and intestinal catarrh, with inflammation of the intestinal mucous membrane,
fever and diarrhea. Pain in the region of liver and spleen. Abdomen distended, distension does not abate in
spite of stools passed.
After gurgling in the stomach, copious watery and offensive stools appear. Diarrhea with fever and cold, cough,
pneumonia, broncho-pneumonia and bronchitis. Involuntary stools.
Irregular, long lasting menses. Leucorrhea. Uterine complications after delivery. Terribly offensive lochia, of
unnatural color, long lasting. Discharge mixed with mucus, is pus-like and like washing of fish.
Ocimum sanctum is supposed to drive away mosquitoes; it may prevent malarial fevers if cultivated near a
house.
REFERENCES Ghose.

name: Oenanthe Crocata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oena. Oenanthe crocata. Water dropwort. Hemlock drop-wort. N. O. Umbel- liferae. Marshy
places. Tincture of fresh root at time of flowering. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amenorrhea. Breast, pain. Coma. Convulsions. Cough. Delirium tremens.
Diaphragm, spasm. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Gastroenteritis. Hysterical, epilepsy. Ichthyosis.
Insanity. Leprosy. Menstrual, convulsions. Nausea. Priapism. Puerperal, convulsions. Sciatica. Speech, lost.
Status, epilepticus. Stomatitis. Strokes. Tetanus. Tongue, swollen. Tongue, ulcerated. Tympanites. Vertigo.
Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Oenanthe crocata is one of the most poisonous of the Umbelliferae, and many accidents
have occurred from the use of the root in mistake for parsnips and of the leaves in salads and soups. These
have fumishedmany of the symptoms of the pathogenesis.
Epileptic convulsions, worse during menstruation and pregnancy. Epilepsy, utters a loud cry before
falling backward. Status epilepticus. Face swollen, convulsive twitching of facial muscles, foaming at mouth,
lockjaw. Cold as if dead during convulsions, noise in throat as if being choked. Burning heat. Numbness. Legs
stretches straight out.
Skin affections, especially leprosy and ichthyosis. Rosy red blotches on face and chest, arms, abdomen.
Profuse, offensive sweat. Burning in throat and stomach, nausea and vomiting. Obstinate vomiting for days,
not relieved by anything.
MIND - Epileptic condition at periods when menses are due, in amenorrhea. Epileptic insanity. Coma after
convulsions. Sudden and complete loss of consciousness. Insanity, hallucinations. Delirium tremens. Furious
delirium. Tendency to cry over little things. Averse to be questioned.
Abdomen - Great tenderness, slightest touch on any part of abdomen causes great pain. Distended with colic
pains. Gastroenteritis with violent pain and vomiting. Tympanites with the convulsions.
Back - Pain along spinal column. Intense action of dorsal and lumbar muscles, opisthotonos.
Breasts - Swollen breasts. Pain in breast. Nipples painful to least contact.
 Causations - Menstrual disturbances. Injuries.
Chest - Pain in right side under the ribs. Chest firmly fixed. Pleuritic exudation. Lungs hyperemic, hepatized in
spots.
Eyes - Sunken, full and projecting, inflamed. Redness. Pupils first contracted, then dilated. Eyes turned upward
and inward, firmly fixed. Vision disturbed, obscured.
Face - Countenance livid, rose-colored spots on face. Lips blue. Eyes fixed, pupils dilated. Rapid, convulsive
twitching of facial muscles. Trismus, foaming at mouth, locked jaws. Risus sardonicus.
Food - Total loss of appetite with debility. Thirst, craves cold drinks, evening. Cannot bear to drink anything
hot.
Head - Hyperemia of brain, extravasation and serous exudation. Pains all over head, dizzy. Headache and
giddiness. Violent pain in head. Apoplectic conditions. Suddenly falls down backward. Hair fell off.
Heart - Pain in region of heart. Pulse is small, feeble, irregular and scarcely perceptible, accelerated before
the fit.
Kidneys - Painful urination. Urine copious, dark, turbid, reddish, with thick yellow
sediment.
Limbs - Numbness and feebleness of limbs. Pain along crural and sciatic nerves, commencing in back. Cold
hands and feet. Numbness of hand and foot. Cramps in calves. Arms flexed at elbow in a right angle. Hands
clenched during tetanus. Convulsions, opisthotonos.
Lungs - Spasms of the diaphragm. Heavy, spasmodic, stertorous breathing. Tickling cough with rattling in the
lower part of the chest. Cough, worse at night, excited by tickling at top of throat. Rattling in the chest, sputa
thick, heavy, white and yellow. Thick, frothy expectoration, reddish, bloody, white.
Male - Priapism.
Modalities - Worse from water, injury, sexual and menstrual disturbances. Pressure aggravates pain in throat,
but ameliorates deep pain in thorax. Swallowing causes soreness of throat.
Mouth - Mouth dry and parched. Foaming at mouth, bloody mucus. Excoriation inflammation, blisters.
Convulsive movement of teeth. Loss of speech.
Nose - Nosebleeds.
Rectum - Involuntary stool, diarrhea.
Sensations - As if a bug creeping under the skin about the waist, worse touch of clothes.
Skin - Rose colored rash on face, chest, arms and abdomen. Loss of nails and hair.
Sleep - Much yawning. Drowsy. In a deep sleep, snoring loudly and moaning. Roused with difficulty.
Stomach - Tender stomach. Burning heat in stomach. Esophagitis. Distressing hiccough. Nausea, better if
vomiting occurs. Vomit is clear water liquid, blood. Vomiting and diarrhea.
Temperature - Extreme coldness, loss of animal heat. Deadly cold and pale. Face and limbs cold and blue.
Burning heat that mounted to head. Slight fever with pain at pit of stomach. Profuse, offensive sweat,
accompanies symptoms.
Throat - Burning and constriction in larynx. Pharyngitis. Violent constriction and burning in the throat. Pressure
on throat gives pain, sore when swallowing. Power of swallowing lost.
Tongue - Tongue sore, swollen and protruded. Tongue slightly furred, raw at tip, ulcerated at edges. Tongue
clean, moist, trembling. Tongue half bitten through.
Vertigo - Vertigo with falling. Vertigo with nausea, vomiting, syncope and convulsions.
COMMENTS - Oena. is a valuable con vulsive remedy, useful in epileptiform, puerperal and uremia
convulsions. Hormonal epilepsy, since or during pregnancy, in childbirth, abortion, miscarriage, menstrual
period, amenorrhea, and menopause. Epileptic symptoms since birth control pills. Epilepsy after vaccinations.
Epilepsy after errors in diet.
Severe, violent epileptic attacks. Sudden attacks (Bell.). Grand mal, petit mal, and particularly statusepilepticus
attacks. Risus sardonicus, a fixed smile. Feeling of dread and anxiety before attacks. Can hear bells ringing
before. Followed by deep sleep or coma. Vomiting after epilepsy.
Vertigo during the menstrual period. Toxemia during pregnancy with convulsions and protein in the urine. All
symptoms are worse from water and drinking.
D. A. Baldwin of Englewood, N. J., entirely controlled the convulsions in a young man of 16 with Oena. Dr. Ord
reported a case of petit mal cured with Oean. 3x. In a South American homeopathic journal a Dr. Rappaz
reported the cure of a case of three years' standing with increasing seizures with the remedy in doses ranging
from the 6c to 12c.
Henderson reported the cure of an epilepsy case of 9 years standing, where the patient was almost idiotic, the
convulsions were relieved and the mental condition was greatly relieved and improved. In two other cases
equally satisfactory results were had.
 S. H. Talcott, in the report of the Middletown Asylum. 1893, noted that Oena. possesses a marked power in
epilepsy. He stated that it makes the attacks less frequent, less violent and improves the mental state of the
patient. Talcott prescribed it in the tincture, 1 to 6 drops daily.
F. H. Fisk reported the cure of a case that had lasted two years with the tincture. This patient was having 6 to
10 attacks daily during the last month before Fisk took the case.
Dr. Garrison of Easton, Penn, reported a case of reflex uterine of hystero-epilepsy in which the Oena. 2x acted
promptly. J. S. Cooper of Chillicothe, Ohio, reported the cure of a case of 25 years standing with Oena. 4x.
J. Ritchie Horner reported that the Oena. 3x greatly modified the attacks in a woman who had the disease over
20 years and who, for the two months previous, had a convulsion daily.
W. A. Dunn reported a cure of a young woman of 16 who had been epileptic for 7 years, having as many as 4
or 5 attacks during a night. The remedy caused these attacks to disappear entirely. The girl commenced
menstruating at age 12, so the establishment of the menses had nothing to do with the cure.
Charles A. Wilson of San Antonio, Texas, reported a number of cases cured with Oean. 3x, and the same
potency greatly lessened the number of seizures in others. Dr. Purdon of the University of Dublin, related a
case of epilepsy cured with this remedy in 1 to 6 drop doses several times a day.
F.   E. Howard, in a case that had 3 or 4 attacks a week, gave 5 drops of the tincture every two hours, which
caused violent pains in the head, but complete recovery followed on reducing the dose.
McClellan of New Jersey told of a case of his in which a young woman, 19, of a very healthy family, who had
never menstruated and had become almost idiotic in consequence. At the periods when the menses should
have come on there were epileptiform seizures of minor intensity. The state of mind was such that after taking
the best advice in Paris and the States without avail, the patient was about to be put away.
Oean. was given and the next period passed without any epileptic symptoms. But there was no sign of the
flow. Bell, was given and at the next period, the flow came on and the patient's mind was entirely restored.
J. S. Cooper related the case of a clergyman in attendance on one of the Federal generals at the battle of
Gettysburg, who was wounded in the forehead by a fragment of shell, taken prisoner and kept in prison twenty
months.
On his release he was quite a wreck and soon began to have light epileptic seizures, which gradually got
worse. When seen by J. S. Cooper, twenty-five years later, he was having four or five fits a day, could write
his name and at time would take to his heels and run four or five miles into the country before he could be
caught.
Oean. 4c, five drops every four hours, was prescribed. After the first dose he had a very bad fit. The dose was
then diminished. He began to improve and in less than a year was in perfect health. Oean., was not taken
continuously, but when he “felt nervous” he would take a few doses.
F. H. Fish cured a girl, 16, sanguine, well grown, who at eight began to have fits of absentmindedness at
irregular intervals. At 12, menstruation commenced; at 14, epileptic seizures occurred, having no relation to
the menstrual periods. The fits were so severe that sixty to one hundred grains of potassium bromide were
required to keep them under control.
Oean. tincture was given, five drops in six ounces of water, a teaspoonful every three hours, and later less
often. She had not another spasm, lost her absentmindedness and became cheerful and active.
W. K. Fowler reported a case of a teamster, 60, who had gotten into a fight nineteen years before from which
he had three ribs broken and was struck in stomach with the butt of a gun.
Two weeks later, he had pneumonia on the injured side, and after that, epileptic seizures. Before the attacks
he had a pain in the stomach going through to the spine and pain in the second cervical vertebra. Attacks were
induced by worry and by becoming very tired. He had severe attacks when the day's work was finished.
Oean. was given on discs, four discs every three hours for a month. After this there was only one slight attack
after a hard day's
work during the four months he was under observation.
Several cured cases of epilepsy have been reported in which Oena. alternated with Sil. or some other drug,
but they need not be given as it was unclear which remedy cured.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cic., Kali-br. (2) Phel., Con. (3) In epilepsy, Bufo. (4) In priapism, Pic-ac.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Oenothera Biennis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oeno. Oenothera biennis. Large evening primrose. Tree primrose. N. O. Onagracee. North
America. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cholera infantum. Diarrhea. Hydrocephalous. Nervous exhaustion. Paralysis.
 HOMEOPATHIC - T. Riker Nuted recorded a proving on a woman who took Oeno. twice, the first, a
teaspoonful, the second, 30 drops of the liquid extract for the relief of a wearisome feeling of mental and
physical oppression. On each occasion, notably the first, distinct poisoning symptoms were developed.
General paralysis of mental and bodily forces, with copious and easy evacuations of bowels and bladder,
followed by relief of the general symptoms. General numbness, general warm sweat with urgent desire to
urinate, better after evacuation of bowels and bladder. Effortless diarrhea.
Farrington gave the indication exhausting, watery diarrhea without effort with nervous exhaustion, even
incipient hydrocephalous. Hurd cured a man, 65, who had “severe pains in his stomach after meals for over
two years” with 25 drop doses of the tincture.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In diarrhea, Ip., Gnaph., Nuphar. (2) In better from copious urination, Ign., Gels.
(3) In better after stool, Bry., Colch., Coloc., Crot., Oxyt., Rhus-t., Spig., Sulph. (4) Paralytic symptoms, Gels.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Oleander
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - olnd. Oleander. Rose laurel. Nerium oleander. N. O. Apocynaceae. South Europe, North Africa,
West Asia. Thrives best in moist ground. Tincture of the leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Brain, disorders. Eczema. Fainting. Headaches. Hyperesthesia. Lienteria. Memory, weakened.
Numbness. Nursing, disorders. Palpitations. Paralysis. Perichondritis. Rheumatism. Scalp, eruptions. Spasms.
Spine, disorders. Strabismus. Tongue, coated. Vertigo.
HERBAL - In the Cap de Verde Islands, the petals of oleander blossoms are used with dried orange-peel in
all kinds of fevers to promote perspiration and drive out the rash.
HOMEOPATHIC - Olnd., which is one of the remedies proved by Hahnemann, has been recognized as a
powerful poison from antiquity. In animals poisoned by it. the heart becomes paralyzed, first the auricles, then
the entire heart.
Goullon referred to poisoning cases in which “anguish inflammation of the stomach, diarrhea, swoons,” and
even death had occurred. “Palpitations of the heart, anxiety insomnia and unconsciousness,” were observed
by Petrus de Alvano, and Morgagni noted “vomiting, thirst, slumbering, speechlessness and death.” Goullon
also quoted instances of suffering from exhalations of the flowers and even from the plants when not in flower.
Marked action on the skin, heart and nervous system. Paralytic conditions with cramp like contractions of upper
limbs. Hemiplegia. Paralytic rigidity. Paresis after infantile paralysis.
General crampings. Numbness. Sopor. Weakness with trembling in nursing women. Sense of vibrations.
Difficult articulation, or unable to speak. Emptiness in stomach and chest after eating, betterbrandy. Involuntary
discharges.
MIND - Memory weak, slow perception. Morose. Peevish. Sadness with lack of confidence and power.
Melancholy with obstinate constipation.
Abdomen - Borborygmus with profuse, fetid flatus. Gnawing around navel.
Chest - Oppression as from a weight, asthmatic when lying down. Obtuse stitches in chest.
Eyes - Sensation as if eyes were drawn back into the head. Lachrymation, when reading. Double vision.
Can see objects only when looking at them sideways.
Face - Pale, sunken, with blue rings around eyes (Ph-ac.). Numb upper lip. Lowerjaw trembles when yawning.
Female - Tremors after nursi ng, so weak she can scarcely walk across the room.
Food - Desires cold water. Aversion to cheese.
Head - Numb feeling. Dull, unable to think. Indolence. Pain in brain, as if head would burst. Headache better
by looking crossways, sideways or squinting. Corrosive itching on forehead and edge of hair, worse heat.
Eruption on scalp. Humid, fetid spots behind ears (Graph., Petr.) and occiput, with red, rough, herpetic spots
in front.
Heart - Palpitations with weakness and empty feeling in chest, better brandy. Pains on stooping.
Kidneys - Involuntary urination.
Limbs - Limbs stiff and cold. Crampy contraction of upper limbs in paralysis. Stiffness of joints. Weakness of
lower limbs. Painless paralysis. Paralysis of legs and feet. Trembling knees when standing. Edema. Swelling,
burning stiffness of fingers. Veins on hands swollen. Constant cold feet.
Lungs - Dyspnea.
Modalities - Better from looking sideways, brandy. Squinting helps headache. Worse in open air, draft,
undressing after nursing. Worse rubbing, scratching, friction of clothes. Worse rest, looking sideways. Rising
up aggravates headache, vertigo. Stooping causes pain over heart.
Mouth - Toothache only when masticating. Tongue numb. Loss of speech.
 Rectum - Ineffectual urging. Burning pain in anus. Passes food undigested in the morning. Stools, pass
when emitting flatus, thin involuntary.
Sensations - Peculiar sensations suggestive of paralysis. Numb or painless paralyzed feeling as if inner parts
were distended. Buzzing and humming. Pulsations in outer parts. Gnawing, itching, biting or pungent pain after
scratching. Numbness of skin or itching numbness.
Skin - Very sensitive skin, slightest friction causes soreness and chapping. Nocturnal burning. Violent
itching eruption, bleeding, oozing, want of perspiration. Itching, especially of scalp, which is sensitive.
Itching, scurfy pimples, herpes, sensitive and numb. Eruptions with itching, biting as of lice. Skin numb.
Sleep - Sopor. Yawning with trembling of lower jaw.
Stomach - Canine hunger with hurried eating without appetite. Thirst. Empty feeling even after eating, better
brandy. Extreme debility of digestive power. Throbbing in pit. Empty belching. Vomiting of food, greenish water.
Temperature - Heat from mental exertion.
Throat - As if a cool wind blowing on throat (left).
Vertigo - Vertigo for a long time before paralysis. Vertigo, worse looking fixedly at an object or looking down,
turning to either side in bed with diplopia.
COMMENTS - A young man, 18, fell sick, had attacks of vertigo, suffered from great weakness of the muscles,
headache better in evening, worse every morning after waking, which was a difficult process.
He had a pale face, white-coated tongue, slow pulse. On leaving for change of air he soon got quite well, but
ill again as soon as he returned. Some oleanders in his bedroom were then suspected by his doctor, and on
their removal all the trouble vanished.
The doctor recalled that when he was a student he had some oleanders before his windows and in autumn,
when the nights were cold, he took them into his bedroom. On waking in the morning, he had a heavy
head and sensation of weariness, could only leave his bed by great exertion.
As soon as be put his foot to the ground, he was seized with vertigo and reeled. Having traced this to the
oleanders, he purposely repeated the experiment, always with the same result.
Weak memory and slow perception. Pres- sive and stupefying headache. Pressure as if a hundredweight were
pressing brain forward and as if everything would come out at forehead. Headaches better by looking cross-
eyed or looking sideways.
Cloudiness of vision, worse by looking sideways. Momentary loss of sight. Eyes distorted. Strabismus.
Functional paralysis. The left side is most affected, violent contraction of muscles, worse left side. Numbness
of upper and lower limbs.
Digestion is paralyzed, the food passes completely undigested. Gastro-enteritis. Involuntary evacuation of
feces and urine. Infants soil their diapers every time they pass flatus. “Trembling after nursing” in nursing
women.
The skin is very sensitive and easily chafed and chapped. Olean, is in the front rank of remedies affecting the
scalp, more particularly the back part of the scalp or commencing there.
Clarke confirmed the symptoms “desquamation of the epidermis of the scalp,” and “violent gnawing itching on
the scalp, as from lice after scratching, a smarting as if scratched raw.”
Cooper reported a case of a schoolboy whose head was very sore and irritable, covered with crusts, sore to
the touch. Glands in his neck were swollen and sore to the touch. Olean, was given, two drops in a powder at
bedtime on November 14th.
On November 27th an aggravation was reported and the eruption had spread from the head to the back. From
this time rapid improvement set in. Cooper noted that a single dose of the tincture may give the best possible
results in such cases.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. - acute effects, Sulph. - the chronic effects. Compare: (1) Con., Nat-
m., Rhus-t„ Caust., Lath. (2) Oleander contains Oleandrin and also Nerein which is said to be closely related,
if not identical with Digitalin. (3) In irritability, Staph., Hyos., Nux-v. (4) In fits of passion followed by
quickrepentance,Croc. (5)disordersofnursing women, Carb-an. (7) Inlienteria, Ferr., Ars. has diarrhea from
chilling stomach indigestion of cold things, stool yellow with stool great pain, burning, worse after midnight,
great thirst. (8) Arg-n. - bowels act as soon as patient drinks. (9) Chin. - watery stool containing undigested
food, very debilitating, stools may escape involuntarily after a meal, caused or worse by eating fruits. (10) Apis,
Phos. and Ph-ac. - wide-open anus. Compatible: Con., Lyc., Nat-m., Puls., Rhus-t., Sep., Spig.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
