name: Oleum Animale
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ol-an. Oleum animale. Dippel's animal oil. Aethereum dippeli. Oleum cornu cervi. Bone-
 naphtha. Dilutions in alcohol. This volatile oil is prepared by Dippel first by distillation of stags' horn. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Breast, disorders. Cancer. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Facial, paralysis. Faint.
Gonorrhea. Headaches. Migraines. Neurasthenia. Polyuria. Prostate disorders. Spermatic cord, neuralgia.
Testes, neuralgia. Testes, retraction.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ol-an. is an oil obtained from the preparation of bone-black and further distilled and rectified
for medicinal use. It was discovered in 1711 by Johann Conrad Dippel, the alchemist, who was the discoverer
of Prussian blue.
Dippel obtained it in the first instance by a distillation of stags' horns, the deciduous horns of the stag partaking
more of the nature of bone than the permanent horns of cattle. This lead to the name Oleum cornu cervi, with
which the Ol-an. is at present prepared is considered identical.
Sircar noted that though it is not the panacea which Dippel imagined it to be when he discovered it, Ol-an. in
a very powerful medicinal substance and since it has been well proved by Nenning, Schreter and Trinks, it has
a definite place in the Homeopathic Materia Medica.
Grimmer indicated it in cases of breast cancer with burning or sticking and pressure radiating in all directions,
relieved by rubbing and in the open air. A uterine tumor cured with several doses of Ol-an. 1000c potency
given at long intervals shows its relationship to new growths.
Pain in spots. Stitches, burning pains, as with red hot needles. “Pulled upward’’ and “from behind forward”
pains in malar bones, testicles, breasts. Flesh feels torn from bones. Affected part feels sore. Symptoms
appear here and there or in single parts.
Affects the nerves, especially pneumogas- tric nerve, digestive organs. Neurasthenia. Migraine, neuralgia of
spermatic cord. Tremulous weakness of hands, knees, feet etc. Shuffling gait.
Icy coldness from tips of teeth in throat, stomach etc. Chilliness (and coryza) are worse in a warm room and
better in open air. Sensation as if stomach were full of churning water. Urinous odor with belch- ings, leucorrhea
etc.
MIND - Ill-tempered. Nervous irritability. Sad introverted, absorbed in self, speaks in whispers. Indolent,
inclined to sit, taciturn. Vanishing thoughts. Faintness from gastric origin.
Abdomen - Flatulence and rumbling.
Bruised pain in abdomen after stool.
Back - Cracking in cervical vertebrae on raising the head. Aching in right scapula, better pressure. Sprained
feeling in sacrum. Unsteady gait.
Breasts - Stitches in breast from behind forward.
Causations - Ill effects of suppressions, especially of foot sweat.
Chest - Stitches at clavicle. Chest feels constricted. Oppression.
Eyes - Smarting in eyes, misty vision. Lachrymation when eating. Short-sighted. Glistening bodies before the
eyes. Twitching of lids (Agar.). A skin seems to over-
hang the eyes.
Face - Cramp-like pains. Feels drawn. White of an egg seems dried on lips. Twitching of lips. Malar bone
feelspulled upward. Swelling beneath right lower jaw. Toothache, better from pressing teeth together.
Female - Stitches in breast from behind forwards. Sore breasts before menses, outward stitches in nipples in
scirrhus. Menses, early, scanty, black flow. Urinous leucorrhea.
Food - Drinking cold water causes pressure in stomach, worse from hot drinks. Desires bread. Worse eating
(sweat, lachrymation, headache). Especially worse after dinner.
Head - Migraine with polyuria. Pain in spots. Tearing pain with sadness and irritability, worse after dinner,
relieved by rubbing. Itching, burning vesicles, better friction. Malar bones feel pulled forcibly upward.
Heart - Anxious palpitations. Pulse slow.
Kidneys - Polyuria. Frequent and urgent want to urinate with tenesmus and scanty emission. Small stream
of urine. Profuse, pale urine of fish brine odor, worse hysteria, migraine. Greenish urine. Itching in urethra.
Limbs - Sprained feeling in small of back. Cracking of vertebrae on raising head (Aloe, Nat-c., Thuj.).
Rheumatic pain in shoulders. Restlessness. Fish-brine odor of sweat of heels.
Lungs - Asthma from suppressed footsweat.
Male - Desire increased, ejaculation too soon. Pain along spermatic cord to testicles. Testicles feel seized
and pulled forcibly upward, worse right. Pressure in the perineum. Prostate hypertrophy. Seminal losses,
on straining at stool.
Modalities - Better from rubbing, pressure. Better stretching, changing position. Better in open air. Better
eructation. Worse from cold. Worse in warm room, hot drinks. Worse eating. Worse suppressions, noise.
Worse from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m. Worse before, during and commencement of menses.
 Mouth - Bites cheek while eating (Caust.). Snow-white cottony saliva. Greasy feeling in mouth. Tongue sore
as if scalded. Toothache, better pressing teeth together with sensation of coldness coming out from tips.
Nose - Watery, excoriating discharge, worse in open air.
Rectum - Ineffectual urging to stool, with burning in anus.
Sensations - Sensation in scalp as if skin had been cut and reunited. As if blood were rushing to head to
occiput on entering a warm room. As if red-hot needles in chest. As if testicles were seized and pulled forcibly
upward. As if thumb (and toe) would ulcerate.
Skin - Excoriation in bends of joints.
Stomach - Sensations as if water were in stomach, of coldness, constriction, and burning, better belchings.
Urinous belchings. Water brash, better chewing tobacco.
Temperature - Alternate chill and heat. Cold, foul foot-sweat, fishy smell on heels.
Throat - Sore, dry, constricted, empty swallowing difficult, though food and drink pass easily. As if cold air
penetrates the throat. Acrid vapor or raw streak in throat, worse cough. Hawks out gluey, brown lumps.
Vertigo - Vertigo from gastric origin, better bending head backwards.
COMMENTS - Dippel's Animal Oil is “a colorless or slightly yellow, thin, oily liquid with a penetrating but not
disagreeable odor and an acrid, burning taste, which changes to a cool and bitter one. It darkens and thickens
on exposure to air and light and is extremely volatile. A drop on paper evaporates without leaving a greasy
stain.’Tts composition is extremely complex, but it may be regarded as belonging to the group of volatile
carbons.
Burning pains and burning sensations in almost all parts, stitching pains, “stitches as with red-hot needles”
(Kali-c., other carbons). Stitches and pressure in all directions, particularly from behind forward.
Cramp-like pains indifferent parts. Sensation of part being pulled upward. The left side is predominantly
affected, when direction is noted it is from before backward and from behind upward. Cracking in vertebra of
neck on raising head.
Twitching of lips and swelling beneath right lower jaw. Malar bone feels as if pulled forcibly upward. Greasy
feeling in mouth and accumulation of quantities of saliva white as snow. Relaxation of buccal mucus
membrane, patient cannot avoid biting cheek when he eats.
Sensation as of white of egg dried on lips. Soreness of tongue as if scalded. Sensation as if cold air penetrated
throat although the air is warm, better eating and drinking, worse empty swallowing. Desire for soft-boiled eggs
or for bread, with aversion to meat. Sensation as if water were in stomach, as if a lump of ice there. Belchings
taste like urine and burn.
Both testicles are drawn up and very painful. “Stitches from behind forward in breasts, pressure from both
sides of the back extends forward.” Menses too early and too scanty.
Clarke gave great relief in a case of cancer of right breast in which the patient complained of pains darting
forward out of the nipple.
Dr. Leggett related the case of a very stout Dutch woman, 56, who had been under constitutional treatment for
uterine tumor, engorged liver and cerebral congestion. She fancied the tumor had increased to the size it was
years ago. She had the sensation as if water rushing back and forth in stomach. She had been walking,
standing and shopping and had eaten many sweets.
Of the remedies having “stomach as if full of water,” Ol-an. was chosen as more similar to the case than Mill,
or Phell. and was given in 1000c potency, a single dose. A month later she was better in every way and a
second dose brought still further improvement.
A case of long-standing neuralgia of the spermatic cord was cured. There were excruciating attacks three or
four times every year, pains as if testicles were seized by a hand and pulled very severely. Ol-an. 18c gave
almost instant and permanent relief.
Dever cured a toothache in an extremely irritable patient, pain better by pressing the teeth together. The
provings had “stitches in right upper molar removed by pressure after dinner.”
The cure of a case of migraine is quoted in H. M., July, 1895. Zwingenberg, after failing with Sang., gave Ol-
an. 2x, five drops in warm water, morning and evening to a woman who always suffered from migraine the day
after a party, at which she usually wore a heavy diadem on her head.
Polyuria of clear urine accompanied the migraine and suggested the remedy. This accompaniment may
indicate Ol-an. in any nervous disorder. Zwingenberg also cured a case of nervous asthma following repelled
foot-sweat.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Camph., Nux-v., Op. Compare: (1) Puls., Ars., Sil., Sep. (2) in headache with
concomitant polyuria, Ign., Gels. (3) Twitching eyelids, Agar. (4) Gastric symptoms after drinking cold water,
Ars., Phos., Carb-v. (5) Pains in testicles, Puls. (6) worse by noise, Graph, better by noise. (7) better by rubbing,
Phos., Nat-c., Carb-ac., Canth. (8) Coryza worse in open air, All-c. (9) Numb head, Graph. Cracking in nape
 on moving head, Nice. (10) Dried white of egg sensation, Alum., Bar-c., Mag-c., Ph-ac., Sul-ac. (11) better
eating and drinking, worse empty swallowing, Lach. (12) Belchings taste like urine, Agn., smell like old urine.
( 13) Sad. despondent, Puls. - unlike Puls., bad tempered. Follows well: Bry. Followed well by: Sep.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Oleum Jecoris Aselli
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ol-j. Oleum jecoris aselli. Cod liver oil. Oleum jecoris morrhue. Oil obtained from the livers of
Gadus morrhua and some other allied fishes. N. O. Gadide. Tincture. Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Addison's, disease. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Asthma. Bones, disorders. Bright's, disease.
Cold, abscess. Constipation. Coryza. Coughs. Diarrhea. Dwatfishness. Emaciation. Fever. Fistula. Goiter.
Hair, abnormal. Headaches. Indigestion. Intermittent, fever. Joints, stiffness. Liver, diseases. Lumbago.
Malnutrition. Marasmus. Palpitations. Pneumonia. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Sacrum pains. Sciatica.
Scrofulous ophthalmia. Sleeplessness. Spinal irritation. Tuberculosis. Vision disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - The number of people who “cannot take cod-liver oil” is very great, which means that Ol-j.
is a pathogenic as well as a curative agent.
Neidhard proved it and elicited some very definite symptoms and to these have been added curative and
pathogenic effects observed on patients. The oil contains a large number of proximate principles of great
complexity to which its specific medicinal properties are due.
Decided pains in the liver and liver region with great soreness were noted in Neidhard's provings and these
symptoms give one of the keynotes of the remedy as soreness. Not only the liver, but the throat, chest,
abdomen, kidneys, ovaries, joints and back are all sore. The spine is sore as in spinal irritation.
Sore pains. Burning in spots. Rheumatic disorders. Pains in liver region. Yellow discharges. Scrofulous
diseases. Faulty nutrition. Emaciation. Anemia, weakness. Deficiency of vital heat. Always taking cold.
Lassitude. Hot hands and head. Frontal headaches, over right eye, bursting after coughing. Palpitations of the
heart, with cough, short breath.
The nutrition of the skin is improved and the medicinal properties of the oil are
absorbed without any tax being put on the organs of digestion. Burnett said that olive oil and almond oil acts
as well.
Atrophy of infants, emaciation with hot handle and head, restless and feverish at night. Emaciated,
dwarfish, chilly babies and children, a nightly rubbing with cod liver oil soon revolutionizes their condition.
Children who cannot tolerate milk.
Abdomen - Soreness and heaviness in the region of liver, worse exercise.
Back - Chilly or fluttering from sacrum up back to occiput.
Causations - Malnutrition.
Chest - Sharp, stitching pains. Burning spots. Soreness through chest. Coughing causes soreness of chest,
headache.
Face - Growth of short, thick hair on chin and upper lip in women.
Female - Establishes menses. Yellow leucor- rhea with weak back.
Food - Children who cannot take milk.
Heart - Palpitations, accompany other symptoms.
Limbs - Chronic rheumatism with rigid muscles and tendons. Aching in elbows and knees, in sacrum. Burning
in palms. Palms hot toward evening.
Lungs - Dry, hacking, tickling cough, especially at night. Cough with palpitation. Soreness or stitches in
chest. Yellow sputum. Hemoptysis (Acai., Mill.). Early tuberculosis. Whooping cough in miserable, scrofulous
children. Dahlke indicated giving give drop doses increasing daily, one drop up to twelve, then descend in the
same way for whooping cough.
Modalities - Worse from milk. Worse from exposure to cold, draft of air. Worse living in cold. Worse damp
localities. Worse touch, motion. Worse raising arm, bending side inwards. Worse stooping, walking. Worse
riding, falling. Laughing aggravates cough. Lying down causes oppressed feeling.
Mouth - Tongue yellow. Fetid breath.
Skin - Yellowness. Cold abscesses. Milk crusts. Ringworm (local application).
Temperature - Constantly chilly towards evening. Hectic fever. Night-sweats.
Throat - Hoarseness.
COMMENTS - Ol-j. is a liver remedy, an ally of Choi., confirmed by the provings. Burnett noted that cod liver
oil is a nutrient and affects the chest, liver, pancreas and tendons. Internally, a nutrient and a hepatic and
 pancreatic remedy.
Burnett showed that ringworm generally has its constitutional basis in a tuberculosis miasm. In recent
ringworm, the application of the plain oil at bedtime is at once the most innocent and most effectual of known
local measures. Before the application, the part should be washed well with soft soap.
“Dry, hacking cough, night-cough, cough with tough expectoration, yellow or white, soreness of chest,
especially on coughing, sharp stitches here and there, through chest, burning through to back, burning in
spots.”
Tuberculosis, in the beginning stages. Scrofulous diathesis. Cough is worse from exposure to cold, worse in
damp weather. Cough relieved by onset of fever.
Marked fever symptom, both hectic and intermittent. “Fever worse towards evening with burning in palms.”
Chilly, sensitive to drafts, feels as if continually taking cold. Chills running down the back. Feet constantly cold.
Sensitive to chill and damp. Thirst before and during the chill.
Affection of the spleen. Y ellow discharges, particularly expectoration, coating of the tongue, yellow mucus
from sore throat.
Increases the menstrual flow, and restores it when in abeyance. Abnormal growth of hair on the face of a
woman. Yellow leucorrhea. Passage of mucus from urethra with burning during stool.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Iris v. (chill with sick stomach and diarrhea). Compare: (1) Choi., Tub., Phos.,
lod. (2) One liter of Ol. Jecoris contains 0.4 gram of iodine. (3) Gad., Cod, - frequent breathing with flapping of
ala nasi, rush of blood to chest, pain in lungs and cough, dry heat in palms. (4) Fei. and sarcodes generally.
(5) In tuberculosis, ringworm, emaciation, Bac., Phos. (6) Emaciation and ravenous appetite, lod. (7)
Intolerance of milk, Aeth., Calc., Lac-v„ Mag-c. (8) Pains in head with cough, Caps., Bry., Nat-m. (9) Chilly,
effects of damp localities, Nat-sulph., Aran.
(10) Heavy eyelids, Gels., Op.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Oleum Olea Europea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ol-o-e. Oleum olea europea. Olive oil. N. O. Oleaceae. Historical dose: Tincture, oil and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Constipation. Dehydration. Heart, disease. Malnutrition. Skin, disorders.
HERBAL - Olive oil is obtained from the fruit of the olive tree, now common to the shores of the Mediterranean.
It is used in cooking, cosmetics, soaps and as a fuel for traditional oil lamps.
Olive oil is pleasant and bland, very nutritious, and mildly laxative. It is regarded as a healthful dietary oil
because of its high content of monounsaturated fat (mainly oleic acid) and polyphenols.
Very well tolerated by the stomach. It's protective function has a beneficial effect on ulcers and gastritis.
Activates the secretion of bile and pancreatic hormones, lowering the incidence of gallstone formation.
For infants it is especially serviceable as a cathartic, being easily taken and of mild action. Suitable for adults
in irritated or inflamed conditions of the bowel or stomach, and may be given after acrid poisons. As a laxative
enema, one to two fluid ounces should be taken, two teaspoonfuls or less for a child one year old.
Externally, it is a lubricant and is valuable for shielding irritated surfaces, relax contracted tendons, and promote
healing. Olive oil massage is helpful in preventing dehydration from fever. Daily breast massage with the oil is
helpful in preventing breast cancer and tumors. Olive oil foot massages are good for relaxation and will promote
sleep.
Olive oil is often the basis in which to incorporate other medicaments, or is compounded with dense fatty or
resinous substances to give them pliancy in the formation of ointments, cerates, or plasters.
RELATIONS - Compare: Alf., Mel., Aloe-v., Calen., castor oil.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Oleum Santali
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ol-sant. Oleum santali. Sandalwood oil. Oleum santalum. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Bronchitis. Colds. Colic. Coughs. Cystitis. Diarrhea. Gonorrhea. Kidney, pain. Laryngitis.
Nausea. Skin, dry. Sore throats. Wrinkles. Wounds.
HERBAL - Ol-sant. is a stimulating, disinfectant expectorant and antispasmodic. Antiseptic, anti-inflammatory,
and a mild pain reliever. Acne, wounds, dry skin and wrinkles.
Two or three drops on sugar will frequently relieve the hacking cough, when only little sputum is expectorated.
 Bronchitis when the cough is dry and hacking. Coughs, sore throats and laryngitis.
Affects the urinary and sexual spheres. Gonorrhea, discharge is thick and yellow. Swelling of the prepuce,
painful erections. Urine is passed slowly and causes burning and smarting of the urethra. Gonorrhea where
the prostate gland is implicated and there is pain deep in the perineum.
Nausea, diarrhea and colic. Aids in digestion, relaxes the muscles of the digestive tract. Stimulates the
production of urine, restores hormonal balance.
MIND - Aggression and irritability. Stress, anxiety, nervous tension and depression. Difficult concentration.
Bladder - Chronic cystitis. Frequent, burning, smarting, swelling and redness of meatus. Sensation of a ball
pressing against the urethra, worse standing.
Kidneys - Aching in kidney region. Gleet with profuse, thick discharge. Stream small and slow.
Lungs - Bronchitis when the cough is dry and hacking.
Male - Gonorrhea. Thick, yellowish, muco-purulent discharge. Deep pain in perineum. Swelling of the
prepuce. Painful erections.
RELATIONS - Compare: Cann-s., Buchu, Cop.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Blackwood. Clarke.

States of exhaustion in mind/emotions, body and spirit. Weariness and exhaustion. Emotional weariness.

name: Oniscus Asellus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - onis. Oniscus asellus. Wood louse. Oniscus armadillo. Armadillo officinalis. Sow-bug. Sow-
louse. Cellar-worm. Millipedes. N. O. Isopoda, class Crustacea of the Articulate. Tincture of whole animal.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Asthma. Bladder, disorders. CoZfr. Epilepsy. Hemoptysis. Rectum, disorders. Strangury.
Tenesmus. Toothache.
HOMEOPATHIC - In Germany, Onis. has a popular reputation as a remedy for epilepsy. Hering proved a
tincture and Wolf recorded the effect of swallowing three cellar-worms in a glass of brandy before an attack of
fever. This experience provided the most characteristic symptoms of the remedy, showing it to be related to
Canth., Apis and their cognates.
The symptoms of Hering's proving showed pains in the head, over the eyes and down the nose. Constriction
of gullet and stomach. Hawking up of blood-streaked mucus. Burning in anus. Many erections with
disinclination to work (Canth.). Frequent yawning and desire to stretch.
Asthmatic conditions with bronchial catarrh. Pale face, wild expression, constant vomiting. Very severe colic
with meteor- ism and tension of abdomen. Tenesmus of bladder and rectum. Cutting burning in urethra.
Dropsy.
Abdomen - Distended, meteorism, very severe colic. Very severe colic with meteorism and tension of
abdomen.
Bladder - Cutting burning in urethra. Tenesmus of bladder and rectum with absence of stool and urine.
Face - Pale face, wild expression.
Head - Boring pain behind right ear in the mastoid bone (Caps.). Violent pulsation of arteries (Poth., Glon.).
Painful pressure above the root of nose.
. Kidneys - Cutting, burning in urethra.
Lungs - Hawking up of blood-streaked mucus. Asthmatic conditions with bronchial catarrh.
Male - Many erections with disinclination to work (Canth.).
Rectum - Burning in anus. Tenesmus of rectum with absence of stool and urine.
 Stomach - Persistent pressure in cardiac orifice. Constant vomiting.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Poth., Canth., Glon.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Ononis Spinosa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - onon. Ononis spinosa. Rest- harrow. Ononis arvensis. Cammock. N. O. Leguminose.
Papilionoideae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Epilepsy. Headaches. Nephritis. Nosebleeds.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany notes that ononis arvensis is indigenous to Britain, growing on barren
pastures and on the borders of ill-cultivated fields. It owes its name, “Rest- harrow,’ ’ to its tough underground
roots, which cause stoppages to harrow and plough.
In some parts it is called “Cammock,” and the country people, having the idea that it communicates its
nauseous, goat-like odor to cheese made from the milk of cows who have eaten it, call the cheese so tainted
“Cammocky.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Nosebleed three or four times in one day, worse when washing his face. Hansen gave
“chronic nephritis” as having been cured by Onon.
COMMENTS - Cooper recorded the case of a brick field laborer, 45, who at 13 was prostrated for a week,
apparently with sunstroke, something seemed to catch the back of his head. At 25, had similar attacks. In
March, 1900, he began to have daily attacks.
An aura seemed to spread over his head from the occiput, he made frightful grimaces, but did not scream out,
became unconscious, turned deathlike and blue in face and fell down.
After the attacks he had a violent headache, giddiness and wakeful nights. Onon. tincture in single doses at
rare intervals produced improvement at once and cured in nine months.
REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Onopordon Acanthium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-onop. Onopordon acanthium. Cotton thistle. Scotch thistle. N.O. Com- positae.
CLINICAL - Chilliness. Headache. Heart, disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - Constriction in left side of chest. Sensation as of a stone in the chest. Characteristic heart
rhythm disorders. Excessive depressive tendency. Headache better change of weather, to warm and dry
weather. Stuffed sensation in ears and nose. Pain in right maxillary sinus.
Increased sensory perceptions. Chilliness. Sensitiveness to cold and to drafts of air. Worse cold, damp
weather. Better warmth and rest. Pains in back and limbs, better motion, and worse sitting and after sleep.
Sensation of cold and the dryness of the mucous membranes of nose and throat. Dryness of mouth, lips. Better
eating. Desire for sweets. Swelling and redness of the part of the abdomen where a belt is worn. Cold feeling
in lower abdomen during scanty menses. As if icicles in rectum.
MIND - Difficult concentration. Sensitiveness to external impressions. Euphoria, alternating with sadness.
Food - Desires sweets.
Head - Headache better change of weather to warm and dry weather.
Heart - Dull pain in region of heart, extending to left arm.
Limbs - Fleeting pains in small joints. Limbs heavy like lead. While walking, feet turn frequently.
Modalities - Better warmth and rest. Better eating. Worse cold, damp weather.
Nose - Smell more acute.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Onosmodium Virginianum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - onos. Onosmodium virginianum. False cromwell. Lithospermum virginicum. N. O. Boraginacee.
Tincture of entire fresh plant including root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Aphasia. Bladder, irritation. Breasts, disorders. Colic. Colorblindness. Debility.
Diarrhea. Diplopia. Eye, disorders. Eyestrain. Headaches. Locomotor ataxia. Meniere's disease. Migraines.
Neurasthenia. Nose, dryness. Paralysis. Pregnancy, sickness. Presbyopia. Seminal emissions. Sexual,
weakness. Spine, congestion. Throat, sore. Tinnitus. Urethra, irritation. Uterus, prolapse.
HOMEOPATHIC - Onos, is a member of an American branch of the borage family closely resembling the
British Onosma. Its common name is False Cromwell, the real Cromwell being another borage, Lithospermum.
 It was proved in material doses by W. E. Green of Arkansas. The most remarkable feature of the proving was
the want of power of concentration or coordination produced by the drug. This appears in an inability to
concentrate thought, to focus eyes, to coordinate muscles, or to judge the height of impediments on stepping.
General prostration, weariness. Acts and feels as if born tired. Seems to tread on cotton. Staggering. Vertigo,
numbness with muscular prostration. Neuralgic pains. Aching, soreness and stiffness of muscles after a pain.
Marked association of head and eye symptoms with muscular tiredness and weariness. Disturbance in the
sense of proportion. Migraine headaches. Onos, has probably cured more cases of headache associated
with eye-strain (Ruta), than any other remedy since it was proved.
Headaches from sexual weakness. Diminution of sexual desire in both sexes, similar to sexual neurasthenia.
Depressed or lost sexual life in women.
MIND - Loss of concentration and coordination. Confused mind, slow thinking. Irresolution. Aphasia. Forgetful,
loss of memory. Fear of falling on going up or down stairs.
Abdomen - Distended feeling, better removing clothing, with griping and grumbling. Colic is better bending
backward.
Back - Tired feeling in lower part of the back. Pain in dorsal and lumbar regions. Numbness and tingling in feet
and legs.
Breasts - Sore, aching in breasts, feel swollen and sore. Nipples itch.
Causations - Eyestrain. Sexual excess.
Ears - Fullness in ears. Hearing impaired, ringing as from quinine.
Eyes - Eyes heavy and dull. Eyestrain, strainedfeelingin eyes, worse using eyes. Muscular asthenopia.
Ocular muscles tense. Internal eye muscles paretic. Pain in eyeballs between orbit and ball, extending to
left temple. Eye symptoms with ovarian symptoms.
Female - Sexual desire completely loss. Feels as if menses would appear. Menses too early and too
prolonged. Leucorrhea, acrid, yellow offensive, profuse, running down the legs. Severe uterine pains, bearing
down pains, old pains return. Soreness in uterine region. Pains alternate between ovaries. Soreness of ovaries
with rectum.
Food - Craving for ice water and cold drinks, wants to drink often. Distaste for water. Appetite and thirst
diminished. Appetite increased. Hunger after siesta, nervous, all day.
Head - Migraine headache from eyestrain or sexual weakness. Dull, heavy, dizzy, pressing upward in
occiput. Occipital headache as if screwed, worse eyestrain and lying down. Occipital-frontal pain in morning
on waking, Chiefly on the left side. Pain up and down from occiput (left) to shoulder worse exertion. Pain in
temples and mastoid (Caps.).
Heart - Pain in heart causing fear of death. Pain in region of apex. Oppression of heart. Depressed feeling in
heart, as if it would stop beating. Pulse rapid, irregular and weak, and slow. With every third or fourth beat the
diastole is prolonged.
Kidneys - Pain in prostatic urethra before and after urination. Seldom any desire to urinate. Urination frequent,
scanty. Urine is high-colored, very acid, aromatic, of balsamic odor and heavily loaded with urea.
Limbs - Great muscular weakness and weariness. Pain in back. Pain in left scapular region. Tired and numb
feeling in legs, popliteal spaces and below knees. Staggering gait. Sidewalk seems too high.
Lungs - Hacking cough with sticky, white sputum, better drinking cold water.
Male - Burning in urethra with itching. Sexual excitement. Constant, severe erections. Speedy emissions.
Psychological impotence. Loss of sexual desire. Deficient erections.
Modalities - Better from cold drinks, eating, undressing. Better lying on back, rest, sleep. Worse eyestrain,
sprains, jarring, motion, tight clothing. Worse sexual excess, darkness, warm, humid air.
Mouth - Dryness of mouth, and of lips, without thirst, better cold water, with scanty saliva. Clammy, sticky,
feeling in mouth. Bitter taste.
Nose - Dryness of nose, with feeling as from taking cold. Pain in nasal bones. Stuffed feeling or discharge in
posterior sinuses. Sneezing in morning, left side of nose and left eye seem affected.
Rectum - Stools with tenesmus, yellow, mushy, hurrying him out of bed in morning. Stool is shining, bloody
and stringy.
Skin - Formication in calves.
Sleep - Sleeplessness. Sleep is uneasy and interrupted, restless and waking early. Many, varied dreams.
Temperature - As if would have a chill every day about twelve or one o' clock. Hushed feeling over body. No
perspiration in very warm weather.
Throat - Severe dryness and tightness, all symptoms are better by cold drinks and eating. Raw, scraping.
Laryngeal cough, better from drinking cold water, with expectoration of whitish, sticky phlegm. Husky voice.
Vertigo - Vertigo, numbness and muscular prostration. Vertigo with headache, worse lying on left side, raising
 the hands above the head.
Vision - Vision blurred, optic disc hyperemic and retinal vessels enlarged. Misjudges distances. Color
blindness for red and green.
COMMENTS - Vertigo and sensations of numbness and general muscular prostration. Neuralgic pains, dull,
heavy aching, affecting the cervical and spinal nerves, pelvic organs, eyes, occiput and sacrum. These are the
chief centers of pain along with the throat, bowels, breasts, heart and limbs. The left side of the body is more
affected than the right.
Characteristic paralyzing effects on the internal eye muscles. “Feeling of tension in the eyes, as from straining
them to read small print,” and “desires to have things far off to look at them.” The eyeball aches, aggravated
by reading small print. Glaucoma. Blurred or double vision. Eyestrain headaches (Ruta.).
Marked “soreness and stiffness.” In the occiput there is pressure upward and the pains may go from the eye
backward. Gluey expectoration with laryngeal cough. Catarrh of the Eustachian tube (Kali-m„ Merc-d.).
Meniere's disease.
Characteristic dryness of the nose, mouth and throat. Ameliorated by a great thirst for cold water. Strictures of
the urethra where there's painful urination and there are adhesions or blockages in the urethra.
Great loss of sexual desire. Fibroids. History of enlarging breasts when given in tincture (Sabad.). Equalizes
the size of unequal breasts.
E. S. Norton published several illustrative cases including the case of Miss C., 23, who suffered three years
from a headache. Pain especially in occiput, which felt “sore and stiff,” often extending down spine, which was
somewhat sensitive to touch.
There was a dull, aching pain on the left side of head, with occasional darting pain through the eyes. Aching
in eyes, stiff, strained feeling in them if she read a lot, worse on the left. Headache worse in the
morning with some dizziness. The patient had some astigmatism that was corrected with glasses and Onos,
lx at once relieved all the symptoms.
Norton also noted the case of Mrs. D., who had excessive myopia and a severe headache with a constant dull,
stupid ache in right occiput and right eye, worse when tired, from coughing or from any sudden motion. There
was a little vertigo and a strained feeling in right eye. Onos. 3x cured.
Norton suggested that neurasthenia and neurasthenic headache may be met with Onos, when connected with
strains of other kinds besides eye strains. He pointed to the case of Mrs. B., who was deaf for nine years.
For four years she had a constant roaring, hissing noise in both ears with constant dull, pressing pain in occiput,
worse in the evening. She had some pain in the ear and sharp shooting pain in front of auricle, with slight
vertigo. Chronic catarrh of both middle ears, membranes thickened. Onos, lx immediately relieved all the pains,
though it did not alter the hearing or noises.
H. F. Ivens cured a case of headache of ten years duration, with the modality worse in the dark. The pain was
in the left temple and over the left eye, not worse by noises, light or use of eyes, but worse in the dark and on
lying down. Pellets of Onos, tincture were given every twelve hours.
W. A. Yingling found that the depressing action of Onos, extends to the generative sphere, desire being
abolished in both men and women. He quoted S. A. Jones as suggesting that this is the primary action of the
drug, thereby distinguishing it from Pic-ac. in which excitement precedes debility.
Onos, will correspond to the developed consequences of sexual abuse and Pic-ac. to the initial step of sexual
debility manifested in weakness. Yingling many times verified “complete loss of desire” as a leading indication.
Yingling had an interesting experience in the case of a woman to whom he gave Onos, for dryness of the nose
and throat.
Not only did it cure this, but it also restored the breasts, which were diminutive and almost absent to their
normal size. Yingling's results were from the tincture, and not marked from 30c.
W. J. Guernsey greatly relieved with Onos, a man, 38, who suffered from seminal emissions, the result of
masturbation. The pains were better by undressing and lying on the back.
Green published some very striking cases with some pathogenic symptoms as well as cures, and also gives
an interesting comparative experience with potencies.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-m., Lil-t, Gels., Ruta. (2) Myos., Helio., Symph. (3) In uterine misplacement,
Helio., Helon., Lil- t., Sep.. Nat-m., etc. (4) Disorder of vision, Lil-t. - astigmatism, Pic-ac. - myopia, Nat-s. -
Myopia. (5) Ocular headache, Gels, more right, Onos, more left, Lil-t., Spig., Bapt. (6) Eyestrain - Ruta.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Operculina Turpethum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oper. Operculina turpethum. Nishope. N. O. Convolvulaceae. Historical dose: All potencies.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Fevers. Delirium associated with restlessness, loquacity. Tendency to escape from bed,
ravings, pains cause fainting.
Bubonic plague. Lymphatic glands are enlarged and indurated. Boils and slowly suppurating abscesses.
Hemorrhoids. Cholera morbus. Watery diarrhea, profuse with sinking sensation.

name: Opium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - op. Opium. Poppy. Papaver officinale. Papaversomniferum. Thebaicum. N. O. Papaveracee.
Opium is the gummy exudation of the unripe capsule of the poppy, contains morphine. Tincture. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - After-pains. Bladder, paralysis. Brain disorders. Cancer. Catalepsy. Chilblains. Colic. Coma.
Constipation. Delirium. Delirium, tremens. Diabetes mellitus. Dreams. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Fear,
effects. Fetus, movements. Hernia. Hystero-epilepsy. Ileus. Intestines, obstruction. Laborpains, abnormal.
Lead, colic. Marasmus. Measles. Melancholia. Meningitis. Opisthotonos. Paralysis. Puerperal convulsions.
Shock. Sighing. Sleep, abnormal. Snoring. Starting. Strokes. Sunstroke. Trauma. Tympanitis. Uremia.
Urine, suppression. Uterus, inertia. Veins, fullness. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Opium is one of the most complicated substances in the Materia Medica. Opium contains
about eighteen alkaloids of which the apomorphine, morphine, heroin and codeine are well known. Brunton
noted that besides mucilage, albumen, fat, sugar and salts of ammonia, calcium and magnesia, it contains
“seventeen or eighteen alkaloids and two neutral substances, as well as a meconic acid.”
Opium played a very prominent part in old-school therapeutics due to its painkilling properties, often with the
end result of addiction. The pathogenesis is made up of provings, clinical observations and, in large part, the
effects observed in opium-smokers and in those poisoned with massive doses.
The effects of a poisonous dose of opium are scarcely to be distinguished from a fully developed attack of a
stroke. There is absolute unconsciousness, complete muscular relaxation, pupils are contracted to a pinpoint
aperture, turgid, bloated. Very red or bluish face, stertorous breathing, pulse slow and full. Death takes place
by asphyxia, the heart continuing to beat after breathing has ceased.
Smaller doses produce a deep sleep, pleasant, fantastic or frightful dreams, and delirium like delirium tremens.
On waking there is a severe headache, nausea, furred tongue, and a loss of appetite.
Want of susceptibility to remedies even though indicated. Insensibility of the nerves, painlessness,
depression, drowsy stupor, torpidity and general sluggishness of function and lack of vital reaction, a kind of
negative state. All complaints are characterized by a stupor.
Lessens voluntary movements and contracts the pupils. Painless paralysis of brain, tongue, bowels etc.
Depresses higher intellectual powers, lessens the self-control and power of concentration, judgment.
Stimulates the imagination. Useful for diseases that originate from fright. Idiocy from masturbation.
Tremors, twitchings, jerking during sleep. Convulsions, worse heat of room or bath. Epilepsy in sleep, from the
approach of strangers (children), from fright, worse glare of light, from anger, insult. Throws limbs or stretches
arms at right angle to the body, stupor between spasms.
Strokes. Venous, passive congestion. Faints every fifteen minutes. Stupid sleep, accompanies all complaints
during spasms, violent chill etc. Complaints arepainless and are accompanied by heavy, deep sleep, and
stertorous breathing. Sensation of bodily well-being, great happiness. Painless ulcers. Suppuration.
Checks all secretions except that of the skin. Sweaty skin. Hot sweat, hand. Complaints appear with sweat.
Reappearance and aggravation from becoming heated. Bed seems hot, hunts a cold place. Internal dryness.
Dropsical swelling of the whole body. Dark, mahogany-brown face.
MIND - Apoplectic (stroke) state. Coma from drug overdose, fright, stroke or injury. Loss of
consciousness. Dreamy. Sluggish. Dull. Stupid. No will power. Placid. Wants nothing, says nothing ails him.
Unable to understand or appreciate his sufferings. Indifferent to pain or pleasure. Nervous, irritable, tendency
to start.
Frightful fancies, visions of mice, scorpions. Fears after fright, which remains. Delirium tremens with terror.
Delirious talking with wide-open eyes. Exaltation of the mind, vivid imaginations. Gaiety. Talkative. Rash. Bold,
increased courage. Tendency to lie. Deceptive, vision, taste touch, perversion of all senses. Imagines parts of
his body are very large. Thinks he is not at home. Carphology.
Abdomen - Hard, bloated, tympanitic. As if a weight in the abdomen. Lead colic. Colic with urging to stool
and discharge of hard feces. Intestinal spasms, child cries day and night. Incarcerated umbilical or inguinal
hernia. Difficult emission of flatus. Bowels feel completely obstructed. Paralytic atony of bowels after
laparotomy.
 Back - Pulsating arteries and swollen veins on neck. Opisthotonos.
Causations - Ill effects of fear, fright, anger, shame, rape, sudden joy. Charcoal fumes, alcohol, lead, drug
overdose, sun.
Chest - Heat in chest, burning about heart. Tension and constriction in chest. Compression of diaphragm.
Aching in chest with shootings in sides.
Constitutions - Suited to persons of light hair, lax muscles and want of bodily irritability. Children and the
elderly. Persons insensitive to well-chosen remedies. Alcoholics.
Ears - Acuteness of hearing, clocks striking at a great distance keep her awake. Tinnitus like sea roaring.
Buzzing, tinkling in ears.
Eyes - Red, bulging eyes. Staring, glassy. Pupilsfixed, contracted, dilated, nonreactive to light. Embolism
of central artery of retina. Visual hallucinations. Cloudiness of sight. Sensation as if eyeballs were too large, or
of dust in eyes. Quivering of eyes and lids. Eyes half open and are turned upwards. Eyelids hanging, as if
paralyzed. Ptosis (Gels., Caust.). Swelling of lower lids.
Face - Red, bloated, swollen, dark suffused, hot. Looks intoxicated, besotted (Bapt., Lach.). Distorted.
Trembling, spasmodic facial twitching, especially corners of
mouth. Veins of face distended. Lips swollen, protruding. Lower jaw hangs down. Lockjaw. Old look after
cholera infantum.
Female - Dysmenorrhea, forcing her to bend double with urging to stool. Suppressed menses from fright.
Prolapse from fright. Softness of uterus. Horrible labor-like pains in uterus. Hiccough during pregnancy
.Livelyorviolentfetal motion. Threatened miscarriage from fright with sopor. Puerperal convulsions,
drowsiness or coma between paroxysms. Convulsions from stoppage of labor pains. Suppression of lochia
from fright.
Food - Hungry, but no desire to eat. Attacks of bulimia with want of appetite and repugnance to all food.
Slowness and weakness of digestion. Burning thirst, especially for beer.
Head - Heavy occiput. Pain in back of head, great weight there (Gels.). Bursting feeling. Head hot with hot
sweat. Paralysis of brain. Confusion in head. Dull, heavy, stupid. Complete insensibility, no mental grasp for
anything.
Heart - Weakness. Burning about the heart. Pain in heart with great anxiety, trembling, sleeplessness, talkative
delirium. Palpitations after stressful events, fright, grief, sorrow, etc. Full, slow pulse.
Kidneys - Kidney colic, pain radiates to bladder and testicles. Loss of power or sensibility of bladder. Paralytic
atony of bladder after laparotomy. Retained or involuntary urination after a fright. Retention of urine in
nursing children from spasms of neck of bladder. Slow to start, feeble stream.
Limbs - Trembling of the limbs after fright. Twitching of limbs. Jerks as if flexors were overacting.
Convulsions, worse from glare of light, coldness of limbs. One or other arm moves convulsively to and fro.
Shuffling and trembling gait. Feels as if lower limbs were severed and belong to someone else. Numbness,
weakness. Painless paralysis (Olean.). Veins of hands distended.
Lungs - Stertorous breathing. Difficult, intermittent, deep. Hoarse. Sighing. Deep snoring with rattling,
unequal breathing. Breathing stops on going to sleep, must be shaken to start it again (Grind.). Cough, tickling
with blue face or profuse sweat on whole body, better drinking water. Cough with dyspnea and blue face with
bloody expectoration. Hemoptysis. Y awning after cough.
Male - Increased sexual desire with frequent erections and pollutions. Diminished sexual desire and
impotence. Spasmodic stricture from drinking poorly fermented liquor and in alcoholics.
Modalities - Better from cold, uncovering, constant walking. Worse heat, sunstroke. Worse odors, stimulants,
alcohol, suppressed discharges and receding eruptions. Worse emotions, fear, anxiety, reproaches,
shame joy. Worse during and after sleep (Apis, Lach.).
Mouth - Dry. Intense thirst. Copious salivation. Bloody froth. Hemoptysis. Ulcers in mouth and on tongue.
Difficult speech and swallowing. Blubbering of lips. Looseness of teeth.
Nose - Loss of smell.
Pulse - Pulse is full, slow, quick, hard, irregular, imperceptible.
Rectum - Involuntary stools after fright, black offensive, frothy. Obstinate constipation, no desire to go to
stool. Round, hard, black balls. Feces protrude and recede (Thuj., Sil.). Spasmodic retention of feces in small
intestines, from ileus. Violent pain in rectum as if pressed asunder. Bloody mucus oozes from open anus.
Sensations - As if from smoke on the brain. As if flying or hovering in air. As if drunk. Asif eyes too large for
orbits, as if sand or dust in eyes. As if eyelids paralyzed. As of a band around chest. As if something was
forced through a narrow space in abdomen. Rolling, as of a hard body in right hypochondrium. As if intestines
would be cut to pieces, as of a stone in abdomen. As though anus closed. As if lower limbs severed from body.
Skin - Dry. Rough and dirty. Whole body looks red. Skin blush with blue spots. Hot perspiration over whole
 body, except lower limbs. Constant desire to uncover. Dropsical swelling of whole body. General itching.
Crawling here and there. Erythema, scarlatina-like eruptions. Painless indolent ulcers. Desquamation of
epidermis. Chilblains.
Sleep - Great drowsiness (Gels., Nux- m.). Falls into a heavy, deep sleep. Profound coma. Suffocates on
falling asleep (Grind.). Sleepy, but cannot go to sleep. Sleeplessness from acuteness of hearing, distant
noises keep him awake. Bed feels so hot cannot lie on it. Picking at bedclothes. Dreams of cats, dogs, black
forms. Pleasant, fantastic, amorous dreams. Coma vigil.
Stomach - Painful sensitiveness and inflation of stomach and epigastrium. Heaviness and pressure in
stomach. Incarcerated hernia. Nausea with vomiting and retching. Retching from emotions. Vomiting with colic
and convulsions. Vomiting of blood or of greenish matter. Vomiting in peritonitis of fecal matter, of urine.
Temperature - General low temperature with inclination to stupor. Hot, sweaty and drowsy with cold limbs.
Heat extending over body. Hot perspiration. Sweats without relief. Puise full and slow. Fever characterized
by stupor, snoring respiration, twitching of limbs intense thirst and sleepiness.
Throat - Dryness of throat. Inability to swallow. On swallowing food either goes the wrong way or returns
through the nose. Bitter or sour taste in throat. Aphonia from fright. Voice weak with inability to speak loudly
without great exertion.
Tongue - Tongue purple, white, black. Tongue protrudes to right side, dry. Paralysis of tongue and difficult
speech.
Vertigo - Vertigo after fright. Lightness of the head in the elderly from injuries to head.
COMMENTS - Complaints brought on by fear, fright, anger, shame, shock. Ailments from excessive joy (Aeon.,
Coff.). Also from alcohol, lead, charcoal fumes. For fright where
the image reoccurs. Fright leading to an excited state, hypersensitive, sleepless.
Mentals similar to those of drug addicts. May lie and steal, lack of conscience. Pathologically courageous
people. State of confusion or delirium. May go in and out of a stupor. Time seems to move too slowly.
Frightened terror (Aeon.). Fear of being murdered, of impending death.
Visions and nightmares, wakes in a panic. Visions of fire and ghosts. Visions of great beauty and misery,
similar to manic-depression. Astral visions. Exhilaration. Ecstasy (Aeon., Phos.).
Shock, total painlessness (Arn., Resc-b.), improbable lack of pain. More rarely, shock with unbearable
headaches. Deception in their symptoms and behavior, their senses can be deceptive. State of desirelessness.
Stupor. Pinpoint, frozen pupils, irregular pupils.
Polarizing narcosis. In crude doses it causes insensibility, numbness. Total relaxation, calmness, tranquility.
Can also cause hypersensitivity, insomnia, heightened senses. Sensitivity to light and noises (Coff.).
Hyperacute hearing (Lach.).
Grimmer noted that “this is a remedy of many phases and opposite extremes and alternating states, and of
symptoms such as diarrhea with burning pains and violent tenesmus, and involuntary stools. Or there may be
an inveterate constipation, often ending in complete bowel obstruction and paralysis of the bowels, cancers
and gangrenous ulcerations are most often painless.”
Hahnemann described a “deathly paleness, coldness of the limbs and whole body, cold perspiration, timorous
anxiety, trembling and despair, mucus stools, transient vomiting and short cough and very rarely certain kinds
of pain.” He noted that it was a rare and transient effect in excitable subjects, occurring as a reflection of the
secondary state.
Keynote abnormal painlessness, but there are also acute pains. Hahnemann recorded one example, “horrible
labor-like pains in uterus, which compelled her to bend the abdomen double with anxious, almost ineffectual
urging to stool.”
Characteristic drowsiness. Inertia, torpor. Absence of sensation, absence of reaction. Great stupor,
painlessness, complains of nothing, wants nothing. “Want of susceptibility, trembling.” Lack of vital reaction.
Exalted sensitiveness and timidity, sensitiveness to fright and other emotions. Sleepy but cannot sleep,
sleepless with acuteness of hearing disturbed by sounds ordinarily not heard at all. Nervous and irritable,
tendency to start. Twitching, trembling of head, hands and arms.
Spasms in children at the approach of strangers, from nursing after the mother has had a fright, from crying,
eyes half open and upturned. Screaming before and during a spasm. Tetanus, the spasms are ushered in with
a loud shriek.
Epileptic attacks occur during sleep. Epilepsy after a fright. Deep sleep after attacks. Deep, rapid breathing,
stertorous breathing while sleeping. Children sleep deeply and snore, as if in a coma. Coma, near death-like
states (Carb-v., Ant-t.). Coma from uremia, kidney failure. Comatose-like states with high fevers.
Fever, the skin is hot and damp. Secretions are generally checked except that of the skin. Sweat is a
characteristic concomitant. “Very hot, sweltering perspiration.” Guernsey noted that the “patient may not feel
 cold all day, but may have only a little chill and at night, when in bed, complain that the sheets feel so very
hot.”
T. F. Allen remarked that the Op. fever may be closely allied to that of Aeon, because the Ranunculaceae are
not far removed from the Papaveracee. May have a high temperature without a distinct inflammatory process.
Intense thirst and great sleepiness, without the anguish, fear and restlessness of the Aeon, fever.
Fever is similar to Gels., but with thirst. May be periodic, intermittent or remittent. Happy with a high fever.
Brain damage from high fevers, lack of oxygen or drugs, particularly in children (Hell.).
Delirium with great loquacity, visions of animals starting out of various parts of the room. Feels well in delirium.
Delirium tremens, very little drink is sufficient to bring on an attack. The bed feels too hot. Better cool, fresh
air, worse warmth (Apis.).
Besotted face, dusky, mottled (Bapt.). Can be bloated, purplish with dark blue color. Emaciation, wrinkled skin,
sunken eyes. Dry skin. Wasting infants who look aged, jerking and twisting of the body. Constant expression
of fright.
Pinpoint pupils, unequal, fixed. Glassy eyed children, especially with an arched back and high fever. Childhood
meningitis, arched backs, high fever, may have convulsions. Dreamy, sleepy state in meningitis (Gels.).
Stroke with dizziness and paralysis (Arn., Plb.). Deep red face. Strokes with labored breathing, a dusky, dark
color on the face, fixed pupils. Stroke, with insensibility and partial or complete paralysis, resulting from
charcoal vapor, inhaling gas, alcohol, fright, the fear still remaining. After a stroke, dropped jaw, paralyzed
bowels, and dry skin. Multiple sclerosis with paralysis.
Paralysis of sphincters. Severe constipation (Plb.), painless, after a shock or fright. Impacted bowels,
particularly in babies. Complete constipation with no desire for stool (Alum.). Lack of sensation, cannot strain.
Retention of urine due to lack of sensation. Constipation with round stool, hard, black balls that look like sheep
dung.
Involuntary and unconscious passage of urine and feces. Reversed peristalsis and fecal vomiting. Ileus and
strangulated hernia. Inertia of the intestines results in constipation of the bladder, retention of the uterus,
suspension of the menses.
Threatened abortion or miscarriage from fear. Uterine inertia during labor. Excessive fetal movements. Birth
trauma. Asphyxia of the newborn (Aeon.), the child is unaware. Puerperal convulsions.
Drug overdoses. Stupor and slurred speech from overdose (Gels.). Nausea or constipation from drugs.
Antidotes the effects of morphine (Nux-v.). Side effects of chemotherapy (Ip.). Antidote for lead poisoning,
especially where there is constipation, colic, cramps in the colon.
J. P. Willard repeatedly gave permanent relief in cases of suffering with Op. 2x without producing any narcotic
effect.
J. B. S. King noticed that in seven opium eaters, there was marked arching of the back, especially of the upper
part of the back. In as many morphine takers he had not met with a single case of arched back.
Villers cured with Op. 200c a case of hystero-epilepsy in which the attack was preceded by a sensation of
swelling of body. Veins protruded, face bluish red. Complete unconsciousness.
In one of the worst cases of painful menstruation Clarke ever treated, Op. 30c gave greater and more lasting
relief than any other remedy. In one patient he gave Op. 30c for constipation. With the onset of the next period,
Op. caused a “sharp pain which caused vomiting and a desire to sit doubled up and keep warm.”
C. N. Payne related the case of a little girl, aged two, who had never slept properly since birth. She went to
sleep at the usual time and slept until 10p.m., when she woke moaning, crying and tossing about. Seemed
frightened, almost fell asleep again but woke with a start. She screamed and kept one arm and one leg in
motion after waking. Seemed sleepy but could not sleep. Usually napped during the day.
Nux-v., Bell., Cham, were given in succession in vain. It then transpired that before the baby was twelve hours
old it had four different medicines put into its stomach. One of them was paregoric, and had been given since,
as well as a “quieting medicine.”
During the early months the baby had colic with constipation, stools in dark, hard, round balls. Clearly, it was
a proving of opium. Op. 200c was given. The first night she slept much better, rapid improvement and cure
followed.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Strong coffee, Atropine, Kali-perm, solution, oxygen inhalations, Camph., Bell.,
Ip., Nux-v., Chronic opium poisoning. Ip., Nux-v., Passi., Aven, is useful to counteract opium, morphine or
heroin habit. Antidote to: Bell., Dig., Lach., Merc., Nux-v., Stry., Plb., Stram., Ant-t. Compare:
(1) The alkaloids, Apom., Cod., Morph., Chel., Sang. (2) Apis, Bell., Gels., Nux-m. (3) Morphine - an extreme
susceptibility to all pain, twitching, tympanites, much itching, (4) Codeine - dry, teasing incessant cough, twitch-
ing of muscles, especially those of eyelids. (5) Esch. - California Poppy - a harmless soporific. (6) Stroke of
alcoholics, Bar-c. (7) Lack of vital reaction, Psor. (8) Spasms after fright - Hyos., from anger, Cham., Nux-v.,
 Effects of fright, the fear still remaining. Aeon., Hyos. (9) Diarrhea from fright. Gels., Puls., Verat. (10) Effects
of sudden joy, Coff. (11) Violent movements of fetus, Arn., Sil., Thuj., Sulph., Croc. (12) Uterine inertia, Morph.,
Chloral., Sec. Followed well by: Aeon., Bell., Bry., Hyos., Nux-v., Nux-m., Ant-t.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - op. Opium. Poppy. Papaver officinale. Papaversomniferum. Thebaicum. N. O. Papaveracee.
Opium is the gummy exudation of the unripe capsule of the poppy, contains morphine. Tincture. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - After-pains. Bladder, paralysis. Brain disorders. Cancer. Catalepsy. Chilblains. Colic. Coma.
Constipation. Delirium. Delirium, tremens. Diabetes mellitus. Dreams. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Fear,
effects. Fetus, movements. Hernia. Hystero-epilepsy. Ileus

name: Opuntia Vulgaris
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - Opun-v. Opuntia vulgaris. Prickly pear. Cactus opuntia. Opuntia alba spina. Opuntia itálica.
Opuntia pumila. N. O. Cactaceae. Opuntiae. Tincture of flowers. Tincture of the juice, stems and leaves. His-
torical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Enteroptosis. Nausea. Priapism. Spleen, pains.
HOMEOPATHIC - Two kinds of “Prickly pear” have been proved, Opun. vulg. and Opun. alba spina. Burdick
took one or two deep inhalations of the tincture of the flowers of the former. J. Fitch, who proved many of the
Cactaceae took ten drops of the tincture of the second potency.
Opun-v. has a sick feeling in the lower third of the abdomen. Feels as if bowels were settled down in lower
abdomen. Diarrhea with nausea. Enteroptosis with loose and frequent evacuations.
COMMENTS - The bulk of the symptoms of the proving are Fitch's, but the most peculiar symptom (which has
also been verified) is Burdick's, “Nausea extending from stomach down into bowels with sensation as if
diarrhea would set in.” Also “feeling as if bowels had settled down into lower abdomen.” Fitch had actual
diarrhea. All the urinary and genital symptoms were his except “bloody urine,” which is an effect of Opun-v.,
but not Burdick's. Coldness was observed by both provers. The peculiar mental symptoms recalling the
swearing tendency of Anae., are Fitch's. Sticking and pricking pains predominate, also numbness and tension.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chap. - which Mexican physicians laud as a specific in chronic diarrhea. (2) Ric.
- diarrhea, dysentery, obstinate chronic diarrhea. (3) Cact., Cer-b., Anh. (4) In nausea and sinking-down
sensation in stomach and abdomen. Ip. (5) Blasphemy, Anae.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Orchitinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - orch. Orchitinum. Testicular extract. Sperminum. A sarcode. Trituration. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL- Debility. Hot flashes. Impotency. Menopause. Senility. Sexual, weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - The use of a testicular extract in cases of senile decay and nervous breakdown was first
proposed by Brown- Sequard, and formed one of the examples by which he illustrated his doctrine of “inner
secretions.”
He maintained that the various glands of the organism had, in addition to their obvious secretion or excretion,
an additional secretion which was not obvious, but which materially contributed to the welfare of the organism.
The doctrine is now generally accepted and the use of the sarcodes in general is based upon it. Homeopathy
can use these remedies in both ways.
Orch. has been used with success in the triturations in menopausal sufferings and in old-school practice in the
sequelae of ovariotomy in cases of debility, sexual weakness and premature senile decay.
COMMENTS - Generally a remedy for men. Impotency (Sei.) and sexual debility. Weakness in the testes,
particularly before puberty. Hot flashes. Senility.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy.

name: Oreodaphne Californica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oreo. Oreodaphne californica. Califomialaurel. Mountain laurel. Spice-bush. Balm of Heaven.
N. O. Lauracae. Tincture of the leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Backache. Colic. Diarrhea. Headaches. Meningitis. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Oreodaphne is a tree which grows to a hundred feet in height. When bruised, it emits a
strong, spicy odor which may cause sneezing.
J. Murray Moore proved on himself and friends a tincture of the leaves and produced well-marked fronto-
occipital headache, worse by movement, better by rest. The symptoms were more violent when the tincture
was smelled than when taken internally.
Neuralgic headaches, cervical-occipital pain, cerebro-spinal meningitis. “Dull ache in occipital and cervical
regions, extending down to scapula, great heaviness of the head with a constant desire to move the head,
 which, however, gives no relief.” Atonic diarrhea and intestinal colic.
Back - Constant, dull ache in cervical and occipital region, extending to scapula down spine.
Eyes - Drooping eyelids. Eyelids heavy, Head - Head heavy, twitching. Intense aching with pressure at inner
angle of either orbit. Headaches, worse light, noise, better closing eyes and perfect quiet. Pains, worse left
side, extending through brain and across scalp to the base of the occiput. Pain extending to ears.
Rectum - Atonic diarrhea.
Vertigo - Dizziness, worse on stooping or moving.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Organophosphate
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - org-p. Organophosphate. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Ataxia. Chronic fatigue. Chemical, sensitivity. Colic. Coma. Convulsions. Cramps.
Dementia. Dystonia. Food, allergies. Heart disease. Incoordination. Multiple sclerosis. Muscle weakness.
Nausea. Neuropathy. Palpitations. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Osteoporosis. Twitching. Vertigo. Vomiting.
Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Organophosphate compounds are a diverse group of chemicals used in both domestic and
industrial settings. Examples include insecticides (malathion, parathion, diazinon, fenthion, dichlorvos,
chlorpyrifos), nerve gases (soman, sarin, tabun, VX), ophthalmic agents (echothio- phate, isoflurophate), and
antihelmintics (trichlorfon). Herbicides (tribufos [DEF], merphos) are tricresyl phosphate-containing industrial
chemicals.
Severe anxiety. Restlessness. Confusion. Impairment of concentration and memory. Confusion, irritability,
lethargy. Tearfulness. Depression, with suicidal tendencies. Hallucinations. Psychosis.
Muscular contractions. Ataxia. Seizures. Convulsions. Dysarthria, tremors. Polyneuropathy. Paralysis.
Insomnia. Cancer. Coma.
Respiratory distress. Bronchospasm and .laryngeal spasm, can lead to airway obstruction. Weakness and
paralysis of respiratory muscles. Chest pain. Cerebral ischemia.
Chronic fatigue syndrome. Malaise. General sick feeling. Severe, debilitating fatigue which is physical and
mental. Loss of muscular strength. Muscle aching, flitting from one group of muscles or joints to another.
Degeneration of handwriting. Episodic blurred vision.
Immune weakness, tendency to acquire infections and difficulty getting rid of infections, autoimmunity. Multiple
chemical sensitivity. Drug intolerance (such as alcohol, antidepressants). Food intolerances. Birth defects.
MIND - Poor short term memory. Unable to learn new things. Poor concentration, Speech difficulty with poor
word finding. Irritability and aggression. Severe anxiety. Nervousness and apprehension. Impairment of
concentration and memory.
Destabilization of mood. Mood swings. Increased tearfulness. Depression and psychosis. Impulsive suicidal
thoughts. Dementia. Rage. Hallucinations.
Abdomen - Abdominal pain and bloating. Colic. Irritable bowel syndrome.
Chest - Chest pain.
Eyes - Optic neuropathy. Retinal degeneration. Myopia, and miosis. Pupils dilated. Excess lachrymation.
Blurred vision.
Female -
Food - Loss of appetite. Hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia. Food allergies.
Head - Headache. Cerebral ischemia.
Heart - Heart disease. Cardiac arrhythmias. Palpitations. Bradycardia. Hypotension, hypertension.
Kidneys - Frequent urination. Urinary incontinence.
Limbs - Muscle weakness. Muscle aching. Muscle twitching or cramps. Clumsiness. Incoordination.
Dystonia, cogwheel rigidity. Paralysis. Osteoporosis.
Lungs - Shortness of breath. Pulmonary edema.
Modalities - Worse from diesel fumes, perfumes, cigarette smoke, alcohol.
Mouth - Salivation.
Nose - Allergies. Acute sense of smell. Perspiration - Increased sweating.
Rectum - Bowel incontinence. Diarrhea and constipation.
Skin - Numb patches.
Sleep - Sleep disturbance. Insomnia.
Stomach - Nausea and vomiting.
Temperature - Hypothermia. Heat flushes.
Vertigo - Vertigo, with poor balance and dizzy spells.
 RELATIONS - Compare: Mal., Phos., Ph- ac., Phys.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Origanum Majorana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - orig. Origanum majorana. Sweet marjoram. N. O. Labiate. Tincture of whole fresh plant. The
whole plant, without the root, gathered when in flower, is macerated in two times its weight of alcohol.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Breasts, disorders. Headaches. Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Masturbation. Nipples, irritation.
Nymphomania. Restlessness. Seminal, emissions. Sexual, mania.
HERBAL - The “Wild Marjoram” of this country is Origanum vulgare, grows on limestone or chalky soil and
yields an oil called Oil of Thyme.
HOMEOPATHIC - Orig., the “Sweet Marjoram” which is used for seasoning in cookery, was proved by Dr.
Cessoles, on himself and two young women. The symptoms of the proving showed a distinct relation to the
sexual organs, which clinical experience verified and expanded.
Orig. strongly affects the female sexual organs. Acts on the nervous system generally and is effective in
masturbation and excessively aroused sexual impulses. Increases the desire for sex.
Sexual excitement driving her to masturbation. Lascivious ideas, impulses, dreams. Affections of the breasts
(Bufo.). Great physical prostration. Desire for active exercise impelling her to run.
MIND-Lascivious ideas, impulsesanddreams, with sexual irritation. Great sexual excitement driving her to
masturbation. Eroticmania with inclination to commit suicide.
Sadness the whole day, followed by lively mood and excessive joyfulness. Thoughts of marriage, which dispel
sadness. Fearful, silent, sad, discontented, despairing and weary of life. Irritable. Uneasiness. Restless with
great anxiety and full of ideas. Need for active exercise of running in open air. Impulses to run.
Abdomen - Violent pain in abdomen wakes her from sleep at night.
Back - Pains beneath the scapula.
Breasts - Swelling and itching of nipples and pains in breast.
Female - Great sexual irritation, deep moroseness, believes herself lost or despised. Great sexual excitement
driving her to onanism, daily indulgence. Nearly idiotic from masturbation. Sexual mania, powerful lascivious
impulses. Sexual mania with inclination to suicide in a young girls. Hysteria. Sexual irritation with leucorrhea
and irritation of pudenda. “Flatulence of uterus.” Infertility.
Food - Loss of appetite. Excessive thirst at night
Head - Headache in temples. Heat of head, as heat increased, head was involuntarily turned from side to side.
Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate, waking him from sleep as many as four times in one night.
Limbs - Cramp in sole of right foot, in left leg, in fingers and shoulders. Pains in right hand. Rheumatic pains
in right foot frequently recurring and disappearing. Pains in the toes.
Male - Nocturnal emissions.
Nose - Tickling and sensation of constriction in tip of nose. Nosebleeds.
Skin - Pale red spots on legs, thighs and abdomen. Painful red pimples on outer portion of both legs.
Sleep - Frequent waking from sleep in fright, with trembling. Vivid, anxious, lascivious, exciting dreams.
Stomach - Hiccough.
Temperature - Heat of head, as the heat, as the heat increased the head was involuntarily turned from side
to side.
Vertigo - Vertigo on lying down in evening.
COMMENTS - A treatise on the “Sexual Passion,” by Dr. Gallavardin, Lyons, France, reported that a clergyman
of Mississippi, the founder of an orphan asylum, discovered that Origanum majorana, or common marjoram,
in a certain sense may be considered as a specific against sexual passion. It proved effective in masturbation
and excessively aroused impulses.
Gallavardin used it in the 4c dilution as he has not found the higher potencies effective. He dissolved five or
six globules of this dilution in four teaspoonfuls of fresh water and the young masturbator takes of this every
two days, a quarter of an hour before the meal, one teaspoonful.
If the cure is not accomplished eight days after this solution is used up, the same dose is repeated in the same
way.
When desired, this remedy can be used according to Gallavardin without the knowledge of the patient, by
pouring a teaspoonful into the soup, milk or chocolate. The effect frequently appears very rapidly, but some-
times it does not appear.
Clarke verified the power of Orig. in morbid sexual excitement in both sexes.
 The sexual symptoms were developed chiefly in the female provers and included sadness followed by
joyfulness and thoughts of marriage. Lascivious dreams. Increased desire for sex. Swelling and itching of
nipples and pains in breasts.
“Impulse to run.” “Heat of head, as the heat increased the head was involuntarily turned from side to side.”
Symptoms were worse evening on lying down (vertigo) and worse at night (excessive thirst).
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Ferul. - in violent sexual excitement in women, icy coldness in occiput. (2) Plat.,
Valer., Canth., Hyos. (3) In masturbation in girls, Grat. (4) In masturbation, desire to run, heat to head and
movements of head, disorders of breasts, Bufo. (5) In impulse to run, lod. (6) Canth., Cann-i., Coll., Hedeo.,
Helon., Plat., Valer.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Origanum Vulgare
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - orig-v. Origanum vulgare. Wild oregano. Wild marjorum. Greek oregano. N. O. Lamiaceae.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Arthritis. Asthma. Athlete's foot. Bad, breath. Bed-sores. Bites. Boils. Bronchitis. Bruises.
Burns. Bursitis. Candida. Canker, sores. Cellulitis. Cold, sores. Colds. Coughs. Cystitis. Dandruff. Diaper rash.
Diarrhea. Ear, infections. Eczema. Fleas. Food, poisoning. Frostbite. Fungus. Giariasis. Gum, disease.
Headaches. Hepatitis. Hives. Impetigo. Leg, cramps. Lice. Nail, fungus. Peptic, ulcer. Pneumonia. Poison, ivy.
Poison, oak. Psoriasis. Prostate, disorders. Radiation, burns. Ringworm. Rosacea. Scabies. Shingles.
Sinusitis. Sore, throat. Thrush. Toothache^ Tuberculosis. Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Warts. Wounds.
HERBAL - Oregano grows wild in the mountains of the Mediterranean region. The name is derived from a
Greek word meaning “joy of the mountains.”
It was used by Greek physicians for trauma, wounds, headaches, lung disorders and venomous bites and was
the traditional cure for hemlock poisoning. Over the centuries it gained widespread use for lung conditions,
asthma, pneumonia, bronchitis, sinusitis, allergies, and cough.
Britain's Gerard, in his 17th century manuscript, explained the use of oregano as a top remedy for head colds.
The 19th Century eclectic physicians used oregano as a general tonic and a promoter of menstruation (which
is why it should not be used during pregnancy).
REFERENCES - Murphy.
