name: Ornithogalum Umbellatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - omi. Ornithogalum umbellatum. Star of Bethlehem. N. O. Liliaceae. Hyacinthaceae. A plant of
which there are many varieties, nearly allied to garlic, Allium sativum. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cancer. Constipation. Depression. Flatulence. Gastric, ulcer. Prostration. Restlessness.
Stonuich, cancer. Stomach, ulcers. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Orni. is to be considered in chronic gastric and other abdominal indurations, like cancer of
intestinal tract, especially of stomach and cecum.
Pains in stomach with sickness, vomiting two or three times a day. Swollen feeling across lower chest.
Flatulence. Heartburn and rising of food. Gastric ulcer and cancer. Painful contraction in the pylorus with
duodenal distention. Feels as if a bag of water turns when she turns over in bed.
Complete prostration. Cold before the pains. Feels a pressure in every nerve of the body, sometimes in one
part or another with pain across chest, sometimes after food or at night and sometimes on an empty stomach.
Restlessness on account of creepy feeling in feet, cannot sit still, cannot read without walking about. Painful
sinking across pit of chest and a feeling of sickness that kept her awake the greater part of the night. Writhing
in agony, unable to keep anything long on stomach, better by warm food, worse by cold drinks.
MIND - Hateful. Depression and desire for suicide.
Abdomen - Hardness and distention of abdomen, with frequent belching of mouthfuls of offensive flatus. Wind
rolling in balls from side to side. Obliged to loosen clothing.
Limbs - Legs and feet go to sleep on sitting. Legs and feet swollen, preventing walking. Legs swollen, great
red streaks and patches coursing along them. Right leg felt bruised and sore, later, angry and
Ornithogalum umbellatum red. Creepy feeling in legs keeps him awake at night.
Mouth - Tongue red, coated towards back. Nasty taste in morning.
Rectum - Constipation. Diarrhea, which ameliorates.
Sleep - Great difficulty in going to sleep because of acreepy feeling in limbs. Sleep disturbed by pains. Waking
 in perspiration at night. Wandering dreams.
Stomach - Loss of appetite. Painful sinking across epigastrium. Agonizing feeling in chest and stomach,
starting from pylorus with flatus that rolls in balls from one side to the other. Pains increased when food
passes pyloric outlet. Frequent belching of offensive flatus. Phlegm retchings and loss of weight. Vomiting
of coffee-ground looking matter. Gastric ulceration with hemorrhage.
COMMENTS - For stomach cancer (Hydr., Cad-s.), stomach ulcers, or a history of ulcers followed by stomach
cancer. Stomach cancer after a vaccination. The abdomen is distended and hardened. Writhing in agony from
stomach pain. Keynote belching. Emaciation (Hydr.). Used in the Bach Flower system for shock.
In his “Cancer and Cancer Symptoms” Dr. Cooper published several cases of cancer helped by Orni. Cooper
particularly insisted on his method being followed: a dose of a single drop being allowed to act until all trace of
its action has disappeared.
Cooper noted the case of a man named George, 40, who suffered from stomach cancer. His father had died
of a stomach ulcer at 73. He was sent to the cancer hospital in London. They began to operate, but abandoned
the operation because of overwhelming numbers of adhesions.
Cooper first saw him July 22, 1898. The patient was writhing in agony on his bed, unable to keep anything
down. He was better by some warm foods, worse by cold drinks. The pains were worse at night.
Cooper gave one drop of Orni. tincture on July 23 at 6:00, this was followed by an aggravation of great pains
and the patient was frantic until 3:00 a.m. At 1:00 p.m. the next day he had a bowel movement.
Then he developed flatulence and pain, and was given Carb-v. 3x as an acute, which cured those symptoms.
Three days later, Cooper saw the patient and the pain that was in his stomach had begun spreading out to the
rest of his body.
A second dose of Orni. was given on the evening of July 28. Immediately after taking that dose, he vomited a
black, jelly-like substance that greatly relieved the pains and generally improved his energy and appetite. From
that time on there was steady progress.
On August 29th, the patient reported that he was getting some pain in the lower abdomen. He had difficulty
getting to sleep and he had started getting creeping sensations in his legs.
He repeated a dose on September 9. On September 18, he reported that he was sleeping better, there was
more pain in the legs, but it was not so bad, and there were slight pains in the stomach. His appetite and
energy were improved. On September 23, his right leg felt bruised and began to swell. He started choking on
food. He was given another dose.
Some flatulence returned. In a few days, the man came to Cooper's office in a great fright. Both his legs were
swollen with red streaks. Believing these were to do with the rapid elimination of the cancer. Dr. Cooper thought
he was being too aggressive in the case, so he gave no medicine. The man was astonished.
The legs became swollen and inflamed, then returned to normal. In July 1901, Cooper visited his patient to
find him in good health without any signs of cancer or pain.
In the same volume, Cooper reproduced from H. W. (April, 1898) cases of ulceration of the stomach in elderly
women cured with the same remedy.
Miss J., 50, was a thin, drawn-featured woman. Her sister died of stomach cancer. She had vomited blood
fifteen years ago and had been subject to gastric pains since. Pains in stomach with sickness. Vomited two or
three times a day. Felt a pressure in every nerve of body, sometimes in one part, sometimes in another, with
pain across
Ornithogalum umbellatum the chest. Pain at night, or after food and sometimes on an empty stomach.
She had a great deal of wind and sometimes a swollen feeling across the lower chest. Occasional heartburn
with rising of food. Nasty canker taste in the morning. Could not sleep from the pains, had wandering dreams.
Bowels were confined.
Orni. tincture was given, one dose, on November 6. On November 13, the patient was seen again. Symptoms
had moderated, vomiting ceased. A new symptom appeared, “wakes in perspiration at night.” That diminished
by November 27. Pains better, “gets cold before the pains.” No heartburn, still a nasty taste and confined
bowel. The dose was repeated.
The day after this dose, the bowels loosened with general relief. This went on, increasing under more doses
of the remedy, until the patient regained almost perfect health and was quite changed in appearance.
Mrs. K., 62, had been seized with profuse vomiting of blood eighteen months before. Since then she lived on
slops and Quaker oats. Lately, she spat up clots. Whenever she turns in bed she “feels as if a bag of water
turns also.” Feet and legs swollen, unable to walk with ease. A brother is said to have died of cancer.
On January 12, 1898, one dose of Orni. in tincture was given. On January 23, she was so much better that
she could hardly believe the effect. The oppression of the stomach was gone. The “fluid sack” that rolled about
in her seemed to go down and she felt nothing of it. She felt cheery and light. On February 10, there was a
 threatened return of the symptoms, but another dose permanently removed them.
Cooper added the account of how he was led to think of Orni. in cancer. “My acquaintance with it in cancer
cases was due to the very distinctive disturbance it produced in a woman very sensitive to all alliaceous flavor-
ing substances in food. The dose was taken at midday and the same evening distention of the stomach and
duodenum came on.
“Also frequent belching of mouthfuls of offensive flatus obliging her to loosen her clothes. This was
accompanied by the most hateful depression of spirits and desire for suicide. A feeling of complete prostration
and painful sinking across the pit of the chest. A feeling of sickness that kept her awake the greater part of the
night and that did not pass off for several days.
“The subject of this disturbance was about fifty-four years of age of quite a sanguine temperament inclined to
the enfeebled digestion and with a history of pleuritic seizures and a possible tubercular tendency, but
otherwise not subject to any settled form of disease. Since the medicinal thrill above recorded, her general
strength, digestion and capacity for the enjoyment of life have manifestly improved.
“The Ornith. in those sensitive to it goes at once to the pylorus, causes painful spasmodic contraction of it and
distends the duodenum with flatus, its pains being invariably increased when the food attempts to pass the
pyloric outlet of the stomach.”
Clarke had several opportunities to confirm Cooper's observations on the action of Orni. for cancer the
stomach, including the case of Mr. W., 44, who came to him in August, 1899. Both parents had died of cancer.
He had a weak stomach for two or three years and was wasting. He had to get up in the night to vomit, bringing
up green and yellow liquid.
He had much flatus, “swells up in balls of wind.” His abdomen was large and hard, with a rather large spleen.
Venous zigzag. Stools were loose, watery, slate-colored. Urine was scanty, dark. He had been vaccinated
three or four times.
He made good progress under Thuj. 30c once a week, the vomiting ceased and he began to put on flesh. He
developed an offensive body odor, which disappeared under Sulph. 30c, but on October 13, symptoms were
rather worse. He had some distention, wind did not pass freely. Rumbling before stool. Balls of wind rolled
about, but not as badly as at first. Frothy, acid vomiting, which relieved.
Clarke then gave Orni. tincture, one dose, repeated three weeks later with manifest improvement in the
symptoms. His body was much less hard and distended. Sleep and appetite were good, cessation of vomiting
and gain of three pounds in weight. When he returned, the symptoms were different and another remedy was
required and then he considered himself cured.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) All-s„ in flatulent indigestion. (2) Abies-n., Cham., Chin., Carb-v., Lyc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Oscillococcinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oscilloc. Oscillococcinum. Lysate fromOscillococcus. Virus. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Aches. Anxiety. Bronchitis. Conjunctivitis. Ear pain. Epidemic, influenza. Fears.
Headaches.Influenza. Gastro-intestinal disorders. Mastoiditis. Otitis. Rhinitis. Sinusitis. Varicose ulcer.
HOMEOPATHIC - In the year 1925, Joseph Roy is believed to have observed in some conditions of a culture
the existence of a germ animated by an oscillating movement. He named the nosode Oscillococcinum because
of this fact. These researches helped him to describe a remedy of which the clinical experiments in the
infections of influenza were carried out in particular by Paul Chavanon.
Oscilloc. was developed by Boiron Laboratory in France. Pierre Schmidt said Oscilloc. is for “influenza at the
beginning as a preventive, as well as during convalescence”
Influenza of all types, especially in the earlier stages. Epidemic influenza. B ursting headaches and muscle
aching. Gastro-intestinal troubles with the influenza. Beginning of influenza, rhinitis and otitis. Tendency to
get influenza.
Given early it is very efficacious. To obtain good results in a case which begins and to cut short the
manifestations of influenza, it is necessary to use one dose of Oscillococcinum 200c every 2 to 3 hours or
repeat only if necessary.
Anxiety, paleness, chill. Sensitiveness to barometric weather changes. Tuberculous patients sensitive to cold.
Asthenia, hyperthermia. Eye and nasal catarrh. Bronchial congestion. Painful congestion of the ear drum.
Schmidt noted it for “Mastoiditis, at the beginning of a disease which does not develop.”
MIND - Subjects with fixed ideas, obsessions. Obstinate. Agony, anxious without any motive. A busy body.
Maniac, cannot bear disorder. Fear of dirt, of being polluted. Has the need to wash his hands very often and
is afraid of giving his hand to others for the fear of pollution, contagion.
Abdomen - Abdominal cramping pains followed by fetid diarrhea. Pains in the appendix region.
 Ears - Pains sometimes as if from needles in one or both ears. Tympanum red and swollen. Mastoiditis.
Diminution of hearing acuity.
Eyes - Yellow conjunctiva. Conjunctivitis of influenza. Eye catarrh.
Face - Pain in the frontal and maxillary region.
Food - Can digest neither milk nor eggs.
Head - Bursting headaches. Headache with considerable throbbing.
Kidneys - Turbid urine, less abundant, deep color. Painful urination.
Lungs - Muco-purulent expectoration with humid cough.
Modalities - Better by heat, rest. Worse by milk, eggs.
Mouth - Tongue white.
Nose - Nasal voice. Nasal catarrh. Stuffed nose, nasal obstruction, sneezing. Serous discharge from the nose,
then mucopurulent.
Rectum - Constipation.
Skin - Varicose type of ulcers of the legs.
Stomach - Swelling of the stomach. Putrid regurgitations. Vomiting of water or food.
Temperature - Bruised sensation, chill, hyperthermia.
Throat - Aphonia, dry painful cough.
RELATIONS - Eup-per. is to be associated with it. Compare: ( 1 )Eup-per., Gels., Pyrog..Bapt., Ars., Influ. (2)
Gaulphimia glauca - Hyperse-
cretion of the nasal and ocular mucous, sneezing, hypersensitivity to change of weather. (3) Gelinsoga
purviflora - Morning headache, makes mistakes when writing numbers and letters, stuffed nose, augmentation
of diuresis, joint pains, lassitude, feels as if bruised. (4) Gink. . Pale face, drawn traits, numbness and chill.
Laryngeal irritation with cough, frontal and left supra - órbita pain. (4) Luf-op. - Frontal-occipital headache,
acute or chronic inflammation of the mucus membrane of the nasal fossa, lassitude and bodily fatigue.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Osmium Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - osm. Osmium metallicum. Osmium metal. Osmium tetroxide. The element (At. Wt. 190.3).
Trituration of the precipitatedmetal. Osmium acidum. Dilutions with absolutely pure water. Historical dose:
Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Bronchitis. Colds. Coryza. Cough, spasmodic. Eczema. Erections. Glaucoma.
Headache. Hernia. Herpes iris. Larynx, pain. Penis, sores. Pollutions. Postnasal bleeding. Post-nasal, growths.
Spermatic cords, pains. Sternum, pain. Syphilis. Syphilitic eruptions. Testicles, pains. Tongue, sore. Trachea,
pain.
HOMEOPATHIC - Osmium is a metal of the platinum group in association with which it is always found. It is
the heaviest of them all and the most refractory, having never been fused. It derives its name from the pungent
odor of the fumes of osmic acid, which are evolved in the process of separating platinum from its ore.
The odor of Osmium closely resembles that of chlorine, as also do its irritating effect on the respiration mucus
membrane. The odor imparted to the secretions is various, it makes the urine smell like violets, the belchings
like radishes, the axillary sweat like garlic.
Triturations of the pure metal have been proved. The symptoms of the metal and of the acid are taken together.
Osm. affects the respiratory tract, especially the trachea. Irritation and catarrh of respiratory organs. Pain in
trachea.
Pains go up and down. Crawling on back and shoulders. Increases and gives odor to local perspiration.
Albuminuria. Eczema. Causes adhesion of the nail fold.
MIND - Morose, irritable, impatient. Weeping mood, screaming with cough. Weak, gives up. Consciousness of
mental weakness, misplaces words. Thoughts of accidents having happened to others. Disinclination for work.
Abdomen - Distention of stomach and abdomen in evening, with difficult passage of flatus. Rumblings. Pain
in groins, on coughing the pain extended into testicles. Weakness in groins towards spermatic cords. Pressure
on inguinal rings. Constriction in epigastrium before dinner.
Back - Crawling on back and shoulders. Pressive pain in back and loins. Pain in sacral region. Peculiar pain
extending from scapula to sacral region, worse motion and cough.
Chest - Oppression, better deep inspiration. Tightness. Dryness in chest. Sticking near left lower rib. Pain
beneath sternum on coughing, extending to sides of chest. Sternum is sore, painful to touch, independent of
cough. Shooting up and down in sternum. Wandering pneumonia.
Ears - Earache evenings, first right then left ear. Perforations with irritation of meatus. Itching in the ears,
 profuse nasal catarrh. Tingling and pain in right ear. Ringing in right ear. Deafness, ears pain when nose is
blown, mouth open, sleep noisy.
Eyes - Increase in intra-ocular tension, dim sight, photophobia. Conjunctivitis. Glaucoma with iridescent vision.
Green colors surround candlelight. Greenish or rainbow colors around the light. Violent supra and infra-
orbital neuralgia, violent pains and lachrymation.
Food - Aversion to cocoa, coffee and tobacco, disgust at their odor.
Head - Feels as if a band around head. Dull, heavy headache. Violent headache above and under the eyes.
Sharp bewildering pain in center of forehead. Aching in base of brain and jaws at night. Pain in vertex and
occiput, worse throwing head backward. Falling off of hair (Kali-c., Fl-ac.).
Heart - Anxious palpitations. Pulse rapid.
Kidneys - Bright's disease. Diminution or suppression of the urinary secretions. Urine is albuminous, strong-
scented, smelling of violets. Urine is high-colored, full of bile, dark brown and scanty. Deposits bright-red
sediment.
Limbs - Heaviness and weariness of limbs, worse knees. Twitching of fingers with spasmodic cough. Fold of
skin remains attached to growing nail. Axillary sweat smells like garlic.
Lungs - Sensitive air passages. Dread of breathing, sore pain when air enters lungs. Moist rales on breathing
and in larynx. Convulsive cough, feels as though membrane were torn from larynx. Noisy, dry, hard, cough
in violent short bursts, coming from low down, shaking the whole body. Spasmodic cough, sounds as if
coughing in an empty tube with torn loose feeling and sticky sputum. Twitching of fingers with spasmodic
cough.
Male - Steady aching in glans penis. Violent pain on the point of penis and prepuce. Pain in testes and
spermatic cord. Pain in testicles, preventing sleep. Erections every morning, earlier and harder.
Modalities - Open air helps the smarting in eyes. Worse coughing, talking, riding, touch. Worse in evening.
Cough worse until midnight. Open air aggravates coryza, cough.
Mouth - Aching in jaws, pain in muscles of mastication. Mouth sticky and pasty. Copious salivation. Taste of
blood, metallic, cigars cannot be smoked, because they provoke cough and worse the rawness in larynx, taste
blunted.
Nose - Nose and larynx sensitive to air. Full feeling in nose. Coryza, fluent with a feeling of stoppage. Snuffling.
Small lumps of phlegm from posterior sinuses.
Rectum - Constipated. Stool hard, then soft, mushy, frequent. Bilious stools with burning at anus. Burning in
anus during and after stool. Tendency to hemorrhoids.
Sensations - As of a band around head. As if he had swallowed broken stones. Cough as if caused by
resonance of contiguous parts. As if insects crawling on back and shoulders. Legs and feet as if too full.
Skin - Irritated skin. Eczema. Itching pimples. Bromidrosis, sweat in axilla smelling of garlic, worse evening
and night. Fold remains attached to growing nail.
Sleep - Sleepless. Restless sleep, with painful dreams. Sleepiness is overpowering. Sleep heavy, interrupted
by nightmare. Dreams of fire, confused, but not frightful. Dreams of activity and of serious events. Dreams not
remembered.
Stomach - Feels full of broken stones or lumps. Qualmishness and extreme discomfort with dull pain and
heaviness in pit of stomach. Belchings smelling like radishes. Nausea in morning. Vomiting of watery mucus
of the odor and taste of the acid. Chronic vomiting, with pressure in stomach.
Temperature - Shivering, worse back. Fever, with difficult respiration, fever, with hot and dry skin. Sweat in
axilla, smelling of garlic, worse evening and night.
Throat - Acute laryngitis, cough andexpec- toration of tough, stringy mucus. Talking causes pain in the larynx.
Hoarseness, sore sternum.
Tongue - Tongue coated, red stripe in middle, fissured, one spot denuded. Tongue edges rough and covered
with pimples. Tongue sensitive to touch when eating and drinking. Bad taste to coffee.
COMMENTS - The respiratory tract is irritated and pained from beginning to end. The nostrils and larynx are
sensitive to cold air. Pain in larynx, trachea and in and under sternum on coughing. Talking causes pain in
larynx.
Cough convulsive in paroxysms, hollow sounding as if one coughed into an empty tube, caused by irritation in
larynx or low down in chest. Violent headaches, affecting the base of the brain.
Skin irritation, irritating eruptions, eczematous and herpetic. In the provings, the erections were severe almost
to priapism and the ejaculations were longer-lasting and more copious than normal.
A woman, 62 to whom Clarke once gave Osm. 2x for a spasmodic cough with pain in the head had a severe
aggravation, the headache taking this form: “Sharp pain in center of forehead going through to back, better by
hard pressure on forehead.” She discontinued Osm. and in two or three days that pain went away, leaving only
 an ordinary headache. The cough was not relieved.
S. Norton suggested that Osm. may be a remedy in many cases of glaucoma.
Cooper had a case of a girl of 14 with postnasal growths who improved rapidly under Osm., 3x, but was seized
with exhaustion, then under Hydr-ac., got quite well.
In one of Blackley's cases, a child born during the time that his father was under the influence of Osm.
developed eczema, though none of the previously born children were eczematous. The kidneys were affected
in another of Blackley's cases, incipient nephritis being set up.
M. Boger cured a case in which there was pain in both directions, “Stitching pain upward in left spermatic cord.
Creeping sensation downwards in left spermatic cord. Weakness in calves, they give out while walking.”
Shootings in the sternum are up and down.
In another case of a man, 44, syphilitic was cured of “dull, steady pain in hypo- gastrium, sore to pressure.
Steady aching in glans penis.”
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Sulfuretted hydrogen, Phos-ac., Sil. - swollen gums. Hep. and Psor. - pain in
larynx, Bell, and Merc. - laryngeal catarrh. Compare: ( 1 ) Arg-n., Sei., Mang. (2) Irid., Tell., Thal., Plat., Pall.
(3) In eyes and lungs, Chlor., Brom. (4) Skin of nails, Fl-ac. (5) Itch, Sulph. (6) Coryza, cough with pain in
larynx, All-c. but it has better in open air. (7) Eruptions, Ars., Rhus-t.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Osteo-Arthritic-Nosode
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - o-a-n. Osteo-arthritic-nosode. Made from the synovial liquid of arthritic joints. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Joint, pains. Osteoarthritis. Rheumatism.
HOMEOPATHIC - A proving of the Osteo- arthritic-nosode of hip was read in the 18th All India Homeopathic
conference at Madras on lOOct., 1970. The O-A-N. that originated from Dr. Foubister, comes from the knee of
a patient suffering from an osteo-arthritic affection, and the other stock from the hip of a similar case.
State of stupor, indifference to others. Extreme weakness with somnolence in the afternoon and profound
sleep. Weakness, worse in the morning when waking up. Great desire for sleep, with deep sleep at night.
MIND - Apathy. State of indifference. Nonchalance. Idleness, no desire to work. Indecision, needs relaxing.
Irritability, worse towards evening.
Eyes - Styes of upper eyelid of the left eye.
Kidneys - Highly colored urine and less abundant, worse at noon.
Limbs - Pain in the right shoulder. Temporary redness and swelling of the right shoulder. Redness and swelling
of the right forearm and right wrist. Muscular pain of the right hip. Pain of the Achilles tendon. Pain aggravated
by the first movement, ameliorated by continued movement.
Male - Increase of sexual desire in men. Furuncle on the scrotum.
Modalities - Aggravation by the first movement, at night. Better by prolonged movement. Worse right side.
Skin - Furuncles.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc., Calc-p.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Ostrya Virginiana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ost. Ostrya virginiana. Ironwood. Hop-hornbeam. Lever-wood. N. O. Cupulifere. Betulaceae.
Tincture of heart wood. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Headache, dull. Head, numb. Intermittent fever. Liver disorders. Lumbago. Malaria.
Nausea.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ost. is sometimes regarded as a variety of the common Hornbeam naturalized in America,
though native to southern Europe. The chief difference between them is that Ost. vulg. has pendulous catkins,
and Ost. virg., upright. The wood is exceedingly hard and heavy.
The preparations of which the provings by Burt and others were made were from the wood. Marked action on
the liver with the usual dull headache and pain in back and shoulders, cutting, sinking pains in abdomen.
Nervous, languid, weak, uneasy. Very nervous with dull headache.
Increased appetite, hunger wakes the patient at 4 a.m. Sinking at the epigastrium. Sickening pains. Black
stools. Bilious conditions and intermittent fever. Anemia from malaria.
Abdomen - Dull pains in right lobe of liver with sour belchings. Retraction of umbilicus. Rumbling, flatus, pain
waking him in night.
Back - Back so painful, can hardly turn in bed, cannot sit up (better from Macro., Bry., Nux-v). Dull pain in
 whole dorsal region, extending to left hypochondrium. Constant lumbar and sacral pain, worse stooping or
walking.
Ears - Drawing pain deep in left ear.
Face - Moist freckles in face, head and hands.
Food - Appetite greatly increased, woke with hunger at 4 a.m. Loss of appetite.
Head - Dull headache with numb, prickly feeling in head, face and hands, worse head. Dull, frontal headache
with nausea. Right side headache, morning.
Limbs - Aching, dull pains in arms and legs. Fine drawing rheumatic pains in left fingers, morning. Drawing
pains in right ankle.
Modalities - Worse moving, walking, stooping. Worse 6 a.m., 4 a.m., 3 p.m.
Mouth - Tongue yellow, coated at the root. Taste is coppery, slimy, sweet, slimy, bitter, rough. Boring and
sharp pain in right lower molars.
Rectum - Rectum feels sore, protruded feeling after stool.
Stomach - Sour stomach. Nausea and distress after riding in cold air. Burning distress in epigastrium. Hard
sickening pains in epigastric and umbilical region, awaking him at night. Sinking in epigastrium. Frequent
nausea with dull, frontal headache. Sickening pains.
Stool - Loose stools, bilious with tenesmus and straining, loose without tenesmus. Tenesmus followed by
diarrhea stool. Mushy stool with burning at anus and tenesmus. Black stools, dry lumps.
COMMENTS - Allen mentioned "Tongue coated yellow at root. Loss of appetite for breakfast and dinner.
Frequent nausea with the dull frontal headache.”
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Macro., Bry., Nux-v. (lumbago). Compare: (1) Waking in night hungry, Ign., Lyc.
(2) Black stools, Lept.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Ovary Gland
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-ov. ovar. Ovary gland. Oophorinum. Ovininum. Ovarian extract. A sarcode. Trituration of
expressed juice of ovary gland of sheep or cow. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne, rosacea. Hormonal, imbalance. Hot flushings. Infantile, genitalis. Infertility. Menopause.
Menstrual, disorders. Nervousness. Oophorectomy. Ovaries, disorders. Ovaries, cysts. Ovaries, tumors.
Prurigo. Seborrhea. Sexual, weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ov. has been used with much success in cases of suffering following excision of the ovaries
(Sep.) and for the
menopausal sufferings of women. Clarke had good results with it in such cases in the lower triturations.
Ov. has been suggested as a remedy in ovarian cysts. Menopausal disturbances in general. Cutaneous
disorders and acne rosacea. Prurigo.
Female - Menses are frequent, too early. Menses are clotted, coagulated, copious. Menses of short duration.
Infertility. Hot flashes. Menopause. Infantile genitalis.
COMMENTS - Characteristic amelioration from the menses, all symptoms better during menses (Lach., Zinc.).
Generally associated with ovarian conditions, often after removal of ovaries (Staph., Phos.). Ovarian cysts
(Thuj., Sil.), when nothing else works. Useful for menopausal symptoms, particularly hot flashes (Sep., Puls.,
Thuj.).
Severe hormonal acne (Sep., Puls., Thuj.). Spacey. Indecision, difficulty deciding who they are, about changing
careers, about health.
E. Saalfeld, in view of Landau's observations on the effect of Ov. on the nervous sufferings of women at
menopause, gave Ov. to women suffering from acne rosacea and other skin disorders of menopause.
A woman, 20, after a double oophorectomy, had lichen-like eczema. This was relieved by Ov. as well as the
accompanying nervous symptoms and adiposity.
Saalfeld also obtained good results in some non-menopausal cases, including acne and seborrhea in chlorotic
women. He had a case of prurigo that had lasted from childhood in a woman of 26. In this case, the itching
was better for a short time after the period.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Orchitinum, Testicular extract - after ovariotomy, sexual weakness, senile decay.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Ovi Gallinae Pellicula
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ovi-g-p. Ovi gallinae pellicula. Egg shell membrane. Membrane of the shell of a hen's egg. The
 fresh membrane is triturated in 95% alcohol, allowed to digest several days and then potentized (Swan).
Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Backache. Catarrh. Coryza. Debility. Heart, oppression. Hip, pain. Leucorrhea.
Menstruation, irregular. Ovaries, pains. Post-nasal catarrh. Pruritus vulvae. Throat, sore. Uterus,
displacements, retroverted. Vertebra, pain. Vulva, soreness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Historically, egg shells were used powdered, fresh, or roasted, in the treatment of oxyuris
vermicularis. Swan prepared the membrane. As an ovarian product, it might be expected that all parts of the
egg should have an action on the ovaries, and that eggs would have a stimulating effect on the sexual
functions. The provings confirmed this relation.
Sudden onset and ceasing. Sudden pains. Bearing-down sensation. Pushing and rushing feeling in womb, as
if blood might rush out in torrents. Sensation as if something turned over inside.
Debility. Heat in sacrum, the rest of the body being cool. Pain in heart and left ovary. Backache and pain in left
hip. Intolerance of bands on wrists, arms, waist, etc. Jerkings on going to sleep and in sleep.
Causations - Over-exertion. Strain.
Modalities - Dyspnea better bending backward, jarring or beating breast. Worse by movement, reaching, lifting
arms, descending stairs, over-exerting. Worse pressure and touch, pressure of clothing, at full moon. Worse
before, during and after menses, though some symptoms were better when flow appeared.
COMMENTS - This preparation was made by Swan. He noted that it has an ancient reputation for “immoderate
flux of the menses” (Calc.) and for nocturnal bedwetting.
The first prover was a young woman, a patient of J. C. Boardman, who was known to be unable to bear any
extra exertion, but the details of this were not known until after she had taken the first dose of the Ovi-g-p.
100,000c sent by Swan.
Some years before, she had felt something “give way” in the groin while shoveling snow, bringing on a left
ovarian pain, extending down the left limb. The trouble was suddenly removed after the dose. The
sensitiveness to exertion never returned, though the dose created much disturbance of the generative
functions before it had finished its action.
The symptoms of a second prover, a married woman who took the Ovi-g-p. 30c, confirmed the symptoms
experienced by the first. This prover had also hemorrhage from the rectum, incontinence of urine while
sneezing or coughing, and post-nasal catarrh.
Yingling contributed the case of H. E., 42, blonde, who had a dull, hard, heavy aching in region of heart,
generally about apex, extending at times to left ovarian region.
Occasionally a cutting which extended to base of heart and prevented breathing, after the cutting a sensation
as if something went “thud,” after which pain seemed to recommence at apex. At times, heavy aching in base
of heart, which made breathing very difficult. Only bending backward alleviated respiration.
Ovi-g-p. (a preparation of Fincke's) was given, one dose, dry on the tongue. In a very few minutes the pain
was all gone. “Feels splendidly since taking the remedy.” Without knowing what it was, said she had “a taste
of fresh eggs in the mouth since taking the powder.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc., Naja. (2) Ova tosta - Tosta preparata, Roastedegg-shells. Calc-o-t. - has
leucorrhea and backache. A feeling as if the spine were broken and wired or tied together with a string. Pain
of cancer. Warts. (3) Egg vaccine for asthma. Much interest is shown in Dr. Fritz Talbot's method to cure one
form of asthma in children by the use of egg vaccine. Asthma due to susceptibility of the protein substance in
eggs can be cured by immunizing against egg poisons by repeated doses of egg white. After the skin has been
cleansed with soap and alcohol the egg-white is rubbed into a slight scratch.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Oxalicum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ox-ac. Oxalicum acidum. Oxalic acid. Sorrel acid. Hydrogen oxalate. Trituration. Tincture.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Angina, pectoris. Aphonia. Backaches. Bedwetting. Chest, disorders. Cholera,
infantum. Convulsion. Deltoid, rheumatism. Dyspnea. Eyes, disorders. Gastrodynia. Gout. Gravel. Hernias.
Hives. Indigestion. Kidney, stones. Meningitis. Myelitis. Nails, blue. Neuralgias. Neurasthenia. Nose,
disorders. Numbness. Oxaluria. Pains, severe. Paralysis. Pregnancy, sickness. Side, pain. Spasms.
Spernuitic cord, pain. Stomach, disorders. Tetanus. Testes, pains. Tongue, disorders. Tuberculosis. Urine,
abnormal. Voice, altered.
HOMEOPATHIC - Although certain oxalates are constant constituents of vegetable food and of the human
body, the acid itself is a violent poison when taken internally, producing gastro-enteritis, motor paralysis,
 collapse, stupor and death.
If Op. is the painless remedy, Ox-ac. may be considered its antithesis. It causes the most excruciating pains
beyond description, which are all worse when the patient thinks of them.
Thinking of pains and conditions will bring them on when they are not actually present. Symptoms are worse
by touch (small spots on head), slightest touch causes excruciating pain. Worse motion andthink- ing of
pains.
Neuralgias. Excruciating pains like lightning in streaks, burning in spots. Violent pains in spots (Kali-bi.).
Rheumatism of left side. Periodical disorders. Periodical remissions.
Neurasthenia. Weak, cold, livid and numb all over, worse lower limbs. Influences the spinal cord and produces
motor
Oxalicum acidum
paralysis. Paralysis of the left side from spinal meningitis.
Spasmodic symptoms of throat and chest. Angina pectoris, sharp, sharp pain in left lung coming on
suddenly, depriving of breath. Tuberculosis. Severe back and kidney pains. Kidney stones.
After eating pains at navel, colic, rumbling in abdomen, urging to stool, weakness. Pain in stomach, better from
eating. Gnawing in stomach better from soup. Cannot eat strawberries, severe allergies. Sugar, coffee and
wine disagree. Worse from shaving.
MIND - Exhilarated, quicker thought and action. Nervous and sleepless. Symptoms worse by thinking of
them, thinking of the conditions will bring them on when they are not actually present.
Abdomen - Stitching pains in the liver, better deep breathing. Burning in small spots in abdomen. Pain in
upper part of abdomen after eating, with much flatulence. Chronic inflammation of bowels. Colic about the
navel or involuntary muddy brown stools better lying. Flatus passes with difficulty. Fainting and vomiting during
stool.
Back - Numb pricking in back. Backaches, feels numb. Back feels too weak to hold the body. Cold creeps up
spine.
Chest - Chest fixed. Sharp pain through lower region of left lung, extending down to epigastrium. Left lung
painful.
Eyes - Severe pain in eyes, feel expanded. Hyperesthesia of retina. Small, and especially linear objects,
appear larger and more distant than they are. Sight vanishes with the nosebleed.
Face - Pale, cold, livid. Feeling of heat.
Food - Cannot eat strawberries, severe allergies. Sugar, coffee and wine disagree.
Head - Headache, before and during stool. Band like sensation about the head, as of a screw behind each
ear, better after stool. Sense of heat. Numb pricking in occiput. Sore tender spot on scalp.
Heart - Precordial pains which dart to the left shoulder. Angina pectoris, sharp, sharp pain in left lung
coming on suddenly, depriving of breath. Palpitations and dyspnea in organic heart disease.worse when
thinking of it. Palpitations worse lying down. Pulse feeble. Beats of heart intermit when thinking of it. Aortic
insufficiency. Fluttering in heart. Heart symptoms alternate with aphonia.
Kidneys - Severe kidney pains. Kidney stones. Must urinate when thinking of it. Frequent and copious
urination. Oxaluria. Burning in urethra and pain in glans when urinating.
Limbs - Multiple sclerosis. Myelitis. Muscular prostration. Numb, tingling. Numbness extends from shoulders
to fingertips. Lower limbs blue, cold insensible. Weak trembling, hands and feet. Hands cold as if dead.
Drawing and sharp pains shooting down limbs. Pains start from spine and extend through limbs. Sharp pains
in various parts, jerking pains. Wrist painful, as if sprained (Ulm.). Pain in fleshy part of thumb (right).
Liver - Stitches in liver.
Lungs - Spasmodic breathing with constriction of larynx and chest. Dyspnea, short, jerking inspirations.
Burning sensation from throat down. Left lung painful. Hoarseness. Paralysis of the tensors of vocal cord.
Aphonia.
Male - Seminal vesiculitis. Neuralgic pains in spermatic cord, worse from slightest motion. Testes, throb or
feel crushed. Testicles feel contused and heavy.
Modalities - Better after stools. Change of position helps pain in back. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse
from light, mental exertion, motion, left side, slightest touch, shaving, cold. Worse from strawberries, sour
fruits, grapes. Worse evening, night and early morning. Worse from being aroused about 3 a.m. with gastric
and abdominal pain. Lying down causes swimming sensation.
Mouth - Sour taste. Belchings, with difficult swallowing.
Rectum - Diarrhea from coffee.
Sensations - Sensation as if all blood had left the brain. As if blood in head was coursing upward and outward.
As from a screw behind each ear. Hypogastrium as if bound. Back as if broken or bruised. Wrist as if sprained.
 Hands as if dead. Jerking pains
like short stitches, confined to small spots, lasting only a few seconds. Sensation as from chafing during
shaving.
Skin - Sensitive, soreness, smarting, worse shaving. Mottled, marbled in circular patches. Perspires easily.
Stomach - Emptiness with gnawing, compelling one to eat. Burning pain goes upwards, worse slightest touch,
sugar. Cannot eat strawberries. Violent pain in epigastrium, discharge of flatus relieves. Gastralgia,
heartburn, sensation of coldness below epigastrium. Bitter and sour eructation, worse at night.
Throat - Hoarseness with cardiac derangements. Voice altered. Low voice. Nervous aphonia (Coca, Hydr-
ac.). Aphonia from paralysis of vocal cords.
Vertigo - Confusion and vertigo. Vertigo, swimming sensation on lying down, while looking out of window.
COMMENTS - Ox-ac., the chief constituent of Sorrel (Rumx-a.) and Wood Sorrel (Oxal.), exists in plants that
are ordinarily deemed anti-scorbutic and are remarkable for the grateful acidity of their herbage.
Ox-ac. is said to enter largely into the inspissated juice of the Clover (Trif-p.) which formed Thomson's “Cancer
plaster,” and which is strongly escharotic.
Inspissated solutions of sorrel have been used successfully as local applications for epithelioma and with a
solution of Ox-ac. and of Tannic acid, applied locally. With a solution of 5 grains to 3 ounces of water. Cooper
removed troublesome small nevi in infants upon the face and elsewhere, using it for weeks or even months.
Cooper removed a large patch of erythematous lupus on the cheek. From this it would appear, taking into
account that Ox-ac. produces wart-like growths, it may have a beneficial influence, locally and probably
internally as well, upon epithelial proliferations of the cuticle.
In an interesting study of Ox-ac., J. W. Ellis cited a fatal case of poisoning recorded by Boericke through
exposure of the hands to a saturated solution used for chemical purposes.
The symptoms were intense pains in head, hyperesthesia, especially to light. Spasms of pain down limbs,
along throat muscles and through spermatic cord. Sensitive spots on spine.
Excruciating pain in lower back and loss of power in the lower limbs shows an unmistakable action on the
spinal cord and its meninges. These symptoms are better seen in less severe cases of poisoning. In animals
poisoned with Ox-ac. the first symptom is stiffness of hind limbs. .
Farrington summed up the indications of Ox-ac. in spinal affections, including weak loins, hips, legs, numb
back, numb limbs. Limbs blue and cold, weak and numb, worse going up stairs. Limbs stiff, paroxysm of
dyspnea (as in spinal meningitis). Pains in small spots, especially linear spots. Pains worse when thinking of
them. Erections with dullness in occiput. Left-side rheumatism.
Sharp shooting pain in left lung and heart, extending down to epigastrium. In afternoon, stitches several times
in left lung. Sharp, sharp pain in lower lobe of left lung, coming on so suddenly that it deprives him of breath
for a few seconds. Sore sticking in chest extending back to between scapula.
Pleurisy, pneumonia, tuberculosis. The heart may be paralyzed, becomes flaccid or distended with blood.
Angina pectoris. Coldness of surface, numbness. Mottled skin, blue nails. Generally left sided.
Sugar aggravates the stomach pain. Wine causes headache. Oxaluria, with backache, numbness. Frequent
ineffectual urging to stool, preceded by a sick, distressing feeling from navel downwards, worse when thinking
of it, worse from drinking coffee. Faintness and vomiting during stool. Pain in back better after stool.
John Moore reportd the case of a sea captain who suffered from indigestion. Two years before Moore saw him
he had to undergo an operation for strangulated hernia. Ever since he had been subject to pain in region of
navel coming on two hours after eating, accompanied by much flatulence and bitter and sour belchings.
Pain worse in night, arousing the patient 3 a.m. and keeping him awake. Burning sensation from throat
downwards to the region of the pain. The patient had always has a weak digestion and had met with many
severe accidents at sea.
He was given Ox-ac. 3c, two drops, an hour after meals. He was a little better the first night and after that slept
the night through and said he had not had so much comfort for years.
Bedwetting has been cured with Ox-ac. 6c in a blonde boy of six. The guiding symptom was “Sharp shooting
pain in left chest, close to sternum and parallel to it.”
C.     Walker told Clarke of a case of his in which the patient, an elderly, gouty man, was suddenly seized with
congestion of spinal meninges with great coldness, blueness and numbness with complete prostration of
strength. Ox-ac. 6c rapidly cured.
A patient of Clarke who used Ox-ac. in his work suffered from “Rheumatism of left side. Starting on falling
asleep. When actually at work, acidity.”
W. M. Butler gave great relief with Ox- ac. 3c. in a case of paraplegia, affecting first the right then the left leg
of a year's duration in an American woman, mother of four children.
In a few weeks the motor symptoms were better then the sensory. Sensation to heat and cold was restored,
 general tactile sensibility was improved. Some control was gained over bladder and rectum.
Hale cured a case of palpitation with action of heart irregular in force and rhythm, alternating with aphonia with
Ox-ac. 6c. It was a favorite remedy with S. A. Jones in cardiac trouble, occurring in highly “nervous” patients.
Ellis suggested that Ox-ac. corresponds to many cases of neurasthenia.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Carbonates of lime and magnesia. Lime water, antidote to poisoning of Ox-
ac.Compare;(l)Ars.. Colch., Arg-n., Pic-ac. (2) Cice.. Chickpea - Lithiasis, jaundice, liver affections, diuretic.
(3) Scol. - terrible pains in back and loins, extending down limbs, return periodically, commencing in head to
toes. Angina pectoris. Inflammation, pain and gangrene. Pustules and abscesses. (4) Caes. - Pain in lumbar
region and testicle. Headache, darting through temples. Diarrhea and colic. Languor. (5) Kali-ox. (6) In cholera
infantum, Ars., Ip., Verat. (7) In gastralgia, Colch. (8) In spinal disease, Pic-ac., Arg-m., Ph-ac. (9) Induration
of testicles. Puls. (10) Headache worse from wine, Zinc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Oxalis Acetosella
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-oxal. Oxalis acetosella. Wood sorrel. N. O. Geraniaceae. Great Britain. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
HERBAL - Diuretic, refrigerant. Reputed of value in febrile diseases, urinary affections, catarrh, and
hemorrhages. The herb may be infused with water or boiled in milk and administered freely, although excess
should be guarded against.
Joseph Miller said, “The juice, when clarified is a fine red color and makes a very agreeable syrup.”
RELATIONS - Compare: Ox-ac. Rumx-a.
REFERENCES - Potter.

name: Oxydendron Arboreum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oxyd. Oxydendron arboreum. Sorrel-tree. Sour-wood. Elk-tree. Andromeda arbórea. N. O.
Ericacee, tribe Andromedee. Rich woods of the Alleghenies. Tincture of leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ascites. Bladder stones. Dropsy. Prostatic enlargement.
HOMEOPATHIC - Oxyd. is the only species of its genus. It is an unproved remedy for dropsy, ascites and
anasarca. Deranged portal circulation. Prostatic enlargement. Suppressed urine. Bladder stones. Irritation of
neck of bladder.
COMMENTS - M. E. Douglass treated Mrs. H. for general dropsy, ascites and anasarca, which dated from an
attack of measles treated with ice-drinks and ice-applications seven months before.
When Douglass saw her, the urine was nearly suppressed, but contained very little albumen. Great difficulty
of breathing even when sitting, lying down impossible. Had to sit in one chair with feet in another. Menses
suppressed.
After the failure of Apoc. and several carefully chosen medicines, the legs having burst in several places,
Douglass was about to tap the abdomen, but before doing so put Oxyd. 3x in a tumbler of water and gave
three teaspoonfuls every three hours.
In forty eight hours the breathing was better and urine increased. Oxyd. was continued (with the exception of
three days during which Rhus-t. was given to combat erysipelas which had set in on left leg).
On the tenth day, the patient lay down on the bed and slept for three hours. Appetite increased, and in two
months she was quite free from dropsy and felt perfectly well though much emaciated.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ceref. - dropsy, Bright's disease, cystitis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oxyg. Oxygenium. Oxygen. Ozonum. Nascent Oxygen. Oxygen including ozone, which is
nascent oxygen. Oxygen (At. Wt. 16). Dilutions of distilled water charged with the gas. Dilutions. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Cancer. Canker, sores. Coryza. Cough. Diabetes. Influenza. Morphine, poisoning. Mouth,
sores. Strychnine, poisoning. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Oxyg. is said to liberate oxygen in nascent state in the tissues when it is taken internally,
diluted with five or six parts of water. Undiluted, its taste is disagreeably metallic, though it can be used as a
 gargle without inconvenience. Diluted, it has no taste at all.
When taken as directed in doses of a tablespoonful with six of water it sometimes causes relaxation of the
bowels followed by constipation.
Clarke said it set up all the symptoms of a common cold. Clarke found it of great value as an anti-septic lotion
and application, and as a gargle in cases of sore throat. It has been known to stop the irritation of a raw throat,
when ushering in a cold, from going further either up or down.
In cases of gonorrhea. Oxyg. renders the urine anti-septic, supplying an anti-septic lotion from within without
interfering with the action of a specific homeopathic remedy.
Clarke gave it in a number of cases of cancer, and obtained favorable temporary results in some. Inhalations
of oxygen have palliated some late cases of cancer, producing profuse discharges from the ulcerating mass
of tumor with reduction of its growth, but no cure followed and death supervened.
Abdomen - Great flatulence, passing large quantities at stool.
Back - Excessive pains in whole sacral region, apparently in articulations, especially a sensation of tiredness
all through pelvic viscera, even in perineum.
Causations - Morphine. Strychnine.
Chest - Bursting sensation in chest. Suffocating feeling in chest, tendency to breathe slowly. Tightness under
sternum, worse bringing shoulders forward.
Eyes - Lancinating, paroxysmal pain in right eyeball, a little to left of pupil. Occasional rush of pain, filling whole
right eyeball and extending into right temple, which then became hot. Tingling of conjunctive and skin of face.
Face - Tingling of skin of face. Rawness in throat.
Head - Dull frontal headache, worse in spot over left eye. Headache in outer half of right eyebrow, pain still in
frontal region. Pain in left temple, which feels cold to touch. Continued sweat on scalp.
Limbs - Thighs and legs as if overworked, excessively fatigued. Eruption of pimples in the fold of right side of
buttocks, near anus, becoming very sore and seemingly like blisters, as skin rubbed off it was left very sore.
Itching of skin of metacarpal end of first phalanx of left index finger, no redness of eruption.
Lungs - Irritation of respiratory tract as when recovering from attack of influenza. Violent irritating cough and
sneezing, followed by rawness in throat and air passages. Hoarseness and hard, shaking, tearing cough from
tickling under sternum in night, worse lying either side, better lying on back with profuse, lumpy, tasteless
whitish sputa. The sputa occasionally yellow, purulent. Dry, hacking cough, 2 to 5 a.m. Cough causes hawking,
blowing nose, and a bursting sensation in chest.
Male - Fine stinging rash on right side of scrotum, lasting one day.
Mouth - Canker sores in mouth and cheeks.
Nose - Much indurated mucus in nose, necessitating frequent picking in morning, blowing out of lumps,
generally tough, opaque, whitish yellow. Sneezes with the cough.
Perspiration - Sweat all over and headache between eyes. Sweat on scalp and slight moisture over body.
Rectum - Flatus seems to accumulate in rectum, causes desire for stool and fears to pass flatus lest stool
should also pass.
Skin - Tingling of skin of face and conjunctive.
Throat - Rawness in throat. Irritation of fauces and glottis. Slight hoarseness, dryness of throat towards
evening dryness increased around rim of glottis, at midnight woke with choking, burning dryness of glottis and
upper larynx, no thirst. Aphonia with difficulty of controlling voice.
COMMENTS - Oxyg. is not chemically distinguishable from hydrogen peroxide, but it has none of the
disagreeable features of that substance; it does not bleach articles it may touch or cause effervescence.
A cure of diabetes with large doses of Oxyg. is on record and many cases of whooping cough have been cured
with inhalations of ozone. Dilute Oxydol is a useful preparation as a mouth wash in canker sores.
D. T. Playfair cured a desperate cases of morphine poisoning (30 grains Morph, had been taken) in a young
woman of 37 with inhalation of oxygen kept up for ten hours. All the usual antidotes had been given before
without avail. The patient was entirely well in twenty-four hours.
In one case, an elderly working class woman had a large fungating cancer of the left breast. Oxyg. was given
internally and applied externally. It caused excessive discharge with corresponding reduction of the tumor.
After several, weeks the patient's legs suddenly swelled, rapidly increasing, and she sank, the tumor had at
least three-quarters disappeared. The effect of the Oxyg. was probably to liberate the disease elements too
rapidly for the organism to eliminate them, as Dr. Cooper suggested in his account of Orni.
Oxyg. 1,000c cured a case of cough from dryness in upper larynx and constant tickling in throat-pit. Hard,
shaking cough causing soreness in epigastric region. Expectoration with every cough, thick, lumpy, tasteless.
Oxyg. 100,000c cured a cough excited by tickling in throat and causing soreness of chest, 2 to 3 a.m., better
lying on back. In another case, Oxyg. 100,000c cured a case in which the patient was passing quantities of
 uric acid like ruby sand.
RELATIONS - Antidote to: Morphine and strychnine poisoning. Antidotes, Camph. Compare: Ozone. Chr-
ac., Kali-bi., Kali-chl., Kali-perm., Osm., and oxidizing agents generally, Chlor., Electr.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Grimmer. Mur- Phy.

name: Oxytropis Lamberti
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - oxyt. Oxytropis lamberti. Locoweed. Oxytropis campestris. Rattle-weed. Astragalus campestris.
N. O. Leguminose. Papilionoideae. Tincture of fresh plant without the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Apathy. Belch- ings. Bladder, irritability. Coughs. Delirium. Depression. Fevers.
Impotence. Locomotor ataxia. Mania. Ovary, pain. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Spermatic cord. Sphincters,
relaxation. Staggering, gait. Testicles, pain. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - The “Crazy-weed” or “Loco-weed” is of Spanish origin and has been variously identified by
Gray as Astragalus legum, by others as Astragalus mollisimus, and by W. S. Gee, who made the proving, as
Oxytropis Lamberti.
In Gee's proving, the tincture and potencies from lx to 30x were used. A number of mind and brain symptoms
were produced including despondency, forgetfulness, a feeling as if consciousness would be lost, fullness in
the head and instability standing. There were pains both in testes and ovaries, and one male prover, naturally
passionate, became impotent.
W. D. Gentry in June. 1895, sent Boericke & Tafel specimens of Oxyt. and as this firm is extremely careful
about the botany of the plants they make their tinctures from, Gentry made these remarks concerning the
plants he sent:
“My attention was first called to this plant last winter during January. Soon after my arrival on the territory, as
it was almost the only green thing showing itself above the snow. Which covered the ground at that time for
two or three days.
“Some cattle had been eating the weed and as I approached them they tried to move away, but in spite of their
efforts they backed towards me and in their efforts to escape made some ludicrous maneuvers. I observed
them closely for more than an hour and was reminded most forcibly by their actions of the symptoms of
locomotor ataxia.”
Gentry's observation of loco-disease in winter bears out what is said by other writers, namely, that it is only in
winter, when food is scanty, that animals can be induced to commence eating the weed and then they cannot
leave off.
Gentry made provings of the tincture of the whole plant and seeds on three persons. Two provers had
“symptoms worse when thinking of them.” They had “pleasant intoxicated feelings.”
Both Gentry’s and Gee’s provers had well- marked pains in the eyes and disturbance of vision and Gentry's
had “numb, pithy or woody feeling about and on the spine,” and “loss of power to control movements of limbs.”
Marked action on the nervous system producing uncertain, staggering or backward gait. Staggering gait.
Reflexes lost. Trembling, sensation of emptiness. Vertigo. Congestion of spine and paralysis. Pains come and
go quickly. Sphincters relaxed. Urging to urinate when thinking of it. Great mental depression.
MIND -All symptoms worse when thinking of them (Ox-ac.).Stimulation of mind, pleasant, intoxicated
feeling (Gent.). Mono-maniac tendency. Cannot think or concentrate his thoughts. Very forgetful of familiar
words and names. Indifference to all interests. Depression. Feeling as if he would lose consciousness.
Disinclination to talk or study. Desires to be alone.
Abdomen - Full feeling in abdomen, causing short breathing after lying down in bed. Sharp, sharp pains all
through abdomen. Sharp pain, running from right to left across bowels. Slight griping pain in region of
umbilicus. Tenderness in epigastric region.
Back - Pain and stiffness of muscles of back of neck. Numb, pithy or woody feeling about and in the spine
(Gent.).
Chest - A warm tingling sensation over left chest, just under skin. Oppression in lungs at 9 p.m.
Ears - Roaring sound in ears.
Eyes - Sight obscured, pupils contracted, do not respond to light. Paralysis of nerves and muscles of eyes.
Female - Pain in left ovary like something grasping or holding tightly.
Food - Loss of appetite. Appetite gradually increasing. Symptoms worse after eating, better after an hour.
Head - Full, warm feeling about head. Feeling of intoxication with loss of vision. Pain in maxillary bones and
masseter muscles. Pressure on head, better after sleep.
Kidneys - Pain in kidneys, worse in right, with some tenderness (Berb.). Awoke with a heavy pain in kidneys.
 Urging to urinate when thinking of it. Profuse flow of urine.
Limbs - Pain along ulnar nerve. Pains come and go quickly, but muscles remain sore and stiff. Numb feeling
about spine. Staggering gait. Patellar tendon reflex lost. Loss of coordination.
Lungs - Short and quick breathing from the full feeling in abdomen. Hard breathing, as though lungs and
bronchials were closing. Short cough with tightness across chest. A dry cough, from any little exercise.
Male - No desire or ability. Pain in testicles and along spermatic cord and down thighs.
Modalities - Better after sleep, on side lain on. Pains better when moving about, better in cool air. Worse
thinking of symptoms, every other day. Worse immediately after eating, better an hour after.
Mouth - Mouth very dry, especially in morning. Metallic taste in mouth. Gumboil on left lower jaw, profuse
saliva. Pain in left lower jaw.
Nose - Frequent, violent sneezing with fluent coryza. Fluent coryza, somewhat bloody. Nose very dry, scabs
form in it. Nose feels as if sunburned, red and shining, especially on ale. Feeling of pressure over bridge of
nose.
Rectum - Sphincter seems relaxed. Looseness of bowels. Stools slip from anus like lumps of jelly, mushy.
Sleep - Twitching of muscles on falling asleep. Wakes often. Restless, dreams of quarrel. Dreamed of spiders,
bugs, of swimming in water. Dreams of a pleasant or lascivious nature. On rising feels sad, weary, despondent.
Stomach - Belchings with colicky pains. Belchings, as after taking soda-water with colicky pains. Stomach
cold during the chill.
Temperature - Chill lasted until 2 p-m., then disappeared. As chill passes off a smarting in throat and a feeling
as though lungs and bronchials would close up, making breathing very difficult. No thirst in either stage.
Throat - Throat dry and sore. Slight inflammation of pharynx, a “husky” feeling. Slight accumulation of mucus
in larynx, hard to cough it up.
COMMENTS - The botanical articles in the Century Dictionary noted that Loco-weed is “any one of the several
Leguminous plants producing the loco-disease in animals. Among them are Astragalus mollisimus and A.
Hornii with several other species of the genus and Oxytropis Lamberti.”
Henry's Botany reported that the foliage of “Oxytropis Lamberti is said to be injurious to cattle,” so Dr. Gee was
quite justified in taking this plant for the proving. The Astragali are very closely related to the Oxyt.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Astrag., Lath., Ox-ac.,Bar-c. Loco plantisrich inBaryta. Lol. (2) Lath., Astra-me.,
Phys, and other Legumi- nose. (3) In symptoms worse when thinking of them, Ox-ac. (better, Camph.). (4)
Pain in cord and tests, Ox-ac. (5) Pains right to left, Lyc. (6) better moving about, Rhus-t.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Gen- try.

name: Ozonum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ozone. Ozonum. Ozone. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphonia. Backaches. Belching. Cancer. Heartburn. Hoarseness. Keloids. Nausea. Night-sweats.
Photophobia. Sinusitis. Vertigo. Vitiligo. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The name ozone derives from the Greek, which means “to smell,” “to spread an odor.”
Back - Backache in lumbar region. Lancinating and cutting pains.
Eyes - Tired eyes. Burning and twitching. Photophobia.
Nose - Sinusitis. Thick nasal discharges. Sensitive to smell.
Perspiration - Night-sweats.
Skin - Dry skin. Darker coloration of different parts of skin. Vitiligo. Itching. Scars that itch. Keloids.
Sleep - Falling asleep difficult despite tiredness, with tension. Sleep unrefreshing, troubled, wakes up often,
tosses and turns. Frequent yawning and tired eyes, better after nap.
Stomach - Heartburn. Sour belching. Nausea and vomiting.
Throat - Dry throat in heated rooms, better fresh air with open window. Feeling as if a lump of mucus in throat,
worse swallowing. Tries to get the lump out by coughing and clearing my throat, but this doesn't help. Shrill
voice. Hoarseness. Husky voice when singing. Aphonia.
Vertigo - Vertigo, tottering, staggering on rising from crouching, with nausea. Sensation of falling, worse
bending down, better lying down.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Oxyg., Carb-v.
REFERENCES - Murphy. Schadde.

name: Paeonia Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - paeon. Paeonia officinalis. Peony. N. O. Ranunculaceae. Tincture of the fresh root dug in spring;
 in autumn the root is said to be inert. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Anal, disorders. Bedsores. Breast, ulcerations. Ciliary, neuralgia. Coccyx, ulcer. Colic.
Fissure. Fistula. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Nausea. Nightmares. Perineum, ulcer. Sternum, pain. Ulcers.
Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Vomiting.
HERBAL - Paeon, belongs to the great order of Ranunculaceae, which includes the aconites, acteas and
hellebores.
HOMEOPATHIC - Chronic ulcers on lower parts of body, leg, foot toes, also breast, rectum. Skin is very
sensitive, ulcerations from pressure of tight boots, bed sores etc. Shooting or splinter like pains. Rolls on floor
from pain.
Congestion. Rush of blood to head. face. chest, burning heat and redness of eyes and face, burning, itching
and swelling of anus, heat in throat in skin. Varicose veins. Anal varicose veins. Anal disorders such as fissure,
fistula, abscess and hemorrhoids. Biting, itching, swelling, burning. Intolerable during and after stool. Oozing
of moisture.
Both Dioscorides and Pliny cured nightmares with Paeon., the former with the seeds, the latter with the root.
The dreams experienced by the provers were of a terrifying nature.
MIND - Ill-humor. Depression with irritability. Much affected by bad news. Excitement. Nervous. Apprehension
in evening with anxiety. Anxious, afraid to talk with any one. Delirium.
Abdomen - Griping pain. Pinching in muscles. Cutting in umbilical region. Sensitiveness, worse along
transverse colon and epigastric region. Crawling in abdomen. Colic with diarrhea, transversely
across upper abdomen. Borborygmi.
Back - Sticking in last cervical vertebra. Pinching or griping. Boring in left scapula, better motion. Ulcers over
sacrum, bedsores.
Breasts - Ulcer on lower part of left breast, consequent on abscess.
Chest - Heat in chest. Dull shooting from chest to back through the heart. Sticking pain in left chest. Cutting in
left side when sitting bent over. Sharp pain in ribs above hepatic region in morning.
Ears - Jerking in cartilages. Sticking outward in right ear. Pinching behind right ear. One ear cold, the other
hot. Itching in concha. Ringing, roaring in ears.
Eyes - Eyes red and watery. Dry and smarting, not easy to open. Burning, itching and dryness of eyes and
lids. Conjunctivitis with lachrymation and contracted pupils. Inflammation of left ball with pain as if a grain of
sand were under upper lid. Sticking in right upper lid towards inner canthus.
Face - Face red and puffy. Burning heat in face. Crawling in upper lip.
Female - External genitals swollen and painful.
Food - Appetite lost. Thirst.
Head - Rush of blood to head and face. Pain and confusion of head. Dullness, heaviness, vertigo and feeling
of heat in head. Gnawing headache. Boring outward in right temple. Pain in occiput and in nape. Heaviness in
occiput.
Heart - Pain beneath the heart as from anxiety. Dull shooting from front to back through heart. Pulse
contracted.
Kidneys - Frequent and copious urination, disturbing sleep at night. Constriction in region of neck of bladder,
so that urine passed only in droplets. Burning and scanty urine.
Limbs - Pain in wrist and fingers, knees and toes. Cramp in ulna at wrist. Weakness of legs, inhibiting walking.
Jerking and tearing in limbs, then numbness. Weary pain in ankles when sitting. Pain in corns.
Modalities - Drinking water helps vertigo with nausea. Worse from touch orpressure, motion. Worse coming
into warm room, night, during stool.
Mouth - Tongue red.
Nose - Stoppage of nose, in evening in morning in bed with dryness. Crawling in tip of nose.
Rectum - Diarrhea with burning and internal chilliness. Sudden, pasty diarrhea with faintness in abdomen.
Excruciating pain at anus, continues long after stools, must rise and walk about. Biting, itching in anus, orifice
swollen. Burning in anus, then internal chilliness. Ulceration of anus and perineum, purple, covered with
crusts. Painful ulcer, oozing offensive moisture on perineum. Analfissures. Analfistula. Hemorrhoids, large
and ulcerated.
Skin - Sensitive, painful. Sensitive ulcers on lower part of body. Ulcers from pressure, bedsores. Painful ulcer,
oozing offensive moisture on perineum, near anus. Ulcers below coccyx, around sacrum, varicose veins.
Itching, burning, as from nettles.
Sleep - Sleepiness all afternoon. Sleep is restless. Sleep unrefreshing, disturbed by many dreams. Terrifying
dreams, nightmares, of the death of relatives.
Stomach - Anxious aching in epigastrium. Periodical sticking upward from middle of epigastric region. Burning
 in epigastric region at night. Nausea. Vomiting and painful diarrhea.
Temperature - Shivering. Coldness of limbs with (burning) heat in face, back and chest. Rush of blood to head
and face with sweat. Hot skin. Heat at night, disturbing sleep.
Throat - Biting posteriorly in palate in evening. Swallowing difficult. Scraping in throat. Sensation as if an acrid,
burning vapor ascended throat. Heat extending to pharynx in throat and esophagus, worse hawking. Hawking
caused by tenacious mucus in throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo when moving. Vertigo on every motion in a warm room. Vertigo with constant reeling and
staggering.
COMMENTS - “Small ulcers on perineum near anus that constantly oozes very offensive moisture, painful for
eight days.” This symptom has been expanded by clinical observation, principally Ozanam's, into ulceration in
general, ulcers from pressure, as bedsores and from ill-fitting boots.
“Sensation of splinter sticking in skin of right great toe when touched and violent pain as from pressure in left
little toe.” Ulcers are the seat of severe shooting pains. Tissues sensitive to pressure and injury, sensitive mind
(Hell.).
“Griping pain in the abdomen, preceded and especially followed, by anxiety, trembling of legs and arms as
though he were frightened, he became apprehensive if any one spoke to him and unpleasant news affected
him exceedingly.”
Fainting with diarrhea, stools are followed by intense chilliness, occurring generally a few hours after he felt
the worst. Bad pain in anus compelling him to walk the floor all night or to roll on the floor. Symptoms worse
by motion, walking. The right side is more affected than the left.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aloe., Rat. Compare: (1) Glech. - rectal symptom. (2) Harn., Sil., Aesc. (3) Rat.
- great constriction of anus, stools forced with great effort. (4) in varicose veins, Ham. (5) In splinter sensation,
anal fissures and abscess in ulcer, Nit-ac. (6) In splinter sensation and ulcers, Arg-n„ Hep. (7) In ulcers, Hell.,
Hell-v., Sil. (8) In ulcers about the toes, M-aust. (9) In diarrhea, Sulph. (10) In effects of bad news, Gels.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Palladium Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-pall.Palladiummetallicum.Pal- ladiummetal. (Pd, At. Wt. 1065). Trituration. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Constipation. Egotism. Eyelids, blisters. Flatulency. Headaches. Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Oophoritis.
Ovaries, disorders. Ovarian, tumors. Sciatica. Sexual weakness. Tumors. Uterus, disorders. Uterine,
prolapse. Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Palladium, one of the rare metals, was first separated from native platinum by Wollaston in
1803 and was named after the planet Pallas, which had been discovered just before that time by Olbers. The
metal is closely associated with platinum and gold.
Hering, who made the first provings in 1850, said that platinum and palladium, both proved in dust form,
showed such similarity in their effects that the question arose whether corresponding differences might be
found. Subsequent clinical experience has done much to distinguish between these two remedies.
F. Aguilar noted that Pall, is indicated in gynecological conditions where the disease had its inception in the
right ovary, the uterine prolapse and retroversion, sub-acute pelvic peritonitis and concomitant symptoms be-
ing secondary.
Pall, affects the ovaries, especially the right, the uterus and the mind. Disorders of the right ovary, attended
with pains that are better from pressure. Chronic oophoritis.
Bruised soreness. Stitches, rheumatic pains, suddenly changing and often lasting but a short time. Pains
fleeting, transient. Every step causes pain in groin. Motor weakness, averse to exercise. Undressing causes
itching all over body.
MIND - Love of approbation. Seeks the good opinion of others and attaches great importance to them.
Desires flattery. Haughty. Pride, easily offended. Wounded pride and fancied neglect. Effected profoundly by
slight offensives, real or imaginary.
Irresolution in morning. Irritability, takes everything in bad part. Irritability and impatience from headache. Very
impertinent. Tries to appear as amiable as possible, but is obstinate. Anger with trembling. Inclined to use
violent language. Curses and swears (Anae.).
Weeping mood. Keeps up brightly when in company, much exhausted afterwards and pains aggravated.
Excitement in company. Conversation aggravates. Desire for company, worse when alone.
Averse to mental exertion. Apprehension that something horrible will happen. Depressing news aggravates all
symptoms. Ailments from bad news. Feels as if she were going crazy. Time passes too slowly. Delusion that
 he is neglected, that she is not appreciated, that he has been insulted. Delusion had grown taller while
walking. Abdomen - Soreness of abdomen, swelling in right groin. Hollowness in groins. Shooting pain from
navel into breasts or pelvis, better after stools. Intestines feel strangulated. Sensation as if intestines were
bitten off. Flatulency. Abdomen feels sore after menses. Pain in abdomen worse coughing and sneezing.
Back - Tired feeling in small of back. Frequent, painful spasm in muscles of right side of neck, especially
morning. Painful drawing in neck, shoulders and down left arm. Pain in back and hips with coldness of limbs.
Breasts - Sharp, stitching pain in right breast near nipple, worse from deep inspiration.
Causations - Ailments from bad news.
Chest - Stitches in right side of chest, through to the back. Worse from taking a long breath, better when
walking in the open air.
Eyes - Blue half-circles under eyes. Dryness and itching of eyes in evening, which is not better by rubbing.
Sensation of dryness on the edges of the lids. Small watery blisters on edges of lower lids. Dull, heavy pain in
and behind left eye. Pain around left eye, extending beyond right eyebrow. Pain in right eye, temple and ear.
Pustule under right eyelids, worse touch.
Face - Sallow complexion, blue. Soreness and painfulness of the right corner of the mouth. Pain in right and
left lower jaw. Itching pimples on the face, the nose, behind the ears, in facial hair. Slower growth of facial hair.
Female - Menses come on at full moon. Menstrual discharge while nursing. Glairy, yellow leucorrhea before
and after menses. Pain and swelling in region of right ovary. Ovarian tumors. Ovarian pains, better
pressure. Uterine prolapse with retroversion. Cutting pains in uterus, relieved after stool. Sub-acute pelvic
peritonitis with the right-sided pain and backache, menorrhagia. Pelvis leaden heavy, worse standing. Shooting
or burning pain in pelvis. Bearing-down pains, relieved by rubbing. Soreness and shooting pain from navel to
breast.
Food - No desire for beer. Headache at dinner and after coffee.
Head - Headache, causing irritability and impatience. Headache, better fixing attention on it. Morning headache
with weakness in back. Pain across top of head from ear to ear, worse after an evening's entertainment with
irritability and sour belchings. Temporo-parietal neuralgia with pain in shoulder. Sensation as if head were
swung from behind forward, as if brain were being shaken. Itching on sides of head.
Heart - Pain in region of heart. Heart pain with paralysis of left arm. Pressing deep in the left side of the chest
periodical, as if in the heart.
Kidneys - Cutting pain in bladder, better stool. Pressure in bladder, as if very full, but little urine is passed.
Dark urine with brick-dust sediment or coloring the vessel red. Muddy (not dark) urine, urine like water mixed
with blood.
Limbs - Fleeting neuralgic pains in various parts of the body. Sciatica. Rheumatic pain in right shoulder, in
right hip. Heavy and tired limbs. Tired feeling in small of back. Darting pains from toes to hips. Itching.
Lungs - Stitches in chest on taking a deep breath. Frequent hawking of small solid lumps that he must swallow.
When ex
pectorating, sensation as if something were pushed into head. Abdominal pain is worse coughing and
sneezing.
Male - Single stitches in urethra, extending down to corona glandis. Sensation as if testicles were bruised with
pain in abdomen. In evening and at night no proper erection could be obtained.
Modalities - Better from diversion, touch, pressure, rubbing, after sleep, rest and stools. Sciatica, and colic
are better from warmth (hot cloths). Worse from lively emotions, chagrin, social excitement, social functions.
Worse standing, exertion.
Mouth - Tongue red in the middle (morning). Burning sensation on surface of tongue near tip. Tough mucus
in mouth, slimy taste. Sensation as if upper incisors projecting. Left upper and outer incisor sensitive and feels
like a foreign body.
Nose - Burning in nose with coryza, in evening. Painful pustule on point of nose, bleeds long after being
squeezed. Blood' pustule on right cheek, near wing of nose. Abdominal pain worse when sneezing or coughing.
Rectum - Constipation, stools are hard, frequently whitish like chalk. Dull pains in rectum, as from too long
retained stool without urging. Frequent soft stool. Diarrhea with very little pain, night and day.
Sensations - As if he had grown taller. As if she could not touch anything. As if head were swung from behind
forward. As if brain were being shaken. As if neck becoming stiff. As if bladder was filled. As if uterus would
prolapse. As if parts of groins would tear. As if testicles were bruised. As if heads of femurs were forced out of
their sockets and expanded. As if hand shattered.
Skin - Itching all over after undressing. Itching and crawling as from fleas on different spots, back, arms,
abdomen, thighs, ankles. Redness of knuckles, warts on knuckles.
Sleep - Great sleepiness in afternoon (3 p.m.) and early evening. Wakeful until 2 a.m. Starting in afternoon
 sleep. Dreams every night of buildings, wide stairs, many rooms. Symptoms better by sleep.
Stomach - Nausea. Tasteless belchings, which do not relieve.
Temperature - Chilliness with cold hands and feet, with colic. Coldness of the limbs with pain in the back.
Throat - Tough mucus in throat, slimy taste. Glairy mucus from throat. Frequent hawking of small solid lumps,
which he must swallow. Tickling (or sticking) as if a crumb of bread had lodged in throat. Sensation when
swallowing as if something hanging near hyoid bone. Dryness in throat and on tongue without thirst.
Vertigo - Reels on coming into a room from exhaustion.
COMMENTS - Right-sided ovarian tumors (Thuj. for the left side). Uterine and ovarian disorders. Bearing down
feeling, achiness. Uterine prolapse. “Headache across top of head from one ear to the other.” Hering noted
that the pains are fleeting, transient and hard to describe. Pressure relieves pains.
“Love of approbation.” Easily hurt from slights, real or imaginary. “Wounded pride and fancied neglect.”
Depressed, weep easily (Puls.). Irritability, leading to violent expressions. Can curse and swear (Anae.). Better
in society and worse after the party or entertainment.
Skinner cured a young woman who had excessive pain in the right ovary during the menses with Pall. The
only relief she could get was by inducing her sister to sit on that region. This “better by pressure" distinguishes
the pain of Pall, from the similar ovarian of Plat.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Chin, (diarrhea), Glon. and Bell, (headache). Compare: (1) Irid., Osm., Plat. (2)
Right ovary, Apis, Graph.. Podo., Plat. (3) Left ovary, Arg-m. - feeling as if left ovary growing enormously large.
Lach. - worse pressure. Lil-t., Cimic., Sulph. (4) Tired backache, Helon. (5) Hysteria introverted state of mind,
Tarent. (6) Crumb in throat, Hep. (7) Pain in spleen, Cean. (Pall, at menses). Complementary: Arg-n., Helon.,
Lil-t., Apis. Plat.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
