name: Physostigma Venenosum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - phys. Physostigma venenosum. Calabar bean. Ordeal-bean. Esere. N. O. Le-
guminosae.Papilionoideae. Trituration of the bean. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Astigmatism. Backache. Bathing, effects. Blepharospasm. Chorea. Ciliary spasm. Constipation.
Coccyx, pain. Dentition. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Epilepsy. Eyes, disorders. Glaucoma. Headaches. Heart,
disorders. Hemiplegia. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Hiccough. Hysteria. Iris, prolapsed. Leucor- rhea.
Locomotorataxia. Meningeal, irritation. Menopausal. Muscular atrophy. Myopia. Navel, inflammation.
Palpitations. Paralysis. Paraplegia. Parkinson's disease. Polymyelitis. Prostration. Sleeplessness. Spinal,
irritation. Spinal sclerosis. Stiff neck. T remors. Tetanus. Throat, sore, fish-bone sensation. Water, effects.
Wounds.
HERBAL - Calabar is the type of a genus of Leguminosae of the tribe Phaseoleae. It has flowers very like
Phaseolus except that its bearded style is terminated by a great oblique hood, covering the blunt stigma. It is
 this hood that distinguishes the genus and gives it its name. It is a great twining climber and has purplish
flowers.
Physostigma is the “ordeal-bean” of old. The seeds are very poisonous and are used by the Calabari to
determine guilt and innocence. When ingested, the person either vomits or dies, if they die they are considered
guilty, if they vomit, they are innocent.
Observed cases showed twitchings, especially in the back, and death in thirty minutes. In poisoning cases, the
most notable feature was complete muscular prostration.
A group of children in Liverpool ate beans that they found among the sweepings of a ship from Africa. Forty-
six were admitted to a hospital with loss of muscular power, prostration, feeble, slow pulse.
Cold, perspiring skin, cold limbs, vomiting in nearly all cases, diarrhea in one-third of them. At first there was
colic, but later on remarkable freedom from pain.
Pupils contracted in many, in one they contracted during sleep, dilated when aroused.
Only one (a tubercular boy) succumbed. He staggered as he walked, then fell, kicking and rolling as if in pain,
but afterwards became quiet, much purged, pulse hardly perceptible, skin cold, face livid, quite conscious and
able to swallow water.
Directly after drinking he died without a struggle, some froth issuing from nose and mouth. After death the
blood was found to be fluid, the heart distended with it and its muscular substance very flaccid.
HOMEOPATHIC - Physostigma and its active principle, eserine, form a valuable addition to the Materia
Medica. Stimulates heart, raises blood pressure and increases peristalsis. Causes contraction of the pupil and
of the ciliary muscles. Induces a condition of near-sightedness. Eserine is used locally to produce contraction
of pupil.
Spinal irritation, loss of motility, prostration with very sensitive vertebrae. Depresses the motor and reflex
activity of the cord and causes loss of sensibility to pain, muscular weakness. This is followed by complete
paralysis, although muscular contractility is not impaired. Meningeal irritation with rigidity of muscles. Paralysis
and tremors. Chorea.
Fluttering tremors in the muscles, they do not respond to the will, or draw into knots, even the intestines are
seen twisted in knots. Fibrillary tremors. Ataxic gait, shooting pains down the limbs. Tetanus. Trismus.
Tremors. Polymyelitis anterior. Progressive muscular paralysis. General paralysis of the insane.
Horror of cold water, drinks or bathing. Cold water feels too cold. Shuddering worse every draft. Floating
sensation. Darting pain here and there. Flushes of heat, worse palms. Pain, beginning at any hour, continues
to 12 o'clock following, either noon or midnight.
MIND - The mind is active even during sleep. Nothing was right. Too many things in the room, continually
counting them. Paralytic state of mind and body from grief.
Abdomen - Navel, sore, bloated, red. Hy- pogastrium sore, bloated worse standing. Gripe in right
hypochondrium. Groins pain alternately. Colicky pains, worse diarrhea, better extending legs.
Back - Sensitive spine. Cramp-like stitches up and down the spine. Drawing on turning head. Creeping
numbness from occiput down spine. Chilly, creeping sensations up back. Dull pain in back. Backache in kidney
region. Back very weak, unable to stand erect.
Breasts - Stitches in left breast, unable to draw in breath.
Causations - III effects of emotions, grief. Injuries, falls, blows, and bathing.
Chest - Stitches in the chest. Stitches under inferior angles of scapulae during expiration. Heavy weight at
chest. Twitches across pectoral muscles.
Ears - Sharp, shooting pains in the ears. Sudden pain from throat to middle ear, worse eructation. Pain in the
ear when writing. Painful pressure on tympani. Crawling in left ear. Sensitive to every sound. Hissing, buzzing,
ringing in the ears. Fullness. Stopped feeling. Partial deafness.
Eyes - Bloodshot eyes with burning. Muscae volitantes, flashes of light. Glaucoma, especially afterinjury.
Contraction of pupils. Visiontiembhng. Increasing myopia. Accommodation affected, astigmatism. Night-
blindness, photophobia. Profuse lachrymation. Exophthalmus. Spasm of ciliary muscle with irritability after
using eyes. Post-diphtheria paralysis of eye and accommodation muscles. Twitching of eye muscles. Pain
over orbits, cannot bear to raise eyelids. Eyelids tense, cannot close or open them.
Face - Face pale, flushings of the face, heat. Lips numb, licks them. Lockjaw. Neuralgic pain in right side of
face. Spastic conditions of the face muscles. Sensation of cramps or spasms in face.
Female - Pain as if menses were coming on. Menses are irregular with palpitations. Leucorrhea worse during
the day, when exercising. Sighing, worse when leucorrhea is worse. Metrorrhagia. Rigid muscles. Numbness
of womb with pain in back.
Food - Hunger but can find nothing to satisfy it. Food has a flat taste. No appetite, disgust for food, tobacco
and coffee, and especially for cold drinks.
 Head - Headache unbearable, worse atnight. Constant pain on vertex. Pain over orbits. Headache, cannot
bear to raise eyelids. Pain from forehead down nose. As of a band about the head, as of a tight cap on head.
Heartbeats felt in head on lying down. Cerebro-spinal meningitis, general tetanic rigidity. Brain, falls to side
lain on, wavering in. Tremors in head.
Heart - Fatty degeneration of heart (Phos., Cupr-acet.). Fluttering of heart felt in throat. Heartbeats distinctly
perceptible in chest and head. Feeble pulse. Palpitations, spasmodic action with feeling of pulsation through
the whole body.
Kidneys - Bruised, sore feeling in region of kidneys. Bladder feels distended. Frequent desire to urinate, often
ineffectual. Urine is yellow, high colored, strong-smelling, clear, muddy, pale and copious.
Limbs - Limbs feel weary, as after great fatigue. Sudden jerking of limbs on going to sleep. Tetanic
convulsions. Locomotor ataxia. Numbness in paralyzed parts, crampy pains in limbs. Pain in deltoid (right)
better violent motion. Pain in right popliteal space. Burning and tingling in spine. Hands and feet numb.
Flushes of heat in palms. Offensive odor from hands.
Lungs - Labored, sighing respiration, yawning. Cannot fill left lung as inspiration causes dull pain at left apex,
better by pressure. Cough from tickling in throat. Slight constant inclination to cough from filling lungs.
Male - Frequent erections with but slight desire. Emissions without dreams or excitement. Strong-smelling
sweat about genitals.
Modalities - Better in cool open air, exerting the will. Better closing eyes, sleep, warmth to feet, lying on right
side, lying on abdomen or with head low. Hiccough better by sleep. Worse lying on left side,
Physostigma venenosum on waking, in church. Worse motion, stepping, descending, misstep, jar, falls,
blows. Worse pressure, bathing, heat and cold, cold water, cold bath, change of temperature at 4 p.m. (Lyc.).
Mouth - Bad taste in mouth. Profuse salivation, thick, leathery saliva. Tongue feels sore on tip. Tongue feels
oily, scalded, swollen in chorea. Feeling of loose skin on roof of mouth. Teeth feel rough. Dentition stressful in
nervous children.
Neck - Pain at base of brain. Inclination to stretch out neck. Stiffness in neck. Rheumatic pains in left neck.
Nose - Fluent coryza, burning and tingling of nostrils, nose stuffed and hot. Fever blisters around nostrils.
Small boil inside right nostril. Nosebleed while at supper. Smarting at end of nose. Twitching of muscles of
nose. Tension in skin of nose and forehead.
Perspiration - Easy sweat with excitement. Copious, cold sweat in drops over whole body. Strong-smelling
sweat around genitals.
Sleep - Irresistible desire to sleep, soporific sleep. Restless sleep with dreams. During sleep, mind so active
was unaware he had been asleep.
Stools - Copious stools, soft, thin, watery. Yellowish stools, bilious, part natural, part black like tar. Stools
lumpy, mixed with watery discharge, dark and offensive.
Rectum - Constipation from atony. Tenesmus and burning with diarrhea. Stools are irregular and loose.
Sphincter swollen and rigid, evacuation painful. Anus sore and inclined to protrude. Severe hemorrhoids,
following childbirth.
Sensations - Sensations of contraction and tension. Wavering in brain. As if she will lose her mind. Tongue
as if burnt, swollen and paralyzed. As if a ball were coming up throat. As if stomach were full. Weak feeling in
stomach. Back as if paralyzed. Lower limbs as if asleep.
Sleep - Attacks of overpowering sleepiness with feeling as if to lose consciousness.
Stomach - Great pain immediately after eating. Sensitive to pressure in epigastric region. Pain extends into
chest and down arms. Gastralgia, chronic constipation. Hiccough with short break, better from sleep.
Temperature - Cold, clammy skin. Hands and feet cold. Every movement and draft causes shuddering.
Creeping, chilly sensation in back. Heat in head and face, flushed and hot. Dry burning in hands. Perspires
very easily.
Throat - Tonsils enlarged, swollen. Elongated uvula. Feeling as if a ball came up throat. Strong heartbeats felt
in throat.
Vertigo - Vertigo, stumbles on ascending or descending steps. Vertigo with constrictive feeling of head.
COMMENTS - According to Brunton, the tetanus properties of the bean belong to the alkaloid calabarine. The
paralysis, to eserine, or as it is now called, physostigmine.
In cases of poisoning, people experience a speedy general paralysis. Death occurs from failure of respiration,
although the heart may be poisoned both directly and through its nerves.
The paralysis is seated in the spinal cord. The muscles are affected by fluttering tremors. Involuntary muscles
are excited to active movements and expulsive efforts. The intestines are often twisted up in knots. All the
secretions are somewhat increased.
Many provings have been made with Phys., among which a proving made by Christison on himself is
 remarkable. Simpson and Douglas MacLagan were sent for to attend to him in his collapsed state. Simpson
could only compare it to the state produced by severe flooding, though Christison's only sensation was one of
“extreme but not unpleasant faintness.” MacLagan thought it a lot like aconite poisoning. Christison could not
get his will into his muscles except by a tremendous effort.
Warmth to Christison’s feet and a mustard plaster to his whole abdomen gave great relief and he was then
able to turn on his left side, but only remained there a very short time on account of the tumultuous action of
the heart it caused.
He became drowsy and slept, but his mind was so active in sleep that on awaking he did not know that he had
slept. The tumultuous
Physostigma venenosum action of the heart continued on waking, but strong coffee quickly restored the
whole condition and made the heart regular.
Indigestion was observed by Christison and many other provers, “as if large pieces of food had been suddenly
swallowed.” It began under the upper sternum, descending and increasing in intensity until it reached the
epigastrium.
Belchings then occurred and a reversal of direction followed, the sensation ending where it began. With other
provers, there was a sensation of weight and hardness. Christison also experienced giddiness and dimness
of vision.
Phys., and its alkaloid eserine, are best known in old school practice for its action on the eye, especially of
contracting the pupil. The effects are more definite when the drug (tincture, extract or solution of alkaloid) is
applied to the eye directly, but one myopic prover had his myopia much diminished.
Dudgeon related the case of A. E., 26, struck by the cork of a soda-water bottle on the inferior and outer part
of the left eyeball. Intense burning pain and effusion into the eyeball followed.
Under Arn., prescribed by Mr. Engall, the effusion disappeared and later the pain and inflammation subsided
under Aeon, and Merc-c. The pupil was now egg-shaped, the long diameter perpendicular, smaller end
downwards, vision extremely myopic.
Bell, dilated the pupil, but it had no effect on the vision. Engall sent the patient to Dudgeon, who found the
pupil was sluggish and a book had to be held within four inches of the eye to be read. Phys. 3x, every three
hours, was given.
After the first dose, objects could be seen at a considerable distance and the next day sight was nearly as
good as ever. Dudgeon believed that the lens was tilted by the blow and that Phys, restored the over-stretched
or paralyzed portion of the ciliary muscle.
Woodyatt stated that Phys, produced corneal astigmatism in a young woman who found any attempt at close
work caused redness of tarsal edges and a hot, sandy feeling
in conjunctiva. Lil-t. 30c cured.
For ocular tension, especially when glaucoma has been the result of injury. Eye injuries (Calen., Hyper.).
Conjunctivitis with sharp, shooting pains. Pinpoint pupils (Op.). Paralysis of certain eye muscles.
Astigmatism. Double vision, severe blurry vision, worse in the right eye. Holes in the field of vision. The eye
feels full of fluid. Eye problems associated with extreme insomnia. Muscae volitantes.
Paralysis and tremors predominate, but also cramps, twitchings, stiffness and tension. Tetanus. Paralysis and
numbness is more apparent on the left side, especially in left arm. Nervous disease with extreme tremors or
trembling. Paralysis of the spinal cord and respiratory failure. Parkinson's. Guillain-Barre syndrome.
Muscular prostration. Polio, diaphragm paralysis (Con.). Labored respiration. Paralysis with an inability to get
the will into the muscles. Paralytic state of mind and body from grief.
Ataxic gait, shooting pains down limbs. Locomotor ataxia. Spinal, sacral and coccygeal pains, with numbness
of the womb. One prover noted a feeling of levitation on stepping.
Dread of cold water, aversion to bathing. Weakness on change of weather and on cold, bracing days.
Sleeplessness.
Nash cured with Phys. 12c and 30c persistent sleeplessness in a patient who had been in an insane asylum
and feared she would have to go again. Her symptoms were “If we chanced to get a nap she awoke suddenly
as if in a fright and felt no better from what she had slept.”
H. L. Chase, another prover, had a “very severe pain in the right popliteal space,” and he afterwards cured a
patient who came to him with pain in the same region two years later.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Phytolacca Decandra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - phyt. Phytolacca decandra. Poke root. Poke weed. Virginian Poke. Pole-root. Red ink plant.
 Garget weed. N. O. Phytolaccaceae. Tincture of fresh root dug in winter. Tincture of the ripe berries. Tincture
of fresh leaves. Solution of the resinous extract, Phytolaccin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenitis. Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Anus, fissure. Asthma. Barber's itch. Boils. Bone,
diseases. Breasts, disorders. Breast-feeding. Breasts, tumors. Cancer. Cholera. Ciliary, neuralgia. Colic.
Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Cough. Dentition, difficult. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Diplopia. Dysentery.
Dysmenorrhea. Ears, disorders. Erythema nodosum. Eustachian tubes disorders. Galactorrhea. Gland,
disorders. Glands, enlarged. Glossitis. Gonorrhea. Gout. Headaches. Hearing, disorders. Heart, disorders.
Hepatitis. Hemorrhoids. Impotence. Influenza. Laryngismus. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Liver, disorders. Lumbago.
Lupus. Mastitis. Mercury, effects. Miscarriage, threatened. Mouth, ulcerated. Mumps. Nephritis. Neuralgia.
Nipples, painful Nursing, painful. Obesity. Orchitis. Ozaena. Paralysis, diphtheria. Parotiditis. Prostate,
disorders. Rectum, cancer. Respiration, abnormal. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Rodent, ulcer. Salivation.
Scabies. Scar. Sciatica. Sewer-gas poisoning. Spinal, irritation. Spleen, pain. Stiff-neck. Syphilis. Tetanus.
Throat, sore. Tinea capitis. Tonsillitis. Toothaches. Tumors. Ulcers. Uterus disorders. Venereal buboes.
Warts. Wens.
HERBAL - Phytolacca is a branching herbaceous plant with a thick, perennial root, sometimes larger than a
man's leg in diameter. The plant is common throughout North America, the Azores, North Africa and China. It
grows in damp places.
The young shoots, though extremely acrid, are rendered harmless by boiling and are eaten like asparagus in
the United States. The berries have a popular repute as a remedy for cancer and rheumatism.
The berries of Phytolacca octandra are used in Mexico and the West Indies as a soap.
According to Raffinesque, the ash of the plant is 45 percent caustic potash, and the plant contains an acid,
phytolactic acid, which is closely allied to malic acid. Phytolacca has been used as an escharotic in cancers,
ulcers, etc.
HOMEOPATHIC - Phyt. is pre-eminently a glandular and rheumatic remedy. It powerfully affects the fibrous
and osseous tissues, and the sheathes and fascias of muscles. Hence it becomes an admirable remedy in
rheumatic affections.
It has a special affinity for the muscles of the shoulders and arms. Acts on the muscles of the neck and back,
tendons and joints, periosteum, throat, digestive tract and the right side.
General soreness over the whole body, the patient moans and groans every time he moves. Lameness,
soreness and a bruised feeling are felt all over the body. It combines with the pain, intense prostration and
great exhaustion.
Rheumatic pain, tendency to affect the outer aspect of limbs. Sudden achiness. Pains come and go suddenly,
change places. Sore, hard aching pains. The pain occurs in such quick succession that it renders the leg
powerless numb and heavy. Each movement elicits groans. Spreading pains.
Rheumatism after tonsillitis. Lassitude with rheumatism, makes him lie down every now and then. Sciatica
and hip joint disease, with pain shooting from sacrum down the outer aspect of thighs to knees and toes.
Syphilitic bone pains, chronic rheumatism.
Glandular swellings with heat and inflammation, particularly breasts and tonsils. Hard and painful nodes.
Acts on scar tissue. Hastens suppuration. Pus is watery, fetid, ichorous. Discharges are shreddy, stringy,
stools, menses etc.
Affinity for the breasts and glands of women, which are prone to become cancerous in those of a cancer
constitution.
Breast cancer, as well as cancers of the uterus and rectum. Mastitis, breast disorders . Pressure with hand
ameliorates pain in breasts. Great sensitivity in breasts.
Sore throat, quinsy and diphtheria. Sore throats, right-sided, relieved by swallowing cold drinks, worse from
warm drinks and empty swallowing. Enlarged and painful cervical glands accompany the inflamed sore throats.
Bluish-red parts, throat glands. Burning pains in cancerous ulcerations and in inflamed throats.
Restlessness and prostration. Tetanus, general muscular rigidity, alternate spasms and relaxation of muscles.
Opisthotonos. Decrease of weight. Obesity. Retarded dentition.
MIND - Irritable and nervous. Restlessness. Indisposition to mental exertion. Disgustfor business. Feels faint
on rising. Stupefaction with vertigo and dimness of vision. Refuses food in spite of continuous insistence.
Irresistible compulsion to clench the teeth.
Melancholy, gloom, indifference to life. Depression of spirits with headache. Weeping at night during menses.
Great fear, sure she will die. Predicts death, with mastitis. Desires death in morning on waking.
Confusion while sitting, better open air. Delirium. Loss of personal delicacy, complete shamelessness and
indifference to exposure of her person. Oversensitiveness to pain. Cannot endure pain, it is intolerable.
Unconsciousness from pain.
 Abdomen - Great rumbling in abdomen and pain in umbilicus. Heavy aching pain in the hypochondrium, worse
lying on affected side. Sore spot in right hypochondrium. Soreness and pain in right hypochondrium during
pregnancy. Rheumatism of abdominal muscles. Bruised feeling through the epigastrium and abdomen. Colic
at navel, with burning griping pains. Bearing down pains. Intense vomiting and purging with griping pains and
cramps in abdomen. Ulceration of mucus membrane of upper part of digestive tract.
Back - Pains streaking up and down the spine. Back stiff, especially in morning on rising and during damp
weather. Aching pain in lumbar and sacral region. Shooting pain in sacrum. Weakness and dull pain in region
of kidneys. Hardness of glands in right side of neck. Neck stiff in morning on waking. Pale red spots on neck
and arms. Both scapulae ache continually.
Breasts - Heavy, stony, hard swollen or tender breasts. Severe stinging pains, throughout breasts, with
oozing out of milk, better pressure with hands. Swollen breast. Irritable breasts, before and during menses.
Tender and sore breasts, before and during menses. Mastitis, with breasts hard and very sensitive. Mastitis
from taking cold. Mastitis during pregnancy. Galactorrhea (Calc.), causes great exhaustion. When child nurses,
pain goes from nipple all over body. Milk thick, scanty and unhealthy, dries up too soon. Breast hard as a
stone, after weaning. Cracks and small ulcers about nipples. Nipples, cracked, very sensitive inverted. Tumors
or hard nodes of the breasts with enlarged axillary glands. Breast is hard, painful and of purple hue. Breast
cancer, with shooting, lancinating pains, great exhaustion and prostration. Breast abscess. Bloody, watery
discharge from breasts. Affection of old scars in breasts.
Causations - Emotions, grief, injuries, blows, bathing, and exposure to cold, damp weather.
Chest - Aching pains in chest, through mid-sternum with cough. Rheumatism of lower intercostals, from
exposure to cold and dampness. Tenderness and lameness of muscles of chest, as if bruised. Swelling of
axillary glands.
Constitutions - Suited to rheumatic or syphilitic subjects, sensitive to damp weather. Cancer constitution.
Ears - Shooting pains in both the ears, worse swallowing. Obstruction in left Eustachian tube. Irritation in one
Eustachian tube. Increased sense of hearing with pain in forehead.
Eyes - Dull aching in eyes, worse motion, light or exercise. Orbital cellulitis. Burning, smarting, tingling in
eyes. Feeling of sand under lids. Profuse hot lachrymation. Fistula lachrymalis (Fl-ac.). Lids agglutinated
and edematous. Lids as if on
fire. Tarsal edges feel hot. Photophobia. Green vision. Eyeballs ache on reading and writing. Diplopia. Motion
of one eye only, independent of the other.
Face - Face very pale, hippocratic. Yellowish, sickly. Blotches in face, worse evening, after washing and eating.
Blueness around eyes. Chin drawn closely to sternum. Glands swollen at the angle of jaw. Jaws ache, as in
mumps. Aching malar bones. Mumps. Tension and pressure in parotid gland.
Female - Amenorrhea, with ovarian irritation or disease. Menses too copious and frequent, followed by
leucorrhea. Menses with salivation and lachrymation. Dysmenorrhea in barren women with erosion of cervix
membranous. Leucorrhea, thick, tenacious and irritating. Leucorrhea profuse, thick, tenacious. Ovarian neural-
gia of right side. Ovaritis with rheumatic complications. Venereal buboes. Swollen nabothian cysts. Glandular
swellings and abscesses. Suppression of lochia.
Food - Intense thirst. Hunger, soon after eating. Loss of appetite. Can't swallow any hot food ordrinks (Lach.),
causes choking. Diarrhea after lemonade. Vomiting of food and milk, in teething children.
Glands - Swelling and induration of glands. Swollen glands and burning pains, worse at night. Glands swollen
at the angle of jaw. Glandular abscesses. Venereal buboes. Hardness of glands in right side of neck. Swelling
of axillary glands.
Head - Pain from frontal region backwards. Pressure in temples and over eyes. Brain feels sore, head as if
beaten. Violent headache, with stupid expression of face and enlarged pupils. Headache with vertigo and dim
vision. Nausea and headache better eating, but returns soon with vomiting. Rheumatism of scalp, pains come
on every time it rains. Cold sweat on forehead. Scaly eruption on scalp. Tinea capitis.
Heart - Feeling as if heart leaped into throat (Podo.). Pains in region of heart, worse walking. Shock of pain in
cardiac region alternating with pain in right arm. Fatty heart. Small, irregular pulse with great excitement in
cardiac region.
Kidneys - Dull and sore pains in kidneys. Pains in kidney region, with scanty, suppressed urine. Hard aching
pain in kidney with scanty urine. Nephritis. Urine coffee-colored. Dark red urine, chalky sediment. Urine stains
the clothes yellow. Albuminuria after diphtheria, scarlatina. Copious nocturnal urination.
Limbs - Rheumatic pains, worse in morning. Syphilitic sciatica. Pains fly like electric shocks, shooting,
lancinating, shifting rapidly (Puls., Kali-bi.). Wandering pains passing from one joint and place to another, with
swelling and redness. Muscular soreness all over. Shooting pain in right shoulder with stiffness and inability
to raise arm. Painful, hard, shiny swelling of finger joints. Pain in hips and thighs on change of weather. Sharp
 cutting, drawing pains in the hip, legs drawn up, cannot touch floor. Pain in legs, patient dreads to get up.
Aching of heels, re lie ved by elevating feet. Feet puffed, pain in ankles and feet. Neuralgia in toes. Cold
hands and feet.
Liver - Chronic hepatitis (Chin., Phos.), with enlargement and induration of liver.
Lungs - Difficult breathing. Pains and suffocating feeling in throat and lungs. Panting breathing. Hoarseness.
Paroxysmal cough and very profuse and exhausting expectoration of thick starch-like mucus. Dry hacking,
tickling cough, worse at night (Menth., Bell.). Cough with burning in trachea. Cough as soon as he lies down.
Cough with pain in chest and side. Croupy cough, with burning in larynx and trachea, worse night and in cold,
damp weather. Chronic cough, generally hard and dry. Thick, tough expectoration. Thick expectoration, starch-
like mucus, profuse and exhausting. Copious, yellow mucus.
Male - Shooting along perineum to penis. Painful induration of the testicles. Orchitis, acute and chronic,
with suppuration and fistulous ulcer. Spermatic cord sore. Gonorrhea and gleet. Venereal buboes. Ulcers on
genitals. Impotency.
Modalities - Better warmth, dry weather. Better from lying on abdomen or left side, lying on stomach, rest.
Rubbing
Phytolacca decandra ameliorates pain in hip. Pressure on trachea facilitates expectoration. Sensitive to
electric changes. Worse exposure to damp, cold weather, rain, cold night, changes of weather, washing,
heat. Worse movement, raising up, stepping down from high step, right side, from touch, during menses.
Worse from swallowing, particularly hot drinks. Pressure aggravates pain in joints and ulcers. Riding
aggravates nose and breathing.
Mouth - Dry sensation in mouth, from cough. Metallic taste in mouth. Much stringy saliva. Profuse saliva,
sometimes yellowish, often thick, ropy, tenacious. Bleeding from mouth. Very painful small ulcers on side of
cheek, cannot chew on that side. Jaws firmly set, chin drawn down on sternum. Ulcers on lips. Upper lip
excoriated. Lower lip drawn down. Lips everted and firm.
Nose - Coryza with lachrymation and photophobia. Acrid coryza. Coryza, flow of mucus from one nostril
and from posteriorsinuses. Thin watery discharge from nose. Feels congested and heavy. Pain at root of
nose, with stoppage. Obstruction of nose while riding. Mucus hangs down in strings from posterior nares,
hawked with difficulty. Cancerous affection of nose, lupus.
Rectum - Continuous urging to stools, even in sleep. Constipation of the aged and those with weak heart.
Diarrhea after lemonade. Dysentery, passage only of mucus and blood or like scraping from the intestines.
Stools thin, dark brown. Bloody discharges with heat in rectum. Bleeding from rectum. Bleeding hemorrhoids.
Fissures of anus. Cancer of rectum.
Sensations - Brain as if bruised. Right side of head as if pressed firmly. As if sand in eyes. As if eyes too
large. As if lids granulated. As if tarsal edges raw. As if lids on fire. As if lump in throat. As if apple core in
throat. Throat so full it felt choked. Pharynx feels like a cavern, chest as if it were a big empty cask. Body as if
bruised, pounded all over. As if joint were being chopped with an ax.
Skin - Dry, harsh, shriveled. Skin becomes dry, shrunken, pale. Itching. Papular and pustular lesions.
Erythematous blotches, irregular, slightly raised, pale red, ending in dark red or purple spots. Disposition to
boils and carbuncles, with swollen glands and burning pains, worse at night. Painful boils on back and behind
ears. Squamous eruptions. Syphilitic eruptions. Swelling and induration of glands. Scarlatina-like rash. Warts
and moles. Lipoma. Corns. Barber’s itch. Lipoma. Pityriasis. Ringworm. Ulcer, chronic, surrounded by boils.
Cancerous ulcers.
Sleep - Frequent yawning and drowsiness. Restlessness at night. Pains drive him out of bed. On awaking,
feels wretched.
Stomach - Hunger soon after eating. Heat in stomach. Stomach cramps and coldness. Pain in region of
pylorus. Pains, worse deep breathing. Nausea, eructations of flatus and sour fluids, with severe pain in
umbilical region. Easy vomiting without nausea. Violent vomiting with retching, desires death to relieve
vomiting. Vomiting of clotted blood and mucus. Vomiting and diarrhea, with griping pains and cramps in
abdomen.
Teeth - Difficult dentition, better biting on something hard. Teething children with irresistible desire to bite
the teeth together. Teeth and jaws clenched. Teeth feel sore and elongated. Inflamed gums and teeth, with
mercurial ptyalism.
Temperature - Chills at night and every morning. Cold hands and feet. High fever, alternating with chilliness
and great prostration. Mastitis. Mumps.
Throat - Aphonia. Dark red or bluish red. Much pain at root of tongue, soft palate and tonsils swollen.
Sensation of a lump in throat (Bell., Lach.). Throat feels rough, narrow, hot. Ulcerated sore throat and
diphtheria, throat feels very hot, pain at root of tongue extending to ear. Pseudo-membranous exudation,
 grayish- white, thick, tenacious yellowish mucus. Shooting pain into ears on swallowing. Cannot swallow
anything hot (Lach.). Tension and pressure in parotid gland. Tonsils swollen, especially right, dark-
Phytolacca decandra red appearance. Tonsillitis with fauces swollen with burning pain, cannot swallow
even water. Uvula large, dropsical. Follicular pharyngitis.
Tongue - Tongue thickly coated, yellow at base, fiery red at tip. Tongue mapped, indented, fissured, with
yellow patch down center. Tongue feels rough and scalded, burnt on back of tongue. Pains at root. Tongue
protruded.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising, feels faint. Vertigo, staggering with danger of falling. Vertigo with dim vision.
COMMENTS - Closely related to Merc, and Kali-i., especially in syphilitic rheumatism. General action of tissue
absorption, especially new growths. Tumors and indurations of the glands. Muscles, joints, bones, brain and
spinal cord, as well as the special senses, were all more or less disordered.
In cases of poisoning, the most common symptoms were vomiting, diarrhea, frontal headache and a sore
throat. Irritation of the eyes, nose and throat, a severe headache and diarrhea have occurred after inhaling the
dust of the powdered dried root, or from the odor of the fresh root when it is sliced.
Phyt. has caused convulsive symptoms, vomiting and vomiting of worms when given to animals. Wild pigeons
and other birds that eat the berries acquire a red color and lose fat. This observation has led to the use of a
tincture of Phyt. berries as an anti-fat remedy, and successful results have been reported.
Hale tells us that among American dairymen the root is used to regulate any abnormality in cows' milk, whether
it is scanty, thick, watery, curdy, or containing blood or pus. Its chief repute is for caked udders.
One boy, who drank two or three drachms of a tincture of the root, developed complete tetanus in which his
limbs were stiff, hands firmly shut, feet extended toes flexed, lower lids drawn down, teeth clenched, lips
everted and firm, general opisthotonos. Respiration was difficult, rales were heard all over the room.
For an hour muscular rigidity increased with convulsive action of muscles of face and neck, chin drawn close
on sternum.
This condition lasted five or ten minutes, followed by perfect relaxation and return in twenty minutes more with
the same violence.
After cold-water infusion, cupping, and mustard plasters, the boy slept about twenty-five minutes. On waking
he had some twitchings, especially of lower limbs, pain in back of head and stomach. The next day he was
quite recovered.
A boy, 8, who ate a quantity of the berries, was found in great agony, complaining that his stomach was “inched
together.” He had nausea, violent vomiting, his throat was sore and dry, fauces dark red, tonsils swollen.
After his vomiting ceased, purging set in, stools dark brown and thin, severe pain in stomach on pressure,
extorting a cry. Later he had burning griping in umbilical region, dim vision, tongue coated white, and
spasmodic jerkings in his arms and legs.
In a woman, 45, who took Phyt. as a “blood purifier,” a general rash in appearance not unlike the rash of
secondary syphilis was set up.
A family of four was poisoned by eating the root with their food by mistake. They had a dread of movement.
Seemed stupid, fell asleep after a paroxysm of cramping pain had ceased. Pain in the forehead, worse after
eating.
Vomited clotted blood and slime. Copious discharge of blood and mucus that looked like scrapings of the
intestines. Involuntary stools from straining, which occurred even in sleep.
In the mother of the family, who was seven months pregnant, it nearly produced miscarriage. The uterus could
be felt contracting under the hand, and there was involuntary straining and hemorrhage from the vagina.
Intense griping pain in small of back and cramps in legs coming and going suddenly. Coldness and withered
appearance of limbs, the whole body cold.
Phyt., used externally, produces good results in cases of ulceration. Clarke found that a gargle of a few drops
of the tincture in a tumbler of water was useful in many throat cases.
Hundall successfully used a preparation of the leaves as an external application for cancerous growths in dogs.
An ointment prepared with a strong tincture of the leave, as well as the juice of the leaves, has been used for
malignant ulcers in humans.
A case of cancer of the rectum was cured with Phyt. 3x. Nash removed many breast tumors by giving a single
dose of Phyt. 100,000c during the wane of the moon. The tincture may take away nondescript lumps in the
breast when there are few symptoms.
Breast cancer, especially with axillary involvement, especially right sided. Breast cancer that suppurates with
horrible burning pains in the breasts. Advanced cases of cancer or tumors. Hard nodules with a bluish
appearance and enlarged axillary glands. Scirrhus tumors, hard like cement (Con.). Scars of the breast, cicatrix
(Graph., Sil.).
 Sharp pain from the breast. Breast neuralgias, painful nerve irritation. Swollen glands, indurated (Brom.).
Paget's disease of the breast. Breast induration and abscesses in nursing women.
Mastitis with a hot, painful, congested and sensitive breast, worse cold and damp. Breasts are hard and lumpy,
heavy with mastitis (Bry.). Cracks and fissures in the nipples. Blocked ducts in the breast. Problems with
nursing, if the milk dries up, bad milk, thick or lumpy milk. Painful, sore nipples in nursing women. Pain radiates
all over the body when the child is put to the breast.
Rheumatic swellings are hard, tender and intensely hot. Arthritis, particularly of the shoulder (Rhus-t.), the
joints swell before a storm or when damp. Worse at night, change of weather. Wandering pains, migratory
arthritis.
Sciatica with sharp, cutting pains in the hip and down the thigh. Stiff neck. Generally swollen, stiff and sore,
worse on the right side. Electric shocks, sharp pain in the joints with the stiffness (Ruta.). Very restless, but
worse from motion. The tendons feel too short (Ruta.).
When pain in intestines disappears, pain in limbs comes on. Pain leaves heart and appears in right arm. Pains
in head and chest go from before backward.
Pains run down spine from nape, from sacrum down outer aspect of thighs to toes. The outer aspects of the
limbs are chiefly affected.
Frontal headaches, pressive, involving the eyes, worse right side. Headache associated with increased sense
of hearing. Apathetic, gloomy. Restless with a fear of dying (Ars.). Generally self-centered (Ars.). Nervous
irritability.
Disorders of dentition. Teething, better pressure. Teething with bad breath and sores in the mouth. Irresistible
inclination to bite the teeth or gums together. Toothache with digging in pain, shooting pain. Sensation as if
the teeth are too long. Jaw problems, with or without swollen glands. The tongue feels burnt and rough, may
be blistered, with a red tip (Rhus-t.).
Influenza with general body ache, back pain and wandering joint pains. Swollen, tender glands with throat
symptoms. Stiffness. Bone ache. Fevers with pain and vertigo (Gels.). Apathetic, internal shivering (Gels.).
Feels sore and bruised (Bapt., Eup., Arn.). Delirium.
Diphtheria (Lac-c.). Sore throat, strep throat, tonsillitis. Burning in the throat with a stiff neck (Rhus-t.), worse
from warmth. Dry, raw, rough sore throats. Throat appears dark and purplish. Very swollen and tender glands,
particularly on right side of the throat. Great pain at root of tongue when swallowing, pains shooting from throat
into ears on swallowing, worse on right side.
Hot feeling as if a red-hot ball in throat, burning worse by hot drinks. As if a red-hot iron in the throat (Kali-c.,
in the rectum; Alum., in the spine). Throat feels plugged (Caust.). Dark redness of fauces. White or gray
patches on the tonsils, with offensive breath. Tonsils may appear ulcerated, with crypts. Tenacious, thick
mucus in the throat, especially in the morning. Burning of the tongue. Ulcers of the mouth.
The Eclectics gave the expressed juice of the berries in “spasmodic or membranous croup or diphtheria.”
Clarke used Phyt. 30c for the so-called “diphtheria sore throat.”
With the throat symptoms there are generally headache, backache, wandering
rheumatic pains and fever. Nash relieved chronic follicular pharyngitis in public speakers when there was much
burning, as if a hot substance in throat.
Rapid and profound prostration. Diphtheriaparalysis. Faint and dizzy when standing. Soreness of the muscles.
Restlessness, but he fears to move because motion worse the pains. Stiff neck, especially right side.
Angina. Sense of constriction in the chest. Radiating pains down the right arm (Lil-t.). Heart palpitations
followed by severe aching down the right arm. Sensation of the heart beating in the throat.
The right side is most affected. Many symptoms were experienced in the liver and the spleen. Liver pains were
worse lying on right (painful) side. The spleen pain was better lying on left (painful) side. Hepatitis with an
enlarged, indurated liver.
Sensation in the stomach as if something is being pinched with violent vomiting attacks and pains in the pit of
the stomach. Colic during teething, clenching their teeth with severe stomach or abdominal cramps, diarrhea.
One characteristic pain, noted in a case of constipation, is a shooting pain from anus to lower part of rectum,
along perineum to middle of penis.
“Gurgling sensation in the prostate gland, repeatedly in the afternoon,” was noted by one prover along with
pains in spermatic cords. Suspension of sexual appetite with relaxation of the genitals. Syphilis, with bone
pains, ulcers on the genitals and sore throats, worse at night.
Discharges are tough, stringy, difficult to detach. Generally offensive and acrid. Clinkers. Shreddy discharge
in certain forms of intestinal catarrh and dysmenorrhea. Hemorrhagic and hemorrhoidal, acting strongly on
rectum and anus, curing tenesmus, bloody discharges and heat.
Psoriasis, ringworm and barber's itch. Chronic eczematous eruptions of the face. Old scars that never heal,
 and when the weather changes the scars flare up and become painful (Graph.).
RELATIONS-Antidotes: Milk and salt, Bell., Mez. Compare: (1) Tincture of Phyt. berry - sore throats and in
the treatment of obesity. (2) Bry., Rhus-t., Kali-hp., Merc., Sang., Arum-t. Inimical: Merc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - phyt. Phytolacca decandra. Poke root. Poke weed. Virginian Poke. Pole-root. Red ink plant.
 Garget weed. N. O. Phytolaccaceae. Tincture of fresh root dug in winter. Tincture of the ripe berries. Tincture
of fresh leaves. Solution of the resinous extract, Phytolaccin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenitis. Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Anus, fissure. Asthma. Barber's itch. Boils. Bone,
diseases. Breasts, disorders. Breast-feeding. Breasts, tumors. Cancer. Cho

name: Picricum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pic-ac. Picricum acidum. Picric acid. Picronitricum acidum. Trinitrophenolum. Carbazotic acid.
Tri-nitro-carbolic acid. Trituration. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Anemia. Backaches. Bedwetting. Boils. Brain, pain. Brain-fag. Burns. Cachexia. Cancer.
Condylomata. Conjunctivitis. Deafness. Debility. Dementia. Diabetes. Ears, boils. Emissions. Erythema.
Hands, sweat. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hemoglobinuria. Jaundice. Leucorrhea. Leukocythemia. Liver,
congestion. Locomotor. ataxia. Masturbation. Memory, weakness. Myelitis. Neurasthenia. Nosebleeds.
Otitis. Ovary, pain. Paralysis. Paraplegia. Pernicious, anemia. Priapism. Pruritus, vulvae. Sexual, mania.
Spinal, exhaustion. Spinal, irritation. Spinal, sclerosis. Styes. Sycosis. Uremia. Urine, bloody. Writer's cramp.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pic-ac. was discovered by Hausman in 1788. It is formed by the action of nitric acid on
carbolic acid, salicin, silk and many other substances. Pic-ac. and its compounds are among the most powerful
explosives known, lydite being an example.
Picric acid crystallizes in bright yellow needles or scales of very bitter taste, sparingly soluble in water. The
yellow color is imparted to the eyes and skins of patients who take it in the crude, and it not only produces a
semblance of jaundice, but actually disorganizes the liver if pushed.
Acts upon the brain, spinal cord, lumbar region, occiput, kidneys and sexual organs. Weakness, heavy, tired
feeling in body and mind. It causes degeneration of the spinal cord with paralysis. It acts upon the generative
organs probably through the lumbar centers of the spinal cord.
Occipital and bursting headaches (Glon.). The headache, frontal or occipital is worse on any attempt to use
the mind and it may extend down the spine. Headache extending from the top of the spine up over the head
to the eyes.
Neurasthenia (Ox-ac.). Worn out persons, mentally and physically. Cachexia. Progressive, pernicious
anemia. Prostration, weakness and pain of back. Muscular debility. Heavy tired feeling. Numbness.
Formication. Pins and needle sensation in limbs. Burning in many parts, along spine in legs.
Sallow complexion. Uremia with complete anuria. Brain-fatigue and sexual excitement. Degeneration of the
spinal cord with paralysis. Myelitis with spasms and prostration. Acute ascending paralysis. Typist's or writer's
palsy.
Thery of Paris accidentally discovered in Pic-ac. solution a remedy for burns. He twice dropped burning matter
on his hands while working with a Pic-ac. disinfectant and was astonished at the absence of pain or injury.
From that date Pic-ac. became his principal remedy for burns and though others have complained that it
caused violent pains, Thery has only once in some thousands of cases had to abandon its use on that account.
A one percent solution applied on lint is the best application for burns until granulations begin to form.
MIND - Anxiety. Dread offailure at examination. Mental weakness after prolonged strain and anxiety.
Memory, weakness. Forgetfulness. Mental exertion aggravates. Mental prostration after reading a little,
worse after writing a little. Inability to collect thoughts or to study. Brain-fag. Inability to exert the mind, talk or
think. Lack of willpower, disinclined to work.
Aversion to talking or movement, during headache. Sits still and listless, does not take interest in surroundings.
Cerebral softening. Dementia with prostration, sits still and listens. In women, although enjoying the society of
men, idea of marriage unendurable. Lascivious thoughts in presence of any woman. Lewdness.
Delusion that parts of body enlarged. As if stairs or ground coming up to meet him.
Abdomen - Fullness of the abdomen. Sharp pain in left side of umbilicus. Shooting, wandering pain. Crawling,
stinging. Rumbling in small intestines with colic. Crampy pain and flatus. Emission of flatus during the day in
evening.
Back - Burning along spine. Painful boils on nape of neck. Backache with languor, patient is unable to sit
straight and burning along spine, worse study. Keeps legs wide apart when standing. Aching, tired legs.
Writer's cramps orpalsy. Back seems as if bandaged, also limbs. Anesthesia of legs as if one has on elastic
stockings. Legs weak, heavy like lead, lifts with difficulty.
Chest - Tightness of chest, as if encircled by a band. Numbness in lower part of sternum.
Constitutions - Suited to dark complex- ioned persons with a dirty appearance from bile pigments, anemic
and cachectic persons. Worn-out person, overtaxed mentally and bodily.
Ears - Boils within ears and back of neck. Painful boils in meatus. Puffy and burning sensation in ears.
 Buzzing and hissing in ears. Noises in ears with vertigo and headache at the base of brain. Chronic deafness.
Eyes - Pupils dilated. Eyes yellow. Catarrhal conjunctivitis with copious, thick yellow discharge. Lachrymation.
Styes with a sore pain.
Female - Pain in left ovary and leucorrhea before menstruation. Extreme exhaustion at menstrual periods.
Pruritus vulvae.
Food - Appetite increased, then lost for breakfast. Aversion to food, at noon. Great thirst with bitter taste,
unquenchable. Thirst for cold water.
Head - Headaches, relieved by bandaging tightly. Headache, worse mental exertion, better nosebleed.
Headache, worse with sexual excitement and violent erections. Headache during daytime better in sleep.
Headache of businessmen, teachers and students from grief and other depressing emotions. Brain-fag.
Occipital pain, worse slightest mental exertion. Heavy
Picricum acidum occiput, down spine and lower limbs.
Kidneys - Inflammation of kidneys with profound weakness, dark, bloody, scanty urine. Dribbling urine.
Albuminuria. Ammoniacal. Urine contains much indican, granular cylinders and fatty degenerated epithelium.
Uremia with complete anuria. Diabetes. Nightly urging.
Limbs - Great weakness, tired, heavy feeling all over body, especially limbs. Worse exertion. Acute
ascending paralysis. Feet cold. Cannot get warm.
Liver - Liver full of fat granules. Sticking through hepatic region, worse in muscles. Tendency to jaundice.
Jaundice with itching.
Male - Enlargement of the prostate gland. Hard erections with pain in testicles up spermatic cord. Priapism,
penis distended. Lascivious thoughts in presence of any woman. Extreme prostration from frequent seminal
emissions. Impotency with tendency to boils and carbuncles.
Modalities - Better from cold air, cold water, sun. Better tight pressure, bandaging, rest. Worse least exertion,
especially mental, fatigue, study, mental shock. Worse after sleep, seminal losses. Worse wet weather, hot
weather.
Mouth - Bitter taste with thirst. White, frothy saliva hang in strings to the floor.
Nose - Boil in left nostril. Stinging on right side of nose. Acne. Nose full of mucus, can breathe only through
mouth, better open air.
Rectum - Diarrhea from mental exertion. Stools thin, yellow, oily. Burning in rectum while passing stools.
Sensations - As if sand or sticks in eyes. As if throat would split. As of a lump back of thyroid cartilage. As if
chest encircled in a tight band. As if legs enclosed in elastic stockings. Pricking as from needles in legs. As if
stairs or ground coming up to meet him. As of ants crawling over surface.
Skin - Jaundice. Small, painful, sore boils, especially on neck.
Sleep - Sleepy during day and sleepless during night. Sleepiness. Sleep sound but unrefreshing.
Stomach - Vomits suddenly, without warning. Vomit bright yellow, bitter.
Throat - Redness of throat with raw, scraped, stiff and hot feeling. Soreness back of and above soft palate
with debility. Dry and husky.
Vertigo - Vertigo and noises in ear.
COMMENTS - Grimmer said this remedy's sphere of action centers in the brain, spinal cord and the
bloodstream. It produce in the provings a marked cachexia and pernicious anemia and these conditions in the
sick have many times been cured.
In some experiments by Parisel, symptoms were observed including buzzing and whistling in ears, sparks,
whirling around of objects, heaviness of head alternately with sense of emptiness. Copious, oily-looking,
yellowish stool with amelioration of cerebral symptoms.
Pulse slow, small, very feeble. Great weakness, compelling to lie down, limbs hardly able to stir themselves,
no anxiety, profound calm. Vivid coloration of sclerotics and tissues, urine colored blood-red. These were
effects of 0.5 grains doses. Slow poisoning set up an intermittent fever of quotidian type and “anorexia, thirst
often sweat, cancerous tint about skin, tendency to cachexia.”
These observations give the chief features of the remedy's action: fatigue, mental and bodily, symptoms worse
by least exertion, fatigue going into actual paralysis, brain fatigue, nerve fatigue, at the same time absence of
anxiety indifference. The right upper part of the body is more affected than the left, the left leg more than the
right.
Cachectic tint to skin, suggestion of malignancy, skin merging into a jaundice as the disease advances.
Cachexia and cancerous tints. “Tired-out, washed-out feeling must give in.” Jaundice, with itching. Small, pain-
ful furuncles, particularly in the auditory meatus. Fig warts. Erythema and itching of abdomen and feet.
Heat and congestion of the head, with nosebleeds. Heaviness of head alternates with emptiness. Frequent
severe headache. Pain in eyes, worse from lamp light, strong light, moving the eye. Spinal congestion. Colds.
 Chilliness predominates.
Amorous fancies. Lascivious thoughts in the presence of any women. Great sexual desire with emissions.
Terrible erections, disturbing sleep. Long-continued erections at night with emissions, followed by more
erections and lewd dreams, priapism day and night. Priapism, penis distended almost to bursting. Gonorrhea.
Burning during and after urination.
Exhaustion and complete prostration of mind and body from sexual excesses, mental and physical fatigue.
Over-excitement of sexual system is associated with spinal or cerebral disorders in either sex.
A. C. Blackwood detailed the uses of Pic-ac. for burns of the first and second degree. He used a saturated
solution diluted with one quart of water. The clothing was removed and the burnt surface cleansed with the
solution and absorbent cotton. Blisters were opened but he carefully preserved the epithelial covering.
If extensive, the whole surface might be bathed with the solution and strips of sterilized gauze soaked and
applied to entirely cover it, a layer of absorbent cotton held with a light bandage over all.
After three or four days the dressing was removed carefully after thorough moistening, as it adhered closely.
The second dressing was applied as at first and allowed to remain a week. The staining of the hands and linen
caused by the dressing can be removed by boric acid.
Blackwood found it painless, anodyne, antiseptic, preventing inflammation, suppuration and septic poisoning.
It coagulates the albuminous exudation and healing takes place under the coagulum.
Gaucher removed acute vesicular eczema by the same treatment. He noted that the skin and kidneys are
intimately related and Pic- ac . has a powerful action on the latter. Among other disorders, it has cured diabetes.
Kent said Pic-ac. cures fig-warts and gonorrhea, he was led to infer its relation by its power over pernicious
anemia, which he had often traced to a gonorrheal base.
In a case of spinal irritation, Clarke relieved with Pic-ac. 30c a pain which shot up from the spine into the head.
The pains referable to the spinal cord are strongly marked. Any attempt to study causes burning along spine
with great weakness of back and legs, soreness of muscles and joints.
Halbert reported a case illustrating the power of Pic-ac. over the effects of fatigue in professional neuroses. A
stenographer and typewriter, after using her right index finger continuously for six years, noticed weakness of
her thumb and index.
Then, she noticed the inability to hold a pen or pencil. Next there was difficulty in striking correctly the keys of
the typewriter and some wrist-drop. The finger, when Halbert first saw her, was quite rigid and straight, showing
extreme spasticity.
Massage, electricity, etc., had failed to give any relief. Pic-ac. 3x six times daily cured the case and made great
improvement in the patient's general health.
Halbert reported the case of Mrs., C., 49, who had “nervous prostration” since the shock of the loss of a child
three years before. Wasting with great appetite. Intense thirst and copious urination, especially at night.
Great perspiration and some jaundice. Heart flabby, mitral bruit, Dyspnea, emaciation, anemia, exhaustion.
Urine 1040,7 1/2 percent of sugar and some albumen. Pic-ac. 6x six times daily was given, rapid and
continuous improvement followed.
Nash cured an old man who have been failing for a year with Pic-ac. 6c trituration. The man complained of
heaviness in the occiput, inability to exert the mind, talk or think and general “played-out” feeling. Nash had
feared brain softening.
Evans found it curative in girls and young women who, under the strain of many studies, show signs of breaking
down. They lose appetite, sleep lightly and lie awake, exhaustion after the day's studies, fatigued even from a
short walk, twitchings of muscles when asleep or awake, hysterical state, loss of will power, constant
headache, irregular menses. Such patients are usually given iron, which does little or no good.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ox-ac., Gels., Phos., Sil., Arg-n. (2) Zinc-pic. - facial palsy and Parkinson's
disease. (3) Ferr-pic. - buzzing in ears, deafness, chronic gout, nosebleed, prostatic troubles. (4) Calc-pic. -
boils in and around ears.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - pic-ac. Picricum acidum. Picric acid. Picronitricum acidum. Trinitrophenolum. Carbazotic acid.
Tri-nitro-carbolic acid. Trituration. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Anemia. Backaches. Bedwetting. Boils. Brain, pain. Brain-fag. Burns. Cachexia. Cancer.
Condylomata. Conjunctivitis. Deafness. Debility. Dementia. Diabetes. Ears, boils. Emissions. Erythema.
Hands, sweat. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hemoglobinuria. Jaundice. Leucorrhea. Leukocythemi

name: Picrotoxinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - picro. Picrotoxinum. Picrotoxin. Alkaloid obtained from the fruit of Coc- culus indicus.
Menispermaceae. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Hernia. Locomotor ataxia. Night-sweats. Urine, excess.
HOMEOPATHIC - Falk noted that Cocc. is used to stupefy fishes and when Picro. is added to water in which
fishes are swimming “they make winding and boring movements of the body. Alternating with quiet swimming,
open their mouths and gill caverns frequently, fall on their side and rapidly die of asphyxia.”
 J. H. Henry proved Picro. on himself. The symptoms were so severe that he was alarmed and took Op. and
Camph. to antidote them.
Nausea with tendency to faint, violent intestinal pain and purging, dysenteric diarrhea and excessive secretion
of urine, cramps and paralytic sensations were experienced. The symptom which gave the most concern was
the pain in the bowels and sensation as if the bowels would protrude at left inguinal ring.
COMMENTS - Brunton said the local application of Picro. as an ointment to the head for tinea capitis and to
destroy lice has been followed by convulsions and death.
Hansen mentioned that it has been given at bedtime to relieve the night-sweats of tuberculosis. With Pictx-ac
3x, Dorr cured in a few weeks a case of advanced locomotor ataxia with amaurotic amblyopia.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cocc. (2) In tetaniform convulsions, Nux-v. with Piero, respiration is accelerated
more from spasm of glottis then of respiration and there is less susceptibility to slight touch, more chorea
symptoms.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Pilocarpinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - piloc. Pilocarpinum hydro- chloricum. Pilocarpine. Jaborandi alkaloid. Pilocarpinum muriaticum
nitricum purum. Rutaceae. Solution in distilled water. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Alopecia. Convulsions, uremia, Deafness. Exhaustion. Eye, disorders. Faintness.
Hair, loss. Meniere's disease. Mumps. Myopia. Paralysis. Perspiration, excessive. Pregnancy, nausea.
Salivation. Tinnitus. Vertigo, aural.
HOMEOPATHIC - Piloc. is one of the most characteristic of several alkaloids which have been isolated from
jaborandi (Pilocarpus pin- natus). It has been used like Jab. to produce and cure profuse sweating, and by
oculists to produce contraction of the pupil, which it does whether it is injected subcutaneously or applied
directly to the eye. It has also an action on the ear.
The hair as well as the skin is affected by Piloc., which is an ingredient in many “hair restorers." Schmitz of
Cologne treated two bald men with injections of Piloc. mur. to produce absorption of inflammatory residue
within the eye.
In both a secondary effect occurred, the growth of young downy hairs on the bald parts of the scalp. One, age
60 in four months and his head covered “partly with gray and partly with black hairs” of considerable growth,
so as to entirely obliterate his previous baldness. Piloc. has also been known to turn white hair black.
In a case of lead paralysis, it produced profuse salivation and sweat with sensation of great coldness and
excessive tremors of limbs. Salivation and sweating speedily occur.
Dilatation of blood vessels, temporal artery becomes a thick, pulsating cord, veins of forehead stand out blue.
Exhaustion (after the perspiration) during which most of the patients fell asleep. Faintness.
Ears - Aural vertigo. Tinnitus of left ear. Deafness with tinnitus. Labyrinthine deafness, worse when tired.
Increased secretion of wax.
Eyes - Profuse lachrymation. Pupils contracted to pin-head. Sight for distance improved.
Face - Forehead and face red, veins stand out. Perspiration begins on face.
Female - Menses two days early.
Food - Intense thirst following the sweating.
Head - Throbbing in temples with acceleration of pulse. Turns white hair black.
Heart - Weakness of the heart. Pulse accelerated, blood pressure diminished. After the perspiration the pulse
sinks to normal.
Lungs - Increased bronchial mucus, much cough and expectoration. Constantly taking cold and in fear of
bronchitis.
Mouth - Saliva thick, stringy, exceedingly tenacious. Sudden salivation, maximum reached in fifteen minutes,
continues two hours, one and a half pints of thin saliva being secreted in that time.
Nose - Nasal secretion increased.
Rectum - Urging to stool.
Skin - Irritable skin.
Sleep - Patients fall asleep under its influence.
Stomach - Nausea, only occurring when salivation is complete (does not go on to vomiting as that of Jab.
does). Nausea and retching.
Temperature - Sensation of coldness and shaking chill without fall of temperature. Increase of temperature
with feeling of intense cold. Sweat profuse, may lose Vom tow to tow powvts tu fet sw catwg. After sweat,
thirst, feeling of relief and sense of increased vigor.
 COMMENTS - G. P. Field gave it with good effect in labyrinthine deafness, tinnitus and auditory nerve vertigo.
The cases least amenable to its influence were those in which the hearing was better in a noise as of a train,
etc. and those in which the hearing is worse after a cold. Subjects of syphilis, hereditary or acquired and
patients who are more deaf when tired, are the most suitable.
Wood went to see a woman three months pregnant. She was a picture of distress and despair. For eight weeks
she had saturated from six to ten handkerchiefs daily with tenacious saliva. Nausea and vomiting were
constant, emaciation extreme. Nausea worse by slightest movement.
Alternate redness and paleness of face, flushes of heat and perspiration. Urine scanty, high colored, depositing
much uric acid. Very chilly, obstinate constipation. Piloc. was given, a teaspoonful every two hours.
The next day Wood found his patient sitting up, cheerful and free from nausea and salivation. The
improvemen,t with some fluctuations, continued. Merc., Ip., Nit-ac., Kali-bi., Hydr., Cimic. had all previously
failed.
A woman who had Piloc. injections complained to Cooper that thereafter she had been constantly catching
colds and had fears of getting bronchitis. Her skin too, became irritable. Piloc. 3x is Burnett's chief remedy in
mumps. He regarded it (and Jab.) as an organ remedy of the sweat glands, parotid and pancreas.
Frohling related a case showing the power of Piloc. over debilitating sweats left after acute diseases. With
Merc. 12c he cured a case of rheumatic fever so far as the joint affection was concerned, but the sweats
persisted and strength declined in spite of remedies until Piloc. was given, when the sweating stopped after
the first dose.
RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Atro., Am-c. (sal volatile), brandy. Compare: (1) Jab., Myos., Esin., Phys.
Follows well: Merc, (in sweating of rheumatic fever).
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Pimenta Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pime. Pimenta officinalis. Allspice. Pimento. Eugenia pimenta. Eugenia acris. Myrtus pimenta.
Jamaica Pepper. N. O. Myrtacae. West Indies. Pimento consists of the dried berries. Tincture of the fruit.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Chills. Neuralgia.
HERBAL - “Allspice” is so named because its odor is said to resemble a combination of cinnamon, nutmeg
and cloves. A tincture was proved by Becket, and developed one-sided neuralgias and disturbed sensations
of heat and cold.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pime. has helped disturbances in the body's temperature and sensitivity. Parts of body
burning hot, other cold. Peculiar cold sensation as if sponge filled with cold water passed here and there over
the surface, succeeded by sensation of heat, as in the reaction after a cold bath. Very imperious desire to eat.
Semi-lateral neuralgic lesions.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Eucal., Eug.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Pimpinella Saxifraga
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pimp. Pimpinella saxífraga. Bibernell. Pimpinella alba. Burnt saxífraga. N. O. Umbelliferae.
Saxifrage. Tincture of the fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Chilliness. Coms. Nosebleed. Fever. Headache. Lumbago. Stiff neck. Tinnitus.
HOMEOPATHIC - The majority of the symptoms were obtained by Shelling from chewing the fresh root. The
rest were contributed by Berridge, who proved the lx on a man.
Marked chilliness, chilly in the back even in a warm room and much worse if a window was opened. Sensitive
to drafts. Sensation of coldness in occiput as from a cutting wind behind.
Cold stream from hip and into right leg. the pains and sensations extended from one part to another, principally
from above downward and from before backward (temples to nape, forehead to eyes, nape to shoulders) from
within outward or alternated between different parts.
Rush of blood to head, followed by nosebleed, whizzing in head, roaring in ears. Sinking sensation in intestines.
Weariness and falling asleep of parts rested on. Frequent yawning and desire to take a long breath, which was
difficult. Great drowsiness.
Modalities - V ertigo and sweat worse morning. Heat and rush of blood to the head, worse afternoon. Weary
pain in limbs worse from rest. Worse reading, writing, reflecting. Worse by chewing, standing, stooping,
walking. Worse by opening window in warm room.
 RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rush of blood preceding nosebleed, Graph. (2) Occipital pains. Hell., Nat-s.,
Glon.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Pine
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pine-b. Pine. Pinus sylvestris. N. O. Pinaceae. Twigs with male and female flowers are picked
and boiled for half an hour. The boiled water is strained and prepared as medicine.
Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol,
if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth
or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pine-b. belongs to Bach's group of Despondency and Despair, with the remedies of Crb-
a-b., Oak-b., Will-b., Star-b- b., Sw-ch-b., Elm-b. and Lar-b.
States of guilt, regret and self-reproach. Obsessive-compulsive states and too much over-conscientiousness.
The body may show signs of becoming burdened, depressive, or rigid, due to excessive introversion and self-
blame. Deep-seated conflict and obsessive guilt. Gastric and duodenal ulcers, irritable colon, nervous
breathing syndrome and insomnia (Must-b., Wh-ch-b.). Skin disorders with itching.
MIND - Introverted, subdued by the burdens of guilt and regret. Preoccupied or obsessed with guilt and self-
reproach. Deep sense of unworthiness. Internal sense of failure. Overconscientiousness.
Feelings of shame, regret and self-blame at not having fulfilled one's high ideals. Despondency and despair.
Unable to forgive self. May assume responsibility and blame for failure caused by others. Frustration, anger,
rigidity and alienation from oneself and others.
Obsessive-compulsive, self-punitive and perfectionist or ritualistic behavior and thinking, as in obsessive-
compulsive personality disorder (Crb-a-b., Rck-w-b., Verv-b.). Delusions and paranoid personality disorders.
Fear of being punished or persecuted (Asp-b.).
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Pinus Lambertiana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pin-1. Pinus lambertiana. Sugar Pine. N. O. Confierae. Pinaceae. North America. Trituration of
inspissated sap. Historical dose: Trituration, all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abortion. Amenorrhea. Constipation.
HERBAL - The inspissated sap of Pinus lambertiana makes a sugary substance like manna. A small quantity
from a bit the size of a pea to a teaspoonful, has a decided but gentle laxative action, and in larger quantities
emphatically so.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pin-1, has also an action on the menstrual function, restoring menses when suppressed
and producing abortion in pregnant women. It was used by Indian women to restore the menstrual flow and
remove painful sensations resulting from the suppression. It has a gentle cathartic action.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sabin., Juni., Pin-s. and other coniferae.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Pinus Sylvestris
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pin-s. Pinus sylvestris. Scotch pine. Scotch fir. Red Norway. Riga Pine. Baltic Pine. N. O.
Coniferae. Pinaceae. The typical pine of Europe. Tincture of leaves and young twigs. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ankles, weak. Anus, itching. Bronchitis. Constipation. Diarrhea. Dysuria. Emaciation, lower limbs.
Glands, swollen» Gout. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Joints, stiff. Kidneys, pains. Liver, enlargement. Lumbrici.
Palpitations. Rheumatism. Scrofula. Squint. Tinnitus. Urine increased, strong. Vertigo. Walking, late. Worms.
HERBAL - Pine baths may also be made by adding Oleumpinus sylvestris to an ordinary bath in the proportion
of one minim to the gallon. These baths have a reputation in the treatment of rheumatism, gout, paralysis,
scrofula and skin diseases.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pin-s. was proved by Demeures in the tincture, and Patzack observed the effect of bathing
in an infusion of the leaves.
Rheumatic, bronchial and urticaria symptoms. Rheumatic, gouty and paralytic pains in limbs, bones and joints.
Stiffness. Glandular swellings. Enlarged and painful liver and spleen. Sensitiveness to touch. Scalp sensitive.
Chest walls sensitive with a feeling of thinness, as if they would give way at a touch.
 Chilliness alternating with flushing, the face is alternately red and pale. Itching in general. Emaciation of lower
limbs. Weak ankles. Late walking in scrofulous and rickety children.
Bronchial mucus was increased. The kidneys were stimulated, burning on urination, flow increased, urine
strong. Itching of the nose and discharge of round worms was noted. The menstrual function was deranged.
MIND - Anxiety. Despondency. Mind dull, unable to think, caused by any exertion. Wants to do many things,
undertakes all and finishes none.
Abdomen - Distention of hypochondrium with pressive and burning pains. Enlargement of liver. Pressure and
fullness in liver and spleen. Colic with incarcerated flatus. Pain in inguinal glands with swelling.
Back - Drawing and stiffness in nape extending into occiput. Pressive, tensive drawing pain between shoulders
and small of back, motion difficult.
Chest - Oppression. Anterior portion of chest painful to touch. Burning in sides of chest. In middle of sternum
sensation - as if a cupping-glass had been applied inside.
Ears - Sticking in ears. Roaring in ears.
Eyes - Eyes inflamed. Margins of lids red. Vision dim, veiled. Squint.
Face - Face alternately pale and red. Tearing in face.
Female - Menses, earlier, delayed. Menses, usually scanty, became more profuse.
Food - Appetite at first decreased, afterwards increased.
Head - Dullness, fullness, heaviness of head. Tearing in temples. Pressive headache. Headache worse by
any movement of eyes. Scalp sensitive.
Heart - Palpitations.
Kidneys - Violent boring-burning pains in kidneys, extending along ureters. Burning pains when urinating.
Spasms of bladder. Urination is difficult. Very greatly increased secretion of urine. Urine of strong odor.
Limbs - Stiffness, gouty pain in all joints, especially finger joints. Cramps in calves.
Lungs - Hoarseness. Breath tight, especially when walking. Increased bronchial mucus. Short, dry cough.
Expectoration greater when coughing.
Modalities - Worse by exertion, walking, touch. Worse in morning, evening.
Mouth - Pain in teeth with heat of face and pain in head. Dry mouth with increased thirst.
Nose - Violent nosebleed several days in succession. Mucus discharge from nose. Sensation of coryza. Itching
of nose.
Rectum - Constipation. Stool thin, pasty with colic and great excitement, bilious. Bloody, slimy, hemorrhoidal
discharge. Troublesome itching at anus. Discharge of round worms.
Skin - Nettle-rash. Itching all over, especially about joints and on abdomen. Nose itches.
Sleep - Great sleepiness, especially forenoon with restless sleep in evening. Sleepless. Dreams which seem
when remembered like real occurrences.
Stomach - Pressure in pit of stomach after eating with great distention.
Temperature - Chilliness, especially towards evening, alternating with flushes of heat. Perspiration general,
easy.
Throat - Uneasiness in throat as if something in the way. Painful swelling of submaxillary glands.
Vertigo - Vertigo, even to falling down.
COMMENTS - In a patient of Cooper's, Pin-s. caused a “headache worse by any movement of the eyes” and
it cured a case of squint.
Hansen gave “emaciation of lower limbs” and “weak ankles in children" as indications for it and mentioned that
the tinctures may be used externally, while the potencies are given internally.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Pin-1. - constipation, amenorrhea, miscarriage. Pinus lamber- tina sap is a
decided cathartic. Delayed and painful menstruation. (2) Abies-c., Abies-n. (3) Terebe., Sabin., Juni., Thuj.,
Aloe., Pix. (4) Strong urine, Benz-ac. (5) Red margin of eyes, Sulph., Bac.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
