name: Platinum Muriaticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - plat-m. Platinum muriaticum. Platina chloride. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Bone, disorders. Cancer. Caries. Condylomata. Gonorrhea. Fever. Headaches.
Laryngismus. Syphilis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Plat-m. was experimented with by Hofer of Pau, who applied a saturated solution locally
and administered solutions internally.
There is only a fragmentary proving, the mental symptom “thinks she has been poisoned” might be helpful
as a guide in certain cases. The local application produced acute irritation of the skin and glans penis with an
eruption on the latter like commencing chancre.
Decay and caries of the nasal and tarsus bones. Syphilitic caries and syphilitic rheumatism. Laryngismus.
Stricture of esophagus and cancer of the stomach. Canker, condylomata. Acne. Mercury abuse. Chronic
gonorrhea.
Involuntary movement of tissues of muscles of nape, back and limbs for several hours. Fever, headaches,
constricting sensations and fibrillary twitchings were induced by internal doses.
Plat-m. has achieved beneficial results after Kali-i. failed to cure in syphilitic affection, violent occipital
headaches, dysphagia and syphilitic throat and bone affections, decay of bones of feet.
MIND - Thinks she has been poisoned (Ars., Lach.).
Head - Some headache with slight acidity of stomach. Severe headache, especially in occiput with fever.
Kidneys - Acute inflammation of urethra, pain on urinating, slight dysuria.
Male - Violent itching on glans and prepuce with sensation of warmth. Eruption about glans penis, somewhat
livid, raised, size of pin head, looks like commencing syphilitic sore, but disappears in twelve hours.
Mouth - Metallic taste.
Skin - Discolored yellow. Skin becoming covered with rosy red eruption that disappears after a few minutes
from local application.
Stomach - Acidity of stomach with headache. Warmth and heaviness in epigastrium. Nausea and vomiting.
Temperature - Slight shuddering, pulse accelerated, warmth in epigastrium.
Throat - Violent constriction of larynx, so that speech and swallowing were impeded.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Platinum Mur. Natronatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -plat-m-n. Platinum muriaticum natronatum. Sodium chloroplatinate. Solution. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Eructation. Flatus. Nausea. Polyuria. Salivation. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hofer experimented with Plat-m-n. on the same man who took Plat-mur. The chief additional
symptom was decided increased secretion of urine and saliva.
 Slight headache. Feeling of warmth and heaviness in stomach. Rumbling in abdomen. Transient colic.
Emission of flatus. Eructation of gas. Nausea and inclination to vomit.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Plectranthus Fruticosus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - plect. Plectranthus fruticosus. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abdomen, coldness. Cholera. Cramps. Dentition. Diarrhea. Dysphagia. Fever. Intermittent, fever.
Lumbrici. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. Shoulder, pains. Spastic, paralysis. Stiff neck. Sweat, local. Throat, sore.
Toothache. Wrists, pains.
HOMEOPATHIC - Plect. was proved by the Austrian Provers' Association. Severe symptoms were induced in
the head, throat, intestinesandrectum, limbs and joints. Hansen mentioned spastic paralysis as having been
remedied by it.
Toothaches with swelling of face and difficulty of opening mouth. “Pain near right jaw joint as if a tooth were
coming through” suggests a use for the remedy in difficult cutting of wisdom teeth.
Burning sensation throughout the digestive tract. Coldness of abdomen, better in open air. Pressure on rectum
and bladder. Discharge of white mucus from anus, causing scratching. Whites of eyes yellow, worse left. Sweat
of right foot, left foot dry of right foot and both hands and no other part of scalp.
Pains and other symptoms come and go suddenly. Exhaustion, bruised sensation, genera] discomfort. Cramps
and paralytic pains in joints. Pains of many kinds in right shoulder. Pains about the navel. Affects the right side
more than the left.
Modalities - Better by application of ice, belchings. Burning in mouth worse from all food and drink. Chewing
causes pain in temples. Worse by motion, moving head, turning body, swallowing. Worse while urinating,
better after urinating. Worse by warmth of stove. Pressure in stomach, pain in umbilical region, worse after
eating.
Sensations - Cool sensation followed by burning at root of tongue and palate. As if a morsel stuck in the throat
after swallowing. Pressure as from a heavy weight in stomach. As through air were piercing
Plectranthus fruticosus the marrow of the bones.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Urinary symptoms, Oci. (2) Black stools, Lept. (3) Stitches in chest, Kali-c. (4)
Pains come and go suddenly, Lyc., Bell. (5) Crumb in throat, Hep., Nit-ac., Arg-n.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Plumbago Littoralis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - plumbg. Plumbago littoralis. Plumbago scandens. Bay of Rio Janeiro. N. O. Plumbaginaceae.
Tincture of leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Blisters. Eyes, inflammation. Fever. Kidneys, pain. Saliva, milky. Ulcerations. Vertigo.
HERBAL - Mure says Plumbg. is a creeper inhabiting the shores in the bay of Rio de Janeiro. Many of the
plants of this genus are acrid and caustic in the highest degree.
The Treasury of Botany noted that the root of Plumbago scandens, the Herbe du Diable of San Domingo, is a
blistering agent when fresh, so also is that of Plumbago rosea. The beggars employ Plumbago europea to
raise ulcers on their body to excite pity, and used internally it is said to be as good an emetic as ipecac.
HOMEOPATHIC - Mure proved Plumbg. The most peculiar symptoms were profuse, milky saliva. Ulceration
of commissures of lips, which is an evidence of its acridity. Costiveness with red urine. Pain in humerus on
lifting anything. Hot arms with cold hands. Vertigo after eating. Aversion to everything.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Costiveness wifi red urine, Lyc. (2) The Plumbaginaneae an allied to the
Primulaceae. (3) Plantaginacea< - the root of Plumbg-eu. is used dried as ; remedy for toothache.
REFERENCES Clarke.

two drams of the Liquor plumbi sub-acetatis to the ounce of water. Also in pruritus pudendi, equal parts of the

Plb-acet. has painful cramps in paralyzed limbs, severe pain and muscular cramps in gastric ulcer, locally, as

PHARMACY-plb-chr. Plumbumchromicum. Lead chromate. Chrome yellow. Trituration. Historical dose: All

HOMEOPATHIC - Several cases of poisoning by Plb-chr. have been observed. The symptoms present the
cardinal features of lead poisoning. Cramps. Convulsions with terrible pains. Pupils enormously dilated. The
face was red and hot and there was heat of the body generally.
Erythematous redness of chest and abdomen. Retracted abdomen. Violent diarrhea of yellow color. Yellow
stools with constipation. The symptoms were worse towards evening. Better by drinking warm milk.

name: Plumbum Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - plb. Plumbum metallicum. Lead metal. The element (Pb. At. Wt. 206.39). Plumbum aceticum.
Lead acetate. Sugar of Lead. Plumbum carbonicum. Lead carbonate. Pure White Lead. Trituration.
Historicaldose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Anus, prolapsed. Anemia. Anesthesia. Aneurysm. Anidrosis. Appendicitis.
Arteriosclerosis. Asthma. Atrophy. Bone, tumors. Brain, disorders. Bright’s disease. Colic. Coma.
Constipation. Convulsions. Cramps. Cystitis. Depression. Diplopia. Dropsy. Dysuria. Emaciation. Epilepsy.
Epulis. Esophagus, stricture. Eyes disorders. Ganglion. Glaucoma. Gout. Hemoptysis. Headaches.
Hemorrhoids. Hernia, strangulated. Hyperesthesia. Hypertension. Hypopion. Ichthyosis. Intermittent fever.
Intestines, obstruction. Intussusception. Jaundice. Jaw, tumor. Kidneys, disorders. Lead, poisoning. Liver
disorders. Lockjaw. Locomotor ataxia. Marasmus. Metrorrhagia. Multiple sclerosis. Myelitis. Nephritis.
Neuritis. Numbness. Painter's colic. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Penchondritis. Progressive
muscular atrophy. Rectal pain. Sciatica. Spasms. Spine, diseases. Spleen, disorders. Stricture. Strokes.
Tabes mesenterica. Tobacco habit. Tongue, paralysis. Typhlitis. Umbilicus, disorders. Uric acid. Vaginismus.
Varicose veins. Wristdrop.
HOMEOPATHIC - Plb., the Saturn of the Alchemists, has been proved by Hartlaub, Trinks, Hering and
Nenning. To those symptoms have been added those of numberless cases of poisoning among workers with
lead and painters, symptoms from drinking lead contaminated waters, from the use of lead in cosmetics, and
from cases of suicide.
Teste noted that metallic lead was seldom used in old school practice as it was considered inert, but Boerhaave
gave it internally, reduced to an impalpable powder, forleucor- rhea, dysentery, syphilis and gout.
The salts of lead, in the form of plaster and “Foulard water,” have been largely used as external applications
in skin diseases, vaginal and urethral injections. Injury has frequently resulted, especially from repelled
eruptions.
Among painters and lead manufacturers, the best-known symptoms are colic and wrist drop. Kidney irritation
with albuminuria, ending in granular degeneration with attendant heart hypertrophy, optic neuritis and
blindness.
There is an excess of uric acid in the blood of persons under the influence of lead and actual gouty deposits
and gouty attacks have been observed. In one case of lead poisoning, there was an enlargement of the knees
and contraction of the lower limbs, completely crippling the patient.
Useful for general sclerotic conditions. It affects the muscles, nerves, spinal cord, abdomen, navel, kidneys,
blood vessels and blood. Particularly affects the blood, alimentary and nervous systems.
Lead paralysis is chiefly of extensors, forearm or upper limb from center to periphery with partial anesthesia
 or excessive hyperesthesia, preceded by pain. Localized neuralgic pains, neuritis.
Progressive muscular atrophy. Infantile paralysis. Locomotor ataxia. Bulbar paralysis. Peripheral disorders.
Paralysis of single parts, wrist drop, flaccid with hyperesthesia, worse touch. Tremors, followed by paralysis.
Attacks of the neural axons and the anterior horns. Multiple sclerosis, posterior spinal sclerosis. Contractions
and boring pain. Retraction, sense of a string pulling back or in. Constrictive sensation in internal organs.
Violent contractions.
Convulsive trembling and jerking of the limbs. Convulsions, chronic epilepsy with
marked aura with hemorrhages. Boring, cramps. Lightning pains that extort cries. Small aneurysms all over
the body. Dropsical swelling. Arthralgia.
Symptoms appear slowly, insidiously, progressively, often with violent side effects of very changeable and
incoherent character, coming in single parts, etc. Anesthesia is as marked as excessive hyperesthesia.
Exaggerates her condition. Perception slow, comprehension is difficult. Delirium, coma and convulsions.
Hematosis is interfered with, rapid reduction in number of red corpuscles, causing pallor jaundice, and anemia.
Hypertension and arteriosclerosis. Gout. Acute nephritis with amaurosis and cerebral symptoms.
Impulse to stretch with abdominal distress. Retraction of abdomen, anus, testes, navel etc. Excessive and
rapid emaciation. Emaciation of limbs with plump body, of paralyzed parts, of single parts after neuralgias.
Marasmus of infants in apparently hopeless cases, abdomen large and hard and constipation extreme.
MIND - Mental exhaustion from physical labor. Confusion of mind while standing. Weakness or loss of memory
(Anae., Bar-c.). Deficiency of ideas. Increasing slowness and apathy. Slow perception. Stupid, imbecile. Timid,
restless and anxious. Unable to find proper word while talking. Amnesia aphasia.
Mental depression. Quiet and melancholy. Gloom alternating with excitement. Censorious. Taciturn. Aversion
to company. Timidity about appearing in public. Restlessness at night, wants to go from one bed to another.
Anxiety with restlessness and yawning. Hysteria, only while being watched. Screams from time to time. Fright
without cause. Frantic, bites, strikes. Fears of poisoning, of being assassinated. Thinks every one about her
is a murderer. Delusion of dead persons. Paretic dementia.
Feigns sickness or exaggerates her condition. Inclined to cheat and deceive. Plays antics. Foolish behavior.
Cursing. Wild delirium with distorted face.
Delirium, nocturnal, alternating with colic or pain in the limbs. Delirium from hearing music. Delirium after
epilepsy. Disposition to suicide or do himself some bodily injury. Time passes too slowly.
Abdomen - Colic, accompanies many symptoms. Colic alternates with delirium and pain in atrophied limbs.
Obstructed flatus with intense colic. Abdominal wall feels drawn by a string to spine. Navel feels retracted.
Abdomen is drawn into uneven lumps. Radiating abdominal pains to all parts of the body. Hernia, navel. Intus-
susception, strangulated hernia. Boring or as if forced through a narrow place. Pain causes desire to stretch.
Back - Spinal cord sclerosis. Lightning-like pains, temporarily better by pressure.
Breasts - Stitches and burning pains in breasts (Apis, Con., Carb-an., SiV). Induration of breasts.Breasts
become momentarily harder or smaller with colic.
Causations - Ill effects of repelled eruptions. Sexual excess. Lead, cadmium or aluminum poisoning.
Chest - Oppression of chest, appearing periodically. Pressure on chest, especially when breathing deeply or
laughing. Shootings in chest and sides, sometimes with obstructed respiration. Apices of lungs affected. Small
red papules on chest, desquamation.
Constitutions - Particularly adapted to adults, males more than females, particularly to persons of a dry,
bilious constitution with somewhat jaundiced, irascible, hypochondriac or disposed to religious monomania.
Ears - Tinnitus (Chin., Nat-sal., Carb-s.). Hears music with frightful delirium. Occasional sudden deafness.
Eyes - Pupils contracted. Yellow or deep bluish red sclerotics. Optic neuritis, central scotoma. Intra-ocular,
suppurative inflammation. Glaucoma from spinal disorders. Sudden loss of sight after fainting. Paralysis of
upper lid. Profuse hot lachrymation.
Face - Yellow, corpse-like, cheeks sunken. Skin, greasy, shiny. Pale and emaciated. Swelling of face, one
side. Twitching of side of face (right). Tremor of naso-labial muscles.
Female - Vaginismus with emaciation and constipation. Vulva and the vagina hypersensitive. Ovarian pain,
better stretching legs. Menorrhagia with sensation of string pulling from abdomen to back. Cannot pass urine
in pregnancy from lack of sensation or paralysis. Tendency to abortion from undeveloped uterus. Feeling of
lack of room for fetus in uterus.
Head - Headache, as if a ball was rising from the throat into the head. Delirium alternating with colic. Hair very
dry, falls from beard.
Heart - Cardiac weakness. Pulse soft and small, dicrotic. Pulse wiry, slow sinks even to 40. Painful constriction
of peripheral arteries.
Kidneys - Chronic interstitial nephritis with great pain in abdomen. Contracted kidney. Paralysis of bladder,
 difficult urination or retention, suppression. Frequent ineffectual tenesmus. Scanty urine. Urine profuse, but
flows slowly, drop by drop. Albuminous, low specific gravity. Diabetes mellitus. Uremia.
Limbs -Paralysis oflowerlimbs. Paralysis of single muscles. Pain in atrophied limbs, alternating with colic.
Sciatica and muscular atrophy. Lightning like pains better by pressure. Stinging and tearing in limbs, also
twitching and tingling, numbness, pain or tremor. Weakness and painful lameness of arms and hands.
Extension is difficult. Paralysis from overexertion of the extensor muscles in piano players (Cur.). Arms shaky
when attempting to use them. Wrist drop. Paralysis of lower limbs after childbirth. Pains in muscles of thighs,
come in paroxysms. Cramps in calves. Loss of patellar reflex. Hands and feet cold. Feet swollen. As if feet
were made of wood. Pain in right big toe, very sensitive to touch.
Male - Testicles drawn up, feel constricted. Frequent pollutions. Loss of sexual power.
Modalities - Bending back ameliorates pressure in stomach, pain in epigastrium, pain in back. Bending double
ameliorates colic. Better by hard pressure, rubbing, physical exertion, stretching limbs. Better at rest, lying
down. Worse from motion, grasping smooth objects, touch. Worse mental exertion, company. Worse at night,
open air, clear weather, foggy weather. Damp weather causes profuse salivation. Swelling in abdomen and
cough are worse lying on right side.
Mouth - Sweet taste. Sticky saliva, blue. Yellow inside the mouth. Aphthae, fetid ulcers. Gums swollen, pale.
Hard tubercles on gums. Distinct blue lines along margins of gums. Tongue tremulous, red on margin.
Cannot put it out, seems paralyzed. Loud motion of lower jaw and frightful grinding of teeth.
Nose - Coldness of the nose. Erysipelatous inflammation of nose. Obstruction of nose. Accumulation of
tenacious mucus in nostrils. Fluent coryza with discharge of serous mucus. Fetid smell in nose. Loss of smell
with epilepsy.
Rectum - Anus feels drawn up or painfully contracted. Neuralgiaofrectum. Prolapsed anus with paralysis.
Constipation. Stools, hard, lumpy, black with urging and spasm of anus. Stools, granular, hard black balls
like sheep dung, passed with an urging cramp in anus. Obstructed evacuation from impaction of feces (Plat.).
Stubborn constipation or colics of infants.
Sensations - As if everything were weighed down. As if something were working at top of head with a sense
of screwing from throat into brain. As if a wheat hull in throat. As if abdomen and back were too close together,
abdomen drawn to spine with a string. Bowels as if twisted, constricted, distended with gas. As if abscess
forming near umbilicus. Anal sphincter as if drawn in. As if a bag not quite filled with fluid lay in bowels. As if
fluid rolled from one side to other of abdomen. As if thighs pierced with needles. As if feet made of wood.
Skin - Oversensitive to open air. Dry, wrinkled, shriveled and drawn over the bones. Jaundice. Yellow, dark-
brown liver spots. Bluish, red spots. Dilated veins of forearms and legs. Small wounds easily inflamed and
suppurate. Dry, burning ulcers. Bed sores. Blisters, corns, bunions. Gangrene.
Sleep - Falls asleep while speaking, talking during sleep. Nocturnal sleeplessness with abdominal spasms.
Jerks during sleep. Odd position during sleep. Must stretch in every direction. Many dreams, sometimes
lascivious with erections. Coma and lethargy, sometimes with dizziness.
Stomach - Contraction in esophagus and stomach, pressure and tightness. Gastralgia, better hard pressure,
bending backwards. Foul or fecal belchings. Periodical or persistent vomiting of food. Vomiting of brown-black
liquid or of green mucus. Vomiting of fecal matter with colic and constipation.
Temperature - Coldness from exertion. General cold sweat during stools. Feet cold, only when walking.
Throat - Solids cannot be swallowed. Dysphagia, fluids can be swallowed. Paralysis of gullet with inability to
swallow. Globus hystericus. Stricture of esophagus from spasms.
Vertigo - Fainting in a room full of people or on going from one room to another.
COMMENTS - Tunzelmann reported a number of cases of acute poisoning from drinking water containing
lead.
In one such case, a cook was ill for three weeks. Unable to retain any food in the stomach, constant nausea
and, even when no food was taken, frequent vomiting of greenish watery fluid, worse at night.
Skin was yellowish, conjunctiva decidedly yellow. Tongue was furred, coated at back, very yellow, horrible
taste, fetor of breath, bowels confined. Extreme debility. Hydr. 3c gave great relief, but three months later the
hands became paralyzed, which led to the testing of the drinking water and the discovery of lead.
A boy, age 12, had bronchial catarrh with a loose cough and consolidation of left apex. As soon as the poisoned
water was stopped, he rapidly recovered.
An elder brother had hemoptysis, and coughed up half a pint of blood. Nothing was found wrong with the lungs
beyond a slight feebleness of respiration at the apices. Three months later, after a day's rowing, the
hematemesis returned with a nosebleed. Now distinct dullness was found at right apex. Rapid recovery
followed stopping the water.
Women who work with lead frequently abort. Women who do not work with lead but whose husbands do, abort
 in even greater proportion. Children bom under these conditions are frequently idiotic or epileptic.
Characteristic retraction and sense of retraction. Sensation of or actual drawing in of abdominal wall, were
drawn back by a string to the spine. The cheeks are retracted, sunken. Excessive and rapid emaciation.
Emaciation of certain parts (Caust.). Anemia. Memory loss.
Progressive muscularatrophy. Parkinson's disease. Paralysis of single muscles. Paralyzed parts lose flesh.
Progressive locomotor ataxia. Stroke, with spastic paralysis. Epilepsy preceded by vertigo, sometimes sighing,
followed by a stupid feeling.
Cramps, spasms, convulsions, paralyzes, tremors. Clonic or tonic convulsive movements of limbs from
cerebral sclerosis or tumor. Cramps in the fingers. Wrist drop, weak wrist from ovemse. Lead palsy.
Spasm of bladder of esophagus. Violent colic. Strangulated hernia. Colon spasms. Painful impacted bowels
(Alum, and Op. are painless). Vaginismus, spasm of utems and expulsion of its contents. Useful for vaginismus
resulting in paralytic symptoms. Sensation as if there was not room enough for fetus.
Anesthesia and hyperesthesia. Restlessness, lassitude, faintness. Sensation in abdomen at night that causes
patient to stretch violently for hours, must stretch in every direction. Assumes strange positions in bed at night.
Pains are wandering or radiating, vague, paroxysmal. Ailments develop slowly and can intermit for a time.
Alternations are common, delirium with colic, diarrhea and constipation jerks of flexors and extensors, paralysis
and colic. Right side is most affected, symptoms go from left to right (throat). Symptoms worse 8 a.m. to 9 a.m.
Frohling related the case of N., a farmer, 46, who was taken ill in November 1893 with attacks of colic with
vomiting and extreme constipation, action only obtained by large enemata. Had been constipated in former
years, but without illness. Op. had given only temporary relief.
After December 1983, vomiting was rare, but colic increased in intensity up to February 1894, when Frohling
saw him first and found him wasted to a skeleton, abdomen drawn in, appetite bad, feeling ill.
His mind was somewhat affected, unable to give sensible answers to questions. Constant urgent call to stool,
but only small, hard, black balls were passed. Liver dullness only heard from upper border of sixth to upper
border of seventh rib.
Lead poisoning was suspected, but as no evidence of it could be found, Plb. 6c three times a day was
prescribed. In six days the colic attacks were less frequent and less severe, two stools passed without enema,
his mind clearer.
Improvement continued in all respects, and in fourteen days N. was able to leave his bed to which he had been
confined since November. By the middle of March he made an hour's journey to see Frohling and was hardly
recognizable, he had gained so much flesh and his liver was of normal size.
Wingfield reported two characteristic cases. The first concerned Mrs. D., 50, no children, sparely built, very
nervous, constipated fifteen years, took a teaspoonful of Cascara extract every other night. Tongue coated
with yellowish white fur. Had constant headaches and after each motion was thoroughly exhausted and had
to lie down the rest of the day.
Plb. 6x was given, three grains twice a day. In two days, bowels began acting naturally.In three weeks the
headaches were gone, tongue clean, much less nervous.
Wingfield's second case was Miss M., 25, florid, had boils appear on face and arms and chronic constipation.
The constipation had been a trouble since she was twelve years old. Slight spinal curvature. Tongue furred,
occasional headaches. Suffered much during menstrual periods. Plb. 6x twice daily at once relieved the
constipation and soon the boils disappeared. Patient soon felt quite well.
Arriage, of Mexico City, reported the case of a woman, 73. seized with symptoms of intestinal occlusion, violent
colic, nausea, constipation, meteorism, complete anorexia and no fever. Nux-v. relieved the colic, and then
Plb. 12c and later 13c, gradually brought about recovery in four days.
Nash cured a severe case of post-diphtheria paralysis in a middle-aged man. The leading symptom was
excessive hyperesthesia, he could not bear to be touched anywhere due to the pain. A single dose of Plb.
40,000c cured.
Nash told of a man, 70, attacked with severe pain in his abdomen and finally a large, hard swelling developed
in the ileo-cecal region, very sensitive to contact or least motion. It began to assume a bluish tint and, on
account of his age and weakness, the man's life was despaired. But his daughter, the wife of a medical man,
found the symptoms in Raue under Plb. in the chapter on Typh., and Plb. 200c cured.
Theuerkaufcured a case of hypopion with great pain in six weeks using Plb. 6c.
Skinner cured a case of epilepsy in which the head turned to the right after a fit.
W. H. Woodyatt reported a case of “vasomotor neurosis” affecting the left eye. Mrs. D., 29, had been ill for two
weeks and supposed she had caught cold in the eye. She had a drooping upper lid, intense photophobia, very
profuse lachrymation of hot teai s, peri-corneal injection, deep bluish redness of sclerotica, most marked at
corneal margin. Cornea was very faintly hazy. Pupil contracted. Sight misty.
 Ars. 6x and Plant. 6x failed to relieve. Plb. 6x was then given with immediate
Plumbum metallicum improvement, which went on to cure in seven days.
Plb. cured acase of right-sided sciatica that had been greatly benefited by Gnaph. 1c, but which had returned.
The symptoms included stiffness, soreness from great trochanter and point of exit of nerve to knee, weakness
in thigh, worse by stooping, walking causes sensation as if pushing a knife in thigh.
Plb. 6c was given four times day. Up to the twelfth day there was no change, on that day, the pain suddenly
disappeared. The case had lasted nine months.
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Plat., Alum., Petr. Compare: ( 1) Plb-acet. (2) Plb-i. Alum., Plat., Op., Podo., Merc.,
Thal. (3) Plect. - paralysis, spastic, spinal form, (4) Plb-chr. (5) Plb-p. - loss of sexual power, locomotor ataxia.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Plutonium Nitricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - plut-n. Plutonium nitricum. Plutonium. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - AIDS. Bone, cancer. Bone marrow, affections. Brain, tumors. Cancer. Diarrhea. Fatigue. Fibrosis.
Hodgkin's diseases. Leukemia. Lung, cancer. Lung, complaints. Radiation, poisoning. Thyroid, enlarged. Virus
infections. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Very serious pathologies. Cancers, leukemia. Periodicalfatigue. Paralyzing fatigue.
Chilliness and shivering, yet great feeling of heat in head and face.
Desire to lie down from feeling of extreme heaviness. Body seems to be heavy like lead. Head very heavy, like
an enormous weight, difficult to keep head up. Feels the pull of gravity. Desire to lie down on one's back and
on the floor.
Sensation of dryness in throat, as if swallowing of food would be impossible. Paralyzing pain in sacral region.
Pain as if broken or twisted. Great restlessness at night. Weakness of lower limbs. Cannot walk upright, must
crawl on all fours.
MIND - Serious, no smile on the face, as if carrying burden of world on their shoulders. Extremely
conscientious. Delusion of having too many responsibilities. Fastidious, impulse to put things in order. Deep
religious feelings or philosophical thoughts. Feels alone and empty.
Aggressive, reckless impulses. Irritability and aggression. Resentment, controlled anger. Reproachful,
reproaches his wife. Outbursts of violence. Aggressive fantasies. Dominant behavior.
Anxiety about health. Fear of falling ill, of catastrophes. Fear of narrow places, claustrophobia. Fear of one's
own impulses, of being too aggressive. Panic-stricken. Persistent feeling of existential threat. Delusion of being
threatened. Delusion of decaying and disintegrating.
Depressed, dark gloomy mood. Weeping on account of physical pain. Sadness better company. Restlessness,
cannot find a place or position to relax. Delusion of changing one's identity. Clairvoyant. Severe mental
illnesses.
Abdomen - Cutting pain, better bending double.
Back - Paralyzing pain in sacral region. Back pain extending to posterior part of thigh and popliteal region.
Breasts - Sensation of heaviness and fullness in breasts. Sensation of tension in breasts, desire to wear a
bra.
Eyes - Burning sensation.
Food - Desires bacon, raw meat, lamb, pork, ham, fat.
Head - Shattering headache, in forehead. Pain as if vertex comes up, as if it would explode. Pressing pain in
forehead. Sensation of enormous heaviness. Sensation of great heat in head and face.
Limbs - Sensation of leaden heaviness. Sensation as if left leg were shorter. Pain in soles of feet on account
of vesicles on toes.
Modalities - Better warmth, sitting in the sun, hot applications, hot bathing. Better massage, strong
pressure, after long sleep. Worse from walking. Worse 3 p.m., sunset, evening, night. Worse overcast weather,
first ray of sun.
Rectum - Anal warts. Sensation of insecurity in rectum when passing flatus.
Sleep - Short sleep improves. Sleeplessness and restlessness from pain in sacral region, tossing about to
relieve pain; sleeplessness from feeling of heat. Dream of falling. Dream of killing or murders, of dead people,
of bodies.
RELATIONS - Compare: Androc., Aur., Care., Hydrog., Med., Rad-br., Stram., Syph., Tarent., Uran-n., X-ray.
REFERENCES - Sherr.

name: Pneumococcinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pneu. Pneumococcinum venenosum. Pneumococcus nosode. Bacteria of the Diplococcus
genus, Micrococcales. Non-pathologic bacteria of the mucus membranes. Nosodes. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Hemicrania. Hypochondria. Memory, loss. Neuralgia of the skull. Pneumonia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pneumococcus is a gram positive bacteria of the Diplococcus genus and of the
Micrococcaceae family. Pneumococcus is a saprophyte host of the mucus membranes. It is found in the saliva,
nasal and pharyngeal mucus, orthe conjunctiva of 50% of healthy subjects. Sevaus conducted a clinical
symptomatological study, but there is no homeopathic proving.
Respiratory complaints localized in the bronchial region. Cardiac palpitations. Dysmenorrhea with late menses
and premenstrual syndrome. Intoxication.
Depressive condition associated with pains situated all over the cervical and dorsal regions. Acute pains, which
come suddenly of the stinging (Nit-ac.) or cramping type (Cupr.), lasting only a short while. Constricting pains,
as if in a vice (Cact.).
MIND - Loss of memory. Depressive condition with anguish, anxiety. Desire to stay at home, horror of going
out (Sep.). Lack of taste for life. Impression that the patient is going to collapse, that he cannot walk. Very
afraid of being ill, of dying.
Abdomen - Bad digestion. Hepatic deficiency. Air in the stomach and colon. Distention and pain in the left
hypochondrium, eased by expulsion of wind. Gas with alternation of constipation and fetid stools.
Back - Dorsal and lumbar arthrosis. Dorsal pains, preventing standing.
Constitutions - Bilious and nervous, depressive, anxious. Allergic, psoric constitutions. sycotic, cancerous,
and tubercular constitutions.
Ears - Otitis media.
Eyes - Fatigue from neon light. Frontal pains above the eyes.
Female - Premenstrual aggravation. Menstrual cycle short, every 22 or 24 days. Menses stopping on the 2nd
day. Menses late, scanty, legs heavy and swollen before menses. Menstrual migraines and vertigo. Bearing
down pain and crosses legs (Sep.). Burning sensation during intercourse in cases of fatigue. Frigidity. Lack of
orgasm.
Food - Ameliorated by eating (Anae.).
Head - Pains in left frontal sinus. Headaches lasting for 3 to 4 consecutive days. Headache on coughing or
bending the head. Frequent headaches, localized at the nape of the neck, worse by noise. Right or left
hemicrania, worse by walking, which causes throbbing in the head. Feeling of liquid in the head on stooping.
Heart - Aching in the precordial region with pains. Cardiac neurosis. Basedow's heart. Rhythmic anomalies.
Emotive palpitations. Frequent palpitations at any time of the day. Palpitations forcing him to stop when walking
rapidly or climbing stairs. Frequent redness of the face when going into a hot room.
Kidneys - Weakness of the bladder. Passes urine when coughing (Caust.).
Limbs - Pains in the arms. Pains in the legs. Legs restless, especially before menses (Zinc., Lach.). Legs
heavy in the morning on waking. Trembling in the legs. Cramps in the feet. Poly-arthrosis.
Lungs - Sinusitis. Tracheitis. Chronic bronchitis. Emphysema. Incessant cough with no expectoration,
especially at night with
nausea. Feeling of having a feather in the throat (Kali-bi.). Dry cough in the cold or heat. Coughs in the heat,
particularly when entering a hot room and clears the throat (Rhus-t.). Sickening cough in the morning after
breakfast. Does not cough any more after 9 a.m. Coughs a great deal as a result of frequent bronchitis during
childhood. Has to stoop to cough.
Modalities - Better from the open air, in the country. Better from movement, a hot foot-bath, a short nap after
meals (Nux- v.). Worse on entering a warm room, from damp before menses. Worse from inactivity (Rhus-t.),
sitting for a long time, especially when remaining motionless, rest at night. Pains aggravated by rest, at night,
better by movement (Rhus-t.).
Mouth - Aphthae in the mouth.
Neck - Neck pains with frontal aching.
Cervical pains with back aching. Chronic degenerative rheumatism of the cervical column.
Rectum - Gas with the alternation of constipation and very fetid stools. Constipation with empty urging (Nux-
v.). Constipation when traveling (Ign.).
Skin - Itching with eruptions spread over the neck and forehead. Small eruptions on the face. Hands clammy.
Sleep - Sleepiness around 3 p.m.
Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Frequent nausea after eating. Gastric pains, especially when hungry. Stomach
cramps with burning sensations.
 RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Med. - amnesia for recent facts. Hasty with restless legs and burning in the heels.
Burning pains in the joints and vertebral column. Improvement at the seaside and in the knee-chest position.
(2) Thuj, - hydrogenoid condition, melancholy, worse from changing weather or after a trauma. Flatulence,
diarrhea, periodic skin complaints.
REFERENCES-Julian.

CLINICAL - Hemicrania. Hypochondria. Memory, loss. Neuralgia of the skull. Pneumonia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pneumococcus is a gram positive bacteria of the Diplococcus genus and of the
Micrococcaceae family. Pneumococcus is a saprophyte host of the mucus membranes. It is found in the saliva,

name: Podophyllum Peltatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -podo. Podophyllum peltatum. May-apple. American mandrake. N. O. Berberidaceae by some
placed in Ranuncu- laceae. Closely related to both. Tincture of root gathered after ftuit has ripened of whole
fresh plant of ripe fruit. Solution of resinous extract, podophyllin. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acidity. Amenorrhea. Anus, prolapsed. Asthma, bronchial. Bedwetting. Bilious, attack.
Bronchitis. Cataract. Cholera. Cornea, ulcer. Dentition. Deafness. Depression. Diabetes. Diarrhea.
Duodenum,catarrh. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Fevers. Flatus. Gagging. Gallstones. Gastric,
disorders. Goiter. Headaches. Heart, pain. Hemorrhoids. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Ovary, disorders. Ovarian,
tumor. Palpitations. Pneumonia. Proctitis. Prolapsed, uterus. Prolapsed, rectum. Prostatitis. Pustules.
Sciatica. Stomatitis. Strabismus. Taste, disorders. Tenesmus. Tongue, burning. Urticaria. Uterus, prolapsed.
Vomiting. Whooping cough. Worms. Yellow, diarrhea.
HERBAL - Podophyllum grows throughout the United States in damp, shady places, usually in woods. It has
five to nine-lobed leaves, large white nodding flowers, and yellowish, egg-shaped fruits. The fruits are not
unlike a small lemon, hence the plant is sometimes called “wild lemon.” It flowers in May and June, and the
fruit ripens in October.
Indian tribes used the root to expel worms, and dropped the juice of the root into the ear to cure deafness. “All
the tribes are fond of the fruit,” said Raffinesque, quoted by Hale, who gave an account of the medicine.
The herbal practitioners adopted the remedy and used it as the “vegetable mercury.” The first homeopathic
proving was made by Williamson.
HOMEOPATHIC - Podo, is a remedy for bilious constitution. It affects chiefly the duodenum, small intestines,
liver, rectum, ovary, scapula and throat. It generally affects the right side.
Torpidity of the liver. Jaundice. Hypogastric pain. Gastro-enteritis with colicky pain and bilious vomiting.
Painless cholera morbus. Profuse diarrhea. Stool is watery with jelly-like mucus, painless, gushing and
offensive. Diarrhea, while being bathed or washed, of dirty water soaking through napkin, with gagging.
Portal engorgement with a tendency to hemorrhoid. Fullness of superficial veins. Relaxed sphincters.
Prolapsed uterus. Pendulous abdomen after confinement. Troubles during pregnancy.
Alternating conditions, diarrhea alternating with constipation, headache alternating with diarrhea. Sudden
shocks from jerking pains. Constantly shaking and rubbing region of liver with hands.
Much drowsiness and desire to stretch. Great loquacity during chill and heat. Thirst for large quantities of cold
water. Viscid mucus in mouth, coating teeth. Intense desire to press the gums together.
MIND - Fidgety and restless, cannot sit still. Whining. Child wants to be carried. Depression of spirits. Disgust
for life, during headaches. Imagines he is going to die or be very ill. Delirium from eating acid fruits.
Fatigue of mind from business. Aphasia. Want of power of expression even of simplest ideas. Absurd words
being chosen in place of right ones. Stupid during paroxysm of fever patient.
Loquacity during chill and fever, afterwards forgets what has passed. Inclined to talk, but would drop a sentence
before half finished. Great desire to talk during chill, but can't because he forgets words.
Abdomen - Distended abdomen, heat and emptiness. Sensation of weakness or sinking. Can lie
comfortably only on stomach. Fullness in right hypochondrium, with flatulence, pain and soreness. Rumbling
and shifting of flatus in ascending colon. Rubs for relief. Weight in hypogastric region. Pain in right inguinal
region, shoots down inner thigh to knees. Colic, in abdomen, with cramp-like knots, better flexing limbs. Colic
continues after stool. Abdominal viscera are sore, worse during vomiting, diarrhea, before and during menses.
Abdominal pains and stool excited by eating and drinking. Sick, empty feeling after stools.
Back - Nape of neck stiff, muscles sore. Pain under right scapula. Pain between shoulders. Pain in small of
back. Pain in lumbar and sacral regions, worse during stool, and still worse after stool. Pain in loins, worse
walking on uneven ground or from misstep.
Chest - Oppression in chest. Pains in chest worse by deep inspiration. Catarrh of chest during dentition.
Constitutions - Suited to persons of bilious temperament, especially after mercury poisoning.
Ears - Aching pain in right ear, with rough feeling extending along right Eustachian tube.
Eyes - Jaundiced. Eyes sunken. Eyes glazed and motionless. Cataract. Smarting, inflammation of lids. Lids
half closed. Pain in eyeballs and temples.
 Face - Hot. Cheeks flushed during diarrhea. Jaundiced.
Female - Suppressed menses with pelvic tenesmus. Menorrhagia from straining. Sensation as if the genitals
would come out during stool. Pain in the region of the ovaries (right), down the crural nerve worse stretching
the legs. Ovarian tumor with pain extending to shoulder. Pain in uterus and right ovary with shifting noises
along ascending colon. Can lie comfortably only on the abdomen during early months of pregnancy. Swelling
of labia during pregnancy. Hemorrhoids with prolapsed anus during pregnancy. Prolapsed uterus on straining
or overlifting after childbirth.
Food - Thirst for large quantities of cold water (Phos., Bry.). Appetite variable, at times voracious. Indifference
to food. Loss of appetite. Smell of food causes loathing. Satiety from small quantity of food, followed by nausea
and vomiting. Craves acids, which disagree. Worse after eating and drinking, especially acid fruit and milk.
Diarrhea after sour milk, canned fruits, acid fruit and milk.
Head - Headache, dull pressure, worse
Podophyllum peltatum morning, with heated face and bitter taste. Headache alternating with diarrhea, or
better by diarrhea. Darting pain in forehead, must close the eyes. Rolling of head from side to side with
moaning, during dentition, from business worry. Child perspires on head during sleep.
Heart - Palpitations with a clucking sensation, rising up to the throat, from emotions.
Kidneys - Frequent urination, at night, during pregnancy. Urinates immediately after drinking. Bedwetting.
Diabetes mellitus and insipidus.
Limbs - Paralytic weakness on left side. Pain between shoulders, under right scapula, in loins and lumbar
region. Pain along ulnar nerve of both arms. Pain in right inguinal region, shoots down inner thigh to knees.
Cramps in calves with stools.
Liver - Sore and painful liver, better rubbing. Stitches in liver region, worse while eating. Liver and whole
abdominal viscera are sore. Jaundice with gallstones.
Lungs - Inclination to breathe deep, sighing. Sensation of suffocation. Pneumonia. Chronic bronchitis.
Bronchial asthma, worse after Catching cold. Loose, dry, hacking cough, with remittent fever. Whooping cough
with constipation and loss of appetite.
Male - Diseases of prostate gland associated with rectal troubles.
Modalities - External heat ameliorates pain in bowels. Better by pressure, rubbing or stroking liver. Better
lying down, lying on abdomen, stretching in bed. Hot weather, summer, aggravates diarrhea. Worse in early
morning, 2 a.m. to 4 a.m., night. Worse open air, washing. Worse eating, swallowing, drinking, acid fruits,
milk. Worse before, during and after stool, dentition, mercury. Worse from motion, walking, ascending stairs,
exertion.
Mouth - Offensive odor. Bitter, foul, putrid taste. Everything tastes sour or putrid. Loss of taste, could not tell
sweet from sour. Tongue, broad, large, moist. Tongue coated as of mustard spread on it. Burning, rough or
flabby indented tongue. Grinding the teeth at night. Difficult dentition with intense desire to press the gums
together (Phyt.).
Rectum - Fetid flatus. Long standing diarrhea. Diarrhea alternating with other symptoms. Diarrhea early in
morning, during teething, with hot, glowing cheeks. Diarrhea while being bathed or washed, in hot weather,
after acid fruits. Morning, painless diarrhea when not due to venous stasis or intestinal ulceration. Gurgling
through the bowels, then yellow profuse putrid stools gush outpainlessly. Cholera infantum and morbus.
Constipation alternating with diarrhea (Ant-c.). Constipation, clay-colored, hard, dry, difficult. Prolapse of
rectum before or with stool. Internal and external hemorrhoids. Sensation of weakness in rectum. Severe
burning, deep in rectum, after stool. Anus feels very sore, sensitive and swollen.
Perspiration - Profuse, offensive sweat with sleep. Warm sweat on head and legs. Sweats on head with
coldness of skin.
Sensations - As if strabismus would occur. Pain in head as from ice on occipital protuberance. As if tongue,
throat and palate had been burned. Ball in upper esophagus. As if heart ascending to throat. As if a thousand
live things moving about in abdomen or of fish turning over. As if everything would drop through pelvis.
Skin - Moist, warm, jaundiced. Cold, clammy skin. Sallow skin jaundice, also in children. Rawness and itching
of genitals. Erysipelas. Intolerable itching of body and arms. Urticaria. Pustules, slow in healing. Scabs on
arms and legs.
Sleep - Sleepy after paroxysms of malaria. Heavy sleep, fatigue on waking. Moaning and whining during sleep.
Rising up in sleep without waking. Sleep disturbed, full of confused dreams.
Stomach - Stomach so weak that rice wouldn't digest. Heartburn, gagging or empty retching. Hot, sour
belching, nausea and vomiting. Belchings smelling like rotten eggs. Constant gagging. Vomiting of a hot, frothy
mucus. Vomiting of milk in infants.
Stool - Stools yellow with undigested food. Stools green, watery, at times mixed with
 Podophyllum peltatum mucus, gushing. Yellow, fetid profuse diarrhea. Stools, white like water. Pale, hard,
chalky stools. Stools foaming with meal-like sediment. Stools run right through the diaper, followed by
weakness. Muco-gelatinous stools after miscarriage. Stools involuntary during sleep, when passing flatus.
Temperature - Chills at 7 a.m. with pain in hypochondria and knees, ankles, wrists. Great loquacity during
fever.
Throat - Gagging in infantile diarrhea. As of a lump in esophagus. Sore throat, pain extends to ears. Dryness,
swallowing painful. Sore throat right extends to left. Rattling of mucus in throat. Goiter.
Vertigo - Vertigo, tendency to fall forward. Vertigo with sensation of fullness above eyes. Vertigo while standing
in open air. Vertigo from gastric or bilious disorders.
COMMENTS - An unintentional Podo, proving recorded by E. V. Rose brought out the chief characteristics
and showed that its reputation as a “vegetable mercury” is well deserved.
At 11 a.m., Mr. J., 26 took grains x of Podo, lx to “stir up his liver.” At 6 p.m. he was taken with an indescribable
sick feeling all over and a persistent, dry, rough feeling in pharynx and esophagus, extending along right
Eustachian tube with dull, aching pain in right ear, feeling as though a ball or lump in upper esophagus.
At 8 p.m., he had a dull and stupefying headache, chiefly frontal, worse lying down. Fullness in stomach,
belching of gas, sour belchings, marked salivation and an offensive odor from the mouth. Sleep was disturbed,
full of confused dreams, rolled and tossed about, bed felt too hard and a feeling as though head and shoulders
were lying too low.
At 3 a.m., urge to stool, which was profuse, watery, and dark green. Frequent urging. Before stool there was
a peculiar weak, dull, griping pain below umbilicus, fullness in rectum. During stool there was a weak feeling
in the stomach. After stool, tenesmus and faint feeling.
These symptoms passed off in two or three days, the diarrhea was followed by
Podophyllum peltatum constipation, which was quickly removed by Nux-v.
External irritant. Produces a rawness like intertrigo when applied on the skin. The dust of the powdered root
sets up intense inflammation, ulceration and leucoma if it gets into the eyes. Useful in potency for eye
disorders.
Irritation of the brain, generally reflected to the abdominal viscera (cholera infantum), or the teeth (dentition).
Moaning and whining during sleep, the head is thrown back and rolls from side to side, the child grates its
teeth. Great desire to press gums or teeth together. Salivation, foul breath and moist, tooth-indented tongue
(Merc.). Burning sensation on the tongue. Thirst.
Bilious, remittent, and intermittent fevers. Loquacity during chill and heat. Prone to sweat. Delirium, apt to be
loquacious. Much drowsiness and desire to stretch. Congested, sensitive liver with excess or absence of bile.
Generally for diarrhea with any other symptoms, painful or painless. Children's diarrhea (Ars., Nit-ac.). Yellow,
profuse, offensive and excoriated diarrhea in infants with a raw and burning anus. Profuse stools, yellow or
white. Early morning diarrhea. Dysentery, colitis. Cholera. Hepatitis concomitant with severe diarrhea. Severe
cases of jaundice, gallstone attacks, and worms.
The stools may be painless or may be preceded, accompanied, and followed by colic, tenesmus and other
symptoms. Pains in sacrum in lumbar region with rectal and uterine symptoms, cramps in calves with stools.
Fullness and tenderness of the rectum. Proctitis, inflammation of the rectum and anus. Tendency to prolapse
in the rectum and genital organs. “Symptoms of prolapse uterus with pain in sacrum with muco- gelatinous
stools,” and “sensation at stool as if the genital organs would fall out.”
Pains in the ovaries, especially the right, extending down the anterior and inner side of thighs. Vomiting during
pregnancy. Swelling of labia during pregnancy. “Can lie comfortably only on stomach” during the early months
of pregnancy. Severe after-
Podophyllum peltatum pains with strong bearing-down sensation, hemorrhoids and prolapsed rectum after
confinement.
Alternating conditions. Diarrhea alternating with constipation, headache alternating with diarrhea, headache in
winter, diarrhea in summer, inflammation of scrotum or of the eyes, not of both. Antidotal to mercury. Worse
hot weather.
Nash cured an obstinate case of intermittent fever with violent chills, followed by intense fever with great
loquacity. When the fever was past, the patient fell asleep and, on waking, remembered nothing of his
loquacious delirium.
W. A. Burr related a case of a young man who had for some weeks a burning sensation along the left edge of
his tongue, occasionally shooting to tip or through to opposite edge. He had been in poor health, “bilious,” for
years. With catarrh of stomach, duodenum and bile ducts, extreme discomfort followed even the blandest
foods. Podo. 3x improved in two days and the tongue was well in a week.
Clarke often cured prolapsed anus in children with Podo. 6c. With Podo, lx, Mr. Knox Shaw relieved “continual
 urging and straining” in a case of rectal cancer too far gone for operation.
L. M. Barnes noted the case of a stout woman, 60, who complained of burning, aching, cutting pain in rectum.
She was obliged to be on her feet all day. Nervous, cross, irritable. Podo, cured.
Barnes also reported the case of a woman who, for four months after a miscarriage, had ovarian pain, worse
at night. She was sleepless, nervous, restless. Bearing down in abdomen and back. She was a large, stout
woman with a pendulous abdomen. Podo, cured after Puls, and Cimic. had only partially relieved.
Guernsey mentioned that it is often called for in complaints of pregnant and parturient women with the
sensation as if intestines were falling down. He mentioned also whooping cough with costiveness and loss of
appetite.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Mand. – Great desire for sleep, exaggeration of sounds and enlarged vision.
Bowels inactive, stools large, white andhard. (2) Aloe, Chel.,Merc., Nux-v., Sulph. (3) Prune. - colitis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Polygonatum Multiflorum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - polygo-m. Polygonatum multiflorum. Solomon's Seal. Lady's Seals. St. Mary's Seal. Sigillum
Sanctae Mariae. N.O. Liliaceae. Tincture of the root Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Alopecia. Back, pain. Bone, disorders. Bone, injuries. Bone, spurs. Bruises. Bunions.
Calcifications. Carbuncles. Constipation. Dysentery. Erysipelas. Hair, loss. Hemorrhoids. Hyperlipidemia.
Injuries. Joint, pains. Joint, weakness. Leucorrhea. Malaria. Metrorrhagia. Muscle, weakness. Pyorrhea.
Sores. Sprains. Tendon, disorders. Tinnitus. Tumors. Vertigo. Wounds.
HERBAL - Polyg-m., in material doses of tincture or low potencies, has been found useful in treating all kinds
of musculoskeletal disorders.
Astringent, demulcent and tonic. Combined with otherremedies, Solomon's Seal is given in pulmonary
consumption and bleeding of the lungs. It is useful also in female complaints.
It is used mainly in the form of a poultice and is believed to pre vent excessive bruising and to stimulate tissue
repair.
The infusion of 1 oz. to a pint of boiling water is taken in wineglassful doses and is also used as an injection.
It is a mucilaginous tonic, very healing and restorative, and is good in inflammations of the stomach and bowels,
piles, and chronic dysentery.
A distilled water made from the whole plant has been used as a skin tonic and is an ingredient of expensive
cosmetics.
Young shoots can be cooked, boiled and used as an asparagus substitute, they make an excellent vegetable
and are widely used in Turkey. Root - cooked. Rich in starch. The root should be macerated for some time in
water in order to remove bitter substances. Normally only used in times of famine, the root was powdered and
then made into a bread by the North American Indians.
COMMENTS - According to the English- Chinese Rare Chinese Materia Medica, raw ho-shou-wu, that is, the
dried root that has not been prepared with soybeans, is used to treat toxicosis (infections yielding abscess,
swellings beneath the skin, sores, carbuncles, and eruptive diseases like rubella), inflammation, constipation,
and hyperlipidemia.
The soybean-prepared ho-shou-wu is used as a tonic for yin and blood, nourishing the hair, strengthening the
bones and muscles, and used to treat pale complexion, dizziness, tinnitus, premature graying of hair,
weakness of loins and knees, numbness of extremities, metrorrhagia, profuse leucorrhea, weakness due to
lingering diseases (e.g., malaria), and hyperlipemia.
According to evaluations done with raw and processed ho-shou-wu, the processed version does have different
properties, and is the one with the most dramatic effects on preserving the immune system functions.
Processed ho-shou-wu is currently the only one that is regularly exported from China. During the past thousand
years in China, processed ho-shou-wu has been used to nourish the liver and kidney, promote the growth of
hair, treat alopecia, and premature graying of hair.
RELATIONS - Compare: Bell-p., Ruta, Calc., Symphytum.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Polygonum Punctatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - polyg. Polygonum punctatum. Smartweed. Polygonum hydropiper. Polygonum acre. Persicaria
urens. Water pepper. Pursh. N. O. Polygonacae. Britain, North America. Tincture of whole fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Antrum, pain. Blepharitis. Colic, flatulent. Cough. Diarrhea. Dysentery.
Dysmenorrhea. Dysuria. Eczema. Epilepsy. Gonorrhea. Gravel. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhoids. Hysteria.
Laryngitis. Nephritis. Neuralgia. Orchitis. Prostatitis. Sciatica. Spermatic cord, pain. Spleen disorders.
Strangury. Ulcers.
HERBAL - The Polygonum are named by Gerarde “Arse-smarts.” Burnett regarded it as a splenic and as
useful in old cases of syphilis. As a splenic, he found it was often required in cases of gout and in gouty eczema
with much irritation; he used it with much benefit in the 6c, 12c and 30c.
Hale stated, “Smart Weed is a popular domestic remedy throughout U.S.A. Applied externally it has the effect
of a mustard plaster and the leaves saturated with hot water are applied to relieve cramps and colic. Also as
an emollient in inflammation and sprains.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Polyg. was proved by W. E. Payne and others. The provers were all men, but clinical
experience has shown a definite action in the female generative sphere, as amenorrhea, aversion to sex and
congestion of the ovaries have been cured by it.
Acts upon the genito-urinary organs and the intestines, causing cutting pains, along the ureters, along
ovarian ducts, up spine with bearingdown. Pulsating, flashing, wandering pains in prostate. Coldness
alternating or coincides with heat in the same or other part, burning in chest with cold feeling in pit of stomach.
Smarting discharges.
Leading symptoms include aching pains in hips and loins with weight and tension in pelvis and tearing in groin,
worse right. Metrorrhagia, also amenorrhea in young
Polygonum punctatum girls. Varicose veins, hemorrhoids and rectal pockets. Burning in stomach followed
by feeling of coldness in the pit of the stomach.
Abdomen - Cold feeling in stomach with burning in chest. Cutting pains with great rumbling, as if whole
intestinal contents were in a fluid state. Griping pain with great rumbling, nausea and liquid feces. Flatulent
colic. Nausea.
Breasts - Shooting pains through the breasts.
Ears - Acute pain, on bending head down, better bending backwards.
Eyes - Puffiness under right eye. Lids twitch when closed and when lying down.
Face - Coldness in right face, when pain is most severe in left.
Female - Metrorrhagia, amenorrhea in young girls. Cutting pain along the fallopian tubes with bearing down.
Aching pains in hips and loins. Sensation as if hips were being drawn together. Sensation of weight and
tension within pelvis.
Head - Acute pulsative pains in temples.
Kidneys - Nephritic colic with grinding, griping, cutting bellyache. Suppurative nephritis. Cystitis. Painful
constriction at neck of bladder. Cutting pain along ureters. Urine scanty, dribbling, dark or calcareous, adherent
sediment.
Limbs - Aching in lower limbs. Feet alternately hot and cold. Sore pains in heels.
Male - Scrotum excoriated. Pulsating, burning pain in prostate on urinating. Pain in testes, spermatic cord on
urinating.
Modalities - Better from warmth. Worse pressure of clothes. Worse by cold, damp, change of temperature.
Lying down causes pressure in occiput, dizziness and wavering of sight. Rising causes sudden pain in occiput.
Mouth - Itching, burning palate, wants to scratch it. Tongue feels swollen.
Rectum - Hemorrhoids with itching. Interior of anus studded with itching eminence. Liquid feces.
Sensations - As of sudden rising of scalp. As if whole intestinal contents were fluid. As if hips drawn together.
As of galvanic shock through lower limbs.
Skin-Superficial ulcers and sores on lower limbs, especially in females at menopause. Urticaria.
COMMENTS - Lancinating, cutting, pulsating, shooting, wandering and flashing pains. One prover described
them as like aurora borealis, and a case of sciatica with pains of this description was cured with Polyg. The
left temple was markedly affected, left side generally more so than right.
Epilepsy and hysteria. Marked diarrhea (Rheum, and Rumx.) and dysuria. Excessive weakness, trembling and
 sensitiveness to cold.
Cold sensations, alternating or coinciding with heat in the same or other parts. Coldness of right side of face
when pain in left side was most severe. Burning in chest with cold feeling at pit of stomach. Feet burning, then

COMMENTS - Great lassitude. Congestion of head with vertigo, face hot and flushed, prickling sensation all

Restless at night from pain in wrists and knee, rheumatic pains. Profuse perspiration.

pain in shin bones, preventing sleep. (2) Bol-lu., Agar.

name: Populus Candicans
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pop-c. Populus candicans. Balm of Gilead. Populus balsamifera. N. O. Salicaceae. The name
Balm of Gilead tree is given to the Black Italian Poplar. Tincture of the resinous buds. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphonia. Asthma. Brain, congested. Bullae. Colds. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia.
Dysphagia. Ecthyma. Heart disorders. Liver, disorders. Phosphaturia. Sinusitis. Sunstroke. Throat, sore.
Vagina, burning.
HERBAL - The name Populus balsamifera applies especially to the variety Populus candicans, but also to all
P. balsamiferae. In England, the name “Balm of Gilead tree” is given to the Black Italian Poplar, which abounds
in Italy, but the origin of which is not known.
C. F. Nichols gave an account of Pop-c., the effects of which he observed. “The resinous gum exuding from
buds and stalks, deliciously aromatic in perfume is widely used to heal wounds, open sores and eruptions and
often suppresses these latter to the harm of the patient.”
As an application, Nichols said, it is like Arn., dangerous, though most people are not susceptible to its
poisonous effect. He never saw blisters of the size of those of Pop-c. produced by any other drug. Blisters
hung down like bags of water the size of walnuts. Burning was a common symptom in the eyes, nose, throat,
bowels, vagina.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Pop-c. seems to have a remarkable power over acute colds, especially when accompanied
by a deep, hoarse voice or even aphonia. Instantaneous voiceproducer (Coca).
General insensibility of surface, worse back and abdomen, rubbing and pounding borne without pain and is
grateful on account of warmth produced. Fingertips thickened, horny insensible to pinching and prickling.
MIND - Loquacity. Discusses her symptoms with everyone. Hopeless foreboding, worse after sleep. Fear and
anguish. Expectation of death. Feels as if the will were paralyzed. Vanishing of thought. Forgets to finish a
sentence. Voices sound distant and words just spoken seem as if uttered long ago, objects seem multiplied.
Abdomen - Flatulent colic, doubling the body forward. Pain in right hypochondrium with enlargement. Wears
her clothes loose.
Back - Numbness in back radiating from spine. Burning weariness in lower back.
Chest - Rawness, soreness of chest, throat.
Eyes - Sensation as if left eye were twisted during the headache. Burning irritation in eyes, nose, mouth, throat,
and air
passages.
Face - Face yellow. Burning, prickling on face.
Female - Menses scanty, usually delaying, afterwards absent, then abundant, early, with dysmenorrhea, better
hot cloths. Vagina burns as if scalded.
Food - Appetite lost, loathes meat. Nothing relished. Hungry but dares not eat for fear of choking.
Head - Weight on vertex. Hot head with cold limbs. Cold-sores on lips (Nat-m.). Burning irritation of eyes, nose,
mouth, throat and air passages.
Heart - Pain in heart, stitches. Palpitations when rising or lying on left side with vertigo. Heart’s sound irregular,
usually muffled, worse before menses.
Kidneys - Urine strong, high colored, hot, scanty, increased, variously colored, red, dark, light, phosphates
abundant. Urine dark, straw color, smoky.
Limbs - Fingertips thickened, horny, insensible to pinching and pricking. Nails blue as in ague (not thickened).
Lungs - Suffocation. Breathing dry, asthmatic with dyspnea. Sits bent forward with dry cough, worse lifting
arms. Dry cough when tired. Cough caused by “cobwebs” in his throat. Cough of children caused by naso-
pharyngeal catarrh, mucus drops from posterior sinuses.
Modalities - Better hot applications. Worse on moving, lifting arms, contact of clothes. Worse after sleep,
before menses. Worse after food and drink.
Mouth - Speech thick. Taste bitter, sweet in morning.
Rectum - Stools small, round, preceded by cramps in abdomen, lack of expulsive power. Constipation, bowels
feel hot and dry. Stools watery, green, alternating with constipation.
Sensations - Whole body feels swollen, bruised, lame, sore and painful, exhausted as in dry, sultry weather.
Eye feels twisted with the headache.
Skin - Skin harsh, dry and cold with burning-stinging. Burning, prickling on face, chest, and hands. Blisters
hanging down like bags of water.
Sleep - Sleepless after midnight with restlessness. Dreams frightful, vivid, fearful after fitful sleep.
Stomach - Belching of gas, feeling like hot steam. Nausea with a sinking in epigastrium. Vomits bile.
Temperature - Fever and unrest. Fever with congestion of brain, fullness, heaviness, dullness, soreness. Dry
heat. Sweat on head and neck. Sudden coldness of limbs with numbness of them and heat of head.
Throat - Rawness and soreness of throat. Throat is red, dry. Throat and nostrils burn. Burning and paralysis
in throat. Pharynx and larynx feel dry and the voice weak and toneless. Acute hoarseness.
Tongue - Tongue white, dry, feels thick and numb. Tongue and mouth feel burnt and dry, but are moist, worse
after food and drink.
Vertigo - Vertigo from lifting head. Vertigo and heat of head as if scorched by sun.
COMMENTS - W. C. Stilson related a case of poisoning in a man who one evening drank rum in which Balm
of Gilead buds had been placed for making a liniment. A few hours later his wife heard him breathing heavily
and on waking him found he could not speak.
Stilson found him only able to speak in hoarse whispers and he would forget in the middle of a sentence what
he was going to say. Face ashy pale, wild look. Tongue and mouth dry. Throat dry, burning, constricted, felt
as if spiders had spun webs on it. It was some days before he recovered.
Since this occasion, Stilson cured several cases of catarrhal hoarseness and aphonia with Pop-c. and one
case of nervous aphonia. Mrs. S. had nervous prostration and, during the attack, aphonia. The aphonia
remained after the patient got well otherwise.
Among the peculiar symptoms observed by Nichols is surface anesthesia with or without numbness. The
fingertips are thickened, horny, insensible to pinching and pricking. Skin is harsh, generally dry and cold with
 a stinging burning behind the surface as if an eruption would appear or as if sweat would break out.
Numbness in back radiating from spine. Constipation, bowels feel hot and dry. The menses were at first scanty,
later abundant and early, with dysmenorrhea pain, better by application of hot cloths.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Rhus-t. Compare: (1) Salx-a., Pop. (2) Salicylates. (3) worse contact of clothes,
Lach.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Populus Tremuloides
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pop. Populus tremuloides. American aspen. Aspen. Poplar. N. O. Salicaceae. The American
Aspen; the British Aspen is Populus trémula. Tincture of inner bark. Solution of Poplin. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Acidity. Ague. Ardor urine. Bladder, catarrh. Flatulence. Gleet, chronic. Indigestion. Malaria.
Nausea. Night-sweats. Prostate, enlarged. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pop. is a good remedy in bladder troubles after operations and in pregnancy. Dyspepsia
and catarrh of the bladder, especially in elderly people. Cystitis. Fullness of head. Sensation of heat of the
surfaces of the body. Nightsweats. Ague.
Bladder - Severe tenesmus, painful scalding. Urine contains mucus and pus. Pain behind pubis, at end of
urination.
Male - Prostate enlarged.
Stomach - Indigestion with flatulence and acidity. Nausea and vomiting.
COMMENTS - The symptoms were provided by Pane (an eclectic), whom Hale quoted. Pane used Populus
tremuloides in disorders of the bladder, urethra and prostate. Hale confirmed its action in bladder tenesmus
and inflammation of the neck of the bladder.
Hale gave the case of a woman who had metritis, vaginismus and cystitis and was apparently cured. A ride on
the cars brought back weight, pressure and aching in pelvis and bladder tenesmus with frequent desire to
urinate. Pop. 3x removed all these symptoms in three days.
Hale noted that in the cases he cured there was little pain during urination, but as soon as the last drops were
voided or a little before, there was a severe cramp-like pain just behind pubes, lasting ten to fifteen minutes.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Pop-c., Salx-n., Gaul. (2) Salin, and Salicylates. (3) Nux-v., Chin., Com-f., Cann-
i., Canth. Follows well: Cann-s.,Canth. (succeeded afterthey had only partially helped).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Prednisone
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - predn. Prednisone. A synthetic corticosteroid drug. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Adrenal glands. Allergies. Arthritis. Asthma. Blood, disorders. Bone, fractures. Bruises.
Cancers. Cataracts. Colitis. Connective tissue. Crohn's disease. Cushing's syndrome. Enteritis. Eye, diseases.
Facial, swelling. Fluid retention. Glaucoma. Growth, stunted. Headache. High blood pressure. Hives. Lung,
diseases. Lupus erythematosus. Meningitis. Menses, irregular. Multiple sclerosis. Muscle, weakness.
Nephrotic syndrome. Osteoporosis. Poison ivy. Rheumatism. Skin, diseases. Stomach, ulcer. Thyroiditis.
Trichinosis. Tuberculosis. Ulcerative colitis. Urticaria. Vertigo. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Prednisone is a synthetic corticosteroid drug. Abnormal adrenal gland development.
Cushing's syndrome. Thyroid gland inflammation. Certain cancers. Blood disorders. High blood pressure.
Congestive heart failure.
Increased appetite. Weight gain, “moonfaced” appearance. Stunted growth in children. Sweating. Distended
abdomen. Inflamed esophagus or pancreas. Fluid retention due to nephrotic syndrome. Peptic ulcer. Irregular
menses.
Muscle weakness. Brittle bones, bone fractures. Osteoporosis. Painful hips of shoulders. Convulsions. Vertigo.
Nervousness. Insomnia. Hyperactivity. Depression, mania or other psychiatric symptoms. Un
usual fatigue or weakness.
Diseases of the connective tissue, including systemic lupus erythematosus. Flare-ups of multiple sclerosis.
Rheumatoid arthritis and related disorders. Severe flare-ups of ulcerative colitis or enteritis. Lung diseases,

Skin diseases. Severe allergic conditions. Hives. Acne, rash. Thin, fragile skin. Purplish stripe marks on the
skin. Bruising. Poor healing of wounds. Infections. Eye diseases of various kinds, including eye infection,
cataracts and glaucoma. Bulging eyes. Blurred vision. Increased pressure in the eyes or skull. Headache.
 Meningitis.
MIND - Euphoria, severe depression. Insomnia. Mood changes, personality changes, psychotic behavior. May
worsen any existing emotional instability.
RELATIONS - Compare: Cortico., Ars.

name: Primula Obconica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - prim-o. Primula obconica. Primrose. Tibetan Primrose. N. O. Primulaceae. Primulae. Tincture
of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Blisters. Chapped, hands. Eczema. Eyes, inflammation. Itching. Liver, pain. Skin, disorders.
Spleen, pains. Weakness.
HERBAL - Prim-o. is an ornamented variety of primrose. Gardeners, amateur and professional, have
discovered after much suffering that in some people it has a powerful action on the skin, taking place chiefly
by contact but partly by effluvia.
HOMEOPATHIC - The poison of the Primrose is in its glandular hairs, which break easily and discharge an
irritating fluid which is absorbed into the skin. But skin symptoms of poisoning appear in sensitive patients even
without coming in direct contact with the plant, mere nearness begin sufficient, like poison ivy.
Prim-o. has deep infiltration and tension of tissues. Paralyzed sensation. Weakness. Pain in liver and spleen.
Pharyngeal soreness alternates with diminished facial irritation. Blisters. Intermittent symptoms, worse right
side.
Abdomen - Pain in region of liver, and a less severe pain in spleen, worse by bending from side to side.
Eyes - Burning irritation of eyeballs and eyelids, nostrils, and mouth. Lids greatly swollen, covered with large
bullae. Lids half closed, stiff and immovable.
Face - Moist eczema. Papular eruption on chin. Burns at night. Urticaria-like eruption. Eyelids swollen.
Limbs - Eczema on arms, wrists, forearms, hands, papular and excoriated. Purple blotches on back of hands,
palmar surface stiff. Blisters on fingers. Palms dry and hot. Cracking over joints and fingers. Rheumatic pain
around shoulder.
Skin - Eruption between fingers. Great itching, worse at night, red and swollen like erysipelas. Tumefied.
Small papules on a raised base. Skin symptoms accompanied by febrile symptoms.
Temperature - At night feverish, hands and face would burn, then intolerable itching.
COMMENTS - The Rev. F. H. Brett, who was one of the first to notice its poisonous properties, undertook to
prove it. He had handled the plants freely up to that time without experiencing any ill effect. He cut up some
young plants and added some vigorous fresh leaves of an old one and made a tincture.
This he allowed to stand for a week and then took three or four drops, three times a day for four days. Two
 days after ceasing to take it symptoms began to develop in the right little finger and two days afterwards in the
right thumb. These became very intense and ran a chronic course.
He could not go near a plant of Prim-o. without worsening the symptoms. They were also worse at night, and
by rubbing or scratching. At the same time, Brett noted that the pains in the liver and spleen to which he had
been subject now troubled him no more. The right hand was much more affected than the left.
Clarke cured a chronic psoric dry eruption on the leg of a woman with Prim-o. 3c. Cooper relieved a case of
severe eczema on the leg with bleeding.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-t., Fago, (antidotal). (2) Hume., similar skin symptoms. (3) Anag., Prim-v.,
Verat.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Primula Veris
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - prim-v. Primula veris. Cowslip. Primula vulgaris. Primula officinalis. N. O. Primulaceae.
Primulae. Tincture of entire fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Dropsy. Eczema. Fevers. Gouty, pains. Migraine. Neuralgia. Rheumatic pains. Strokes,
threatened. Vertigo. Voice disorders.
HERBAL - According to The Treasury of Botany, the flowers of Prim-v. are said to be narcotic. “Cowslip wine”
is a favorite remedy in the country for many small disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - Schier, of Mentz, proved a tincture of the fresh plant including the root. The duration of
action is only a few days in healthy persons.
Prim-v. has threatened strokes, arising from depression. Cerebral congestion with neuralgia. Migraine.
“Pressure at heart.” Wandering dropsy. Rheumatic and gouty pains. Chronic eczema.
Ears - Buzzing in ears, better in open air.
Head - Sensation of a band around head, cannot keep hat on (Carb-ac.). Skin of forehead tense.
Kidneys - Urine smells strongly of violets.
Limbs - Weight and lassitude in limbs, especially the shoulders. Right axillary muscles painful. Burning in
hollow of right hand. Drawing pain in thumb and big toe.
Lungs - Cough with burning and prickling in respiratory tracts. Weak voice.
Modalities - Worse by bent position, stooping, movement. Worse in a room, in a closed carriage, traveling by
rail. Worse in open air.
Vertigo - Violent vertigo, as if everything turned around. Fear of falling when standing up.
COMMENTS - Schier commended it as an external application when there is no skin lesion, “as this remedy
has a certain relation with the skin. Prudence is necessary here, especially for persons with sensitive and
easily vulnerable skin.”
Cooper cured with Prim-v. a case of eczema of the hands after Prim-o. had failed. He also cured with it eczema
palmaris of years' duration in a man, aged 70.
Cooper also cured a case of wandering dropsy with Prim-v. In a cancer case, one dose caused the
disappearance of dropsy from the leg and led to oppression at the heart. Cooper thought this a characteristic
aggravation.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cycl., Ran-b. (2) Evening Primrose - exhausting, watery diarrhea, cholera
infantum, hydrocephalus.
(3)   Prim-f. - the wild primrose - dermatitis, especially on index fingers and thumbs.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Prinos Verticillatus
