name: Pulmonaria Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pul-o. Pulmonaria officinalis. Lungwort. Pulmonaria maculosa. Jerusalem sage. N. O.
Boraginaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Bronchitis. Coughs. Hemoptysis. Hemorrhoids. Lung, disorders. Urinary, incontinence.
Tuberculosis.
HERBAL - Pulmonaria officinalis is an evergreen perennial species of lungwort, native to locations throughout
Europe. A rhizome, P. officinalis produces small bunches of pink flowers which turn to blue-purple in spring.
The plant has been cultivated for centuries as a medicinal herb, the ovate spotted leaves were thought to be
symbolic of diseased lungs. The appearance of the plant makes it easy to see why the lungwort was used for
diseases of the lung (putrid bronchitis, hemoptysis), and also for hematuria, and urinary incontinence (see also
under Myos.).
The medicines are prepared from the fresh, flowering herb. It is an astringent, demulcent, diaphoretic, diuretic,
emollient, expectorant, ophthalmic, and resolvent.
The leaves and flowering shoots are often used for their healing effect in pulmonary complaints. The leaves
can also be used externally to stop bleeding. They are harvested in the spring and dried for later use. A distilled
water made from the plant is an effective eyewash for tired eyes.
The tannins in lungwort have a slight astringent effect when applied to the skin, thereby reducing secretions,
relieving irritation, and improving tissue firmness.
It has been used as a wash, poultice, or soak for hemorrhoids and minor skin injuries such as scrapes and
sunburn.
Lungwort has a high mucilage content and this makes it useful in the treatment of chest conditions, being of
particular benefit in cases of chronic bronchitis. The herb is very mucilaginous and contains silica, tannins and
saponins. It combines well with other herbs such as coltsfoot (Tus-fa.) in the treatment of chronic coughs
including whooping cough and can also be taken to treat asthma.
Lungwort is good for coughs, hoarseness, and mild lung problems. It acts as a good expectorant, which breaks
up chest congestion. Soothes throat irritation. It can also be used for diarrhea, which makes it useful for a
stomach virus accompanied by a cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pul-o. is used in the treatment of bronchitis, coughs and diarrhea. Bronchial catarrhs, colds.
In the past, lungwort was given for the coughing up of blood arising from tubercular infection.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Pulsatilla Nigricans
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - puls. Pulsatilla nigricans. Wind flower. Pasque flower. Pulsatilla pratensis. Anemone pratensis.
N. O. Ranunculaceae. Pastures in Central and Northern Europe, parts of South of England. Tincture of entire
fresh plant when in flower (it flowers in spring and again in autumn). Historical dose: Tincture and all
 potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Allergies. Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Bladder, catarrh. Blepharospasm. Breast-
feeding, disorders. Breasts, pain. Bronchitis. Cataract. Catarrh. Chest, pains. Chickenpox. Chilblains. Clavus.
Colds. Conjunctivitis. Coughs. Diarrhea. Distention. Dysmenorrhea. Earache. Epilepsy. Ear, disorders.
Eye, disorders. Fears. Feet, painful. Fetus, mal-position. Freckles. Gonorrhea. Gout. Hands, painful. Heart,
palpitations. Heartbum. Hemorrhoids. Hydrocele, congenital. Hysteria. Intermittent, fever. Faints. Labor, pains.
Leucorrhea. Measles. Menstruation, abnormal. Moles. Mumps. Neuralgias. Nose
bleed. Nymphomania. Ophthalmia. Otitis, media. Ovaries, inflammation. Phlegmasia alba dolens. Pregnancy,
troubles. Priapism. Prostatitis. Prostatorrhea. Puerperal convulsions. Puerperal fever. Puerperal, mania.
Retained, placenta. Rheumatism, gonorrheal. Sinusitis. Smell, loss. Spine, curvature. Styes. Synovitis.
Tapeworm. Taste, lost. Tongue, coated. Toothaches. Urinary, incontinence. Uterus, prolapse. Vaginitis.
Varicose veins. Whitlow.
HERBAL - Pasque flower is in bloom at Easter, its flowers have been used for coloring Easter eggs. It is a
medicine of ancient times, and its affinity for the eyes seems to have been noted from the beginning. Perhaps
its tearful propensities gave rise to the legend that it sprang from the tears of Venus. Dioscorides mentions it
as a remedy for headache and ophthalmia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Stoerck was the forerunner of Hahnemann in the modem use of Puls.; he employed it
especially in chronic disorders of the eyes (catarrh, amaurosis, spots on cornea). Pulsatilla affects the emo-
tions, veins, mucus membranes, respiration and one side. It is pre-eminently a female remedy, especially for
mild, gentle, yielding disposition.
Useful in acute as well as chronic diseases. Most suitable when not only the physical symptoms correspond
but also when the mental and emotional disorders peculiar to the remedy encounter similar states in the
disease to be cured, or at least in the temperament of the patient.
The disposition and mental state are the chief guiding symptoms. Sad, crying readily, weeps when talking.
Moody, contradictory. Changing, shifting symptoms, known as a weather cock remedy. Alternations.
Symptoms rise to a certain pitch, then suddenly cease.
Changeable nature. Erratic temperatures in fevers. Alternate pallor and redness of face. Wandering pains
shift rapidly from one part to another, also with swelling and redness of the joints. Hemorrhages apparently
stop and in a few hours return. Stools constantly changing color, no two stools alike.
When one set of symptoms comes on another vanishes. Symptoms appear on one side or go to side lain on.
The patient seeks the open air, always feels better there, even though he is chilly. Thirstless, chilliness
and shortness of breath with digestive or menstrual disorders. Chilliness with pains but burning with stitching
pains with numbness.
Mucus membranes are all affected. Mucus discharges are profuse, bland, thick, yellowish-
green.Metastasis. Hemorrhages, passive, vicarious, blood dark, easily coagulating. Varicose veins. Anemia.
Emaciation of suffering parts. Symptoms in distant parts of the body cause dyspnea.
Epilepsy with absent or irregular menses. Never well since puberty. Chorea from amenorrhea or
dysmenorrhea.
Peevish. Great sensitiveness. Scraping, jerking, tearing, ulcerative pains, wandering pains. Numbness,
partial, hands, feet etc. of the part lain on of suffering parts. Heaviness. Pulsation through whole body. Wants
the head high. Feels uncomfortable with only one pillow. Lies with hands above head. The longer he lies in the
morning, the longer he wishes to lie. Child wants to be carried slowly.
Sensation of distention in size, as if one part or every part were growing too large during pain. Bandaged
sensation. Wearing of flannels or woolen clothes cause itching and eruptions. Great inclination to stretch feet.
Often indicated after abuse of iron tonics and after badly managed measles.
MIND - Changeable moods. Timid, irresolute. Mild, emotional and tearful. Highly emotional, easily moved
to tears and laughter. Craves affection and sympathy. Desires company. Capricious. Easily discouraged.
Whining. Wandering thoughts.
Forsaken feeling. Sadness from disagreeable news. Sadness from injuries of head. History ofabandonment
or grief. Silentgrief with submissiveness. Remorse in evening.
Weeps easily. Can hardly give her symptoms without weeping. Better being held and hugged. Weeps at
everything, whether it is joyful or sorrowful.
Weeping when disturbed at work. Weeps easily before menses.
Over-sensitiveness to pain. Given to extremes of pleasure and pain. Consolation improves all symptoms.
Children like to be carried slowly and held. Children like affection and caresses. Children are extremely
affectionate, which they manifest by kissing and caressing.
Very irritable, touchy, feels slighted or fears slight. Sensitive to reprimand. Easily offended. Answers yes or no
 by nodding head. Selfishness. Miserly. Jealousy. Envy. Delusion she is alone in the world, that she is always
alone.
Suspicious. Disgusted at everything. Fastidious. Fixed ideas about food, sex, religion. Imagines that certain
articles of food are not good for the human race. Fixed ideas about marriage. Thinks that sex is a sinful act.
Religious melancholy. Religious mania. Mania from suppressed menses. Despair of salvation, seeks aid in
constant prayer. Weary of life, thinks of drowning.
Full of cares about domestic affairs. Anxiety better open air, better motion. Anxiety and uneasiness in bed,
must uncover. Fear, wants to hide or run. Fear of abandonment, of being unlovable. Fear of marriage.
Morbid dread of opposite sex. Fear of being alone, of dark, of ghosts in the evening. Fear of high places. Fear
of insanity.
Abdomen - Great soreness of epigastrium. Cutting, pulsation in epigastrium. Abdominal walls sensitive and
swollen, tender to touch. Feeling of numbness. Chilliness from abdomen. Tense distension in upper abdomen.
Pressure as from a stone. Painful, distended abdomen loud rumbling. Abdominal colic from ices, fruits,
pastries, fat or greasy things. Colic, with chilliness in evening. Colic and rumbling of wind in upper abdomen.
Colic from getting feet wet. Incarcerated flatus. Flatulence. Cholera morbus from drinking ice-water. Pains
extend into groins. Hard painful lumps in both groins.
Back - Curvature of the upper part of the spine. Pain in back and small of back as from prolonged stooping.
Back painfully stiff, like a board. Backache worse lying on back, better lying on sides or changes of position,
especially during pregnancy. Back feels bandaged. As if cold water was poured down the back. Chilliness and
pain in sacral region during menses. Chilliness in lumbar region after stool. Lumbago, must move, yet motion
gives no better. Shooting pain in the nape and back, between shoulders, in sacrum, after sitting. Swelling of
cervical glands. Stiffness of neck after stool.
Bladder - Region of bladder painful to touch. Sensation as if a stone rolling in bladder. Sharp pain, pressure
on neck of bladder. Burning in orifice of urethra during and after urination. Pain and tenesmus in urinating.
Constrictive pain in region of bladder with urinary tenesmus and involuntary emissions of a little urine.
Spasmodic pain in bladder, after urinating. Urination more frequent during attack of headache. Hematuria with
burning at orifice of urethra. Retention of urine after childbirth. Involuntary urination at night, on coughing
orpassing flatus. Involuntary urination on laughing, sneezing. Dribbling of urine from anger.
Nocturnalbedwetting after measles, worse in autumn, especially little girls.
Breasts - Lumps occurring in breasts of young girls, painful and affecting arm of corresponding side. Thin,
milky fluid escapes from breasts before puberty. Aching, sore breasts. Secretion of milk during menses. Milk
suppressed or very scanty. Weeps when the child is put to breast. Child refuses breast. Galactorrhea, in
women who are not nursing their children. After weaning, breasts swell, feel stretched, tense, intensely sore,
milk continues to be secreted.
Causations - Ill effects of suppressions, otorrhea, menses, lochia, milk etc. Abandonment. Grief. Eating ice
cream, pork, fats, pastry, desserts, mixed rich diet, tea. Chill. Wetting feet.
Chest - Smothering sensation on lying down. Pressure and soreness upon the chest. Chest oppressed, as
by a load. Soreness beneath clavicles. Tension in chest, worse drawing a long breath. Pain as from ulcer
Pulsatilla nigricans in middle of chest. Paroxysms of burning in chest. Hard, painful, throbbing glandular
swelling in right axilla. Congestion to chest and heart at night with anxious dreams. Chest symptoms, worse
lying on painful side.
Constitutions - For females of mild, gentle, plethoric, yielding disposition, who cry readily and weep when
talking. Pale, chilly blondes.
Cough - Dry cough in evening and at night, must sit up in bed to get relief. Loose cough in morning, with
copious mucus sputum. Dry, hacking cough from tickling in epigastrium. Short, dry cough, worse becoming
warm and after sleeping. Cough from dryness in larynx and trachea, worse eating and evening. Dry cough,
often with palpitations, nausea, retching, headache, backache. Loose cough by day, dry after every sleep.
Cough with retching and desire to vomit. Loose cough, with vomiting of mucus. Cough with diarrhea. Cough
after measles.
Ears - External ear swollen and red. Lobes of ear swollen. Catarrhal otitis media. Ear infections, worse at
night. Otorrhea, discharge of pus, blood, thick yellow humor, offensive after exanthemata. Threatened
ulceration and perforation of tympanum. Itching deep in ears. Severe earache, not better warm applications.
Earaches, worse night. Sensation as if something were being forced outward. Hearing difficult, deafness, as if
ears were stopped up. Can hear better in car and in a warm room. Deafness after suppressed measles.
Impaired hearing, worse cold, damp weather, better in warm room. Sounds of wind or rushing water.
Eyes - Pupils dilated or contracted. Ophthalmia neonatorum. Ophthalmia after suppressed gonorrhea.
Ophthalmia with amenorrhea. Spots on cornea. Superficial ulcers on cornea. Incipient cataract. Catarrhal
 conjunctivitis. Sub-acute conjunctivitis with dyspepsia, worse in warm room. Conjunctivitis from colds. Thick,
profuse, yellow, bland discharges. Burning, itching in eyes, must rub. Child frequently rubs eyes. Profuse,
acrid
lachrymation and secretion of mucus. Pressure, as from sand in eyes, when reading. Weeping eyes. Fistula
lachry- malis, discharging pus on pressure. Lids inflamed, agglutinated. Veins of fundus oculi greatly
enlarged. Styes, recurrent, upper lids. Blepharitis with acne of face. Oversensitive to light. Allergies.
Face - Face puffed, blue, red. Flushes. One cheek red, the other pale, during fever. Paleness of face during
vertigo. Painful sensitiveness of skin of face. Facial erysipelas with stinging, pricking pains, skin peels off. Acne
of young, growing girls. Prosopalgia towards evening until midnight, chilly with pain. Facial neuralgia. Right-
sided neuralgia, with profuse lachrymation. Mumps, especially metastatic to the breast or testes. Tension
of face and fingers, as if parts would become swollen. Boring pain in left malar bone. Frequently licks dry lips.
Swelling of lower lip. Licks lips, crack in center of lower lip. Sweat on one side of face.
Female -Amenorrhea (Ign., Cimic., Polyg., Senec.), from wet feet, nervous debility, anemia or chlorosis.
Menses delayed at puberty. Suppressed menses. Dark, thick menses. Menses too late, scanty after
bathing. Mensesclotted,changeable. Flow more during day while walking about. Menses intermittent, irregular,
or vicarious. Tardy menses. Bearing down pain, worse lying. Dysmenorrhea beginning in puberty.
Dysmenorrhea, with chilliness, paleness of face, stretching and yawning. Metrorrhagia after abuse of quinine
and iron. Leucorrhea worse lying down. Acrid, milky leucorrhea, thick like cream, with swollen vulva.
Leucorrhea with pain in the back and exhaustion. Leucorrhea after masturbation. Vaginismus. Serous cysts,
indurations or polyps in vagina. Promotes expulsion of moles. Nymphomania. Threatened miscarriage after
fright. Malposition of fetus, breach position. Labor pains causes palpitations. Labor pains too weak or
ceasing, with somnolence. Weak labor pains. Bearing down pain, worse lying. After-pains too long and too
violent. Post-partum hemorrhages from
retained placenta.
Food - Hunger, but doesn 'tknow for what. Changeable appetite. Sudden loathing, worse eating. Food
tastes too salty. Thirstlessness with nearly all complaints. Aversion to butter, pork, meat, fats, milk, bread,
buckwheat. Aversion to warm food and drink. Aversion to smoking. Craving for what disagrees, pungent food,
cheese, sweets, ice cream, peanut butter, soft-boiled eggs, herring. Craves or dislikes butter. Desire for tonics,
acids, sour, lemonade, refreshing things, beer or alcoholic drinks. Worse from rich foods, fats, pork. Worse
pastries, desserts, ice cream. Bad effects from onions.
Head - Confusion of head as after intoxication. Headaches from overwork, suppressed sexual desire,
indigestion. Headache from overloaded stomach, from pastry, fats, ice cream. Headache from abuse of
coffee, spirits or chamomile tea. One-sided headaches, pulsating, bursting, with scalding. One-sided
headaches, lachrymation of the affected side. Headaches of schoolgirls at puberty. Headaches, better
walking in open air. Occipital pain, worse coughing. Numbness of head during headache. Occipital headache
worse coughing. Shooting pains in temples. Wandering stitches about head, pains extend to face and teeth.
Frontal and supra-orbital pains. Neuralgic scalding pains, beginning in right temporal side. Pressure on
vertex. Head seems heavy, cannot hold upright, cannot raise it. Sensations of emptiness in head. Humming
in head. Tumors on scalp, suppurating. Profuse sweat on hairy scalp.
Heart - Burning in region of heart. Catching pain with short breath, better by pressure of a hand and walking.
Murmur in jugular veins. Anxious palpitations with amenorrhea, from emotions, after dinner. Nervous
palpitations in young girls during puberty, or from amenorrhea. Palpitations, worse lying on left side. Pulse with
distended blood vessels. Beat of pulse is felt in pit of stomach. Pulse frequent in evening. Pulse slower in
morning. Heart symptoms reflex from indigestion.
Kidneys - Cystitis with weeping. Urging to urinate when lying on back. Sensation as of a stone rolling in the
bladder. Stricture, urine passed only in drops and stream interrupted (Clem.). Urine dribbles when angry.
Spasmodic pain in bladder after urinating. Burning in orifice of urethra during and after urination. Hematuria
after urination. Heavy pressure or cramp in bladder after urination. Involuntary urination at night during sleep,
while coughing, sneezing or passing flatus. Involuntary on lying down, laughing, hearing sudden noise after
surprise, shock.
Limbs - Swollen, red joints. Pains down lower limbs, alternating sides. Pains, worsefrom letting the affected
limb hang down (Vip.). Tensive pain, letting up with a crack. Drawing, tensive pain in thighs and legs with
restlessness, sleeplessness and chilliness. Pain in limbs, shifting rapidly. Rheumatism caused by getting
wet. Rheumatism from protracted wet weather. Legs feel heavy and weary. Numbness in legs when after long
standing. Painful hip joint. Knees swollen with tearing drawing pains. Sticking in tibia worse lying better cool
air and walking. Milk leg. Periostitis. Inclination to stretch the feet. Feet red inflamed, swollen, edematous.
Boring pain in heels toward evening. Cold sweat on legs. Foul foot sweat. Arms feel broken and dislocated.
 Elbows numb. Veins in forearms and hands swollen. Veins full, varicose, painful.
Lungs - Craves open fresh air, must open the window. Shortness of breath, anxiety and palpitations
worse lying on left side (Phos.). Smothering sensation on lying down, worse in warm, stuffy rooms. Asthma
in evening after a meal. Asthma from suppressions. Dry, hacking cough, from tickling in epigastrium. Dry cough
in evening and at night. Cough must sit up in bed to get relief. Loose cough in the morning with copious
mucus expectoration. Urine emitted with cough (Caust.). Cough after measles. Expectoration, thick, purulent,
slimy, sweet, salty, bitter as it loosens up. Bland, yellow, greenish expectoration. Large quantities
of yellow, thick, lumpy mucus, worse mornings. Groaning or rattling breathing. Broncho-pneumonia in chlorotic
or anemic women. Acute suppuration of lungs. Pneumonia from hepatic troubles or during measles.
Male - Orchitis, pain from abdomen to testicles. Orchitis, gonorrheal or from sitting on cold stones. Testicles
hang low down. Soreness of testes. Burning and aching of testes, with or without swelling. Burning down left
spermatic cord. Epididymitis. Acute prostatitis with pressure and great heat in perineum. Enlarged prostate.
Hydrocele, varicocele, sarcocele. Thick, yellow discharge from urethra, late stage of gonorrhea. Bloody
emissions. Pain and tenesmus while urinating, worse lying on back. Venous congestion of penis. Sexual
desire in morning on waking, long-lasting morning erections. Nocturnal emissions, without dreams. Sexual
excesses resulting in headache, backache, limbs heavy.
Modalities - Better from cool, fresh, open air. Better uncovering, cold applications, cold food and drinks,
though not thirsty. Better from erect posture, lying with head high. Better continued, gentle motion, pressure,
rubbing, massage. Worse from warmth of air, stuffy rooms, clothes, bed, sun. Worse getting feet wet, before
and during thunderstorms. Worse at twilight, sunset, evening and night. Worse rest, beginning motion.
Worse lying on one side, hanging down limbs. Worse puberty, before menses, pregnancy. Worse from
eating, long after. Worse from rich foods, pastry, fats, ice cream, pork, eggs, tea. Worse hot food, is vomited
immediately, aggravates toothache. Worse from iron, quinine. Never been well since puberty (anemia,
bronchitis, phthisis).
Mouth - Crack in middle of lower lip. Frequently licks dry lips. Offensive breath. Offensive odor from mouth
(Aur., Merc.). Copious salivation during pain in stomach. Much sweet saliva. Tenacious saliva, like frothy
cotton. Watery saliva like water brash. Dry mouth without thirst, wants it rinsed frequently. Yellow or white
tongue, covered with a tenacious mucous. Dimin-
ished taste and smell to all foods. Loss of taste with nasal catarrh. Alterations of taste, bitter, bilious, greasy,
salty. Foul taste. Greasy taste. Food, especially bread, tastes bitter. Food leaves an aftertaste. Taste as of
bad meat.
Nose - Foul discharge or odor before the nose. Bad smells, as of old catarrh. Imaginary smells. Stoppage of
nose with loss of smell, taste and appetite. Coryza, stoppage of right nostril, pressing pain at root of nose,
better going out in the open air. Chronic bland yellow discharge. Yellow mucus, abundant in morning.
Sinusitis with thick yellow, green nasal discharge. Yellowish-green discharge, worse indoors, better
open air. Nose stopped up in house, fluent in open air. Nose swollen and itching in evening. Frequent
sneezing. Sneezing in sleep. Large green fetid scales in nose. Sore nasal bones. Nosebleed, before, during
menses. Nosebleed from suppressed menses.
Perspiration - One-sided pains during sweat. Sweats only on face and scalp. Sweats at night, with stupid
slumber. Profuse sweat in morning. Sweats during cough. Sour, musty sweat. Sweetish acid odor sweat.
Sweat like musk.
Rectum-Changeablestools. Notwostools alike after fruit (Ars., Chin.). Rumbling, watery, worse at night.
Obstinate constipation. Constipation with headache, irregular menses. Constipation alternating with
diarrhea. Frequent urging, as if diarrhea would occur. Dysentery, mucus and blood with chilliness (Merc.,
Rheum.). Diarrhea in jaundice with sensation of heat. Diarrhea after fright. Diarrhea during or after menses.
Discharge of blood from rectum even when not at stool. Pressure in rectum after stool. Burning and cutting
pains in rectum during stool. Smarting of anus after stool. Blind hemorrhoids with itching and sticking pains,
worse menses, lying down.
Sensations - As if beside himself. As if death were near. As if looking through a sieve. As if one had turned in
a circle a fong time, as if he would fall, as if he were dancing. As if in a hot atmosphere.
Chill as if drenched with cold water. As if brain would burst and eyes fall out of head, on coughing. Limbs as if
bruised, as if asleep. Tongue as if burnt. Pain as from subcutaneous ulceration. As of a hot coal above ulcer.
Skin - Skin itches on being heated. Itching as from numerous fleas. Herpes zoster. Erysipelas. Moles or
freckles in young girls. Urticaria after rich food, with diarrhea. Urticaria from delayed menses, worse
undressing. Urticaria in summer. Acne at puberty. Ulcers with hard, red, glistening areola. Wounds suppurate.
Pus thick, yellow, bland, too profuse. Swollen glands. Measles with catarrhal symptoms. Varicose veins.
Sleep - Sleeps late in morning. Wakes unrefreshed, confused. Great sleepiness during day. Irresistible
 sleepiness in afternoon. Frequent yawning. Yawning during cough. Sleeplessness on account of an anxious
sensation of heat. Sleeplessness from ideas crowding on mind. "Wide awake in the evening, restless first
sleep. Talks, whines or screams during sleep. Chattering in sleep. Lies upon back, with hands over head,
or with arms crossed on abdomen and feet drawn up. Dreams, frightful, disgusting, voluptuous, confused.
Anxious dreams when lying on left side. Dreams of cats, of black beasts, of men, of falling. Sad dreams with
weeping.
Stomach - Pain as from subcutaneous ulceration. Visible pulsations in the pit of stomach (Asaf.). All-gone
sensation, especially in tea drinkers. Weight as from a stone, especially in morning on awakening. Gnawing,
hungry feeling (Abies-c.). Bitter taste, diminished taste of all food. Stomach disordered, feels heavy. Pain
in stomach an hour after eating (Nux-v.). /ndigestionfrom rich, greasy, fatty foods. Worse after ices, fruits,
pastry. Dyspepsia with great tightness after a meal, must loosen clothing. Flatulence. Heartburn. Water brash
with foul taste in the morning. Belchings, taste of food remains a long time. Hiccough when smoking
tobacco. Persistent nausea. Nausea, with colic, better after vomiting. Vomiting after fruits, fats, pastry,
ices. Vomiting with pale face and chilliness. Vomiting of food eaten long before. Morning sickness.
Stools - Changeable stools. No two stools alike after fruit (Ars., Chin.). Green, bilious, stools. Stools
resembling stirred eggs, perfectly white, yellowish white. Discharge of acrid, mucus stools, with sensation of
weakness in loins, during urination. Mucus, blood, mixed with stool.
Teeth - Sensation as if teeth would be forced out. Sharp, shooting pains in teeth. Looseness of painful teeth.
Toothache, better holding cold water in mouth (Coff.). Toothache from picking teeth. Toothache from abuse of
quinine. Toothache better outdoors, returns on coming into room. Sore gums, with gnawing pain.
Temperature - Body hot, limbs cold. Childhood fevers, chickenpox, earaches, measles and mumps.
Prophylactic for measles. Erratic temperature in fevers. Feverish, hot, body temperature normal. Moaning
during fever. Attacks of flushes of heat. Feverjust at sunset. External heat is intolerable. Intolerable burning
heat at night with distended veins. Heat in parts of body, coldness in other. Partial sweat. During apyrexia,
headache, diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea. Chilly, yet averse to heat in warm, stuffy rooms with pain, on
lying down at night. Chilliness without thirst. Chilly with pains in spots, worse evening. Chill about 4 p.m.
One-sided coldness with numbness. One hand cold.
Throat - Great dryness of throat, in morning. Dry, sore throat with sense of dysphagia. Food lodges in throat.
Constricted feeling about throat. Rawness and scraping. Stinging, sharp pain worse swallowing saliva or after
food. As if a lump in it, when swallowing. Tough mucus in throat, worse night and morning. Hoarseness, comes
and goes. Hoarseness and roughness of throat, can't speak a loud word. Nervous aphonia. Sensation of a
worm wriggling up. Dilated or varicose veins in throat. As of a sulphur vapor when coughing.
Tongue - Dryness of tongue in morning. Edges of tongue feel sore as if scalded, middle of tongue feels as if
burnt. Tongue feels too broad, too large. Yellow or white tongue, covered with tenacious mucus. Tongue bright
red and covered with a network of dilated and congested veins. Blisters on sides and tip of tongue. Biting pain
on tip of tongue. As if tongue would be torn out.
Vertigo - Vertigo caused by indigestion. Vertigo with nausea and gastric disturbances. Vertigo on stooping,
with nausea. Vertigo as if intoxicated, with whirling. Vertigo with loss of sight. Vertigo, better in open air,
worse sitting up, looking up. Vertigo before, during menses, after suppressed menses.
Vision - Diplopia. Amblyopia, with diminished hearing. Obscured vision in morning on rising, and on going into
a warm room. Dim vision, as from accumulation of mucus. Dim vision, after getting warm from exercise, before
menses. As if veil before eyes, worse in bright light. Loss of vision at night, as if eyes were tightly bound by a
cloth, with menstrual disturbances. Day blindness with amenorrhea. Fiery circles. Bright streaks and rainbow
colors.
COMMENTS - Hahnemann gave in the picture of Puls, “a timid, weeping disposition with a tendency to inward
grief and silent peevishness or at all events a mild and yielding disposition. Especially when the patient in his
normal health was good-tempered and mild or even frivolus and good-humored.
“It is therefore especially adapted for slow, phlegmatic temperaments, on the other hand, it is but little suitable
for persons who form their resolutions with rapidity and are quick in their movements, even though they may
appear to be good-tempered.
“Puls, acts best where there is a disposition to chilliness and thirstlessness. It is suitable for females when their
menses come on some days after the proper time. Especially when the patient must lie long in bed at night
before he can get to sleep and when the patient is worse in the evening. It is useful for the ill effects caused
by eating pork.” Rapid, changeable moods and desires. Capricious. Changeable and soft. Generally healthy,
affectionate, loving, humble, particularly as children. Very sociable, needs attention, desires company.
Exaggerated mothering instincts (opposite of Sep.). Better from consolation. Babies better from picking up,
gentle rocking.
 Strong fear of loneliness, often an etiology. Fear of abandonment, grief over abandonment, “forsaken feeling.”
Helpless feeling. Depression, insomnia, stemming from loneliness. Fear of being alone, the dark, more often
in children. Fear of being unlovable.
Weeps easily, poor confidence, jealous. Self pity. Dependent, strong desire to please. Inability to make
decisions. Fixed ideas, from parents, about diet, relationships, religion. Seeks stability. Can smother people in
relationships, drive them away because of their neediness. Likes sex because of closeness, company.
Generally soft and fleshy. Great desire for fatty, creamy, buttery foods. Worse from fatty foods, rich foods,
pastries, pork, sweets. Can have digestive problems, even nightmares, from overly rich foods. Dependency
on food, eats when depressed. Emotional addiction to food, bulimia. Obliged to exercise to lose weight and to
rationalize food choices.
Food cravings, but doesn't know what for. May eat too late in the evening, leading to nightmares, headaches
and stomachaches. All-gone sensation in stomach, especially in tea-drinkers. Thirstless. Great dryness of
mouth without thirst.
Chilly or warm blooded, but susceptible to cold, wet weather, worse sinus and menstrual symptoms. Craves
fresh, open air. Will cover themselves with many blankets, then open a window to feel a cool breeze.
Loves to walk slowly outdoors, improves symptoms. Likes the seashore, walking by the ocean. Better slow,
passive motion in the open air. Worse from warm, stuffy rooms. Dislike the confines of clothing. Fear of suf-
focating, drowning. Feels closed in.
Better lying with the head higher than the rest of the body. Worse at twilight, sad at twilight (Rhus-t., Phos.).
Measles, mumps, typhoid fevers, bilious, catarrhal intermittent, or rheumatic. In fevers, “chilly, worse by
warmth, thirstless.” Chilliness may be one-sided and associated with numbness. Chilliness flitting in spots,
now here, now there. Heat with distended veins and burning hands that seek cool places, without thirst. Profuse
sweat, may be one-sided, sour, sweetish sour or musty in odor.
“Mousey” odor, similar to measles, as well as a cough, catarrhal symptoms and rash. Ear trouble as a sequelae
or complication of measles or other fever. Effects of suppressed rashes and metastases, as of mumps to testes
or breasts. Prophylactic against measles (Bell.). For scarlatina, give 3c three times a day.
Pains appear suddenly and leave gradually, or tension increases until very acute, then “lets up with a snap.”
Characteristic wandering pains. When lying down, pain is in side on which patient is not lying, but when
changing position, pain goes to the side that had been lain on before change of position. Rheumatoid arthritis.
Rheumatic pains shift from joint to joint. Suffering parts emaciate. Vascular engorgement.
Congestion in respiratory system. “Pressure upon the chest and soreness.” Coughing with a copious
expectoration. Sinusitis. Secretions are generally thick, bland and yellowish green. Earaches (Cham.), sore
throats, particularly with clinging and changeable moods. Colic, in babies. Can have a history of many acute
infections and drug treatment.
Can almost be regarded as an organ remedy for the generative organs of both sexes. Gonorrhea with thick,
purulent secretion. Effects of suppressed gonorrhea orchitis and cystitis, prostatitis, sarcocele, varicocele, and
hydrocele. Metastasis of mumps to testes or breasts.
Useful for the sexual period from puberty to menopause, including menstruation, pregnancy, the puerperium
and breast-feeding.
First serious impairment of health is referred to age of puberty, “never been well since,” anemia, bronchitis,
tuberculosis.
Premenstrual syndrome. Irritable before menses, weeps easily. Delay of menses in spite of evident symptoms
of a flow of blood towards the uterus. Menstrual blood is black, coagulated, impoverished if menses either too
early or too late. Menstrual cramps with chills and weeping. Epilepsy with absence or irregularity of menses.
Vaginitis with thick yellow or yellow green discharge, or without specific symptoms (Thuj., Nat-p.), may or may
not have itching. Menopause with heat and flushing, desire for fresh air.
Weeping during pregnancy. Fears during pregnancy, that they are unloved, that no one will help with the baby.
Feelings of helplessness, lead to weeping. Fear that they will not be a good mother, that something is wrong
with the baby. Morning sickness with headaches, vomiting and nausea, and a large appetite. Labor pains.
Ineffectual and weak labor (Caul.).
Bojanus related two cases, the first in which agir!, 18, of good constitution with no hereditary predisposition,
had amenorrhea for six months and a fit occurred at the time each period was due. In the epileptic aura, she
looked sad, pale as death, had chewing movements. Puls. 6c one dose a day was given. The next month,
menses returned and there were no more fits.
The second case was of a robust girl, 14, with no hereditary predisposition. She had fits for twelve months.
The exciting cause was the non-appearance of menses. She had one great fit per month, small fits daily. In
the epileptic aura she was self willed, angry, stood on one spot, stared into vacancy, stamped her foot. In the
 fit she cried, had deathly paleness, bit her tongue, urine flowed. She continued the occupation she was
engaged with at the beginning of the fit. Puls. 30c one dose a day was given.
Some weeks after, she had a slight fit. A month later, menses came on for first time, she had no great fits, and
small ones were rare. She was given Puls. 30c one dose a week. A month later, she had a great fit.
Puls, was then given once a day. She had no more great fits, only a few small ones. The cure was permanent.
Teste noted a case of Stoerck's, in which a young girl who had amaurosis of both eyes since infancy. Stoerck
cured in two months, administering an extract internally and externally a dry powder. The latter caused at first
an acute pain and profuse flow of tears after which the pains, which had existed previous to the lachrymation,
diminished as soon as it commenced and finally disappeared with it.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Cham, and Puls, antidote each other and follow each other well. If either one
has over-acted the other will probably neutralize the ill effect and carry on the good. Coff., Ign., Nux-v. When
the improper use of Puls, has affected the air passages, Calc-p. has proved the best antidote. Antidote to:
Chin., Chin-s., Ferr. (in chlorotic girls who have been damaged by iron, Puls, has excellent effect). Compare:
(1) Puls., similar effects. Cycl., Kali-bi., Kali-s., Sulph. (2) Tearfulness, Sep., Nat-m., Ign. (3) Varicose veins,
varicocele, orchitis, milk leg, Ham. (4) Ophthalmia, Arg-n. (5) All-c., both have worse in room, better open air,
but All-c. discharge is thin and excoriating, Puls, thick and bland. (6) Stinging pains in throat worse swallowing
saliva and after eating, Apis. (7) Feeling as if food lying in esophagus, Chin., Abies-n. (8) Effect of fat food, Ip.
Thuj., Carb-v. (9) Effect of ice cream, Ars., Carb-v., Ip., Bell-p. (10) Mixed diet, Nux-v., Ip., Chin. (11) Desire
for lemonade, Cycl., Sabin., Bell. (12) Gastric ailments from pork, (13) Retained placenta, Canth. after-pains,
Cham., Xan., Cupr. (14) Non-appearance of milk, Urt-u., Ric., Agn. (15) Uterine affections, Caul., Melon., Alet.,
Cycl., Hydr., Lil-t. (16) Measles, Morbill., Kali-bi. (17) Earache, Bor. Compatible: Ars., Bry., Bell., Ign., Kali-bi.,
Lyc., Nux-v., Phos., Rhus-t., Sep., Sulph. Complementary: Coff., Cham., Nux-v., Pen. often indicated after
Puls, in later colds.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Pulsatilla Nuttaliana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - puls-n. Pulsatilla nuttalliana. American pulsatilla. American Pasque Flower. Anemone
Ludoviciana. Anemone nuttaliana. N. O. Ranunculaceae. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Clavus. Cold, liability to. Deafness. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Feet, fidgety.
Homesickness. Knees, rheumatism. Liver, pains. Measles, prophylaxis. Menses, retarded. Ptosis.
Rheumatism. Sciatica. Shoulder, pain. Tinnitus. Uterus, pains.
HERBAL - The American pulsatilla is more similar to Puls, vulgaris than to Puls. nig. in its botanical characters.
It flourishes especially in the dry and sandy bluffs which form the bed of the Mississippi.
Hale wrote “The flower is pale purplish. The odor of the dried plant is rather faint, being slightly camphor-like,
the taste of the dried flowers simply sweetish and herbaceous, that of the leaves more astringent with very
slight acrimony. The taste and to some extent the odor of the fresh plant are both acrid and irritating.”
A. W. Miller, a pharmacist, analyzed Puls-n. The extracted substances had an acrid, almost caustic taste and
well-marked camphor-like odor. When volatilized, they produced an irritating, pungent vapor, affecting the eyes
and causing sneezing.
His analysis revealed constituents including organic grape-sugar, gum, resin, an alkaloid and anemonic acid.
Inorganic sulphate of potash, carbonate of potash, chlorate of potassium, carbonate of lime, magnesia and “a
proto-salt of iron.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. W. H. Miller, an allopath, claimed to have used Puls-n. with success in many chronic
eye affections, particularly catarrh, amaurosis and corneal opacities, skin eruptions and secondary syphilis.
Homesick feeling. Trembling weakness, weariness, heaviness. Great debility, on rising in evening. Languid,
feverish, depressed. Snapping noise in ears. Hands constantly hot and dry. Stiffness of fingers.
Fidgety feet. Colic before and after stool. Colic after eating a pear.
MIND - Sad, gloomy, with frequent belchings. Homesick, despondent. Anxiety, at night. Irritable, quick, nervous
motions. Dull, disinclined for work.
Abdomen - Dull pains in the right hypochondrium. Aching in one spot worse by moving. Aching in left groin,
above left iliac crest on moving or bending. Dull pains in the abdomen, by spells in hypogastrium. Severe pain
in umbilicus, 6 a.m., with desire for stool, stool dark, covered with mucus, severe pains for half an hour after.
Rumbling after dinner of wind in distended abdomen moving from epigastrium to hypogastrium. Colicky pains
after eating a ripe pear.
Back - Stiffness right side of neck, in the morning. Backache. Woke frequently with backache. Lameness in
 back, especially loins. Weakness of loins, feeling as if menses coming on.
Chest - Sharp, stabbing pain in pectoralis major muscle, followed by burning distress. During evening, severe
pain under left arm nearer back. Aching pain in chest all forenoon. Itching blotches on right breast, right side
chest.
Ears - With the pains in head and eyes, frequent drawing pains in ears from within out. Hard, drawing pains
along right Eustachian tube. Sharp pains in right ear and temples. Left ear feels closed, later both. Snapping
noises in ears, fluttering in right. Deafness with edema of left upper eyelid.
Eyes - Neuralgic pains in eyeballs, while walking, worse right side. Dull pain deep in eyes with smarting.
Dryness, smarting, profuse flow of tears. Profuse secretion of mucus from eyes. Profuse lachrymation with dull
pains in eyeball extending to malar bone. Tarsal edges red, dry, irritable. Eyelids agglutinated, profuse
secretion of soft, yellow or white matter. Paralysis of lids. Edema of left upper lid. Twitching of left brow and
upper lid for half an hour after going to bed, right lids worse reading.
Face - Face red, hot, flushed. After eating, flushed, pressure of blood in face. Complexion at first rough, later
very clear after disappearance of rash. Painful drawing in left cheekbone and jaw. Lips dry.
Female - Feeling as if menses coming on. Menses, weak, too soon (discharge, which had been formerly too
dark and with pain, was this time natural in color and painless). Menses, always copious, increased to flooding
and lasted three days. In morning on awaking found menses had returned first time since weaning babe (two
months). Painless leucorrhea. Leucorrhea, bland but so profuse and with so great depression that the prover
refused to take more of the drug although it removed a pleuritic pain. Stinging, darting pains passing through
uterus from side to side.
Food - Great hunger, rapidly returned after eating. Loss of appetite. More thirst than usual, cold water
extremely grateful.
Head - Dull heavy headache, in the mornings, better by active exercise before breakfast. Dull, oppressive,
frontal headache, on waking. Hard pains in upper forehead pass in wave to occiput involving whole brain.
Flying pains in head and feet. With headache cutting pains in the epigastrium. Hard pain over left eye, as if a
nail being pressed into forehead. Pain over right eye afternoon, better walking in open air, worse in warm room
with sense of heat, fullness in head and dryness of eyes. Sharp, shooting pains through both temples in right
temple. Dull pain in right temple in vertex. Severe throbbing on vertex. Full, hot feeling at cerebellum. Headache
arising from nape of neck and upwards.
Heart - Audible pulsation of heart. Pulse accelerated.
Kidneys - Frequent urination. Tenesmus, extending up ureters, uneasiness in kidneys. Pain on urinating, at
end of urethra. Urine pale, albuminous, excess of water, skunk-like odor.
Limbs - Muscles stiff. Cramp. Nervous sensation, irresistible fidgets, worse night, with desire to urinate
afternoon and at night. Legs heavy while walk
ing, trembling weakness, nervous pains. Aching in limbs and loins wakes him frequently. Sharp neuralgic pains
along sciatic nerve from hip joint to middle of thigh. Pain in both knees, rheumatic. Dull pain in ankles, flying
pains. Very cold feet, evening. Frequent flying pains in hands, feet, toes. Rheumatism of right shoulder.
Lameness in muscles of right upper arm. Frequent momentary pains in wrists and fingers. Hands dry and hot
all day. Fingers stiff.
Lungs - Constant inclination to cough. Small sore spot in upper trachea.
Male - Distressing erection, soon subsiding. Emission. Pain in penis on waking, worse on urinating. Hard,
sticking pains in left spermatic cord and testes. Dull pains in testes, worse right.
Modalities - Better walking in open air. Better from rubbing with brush, scratching. Worse coming in from open
air, warmth, at night. Worse from reading, walking, urinating, after eating, eating a pear.
Mouth - Tongue coated white, covered with tough slime, red, rather dry and swollen, yellowish coat along
center, unusually red after eating. Teeth indented on tongue. Breath offensive to self and others after eating.
Mouth filling with saliva. Mouth and lips dry. Smarting of velum palati. On waking, dry, flat, pappy taste in
mouth, as if tongue thickly coated (which it was not). Flat, bitter, rough, sweetish, bad taste. Wakes with
vinegar-like acidity in mouth and dull, pressing pain in stomach.
Nose - Dryness and heat in nose.
Rectum - Feeling as if must go to stool immediately, with constant distress in lower epigastrium and umbilicus.
Constipation. Sudden attack of diarrhea while riding on horseback. Stools dark, thin, pap-like, watery, light
yellow, painless, mushy, dark, slightly covered with mucus, dry, hard, lumpy.
Skin - Red rash on body, face, neck, back, chest, abdomen, limbs, worse chest and abdomen. Itching,
scattered pimples, right side of chest, light red, rash-like blotches on right breast, itching severely at night,
worse when heated. Slight rash on back
and shoulders. Elevated, blotchy eruption on legs and back. Erythema, nodules, turn white after scratching.
 Intense itching all over, worse night before bedtime, better rubbing, worse riding in cold air, returned repeatedly
throughout the winter.
Sleep - Sleepy, sleep not refreshing. Sleepless for an hour at 4 a.m., for several hours from over-eating.
Restless with frontal headache. Many confused dreams.
Stomach - Gnawing, empty sensation. Painful emptiness, pressure, then rising towards esophagus like
heartburn. Emptiness after action of bowels, after eating. Fullness in stomach preventing eating in spite of
appetite. Weight and pressure in stomach after eating with faintness. Distress with severe cutting pains in
epigastrium. Heartburn. Belchings, of food, hot, tasteless wind, sour air. Thick gulping. Nausea and dull
headache, then faintness at stomach, on entering house.
Temperature - Chilly, with a full, uncomfortable feeling in stomach, with inclination to yawn, with papescent
stool, shaking. Heat, feverish with debility, skin hot, flaccid, better cool, blustering wind. Hot face, cold feet,
hands hot and feverish.
Throat - Scratchy, husky feeling in throat. Sensation of plug in lower throat. Frequent inclination to clear throat.
Throat dry, smarts on waking, contains much tough mucus that is hard to dislodge. After eating, slight irritation
in throat with easy expectoration of white, tough mucus.
Vertigo - Dizziness on entering house from open air, sudden in afternoon, with fullness of head.
COMMENTS - Hale instituted the first homeopathic research and Burt was the first prover. The symptoms
have a strong resemblance to those of Puls, and cases cured with Puls-n. are mostly such as would be
amenable to Puls.
The Puls, flying pains were very noticeable in the proving. Feeling as if needles being pressed through
stomach. Heat in stomach gradually increasing to pain, worse in spots under sternum, burning, pricking
burning.
The proving showed a powerful effect on the menstrual function and Hale reported
many cures of amenorrhea, including the case of a young woman, formerly subject to retardation of menses.
She had constant chilliness, cold hands and feet, loss of appetite, sour belchings, nausea after meals,
hemicrania, toothache, melancholy, and general malaria. Menses were two weeks late, took a chill at the time
they were due, when she had precursory symptoms, no symptoms of menses now.
Hale gave Puls-n. lx in water every two hours. After the first dose, the menses came on and the constitutional
symptoms cleared off.
Hale also noted the case of a plethoric, usually healthy young woman, who had menses delay two weeks.
Continual severe headache, a heaviness and fullness, worse moving or stooping. Sight dim, complete
blindness on stooping or rising suddenly, weight in uterine region severe aching extending to back, worse
evening. Hands and feet cold, weakness in lower limbs. Act. failed to relieve.
Puls-n. lx, 5 drops every three hours, brought speedy improvement. The next day menses came on profusely
but without pain, two days before the expiration of the eighth week.
Hale reported the case of a strong, healthy looking man who had wandering rheumatic pains chiefly in dorsum
of right foot, loins, thighs, chest, arms, head. The head pain was a dull, heavy pressure in vertex, nearly
constant with occasional sharp pains.
Some fever but no local inflammation of joints or muscles. Urine scanty, depositing gravel. Acidity of stomach.
Appetite good. Bowels normal. Puls-n. lx cured in three days.
A patient of Clarke’s was incidentally cured of a tendency to catch colds by taking Puls-n. for some weeks as
a prophylactic against measles.
Burnett cured with Puls-n. a case of deafness and edema of left upper eyelid.
RELATIONS Antidoted by: Ant-c. Compare: (1) Puls. (2) In fidgety feet, Zinc, Caust.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Pyrarara
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pyrar. Pyrarara. Amazon fish lard. The lard of the Pyrarara fish of the Amazon river. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Chloasma. Dermatitis. Elephantiasis. Gangrene. Leprosy. Nodules. Scleroderma. Syphilis.
Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vitiligo. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pyrar. has been used clinically for various skin affections, leprosy, tuberculosis, syphilis,
varicosities, etc.
COMMENTS - Dr. Frederick M. Dearborn, New York, 1915, who brought some of the “lard” from South America
and turned it over to Boericke and Tafel wrote, “I had curiosity enough to inquire of my homeopathic friends,
while visiting Rio recently, if they knew of any 'new' remedies.
 “While a number were suggested that I had never heard of, Pyrarara appealed to me because of its manifest
dermal indications and because I was able to procure, through the endeavors of Dr. Theodore Gomes, a small
supply of the extract, and by the courtesy of Dr. Marques de Oliveira, a genuine clinical record.”
“Before proceeding to the recital of the clinical case, it might be well to mention that the use of Pyrarara is not
limited to the treatment of leprosy, but has been used to relieve a number of dermatoses.”
“The exact diagnoses of these conditions were hard to determine, but their descriptions would lead me to think
of the tuberculosis, the syphilis, scleroderma, vitiligo, chloasma, elephantiasis, varicosed vessels and the
attendant dermatitis, gangosa, jaws and the varieties of gangrene. I received some positive assurances as
regards its use in varicosities.”
“Pyrarara is not listed in any group of Brazilian or South American remedies that I can discover and has not
been scientifically proven, but I hope the following translation of Dr. Oliveira's notes may be of interest:
“The lard of the Pyrarara, a fish of the Amazon river, was brought from Acre by Major Carpenter of the
Engineers, who offered it as a curiosity to Mr. Liberato dos Santos. The Major said that he had heard from the
inhabitants of the Amazon valley that the lard has the property of changing the color of the plumage of parrots
fed upon it, and that a person abusing the use of the fish, as a food, would develop leprosy or symptoms similar
to that disease. After a talk with Mr. dos Santos, he gave me some of the lard for homeopathic experimentation
on people affected with leprosy.”
“The following is the result: Maria Theresa, 36 years old, has suffered from leprosy since she was 19 years
old. The first appearance of the disease was on the extremities of her fingers and on her face after suppression
of menstruation. She was treated by Dr. Gabizo for three years without any result and by many other doctors,
using various medicines and electricity, but still no result was attained.”
‘The disease had reached the highest state of development; her anatomic structure had become deformed
and her facial changes took away from her the appearance of a human being. Her body was covered with
nodules and ulcers in constant suppuration; her ears were inflamed and deformed; her nose was ulcerated
and corroded; her lips were tumefacted and ulcerated; her throat was so affected that her voice was completely
lost; her arms looked like a piece of raw flesh; and the phalanges of all her fingers were destroyed. Certain
areas of the skin were anesthetic and there was a general coppery discoloration.”
“It was at this period that she came to me. I proposed experimenting upon her with the new medicine, which
she reluctantly accepted, after many days of insisting. In June, 1905, we began our treatment, at first using
the 3x trituration with a dose of three tablets every three hours applying, externally, vaseline with calendula.
The first month there was no apparent dermal improvement, but her appetite increased. I then began to use
the 5x potency and during the first two weeks there was a great transformation.”
“Through the open lesions came an abundant discharge of a whitish color tinted with blood and very thick, and
the body was covered with bullae, where there were no ulcers before, but always the same kind of discharge.
Her appetite became very good and digestion regular, but she became prostrated and suffered from neuralgic
pains in the head, face, and feet. During the month of August the inflammation of the lips was disappearing
and the wounds of the lips healing. She was very cheerful with the result. As her sight was getting feeble,
Asafoetida was given to her and the eye symptoms improved to a great extent.”
“At the beginning of September the ulcers had ceased suppurating, the bullae did not appear any more and
her general state was very good. As the menstrual periods came, she felt great pain in the lumbar and ovarian
regions and Pulsatilla 30th was given to her and the menses appeared, although very feeble. I then gave
Pyrarara in the 30x potency for a few days and she continued to improve. The nodules diminished in size and
the ulcers became almost dry, with scant discharge, while the tumefaction disappeared.”
“About this time Aurum met. 5th potency and afterward Apis 5x potency and Cuprum met. 5x potency were
used as the symptom called for. On the following month the menses came freely. In November I returned to
the use of Pyrarara 30x potency. The healing of the wounds continued and only three ulcers were to be found
on the whole body, one on the forearm, on the foot, and one on the middle finger. The tumefaction gradually
disappeared, except on the ears. General condition was very good. By the 25th of December one could hardly
detect her sickness.”
“The intense redness of her face was gone; the forehead was white, the natural color having returned; the lips,
mouth and throat were normal; while the ears were still tumefacted, the nodules had disappeared; the body
was free from ulcers and nodules;
the forearm completely well. Only one ulcer on the middle finger was to be found. Her organic functions were
re-established, sensibility had almost returned and she could move the deformed fingers, but the sense of
touch was not complete. By January, 1906, after seven months of treatment, she disappeared.”
“This medication has been tried since on different people with splendid results, but lack of persistency has
prevented complete cures. On the other patients the Pyrarara has been used, employing the centesimal scale
 of potencies.”
REFERENCES - Anshutz.

name: Pyrethrum Parthenium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -pyre-p. Pyrethrum parthenium. Feverfew. Chrysanthemum parthenium. Anacyclus officinarum.
Leucanthemum parthenium. N. O. Compositae. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of dried roots. Historical
dose: Tincture, all potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Fevers. Loquacity. Rheumatism.
HERBAL - Pyrethrum has bitter tonic properties like those of chamomile (Anthémis nobilis) and is a popular
remedy in slight fevers, hence the name “feverfew.”
The Treasury of Botany noted that the smell of the whole herb is said to be particularly offensive to bees. Some
popular insect powders were made of the dried flowers of Pyrethrum roseum.
Radix pyrethri, or Pellitory of Spain, which is used as an irritant and as a toothache cure is the root of
Anachycles pyrethrum. The roots of the genus have a hot taste, the source of the name pyrethrum (fire).
HOMEOPATHIC - One observation was recorded with pyrethrum; a boy, 3 1/2 took 50 minims of the tincture.
It nearly proved fatal, causing diarrhea, convulsions of a tetanic nature, twitchings, loquacious delirium,
restless, rapid and weak pulse and profuse sweat at night.
Twitching of muscles, of limbs, subsided by morning of third day. Violent convulsions lasting an hour and
leaving the child apparently moribund, but he gradually recovered.
Feet, legs and body, which were swollen, were decidedly reduced and the next menstrual period was dark and
deficient in a gouty woman, age 50. She also had convulsive movements like tetanus. Restlessness. Stupor.
Cooper cured cases of sub-acute rheumatism with Pyrethrum roseum.
MIND - Very excited, talks incessantly for hours. Lying in state of stupor, easily roused but quickly relapsing.
Limbs - Old sub-acute rheumatism of hands and small bones.
Mouth - Soreness of tongue.
Pulse - Pulse very rapid (120 to 130) and feeble.
Rectum - Tenesmus followed by involuntary evacuations of mucus, slightly tinged with blood, better next
morning. Diarrhea, 5 a.m. w ith pain, at first profuse and exhausting.
Temperature - Profuse perspiration and restlessness at night.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cham., Cina, Absin., Art-v. (2) other Compositae.
REFERENCES Clarke.
