name: Pyrogenium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pyrog. Pyrogenium. Rotten meat pus. Pyrogen. Pyrexin. Sepsin. A product of the decomposition
of chopped lean beef in water, allowed to stand in the sun for two or three weeks. Nosodes. Dilutions.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Appendicitis. Bedsores. Bites. Blood,poisoning. Boils. Bright's disease. Boils.
Bones, pain. Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Eczema. Enteric, fever. Fevers, high. Fistula. Food
poisoning. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hectic, fever. Hepatitis. Influenza. Injuries. Intestines, ulceration.
Lymphangitis. Malaria. Miscarriage. Offensive, discharges. Ovary, abscess. Palpitations. Peritonitis.
Plague. Ptomaine, poisoning. Puerperal, fever. Pyemia. Tabes mesenterica. Tuberculosis, lungs. Typhoid.
Restlessness. Septic,fever. Septicemia. Sores. Syphilitic. Ulcers. Varicose veins. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - John Drysdale, in 1880, was the first to suggest the use of this substance as a medicine.
This nosode is prepared from decomposed lean beef allowed to stand in the sun for two weeks, or from septic
pus.
Pyrog. is the great remedy for septic states with intense restlessness. H. C. Allen indicated that it is an anti-
septic, useful in septic fevers, especially puerperal. Chronic complaints that date back to septic conditions.
For all types of septic states when blood is disorganized. The heart becomes weak and muscles prostrated.
Hectic, typhoid, typhus, ptomaine poisoning, and diphtheria states. Dissecting wounds. Sewer-gas poisoning.
Characteristic carrion-like odor of bodily emaciation, secretions and excretions. Horribly offensive
discharges, foul, menstrual, lochia, diarrhea, vomit, sweat, breath, taste, body odor. Constipation from
impacted feces in fevers, stool large, black, carrionlike. Great pain and violent burning in abscesses.
Septic fevers. Temperature rises rapidly. Quickly oscillating temperature. Fever commencing with pains in
the limbs. High fevers with sore limbs and delirium. Threatening heart failure in zymotic and septic fevers.
Influenza, typhoid symptoms. Cerebrospinal meningitis. Chronic malaria. Rosy red streaks, lymphangitis.
 After-effects of miscarriage. Food poisoning.
Great heat with profuse sweat, but sweating does not cause a fall in temperature. Sweats without relief.
Shivers and begins to move about restlessly. Cold and chilly all day. No fire will warm, sits by fire and chilly
whenever he leaves it. Chill begins in back, between scapulae. Severe general chill of bones and limbs.
Aching, bruised, sore pains and prostration, yet restless. Bones pain. Restless, must move to ameliorate
the soreness of parts. Cannot lie more than few minutes in one position, better change. Bed feels too hard
(Bapt., Arn.), aching all over. Great muscular debility, rapid recovery in few
hours. Debility in morning, staggered on trying to walk.
MIND - Sensitive, anxious, confused. Confusion of mind. Active mind, making speeches and writing articles at
night. Loquacious, thinks and talks faster than ever before. Prostration of mind, mental exhaustion, brain fag.
Weeping, tearful mood. Morose, sulky, cross, fretful, ill-humor, peevish. Anxiety in morning. Full of anxiety and
insane notions. Desires to be rocked. Talks or whispers to herself in sleep. Cannot tell whetherdreaming
while awake or asleep. Semi-conscious and muttering. Stupor.
Bed feels too hard (Bapt., Arn.). Restlessness, tossing about in bed. Restlessness and delirium with
fever. Delirium on closing the eyes. Delirium, anxious and confused. Delirium from sepsis.
Delusions, sees images, phantoms. Delusion that he is very wealthy. Delusions, he is enlarged, body parts
were scattered about bed. Sensation as if she covered the whole bed. Feels if crowded with arms and legs.
Confusion as to his identity. Sensation of duality. Feels when lying on one side, one person, and another
person, when turning, on the other side. Disgust at his own body odor.
Abdomen - Distension. Full feeling of abdomen. Bloated, sore, cutting pain. Soreness of abdomen can hardly
breathe or bear any pressure over right side. Sore, bruised pain and tenderness. Cutting pain. Cramping,
griping pain in hypochondria. Severe cutting pains right side going through back, worse by every motion.
Bubbling or gurgling sensation in hypochondria, extending back to left of spine. Rumbling, gurgling noises.
Colitis. Peritonitis, enteritis. Tabes mesenterica. Pain in umbilical region with passage of sticky, yellow stool.
Ileus, obstruction of bowels, impaction. Appendicitis. Hepatitis. Cholecystitis. Buboes.
Back - Weakness, tired feeling in back. Weak feeling in back, stitching pain on coughing. Coldness, chill.
Sharp, shooting pain. Caries, necrosis of spine. Lumbago. Pulsation, cervical region. Throbbing of
vessels of neck running up in waves from clavicles.
Breasts - Sore, bruised pain. Pains in the region of left nipple.
Causations - Chronic complaints since septic conditions. After-effects of miscarriage. Remote effects of
hepatitis, diphtheria, chronic malaria. Typhoid fever, puerperal fever. Bites, cuts, dissecting wounds, blood
poisoning. Ptomaine poisoning, sewer-gas poisoning.
Chest - Pain in right lung and shoulder, worse talking or coughing. Aching pain behind sternum. Chest sore,
with purple spots. Oppression of chest. Severe contracting pain within lower sternum, sometimes extending to
rib joints and up to throat, as if esophagus was cramped.
Cough - Cough with large masses of phlegm from larynx, worse by motion, in warm room. Coughs up yellow
sputa at night. Cough, with night-sweats, frequent pulse. Cough causes burning in larynx and bronchi. Cough
better sitting up, worse lying down.
Ears - Burning pains. Discharges, offensive. Ears red, as if blood would burst out of them. Ears feel cold.
Pulsation, synchronous with pulse. Noises like steam escaping. Loud ringing like a bell.
Eyes - Cornea, keratitis. Sore, bruised pain. Eyeballs sore, worse looking up and moving eyes, particularly left
eyeball. Swelling of eyes. Projecting eyes. Photophobia. Roughness of margins, edges of lids. Styes.
Face - Face, burning, yellow, very red, pale, greenish, chlorotic, sunken and bathed in cold sweat. Hippocratic.
Bluish around eyes. Circumscribed redness of cheeks. Hectic flush 3 p.m. to 4 p.m., lasting until midnight, then
covered with large drops of cold perspiration.
Female - Fever at each menstrual period. Menses, bright red, clotted. Menses horribly offensive, carrion-
like. Menses too short, last but one day, then a horribly offensive, bloody leucorrhea. Genitals severely swollen
(Bright's disease). Pelvic peritonitis or cellulitis. Abscess in ovaries. Abscess of left ovary, acute throbbing pain,
great distress with fever and rigors. Ovaritis. Pulsating pain in ovaries. Salpingitis. Prolapse uterus, better
holding the head and straining. Uterine hemorrhage of bright red blood with dark clots. Metrorrhagia, bright
red, clotted, coagulated. Puerperal peritonitis with extreme fetor. Septicemia following a miscarriage with the
fetus or placenta retained and decomposed. Retained placenta. Septic infections after childbirth. Lochia
thin, watery. Lochia, acrid, offensive, bloody, intermittent. Lochia suppressed, followed by fever, chills and
profuse fetid sweat. Post-operative cases with overwhelming sepsis.
Food - No appetite or thirst. Great thirst for small quantities of cold drinks, but the least liquid is instantly
rejected. Better by drinking very hot water. Nausea, better very hot drinks.
Head - Excruciating, violent, throbbing headache, better bandaging. Bursting pain with restlessness. Great
 throbbing of arteries of temples and head. Painless throbbing all though front of head, sounds like escaping
steam. Dull throbbing in mastoid region. Rolls head from side to side. Skull-cap sensation. Forehead bathed
in cold sweat. Erysipelas.
Heart - Anxiety in region of heart. Consciousness of the heart. Sensation as if heart enlarged, too full of blood.
As if the heart were pumping cold water. Purring at region of heart. Cardiac weakness from septic conditions.
Threatened heart failure in zymotic and septic states. Fluttering sensation. Heart tired, as after a long run,
increased action worse least motion. Palpitations, worse by motion. Palpitations are increased without
corresponding increase of temperature. Pulse quick, out of all proportion to temperature or the reverse.
Loud heartbeats, audible to herself and others. Throbbing felt in head and in ears, preventing sleep.
Kidneys - Bright's disease. Intolerable tenesmus of both bladder and rectum. Urging to urinate before fever.
Frequent calls to urinate as fever comes on. Urination twice a day, scanty. Urine clear like water,
Pyrogenium adhesive, red, slimy, sediment, deposits like red pepper. Putrid smelling urine, horribly
offensive, carrion-like odor. Urine scanty, yellow after standing, cloudy with substance looking like orange
peel. Urine, containing casts. Red sediment in urine hard to wash off. Albuminous urine during and after
delivery, parturition. Suppression of urine, anuria.
Limbs - Soreness, better from motion (Rhus- t.). Aching in bones, all over body as from a severe cold with
soreness. Bed feels too hard (Bapt., Am.). Rapid bedsores of septic origin. Great debility in the morning.
Chilliness. Cold limbs. Numbness of hands, arms and feet, extending over whole body. Cramps. Pain in right
shoulder, worse coughing, talking. Automatic movement of right arm and right leg, in cerebrospinal meningitis.
Tingling in right little toe as if frostbitten. Feet and legs swollen (Bright's disease). Milk leg, phlegmasia alba
dolens, phlebitis. Perspiration on limbs. Ulcers. Varicose ulcers on lower limbs. Panaritium. Exfoliation of nails.
Nails threaten to fall off or feel loose.
Lungs - Pain in right lung, worse coughing, talking. Neglected pneumonia. Pleuritis. Empyema. Tuberculosis,
last stage. Difficult breathing during sleep. Dyspnea, better open air. Wheezing when expiring. Horribly
offensive expectoration, rusty mucus. Bloody expectoration, spitting of blood. Rusty sputum. Rattling ex-
pectoration. Thick, offensive, purulent, viscid expectoration. Abscess opens, discharging pus.
Male - Testes hang down, relaxed. Relaxed scrotum. Scrotum looks and feels thin. Prostatitis.
Modalities - Better from heat, hot bathing, hot drinks. Better from pressure, stretching, motion, changing
position, hard rocking and walking. Worse cold, damp. Worse sitting, motion, moving eyes, passing flatus.
Mouth - Dryness of mouth. Horribly offensive, cadaverous, putrid breath. Taste sweetish, terribly fetid.
Excoriation of mucus membrane. Sordes. Abscess of teeth, roots.
Nose - Cold feeling in nose. Obstruction, alternating sides. Fan-like motion of the alae nasi. Sneezing from
uncovering. One-sided coryza. Nosebleed with sepsis. Nosebleed during fever. Nosebleeds, awakened by
dreaming it and found it was so. Disgust at his own body odor.
Perspiration - Clammy sweats. Shivering with sweats. Great heat with profuse hot sweat. Sweating does
not cause a fall in temperature. Sweats without relief. Profuse sweats at night. Perspiration horribly
offensive, carrion-like. Sour smelling sweats. Disgust, up to nausea, about any effluvia arising from her own
body.
Rectum - Inactivity of rectum. Constipation with complete inertia (Op.). Obstinate constipation from impaction.
Constipation, stool remains long in rectum with no urging. Intolerable tenesmus of both bladder and rectum.
Involuntary stool during urination. Diarrhea with fever. Diarrhea from excitement, emotions. Diarrheafrom
septic conditions. Painless diarrhea. Hemorrhage from anus. Sore, bruised pain. Fistula. Perspiration about
the anus and perineum.
Skin - Pale, cold, dry. Dryness and burning. Unhealthy skin, every scratch festers or heals with difficulty. Small
cut or injury becomes very swollen and inflamed, discolored. Septic cuts, bites, wounds. Abscess. Ulcers
offensive, putrid, purulent, fetid, sloughing. Ulcers with bloody discharges. Varicose ulcers. Offensive ulcers
of old persons. Bedsores during fever. Lymphangitis, red streaks on skin. Boils. Blood boils. Carbuncles.
Scarlatina. Smallpox. Purpura hemorrhagica. Obstinate varicose veins. Erysipelas. Ecchymosis.
Actinomycosis.
Sleep - Restlessness. Unable to sleep for brain activity and crowding of ideas. Sleepless from fevers.
Sleeplessness, bed feels too hard. Sleeplessness from thoughts. Kept awake by purring of heart. Seems to
be in semi-sleep. Position changedfrequently. Slept awhile, wakes to roll and tumble. Whispering in sleep.
Cries out in sleep that a weight is lying
Pyrogenium on her. Restless sleep from dreams. Vivid dreams all night, of various things, of business.
Frightful, anxious dreams.
Stomach - Coldness, chilliness in stomach. Stomach feels too full. Eructations sour. Belching of sour water
after breakfast. Nausea, vomiting and purging. Urging to vomit with cold feet. Nausea, better very hot drinks
 and vomiting. Vomits water when it becomes warm in stomach. Persistent, brownish vomiting, offensive
smelling. Bile or bloody vomit, or like coffee-grounds. Vomiting, fecal with impacted or obstructed bowels.
Vomiting with constipation.
Stool - Hard, dry stools, like small black balls, sheep dung. Knotty, nodular, lumpy stools. Offensive, putrid,
carrion-like stools. Bloody streaks in stools. Mucus, slimy bloody stools. Long, narrow stools. Horribly
offensive, brown-black diarrhea. Painless, involuntary stools. Insufficient, incomplete, unsatisfactory stools.
Temperature - Chilliness with perspiration. Cold sweatoverbody. Violentchill, begins in back between
scapula, felt in bones with sweat, at night. Shivers and begins to move about restlessly. Cold and chilly all
day, no fi Temperature rises rapidly. Quickly oscillating temperature. Great heat with profuse sweat. Sweating
does not cause a fall in temperature, re would warm, sits by fire and chilly whenever he leaves it. Cold, then
hot. Quotidian fever. Septic fevers. Latent pyrogenic condition. Cerebrospinal meningitis. Fever commencing
with pains in the limbs. High fevers with sore limbs and delirium. Slowly advancing hectic fever. Fever and
pulse don't match, high fever, slow pulse. Frequent calls to urinate as soon as fever came on, urine clear
as water.
Throat - Septic sore throats. Abscessed tonsils. Diphtheria with extreme fetor. Membrane, exudation,
malignant diphtheria. Dry throat, difficult articulation. Hoarseness. Voice husky, weak.
Tongue - Tongue red and dry, clean, cracked, smooth, as if varnished. Brown streak down center. Red
stripe down center. Cracked, fissured tongue. Excoriation of tongue. Fiery-red, glistening, tongue. Yellow
tongue. Smooth, shining, glazed, glistening, glossy tongue. Large, flabby tongue, with imprints of teeth. Clean,
clear tongue. Protruding the tongue is difficult.
Vertigo - Staggers as if drunk on rising in morning. Dizziness on rising up in bed.
COMMENTS - Drysdale prepared a tincture of Pyrog., which he preferred to call Pyrexin since it is not a mere
fever-producer. Others have called it Sepsin, but this is too close to Septicemia, a name given to a related and
perhaps identical nosode.
The provings and most of the clinical experience have been obtained from this preparation. Subsequently, Dr.
Swan po- tentized some septic pus, which has also been proved and clinically applied. There does not seem
to be any marked difference in their effects.
As Drysdale put it, “The most summary indication for Pyrog. would be to term it the Aconite of the typhus or
typhoid quality of pyrexia,” and it is likely useful wherever there is poisoning by bacterial products (e.g. in the
hectic of tuberculosis). Sepsis is the essence of its action.
H. C. Allen, who published the proving and most of the cases in Med. Adv., rightly describes Pyrog. as a
“Product of Sepsis.” He gave the indication for its use in septic state, “When the best selected remedies fail to
relieve or permanently improve,” analogous to the action of Psor. and Sulph. in other conditions.
Drysdale's original cases include a number in which threatened typhoid was averted, a case of tabes
mesenterica cured, and one of ulceration of the colon greatly benefited. Drysdale's success was encouraging,
but as he continued to use the tincture and the lowest potencies it was difficult to keep the preparation.
The remedy did not come into extensive use until Burnett published his pamphlet on Pyrogenium in Fevers
and Blood-poisoning in 1888. Burnett used chiefly the 6c dilution, which is perfectly harmless and which will
keep indefinitely. Heath, who made one of the preparations used by Burnett, gave some of it to Swan of New
York, who ran it up into the high infinitesimal.
Much of the American experience is with Swan's potencies, including a proving by Sherbino. Yingling collected
symptoms from many reported cases and arranged them with the symptoms of the proving.
In Sherbino's proving, he was cured incidentally of a consciousness of the heart, and its working and palpitation
from least excitement or anxiety, worse beginning to move, congestion to head as if a stroke would ensue.
Cact. had done no good.
Sherbino cured a case of puerperal fever with Pyrog., being led to its selection by the very high pulse rate. He
also had a case of relapsed typhoid, with pulse 140, temperature 102 F., both were normal in twenty-four
hours.
He had a third case of a young woman, 17, with a fever and aching bones where the bed felt very hard. She
had a numb, paralytic feeling. As the fever left, the pulse kept mounting up. Sherbino used Swan's potency,
Pyrog. 100,000c, repeated as often as effect ceased.
Clarke had ample opportunity to observe the power of Pyrog. over typhoid fever, typhoid, and hectic states,
including one of discharging abscess connected with Pott's disease of the spine.
Burnett had cases of fully developed typhoid cut short at the height by Pyrog. 6c given every two hours. In his
pamphlet he included Dr. Shouldham's successful experience with Pyrog. 6c in two cases of diphtheria sore
throat.
Burnett also recorded that Pyrog. 5c, five drops in water night and morning, assisted in the cure of a case of
 anal fistula. Under its action a sweating at the seat, which the man had for many years, disappeared. The skin
of his hands, which were subject to dry eczema, assumed a much cleaner aspect.
J. S. Hunt reported five cases of varicose ulcers, all of which healed quickly under Pyrog.
Bellairs gave Pyrog. 200c to an elderly woman who suffered for years with an ulcerated leg, which was riddled
with deep, burrowing wounds, extremely painful and discharging freely. Hep., Sil., Ars., and Ham. did no good.
Under Pyrog. once or twice a day, “a large boil” formed on the calf of the leg and discharged its contents after
which the various ulcers healed up directly.
Septicemia (Bapt., Merc., Rhus-t., Lach., Ars., Echi.), after surgery. Septic bites, cuts, wounds, and snakebites
(Led., Hyper.). Blood poisoning, from dissecting wounds. Gangrene (Sec.).
Abscesses with violent, burning pain. Abscesses in the muscles and major organs. Abscesses of the ovaries.
Ruptured abscess of the lung, pus in the lungs. Ruptured organs, blood filled with pus. Septic organs, rotting
away.
Septic kidney with offensive urine. Ulceration of the colon with blood and pus in the stool. Severe, acute,
abdominal infections; acute appendicitis, peritonitis. Septic varicose veins. Large boils with accompanying
fever.
Septic fever with pus, decomposed tissue, abscesses (Aeon, and Bell., are clean, inflammatory). Sudden,
septic onset (Bapt.). Infected bite, cute or wound that lead to an infected fever. High fevers, 105-106 F.
Fever and pulse don't match, high fever, slow pulse. Throbbing pains, sudden chills, rigors. Chill felt in the
bones. Cold, clammy hands. Never well since septic fever (Bapt.). Typhoid, diphtheria. Toxic flu (Ars., Nux-v.).
Delirium. Loquacity. Confusion about the body, delusion of too many limbs. Feel as if their body fills the whole
bed. Cannot find their body. Delusion of a man at the foot of the bed. Staggers as if drunk, vertigo. Confused,
muttering, talking in a whisper.
Toxic state. All discharges and odors are offensive and fetid, diarrhea, sweat, breath, menses.
Putrid, fetid, offensiveness. Stench-like odors; cadaver-like (Kreos., Bapt.). Offensive perspiration (Merc.).
Bitter, offensive taste. Tongue is brown, yellow at the back. The tip of the tongue can be red (Rhus-t.).
Constipation with black, putrid balls. Infected anal fissures with abscesses and offensive pus. Vomit of bile,
blood and water, coffee grounds (Ars., Cadm-s.).
Rapid, irregular heartbeats, high pulse. Feels as if the heart is pumping cold water. Hemorrhage of dark,
offensive blood with high fever, especially with pelvic infections and abscesses. Nosebleeds with offensive
blood.
Uterine hemorrhage. Horribly offensive menses (Kreos.). Bloody, vaginal discharges that are offensive, no
matter the cause. Septicemia after a miscarriage. For expelling a dead fetus (Sec.), beginning to decompose
in the womb, with a fever. Decomposing placenta after labor.
Severe muscle aches and soreness. Restless in bed. The bed feels hard (Arn., Bapt.). Difficulty getting
comfortable. Flesh feels tender and sore. Bone aches, bruised feeling (Arn.). Pains better motion. Cannot lie
in the same place very long, must move (Ars.).
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Echi., Carban., Ars., Lach., Rhus-t., Bapt. (2) Sepin. - a toxin of Proteus vulgaris,
prepared by Dr. Shedd, same symptoms as Pyrogen of which it is the main constituent. (3) Malar., Lach. (4)
In typhoid with soreness, bed feels hard, Bapt., (5) Arn., Rhus-t., better motion and stretching limbs, Rhus-t.
(6) Cough worse by motion and in warm room, Bry. (7) Uterine hemorrhage, Ip. (8) Offensive diarrhea, Psor.
(9) Black stools, Lept. (10) Constipation, Op., Sanie., Plb. (11) Lochia thin, fetid, Nit-ac. (12) Vomits water as
soon as warm in stomach, Phos. Complementary: Ars., Bapt., Bry.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

of chopped lean beef in water, allowed to stand in the sun for two or three weeks. Nosodes. Dilutions.

name: Pyrus Americanus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - pyrus. Pyrus americanus. Mountain ash. N. O. Rosaceae. The British is Pyrus aucuparia.
Swamps and mountain woods from Maine to Pennsylvania. Tincture of fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, irritation, prolapse. Chills. Clairvoyance. Dyspepsia. Gout. Heart, disorders. Hysteria.
Rectum, constriction. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Tongue, paralysis. Uterus, prolapse.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pyrus Americanus, the Mountain Ash, was proved by Gatchell on himself, a married woman
and two boys. Gatchell's only symptom was “irritation of the eyes.” Another prover had a similar symptom.
By far the greatest number were induced in the woman, though hers were largely confirmed by those of the
boys, and included severe neuralgic pains, and rheumatic and gouty symptoms. Labor-like or spasmodic pains
were frequent in uterus, in bladder, like prolapse. Constrictive at base of lungs and around waist, like spasm
of heart.
 Aches in every joint, acute intense pains like inflammatory rheumatism. Pains seem to move in lines. Worse
motion, dreads to move on account of joints. Feels as if full of cold water. Worse cold, sensitive to cold and
air.
MIND - Brain active, intellect clear, thoughts vivid, whole being intensified. Indolent, indifferent, no inclination
to read. Full of gloomy determination. Feels gloomy and discouraged but cannot cry. Sad, weeping mood,
tears will come.
Hypochondriac, not nervous, lazy, would like to lie in bed and be waited on. Feels weak as if about to die,
moans, groans, calls for help. Cries and feels apprehension, fears something terrible going to happen. Seems
to her that fundus of stomach is depressed in abdomen and pyloric end of fire, a red spot like raw beef there
as if stomach burnt up with raw whiskey.
Thinks she is clairvoyant, can read character and understand motions, see into herself. Seems to be able to
go out of herself for a short distance to walk around and return into her body.
Abdomen - Feels constricted around waist, obliged to loosen clothes at once.
Back - Sick feeling under right scapula.
Chest - Feels as if lungs congested, especially at base and constricted.
Eyes - Irritation of eyes. Eyes feel as if they had been crying a long time, smart.
Female - Bearing down and pressing out as if swollen and burning all over. Sense of prolapse of womb.
Food - Craves hot tea. Wants soft food, feels as if meat would not digest.
Head - Headache begins over eyes, pains knife-like, left side of headaches terribly like a toothache. Headache
extends to right side. Head feels as if it would burst. Great weight at vertex. Shooting pains in forehead.
Headache penetrating in temples.
Heart - Oppression about heart as if it had stopped beating, as if going into convulsions. Sense of spasm at
heart, as if blood too thick to circulate (better by Camph.). Heart aches as if from some great sorrow.
Kidneys - Irritation of bladder and urethra. Sensation as if bladder prolapsed.
Limbs - Twinging pains in arms, legs and toes. Drawing, cutting pain. Joints feel constricted and sore. Some
pain in finger joints. Pains drawn, rending along backs of thighs to toes, worse left. Feels as if left leg drawn
up and would never straighten again. Tight feeling of patella. Pain in knees is followed by pain in tendons and
along calves. Knees and toes feel as if immensely swollen and ache. Left great toe feels as if torn from its
socket. Toes burn. Unendurable aching of bones of toes.
Lungs - Can hardly breathe, as if cold water in stomach. Spasmodic breathing as of nervous women. Dry
cough, as if pharynx stuffed with cotton. Hoarseness. Can't talk loudly, voice gone.
Mouth - Tongue partially paralyzed, cannot direct it.
Rectum - Sensation as if rectum were shrunken and dried up.
Sensations - As if she were outside of herself and could see into herself. As if stomach full of cold water,
coldness extends up esophagus under sternum. As if rectum were shrunken and dried up. As if left leg drawn
up and would never straighten again.
Skin - Clammy feeling of skin.
Stomach - Stomach feels weak as if nothing would digest, it feels dry and wrinkled. Feels as if stomach full of
cold water. Thinks mucus accumulated in cold stomach. Feeling of coldness extends up sternum and
esophagus.
Temperature - Chilly when air strikes him. Chilly down back and both legs. Very cold, shivering internally,
thinks she must look blue. Cold creeping all over. Chilly and with a very tranquil feeling, especially of
consciousness. Glow all over, hands sweat.
Throat - Throat feels obstinate.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1) Neuralgic and gouty pains, Prun. (2) Heart, Crat. (3)
Chilliness, Camph.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Quassia Amara
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - quas. Quassia amara. Quassia wood. Picrena excelsa, (Jamaica) and Quassia amara
(Surinam). N. O. Simarubacee. Tincture or cold infusion of the wood. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Ascites. Cataract. Cirrhosis. Dyspepsia. Dysentery. Headaches. Heartburn.
Indigestion. Intermittent fever. Threadworms. Worms.
HERBAL - The Quassia now found in the shops in the form of “Quassia chips” is the wood of Picrena, the
Jamaica Quassia. The name “Quassia” was given by Linneus to Quassia excelsa of Surinam from the name
 of a healer, Quassi or Coissi, who employed its bark as a remedy for fever.
The wood of this tree was formerly employed under the name of Surinam Quassia. The wood is very bitter and
yields its properties best to cold, distilled water. In the old school the infusion is used as a bitter tonic in
dyspepsia, and in enemas for clearing the rectum of threadworms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Quas. acts on digestive organs as a tonic (Gent., Hydr.). Pressure and stitches in liver and
sympathetically in spleen. Pain in right intercostal muscles above the liver. Seems to possess a marked action
on eyes, producing amblyopia and cataract.
Abdomen - Sticking pains between umbilicus and stomach. Abdomen feels empty and retracted. Abdomen
hard and distended.
Back - Sensation of coldness running over back with constant inclination to yawn and stretch out the feet.
Head - Constant dullness of head.
Kidneys - Excessive desire, impossible to retain urine. Secretion of urine increased, solid constituents
diminished. Copious urination day and night. As soon as the child wakes up the bed is drenched.
Limbs - Prostration, with hunger. Inclination to yawn and stretch (Rhus-t.). Sensation of coldness over back.
Cold limbs with sensation of internal coldness (Helo.). Drawing pain in calves.
Liver - Very acute sticking in hepatic region, followed by dull pain. Cirrhosis of liver with ascites.
Neck - Severe drawing pains in cervical muscles.
Rectum - Stools at first hard with great effort, afterwards pasty, once very thin.
Stomach - Dyspepsia after infectious diseases, especially influenza, dysentery. Atonic dyspepsia with flatus
and acidity. Heartburn and gastralgia. Regurgitation of food.
Tongue - Tongue dry or with brown sticky coating.
COMMENTS - There is a short homeopathic proving. J. O. Muller took a single dose of the tincture, Eidherr
four doses of Quas. 30x. Lembke took the extract.
The most peculiar characteristic symptoms were drawing in hypochondria and sensation as if abdomen were
empty and retracted, with sensation as if he would have a stool. Stool at first hard with effort, later pasty.
Sticking in liver and abdomen. Peculiar beating through abdomen, extending into limbs.
Eidherr had “coldness running over back with constant inclination to yawn and desire to stretch out the feet,”
which gives a clue to its action in fevers.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Fevers - Cedr. (2) Worms - Cina.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Quebracho Aspidosperma
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -queb. Quebracho aspidosperma. White quebracho. Aspidosperma quebracho. N. O.
Apocynaceae. Tincture and trituration of the bark. Trituration and solutions of the alkaloid aspidospermine and
its salts. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Cardiac, asthma. Cyanosis. Dyspnea. Emphysema. Fever. Heart, disorders. Paralysis.
Pulmonary stenosis.
HERBAL - Quebracho is a Brazilian herbal remedy from which the alkaloid aspidosper- mine has been
isolated. The alkaloid takes the form of small, very brilliant, white crystals, sparingly soluble in water, readily
soluble in alcohol and ether.
Queb. removes obstruction to the oxidation of the blood by stimulating respiratory centers. Increases oxidation
and excretion of carbonic acid.
HOMEOPATHIC -Shortness of breath during exertion. Dyspnea, respiratory paralysis, slowed heart and
paralysis of limbs. Dyspnea with cyanosis. Dyspnea in tuberculosis and pleurisy. Uremic dyspnea. Asthma,
cardiac asthma. Emphysema. Pulmonary stenosis. Thrombosis of pulmonary artery.
COMMENTS - Dr. Hale reported that Aspin, or Queb. is derived from the Chilean “White Quebracho”
(Aspidospermine Quebracho). At Santiago de Chile, the bark is used as a substitute for chinchona as a
febrifuge. The alkaloid forms salts with citric, hydrochloric and sulphuric acids.
Hale said Queb. produces in animals dyspnea, respiratory paralysis, slowed heart and paralysis of limbs. It
relieves dyspnea in tuberculosis and pleurisy, but without influencing the fever.
The lx relieved asthma with livid face, and dyspnea with cyanosis is frequently relieved by it. Following this
were signs of emphysema and severe attacks of asthma. Rales were heard and “pearls” of rounded gelatinous
masses were expectorated. Aspin. 3x gave more relief than any other remedy.
Hale noted two cases relieved by it, one of mitral incompetence and stenosis with severe nocturnal dyspnea,
the other of fatty heart (Queb. had no influence on the edema, which was removed by Dig.).
Jos. P. Cobb recorded a case of heart affection of some duration in a man, age 24. There was some heart
 enlargement, especially of right side. Much dyspnea and a slight mitral murmur.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale.

name: Quercus Glandium Spiritus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - querc. Quercus glandium spiri- tus. Acom kernels. Aqua glandium quercus. Quercus robur var.
English oak. Quercus pedunculata. Quercus sessilifera. N. O. Corylacee or Cupulifere. Fagaceae. Tincture of
acoms are peeled and crushed or shredded. Water extract of acoms with addition of alcohol for Aqua glandium
quercus. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Breath, offensive. Constipation. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Fistula. Giddiness. Gout.
Intermitting, fever. Leucocythemia, splenica. Liver, disorders. Spleen, disorders. Spleen, dropsy.
HERBAL - Rademacher gave the tincture of acorns to an old brandy drunkard who had long suffered from the
spleen, which was at times very painful and who was at that time “sick unto death” with ascites and dropsy
of the legs. The urine at once increased, but the patient complained that each dose of the medicine caused
constriction of the chest.
This led Rademacher to prepare the Distilled Spirit and finally the Aqua, as milder preparations, which they
proved to be, for the remedy completely cured the patient without causing further constriction of the chest.
In the course of cures of spleen cases Rademacher noticed that not only was the flow of urine increased, there
was also, especially in old spleen engorgements, an eliminative diarrhea with amelioration of the symptoms
generally. A passing diarrhea often appears for a time when using it.
HOMEOPATHIC - Querc. is one of Rademacher's splenic remedies. It was introduced to homeopathic practice
by Burnett, who published a translation of Rademacher's account of the remedy.
Chronic spleen disorders and spleen dropsy. Dropsy and liver disorders. Useful in gout, old malarial cases
with flatulence. Flushed state. Vertigo, deafness with noises in head. Exceedingly nervous.
Antidotes effects of alcohol. Desire for alcoholic drinks. Burnett does not find Querc. a remedy for the liquor
habit, it stops short at that, but it diminishes the craving and antidotes the alcoholic state.
Clarke noted that Querc. acts well in trituration of the Acorn 3x in splenic cases, flatulence, old malaria and
alcoholic history. Missionaries who used Querc. on Burnett's indications in spleen disorders found it no less
effective in the intermittent fevers which gave rise to the enlarged spleens.
Powdered oak bark is an excellent dry dressing for ulcers and discharging wounds.
MIND - Nervous, depressed, glum, taciturn. Easily moved to tears, not quite capable of stating his own case.
Abdomen - Pain in spleen region. Pain in hypochondria, worse left, much worse by stooping. Ascites.
Chest - Constriction of chest in précordia. Ears - Deafness and noises in the head. Eyes - Eyes yellow, puffy
underneath. Face - Flushed.
Head - Peculiar sensation in head, feel as when drunk, sensation lasts a minute or two. Gouty eczema of
scalp, poll and backs of hands.
Heart - Fluttering, irregular heart. Kidneys - Increased flow of urine. Limbs - Gouty eczema of backs of hands.
Hands tremble. Dropsy tottering gait. Varicose veins.
Liver - Enlarged liver and spleen.
Mouth - Foul breath, stercoraceous. Tongue foul.
Rectum - Diarrhea. “It keeps his bowels open. ” Fistula in alcoholics.
Stomach - Gnawing at pit of stomach. Flatulent dyspepsia. Removes craving for alcohol.
Vertigo - Wheeling vertigo. Vertigo with disorders of spleen and left side. Afraid to move for fear having a
stroke or giddiness would come on.
COMMENTS - Burnett noted the symptom “Certain few people feel, as soon as they have taken it, a peculiar
sensation in the head, lasting barely a minute or two, which they say is like being drunk.” This led him to use
it in the treatment of alcoholism and its effects, which he elaborated in his Gout and its Cure.
The first case Burnett noted was that of a military man, 64, broken down with gout and alcoholism and pretty
severe chronic bronchitis. Heart irregular. Liver and spleen enlarged. Complained bitterly of gnawing at pit of
stomach. Gait tottering, hands quivered.
He had lost his wife and had to keep himself up with nips of spirits, for which he had a constant craving. Querc.,
ten drops in water, three times a day, completely revolutionized his state and took away his abnormal craving
for spirits.
In a merchant of 57, given to nips of sherry, Querc. threw out a gouty eczema on scalp, poll and backs of
hands, which took three months to cure after which Querc. was again given and completed the cure.
An officer who drank too much had foul breath, eyes yellow, puffy underneath. Querc. cured.
A hunting man, 40, free liver, gouty, had varicose veins of legs originating apparently in enlarged spleen, left
 by typhoid fever. Querc. cured. The patient said it kept his “bowels very regular.”
A country squire, 60, bachelor, appeared in a hopeless condition. Was unable to state his own case. Flushed,
much pain over the eyes and in both rib regions. Stooping caused great pain, worse left hypochondrium. Liver
and spleen much enlarged. Nervous, depressed, glum, taciturn, easily moved to tears. Could not walk without
support on account of his great giddiness.
Breath in highest degree disgustingly stercoraceous, nearly caused Burnett to vomit when examining him. That
smell of breath, said Burnett is an unmistakable sign of the chronic tippler indicating undigested alcohol. Burnett
subsequently ascertained that he was quite a sober man, but took frequent nips, particularly when confined to
the house by wet weather.
The pain in left side, giddiness, and flushed state indicated Querc., which was given. In a week the breath was
normal, giddiness a little better, tenderness of rib region much diminished. In six weeks he was quite well.
Clarke, noting that giddiness with spleen trouble is met by it, gave Querc. to a young woman for extreme
whirling vertigo, an affect of influenza. The patient was greatly relieved when she took it in a severe attack, but
if she took it when the giddiness was only slight it caused severe aggravation.
Patients to whom Cooper gave Querc. complained that they “felt as if in a vice, dared not move for fear of
having a stroke or an attack of giddiness.” “Deafness with noises in the head” is another effect observed by
Cooper.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ange., Nux-v. (2) Lach., Nat-m. (3) Helia., Cean. - spleen enlarged and painful.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Quillaya Saponaria
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - quill. Quillaya saponaria. Chile soap bark tree. N. O. Rosaceae. Soap bark contains saponine.
Tincture of the dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Catarrh. Colds. Coryza. Coughs. Lung, disorders. Sneezing. Sore, throats.
HOMEOPATHIC - Quill, is most effective in the beginning of colds, coryza, often checking its further
development. Colds with sore throat, heat and dryness of throat. Acute catarrh, sneezing and sore throat.
Coughs with difficult expectoration. Squamous skin.
COMMENTS - Quill, is used herbally to loosen cough in chronic bronchitis and pulmonary complaints. The
infusion of 1/2 oz of bark in 1 pint of boiling water is taken in tablespoonful doses or more as required. It is also
used externally as a cleansing application to cutaneous ulcers and eruptions.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali-hp., Gels., All-c., Squil. (2) Sapo. - sore throat involuntary urination. Seneg.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Murphy.

name: Radium Bromatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rad-br. Radium bromatum. Radium bromide. Triturations. Radium brom. of 1,800,000radio-
activity was employed (At. Wt. 226). Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Albuminuria. Appendicitis. Arteritis. Arthritis. Atheroma. Backaches. Bones, disorders.
Burns. Callosities. Cancer. Carbuncle, urethra. Corns. Dermatitis. Diarrhea. Duodenal, ulcer. Eczema.
Epithelioma. Erythema. Eyes, disorders. Gout. Hemorrhage. Headaches. Itching. Leucocytosis. Lumbago.
Lupus. Menopausal, flushes. Moles. Nephritis. Neuralgia. Neurasthenia. Nevus. Nose, disorders. Nosebleeds.
Ophthalmia. Phimosis. Prurigo. Pruritus, anus. Pruritus, vulvae. Psoriasis. Radiation, burns. Radiation,
ulcers. Rheumatism. Rodent ulcer. Sclerotitis. Skin disorders. Tic douloureux. Trachoma. Ulcers. Warts. X-
ray dermatitis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pure radium is a white metal which “oxidizes in water, bums paper, turns black on exposure
to air and has the property of adhering firmly to iron.” This last quality is not without significance and shows a
close affinity with fenrum. It is found in ore pitchblende.
The discovery of radium and its properties in 1898 by Pierre and Marie Curie set many persons thinking and
among them, naturally, those who are engaged in the healing of the sick. Curie himself made the first “proving.”
He put a tiny bit of radium salt in an India rubber capsule and fastened it to his arm, leaving it there for ten
hours. When he took it off the skin was red, the place turned into a wound, which took four months to heal,
leaving a white scar the size of a shilling surrounded by discolored, puckered skin.
On another occasion he left it for half an hour. A wound appeared at the end of a fortnight and took another
fortnight to heal. On a third occasion, it was left for eight minutes only, two months later the skin became red
and a bit sore, but it soon passed off.
Skin and nerves are affected. Acne rosacea, nevi, moles. Cancer. Lymphoid tissue. Ulcers due to radium
 burns, that take a long time to heal. Effects of x-ray burns. Effective for rheumatism and gout. Chronic
rheumatic arthritis.
Severe aching pains all over with restlessness, better moving about. Nerves are affected causing suddenly
shifting or electric pains, must lie down. Electric shocks through the body during sleep.
Dull, hard aching pains all over, deep in joints, very restless. Numbness, worse stretching the part. Dry burning
heat, as if on fire, through the entire body, craves cool air.
Constriction of the chest, heart etc., with air hunger. Lowered blood pressure. Necrotic changes. Marked
increase in the white bloodcells. Lateness in appearance of symptoms. Weakness, lassitude, tiredness. Great
weakness.
MIND - Apprehensive, depressed. Tired and irritable. Cross. Easily vexed. Torpid, apathetic. Great desire to
be with people, wants to have someone near. Fear of being alone, of the dark.
Abdomen - Alternating with chest or ear symptoms. Pain over McBurney’s point and at location of sigmoid
flexure. Colic better bending double and passing stools. Pain, violentcramps, rumbling, full of gas. Much
flatulence.
Back - Aching in back of neck. Pain and lameness in cervical vertebrae, worse dropping head forward, better
standing or sitting erect. Weakness between scapulae. Backache between shoulders and lumbar- sacral
region, better after walking. Lumbar and sacral aches, pain appears to be in bone, continued motion relieves,
better hot bath, worse going upstairs.
Breasts - Right breast sore, better hard rubbing.
Causations - Ill effects of x-ray, radiation burns.
Chest - Tightness of chest. Chest pain alternating with indigestion and stuffed up feeling.
Ears - Sound of rushing water, better lying on face.
Eyes - Red, smarting, worse reading. Sensation as if pieces of cotton in eyes, better rubbing.
Face - Flushed. Acne rosacea. Aching pain in angle of right lower jaw. Violent trifacial neuralgia.
Female - Itching genitals, pruritus vul- vae. Aching over pubes during menses. Delayed and irregular
menstruation and backache. Menses last one day, then bloody leucorrhea. Leucorrhea, white and scanty,
curdy and cheesy. Uterine hemorrhage (Ip.). Lochia putrid, scanty or suppressed.
Food - Nausea, better eating. Usual food not relished, sour things taste good. Craves pork. Aversion to sweets,
ice creams, of which she is usually very fond.
Head - Both eyes ache. Severe pain over right eye, spreading back to occiput and to vertex, better in open air.
Occipital and vertex pain, accompanying severe lumbar aching. Frontal headache. Head feels heavy. Aching
pain of right lower jaw. Violent trifacial neuralgia.
Heart - Constriction. Wakes with palpitations. Pulse, rapid, irregular, fluttering. Low blood pressure.
Kidneys - Nephritis with rheumatism. Kidney irritation, albuminuria, granular and hyaline casts. Increased
elimination of sediment. Bedwetting.
Limbs - Arthritis, aching pains, worse at night. Deep pain in joints, knees and ankles. Muscles of legs and
hips sore. Pain in toes, calves, hip joint, popliteal spaces. Legs, arms and neck feel hard and brittle, as though
they would break on moving. Cracking in shoulder. Sharp pains in shoulders, arms, hands and fingers. Arms
feel heavy. Rheumatism of the hands. Dermatitis of the fingers. Trophic changes in the fingernails.
Lungs - Tightness of chest, feels as if she could not get enough air. Spasmodic cough. Persistent cough from
tickling in throat pit. Cough, worse lying, smoking, better eating and open air, sitting up, exercise.
Male - Eczema of penis and inner surface of thighs. Itching. Dysuria, then erection.
Modalities - Better lying down, after sleep. Better continued motion, pressure, hot bath, open air. Better eating,
cold drinks. Worse from smoking, shaving, washing. Worse getting up, warmth of the bed. Worse at night,
noon, 3 a.m., 4 a.m., 7 a.m., and 11 a.m.
Mouth - Dry mouth. Breath seems hot. Metallic taste. Prickling sensation on end of tongue.
Nose - Burning in nose. Itching and dryness of nasal cavities, better in open air.
Rectum - Alternating constipation and loose movements. Stools, soft, dark or offensive, slate colored. Rectum
sore, prolapsed. Itching of anus and hemorrhoids.
Sensations - As if skull too small, as if foreign body in eye, as if something dropped into trachea. Knees feel
as if the bones would protrude. Intolerance of tobacco can be produced.
Skin - Itching all over body, burning of skin, as if on fire. Irritable, thick, moist if scratched, worse face and
genitals. Erythema and dermatitis with itching, burning, swelling and redness. Eczema. Psoriasis. Small
pimples. Branny scabs. Scabby on ears. Scleroderma. Callosities. Cancer. Necrosis and ulceration. Epi-
thelioma.
Sleep - Restless. Sleepiness with lethargy. Wakes panting with palpitations. Dreams vivid, busy, of fire, which
seems true.
 Stomach - Empty feeling in stomach. Warm sensation in stomach. Nausea and sinking sensation, belching of
gas.
Temperature - Cold sensation internally, with chattering of teeth. Internal chilliness followed by heat of the
skin, associated with bowel movements and flatulence.
Throat - Dry, sore, raw with earache. Feeling in throat as from eating pepper.
Vertigo - Vertigo with pain in back of head, left when in bed.
COMMENTS - After investigating radium for ten years, Dieffenbach reported that when the provings
commenced, one prover’s hands had eczematous eruptions, cracks, scaly excrescences and wart-like growths
as a result of X-ray and radium-ray experiments. These gradually disappeared after his proving with 6x.
This is confirmed by a case reported by Mr. E. S. Pierrepont. A girl employed in the X-ray department of the
hospital with which he was connected developed dermatitis of the right hand and fingers. An ointment was
prescribed without benefit, and cracks appeared on the skin. Two doses of Rad- br. 30c were given, on Mr.
Pierrepont’s suggestion, one in the morning and one in the evening.
The following day the patient came out in a rash, which the matron mistook for measles. Her eyes watered,
fingers very sore and she felt very ill. By the following day, the rash had disappeared and she felt well. The
fingers were now better and they got quite well, except that a sore feeling was left after washing.
A feature of Dieffenbach’s proving was the disappearance of small nevi, which is significant as the rays are
used for the destruction of nevi.
Useful for indolent and phagedenic ulcers. Sores that refuse to heal. Skin cancers, especially cancerous ulcers.
Severe psoriasis. There is some history of moles and birthmarks disappearing.
Dermatitis and eczema after radiation exposure. Radium burns. Ulcers due to radiation treatment (Fl-ac.). After
affects of radiation exposure, weakness, tendency to infections, where nothing else seems to work (Stront.).
Rad-br has been used in cases of lupus, epithelioma, carcinoma of the cervix uterus and urethral caruncle.
There are numerous cases of skin cancers cured with Rad-br. in potencies.
T. Simpson recorded one such case. A retired officer had an intractable eruption on his genitals and the inner
surface of thighs and legs that had prevented him from getting any refreshing sleep for three years. One tablet
of Rad-br. 30c each morning was prescribed for a month. All conditions were vastly improved and the patient
got well without further medication.
Clarke reported the case of a young, unmarried woman who, after the application of a belladonna plaster to
the back for lumbago, developed an edematous rash involving the whole face and neck. It was extremely
irritating, worse at night, preventing sleep.
At the back of the neck was a sore, oozing patch. After temporary relief from some remedies, there still
remained an irritating, oozing rash, sore eyes, first right, then left, lids swollen, oozing from corners, lips hard,
swollen.
One dose of Rad-br. 30c was given. The result was dramatic. The first night she was able to sleep, waking
only once. Two days later, the rash had nearly gone and the eyes had ceased to water. In a few days all had
vanished and the patient could enjoy open air.
Dr. S. L. Guild-Leggett recorded the case of a girl, 2.5 years, who had shifting rheumatism from her left foot to
right knee, then to left knee, hands and toes. She had also a peculiarity about her stools, they were slate-
colored, very offensive, urgent and came at noon during a meal.
Guild-Leggett used symptoms from Dieffenbach’s proving: “defecation at noon, stool soft, dark or offensive,
slate-color, clay-color, pains in limbs, wakes 4 a.m., pains in all joints knees, ankles, feet, could not walk, had
to lie down.” Rad-br. was given and cured entirely.
RELATIONS-Antidotes: Rhus-v., Tell. Compare: ( 1 ) Anae. - the ulceration produced by it is like radium. It
may appear elsewhere than on place of contact and appear late. (2) X-ray, Rhus-t., Sep., Uran-n., Ars., Puls.,
Caust.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Radon
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rado. Radon. Radioactive gas. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Adenocarcinoma. Emphysema. Lung cancer. Lung, disorders. Pneumonia, interstitial.
Pulmonary fibrosis. Respiratory lesions. Silicosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Radon is a toxic radioactive gas, formed by the natural radioactive decay of uranium in
rock, soil, and water. It is colorless, odorless, tasteless, and chemically inert.
Radon gas decays into radioactive particles that can get trapped in the lungs when breathed in. The primary
adverse health effect associated with chronic exposure to radon is lung cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma.
 Small cell carcinoma. Large cell carcinoma. Adenocarcinoma.
Other harmful respiratory effects associated with chronic exposure to radon include emphysema, pulmonary
fibrosis, respiratory lesions. Chronic interstitial pneumonia. Silicosis.
COMMENTS - Uranium changes to different elements as it decays down to its final element of lead. All of the
elements it changes into are solids except one, radon, which floats freely in the soil and is easily drawn into
the lower level of homes by the natural flow of air.
Radon’s primary hazard is caused from inhalation of the gas and its highly radioactive heavy metallic decay
products (polonium, lead, and bismuth) which tend to collect on dust in the air.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Rajania Subsamarata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - raja-s. Rajania subsamarata. Amphypterygium adstringes. N. O. Anacar- diaceae or
Dioscoreaceae family. Tincture from the triturated and macerated bark in 80% alcohol. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Anthrax. Bacillary, dysentery. Blepharitis. Boils. Colitis. Diphtheria. Encephalitis.
Fevers. Mastoiditis. Measles. Meningitis. Myelitis. Typhoid. Vaccination, reactions.
HERBAL - Rajania subsamarata is a shrub 1.50m high, which grows in the Michoacan in the warm territories
of Morelos and Guerrero. It has dioecious leaves, a trilocular herbaceous stem and the limb is cut near the
top. It has six fibrous stamens, an ovary linked to the perigon tube with two to three seeds in the receptacle.
HOMEOPATHIC - De Legarreta proved the remedy, reporting symptoms of high fevers, general exhaustion.
Stares, stunned, closes eyes as if to think more easily. Jaw hangs, muscles relaxed, slips into bed. No longer
has the strength to speak.
Swelling of the neck and parotid region. Measles, diphtheria or whooping-cough. Epidemic spinal and cerebral
meningitis. Acute post infectious encephalitis in the child. Post-vaccination encephalitis.
Circumscribed inflammation of the skin with swelling or ulceration. Congestion of the nerves and blood vessels.
The diarrhea is muco-purulent and blood-streaked. Metrorrhagia of black, putrid blood.
MIND - Indifferent towards everything around him, bewildered. Loss of sense of identity. Mumbles in his
delirium, weeps and sighs and speaks incoherently. Sings bawdy or religious songs. Fits of exaltation, fury
and lasciviousness.
Abdomen - Hypogastric region painful, especially when speaking. Abdomen retracted into a boat shape.
Rumbling and abdominal wind. Gurgling in the right iliac cavity and pain at McBurney’s point. Cholera-like
enteritis. Enteritis. Ileitis. Bacillary dysentery. Hemorrhaging recto-colitis.
Ears - Mastoiditis. Catarrhal discharge. Suppurating inflammation of the eardrum. Sensitive to sharp sounds.
Buzzing. Sensation of blocked ear, as if full of earth. Sounds seem far off like distantrain. Later total deafness.
Eyes - Eyes bloodshot. Eyes bright at first, then lusterless, as if covered with a film of gum or tears, which are
burning and corrosive. The pupil is contracted and insensitive to light. Conjunctivitis. Eyelids are heavy,
eyelashes stuck together. Blepharitis.
Face - Face dull, serious at first, then aspect becomes hippocratic, cadaverous. Earthy, dirty, moist.
Female - Menses ameliorate the general condition. Menses with evil-smelling blood, black and irritating.
Menses with a bitter odor. Metritis. Profuse, sticky leucorrhea, causing vaginal insensitivity. Labia majora
excoriated. Puerperal fever. Venereal granuloma. Ulcerous vulvar elephantiasis.
Head - Acute headache, like a nail being driven into the head. Pain in the head persisting for a long time,
accompanied by anguished lamentation.
Heart - Fall in arterial tension. Sub-acute myocarditis. Pericarditis. Palpitations and diffuse pains in the
precordial region. Pulse thready, weak. Heartbeat irregular, moderate tachycardia. Hears the heart heat when
lying down, as if the heart were on the pillow.
Limbs - Limbs trembling and slack with convulsions. Limbs are cold, purple. Continual involuntary movements
of the hands, as if seizing particles in the air.
Lungs - Chest swollen, panting and anguish. Respiration weak, becoming imperceptible. Pulmonary
gangrene. Pulmonary abscess. Breath fetid.
Male - Soft canker. Ulcers. Epithelioma of the glans. Penis limp, scrotum slack. Fetid sweating, smelling of
rancid cheese.
Modalities - Better from coolness, discharges. Worse from moving, speaking.
Mouth - Breath fetid, putrid, repulsive. Sticky saliva, nicotine-colored like that of a tobacco chewer. Aphthae
and ulcerations which bleed at times, on the tip of the tongue. Tongue fissured with black stripe injhe middle
and red, excoriated edges. Teeth tarnished with yellow, then brown, deposit, despite frequent brushing. Lips
swollen. Mouth open, lowerjaw dropping.
 Slight trismus at times.
Nose - Rhinitis. Sinusitis. Ozaena. Nose dry. Hairs inside the nose bristling, as if dusty. Attacks of nosebleed,
which ameliorate. If abundant, they are exhausting.
Rectum - Constipation for the first few days, then diarrhea. Diarrhea, mucopurulent, blood-streaked, loosely
bound, very fetid.
Skin - Skin rough, sticky sweat. Earthy appearance with petechiae on the chest, abdomen and on the inside
of the arms. Erysipelas. Pimples, boils, suppurating abscesses. Bedsores. Varicose ulcers. Painful, purulent
anthrax. Soft canker with fetid, blood-streaked discharge. Gangrenous patches. Septic gangrene. Cancerous
tumors and ulcerations with blue-black edges, painful and bleeding.
Stomach - Paresis of the esophagus with difficulty in swallowing. Hiccoughs, nausea, vomiting.
Temperature - Fever high, general exhaustion. Temperature between 39.5°C and 41 °C.
Throat - Throat dry with need for liquid in order to swallow. Cold foods go down better than warm foods.
External swelling of the throat and parotid region.
COMMENTS - Rajania has been used in compress form for ulcerations, diluted in water with 1% or 2% of the
mother tincture.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Mur-ac. - Adynamic conditions, prostration, hyperthermia, deep, bleeding
ulcerations. The patient is so exhausted that he falls into bed. (2) Lach. - Acute infections, adynamic condition
with tendency to hemorrhage and decomposition of the blood. Loquacity, burning pains, cannot bear anything
tight, cardiac failure, ameliorated by drainage, spontaneous ecchymosis. (3) Anthr. - Septic infections, burning
pains, extreme prostration. (4) Bapt., Hyos., Bell., Stram. and Crot-h.
REFERENCES-Julian.

name: Ranunculus Acris
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ran-a. Ranunculus acris. Goldcup. Crowfoot. Ranunculus acer. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture
of whole plant. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Erysipelas. Fever. Gangrene. Lumbago. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. Ulcers.
HERBAL - Ran-a. is distinguished from Ran- b. by its slender cylindrical flower-stalk, that of Ran-b. being
furrowed. Both are common buttercups, and have acrid and poisonous properties.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-a. was proved by Franz and Lembke. The chief skin symptoms were observed in a
woman of seventy who applied a handful of the herb to her limbs with the result of setting up violent
constitutional symptoms, fever and intense inflammation, going on to gangrene of the skin of the legs.
Rheumatic pain in the muscles and joints, especially ankles and wrists. Pains when walking and at rest. Lumbar
pains, worse on bending or turning the body. Heat, faintness and fever.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ran-b.
REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Ranunculus Bulbosus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ran-b. Ranunculus bulbosus. Buttercup. Bulbous crowfoot. North America. N. O. Ranunculacee.
Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Adhesions. Alcoholism. Breast, pain. Cachexia. Chest, pains. Chilblains. Corns. Delirium
tremens. Depression. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dyspnea. Eczema. Epilepsy. Feet, pains. Gastralgia. Hangovers.
Hay fever. Herpes zoster. Hiccoughs. Hydrocele. Hydrothorax. Intercostal, pain. Jaundice. Liver,
pain.Neuralgias. Nyctalopia. Ovaries, neuralgia. Pemphigus. Pleurodynia. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Spinal,
irritation. Warts. Writer’s cramp.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-b. was proved by Franz and some effects of its external application have been
observed and results of inhaling the fumes while preparing the plant or when it has been burned. The last
caused headache and in one instance epilepsy, followed by cachexia, gout, headache and death.
One prover, who expressed the juice with the fingers, reported a long-lasting and recurrent eruption of vesicles
on the fingers, with blue vesicles and horny scabs.
“Small, deep, transparent, dark blue little elevated blisters of the size of an ordinary pin ’ s head. Crowded
together in oval-shaped groups of the size of a coin with intolerable burning itching, emitting when opened a
dark yellow lymph afterwards becoming covered with a herpetic, horny scurf.”
Symptoms rising from the acrid vapor while the juice of the plant was being prepared included “Smarting from
eyes as from smoke in evening. Smarting in eyes, nose and fauces, the eyes run and are very painful. He has
to stop using them for half an hour because he cannot see anything, whites slightly inflamed, mucus runs in
 torrents from nose.”
Ran-b. is a painful remedy, affecting nerves, muscles, eyes, serous membranes, chest, skin, fingers toes and
left side. Its most characteristic effects are upon the chest walls like pleurodynia. Hydrothorax. Fauces painful
as if sore during an inspiration, less during deglutition. Hay fever.
Pains are stitching, stabbing, shooting, extort tears with shuddering, cannot rest in any position. Burning, biting,
bruised soreness or as of deep ulceration. Sore, spots. Burning in small spots from sedentary living. Neuralgia.
Herpes.
Bad effects of alcohol, including hiccough, epileptiform attacks, and delirium tremens. Spasmodic hiccough.
Epilepsy of alcoholics. Weak and tottering patients, from the prolonged use of whisky, brandy or other alcoholic
stimulants.
Sudden weakness and fainting. Trembling from anger. Distended feeling. Shocks throughout the whole body.
Sensitive to air and touch. As of a cold wet cloth, especially on chest, worse on going into cold air.
Caustic and pain producing properties. Ran-b. forms a constituent of some arsenical plasters used to disperse
cancers.
M. Jousset noted it for chronic sciatica, he applied the tincture to the heel of affected leg.
MIND-Quarrelsome, angry mood. Irritability, with pains. Anxious. Worse thinking of complaints. Restlessness
at night. Obtuse intellect. Vanishing of thoughts on reflection. Stares at one point. Cowardice. Weeping in
evening. Depression of spirit and desire to die.
Great fear of ghosts in evening, dares not be alone. Ailments from fright, vexation or anger. Delirium tremens,
with hiccough. Delirium tremens, with talkative mania, unusual exertions and powerful efforts to escape from
bed. Bad mental effects of alcohol.
Abdomen - Hypochondria bruised. Tenderness of abdomen to pressure. Pinching colic, alternating with
chest pains.
Back - Muscular pain along lower margin of the shoulder blade. Pain extending through lowerhalfof left
chest. Burning in small spots from needlework, type writing, piano playing. Scapula adherent. Muscles of neck
rigidly contracted, can speak only by moving shoulders up and down.
Causations - Bad effects of alcohol injury, fright, vexation. Cold air brings on all sorts of ailments.
Chest - Various kinds of pains and soreness, as if bruised in sternum, ribs intercostal spaces and both
hypochondria. Intercostal rheumatism. Rheumatic pain in chest. Sharp, cutting, stitching in chest, bilateral.
Stitches in chest, worse when inspiring, moving. Small sore spot as from subcutaneous ulceration in chest.
Herpes zoster. Pleurodynia. Pleurisy, adhesions after intercostal neuralgia. Chilliness in chest when
walking in open air.
Ears - Shootings in ears, especially in evening. Cramp-like sensation in and on ears.
Eyes - Herpes vesicles on cornea with intense pain, photophobia and lachrymation. Eyeballs sore on moving
them. Hemiopia during pregnancy. Day-blindness, mist before eyes, pressure and smarting in eyes,
as from smoke. Night-blindness. Lids burn. Pain over right eye, better standing and walking.
Female - Acrid and gnawing leucorrhea. Ovarian neuralgia always excited by atmospheric changes.
Food - Thirst augmented in afternoon. Feeling of hunger and rumbling in stomach early in morning. Butter
tastes too sweet. Bitter, empyreumatic taste while eating or after having eaten dry food.
Head - Irritable with pains in forehead and eyeballs. Aching in forehead and vertex as if pressed asunder with
nausea and sleepiness. Pressing pain in forehead from within outward. As if too large and distended. Creeping
sensation in scalp.
Limbs - Crawling and tingling in fingers. Itching palms. Sudden jerking, stitching pain in forearm (right) while
writing. Pain in heels as if pinched by boots.
Liver - laundice with itching of body, especially palms.
Lungs - Anxious, oppressed breathing with desire to draw deep breath. Dyspnea from anger.
Modalities - Better from standing, sitting bent forward. Worse from open air, drafts, change of temperature,
atmospheric changes. Worse damp, cold, rainy and stormy weather. Worse from change of position, motion
of arms, standing, breathing, touch. Worse evening and morning. Worse after eating, alcohol. Worse from
fright, vexation, anger.
Mouth - Increased saliva. Butter tastes too sweet. Crawling on palate, wants to scratch it. Cramp, spasms of
lips.
Nose - Crawling and tingling in nostrils^ in posterior sinuses. Tries to relieve it by hawking and blowing the
nose.
Sensations - Confusion of head as if intoxicated. As if head would be enlarged. As if head pressed asunder.
Hypochondria in lowest ribs painful as if bruised. Burning in left side of chest in region of short ribs. As if a full
breath could not be drawn. As of a knife thrust through side and into back. As if something tearing in chest. As
 if cold wet cloths applied.
Skin - Herpetic eruptions with great itching. Vesicular and pustular eruptions. Shingles, bluish vesicles.
Burning and intense itching, worse contact. Flat, burning, stinging ulcers. Pemphigus. Blister-like eruption
in palms, itching. Fingertips and palms chapped. Horny scabs. Hard excrescences. Corns, smart or burn worse
touch.
Stomach - Pains in stomach. Pressure on scrobiculus. Frequent risings. Nausea in afternoon or evening,
sometimes with headache. Spasmodic hiccoughs of alcoholics.
Temperature - Chilliness, worse open air. Shivering in evening with heat in face. Heat in head with coldness
in hands.
Throat - Inflammatory burning pains. Scraping, burning down the throat. Accumulation of much tough mucus
in throat. Spasmodic sensation of something which ascends esophagus and passes into throat.
COMMENTS - Pains in nerves, serous membranes, muscles, tendons, joints, eyes and internal organs. The
pains are lancinating, pressing and outpressing, jerking and sticking, as if bruised with external sensitiveness.
Pains are sharp, stitching, shooting, come in paroxysms.
Pains are induced by atmospheric changes, sudden exposure to cold or heat, worse in wet, stormy weather,
from touch, motion or turning the body. General sensitiveness to cold air and change. “Worse during
inspiration.” Sensitiveness to touch with a sore, bruised sensation, soreness of parts affected.
Pains particularly in the chest. Muscular pains about the margins of shoulder blades in women of sedentary
employment. H. C. Allen noted burning pains in small spots from close work.
“Jerks and shocks and sudden tearings in right forearm and between thumb and index finger while writing.”
Writer’s cramp and professional neuroses. “Pressure and smarting in eyeballs.” Day-or night-blindness.
Herpes. Spinal neuralgia.
White-coated tongue. Bitter, sour or sweetish taste with accumulation of saliva.
Scraping, burning in throat. Spasmodic hiccough, spasmodic feeling in esophagus and pharynx, ascending.
Painful indigestion. Belchings, nausea.
Pressure on sternum with labored breathing. Violent burning in cardiac end of stomach, hunger early in
morning, thirst in evening. Pains in liver and spleen region, worse by touch. In pleurisy, pleurodynia intercostal
neuralgia.
Hering mentioned “hemeralopia” as having been cured with Ran-b. in a woman during pregnancy and in her
three-year old son. The word “hemeralopia” has been used to denote both day-blindness and nightblindness.
Hering used it in the latter (rarer) sense, for he says of the woman, she “can see well during the day.”
The concomitant symptoms were “heat, biting and pressure in eyes, redness of conjunctiva and lids, especially
inner surface of lower lids, lachrymation, pus in canthi, pustules on eyes. Eyes look weak, pupils dilated,
candlelight appears as a bright circle, can see well during day.”
In a child who was cured of ague with subsequent dropsy and hydrocele by applying Ran-b. to the wrist, ulcers
of the fingers penetrating down to the flexor tendons were produced.
The “cold-water feeling” occurred in a patient of Burnett’s. A woman, 30, had a fall two years before Burnett
saw her and ever since had the peculiar sensation that whenever she goes out of doors she feels as if wet
cloths were applied to three different parts of the anterior walls of thorax-both infra-clavicular fossae and under
left breast. Never felt indoors, but constant as long as she is out.
Guided by this symptom, “Unusual chilliness of outer parts of chest when walking in open air, with the worse
in open air and worse walking in open air,” Burnett gave Ran-b. In two days, the patient was better; in three
weeks, the sensation had completely gone and the general health very much improved.
Dudgeon reported the case of a woman, 27, who went for a drive three weeks after confinement.
The day was cold and an accident occurred to the carriage which frightened her.
In the evening she had a slight rigor and complained of pain in her left side about sixth and seventh ribs. Worse
slightest movement, better sitting rather bent forward and leaning a little to the left. Pulse 120, no heat of skin.
No signs of lung or pleural involvement.
Bry., and later Arn., gave no relief and for two days the symptoms grew worse. The patient had to be propped
up with pillows, leaning forward and to the left. Her head rested on her breast, not daring to breathe at all
deeply.
Ran-b. 1c relieved her in ten minutes, when she “felt a wrench in her side and the pain was gone.” She was
able to lie down, slept all night and made a rapid recovery. There were some slight returns of pain, now on one
side, now on the other. But Ran-b. soon removed them.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bry., Camph., Puls., Rhus-v. Compare: (1) Rad-a. - pain in lumbar muscles and
joints by bending and turning body. (2) Rad-g. (3) Rad-r. - crawling sensation in forehead and scalp in evening
in bed. (4) Rad-fl. (5) Bry., Crot-t., Mez., Euph. Incompatible: Sulph., Staph., Nit-s-d., alcohol, wine, vinegar.
 REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Ranunculus Ficaria
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ran-fi. Ranunculus ficaria. Lesser celandine. Pilewort. Ficaria ranunculoi- des. Ficaria venia.
Scrophularia minor. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Hemorrhoids.
HERBAL -The “lessercelandine” is not botanically related to the true celandine, Chelidonium majus, or to the
Figwort tribe (Scrophularia) although it is named Scrophularia minor in old books.
Ran-fi. is in all respects a true crowfoot except that it has three deciduous instead of five persistent sepals and
nine petals instead of five. Gerarde noted that “It growth in meadows, by ditches and trenches and it is common
everywhere in moist and dark places.
It comes forth about the Calends of March and flower a little after: it beginneth to fade away in April, it is quite
gone in May afterwards it is hard to be found, yea scarcely the root.”
Gerarde wrote that the idea of its use in hemorrhoids was derived from the cluster of small tubers growing
around the crown of the root, which bear a striking resemblance to a bunch of hemorrhoids.
REFERENCES Clarke.

early morning headache, better by rising. General copious night-sweat, especially abundant on thighs.

name: Ranunculus Repens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ran-r. Ranunculus repens. Creeping buttercup. N. O. Ranunculacee. Tincture of whole plant.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Back, pulsation. Coma. Eyes, disorders. Feet, weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-r. has furrowed flower-stalks like Ran-b., but it has a spreading calyx and creeping
scions.
Franz reported a number of symptoms experienced from preparing the juice of this plant, including
phantasmagoria.
Jahr quoted an account of the effects of eating Ran-r. observed in a flock of sheep. Several fell down as if
struck by lightning, eyes rolled, breathing hurried. Some reeled and died with heads bent towards left groin.
Great weakness in feet remained behind. Sleep, short butrefreshing. Mucus membranes of eyes injected,
mouth dry. Abdomen slightly distended, ruminations ceased. Bleeding worse. Some raised themselves, reeled,
fell down again, bleated piteously, most were in profound coma. Ether in milk gave much relief.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
 ***RANUNCULUS SCELERATUS
(Marsh Buttercup)
PHARMACY - ran-s. Ranunculus sceleratus. Marsh buttercup. Marsh crowfoot. Celery- leafed crowfoot. N. O.
Ranunculacee. Europe, North Asia and North America. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: All
potencies..
CLINICAL - Aneurysm. Anus, itching. Blisters. Chest, sternum, pain behind. Coms. Coryza. Diphtheria.
Earache. Glossitis. Gout. Hemorrhoids. Herpes, zoster. Liver, pain. Neuralgia. Nose, ulceration. Pemphigus.
Quinsy. Sternum, pains. Stomatitis. Toes disorders. Tongue, peeling, mapped. Varicose veins.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ran-s. has the most acridity of all the Ranunculi, causing burning in mouth, throat, stomach,
chest, urethra and other parts. It causes blisters on the skin which leave a raw surface with acrid discharge.
The effects of Ran-s., which German shepherds call “cold fire,” on horned cattle is loss of appetite, trembling
and shivering, and distention of abdominal veins. A dog poisoned with it became anxious, howled, tossed
about, bent double, and was very restless at night.
Affinities for the chest, skin, vertex and right side. Rawness, burning, smarting, gnawing or boring pains.
Overall sore feeling. Convulsive twitchings. Periodical complaints. Shortness of breath. Fainting with pain in
stomach.
Burning in the mouth, throat, stomach, chest, urethra. Sensation as of a plug. Characteristic “mapped or
peeled tongue,” with smarting, burning and rawness. Pemphigus.
Ran-s. cured pemphigus in a three-months old infant with continual thirst, weak intermitting pulse, trembling
with anxious features. After Ars. 4c had caused improvement, Ran-s. 3c healed up the resulting ulcers.
MIND - Indolence and aversion to mental work. Sadness and melancholy in the evening.
Abdomen - Sensation of a plug behind umbilicus. Pressure as of a plug behind right false ribs, worse deep
inspiration.
Chest - Integument sensitive. Bruised pain and weakness in the chest every evening.
Sore burning behind xiphoid cartilage. Face - As if covered with cobwebs.
Head - Fluent coryza with sneezing and burning urination. Gnawing pain in small spot on vertex or either
temples. Biting, itching on the scalp. Frightful dreams about corpses, serpents, battles, etc.
Heart - Sensation as if a plug in heart.
Limbs - Boring pain. Gnawing in knee, left palm. Gout of fingers and toes. Sudden burning, sticking pain in
right toe. Sudden stitches in big toes, passing into burning. Corns with burning and soreness, especially when
feet hang down.
Liver - Pain over region of liver with sensation as if diarrhea would set in.
Lungs - Stitches in chest muscles, chest and sternum are sensitive to touch. Sore burning behind sternum.
As of a plug forced between ribs, worse deep breathing.
Modalities - Pains better after midnight. Worse from motion, walking, letting limb hang down. Worse by touch,
pressure, blows. Worse deep breathing, open air. Worse evening, after midnight, morning. Worse after a meal.
Mouth - Burning and rawness of tongue. Tongue cracks and peels off, denuded patches. Tongue mapped.
Mouth sore and raw. Teeth and gums sensitive. Blunt teeth with toothache.
Nose - Fluent coryza, with sneezing, with burning urination.
Skin - Vesicular eruption with tendency to form large blisters. Acrid exudation, which makes surrounding
parts sore.
Sensations - As if head were too full and too large. As if a plug were lodged in umbilicus. Pressure as from a
dull instrument. As if diarrhea would set in. As of a needle thrust deep into big toe. With pains in stomach there
is fainting. Convulsive twitches of limbs. Gnawing and boring sensations.
Skin - Yellow vesicles. Bullae with acrid contents. Pemphigus.
Sleep - Dreadful dreams of dead bodies, snakes and fights.
Stomach - Nausea worse after midnight. Pain with fainting.
Throat - Burning scraping in throat.
COMMENTS - External sensitiveness, especially of chest and sternum. Chest disorders, including aneurysm.
Arrest of breathing. Pains in liver, spleen, chest or heart, worse on deep inspiration and associated with
external soreness.
Most of the symptoms are right-sided, but there is one left-side symptom that is peculiar: continual gnawing in
left palm. The right toes, especially the right big toe, are the seat of many acute pains, giving the remedy a
high place in acute attacks of gout and painful corns.
Mahoney cured with Ran-s. 3c an aged woman subject to gout aching in dorsum of feet, especially the right,
with wakefulness at night. Kali-c. 30c had previously removed pain passing downward over the glutei.
 RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Puls. Wine and coffee antidote only partially. The ulcers were somewhat relieved
by Peruvian Balsam. Compare: (1) Ran-b. - Ran-s. more irritative. (2) Headache, gnawing in small spot at
vertex, Puls. (3) Mapped tongue, Nat-m., Ars., Rhus-t., Tarax. (4) Ran-s. has more burning and rawness than
any. (5) Cobweb sensation, Am-c., Bor., Brom., Bry., Calc., Con, Graph., Mag-c. Follows well: Ars. in
pemphigus. Followed well by: Lach, in diphtheria with denuded tongue.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
