name: Rhus Glabra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rhus-g. Rhus glabra. Smooth sumac. Rhus Carolinas. Rhus elegans. Rhus virginica.
Pennsylvania sumac. Upland sumac. N. O. Anacardiacae. Rocky or barren soils in North America. Tincture of
fresh bark of root. Tincture of berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphthae. Debility. Diarrhea. Dreams, annoying. Dysentery. Hemorrhages. Headache. Mouth
ulcers. Nosebleed. Pharyngitis.
HERBAL - Rhus trypanosomiasis, Rhus glabra and Rhus coriaria have acid fruit and astringent bark, which is
used in tanning. Rhus-g. is a deciduous shrub with a stem 2 to 12 feet high and has terminal flowers and fruit
clothed with acid crimson hairs like the other non- poisonous Rhus.
A tincture made of the whole pannicle, “Sumac-bobs" cured a patient who had
every spring an attack of laryngeal cough with dyspnea and almost complete loss of voice. Farmers place
“bobs ” in the mangers of hoses who have “heaves. ”
HOMEOPATHIC - The tincture of the bark was proved by Dr. A. V. Marshall on himself with very substantial
doses. The symptoms are his and they bear out the traditional uses of the remedy.
One of these is “profuse perspiration arising from debility.” Marshall had “profuse sweat during sleep” and
such a degree of debility that he was obliged to leave off the proving.
Hale mentioned that an infusion of the root had a popular repute in diarrhea and dysentery, especially when
the discharges are fetid, and that the berries were used for chronic cough, wheezing cough and laryngeal
asthma.
It was claimed that this remedy will so disinfect the bowels that the flatus and stools will be free from odor. It
acts well in putrescence conditions with tendency to ulceration. Fetid flatus.
Used locally on soft, spongy gums, aphthae, pharyngitis, etc. Ulceration of mouth. Nosebleeds and occipital
headaches. Dreams of flying through the air (Stict.). Exhaustion and painful fatigue. Loss of weight.
MIND - Stupid, forgetful, indifferent to surrounding objects. Distaste for society.
Abdomen - Sharp cutting in umbilical region and abdomen. Umbilical region tender to pressure.
Back - Pain in small of back.
Food - Loss of appetite. Hunger at breakfast, could eat but little though feeling as if he had fasted many days.
 Head - Dull, heavy headache on waking, better by exercise. Dull heavy pain in front and top of head.
Kidneys - Scanty, high-colored urine.
Limbs - Aching and fatigue of lower limbs, can hardly stand.
Modalities - Better by movement. Worse after sleep. Abdomen, ulcers in mouth, worse from touch.
Mouth - Taste flat, alkaline. Taste of drug remains long. Tongue furred white. Bleeding from mouth. Aphthous
stomatitis. Several small, very sensitive ulcers on mucus membrane opposite the bicuspids. Scurvy, nursing
sore mouth (Vero-o.).
Nose - Bleeding from left nostril and mouth. Bloody scabs in left nostril. Left nostril hot and dry.
Perspiration - Profuse perspiration arising from debility (Chin.). Sweat, profuse during sleep.
Rectum - Diarrhea in afternoon, worse towards evening. Dry, hard stool, latermoist, then natural, and again
diarrhea.
Sleep - Sleep disturbed by annoying dreams, very restless. Dreams of flying through the air.
Stomach - Distress in stomach, disturbed, very restless. Pain in stomach, much worse by all food or drink.
Temperature - Sense of coldness while there is actual increase of heat in the skin. Skin hot, dry with thirst.
Throat - Expelled two clots of blood from throat soon after waking.
COMMENTS - Cooper observed an aggravation in a case of psoriasis in which the patient felt irritable and
despondent and the skin became irritable. Aggravation of stomach symptoms by either food or drink.
In the proving there were dull, heavy headaches, better by exercise. Hale said Rhus-g. has cured occipital
headaches.
RELATIONS - Said to be antidotal to the action of Merc, and has been employed in the treatment of secondaty
syphilis after mercury. Compare: (1) Rhus-t. Anae, and other Ana- cardiace, and the Xanthoxylaces, which
are an allied order.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Pennsylvania sumac. Upland sumac. N. O. Anacardiacae. Rocky or barren soils in North America. Tincture of

name: Rhus Laurina
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rhus-1. Rhus laurina. Laurel sumac. N. O. Anacardiaceae. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Edema. Itching. Skin, eruptions. Swelling. Urticaria. Vesicles.
HERBAL - This variety grows abundantly in the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, as well as in the
mountains and is found in all parts of California. It differs from Rhus-t. principally in the shape of the leaves,
and in the entire absence of the slightest pubescence, both on their superior and inferior surfaces.
The sap of the plant is a thin milky fluid, but when allowed to touch the skin, it produces a dark purple stain,
and for three or four days afterwards, whenever the part is washed, it looks as if it had been recently touched
with silver nitrate.
HOMEOPATHIC-M. J. Rhees, M.D. wrote, “Some persons are much more readily and severely affected by
this plant than others, while a very few are entirely exempt from its influence. The great majority are more or
less susceptible to its action. I have seen very many cases of poisoning by it.
“Some have presented the same symptoms and the same kind of eruption as were present in my own case,
but in more severe form. I have seen eyes completely closed for 24 hours by the swelling, and the scrotum
and prepuce have been so badly swollen in a few cases as to render it necessary to support them with a
suspensory bandage.
“In other instances, the vesicles are much longer than in my case, and become confluent, forming a dark scab
of an inch or more in diameter. I have not seen any case in which the tongue or pulse were materially
disordered. I have been informed by a gentleman in this city, that two persons with whom he was acquainted,
died from the effects of the poison, but I have been unable to learn anything concerning their symptoms.
“Dr. Lewis Post, of San Jose, California, informs me that if he rides within ten feet to leeward of the plant, he
is speedily affected by it, particularly and almost exclusively on the scrotum and prepuce. It seems to have a
great affinity for this part of the body, as almost all the cases I have seen have complained of the intense
voluptuous itching of the external genital organs and the inside of the thighs.”
COMMENTS - Recorded in proceedings of the American Institute of Homeopathy on rhus-1., M. J. Rhees,
M.D. wrote, “On the 4th of the present month, at 10 o’clock a.m., I procured several branches of both sexual
varieties of Rhus laur., and cut the leaves tenshoots, and clusters of flowers into small fragments, and put
them into a vial, with the intention of making a tincture.
“While doing so, I was troubled with a smarting and burning in the eyes. My hands were protected at the time
by kid gloves, and I washed them carefully with strong soap before I touched any part of my body. In the
evening I began to experience slight itching and burning in the face, particularly about the eyes and forehead;
and voluptuous itching on the scrotum and prepuce. At night, felt a sense of oppression as if the air was too
 heavy.
“April 5th. Last night the sleep was disturbed and full of dreams, which were lascivious, and of venereal
pleasure; felt heavy and unrefreshed in the morning; during the day the itching in the face has increased and
spread over the nose, the edges of the nostrils, the upper and lower lips, the external ears, and the inferior
portion of the neck immediately above the sternum and clavicles; the skin on these parts feels rough, and is
covered with a minute eruption of lenticular vesicles, filled with transparent serum.
“Itching on the back of the hands, particularly between the fingers. The itching on the scrotum and prepuce
has become more troublesome, and is much increased by scratching; scratching, or rubbing of the parts is
followed by intense burning; the prepuce is slightly swollen. In the evening the nose is quite red and shining;
the redness is not removed by pressure.
“April 6th. This morning I felt weak and languid. Dull, aching pain, and weakness
across the loins. Redness, and swelling of the skin of the forehead, eyelids, nose, cheeks, lips, and ears,
behind the ears, and on the front of the neck.
“The skin on these parts is covered with the minute lenticular vesicles spoken of yesterday, which are more
filled with serum. These vesicles seem to be situated in the rete mucosum; at least they involve a deeper tissue
than the cuticle. During the day some of them find their way to the surface, and are ruptured while being
scratched.
“The itching is so intolerable that it is impossible to resist the inclination to scratch. After scratching, the parts
burn and sting, become more swollen, and feel stiff and dry; the prepuce is much swollen and very red, and
the itching is unbearable about once in five or six hours on this part and the scrotum; the scrotum is red,
swollen, and much corrugated.
“After scratching for a few minutes, the itching is entirely relieved for several hours; eruption of pimples and
minute vesicles with excessive itching on the backs of the hands and between the fingers; itching on the inside
of the thighs.
“April 7th. The same symptoms continue as were noted yesterday, but with increased violence. The eyes were
nearly closed in the morning, by the swelling of the lids. Chilly sensation during the day, through the whole
body, while sitting in a warm room.
“April 8th. The itching and swelling on the face, between the fingers, and on the scrotum and prepuce, became
so intolerable, that, fearing it would incapacitate me for business, I took Rhus tox. 6th, every four hours, and
bathed the parts with cream. This treatment alleviated the symptoms somewhat. At night itching and redness
on the inside of the thighs, from the perineum to the knees.
“April 9th. The itching and swelling in the face is very much abated, as well as that on the scrotum and prepuce.
The itching on the hands and between the fingers is very harassing, and is much increased by rubbing and
scratching.
“The itching comes on at intervals of 5 or 6 hours, but it may be produced at any time by rubbing or scratching.
Scratching is followed by excessive burning, and between the fingers by a dull, aching pain, the skin becoming
more swollen, hard, and white, as in urticaria.
“This evening took a hot bath, as hot as it could be borne, using Castile soap and the flesh-brush freely. This
was followed by immediate and complete relief for several hours. Continued the Rhus tox. as yesterday, and
the cream externally.
“April 10th. The itching in the neck returned at bed time, last night, and was somewhat troublesome through
the night. This morning the itching returned with great severity in the hands, and was again relieved by bathing
them in hot water, which was repeated this evening.
“The face is very dry and rough, and has a scurfy appearance, and the skin seems to be thickened and
indurated; all other parts have been comfortable through the day, with the exception of the thighs and the skin
covering the lowerportion of the abdomen, which has at long intervals itched considerably.
“April 11 th. Bathed the hands in hot water this morning, and they have not been at all troublesome through
the day. There has been some itching on the thighs and scrotum, but not nearly so much as formerly.
“April 12th. The hands have been very troublesome at intervals of 12 hours during the day. This morning
vesicles made their appearance in the palm of the left hand wherever the sap of the plant had touched the
skin, in gathering it.
“April 19th. Up to the present time, the itching and burning in the palm of the left hand, and between the fingers
of both hands, have been very annoying, almost painful, at intervals of 10 or 12 hours. Wishing, however, to
know how long the effect of the plant would continue, I have made use of no remedies since the 11th. It is now
evidently abating.”
RELATIONS - Compare: Rhus-t. Anae, and other Anacardiace, and the Xanthoxylaces, which are an allied
order.
 REFERENCES Rhees.

name: Rhus Radicans
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rhus-r. Rhus radicans. Climbing poison ivy. Poison vine. Toxicodendron radicans. N. O.
Anacardiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves gathered at sunset just before flowering time. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Backaches. Boils. Chills. Colic. Constipation. Cough. Debility. Dermatitis. Diabetes.
Dislocated,joints. Dyspnea. Eczema. Erysipelas. Faintness. Fever, blisters. Fevers. Fibrositis. Glossitis.
Headaches. Herpes zoster. Hives. Housemaid’s knee. Influenza. Injuries. Intermittent fever. Joint, pains.
Lumbago. Muscular, pains. Nausea. Neuralgia. Nosebleeds. Palpitations. Palsy. Paralysis. Periosteum,
pains. Poison ivy, oak. Rashes. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Spine, diseases. Sprains. Stiffness. Strains.
Tendonitis. Typhoid fever. Typhus. Ulcers. Urticaria. Vesicles. Vertigo. Whiplash.
HERBAL - Dispute whether Rhus radicans differs from Rhus toxicondendron continues. Botanists agree in
recognizing little distinction other than that of habit between the two.
Millspaugh, in his book “American Medicinal Plants,” tells in his account of the plant that he had seen the two
varieties springing from the same root-stock. He advises that the tincture should be made from specimens of
both.
Rhus-t. is a dwarf, erect, shrub, while Rhus-r. is a climber, with stem five to forty feet long, furnished with
numerous radicles by which it adheres to trees and climbs up them like ivy. The leaves of Rhus-t. are almost
entire and glabrous. The leaves are smoother at the margins than Rhus-t.
HOMEOPATHIC - Under the name “Rhus,” Hahnemann published his proving of “Rhus radicans, also called
Toxicodendron.” The two forms have been proved independently. The American provings were made with
Rhus-r. and the majority of the poisonings have occurred from this plant.
It acts on the brain, mucus membrane, skin, muscles, joints, and tendons. Inflammation of fibrous tissues.
Neuralgias. Palsy of the limbs.
Rheumatism of the chest, neck, and back. Wandering, rheumatic pains, first one joint, then another. Pains
and stiffness are often semi-lateral and in various parts, often remote and successive.
Traumatic inflammation of the joints. Sprains. The pains are worse when first beginning to move in the
morning, relieved during the day, when occupied, and when walking in the open air.
Ailments from straining a single part, muscle or tendon, over-lifting, particularly from stretching high up
to reach things. Whiplash. Dislocated, joints. Injuries and traumas to the joints. Tendonitis. Sprained joints.
Severe backaches, chronic, low back pain. Burning in the spine. Stiffness in the sacrum, better with cracking
and adjustments. Coldness in left tibia. Old injuries that never healed, stiffen with weather changes.
Headache in occiput, even pain in nape, and from there pains draw over the head forwards. Jaws are tight and
stiff, can crack and pop. Inflammation of the tongue Burning in tongue, tip feels sore (Rhus-t.).
Erysipelas, red, itching, phlegmonous swelling, with vesicular eruption extending like a band around right
ankle. Large open ulcer on ankle, pain worse after, not during motion (Rhus-r. cured after failure of Rhus-t.).
Intermittent fever. Fever with debility. Excessive debility. General languor. Inclination to lie down. Faintness
and dyspnea. Typhoid. Typhus conditions. Diabetes.
Symptoms better after a storm has thoroughly set in, especially after an electric storm. Pronounced yearly
aggravation (Lach.). Symptoms increased after drinking cold water.
MIND - Unfit for any mental labor. Confusion at night on lying down. Irresolution in projects. Mistakes in
speaking. Jesting. Melancholy. Mental depression. Great discouragement and apprehension about the future.
Delusion that she is criticized. Unconsciousness while standing.
Abdomen - Distention and flatus. Constriction and pain in left hypochondria. Dull pains. Lancinations in right
hypochondria during inspiration. Sharp pains. Shooting pain after drinking cold water. Griping colic. Colic that
compels him to flex the trunk.
Back - Backaches and stiffness. Severe backaches, chronic, low back pain. Stiffness of back in the
morning. Aching in the back and in the renal region. Aching in the lumbar spine and ileum when lying down
at night. Lumbago. Pain across the back, loins and quadratus lumborum. Stiffness in the sacrum that’s
better with cracking and adjustments. Weakness in the whole spine. Burning in the spine. Pains in and between
the scapulae. Rigidity of the neck. Stiff neck. Pain in the cervical muscles on motion, feel tender.
Chest - Chest sensitive to pressure. Chest pains that seem to proceed from the stomach. Pain in chest, near
the nipple. Dull pain. Pains worse on inspiration.
Ears - Pain in one ear. Small boil. Sensation as if the beating of the heart and arteries were heard. Sound of
rushing water.
 Eyes - Pain in the eyes when opening them. Burning, smarting in the eyeballs. Lachrymation. Itching at the
inner canthus. Swelling and redness of the lids, with itching and burning. Edema of the lids. Confusion of sight.
Vision obscured. Dimness at candlelight.
Face - Neuralgia. Pain in the left side of the face and lower jaw. Erysipelas, burning, smarting, heat, and
redness. Boils. Pustules. Vesicles. Pimples on the face and forehead. Large red pimple on the cheek. Eruptions
at the angle of the mouth.
Food - Appetite deficient or lost.
Head - Head feels as if it were swelling, and had become too large. Heaviness, fullness. Sensation as if the
crown of the head were rising up. Heat, pain, and throbbing in the head. Continual dull pain in forehead. Semi-
lateral pain in the temple. Pain over the eye. Headache, with nausea worse when lying down, better after rising.
Pain in vertex and nape of neck. Scalp tender. Small elevations. Eruptions. Itching.
Heart - Palpitations of the heart with fullness in the head. Pulse frequent and small.
Kidneys - Pressure on the bladder. Increased secretion and flow of urine. Milky urine. Deep red urine, with
pink deposit.
Limbs - Rheumatism. Inflammation of the joints with heat, redness, and swelling. Wandering pains from
joint to joint. Traumatic inflammation of the joints. Instability. Stiffness of joints. Weakness, and feeling
of heaviness in the limbs, when walking. Sprains. Dislocatedjoints. Pain as though the muscles or
tendons were strained. Pain and stiffness in hip. Soreness and excoriation about the nates. Swelling,
stiffness and lameness of the knee, ankle. Pain in knee, near the patella, worse on moving the joint. Pains
in calf when walking. Cramps in the calf when lying in bed, or extending the limb. Pains at the ankles. Sharp
pains in the feet. Pains in the sole of the right foot. Coldness of the feet. Coldness, with numbness. Severe
pain in shoulder and the acromion process. Aching in the wrists, especially during exertion of the fingers.
Numbness of the arms, hands and fingers. Erysipelatous inflammation of the hands and fingers. Vesicles
between the fingers. Scratches and injuries tend to inflame and suppurate. Itching, red eruption on the legs,
and about the ankles. Vesicles.
Lungs - Dry cough. Hacking cough, excited by tickling. Cough on movement or lying down.
Male - Penis swollen, bloated. Scrotum, inflamed and irritated by walking. Rash in genital area. Vesicles.
Mouth - Increased saliva. Disagreeable bitter or metallic taste. Air feels unusually cold in the mouth. Sore pain,
as if the mouth had been scalded. Ulcers. Vesicles inside the mouth. Gums inflamed, tender. Transient
throbbing in the teeth. Pains in carious teeth. Toothache, with flow of saliva.
Nose - Frequent sneezing. Nostrils excoriated and encrusted. Fluent coryza, with copious secretion of mucus.
Nosebleed.
Rectum - Anus, sore, excoriated, especially after walking. Constipation with head-
Rhus radicans ache. Diarrhea, with slimy, yellow stools. Pale evacuations. Evacuations streaked with blood.
Bright blood after a stool.
Skin - Itching, pricking, stinging. Dermatitis. Poison ivy and poison oak rashes. Hard, red eruptions. Inflamed
tubercles, elevations, hard pimples. Pustules, blisters, watery pimples. Vesicular eruption, some disappear
without rupture of the cuticle, others burst. Yellow, acrid fluid from eruptions. Erysipelas, especially in hot
weather. Small boils. Ulcers. Swelling of the lymphatic glands.
Sleep - Sleepy by day, and early in the evening. Imperfect sleep at night, disturbed by frequent waking. Dreams
of danger and horses. Fear on waking.
Stomach - Stomach sensitive to pressure. Severe pain in stomach with dizziness. Shooting, sharp pain. Pain
after food. Pressure and fullness in epigastrium. Empty eructations. Nausea. Vomiting of tasteless water.
Temperature - Chills, general or partial, generally in the back. Coldness of the extremities. General body heat
with dry skin. Intermittent fever, every day, at 1 p.m. Fever, with pain in the legs. Typhoid fever with brown
tongue, red tip.
Throat - Rawness, excoriation. Pricking, smarting, stinging, irritation. Red, hot, burning, and swollen,
constriction. Painful deglutition.
Tongue - Tongue feels dry, sore. Burning, pricking. Scalded feeling, tip of the tongue feels sore or burnt.
Vesicles at tip. Rough tongue. Yellow coated tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo, and pains in the limbs. Vertigo with confusion and momentary loss of consciousness.
COMMENTS - Rhus-r. has almost identical action as Rhus-t.; characteristic burning in the tongue, tip feels
sore. Pains are often one-sided and in various parts, often remote and successive. Pronounced yearly
aggravation (Lach.).
H. C. Allen noted a periodicity in Rhus- r. that marks it as a great anti-psoric. It is, he said, on deeply psoric or
tubercular constitutions that its toxic effects are most felt and longest lasting, and these constitutional effects
“seem incurable without the anti-psoric.”
 Guernsey considered Rhus-r. deeper acting than Rhus-t., being indicated in phlegmonous erysipelas,
especially where it begins in ankles and moves gradually up the leg, moving in the deeper tissues, with no
fever, and for axillary glands when the swelling is very deep and hard.
Millspaugh summarized the effects of Rhus poisoning: the majority of poisonings have been caused by Rhus-
r., as first redness and swelling of the affected part with intolerable itching and burning, flowed by vertigo,
weariness and a sort of intoxication.
Farrington gave, as distinctive indications for Rhus-r., an occipital headache with rheumatic stiffness of the
nape. Drawing, tearing pains in legs. Pleurodynia when the pains shoot into the shoulders.
Mahony reported a case of eczema on the perineum and scrotum with sweat in cleft of buttocks, both relieved
in a week with Rhus-r., 12c, twice daily.
RELATIONS - Rhus-r. is said to be antidotal to the action of Rhus-t. and has been employed in the treatment
of cases where Rhus-t. had failed. Compare: Rhus-t. Anae, and other Anacardiace, and the Xanthoxylaces,
which are an allied order.
REFERENCES - Buck. Clarke.

name: Rhus Toxicodendron
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rhus-t. Rhus toxicodendron. Poison oak. N. O. Anacardiaceae. Tinctureof fresh leaves gathered
at sunset just before flowering time. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abortion. Acne, rosacea. After- pains. Allergies. Amenorrhea. Ankleinjuries. Anus, fissure.
Appendicitis. Appetite, lost. Arthritis. Beriberi.Back,injuries. Bones,pain. Cecum, inflammation. Chilblains.
Circulation, poor. Cyanosis. Dengue fever. Dermatitis. Diarrhea. Diphtheria.Dislocated,joints. Dysentery.
Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Ear, eczema. Ecthyma. Enteric fever. Erysipelas. Erythema nodosum. Exostosis.
Eyes, disorders. Fever, blisters. Fevers. Gastro-enteritis. Glandular, disorders. Gout. Hemorrhages. Hemor-
Rhus toxicodendron rhoids. Hernia. Herpes. Herpes zoster. Hives. Hoarseness. Housemaid’s knee.
Hydrocele. Influenza. Injuries. Intermittent fever. Joint, injuries. Liver, abscess. Lumbago. Measles.
Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Muscular, pains. Neuralgias. Ovary, tumor. Paralysis. Paraphimosis. Pemphigus.
Periosteum, pains. Pleurisy. Pleurodynia. Pneumonia.Poison ivy. Poison oak. Ptosis. Pyemia. Rashes.
Relapsing fever. Rheumatism. Rhus, poisoning. Scarlatina. Sciatica. Sleep, restless. Smallpox. Spine,
diseases. Sprains. Strains. Strictures. Tendonitis. Throat, sore. Tongue, disorders. Typhoid fever. Typhus.
Urticaria. Vesicles. Warts. Whiplash. Wens. Yawning.
HERBAL - Poison ivy grows in thickets and low grounds in North America, flowering in June. It was introduced
into England as a plant in 1640. In 1798, Dufresnoy of Valenciennes first used it as a medicine.
It was brought to his notice by the cure of a young man of a herpetic eruption (darter) of six years duration,
through his being accidentally poisoned with the plant. Dufresnoy used it successfully in eruptive diseases,
paralysis, rheumatism and amaurosis.
A peculiarity of the plant is that it is more poisonous during the night, and when bursting into leaf, or at any
time in June or July when the sun is not shining upon it. The absence of sunlight together with dampness,
seems to favor the exhalation of toxicodendric acid.
“An acrimonious vapor, combined with carburetted hydrogen, exhales from a growing plant of the Poison Oak
during the night. It can be collected in ajar and is capable of inflaming and blistering the skin of persons of
excitable constitution who plunge their arms into it.”
Though it is not certain that Hahnemann used Rhus-t. at all orexclusively, Jahr gave aseparate presentation
of the Rhus radicans symptoms. Under the name of Rhus, Hahnemann published his proving of “Rhus
radicans, also called Toxicodendron.”
Botanists agree in recognizing no distinction other than that of habit between the two. The milky juice, which
turns black on exposure, is used as a marking ink (like Anae.), and as an ingredient in varnishes for finishing
boots.
HOMEOPATHIC - Rhus-t. affects the fibrous tissuejoints, tendons, sheaths, etc., producing pains and
stiffness. Irritating agent to the skin, especially of the face, scalp, genitals and mucus membranes.
Rheumatism in cold damp season. Stiffness of muscles and joints. Motion “limbers up” the Rhus-t.
patient, hence he feels better for a time from a change of position. Inclination to stretch. Dislocated joints.
Stretching causes cracking in knees, soreness in abdomen. Sciatica, better by warmth from exercise.
Ailments from straining a single part, muscle or tendon, over-lifting, particularly from stretching high up
to reach things. Injuries and traumas to the joints. Tendonitis. Sprained ankles. Whiplash. Old injuries that
never healed, stiffen with weather changes.
Pains are tearing, shooting, stitching, worse at night, cannot rest in any position. Tearing asunder pains.
 Parts feel sore, bruised and stiff. Pains as if the flesh was torn loose from the bones. Dislocated joints
sensation. Soreness of prominent projection of bones. Muscles twitch. Crawling, trembling. turning, swelling
and lividity.
Severe backaches, chronic, low back pain. Burning in the spine. Stiffness in the sacrum that’s better with
cracking and adjustments. Affections of nerves and spinal cord give rise to paretic effects. Numbness of
parts paralyzed.
Unwanted exercise causes paralysis. Hemiplegia, right sided, sensation as if gone to sleep. Infantile paralysis
from exposure to cold damp. Paralysis after unwonted exertion, after childbirth. Over-exertion causes
palpitations, aggravates coxalgia. Limbs lain on fall asleep, no sweat on them. Ailments from getting wet, while
perspiring.
Septic conditions. Cellulitis and infections, carbuncles in early stages (Echi.). Septicemia.
Inflammation and swelling of the long bones, scraping, gnawing, tearing loose in periosteum. Strictures after
inflammation. Mucus discharges are acrid, rusty red like meat water, musty, causing eruptions. Postoperative
complications.
Influenza. Smallpox. Glands are swollen, hot and painful indurated, suppurating. Boils, abscesses. Typhoid-
like fevers. Headache in occiput, even pain in nape of neck, and from there pains draw over the head
forwards. Jaws are tight and stiff, can crack and pop. Coldness in left tibia.
Symptoms appear on the left side or go from left to right. Characteristic modalities, particularly worse at night
and from damp. “The more he moves the better he is,” (opposite of Bry.). Worse during rest, and after rest.
Nausea, worse after eating. Craves cold water, which is vomited immediately. Many symptoms are better after
a storm, especially after an electric storm.
MIND - Confusion. Mind and senses becomes cloudy. Low, mild delirium, incoherent talk, answers correctly
but slowly, or hastily, or reluctantly. Forgetful and cannot remember the most recent events. Recalls with
difficulty things and names. Vanishing of thoughts while standing. Can’t hold mind on one subject long enough
to answer. Stupefaction, with tingling in head and pains in limbs, better motion.
Anxious, sadness, helplessness and profound despondency. Causeless weeping, without knowing why.
Inclination to cry, worse in evening without knowing why, with desire for solitude. Forsaken feeling.
Inexpressible anxiety with pressure at heart. Anxiety about one’s children. Anxiety, worse twilight, with restless
change of place. Great apprehension at night, cannot remain in bed. Mental and physical restlessness at
night. Extreme restlessness with continued change of position. Restlessness during menses.
Anguish as if she had committed a crime or as if some terrible calamity impended, driving her from one place
to another. Superstitious fears. Fears, with sighing, worse
at night. Fear and despair on account of sad thoughts. Delirium withfearofbeingpoisoned (Hyos.). Complaints
from fright.
Fretful, impatient, ill-humored, easily vexed. Irritability at night, better walking in open air. Discouragement
and dissatisfaction. Satiety of life. Dwells on past disagreeable occurrences after midnight. Talking of
business in sleep.
Aversion to company alternating with bursts of pleasantry and sarcasm. Delusion he is roaming over fields, or
hard at work. Delusion of being watched. Suicidal disposition in twilight. Thoughts of suicide, wants to drown
himself.
Abdomen - Ileo-cecal symptoms, appendicitis. Swelling of inguinal glands. Incarcerated hernia. Hourglass
contraction. Excessive distention after eating. Mucus colitis. Colic after getting wet. Colic, compelling to walk
bent. Violent pains, relieved by lying on abdomen. Pain in region of ascending colon. Rumbling of flatus on
first rising, but disappears with continued motion. Soreness of navel. Sensation as if water swashing in
abdomen. Sensation as if a lump in abdomen.
Back - Back strain or injury. Pains from over-lifting or overuse. Backache, as if back would break, better
hard pressure. Backache, compelling him to move constantly in bed. Contractive or breaking backache,
better hard pressure, lying on something hard, walking about or bending backwards. Pain and stiffness in
small of back, better motion or lying on something hard, worse while sitting. Pain between shoulders on
swallowing. Aching and stiffness in lumbar region as after long stooping or bending. Burning in lumbar region.
Lumbago, coccyx aches into thighs. Curvature of dorsal vertebrae. Acute spinal paralysis of infants. Spinal
membranes inflamed, from getting wet or sleeping on damp ground. Myelitis. Stiffness and lameness in
sacrum, worse resting.
Breasts - Great soreness of nipples after confinement. Breast pain with itching, burning papular eruption about
nipples.
Causations - Effects of drinking cold water (Bell-p.), beer (headache). Cold, getting wet, especially after being
heated, cold bathing, sea bathing (Mag-m.). Wetting head, damp sheets, bathing. Slightest anger. Strains,
 over-exertion, over-lifting. Raising arms high to lift things.
Chest - Oppression of the chest, cannot get breath, with sticking pains. Tickling behind upper sternum, causing
dry. hoarse, tearing, tormenting cough. Tingling in chest with tension in intercostal muscles, worse rest. Numb
sensation in chest. Chest pains worse using arms. Pleurodynia, chest pains shoot into shoulders. Pain as if
sternum were pressed inward. Stitches in chest and sides of chest. Herpes axillaris. Axillary abscess after
delivery.
Constitutions - Suited for the psoric or tubercular constitutions. Rheumatic constitutions.
Cough - Bronchial coughs in old people, worse on awaking and with expectoration of small plugs of mucus.
Dry teasing coughs. Dry coughs from midnight until morning. Coughing and sneezing worse uncovering body
(Rumx.). Coughing during chill, or when putting hands out of bed. Coughing prevents sleep at night. Cough
with profuse sweat and pain in stomach. Frequent hacking cough with bitter taste in throat.
Ears - Lobes swollen. Swelling of ears. Otalgia. Pain in ear with a feeling as if something were inside. Painful
throbbing in ear at night. Discharge of bloody pus, with deafness.
Eyes - Orbital cellulitis. Suppurative iritis. Iritis after exposure to cold, dampness. Iritis of rheumatic origin.
Corneal injection with intensive ulceration. Suppuration of cornea. Ulceration of cornea. Glaucoma. Pustular
inflammations. Saccular conjunctiva. Acute retro-bulbar neuritis. Swollen, red, edematous. Profuse flow of
yellow pus. Lachrymation when yawning. Profuse gush of hot, scalding tears upon opening lids. Photophobia.
Eye painful on turning it or pressing. Paralysis of the eyeball muscles. Eyelids, stiff agglutinated, dry, firmly
closed. Edema of lids. Ptosis. Styes or abscesses, on lower lids. Old eye injuries.
Face - Pale, sickly look, with sunken eyes. Blue rings about eyes. Cyanosis of face and hands. Swollen face.
Erysipelas, shining redness with formation of vesicles. Moist eruptions and thick scabs on face. Suppurating
eruptions on face. Acne rosacea. Crusta lactea (Calc., Viol-t.). Corners of mouth ulcerated. Fever blisters
around mouth and chin (Nat-m.). Red spots on left cheek. Parotiditis (left) with fever. Joints painful. Pains in
maxillary joint. Painful cheekbones, sensitive to touch. Facial neuralgia with chilliness, worse evening.
Female - Amenorrhea, from getting wet with milk in breast. Menses early, profuse and prolonged, acrid.
Menstrual flow light-colored and acrid, causes biting pain in vulva. Dysmenorrhea, cramping, with backache,
worse lying on back. Membranous dysmenorrhea in rheumatic women. Violent pain in vulva during menses.
Soreness in vagina shortly after sex, or preventing coition. Swelling with intense itching of vulva. Bearing down
pain when standing or walking, with backache. Pelvic joints stiff when beginning to move. Consciousness of
uterus. Prolapse uterus from lifting oroverstraining. Uterine infection, septic. Polyps of uterus after getting
chilled from sea-bathing. Metrorrhagia, clotted blood, with labor-like pains. Miscarriage from a strain. Lochia
thin, protracted offensive diminished (Puls., Sec.). Lochia with shooting pain upwards in vagina (Sep.).
Frequent after pains.
Food - No appetite for any kind of food. Drowsy after eating. Food tastes bitter, especially bread. Desire for
sweets, oysters, tonics, beer, acids. Desires cold milk, yogurt and cheese. Dairy relaxes. Nausea worse
from ice cream. Aversion to meat and bread. Great thirst with dry mouth and throat. Drinks little and often
during fever. Craves cold drinks, though they aggravate cough, chill. Worse after ice-water. Sweats from warm
drinks. Pulse affected by beer, coffee or alcohol. Aversion to spirituous liquors, beer.
Head - Headache in occiput (Rad-br.), painful to touch. Stupefying headache, must lie down, worse least
chagrin. Headache after taking a cold bath, from beer, immediately after a meal. Heavy feeling in head. Pain
in forehead, proceeding backward. Feels as if a board were strapped on the forehead. Brain feels loose and
as if struck against skull on walking or rising. Burning in forehead when walking. Aching in occipital
protuberances. Painful tingling in head, occiput. Vesicular erysipelas of scalp, going from left to right. Dry
herpes on hairy scalp. Scalp sensitive, worse on side lain on. Humid eruptions on scalp, itching greatly.
Heart - Hypertrophy from overexertion. Weak and tremulous feeling about heart, after walking. Acute, stabbing
pains in cardiac region on deep inspiration or raising left arm suddenly. Heart feels tired, pains go down left
arm. Left arm aches with heart disease. Anxious palpitations in morning on awaking. Palpitations after
overexertion. Severe palpitation and pain in heart when lying on left side. Trembling and palpitations when
sitting still, better from walking. Pulse quick, weak, irregular. Pulse intermittent with numbness of left arm.
Limbs - Arthritis and rheumatism. Stiffness of all the joints, better warmth, motion and massage. Hot,
painful swelling of joints. Cracking of joints when stretching. Synovitis. Rheumatic pains spread over a large
surface at nape of neck, loins and limbs, better motion (Agar.). Pains tearing in tendons, ligaments and
tissues. Sciatica, worse cold, damp weather, at night. Sciatica better warmth, exercise. Limbs stiff,
paralyzed, the cold fresh air is not tolerated, it makes the skin painful. Numbness and prickling in limbs
after over-work and exposure to damp. Paralysis, trembling after exertion. Paraplegia after childbirth, sexual
excess, fever. Pain along ulnar nerve. Soreness of condyles of bones. Tension as from shortening of muscles.
Legs feel dead, wooden. Involuntary limping. Tearing pains down thighs. Tenderness about knee. Cramps in
 calves.
Ankles or knees are swollen, stiff after sprain or injured. Tingling in feet. Sensation as if walking on
needles. Itching of legs and feet. Gangrenous ulcers on legs, runs bloody water, on dropsical legs. Cold hands
and feet. Arms nervous and shaky (left). Paralytic pains in elbows. Loss of power in forearm and fingers,
crawling sensation in the fingertips. Cracks on back of hands. Palms, dry, hot, cracked and sore, washing
causes burning.
Lungs - Oppressed breathing, as if breath were stopped at pit of stomach. Anxious breathing, as if not able to
draw a long breath. Hurried and very short breathing at night. Dyspnea from pressure and painfulness in pit of
stomach. Hot air from trachea. Shortness of breath during stool. Asthma alternating with skin eruptions.
Hemoptysis from overexertion or from blowing wind instruments. Hemoptysis bright blood. Sudden hypostasis
or edema of lungs. Pale, clotted or brown blood. Rust colored sputum. Expectoration, acrid pus. Gray-green
cold mucus of putrid smell. Pneumonia with typhoid symptoms, often after reabsorption of pus.
Male - Painful, persistent erections, better lying on back. Erections at night with desire to urinate. Intense
itching of genitals. Dark-red, erysipelatous. Humid vesicles on glans. Humid eruptions on genitals and
between scrotum and thighs. Swelling of glands and prepuce. Paraphimosis. Hydrocele from over-lifting.
Scrotum, swollen, edematous. Scrotum thick and hard, with intolerable itching. Edema of scrotum and penis
after scarlatina, with recurrence of fever. Metastasis of mumps to testes.
Modalities - Better from heat, hot bath, warm wrapping, warm applications. Better warm dry, weather. Better
stretching limbs, continued motion, change of position, walking. Better rubbing, holding affected part,
abdomen, head. Better from nosebleed. Worse from cold, dampness, wet rainy weather. Worse before
storms, after rain. Worse exposure to wet, cold. air, draft. Worse being chilled, when hot or sweaty, ice cold
drinks. Worse uncovering parts. Worse beginning of motion, rest,
sprains, blows, jar. Worse overexertion, lifting, after exertion. Worse prolonged sitting, rising from bed or a
seat, riding. Worse at night, after midnight, during sleep, lying on back or right side. Worse on side lain on.
Mouth - General dryness of the mouth, with thirst. Coppery, herby, or bitter taste (Cupr.). Salivation, must
spit frequently. Much tough mucus in mouth and throat. Bloody saliva runs during sleep. Gums sore. Mouth
filled with herpes sores. Herpes on lips. Fever blisters around mouth and chin (Nat-m.). Lips dry and
parched, covered with reddish-brown crusts. Lips, dry, brownish, cracked, at corners, crusty. Corners of mouth
cracked, ulcerated. Jaw’s crack when chewing. Cramp-like pain in joint of jaw, when yawning. Pain in
maxillary joint. Easy dislocation of jaw (Ign., Petr.).
Neck - Carbuncle on nape. Neck strain or injury with stiffness. Neck stiff after injuries. Whiplash. Stiff neck
with painful tension, when moving. Stiff neck from a draft, or dampness, better heat and massage.
Nose - Swelling of nose. Violent aching in bones of the nose. Red, sore, ulcerated tip of nose, drips water.
Soreness in nostrils. Hot breath burns nostrils. Dryness and stoppage of nose. Sneezing with fluent coryza,
from getting wet. Spasmodic sneezing after sudden cessation of cough. Sneezing and coughing worse
uncovering body. Nasal discharge thick, yellow mucus, green, offensive pus. Nosebleed, worse at night,
stoopingv at stool, gives relief in fevers. Loss of smell.
Perspiration - Sudden outbreak of sweat while sitting, often with violent trembling. Sweats with violent itching
of eruptions. Perspires with pains, often with trembling. Sour, musty, putrid sweat. Perspires all over, except
on head. Profuse sweat on exterior parts of body, but not on parts on which she lay. Sweat, worse during pain,
with sleepiness. Night sweat with miliary itching eruption. Profuse sweat in morning.
Rectum - Constriction in rectum. Shooting pain up rectum. Painful tenesmus without stools. Colitis mucosa.
Dysentery with tearing pains down thighs. Diarrhea alternating with constipation. Diarrhea of blood, slime and
reddish mucus. Diarrhea after walking through moist ground with bare feet. Remission of pains and urging
after stools. Fissure of anus, with periodical profuse bleeding. May abort a beginning suppurative process near
the rectum. Hemorrhoids, worse lifting. Hemorrhoids protruding after stool, with pressing in rectum, as if
everything would come out.
Sensations - As if intoxicated. As if asleep. As of a band strapped across forehead. As if head were swelling
out. Brain, as if loaded, as if torn, as if loose, as if fluctuating, as if a quantity of blood shot into it when stooping.
As of a weight behind right orbit. Legs as if made of wood. As if hamstrings and tendons of limbs too short. As
if walking on needles. Joints as if bruised. As if bones ached. As if sinking through bed. As if whole body was
burning. As if cold water poured over him. As if blood ran cold through veins.
Skin - Skin sensitive to cold air. Dry, hot, burning. Red, swollen, intense itching. Cellulitis. Dermatitis.
Eczema. Burning eczematous eruptions with tendency to scale formation. Poison ivy, oak. Shingles, herpes
zoster. Burning and neuralgic pains after herpes zoster. Herpetic eruptions alternating with dysentery and
pains in chest. Boils and abscesses. Vesicles, herpes, pemphigus, erysipelas, vesicular suppurative
conditions. Vesicles over abscess. Hives. Urticaria from getting wet with rheumatism. Urticaria during chills
 and fever. Bluish, gangrenous carbuncles. Smallpox. Swollen glands. Milk crusts. Baker’s itch. Warts on hands
and fingers. Pus erodes the hair. Itching better hot water. Itching with burning and smarting, feeling as if
pierced with hot needles. Itching all over, worse on hairy parts. Itching worse sweating. Burning after
scratching. Rubbing affected part aggravates eruptions. Eruptions, alternat
ing with dysentery.
Sleep - Drowsy after eating. Yawning, frequent, violent, spasmodic. Yawning without inclination to sleep. Y
awning with stretching. Sleepy during day, sleepless at night, with inability to remain in bed. Sleepless before
midnight. Sleeplessness at night with burning of whole body. Restless sleep tossing about can’t get
comfortable. Sleep prevented by cough. Heavy sleep, as from stupor. Sleeps with mouth open. Somnolence
with snoring, muttering and grasping at objects. Laborious dreams. Dreams of great exertion, rowing,
swimming, working hard at his daily occupation. Dreams that the world was on fire, with palpitations on
awaking. Awakens, stiff and sore must stretch. Awakes tired or nervous.
Stomach - Hunger and emptiness in stomach, without appetite. Fullness as if overloaded. Pressure as from a
stone (Bry., Ars.). Pressure in pit, as if swollen or as if drawn together. Pain in stomach after ice water.
Ulcerative pain in stomach. Violent throbbing in epigastric region. Eructations with tingling in stomach, worse
rising from lying. Nausea, vertigo and bloated abdomen after eating. Nausea, worse from ice cream, at night.
Vomiting while lying on back. Vomiting from coughing.
Stools - Involuntary stools with great exhaustion. Stools involuntary during sleep, or with tenesmus, worse
drinking. Stools, lumps of transparent mucus. Stools, frothy, watery, slimy, gelatinous, painless, bloody. Black
blood from bowels. Stools of cadaverous odor.
Teeth - Teeth feel as if asleep. Teeth feel loose and long. Sensation as if teeth were being torn out. Shooting
pain, in evening and night, better external heat. Teeth painful with stinging at root of nose. Toothache at night,
better application of cold hand. Toothache worse at night, cold, vexation. Sordes on teeth. Gums sore.
Temperature - Easily chilled, worse least uncovering with pain in limbs. Chills, as if cold water were poured
over him, followed by heat and inclination to stretch the limbs. Chills as if cold water in the veins, preceded by
cough, alternating with heat. Chill in single parts. Wants to yawn and stretch during chill. Intermittent fever,
chill with dry cough and restlessness. Rapid alternations of burning heat and shivering. Sudden flushes of heat
follow or alternating with chills. Fever after chill, with sweat which better. General heat, as from hot water or
hot blood running through veins. Influenza fever, restlessness, stiff and sore, with aching in all bones (Eup-
per.). typhoid fever, tongue dry and brown, sordes, bowels loose, great restlessness. Fever with busy
delirium. Urticaria during fever. Hydroa.
Throat - Sore, stiff feeling in throat after straining throat. Sore throat with bruised pain. Soreness, better
warm drinks with swollen glands. Hoarseness from overstraining the voice (Arn.). Hoarseness, better after
talking a while. Hoarseness with roughness and soreness in chest. Hoarseness, worse evening and change
of weather. Red, puffy itching fauces. Sensations of dryness of throat. Sore throat with swollen glands.
Esophagitis from swallowing corrosive matter. Tonsils covered with yellow membrane. Larynx cold when
breathing. Sticking or stinging pain in tonsils, worse beginning to swallow. Difficult swallowing of solids as from
contraction of saliva.
Tongue - Tongue, red and cracked, dry and red at edges. Tongue shows imprint of teeth. Tongue coated,
except red triangular space at the tip. Tongue coated diagonally or on one side only. Yellowish- white
coating at root of tongue. Tongue coated with brown mucus, except on edges, in morning on rising. Feeling as
if tongue covered with skin.
Urinary - Nephritis. Tearing pain in region of kidneys with edema, worse after exposure to wet. Dysuria with
loss of blood. Retention of urine, with restlessness and backache. Tenesmus of bladder, with discharge of a
few drops of blood-red urine. Dark, high colored, white sediment, scanty urine. Urine turbid when passed.
Urine passes in a divided stream. Frequent, profuse urination day and night. Frequent and
painful urination from prolapsed uterus. Incontinence or urine, worse lying at night, or sitting in boys. Dribbling
of urine in cold air or from becoming cold.
Vertigo - Vertigo with heaviness in limbs.
Vertigo when rising, as if she were going to fall forward or backward. Vertigo while walking. Vertigo with
staggering, as if intoxicated. Vertigo in the aged, whirling, then headache. Nausea, vertigo and bloated
abdomen after eating.
COMMENTS - The worst poisonings with Rhus divers, happened to persons who were moist and heated. One
prover of Rhus-t. was not influenced by contact with the leaves when his skin was dry, but only when perspiring.
Millspaugh noted several instances of rhus poisoning. In one poisoning case, ten men were employed to clear
a piece of land of shrubs, among which the poison vine predominated; only four escaped without symptoms.
“Most of the men soon began to show signs of being tired and at the end of the fourth day six of them were
 flat on their backs too sick for anything.”
Actual contact with the plant is not necessary in order to produce its effect. One such instance occurred on a
sultry day in June. A young woman drove a croquet ball across a lawn to a clump of poison ivy that grew beside
it. Knowing her susceptibility, she reached under the plant and drew out the ball without touching a leaf.
In the evening of the same day her face began to itch and bum. That night her face swelled so badly that the
eyes were not merely closed, but the lashes even disappeared in the swelling. It took nearly two weeks for her
to recover.
Generally, there is infiltration of the face and eyes, and agglutination of the lids after sleep. Great restlessness,
pain, thirst and fever. The surface of the skin becomes studded with confluent bullae where the cellular tissue
is loose.
Then a dermatitis follows, resembling erysipelas; this may spread rapidly and finally be communicated to the
mucus membranes. This is followed by swelling of the mouth and throat, cough, nausea and vomiting.
Rheumatoid pains develop about the joints and a painful stiffness asserts itself in the lumbar region while the
legs and arms become numb. Confusion of mind and delirium may then set in, during which the patient may
become so ill-humored, restless and anxious that he will jump out of bed.
Concomitants include inflammation of the eyes, dilation of the pupils, weak vision, and sometimes diplopia.
Nosebleed, brown-coated tongue with tri angular red tip. Swelling of parotids, difficult swallowing. Griping,
diarrhea, profuse urination. Oppression, rapid pulse, prostration, soreness of muscles, worse by exercise,
bleariness, chilliness followed by fever and copious sweat.
Neidhard added a note which brought out a modification of “worse by rest,” which is of the greatest practical
importance. Neidhard said that the disease in which he had made the most use of Rhus-t. is a form of
rheumatism common in North America and characterized by the following symptoms:
“Rigidity, paralytic weakness of thejoints with stinging pain along the tendons and muscles. Swelling and
redness on or near thejoints. Rheumatism of the hip joint and wrist seem to be most effectually controlled by
its action. The greatest rigidity and pain is experienced on first moving the joints after rest and on waking up
in the morning. After the joints are moved for a while the pain is lessened.”
Nash noted that the restlessness of Rhus-t. will be found to qualify the symptoms in a large proportion of the
cases in which it will be called for. It is as restless as Aeon, and Ars., but in a different way from either. With
Rhus-t. it is due to the pain and soreness, temporarily better by movement or a nervous internal uneasiness
which makes the patient want to be on the move when there is no particular pain present.
Conditions can often change from Rhus-t. to Bry., as well as the reverse. Hahnemann wrote about “these two
antagonistic sister remedies.”
Each in its place successfully met with typhus which prevailed in the countries desolated by the war which
raged from the summer of 1813 and onwards. Of 183 cases treated by Hahnemann in Leipzig, not one died.
Hahnemann perceived the keynote of the Rhus-t. symptoms: “We observe,” he said in his preface to the
proving, “this curious action, the severest symptoms and sufferings are excited when the body or the limb is at
rest and kept as much as possible without movement.
“The opposite of this, namely, an increase of the symptoms by movement in much more rarely observed.” He
contrasted Rhus-t. with Bry., which has almost the same rheumatic pains but with opposite modalities.
Hahnemann pointed out another keynote of Rhus-t. : “Multiplied experience has taught me that Rhus-t. is the
most efficacious and the specific remedy for the frequently fatal effects of over-lifting inordinate exertions of
the muscles and contusions.” He mighthave been led to this inference by the “bruised and sprain-like pains”
and “stiffness” of the provings. Rhus-t. is in the front rank of vulneraries.
Restlessness in fevers, typhoid and other. Clouded sensorium, stupefaction, muttering delirium. Characteristic
stiffness, better heat, manipulation. Worse remaining inone place and sitting. Worse damp weather, causes
stiffness. Worse in the morning, better from hot shower. Worse twilight (Puls., Phos.).
Demands exertion, better from exertion, exercise. Tendency to overwork physically. Stiff personality.
Worrisome. Tendency to dwell on things. Projects into the future. Difficulty relaxing. Can turn to exercise as a
cure for tension, may become an addiction.
Irritable, bored without a physical outlet. Can have fixed ideas, superstitions. Fear of notfunctioning, of injury.
May have ahistory of auto accidents, fear of accidents, of fast motion in a car (Calc.). Fear of infection.
Rheumatoid arthritis. Rheumatic paraplegia from getting wet, lying on damp ground, sleeping in damp sheets
after exertion, after childbirth, sexual excess or fevers. Paralysis of single limbs. Numbness of parts paralyzed.
Facial neuralgia, lumbago and sciatica (left side) with restlessness, coming on after a wetting or after a bath.
Ptosis. Neuralgic pains.
Burning pains, better heat, particularly in blistering skin rashes or allergic reactions. Skin can feel tight, like its
wrapped. Dermatitis. Chickenpox (Puls., Sulph., Ant-t., Ant-c.). Scalp sensitive, worse turning hair back.
 Herpes zoster. Herpes alternating with asthma and dysentery. Fever blisters around mouth, herpes in the
mouth. Yellow blisters in herpes. Shingles. Inflamed and burning blisters.
Rheumatic fever. Flu. Chronic sinusitis, colds and sore throats. Sore throat with hoarseness. Straining,
rheumatic coughs. In intermittents, “cough during the chill.” Taste of blood with cough (no blood being raised).
Chokes easily on swallowing. Swallowing causes pain in middle of back.
Tongue is dry or dark, coated with a triangular red tip. Craving for cold drinks, milk, yogurt and cheese. Dairy
relaxes. Likes sweets. Aversion to meat and bread. Anorexia. Nausea in chest. Hour-glass contraction of
abdomen.
Threatened miscarriage from a sprain. Prolonged after pains and other effects of the strain of a severe labor.
Axillary abscess from severe labor.
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Bathing with milk and Grindelia lotion very effective. Aloe vera gel topically.
Desensitizing against Poison Ivy by use of ascending doses of the low potencies by mouth is recommended.
Especially for acute reactions: Rhus-t. 30c and 200c and Anae., Crot-t.. Grind., Mez., Cypr., Plumbg. - eczema
of vulva., Graph. Compare: (1) Rhus-r. (2) Rhus-d. - California Poison-oak, antidote to Rhus-t., violent skin
symptoms with frightful itching, much swelling of face, hands and genitals, skin very sensitive, eczema and
erysipelas, great nervous weakness, tired from least effort, goes to sleep exhausted. (3) Xero. - dysmenorrhea
and skin symptoms. (4) Am., Bapt., Lach., Ars., Hyos. (4) Op. - stupefactions more profound. (5) Mim-h. -
Sensitive Plant - rheumatism, knee stiff, sharp pains in back and limbs. Swelling of ankles. Legs tremble. (6)
Ampe-tr. - Toxic dermatitis due
to vegetable poisons. Very similar to Rhus poisoning. Complementary: Bry., Calc-f. Phyt. (Rheumatism). In
urticaria follow with Bov. Inimical: Apis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - rhus-t. Rhus toxicodendron. Poison oak. N. O. Anacardiaceae. Tinctureof fresh leaves gathered
at sunset just before flowering time. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abortion. Acne, rosacea. After- pains. Allergies. Amenorrhea. Ankleinjuries. Anus, fissure.
Appendicitis. Appetite, lost. Arthritis. Beriberi.Back,injuries. Bones,pain. Cecum, inflammation. Chilblains.
Circulation, poor. Cyanosis. Dengue fever. Dermatitis. Diarrhea. Diphtheria.Dislocated,joints. Dysentery.
Dysmen

name: Rhus Venenata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rhus-v. Rhus venenata. Poison elder. Poison sumac. Swamp sumac. N. O. Anacardiacae. North
America in swampy ground. Tincture of fresh leaves and stem. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Boils. Chilblains. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysphagia. Eczema. Emptions. Erysipelas. Erythema
nodosum. Glands, cervical, ulceration. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Hydroa. Impetigo. Irritation. Lips, swollen, sore.
Lumbago. Measles. Menorrhagia. Ophthalmia. Paraplegia. Prurigo. Purpura. Scabies. Sore throat. Stiff neck.
Tongue, cracked. Urticaria.
HERBAL - Named “Rhus Vernix,” the name belongs properly to the allied Vamish-tree of Japan. Rhus-v. in
one of the most actively poisonous of the Rhus.; the skin symptoms of this species are most severe.
HOMEOPATHIC - P.B.Hoyt,whofirstdrew attention to it and made the first provings, said it is more poisonous
than Rhus-t., which he could handle with impunity, while he was violently affected by Rhus-v. in spite of
extreme caution. Further, he considered it more actively curative in a case of Rhus sore throat, when Rhus-t.
failed, Rhus-v. acted with excellent effect.
Persons poisoned by Rhus-t. are more liable to be poisoned by Rhus-v. Children are more readily poisoned
than adults. Rhus-v. in the potency is credited with the cure of Rhus-t. poisoning.
Butman observed that blondes are more susceptible to Rhus-v. poisoning than brunettes. When once affected,
persons are liable to a renewal of the affection (without further poisoning) each year at the same time.
Rhus-v. has many symptoms referring to the bones and, according to Hering, it affects those parts where the
bones are directly covered with skin, especially the forehead, backs of fingers, etc.
Pain as if sprained. “Pain half way down the esophagus” which is probably a variant of the Rhus-t. “Pain
between the shoulders on swallowing food.” Eating raw things aggravates burning of lips. Diarrhea 4 a.m.
Washing with cold water or snow improves itching on back. Chills in warm room.
Clarke found Rhus-v. an excellent remedy for arsenical overdosing. A minor use of Rhus-v. is as a topical
remedy in itching, burning chilblains. The tincture painted on relieves almost instantly and practically cures the
chilblains in a large number of cases.
MIND - Great melancholy. Gloomy and depressed. No desire to live.
Abdomen - Pain in hypogastrium before every stool. Stools with colicky pains, expelled with force. Profuse,
watery, white stools in morning, 4 a.m.
Back - Back very stiff. Sharp pain under left scapula, extending through to ribs. Rheumatic pains between
scapulae. Lumbago from a strain or a cold.
Breasts - Burning in left breast and left side of body. Breast must be supported, it aches when it hangs down,
Chest - Violent stitches through chest with great suddenness.
Ears - Transient stitches in right concha. Jerk-like tearing in bone behind right ear. Earache, hammering-
 throbbing deep in ear after dark. Jerk-like cutting stitches in ear. Vesicular inflammation of ears.
Eyes - Eyes nearly closed with great swelling, red. Eyes ache as though pressed on. Eyes feel as if sand in
them.
Face - Heaviness in swollen face. Boring in right upper jaw. Itching of upper lip and chin. Lips sore, swollen,
blistered, cracked. Sensation as if sand on lips.
Female - Menses with very large clots like pieces of meat. Soreness of vagina during menses.
Head - Heavy, frontal headache, worse walking or stooping.
Limbs - Paralytic drawing in right arm, especially wrist and extending to fingers.
Modalities - Better moderate exercise or open air. Better hot bath, gently rubbing and scratching. Worse
before stools. Worse damp days, hot weather. Worse rest, after waking, morning. Worse mental exertion,
touch and pressure. Motion aggravates pain in elbow. Walking aggravates frontal headache.
Neck - Stiff neck or crick in neck. Ulceration of cervical glands.
Nose - Nose red and shiny, redness not removed by pressure. Nose dry, sore. Erysipelas. Both nostrils filled
with tenacious mucus. Loss of smell.
Rectum - Neuralgic pains in anus. Intolerable burning and itching in anus. Bleeding hemorrhoids with
extensive itchings and burning. Discharge of blood from rectum after a stool.
Sensations - As if mouth and throat had been scalded. As if sand on lips in mouth. Sensation in arm as if the
bone would break. Pains wander about, upward and downward along the periosteum, come and go suddenly,
chill runs up back.
Skin - Vesicles. Erysipelas, skin dark red. Itching, relieved by hot water. Erythema nodosum with nightly
itching and pains in long bones.
Temperature - Chills over whole body, run up back even when warm and in a warm room. Feeling of coldness
when moving.
Throat - Irritation and acridity about throat and eyes. Tonsils red, congested, dull aching distress in them.
Soreness left side throat. Frequent desire to swallow. Swallowing difficult.
Tongue - Red at tip. Fissured in middle. Vesicles on under side.
COMMENTS - Hoyt, wishing to prepare a tincture, went to a swamp and procured a sample. He wore a pair
of buckskin gloves and kept carefully to the windward side of the plant.
Nevertheless, in an hour and a half a most intense itching and burning (more burning) set in scrotum and
penis. The glans was very painful, slight friction better for a moment the itching but nor the burning.
The symptoms continued through the next day. At 11 a.m. he made the tincture, using great caution in
manipulating the plant. At 3 p.m. itching and burning began on back of right hand. A restless night followed.
He awoke in the morning with itching, especially on palmar surface of wrists. This spread all over his body,
symptoms steadily advancing. Dizziness, eyes and ears became affected, fever set in. When the symptoms
passed off it was found that some chronic dyspeptic symptoms and inflammation of the eyes had been much
benefited.
Clarke frequently used Rhus-v. with good effect in skin diseases. Bayes told him of a case of universal eczema
with intense in an old man which he cured in a fortnight with Rhus-v.
A case of pemphigus in a young man of 27 came after years of treatment under allopathic specialists who had
given him arsenic until they could give no more, telling him at the same time that nothing but arsenic could do
him any good. Rhus-v. 3x and 30c completely cured in a few month and the cure enabled the patient to marry.
Hale had a case showing the comparative action of Rhus-v. with Rhus-r and Rhus-t. A woman had several
times every year a sore mouth with intense redness of mucus membrane of tongue, cheeks and fauces, in
small vesicular points intense burning and feeling as if mouth and throat had been scalded.
If unchecked, every mucus membrane, including those of rectum and vagina, became involved. No remedy
helped until Rhus was tried. Rhus-r. and Rhus-t. only slightly relieved, but Rhus- v. 3c always removed the
affection quickly.
RELATIONS -Antidote: Clem. The California Poison-oak (Rhus-d.) is identical with it. It antidotes: Rad. and
follows it well. Compare: (1) Skin - Anae., Com., Rhus-t. (2) Stitching pains, Kali-c. (3) Wandering pains, Puls.
(4) Pains come and go suddenly, Lyc. (5) Pain at root of tongue, Kali-i.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Ribes Nigrum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ribs-n. Ribes nigrum. Black currant. Leaves, fruit. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Arteriosclerosis. Arthritis. Colic. Gout. Gums, bleeding. Hoarseness. Kidney, problems.
Rheumatism. Sore, throat.
 HERBAL - Ribes nigra is a diaphotic, diuretic, sudorific, refrigerant, detergent, and has been used as a
substitute for tea as it also contains tannins. The leaf tea stimulates the kidneys and is good for gouty and
rheumatic problems, as well as for arteriosclerosis. Drunk cold, it is also useful for hoarseness and other throat
ailments.
Both the leaf tea and the expressed juice of the berries can be used for whooping cough in children. The
berries or their juice is beneficial for kidney problems and colic pains. An infusion of the dried berries can be
used as a gargle for inflammation in the mouth and throat and as a mouthwash for bleeding gums.

name: Ribonucleinicum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rib-ac. Ribonucleinicum acidum. RNA. Ribo nucleinic acid. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Cancer. Eczema. Epilepsy. Herpes. Hypoglycemia. Hypotension. Hypothyroidism.
Insomnia. Leukemia. Urticaria. Varicose ulcer. Weight, unstable.
HOMEOPATHIC - The proving of RNA was conducted in 1971 and 1972, by O. A. Julian. Twenty-two people,
two females, took part in the experiment, taking the 3x, 7c, and 30c potencies, plus a placebo, in a single-blind
trial.
Symptoms are the result of provings incorporated with the clinical research of several Belgian homeopaths,
including Dr. Guiot of Wavre who gave a report on a self-proving. Recommended by Jenaer for treatment for

Lively feeling, optimistic, dynamic. General lassitude. Lessened physical strength. Feels depressed, ill at ease
in his skin. Wants to run, to disappear. Tiredness, vertigo, stiffness. Tired in the morning to the point of not
hearing the alarm bell ring. Sleepiness.
Extreme chilliness. Cortical and medullary hyposthenia. Endocrine glands produce a mucus which is too
viscous. Slight edema of the feet and hands.
Desire to sleep, to eat, to make love. Hunger with need to nibble throughout the day, especially sugar.
Unstable weight, sudden increase in weight, then sudden loss of weight two days later.
WIND - Psychological and physical slowness. Mental over-exertion. Cannotconcentrate on intellectual work.
Dullness of mind. Slowness at schoolwork. Personality disorders in children.
Ugly character. Aggressiveness. Wants everything and nothing. Cannot bear anything, cries at anything.
Clings on to everything, breaks everything and becomes even more annoyed. Feels as if he is living on his
nerves. Desire to go away, to escape. Feels weary and leaves everybody.
Abdomen - Distention, especially at the end of the afternoon. Cramps in the transverse colon at 4 p.m. Biliary
sycosis. Entero- pancreatic syndrome.
Back - Joint pains in the shoulders and feet. Pain all along the vertebral column.
Blood - Circulatory discomfort. Hypotension. Leucopenia. Leukemia.
Constitutions - Allergic, psoric, tubercular constitutions. Cancerous conditions.
Female - Increase in libido. Sexual weakness. Frigidity. Fetid leucorrhea. Mycosis vaginitis.
Food - Extreme hunger. Must eat often. Strong desire and need to eat sugar. Hypoglycemia. Hungry
sensations. Desires vinegar and cold, spicy food, which goes down more easily. Aversion to fats and hot food.
Loss of appetite.
Limbs - Lymphaedema. Arthralgia in the back and lumbar regions. Swelling of the lower limbs, more marked
in the morning and the evening. Hands and feet slightly swollen. Infection around the nails, es
pecially of the index, second and third fingers of the right hand.
Male - Increase in libido. Impotence.
Modalities - Better from lying on the stomach (Med.), worse from lying on the back. Worse from the cold.
Mouth - Fever sores on the middle of the lower lip.
Nose - Small pimples in the nostrils.
Rectum - Tendency to constipation. Watery diarrhea with colic.
Skin - Recurring herpes. Tendency to eczema. Chronic recurring eczema. Small red patches on the forehead,
disappearing rapidly. Urticaria. Varicose ulcer. Fissures on the heels and the skin of the heels flakes off in long
strips. Tendency to reopening of old healed ulcerations.
Sleep - Sleepiness around noon, beginning of the afternoon. Persistent insomnia, between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m.
Sleeps badly, wakes up excited and tired.
Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) DNA, Sil., Cor- tiso.. Tub. (2) Alf. - increase appetite, weight gain. (3) Cann-s. -
appetite increased, desire for sweets.
 REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Ricinus Communis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ric. Ricinus communis. Castor oil bean. Palma christi. N. O. Euphorbiaceae. Tincture made with
hot alcohol and water. Trituration of fresh seeds. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Aphthae. Arthritis. Breast, disorders. Breast-feeding. Cholera. Cholera infantum.
Constipation. Diarrhea. Duodenum, catarrh. Dysentery. Eruptions. Gangrene. Gastro-enteritis. Jaundice.
Muscle pain. Peritonitis. Sprains.
HERBAL - The castor oil plant is a native of Egypt and India. In the tropics, it is a small tree growing to the
height of eight or ten feet. It can be cultivated as an annual, its stems reaching from three to five feet.
Castor oil, obtained from the seeds, can be rubbed into muscles and joints. Castor oil packs, warm oil-soaked
flannel, can beapplied to inflamed tissues or organs. Leaves can be applied topically.
The blandest form in common use is “cold drawn,” i.e., expressed without the aid of heat and contains the
smallest amount of the acrid principle. A decoction of the seeds, used in the East and West Indies, contains a
much larger proportion.
Ric. has great power over breast-feeding. O. McWilliams observed in the Cape Verde Islands that the leaves
of the plant were applied to the breasts to increase the flow of milk if it were delayed and even to produce it in
women who had never borne children or who had not suckled for years.
In increasing the flow of milk in nursing women, the breasts were fomented with a decoction of the leaves of
the plant, the boiled leaves being afterwards thinly spread on the breasts.
For producing milk in others more vigorous measures were resorted to. The women had to sit over a boiling
decoction of the leaves, care being taken to prevent the escape of steam. When the decoction was sufficiently
cool the parts were bathed with it, and also the breasts to which the leaves were applied as in the other case.
Women with well-developed breasts were more easily influenced. When the breasts were small and shriveled
this treatment acted more on the uterine system, bringing on the menses long before their time or causing
immediate flow if the time is near.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hale made the first collection of the pathogenetic effects of Ric. and pointed out its analogy
to cholera, which Salzer confirmed.
Cases of poisoning, some of them fatal, have been recorded from the ordinary oil, but the greater number of
the pathogenetic effects have resulted from eating the seeds. Fatal effects have followed eating three seeds,
and one seed has caused violent effects. After twenty seeds, gastroenteritis and death preceded by general
convulsions and collapse occurred.
Ric. has marked action on gastro-intestinal tract. Vomiting and purging. Very painful cramps in trunk and limbs.
Collapse. Con-
vulsions. Muscular contractions. Languor and weakness. Pale and listless. Anemia. Profound adynamia.
The leaves have an especially powerful action on the breasts and female generative organs. Increases the
quantity of milk in nursing women.
Abdomen - Rumbling. The different parts of the abdominal muscles can be seen successively and individually
contracting under the skin. Feels as if all the intestines violently drawn together. Violent colic and yellowish
green vomiting. Cramps with the diarrhea. Pain over abdomen, worse by pressure.
Back - Pains in back like after-pains.
Breasts - Breasts thick, swollen with swelling of axillary glands and pains running down arms. Thin discharge
from breasts, becomes milky. Brings milk in breasts of virgins and women who have not nursed for years.
Ears - Buzzing and humming in ears.
Eyes - Conjunctiva is injected. Copious lachrymation, pupils only moderately dilated. Eyes convulsed and
turned up.
Face - Face slightly congested. Face pale, features strongly contracted. Twitchings of mouth.
Female - Menses too early, excessive. Leucorrhea.
Food - Anorexia. Thirst, great, burning.
Head - Brain seems exhausted and easily overpowered, in open air. Severe headache. Sudden pain as if
seized by something in occiput extending around to backs of ears, eyes and forehead with rush of blood to
head and shocks which come and go as from electricity, thirty times in five days.
Heart - Pulse is extremely small, scarcely perceptible, though normal in frequency.
Kidneys - Complete anuria. Passes a little dark, thick, highly albuminous urine.
Limbs - Prurigo on wrists and bends of knees. Gangrene of one foot necessitates amputation.
Mouth - Tongue, coated white and dry, furred. Salivation.
 Rectum - Incessant diarrhea with cramps and chilliness, colliquative like cholera. Diarrhea without pain. Violent
purging with the diarrhea. Rice-water stools. Stools serous liquid mixed with mucus. Bloody diarrhea. Complete
confinement of bowels for five days, causing headache.
Skin - Pronounced jaundice, skin saffron yellow. Pruriginous eruptions or redness and itching, at wrists and
bends of knees.
Sleep - Great desire for sleep.
Stomach - Pit of stomach very sensitive, pains radiate from this center, shooting to umbilicus and
hypochondria. A kind of bar across stomach, which caused profound anguish. Cramps, burning in stomach.
Heartburn. Nausea and vomiting persistent, vomited mattery liquid, slightly colored by a little bile, contains only
a few mucus threads in suspension. Vomiting and purging. Painless vomiting. Vomiting profuse with burning
in gullet and all the symptoms of Asiatic cholera.
Temperature - Chilliness with the diarrhea. Skin moist and cool, especially lower limbs. Forehead covered
with cold sweat. Perspiring freely.
Throat - Burning pain in the gullet accompanied the vomiting. Voice altered, veiled.
COMMENTS - Salzer gave to Ric. the same importance in cholera with diarrhea that Camph. occupies in
relation to spasmodic cholera. The stools of Ric. correspond exactly to the rice-water stools in cholera, while
those of Ver-a. do not.
Ric. also has painless evacuations which are met with in many cases of cholera. Ric. therefore corresponds
to the diarrhea stage of cholera and also to the collapse stage if vomiting and purging continue.
Salzer quoted B. L. Bhaduri as having observed “rice-water stools, cramps and suppression of urine brought
on by eating the seeds.”
Hale said that before he had learned to used Ric. as a homeopathic remedy he has often been discomfited by
seeing aphthous diarrhea cured with small (half-teaspoonful) doses of castor oil, repeated three or four
times a day, by old nurses or impatient mothers.
Such diarrhea often arises in improperly- fed children. It begins with sickness, frequent and griping
evacuations, greenish yellow to dark green, becoming more liquid and more or less mixed with slimy or
gelatinous mucus or blood.
Each stool is accompanied with pain and tenesmus, mouth dry and aphthous. The anus is inflamed, belly tumid
and painful, child becoming more and more feverish and somnolent.
Hale later gave a Ric. lx trituration of the oil with sugar. In acute and chronic dysentery and in those cases in
which there is impaction of feces. Hale saw the oil promptly curative.
Hering remarked that puerperal fever had become much less common in Philadelphia (where it used to be
very common) since homeopaths interdicted the use of castor oil in confinements.
Tyler Smith experimented with the leaves, in his cases the application produced swelling of the breasts,
throbbing and other pains in them, swelling of the axillary glands with pains running down the arms.
Pains in the back like after-pains were caused in every case. Leucorrhea was increased. Discharges from the
breasts became milky and menses came on too soon. The radiating pains, bar sensation, constricting and
cramping pains are the most peculiar.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Tea tree oil. Olive oil. (2) Crot-t., Jatr. and Euphorbiaceae. (3) In cholera, rice-
water stools, Agar. Phos., Jatr. (4) Galactagogues, Alf., Agn-c. Asaf., Lee., Puls.
(5) Duodenal catarrh, Berb., Chin., Hydr., Lyc., Merc., Podo.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
