name: Ritalin
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rital. Ritalin. Methylphenidate hydrochloride. An allopathic stimulant drug. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Attention deficit disorder. Bi-polar. Coma. Convulsions. Delirium. Depression.
Dermatitis. Dizziness. Drowsiness. Dyslexia. Fever. Glaucoma. Hair, loss. Hallucinations. Headaches. Hives.
Hyperactivity. Insomnia. Learning, disability. Narcolepsy. Nausea. Nervousness. Palpitations.
Schizophrenia. Tremors. Tourette’s syndrome. Twitchings. Urticaria. Vomiting. Weight, loss.
HOMEOPATHIC - Methylphenidate is a central nervous system stimulant. Excessive doses of Ritalin over a
long period of time can produce addiction; it is also possible to develop tolerance to the drug, so that larger
doses are needed to produce the original effect.
Common side effects may include an inability to fall or stay asleep, nervousness. In children, loss of appetite,
abdominal pain, weight loss during long-term therapy, inability to fall or stay asleep, and abnormally fast
heartbeat.
 Chest pain. Abnormal heartbeat. Palpitations. Fluttery or throbbing heartbeat. Pulse changes. Rapid heartbeat.
Blood pressure changes. Dizziness. Abnormal muscular movements. Jerking. Joint pain. Severe twitching.
Reddish or purplish skin spots. Hives. Skin reddening. Skin inflammation with peeling. Skin rash. Hair loss.
Headache. Fever. Drowsiness. Abdominal pain. Loss of appetite. Nausea. Retardation of growth in children.
MIND -Attention deficit disorder. Distracted. Short attention span. Learning disability. Dyslexia.
Hyperactivity. Agitation. Confusion. Emotional impulsivity. Feeling of elation. Nervousness and
restlessness. Depression.
Delirium. Hallucinations. Psychotic episodes. Paranoia. Bipolar disorder. Schizophrenia. Minimal brain
damage.
Tourette’s syndrome.
Abdomen - Abdominal pain.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Chest pain.
Blood - Increased blood pressure. Leukopenia, and anemia. Necrotizing vasculitis. Thrombocytopenic
purpura. Increased blood sugar.
Eyes - Dilated pupils. Glaucoma. Blurred vision. Difficulty with accommodation.
Food - Loss of appetite. Weight loss. Head - Headaches. Alopecia. Hair loss. Heart - Angina pectoris. Blood
pressure changes. High blood pressure. Cardiac arrhythmias. Abnormally fast heartbeat. Palpitations and
irregular heartbeats.
Limbs - Arthralgia. Joint pain. Muscle cramps. Hyper reactive reflexes. Abnormal muscular movements.
Jerking. Convulsions. Tremors and tics. Twitchings. Tourette’s syndrome (severe twitching).
Skin - Reddish or purplish skin spots. Pruritus. Urticaria. Hives. Skin reddening. Skin inflammation with peeling.
Exfoliative dermatitis, erythemamultiforme. Dryness of mucus membranes.
Sleep - Insomnia. Inability to fall or stay asleep. Drowsiness. Narcolepsy.
Stomach - Loss of appetite. Nausea, vomiting.
Temperature - Extremely elevated body temperature. Heat, flushing.
Vertigo - Dizziness.
COMMENTS - Exaggerated feeling of elation. Hyperactivity. Agitation, confusion. Transient depressed moods.
Nervousness and insomnia. Delirium. Psychotic episodes including hallucinations.
Dry mucus membranes. Dilated pupils. Extremely elevated body temperature, flushing. Fever. Sweating.
Vomiting. Dizziness, drowsiness, headache, and dyskinesia. Headaches. High blood pressure. Irregular or
rapid heartbeat.
Rash, pruritus, urticaria. Exfoliative dermatitis, erythema multiforme with histopathological findings of
necrotizing vasculitis, and thrombocytopenic purpura. Alopecia. Arthralgia. Muscle twitching. Tremors.
Convulsions, muscle cramps, choreo- athetoid movements, tics, or exacerbation of pre-existing tics, Tourette’s
syndrome.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Robinia Pseudacacia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rob. Robinia pseudacacia. Yellow locust. Common acacia. False acacia. North American locust.
N. O. Leguminosae. Papilionoideae. Tincture of fresh bark of young twigs. Trituration of the beans. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Acidity. Belchings. Coryza.Dys- pepsia. Flatulence. Headaches. Heartburn. Hyperchlorhydna.
Indigestion. Intermittents. Neuralgia. Stomach, disorders. Urticaria.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany stated “The roots of Robinia have the taste and smell of liquorice, but are
a dangerous poison and accidents have occurred from their being mistaken for liquorice roots.”
HOMEOPATHIC - The recorded poisonings were due to eating the beans or chewing the bark. Of thirty-two
boys so poisoned, in the mildest cases there was vomiting of ropy mucus, dilatation of pupils, dry throat,
flushed face.
In the severest, the vomit was more copious and mixed with blood with retching, epigastric pains, debility,
stupor, cold limbs, dusky pallor, heart’s action feeble intermittent, limbs pulseless. Recovery took place in two
days.
Acidity of children. Child cries when its arms were laid hold. Sour infants with sour smell of the body,
sour stools and vomiting of sour milk.
Hyperchlorhydria, when the belchings and taste is sour and vomiting is so sour that it sets the teeth on edge
or dulls them. The gastric symptoms with the most pronounced acidity are well authenticated and are the
guiding symptoms. Acid dyspepsia. Burning in stomach and between scapulae. Squeezing in stomach.
 Heartburn and acidity worse lying down especially at night. Water brash.
Albuminoid digestion is too rapid and starch digestion is perverted. Intensely acrid belchings. Acrid and
greenish vomiting, colic and flatulence, nightly burning pains in stomach and constipation with urgent desire.
Stools and perspiration sour. Incarcerated flatus. Acidity accompanied by frontal headache. Constant dull
frontal headache worse motion and reading. Sick headache with acid vomiting.
MIND - Excessively irritable. Very low-spirited. Tried to write but could not. Can hardly tell what she is doing.
Abdomen - Constant dullness in epigastric region with cutting pains in stomach and bowels and a good deal
of rumbling. Burning distress in stomach and region of gallbladder. Bowels greatly distended with flatulence,
seemed to fill up whole abdomen, tympanites, better passing flatus. Soreness in bowels when moving or from
pressure.
Causations - Ill effects from fat, gravies, flatulent food, cabbages, turnips, new bread, ice cream, raw fruit, etc.
Eyes - Eyes sunken. Eyes sore, watery with rough throat. Pupils contracted (in poisoning cases, dilated).
Face - Neuralgic face ache, spreading to eyes, forehead, ears and teeth, changing the whole features.
Spasmodic pains in jaws, feels as if they would be broken or dislocated, intensely sour taste in mouth. Face
flushed (in mild poisoning cases), dusky, pale (in severe cases).
Female - Menses too late, black. Bleeding between the periods, accompanied by purulent leucorrhea.
Leucorrhea, acrid, fetid, whitish, greenish, yellowish, thick and purulent. Ulcerative pains in vagina with acrid,
yellowish leucorrhea of most fetid smell. Cramps in uterus. Tumefaction and bruised feeling in neck of womb
and general prostration. Hard swelling of uterus. Herpes on vagina and vulva. Nymphomania.
Food - Worse from eating, fats, cabbages, turnips, raw fruit, ice creams. Thirst.
Head - Constant dull, heavy, frontal headache, much worse by motion and reading. Dull headache, with
profuse nasal discharge and frequent sneezing, with sharp stitches in temples. Stinging pain in temples,
changing from right to left side. Gastric headache with acid vomiting. Sick headache with sour stomach from
fat meat, gravies, flatulent food, cabbage, turnips, warm bread, pastry, ice creams, raw fruits. Steady headache
with sensation as if head full of boiling water. As if brain struck against skull when moving. Unable to hold his
head upright.
Heart - Almost pulseless. Heart’s action is very feeble, embarrassed when moved from horizontal position.
Kidneys - Urine scanty, painful or profuse, turbid.
Limbs - Could not move in slightest degree fingers, hands, arms or legs, later could move fingers of right hand
a little, later could stir legs, but not draw them up, tickling feet caused much distress.
Lungs - Voice reduced to a whisper and efforts to cry exceedingly feeble, suddenly ceasing with a slight sigh,
as if from exhaustion. Feeble respiration.
Modalities - Worse at night, by motion. Neuralgia from contact of food, worse by touch. Headache worse by
reading. Heartburn and acidity worse lying down. Nausea and vomiting worse being raised from the horizontal.
Mouth - Burning, sharp pains, especially in carious teeth, spreading to cheeks, eyes and temples, worse at
night or on contact of food, especially if cold or spiced. Teeth become loosened from the spongy and easily
bleeding gums. White coating on tongue with red tip. Tongue covered with whitish-brown fur, smooth and
slimy. Mucus membrane of mouth pale.
Nose - Profuse continual discharge from nostrils with sneezing and dull headache. Wax-like tumor on nose.
Rectum - Heat and pressure in epigastrium, cramps. Bowels costive with frequent ineffectual desire for stool.
Desire for stool, but only flatus passes, finally constipated stool. Sudden attacks of purging and vomiting. Stools
are loose, black,
Robinia pseudacacia fetid with great tenesmus, watery, whitish, excessively frequent and generally
involuntary. Sour stools of infants with sour smell from body and vomiting of sour milk. Diarrhea stools,
yellow, green, burning with nervous agitation, weakness, cold sweat, dyspnea. Sensation as if whole body
would pass away with stool. The daily motion has a slimy look and bilious tinge.
Sensations - As if head were full of boiling water. As if brain revolved. As if brain struck against skull. Jawbone
as if dislocated. Stomach as if scalded. As if whole body would pass away with stool. The left side was most
affected. A sleepy, dull feeling in head and limbs changed from right to left.
Skin - Covered from head to foot with urticaria.
Sleep - Sleepiness and dullness in limbs and head. Restless sleep all night on account of frequent sneezing
from indigestion.
Stomach - Everything turns to acid. Sour stomach. Regurgitation of acid and bitter substances. Heartburn
and acidity of stomach at night on lying down. Heavy, aching dullness in stomach. Very severe, sharp pains in
stomach all day and night. Great distention of stomach and bowels. Flatulent colic (Cham., Dios.). Nausea
with sour belchings. Profuse vomiting of an intensely sour fluid (Sul-ac.). Vomiting of ropy mucus, tinged
with blood, retching and epigastric pains. Vomiting with slight convulsions.
 Temperature - Hands and feet cold. Hectic fever with night-sweats. Paroxysms of pain late in afternoon,
lasting until 3 to 4 a.m., face hippocratic, much flatulence.
Throat - Dry scratching in throat, with flushing of face. Rough soreness, with sore eyes.
Vertigo - Faintness, worse when raised from horizontal position. Vertigo and dullness of head in whatever
position it is placed. Sensation as if brain revolved, worse lying on right side. Vertigo with unsteadiness and
nausea.
COMMENTS - The provings of Burt and Spranger developed the symptoms which have led to the chief clinical
uses, but some of Houatt’ s symptoms have also been confirmed. Clinical experience has added to the
symptoms.
Among Houatt’s symptoms was a facial neuralgia spreaditig to eyes, forehead with contraction of the jaw and
features and also a sensation as if the jaws would be dislocated or fractured. Hering gave a case of neuralgia
as having been cured with Rob. “Jawbone feels as if dislocated intensely sour taste and vomiting.”
The paralytic symptoms were very marked in one of the poisoning cases. Flatulence and diarrhea were
produced and also constipation with constant ineffectual urging.
The chief keynote of Rob. is acidity, especially at night. Cooper observed improvement under Rob. cease at
night-time.
Sour stomach, heartburn and acidity coming on when lying down at night and preventing sleep. Vomiting of
intensely sour fluid which set the teeth on edge. Belchings of a very sour fluid. Sour stools of infants with sour
smell of body and vomiting of sour milk.
Halbert related a case of hyperchlorhydria treated with Rob. Mrs. S., 40, had stomach troubles for many years,
for which she had bitter tonics, stomach douching, and electric massage. She had acid belchings and vomitings
of intensely sour food.
Extreme appetite, but gastric pains an hour or two after meals. Stomach and bowels distended with gas almost
constantly, and extremely irritating flatulence. Craved meats, but could not tolerate vegetables. Craved solid
food, but did not dare take it. Emaciated and cachectic.
Lavage was performed every alternate day and after it the patient was directed to eat a full meal. Rob. 3x was
given every two hours and steady improvement occurred in ally particulars, until health was practically
restored.
Burt had a severe neuralgia in left temple, preventing sleep from midnight to daylight. He had also a “dull,
heavy aching in stomach,” and a “constant dull, heavy frontal
Robinia pseudacacia headache, much worse by motion and reading.” The combination of gastric and head
symptoms has placed Rob. among the chief remedies in migraine and sick headaches.
A. L. Fisher relieved with Rob., when everything else failed, the intensely acid vomiting in four cases of gastric
cancer.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cyt-1. (2) In acidity, Rheum, Calc., Aeth., Mag-c., Puls. (3) In neuralgia, Ars.,
Chin., Flatulence, Chin., Carb-v., Lyc. (4) Ineffectual urging to stool, Nux-v. (5) Gastric headaches, Iris- v. (6)
Jawbone as if dislocated, Rhus-t. (7) Changing sides, Lac-c. (Rob. Right to left). (8) Heart, Phase. (9) Dilated
pupils, dry throat and flushed face, Bell.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Rock Rose
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rck-r-b. Rock rose. Helianthe- mum nummularium. Rock Rose flowers are gathered and put in
a sunlit bowl of water for several hours. The water imbued with healing power is strained and prepared as
medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy
or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into
the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - This remedy belongs to Bach’s group “For Those who Have Fear,” with Mimul-b., Cher-
p-b., Asp-b. and Rd- ch-b. Rck-r-b. treats states of intense fear and panic, plus a chronically weakened nervous
system.
Acute anxiety states cause accelerated heartbeat and breathing, shortness of breath, choking sensation, dry
mouth, indigestion with possible nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, dizziness and fainting and internal and
external trembling.
Chronic, advanced nervousness, characterized by nervous weakness, insomnia, lack of physical and
mental/emotional endurance, shakiness, digestive problems including lack of appetite, heightened sensitivity
to noise and touch,first signs of a nervous breakdown and other typical symptoms of an exhausted nervous
system.
 Restores equilibrium after a nervous breakdown (Cher-p-b., Verv-b.).
MIND - Fright and heightened anxiety. Extreme agitation and nervousness. Chronic state of nervousness,
frequent starting and inner trembling. Anxiety disorders. Prolonged fearful worry, chronic loss of sleep. Exhaus-
tion of nerve power.
Anger, hatred, irrational resentment. Impatience, aggressiveness. Feelings of helplessness, despair. Easily
aroused weeping. Longing for help. Desire for peace and rest.
Frequent nightmares, fixations and obsessions of a fearful nature, as in phobias or panic disorders. Fright from
near death or the near death of a loved one. Post- traumatic stress disorder and adjustment disorder, trauma
was related to fear or terror (Star-b-b.).
Repeated fearful experiences or one-time traumas of fright have become linked with a certain person, object,
or circumstance which will trigger renewed fear on contact even when the real danger has passed.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Rock Water
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rck-w-b. Rock water. Aqua petra. Water from any special well known to carry healing power is
placed in a sunlit bowl for only one hour and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the
stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks).
This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - This remedy belongs to Bach’s group “Over-Care for Others’ Welfare,” along with Beech-
b., Vine-b., Verv-b. and Chic-b. These remedies heal the tendency to overly infl uence and control others.
Rigidity and hardening of physical structures. Excessive willpower resulting in inner tension and strain.
MIND - Disappointment or despair, leading to a sacrifice or loss of pleasure.
Inner conflict. Intense self-control, leading to personal pride and the desire to inspire others to be equally
strong. Rigidity and self-centered toughness, with frustration, sadness, depression, or anger. Hardened. Sense
of loss.
Ritualistic, perfectionist, obsessive- compulsive behavior (Cher-pl-b., Crb-a- b., Pine-b., Verv-b.). Tendency to
adhere to routines and one-sided acceptance of limitations. Self denial and habitual patterns in the
rehabilitation of addictive drugs or behavioral patterns.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Rosa Canina
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ros-ca. Rosa canina. Dog-rose. Cynorrhodon. N. O. Rosacea. Europe. Tincture of ripe fruits.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, disorders. Dysuria.
HERBAL - Rose hips are used for making the very pleasant “Confection of Roses” used in general medicine
as a basis for pills and electuaries. Rosa canina has been used in ancient times as a remedy in urinary

HOMEOPATHIC - A proving only evoked a somewhat increased flow of urine and a little heat in the urethra.
Burnett confirmed this to some extent.

***ROSA DAMASCENA (Damascus Rose) PHARMACY - ros-d. Rosa damascena. Damascus rose. Damask
rose. N. O. Rosacea. Tinctures of the flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Coryza. Deafness. Eustachian, catarrh. Hay fever. Hearing, problems. Rose-colds.
Tinnitus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hay fever and allergies. Hardness of hearing, tinnitus. Rose-colds. Eustachian catarrh
(Kali-m., Merc-d.), Eustachian tube swollen.
Farrington mentioned that Ros-d. was introduced by Jeanes as a remedy at the beginning of rose-cold when
the Eustachian tube is involved with some degree of deafness and tinnitus.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In hay fever: Phle., (Timothy grass) - Hay fever with asthma, watery coryza,

Kali-m., Merc-d. (3) Succ-ac, Sabad., Euph., Psor., Kali-hp., Napht.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Rosmarinus Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rosm. Rosmarinus officinalis. Rosemary. N. O. Labiatx. Tincture of whole plant. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Baldness. Dandruff. Dizziness. Headache. Lice. Menses, too early. Memory, weak. Miscarriage.
Sleeplessness.
HERBAL - Rosemary oil has an ancient reputation as a remedy for baldness, headache and flagging mental
powers. It has been called the “Herb of Memory,” which Shakespeare alludes to when he has Ophelia say,
“There’s Rosemary, that’s for remembrance.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Memory deficient. Head heavy, drowsy. Menses too early, violent pains followed by
uterine hemorrhage. Chilly with icy coldness of lower limbs without thirst, followed by heat.
MIND - Anxiety. Memory weak. Dullness.
Female - Violent pains followed by uterine hemorrhage and miscarriage, succeeded by faintness, spasms of
chest, cold hands and feet, small, rapid, irregular pulse. Menses four days too early.
Head - Headache. Heaviness and dullness of head. Weight and tension around head. Baldness.
Lungs - Oppression of breathing. Spasms in chest.
Skin - Hair loss. Dandruff. Lice.
Sleep - Overpowering sleepiness with yawning. Sleeplessness.
Temperature - Coldness so that she could not leave the bed. Chill over whole, legs icy cold, no thirst and no
subsequent heat.
Vertigo - Dizziness.
COMMENTS - The most violent of the symptoms of Rosm. were observed on a woman who took a strong
infusion for eight days resulting in a miscarriage. In another woman, it brought on the menses four days too
soon. Chilliness predominated, the chill not being followed by heat.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hedeo., Menth., Puls.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Rubus Fruticosus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rubu-f. Rubus fruticosus. Blackberry. Brambleberry. Dewberry. Cloudberry. Tincture of the
leaves. N. O. Rosaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Anemia. Appendicitis. Coughs. Cystitis. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Eczema. Gingivitis. Gums,
bleeding. Hemorrhoids. Insect, bites. Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia. Mouth, sores. Pharyngitis. Sore,
throat. Tonsillitis. Toothache. Ulcerations. Whooping cough. Wounds.
HERBAL - Blackberry is also known by the common names brambleberry, dewberry, and cloudberry. The
berry grows on small, bushy vines, each berry being a cluster of tiny black knobs. In England, they are often
referred to as brambleberries because of the prickly thorns, or brambles.
It is astringent, tonic, mild diuretic, and hemostatic. The fruit and juice is considered a refrigerant and tonic.
The root-bark and the leaves are strongly astringent, depurative, diuretic, tonic and vulnerary. Blackberry leaf
is more specific to the stomach and intestines. The fruit is more specific to liver and kidneys.
The root is the most astringent part. It has been used as a preventative for dropsy. It makes an excellent
remedy for diarrhea, hemorrhoids, and cystitis. The root-bark as well as the dried and powdered fruit have
been used for dysentery. Extract of the root has been used for stomach problems as well as an antidote to
poison.
In American folk medicine the root was also used for tonsillitis. It has been used as an anti-inflammatory for
conditions such as laryngitis and pharyngitis. The root decoction was once used during the spasmodic phase
of whooping cough. A decoction of the root has been used for lung problems in general, as well as amenorrhea.
Medicinally, the leaf of the Blackberry is most often used. The white underside of the leaves was said to “draw”
 while the smooth green upper side was said to “soothe.”
The leaves, root, and root bark have been used for inflammation of the throat, mouth and gums (also bleeding
gums), as well as hemorrhoids and leucorrhea. The leaves were used in England for burns and scalds.
Blackberry leaves were also used as a poultice for wounds and insect bites, and as a wash for oily skin.
Blackberry leaves have been made into a tea to ease the discomfort of sore throat. It has also been used
internally to loosen phlegm. The leaves were chewed to treat bleeding gums and mouth sores. Blackberry leaf
tea was used as a gargle to treat sore throats, mouth ulcers and gum inflammations.
A strong tea of the leaves has been used externally for eczema. Another method was to soak leaves in hot
wine to make an infusion, then placing a cloth dipped in the liquid on the ulcerations morning and evening. A
decoction of the leaves was once used as a fomentation for ulcerations.
Blackberry leaves have also been used to inhibit excessive menstrual bleeding. Blackberry tea made from the
roots was a remedy for pregnant woman who were in danger of miscarrying due to overwork. The leaves have
been used as a uterine tonic.
Blackberry tea, made of the scrapings of the bark of the branches, was used for bronchial infections. As a
poultice, it was used to treat pneumonia. Boiled vines, roots, and berries for a drink for those vomiting and
spitting blood. Boiled the cane to use as a diuretic and used a root tea for diarrhea.
The fruit and juice have been used for anemia and to regulate menses. The flowers and fruit were once used
for venomous bites and the young shoots eaten to tighten loose teeth. The ancient Greeks used blackberries
to treat gout, mouth infl animation, and bowel inflammation.
Blackberry was believed useful for appendicitis. Steeped berries in water was drunk as a vermifuge. European
settlers to North America used blackberry jam to remedy diarrhea.
Blackberry jelly was an English folk remedy for swelling of the limbs (especially those associated with heart
problems). The jelly was added to apple cider vinegar and used as a compress. Blackberry glycerite was also
used as a compress on swollen joints.
COMMENTS - The common name blackberry also includes the species Rubus villosus. Rubis lacinniatus,
Rubus procerus, and other Rubus species, which are used interchangeably with Rubus fructicosus.
The primary constituents of this herb include tannins, gallic acid, villosin, and iron. The fruit portion contains
vitamin C, niacin, pectin, sugars, anthocyanins, and flavonoids (kaempferol, quercitin).
The tannin content of blackberry leaves makes it an effective astringent. It also has diuretic properties. The
tannins in blackberries also contribute to the plant’s ability to treat diarrhea and dysentery, as well as to
constrict blood vessels, which inhibits bleeding.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Ruby
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -ruby. Ruby. Gemstone. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Anemia. Anger. Angina. Belching. Blood, disorders. Circulation, weak. Constipation.
Cough. Debility. Diarrhea. Earache. Flatulence. Heart, disorders. Heartburn. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids.
Hepatitis. High blood pressure. Immune, disorders. Infections. Leucorrhea. Migraine. Nausea. Nosebleed.
Palpitations. Vomiting. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ruby has an affinity for the blood, immune system, heart and circulation. It is a blood
cleanser, blood tonic. Wounds, stab or lacerations. Hemorrhages. Encourages speedy coagulation. Anti-septic
properties. For the after-effects of bacterial and viral infections.
Chronic fatigue and all states of debility. Poor vitality due to liver dysfunction. Chilliness, affecting one side of
the body, generally the right. Patches of cold, especially if they are felt to move around the body.
Affinity for children and adolescents and for those from the Indian sub-continent and Southeast Asia.
MIND - Clear mind, sensation of energy breaking free all over body. Mental and physical clutter. Mental
blankness with an inability to focus one’s ideas or thoughts. Forgetful. Cannot remember details. Fastidious.
Feels isolated. Helps to restore a sense of self-worth (Aur.). Feeling of unworthiness due to the recognition of
how much worse off are others, while feeling that there is nothing that can be done to redress the balance.
Sense of being consumed by worldly events or by family emotions. Inability to
let go of emotions. Guilt and shame. Resentment. Confused and distressing thoughts. Escapist daydreaming.
Anger comes up in outbursts. Anger that is expressed inappropriately. Suppressed anger (Staph.). Anger
associated with sexual frustration. Vehemence and intolerance. Impatience with slowness and poor articulation
of expression. Teenage anger.
Anticipation. Shaking or trembling with fear. Fear of new situations. Fear of the dark. Fear of one’s own dark
side, of being in someone else’s power. Fear of death, of being sacrificed.
 Abdomen - Ache in epigastrium. Epigastrial discomfort, as though the lateral edges of the muscles contract
in towards each other, better with massage. Ache in left hypochondrium. Pain in right hypochondrium. Fullness
and heaviness in lower abdomen. Sharp tweaks in lower abdomen, right side (psoas muscle), constant
heaviness like pressing down. Mild cramping in lower abdomen, comes straight up midline. Bloating more than
usual. Foul gas, nimbly (not painful), very bloated lower abdomen. Loud, painless gurgling in stomach.
Reduction in abdominal gas.
Back - Pain in lower sacral, right side. Bladder - Frequent urination.
Blood - Anemia. Blood disorders. Immune disorders.
Chest - Heat in chest and pressure in the morning, around esophagus, centrally located. Heavy constricted
chest, all day belching and heartburn, need to burp feeling, know it will taste bad. Dull pain in heart region,
lasted several minutes. Circulation feels dull.
Ears - Aching pain in left ear, with fullness like earache. Ears feel full. Hearing not registering. Heightened
sense of hearing, all sounds are so clear.
Eyes - Pupils dilated, eyes were very wild and maniacal looking. Bloodshot and glassy, red and dry. Eyes tired
and burning, itching. Pain in the corner of the right eye as if stabbed by a finger. Heavy eyelids, burning
sensation.
Face - Face puffy. Tingly cheeks. Face grayish with blemishes, irritated.
Female - Labia feels swollen and itchy. Vaginal discharge yellow and curdsy. Leucorrhea, yellow, lumpy, and
not itchy. Early sexual awareness. Increased desire. High sexual energy. Uses sex as a way of avoiding hidden
emotions. Decreased or absent sexual desire.
Food - Appetite diminished, not hungry. Appetite increased, very hungry, wakes hungry. Thirsty. More
thirstless than usual. Craving meat, salty food, fatty foods, bread.
Head - Head pain started at left front and moved to the back of my head. Migraines with nausea and vomiting,
especially when the liver is involved. Pain from the cervical area and up and over the head to the forehead.
Compression down the back from the head and neck. Sensation of pushing down on the vertex or of pushing
inwards. Head feels split. Hair fuller, thicker, healthier and stronger. Hair feels dry. Cannot detangle hair at
nape of neck.
Heart- Heart disorders. High blood pressure. Compression of the cardiac area. Pain in heart, seized up, sharp
constriction for five minutes. Pain behind the sternum as if a heart attack would come on. Angina. Palpitations.
Limbs - Right side feels alive while the left side feels dead. Tingling in the legs. Fidgety and restless. Pins and
needles in the right leg. Itching and aching in the right leg. Tweak in right hip. Feet and legs are cold.
Goosebumps on upper arms and thighs. Poison oak like rash between wrist and elbow, itching and oozing.
Mark on right arm (the underside in the middle of forearm which itches on occasion). Backs of the hands feel
itchy. Nails healthier and stronger.
Liver - Useful after hepatitis when the body is weakened and cannot restore itself to full strength.
Lungs - Cough in the middle of the night. Dry, gagging cough, with thick phlegm. Wakes with choking cough.
Male - Anger associated with sexual frustration. High sexual energy. Not interested in sex.
Mouth - Taste somewhat enhanced. Food tastes funny. Burning, dryness on sides of tongue. Pain under left
side of tongue,, at the root, could be felt even exteriorly. Sore under tongue, behind teeth, very painful. Sores
on inside of lip, on lower gums. Swollen gums.
Nose - Middle separation of nostrils is sore to touch. Rawness in nose and throat came and went, itchy and
dry. Nose very wet and damp in the morning. Pain at the root of the nose as if it is blocked. Nose plugged,
crusted, hard. Nose mucousy, tight without discharge. Intermittent sneezing, relieves. Sneezing, nose is
running, like allergies or hay fever. Profuse nosebleeds. Sensitivity to smells, especially vinegar and beer.
Everything smells different.
Perspiration - Body sweaty, unusual. Sweating at peak of anxiety attack. Sweats all night long. Hot and sweaty
had to take covers off. Apple-like smell coming off body.
Rectum - No bowel activity. Constipation. Diarrhea, explosive, loose, watery, painless. Gassy diarrhea, gassy
expulsion. Bouts of loose stool with sudden urge (9 a.m. to noon). Small stool with urination. Foul gas, nimbly,
painless. Blood from the hemorrhoids with each stool. Prolapsed old hemorrhoids.
Skin - Flushed, mottled skin. Itching rash, especially on buttocks. Itchy all over, better with scratching.
Sleep - Deep sleep. Sleep interrupted, woke often beginning at 2 a.m. then 3 a.m., 4 a.m. Awoke unrefreshed,
feeling almost drugged, hard to open eyes. Groggy in morning. Sleepy in the morning. Difficult getting up. Nap
in the afternoon, did not feel good from nap. Can’t get enough sleep.
Stomach - Digestion sluggish. Sensation of a stone in the stomach. Heaviness in the upper abdomen. Empty
pit feeling. Bloating, both flatulence and flatus. Constant heartburn. Belching to the point of interrupting
conversation. Burping loudly, involuntary, repeatedly. Foamy belching. Constant nausea. Empty, nauseous
 feeling. Nausea, not from stomach but umbilicus.
Morning sickness. Cancer.
Stool - Diarrhea, explosive, loose, watery, painless. Defecate with expulsion, gassy diarrhea, gassy expulsion.
Five bouts of loose stool with sudden urge. Small, dry stools with blood.
Teeth - Grinding teeth. Hard to floss, teeth are tight.
Throat - Heat around esophagus, in morning, with heat in chest and pressure. Burning esophagus. Closing
up. Rawness in throat and nose, came and went, itchy, dry. Instantly dry throat. Throbbing sore throat. Sore
throat, tight and dry, mild headache, sneezy, running nose. Wakes with slight dryness in back of throat, full
ears.
Urine - Smells acidic, like acidosis.
Vertigo - Some vertigo and weakness in the sun. Dizzy feeling when stands up, like wavering in a clockwise
motion.
COMMENTS - Ruby is one variant of the simple mineral corundum, the other is sapphire. Corundum is a
compound of aluminum and oxygen, AL2 03 (aluminum oxide). Chromium is responsible for the color of ruby,
while iron, titanium and other elements cause the coloration of sapphires.
The name “corundum” is derived from the Sanskrit word “kuruvinda” via the Tamil name for ruby, “kuruntam.”
The name “ruby” comes from the Latin word for red, “ruber.”
Sluggish system with low energy. Circulation feels dull and weak. Heavy feeling, body heavy like lead,
heaviness, hard to exercise. All over tiredness. Felt need to lie down, fighting gravity. Very tired in the evening,
barely made it to bed. Hungover or fluish feeling. No desire to exercise. Better as day goes on. Weight gain.
Body warm all over. Cooler temperature. Goosebumps on upper arms and thighs. Tingling all over body.
Sensation as if air were passing through certain areas of the body. All senses acute. Left ear painful with dull
ache, ear fullness.
RELATIONS - Compare: Amber, Staph., Ferr.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Anemia. Anger. Angina. Belching. Blood, disorders. Circulation, weak. Constipation.
Cough. Debility. Diarrhea. Earache. Flatulence. Heart, disorders. Heartburn. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids.
Hepatitis. High blood pressure. Immune, disorders. Infections. Leucorrhea. Migraine. Nausea. Nosebleed.
Palpitations. Vomiting. Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ruby has an affinity for the blood, immune system, heart and circulation. It

name: Rumex Acetosa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rumx-a. Rumex acetosa. Sorrel. N. O. Polygonacae. Tincture of the leaves. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Esophagus inflammation. Gastritis. Paralysis. Throat, sore. Uvula, elongated.
HERBAL - Sorrel was at one time cultivated as a salad. The Buckler-shaped or French Sorrel is cultivated in
France, where it is considered a powerful anti-scorbutic. The leaves contain a large quantity of Bin oxalate of
Potash (Kali-ox.).
HOMEOPATHIC - The Rumx-a. symptoms were observed on three men who ate largely of the leaves. In one,
very violent convulsions were induced of a peculiar kind, the limbs being thrown reciprocally backwards and
forwards and the head from side to side. The hands being alternately clenched and unclenched, the eyes
prominent.
Other remarkable symptoms included swelling of the lower eyelid. Elongated uvula. Pain all down esophagus
worse by swallowing. Persistent short, dry cough. Complete paralysis of bodily powers, copious green vomit,
constipation.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kali-ox., Lapa. (2) In persistent cough, Rumx.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Rumex Crispus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - rumx. Rumex crispus. Yellow dock. Curly dock. Sour dock. Narrow dock. N. O. Polygonaceae.
Tincture of ftesh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abortion. Acne. Anemia. Aphonia. Asthma. Botborygm.Bronchitis. Catarrh. Coms. Coryza.
Coughs. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Dyspnea. Feet, tender. Flatulence. Gastralgia. Headache. Heart, disorders.
Heartbum. Hiccough. Indigestion. Irritation. Jaundice. Lichen. Miscarriage. Mouth, ulceration. Nausea.
Nosebleeds. Phimosis. Prurigo. Rheumatism. Throat, sore. Trachea, disorders. Tuberculosis. Urticaria.
HERBAL - Rumex is an old Latin word for “lance,” referring to the shape of the leaves. Crispus means “curly,”
also in reference to the leaf shape. The yellow dock or curly dock is a common British weed, a member of the
buckwheat family. It grows abundantly throughout North America.
The common yellow dock includes the species Rumex occidentalis, Rumex venosus, Rumex obtusifolius and
Rumex sangineus, which are used interchangeably with Rumex crispus.
 The common dock of fields and roadsides, Rumex obtusifolia has a well deserved reputation among children
as the best antidote to the nettle’s sting. Rumex crispus, according to Joslin, was used by herbalists internally
and externally for the cure of scabies.
Yellow dock has been used for hundreds of years for its astringent properties, treating a variety of skin
problems, including boils, rashes, blemishes and burns. Topically, the crushed leaf of yellow dock can soothe
the stings from nettle plants.
It can also be added to a tooth powder for spongy gums, and to a gargle for laryngitis. Salves, poultices or
compresses of this herb have been used for eczema, hives, itchy skin, scabies and ringworm.
The properties of this herb are alterative, laxative, purgative, cholagogue, and astringent. It has been used for
nutritional support of the blood, lungs, and urinary system. Yellow dock is valued today as one of the best
available sources of iron. Its high iron content makes it beneficial for treating anemia and pregnant women.
Yellow dock has also been known to help improve bladder and liver functions, and reduce bowel inflammation
and glandular swelling. This herb can be used to treat some cases of jaundice, and skin eruptions associated
with the toxicity of the intestines.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hale noted that among the constituents and salts of Rumx. are Sulph. and Calc-p., and
Sulph., Calc, and Phos. are strongly represented in its action. Rumx. is a close ally of Rheum and has
analogous purgative and other properties.
The provings were made by Houghton,
Joslin, Paine, Bayard, Rhees and Co., both with the tincture and potencies, and its characteristics were well
defined.
Dry, hacking, tickling cough (Bry.). Constant tickling in the pit of the throat, runs into bronchi. Trachea sore
to external pressure, feels excoriated, as do the fauces. Lump sensation in the throat that descends and comes
back up after they swallow.
Cough is excited by pressure on throat. Touching the throat brings on the cough. Violent cough with a scanty
difficult expectoration. Rattling cough. Coughing as if a piece of phlegm is stuck in chest.
Cough caused by an incessant tickling in the throat, tickling runs down to the bifurcation of the bronchial
tubes. Cough, worsefrom the least cold air or uncovering. Cough ceases by covering the body and head
with bedclothes.
Marked action on the skin, producing an intense itching. Numerous and varied pains, neither fixed nor
constant. Sharp pains, neuralgias. Acts on joints, especially ankles, the skin, left side, chest. Cold affects the
joints. Obesity.
Rumx. diminishes the secretions of mucus membranes and at the same time exalts sensibility of the mucus
membranes of the larynx and trachea. Dry and sensitive mucus membranes. Mucus secretions decrease
causing stickiness with burning. Lymphatics are enlarged and secretions perverted.
MIND - Disinclination to mental exertion. Indifferent about his surroundings. Restlessness in evening. Patient
refuses to speak or even listen to conversation, lest his attentio.i should be withdrawn from the supervision of
his respiratory acts. Low spirited with serious expression of the face. Suicidal mood. Feels like killing herself
in despair.
Abdomen - Annoying rumbling flatulence in women. Flatulence. Flatulent abdominal colic soon after a meal.
Creeping near navel better by discharge of offensive flatus.
Back - Pain under scapulae, right.
Breasts - Pain in the left breast after meals.
Chest - Pain under sternum, under right nipple. Pain in left side of chest after meals with flatulence. Burning,
sticking pain in left chest near the heart, worse deep breathing. Rawness or burning under clavicle as if the
air penetrated there, worse hawking. Clavicular pain, worse hawking. Soreness behind sternum, especially left
side in region of left shoulder.
Constitutions - Tubercular or nervous constitutions.
Cough - Suffocative choking coughs. Tickling in throat causes cough. Dry, tickling cough, preventing
sleep. Barking cough. Cough worse by pressure, talking, lying on left side, inspiring cool air and at night.
Cough provoked by changing rooms. Cough by change from cold to warm and warm to cold. Cough from
uncovering, drafts. Cough comes regularly at 11 p.m., 2 a.m. and 5 a.m., in children. Continuous coughing.
Cough in the daytime only. Cough worse during early pregnancy, may cause miscarriage.
Ears - Ringing in ears. Itching deep in ears. Pain, throbbing, stopped sensation in ears.
Eyes - Burning indoors, puffed up in morning. Pain in eyes as from dryness, lids inflamed, worse evening.
Sore feeling in eyes without inflammation. Deep-seated pain in right eye. Sharp, shooting pain in left eye.
Lachrymation when yawning.
Face - Sodden complexion. Pale, while standing. Pain in right jaw, morning.
 Female - Pain from right ovary to back. Tendency to miscarriages, in early stage of pregnancy (Sep.).
Miscarriage with dry, shaking, spasmodic cough, in paroxysms of great violence.
Food - Ravenous appetite. Worse when eating and after meals. Worse after excessive use of alcohol. Gastric
disturbances, from tea drinking. Can’t eat meat, it causes eructations, pruritus. Worse from apples.
Head - Headache after waking in morning. Headache and nausea after eating. Catarrhal headache with great
irritation of larynx and trachea. Darting or sharp piercing pains, in left side. Bruised feeling in forehead. Dull
feeling in head
Rumex crispus during cough.
Heart - Feels as if suddenly stopped, followed by heavy throbbing through the chest.
Kidneys - Sudden urging, involuntary with cough. Copious, colorless urine in afternoon. Urine less copious,
flocculent deposit, oily surface, marked brick-dust sediment.
Limbs - Pain in left shoulder on coughing, on raising arms. Hands cold when coughing. Spasmodic cramps in
ankles and feet.
Liver - Jaundice after excessive use of alcohol.
Lungs - Dyspnea on retiring. Better closing the mouth or covering the head. Breathing worse in wind. Asthma.
Copious mucus discharge from nose and trachea. Profuse, frothy, thin expectoration, stringy and tough, by
the mouthful.
Male - Tendency to phimosis. In evening, feeling of soreness and excoriation with redness of end of prepuce.
Itching of prepuce. Sexual desire diminished, lost.
Modalities - Better from covering mouth. Better wrapping up, lying on right side. Better from discharge of
offensive flatus. Worse weather change, warm to cold, cold to warm. Worse from cool air, inhaling, open air.
Worse deep or irregular breathing. Worse uncovering. Worse motion, riding, lying on left side. Worse from
pressure on trachea, talking. Worse eating, after meals. Worse evening and night, morning, on waking. Worse
3:30 p.m., 11 p.m., 2 a.m. to 5 a.m.
Mouth - Bitter taste in morning. Dry tongue and mouth. Tongue sore at edges, coated. Tongue feels as if
burned. Tongue coated yellowish-brown or reddish-brown. Toothache, entirely better after dinner, rinsing
mouth with cold water. Toothache with acute colds. Ulceration of mouth and throat.
Nose - Nose obstructed, dry sensation in posterior sinuses. Copious mucus discharge from nose and trachea.
Yellow mucus from posterior nares. Sneezing attacks, fluent coryza. Violent sneezing and painful irritation of
nostrils. Itching that extends from the end of the nose to pharynx. Desire to pick nose. Nosebleed.
Rectum - Brown, watery diarrhea, early in morning with cough, driving him out of bed. Sudden, profuse,
foul, painless, brown, black or thin, watery stools. Itching of anus with sensation as of a stick in rectum.
Hemorrhoids. Valuable in late stage tuberculosis (Seneg., Puls., Lyc., Ars.).
Sensations - Eyes pain as if from dryness. Tongue as if burned. As if cough did not reach low enough to raise
phlegm. Lump in throat, it descends on deglutition, but immediately returns. Hands cold when coughing. As if
head would fly to pieces with cough. As if he might raise blood any minute. Hard substance in pit of stomach.
As if heart suddenly stopped. Pressure of a stick in rectum.
Skin - Acne vulgaris on back. Intense itching of skin, especially of lower limbs, worse exposure to cold air
or when undressing. Urticaria, contagious prurigo. Jaundice after excessive use of alcohol.
Sleep - Sudden sleepiness. Sleep disturbed, wakeful, restless, short naps and unpleasant fancies, even when
awake. Unpleasant dreams of danger and trouble.
Stomach - Tight, suffocative, heavy ache in epigastrium to back, clothes feel tight. Chronic gastritis, aching
pain in pit of stomach and shooting in the chest, extends towards the throat, worse any motion or talking.
Hiccough, heartburn. Nausea, better by belchings. Eating meat causes belching and itching.
Teeth - Pain in teeth of both sides, morning. Toothache better after eating dinner, better by rinsing with cold
water.
Temperature - Sweat on waking from a sound sleep.
Throat - Throat feels hollow. Rawness of larynx and trachea. Hawks much tenacious mucus. Lump, not better
by hawking, descends and rises again after swallowing. Irritation in larynx when eating, causes cough.
COMMENTS -Guernsey described the cough of Rumex as a “cough caused by an incessant tickling in throat-
pit, which tickling runs down to the bifurcation of the bronchial tubes
touching the throat brings on the cough, by covering up all the body and head with the bed-clothes there is no
cough.”
Shakes head as if it would fly to pieces and chest so that he feels he might raise blood any minute. Exhausting
paroxysms, rapid coughing spells (Coc-c., Cor-r.). Coughing if the hands get cold. Headache during cough.
Cough causes expulsion of urine and it may even cause expulsion of the fetus in pregnant women. Palliates
late stage tuberculosis (Phos., Ph-ac., Stann.).
 Cold air and drafts bring on coughing spells, as well as itching and skin aggravations. Characteristic sensitivity
to cold air. The cough and skin symptoms are worse by uncovering or exposure to air. Wants to be covered
(Hep.).
Worse from change of weather, temperature, talking with cough, eating. Worse motion, lying on the left (Phos.).
Worse touching the throat. Irritated by irregular or deep breathing. Coughing worse at night around 11 p.m.,
and from 2-4 a.m.
Flu with a dry, hacking cough. Dryness of the nose and throat. Tendency to colds easily, with cough. Asthmatic
cough, allergic asthma with constriction and a hacking, tickling cough.
Allergies with more coughing than sneezing, with a runny nose. Irritation of the nose. Burning, smarting,
rawness in nasal passages (Caust.). Rapid sneezing. Severe sinus headaches, especially when the discharge
dries up.
Thick, white discharges deep in the lungs or in the sinuses. Mucus or dryness alternating with total obstruction
of thick mucus. Catarrh of the nose, eyes and chest that is gluey, thick, white, gelatinous, ropy and lumpy (Ant-
t.). Nosebleeds from hawking.
Lachrymation of the eyes. Aphonia, aphasia. Hoarseness and change of voice (Spong.). Toothache, worse
from inhaling cold air, may be better from cold drinks. Raw, burning sensation on inhaling.
Disturbed circulation. Violent palpitations of the heart and throbbing throughout the whole body. Itching with
burning, worse scratching, after bathing (Sulph.). Skin is worse being uncovered (Hep.). Scabies with severe
itching. Eczema with small, red pimples. Itching without eruptions (Spong., Alum., Sulph.).
Sensation of weight in stomach. Borbo- rygmi, particularly on the left. Flatulence and rumbling. Diarrhea in the
early morning, driving the patient out of bed. Morning diarrhea, brown, watery, offensive. Diarrhea after catarrh,
often associated with a cough.
Sadness and aversion to work, with irritability. Restless, sleep with vivid dreams, especially when the cough
wakes them. Dreams of danger and robbers. Can wake up coughing or with diarrhea.
Paine noted a particular symptoms that led to many cures of skin cases where exposure to air is the exciting
cause, “while undressing and for some time after, considerable inching of surface of lower limbs.”
P. P. Wells related the case of Mrs. X., who had eight miscarriages all in the early months of pregnancy. Each
miscarriage was attended with a severe dry, shaking, spasmodic cough in violent attacks. This was regarded
as the cause of the miscarriages.
At the beginning of the ninth pregnancy she came under homeopathic treatment. The cough came on very dry,
harsh, loud, shaking, worse at night, preventing sleep, excited instantly by pressure on the trachea. Rumx. 30c
promptly relieved.
Wells also cured with Rumx. 200c a cough in a man that began with tickling behind top of sternum, sometimes
in paroxysms lasting for five to ten minutes.
Joslin pointed out the left chest had more verified symptoms than any other region. Conditions are worse lying
on left side, better lying on right side. Worse at 11 p.m. and 4 a.m.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Bell., Hyos.,Con., Lach., Phos. Compare: ( 1 ) Caust., Sulph., Bell.,
(2) Rumx. contains chrysophanic acid to which the skin stitches correspond. (3) Rumx-a. - Sheep sorrel -
Gathered in June and dried, used locally for Epithelioma of face.
Dry, unremitting short cough and violent pains in bowels, uvula elongated inflammation of esophagus, also
cancer. (4) Rumex obtusifolius - Broadleaf dock - nosebleed and headache following, pain in kidneys,
leucorrhea.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Russula Foetens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - russ. Russula foetens. N. O. Fungi. Tincture of the fresh mushrooms. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bedwetting. Blindness. Chorea. Coma. Convulsions. Cyanosis. Dyspnea. Spasms. Tremors.
HERBAL - Some species of Russula are edible and are much esteemed as a food.
HOMEOPATHIC - Alphonse Barrelet observed the effects of eating cooked Russula foetens, which produced
a very severe poisoning. Russ, has produced hallucinations, muscular tremors and clonic spasms recall the
effects of Agar.
The eye symptoms were even more pronounced, complete blindness lasting many days occurred with this
peculiarity of the pupil, that it was sometimes normal, sometimes dilated and sometimes contracted.
Constant trembling of muscles, at times interrupted by tonic contractions increasing to general clonic spasms
with complete loss of consciousness. Muscular spasms, deathly anxiety, dyspnea. Patient recovered after two
or three weeks.
 MIND - Hallucinations constant for three days after spasms ceased. Unconsciousness. Deathly anxiety.
Abdomen - Nausea, colic, vomiting, diarrhea, with cold limbs.
Eyes - Pupils at one time normal, at another time dilated, at another contracted. Consciousness returned on
third day, patient could hear but was completely blind.
Face - Cyanosis.
Kidneys - Involuntary urination.
Lungs - Dyspnea.
Pulse - Pulse small and contracted.
Skin - The attack was followed by pseudoerysipelas on elbows and painless furuncles over whole body,
especially on scapulae and small of back.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
