name: Sacharum Album
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sac-alb. Sacharum album. Cane sugar. Sucrose. Sacharum officinale. White sugar. Sugarcane.
N. O. Gramineae. Trituration. Solution. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Acidity. Anal, itching. Anorexia. Aphthae. Ascites. Bilious. Blood, sugar. Bulimia. Cachexia.
Cataract. Chills. Chlorosis. Constipation. Cornea, opacity. Cramps. Coughs. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dropsy.
Dyspepsia. Edema. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Fainting. Fatigue. Fever. Gangrene. Gout. Hair, growth. Headache,
periodic. Heartburn. Hemorrhoids. Hoarseness. Homesickness. Hyperactivity. Hypoglycemia. Hysteria.
Intermittent, fever. Insomnia. Leg, ulcers. Liver, disorders. Malnutrition. Migraine. Myocardial, degeneration.
Nausea. Neurasthenia. Ophthalmia. Pancreas, disorders. Panaritium. Poisoning. Quinine, effects. Ranula.
Restlessness. Rheumatism. Rickets. Scurvy. Sleeplessness. Spleen, disorders. Sugar, effects. Tabes
mesenterica. Teeth, decay. Ulcers. Vertigo. Vomiting. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Hering, a large proportion of chronic diseases of women and children are
developed by using too much sugar. Like so many other articles of diet, Sugar may be a poison and a medicine
as well as a food. Sugar preserves food, as salt does, and both sugar and salt have produced scurvy.
Cases of scurvy, rickets in bottle-fed children have been traced to excess of sugar in their food and the
exclusion of sugar from the dietary of the gouty, rheumatic and the
diabetic, shows the pathogenetic power it is credited. Acidity of the stomach and itching at the anus are
common effects of taking too much sugar.
Sugar is an antiseptic. Combats infection and putrefaction. It has a solvent action on fibrin and stimulates
secretion by the intense osmotic changes induced, thus rinsing out the wound with serum from within outward,
 favoring healing. Leg ulcers.
Sensitive to pain or not sensitive to pain at all. Fainting from pain. Fainting on seeing blood. Fainting from
a blood puncture. Fainting spells. Plethora. Weakness, lack of energy. Sudden weakness, ameliorated by
eating. Weakness after sweets.. Physical tension. Waking very early in the morning.
Extreme dryness, dryness of skin, hair, nails, hands, feet, inside of nose, eyes, mouth, throat, vagina, stool.
Tingling in the limbs. Pains in bones from head to foot. Edema of feet.
Cold expectoration. Opacity of cornea. Dim sight. Myocardial degeneration. Headache every seven days.
Emaciation with great appetite. Obesity with compulsive eating, especially sweets, cakes and pastries.
potato chips, anything. Acidity and anal itching.
Children who are cross, peevish, whining, capricious. Very aggressive children, often emaciated. Children
who want dainty things, tidbits and refuse substantial food. Scurvy, rickets in children. Fat, bloated, large limbed
children. Family history of diabetes and cancer.
MIND - Discontented with himself and with everything. Hard to please. Lack of joy in life, feeling that life is
not worth living. Want of childish cheerfulness. Sadness, worse after sweets. Loneliness. No real feelings
of relationship with other people and with life in general. Longing and melancholy, as if homesick.
Lack of love. Possessive love. Jealousy, from fear of losing the loved one. Fundamental frustration in
affection in the past, mostly in early childhood. Very uncertain about the love of partner or parents.
Fear of failure. Sensitive to criticism.
Great need of approbation. Ailments from lack of affection, lack of physical contact in early childhood. Lack
of attention. Loquacity, mostly to have attention. Plays antics to have attention. Forsaken feeling. Desire to
be held in the mother’s arms. Desire to be carried.
Great need to be caressed and touched, or difficulty in admitting this need and refusing every contact. Often
a lack of contact with the mother. Sucking the fingers or thumb. Sucking thumb almost the whole day and
during the night, or never sucking the thumb at all. Sucking the thumb until an advanced age. Biting nails, up
to the quick. Biting toenails. Touches everything.
Alternating moods, gentleness alternating with aggression. Peevishness. Melancholic mood with chilliness.
Capriciousness. Low spirited, hypochondriacal mood. Restlessness, aggravated after eating sweets.
Indifference. Disinclined to talk, want of interest. Antisocial. Thinks he is neglected and placed at a
disadvantage. Feels despised. Envious. Jealous. Lack of self-confidence. Timidity. Increased modesty of
women. Great modesty. Stupidity. Irresolution. Dainty, cross and whining, indolent.
Anxious. Worries about all sorts of things at night. Fear of fainting, of seeing blood. Fear of falling. Felt afraid
to go to bed, of the dark. Fear of failure (Care.). Fear of losing beloved persons and parents. Hypochondriacal
mood. Intense nervousness. Jumps from her seat at the least unusual noise. Seems as if she would fly out
of her skin.
Irritable, in morning, until breakfast. Irritable when hungry, better by eating. Offended easily. Cross and
fault-finding. Censorious and sarcastic. Bilious sanguineous temperament.
Quarrelsomeness. Violent temper. Extremely aggressive, quarrelsome, violent, malicious and defiant,
especially after eating chocolate or sweets. Fits of anger, unapproachable. Kicks and hits. Ailments from
anger. Bad effects from violent anger. Ailments from excitement, stress. Fainting from pain.
Delusion of being persecuted. Delusion that her parents don’t love her or that she
is less loved than her siblings. Imagined that her mother wanted to kill her. Imagines that some one is behind
her. Feeling that everybody in the world is against him.
Abdomen - Abdomen swollen and enlarged.
Abdomen as hard as a stone. Painful hardness of the abdomen. Hard swollen abdomen after scarlet fever.
Swelling and induration of the mesenteric glands. Tabes mesenterica. Abdomen shows the presence of water
on percussion. Dropsy. Flatulency. Pain in the spleen (from a blow received a long time ago) and liver.
Swelling of the spleen.
Breasts - Atrophy of breasts. Fullness and swelling of breasts before menses. Pain in breasts before menses.
Causations - Sugar. Anger.
Chest - Sharp pains in the left side of the chest. Rheumatic pain in the region of the heart. Fullness in the
chest, in the morning and relieved by expectoration of mucus. Swelling of the lower part of the sternum.
Emaciation of the chest, the muscles dwindle away.
Constitutions - Bilious, sanguine temperament. Plethoric constitution.
Ears - Discharge of pus from the ears.
Eyes - Dullness of eyes. Dryness. Eyes closed by swelling and inflammation of lids. V aricóse distention of
vessels of eyes. Ophthalmia. Cataract, opacity of lens. Opacity of cornea. Dimness of the cornea. Dimness of
sight. Obscuration of sight. Inflammation of the eyelids. Edematous swelling of the eyelids.
 Face - Changed expression of the countenance. Face pale, deathlike. Face bloated, edematous. Healthy
fresh color of the face. Twitching of muscles of right cheek, over malar bone.
Female - Amenorrhea. Menses diminished, scanty. Menses painful, dysmenorrhea. Menstrual pale blood,
watery. Painful ovulation and menses. Brown leucorrhea. Suppressed leucorrhea. Complaints before menses
including sadness, irritability, swelling and painful breasts (Sep., Care.). Brown bloody discharge preceding
menses. Leucorrhea, bloody before menses. Dryness of vagina. Increased sexual
desire. Swelling of the genitals.
Food - Compulsive eating. Bulimia with obesity. Ravenous appetite soon after eating with feeling of
emptiness in stomach and general weakness. Insatiable appetite not ameliorated by eating. Morbid hunger
with the fever. Anorexia, no feeling of hunger at all at any time, no desire to eat. Little or no appetite in the
morning, but insatiable appetite in the evening, especially for sweets. Hypoglycemia. Has to eat at the normal
times, otherwise weak, dizzy, trembling, headache. Tendency to eat frequently between meals. Better after
eating, after breakfast, from sweets. Desires sugar, sweets, chocolate, pastries and cakes. Desires sweets
after dinner and before menses. Desires bread, butter, fat, salt, sour, lemons, mustard. Desires raw
vegetables. Worsefrom chocolate, sweets. Aversion to sweets, butter, fat, warm milk, warm food, cooked
vegetables. Aversion to anything except sweets. Thirst for large quantities. Thirstlessness. Desires licorice.
Desires cold drinks, especially water, tea, warm milk. Desires alcohol. Bad effects from spirituous liquors.
Head - Giddiness from indigestion. Migraine. One-sided headache. Headache every week the same day.
Severe headache with the chill. Cold in the head. Hair grows rapidly. Perspiration only on the head.
Heart - Myocardial degeneration. Endocarditis. Rheumatic pain in heart region. Weakness of heart. Pulse
weak and irregular.
Kidneys - Great pains in kidneys. Sharp burning pains run from kidneys to shoulders, passing under scapulae.
Increased urination, strong odor, white sediment. Diabetes mellitus. Sugar in urine. Urine diminished. Scanty
urine.
Limbs - Stiffness. Legs swollen and as hard as a stone. Emaciation, especially of lower limbs. Heat of lower
limbs, must uncover feet. Gouty pains, wandering. Sharp pains. Weakness of the legs. Tingling in limbs.
Restlessness of legs. Cramps in the calves of the legs. Caries on the feet. Ulcers on legs. Edematous
swelling of the legs, water oozes out from them. Sensation
as if water, oozing from legs. Swelling around the ankles. Panaritium. Felon. Nail disorders. Edematous
swelling of the right arm with stinging, less painful when uncovering the arm, more painful in the evening
and during damp weather. Fistulous ulceration of the rightforearm with tingling and stitches, discharge
of yellowish thin pus (Bute-j.).
Liver - Pain in liver and spleen. Liver is swollen, indurated. Increased secretion of bile. Hypoglycemia.
Lungs - Breathing oppressed with cold expectoration. Suffocative attacks, must be bolstered up. Can only
breathe in an erect position. Respiration difficult, oppressed in the morning, relieved by expectoration.
Accumulation of mucus in the lungs. Expectoration with the cough is very offensive. Suppressed
expectoration is restored. Expectoration very fetid, offensive odor. Expectoration white, yellow.
Expectoration tastes salty. Expectoration thin, watery, while walking in open air. Dry, loose cough. Cough with
children. Pneumonia.
Male - Enormous swelling of scrotum, right genitals. Swelling of the penis. Increased sexual desire. Frequent
involuntary emissions.
Modalities -Better after eating, in evening. Dyspnea better in erect position. Worse in early morning, difficulty
starting the day. Worse from warm weather. Worse from anger (Staph., Coloc., Cham.). Worse sugar, sweets,
chocolate. B ad effects from spirituous liquors.
Mouth - Dryness of mouth. Salivation. Inflammation of salivary glands. Inflammation of lining membrane of
mouth. White coating on tongue, so thick as to cause stiffness in it. Cracked, fissured mouth, tongue.
Ranula. Thrush. Aphthae of children. Scorbutic gums. Teeth feel as if on edge. Dullness of teeth with sour
vomiting. Scurvy. Sucking the fingers or thumb. Children put fingers in the mouth. Biting nails.
Nose - Dryness inside nose. Coryza, dry without discharge. Sneezing.
Perspiration - Perspiration day and night. Profuse sweat at night, especially on head. Sweats on head, neck
and shoulders. All perspiration is suppressed.
Rectum - Lump sensation. Dragging and heaviness sensation in rectum. Constipation alternating with mucus
diarrhea. Constipation, stools difficult, dry. Diarrhea, stools watery and debilitating. Stools of mucus and blood,
bilious. Itching at the anus. Congested and painful hemorrhoids. Hemorrhoids bleed. Painful hemorrhoidal
tumors. Worm affections of children.
Skin - Dryness of skin. Chlorosis, after anger, with dropsy. Eruptions, red blotches. Pale red blotches over
the body. Anasarca after scarlet fever. Scurvy. Panaritium. Ulcers. Excessive granulation in the ulcers.
 Proud flesh in the ulcers. Gangrenous ulcers, cold dry gangrene. Old herpes.
Sleep - Sleeplessness. Starts in sleep. Dreams of dead persons, of falling. Slow to wake up and revive after
rising in the morning.
Stomach - Acidity of the stomach. Disordered stomach. Slow digestion. Indigestion, weak with acidity.
Burning at pit of stomach. Stomach bloated, overloaded with sour mucus. Empty, weak, hungry feeling in
stomach. Painful constriction of stomach. Painful sensitiveness of the pit of the stomach. Coldness or heat in
the stomach. Gurgling and rumbling noises in stomach. Pressure in the stomach in the morning when
fasting. Stomach pain with hypochondriacal persons. Nausea early in morning. Violent retching and gagging.
Vomiting of white, viscid tough mucus. Vomiting of blood. Vomiting acid, making teeth dull. Vomiting,
occasional with the chill. Periodical vomiting. Vomiting of alcoholics. Malnutrition.
Temperature - Instability of body temperature. Extreme chilliness alternating with heat, especially at night.
Chilliness from 10 a.m. until evening with melancholic mood. Chills beginning in lower back, spreading up and
down. Chilliness alternates with perspiration. Chill followed by profuse sweat. Intermittent fever every one, two
or three days, irregular in its type. Evening
fever. Rheumatic fevers. Malignant plague fevers. Suppressed fevers from quinine sulphate. Hot feet, sticks
them out of bed, often only one foot. Sticks one or two arms out of bed or sleeps with the upper half of body
uncovered.
Throat - Dryness of throat. Dry, rawness in the larynx. Irritation of larynx, causing a slight hacking cough with
yellow, salty sputa, which floats on water. Ulceration of the larynx. Ulcers in throat. Hoarse, catarrhal voice.
Hoarseness from reading but a short time.
Vertigo - Fainting attacks. Giddiness from indigestion. Harassing giddiness with gout. Vertigo with low
blood sugar, weakness. Vertigo better after eating. Vertigo while lying down. Vertigo as if sinking down through
the bed.
COMMENTS - Restlessness, aggravated after eating sweets. Running, moving all the time. Restless while
sitting. Difficult concentrating, particularly when eating sweets. Very uncertain. Fear of unknown situations
(Lyc., Stram.). Sensitive to reprimand, or not sensitive to reprimand at all (Tub.). Impossible to correct.
Alternating moods, gentleness alternating with aggression. Extremely aggressive, quarrelsome, violent,
malicious, and defiant, especially after eating chocolate or sweets. Kicks and hits. Fits of anger. Insolence.
Disobedience. Unapproachable.
Waking early in the morning. Aphthae.
Profuse salivation.
To these symptoms have been added others observed by Swan from a patient who accidentally discovered
after twenty-five years of suffering, that the cause of his trouble was sugar. All the symptoms disappeared
when he abstained from sugar in food or drink and only reappeared when he took it again by way of experiment.
Then from two to four days after taking sugar, the same train of symptoms invariably occurred. Burning at pit
of stomach. A white coat on tongue, so thick as to cause stiffness of it. Sharp burning pains run up from head
to foot, causing a rigidity of the muscles so that it was impossible to rise from bed until he had been rubbed.
Chill commencing in small of back and spreading up and down. Severe headache and occasional vomiting
with the chill. Fever followed with headache, morbid hunger and a hectic flush.
Increased urine, strong odor, white sediment. Great pain in kidneys. Constipation. Sleeplessness. Edema of
feet and ankles. Weakness of legs, as if paralyzed, causing staggering. Painful jactitation of feet and legs
during the burning in the stomach. Oppression of chest with a cough. Profuse cream-like expectoration, that
was very offensive and cold.
Sac-alb. 10,000c and 5,000c cured him of some remaining symptoms and the 41,000c enabled him to eat
sugar with impunity.
Swan also reported the case of a woman who was continually eating candies of which she was very fond, until
her digestive organs were affected. A few doses of Sac-alb. 30,000c changed her taste so that she ate no
more and could not even bear the sight of them.
Farrington traced a great similarity between Sac-alb. and Calc. Sac-alb. is indicated, he said in children who
are large- limbed, fat and bloated with a tendency to dropsy.
Sac-alb. has produced opacity of the cornea and ought to cure it. The children are dainty and capricious, care
nothing for substantial food, but want little “knick- knacks,” always cross and whining and, if old enough, are
insolent and do not care to occupy themselves in any way. Everything is too much trouble.
H.    C. Allen related a case of opacity of cornea cured with Sac-alb. and with the same remedy in 2,000c
potency he cured swelling around the ankles following rheumatism.
According to Lippe, black-and-tan terrier dogs that eat sugar go blind. The cataract and amblyopiaof diabetics
are well known. Here, again, salt and sugar meet as Burnett has shown in his super salinity of the blood that
 excess of salt in food has been an important factor in the production of cataract.
Sugar must be considered a sustainer and developer of the musculature of the heart and
hence useful in failure of compensation and a variety of cardio-vascular troubles. It acts as a nutrient and tonic
in wasting disorders, anemia, neurasthenia, etc. increasing weight and power.
One ounce of lump sugar morning and evening valuable adjunct in the treatment of obstinate cases of heart
failure due to deficient heart muscle without valvular lesion. Epilepsy, blood with reduced sugar content irritates
the nervous system with tending to convulsions.
Sugar as an oxytocic has its most suitable application toward the end of labor when there is no mechanical
obstruction and delay is due to uterine inertia. 25 grams dissolved in water, several times every half hour.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Sac-1., (2) Sacchin - hinders both the salivary and peptic ferment actions with
consequent dyspepsia. Prof. Lewin believes its action to be on the secretory cells themselves and it has caused
pain, (right hypogastrium). loss of appetite, diarrhea and wasting. (3) Arg-n., Lyc., Sulph. - craving for sweets.
(4) Sil. - rickets. (5) Arg-n. - diabetes, swollen ankles, (6) Santa. - Kidney ache.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Lippe. Smits. Swan.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sac-alb. Sacharum album. Cane sugar. Sucrose. Sacharum officinale. White sugar. Sugarcane.
N. O. Gramineae. Trituration. Solution. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Acidity. Anal, itching. Anorexia. Aphthae. Ascites. Bilious. Blood, sugar. Bulimia. Cachexia.
Cataract. Chills. Chlorosis. Constipation. Cornea, opacity. Cramps. Coughs. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dropsy.
Dyspepsia. Edema. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Fainting. Fatigue. Fever. Gangrene. Gout. Hair, growth. Headache,

name: Sacharum Lactis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sac-1. Sacharum lactis. Milk sugar. Lactose. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Angina pectoris. Body, odor. Diabetes. Dyspepsia. Earache. Gout. Headache.
Hysteria. Labia, soreness. Nervousness. Neuralgia. Ovaries disorders. Over-exertion. Ptosis. Sciatica.
Sighing. Styes. Umbilicus inflammation.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann chose globules of Sacharum lactis as the chief vehicle of his remedies because
he considered it the most inert substance he could find. But his method of attenuating remedies had shown
that no substance is inert in potencies and experience shows that no substance is absolutely inert in any form.
Sac-1, in large doses develops the bacillus acidophilus to correct putrefactive intestinal conditions and also
constipation. Diuresis. Amblyopia.
Sensitive in every part of body. Small shooting pains all over in morning. Throbbing in parts of body. Cold
pains, as if produced by fine, icy cold needle with tingling, as if frost bitten. Great physical exhaustion and
weakness, caused by overwork. Prostration from mental excitement.
MIND - Extremely nervous, jumps from her seat at least unusual noise. Sudden fear and trembling of whole
body, as from fright. Sarcastic and fault-finding, could not speak a pleasant word to any one. Laziness.
Longing and melancholy as if homesick, with oppressed breathing. Her heart aches as if it would burst, yet
she cannot weep. Fear of death during pain in heart. Hysteria in evening, laughing and crying, jumping up and
lying down.
Sensation as if she were kept together by a great effort. Loses her way in well-known streets. Imagines that
there is a large hole in her back just above sacrum, that her mother wants to kill her, that some one is behind
her.
Abdomen - Sore to touch, painful from the jar caused by walking. Severe pain passing through abdomen
during stool. Sharp pain passing across bowels just above navel and all around body. Pain in left
hypochondrium passing under left breast. Pain above left hip, which would come when leaning back, followed
by severe pain in forehead.
Back - Dull ache all over back and in right arm. Backaches the whole length of spine. Pain passing up and
down along right side of neck. Hot flashes all over back of neck and shoulders. Pain with soreness at upper
right scapula. Pain in sacral region, worse when taking a breath. Pain passing up back from sacrum. Pain in
lumbar region, worse by leaning backward.
Breasts - Sharp pain into right breast, very sore to touch. Constant pain under left breast, worse when bending
forward. Severe pains under left breast at every inspiration.
Causations - Mental excitement. Overfatigue.
Chest - Feeling as if ulcerated over right short ribs, worse from touch and when stooping. Pain in axilla.
Ears - Pain in right ear and underneath it. Painfulness of right external ear with burning like an ulcer, also when
touched. Pain passing from right ear to shoulder. Pain from right ear to lower part of inferior maxillary bone.
Pain in left ear and sensation as if there were a gathering. Shooting pains in and behind ears and all over face.
Pains in external ears and behind them. Reverberation of voice when speaking. Buzzing sound in right ear.
Sensation as if she could not hear, but she could.
Eyes - Pain through right eye inwards. Sensation as if needles were sticking in eyes. Dryness of eyeball so
that the lid would stick to it. Looking at bright light dazzles and makes her close eyes, no pain. Sight fails, eyes
tire very easily. Styes. Swelling of right upper lid. Can only elevate upper lids half way.
 Face - Sad expression of face, eyes look as from weeping, though she has not wept. Wretched appearance.
Great pallor efface with dark places under eyes. Burning in cheekbones towards temples and lower jaw. Pain
passing from corner of mouth of forepart of right axilla. Pain all over face, then centering in right ear. Corners
of mouth, chin smart and burn.
Female - Menses commenced too early, no pain. Menses very dark. Profuse greenish- yellow leucorrhea.
Bloody leucorrhea. Soreness and rawness of labia with profuse greenish-yellow leucorrhea. Itching of labia.
Lobulated growths on each side of vagina, extremely sore and sensitive to touch. Pain in region of right ovary.
Ovarian region very weak and painful when walking. Dragging-down sensation in pelvic region.
Food - Hungry all the time. When first getting out of bed feels faint for something to eat. Desire for dainties.
Feeling of distention after eating. Great thirst, wanted large quantities of very cold water.
Head - Sharp pains behind right ear. Pain in left eyebrow. Left temple sore to touch. Burning like fire, extending
from right frontal eminence to vertex. Sensation as of pressure on frontal bone at inner canthi of left eye, felt
very sore. Sharp darting pain on left side of head from temple to occiput. Forehead feels very heavy with a
tendency to fall forward. Sharp pain in forehead from one temple to the other. Head feels large and as though
all the blood in the body had gone into the head. Head feels confused and as if it were tossing on a rough sea.
Heart - Sensation as if a fire in heart. Feeling as if heart would burst. Awoke at midnight with severe numb
pains about heart, great fear of death, when the pains passed off they left great soreness around heart. Pulse
intermittent.
Kidneys - Constant pain in region of left kidney. Soreness of urethra during urination. Constant, urgent desire
to urinate with cutting pain up urethra. Sound of running water produced urination, no power to restrain it.
Involuntary urination during night. Urinates large quantities very frequently. Urine causes intense pain when
coming in contact with the labia, which are very sensitive. Urination followed by a thick yellow discharge. Urine
stains a dark yellow.
Limbs - Pain from right shoulder passing down to waist. Pain from right shoulder to left breast. Pain in forepart
of right upper arm. Pain in right wrist. Pain, itching in palm of right hand. Grasping anything with right
handcauses pains to pass from all the fingers into palm. Sharp pain in all right fingers except little finger. Skin
under nails looks dirty. Awful pain extending down the right sciatic nerve. Pains in thighs and hips. Hot flashes
in lower limbs. Pain in right instep when bending foot. Pain like gout in right toe. Balls of feet covered with little
corns, which are very painful when walking.
Modalities - Worse by a coming storm, the approach of which was felt some twelve hours previously. Pains,
worse in damp room or basement, but better if there
was a fire. All symptoms better after 4 p.m. Worse by blue and yellow colors, better by red.
Mouth - Burning in whole mouth. Sensation of coolness as of ice in mouth and throat. Roof of mouth sore.
Soreness like blisters in mouth and on tongue. Sore on left side of tongue. Tongue, coated white, yellow. Taste,
putrid in mouth after eating or fine spicy taste like fresh nuts. Thick bitter mucus in mouth during morning. Lips
feel very sore, raw and dry with great thirst.
Nose - Pain in sides, end of nose. Ridge of nose extremely sore, it feels sore to touch or from the least
movement of facial muscles, the left side is the worst and somewhat swollen.
Rectum - Stool preceded by shooting pains across abdomen, which are better by stool. Before stool, pains in
breasts and upper abdomen. Urgent inclination to stool, felt as though there were a great ball in rectum, much
straining and some flatulence, but no stool and not better from the flatulence. Stools smell like rotten eggs.
Soreness around anus, extending up rectum. Creeping, itching and crawling around anus, extending inside
rectum. Shooting pains in rectum.
Skin - Very restless at night from itching all over body as soon as she is covered in bed. Itching of both
shoulders.
Sleep - Yawning all day. Sleeplessness after midnight. Cannot sleep on right side. Cannot go to sleep without
putting arms over head. Impossible to lie straight in bed, finds herself continually lying diagonally across bed.
Has to lie on left side. Fatiguing dreams all night. Awoke with the impression that she had dreamed of dreadful
pains in chest, does not know whether it was a dream or a reality.
Stomach - Pressure in stomach as if she had eaten something indigestible. Dyspepsia after eating hot pie-
crust. Heartburn with sweet taste coming from stomach without water brash. Violent sickness, going on all day.
Nausea does not affect appetite. Nausea like seasickness.
Temperature - Great coldness as if a chill were coming on. Fingers, feet toes, icy cold, could not keep warm
in bed covered with clothes. Hot flashes inside body pressing from below upward. Feeling of heat all over, the
body is covered with a light sweat, enough to feel uncomfortable. Strange restlessness at night.
Throat - Spasmodic stricture in esophagus. Globus hystericus after lunch at noon with dull, sick headache.
Throat very sensitive to external pressure, the least pressure causes a feeling as if she were choking.
 Sensation when swallowing as of a fishbone in throat.
COMMENTS - Swan is the authority for Sac- 1. as a homeopathic remedy. He published a full pathogenesis
of Sac-1., proved in the potencies from 30c upward, together with confirmed and cured symptoms.
One of Swan's pro vers had the symptom “Sight fails, eyes tire very easily." Another patient, when taking
pilules of Sac-1, three times a day complained that they made his “eyes ache and feel weak.”
Sensations of both coldness and heat. One of the cold sensations is “Sensation of extreme cold passing in a
fine line from center of pubes to a point two or three inches above.”
Swan regarded cold pains as a keynote and recorded the case of Mr. S., who had an excessively cold neuralgic
pain in the cartilage of both ears, the right being the worst with tingling as if frost-bitten, rubbing with difficulty
restored the warmth.
Lancinating, neuralgic pains in forehead in occiput, extending from region above ears down through ears into
muscles of neck in both eyes, worse by least breath of air, skin sensitive to touch as in inflammatory
rheumatism.
These pains were icy cold, as if produced by an extremely fine ice-cold needle. As Sac-
I.   has “fine cold pains” and pains passing in all directions, Sac-1. 1.000c was given and relieved all the pains
within an hour.
H. A. Hare said of Sac-1.. “Scientific and clinical studies have shown it to be possessed of very great diuretic
powers when given
in full doses.”
He said further, that its direct action on the kidneys and its slight action elsewhere indicate it in kidney dropsy
and kidney inactivity, that it acts best in cases where albuminuria is absent and that it causes profuse diuresis
in infants fed on it.
RELATIONS - Camph. aggravates the effects of Sac-1. Compare: (1) Sac-alb. in rickets, acidity, fat children.
Calc., the Lacs. (2) Right cheekbone, Mag-c. (3) Roof of mouth, Mang. (4) Ball sensation in rectum pains, Kali-
bi. (5) Kidney ache, Santa, Sacchin. (6) Fatigue, Pic- ac., Mag-c. (7) Heat in heart, Lachn. (8) better lying on
left side, Lil-t. (9) worse from damp, Dulc. ( 10) Sensitiveness, Kali-i. Mag-c.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Salicylicum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sal-ac. Salicylicum acidum. Salicylic acid. Acetylsalicylicum acidum. Found in spiraea
blossoms. Gaultheria. Prepared from Phenol. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Arthritis.Belching. Bone, decay. Canker sores. Colds. Colitis. Coryza. Deafness. Diarrhea.
Diphtheria. Dyspepsia. Flatulence. Foot-sweat, suppression. Gastritis. Hematuria. Hot flashes. Influenza.
Intestine ulceration. Iritis. Melancholy. Meniere’s disease. Menopausal. Necrosis. Pharyngitis, herpetic.
Puerperal fever. Purpura. Rheumatism. Rheumatoid arthritis. Scarlatina. Sciatica. Septicemia. Stomatitis.
Tapeworm. Throat, sore. Tinnitus. Ulcers. Urticaria. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Salicylic acid is found in nature in the leaves and barks of willows and in wintergreen oil
(Gaultheria), which is one of the chief sources of its supply, and is obtained synthetically from carbolic acid.
Like Carb-ac. it has been largely used as a disinfectant, and, as it is supposed tobe non-poisonous, it is used
for mixing with and so preserving foods.
MacLagan of London and Senator of Berlin, introduced it into medicine as a remedy for rheumatism. It has a
specific relation to rheumatism, but the massive doses given in allopathic practice have been attended with so
many unpleasant symptoms of vital depression, fainting, flatulent dyspepsia and delirium.
Overdoses led to the discovery of its power to set up Meniere’s disease, auditory nerve vertigo, gastric
disturbances and delirium. Roaring and ringing in the ears. Deafness with vertigo. Prostration after influenza,
also tinnitus aurium and deafness. Hematuria. Effects of suppressed foot sweats.
MIND - Melancholy, wants to be quiet, feels faint. Anxiety, worrying, restless. Excited mood. Maniacal
exaltation. Talked incessantly and disconnected. Mistakes in speaking and writing. Awkwardness, drops
things, bumps into things. Delirium, stupid, can hardly collect his ideas, then laughed without cause.
Abdomen - Abdominal distention. Violent, constant pressure in abdomen with feeling of incarcerated flatus.
Ulceration of bowels.
Chest - Spasmodic, flatulent asthma, fetid bronchitis, gangrene of lungs. Firmly seated pressure at side of
sternum as large as the hand, with feeling as if the bone was sore.
Causations - Suppression of foot-sweat. Aspirin overdose.
Ears - Meniere’s disease. Tinnitus, dependent on hyperemia. Roaring and ringing in ears, hears music,
swarm of bees or buzzing of flies. Auditory nerve vertigo with a troublesome nausea accompanying the head
 symptoms. Hearing diminished. Nervous deafness. Deafness with noises in ears, with vertigo.
Eyes - Retinal hemorrhage. Retinitis after influenza, also albuminuric. Plastic iritis following acute rheumatism.
Diminished acuteness of vision.
Face - Dull, heavy aspect, face flushes quickly on slight excitement.
Female - Leuco-phlegmatic woman, frequent hot flashes with irritability, forgetfulness, dull, heavy pain in
cerebellum. Septic puerperal fever.
Head - Piercing pain in temples. Headache commencing on top or back of head, running down neck, which is
tender to touch. Headache, confusion in head on rising suddenly. Dullness of head, stupefaction.
Rush of blood to head. Buzzing sensation in the brain as if blood were forced violently through a contracted
vessel.
Kidneys - Diabetes mellitus. Albuminuria, rheumatic diathesis. Urine scanty, clear, brown.
Limbs - Arthritis and rheumatism. Acute joint rheumatism, worse touch and motion, profuse sweat. Pain
shifts. Sciatica, burning pain, worse at night. Knees are swollen and painful. Copious foot-sweat and ill effects
if sweat is suppressed.
Lungs - Respiration hurried. Spasmodic, flatulent asthma, fetid bronchitis, gangrene of lungs. Dry cough of a
hard, racking, spasmodic character, worse at night, in old people.
Modalities - Better by hot applications, especially by dry heat. Worse by motion. Worse at night, cold air, touch
of anything cold.
Mouth - Taste extremely disgusting, as of something burnt, bitter. Burning, scalded feeling. Burning and
scraping in mouth and throat. Redness of mouth and fauces. Mouth dotted with white patches. Canker sores
with burning soreness and fetid breath. Tongue purplish, leaden-colored, foul breath. Ulcers on tip of tongue.
Stomatitis, mouth hot and dry, tongue covered with burning vesicles.
Nose - Sneezing. Coryza. Incipient catarrh, patients, especially children, sneeze all day.
Rectum - Putrid diarrhea, gastro-intestinal derangements, especially in children, stools like green frog’s spawn
(Mag-c.). Stools green, flushes easily as in hectic, acid, sour, or putrid smelling. Cholera infantum with
peculiarly putrid belchings. Worms. Pruritus ani.
Skin - Hot and burning skin. Itching vesicles and pustules, better by scratching. Skin red and sensitive, points
like flea-bites. Urticaria. Herpes zoster. Purpura. Necrosis and softening of bones.
Sleep - Y awning. Dreams of being pregnant. Frequently awakens from sleep thinking he heard music.
Stomach - Weak, nervous sensation in stomach. Burning inepigastric region. Erosions
and ulcers in stomach and bowels. Putrid fermentation and dyspepsia. Water brash. Flatulence, hot, sour
belching. Gagging, frequent vomiting.
Temperature - Slight chill, crawling in spine, yawning, chill in fingertips. Fever continuous, burning, then sweat
with relief, fever again till exacerbation of symptoms. Weak, faint after fever and sweat. Flushes easily as in
hectic. Profuse sweat, as sweat increased strength declined.
Throat - Burning in throat. Sore, red and swollen. Tonsils red, swollen, studded white. Scraping in throat
causing cough. Hemorrhagic pharyngitis with difficulty of swallowing.
Vertigo - Vertigo, tendency to fall to left side. Deafness with vertigo. Meniere’s disease.
COMMENTS - Sal-ac. has been notably used for corns and warts, as well as to hasten the peeling of palms
and soles after scarlet fever.
Brunton noted that “A mixture of 2 parts with 100 of tallow, applied directly to the feet, not to the stockings, has
been found most useful in preventing sweating and soreness of the feet in soldiers after a long march.”
Sal-ac. has had an accidental proving which has led to some homeopathic uses, including blood-poisoning
conditions, such as puerperal fever and septicemia. Like carbolic acid and other disinfectants, Sal-ac. produces
fermentative dyspepsia and diarrhea with putrid-smelling stools. Disorders following suppressions of foot
sweat.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-sal., Salol. (2) in rheumatism and subsequent weakness, Colch. (3) Piercing
in temples, throat, diarrhea, ulcers, anti-septic properties, Kreos. (4) In anti-septic properties, dyspepsia, fever,
urine, Carb-ac. (5) Tinnitus, Nat-sal., Chin., Chin-s., Carb-s. (6) Bones, Phos. (and throat), Lac-ac. (7) As if
blood forced through contracted vessel, Coc-c. (8) Foot-sweat and suppressed foot-sweat, Sulph. Sil. (9)
Loquacity, Lach.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Salix Mollissima
author: Murphy
full:

Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Neuritis. Rheumatism. Sciatica.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Cooper used Salx-m. with success in rheumatic affections, especially in sciatic neuritis in
nervous subjects in whom the capillary cutaneous circulation showed up visibly and there was some
tenderness and swelling of the limb.

name: Salix Nigra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - salx-n. Salix nigra. Black willow bark. Pussy willow. N. O. Salicaceae. Tincture of fresh tree
bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Emissions. Fevers. Gonorrhea. Impotence. Masturbation. Nightsweats. Nymphomania.
Prostatitis. Satyriasis. Sexual mania. Spermatorrhea.
HERBAL - The black willow of North America has a reputation as a purgative and febrifuge. Salx-n. has been
largely used by herbalists in a great variety of disorders of the genito-urinary system.
HOMEOPATHIC - A proving by E. D. Wright, who took half an ounce of the tincture in a day, is given in Allen’s
Appendix. He developed soreness of muscles, a tired, sleepy state, loose bowels, sore gums and fever.
Salx-n. has a positive action on the generative organs of both sexes. It reduces the irritability of sexual organs,
moderates sexual passion, and controls genital irritability. It has been used after a history of masturbation or
spermatorrhea.
Acute gonorrhea with much erotic trouble, chordee. Satyriasis and sexual mania. Libidinous thoughts and
lascivious dreams. Seminal emissions in presence of woman or when talking with her. Hysteria and
nervousness.
Back - Pain across sacral and lumbar region. Unable to step out quickly.
Face - Red, swollen, especially the end of nose. Nosebleed. Eyes blood-shot, sore to touch and on motion.
Roots of hair hurt.
Female - Before and during menses much nervous disturbance, pain in ovaries, difficult menstruation.
Menorrhagia. Bleeding with uterine fibroid. Ovarian congestion and neuralgia. Nymphomania.
Head - Skin on temples sore to touch. Male - Painful movement of the testicles. Mouth - Gums sore.
Rectum - Looseness of bowels.
Sleep - Disposition to lie down and sleep. COMMENTS - Dr. John Feams wrote of the tonic and anti-septic
properties of this species of Salix, but also of its usefulness as a sedative to the generative system. Asa
sedative on these lines he had very goods results from its use.
Fearns gave Salx-n. in doses of thirty to sixty drops on retiring and repeated at midnight or towards morning,
if needed. He found it particularly useful in cases of acute gonorrhea with much erotic trouble, chordee with
great irritation, and excessive sexual desire, amounting to satyriasis.
Salx-n. seems to control the venereal appetite in a very satisfactory manner. It can be given in cases where
the bromides have always been considered appropriate and it can be given where the bromides would be very
inappropriate and there is no reflex effect on the brain or nervous system.
W. B. McCoy related a number of cases illustrating this action. The first concerned a man, 35, who lost control
of his sexual appetite. The more he indulged the worse the craving became, and indulgence made him a
physical wreck. Salx-n. tincture in teaspoonful doses thrice daily, cured in five weeks.
The second case concerned a youth, 23, who had masturbated since he was a boy. Salx-n. tincture, 20 drops,
four times a day, was given for a fortnight, the quantity being gradually diminished, until in a few weeks the
young man was quite cured.
A teacher, 21, five years before had a spell of fever which left him with a tendency to seminal emissions which
had become very
frequent and had reduced him to a very low condition. Extremely thin, sallow, nervous. Cold hands and feet
even in heat of summer. Extremely cross and irritable.
Salx-n. tincture, 1c one drop four times a day, was given with speedy improvement. Later on the dose was
reduced to thirty drops. The losses ceased and in three months the patient had gained 41 pounds in weight.
A man, 53, had sexual desire but without ability, yet during the night he would have emissions without
erections. Salx-n. tincture, 15 drops, four times a day, cured in three weeks.
McCoy also used Salx-n. successfully in gonorrhea, but other remedies were given as well.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Dam., Yohim., Canth., Con., Agn., Pic-ac. (2) In gonorrhea, Salol, Petros. (3)
Aven., Sabal.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Salix Purpurea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - salx-p. Salix purpurea. Purple willow. Red willow. N. O. Salicaceae. Tincture or infusion of fresh
bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Fever. Parotiditis. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC -T. C. Duncan and his wife proved Salx-p., taking drachm doses of the infusion of the bark.
The chief symptoms were giddiness, loose stools, swelling of the right parotid gland. Fever, marked by heat
preceding chill and perspiration.
Duncan chewed the bark on one occasion and this caused the astringent effect on the mucus membrane of
the mouth. The only rheumatic symptom was aching in right acetabulum.
MIND - Very nervous, irritable and despondent all day. Dullness of intellect.
Abdomen - Pain in abdomen. Flatulence. Face - Swelling of right parotid gland. Head - In a few minutes dizzy
feeling commencing just in front of ears and passing up to vertex like a wave, compelled to
sit down.
Heart - Pulse feeble, circulation torpid.
Kidneys - Urine slightly acid, excess of phosphates and epithelium, less uric acid crystals.
Limbs - Aching in right acetabulum.
Mouth - Peculiar astringent taste, puckering mucus membrane and closing Sténo’s duct. Taste of undigested
food.
Rectum - Bowels loose, two stools in one day with griping.
Sleep - Rested poorly, woke often, first too hot, then too chilly.
Temperature - First too hot, then chilly and at last towards morning in a profuse perspiration.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Salmonella Typhi
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - salm-t. Salmonella typhi. Salmonella nosode. Bacteria. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Cholecystitis. Dehydration. Diarrhea. Enteritis. Fever. Food poisoning. Gastroenteritis.
Heartburn. Nausea. Pancreatitis. Salmonellosis. Typhoid fever. Ulcers. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The attenuations of this bacteria nosode are prepared from washings of a culture of
Salmonella typhi. Disease-causing salmonellae have recently been re-classified into a single species,
Salmonella entérica, which has numerous strains. Salmonella typhi is a well-known strain that causes typhoid
fever.
Other salmonellae are frequent causes of food-borne illness, especially in poultry and raw eggs, and more
generally from food that has been cooked or frozen, and not eaten straight away.
The acute symptoms of salmonella gastroenteritis include the sudden onset of nausea, abdominal cramping,
and bloody diarrhea with mucus. The onset of symptoms usually occurs within 6 to 72 hours after the ingestion
of the bacteria.
Salmonella infections usually resolve in five to seven days, and often require no treatment, unless the patient
becomes severely
dehydrated or the infection spreads from the intestines. Persons with severe diarrhea may require rehydration,
often with intravenous fluids.
Some salmonella bacteria have become resistant to antibiotics, however, and this has occurred possibly as a
result of the use of antibiotics to promote the growth of feed animals.
Confusion and mental vagueness, e.g. in cerebral degeneration. Highly febrile illnesses. Enteritis. History of
intestinal infections or acute inflammatory fever. Chronic cholangitis and cholecystitis. Cholelithiasis. Duodenal
and gastric ulcer. Chronic pancreatitis.
RELATIONS - Compare: Ars., Echi., Pyrog.
REFERENCES - Murphy. Reckeweg.

name: Salol
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - salol. Salol. Phenol salicylate. Salolum. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Fever. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Influenza. Neuralgia. Rheumatism.
Smallpox.
HOMEOPATHIC - Salol, was primarily used as an anti-rheumatic, especially in the treatment of acute cases.
It was given as an antipyretic in 30 to 45 grain doses in powders or tablets. It is soluble in ether and petroleum
spirit, very sparingly, if at all in water.
 It does not disturb digestion because it passes through the stomach unaltered, being decomposed in the
duodenum, by the ferments of the pancreas into salicylic acid and phenol (it contains 38 percent phenol).
These are excreted by the kidneys and the condition of intestinal digestion has been estimated by the iength
of time required after the ingestion of Salol., for them to appear in the urine.
Helbing reported that it has been used in acute diarrhea, dysentery, cholera and other diseases where
intestinal asepsis in indicated and also in disorders of the bladder and urethra as a substitute for ordinary
mechanical irrigations and injections.
Its internal use in gonorrhea (in 5-grain doses three times a day) has met with much success.
Dull aching in head and all over body. Can hardly go up stairs, and it is dreadfully painful to sit on a hard stool.
The hands shrink when cold, cannot straighten the little fingers without much pain.
Head - Dreadful headache, especially over eyes. Dull aching in head and all over body.
Kidneys - Urine smelled strongly of violets.
Limbs - Rheumatic pains. Feeling of stiffness in joints. Limbs sensitive to touch. Pain in shoulder. Pain in right
arm in evening. Pain in wrists. Cramp in hand on writing. Hurts even to carry a book in hand. Buttocks sore.
Pain in left buttock, especially on walking.
Modalities - Worse walking, raising eyes, ascending stairs. Pain in buttocks worse sitting on hard stool. Worse
by touch, in evening.
Skin - Burning and itching eruption. Smallpox.
COMMENTS - The only proving of Salol, was made incidentally onachemistfrommakingup powders of the
remedy. He experienced very severe symptoms from inhaling the odor, and possible also some of the powder.
Rheumatic pains in joints with soreness and stiffness were marked, especially pain and soreness in the
buttocks, knees, and wrists.
The prover was subject to headaches, but he never had so violent a headache as that produced by Salol, and
conversely after the proving, Salol. 12c immediately relieved him when threatened with one of his usual
headaches.
The first symptom he noted was that his urine smelled of violets and it was only when this passed off that the
other symptoms came on. The joints felt stiff, “as if they wanted oiling.”
C. Beg referred to the use of Salol, in smallpox and other skin disorders attended with burning and itching. The
relief of itching in smallpox was a constant and most satisfactory result. When administered early it prevented
maturation of pustules.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bry. Compare: (1) Sal-ac., Salin.., Nat-sal., Carb-ac. (2) Wrist rheumatism, Act-
sp., Led., Viol-o. (3) Urine smells of violets. Terebe. (4) Gonorrhea, Napht., Petros. (5) Smallpox, Carb-ac.,
Sarr., Vario.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Salvia Divinorum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - salv-d. Salviadivinorum. Shepherdess’s herb. Ska pastora. Shka pastora. Maria pastora.
Mexican mint. Yerba de Maria. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and blossom-tips. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amnesia. Ascites. Debility. Delusions. Depression. Diarrhea. Drug, addictions. Edema.
Headache. Intoxication. Memory, loss. Nightmares. Panic attacks. Personality, disorders. Rheumatism. Vi-
sions.
HERBAL - The Latin name Salvia di vinorum literally translates to “sage of the seers.” The genus name Salvia
is derived from the Latin salvare, meaning “to heal” or “to save.” The words salvation and savior also come
from this root.
Salvia di vinorum is a sprawling perennial herb which grows wild only in the Sierra Mazatec region of Mexico.
Its leaves contain the extremely potent salvinorin-A. It has a history of use as a divinatory psychedelic for oral
use and has been widely available since the 1990’s primarily as a smoked herb.
Salvia divinorum is traditionally used by chewing pairs of leaves. Modern use includes both smoking and
chewing the leaves. When the leaves are chewed, the quid and bitter juice are held in the mouth to increase
absorption.
Strong effects can be difficult to attain from smoking dried leaf, but extracts and potency-bred leaves can cause
dramatic, sometimes frightening deep mind-states. Many people who try S. divinorum do not find the effects
at all pleasant and choose not to repeat the experience.
Historical uses include headache, diarrhea, rheumatism, debilitation and ascites. Intense shaking of body.
Inability to control muscles and maintain balance. Tendency to stagger, fall. Depression. May prove to be
 useful for those troubled with addictions.
MIND - Altered perceptions. Clarity of thought. Introspection. Insights into life and existence. Trances and
visionary states of intoxication. Dreamlike experiences. Powerful visions with open orclosed eyes. Visions of
past lives and times. Feels the presence of entities. Delusions and visions.
States of tranquility and ecstasy. Great relaxation and bliss. Uncontrollable hysterical laughter. Restlessness.
Panic attacks./n- tense experiences of fear, terror and panic. Speechless. Complete loss of memory.
Overlapping realities. The perception that one is in several locations at once. Feel detached from reality with
a heightened senses of space, sight smell and sound. Loss of the body and personal identity.
Sensation of dying. Near death experiences. Out of body experiences. Sensation of entering or perceiving
other dimensions, alternate realities. Revisiting places from the past, especially childhood.
Back - Prickling and tingling up and down the spine.
Perspiration - Increased perspiration.
Sensations - Sensation of pins and needles all over my body. Prickling and tingling. Sensation that the body
becomes suddenly very heavy. Sensations of physical push, pressure, or wind. Various sensations of
motion, or being pulled or twisted by forces of some kind.
Temperature - Change in body temperature, flushing.
COMMENTS - One person wrote, “For the next two hours I felt light headed and restless. I couldn’t sit still.
Whenever I sat down I felt compelled to get up. I tried to eat something and drink a little wine in order to get
grounded and relaxed, but I couldn’t seem to swallow anything. I had been shaken to the soul.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Anh., Bani-c., Cann-i., Op.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Salvia Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - salv. Salvia officinalis. Common Sage. N. O. Lamiaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and blossom-
tips. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cough, tickling. Fever. Gums, bleeds. Mouth, sores. Night-sweats. Perspiration, excessive.
Tuberculosis.
HERBAL - Gerard wrote, “Sage is singularly good for the head and brain, it quickened the senses and memory.
Sage strengthen the sinews, restore health to those that have palsy and take away shaky trembling of the
members.”
French doctors called attention to sage for gargling in cases of inflammation of the throat and for washing the
mouth in disorders of the gums.
HOMEOPATHIC - Salv. exerts a tonic influence on the skin. Controls excessive sweating when circulation is
enfeebled. Night-sweats in persons suffering from disorders of the respiratory organs, especially tuberculosis.
Colliquative perspiration. Soft skin, relaxed with enfeebled circulation and cold limbs. Suffocating, tickling
cough. Galactorrhea.
COMMENTS - Salv. should be given in doses of 20, 30 or 40 drops in a tablespoonful of water. The effects
manifest themselves very quickly, two hours after taking a dose, and these effects persist for two to six days.
The tickling cough of tuberculosis and the nightsweats are entirely relieved by doses of 20 to 40 drops in a
tablespoonful of water.
In the numerous experiments made with it, there were never any disagreeable concomitant effects. Salv. acts
even more favorably on the tickling coughs in tuberculosis patients than Bell., Rumx., so that preparations of
morphine and codeine could be dispensed with.
In one case. Ms. Smith had for three weeks an irritating cough following an attack of pneumonia. The irritation
being particularly great, she was given, fresh from the garden, some sage to chew, and the irritation was
instantly relieved.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Phel., Merc., Tub. (2) Chrysan. (3) Salv-sc - tonic influence on nervous system,
dose, teaspoonful to one pint hot water, as inhalant for sponging. (4) Rub-t.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Sambucus Canadensis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - samb-c. Sambucuscanadensis. Elder-bush. Marsh elder-bush. Sambucus humilis. Sambucus
glauca. N. O. Capriflia- ceae. Tincture of buds, flowers, tender shoots and leaves. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Asthma. Blotches. Cuts. Larynx, dry. Lumbago. Wounds.
 HERBAL - The indigenous North American elder grows in rich alluvial soils, flowers in July and fruits in
September.
The species, said Millspaugh is not sufficiently distinct from the European elder (Samb. nigra), differing only in
being less woody and having more loose cymes, larger flowers and more compound leaves.
Millspaugh said of Samb-c. that a decoction or ointment of the flowers and leaves was used as an application
to large wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - The severe chest symptoms and blotched face recall symptoms of Samb. with which it is
probably identical in action. Uneasiness, and unrest. Exhaustion. Recurrence of symptoms.
MIND - Depression and dread of undefined danger.
Back - Back felt sprained. Pressing pain in lumbar region.
Chest - Palpitations. Heaviness and constriction in chest, as from a heavy load. Aroused from sleep by a
terrible constriction of chest and heart, cannot lie down for fear of choking.
Face - Face flushed and broken out in blotches, looks ill.
Head - Severe drawing in head with fullness, motion causes sensation as if water were undulating in it. Head
heavy, confused with drawing and darting pains.
Heart - Constriction of chest and heart, lying down causes choking. Sharp pain in heart (region of valves), with
palpitations, at times visible through the clothes. Heart labors heavily. Pulse rose to 100, but became normal
at end of perspiration.
Kidneys - Pressure in kidney region, followed by profuse flow of clear urine. Frequent urination. Urine
albuminous.
Limbs - Sharp, darting rheumatic pains hands and feet.
Lungs - Breathing labored, asthmatic, wheezing. Has to sit up in bed to get breath.
Modalities - Better by sweat, getting out of bed. Worse from lying down.
Mouth - Mouth parched, dry, desire for drink.
Temperature - Sweat, soon becoming profuse, which gradually ameliorates all other symptoms (except
exhaustion). Head perspired less than rest of body.
Throat - Pharynx and larynx felt dry and swollen, impeding free respiration.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Sambucus Nigra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - samb. Sambucus nigra. Elder. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves and flowers.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Asthma. Chest, oppression. Choking. Colic. Contusions. Coryza, dry. Coughs.
Croup. Cyanosis. Edema. Emaciation. Headaches, catarrhal. Hoarseness. Hydrocele. Ileus. Laryngismus.
Spasms. Snuffles. Suffocation. Tuberculosis. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - Samb. was proved by Hahnemann and appears in his Materia Medica Pura. It acts
especially on the respiratory organs, kidneys and the skin.
Spasm, mainly affecting the respiratory system, larynx, chest and nasal passages. Shortness of breath.
Snuffles in infants preventing breathing and nursing. Dry coryza. When it occurs lower down in the tract, it
causes dyspnea. The child awakens suddenly nearly suffocated, face livid, blue. Sits up in bed, turns blue,
gasps for breath, which it finally gets. The attack passes off but is again repeated. Child inspires but cannot
expire. Sleeps into the attack. The breathing is rattling. Croup, whooping cough, asthma.
Profuse sweat during waking hours, dry heat when asleep, particularly in tubercular or febrile conditions. A
deep, dry cough precedes the fever paroxysm. Fever without thirst. Dreads uncovering.
Edema, dropsical swellings in various parts of the body, especially legs, instep and feet. When edema affects
the nose it may give rise to obstruction. Contusions cause dark red swelling.
MIND - General trembling with anxiety. Constant state of fretfulness. Very easily frightened. Fright followed
by suffocative attacks. Worse from fright or strong emotions. Sees images when shutting eyes. Abdomen -
Pressive pain in abdomen with nausea. Spasmodic tearings, shootings and pinchings in abdominal muscles,
with expulsion of flatus. Colic with nausea and flatulence. Frequent, watery, slimy stools.
Back - Aching in middle of spine during repose and movement. Lancinations in scapulae.
Causations - Ill effects of fright, grief, anxiety, excessive sexual indulgence. Fright causes suffocative attack.
Chest - Oppression of chest with pressure in stomach, nausea and weakness. Pressure on sternum. Sudden
sensation of contraction in sides of chest.
Constitutions - Suited to diseases of scrofulous children that affect the air passages especially. Suited to
persons previously robust and fleshy who suddenly become emaciated.
 Ears - Sharp stitches in right inner ear, with cramp pain in it. Itching, creeping in ears and in throat.
Eyes - Pupils at first contracted, then greatly dilated. Photophobia. Half open in sleep.
Face - Pale, bluish, puffy. Turns blue with cough. Blotches on face. Red, burning
spots on cheeks. Heat and perspiration of face. Hot face with icy cold feet.
Female - Menses too profuse, like metrorrhagia. Debilitating sweats after childbirth.
Food - Thirst without relishing the drinks. Head - Headache as from intoxication. Motion of head causes tension
and dizziness. Pressure and expansion in head. Sudden shocks in the brain. Digging pain in vertex. Scurf on
head with intolerable itching.
Heart - Orgasm in whole body. Occasional omission of heartbeat. Pulse generally very frequent and small,
sometimes slow, full. Intermitting. Angina pectoris where pressure proceeds from spine.
Kidneys - Dropsical symptoms with vomiting of bile and distress in stomach after eating. Acute nephritis.
Profuse urination with a sensation of heat in the body, dry heat of skin. Urine frequent and scanty.
Limbs - Tension in hamstrings as if they were too short. Tearing in legs and ankles. Edematous swelling in
legs, insteps and feet. Icy-cold feet with a warm body. Hands and feet bloated and blue. Drawing in forearms
and bones of hands. Paralytic heaviness in elbow joint. Lancinations in wrists. Trembling of hands (when
writing).
Lungs - Spasmodic croup. Asthma. Cyanosis. Sudden suffocation or strangling on falling to sleep, or waking
him at midnight with violent sweat. Child awakes suddenly, nearly suffocating, sits up. turns blue.
Paroxysmal, suffocative cough, coming on about midnight with crying and dyspnea. Loose choking cough.
Spells of coughing, before fever. Dry coryza. Sniffles of infants, nose dry and obstructed. Cannot expire
(Meph.). When nursing child must let go of nipple, nose blocked up, cannot breathe. Whistling breathing.
Male - Hydrocele from injury. Swelling of scrotum.
Modalities - Better sitting up in bed, motion, from pressure over a sharp edge, and wrapping up. Worse from
dry, cold air, uncovering. Worse cold drink while over heated, eating fruits. Worse motion. Worse sleep, rest,
lying down in bed, on left side. Worse about midnight, after midnight, 2 to 3 a.m., wakes with sense of stoppage
of air tubes. Head low aggravates, must sit up to regain breath.
Mouth - Dryness of the mouth and throat without thirst. Half open in sleep. Toothache with tearing and
lancinations in all the teeth and with a sensation as if cheeks were swollen.
Neck - Pressive heaviness in nape. Deep incisive lancinations in muscles of neck. Sweat on throat and neck
with children.
Nose - Dry coryza with snuffles in infants. Sensation of numbness in nose with itching on bridge. Obstruction
of nose with accumulation of thick and viscid mucus in nostrils. Dry coryza of children.
Pelvis - Pains in loins with drawing pressure. Incisive blows in loins.
Perspiration - Very debilitating sweats. Profuse sweat over entire body during waking hours. Continued
perspiration while awake, changing into dry heat as soon as one goes to sleep. Night sweats, except on head,
worse towards morning.
Rectum - Irritable anus with hemorrhoids. Frequent, watery, slimy stools.
Sensations - As if head were filled with water. Skull as if stretched. As if suffocating.
Skin - Dry heat during sleep. Tingling, itching of skin. Sudden painful drawing in all points over surface while
sitting. Edema, anasarca. Bloated and swollen, general dropsy, profuse sweat on waking.
Sleep - Frequent waking with a start, with obstructed respiration. Child starts up suddenly as if suffocating.
Incomplete sleep with mouth and eyes half open. Sleeps with arms above head. Dry heat during sleep, profuse
perspiration after waking. Lascivious dreams.
Stomach - Pressure in stomach. Acute lancinations under the stomach, worse by pressing upon it. Vomiting
in morning, first of mucus and milk (or food) that had been taken, followed by bile.
Temperature - Shuddering with shivering. Icy coldness of hands and feet. Pricking, tingling in skin. Intermittent
fever.
Dry, burning fever while asleep, copious sweating on waking. Fever with excessive perspiration, especially at
night. Debilitating night sweats (Salv., Acet-ac.').Dreads uncovering. Dry, deep cough precedes the fever
paroxysm. Sweats with cough.
Throat - Hoarseness with tenacious mucus in larynx. Screeching voice. Spasms of glottis. Itching, tingling in
throat.
Vertigo - Dizziness and confusion in the head, during movement, on rising.
COMMENTS - The leaves of Sambucus nigra have an unpleasant odor when bruised, which is supposed to
be offensive to most insects. A decoction of the leaves is sometimes used by gardeners to keep caterpillars
off delicate plants.
Green noted that sheep that have the rot can be cured by letting them eat the bark and young leaves of Samb.
 Herbalists use the inner bark, as well as the leaves, to make an ointment. The flowers serve for fomentations
or are made into a medicinal tea. According to the Treasury of Botany, the berries are the principal ingredient
in elderberry wine.
Millspaugh said that the bark contains viburnic acid, which is identical with valerianic acid. This no doubt
accounts for the odor and suggests a relationship in action between sambucus, valerian and the viburnum.
Nash once relieved with Samb. 200c a very bad case of asthma in an old woman, who had suffocative attacks.
The relief was accompanied by a profuse flow of urine, which carried off a large amount of dropsical effusion
in her legs and abdomen.
Severe croup, whooping cough, bronchitis, and asthma. Infants with chronic snuffles (Thuj., after vaccinations).
Suffocating attacks (Ip.). Tendency for attacks to recur. Croupy attack “passes off but is again repeated.”
Spasms in the throat. Severe coughing with mucus. Thick, white, upper respiratory mucus that suffocates and
gags the person (Ant-t.)
Patient can wake up in the middle of the night, grab at their throat, face turns blue. Waking with a spasm where
the oxygen gets cut off (Cup.). Worse about midnight or after midnight, worse 2:00 to 3:00 in the morning.
Worse dry, cold air.
RELATIONS - Samb-c. may be regarded as practically identical with Satnb-n. Antidoted by: Ars., Camph.
Antidote to: Ars. - relieves ailments from abuse of Ars. Compare: (1) Ip., Meph., Op. (2) Samb-c. - great
value in dropsies. (3) In Miller’s asthma, Arum-d. (4) Dyspnea, inspires, cannot expire. Chlor., Meph. (5) Sleeps
into the attack, Lach. (6) Peculiarities of sweating. Chin., Con., Thuj., Puls. (7) Dreads uncovering, Nux-v. (8)
Fat people emaciate suddenly, lod., Tub. (9) Tenacious mucus in larynx, Kali-bi. (10) Effects of cold drink when
over-heated, Bell-p. (11) Effects of dry cold. Aeon. Snuffles, Am-c., Nux-v. Compatible: Bell., Con., Nux-v.,
Phos., Rhus-t., Sep. Follows well: Op. (effects of fright).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.
