name: Sanguinaria Canadensis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sang. Sanguinariacanadensis. Blood-root. Puccoon. N. O. Papaveraceae. Tincture of fresh
root. The resin, leaves, seeds, seed-vessels, powdered root and expressed juice have also been used.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anemia. Aphonia. Arthritis. Asthma. Bilious, disorders. Blood, disorders. Breast,
tumor. Bronchitis. Cancer. Catarrh. Chest, pains. Cold. Croup. Deafness. Diphtheria. Dysmenorrhea. Dys-
pepsia. Ear, polyps. Gleet. Granular, lids. Headaches. Heartburn. Hemoptysis. Hot, flashes. Influenza.
Keratitis. Liver, disorders. Menopause. Menstruation, painful. Migraines. Nails, ulceration. Neuralgias. Edema,
glottidis. Ophthalmia. Pharyngitis. Tuberculosis. Physometra. Pneumonia, acute. Polyps. Pregnancy,
disorders. Quinsy. Rheumatism. Rhus poisoning. Shoulder, rheumatism. Sinusitis. Smell, loss. Stomach,
neurosis. Syphilis. Tinnitus. Tumors. Vomiting. Whitlow. Whooping cough.
HERBAL - The bloodroot is commonly found throughout the United States and Canada, and is the sole
representative of the genus
Sanguinaria of the Papaveraceae. It is herbaceous, has a thick, branching root stock, which creeps along
underground.
In early spring, it sends up from the ends of the little side branches a single long- stalked leaf and another stalk
bearing a solitary flower. The leaf is wrapped around the flower bud when it rises from the ground and is bluntly
five to nine-lobed, roundish at first, but later kidney-shaped.
The Treasury of Botany noted that Native Americans used the orange-colored juice of the root for smearing
their bodies and for staining various domestic articles. The plant had also been successfully used by American
and French dyers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sang, is a right-sided remedy, affecting the head, liver, chest and deltoid. Affects chiefly
the mucus membranes, especially of the respiratory tract. Suited to pulmonary disorders with liver involvement.
Marked vaso-motor disturbances, as seen in the circumscribed redness of the cheeks, flashes of heat,
determination of blood to head and chest, general pulsations and distention of temporal veins.
Burning heat and ebullitions. Burning in various parts. Burning sensations like from hot water. Burning in
palms and soles. Burning in throat, under sternum, spots or stitches in chest, palms and soles. Burnt feeling
in tongue. Applicable to menopausal disorders.
Influenza coughs. Sudden stopping of catarrh of respiratory tract followed by diarrhea. Tuberculosis.
Mucus membranes become dry. Acrid, blood-streaked or foul discharge. Sick and faint from odor of flowers.
Polyps, nasal, uterine. Fungus excrescences. Pains in places where bones are least covered. Internal
rawness. Lies on back with head elevated. Bilious. Pains increase and decrease with the sun. Symptoms
 ascend or end in bilious vomiting.
MIND - Hopefulness, confident of recovery. Mind confused, better by belchings. Anxiety and dread preceded
vomiting and delirium. Borrows trouble. Grumbling. Angry, irritability, moroseness. Rage after insults.
Disgusting thoughts and ideas. Sensitive to noise.
Mental torpor, stupor, heaviness, sleepiness. Lassitude, indisposed to move or make any mental effort.
Indolence. Dreamy state with eyes open. Sensation as if paralyzed and unable to move while lying on her
back. Recognizes everything but can’t move. Abdomen - Throbbing in abdomen. Tension in epigastrium.
Awoke with severe pain in region of spleen. Violent stitches in spleen. Sensation as if hot water poured itself
from breast into abdomen, followed by diarrhea. Flatulent distention with escape of flatus from vagina. Colic
with torpor of liver.
Back - Soreness down muscles of back. Pain in inner border of right shoulder blade. Pain in sacrum from
lifting.
Breasts - Sore and enlarged breasts, at menopause. Pain in right breast to shoulder. Severe soreness under
right nipple. Hot streaming from breast towards liver. Pain in breast with periodic cough.
Chest - Pain, burning soreness, in right chest to shoulder. Burning in chest, as of a hot steam extending to
abdomen with cough. Tickling behind sternum, causes a constant hacking cough, worse at night on lying down.
Hemoptysis. Hydrothorax. Pneumonia.
Ears - Burning of ears with redness of cheeks. Cracking in right ear while stroking cheek. Earache with
headache. Polyps. Humming and roaring in the ear, painfully sensitive to sounds, at menopause. Throat
disorders causing deafness and earache.
Eyes - Acute conjunctivitis. Yellow sclera, jaundice. Retinal congestion. Catarrhal ophthalmia, granular lids.
Redness of eyes in morning. Burning dryness in eyes, followed by copious lachrymation. Lachrymation with
coryza, tears hot. Vapor or cloud before eyes. Eyeballs painful on moving them. Swelling over eyebrows.
Blepharitis.
Face - Hectic flush, redness and burning of cheeks. Neuralgia, pain extends in all directions from upper
jaw. Fullness and tenderness behind angle of jaws.
Female - Amenorrhea. Before menses, itching of axilla. Menstruation too early with a discharge of black blood.
Menses offensive, profuse. Leucorrhea fetid, corrosive. Uterine polyps. Menopausal disorders, especially
flushes of heat. Burning of palms and soles at menopause.
Food - Loss of appetite with great weakness of digestion. Unquenchable thirst. Craves, knows not for what.
Craving for spicy things. Aversion to butter, leaves a sweetish taste. Sweet things aggravate, taste bitter, cause
burning. Bilious headaches if he goes without food.
Head - Periodical sick headache, pain begins in occiput, spreads upwards or ascending from occiput to
over right eye. Pain in the occiput like a flash of lightning. Pain in small spot over upper left parietal bone.
Veins and temples are distended. Headaches if he goes without food. Headaches, better sleep, vomiting
and passing copious flow of urine. Headaches return at menopausal, every seventh day (Sulph., Sabad.). Sun
headache. Hemicrania increases and decreases with the sun.
Heart - Weak feeling, irregular action. Palpitations. Valvular disease with lung development, phosphates in
urine and loss of flesh. Metastasis of rheumatism (or gout) to heart from outward applications.
Kidneys - Dull, heavy pain across kidneys. Urine dark yellow with jaundice. Copious and frequent, clear, worse
at night. Urine high-colored, red sediment. Ardor urine.
Limbs - Rheumatism of right shoulder.
Pain in shoulder, worse night. Cutting pain or stiffness in right deltoid, worse raising or turning arm. Pain in
arm better swinging arm to and fro. Itching in axilla, worse before menses. Aching and swelling of ball of thumb
(right). Palms wrinkled. Burning of palms and soles, worse covers, at menopause. Rheumatism of left hip
joint and nape of neck. Pain in bones near surface. Neuritis better by touching the part.
Liver - Pain over region of liver. Jaundice. Liver-cough.
Lungs - Severe dyspnea and constriction of chest. Asthma with stomach disorders (Nux-v.). Pneumonia,
catarrhal, right side, better lying on back. Sudden stoppage of catarrh of air passages brings on diarrhea.
Tuberculosis. Hemoptysis from suppressed menses. Cough of gastric origin, relieved by eructation. Cough
with burning pain in chest, worse right side. Tough, rust-colored, purulent, offensive sputum, almost
impossible to raise. Spasmodic cough after influenza andafter whooping cough. Cough returns with every
fresh cold.
Male - Burning in glans. Cheesy secretions from glans (syphilis). Gleet, old cases. Emissions two nights in
succession, after which he felt very well.
Modalities - Better acids, sour things. Better vomiting, passing flatus. Better cool air. Better darkness, sleep,
lying on back or on left side. Worse from motion, raising arms, looking up. Worse touch, right side. Worse
 light, sun, odors, and sweets. Worse 3 a.m., weekly, nightly, periodically. Worse menopause.
Mouth - Ulceration of mouth and fauces with dry, burning sensation. Palate feels scalded. Tongue white, feels
burnt. Anterior tongue looks red, like raw beef. Offensive breath. Sweet things taste bitter.
Neck - Soreness of nape on being touched. Rheumatic pain in nape, shoulders and arms. Pain in right side of
neck as if strained in left side.
Nose - Nasal polyps. Chronic rhinitis, membrane dry and congested. Hay fever. Ozaena with profuse,
offensive, yellowish discharges. Coryza, followed by diarrhea. Pain at the root of nose. Rose-cold with
subsequent asthma. Sensitive to odors. Loss or perverted sense of smell, smell in nose like roasted onion.
Rectum - Alternate diarrhea and constipation. Colic followed by diarrhea. Diarrhea as coryza improves.
Dysentery. Urging to stool, but only discharges of flatus. Ineffectual urging to stool, then vomiting. Bilious,
liquid, gushing diarrhea (Nat-s., Lyc.). Copious apple-green stools with flatus. Hemorrhoids. Cancer of rectum.
Sensations - As if forehead would burst. As of a band across forehead. As if head were drawn forward. As if
electric current shooting through head. As if temples and scalp were alive with irrepressible pulsation. As if
eyes would be pressed out. As if hairs were in eyes. As if paralyzed. As if she was in a railway car that was
moving and jarring her and as if all about her moved rapidly and confusedly.
Skin - Heat and dryness of skin. Prickling heat spreading over body. Burning and itching, worse by heat.
Circumscribed red spots. Red, blotchy eruptions, worse in spring. Acne with scanty menses. Scaly eruptions,
carbuncles. Itching and nettlerash before the nausea. Old indolent ulcers with callous borders and ichorous
discharge. Fungus excrescences. Antidotes rhuspoisoning. Jaundice.
Sleep - Drowsiness causing mental and bodily indolence. Sleeplessness at night, awakens in a fright as if he
would fall. Can’t sleep without brandy. Slightest noise disturbs, yet is sleepy and dreamy. Dreams of sea
voyages with sensation of being rocked. Dreams of frightful business matters.
Stomach - Sinking, faint, all-gone feeling (Phos., Sep.). Stomach pains to right shoulder. Burning in stomach
with headache, and vomiting. Hiccough while smoking. Nausea with salivation, not better by vomiting. Vomiting
of bitter water, sour, acrid fluids, of ingesta, of worms. Spitting of bile, gastro-duodenal catarrh.
Teeth - Looseness of teeth, with salivation. Toothache from picking teeth. Pain in hollow teeth, especially when
touched by food. Pain in decayed teeth after cold drinks. Bleeding, spongy, fungoid gums.
Temperature - Fever, heat and delirium. Intermittent fevers, marsh fevers, nervous fever. Fever from
pulmonary, hepatic or gastric inflammation. Flushes of heat, rising into face and head with headache. Burning,
scanty sweat. Copious sweat, cold sweat. Heat flying from head to stomach. Chill with nausea, headache.
Chill and shivering in back. Shaking chill.
Throat - Dry cough, tickling in throat. Tonsillitis. Ulcerated sore throat, as if raw and denuded. Sore, swollen
(right), pains to ear and chest. Burning, worse eating sweet things. Dry and constricted. Sensation in pharynx
as if scalded by hot drink. Edema of larynx. Larynx, full and dry in singers. Aphonia.
Tongue - Burnt, sore feeling. Tip of tongue burns as if scalded. Crawling, pricking on tip of tongue. Stitches in
left side of tongue. White coated tongue with slimy, fatty taste. Red streak through middle of tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo, worse looking up and moving head rapidly, with nausea, fainting and headache.
COMMENTS - Acts powerfully on the outer chest, sternum and breasts. Reputed to cure cancer, polyps and
new growths (Chel.). Clarke saw breast tumors diminish under its action.
Grimmer stated that this remedy has cured breast cancer with severe burning pains and inflammatory
symptoms of the mucus membranes, the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts, and the skin. Pronounced
heat, flushing and redness of the skin. Characteristic burning pains (wherever pain exists).
S. L. Mitchell recorded the fatal poisoning of workmen who drank the tincture in mistake for brandy. They were
all soon seized with severe racking and burning pains in the stomach and bowels with intense thirst. “Burning”
is one of the leading notes of the remedy and is found in many different parts.
Winterburn published a case illustrating this indication in the region of the stomach. Mr. F., 48, ofsanguino-
bilious temperament, energetic and refined, had been ill with pains in the stomach for several months. A
clairvoyant had recommended “a decoction of blood-root and bone-set in tablespoonful doses.” Each dose
produced “intense burning pains in the stomach lasting for hours,” and it had to be discontinued.
Weeks later, Winterburn was consulted and found Mr. F with burning in his epigastrium with pressure, worse
at night, but coming on soon after lying down and
compelling the patient to rise. Belching gave no relief. Great appetite, torpid bowels, an unsatisfactory relief
each morning, leaving a sense of discomfort.
There was a peculiar drawing pain in the shoulders and arms during sleep, so that when he woke his fists were
tightly clenched and flexed on the sternal end of his clavicle, lameness and weariness of the muscles followed.
Sang. 200c, was chosen aftercareful comparison with Nux-v., Graph, and others. It was given every night at
bedtime. After the first dose, the symptoms disappeared “like magic,” and the patient was soon well.
 Leonard said “a circumscribed burning in the chest, commonly followed by heat through abdomen and
diarrhea,” is a strong indication for Sang, in pneumonic conditions.
Sang, also has the circumscribed hectic flush on the cheeks, as in tuberculosis in which it is frequently
indicated. Flushed face, at times dark red or livid (Op.). It has the “hopefulness” of tubercular patients.
Severe headaches. Migraine, starting at the back of the head and moving to above the right eye (Sil.).
Headaches begin at occiput, spreading upwards and forwards, settling over the right eye. Pains like a flash of
lightning in occiput. Bursting headaches, as if the eyes would be pressed out. Better by sleep. Symptoms begin
in the morning, increase to noon, then diminish. Headaches return at menopause. Right-sided headaches with
the flu. Bilious or gastric headaches.
Hering described the headache as the “American sick-headache.” There is a rush of blood causing faintness
and nausea, pains are sharp or throbbing. Patients cannot bear light, odors, or the least jar, as that of anyone
stepping across the floor. There can be vomiting of food and bile. Pain so violent the patient goes out of her
mind or seeks relief by pressing head against pillow or pressing with the hands.
Cooper gave as a keynote, “If he goes without food, gets bilious headaches.” Violent, throbbing headache with
extreme nausea and vomiting, frequent, fetid belch- ings and great salivation. Severe burning in stomach,
vomits bitter water and sour, acrid fluids. Nausea may not be relieved by vomiting. Sweets taste bitter,
aggravate the burning. Vomiting of worms. Tormenting thirst. Offensive breath and flatus.
Irritation of the nasal mucus membrane. Polyps. Coryza with pain at root of the nose. Influenza, hay fever and
ozaena. Sinusitis, more on the right side. Lost or perverted sense of smell, sensitive to the odor of flowers.
Laryngitis and membranous croup. Tracheal and bronchial coughs in epidemic influenza. Cough after influenza
or whooping cough, particularly in children. Cough returns with every fresh cold. Violent, dry cough, wheezing,
whistling, metallic. Offensive and acrid discharges. Sputa is almost impossible to raise.
Clarke recorded several cases in which Sang, relieved patients who had thick plugs of suffocating mucus
which the patients were too weak to dislodge.
Offensive menses, bright red flow, later blood darker and less offensive. Itching of axillae before menses.
Eruptions on the face of young women, during scanty menses. Menopausal disorders, flashes of heat,
leucorrhea, and painful enlargement of breasts.
Neuralgia of the face, ameliorated by kneeling down and pressing head firmly against the floor. Pain extends
in all directions from the upper jaw.
Rheumatism. Rheumatic pain in right arm and shoulder, worse at night. Cannot raise the arm, but can swing
it to and fro. Frozen shoulder. Great affinity for the right shoulder. Right side generally more affected.
Symptoms go from right to left. Marked periodicity. Pains in places where the bones are least covered.
Cooper gave the case of a woman, 19, who had a condition of her throat from scarlatina three years previously,
and lately increasing deafness. There were noises all over her head and vertigo. Sudden flushings in daytime,
menses too frequent, and profuse leucorrhea. Backache, paining her to walk, forcing her to give up teaching
from the pain.
Poor appetite from the headaches and tinnitus, she often had pain behind the angles of lower jaw and swollen
glands. All symptoms disappeared after a single dose of Sang, tincture, although at first the leucorrhea was
increased.
F. Nichol, in giving Hale his experience with Sang, in croup, said he used a solution of Sanguinarine in vinegar,
and he found that the most effective preparation.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Just. - bronchial catarrh, coryza, hoarseness, oversensitive. (2) Dig. (migraine).
(3) Bell., Iris, Meli., Lach., Ferr., Op. (4) Chel., Op. In rheumatism of right deltoid, Mag-c. (5) Headache
extending forward from occiput and settling over right eye, Spig. (6) Headache better by hard pressure, Chin.,
Indg., Mag-m. (7) Paroxysms of headache ending in profuse urination, Ign., Gels., Verat. (8) Menstrual
headache, Sep. scanty flow, Sang, profuse. (9) Right side, throbbing, congestive headache, worse light and
noise, Bell. (10) Periodic sick headaches, Iris-v. (11) Pneumonia, Phos., Ant-t. Compatible: Bell. - in scarlatina
rashes. It antidotes: Op. Complementary: Ant-t.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Sanguinarinum Nitricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sanguin-n. Sanguinarinum nitricum. Sanguinarine nitrate. Trituration. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenoids. Allergies. Asthma. Borborygmus. Bronchitis. Catarrh. Colic. Colds. Coryza. Coughs.
Deafness. Eustachian catarrh. Hayfever. Headaches./n/7uenza. Laryngitis. Pharyngitis. Polyps. Post-nasal
catarrh. Quinsy. Stiff-neck. Throat, sore. Tinnitus.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Sanguin-n. is a very fine brownish-red powder, pungent, acid, bitter and inodorous. It is
soluble in alcohol, ether, water and oils, but not in the same proportion in all. Pure sanguinarine is a pearly-
white substance, but when combined with any of the acids the result is a salt of some shade of red, crimson
or scarlet. The color of the blood-root may be due to the presence of some native salt of Sanguinarine.
Sang-n. was proved in 3x trituration by Professor Owens of Pulte Medical College. Nasal polyps. Acute and
chronic catarrh. Acute pharyngitis (Wye.). Smarting and burning in throat and chest especially under sternum.
Influenza. Chronic follicular pharyngitis. Lachrymation, pains in eyes and head, sore scalp, sense of
obstruction.
Abdomen - Borborygmus and pains in abdomen, as if diarrhea would set in, with sharp, cutting pains.
Back - Stiffness in muscles of left neck and shoulder.
Causations - Driving in cold wind, winter weather, exposure.
Chest - Pressure behind center of sternum.
Tightness in the chest. Tension in chest, burning and accumulation of mucus behind center of sternum. Short,
hacking cough arising from sensation of tightness in chest.
Ears - Obstruction of Eustachian tube. Roaring in right ear. Difficulty in distinguishing sounds.
Eyes - Sore, aching pain in eyeballs. Burning, pressing aching, and sore pains in eyes. Profuse lachrymation,
tears gush out. Redness and soreness of inner canthi. Redness of lids and conjunctiva. Sight dim, as if looking
through gauze.
Food - Little appetite. Everything tastes dry like chips. Coffee did not taste natural, wanted something
succulent, not pungent, but soothing to mouth and throat.
Head - Pain in supra-orbital region. Burning pain in forehead and root of nose. Sensation of obstruction and
fullness in head, ameliorated by discharge of a large quantity of thick, yellow, sweet-tasting mucus.
Kidneys - Passed urine every hour during the night. Urine had bright yellow or white sediment.
Limbs - Stiffness in muscles of left shoulder and neck.
Lungs - Strong desire for fresh air. Sense of suffocation. Dryness and burning in throat and bronchials.
Feeling as if air passages lined with thick, stiff mucus or pus. Chronic nasal, laryngeal and bron
chial catarrh. Raises thin, frothy mucus, which is very tenacious. Tickling cough. Short, hacking cough with
expectoration of thick, yellow, sweetish mucus. Cough is deep and rattling.
Modalities - Worse touch, at night. Pressure aggravates soreness of eyes. Bathing with warm water
ameliorates heat in forehead. Headache is ameliorates by discharge of much mucus from nose.
Mouth - Acrid, burning sensation on tongue. Ulceration on the side of the tongue. Roughness and dryness
in mouth and throat. Heat in mouth as if pepper had been taken. Increased flow of mucus and saliva with
sneezing and burning in forehead. Bitter taste extending back to root of tongue.
Nose' - Dry and burning nostrils. Feels obstructed. Enlarged turbinates at beginning of hypertrophic process.
Profuse, watery mucus with burning pain, with pressure over root of nose. Sneezing. Secretion scant,
tendency to dryness. Nostrils plugged with thick, yellow, bloody mucus. Small crusts which bleed when
removed. Post-nasal secretions stuck to naso-phar- ynx, dislodged with difficulty. Rawness and soreness in
posterior sinuses.
Sleep - Sleep poor, restless from feverish and irritable condition.
Stomach - Sensation of burning in stomach and esophagus. Belching up of putridsmelling gas though she
had eaten nothing since morning.
Throat - Voice altered, deep, hoarse. Rough, dry, constricted, burning. Right tonsil sore, swallowing difficult.
COMMENTS - The catarrhal symptoms of Sanguin-n. appear in great intensity, the nose, eyes, throat and
bronchi being affected. Sensation of obstruction and fullness in the head, accumulation of mucus obstructing
nose, awakes frequently with dry mouth, the nose being obstructed.
Accumulation of mucus behind center of sternum, sense of suffocation, feeling as if air-passages lined with
thick, stiff mucus or pus. Heat and tension behind sternum is characteristic and so is expectoration of quantities
of sweet-tasting mucus. Expectoration
of thin, frothy, very tenacious mucus.
Lachrymation, pains in eyes and head, sore scalp, obstructed nose and burning pains throughout all regions
were experienced. Symptoms of influenza, even to the loss or perversion of taste. “Sensation arising to nostrils
as if he had eaten strong horseradish.”
Hale reported the case of Mr. B., 40, dark, had for eight years in spite of continuous old-school treatment,
chronic post-nasal catarrh, bronchitis and laryngitis. Voice altered, deep, hoarse, speech with effort, as if from
chest. Severe pressure from behind sternum. Mucus membrane dry, raised only a few balls of gray mucus.
He spent two winters on St. John’s River, Florida, and was better there, but worse again on his return north.
Sanguin-n. 6c trituration, was given every two hours. In one week he was better, there was more moisture in
 his throat than three had been for two years. Voice markedly better.
Sanguin-n. was given every four hours. In ten weeks he regained six pounds of his lost weight and strength in
proportion. The voice not having improved in the same degree, Caust. 6c and afterwards Dros. 3c, were given
and in sixteen weeks he was perfectly well.
Mrs. S., city missionary, 49, had constant hacking cough, raw, sore feeling in throat, sore aching and pressing
behind sternum. She was much exposed to cold winds of winter, which set up coryza and irritation. Sanguin-
n. 6c. every two hours, enabled her to follow her occupation without suffering and in ten weeks she was
completely cured.
O. W., 55, subject to frequent attacks of cold in head, throat and chest. After a long drive in open trap contracted
a severe cold in head, throat, lungs. Sore and lame all over, frequent sneezing, lachrymation.
Next day sore throat very marked, constant tickling in throat-pit, exciting cough, at first short and hacking, but
in two days it became violent and convulsive. Bell, and Dros. did little good. Pressure behind sternum became
very severe.
Sanguin-n. 6c was given every two hours. In four hours copious perspiration came on with frequent sneezing.
Next day, sore throat appeared after waking from a troubled and restless sleep, constriction of throat with
difficult swallowing, tension across chest radiating from behind sternum.
Sanguin-n. was given every hour. In one hour, free discharge from nose set in; three hours, moisture and
relaxation of constriction across chest. The discharge was yellow and sweetish-tasting, continued all day. Slept
well and woke next morning feeling quite free. But little cough or coryza during the day. The following morning
he was quite well.
C. Wesselhoeft regarded Sanguin-n. as the simillimum for “New England colds.” Adenoids and polyps have
been cured with it. There is great craving for air.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sanguin-t. - exophthalmos. (2) Mydriasis, dim vision. Arum- t., Psor., Kali-bi.,
Sang. (3) Burning in nostrils, Arum-t. (4)Tenacious mucus, Kali-bi. (5) Hay fever, Psor. (6) Sweet expectoration,
Stann.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Sanguinarinum Pura
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sanguin. Sanguinarinum pura. N. O. Papaveraceae. Trituration. Solution in vinegar. Historical
dose: All potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sanguin, is a pearly white substance. Thomas noted that in smallest physiological doses it
acts as “expectorant,” in large, it causes nausea and still larger vomiting. In repeated doses, it lowers the
pulse rate.
Useful for croup. Pseudo-membranous croup. Great dyspnea. Hoarse, muffled cough, with complete aphonia.
Grasped his throat in agony. Nausea and vomiting.
COMMENTS - T. Nichol gave his experience with a solution of one grain of Sanguin, in two ounces of vinegar
in cases of pseudomembranous croup. He related the case of W. G., age 5, who had been ill some days.
Nichol found him with a hoarse, muffled cough, complete aphonia, pulse 132. Soft palate and fauces covered
with pearly, fibrinous exudation, a hissing sound was heard on auscultating larynx.
Great dyspnea. The child stretched back his head and grasped his throat in agony. Features swollen and dark.
Sangn. acet, was given and in fifteen hours there was notable improvement. In forty-eight hours the boy was
out of danger.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Sanguinarinum Tartaricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sang-t. Sanguinarinum tartari- cum. Sanguinarine tartrate. Papaveraceae. Trituration.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Exophthalmos. Mydriasis. Stool, bilious. Vision, dim.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tully and Terry experimented with Sang-t. in considerable doses. Tully said he repeatedly
witnessed all the effects of sanguinaria root, save the neuralgic pains and the convulsive disorders, from the
use of Sang-t.
The most peculiar of the symptoms are starting and protrusion of the eyes, extreme mydriasis, haggard
expression and cold surface and cold sweats.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Sanicula Aqua
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sanie. Sanícula aqua. Mineral Springs of Ottawa, Ill., USA. Containing, approximately in grains
per gallon, Nat-m. 93, Calc-m. 23.5, Mag-m. 23.25, Calc, bicarb. 14.25, Calc-s. 9.5, Kali-s. 5, Nat-bic. 1, Nat-
br. 3, Fe. bi-carb. 1, Nat-i. 12, Sil. 5, Alum. 01 and traces of Lith. bi-carb., Nat-p., Bor. Dilutions of the spring
water. Triturations of the evaporated salt. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anterior crural, neuralgia. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bee stings. Boils, blind.
Borborygmus. Coccyx, soreness. Condylomata. Conjunctivitis. Constipation, children. Cornea, ulceration.
Coryza. Cough. Dandruff. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Digestion slow. Dropsy, during pregnancy. Eczema.
Emaciation. Excoriations. Foot sweat. Gastritis. Gumboil.
Sanicula aqua Headaches. Indigestion. Influenza. Intermittents. Itch, suppressed. Itching. Leucorrhea. Liver,
soreness. Lumbago. Marasmus. Melancholy. Milk, thin. Morning, sickness. Motion sickness. Mouth, sore.
Neuralgia. Neurasthenia. Night-terrors. Nose, crusts. Ophthalmia, tarsi. Os uterus, dilated. Ossification, early.
Ozaena. Perspiration, excessive. Pot-bellied children. Rectum, cramp. Rheumatism. Rickets. Ringworm.
Scurvy. Seasickness. Shoulder, rheumatism. Throat, sore. Tongue, burning. Toothaches. Uterus, prolapsed.
Uterus, tumor. Vomiting, milk, water. Wrist, boils.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sanie, has sometimes been confused with the plant Sanicula mary- landica. or black snake-
root. The water is odorless and colorless, and has an agreeable and slightly alkaline taste.
Sherbino proved Sanie, in the potencies and a large number of the symptoms of the provings have been
confirmed. It’s a polycrest and anti-psoric of wide range. Guernsey considered Sanie, the chronic of Cham.
Sanie, affects the nutrition, female organs, rectum, neck and skin. Useful for bedwetting, seasickness, motion
sickness, constipation, etc. Rickets. Marasmus. Thick, acrid, yellow pus. Body smells like old cheese.
Bursting in perineum, bowels, bladder, vertex, chest. Shifting pains. Cannot bear to have one part touch
another or cannot lie near another person. Enlarged feeling in throat, vagina etc. Child kicks off covers at night,
wants to lie on something hard though thin. Clothes feel cold, damp.
MIND - Irritable, least word or action would upset her. Misconstrues everything. Crossness quickly alternating
with playfulness in children. Headstrong, obstinate, touchy children. Restless desire to go from place to place.
Instability of purpose. Does not want to be touched. Constant desire to look behind. Dread of downward motion.
Fear of the dark.
Abdomen - Bowels bloated as if they would burst. Sore pains in groin. Loud gurgling, pot-bellied children.
Back - Neck weak and emaciated, child cannot hold its head. Stiff backache, worse least turning, raising arms
or putting hands behind him. Must turn whole body to look around. Sits, head forward, to ease the pain. Cold
lumbar spine. Lumbago, better lying on right side. Lumbar vertebras as if dislocated or were gliding past each
other. As if back is broken in two pieces. As if a damp cloth on sacrum.
Causations - Poor diet, strains.
Chest - Tickling under sternum. Great soreness of upper chest, must hold it with hands when coughing.
Constitutions - Patients are thin and look old, especially children.
Ears - Eustachian catarrh. Soreness behind ears with discharge of white, gluey, sticky substance. Stuffed
feeling in left ear.
Eyes - Lids agglutinated in morning. Lachrymation in cold, open air or cold application. Eyes burn, exuding a
sticky fluid. Ulcerated cornea. Dim sight. Photophobia. Dandruff of the eyebrows.
Face - Acne about eye and cheek. Itching eruptions in beard, especially under chin, worse when warm.
Excoriation of upper lip.
Female - Leucorrhea with strong odor of fish-brine, worse stools. Bearing down as if contents of pelvis would
escape, worse jar, walking. Supports the relaxed parts by placing the hand against vulva, better rest. Vagina
feels large, cannot stop menstruation. Os cervix open and dilated.
Food - Child wants to nurse all the time, yet loses flesh. Craves, salt, bacon or ice cold milk. Eating causes
urging for stool, must leave the table. Feels better after eating. Great longing for the spring water. Thirst little
and often.
Head - Bursting in vertex. As if a cold cloth around brain. Cannot bear cold air on occiput and neck. Profuse
sweat on occiput and neck, worse during sleep. Electric crackling in hair when combed. Profuse scab dandruff,
falling of hair. Small boils on head that do not mature.
Kidneys - Bursting in bladder with urgent call to pass urine. Frequent, profuse, sudden urination, urging ceases
if desire is resisted. Briny urine, stains diaper red. Child cries before urinating, strains to urinate while at stools.
Limbs - Pain in shoulders, worse raising arms or putting them behind back. Hands become sweaty when
putting them together. Cold, clammy hands and feet. Burning of palms and soles. Feet as if in cold water.
Cramps in feet. Foul foot sweat, chafes toes, destroys shoes or stiffens the hose.
Liver - Soreness through hepatic region. Enlargement of liver, sensitive to pressure and jar.
 Lungs - Asthmatic breathing, worse after supper. Wheezing, rattling under sternum, worse during or after
eating. Deep, hollow cough with loud rattling, caused by tickling under sternum. Tickling on lying down at night
and on waking. Rattling cough, child gags and vomits a mouthful of tough, stringy matter. Expectoration of
large, yellow, cheesy masses.
Male - Increased sexual desire at first, then much decreased. Discharge of semen too early, with little
sensation. Scrotum relaxed, clammy sweat about parts. Briny odor of the genitals, a few hours after sex. Child’s
parts smell of fish brine even after bathing.
Modalities - Better from open air, warmth. Better vomiting. Worse from strain, jarring. Worse motion, raising
arm, putting hands behind, descending. Worse cold wind on occiput or neck.
Mouth - Offensive breath. Mouth and palate covered with ulcers, white aphthae. Profuse flow of white, clear,
transparent, stringy saliva when teething. Teeth sensitive to cold air, as if they were very thin. Teeth feel too
long. Gums sore and painful, worse from eating. Gumboils.
Nose - Sneezing and itching of nose. Nose sore and stuffed with yellow scabs. Fluent coryza, worse eating.
Water smells like old, musty rainwater.
Rectum - Constipation with ineffectual urging. Pain, bursting in the perineum during stool. Even soft stool
requires great effort to expel. Stool of one large heavy mass, foul like rotten cheese, or dry, small balls. Stools,
misshapen, changeable, involuntary. Stools must be removed or crumbles at the verge of anus.
Skin - Eczema exuding sticky fluid, behind ears, on wrists, fingers and toes. Itching, worse by scratching. Skin
is dry, brownish, flabby. Skin about neck wrinkled and hangs in folds. Copper-colored syphilitic sores. Fissured
hands and fingers. Cracks on fingers. Tendency to small boils that do not mature.
Sleep - Falls asleep after vomiting. Frequent waking at night. Dreams of robbers and cannot sleep until the
whole house is searched. Dreams of murder and remorse, lascivious dreams. On waking, child rubs eyes and
nose with its fist.
Stomach - Bloating of stomach on beginning to eat. Sensation of a lump in stomach. Thirst little and often,
water is vomited as soon as it reaches the stomach. Sour, rancid, burning belchings. Nausea after eating with
sick feeling, better from smoking. Vomiting of milk soon after nursing.
Temperature - The cold air chills him. Chill every day at same time. Whole body feels too hot at night. Begins
to sweat as soon as covered. Sticky sweat, particularly on side lain on. High fever every night with
sleeplessness.
Throat - Dry throat. Hoarseness following sore throat, must clear throat before speaking. Cold, icy sensation,
like peppermint. Throat feels too large. Can swallow solids better than fluids. Ulcers with yellowish base on
tonsils.
Tongue - Sides of tongue turn up. Tongue adheres to roof of mouth. Tongue, large, flabby, burning, must
protrude to keep it cool, ringworm on tongue. Thick yellow coating on back of tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising from stooping. Vertigo while sitting at table or desk. Vertigo after eating with nausea.
Faint, smothering sensation with great desire for open air. Seasick sensation.
COMMENTS - Itching skin, eczema, worse bathing (Sil.). Sweaty, smelly feet, particularly in children (Sil.).
Fear of the dark, sensitivity to storms (Phos.). Children are very obstinate, stubborn, hard to please.
Offensive vaginal discharges that smell like fish brine or dead fish (Hep.). Strong fishy odor in hemophilis,
gardnerella and
Sanícula aqua trichomonas. Discharge can also smell like rotten cheese.
RELATIONS - W. J. Guernsey considers Sanie, the chronic of Cham. Compare: (1) Sil., Phos., (2) The
constituents of the Sanie, water, especially Nat-m. and Calc. (3) Dread of downward motion, Bor. (4) Head
sweat, Calc., Sil. (5) Soreness behind ears, viscid discharge, Graph., Psor. (6) Ringworm on tongue, Nat-m.,
Ran-s., Tarax. (7) Drinks little and often, vomits as soon as it reaches stomach, Ars. (8) Symptoms change
constantly, Care., Lac-c., Puls. (9) Sphincter not under control, Aloe soc. (10) Stool recedes, Sil., Thuj., must
be removed mechanically, Sei.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Santalum Album
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - santa. Santalum album. Sandalwood. Santalum freycinetianum. Santalum paniculatum. N. O.
Santalaceae. India, Sandwich Islands. The oil distilled from the wood. Dilutions with alcohol. Historicaldose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cystitis. Gonorrhea. Kidney pain.
HERBAL - The word “Santalum” is of Persian origin. Sandalwood oil is obtained from several species of
Santalum, S. album being the chief. Its chief use in old-school practice is in gonorrhea.
 HOMEOPATHIC - Shirtliff observed in a man taking the oil for gonorrhea, soon after each dose, an acute
aching pain felt in the kidney region, so severe that if he was standing he was obliged to sit, which slightly
relieved.
Shirtliff gave the same indication in his case of an elderly man, who looked worn and haggard, complained of
pain in region of left kidney from ribs to iliac crest, brought on by walking, better leaning forward, completely
better by lying down. Better pressing clenched fist into back.
The pain lasted six months and was very acute; Sulph., Berb. and Bry. gave no relief.
Santal, (oil), one drop every four hours, soon gave great relief and entirely removed the pain in two months.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Santoninum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sant. Santoninum. Santonin. A neutral active principle obtained from Ciña. N. O. Compositae.
Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Bedwetting. Blindness. Cataract. Color blindness. Convulsions. Cough. Cystitis.
Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysuria. Eyes, paralysis. Enteralgia. Enteritis. Epilepsy. Gastroenteritis. Hallucinations.
Hemoglobinuria. Hemiplegia. Hysterical. Incontinence. Nephritis. Infantile remittents. Melancholy. Night,
cough. Nosebleed. Photophobia. Strangury. Tetanus. Urination, frequent. Urticaria. Vision, yellow. Vomiting.
Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sant, is the active principle of Santonica, the unexpanded flower heads of Cina Artemisia
Marítima.
Sant, is the favorite anthelmintic of the old school and it has been chiefly given against lumbrici. Fatal
poisonings have caused convulsions, left side paralysis, delirium, vomiting and purging.
Worm affections, corresponding to the “pain in shocks” (Cina.). Gastro-intestinal irritation, itching of nose,
restless sleep, twitching of muscles. Asearía lumbricoides and thread worms, but not tapeworms.
Colorblindness and yellow vision. Visual illusions,yellow sight, violent light not recognized, colors not
distinguishable. Chronic cystitis. Urine deep saffron color. Chronic gastric and intestinal troubles. Night
cough of children. Laryngeal crises and lightning pains of tabes.
Spasms and twitchings. Violent convulsions, unconscious, head hot, face flushed, purplish. Spasm begins in
face and spreads to limbs. Partial paralysis of one (left) side. Restlessness and prostration.
MIND - Delirium. Excited, laughs and sings. Hysterical. Restless and irritable. Wants ev
erything, but satisfied with nothing. Profound and unusual depression with irresolution and want of confidence,
unfitting him for work of any kind. Melancholy like that produced by jaundice. Coma.
Abdomen - Rumbling, very sensitive abdomen. Bruised but soft, hot, full. Severe abdominal pains with
vomiting and purging. Every night pain in intestines before stool.
Chest - Paralysis of lungs, needs artificial respiration.
Eyes - Dark, blue rings around eyes. Eyes rolled convulsively, distorted, staring. Pupils dilated and insensible.
Pressure in eyes. Photophobia with lachrymation. Sudden dimness of sight. Flickering before eyes. Objects
seem to totter and dance, visions of figures, cherries, animals. Color blindness, xanthopsia. Yellow soup
looks red, blue evening sky looks green, objects look green, white looks yellow, violet. Yellow vision, objects
as if in yellow haze or yellow light. Strabismus due to worms.
Face - Red, hot face, staring eyes. Face pale. Pale around mouth, worse afternoon. One cheek white, the
other one is red. Lips swollen, glistening with the distention. Swelling under chin, left side of face. Face pinched,
drawing in of lips over teeth with pinched expression of mouth and nose. Convulsive movements of muscles
of face, especially lips and lids.
Food - Deficient appetite. Thirst intense, continual for ice cold water.
Head - Occipital headache with chronic hallucinations. Head turning and twisting, restless. Dullness of head.
Pain in forehead.
Heart - Pulse is quick and full, rapid, lowered, left absent, right soft and steady.
Kidneys - Nephritis. Feeling of fullness of bladder. Incontinence and dysuria. Bedwetting. Frequent efforts
to urinate, only passes a few drops at a time, that color linen yellow. Urine greenish if acid and reddish purple
if alkaline. Urine deep saffron yellow, thick, sulphur yellow, greenish. Hemoglobinuria.
Limbs - Spasms of limbs. Convulsive jerking of upper limbs. Twitching of hands
and feet. Gait unsteady and tottering, staggered.
Lungs - Coughed incessantly all night from tickling in larynx and trachea. Breath is rapid, sighing, quick and
catchy, rattling.
Mouth - Frothing from mouth. Tongue deep red, dry. Burning pains apparently torment her, as she forces
 everything into her mouth. Hallucinations of taste.
Nose - Nosebleeds. Hallucinations of smell. Things smell peculiar.
Rectum - Well-marked tenesmus. Purging of watery, flaky, foul-smelling stools, followed by vomiting. Stools
copious, grayish, putrid-smelling.
Skin - Urticaria, with edema of nose, lips, and eyelids, over almost entire lids, with vomiting.
Sleep - Sleepy, tired. Sleep restless, disturbed, woke unrefreshed with sickness, frontal headache, and
deficient appetite.
Stomach - Dull pain in pit of stomach. Frequent belchings. Nausea and vomiting. Nausea, better after eating.
Vomiting and purging of yellowish, slimy mucus with severe abdominal pains.
Teeth - Grating teeth during sleep. Teeth clenched.
Temperature - Whole body icy cold, lips and ears blue, face white as snow. Limbs cold, very clammy coldness.
Cold sweats. Hot sweat in occiput, more clammy in front. Violent fever, rapid pulse, burning heat of skin, face
puffy, eyes brilliant, fixed.
Throat - The glands of neck, parotid and submaxillary are swollen.
Vertigo - Giddiness and intense headaches, every object looks bright green.
COMMENTS - A case recorded by Demme was quoted in Brit. Med. Jour., 1892. A boy, 3, was given fifteen
tablets over three days by his mother. Each tablet contained 1/3 grain of Sant.
The symptoms produced were vomiting, dilatation of the pupils, collapse, cyanosis, dyspnea and finally
convulsions. Dilatation of the pupils, collapse, cyanosis, dyspnea, and finally convulsions.
After a warm bath with cold applications to the head and spine, consciousness returned. The temperature was
103.5, nosebleed and hemoglobinuria occurred and a scarlatinalike eruption was noticed.
The child ultimately recovered. After a dose of 7 centigrams, a child, 2, was seized with prostration,
convulsions, cramps and jaundice, followed on the third day by salivation and ulceration of the gum.
Less serious but very characteristic are the effects on the senses, especially the sense of sight. Visions of
figures have been produced and colored vision is a frequent phenomenon, even when the lower triturations
have been used.
Yellow is the predominant color, but green and violet vision are also marked. The urine also is yellow colored
and stains yellow and is passed with much urging and painful burning. A kind of giant urticaria occurred in one
case.
Hale recorded that Sant, cured cases of “nervous blindness.” It was given to an old man, quite blind, for
worms and his sight partially returned. This led to further trials in which it wrs given in nine cases of cataract
and, according to Hale, four were cured, the rest not benefited.
Hale also mentioned bedwetting, strangury, chronic cystitis, as having been cured by it. Chronic catarrh of the
bladder. Infantile remittents with or without worms,. In one prover there was “sensitiveness of the abdomen.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cina, Teucr., Napht., Nat-m. Phos., Spig. (2) Amaurosis, Benz-d., Carbn-s. (3)
Colored vision, Cycl.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - sant. Santoninum. Santonin. A neutral active principle obtained from Ciña. N. O. Compositae.
Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Bedwetting. Blindness. Cataract. Color blindness. Convulsions. Cough. Cystitis.
Delirium. Diarrhea. Dysuria. Eyes, paralysis. Enteralgia. Enteritis. Epilepsy. Gastroenteritis. Hallucinations.
Hemoglobinuria. Hemiplegia. Hysterical. Incontinence. Nephritis. Infantile remittents. Melancholy. Night,
cough. Nosebleed. Photophobia.

name: Saponaria Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sapo. Saponaria officinalis. Soap root. Soapwort. Hedge pink. N. O. Caryophyllaceae. Tincture
of the roots. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ciliary, neuralgia. Colds. Coryza. Exophthalmos. Glaucoma. Sore throat. Trigeminal, neuralgia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Acute colds, coryza, sore throat, etc. Will often “break up” acold. Worse at night, mental
exertion, left side.
MIND - Depressed with sleepiness. Apathetic. Utter indifference to pain or possible death.
Eyes - Violent eye pains. Hot stitches deep in eyeball. Ciliary neuralgia, worse left side. Exophthalmos, worse
reading and writing. Increased intra-ocular pressure. Glaucoma. Photophobia.
Face - Left-sided trigeminal neuralgia, especially supra-orbital.
Head - Stitching pain, supra-orbital, worse left side, evening, motion. Throbbing over orbits. Congestions to
head, tired feeling in nape.
Heart - Impulse weak, pulse less frequent. Palpitations with anxiety.
Nose - Coryza. Stopped up feeling in nose, also itching and sneezing.
Stomach - Difficult swallowing. Nausea, heartburn, full feeling not relieved by eructation.
Vertigo - Sensation of drunkenness with constant endeavor to go left-wards.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sapin. (2) Verb., Cocc. - both containing Sapin. (3) Quill., Anag., Helon., Sars.,
Par., Agrostema, Cycl. and others contain Saponin.
 REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Saponinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sapin. Saponinum. Saponin. A glucoside obtained from Saponaria officinalis. Trituration.
Solution. Watery solution speedily decompose. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Bedwetting. Boils. Colic. Constipation. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Fevers. Headaches.
Leucorrhea. Migraines. Menstrual disorders. Nausea. Photophobia. Rheumatism. Sleeplessness. Spleen,
pain. Strabismus. Tongue, strawberry. Tonsillitis Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sapin., a glucoside found in Quillay a, Yucca, Senega, Dioscorea and other plants, has had
a somewhat extensive proving in potencies ranging from lx to 30c, conducted by A. J. Hills.
One prover, who took the 30c, was for many y ears a sufferer from joint rheumatism, but had none of his usual
pains during the proving and a great enlargement of the left knee was entirely removed.
Tired, indifferent. Migraine. Pain in left temple, eye, photophobia, hot stitches deep in eye. Fifth nerve
disorders. Much pain before the menstrual flow, severe sore throat, worse right side tonsils swollen, worse in
warm room. Sharp burning taste and violent sneezing.
Modalities - Better by stool, onset of menses. Better by cold, cold bathing. Better while sitting. Worse by
moving, even motion of the eyes. Worse mental labor. Worse by warmth. Worse swallowing. Desire to vomit
and defecate, worse when quiet.
COMMENTS - Two female provers had marked disturbance of the menstrual functions, especially pain and
sufferings before the flow. Miliary eruption, colic and leucorrhea before the menses, pain better but not
removed when the flow was established.
Severe sore throat, worse right side, was experienced by several provers, and Hills had so much swelling of
the tonsils that he was obliged to abandon the proving. Bodily and mental depression. Exophthalmos and
strabismus.
Roughness of mouth mucus membrane, raised papillae on palate and tongue. Strawberry tongue. Involuntary
emission of urine when walking. Nausea and vomiting, colic and diarrhea, “nausea more in esophagus and
throat, worse in a warm room.”
This worse by warmth was met with in relation to many symptoms and is probably a keynote. At the same time
there was much chilliness and lowered temperature is a characteristic feature.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tough mucus, Kali-bi. (2) Onset of menses ameliorates, Lach. (3) Spleen pain,
Cean. (4) Kidney pain, Santa. (5) Worse by movement, moving eyes, Bry. (6) Sleepy but cannot sleep, Bell.
(7) Early waking, Bell., Nux-v. (8) Worse in warm room, Puls. (9) As if damp stockings on, Calc., Sanie. ( 10)
Strawberry tongue, Frag., Bac. ( 11 )
Involuntary emission of urine when walking, Ferr., Caust. (12) Seneg.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Sarcolacticum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sarcol-ac. Sarcolacticum acidum. Sarcolactic acid. Dextrum lacticum acidum. Isomer of lactic
acid. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. Chronic fatigue. Diabetes. Dyspnea. Headache. Influenza. Lichen planus.
Myasthenia. Myasthenia. Myotonia. Neurasthenia. Polyuria. Prostration. Psoriasis. Rheumatism. Raynaud’s
syndrome. Rhinitis. Tumors.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sarcol-ac. is formed in muscle tissue during muscle exhaustion. It differs from ordinary
lactic acid in its relation to polarized light. It represents a much broader and more profoundly acting drug and
its pathogenesis is quite dissimilar from the normal acid.
The proving was the work of W. Griggs of the Hering Laboratory, Philadelphia. The experimentation was
carried out in 1940 on eleven people (nine men and two women), using the 4x, 6x, 15x, and 30x potencies.
Wm. B. Griggs found Sarcol-ac. of great value in the most violent form of epidemic influenza, especially with
violent and retching and greatest prostration, when Ars. had failed. Influenza with rhinitis. Locally in the
tuberculous ulceration of vocal cords.
Intra-muscular lactic acid, following prolonged exercise, which generates fatigue. This chronic fatigue, when
pushed to an advanced stage, results in an almost paralyzing weakness with prostration. Spinal neurasthenia,
muscular weakness, dyspnea with myocardial weakness.
Extreme fatigue, anxiety, prostration. Muscular cramping pains, aggravated by movement. Digestive
intolerance. Dryness and itching of the skin. Morning sickness, diabetes and rheumatism offer a field for this
 remedy. Troubles in the breasts.
MIND - Feeling of laziness, weakness. Dejection. Irritability, becomes easily annoyed by
the smallest thing.
Abdomen - Sedative, palliative for gastrointestinal tumors.
Back - Tired feeling in back and neck and shoulders. Paralytic weakness. Cramping pains in the back and
lumbar region, aggravated when standing.
Chest - Aortic pain and rapid pulse after exertion.
Head - Headache and vomiting, pain situated on the forehead and above the eyes, ameliorated by going to
stool.
Heart - Cardiac rheumatism. Raynaud’s syndrome.
Kidneys - Polyuria. Profuse nocturnal urination. Urine clear with traces of proteinuria.
Limbs - Psoric rheumatism. Rheumatoid arthritis. Fibrous rheumatism. Paresthesia, joint numbness and pains.
Extreme weakness from climbing stairs. Stiffness of thigh and calves. Cramp in the calves. Arms feel as if no
strength in them. Wrist tires easily from writing. Writer’s cramp. Difficulty in brushing hair.
Lungs - Dyspnea, feeling of cardiac weakness, croupy cough, especially at night. Bronchitis. Dry, painful
pleurisy.
Modalities - Worse at night. Worse from movement, from standing upright.
Nose - Coryza, throat dry and painful, swallowing impeded, alleviated by day, aggravated at night.
Rectum - Burning hemorrhoids. Stools acrid and expulsion of gases in profuse, easing the condition.
Skin - Intense general itching, improved by the cold. Keratotic eczema. Lichen planus. Psoriasis. Scleroderma
(Graph.).
Sleep - Difficulty in going to sleep, sleep light when it comes. Wakes aching and exhausted.
Stomach - Heavy, painful feeling in the pit of the stomach. Digestive intolerance, especially of cold water.
Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea. Uncontrollable vomiting even of water followed by extreme weakness.
Temperature - General chilliness with coldness of the limbs. Extreme chilliness in bed. The right hand does
not become warm by external heat.
Throat - Constriction in pharynx. Sore throat with tightness in naso-pharynx. Tickling in throat.
COMMENTS - According to Dr. Kuhl, lactic acid has an anti-cancerous preventive action and he recommended
a special diet with additional lacto-fermented products.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Eup-per. - cracking sensation with acute pains in the bones. (2) Bry. -
aggravation by movement. (3) Am. - muscular bruises.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Julian.

name: Sarothamnus Scoparius
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - saroth. Sarothamnus scoparius. Scotch broom. Spartium scoparium. Cystisus scoparius.
Genista scoparia. N. O. Legumi- nosae. Papilionoideae. Europe. The tincture is prepared from the flowers.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne rosacea. Albuminuria. Alopecia. Angina pectoris. Bacillary, dysentery. Cheyne-Stokes.
Choroiditis. Collagen diseases. Diabetes insipidus. Emaciation. Glaucoma. Hay fever. Heart, disorders.
Hodgkin’s disease. Hypertension. Hypotension. Impetigo. Insomnia. Iritis. Kidneys, disorders. Leukemia.
Nephritis. Ozaena. Palpitations. Parasites. Pityriasis. Sinusitis. Tobacco, heart. Worms.
HERBAL - Sarothamnus scopariumis ashrubby tree, widespread throughout Europe. The twigs are used for
the extraction of the official spar- tein, the flowers are rich in flavonoids, and the plant contains aromatic amines.
Sparteine sulphate, an alkaloid found in scotch broom, causes a lowering of the systolic and diastolic pressures
of the provers. It also lowers blood-pressure.
Depresses the heart by its poisonous action on the myocardium, and this, with the stimulating action of the
drug upon the vagus, accounts for the lowered blood pressure and reduced pulse rate. It weakens the cardiac
contraction. The total amount of urine is increased, diuretic properties, useful in dropsy.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hinsdale attempted the
first homeopathic proving in 1918, on three students. In 1897, Schier conducted a proving on six people, using
the tincture and the infusion of the winter root, as well as the tincture and infusion of the fresh flowers.
Mezger undertook a true proving on twenty-seven provers of whom seven were women, at the Robert Bosch
Hospital in 1951-52. He used the 4x, and 2x potencies as well as the mother tincture.
Saroth. is a heart tonic, affects the kidneys, cord, muscles and left side. Sparteine sulphate increases the
strength of the heart, slows it and reduces the blood pressure. Hinsdale reported that it continues the good
effects of Verat. and Dig. without any of the undesirable effects of either.
 Irregular heart action from influenza or other infectious diseases. Arterial hypertension, arteriosclerosis.
Relieves the congestion of kidneys enabling them to eliminate and relieve the distress upon the heart. Heavy
aching.
Cheyne-Stokes respiration. Irregular heart following grip and various infections. Hypotension. Very useful in
sustaining heart after stopping habit of morphine. Indicated when primarily the muscles of the heart and
especially the nervous apparatus is affected. Acts rapidly and lasts three to four days. Does not disturb
digestion.
Specific action on the kidneys, enabling them to eliminate and relieve the stress on the heart. Nephritis.
Albuminuria.
Congestion of the thyroid gland, hands clammy, sleep disturbed, hot flushes, emaciation. Increase in the size
of the thyroid. Extreme tiredness. Leukemia with eosinophil.
MIND - Irritable, loses his temper at the slightest thing. Irritability from trifles. Inner agitation, ideas escape him.
Easily irritated and likely to explode. Excitement at night. Melancholic disposition is upset easily.
Apathetic without spirit, distracted. Absentminded. Everything is too much for him, difficulty in concentrating.
Weakness of the senses and body. General inhibition, but especially erotic. Obsession with erotic thoughts.
Sexual thoughts intrude and crowd around each other.
Abdomen - Stomach and bowels seem to be filled with stones or as a firm mass. Spasmodic entero-colitis.
Flatulency with much mental depression. Sensation of abdominal repletion and stomach feels hollow. Passage
through intestines accelerated with three to six evacuations a day. Bacillary dysentery. Intestinal tuberculosis.
Intestinal parasites.
Back - Pain in the lumbar region.
Blood - Leukemia. Eosinophilia. Attacks of vasodilation at the limbs in the big toe and foot.
Breasts - Nodular congestion of the right breast (especially in men).
Chest - Angina pectoris. Constriction in the precordial region with sensation of tightness and anguish.
Constitutions - Tubercular, thyroidism or nervous. Allergic, psoric constitutions.
Ears - Monotonous rumbling and crackling in both ears, particularly intense between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. Buzzing
and other noises.
Eyes - Chronic glaucoma. Choroiditis. Iritis. Burning and stinging pains, especially behind the left eyeball. Pain
on moving the eyes. When looking at an area of light, the brightness of the light and the rainbow colors of the
halo seem more intense.
Face - Barber's itch.
Female - Excessive menses and long intervals between menses. Menses late and prolonged. Sex drive
increased. Loss of libido, genital deficiency and evil-smelling sweating from the genital region.
Food - Appetite increases, constant need to eat. Persistent feeling of hunger, despite constant feeling of
nausea. Loss of appetite with aversion to food and strangling feeling. Aversion to eggs and meat.
Head - Pulsating headaches, as if the skull would burst. Headache, as if wearing a helmet, going from the
eyes towards the occiput (glaucoma). Congestion in the head. Flashes of heat in head.
Heart - Anxious oppression, radiating to left shoulder and neck. Hypotension. Tobacco heart. Angina pectoris.
Irregular action, disturbed rhythm due to gas, feeble in
Sarothamnus scoparius nervous hysterical patients. Myocardial degeneration, failing compensation. Pal-
pitations with congestion to head.
Kidneys - Drawing pains in the kidneys with colic pains. Increased urination. Very profuse, bright foaming
urine, then burning in the pudendum. Hydronephrosis. Albuminuria. Diabetes insipidus. Frequent need to
urinate at night, especially around 5 a.m. Bedwetting.
Limbs - All the muscles are painful, as if stiff. Shooting pains. Sudden pains, regularly in the sciatic nerve.
Sciatica. Neuralgic pains, beginning on the right side, moving towards the left and diminishing on the right.
Drawing joint pains. Chronic inflammation of the hip. Nocturnal pain in the hips and sacrum, left shoulder, left
elbow and fingers of the right hand. Fidgets in the legs, which prevent him from falling asleep. Strumous edema
of the legs. Deadness of right arm and fingers. Chilblains. Acrocyanosis.
Lungs - Asthma.
Male - Loss of libido, genital deficiency and evil-smelling sweating from the genital region.
Modalities - Better from cool air, rapid motion, passing flatus. Worse turning on left side.
Mouth - Vesicles on the lips and mouth.
Nose - Hay fever. Ozaena. Maxillary sinusitis. One-sided obstruction. Nostrils blocked alternately. Nasal
secretions, streaked with blood and abrasion of the nasal orifices. Tickling in the nose with frequent sneezing.
Small new growths on the nasal wall.
Rectum - Tenesmus, ameliorated by emission of wind. Colic, then bright acrid foaming stools followed by
 burning in anus. Stools yellow, glairy with tenesmus. Stools hard like balls, covered with mucus and mixed
with a frothy diarrhea. Alternating diarrhea and constipation. Hemorrhoids with splinter-like pain.
Skin - Allergic eruptions. Urticaria. Folliculitis. Boils. Pityriasis. Dysidrosis. Adenitis of the sweat glands.
Impetigo. Acne rosacea. Small vesicles, extremely irritating. Eczematous eruption, both damp and dry.
Infiltration and bluish coloring in the joints of the toes. Copious nocturnal sweating with a strong odor. Hair stiff,
dandruff. Loss of hair in patches. Alopecia.
Sleep - Insomnia. Sleep long in coming with abundant ideas. Sleep light, easily woken by noise. Waking
between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m. Dreams are pleasant and colorful. Dreams at times, about disappearances,
murders, deaths. Unrefreshing sleep. On waking, feels tired and has the impression of not having slept enough.
Great need for sleep, spends a large part of the day in bed.
Stomach - Ptosis of the stomach and intestines. Dyspepsia. Aggravation of stomachache by food.
Temperature - Sensitive to the cold, worse in the evening, feeling of head, sweating, numbness.
Throat - Irritation of the larynx with dry cough, coming from the throat. Tickling in the throat. Acute and chronic
laryngitis.
COMMENTS - Weakness of the senses and body. Sensation of uneasiness and cold, which is worrying, only
the head needs fresh air. Sensation of coldness, except for the head, which is better in fresh air.
Pain in the cardiac region and rhythmic anomalies. Pains and cardiac palpitations with tingling and feeling of
soreness, especially when lying on the left side. Palpitations, especially at night and when resting, but also
from slight exertion. Violent cardiac pulsations, which shake the whole body.
Pulse accelerated. Extra systole, notices the irregularity of the contractions. Left ventricular cardiac deficiency.
Angina pectoris. Rhythmic anomaly. Basedow’s heart. Aortitis.
Bubbling sensation in the head. Precordial constriction with anguish. Rheumatic pain, moving from right to left.
Sudden pain in the left sciatic nerve around 10 p.m. Hollow sensation in the stomach and abdominal repletion.
Sleep long in coming.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Kalm. - Pains along the nerves from the center to the periphery and from top to
bottom. Sudden pain, which moves around. Palpitations, worse when lying on the left side. Pulse slow. (2)
Spig. - Violent palpitations with oppression and anxiety. Must lie on the right side with the head high. (3) Iber.
- Violent palpitations at the least exertion. Pulse full, irregular. Aggravated in a warm room and when lying on
the left side.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Julian.

name: Sarracenia Purpurea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sarr. Sarracenia purpurea. Pitcher plant. N. O. Sarraceniaceae. Grows in boggy places from
Canada southward. Contains a very active proteolytic enzyme. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of root.
Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Back, pains. Bones, pains. Bor- borygmus. Constipation. Coxalgia. Diarrhea. Eruptions,
scrofulous. Femur, pains. Herpes. Influenza. Lumbago. Psoriasis. Smallpox. Vision, disordered.
HERBAL - The use of the pitcherplant in smallpox is a discovery of the Native Americans of North America,
the spotted appearance of the plant probably suggesting a resemblance to the disease.
HOMEOPATHIC - A proving by T. C. Duncan, Thomas and others brought out symptoms of fever, backache,
headache and gastric disturbance. Hale collected much confirmatory evidence of its power to antidote the
smallpox poison.
Sarr. is a remedy for variola. Congestion to head with irregular heart action. Sick headache, throbbing in
various parts, especially in neck, shoulders and head, which feels full to bursting. Visual disorders. Chlorosis.
Feels dull and heavy, sweats freely. Insensibility of right side, paralysis of hearing and smell. Debility, heavy,
languid. Dull, heavy, sore feeling in all bones. Phlegmonous swelling with a rosy tint on various parts.
Unrefreshed though slept soundly.
MIND - Melancholy. Great depression of spirits with frontal headache. Dullness of mind. Forgetful. Loss of
memory with the headache. Difficult to concentration. Alternate apathy and intellectual activity. Anxious about
everything.
Abdomen - Transient pains in bowels. Bloated about navel. Borborygmi and some pain in bowels with
constipation, dry throat.
Back - Deep-seated pain in back. Pains shooting in zigzag course from lumbar region to middle of scapula.
Weakness between the shoulders. Warm sensation passed up back into head. Back weak, wants to lean
on something. Pain and soreness in sacrum.
Chest - Pains in third and fourth ribs, with great apprehension of heart disease. Pain in angle of ribs. Soreness
 of pectoralis major.
Ears - Ringing in ears. Sticking pains deep in right ear, transient but recurring often, same in left ear. Intense
earache, fears he will lose his senses. Swelling of parotids.
Eyes - Eyes feel swollen and sore. Pain in orbits. Photophobia. Black objects move with the eye.
Face - Face flushed. Heat and redness of face. Face pale with heat and chill alternating. Erysipelatous swelling
of face. Miliary eruption. Scaly herpes on face. Intense neuralgic pains from temples to jaws.
Female - Bloody discharge at other times menstrual period, as during menopause. Watery or milky leucorrhea.
foul-smelling, with spasmodic pains in uterus. Pulsative pains in womb with swelling as if from a tumor or
dropsy. Uterus swollen as if full of cysts. Cervix swollen, hot. Miliary eruption and heat in vulva.
Food - Hungry all the time, even after a meal. Appetite unusually active. Little appetite, but what is eaten
agrees. Great desire to sleep during eating.
Head - Light feeling in head. Sensation as if he had received a knock on the head, drowsiness and staggering
gait. Sensation as if head were split.
Heart - Congestion to chest, heavy feeling about heart. Feeling of congestion about head, with irregularity of
heart’s action.
Kidneys - Urine phosphatic, scanty, limpid.
Limbs - Limbs cold when still, as from poor circulation. Weakness of limbs with paralytic debility. Limbs weak,
bruised pain in knees and hip joints. Pains and soreness in diaphyses of all long bones. Bones in arm pain.
Lungs - Paroxysms of suffocation and nosebleed. Tuberculosis and bronchial disorders. Cough with desire to
vomit, and vomiting. Hemoptysis, thick cough, continual tickling in larynx and bronchi. Hard cough, shaking
chest and bowels. Expectoration of mucus, tenacious, filamentary, with a bitter, putrid, oily taste.
Modalities - Better in fresh air, out of bed. Worse about midnight, in the morning, at 3 p.m. Worse rising from
lying, trying to walk. Worse in stormy weather. Open air causes chilliness, hands and feet cold, causes head
to be hot. sore and feel full. Cold air causes to chilliness and aggravates bone pains.
Mouth - Tongue is dry, coated brownish white. Mouth dry, lips and mouth parched. Toothache at night in bed,
from least contact, and cold air.
Nose - Nosebleed nearly producing fainting. Nose swollen, red, with pressure and pulsation at root. Fluent
coryza with cold chills and loss of smell. Foul-smelling, green, yellowish, or bloody discharges. Fetid smell.
Rectum - Rectum and anus swollen and inflamed. Much flatus. Much tenesmus, dysenteric diarrhea. Stool
copious, dark, fetid, evacuated with great straining, morning. Stools very hard, covered with mucus, and dark.
First part of stool natural, last diarrhea. Morning diarrhea, faint after stool.
Sensations - Heat in face as if on fire. Left eye as if congested. Swelling in uterus as if from a tumor or dropsy,
as if full of cysts. As if bones of leg were too thick.
Skin - Eruptions similar to crusta lactea. Herpes. Psoriasis. Scrofulous eruptions. Smallpox, aborts the
disease, arrests pustules.
Sleep - Sleepy in daytime, sleep disturbed by strange and frightful dreams. Awakes early in a fright with urging
to urinate.
Stomach - Sleepy during meals. Empty, hungry feeling, can keep nothing in his stomach. Burning pains in
stomach with palpitations and contraction. Pinching pain in stomach, it feels distended and torn. Copious,
painful vomiting.
Temperature - Feverish and shaking chills, worse morning. General chills between shoulder blades. Chills,
heat, and sweat, 5 p.m. Skin hot and dry. Hands hot, warm all over. Head and body warm. Perspires freely.
Throat - Throat dry, not better by tea or water.
Vertigo - Vertigo with cramps in neck, worse at night.
COMMENTS - Hering quoted several instances of Sarr. action. The first was a woman far advanced in
pregnancy who was cured of smallpox with Sarr. 3c, 6c and 9c, delivery as accomplished during her
convalescence, the infant bearing on its body numerous red blotches indicating that it had been affected with
the disease.
A second case concerned an infant a few months old who was attacked with a grave form of smallpox with
variolous angina so severe that it was with difficulty it could take the breast, the mother took Sarr. 3c, 6c and
9c and continued to nurse the infant, which promptly recovered, the mother not taking the disease.
In an epidemic occurring in the environs of Wavre, Sarr. was given to two thousand people living in the very
middle of the disease and coming in constant intercourse with it, but all who took Sarr. escaped. During the
same epidemic, two hundred cases were treated with Sarr. without a death.
Bilden, who used the 1 x tincture in an epidemic with success, concluded that San. is to smallpox what Gels,
is to bilious fever.
HalequotedSurgeon-MajorC. G. Logie’s (an allopath) account of his experience with San. (decoction probably)
 in smallpox: “Four of the cases in my hospital have been severe confluent cases. They have throughout the
disease all been perfectly sensible, have had excellent appetites, been free from pain and have never felt
weak.
“The effects of this medicine, which I have carefully watched, seemed to anest the development of the pustules,
killing, as it were, the virus from within, thereby changing the character of the disease and doing away with
pitting.”
A number of eye symptoms appeared in the provings and Sarr. has cured disordered vision. A case of
“phlyctenoid herpes” has also been reported cured by it. Extreme lassitude and pains in the bones were
prominent in the provings. Week feeling in the arms. Very sensitive to cold air.
Sarr. has the empty, hungry, sinking sensation of the anti-psorics. Dryness of mouth and throat. Faint after
stool. Bladder and rectal tenesmus. Stool smells of musk. The right side was more affected than the left.
RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Podo. Compare: (1) In smallpox, Ant-t., Merc., Vac., Vario., Maland. (2) In bone
pains, Eup-per.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
