name: Sarsaparilla Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sars. Sarsaparilla officinalis. Wild licorice. Smilax officinalis. The root of several species of
Smilax. N. O. Smila- ceae, by some classed as a sub-order of the Liliaceae. Triturations and tincture of the
dried rhizome. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Bedwetting. Bladder, disorders. Blood, disorders. Bones, disorders. Breast, scirrhous.
Bright’s disease. Constipation. Cystitis. Cracks, skin. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Dysuria. Emaciation.
Eruptions. Eyes, disorders. Faintness. Glands, enlarged. Gonorrhea. Gout. Gravel. Hands, chapped.
Headaches. Hernia. Herpes. Hiccoughs. Intermittent fever. Kidney, colic. Kidney, disorders. Marasmus.
Masturbation, effects. Melancholy. Menopause. Mercury, abuse. Mycosis. Nephritis. Nipples, retracted. Plica
polonica. Rheumatism. Seborrhea. Spermatic cords, swelling. Spermatorrhea. Stones. Strangury. Syphilis.
Ulcers. Warts.
HERBAL - The dried root or rhizome of sarsaparilla, as imported, is of the thickness of a goose quill, many
feet in length, reddish brown, odorless, mucilaginous in taste, feebly bitter, and faintly acrid.
It was historically reputed, according to Mile, to be a diaphoretic tonic, alterative. It was given in scrofula and
secondary syphilis and the concomitants of these diseases such as ulcers, cutaneous eruptions, nodes
indurated glands, decay, and necroses. Joint swellings and rheumatism often improve under a protracted
course of it. Some think it a kind of restorative after an exhausting course of mercury.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hahnemann proved Sars., confirming many of the historical uses. Sars. is “restorative ”
after over-dosing with Merc., because it is a homeopathic antidote to Merc. It covers the syphilitic, sycotic and
psoric constitutions.
Affinity for the genito-urinary organs, skin, bones, and lower right extremity. Marasmus, emaciation. Kidney
colic. Marked urinary symptoms. Moist eruptions about the genitals or between the scrotum and thighs.
Periosteal pains due to venereal disease. Retraction of nipples in those of cancerous inheritance or
constitution.
Clears the complexion. Eruptions following hot weather and vaccinations, boils and eczema. Fig warts.
Scratching causes itching to begin in another place, causes eruption on forehead to become humid.
Parts feel screwed together. Nightly bone pains. Pains shoot in different directions and are accompanied by
depression and anxiety. As if salt were put upon the wound. Very sore, gouty nodes. Rheumatism.
MIND - Depression and anxiety from pain. Despondent, gloomy without any cause. Ill humored and taciturn.
Sensitive, easily offended.
Abdomen - Rumbling with sensation of emptiness. Much flatus, rumbling and fermentation. Colic and
backache at the same time, with diarrhea. Cholera infantum.
Back - Emaciation of neck. Backache with colic. Pain from small of back down the spermatic cord after
emission.
Bladder - Bladder distended and tender. Tenesmus of bladder. Urging to urinate before menses. Pain at
meatus, in urethra going back to abdomen. Jerking along the urethra. Can pass urine only when standing,
urine dribbles while sitting. Urine passes in thin, feeble stream. Urine scanty, slimy, flaky, sandy, pus,
bloody. Air passes from bladder during urination. Crusty urinary sediment. Sand on diaper. Severe pain at
conclusion of urination.
Breasts - Sore, shriveled breasts. Nipples retracted or cracked, small and shriveled. Nipples retracted
before menses.
 Constitutions - Anti-syphilitic and anti- sycotic. Suited to children with faces like old people and enlarged
abdomens, to thin, frail, shriveled, old looking persons. To dark-haired persons, and to lithic or sycotic
diathesis.
Ears - Words reverberate in ear to the root of nose.
Eyes - Foggy vision, worse seminal emission. Itch like eruptions on eyelids.
Face - Yellow, wrinkled, old looking. Eruptions on face and upper lip, worse during menses.
Female - Moist eruption and soreness in right groin before menses. Menses late and scanty. Dysmenorrhea,
with retracted nipples or sore breast.
Head - Itching and humid eruption of forehead. Moist eruption on scalp. Scalp sensitive. Crusta lactea
beginning in face. Shooting pain from above right temporal region. Pains from occiput to eyes or to root of
nose. As of a painful tight band around the head. Periosteal pains due to venereal disease. Pains cause
depression.
Kidneys - Pain from right kidney downward. Kidney colic and painful urination, in infants. Child screams
before and while passing urine. Gravel.
Limbs - Rheumatism, bone pains, worse at night. Rheumatic pains after gonorrhea (Thuj.). Paralytic, tearing
pains. Affections of any kind in general in right
lowerlimb. Trembling of hands and feet. Burning on sides of fingers and toes, under nails. Deep cracks on
fingers and toes, worse sides. Cutting sensation under nails (Petr.). Tetter on hands, ulceration around ends
of fingers (Psor.).
Male - Genitals moist and offensive. Itching on scrotum and perineum. Herpetic eruption on genitals. Syphilis,
squamous eruption and bone pains. Intolerable stench on genitals. Bloody semen. Spermatic cord painful after
emission, swollen after unrequited sexual excitement. Jerking along urethra.
Modalities - Better from uncovering neck and chest, warmth. Standing improves difficult urination. Worse at
the close of urination. Worse from cold, wet, dampness, spring, at night. Worse from touch, pressure, tight
clothes. Worse motion, sitting, going up and down stairs. Worse scratching, yawning. Worse after urinating,
before menses, from suppressed gonorrhea.
Mouth - Aphthae, salivation. Offensive breath. Metallic taste, no thirst. White tongue. Pain in jaw, worse
bending head back.
Nose - Stoppage for years. Swelling at the root of nose.
Rectum - Cholera infantum. Obstinate constipation with frequent want to urinate. Sand in stools.
Sensations - As if in a dream. Buzzing as if a large bell had been struck in head. As if he had been hit with a
hammer on top of head. As of a great weight in head. As if breath were stopped by a spasm. Breastbone as if
bruised. As if chest were too short. Limbs as if paralyzed. As if fingertips ulcerated or as if salt were put on a
wound.
Skin - Emaciated, shriveled, skin lies in folds (Abrot., Sanie.). Dry, flabby skin. Skin hard, indurated. Cracks
on hands and feet. New skin cracks and burns. Itching, scaly spots. Dry, itching rash from exposure to open
air, comes on in spring, becomes crusty. Summer cutaneous disorders. Herpetic eruptions, ulcers. Irritating
pus. Copper-colored eruptions. Ecchymoses in old age. Edema.
Sleep - Yawning. Complaints concomitant to yawning. Worse when yawning. Sleep early in evening. Nocturnal
sleeplessness and frequent waking. Frightful dreams.
Stomach - Sensation of emptiness after a meal as while fasting, or else nausea or disgust when thinking of
what has been eaten. Drinking water causes vomiting.
Temperature - Chill starts from region of bladder to back. Influenza.
COMMENTS - Sars. chiefly affects the urinary organs, genitals, rectum, skin and bones, right lower extremity,
right lower side inner, and one-sided head. General “sinking” sensation of the great anti-psorics. General
sensitiveness.
Acute and chronic bladder infections. Kidney stones, and the tendency to form kidney stones. Acute kidney
stone colic (Berb.). Cystitis. Bladder infections in children, the child screams when they feel the urge because
they anticipate the pain (Petros.).
Cannot pass urine freely except when standing, dribbles when sitting. Excessive pain in urethra that runs back
into abdomen. Great pain and burning at end of urination (Equis.). Tenesmus. Urine is turbid, full of flakes and
mucus or gravel, red or gray sand, or particulate matter. Urine with mucus or blood.
Gonorrhea, and the effect of suppressed gonorrhea. Herpes. Moist eruptions on scrotum and thighs.
Spermatorrhea with swollen cords. The semen may be bloody. Offensive odor about genitals in both sexes.
“Moist eruption in right groin before menses.” Painful and disordered menstruation. Nipples are soft,
unexcitable, retracted, inverted. Cracked nipples (Cast-eq.), associated with cancer (Aster., Phyt.). Breast
abscesses (Phyt.), with inverted nipples. Scirrhus of the breast. Helpful in patients of cancerous history with
 retracted nipples.
Herpetic eruptions in all parts. Moist and dry tettery eruptions. Cracks. Itch-like eruptions, prone to appear in
spring. Itching eruption on forehead during menses. Emaciation, causing the skin to be shriveled and lie in
folds.
Pains shoot in different directions. Anxiety accompanies the pains, and can cause depression. Warmth
generally relieves. Warm diet aggravates, cold diet relieves. Warm room aggravates vertigo. Washing, bread
and yawning aggravates.
Grimmer wrote, “Ulcers, cutaneous eruptions, nodes indurated glands, decay, necroses, joint swellings and
rheumatism often improve under a persistent course of this remedy.”
One of Sars. popular uses was for “clearing the complexion.” When it succeeds it is by virtue of its similarity,
for Clarke saw a very extensive crop of blotches it produced in a young woman.
Farrington offered several indications for Sars., including sycotic eruptions with little spots scarcely raised
above the skin, often scaling a little, but looking like the roseola of syphilis and itching intolerably, worse in
spring.
Moist eruption on scalp, the pus from which causes the inflammation of any part it touches. Sycotic headache,
beginning at back of head, coming forward and settling at root of nose with swelling of nose. Moist eruption
about genitals or between the scrotum and thighs.
With Sars., Skinner cured many cases of retraction or flattening of the nipple in nursing women. On two
occasions with high potencies of Sars. he enabled a woman to nurse her child when it was utterly hopeless.
ELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bell., Merc. It antidotes: Merc. Compare: (1) Berb., Lyc., Nat-m., Petr., Sass. (2)
Saur. - Lizard’s tail - irritation of kidneys, bladder, prostate and urinary passages. Painful and difficult urination,
cystitis with strangury. (3) Cuc- c. - Watermelon, infusion of the seed acts promptly in painful urination with
constriction and backache, relieves pain and stimulates flow. Compatible: Hep., All-c., Phos., Rhus-t., Sulph.,
Sep. Complementary: Merc., Sep.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Sassafras Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sass. Sassafras officinalis. N.O. Lauraceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
HERBAL - Sassafras is a warm, aromatic stimulant, alterative, diaphoretic, and diuretic. Also used in diseases
of the kidneys and bladder.
The oil is said to relieve the pain caused by menstrual obstructions, and pain following parturition, in doses of
5 to 10 drops on sugar, the same dose having been found useful in gleet and gonorrhea.
Dr. Shelby of Huntsville stated that it would both prevent and remove the injurious effects of tobacco. The
mucilage of the pith (2 drachms to 1 pint of water) is used as a local application in acute ophthalmia, and is a
demulcent drink in disorders of the chest, bowels, kidneys, and bladder.
Externally, as a rubefacient, in painful swellings, sprains, bruises, rheumatism, etc., and is said to check the
progress of gangrene. A lotion of rose-water or distilled water, with sassafras pith, filtered after standing for
four hours, is recommended for the eyes.
An infusion of the bark administered internally and applied externally is reputed an excellent treatment for rhus
poisoning. Dr. King has also derived some benefit from its internal use in gonorrhea and obstinate gleet, 5 to
10 drops on sugar, 3 times a day.
REFERENCES - King. Murphy.

name: Saururus Cernuus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - saur. Saururus cernuus. Lizard’s tail. N. O. Piperaceae. The entire plant including the root is
macerated in twice its weight of alcohol. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Cystitis, Kidneys, disorders. Prostate, disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - The Saur, plant is an indigenous perennial found in swampy localities in some parts of the
United States. It has been and is still used in domestic practice for those conditions for which Dr. Phares
commended it, including irritation and inflammation of the kidneys, bladder, prostate and urinary passages.
Phares considered it peculiarly adapted to all such cases if they were attended by strangury or painful difficult
urination. He used the remedy both externally and internally and he found that the stomach was very tolerant
of the rather heroic doses he prescribed.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Canth., Berb.
REFERENCES - Anshutz.
 ***SCAMMONIUM
(Scammony)
PHARMACY - scam. Scammonium. Scammony. Convolvulus scammonia. N. O. Con- volvulacae. Triturations
of the dried milky juice of the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Gastro-enteritis. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Scam, is a drastic cathartic, producing copious watery evacuations and griping. Scam, must
be compared with Jalap., another purging convolvulus. Spren- gel recorded a case of fatal poisoning in an
infant whose mother took a large quantity of Scam, and herself suffered no effects. Symptoms includedswdden
vomiting and copious green stools, distention and sensitiveness of the abdomen, and finally death.
Abdomen - Distention and sensitiveness of abdomen. Violent pain and rapid succession of stools, leaving
inactivity of lower intestines for several days.
Rectum - Copious green stools. Loose evacuation of feces with slight pain in stomach. Rapid succession of
stools.
Stomach - Sudden vomiting. Pain in stomach with the bowel movements. Inflammation of mucus membrane
attended with - loss of appetite and headache.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Scarlatininum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - scarl. Scarlatininum. Scarlet fever nosode. Nosodes. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Nephritis. Scarlet, fever. Skin disorders. Throat, sore.
HOMEOPATHIC - Scarl. has been used, like other nosodes, for the prevention and cure of the disease from
which it takes origin. Its well-known affinity for the skin, throat and kidneys suggests its applicability for
disorders of those organs.
COMMENTS - Zinke reported a case in which a patient suffered from angina with hyperthemia. Profound
asthenia and infectious look. Grave hyperthemia of tonsils swollen, pillars, the uvula dark red, the submaxillary
glands swollen, painful. The patient had suffered from scarlatina treated by penicillin. Since that time the
general condition was bad.
Zinke prescribed Scarl. 12x, twice 2 globules the first day. Immediate amelioration which the patient had not
had till then. Repeated once 12 and 14 days after one dose of Scarl. 30x. The patient was cured.
RELATIONS - Bell, is the nearest analog and should be its antidote and the various Mercuries come next.
Compare: (1) Apis, Ars., Rhus-t., Morbill., Diph.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Schinus Molle
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - schin. Schinus molle. N. O. Anacardiacae. Tincture of leaves and berries. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Esophagus, dryness. Flatulence. Heartburn. Liver, pain. Spinal cord, drawing. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Allen reported that schinus is an evergreen shrub, native of Mexico and South America and
frequently cultivated in Southern California under the names “Pepper tree” and “Chili pepper.”
The Schin. symptoms were observed by Dr. P. W. Poulson on a young woman who ate a few berries after
dinner, as well as on himself. He ate the leaves as well as the berries and experienced heartburn, griping in
liver and “a kind of drawing sensation a in the spinal cord and cerebellum.” Abdomen - Rolling and flatulence
in the bowels. Griping sensation in the liver.
Back - Drawing sensation as in the spinal cord and cerebellum.
Rectum - Painless diarrhea following painful vomiting. Profuse diarrhea continuing all night.
Stomach - Long continued vomiting, “as if all the bowels would be emptied out.” Vomiting very painful, as
the vomiting subsided diarrhea came on, the diarrhea being painless. Heartburn, dryness of esophagus.
RELATIONS - Compare: Anae., Rhus, Com.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Scirrhinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - scirr. Scirrhinum. Cancer nosode. Durum. Carcinominum. The nosode of scirrhus cancer.
Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Breast, cancer. Cancer. Glands, enlarged. Hemorrhages. Tumors. Varicose veins. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Burnett is the authority for this nosode. He proved it on himself and produced “a tremendous
 sinking at the navel,” which he regarded as a keynote for its use. Burnett particularly noted its usefulness on
cases of breast tumors.
This cancer nosode corresponds to cancerous diathesis, cancer of the breast with enlarged glands. A valuable
intercurrent remedy to be given during the course of the broad constitutional treatment, enhancing and
complementing the action of the other indicated remedies.
Constitutions - Cancerous diathesis.
Modalities - Worse 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. Worse irregularly on through the night.
COMMENTS - A patient to whom Burnett had given Scirr. mentioned to him that it had caused the passage of
an enormous number
of thread worms. On this hint, Burnett gave it with great success in many cases of this troublesome complaint.
In inveterate cases where Cina and Teucr. have given little relief, Scirr. has wrought a great change for the
better.
With Scirr., Burnett cured a man of hard glands which appeared on the left side of the neck after other glands
had been removed by the patient's brother, a surgeon. Hemorrhages and varicose veins of legs and feet with
purple points, have also been cured by Scirr.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Con., Care. (2) Worms, Cina, Teucr., Sulph., Sabal. (3) Sinking sensation,
Sulph., Sep., Hell., Hydr. (4) Cancer, Con., Hydr., Phyt., Sang., Care., Cund., Ars.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Grimmer.

name: Scleranthus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - scler-b. Scleranthus. Scler- anthus annuus. The flowering sprigs are placed in a bowl of water
and left in the sun for several hours. The water is strained subsequently and used as medicine. Historical
dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle
will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed
in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Scler-b belongs to Bach’s group For Those who Suffer Uncertainty, with Cer-b., Gent-b.,
Gors-b., Hom-b. and Wld-o-b.
States of indecisiveness and vacillation between options. The body is marked by a changeability of symptoms
as well. Symptoms may alternate between mental, emotional and physical states.
Vacillating between feeling loved and rejected. Bipolar disorders, manic-depressive states, dissociative
personality disorders, such as multiple personality disorder and in conversion disorder (Chic-b., Heath-b.).
Hysterical neurosis when symptoms vacillate between extremes.
Quick changes in weight. Travel sickness due to disturbance in equilibrium. After head injuries (Horn-b., Must-
b., Wld-o-b.), when the mind is imbalanced or over-stimulated, with a sense of chaos. Susceptibility to lung
tuberculosis, other lung conditions.
Gives mental calm and restores the mind’s ability to be in charge, to regain an overview (Elm-b.). State of
prolonged indecisiveness, usually in regard to a vital decision, has been found to precede the onset of illness.
MIND - Inner uncertainty. Unable to come to a satisfying decision. Changes mind frequently. Preoccupied,
over stimulated with internal arguments, disoriented and exasperated. Dread about possibly making the wrong
choice paralyzes the mind.
Over stimulated by details and cares. Confusion. Inability to calm the mind. Feels overwhelmed, inadequate.
Emotional instability, Capriciousness, mood swings. Too easily impressed, overreacts. Sudden interest and
disinterest.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Scolopenrda Morsitans
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - scol. Scolopendra morsitans. Centipede. Centipeda. The insect is triturated with sugar of milk
in the usual way. Tincture of whole animals. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Backache. Constipation. Convulsions. Deafness. Dysmenorrhea. Gangrene.
Headache. Hyperacidity. Leucorrhea. Malignant pustule. Nausea. Vertigo. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - When the centipede bites, it secretes a very active venom which contains cyanhydric acid
and sulphuric acid. Swelling, pain inflammation and gangrene of the bitten part, often with appearance like
malignant pustule. Vomiting and precordial anxiety.
In one fatal case the paroxysms of vomiting increased in intensity until the child, in a convulsive struggle,
ceased to breathe. In the case of a man bitten in the arm by a centipede, reported in the Nashville Jour-
 Scolopendra morsitans nal of Medicine, 1870, among the striking symptoms was no perspiration in the arm
for three months.
Dr. Sherman of California reported the following symptoms as prominent in a woman bitten by a centipede:
vertigo with blindness, worse in the morning, nausea and vomiting, unable to retain either food or liquid.
Terrible pain in back and loins, spasmodic and irregular, at times extending down the limbs. Pains returned
every few days for three weeks, commencing in the head and going out at the toes. “Resembled labor pains
as nearly as anything I ever saw.”
MIND - Severe headache that makes him think that he has some brain tumor. Fear he is going to lose his
mind. Delusion that he has been bewitched. Awakes with fear and a start. Loss of memory.
Abdomen - Tympanitis. Weakness in the epigastrium.
Chest - Pain in the chest on the right side. Ears - Severe pain in the ears. Itching in
the ear. Abundant wax. Buzzing noise. Deafness.
Eyes - Burning in the eyes. Pupil is red.
Inflammation of the cornea. Sensation of gravel. Sensation as if the eye would burst. Sensation of pressure
over the eyes. Weakness of vision.
Female - Irregular menstruation. Menses, the blood is black and coagulated. Dysmenorrhea. Leucorrhea,
purulent discharge. Inflammation of the uterus and the vagina. Itching in the nipples.
Food - Anorexia.
Head - Headaches in forehead. Sensation as if the head would split open. Burning pain. Piercing sensation.
Vertigo.
Heart - Precordial anxiety.
Limbs - Feet cold and aching. Cramps from the feet up to the calf. Arm greatly swollen. Erysipelatous blush
extending half over arm. No perspiration on right arm.
Lungs - Respiration short. Dry cough. Mucus rales. Expectoration purulent.
Mouth - Burning of the tongue with diminution of the taste. Tongue is coated. Bad breath. Severe toothache,
especially on the left side.
Nose - Sinusitis with severe pain in the forehead. Acute rhinitis. Itching and sneezing. Greenish discharge.
Rectum - Severe constipation. Stool is hard. Stool of a strong odor.
Skin - A large red spot, becoming black in the middle. Malignant pustules, associated with swelling of lymphatic
glands. Violent itching, followed by violent pain in bitten part.
Stomach - Hyperacidity. Burning in the stomach. Sensation of fullness. Nausea. Vomiting of a pale yellow,
glairy matter, continued at short intervals with increasing violence.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke.

name: Scrophularia Nodosa
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - scroph-n. Scrophularia nodosa. Knotted figwort. Scrophularia mary- landica. American variety
introduced from Europe and Asia. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Apply locally to
cancerous glands (Semp.). Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenoma. Appendicitis. Bedwetting. Breast, disorders. Breast, tumors. Cancer. Colic. Crusta
lactea. Deafness. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Eyes, disorders. Glands, enlarged. Hemorrhoids. Hodgkin's disease.
Liver, pains. Lymphoma. Nodosities. Palms, cramp. Pemphigus. Peritonitis. Rheumatism. Sigmoid flexure.
Sleepiness. Stiff-neck. Ureter, pain.
HERBAL - The plants of the genus Scrophularia generally have an unpleasant smell. The generic name is
derived from the supposed property of the roots to cure scrofula. The Treasury of Botany noted that a decoction
of one of the common British species, S. nodosa, is sometimes used by farmers to cure the scab in swine.
HOMEOPATHIC - Scroph-n., according to Dr. Cooperof London, has an especial affinity for breast tissue.
Adenoma and cancer come within its curative range. Enlarged glands. Hodgkin’s disease. Epithelioma.
Nodosities in the breasts (Scirr.). Breast tumors.
Scrofulous swellings (Cist.). Threatened abscesses that show no sign of disappearing. Lupoid ulceration.
Tubercular testis. Eczema of the ear. Vaginal itching. Painful hemorrhoids.
Pain in all flexor muscles. Cutting pains in the joints (Rhus-t.), but more intense and longer-lasting, worse by
rest and i n open air, better in warm room. Darting pain from knee to ankle joints, which feel stiff. Weakness,
languor, wants to lie down.
MIND - Despondency, much troubled about the past and very apprehensive about the future. Miserable and
sluggish feeling in mind when moving about.
Abdomen - Eczema around the navel. Peritonitis. Pain in sigmoid flexure. Pain in right hypochondrium, worse
 deep inspiration or lying right side. Twistingpinching pain in umbilicus (left side). Dull, heavy, periodic pain
worse when abdomen compressed, legs extended. Colic just below navel. Griping below naval, in the side in
afternoon, 7 a.m., after a slight vexation. As a local remedy for appendicitis.
Back - Pain in spinal column with slight opisthotonos. Stiff neck with pain and contraction of right sternomastoid
muscle.
Chest - Oppression with tremulous movement as from much weeping. Constricted feeling, which causes
uneasiness. Cramplike pain transversely across lower chest. Stitches in right chest, about 6th rib with
shivering. Violent pinching stitches near right last true ribs, while walking during rest, seeming to be in liver.
Ears - Inflammation about auricle. Deep ulcerated auricle. Eczema around ear, behind right ear. Ringing in
ears and sudden loss of hearing. Deafness in bull-necked boys. Deafness before and after menses, improving
during the flow.
Eyes - Scrofulous keratitis. Sore eyeballs. Severe cutting pains in eyes, unable to move them, passed off with
profuse sweat. Distressing photophobia (Con.). Black spots before eyes. On closing the eyes visions of
objects. Pulsating stitches in right eyebrow. Blepharospasm.
Face - Pleasant warmth in cheeks. Recurrent periostitis of lower jaw in a syphilitic.
Female - Recurring metritis with painful hemorrhoids. Irritation, soreness and burning in vagina and anus.
Head - On rising, indescribable pain and fullness in head, especially occiput and vertex, causing congestion
of conjunctive with puffiness, followed by nosebleed. Heaviness and distress in head, as after eating too much.
Pain at exit of right facial nerve from hypo-mastoid foramen, darting to right eye. Headaches above the
eyebrows while walking. Severe headache through temples, appearing every morning, extending to vertex and
occiput. Severe, sharp pain in vertex, forehead and temples, dull and throbbing, returning periodically, worse
resting, worse in open air, worse leaning forward, worse by study. Eczema behind ear.
Heart - Anguish in précordia, worse after food. Indescribable sensation in heart, with severe audible
palpitations. Pulse full, regular.
Kidneys - Pinching and tearing as if in ureter, extending from anterior superior spine of ilium down to pubis.
Increased secretion of urine with burning in urethra. Frequent, scanty emission of urine in afternoon.
Bedwetting.
Limbs - Drawing rheumatic pain in all flexors of arms and legs. Tingling in limbs as from a blow on a nerve.
Deep-seated cutting pain in all muscles of arms. Tingling or buzzing in arms and hands. Sticking and drawing
in right palm from joints of fingers to middle of hand as far as carpal bones, muscular cramp of palms.
Liver - Cutting, pains in liver on pressure.
Lungs - Violent dyspnea, oppression of chest with trembling. On turning on either side, violent dyspnea, worse
on right, with cutting in liver on pressure. Asthma in scrofulous patients. Pain about bifurcation of trachea. Pain
in right lung, on taking a deep inspiration, which causes cough without expectoration. Cutting in upper left lung,
worse breathing cold air.
Modalities - Better in warm room. Worse
lying on right side, in morning. Worse pressure, rest, after food. Worse deep breathing, breathing cold air and
studying in cold air.
Mouth - Bitter taste. Accumulation of sweetish water in several parts of tongue. Sick, sticking taste just above
pit of throat, frequently lasting an hour with sensation as if a soft substance (a plug of mucus) were lodged
there. Increased saliva, then dry mouth. Teeth feel loose. Pain in carious teeth, worse upper jaw. Gums bleed
freely.
Nose - Dry coryza.
Rectum - Rectal pain. Several stools daily with tenesmus. Painful, bleeding, protruding hemorrhoids.
Skin - Sallow. Surface burns when rubbed. Prickling, itching, worse back of hand, inside wrists and between
fingers. Pemphigus gangrenous. Falling off of hair stopped by lotion of Scroph-n.
Skin - Irritating vesicles on inside of lip, loaded with spindle-celled epithelium.
Sleep - Great drowsiness in morning, with weariness and fullness in whole body. Sleep irresistible before
and after a meal. Prolonged afternoon sleep.
Stomach - Appetite greatly increased at first, later nausea with weakness and oppression at epigastrium.
Feeling as if he had missed his regular meal. Dyspepsia.
Temperature - Chilliness for several hours on moving about in cool air, after rising in morning, passing off with
profuse sweat, followed by stupor and absence of all symptoms. Body feels dry and hot with burning sensation,
followed by profuse sweat.
Throat - Thick, tenacious, offensive mucus in throat in forenoon. Rancid taste in throat with great weakness
and stiffness in hollows of knees. Irritation of esophagus.
Vertigo - Dizziness, fullness and pressure in vertex. Vertigo in top of head when standing, even with severe
 aching in supra-orbital region.
COMMENTS - Scroph-n. was proved by Franz, and later in America by W. H. Blakeley, who took from 10 to
60 drops of the tincture several times a day. Blakeley’s proving showed pain in sigmoid flexure. Both Franz
and Blakely noted pains in the liver.
The most remarkable of Franz’s Scroph-n. symptoms included excessive drowsiness in forenoon, in afternoon,
and before and after eating. Sensation of a soft body in the gullet. Constriction of the chest. Oppression of
chest with trembling as after much weeping.
A sickly, giddy feeling with a sense of weakness and sinking at pit of chest, too weak to speak, along with pain
from forehead to back of head. Most of these symptoms were confirmed by Blakeley.
Gerard mentioned “hard kernels” and painful, swollen hemorrhoids as its indications.
Cooper saw Scroph-n., in the form of a poultice, relieve peritonitis affecting the lower abdomen. Colic from
slight vexation occurred in Franz’s proving.
Cooper gave Scroph-n. to a patient who had been poisoned by an Indian arrowpoison which produced
inflammation and suppuration of the glands. Scorph-n. relieved a most painful condition of the rectum and
purulent discharge that had kept up for years afterwards.
Cooper reduced strumous glands with it, cured deafness in a “bull-necked” patient, and cured a case of sycosis
using Scroph- n. externally as well as giving it internally. ’ “Nodosities in the breast” is another indication of
Cooper’s.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Bry. - chest symptoms. Compare: ( 1 ) Dig., Euphr., Grat.
(2)   Pains in joints worse by rest, better in warm room, Rhus-t. (3) Sleepiness, Nux- m., Op., Lup. Lob-e.,
Ruta, Care., Con., Aster. Followed well by: Dig. in enlarged glands.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Cooper. Murphy.
keynote:
PHARMACY - scroph-n. Scrophularia nodosa. Knotted figwort. Scrophularia mary- landica. American variety
introduced from Europe and Asia. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Apply locally to
cancerous glands (Semp.). Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenoma. Appendicitis. Bedwetting. Breast, disorders. Breast, tumors. Cancer. Colic. Crusta
lactea. Deafness. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Eyes, disorders. Glands, enlarged. Hemorrhoids. Hodgkin's disease.
Liver, pains.

name: Scutellaria Laterifolia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - scut. Scutellaria laterifolia. Skullcap. Mad-dog. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ardor, urine. Brain, irritation. Chorea. Delirium tremens. Dentition. Diarrhea. Exophthalmos.
Flatulence. Headache. Hiccoughs. Hydrophobia. Hysteria, insomnia. Nervousness. Night-terrors.
Sleeplessness. Tobacco-heart.
HERBAL - Hale, who introduced Scutellaria into homeopathy, noted that it is in the domestic practice of North
America with the equivalent usage ofvalerianin Europe. “Its calming effects on the nervous system have been
known ever since the settlement of New England.”
HOMEOPATHIC-Scut, is a nervous sedative. Nervous fear or excitement predominates. Chorea, twitching
of muscles. Restlessness. Chronic fatigue. Tired weak feeling. Uneasiness. Languor. Nervous weakness
after influenza. Nervous irritation and spasms of children during dentition.
Cardiac irritability. Tobacco-heart. Like its relation, Lycopus, it caused weak and irregular action of the heart
and protrusion of the eyes.
Hale used Scut, with success in sleeplessness, night-terrors, hysteria, nervous agitation from pain or exciting
emotions, cerebral irritation of children from dentition or intestinal irritation.
MIND - Confusion of mind. Fear of some calamity. Apathy. Irritability. Inability to study orfix the attention
on one’s work (Aeth.).
Abdomen - Gas, fullness and distention, colicky pain and uneasiness.
Constitutions - Suited to persons of a nervo- bilious temperaments.
Eyes -Aching in eyeballs. Eyeballs painful to touch. Eyeballs feel too large, pressed outwards.
Face - Flushed face.
Head - Dull, frontal headache. Migraine, worse over right eye. Nervous sick headaches, worse noise, odor
light, better night, rest. Explosive headaches of school teach-ers with frequent urination, headaches in front
and base of brain.
Kidneys - Frequent urination but quantity small. Quantity of urine diminished. Biliary salts increased.
Limbs - Chorea. Twitchings of muscles, must be moving. Tremors. Sharp, stinging pains in upper limbs.
Nightly restlessness. Weakness and aching.
Male - Seminal emissions and impotency, with fear of never being better.
Modalities - Better by sleep. The hemicrania is better moving about in open air. Headache worse from motion.
Worse by overwork or over-exertion. Worse by work or excitement.
Mouth - Bad taste, sour, bitter.
Rectum - Diarrhea. Light colored. Stools preceded by colicky pain in abdomen.
 Sleep - Restless, must move about. Disturbed sleep and frightful dreams. Night terrors. Sleep is
unrefreshing.
Stomach - Poor appetite. Sour belchings. Nausea. Vomiting of sour ingesta, hiccough. pain and distress in
stomach.
Throat - Sensation of lump in throat which could not be swallowed.
COMMENTS - Provings by G. W. Gordon and G. H. Royal gave the homeopathic data. Royal’s provers took
3x and 30x. Gordon took repeated doses of 10 to 50 drops. Royal had this indication for Scut, given to him by
a friend: “Nervo-bilious headache with the nervous symptoms uppermost and nothing the matter with her.”
He related the case of Miss M., 32, who was the head of a large school, complained of being used up, unable
to sleep or think. Pain in head almost constant, sometimes frontal, mostly at base of brain.
Whenever called upon to overdo herself, she could not sleep that night and then there is either a nervous
explosion the following day or a nervous sick headache, either being followed by complete collapse.
This was in May. Pic-ac. and later Phos- ac., gave relief and in September the patient resumed work. Late in
December there was another breakdown, and Stych-p. was given.
A week later after a very long and fatiguing day’s work, Royal was summoned at 2 a.m. He found the patient
screaming. Every few minutes she had to urinate and passed only a few drops. Stools frequent, loose, watery.
Pulse irregular.
Scut, was given, ten drops every half-hour. Patient was better after the second dose, slept after the fourth.
Since then she kept the medicine by her, but only took it when overworked. She never had another nerve
explosion or headache. In this case there was “nothing the matter with her” i.e., no organic defect to which the
sufferings could be attributed.
Hale quoted many eclectic writers who give various indications King mentioned depression of nervous and
vital powers after long sickness, over-exercise, over-study, long-continued and exhausting labors. It controls
nervous agitation. It was Burnett’s chief remedy in the nervous debility after influenza.
Scudder mentioned chorea, delirium tremens and hydrophobia, as its popular name “Mad dog” suggests.
Rafinesque cited cases of prevention of hydrophobia and Hale observed it produce in a patient taking it
“Spasmodic or constrictive closing of jaws and a tightness of the muscles of the face.”
A writer, quoted in the N. Y. Med. Times, said Scut, has the remarkable effect of calming fear in delirium
tremens.
Paine added the indications subsultus tendinum following fevers in delirium tremens, epilepsy, catalepsy, and
hysteria. Coe, who used Scutellarin, the concentrated preparation, mentioned sunstroke, tenesmus, tetanus,
cramps.
Churton gave 60 drops of the tincture every two hours in a case of “severe and rapid hiccough” which
chloroform, morphine and pilocarpine had failed to relieve permanently. After the eighth dose, the patient slept
and the spasms gradually diminished and stopped for good by the fourth day.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Heart, Grave’s disease. Lycps. (2) Nervous exhaustion, Cypr. according to Hale,
acts more on brain, Scut, on
spinal cord. (3) Trismus, Nux-v. Hydrophobia, Agar., Fagus, Lach., Bell. (4) Overworked women, Mag-c.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Secale Cornutum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sec. Secale cornutum. Ergot of Rye. Spurred Rye. Claviceps purpurea. N. O. Fungi.
Pyrenomycetae. The black, hornlike spur into which the grains of rye cereal are changed by the fungus
Claviceps purpurea. Tincture of the fresh spurs collected just before harvest. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - After-pains. Blindness. Cataracts. Childbirth. Collapse. Debility. Delirium. Diarrhea. Emaciation.
Ergotism. Gangrene. Hemorrhages. Labor, pains. Leucorrhea. Locomotor, ataxia. Lymphoid, tumors.
Mania. Menstrual, colic. Metritis. Miscarriage. Myelitis. Nosebleed. Numbness. Nymphomania. Paraplegia.
Petechia. Prostration. Puerperal, fever. Puerperal, mania. Raynaud’s disease. Tetanus. Thrombosis. Varicose,
veins. Varicose, ulcers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Rye and grasses are apt to be affected with the ergot disease in damp seasons and when
grown on damp, ill-drained lands. If breeding cows are turned on pastures where infected grasses grow, they
are very liable to drop their calves. Ergot has been known to hasten childbirth from remote times.
Secale’s other actions have been, for the most part, learned from the terrible epidemics of “ergotism” which
have occasionally devastated districts in which rye infected with ergot has been ground into flour and eaten by
the population.
 Death takes places in convulsions, from gangrene and consequent exhaustion, or from exhausting
hemorrhages or discharges, as diarrhea. Many who escape immediate death are reduced to a cachectic state
from which they never recover, are paralyzed, have limbs distorted and senses impaired. In general, the
sufferer retains a clear intellect and a good, even abnormally good appetite to the last.
Sec. contracts the muscles of blood vessels and the uterus. It also decomposes the blood, producing
hemorrhage which is thin, fetid, watery, black, oozing continuously. Small wounds bleed much. Mortification,
gangrene. Traumatic gangrene, from application of leeches or mustard, better from cold. Lymphoid tumors.
Useful for old people with shriveled skin or for thin, scrawny, old women. Produces contraction of the unstriped
muscular fibers, hence a tight feeling throughout the body. Produces an anemic condition, with coldness,
numbness, petechiae.
Restlessness, anxiety, extreme debility and prostration. Collapse. Emaciation, though appetite and
thirst may be excessive. Discharges are dark, thin, foul and exhausting. Varicose veins. Thrombosis.
Hinsdale noted that Sec. decreases the flow of pancreatic juice by raising the blood pressure.
Chronic, sharp, stinging neuralgic pains, which burn like fire, better application of heat. Tetanic spasms with
full conscious- . ness. Facial and abdominal muscles twitch. Twitchings, spasms with fingers spread apart.
Gnawing and cramps with stiffness. Numbness. Insufferable tingling, crawling, better rubbing. Sensation of
burning in the whole body or as of sparks falling on them or here and there like fire. Loss of power of voluntary
motion.
Coldness, but does not want to be covered up. Symptoms are better from cold, the whole body is pervaded
by a sense of great heat. Sensation of deadness in any part. Everything feels loose and open. Walking causes
giddiness. The right side is predominantly affected.
MIND - Mania fear or depressed by fear. Anxiety with fear of death, restlessness and difficult breathing. Fear
of death before menses. Suspicious. Unconsciousness during pregnancy or childbirth. Unconsciousness,
with heavy sleep.
Excessive sadness, gradually changes to cheerfulness. Seems besides herself after miscarriage. Forgetful
after sex. Weakness of mind after spasms or exhausting sex. Indifference to exposure of person. Impotence.
Nymphomania during menses. Grasping at genitals during spasms.
Puerperal mania, exposes the body, tears at the genitals, inserts her finger into the vagina and scratches until
it bleeds, all ideas of modesty lost. Sardonic laughing. Madness, inclination to bite or drown himself. Laughs,
claps her hand over head, seems besides herself.
Delirium, abandons her relatives. Mocking at his relatives. Treats his relations contemptuously and
sarcastically. Wants to fight. Rage, followed by continuous deep sleep.
Wandering talk and hallucinations. Raving delirium. Delusion that two sick people were in bed, one of whom
got well and the other did not. Foolish behavior during spasms. Impulse to jump into river.
Abdomen - Excessively inflated and tight, wants uncovered. Empty feeling in hy- pogastrium or bearing down,
must lie doubled up in bed. Twitching of abdominal muscles. Formation of large lumps and swelling in
abdomen.
Back - Spinal irritation, tingling of lower limbs, can bear only slightest covering. Tingling in back, extending to
fingers and toes. Formication and numbness. Locomotor ataxia. Myelitis. Pressure on affected portion causes
pain there as well as through the chest.
Breasts - Suppression of milk with stinging in breasts. Breasts do not fill with milk properly.
Causations - Abortion, miscarriage, childbirth. Hemorrhages, wounds. Suppressions of tears, lochia, milk, or
sweat.
Chest - Dyspnea and oppression with cramp in diaphragm. Boring pain in chest. Angina pectoris. Pains
through chest, on pressing spine. Burning in lungs.
Constitutions - Hemorrhagic diathesis. Suited to irritable, plethoric subjects or to thin, scrawny, feeble
emaciated women. To very old, decrepit persons. Women of very lax muscular tissue, everything seems loose
and open, no action, flabby vessels.
Ears - Great difficulty in hearing, with roaring, humming in ears. Confused hearing or lost, after chorea.
Sensitiveness of hearing, so that even the slightest sound re-echoed in her head.
Eyes - Dilated pupils, distortion and strabismus. Incipient cataract, senile, especially in women. Pustulous
conjunctivitis. Suppuration of cornea. Diabetic retinitis. Ptosis. Catarrh. Suppressed tears. Sparks before the
eyes. Double or triple vision. Blindness. Eyes sunken and surrounded by blue rings. Paralysis of upper lid
from coal gas.
Face - Spasmodic distortion, or sunken. Pale, pinched. Wild look. Livid spots on face. Tingling, twitching,
or cramps in face, which spread over the body. Lockjaw.
Female - Menstrual colic with coldness and intolerance of heat. Menses irregular, copious, dark, continuous
 oozing of watery blood until next period. Passive hemorrhages in feeble, cachetic women. Brownish
offensive leucorrhea. Burning pains in uterus. Threatened miscarriage about the third month (Sabin.).
Never well since miscarriage or abortion. During labor no expulsive action, though everything is relaxed.
Bearing down pain with coldness. Puerperal fever and putrid discharges. Contracted uterus, hourglass labor
contractions. Septic placenta. Severe after-pains. Dark offensive, green lochia. Prolapsed uterus after forceps
delivery. Tympanitis, coldness, suppressed urine. Vagina hot or cool. Weak uterus. Metritis. Gangrene of
female organs.
Food - Unquenchable thirst. Thirst with dry mouth or burning. Unnatural, ravenous appetite. Craves acids
and sour things. Averse to fat and meat.
Head - Passive, congestive headache, rises from back of head. Twisting of head to and fro. Head drawn back.
Feels light or heavy, with tingling in legs. Falling of hair. Hair is dry and gray.
Heart - Precordial tenderness. Palpitations with contracted and intermittent pulse. Palpitations after sexual
excess in males.
Kidneys - Paralysis of bladder. Retention with unsuccessful urging. Suppressed urine, pale, watery. Bloody
urine, white, cheesy deposit. Discharge of black blood from bladder. Bedwetting in the elderly.
Limbs - Paralysis with distorted limbs, of lower limbs, of one side of one arm or one leg, with tingling, numbness
and prickling. Paralysis after spasms. Paraplegia. Locomotor ataxia. Formication, pain and spasmodic
movements. Violent cramps, in hands, legs, feet and cramps. Icy coldness of limbs. Numbness. Fingers
and feet bluish, shriveled, spread apart or bent backwards. Cold, dry hands and feet in heavy smokers, with
feeling of fuzziness in the fingers. Varicose ulcers, foul indolent. Trembling, staggering or shuffling gait, as if
feet were dragged along. Violent pain in fingertips, tingling in toes. Toes drawn up.
Lungs - Heavy, anxious, obstructed breathing with moaning, sighs, sobs. Spitting of blood, with or without
cough. Expectoration of blood during violent efforts to breathe.
Modalities - Better lying doubled up in bed. rocking, forcible stretching. Better cold applications, cold bathing.
Better open air, uncovering, fanning. Better after vomiting. Worse from heat, warmth, warm cover. Worse
touch, motion, exertion. Worse eating, smoking. Worse loss of fluids, sexual excess. Worsejust before or
during menses. Worse pregnancy and after miscarriage.
Mouth - Salivation, with fetid breath. Much acid fluid in mouth. Spitting of blood. Bloody or yellowish green
foam at mouth. Dryness of mouth. Stuttering, indistinct speech. Speech difficult, slow and weak.
Nose - Nosebleed, oozing, dark blood, with great prostration in old people, alcoholics or young women.
Rectum - Cholera-like stools with coldness and cramps. Gushing offensive, painless, watery stools with
collapse and great exhaustion. Olive-green, thin, putrid, bloody stools with icy coldness and intolerance
of being covered. Involuntary stools, no
sensation of passing feces. Anus feels loose and wide open.
Sensations - As if intoxicated while undressing. As of a solid plug in nose. Uterus as if burnt. As if contents of
uterus would fall forward. As if soft air were creeping through back. As if sacrum would be forced out. As if
something alive creeping under skin. As if limbs had been a long time in hot water. As if sparks of fire falling
on different parts. As if mice creeping under skin. Fuzzy feeling in limbs.
Skin-Shriveledskin, numb, mottled, dusky- blue tinge. Skin cold,dry, wrinkled or bluish, worse over affected
part. Raynaud’s disease. Edema neonatorum. Twitchings or quivering in the skin. Formication under skin.
Burning sensation, better by cold, wants parts uncovered, though cold to touch. Aversion to heat.
Petechiae. Dry gangrene, developing slowly. Slight wounds continue to bleed. Bloody blisters. Livid spots.
Boils with green pus, matures slowly.
Sleep - Deep, lethargic, profound and long sleep. Insomnia with restlessness, fever, anxious dreams.
Insomnia of drug and liquor habits.
Stomach - Burning in stomach and abdomen. Tympanites. Hiccough. Belchingsof bad odor. Empty retchings.
Nausea, easy vomiting of blood and coffee-grounds fluid. Hematemesis.
Temperature - Coldness. Cold, dry skin, clammy sweat, excessive thirst. Internal burning with icy coldness
externally, yet averse to being covered, worse abdomen. Heat as of sparks. Puerperal fever. Erysipelas.
Cold or foul sweat destroys shoes.
Throat - Painful tingling, burning. Post diphtheria paralysis. Feeble voice inaudible, stammering. Voice hoarse
and hollow. Painless aphonia in morning, as the day goes on he gets hoarse.
Tongue - Tongue dry, cracked, blood like ink exudes. Tongue coated thick, viscid, yellowish. Cold, livid.
Tingling of tip of tongue, which is stiff. Tongue swollen, feels paralyzed. Stuttering as if tongue were
paralyzed. Tongue clean, with dry, red tip.
Vertigo - Vertigo with stupefaction and heaviness of head. Reeling, inability to stand erect. Vertigo as from
intoxication. Vertigo on slightest motion. Vertigo while sitting.
 COMMENTS - Convulsive nervous symptoms. The body is at times rigid, at times alternating with relaxation.
This is especially seen in the hands, which are either clenched or have the fingers spread widely apart (a
keynote symptom).
The muscles of the face and abdomen twitch. Spasmodic twitchings of muscles in various parts (especially
spreading of fingers), eyes sunk, features pinched, shriveled, dry, as though no moisture were left in the body.
Anesthesia.
Cold to the touch, but cannot bear to be covered. Characteristic burning sensations, burning in all parts of the
body as if sparks were falling on the patient. Worse from warmth and external heat. Characteristic numbness,
tingling as if ants were crawling all over, better from rubbing.
Contraction and then dilatation of blood vessels. Vascular headaches, constriction. Migraines. The fingers turn
bluish black. Hemorrhagic diathesis, persistent offensive bleeding. Hemorrhages with tingling.
Small wounds bleed persistently. Purpura. Hollow viscera and violent palpitations. Dry gangrene. Threatened
amputation. Gangrene aggravated by heat, affected part feels cold. Shriveled, dry skin. Harsh and sallow
complexion. Small and painful boils with green contents, mature very slowly, heal slowly and are very
weakening. Exophthalmic goiter.
Spasmodic retching, the stomach is violently contracted. Incontinence or retention of urine. Involuntary
diarrhea with wide-open anus. In cholera where the patient is cold, almost pulseless. Exhausting and offensive
discharges. Loss of fluids, debility.
Threatened miscarriage, especially at the third month. Tendency to miscarriage. Prolonged, forcing pains,
bearing-down, bearing down forwards (Sep. is bearing down downward). Irregular, too weak, feeble
or ceasing labor pains (Puls., Caul.).
Everything seems loose and open, but no expulsive action. Used to hasten and promote delivery. Fainting.
Hourglass contraction of the uterus. Too long, excessive after-pains. Postpartum hemorrhage of dark, oozing
blood. Retained placenta. Suppression or non-appearance of the milk.
Menses are irregular, copious, dark, fluid, accompanied by labor-like pains in abdomen. There may be a
continuous watery discharge of blood during the whole time between the periods.
Teste recorded the case of a woman, 50, fat, very soft flesh, who had flooding which nothing could stop. After
several useless attempts, Teste gave large doses of Sec. with scarcely any effect. The patient asked for
infinitesimal doses. At that time. Teste had no faith at all in infintesimals, but he yielded to the patient ’ s request
and gave one drop of the 6c. Then the bleeding ceased immediately and permanently.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Op. Compare: (1) Ergot. (2) Pedi-can. - symptoms of locomotor ataxia,

name: Selenium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sei. Selenium. The Element (Se, At. Wt. 79.5). Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Bedwetting. Comedones. Constipation. Debility. Diabetes insipidus. Eczema,
scalp.Hair, loss. Headache. Hoarseness. Impotency. Laryngitis, tubercular. Liver, disorders. Masturbation.
Myasthenia. Prostatitis. Prostatorrhea. Psoriasis. Scabies. Skin, disorders. Spermatorrhea. Stammering.
Sun, effects. Syphilis. Tea, effects.
HOMEOPATHIC - Selenium was discovered in 1818 by Berzelius and was named by him after the moon,
because it is found associated with tellurium (Tellus, the earth). It is also found associated with sulphur. All
 three belong to the same group of elements. Selenium is found either in its natural state or, more often, as a
metallic selenide.
Colloidal selenium has been used as an injection for inoperable cancer. Pain, sleeplessness, ulceration and
discharge are markedly diminished.
Marked effects on the genito-urinary organs. The larynx and liver are also affected. Often indicated in elderly
men. especially for prostration and sexual atony. Bedwetting. Chronic urethritis. Diabetes insipidus.
Irritability after sex. Sexual weakness. Lascivious, but impotent. Loss of sexual power with sexual thoughts.
Prostate weakness with dribbling of urine. Escape of semen especially when straining at stool. Chronic gleet.
Great debility, worse heat. Debility after exhausting diseases, fevers. Patient becomes easily debilitated by
heat or hot weather, a little mental or physical exertion makes him
sleepy. Easy exhaustion, mental and physical in old age. Early senility.
Hemicrania. Neuritis and neuralgia of the head. Marked effects on the supra orbital nerves (left). Myasthenia.
Chronic diseases of the bone-marrow. Emaciation of single parts, face, hands, thighs etc. Pulsation in the
whole body especially in abdomen, worse eating. Cramps, then stiffness. Biting, here and there. Aversion to
draft of air, warm cold or damp.
MIND - Dullness of mind. Difficult comprehension, concentration. Mental labor fatigues. Total unfitness for any
kind of work. Forgetful in work, but dreams of what he has forgotten.
Great forgetfulness when awake with distinct recollection during half sleep. Fails to understand what he hears
or reads. Lack of enthusiasm and of interest, indifference. Apathy. Talkative, when excited, stammers,
pronounces some words incorrectly. Stutters.
Extreme sadness. Depression in the morning, aggravated in the evening. Despair, melancholy. Aversion to
company of intimate friends. Dread of society. Reveries of a religious and melancholy character.
Easily irritated by noise, people and conversation. Easily antagonized. Irritability after sex. Confusion after
emissions. Dipsomania before menses. Erotic thoughts with impotence. Lascivious thoughts. Becomes
drunk easily.
Abdomen - Sensation of abdominal distention on the left side, ameliorated by pressure, aggravated by going
to stool or by coughing. Left abdominal hyperesthesia, spreading towards the left kidney area. Violent shoot-
ings in spleen when walking. Pulsation all over the body especially in abdomen after eating which hinders
sleep.
Back - The back becomes almost paralytic after a temporary illness. Paralytic pain in small of back, better
lying on abdomen. Sensation of paralysis in loins. Pain as from lameness in small of back in morning. Hard
swelling on back. Severe pain in the coccyx, aggravated when sitting, ameliorated by walking. Pain through
left side of neck and down back of left leg.
Bones - Osteoporosis during menopause. Inflammation of the bones and cartilages in the young adult,
attacking the knee, then the elbow and the hip. Bones fragile.
Breasts - More or less acute pain, prickling or dull aching in the left or right breast.
Causations - Bad effects from excess of tobacco or tea. Ill effects of debauchery, alcohol, sugar, salt,
lemonade, loss of vital fluids, masturbation, sexual excess, over-study. Walking, exertion.
Chest - Constrictive or stinging pain behind the sternum and in the upper left thoracic region. Pains in right
side, around under last ribs, especially on inspiration, extending to region of kidneys.
Constitutions - Suited to blondes and persons of light complexion.
Ears - Deafness from hardened wax. Ear stopped.
Eyes - Blurred vision, with difficult accommodation. Myopia. Pains deep in orbits. Discharge of a thick, yellow
secretion, especially in the morning. Heavy, painful, burning, blood-shot with red marks on the eyelids.
Spasmodic twitching of left eyeball. Itching vesicles on eyebrows and margins of lids. Styes. Blepharitis. Dacy-
rocystitis. Falling off of eyebrows.
Face - Great emaciation of face and hands. Twitching in muscles of face. Greasy, shining skin of face. Upper
lip cracked. Comedones.
Female - Rare menses. Menses early, scanty, painful. Menses painful on the first day. Awakened by pain of
menses. Menses copious and dark. Menses delayed about eight days. Throbbing in abdomen during
pregnancy, worse eating.
Food - Thirstless. Anorexia in morning with white-coated tongue. Hunger at night. Craves stimulants, brandy,
tea etc. Desire for alcoholic drinks. Aversion to salty food. Worse from tea, sugar, salt, lemonade, wine.
Sweetish, disagreeable taste after smoking.
Head - Pain over left eye, worse walking in sun, strong odors and tea. Nervous headaches. Headache
from intellectual labor. Headache every afternoon. Headache after drinking lemonade, wine or tea.
Headache of alcoholics, headache after debauchery. Pain in the scalp as if hair were pulled out. Scalp feels
 tense. Does not want hair touched. Hair falls out from eyebrows, whiskers and genitals.
Heart - Pulse very accelerated. Arterial pulsation, especially in the abdominal aorta, preventing him from
sleeping. Pain in the heart region. Rhythmic anomalies. Syphilitic aortitis.
Kidneys - Frequent urination with urgent need to urinate. Sensation in the tip of urethra, as if a biting drop
were forcing its way out. Red, itching irritation at the tip of the penis. Urine dark red, thick, scanty, gritty with
deposits. Dribbling of urine after urination and after stool. Involuntary dribbling, when walking. Urination
predominantly at night. Nocturnal bedwetting.
Limbs - Pains in all the limbs, as if caused by a chill. Legs feel weak, with fear of paralysis after typhus. Sudden
left sciatic pain leaves soreness behind. Itching pimples on buttocks and thighs, near the scrotum. The knees
crack when they are bent. Cramps in calves and soles. Flat ulcers on lower legs. Itching in feet, especially
around ankles in evening. Blisters on toes. Emaciation of hands, of legs. Dry, scaly eruption on palms with
itching, having syphilitic base. Psoriasis of palms. Painful hang-nails. Scabies-like pimples on hand. Tearing
in hands at night with cracking in wrists. Itching at wrist in palms, itching vesicles on and between fingers.
Miliaria in forearm.
Liver - Chronic liver affections. Pain in the liver, especially on taking an inspiration, extending to the kidney
region with sensibility to external pressure. Enlarged with fine rash over liver region.
Lungs - Weak feeling in the chest. Frequent efforts to breathe deeply like sighing. Difficulty breathing when
walking in open air. Respiration obstructed at night, when lying down, by pains. Dry hacking cough, worse in
the morning. Hawking up of mucus and of small clots of blood. Hawks up clear mucus in the morning. Frequent
necessity to clear the throat in singers. Tubercular laryngitis.
Male - Irritability after sex. Loss of sexual power-with lascivious fancies. Lascivious but impotent. Increases
desire, decreases ability. Sexual weakness. On attempting sex, penis relaxes. Easy loss of semen during
sex with feeble erection, but long continued voluptuous thrill during stools. Semen watery, odorless. Dribbling
of semen during sleep. Prostatitis, prostatic adenoma. Oozing of prostatic fluid during sleep, while sitting,
walking and at stool. Hydrocele. Chronic gleet. Bedwetting, chronic urethritis. Papillomas on the penis.
Modalities - Better after sunset. Better inhaling cool air, taking cold air or cold water into mouth. Worse loss
of sleep, night watching, after sleep, rest. Worse in open air, draft, even if warm. Worse hot weather, sun and
with the sun’s increase. Headaches worse every afternoon. Worse singing, mental exertion. Worse by touch,
pressure, motion. Worse after seminal losses, after stools. Worse wine, cinchona.
Mouth - Sweetish taste. Bitter taste in the mouth. Extreme dryness of the mouth. Tongue loaded with a thick
white coating in morning. Burning at the tip of the tongue. Pain under root of tongue. Pain in the left molars,
which spreads to all the teeth. Bleeding gums and ulcerations in the mouth. Stammering speech, articulates
with great difficulty.
Neck - Glands of neck large and hard. Cramp in neck. Rigidity of muscles of neck and nape, which hinders
head being turned.
Nose - Sinusitis. Atrophic rhinitis. Coryza, ending in diarrhea. Fluent coryza in evening. Yellow, thick,
gelatinous mucus in nose. Full of thick glairy mucous. Complete chronic obstruction of nose. Nasal itching with
the need to scratch the inside of the nose. Inclination to bore fingers in the nose. Sense of smell diminished at
times. Smells a repulsive odor like garlic.
Rectum-Anal andrectal itching, especially towards evening. Constipation from rectal weakness with flatulence.
Hard evacuations, followed by a discharge of mucus
or of blood when passing the last portion of it. Stools large, hard, requiring a great effort, even a mechanical
aid to expel them. Stools exceedingly difficult and threaten to tear anus from their immense size. Somewhat
liquid feces with tenesmus. Filament like hair in feces.
Skin - Seborrhea, comedones with an oily surface of the skin. Oily. Frequent tingling in circumscribed parts
of skin with great provocation to scratch. Red rash on region of liver. Miliary eruption. Vesicular eruption
between fingers (Rhus- t., Anae.). Dry, scaly eruption in palms with itching. Itching about the ankles and
folds of skin, between fingers. Acne. Prolonged oozing from parts which have been scratched. Flat ulcers.
Loss of hair from the head, armpits, pubic region and eyebrows. Hair falls off head, whiskers and other parts.
Alopecia.
Sleep - Sleep prevented by pulsation in all vessels, worse abdomen. Sleepless until midnight, awakens
early and always same hour. Insomnia, following alcoholism, infectious diseases, heart diseases. Disposition
to sleep early in evening with imperfect sleep and frequent waking during night. Jerks in body when going to
sleep. Erotic dreams. Dreams of fire, murders, robbers, quarrels and unnatural cruelty. Waking early in morning
and always at same hour.
Stomach - After eating, pulsation all over, especially abdomen. Pressure in stomach as if cramp would occur.
Cramp in stomach. Belching. Hiccough and belchings after smflking. Inclination to vomit. Feels very sick after
 sleep. Nausea, vertigo, thirsty for cold water, general weakness one hour after eating.
Teeth - Teeth covered with mucus. Toothache from tea. Toothache with feeling of coldness, better taking cold
water and cold air into mouth. Toothache which compels use of toothpick until the blood comes. Boring in
molars. The teeth become free of mucus, hard and smooth and crack when rubbed.
Temperature - Chilliness, followed by hot flushes. Constant alternation of heat and cold. Sweating from the
armpits and genital region. Burning heat, extending over the skin. Perspiration from least exertion. Perspiration
as soon as he sleeps, day or night. Tendency to profuse perspiration when walking or during an afternoon
sleep. Perspiration on chest, genitals and under axilla, which leaves yellow or white spots on linen and stiffens
it. External heat with burning in skin and only in single spots.
Throat - Chronic laryngitis. Voice hoarse and husky, as soon as he begins to sing, talk or read, affected by
even cold. Voice rattles. Nodes on vocal cords. Incipient tubercular laryngitis. Throat dry, painful on waking,
especially on the left side with extreme thirst. Cough in the morning, expectoration of a bloody mucus. Much
clear, starchy mucus (Stann.). Laryngeal cough. Hawking and raising transparent lumps of mucus every
morning.
Vertigo - Vertigo on lifting head, rising from a seat, raising himself in bed, moving about with nausea, vomiting.
Faintness, worse for an hour after breakfast and dinner.
COMMENTS - The Sei. proving was conducted by Hering. In London, Raeside repeated a complete proving
on sixteen provers and six controls in 1959-60, using the 6c, 12c, and 30c potencies.
A leading feature of Sei. is the weakness it causes, a weakness involving all parts of the body, easy fatigue
from any labor, night watching, mental exertion and especially from hot weather. The hotter his body the
weaker he is; strength rises as the sun sinks.
Irresistible desire to lie down and sleep, strength leaves him suddenly, especially in hot weather. Sluggishness,
wants to sleep from sheer exhaustion and is worse after. Cannot bear any nervous drain, hence worse after
sex or seminal emissions. Impotence. Debility after fevers, infectious diseases.
Great emaciation of face, hands, legs, feet, affected parts and single parts. Pulsation in whole body, especially
in abdomen after eating. Very great aversion to a draft of air,
either warm, cold or damp.
Irritability, headaches and other troubles following or worse by seminal emissions. Headaches are
accompanied by profound melancholy and may be caused by indulgence in alcoholics or in tea, by hot weather,
by over-study, and they are worse by strong odors. Headaches may be periodical and are frequently located
above the left eye.
Chronic liver disorders. Sensitiveness of liver. Enlargement of liver with loss of appetite. In the morning, sharp
stitching pain worse on any movement or pressure. “Fine rash over liver region.”
Coryza ending in diarrhea. Hungry at night, longing for spirituous liquors, an almost irresistible maniacal desire.
Aversion to salted food. Sensation as if a biting drop were forcing its way out of the urethra.
Constipation from weakness with impacted feces. Dribbling of semen after stool and after urination. Sufferings
after seminal emissions mental confusion, headache, almost paralytic weakness of spine, involuntary escape
of prostatic fluid.
Itching in folds of skin, as between fingers and about joints, especially the ankle-joint (Sulph.). The itching may
occur in small spots and be accompanied by tingling (showing involvement of the nervous system).
Clarke frequently relieved “psoriasis palmaris” with Sei., which shows that it has a relation to syphilis. The
scalp is affected with an eczematous eruption which oozes thin fluid after scratching. Hair falls off scalp and
all parts of body.
Clarke cured with Sei. many cases of hoarseness, the special indications being hoarseness of singers,
appearing as soon as they begin to sing or after long use of the voice with frequent necessity to clear the throat
from accumulation of clear, starchy mucus. Scrofulous and incipient tubercular laryngitis have been cured with
Sei.
RELATIONS -Antidoted by: Ign., Puls., Mur- ac. Compare: (1) Agn., Calad., Sulph., Tell., Ph-ac. (2) Arg-n. -
Nervous imbalance with weakness, trembling, vertigo, ataxia. (3) Alum. - Paretic weakness, especially of the
rectum and bladder. (4) Stann. - Nervous exhaustion and extreme weakness of the respiratory organs.
(5) Calad. - Depressive state as a result of excess of tobacco and sexual over-indulgence.
(6) Rauw. Compatible after: Calad., Nat-c., Staph., Ph-ac. (in sexual weakness). Itch checked by Merc, or
Sulph. often requires Sei. Incompatible: Chin., wine.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Sempervivum Tectorum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - semp. Sempervivumtectorum. Houseleek. N. O. Crassulaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bites, insects. Breast, cancer. Cancer. Hemorrhoids. Herpes zoster, Menopause. Menses,
suppressed. Ringworm. Scir- rhus. Tongue, indurations. Tumors. Warts. Wounds, poisoned.
HERBAL - In Hufeland’s Journal, said Kallen- bach, the fresh juice of Sempervivum tectorum is recommended
in chronic aphthae in grown persons in causal relation to hemorrhoids, as well as in scirrhus indurations of the
tongue.
In many countries, it has a popular reputation for indurations and sores on the tongue. Reichel of Staben,
considered it curative in spasms of the uterus and in menstrual disturbances of all kinds. Cases of too exalted
vascular activity in the sexual sphere. Also in ear troubles consequent on hardened earwax and in inflammatory
exudations of the ear.
It is externally used for bites of insects, stings of bees and poisoned wounds, warts. Herpes zoster and
cancerous tumors. Breast cancer. Ringworm. Hemorrhoids.
HOMEOPATHIC - Grimmer stated, “Sempervivum tectorum has cured many cases of induration and sores on
the tongue, it also has definite action on the uterus and menstrual function in cancer constitutions, it could be
thought of in cases of tongue cancer.”
COMMENTS - Kallenbach was consulted by Mrs. S„ 44, childless of sickly looks, for an affection of the tongue.
For the previous six months menses had appeared only every eight to ten weeks and were accompanied with
Sempervivum tectorum pains darting from small of back to uterus and vulva.
During the six months, she had stitching pain on the right rim of her tongue about 3/4 inch from the point, at
which place after a few weeks, a swelling formed, the size of a small bean.
The swelling bled at times, and at night caused a burning sensation as of a small coal, disturbing sleep. Sour
food caused pain. The swelling was not hard on the surface, but contained two hard nodules the size of lentils,
one of which was denuded and bled on touch.
Three enlarged veins crossed the swelling and entered the tongue muscle behind it. She had been treated for
over a month with Aur., Ars., Carb-v. in vain.
Kallenbach moistened the swelling with the fresh juice of Semp. thrice a day. Within three days it was smaller
and folds appeared, the enlarged veins were contracted, formed thin, tense vessels crossing the swelling and
seemingly tying it.
During the next three days, the patient applied the juice too energetically and Kallenbach found the
surroundings in inflammatory irritation and very sensitive.
The applications was stopped and Semp. 2x was given internally. After a week’s use the swelling had shriveled
to one-third the size, and ten days later the menses, which had ceased altogether, reappeared and continued
very profusely for five days.
The swelling shriveled to the size of a small pea, was firmer, harder, devoid of sensation and gave no further
trouble. The menses continued regularly.
In another instance, Mrs. X., 27, a mother of a six month old healthy boy, formerly frequently afflicted with
swelling of the glands, very sensitive to homeopathic remedies, complained of a pain under her tongue of ten
days’ duration, interfering with eating and speaking.
There was a bluish red elevation on under side of tongue the size of a split bean. It was hard, and along both
sides there were enlarged veins. On the side a denuded spot exuded a whitish albuminous matter which could
easily be wiped off.
Semp. 6c was given, one powder every forty-eight hours. On the second day, the swelling was less sensitive,
and in a week, much smaller. Then the menses reappeared (first time since confinement) and in three weeks
the whole swelling was gone, leaving only in its place a somewhat engorged vein.
Kallenbach treated with applications of lx General V. B. who had nodules on the left rim of his tongue with
swollen veins, the nodules disappeared and the sensitiveness was removed and the patient was so well that
he refused to stay for the completion of the cure and failed to report.
Clarke’s experience with Semp. was in domestic practice. For some child affections of the eyes he used rags
moistened with “house leek and cream” (about equal parts of the juice and fresh cream) were applied and his
recollection of it is that the application was exceedingly pleasant.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer.
