name: Senecio Aureus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - senec. Senecio aureus. Golden ragwort. Senecio gracilis. Squaw-weed. N. O. Compositae.
North America, found in swamps. Tincture of fresh plant in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
 CLINICAL -Amenorrhea. Ascites. Cirrhosis. Coryza. Cough. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Dysuria. Fainting. Gleet.
Gonorrhea. Hemorrhages. Homesickness. Hysteria. Kidney, cohc. Kidney, inflammation. Leucorrhea.
Lumbago. Mania. Menorrhagia. Menstruation, disorders. Nails,brittle. Nervousness. Neurasthenia.
Nosebleeds. Prostate, enlarged. Prostatitis. Puerperal, mania. Sciatica. Spermatic cord, pain. Tuberculosis.
Wounds.
HERBAL - The golden ragwort had a reputation in domestic and eclectic practice as a regulator of menstrual
functions when Hale introduced it into homeopathic practice. Its action on the female organism was clinically
verified.
Lyman Watkins said, “Females taking Senec. generally improve in health and
strength, accumulate flesh, become lightheaded and cheerful. This may be due to some tonic influence.”
HOMEOPATHIC - A. E. Small and others proved it and clinical additions have filled out the picture. Like many
other Compositae, the Ragworts or Groundsels, have power over hemorrhagic conditions, whether arising
from disease or from wounds.
Marked action on female and urinary organs, especially bladder. Lack of reaction in genito-urinary tract.
Hemorrhagic tendency from other organs especially with suppressed or delayed menses. Dropsy after
hemorrhage.
Debilitating or vicarious discharges. Backaches of congested kidneys. Early cirrhosis of liver. Tightness in
nose, throat etc. Muscles draw into a knot. Nervous, pale, weak and sleepless hysterical women. Globus. Very
sensitive to open air, tendency to catarrhs.
MIND - Despondent. Nervous and irritable, whining. Self centered. Elated and sad alternately. Inability to fix
mind upon any one subject.
Abdomen - Pain about umbilical region, spreading in all directions better stools, bending double. Ascites from
suppressed menses.
Back - Lumbar backache, as if to break with amenorrhea. Kidney disease.
Breasts - Burning in left nipple. Pains from ovaries to breasts.
Causations - Ill effects of suppressed or delayed menses, wounds, venesection.
Chest - Chest sore and raw.
Constitutions - Suited to women and little girls of nervous temperament.
Ears - Itching in Eustachian tube.
Eyes - Tears are irritating, causing itching.
Face - Sharp, cutting pain in left side. Dryness of fauces, throat and mouth.
Female - Before menses, inflammatory conditions of throat, chest and bladder after menstruation commences,
these improve. Feels like the menses would come. Menses, retarded, suppressed with concomitant
symptoms, dropsy, cough, backache. Amenorrhea of young girls with backache. Premature and too profuse
menses (Calc., Erig.). Menorrhagia, a copious flow which continues until they become anemic. Anemic
dysmenorrhea with urinary disturbances. Dysmenorrhea after abortion. Leucorrhea, thick, yellow, profuse,
flows down thighs. Profuse flow of mucus from vagina from sexual excitation. Sexual irritation causing, itching,
burning and swelling of labia. Pains from ovaries to breasts.
Food - Aversion to all food, especially sweets and coffee which she was very fond.
Head - Wave-like dizziness from occiput to sinciput. Sharp pains over left eye and through the left temple.
Dull, stupefying headache. Headache precedes leucorrhea and irritation in bladder.
Kidneys - Kidney colic (Pareir., Oci., Berb.). Nephritis. Great heat and constant urging, with kidney pain.
Irritable bladder of children with headache. Dysuria in women with dysmenorrhea or uterine displacements
and in children with headache. Scanty, high-colored, bloody with much mucus sediment and tenesmus.
Limbs - Wandering rheumatic pains, periodical. Feet cold in bed. Brittle nails (Sil., Thuj.).
Lungs - Dyspnea on ascending (Calc.) Acute inflammatory conditions of upper respiratory tract. Loose cough
with copious mucus expectoration and labored breathing. Cough tickling with blood- streaked sputum with
suppressed menses. Dry teasing cough, stitching chest pains. Hoarseness.
Male - Lascivious dreams with involuntary emissions. Prostate enlarged, feels hard and swollen to touch.
Dull, heavy pain in spermatic cord, extending to testicles.
Modalities - Colic is better bending forward and better by stool. Better at onset of menses, from menstruation.
Worse puberty, sexual excitement. Worse dampness, cold open air. Worse at night, in afternoon. Worse sitting,
must keep moving about.
Mouth - Twitching about mouth. Teeth very sensitive.
Nose - Burning in nostrils. Fullness of nasal passages, burning, sneezing, profuse flow. Tightness in nasal
passage. Nosebleed or nasal catarrh take the place of menses when suppressed from any cause. Coryza with
nosebleed.
 Rectum - Thin, watery stool intermingled with hard lumps of feces (Ant-c.). Straining at stool, thin, dark,
bloody with tenesmus. Stools, thin, watery, mingled with hard lumps of feces or thin, dark, bloody.
Sensations - As of a wave from occiput to sinciput. As if he would pitch forward. As of a ball rising from
stomach to throat.
Skin - Dry.
Sleep - Nervousness and sleeplessness.
Sleepless women with uterine troubles and amenorrhea. Drowsy during day. Great drowsiness with unpleasant
dreams. Many dreams, erotic.
Stomach - Sensation of a ball rising from stomach to throat. Sourbelchings. Nausea and vomiting of kidney
origin.
Temperature - Hectic fever with anorexia.
Throat - Dry mouth, throat and fauces. Burning in pharynx, raw feeling in nasopharynx, must swallow, though
painful.
Vertigo - Wave-like sensation of dizziness from occiput to sinciput.
COMMENTS - Hale noted that the country people call Senec. “Wild Valerian,” and use it for nervousness,
hysteria and low spirits, sleeplessness, especially in women.
He referred to this “globus” symptom of the pathogenesis: about the middle of the afternoon, sensation as if a
ball was in the stomach. Rising up into the throat, lasting for about an hour. Sensation of tightness in the throat
with a disposition to attempt to relieve it by swallowing.
Respiration as if greatly fatigued. Coughs and tuberculosis. “It is especially serviceable in mucus coughs.” “In
chronic coughs, catarrhal affections, hemoptysis incipient tuberculosis attended with troublesome cough, the
result of obstructed menstruation.”
Pains are radiating, shifting, lancinating. Symptoms alternate. “Dull, heavy pain in left spermatic cord, moving
along cord to testicle. Prostatic gland enlarged, feels hard and swollen to touch. Lascivious dreams with
pollutions.”
Hemorrhagic function of menstruation. Menses, profuse and early, retarded or absent. Ailments from non-
appearing menses. Nosebleed or nasal catarrh when menses are suppressed.
C. M. Foss reported the case of Miss L., 18, who had seen no period for fifteen months. She was chlorotic,
had a dry. hacking cough with frequent pulse, made still more frequent by any excitement, headache, poor
sleep, constipation. The abdomen had been gradually enlarging for six months and tapping had been decided
upon when Senec. lx was given. All symptoms rapidly cleared up and the menses returned within a short time.
Senec. lx also cured a girl, 21, who had suppression of urine in addition to chlorosis, ascites and suppressed
menses.
S. H. Talcott reported an important case bearing on the same point. Mrs. X., 26, a mother of two children.
Before confinement, the patient was haunted with the idea that her child would be stillborn.
Nine days after its birth, strong andhealthy, she was admitted to hospital in a state of violent acute mania,
which continued with high temperature, for three months, with great physical activity.
The mental state was that of a wild, violent and almost uncontrollable person. There was severe pain in the
head, great nervous irritability and sleeplessness and hysterical weakness.
These symptoms, coupled with the fact (now first ascertained) that the lochia had ceased suddenly after
confinement and the menses had not come on, led to the choice of Senec., which was given in drop doses of
the 3x every two hours.
Steady improvement resulted and after a few weeks the patient was allowed out on parole. A relapse followed
and Bell, did no good. Senec. was again given with good effect and complete recovery took place.
Talcott remarked that recovery from
puerperal mania seldom occurs unless menstruation is re-established. Talcott’s case becomes more significant
in the light of Cooper’s observation of the brain action of Senec-j.
Hale reported the following case of dysmenorrhea: Mrs. X., mother of one child, had an miscarriage three
years before and another (at the second month of pregnancy) four months before Hale saw her.
Since the last miscarriage she had suffered from painful menstruation, which had not been the case previously.
Menses every three weeks, profuse, lasting eight or nine days, accompanied by much cutting pain in sacrum,
hypogastrium and groins. Pale, weak, nervous, slight cough, generally at night.
Senec., 5 drops, was given three times a day until the next period, which came on at the twenty-ninth day and
was perfectly normal in quantity and without pain.
Hale said he also found Senec. useful in advanced stages of gonorrhea and in prostatic disorders.
Small, who proved Senec., recorded the case of a woman, 30, who had been ill six weeks, the symptoms
steadily increasing until the following picture was presented: face bloated, abdomen enlarged, feet edematous,
 urine alternately profuse and watery or dark and scanty, frequent desire to urinate day and night. Senec., 10
drops, three times a day, cured quickly.
Small remarked that he has found Senec. useful in the dysuria of women and children when evidently of
catarrhal origin and in dysuria with uterine displacement. Mucus sediment in the urine is an indication. But the
benefits of Senec. are not confined to the female sex.
Small related the case of a man, 50, nervo- sanguine, subject of kidney inflammation affecting right kidney
generally, causing intense pain, fever, prostration. On one occasion the pain was particularly intense and the
bladder seemed implicated.
Every time he passed water he cried out in agony. Urine reddish, very hot and acrid. Bowels constipated. Dull
headache, mouth and throat dry, chilly, fever and perspiration.
Senec., 20 drops in half a tumbler of water, a dessert spoonful every hour. There was relief from the first dose
and the pain soon subsided entirely, leaving the patient freed from recurrence of the attacks.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Senec-j. - cerebrospinal irritation, rigid muscles, chiefly of neck and shoulders,
also in cancer. (2) Alet., Caul., Sep. (3) Arn., Calen., Bell-p. (4) Uterine, chest and bladder symptoms, Puls.,
Helon. (5) Vicarious menstruation, Bry. Senec. has bloody expectoration. (6) Homesickness, Caps., Ph- ac.
(7) Worse 4 p.m., Lyc. (8) Prostatitis and gonorrhea, Sabal., Solid., Puls., Pip-n., Cop., Thuj. (9) Nervousness,
Coff., Cham., Valer., Ambr. (10) Fidgety feet, Caust., Zinc.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Senecio Jacoboea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - senec-j. Senecio jacoboea. St. James’ wort. Staggerwort. Ragwort. N. O. Compositae. Tincture
of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Brain, disorders. Cerebrospinal, irritation. Depression. Bedwetting. Headaches.
Twitchings. Ulcers. '
HERBAL - This is the common ragwort, which, with its yellow flowers, is such a conspicuous feature of English
roadsides and commons throughout the summer months. Gerarde mentioned “green wounds and old filthy
ulcers” as benefited by it, also “old aches and pains in the arms, hips and legs.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Cooperpublished several observations with Senec-j.
MIND - Depressed in body and mind, it seemed as if brain would not work. Talks incoherently.
Back - Constant rigidity of muscles, chiefly of neck and shoulders, especially at night, seems like a habit, but
finds it most difficult to relax them, it seems to return involuntarily, so that the weight of the head is somehow
held in this way and though touching the pillow does not rest on it.
Head - Exhaustion felt in back of head, after
Senecio jacoboea this felt lighter and better.
Kidneys - The bladder, which had been rather weak, became more so, the bedwetting continuing day and
night for several days.
Limbs - Sometimes in the day the upper part of the legs gets a sort of ague fit of shaking.
Rectum - Bowels (before fairly regular) began acting in gushes, large stools occasionally, but in no way
regular.
COMMENTS - Cooper gave a woman, 57 who had slight otorrhea of left ear with deafness on that side, a
single dose of Senec-j. Immediately after, she began to feel depressed in mind and body, it seemed as if her
brain would not work, for she talked incoherently. The bowels began acting in gushes and a bladder weakness
was aggravated, so that there was bedwetting night and day for three days.
Another woman from a single dose of the same had “exhaustion in the back of the head.”
Yet another woman, 51, had depression all her life, coming in fits. “Memory and everything goes,” could not
talk coherently to herself and dislikes conversation in others.
On July 1, 1900, she wrote, “Have suffered agony from awful feeling of torpor of brain, which has made it an
effort to put words together, memory seemed to go, felt altogether insensible, bowels have been confined.”
One dose of Senec-j. was given and removed the depression and relieved all the other symptoms. It also
produced constant rigidity of muscles, chiefly of neck and shoulders, worse at night, it seems like a habit.
“And I try to relax them but find it most difficult, it to run back involuntarily, so that the weight of the head is
somehow held in this way and though touching the pillow does not rest on it. Sometimes in the day the upper
part of the legs gets a sort of ague fit of shaking.”
On this Cooper remarked, “The exhaustion felt after a dose of Senec-j. in the back of the head in case 2 and
the cropping up as a new
symptom of this strange-looking rigidity of the muscles of the neck, at night chiefly together with the shaking
 of the legs in the daytime, points to incoordinated muscular action due to deranged cerebral control.”
Cooper added the case of a man, 68, many years apoplectically inclined, who had constant twitchings at night
with cascular deafness of right ear, loss of memory, pressure and heat of head. After a dose of Senec-j., he
remained comfortable for three months and hearing improved.
Senec-j. has been used like Senec. in cases of menstrual irregularity.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Cooper.

name: Senega Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - seneg. Senega officinalis. Snake-wort. Snake-root. Polygala senega. N. O. Polygalaceae.
Tincture of powdered dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Amblyopia. Ascites. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bladder, irritable. Blepharitis. Bronchitis.
Chest disorders. Constipation. Cornea, opacity. Coughs. Esophagus, stricture. Facial paralysis. Hay fever.
Headaches. Hydrothorax. Hypopion. Influenza. Iritis. Lungs disorders. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Snakebites.
Sneezing. Sprains. Styes. Throat, sore. Tuberculosis. Whooping cough.
HERBAL - Senega is one of the sources of Saponin. It has a nauseous taste and leaves a scraping sensation
in the throat. It is in disorders of the chest, eyes and bladder that homeopaths have found it of most service
and the extensive provings have supplied excellent data for prescribing.
Teste reported that Seneg. was introduced to medical practice by Dr. Tennant of Virginia, who was led to test
its properties through hearing that the Native Americans used it as an antidote to snakebites as it relieved the
symptoms of snakes’ venom.
Tennant concluded that it might also relieve dyspnea, cough and hemoptysis arising from other causes and
gave it with success in cases of pneumonia, pleurisy and hydrothorax.
Other old-school practitioners used it as an expectorant in chronic respiratory catarrh, acute tuberculosis,
rheumatic fever, dropsies incipient cataract, croup. It is regarded as “a stimulant, diaphoretic and expectorant
in chronic bronchitis.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Seneg. affects the mucus membranes causing catarrhal symptoms especially of the
respiratory tract and bladder. Eyes, serous membranes of chest, muscles and left side are also affected.
Distinct eye symptoms of a paralytic type.
Great soreness of walls of chest. Pressure on chest as though lungs were forced back to spine. Pleurodynia.
Lying on right side causes pain in chest. Motion causes pain under sternum. Motion of arms causes soreness
of walls of chest. Circumscribed spots in chest left after inflammations.
Hoarseness. The throat is so dry and sensitive it hurts the patient to talk. Cough often ends in sneezing. Lying
down causes tickling in larynx. Great accumulation of clear albuminous mucus, which is difficult to expel.
Whooping cough in fat, chubby children, clear mucus like white of egg, difficult to raise, cough worse towards
evening.
MIND - Anxiety with hasty respiration. Fear of suffocation. Inclined to quarrel. Readily takes offense. Suddenly
remembers unimportant regions which he saw long ago.
Abdomen - Boring and digging pains in abdomen. Flatulent disorders with a sensation of a general bearing
down towards hypogastrium.
Back - Bursting, distending pain in kidney region.
Causations - Ill effects of poisonous bites, sprains.
Chest - Chest feels oppressed on ascending. Pressure on chest as though lungs were forced back to spine.
Pain in spots, as if bruised shifting pains on stooping. As of a crushing weight or weakness starts in chest.
Sore from coughing, pressure, sneezing or moving arms. Burning in chest before or after coughing. Dry
scraping in chest worse talking. Thorax feels too narrow. Exudation in pleura. Hydrothorax. Circumscribed
spots in chest left after inflammations.
Constitutions - Suited to plethoric, phlegmatic persons, persons tending to obesity, fat persons of lax tissue,
fat, chubby children and old persons. Suited to females of slender and tall, but having retained a good deal of
sprightliness and moral power.
Ears - Aching in the ear when chewing.
Eyes - Oculomotor paralysis. Muscular asthenopia (Caust.). Opacities of the vitreous humor. Promotes the
absorption of fragments. Staring. Lachrymation. Dryness with sensation as if too large for orbits. Eyeballs
feel distended or like balls of ice. Sensation of trembling without visible trembling. Flickering, must wipe eyes
frequently. Objects look shaded. Double vision, better only by bending head backward. Ptosis. Blepharitis, lids
dry and crusty (Graph.).
Head - Dullness with pressure and weakness of eyes. Pain in temples. Bursting pain in forehead into eyes,
 better cool open air.
Kidneys - Bursting, distending pain in kidney region. Scalding before and after urinating. Increased or
decreased in amount. Greatly diminished urine, loaded with shreds and mucus. Urine, foamy, acrid with mucus
shreds.
Lungs - Bronchial catarrh with sore chest walls, much mucus, sensation of oppression and weight of chest.
Bursting pain in back on coughing. Hacking cough. Cough often ends in a sneeze. Rattling in chest (Ant-
t.). Albuminous or blood-streaked sputum. Exudations in pleura. Pleuropneumonia. Hydrothorax (Merc-s.)
Difficult raising of tough, profuse mucus in the aged. Asthenic bronchitis of old people with chronic
interstitial nephritis or chronic emphysema. Old asthmatics with congestive attacks.
Modalities - Better walking in open air, sweat, bending head backwards, walking in open air. Rest helps dry
cough. Worse from inhaling air, open air, cold, wind, walking in open air. Worse in warm air, warm room. Worse
going up stairs, stooping, bending forward. Worse by touch and pressure, rubbing. Worse rest, morning and
night. Worse looking intently
at an object.
Mouth - Dry scraping in mouth, worse talking. Taste, metallic like urine.
Nose - Dry. Coryza, much watery mucus and sneezing. Sneezes, so often and so violently that the head grows
dizzy and heavy. Nostrils feel peppery.
Sensations - Eyes, as if they were pressed out, as if eyeballs were being expanded, as if soap in eyes. As if
red pepper throughout nostrils and air passages. Dyspnea as from stagnation in lungs. As if lungs pushed
back to spine. As if chest would burst. As if chest too narrow. Wrist as if sprained. Joints as if lame.
Stomach - Loathing and nausea with inclination to vomit.
Throat - Catarrhal inflammation of throat and fauces with scraping hoarseness. Catarrh of larynx. Hawks viscid
mucus in detached small clots. Burning and rawness. Sensation as if membrane had been abraded. Dry
scraping, worse talking. Loss of voice. Voice unsteady, vocal cords partially paralyzed. Hurts to talk.
COMMENTS - The prover took from 40 to 6 drops of the tincture. Extreme tenderness. Worse bending head
forward and worse from stooping. Generally left-sided.
Disordered digestive organs. Gnawing hunger and empty feeling. Irritability and catarrh of the urinary organs.
Frequent urging, scalding in urethra before or after urination. Urine is loaded with mucus threads. Seneg. has
been used as an emetic.
Pressure, dullness, heaviness in the head. Painful sensitiveness of hearing. Eye symptoms as an
accompaniment of head symptoms. “Violent rush of blood to head when stooping, especially to eyeballs, where
a painful pressure is experienced.”
Pains, inflammation both of the exterior and interior of the eye and lids, and much disorder of vision. The eye
troubles are worse when looking intently at an object and better bending head backwards.
The symptom in which it was first noticed was “When walking towards the setting sun he seemed to see
another smaller sun hover below the other, assuming a somewhat oval shape when looking down,
disappearing on
bending head backwards and on closing the eyes.”
Guernsey outlined its action, “Where there is a great burning in the chest, either before or after coughing,
profuse secretion of mucus. Dryness of inner parts which are usually moist, dry skin. General disorders of the
windpipe, left side of chest particularly, right eye, lower eyelids.”
Nash, who had only obtained success with low potencies of Seneg., cured many cases of “cough with great
accumulation of mucus, which seems to fill the chest with much rattling, wheezing and difficult breathing.”
A very stout elderly woman of tubercular family history had pneumonia of both bases, especially right. She had
a very violent paroxysmal cough with ropy, difficult expectoration tinged with blood. Seneg. 30c quickly relieved
a very dangerous condition when other remedies had failed.
Clinton Enos related a case of a very fat girl, age 10, with cold, damp feet and hands and sweating about the
head, had spells of sneezing for two years, even since whooping cough.
Several sneezing spells a day lasting about half an hour. Sharp pains in chest and temples during the attacks.
In nose a large quantity of mucus with stuffed-up feeling. One dose of Seneg. 200c removed the whole trouble
in a week.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Bry., Am., Bell., Camph. Compare: (1) Sapin. - a derivative of Senega root. (2) In
bronchial affections, Am-c. (3) Fat, plethoric people disposed to catarrhs, Calc. (4) Muscular asthenopia, loss
of voice, paralysis (facial, etc.), Caust. (5) Laryngeal and pulmonary catarrh, Phos. (6) Bronchial catarrh,
Spong. (7) Whooping cough, Coc-c., Kali-bi. (Seneg. clear phlegm, cough worse towards evening, Coc-c. clear
phlegm worse morning, Kali-bi. yellow phlegm in morning). Follows well: Calc., Phos., Lyc., Sulph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
 ***SENNA
(Cassia Acutifolia)
PHARMACY - senn. Senna. Cassia acutifolia. Alexandrian senna. Cassia angustifolia. Cassia obovata. N. O.
Leguminosae. Caes- alpinioideae. The leaflets of several species of Cassia. Trituration or tincture of the dried
leaves. Historical dose: Tincmre and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acetonemia. Colic. Constipation. Exhaustion. Fainting. Flatulence. Liver, disorders.
Nitrogenous, waste. Oxaluria. Sleeplessness. Sneezing with heat.
HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms are mostly derived from overdosings. Senn, is used as a laxative in ordinary
practice.
Senn, has proved an excellent remedy in the colicofinfantswith incarcerated flatulence and sleeplessness.
Infantile colic, when the child seems to be full of wind. Constipation with colic and flatulence. Oxaluria with
excess of urea increased specific gravity. Liver enlarged and tender.
Exhaustion. General swelling. Ebullitions of blood at night. “Repeated sneezing, which caused heat (especially
of hands), exhaustion and panting breathing.” Acetonemia, prostration, fainting. Unclean body swell.
Abdomen - Sensation of coldness in the abdomen with emptiness and uneasiness in the stomach.
Accumulation of flatus with grumbling and fermentation in the abdomen and discharge of fetid flatus. Painful
colic from incarcerated flatulence. Colic, especially in children, infants.
Face - Livid lips. Commissure of lips covered with small burning blisters.
Food - Anorexia. Thirst.
Head - Heaviness of the head when stooping, as if it were pressed down.
Kidneys - Specific gravity and density increased. Hyperazoturia, oxaluria, phos- phaturia and acetonuria.
Limbs - Heat in limbs, especially of hands.
Liver - Liver enlarged and tender.
Nose - Repeated sneezing, which caused heat, especially of hands, exhaustion and panting breathing.
Rectum - Burning in rectum with strangury of bladder. Constipation with colic and flatulence. Stools hard and
dark with loss of appetite, coated tongue, bad taste and weakness. Diarrhea with straining and prolapsed
rectum and sore anus in children. Liquid stools with griping pains. Loose evacuation with tenesmus and
followed by a burning sensation in the anus .Yellowish fluid,with pinching pains before. Greenish mucus, never-
get-done sensation (Merc.).
Sleep - Ebullition of blood, especially at night, disturbing the sleep. Sleeplessness with cries and tossing,
especially in the case of infants.
Stomach - Empty or watery and fetid, risings. Loathing and nausea with inclination to vomit. Sinking
immediately after meals.
COMMENTS - Farrington said it is one of the best remedies in the Materia Medica for “simple exhaustion with
excess of nitrogenous waste.” The exhaustion is exemplified in the sinking immediately after meals.
The pods caused an unclean smell from the body of a woman taking them for constipation. Acts as a tonic
where the system is broken down, bowels constipated, muscular weakness and waste of nitrogenous
materials.
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Nux-v., Cham. Compare: (1) Cassi-s., Kali-c., Jal.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Sepia Succus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sep. Sepia succus. Cuttlefish ink. Sepia officinalis. N. O. Cephalopoda. Trituration of dried liquid
contained in the ink-bag. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abortion. Addison’s disease. Alcohol, effects. Amenorrhea. Anal, problems. Appetite, depraved.
Ascarides. Baldness. Bedwetting. Bladder, weak. Birth control pills. Cancer. Childbirth. Chloasma. Chorea.
Condylomata. Constipation. Cortisone, effects. Cushing’s disease. Cystitis. Depression. Dysmenorrhea.
Dyspepsia. Eczema. Estrogen, effects. Eyes, disorders.
Face, yellow. Freckles. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Gravel. Hair, loss. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Hormonal, disorders.
Hormonal, drugs. Hot, flushes. Hysterectomy. Hysteria. Infertility. Jaundice. Labor, pains. Leucorrhea.
Libido, low. Liver, spots. Liver, torpid. Menopause. Menstruation, disorders. Mental, disorders.
Miscarriages. Morning sickness. Neuralgias. Nose, inflamed. Nosebleed. Ovarian, disorders. Ozaena.
Phimosis. Pityriasis, versicolor. Pleurisy. Pregnancy, disorders. Premenstrual, syndrome. Pruritus.
Psoriasis. Ptosis. Puberty, disorders. Pylorus, induration. Quinsy. Rectal, disorders. Ringworm. Sacrum,
pain. Sciatica. Seborrhea. Sexual, disorders. Smell, disorders. Spermatorrhea. Strokes. Styes. Toothache.
 Urinary, incontinence. Uterus, disorders. Uterus, prolapsed. Vaginitis. Varicose, veins. Venous stasis.
Warts. Whooping cough.
HOMEOPATHIC - The inky juice of cuttlefish, known as Indian ink, is one of the remedies of the Chronic
Diseases, and was proved by Goullon, Von Gersdorff, Gross, Hartlaub and Wahle.
It is preeminently a woman’s remedy, although the first symptoms were found by Hahnemann accidentally
proved by a male artist. It affects the generative organs of both sexes and a large number of the symptoms
occurring in other organs have some relation thereto.
Sep. affects the venous circulation, especially of the female pelvic organs and of the digestive tract. It acts
especially on the portal system with venous congestion. Venous stasis, ptosis of viscera. Violent ebullitions
of blood with pulsation throughout the body. Pulsating headache in cerebellum. Bleedings.
Hormonal disorders. Affections in pregnant women. Tendency to miscarriages. Bearing down in pelvic
region. Uterus prolapsed. Hot flashes at menopause with weakness and perspiration. Excess of sexual
indulgence. Loss of vital fluids. Milky secretions.
Upward tendency of its symptoms. Symptoms settle in back, in ileo-cecal region, ovaries. Pains extend down
to back, chills easily. Shuddering from pain. Burning pains in different parts of the body. Rheumatism, chronic
cases. Fits of uneasiness and hysterical spasms. Spasms, clonic, tonic, cataleptic. Jerking in muscles. Fidgety.
Sudden prostration. Easy fainting. Feels cold, even in warm room. Short walk fatigues much. Weariness and
misery. Weakness, yellow complexion. Weak, empty, hollow feeling in epigastrium, chest, muscles, lumbar
back, hips, knees etc. or sensation of fullness. As of a lump or something rolling over internally. “Ball’’
sensation in inner parts.
Females dragged down by overwork. Tubercular patient with chronic hepatic troubles and uterine reflexes.
Children who take cold easily when the weather changes. Relaxed, plethoric females. Weak, potbellied
mothers with yellow complexion. Diseased conditions which drag on, linger. Atrophy of children, their face like
an old man. Warty growths. Big belly, dry flabby skin.
MIND - Mentally and physically worn-out patients. Industrious. Indisposed to mental labor. Repugnance to
customary business, disgust of life. Makes mistakes while writing or reading. Poor memory. Confused, wants
to run away. Confusion of mind when spoken to. Irresolution.
Anxious fear, over trifles. Anxiety during heat flushes. Constantly worries, frets and cries about her real or
imaginary illness. Despair about recovery. Cries when telling her symptoms. Fear of poverty. Fear of thun-
derstorms. Nervous, so that she wants to hold on to something or she should scream.
Sense of helplessness. Feels unfortunate without cause. Weeping, worse from consolation. Breaks down
in spells of weeping. Miserly. Dwells on past disagreeable occurrences.
Self-pity. Complaints and grievances. Sad and gloomy moods. Sad over her health and domestic affairs.
Tendency to burst into tears. They have too much work to do. People are not kind to them. No one realizes
how much suffering they have or with what difficulties they have to contend.
Depression, suicidal. Depression on awaking in morning. Depression related to pregnancy, menses or
menopause. Unhappy married life. Great sadness during pregnancy or lactation. Post-partum depression.
Emotional stillness.
Sexually shut down, no libido. Low sex drive since childbirth, hysterectomy, menopause. Aversion to the
opposite sex. Women who dislike men and men who dislike women. Loss of sex drive and sexual disorders.
Nausea, disgust at the thought of sex. Anxiety after sex. Dullness of mind after sex.
Aversion to those loved best, to family. Aversion to sympathy and company, yet dreads to be alone.
Averse to occupation, house work. Indolent. Desires solitude, lies with closed eyes. Sits quietly and answers
either with yes or no.
Irritable and easily offended. Irritability, alternating with indifference or sulks. Bad- tempered. Resents
criticism of any kind. Spiteful. Lack of sympathy. Angry, sensitive, easily offended and miserable. Anger about
past events. Anger from contradic-. tion. Anger related to pregnancy, menses or menopause. Anger in
morning.
Censorious. Takes pleasure in teasing others. Never seems happy unless annoying someone. Says and does
strange things. Mania before menses. Sensitive to least noise.odors. Excited during thunderstorms.
Cheerful when it thunders and with lightning. Loves to dance.
Abdomen - Brown spots on abdomen. Coldness in abdomen. Lax feeling in abdomen. Falling out or heavy,
bearing down feeling in hypogastrium, better by holding it or crossing legs. Burning and shooting pains. Violent
pain in umbilical region. Bloated abdomen after eating. Loud rumbling in abdomen after eating. Flatulence
with headache. Colic and faintness before menses. Soreness and pain as if menses would appear. Pot-belly
of mothers.
Back - Backache, causes nausea and faint feeling while standing. Sudden pain in back, as if struck by a
 hammer, worse stooping, kneeling. Back pain, better belching, by pressing back against
something hard. Heaviness in back in morning on waking. Burning pressure in spine. Spine tender to touch or

COMMENTS - Historically, physicians used the flesh, the eggs or even the only bone that constitutes the
skeleton of this animal, for “leucorrhea, gonorrhea, catarrh of the bladder, gravel, spasms of the bladder,
baldness, freckles and certain kinds of tetters which is sufficiently remarkable in the light of the provings.”
Sep. acts on the vital forces as well as on organic tissues. The sphincters and all non-striated muscles are
weakened. Sep. disturbs the circulation, causing flushes and other irregularities, throbbings all over, hot hands
and cold feet or vice versa. The flushes run upward and end in sweat with a faint, weak feeling. Nosebleed
may occur from a blow, from being in a warm room, or from suppressed menses. Low thyroid with hormonal
components.
Grimmer stated “This remedy has cured cancer of rectum and uterus, it acts strongly on the sexual organs of
both sexes and a great many symptoms and conditions are manifested in this sphere. Young people of both
sexes frequently have ailments calling for this medicine, women during the pregnant state after childbirth, men
who have been addicted to drinking and sexual excesses are often helped by this remedy. Sex aggravates it
in both sexes.”

or apathetic.

Kunkel reported a case of pulmonary affection in a boy, 14, who had been under treatment five weeks for
cough and hoarseness. Hoarseness was worse evening, cough with purulent sputa during the day. Slept well
but dreamed when he lay on left side. Emaciated. Phos. lOx produced little change.
There was remarkable tightness of the chest on breathing with inclination to take a deep breath, this was better
in open air, on motion, while at work, worse while in the house and at rest. Though the weather was bad he
had a constant desire to be out of doors. Sep. lOx made a rapid cure.
Boenninghausen recommended Sep. in cases of cough, either with or without expectoration with blood-
 streaked, purulent, yellow greenish or stinking sputa, and especially in tuberculosis.
Nash mentioned a case of cholera infantum that he cured with Sep. on the indication “always worse after taking
milk.” He compared it with Ant-c. for moisture oozing from the anus, which has the first place.
Bahr said Sep. afforded considerable help in a certain condition of the system that had only been noticed in
females. After the exacerbation of a chronic gastric catarrh has lasted a few days with intolerable burning
pains, the kidney region becomes painful, more particularly the left side.
Violent burning pain in the kidney region and a quantity of saturated, highly-colored urine is discharged. Urine
deposits copious quantities of urates, or else a clear urine with copious sandy sediment, coated with uric acid.
After the discharge, the pains generally abate and only return if the stomach has not been restored to its normal
condition.
Hering noted its usefulness for “condylomata completely surrounding head of penis.”
Clarke cured a crop of small, velvety warts completely encircling the mouth of the prepuce. Thuja had failed.
Clarke also cured with Sep. 3x a large horn-like wart on the abdomen of a woman. It was as large as a crown-
piece but shaped like a bean and raised a quarter of an inch from the surface.
Clarke confirmed the experience of Dr. Swallow, who found the fresh preparation of Sep. to possess a wider
range than the ordinary preparation and to act as an “organ remedy” in a great variety of uterine disorders not
definitely indicated by the pathogenesis. Clarke used it in potencies from the 5c to 30c.

Condylomata. Constipation. Cortisone, effects. Cushing’s disease. Cystitis. Depression. Dysmenorrhea.
Dyspepsia. Ecze

name: Sequoia Sempervirens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-seq-s. Sequoia sempervirens. Redwood. N. O. Taxodiaceae. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Constipation. Edema. Flatulence. Headache. Lungs, collapsed. Nausea. Pneumonia.
Polyuria. Rheumatism. Salivation. Sneezing.
HOMEOPATHIC - Birch and Rockwell, wrote, in A Homoeopathic Proving of Sequoia sempervirens, 1994,
“The tree grows in the fog where it is damp and wet, it also grows near the ocean.
“The source of the remedy is the burl, a growth on the tree from which new life sprouts. If one were to study
the logging industry, one would find that in man’s greed and desire for more, bigger and better, he shows no
restraint from destroying the last few virginal growths of these incredible giants.
“It seems to affect some people in one way, while in others the effects are opposite. In the lungs there is ease
of breath or there is difficulty of breath. In the heart we find pressure, shooting pains and symptoms from grief,
or absence of symptoms and complete happiness. Blurry vision or clarity of vision.”
Seq-s. is a sycotic remedy. Hydrogenoid propensity, overproduction of mucus, voracious appetite, rheumatic
complaints. Wandering pains. Pains gripping, constrictive, aching. Stiff and tight feeling in body (Guai.).
Feeling of well-being. Great exhaustion. Voracious appetite. Strong desire for whatever is available. Increased
salivation. Fluid retention Absence of fluid being collected. Vision extremely clear. Blurred vision, worse wind.
Worse lying, sitting, continued motion.
MIND - Clarity of thought, as if a fog or haze had lifted in the mind. Feeling of well-being. Feels new and
rejuvenated. Relaxed, in tense situations. Difficult concentration. Confusion. Confused by simple tasks.
Overwhelming feeling of being old
(Gink.). Feels cut down. Desires solitude. Aversion to company, desire to go somewhere where no one will
bother. Sadness, hard to raise oneself to get up and go in the day. Sympathetic, takes on other peoples
sufferings, only feels good while rescuing someone.
Irritability, about trifles, about noises. Desire to scream that gets suppressed. Delusion of being fragile, as if
she would emotionally fall apart. Delusion of being unappreciated. Delusion as if she is falling in love, of having
a broken heart, as if his wife of many years never loves him. Time appeared to be slowed down.
Abdomen - Burning pain in abdomen. Gripping pain in abdomen, worse after eating, motion, better after sleep.
 Back - Pain extending down to hips and knees.
Bladder - Pressing pain in bladder. Polyuria. Desire to urinate even after having just done so.
Chest - Limp feeling in chest. Short sharp pain in right side of chest. Shooting pain in heart from being heart
broken. Band of tightness in diaphragm, desire to stretch, which causes soreness.
Ears - Outward pressing pain.
Face - Looks much older. Sensation of fullness, as if more fluid were under the skin. Obstruction of facial
sinuses. Pressing pain in maxillary area.
Female - Menses starts and stops; copious.
Head - Headache between the eyes.
Heart - Feeling as if he would die from a broken heart. Sensation of a wall of bricks and stones fall away from
the heart and a yellow and white light encompass the heart.
Limbs - Sharp pain in elbows, shoulders and feet. Sensation of tightness in hands and feet.
Lungs - History of collapsed lungs, pneumonia. Feeling as though one couldn’t get enough airinto lungs,
breathing deeper and deeper yet still wanted more. Asthmatic respiration, worse night, better steam and fresh
air. Sore pain in lungs. Coughing up thick mucus. Feeling as if lungs are
hyper-clear, as if more air can move in and out of the lungs.
Male - Sexual desire diminished.
Mouth - Salivation increased. Bitter taste. Sensation of stiffness in jaws. Hard to articulate words that require
more motion of the jaw.
Nose - Burning pain in nasal passages. Sneezing.
Rectum - Constipation during menses. Flatulence, frequent, like rotten eggs. Loose and putrid stool.
Skin - Eruptions, raised circular or oval bumps of a light brown discoloration. Itching, worse night.
Sleep - Sleepiness in the afternoon. Deep sleep, refreshing. Dreams, of being happy and finding someone
who really loves them. Dreams of responsibility, of rescuing some children by the side of the road. Wakes
unrefreshed; wakes in a sweat.
Stomach - Nausea. Thirst diminished.
Teeth - Desire to clench teeth, to scratch teeth.
Throat - Nausea felt in pit of throat.
Vision - Objects have a haze to them. Edges of objects seem to swim. Vision, as if on a hallucinogenic drug.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lyc.
REFERENCES - Birch. Rockwell.

name: Serotonin
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - serot. Serotonin. A brain neurotransmitter. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Alzheimer’s disease. Anxiety. Autism. Bipolar disorder. Bulimia. Clumsiness.
Compulsive disorders. Depression. Drowsiness. Edema. Insomnia. Learning, disorders. Migraine.
Nightmares. Palpitations. Restlessness. Schizophrenia. Suicidal. Twitching. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Serotonin is aneurotrans- mitter produced in the brain known to influence the functioning of
the cardiovascular, renal, immune, and gastrointestinal systems. In the nervous system, serotonin is believed
to play an important role in the regulation of mood, sleep, vomiting, sexuality and appetite. Serotonin has been
thought to play a part in many disorders, notably as part of the biochemistry of depression, migraine, bipolar
disorder and anxiety. Recent research suggests that serotonin also plays an important role in liver
regeneration.
It is well known that abnormal serotonin levels can cause various types of sexual dysfunction such as
anorgasmia, erectile dysfunction, and diminished libido. Serotonin also causes problems such as insomnia,
depression, obesity, eating disorders, premenstrual syndrome, panic attacks, alcoholism, anxiety disorders,
and bulimia.
Serotonin, at increasing levels, stimulates nervous tension, drowsiness, heart palpitations, water retention and
inability to concentrate and perform.
Any disruption in the synthesis, metabolism or uptake of this neurotransmitter has been found to be responsible
for certain manifestations of schizophrenia, depression, compulsive disorders and learning problems.
Increase in brain levels of either of neurotransmitter, serotonin, produces a craving for alcohol, anger, or
anxiety, especially for those who have a history of alcoholism.
Drowsiness. Tiredness. Sustained rapid eye movement. Overreaction of the reflexes. Rapid muscle
contraction and relaxation in the ankle causing abnormal movements of the foot. Clumsiness. Muscle
contraction and relaxation in the jaw. Twitching of the muscles. Rigidity. High body temperature. Sweating.
MIND - Euphoric feelings. Feelings of intoxication. Substance abuse. Impulsive behavior, recklessness,
 exhibitionism. Restlessness. Hostility, argumentative behavior. Violence, violent nightmares. Insomnia.
Depression, anxiety, suicidal tendency. Psychosis. Schizophrenia, mood disorders. Organic brain disease,
mental retardation, autism and Alzheimer’s.
RELATIONS - Compare: Melat.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Serum Anguillae
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - ser-ang. Serum anguillae. Eel serum. Freshwater Eel Serum. Anguilla anguillae.
Ichthyotoxinum. Potencies are made with glycerine or distilled water. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Albuminuria. Anuria. Dyspnea. Edema. Elephantiasis. Heart, disorders. Hemoglobinuria.
Hematuria. Hypertension. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, failure. Lympha- edema. Mitral, insufficiency.
Nephritis. Oliguria. Uremia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Jousset considered Ser- ang. a specific in disorders of the heart and kidneys without much
edema. Ser-ang. affects the kidneys, which becomes acutely affected, either from cold, infection or
intoxication. The attack is characterized by oliguria, anuria and albuminuria.
Jousset’s experiments have demonstrated the rapid hematuria, albuminuria and oliguria caused by it. But its
really specific indication seems to be for sub-acute and acute nephritis. Repressed kidney function and
sexuality. Acute nephritis with threatening uremia. Diuresis. Albuminuria. Kidney failure.
Cardiac uremia. Hypertension and oliguria without edema. Heart diseases in cases of failure of
compensation and impending asystole. Functional heart diseases. Mitral insufficiency. Asystole with or without
edema, dyspnea and difficult urinary secretion.
Warm-blooded. Chilliness when tired. Desire for warm room. Lymphoedema after operation on breast tumor.
Elephantiasis. Faintness and nausea.
MIND - Indifference and lack of will power. Irresolution. Every effort is too much. Aversion to change. Irritability
and dissatisfaction with oneself. Nervousness. Restlessness. Sensitive to noises and odors. Anger from noise.
Mental dullness. Difficult concentration. Memory weakness. Brain fatigue. Mental and physical symptoms
better from appearance of menses.
Abdomen - Pain in abdomen when retaining urine.
Eyes - Sudden sparks before the eyes.
Food - Appetite increased or decreased. Ravenous appetite in evening. Appetite decreased, thirst increased
or vice versa. Desire for salty and pungent foods. Desire for coffee.
Head - Congestive headaches, often onesided. Pressing sensation in head. Sensation as if head enlarged.
Sudden heat in face and head.
Heart - Consciousness of heart. Oppression. Constriction. Stitches in heart. Palpitations. Cardiac uremia.
Heart diseases with failure of compensation and impending asystole. Mitral insufficiency. Hypertension and
oliguria without edema.
Kidneys - Kidney failure. Repressed kidney function. Acute nephritis. Uremia. Hematuria, albuminuria and
oliguria.
Limbs - Wandering joints pains. Pains wander from fingers to elbows and shoulders. Pains wander from toes
to knees and hips. Restless legs, impossible to remain seated, must move.
Modalities - Aversion to warm room. Worse deep inspiration, swallowing, bending head backward. Worse
from noises and odors.
Perspiration - Sweat smells sweetish.
Sleep - Dreams of traveling, of black snakes. Erotic dreams of naked women.
Stomach - Eructations better after eating. Nausea concomitant with heart or kidney diseases.
Throat - Dry feeling in pharynx.
Vertigo - Dizziness on rising. Faintness and nausea.
COMMENTS - The serum of the eel has a toxic action on the blood, rapidly destroying its globules. The
presence of albumin and kidney elements in the urine, the hemoglobinuria. the prolonged anuria (24 and 26
hours), together with the results of the autopsy, plainly demonstrate its elective action on the kidneys.
Secondarily, the liver and the heart are affected and the alteration observed are those usually present in
infectious diseases.
Boericke wrote, “When during the course of heart disease, the kidney, previously working well, should suddenly
become af
fected and its function inhibited and when besides we observe cardia irregularities and a marked state of
asystole, we may yet expect good results from this serum. But to determine here the choice of this remedy is
 not an easy matter.”
RELATIONS - Vip. Compare: ( 1 ) Dig., Lach., Apis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Rohrer.

name: Silica Marina
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sil-mar. Silica marina. Sea sand. Silica maritima. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Constipation. Glands, enlargement. Glands, suppuration. Gonorrhea. Tartar.
HOMEOPATHIC - W. B. Clarke of India napolis told of the use of Sil-mar. as a remedy for constipation. He
used it in patients of all ages with excellent results, giving it in crude doses.
W. B. Clarke’ s preparation was taken from the beach, just as it was left by the tide, on a pan of the coast many
miles distant from a river estuary or a drained town. He preferred the rather coarse sand taken from a river
sand-bar. He thought a finer variety may be better for younger patients.
This was thoroughly washed and baked in an oven. The sand is taken plain or enclosed in capsules or made
into pills. In either case it is washed down with water and water is to be drunk freely during the treatment.
Sil-mar. has Sil. and Nat-m. symptoms. Inflamed glands and suppuration. Constipation.
W. B. Clarke mentioned this case as the hardest he had encountered: a man, 60, had suffered for thirty years
with severe constipation often sitting at stool for an hour and nearly fainting. He took a teaspoonful after dinner
daily for a week without particular effect.
Then he took it three times a day for a week. After this he was able to return to the one dose a day and soon
required it but once a week. “The peculiarity of this treatment is the ease with which evacuation is accomplished
after the first impression is made, the discharges being soft, mushy and yellow and the regular habit then
seems established, for the treatment can then be discontinued.”
If there is any return of the trouble, a dose or two more will be sufficient to put it right. This experience is of
great value and interest as Sil. in the potencies (as well as Nat-m.) is a great constipation remedy. W. B. Clarke
never observed any ill effects of the treatment.
In the case of a child, age 4 to whom Cooper gave Sil-mar. 6x “a thick mass of tartar which had accumulated
behind the front teeth came away in flakes.
COMMENTS - Clarke had a specimen triturated and run up to the 30c potency. He had not long to wait for an
opportunity of testing it. A tall, fair young man of 24, a violinist, presented himself with a mass of scrofulous
glands on the right side of the neck softening at one point.,
Clarke gave him Sil-mar. 3c, three or four times a day and warned him not to poultice. The mass of glands
soon began to diminish. The abscess matured and discharged itself through a minute opening and eventually
healed without leaving a perceptible scar. The rest of the glands, in the meantime, disappeared.
Sil-mar. 3c, three times a day, rapidly cured a case of gonorrhea in a patient who had many previous attacks,
as well as stricture which had been treated with cauterizations and strong silver nitrate.
It was this history which partly led Clarke to give the remedy on account of the Nairn. element contained in it.
The discharge was creamy and there was tenderness in the middle of the urethra.
For three days after commencing the Sil-mar. there was a sharp aggravation, the discharge became very
profuse, was worse at night and accompanied by painful erections.
Burnett told an interesting experience of his in which he was consulted about a boy who persisted in spite of
punishment in eating sand when playing on the beach. Burnett
Silica marina advised the parents to let the boy eat as much as he liked. He kept it up for a fortnight, at the
end of which time he was vastly improved in health and he neither wanted nor ate any more sand from that
day.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
