name: Silica Terra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sil. Silica terra. Pure Flint. Silex. Silicic anhydride. Silicon dioxide. Trituration of pure,
precipitated silica. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Abscess. Acne. Anemia. Ankles, weak. Anus, fissures, fistula. Appetite, depraved. Back,
weakness. Bedwetting. Boils. Bones, necrosis. Brain, concussion. Brain-fag. Breast, abscess. Breast-feeding,
disorders. Bunions. Cachexia. Cancer. Carbuncle. Cataract. Cellulitis. Cephalohe- matoma. Chin, eruptions.
Circulation, poor. Coccyx, pains. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Convulsions. Coryza. Cough. Cysts. Debility.
Diabetes. Ear, disorders. Elephantiasis. Emaciation. Emphysema. Enchondroma. Epilepsy. Eruptions.
Excrescences. Eyes, disorders. Feet, burning. Fester. Fibroma. Fistula. Foot sweat, suppressed. Foreign
 bodies. Fractures. Ganglion. Gastric, catarrh. Glandular, swellings. Headaches. Hernia. Hip joint, disease.
Homesickness. Housemaid’s, knee. Hydrocele. Hypopion. Iritis. Jaw, bone, decay. Keloids. Keratitis.
Kyphosis. Lachrymal, fistula. Locomotor ataxia. Malnutrition. Mania. Ménière’s disease. Meningitis. Metritis.
Metrorrhagia. Migraines. Miner’s, disease. Miscarriage. Molluscum, contagiosum. Morphinism. Morvan’s
disease. Nails, problems. Nails, splitting. Necrosis. Neuralgias. Nodes. Panaritium. Perspiration, offensive.
Phimosis. Pleurisy. Potts’ disease. Psoas, abscess. Pyorrhea. Rheumatism, chronic. Rickets. Scars. Sinuses.
Sleepwalking. Spermatorrhea. Spina bifida. Spinal, curvature. Spinal, irritation. Strains. Strangury. Styes.
Suppurations. Synovitis. Teeth, decay. Tenesmus. Tumors. Ulcers. Urethra, stricture. Urethritis. Urine,
incontinence. Vaccination, effects. Vagina, spasms. Vertigo. Walking, late. Whitlow. Worms. Writer’s cramp.
Wounds.
HOMEOPATHIC - Outside homeopathy, flint is practically unknown as an internal remedy. Hahnemann
introduced it into medicine and it was his method of attenuating insoluble substances that enabled him to
discover its powers. Sil. forms one of the most important remedies for chronic diseases.
Want of grit, moral or physical. Proud flesh. Prostration of mind and body. Tendency to easy exhaustion
and abnormal sweats. Defective nutrition due to imperfect assimilation, especially inchildren. Emacia- tion.
Arrested development.
Enlarged glands. Slow, incomplete inflammation of glands, cellular tissue and skin, then induration. Edema in
morning. Cancer. Contracted sphincters. Cerebral softening. Diseases of bones and cartilages, decay and
necrosis, softening of bones. Exostosis.
Skin is unhealthy, every injury festers. Suppurative processes, stubborn, fistulous openings, abscesses.
Pustulous burrowings. Ripens abscesses, promotes suppuration. Ailments attended withpusformation. Dis-
charges offensive, pus, sweat, stools etc.
Sil. can stimulate the organism to reabsorb fibrotic conditions and scar-tissue. Scars indurated, hard, nodular,
shiny, glassy, tender with shooting pain. Keloid growth. J. Weir noted that it must be used with care in cases
of tuberculosis as it may cause the absorption of scar tissue and liberate the disease. Removes foreign
bodies.
Neurasthenic states with increased susceptibility to nervous stimuli and exaggerated reflexes. Epilepsy, aura
in the solar plexus creeping into the chest and stomach. Convulsions begin in the solar plexus, after
vaccination. Feeling of coldness before spasms or epileptic attacks.
Spinal curvature. Nervous disorders after spinal injury, especially when pressure on spine causes pain in
remote parts. Hysteria, paralysis and obstinate neuralgias caused by dissipation, hard work with close confine-
ment. Progressive locomotor ataxia.
Organic changes, it is deep and slow in action. Periodical states. Ascending effects. Pains are violent and
sticking, localized in ears, throat, ulcers etc. Parts lain on to go to sleep. Sensation as if she were divided into
halves and left side does not belong to her. Sensation of a hair on tongue, in trachea.
Generally cold, chilly, hugs the fire, wants plenty warm clothing, hates drafts, hands and feet cold, worse in
winter. Want of vital heat even when exercising. Intolerance of alcoholic stimulants. Sensitive to pain,
noise, starts at least noise. Restless, fidgety.
Ill effects of vaccination. Scrofulous, rickety children with large heads, open fontanelles and sutures,
distended hot and hard abdomen, slow in walking and wasted in body, especially legs. Children crawl nervously
or are dragged in on their mother’s arms, on running they become pale. Cachectic and senile patients, persons
of fair, clear complexion.
MIND - Complaints from anticipation. Faint hearted, anxious. Nervous and excitable. Loss of self-
confidence. Anticipates failure. Performance anxiety. Fear of speaking in front of a group (Arg-n., Gel., Lyc.,
Nairn.). Timidity about appearing in public. Irresolution. Bashful. Worries about their mind and its ability to
perform. Undertakes nothing lest he fail.
Mental acuteness with physical weakness and torpidity. Cannot express himself correctly. Mental confusion.
Abstracted. Conscience about trifles. Fastidious for details. Inconstancy. Forgetfulness better after eating.
Restlessness while sitting, on waking.
Procrastinates, dread at any mental effort. Intellect lacks stability and clarity. Poor concentration, inability to
focus, poor memory. Brain-fag of businessmen, lawyers, preachers and students. Brain exhaustion (Sulph.,
Cann., Arg-n., Lyc., Pic-ac.). Fear of literary work. Prostration of mind after writing.
Can overexert their minds. Avoid things that take away their energy. Tendency to monitor energy function.
Afraid of draining activities. Anxiety about health, worse during menopause. Fear of injury. Fear of becoming
weak. Fear of being incapable.
Sensitive to all impressions. Starts from slight noise. Timidity. Fidgety. Sensitive weeping mood. Cries when
spoken to kindly. Yielding disposition. Lackscourage. Homesickness. Longing for his relations and home.
 Obstinate, stubborn, headstrong, in children. Mental dullness in children.
Hopeless. Sad. Sullen. Disgust for life, wishes to drown herself. Melancholy and weariness of life during
menses. Worse from mental exertion, talking, nervous excitement.
Mild and yielding when calm but irritable and irascible when aroused. Intolerant of contradiction. Indisposed to
talk loud. Screaming violently, groaning, in epilepsy. Fixed ideas. Fear ofneedles, pins and sharp objects.
Thinks only of pins, searches for them, and counts them. Somnambulism during increase of moon.
Abdomen - Hard, bloated. Distended, hard and hot, with thin legs, especially in children. Abdomen feels thick
and heavy like a weight. Clothing across abdomen feels too tight, after eating. Tightness transversely across
abdomen. Pain or painful cold feeling in abdomen, better external heat. Soreness of abdominal walls. Cracks
on abdominal wall. Much rumbling in bowels. Flatulence with much rumbling. Ascites with great effusion, with
frequent attacks of watery diarrhea. Flatulence incarcerated with constipation. Colic, cutting pain with
constipation. Colic from worms. Inguinal glands swollen and painful. Inguinal hernia.
Back - Constant aching in center of spine. Spinal irritation after injuries to spine. Spine, weak, very sensitive
to drafts on back. Spina bifida. Spinal curvature. Painful kyphosis. Pott’s disease. Decay of vertebrae.
Diseases of bones of spine. Backache as from riding in carriages for a long time. Burning in back, when body
is being heated, after walking in open air. Rheumatism. Aching, beating, throbbing, in lumbosacral region.
Coccyx hurts after riding. Painful coccyx. Lameness in region of sacrum. Stiff neck with headache. Haid,
cold swelling of cervical glands. Boils or carbuncles.
Bladder - Pressure in bladder during urination. Burning and soreness in urethra during urination. Frequent
urination with tenesmus. Chronic urethritis, foul discharge from urethra, thick, curdy, purulent, bloody. Chronic
urethritis with twisting pain. Continuous urging with scanty discharge, or without emission. Renal and vesical
calculi. Involuntary urination. Nocturnal bedwetting in children with worms.
Breasts - Milk suppressed. Sharp pain in breasts and uterus. Breasts swollen, hard and painful. Great itching
of swollen breasts. Scirrhus with itching. Darting, burning, in left nipple. Nipples very sore, ulcerated easily.
Nipples drawn in like a funnel. Fistula in breasts. Fistulous ulcers of breast (Phos.). Threatened abscess of
breast. Hard lumps in breast (Con.). Breast cancer.
Causations - Ill effects oí suppressed sweat, especially of feet. Stone-cutting. Loss of fluids. Injury, strains.
Vaccinations. Splinters, foreign objects in tissue. Overwork, mental or physical.
Chest - General sensation of weakness in chest, can hardly speak (Stann.). Can’t breathe deeply without
chest pain. Sticking pain in chest on inspiration. Bruised pain in chest on coughing. Stitches in chest, through
the back. Painless throbbing in sternum. Tight feeling around chest, as if tied in with tape. Pressure at lower
sternum as from a stone. Eruption like varicella, covering chest and itching violently. Axillary glands swollen,
enlarged. Offensive axillary sweat.
Constitutions - Demineralized constitution. Constitutions that suffer from deficient nutrition due to lack of
assimilating power, oversensitive physically and mentally. Children with large heads, open fontanelles and
sutures, much sweating about the head, which must be kept warm. Distended abdomen, weak ankles, slow in
learning to walk. Nervous, irritable persons with dry skin, profuse saliva, diarrhea, and night sweats. Weakly
persons,
fine skin, pale face, light complexion, lax muscles. Scrofulous children who have worm diseases during
dentition. Stonecutters’ ailments, chest disorders and total loss of strength.
Cough - Cough and sore throat. Cough with expectoration in day, bloody or purulent. Loose cough day and
night. Violent cough when lying down with a thick, yellow lumpy expectoration, suppurative stage of
expectoration (Bals-p.). Cough gagging, shaking, retching, worse cold drinks, talking, lying and after waking.
Dry cough at night, waking patient from sleep. Dry, hacking cough with hoarseness.
Ears - Earaches. Abscess. Boils. Otorrhea, fetid discharge. Crusty formations in ears. Perforated eardrum.
Itching in ears when swallowing. Itching of outer ears. Shooting pain in left ear. Feeling of stoppage in the ear,
better when yawning or swallowing. Decay of mastoid process. Child bores into its ears with fingers when
asleep, causing a discharge of pus and blood. Sensitive to noise. Ménière’s disease. Hissing, roaring in
ears. Hissing in perforated ear. Ringing in the ears or loss of hearing. Loud pistol-like report. Deafness, hears
again with a loud report or on blowing the nose and coughing, worse full moon.
Eyes - Eyestrain and headaches. Keratitis, pustular, perforating. Iritis and irido- choroiditis with pus in anterior
chamber. Perforating or sloughing ulcer of cornea. Abscess in cornea after traumatic injury. Opacities of
the cornea after smallpox. Cataracts and weak vision, from over use. Cataract in office workers after sup-
pressed foot sweat. Inflammation of eyes. Sharp pain through eyes. Eyes tender to touch, worse when closed.
Swelling of lachrymal duct. Stricture of lachrymal duct. Hypopyon. Angles of eyes affected. Affections of
canthi, tear-ducts. Styes. Encysted tumors of lids. Aversion to light, especially daylight, it produces dazzling.
Amblyopia from abuse of stimulants.
 Face - Pale, cachectic, waxy. Red spots on cheeks with burning heat. Lupus. Burning about mouth. Skin of
face cracks. Cracks
in lips, on skin of face. Indurated fissures at the corners of lips. Cancer of lower lip. Comedones. Eruptions on
chin. Herpes on chin. Rheumatic pain in jaw and decayed teeth. Swelling of jaw. Swelling of maxillary glands.
Parotid glands swollen (Bell., Rhus-t., Calc.), enlarged. Facial neuralgia, throbbing, tearing, face red, worse
cold damp. Boring, tearing pains.
Female - Amenorrhea. Watery discharge instead of menses. Early, scanty menses. Increased menses with
paroxysms of icy coldness over whole body. Menses strong-smelling, acrid. Discharge of blood between
menstrual periods. Discharge of blood from vagina every time child is nursed. Leucorrhea milky (Calc., Puls.,
Sep.). Leucorrhea acrid gushing, worse during urination. Burning and soreness about vulva. Cutting pain
around the navel with leucorrhea. Cutting upward in vagina, worse urinating. Vaginal cysts (Lyc., Puls.,
Rhod.). Abscess of labia. Itching of vulva and vagina, very sensitive. Pressing-down feeling in vagina.
Prolapsus uteri in consequence of myelitis. Salpingitis with accumulation of pus or serum that escapes from
uterus from time to time. Nausea during sex. Nymphomania. Sterility. Miscarriage or no conception due to
weakness. Too violent motion of fetus. After-pains felt in hips. Promotes expulsion of moles.
Food - Want of appetite, thirst excessive. Loss of appetite and of taste. Voracious appetite, but disappears on
attempting to eat or loathing of food. Desires only cold things, ice cream, ice water, feels comfortable when
it is in stomach. Aversion to cooked or warm food and meat. Disgust for meat and warm food, milk. Pain in
head better while eating. Worse after eating. Aversion to mother’s milk, child vomits as soon as it nurses. Milk,
aggravates, causes diarrhea and vomiting. Drinking cold water causes dry cough. Warm drinks improves
cough, causes sweat about head and face. Water tastes badly. Intolerance of alcoholic stimulants.
Head - Chronic, periodical headaches since some severe disease. Migraines. Headaches located over one
eye. Headache as if vertex will burst. Vertex throbs. Sick headaches as if coming from spine or occiput.
Headache, then blindness. Headache while fasting or when not eating at proper time. Headache worse by
exertion, study noise, motion, jar, light, cold air, talking and straining at stools. Headache better by wrapping
warmly, binding and pressure. Profuse urination, relieves the headache. Swelling filled with grumous fluid
between scalp and bone. Must keep head covered or catches a cold. Lumps on scalp. Profuse sweats on
head. Moist crusty eruptions on the scalp. Premature falling of hair, baldness. Swelling of glabella.
Cephalohematoma. Fontanelles open with distended abdomen.
Heart - Circulation easily agitated. Heart troubles from nervous exhaustion. Throbbing all over the body, when
sitting or while in motion. Palpitations while sitting, with trembling of hand. Violent hammering palpitation, after
every quick or violent motion. Orgasm of blood at night, throbbing in all vessels. Pulse small, hard, rapid. Pulse
irregular and thenslow. Pulse imperceptible.
Kidneys - Chronic urethritis, foul discharge from urethra, thick, curdy, purulent, bloody. Frequent urination with
tenesmus. Profuse urination, better headache. Urine is bloody, with red or yellow sediment. Pus in urine.
Kidney and bladder stones. Nightly incontinence after a blow upon the head. Nocturnal bedwetting in children
from worms.
Limbs - Pott’s disease. Psoas abscess. Felons, deep-seated pain. Axillary glands swollen, enlarged. Ulcers
around the joints. Sciatica, pains through the hips, legs and feet. The parts lain on go to sleep. Limbs
distorted during convulsion. Slovenly gait. Legs feel paralyzed, trembling while walking. Loss of power in legs.
Pain in knee, as if tightly bound. Calves tense and contacted. Cramp in calves and soles. Weak ankles and
feet. Icy cold and sweaty feet. Voluptuous tingling in soles.
Soreness in feet from instep through to the sole (Ruta.). Pain beneath toes. Bunions. Soft corns in between
toes. Distorted ingrown, yellow nails. Affections °f fingernails, especially if white spots on nails. Nails,
splitting. Nails, rough, yellow, crippled, brittle, white spots, blue in fever. Fingertips, as if suppurating, painful,
dry, at night. Tremulous hands when using them. Paralytic weakness of forearm. Panaritium. Arms (left) shake
before epilepsy.
Liver - Throbbing ulcerative pain in the region of liver. Abscess of liver. Beating soreness in liver, worse motion,
walking, lying on right side.
Lungs - Weak lungs. Shortness of breath, from manual labor, walking fast. Deep sighing. Dyspnea when
lying on back, when stooping, running, coughing. Dyspnea from draft on neck. Breathing so difficult that eyes
seemed to protrude. Neglected pneumonia. Pneumonia resulting in suppuration. Slow recovery after
pneumonia. Emphysema. Emphysema after pleurisy. Stone-cutter’s disorders. Miner’s disease. Sycotic
asthma worse lying down. Asthma with spasm of larynx. Hay asthma coming on about the last of August.
Asthma, can’t bear a draft of airón back of neck. Chronic colds that settle in chest and bring on asthmatic
attacks after being overheated or exertion. Colds fail to yield, sputum persistently muco-purulent and profuse.
Rattling in chest. Profuse foul, yellow, lumpy sputum, granular, offensive when broken.
 Male - Burning and soreness of genitals. Squeezing pain in testes. Sharp pricking pain in penis. Itching moist
spots on scrotum. Elephantiasis of scrotum. Hydrocele. Painful eruptions in pubic region. Chronic urethritis
with twisting pain. Prostate gland enlarged. Discharge of prostatic fluid when straining at stool. Burning in
prepuce after stool. Sexual desire increases or decreases. Sexual weakness, nocturnal emissions Extreme
exhaustion after sex, takes 8 to 10 days to recover. Worse after sex, sensation on right side of head as if
paralyzed. Chronic gonorrhea with thick, foul, urethral discharge.
Modalities - Better warmth, warm room, warm wraps, especially around head. Better summer, wet or humid
weather. Better from profuse urination. Better magnetism and electricity. Worse from change of weather.
Worse cold, air, drafts, damp. Worse lying down, lying on left side. Worse uncovering, bathing, washing
during menses. Worse jarring of spine, touch, pressure. Worse combing hair. Worse mental exertion, talking,
nervous excitement. Worse light, noise. Worse alcohol. Worse suppressed perspiration, especially of feet.
Worse from moon changes, new moon, increasing moon and full moon. Worse night, in morning. Worse from
vaccinations.
Mouth - Saliva runs out of mouth. Inflammation and suppuration of salivary glands. Offensive odor from mouth
in morning. Water tastes badly, vomits after drinking. Dryness of mouth. Sores in mouth. Sore mouth,
gangrenous with perforating ulcer of palate. Abscess at the root of the teeth. Pyorrhea. Boils on gums (Merc-
c.). Gums sensitive to cold air. Sensitive to cold water.
Nose - Obstinate colds, with ear affections. Sinusitis. Chronic catarrh and coryza. Coryza with nosebleed.
Frothy nasal discharge. Acrid, excoriating discharge. Sneezing in morning. Obstructed and loss of smell.
Burning, shooting pain. Drawing pain in root of nose and right malar bone. Nose, dry, cold. Sore, sensitive
nasal bones. Itching at tip of nose. Herpetic eruption around nostrils and lips. Ulcers high up in nose. Cracks
in nostrils. Perforation of septum. Dry, hard crusts form, bleeding when loosened. Nosebleed in infants.
Dryness and stoppage after suppressed foot sweat.
Perspiration - Debilitating at night. Profuse sweats at night, worse towards morning. Foul, acrid sweat, as
soon as he falls asleep. Sweats on upper part of the body, head or affected parts. Wetting pillow. Offensive
sweat, hand and axilla. Profuse sweat of head offensive and extends to neck. Offensive sweat on feet,
itching, acrid,
destroying shoes, suppressed. Warm sweat after epilepsy. Sweats from least exertion. Sour and offensive
sweats.
Rectum - Feels as if rectum is paralyzed. Constant but ineffectual desire for stool. Straining with soft stools,
with exhaustion. Great straining, rectum stings, closes upon stool. Feces remain a long time in rectum. Itching
in rectum and anus during stool. Moist anus, foul flatus. Chronic diarrhea. Diarrhea after milk. Diarrhea of
cadaverous odor. Constipation always before and during menses. Burning, smarting and pressing in anus,
after stool. Pain in anus as if constricted during stool. Painful spasms of sphincter. Cutting, cramping pain in
rectum extending to testes, worse sex. Fistula in anus (Berb., Lach.), alternating with chest symptoms.
Painful hemorrhoids, protrude during stool. Sensation as of a heavy lump in anus during menses. Tapeworm.
Sensations - As if she would die. As if beaten all over. As if he had lain in an uncomfortable position. As if
gradually losing senses. As if feeling for pins. Sensation as if she were divided into halves and that the left side
does not belong to her. As if head would burst with throbbing in it internal and external at same time. As if
forehead would be torn asunder, as from a heavy weight over eyes. As if head were forced asunder. As of a
splinter in finger. As if a panaritium would form in index finger. As if fingertips were suppurating. As if finger
were thick and bone enlarged. As if joints of fingers were being pulled out of sockets. Nails as if decayed.
Skin - Delicate, palp, waxy skin. Unhealthy skin, every injury suppurates. Rosecolored blotches. Coppery
spots. Acne, eruption itches and burns. Acne rosacea. Carbuncles. Felons, abscesses, old scars, ulcers.
Boils and pustules everywhere. Boils come in crops. Long lasting suppuration and fistulous tracts. Impetigo.
Psoriasis inveterata. Herpes zoster. Promotes expulsion of foreign bodies from tissues. Abscesses after
vaccination. Acuminate eruptions. Eruptions itch only in daytime and evening. Proud flesh forms in ulcers.
Ulcers, painfully sensitive, foul, spongy, on feet, toes, and nails, better heat. Sensation of coldness in ulcers.
Offensive pus. Bursitis. Elephantiasis. Leprous nodes. Indurated tumors. Painless swelling of ^taà.læ^te'xj
'«'SJ&.'H'S^ 'JSWJNS. Gooseflesh. Crippled and brittle nails. Dry, cracked fingertips. Keloids. Scars suddenly
become painful.
Sleep - Sleepiness all day. Great sleepiness after eating, and in evening. Excessive yawning. Sleepy but
cannot sleep. Sleeplessness with great orgasm of blood and heat in head. Restless, unrefreshing sleep.
Unrefreshed sleep, wishes to remain in bed. Talks in sleep loudly, whines or laughs. Whining and laughing
during sleep, loud talking. Sleepwalking at new and full moon. Frequent starts in sleep. Lascivious dreams.
Dreams of his youth, past events. Anxious, frightful dreams, wakes with trembling of the whole body.
Nightmares of murders, horrid things, corpses and dead persons. Dreams of some one choking her.
 Stomach - Anguish in pit of stomach, with attacks of melancholy. Pit of stomach painful to pressure. Gnawing,
twisting pain in epigastrium, worse by pressure. Sensation as if a cold stone were in stomach. Sensation of
emptiness in stomach, with nausea. Induration of pylorus. Slow and painful digestion. Griping in stomach after
eating. Screwing, pressing, twisting pain in stomach after drinking. Swallowing food easily gets into posterior
sinuses. Burning or throbbing in pit. Intense heartburn. Sour belchings after eating (Sep., Calc.). Nausea, with
good appetite. Nausea during sex in females. Nausea and vomiting during pregnancy. Vomiting after drinking
(Ars., Bism., Verat.). Sour vomiting. Vomiting of food at night. Water brash with chilliness.
Stool - Stools comes out with difficulty when partly expelled, recedes again. Stools retained for fear of pain.
Stools offensive, painless, lienteric, of cadaverous odor. Stool composed of hard lumps, light-colored and very
hard.
Teeth - Teeth feel too large and too long
Silica terra for the mouth. Tearing pain at night. Constant aching in all teeth. Teeth break down, lose their
enamel, become rough, carious. Stinging toothache, preventing sleep. Toothache during menses. Abscess
&tM>\ ojlt AMitig on gums anú roo) of mouth after extraction of teeth. Pyorrhea (Merc-c.). Boils on gums
(Merc-c.). Cold feeling in upper gums. Gums sensitive to cold air and to cold water. Difficult dentition, teething
delayed.
Temperature - Chilly, worse lying in bed, exertion. Chilliness, very sensitive to cold air. Always chilly, even
when exercising. Shuddering all over body whole day, before menses. Icy chills. Creeping, shivering over the
whole body. Suffering parts feel cold. Cold limbs, feet, even in a warm room. Hectic fever in debilitated
persons, worse after meals. Hectic fever during long suppurative processes. Intermittent fever heat
predominating. Spotted fever. Typhoid fever with desire to be magnetized. Fever during dentition.
Throat - Sore throat. Burning in throat. Chronic pharyngitis. Periodical quinsy. Colds settle in throat. Tonsillitis.
Tonsils swollen, suppurating. Pricking as ofapin in tonsil. Enlarged thyroid gland. Right lobe of thyroid gland
swollen, having the appearance of an elastic cyst. Swallowing is painful, stinging, difficult, hysterical. Sticking
pain on swallowing or on touch. Food is ejected through nose, when swallowing. Swelling of larynx. Roughness
and soreness in larynx. Tickling in larynx causes slight cough and hoarseness. Foreign bodies in larynx. Hawks
foul lumps. Bittertaste. Husky voice, worse mornings with chronic coryza. Hoarseness.
Tongue - Sensation of a hair on tongue. Tongue feels sore. One sided swelling of tongue. Tongue coated
with brownish mucus. Indurations in tongue.
Vertigo - Vertigo when closing eyes. Vertigo from excessive use of eyes. Vertigo as if drunk. Vertigo with
nausea, sleepiness. Vertigo from looking up. when lying on left side (Mag-m., Stront.). Vertigo with tendency
to fall backward. Vertigo better wrapping up warmly, must sit down. Vertigo in neurasthenia and epilepsy.
Ménière’s disease.
Vision - Vision is confused, letters run together on reading. Spotted vision. Objects appear pale. Objects as if
in a fog. Black spots. Day blindness, with sudden appearance of furuncles. Momentary loss of sight. Foggy
vision, better wiping eyes. Lightning-like flashes during headache. Dim vision and flickering, worse after
headache. Dim vision after suppressed foot sweat.
COMMENTS - Sea sand (Sil-mar.) is mainly composed of silica. The spicules of many sponges are made up
of silica. Silicates are taken up by plants and silica is often deposited on the surface or in the interior of their
stems. The strength of straw is due to silica. Equisetum generally contains as much as 18 percent silica. Flint
supplies the “grit” of the earth’s crust, of plant life and to a large extent of animal life also.
Schussler, who was a homeopath before he was a biochemist, noted that silicic acid, from the tissue remedy
point of view, is a constituent of the cells of the connective tissue or the epidermis, the hair and the nails.
It may be used if a suppurative center is formed either in the connective tissue or in a portion of the skin. These
cells are thereby enabled to throw off inimical substances (the pus). In consequences, the pus is either
absorbed by the lymphatics or it is cast out. In the latter case there is a breaking open of the suppurative
center. Sil. may also cause an effusion of blood in any tissue to be absorbed through the lymphatics.
Teste put Sil. in his Puls, group of remedies, the other members of it being Calc., Hep., Graph., and Phos.
According to Teste, Sil. is the “chronic” of Puls. Sil. corresponds to the chronic form of such diseases as Puls,
cures when acute, including rush of blood to the head, especially to the right temple and vertex, headache
every day, photophobia, lachrymation, loss of taste, and aversion to fat food with rancid or oily taste in the
mouth.
The symptoms of Sil. differ from those of Puls., being more constant, more deep-seated and lasting longer.
For instance, the mucus
Silica terra secretions of Puls, easily become purulent under the action of Sil.
Sil. is useful for chronic arthritic or rheumatic affections as it forms a soluble combination (sodium silicate) with
the soda of the urate of soda, this combination is then absorbed and removed through the lymphatics. For the
 same reason it may also be used in kidney gravel.
“Sensitive to noise and anxiety therefrom. Sensitive, weeping mood. Yielding, faint-hearted. Children become
obstinate, headstrong, cry when kindly spoken to.” “Fixed ideas: the patient thinks only of pins, fears them,
searches for them and counts them carefully.”
Nice, sensitive, timid and shy (Sil., Phos. Nat-m.). Obstinate, strong will power but lack of energy. Poor
confidence (Lyc.), due to lack of strength. Afraid of falling apart. Feeling of fragility. Yielding and mild. Arguing
drains them. Irresolution. Lack firmness. Aristocratic, sophisticated. Aggravated by a coarse environment or
people. Well behaved because they lack stamina, energy. Overwhelmed and drained from conflicts and
confrontations. Startled and upset easily.
Poor stamina, poor endurance, easily exhausted. Brain fag, worse mental or physical exertion. Chronic fatigue.
Aversion to exerting themselves. Mental, emotional and physical weakness.
Premature babies with a failure to thrive (Calc-p.). Fontanelles that have slow closures. Slow learning to walk.
Delayed development. Weak and malnourished children. Malnutrition. Protein deficiency, mineral imbalances,
poor assimilation and poor deposition of minerals. Difficulty breast-feeding, tendency to regurgitate milk and
have colic and diarrhea from breast milk (Calc-p.).
Weak muscles and bone structures. Easily injured, weak joints and ligaments, especially when tired. Shin
splints, bones don’t heal well. Curvature of the spine. Stooped shoulders, generally weak. Brittle nails with
white spots. Fragile, brittle hair and nails. Crippled nails, produces inflammation around and under them.
“Sensation as if the finger-tips were suppurating.”
Unhealthy skin, every little injury ulcerates. Inflammation, swelling and suppuration of all the lymphatic glands
and the glands of the skin. Tendency to form scars and keloids. Boils or cysts. Deep scars with unhealthy skin.
Matures abscesses and reduces excessive suppuration. For indurations after suppuration, particularly in
tonsils which refuse to heal after the pus has been evacuated and in abscesses which leave sinuses and
fistula.
Useful to expel foreign objects, especially in the eyes. For splinters under the nails (Hyper.). In the provings,
Sil. produced a sensation of a “splinter in the finger,” of “a pin in the throat.” For foreign bodies embedded in
the tissues. Sil. will cause suppuration and expulsion of necrosed tissues caused from embedded objects. Sil.
should be used with caution as the expulsion of harmless, encysted objects might risk the patient’s life.
For restoring the perspiration of the feet when this has been suppressed, thus it is an indirect remedy in
diseases arising in consequence of such suppression (e.g., amblyopia, cataract, paralysis, etc.). In such a
case, the meatus is dry and enlarged.
Athlete’s foot from suppression of sweat. Heavy foot sweats, foul odor, sweat eats away at their socks.
Pungent, penetrating odor, sour, carrion-like. Sweat on hands and feet. The feet may give off an intolerable
odor without any sweat. Offensive head sweat. Symptoms are better from sweat.
Keynote sensitiveness. Over-susceptibility to nervous stimuli. The senses are hypersensitive. The surface is
tender and the least touch is painful. Brain and spine cannot bear even ordinary vibrations. This condition may
be caused by losses of fluids as in spermatorrhea, or by over-worked brain.
Tendency to paralysis. Paralytic weakness from defective nutrition of nerves, brain, and spinal cord.
Constipation with paralytic weakness. Epileptic convulsions, starting from the solar plexus, worse at full and
new moon, and worse from any overstrain of mind or emotions.
Locomotor ataxia when the fingers feel stiff, with loss of power in them. Spinal irritation. The neck is stiff,
causing headache. The small of the back aches as if beaten. The part of the body lain on goes to sleep.
Sciatica, numbness and tingling around the legs. Worse lifting and straining. Arthritis, worse cold, damp.
Chronic headaches, which may owe their origin to some severe disease of youth. Headaches ascend from the
nape of the neck to the vertex, as if coming from the spine and locate in one eye, especially the right.
Headaches worse from draft of air or uncovering head, better pressure and wrapping head up warmly, better
profuse urination. Headaches from over study (Calc., Nat-m., Phos., Ign.). Head injuries that lead to exhaustion
and convulsions.
Vertigo, ascends from the back of the neck, as if one would fall forward (sometimes backward), worse looking
up, closing eyes, lying on left side. Sleepwalking (Puls.).
Asthma, worse change of weather with yellow mucus. Asthma from exertion. Asthma is worse physical
exertion, worse change of weather and worse cold, damp. Sinusitis, allergies, from low resistance. Shortness
of breath, particularly in the elderly. Emphysema, particularly in those who inhale particulate matter. Problems
with changes in altitude.
“Discharge of blood from the vagina every time the child takes the breast.” “Nipple is drawn in like a funnel.”
Cysts and nodules in the breast. Constipation before and during menses. Prostration after sex.
Constipation, difficult stool. As from inactivity of rectum with great straining, as if rectum was paralyzed. Bashful
 stool, when partly expelled, recedes again. Feces remain a long time in rectum. Cracking and dryness around
the anus. Hemorrhoids. Fistulas and fissures, particularly in the anus, rectum and breasts.
Sensitivity to food. Aversion to milk, meat, fatty foods, sometimes sweets. Thirsty for cold drinks but not for ice
(Phos. would want ice). Desires eggs, cold food. Aggravated by coffee, alcohol.
Weakness after vaccinations. Worse since vaccination (Thuj.) or never well since vaccinations. Epilepsy,
asthma, headaches, chronic infections, abscesses, lack of stamina, loss of weight, excessive sleep, after
vaccinations.
Worse from excessive stress, from pregnancy or surgery. Exhaustion and stress lead to physical ailments.
Worse thinking about problems. Sensitive to noise and pain. Want of vital heat, even exercise will not get up
any warmth. Heated and chilled easily. Chilly, but worse heat and stuffy rooms. Sensitive to cold, damp and
changes of weather. Aggravated from drafts, from getting wet. Sensitive to the moon (Calc.).
Rushmore verified a peculiar symptom of Sil. in a woman suffering from scirrhous of her left breast. She had
a feeling of dryness in her fingertips, as if made of paper, at night. Ant-t. and Sil. have this symptom, but only
Sil. in afternoon. Sil. removed this and took away sharp, stinging pains in the tumor as well.
Clarke recordeda case of recurrent keloids, “Eleanor W., 14, had a growth on left temple. Five months previous
she was an inmate in St. Bartholomew’s Hospital and had a tumor removed from the spot, the tumor having
existed for two years.
“A month after the operation a new growth appeared on the scar. Two months later this was removed. But it
rapidly recurred and when I saw her there was a linear elevation an inch long, three lines wide and raised
about two lines. It was red, shiny and slightly modulated, was tender to touch and the seat of shooting pain.
Before the first operation there had been no pain and no discoloration of the skin.
“Hahnemann gives this symptom in the proving of Sil. “Stitching, aching pain in the spot where an ulcer had
been formerly on the leg.” Sil. 3c, night and morning, was prescribed.
“There was no further increase in the size of the growth, though it was still painful, the pain being apparently
somewhat increased. In three months there was evident diminution in size and from that time the pain began
to diminish. In seven months the growth had entirely disappeared.”

name: Silicone
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - silic. Silicone. Historicaldose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Arthritis. Autoimmune, disease. Fatigue. Fibromyalgia. Headaches. Lupus.
Lymphadenopathy. Neuropathy. Pericarditis. Pleurisy. Rheumatism. Scleroderma. Sleep disturbance.
HOMEOPATHIC - Autoimmune disease. Chronic rheumatism, producing a painful thickening and contraction
of the fibrous structures, interfering with motion and causing deformity. Neuropathy. Diseases involving the
cranial or spinal nerves. Connective tissue diseases. Systemic lupus erythmetosus, polyarteritis, scleroderma.
Dermatosclerosis, hide-bound or skin-bound disease. Thickening of the skin caused by swelling and thickening
of fibrous tissue, with eventual atrophy of the epidermis.
Rheumatoid arthritis. Inflammation or degeneration of connective tissue, accompanied by deposition of
fibrinous material. Collagen disease. Fibromyalgia, aching, soreness, stiffness, with fatigue, sleep disturbance,
headaches. Muscular rheumatism.
Diffuse erythematous skin lesions on the face, neck, or upper extremities, with liquefaction degeneration of the
basal layer and epidermal atrophy. Lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes). Pleurisy or pericarditis.
Glomerular lesions of the capillaries. Anemia, hyperglobulenemia.
RELATIONS - Compare: Calc-f., Sep., Sil.

name: Silphium Laciniatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - silphu. Silphium laciniatum. Rosin-weed. Rosin-wood. Compass plant. Pilot weed. Polar plant.
Turpentine-weed. N. O. Compositae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Bladder, catarrh. Bronchitis. Cachexia. Cancer. Dysentery. Influenza. Nausea.
Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - The leaves of this plant, when they first come up, present their faces uniformly north and
south, later on, when the leaves become heavy, the winds cany them in different directions and the polarity is
not to be observed. The stem of the plant exudes an abundance of resin, as some of its names indicate.
Cooper used Silphu. in single doses of tincture with notable effect in cases of cancer of the throat and mouth.
The great “sensation of emptiness” of the proving shows a relation to the cancer cachexia.
Hale mentioned that Silphu. has been used in all forms of asthma and in chronic bronchitis with large quantities
of stringy,
Silphium laciniatum frothy, light-colored mucus and in catarrh of the bladder. Catarrhal influenza. Dysentery,
attack preceded by constipated stools covered with white mucus.
Chest - Constriction and tightness of chest. Hacking, spasmodic cough.
Kidneys - Frequent urination with sense of heat or burning at meatus during urination. Urine, high-colored,
scanty.
Lungs - Constriction of lungs. Catarrh with copious, stringy, mucus discharges. Irritation of posterior sinuses
involving mucus membranes of nasal passages with constriction of supra-orbital region. Cough with
expectoration, profuse, stringy, frothy, light-colored. Excited by sense of mucus rattling in chest and worse by
drafts of air.
Mouth - Tongue, whitish slimy coat, with dry sensation as if burned with hot soup.
Nose - Irritation extends from throat up posterior sinuses to nose causing sneezing, followed by discharge of
limpid, acrid mucus. Constriction and pressure in supra-orbital region.
Rectum - Stool natural, but covered with slimy mucus.
Stomach - Nausea, sick, faint feeling and a sense of emptiness in epigastrium.
Throat - Scraping, tickling and irritation of fauces and throat. Desire to hawk and scrape throat and throw off
a thin viscid mucus. Engorgement and thickening of mucus membrane of throat extending down.
COMMENTS - Hale gave the case of Mr. H., 55, who had tuberculosis for twenty years. On the slightest
exposure or cold he would have congestion of mucus surfaces, followed by copious expectoration of stringy,
frothy, light-colored mucus (from one to three pints in twenty-four hours). Rapid exhaustion, at times keeping
him in bed for weeks. Silphu. 2x trituration was used, 2 grains every two hours.
During the next night, less than a tea cupful of mucus was raised and its sudden decrease alarmed the patient
so much that he left off the remedy until his doctor assured him that he was very much better and thatM the
remedy had been more successful than he himself had expected.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Aral., Cop., Just., Tereb., Cub., Samb. (2) Silpho. - tuberculosis pulmonum with
incessant cough, profuse night-sweats, emaciation. (3) Polyg-a. has been found useful in tuberculosis, when
given in material doses of the mother tincture, salvia tickling cough. (4) Arum-d. - loose cough at night on lying
down. (5) Just. - bronchial catarrh, hoarseness, oversensitive.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Bladder, catarrh. Bronchitis. Cachexia. Cancer. Dysentery. Influenza. Nausea.

name: Simaruba Amara
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sima. Simaruba amara. Mountain damson. Simaruba officinalis. Simaruba glauca. N. O.
Simarubacae. West Indies and tropical America. Tincture of the dried root-bark. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Dysentery. Snakebite. Worms.
HERBAL - Simaruba bark is used as a bitter tonic and as a local remedy for dysentery and diarrhea. The part
used is the bark, which is really the rind of the root of which, domestically, a decoction is made. “In large
doses,” said the Treasury of Botany, “it is said to actas an emetic, purgative and diaphoretic.”
Simaruba versicolor, a Brazilian species, has similar properties. The fruits and bark are used as anthelmintics,
an infusion of the latter is employed in cases of snakebite. The plant is so bitter that insects will not attack it,
on which account the powdered root has been used to kill vermin.
Simaruba glauca, a native of Cuba, furnishes a glutinous juice which is employed in certain cases of skin-
 disease. And it is well to remember that Cedrón, which is “Simaba Cedrón,” belongs to the same order.
COMMENTS - Clarke’s first practical acquaintance with Sima, as a homeopathic remedy was in the case of a
traveling patient who suffered from a chronic tendency to looseness of the bowels. He had stools like yellow
ochre, for which Gamb. had been very helpful.
When in the south of France, he consulted
Simaruba amara
a homeopath who prescribed Sima, with excellent effect. Since then, Clarke used it in similar cases.
H. H. Beamish said that for dysentery the simaruba bark is boiled and, by way of strengthening the astringent
effect. Alum is added to the decoction. But Simaruba is the specific agent.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Cedr., Ail., Chap., Quas. (2) Vac., Chin., Rheum. Gamb.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Sinapis Alba
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sin-a. Sinapis alba. White mustard. Brassica alba. Senescent. N. O. Cru- ciferae. Trituration
and tincture of the seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, disorders. Backaches. Breast-feeding, disorders. Chills. Colic. Dyspepsia. Esophagus.
Flatus. Gastric ulcers. Gastritis. Headaches. Heartbum. Mouth, inflammation. Pregnancy, problems.
Salivation. Threadworms. Vomiting. Worms.
HERBAL - Sin-a., like Sin-n., is indigenous to Great Britain. The Treasury of Botany reported that “Its seeds
are larger than those of Black Mustard and of a yellow color externally. Chemically they differ in containing a
crystalline substance known as sulpho-sinapisin.
Moreover, its myrosine yields with water a pungent oil of a different character from the Volatile Oil of Mustard.
The seed-leaves or cotyledons of Sin-a. furnish the “mustard” of “mustard and cress,” the “cress” being
Lepidium sativum.
HOMEOPATHIC - Bojanus proved Sin-a., taking substantial doses of the triturated seeds and of a tincture
made therefrom.
Under Sin-a. the prover, who had no sign of threadworms since his thirteenth year, passed many both living
and dead and had all the usual rectal symptoms which accompany their presence. The urine too, was turbid,
as is often the case in helminthiasis.
Marked throat symptoms, especially pressure and burning with obstruction in esophagus, sensation of a
lump in esophagus behind the sternum and with eructations,
similar symptoms in rectum.
The well-known emetic effects of mustard were produced by it and also its “burning” sensations in many
parts, notably anus, stomach and esophagus. Flatulence. Headache, (better walking in open air. worse in
warm room). Salivation.
MIND - Distracted in mind, while reading must make great efforts to keep thoughts from wandering.
Abdomen - Movements in abdomen. Heaviness as of a weight, fullness and distention in abdomen. Rumbling
and gurgling with emission of odorless flatus. Emission of offensive flatus. Griping colic.
Back - Pains in small of back and coccyx, as if sprained and bruised with urging to stool.
Chest - Oppression of chest, compelling frequent deep breathing. Burning beneath sternum.
Eyes - Sudden sensation of warmth with stitching in left eye compelling winking, eye fills with tears, after which
the sensation disappears.
Food - Thirst.
Head - Sensation as if head hollow. Rush of blood to head. Headache better in open air worse in warm room.
Heaviness in the forehead, as from intoxication or too great warmth of room. Pain in left frontal eminence,
paroxysmal, pressive in the evening. Pressive pain in right frontal eminence worse moving head back and
forth. Dullness with obscured vision, especially of forehead over eyes, worse walking.
Kidneys - Urine dark yellow, soon forming transparent cloud, bright golden yellow, dark brown like beer. Many
grains of red sand deposited and iridescent film on surface. Thick, fatty pellicle. Cloud remains suspended in
urine. Sediment white, like chalk and containing grains of white sand.
Limbs - Heaviness in lower limbs.
Male - Emissions without lascivious dreams.
Modalities - Better rest, open air. Worse by touch, pressure, motion, warm room. Crawling in anus worse
swallowing.
Sensation of hard substance in stomach worse after eating.
Mouth - Root of tongue thickly coated yellow, on rising in morning, later extends along sides, especially left.
 Profuse salivation with nausea, nausea better at rest, worse walking about. Saliva frothy, salt.
Pulse - Pulse full and hard.
Rectum - Burning, itching in anus, obliging to scratch. Crawling biting in anus. Violent, sudden pain in anus.
Spasmodic griping in anus, worse after swallowing anything. Sensation as though a hard substance were lying
in anus and could not be evacuated, not better by stool. Stools, black, hard, covered with mucus. Stools, small,
thin, soft, greenish, copious, pasty, partly hard partly soft, sour, fermented, yellowish gray. Stools with dead
threadworms.
Sensations - As if head hollow. As of a plug in throat of hard substance high up in esophagus under sternum,
something hard lying in stomach after a moderate meal, hard substance in rectum not better by stool.
Sleep - Sleeps in afternoon with vivid dreams, aftereating. Vivid dreams of dead people and of death. Dreams
confused and unremembered of foreign countries and dangerous expeditions.
Stomach - Burning, pressure, fullness and distention in pit of stomach. Thirst without heartburn, drinking water
causes sensation of heaviness and fullness in abdomen as after eating. Belchings are tasteless and odorless.
Belchings of acid liquid with griping scalding in pharynx, tasting of food. Nausea, qualmishness inclination to
vomit, salivation. Nausea better at rest, worse by movement. Retching and vomiting of water. Vomits flakes of
mucus with black streaks, yellow, odorless, tasteless matter with much tenacious, jelly-like mucus. After
vomiting, scraping in throat and burning rising from stomach.
Temperature - Creeping chills on moving about, over whole body after vomiting with coldness of hands and
feet and frequent belchings of gas. Inclined to perspire.
Throat - Scraping in fauces, provoking frequent hawking. Burning in pharynx in esophagus rising up from
stomach like heartburn and pressure in esophagus. Sensation of hard body high up in esophagus, worse
swallowing hard food and on empty swallowing in afternoon seems as if a plug sticking in pharynx (this
sensation alternated with biting and crawling in anus). Sensation of constriction on swallowing hard food.
Sensation as if a large morsel of food had been swallowed.
COMMENTS - A. L. Fisher said that for twenty years Sin-a. has had a prominent place in his armamentarium.
He used it on the indications of the proving and he found that the states of pregnancy and breast-feeding seem
to favor development of the conditions calling for it.
He verified “Excessive accumulation of watery saliva or mucus.” “Acute bruised pain, even on slight pressure,
just beneath ensiform cartilage.” “Vomiting, ejecta consisting of flakes of mucus with black veins like clots of
blood.” “Crawling and burning in anus with griping in abdomen.” “Spasmodic griping in anus, appearing at
intervals and especially noticed after swallowing anything.”
He cured with Sin-a. “Sore mouth with intensely red mucus membrane, dotted with minute white ulcers, the
least food, even of blandest character increasing the burning that is present all the time and also in the throat.”
Bojanus noticed an alternation between the symptoms of the anus and those of the pharynx.
Clarke cured with Sin-a. “Sharp, shooting pain in right frontal eminence, worse in warm room, better moving
about and in open air.”
RELATIONS - An overdose of table mustard, which contains both Sin-a. and Sin-n. with starch is immediately
antidoted by smelling bread. Compare: (1) Sin-n. - plug sensation. (2) Anae. - ball in anus, Sep. lump in
stomach. (3) Bry., Abies-n., Nux-v., Puls. (4) Cina, Sant., Teucr., Napht., Scirr., - worms, helminthiasis.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Sinapis Nigra
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sin-n. Sinapis nigra. Black mustard. Brassica nigra. N. O. Cruciferae. Trituration and tincture of
seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL -Allergies. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Catarrh. Chlorosis. Chordee. Chorea. Colds. Constipation.
Coryza. Coughs. Diarrhea. Hay fever. Headache. Heartbum. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Intermittents. Menses,
premature. Mucous, fever. Pharyngitis. Post-nasal catarrh. Priapism. Scurvy. Strokes. Variola.
HERBAL - Sin-n. yields the greater part of the condiment so generally used in England. The plant is
indigenous, but is nevertheless largely cultivated in Yorkshire and Durham.
Like many other Cracifers, Sin-n. has antiscorbutic properties and it has cured cases of ague, mucus fever,
catarrh of bladder of stomach and of air passages. It hasbeen most used in the treatment of hay fever.
Cooper suggested the use of Sin-n. as an aperient. He considered that the chief agent in effecting
dislodgement of feces in constipated states is flatus. His method of producing this is as follows:
A tumblerful of hot water is to be taken in sips in the early morning, the same at breakfast time with some plain
brown bread or with no solid food at all. At 11 a.m. one or two capsules of pure mustard, each containing about
five grains of the powder to be taken, followed by half a tumbler of hot water.
 “This last is most important, as the water drives on the capsule and prevents its staying about the cardiac
orifice of the stomach and consequent distress to the patient. It also causes contraction of the walls of the
stomach and consequent expulsion of flatus into the duodenum.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Sin-n. is of use in hay fever, coryza and pharyngitis. Mucus membrane dry and hot, no
discharge, worse afternoon and evening, either nostril may be affected alone or they may be affected
alternately. Dry sinuses and pharynx with thick, lumpy secretion.
Mucus hawked orcoughed from posterior sinuses felt cold. “Sweat on upper lip and forehead.” Smallpox.
During the proving, symptoms were noted including “It seemed to double him up, could hardly stand, tears ran
from eyes intense pain across epigastric region. Rose late, feeling sore and stiff all over. Weakness in all
muscles.”
MIND - Mind worked rapidly. Better by study or mental diversion. Irritable, difficult to think and study.
Unreasonably cross.
Abdomen - Dull pain in left hypochondriac region. Heavy, dull pain as from weight below umbilical region.
Severe twisting in umbilical region. Pain from left of umbilical region to left iliac region, later to right side,
ascending colon. Accumulation of flatus with twinges of pain about umbilicus. Rumbling. Left inguinal gland
swollen and painful. Sharp pain in right inguinal gland. Dull pain in right inguinal region better by pressure.
Back - Rheumatic pain in intercostal and lumbar muscles, sleeplessness from pain in back and hips. Severe,
dull, pulsating pain under inferior angle of left scapula. Slight backache, becoming intolerable towards bedtime,
better motion.
Bladder - Pain in bladder. Frequent copious urine flow day and night. Desire frequent, flow increased. Urine,
pale, straw colored without sediment.
Causations - Damp weather, summer.
Chest - Wandering pains in chest. Pain in left side of chest in region of heart. Sensation in right chest as if
heart were on right side. Respiration at base of left lung roughened.
Eyes - Eyes feel weak, pressure causes pricking in them. Pressing feeling in eyes.
Face - Shrunken features. Burning prickling in face. Sweat on upper lip andforehead. Lips dry and feel as if
tissues were stiff. Red around mouth with smarting of lips. Sensation as if cheek were bulged outward by
bubble of air, just below malar bone in afternoon.
Female - Menses appear long before the proper time. Amenorrhea and chlorosis.
Food - Appetite good. All food tastes of
Sinapis nigra horseradish, later tasteless. Aversion to sweets.
Head - Headache over right eye worse stooping. Head dull, heavy, better when mind occupied by study,
shutting eyes, in open air, worse in warm room, when thinking of it. Frontal headache, most over bridge of
nose and around edge of orbits. Forehead hot and dry. Sensation as if scalp were adherent to bones. Scalp
hot and itches.
Heart - Dull, continual pain in heart toward apex in evening, seemingly in heart substance. Heart pains return
daily. Sensation as if heart were on right side. Pulse accelerated, full.
Limbs - Dull, heavy ache in legs. Weariness in limbs, with cramps incalves. Weakness in calf-muscles.
Constant pain in ankles and calves. Occasional dull pain in left shoulder joint.
Lungs - Allergies. Asphyxia. Pituitous asthma. Asthmatic breathing. Loud coughing-spells with barking
expiration. Cough is relieved by lying down. Cough mostly dry or with expectoration of lumps of mucus worse
in cold air, better lying down. Expectoration from posterior sinuses much mucus, which felt cold, white in
tenacious masses.
Male - Violent erections during day and night, obstinate, painful and continued. Awakening him at night with
lascivious thoughts, dreams and emissions at night.
Modalities - Better by study or mental diversion. Better sitting erect, shutting eyes. Better hearty meal. Better
lying down at night, except dreams. Worse by touch and pressure. Worse motion, leaning forward, stooping.
Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse warm room, July, August, damp weather. Worse evening, 4 p.m. to 6
p.m., 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Laughing causes cough.
Mouth - Offensive breath, smelling like onions (Asaf., Coch.). Taste of garlic, causing nausea of horseradish.
Profuse saliva. Dry, burning, extending to stomach. Tongue feels blistered. Black tongue. Tongue fissured in
middle, dirty white coat, sore, raw. Teeth sensitive to warm drinks and cold air, especially stopped teeth.
Swollen bleeding gums.
Nose - Severe colds. Allergies. Hayfever. Mucus from posterior sinuses. Scanty, acrid discharges, making
skin smart. Stoppage of left nostril all day or in afternoon and evening. Nostrils alternately stopped. Dry,
hot with lachrymation, sneezing, hacking cough, better lying down. Dryness in both nostrils. Scurvy with
copious and frequent nosebleed.
 Rectum - Before stool uneasy feeling in rectum after stool, smarting cutting low down in rectum and anus.
Desire for a stool without passage. Constipated, stools hard like balls. Diarrhea. First stool normal, second
loose. Stools offensive. Smarting, cutting pain low down in anus after a stool.
Sensations - Vertex as if empty. As if she had taken cold. As if scalp was adherent to bones. As of pins
sticking in eyeballs. Eyeballs as if pressed on from above. As if nostrils stopped up. As if movements impeded
all around the chest. As if something heavy oppressed her on all sides from neck to diaphragm. As if cheeks
were bulged out by a bubble of air below malar bone. Skin of lips as if stiff. As if blisters on tip of tongue. As if
a load on stomach. Pain as if heart were on right side. As of hot water in blood vessels.
Skin - Burning heat and stitches in skin. Skin turns red. Ecchymosis. Chronic eczema. Smallpox. Ulcers on
legs. Frightful suppuration and gangrenous inflammation reaching down to sternum (fatal effects of mustard
applied to swollen glands of neck).
Sleep - Sleepiness during day, sleepless at night. Sleeps little at night, but does not feel loss of sleep. Restless
sleep from pains in back and hips. Vivid or lascivious dreams.
Stomach - Burning in stomach, extending up esophagus, throat and mouth, which is full of canker sores.
Ulceration of stomach and intestines. Pressure in epigastric region. Pain in region of stomach with sensation
of faintness compelling to bend forward,
which relieves. Hiccough. Heartburn and belching. Hot sour belchings. Colic, pains come on while
bentforward, better sitting up straight. Sweat relieves when nausea comes on.
Temperature - Severe chills, chattering of teeth, sensation of general coldness with shrunken feeling (from
mustard bath). Heat through whole body, especially down spine. Quartan ague and inflammatory fever. Sweat
and feeling of hot water in all blood vessels, better when menses came on. Sweat general, especially on
forehead and upper lip. Sweat free from mental or physical exertion, from external heat.
Throat - Hoarseness, evening from 4 p.m. Feels scalded, hot inflamed. Dry sensation back of nose and throat.
Throat sore, left side, on swallowing saliva. Whole throat behind uvula injected light red. Sore throat right side
extending to left.
Vertigo - Vertigo of old people, violent attacks with hard hearing after eating heavy food, fat.
COMMENTS - Hansen added “Acute coryza with thin, watery, excoriating discharge, lachrymation, sneezing.
Hacking coughs, better from lying down. Acute pharyngitis, throat feels scalded, hot inflamed. Loud coughing
spells with barking expiration, heard at a great distance.”
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Smelling bread (immediate effects of taking excess of condiment): Nux-v„ Rhus-
t., or when blistering has been produced by a mustard poultice, soap is the remedy. Compare: (1) Sin-a.,
Thiosin., Coch. (2) Scalded sensation on tongue, Sang. (3) Cough worse laughing, Arg-n., Phos. (4) Cough,
better lying down, Ferr., Mang. (5) Worse from4 p.m. to 6 p.m., Lyc. (6) Amenorrhea, Sulph., Puls. (7) As if hot
water in blood vessels (Rhus-t. as if blood running cold). (8) Sulph., Caps., Coloc. (9) Sin-a.. (10) Mustard oil
by inhalation - acts on the sensory nerve endings of the trigeminal. Relieves pain in middle ear disease and in
painful conditions of nose, nasal cavities and tonsils.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Sium Latifolium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sium. Sium latifolium. Water parsnip. N. O. Umbelliferae. Tincture of root. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Dizziness. Opisthotonos. Spasms. Tetanus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Knowledge of water parsnip is derived from cases of poisoning through eating the root. The
Sium, symptoms bear a strong resemblance to those of the other poisonous Umbelliferae.
The most pronounced features of the convulsions were the drawing of the arms to the middle of the body,
flexure of the fingers and the preponderance of the contractions on the left side.
Opisthotonos. Spasms, at first violently clonic, diminishing with each succeeding convulsion until they became
little more than tremors. Loss of voluntary motion. Lack of mental energy (Aeth.).
MIND - Mentally excited. Lack of mental activity. Fear of death.
Abdomen - Sense of swelling and flatulence about bowels.
Eyes - Pupils dilated, responded steadily to bright light.
Head - Dizziness, headache.
Lungs - Breathing slow and stertorous.
Stomach - Nausea and vomiting, followed by a convulsion.
Temperature - Skin cold and clammy. Head hot, rest of body cold. Wet with perspiration.
Throat - Burning along digestive tract, especially esophagus.
 REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Sisyrinchium Glaxoides
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sisy. Sisyrinchium glaxoides. Blue-eyed grass. N. O. Iridaceae. The fresh root is macerated in
twice its weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Coma. Delirium. Snakebites. Wounds.
HERBAL - Sisyrinchium was one of the old “Thompsonian remedies.” Dr. W. U. Reed of Indiana contributed
the following in 1892 to the Hom. Recorder, concerning this little known remedy.
“The roots of Sisyrinchium are used in the treatment of snake bites. A tincture is made from the roots, it is said
to have been used by the Indians in treating snake bites, by bruising and moistening the roots and applying to
the wound.”
The symptoms of the snake bites cured with Sisy. are bluish black colored skin, as if dreadfully bruised. The
whole body becomes very red, hot and dry, face dark red. The leg and foot are enormously swollen and of the
same general appearance. The foot, calf of the leg and thigh turn black. Patient delirious but would cry out if
touched. Wild delirium all night. Unconscious. Pulse quick and hard.
COMMENTS - Dr. W. U. Reed stated* We have growing in our woods and fields a small plant, which I believe
to be a specific for the treatment of persons or animals bitten by the rattlesnake. From my own experience and
observation in the use of this remedy, I believe it to be a positive cure in all cases if exhibited in any reasonable
time.
“I have never known it to fail in a single instance, even where the alcoholic treatment and many other kinds
had failed. I am not aware of its ever having been used as a medicine by the profession and, so far as I know,
I am the first to prepare and use it in the form of a tincture.”
Dr. Reed gave these cases: “( 1 ) Bessie A., aged six years, while playing in the yard on a farm, some twelve
miles in the country, was bitten in the hand by a rattlesnake which was killed a moment after by the mother of
the little girl who was attracted by the screams of the child.
“Sixteen hours after I arrived, everything having been done in the meantime that had ever been heard of by
the parents, even to applying a poultice the wound with entrails of a black chicken.
“The little sufferer was indeed, an object of pity. The hand and arm were swollen almost to bursting, the swelling
extending to the shoulder and spine, being of a blush black color as if dreadfully bruised. This discoloration
extended over the back to the hips. Skin hot and dry, face flushed, pulse quick and hard. Child unconscious.
“1 felt that the case was hopeless. But, through the earnest entreaties of the mother, I proceeded to do what I
could. Saturating a piece of cotton with the tincture I had prepared, I bound it on the wound, then dropping
twelve drops in a glass of water I directed that a teaspoonful be given every hour, the compress to be renewed
every hour also, until my return.
“I confess I had little hope of seeing my little patient alive again but on my return the following day I was much
rejoiced to find a decided change for the better in the condition of the little sufferer. The swelling was not nearly
so tense, the fever had subsided, the delirium gone and the danger seemed past. The treatment was continued
and a speedy and permanent recovery followed.
“(2) Burt Whitten, aged ten, while out in a marsh with a number of older boys gathering huckleberries, was
bitten in the right ankle by a rattler. He was so frightened when he saw the snake, as it bit him, that he ran all
the way home, a distance of nearly a mile, although the day was very hot.
“This patient came to my hands after the usual alcoholic treatment for twenty four hours by an allopathic
physician with the patient growing worse all the time. I found this patient in about the same condition as the
first.
“The leg and foot were enormously swollen and of the same general appearance, the foot, calf of the leg and
thigh were black, the whole body was very red, hot and dry, face dark red, pulse quick and hard, patient
delirious but would cry out if touched.
“Fifteen drops in a glass of water. Teaspoonful every hour with cotton saturated with the tincture applied to the
wound. In this case the change, I was informed by the father, was quite noticeable in two hours.
“The boy had been in a wild delirium all night and up to the time he received the first dose of Sisy. After the
second dose he
became quiet and in two hours the delirium had passed away. Under this treatment the patient was able to be
out on the streets again in four days, though the discoloration did not disappear for some time after.
“Many more cases might be given where this remedy has been given to both man and beast with the same
results.”
REFERENCES - Anshutz.
 ***SKATOLUM
(Skatol)
PHARMACY - skat. Skatolum. Skatol. Methyl-indol. Minerals, carbon compounds. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Belching. Dyspepsia. Headaches.
HOMEOPATHIC - Skatol represents the ultimate end of protein decomposition and is a constituent of human
feces. Sluggishness with no ambition. Acne with auto-intoxication dependent upon intestinal decomposition.
Stomach, abdominal symptoms and frontal headache.
MIND - Lack of concentration, impossible to study, despondent. Lack of ambition. Desire to be with people.
Irritable. Felt mean towards everyone. Desire to curse and swear.
Food - Appetite increased.
Head - Frontal headache, worse over left eye in the evening, better by short step.
Kidneys - Frequent, scanty, burning, difficult.
Mouth - Tongue coated. Foul taste. Salty taste to all cereals.
Sleep - Increased desire to sleep, wakes unrefreshed, half doped feeling.
Stomach - Belching.
Stool - Light, yellow, narrow, very offensive stool. Intestinal dyspepsia.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Indol., Bapt., Sulph.
REFERENCES Boericke.

***SKOOKUM CHUCK AQUA (Mineral Springs) PHARMACY - skook. Skookum chuck aqua. Mineral springs.
Skookum limechen chuck. Medical lake. Strong Medicine Water. Salts of water from Medical Lake near
Spokane, Wash. A lake in Western USA containing in grains per gallon: sodic carbonate 63.54, sodic chloride
16.37, sodic silicate 10.63, potassic chloride 9.24, ferrous carbonate. 526, Mag-c. 237, Calc. 186, aluminic
oxide. 175 with traces of lithic carbonate, Bor. and potassic sulphate. Trituration of the dried salt. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies, third trituration.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Breast, tumor. Catarrh. Coryza. Eczema. Hayfever. Lithemia. Otitis media. Ozaena.
Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Urticaria. Vaccination, effects.
HOMEOPATHIC - The medical and curative properties of this remarkable lake were known to the Native
Americans of the northwest; they have many legends and tribal history concerning the lake, and it was held in
much reverence by them.
The country around this lake was called “Sahala Lyee Illihe,” or “Sacred Grounds,” and no matter how hostile
the tribes were to each other no members j ourneying to or from the “Skookum Limechen Chuck,” or “strong
medicine water,” were ever molested.
“In the Skookum Chuck we have a remedy for all our ai Iments. We only have to bathe i n and drink its water
and we are made well. If we sign the treaty we will forever offend the Great Spirit, we will sign away our mother
and she will cry. Her tears will dry up these lakes and we will be hungry and sick. We will go the Skookum
Chuck only to find that its water have disappeared.”
It is an anti-psoric remedy. Affinity for the skin and mucus membranes. Skin disorders. Eczema. Urticaria.
Lithemia. Vaccinal eczema. Dry skin. Hay fever. Profuse coryza and constant sneezing. Catarrh. Profuse,
ichorous, cadaverously smelling discharge. Otitis media.
Back - Heaviness in sacrum.
Food - Appetite increased.
Limbs - Severe rheumatic pains in limbs.
Nose - Profuse coryza with constant sneezing as in hay fever.
Skin - Eczema. Urticaria. Dry skin.
COMMENTS - In the U. S. Med. Investigator, 1889, Dr. W. D. Gentry told the story of a Frenchman passing
by the lake, before the properties of the water became known to the white men, with a drove of sheep afflicted
with a skin disease called “the scab.”
As soon as the sheep saw the water they ran to it. but would not drink. They stood in the water for some time,
and in a few days they were well of the “scab.” The Frenchman was suffering with rheumatism and decided to
try the water for his disease. He was steadily cured.
Stories of marvelous cures were reported by the Native Americans and by seeing those who had been taken
there on litter, appearing at the point of death, return in health and vigor.
The cure of many cases of inveterate skin disease is on record, the external use of Skook. soap or ointment
has been employed as well as the internal administration.
 W. D. Ingalls reported the case of Mrs. D„ 48, who had eczema of her feet. Fissured skin, exuding an acrid
secretion. So excessively sore that the patient had not been able to wear shoes or walk any distance for two
years.
Skook. 2x was given internally, an ointment of a drachm to the ounce of vaseline applied and Skookum soap
used for washing. In two months the patient was able to wear shoes and in three months the feet were well.
Mrs. H., 23, had a benign growth in left breast, noticed eight months. No history of tuberculosis or cancer in
family. Skook. was gi ven for the first week, one grain of 1 x every four hours, for the second week, two grains
of Skook. 2x every four hours, for the next seven weeks, five-grain powders of Skook. 3x, when the patient
was cured.
Mr. J., had chronic nasal catarrh, discharge greenish yellow having odor of ozaena, was greatly relieved and
apparently on the way to cure.
B. F. Bailey reported the cure of Mrs.
X., 40 of lithemic diathesis, never free from eczematic trouble for years. At times much rheumatism. Not
infrequently the rheumatism disappears and is immediately followed by styes on the eyelids.
Formerly treated allopathically and also homeopathically. Skook. 3x every four hours. Improvement soon
showed itself and the patient was well in three months and remained so.
Mrs. Y., 26, lithemic with flushed face and yellowish background. Urine, 1030 and with marked uric acid
deposits. Much difficulty of digestion. Great dryness of skin, especially of scalp. Hair falling out to such an
extent that baldness was feared.
Skook. 3x was given every four hours. Hair ceased to fall out. The heated, congested feeling of head and face
disappeared and the patient became well.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Tab. Compare: (1) Nat-c., Nat-m. (2) Skin disorders, Graph., Med., Maland.,
Vac. (3) Saxon. - appears has remarkable cleansing, deodorizing and soothing properties for the skin. Eczema,
scalds, burns, sores and hemorrhoids.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Slag
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - slag. Slag. Pulverized slag. Blast-iron-furnace cinder. Slag silica. Silico-sulphocalcite of
alumina. Slag was analyzed and found to contain the following: Silica, Alumina, Calcium, Sulphur, part of these
occur as Calc-s., Ferrum, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Manganum. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Constipation. Debility. Diarrhea. Flatulence. Headache. Hemorrhoids. Housemaid’s knee.
Lumbago. Spleen, disorders. Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Slag was introduced into medicine by J. Meredith who gave the 6x trituration to a patient
suffering from housemaid’s knee and in addition to relieving this it took away “a dreadful anal itching,
hemorrhoids and constipation as if by magic.”
Meredith confirmed the rectal power of Slag by experiments on his own person. Acting on Meredith’s
suggestion, George Herring instituted a proving with the 3x on himself and others.
Herring’s only symptom was a creeping irritation of the skin or under the skin in the umbilical region, sufficiently
severe to keep him awake.
Drowsiness in evening. Digestive weakness and flatulence. Soreness of the anus. Constipation and diarrhea.
Hemorrhoids with anal itching and soreness. Tuberculosis.
Housemaid’s knee. Lumbago. Spleen disorders. Spleen pain and stitches in heart. A pain (dull, heavy
sensation) alternated between inter-scapular region and spleen. Stiffness at back of head, neck and pain
between shoulders. Dull, stupefying frontal headache.
COMMENTS - One prover, in which Slag produced no symptoms, was cured of flatulent distention in the
evening and an oppressive feeling over the heart. Another prover had constipation relieved, but Slag produced
“soreness of anus.”
In a delicate woman of tubercular history, took Slag 3x twice a day, and experienced diarrhea, debility, quick
pulse, lumbago with pain in back, distention of stomach, so that she had to loosen her dress, profuse night-
sweat, cough and expectoration. Phos., Ph-ac., Carb. v. were given to this patient in succession and all helped.
Another proving of Slag was made by F. C. B. The prover was age 33, rather dark, nervo-bilious, had
chronically enlarged tonsils and tendency to colds in the head. He took Slag by way of experiment, hoping to
cure his tonsils.
RELATIONS - Effects were relieved by: Phos., Ph-ac., Carb-v. Compare: (1) Constipation, flatulence, Lyc.,
Carb-v., Sulph. (2) Anal symptoms, Graph., Nit-ac. (3) Intolerance of tight clothing, Lach. (4) Housemaid’s
knee, Stict., Apis., Sep.
 REFERENCES - Clarke.
