name: Sol
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol. Sol. Sunlight. Lactose is exposed to concentrated sun’s rays and stirred with a glass rod
until saturated. Potencies made by Fincke. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Backache. Burns. Cancer. Cataracts. Chills. Constipation. Dermatitis. Faintness.
Freckles. Headaches. Heat, stroke. Lupus. Menses, premature. Paralysis. Photophobia. Radiation, sickness.
Skin, cancers. Skin, disorders. Snowblindness. Sunburns. Sunstroke.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Finsen, of Copenhagen, revived and confirmed much of the ancient light-therapy. O. V.
Thayer published, in 1893, a series of cases in which he had used concentrated rays of sunlight (solar cautery)
including cases of skin cancer, rodent ulcer, parasitic diseases, moles, small wens, and birthmarks.
H. T. Webster gave details ofacase of epithelioma in which the growth was removed by solar cautery and a
scarcely perceptible scar left. Sunlight has cured skin cancers
' and lupus in the hands of Finsen.
Potentized sunlight has been used for sun dermatitis, heat stroke, cancer and radiation. Chronic sun
headaches ( Verat., Glon., Nat- c, Nat-m.). Violent headache from vertex down to forehead with hot sensation
in face. Keynote photophobia. Very sensitive to sunshine.
Sunburns easily. Never well since severe sunburn. Sunlight damage of the eyes, from over-exposure, snow-
blindness, sunblindness. Cataracts. Radiation exposure with nausea, vomiting, hair loss, emaciation (Cadm-
s., X-ray.).
Mental excitement and anxiousness, at first with trembling of the heart, finally remaining in the stomach pit.
Faintness, prostration and general stiffening up of the whole system, the body strength seems more equalized.
Spasm coming with sunrise and ceasing with sunset. Some spasms appearing at sunset.
MIND-Decisiveness and assertive. Impatient to make decisions. Cheerful. Urge to be healthy, to eat fruit.
Mental restlessness. In control, then out of control. Irresolution. Light headed and mentally disorientated.
Loses his way in well-known streets.
Depression, tearful. Sensitive. Suspicious. Irritable, impatient and frustrated. Irritability over trifles. Fastidious.
Argumentative and angry. Nasty. Desire to bang head and scream. Escapism.
Excitement. Anxiety with trembling in heart. Anxiety in solar plexus. Anxiety if somebody comes towards her.
Nervous, as if ail the nerves were trembling. Very sensitive and easily frightened. Frightened on the approach
of anyone coming toward them. Delusion of being pursued.
Abdomen - Anxiety in solar plexus. Swollen sensation on right side. Distention and hardness. Abdominal
cramps with menses. Cramping pain on right side, better bending double. Griping pain, like diarrhea. Foul
flatulence. Sensation as after childbirth or at conception (with great excitement).
Back - Backaches. Pain in left side of back, hip joint area. Heat rash, red blobs, on back. Spots on back during
menses. Itchiness, worse evening and in bed, better scratching.
Breasts - Tender, swollen breasts, before menses. Sharp pain in left breast.
Chest - Sensation as if a weight on chest. Chest very tight with wheezing. Armpits perspired without exertion.
Sharp pain, top of rib cage.
Ears - Sharp shooting pain from left ear to nose, continued at intervals for some time. Partial deafness.
Eyes - Painful eyes from glare of sunlight. Photophobia. Light offends eyes. Snow-blindness. Diminished
sensitivity of eyes, odd-blindness. Blurry vision with headaches. Suffusion of veins, of sclerotica. Cataracts.
Stinging pains. Sensation of swelling, as if eyes would force themselves out of sockets. Puffiness around the
eyes.
Face - Jaws rigidly set as in trismus. Painful large spot on cheek. Pressing pain with
sensation of heat in face. Perspiration on face, warm and tingly. Hot sweat on face, cold to touch. Dripping
perspiration.
Female - Achy and bloated before menses. Diarrhea before menses, on going to bed. Menses six to seven
days too soon. Menses, bright red blood. Menses slow, spotting. Very heavy menses, bright red blood,
occasional clots, abdominal cramps. Sharp pain in uterus which turned to cramp, worse bending forward.
Spots on back during menses. Green leucorrhea at night, with yellow-brown diarrhea. Itching genitalia, some
discharge.
Food - Diminished appetite and thirst. Loss of appetite first thing in the morning. Desire for hot chocolate.
Desire for juicy, refreshing things, oranges and grapefruit. Desire for cheese and salty foods. Desire for meat,
prawns. Thirst, desires cold sweet drinks, lime juice. Thirstless, sips lemon squash, which relieves the throat.
Head - Light headed and mentally disorientated. Violent headache from vertex down to forehead. Headache
 with the excitement and anxiousness at stomach pit. Left sided headache. Pain in forehead, as if forehead
would crush itself down upon the eyes. Headache from sunshine on bare head, better by laying a glass of
water on solar plexus. Very sensitive to sunshine on the vertex. Extreme painfulness if the sunshine strikes
the bare head. Violent stitches in brain. Stitching pain if she does not gain the shade, stomachache and nausea
follow. Sensation of undulating or floating in head after mental excitement. Instantaneous shock to brain,
followed by prostration and a scalding sensation on top of head. Excessive perspiration of head and neck.
Heart - Anxiety with trembling in heart. Weakness about heart.
Kidneys - Increased urine though drinking less, night as well as day. Polyuria, urinates five times in night.
Nocturia. Urine and stool invariably suspended.
Limbs - Drawing through all his limbs after rising. Right side, arm and foot, weak as from partial paralysis.
Pain in left elbow. Hands and feet cold. The back of hand
exposed to sunshine feels warm, while at same time a coolness appears in palm and runs up whole arm into
temple. Cool, refreshed sensations. Pains as if bruised. Pain like toothache deep inside left hip, better as day
progressed, better walking. Fingers numb with cold, chilled to bone.
Lungs - Wheezing, difficulty in breathing, before bedtime. Wheezing on exhalation and inhalation. Coughs on
talking. Coughed up green catarrh and blood, worse evening.
Male - Loss of libido. Increased libido.
Modalities - Ameliorated by cloudy weather. Better hot bath, when chilled to bone. Better short naps, sleep.
Better bending double, sitting down. Eyes better hot flannel. Throat better cold sweet drinks. Headaches better
pressure, cold application, orange juice. Worse sunlight (Nat-m.), from sunrise to sunset. Spasms coming with
sunrise and ceasing with sunset. Worse from standing. Eyes are worse from wind.
Mouth - Offensive breath. Brown tongue, unpleasant taste on tongue. Food tastes like something she cannot
tell. Food is more palatable if put in the sunshine. Dry mouth in morning. Sore gum, right side, top of mouth.
Nail biting. Stupid, cannot articulate a word. Articulates with difficulty.
Nose - Sneezing with a little sore throat, as if she had taken cold. Stopped up, right nostril blocked completely.
Perspiration - Perspiration streaming out of stomach pit over whole body. Perspiration under armpits with no
exertion.
Rectum - Constipation. Pale colored stool. Diarrhea at night in bed, yellow/brown, painless with green
leucorrhea. Diarrhea on going to bed just before menses. Loose stools. Pains better stool. Hemorrhoids.
Skin - Freckles. Itching, red skin. Red blotches from sunlight. Skin sensitive to sunlight. Sunburns easily.
Never well since severe sunburn. Skin cancer. Dermatitis, often with cold limbs, degenerates into megrim.
Nevi. Painful spot on cheek. Spots on back during menses. Peeling of skin on left hand.
Sleep - Sleeplessness until 3 a.m. to 4 a.m. Head very much excited, could not sleep for hours. Great
sleepiness all through the head and not merely in the eyes, heavy, sound sleep all through night. Sound sleep,
oversleeping. Dreams of being lost, of travel. Tired on waking. Tired all day with irritability, worse early evening,
better sleeping. Sleepiness, better short naps.
Stomach - Anxiety in solar plexus. Heat in pit of stomach. Empty feeling in stomach, as if she had not eaten
anything substantial yesterday and today. Sensation of faintness and vacuity in stomach pit. Nausea, no
hunger, desires cold drinks. Nausea on waking, worse as morning progressed. Nausea after lunch. Slight
inclination to vomit, or actual vomiting. Desire to vomit but unable to.
Teeth - Grinding of teeth as in helminthic spasms.
Temperature - Cold shivers with aching neck glands. Chilled to bone, very cold. An agreeable coolness
extends over whole body. Chills. Running chills of increasing sensation of cold in all limbs from holding wires
partially exposed to the sun. Shivering. Felt cold in night, drew up more cover and perspired. Congestive chill
from exposure to sun right after drinking cold water freely.
Throat - Swollen glands. Yellow ulcer on right side of throat, no pain. Swollen throat, white pus on left side.
Sore, achy throat, on waking, desire for cold drinks. Sore throat better eating, worse after dinner. Catch in
throat after sudden dry mouth in morning. Sensation of loose skin flopping on back of throat on swallowing.
Catarrh.
Vertigo - Vertigo on waking at 6 am, better lying, worse closing eyes. Dizziness with nausea, worse standing,
sitting. Dizziness with nausea, much better lying, sleeping.
COMMENTS - In 1880, Swan published a pathogenesis which contained information obtained from four
provers and from Reichenbach’s experiences from hypersensitives. The common effects of strong sunlight,
such as sneezing, freckling and sunstroke, may be added to the list.
Dr. Thayer, in 1893 in southern California, wrote a paper on sunlight for a homeopathic journal. He described
how to “Concentrate the sun rays to a diseased part until slightly burned or charred and then wait until it heals
and then repeat the procedure.”
 He claimed to have cured all kinds of cancers, removed birthmarks, tattoos, warts, sebaceous cysts, ulcers,
varicose veins and all other types of benign growths. “Unlike other caustics, it can be applied upon the most
delicate of tissues and it causes only slight irritation and most heal with only the slightest scar.”
Dr. Thayer coined the term “solar cauterization.” A magnifying glass was used and the sunbeam was focused
right on the skin cancer, until a burning sensation was felt, then stopped. This would be repeated once or twice
a day. After a week or ten days the melanoma would fall off and it would heal without a scar.
Thayer had a whole practice based on the magnifying glass and focusing the sunlight in 1893 and very few
homeopaths used his methods.
Dr. Foubister revived interest in Sol in its potentized form as an antidote for radiation poisoning from radiation
therapy with cancer patients.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aeon., Bell., Glon., Gels, and other sunstroke remedies. Compare: (1) Luna,
Elect., M-aust., X-ray.
(2)    Cadm-s., radiation poisoning. (2) Dislike of sun, Lach., Nat-c., Nat-m., Glon.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Daws. Foubister. Murphy. Scriven.

name: Solaninum Aceticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - solin. Solaninum aceticum. Solanium aceticum aut purum. An alkaloid obtained from various
Solanums, especially dulcamara and nigrum, also from the potato plant. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Lungs, paralysis. Tetanus. Ticklishness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Solin. is obtained from many of the Solanaceae. and especially from Dulc. It exists in
potatoes, and under certain conditions of germination, potatoes may contain a poisonous amount.
An accident of that kind occurred in soldiers at Pfuhl who were supplied with potatoes containing about 24
percent Solin. Sixty-six soldiers had marked poisoning symptom including shivering, fever, vomiting, syncope
and in one case convulsions. Skin and conjunctiva were tinged yellow.
Clarke’s first acquaintance with Solin. was through seeing the effect of Solin. 2c in solution given by Dr. Hughes
to a diabetic and semi-paralytic man of 60 who had frequent threat of respiratory paralysis with accumulations
of mucus which he was unable to expel. Solin., more than any other remedy, rescued him from danger and
prolonged his life.
Solin. was proved by Clarus and Schroff, among others. Slowed and oppressed respiration was a marked
feature. Respiration was slowed in inverse proportion to the increase in the pulse rate.
Cerebrospinal irritation, hyperesthesia and convulsions, worse by touch. Fainting. Weakness. Sensitiveness
to light, noise and touch. Skin more easily tickled than usual. In animals, the hind limbs were rigid and paralyzed
and in the pro vers the lower limbs were weakened.
MIND - Stupefaction without previous excitement. Fainting.
Abdomen - Rumbling in abdomen.
Chest - Convulsions of thorax, which were associated tonic spasms of limbs.
Eyes - Pupils slightly contracted.
Head - Vertigo. Cerebrospinal meningitis.
Head hot. heavy, dull, painful. Pain in occiput.
Heart - Pulse increased in rapidity, weak, thready. Pulse and respiration slowed. Increased pulse rate with
slowed respiration.
Kidneys - Albumen in urine.
Limbs - Weakness of lower limbs. Slight tonic spasms of lower limbs.
Lungs - Hoarseness. Breathing is slow, superficial, difficult and oppressed, distressed, especially on
inspiration. Moist rattle during inspiration. Frequent violent outcry. Masses of mucus in larger air
passages. Paralysis of respiration.
Mouth - Salivation. Bitter taste. The pure alkaloid has a cooling, acid and salt taste and when chewed causes
a glutinous sensation in pharynx and throat with scraping which extends to stomach, where it becomes a
peculiar sticking pain.
Skin - Yellow discoloration of skin. Skin dry. Hyperesthesia, creeping along spine when touching the skin,
more easily tickled than natural. Itching.
Sleep - Frequent yawning. Great sleepiness with inability to sleep. Sleep restless, frequently disturbed by
frightful dreams. Sleep frequently interrupted, without dreams.
Stomach - Constant belchings. Nausea and diarrhea and vomiting. Nausea, violent ineffectual efforts to vomit.
About 5 p.m., vomiting three times without previous nausea or pain or any intestinal symptoms.
Temperature - Limbs cold. Shivering, fever, vomiting and syncope. Profuse perspiration without weakness.
 Throat - Scraping in throat.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Dulc., Bell., Sol-c., Sol-nig., Sol-tub. or Sol-t-ae. (2) In respiratory paralysis, Dulc.,
Bell. (3) Sleepy but cannot sleep, Bell. (4) Hyperesthesia, Nux-v, Tetox.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Solanum Carolinense
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-c. Solanum carolinense. Horse-nettle. N. 0. Solanaceae. The fresh, ripe berries are
macerated in twice their weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
HERBAL - In 1889 Dr. Napier called attention to Solanum carolinense as a remedy for the treatment of
epilepsy, stating that it was used as a domestic remedy in for convulsions and “that he had successfully
prescribed it in his practice.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Sol-c. has convulsions and epilepsy, twenty to forty-drop doses is of great value in grand
mal of idiopathic epilepsy, where the disease has begun beyond age of childhood, hystero-epilepsy, also in
whooping cough.
COMMENTS - Dr. Charles S. Potts of the University of Pennsylvania, contributed a paper to The Gazette,
Dec., 1895, on the remedy, giving several cases.
H. T., male, aged thirteen years. Idiopathic epilepsy, had his first spell five years ago, averaged one paroxysm
daily. Sol-c. was first given in 10 drops doses without effect. When increased to 25 drops, the spells were
lighter in severity, but occurred about as often.
The dose was finally increased to a teaspoonful four times daily. After being put upon this dose he was under
observation six weeks during which time he had six seizures much lighter in severity.
T. H., male, aged twenty-eight years. He had epileptic seizures for three years, following an injury to the head
which rendered him unconscious, but produced no other visible injury. Since this, however, had almost
constant headache. The first spell was six months after the injury and have been frequent after, averaging
three to four weekly, of an ordinary type.
Sol-c. in 40-drops doses three times daily was given, the spells at once decreased in frequency and severity.
During the last six weeks he was under observation he only had three spells, very mild in type.
A. N., male, aged thirty years. First spell
one year ago, have since occurred every two weeks, good deal of headache. Sol-c. 30c drops three times a
day. No spells for one month and headache ceased. He then stopped attendance.
J. D., female, aged eighteen years. First spell when thirteen years old, had one spell a month at the time of
her menstrual period. About a week before her next period, she was given Sol-c. 40 drops three times a day
and escaped the usual spell. The following month however, she had one.
I. K., female, aged twenty-five years. Nocturnal epilepsy forpast three years, about one spell a month. While
using Sol-c. 40 drops three times a day, went three weeks longer than usual without a spell. The dose was
then increased to 1 fluid drachm, she then ceased her visit.
F. S., female, aged twelve years. First spell five weeks before her visit, had been having them daily since. Sol-
c. 30 drops ordered, this dose was gradually increased to 1 fluid drachm. During the three months that she
was under observation her spells averaged in number about one a week.
H. B., male, aged eighteen years. First convulsion at age of ten years, then had none until three months before
visit, had general convulsions about once daily since. Sol-c. 40 drops ordered. He was only under observation
nine days, having during that time four spells, much milder in character.
A. C., female, aged fifteen years. First convulsion one year before, they had been increasing in frequency, up
to one about every three days. During the three weeks she was taking Sol-c. 30 drops three times a day she
had one spell, occurring during the third week.
H. K., male, aged eighteen years. First spell when fourteen years old. Every three or four days had several
attacks in succession, an average of about one daily. While taking Sol-c. 40 drops, afterwards increased to
 teaspoonful-doses, he had twelve in thirty-eight days, an average of a little less than one in three days, going
six without having any.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

name: Solanum Mammosum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-m. Solanum mammosum. Apple of sodom. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of fresh ripe fruit.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Coxalgia. Coughing. Hemoptysis. Imtabi lity. Sleep, abnormal. Thought, difficult. Tobacco, effects.
Twitching.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hering is the authority for Sol-m. The chief symptoms are irritability and inability to think.
Uneasiness and inability to keep quiet. Sleepiness without being able to sleep, a kind a stupor worse at time
of flood tide, at the full moon, better with ebb tide. Hawking, of blood-streaked mucus. Sensitiveness to tobacco
(Ign.).
MIND - Irritability. Becomes exasperated at what he thinks may happen. Mental confusion. Inability for
continuous thought. Difficulty expressing ideas.
Back - Twitching of large muscle below right scapula, as if the flesh were pinched up by the hand and shaken
back and forth.
Limbs - Sticking pain in left hip joint that made him quite lame, frequently during and after walking,
disappearing after standing and sitting down.
Lungs - Mucus hawked from the larynx contains streaks of bright blood.
Rectum - No stool, stool occurred later than usual and after much pressure.
Skin - Causes blotches over whole body from poisoning.
Sleep - Great weariness and desire to sleep without ability to sleep, followed by slumbering without real sleep.
Deep sleep, from which he awoke and could not collect his senses for a long time and remained long in an
irresolute condition. Sleepy in evening and sleeps well all night, even after afternoon sleeping. Dreams of death
with violent weeping.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Solanum Nigrum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-n. Solanum nigrum. Black nightshade. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Blindness. Chorea. Convulsion. Coryza. Delirium. Headaches. Heartburn.
Hydrocephalus. Mania. Meningitis. Night-terrors. Parotiditis. Peritonitis. Psoriasis. Puerperal convulsions.
Scarlatina. Skin, disorders. Smallpox. Stammering speech. Tetanus. Trismus. Tympanitis. Typhoidfever.
Ulcers. Varicose veins. Vertigo.
HERBAL - Sol-n. is a common weed found in waste places. It has white flowers and black berries.
Green’s Herbal recorded that “The leaves applied externally ease the pain and abate inflammation. Too large
aquantity occasions violent sickness and headaches, giddiness, drowsiness and other dangerous symptoms.
The Arabs apply the leaves to burns and ulcers, skin diseases and scrofulous and cancerous affections, they
are diaphoretic, diuretic and purgative.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Hale said some country practitioners used Sol-n. with much success under the impression
that it was “an indigenous Belladonna,” having been misled by the name “nightshade.”
Hale verified its use in meningitis and headache. Also in scarlatina when the eruption is blotchy. He justly
pointed out the close affinity of Sol-n. with Bell.: Delirium, headache, flushed face, sparkling eyes, pains coming
and going suddenly, fiery rashes, burning skin and sweat.
“Frightful” headaches. Splitting, throbbing, bursting, piercing headaches, worse by least movement of head,
least movement after sitting, light, noise, stooping. Headache is worse in a warm room and better in open air.
Great sensitiveness to cold air.
Marked action on head and eyes. Brain irritation during dentition. Restlessness of a violent and convulsive
nature. Formication with contraction of limbs. Ergotism with tetanic spasms and stiffness of whole body with
mania. Black appearance, bruised feeling all over the body. Chronic intestinal toxemia.
MIND - Mania. Furious delirium, characterized by the cephalic cry, efforts to escape and stammering speech.
Night-terrors. Complete cessation of the mental faculties due to headaches.
Chest - Pain in left side, sore to touch.
Eyes - Pain over both eyes. Alternate dilatation and contraction of pupils, weak sight, floating spots.
 Head - Terrible headaches and complete cessation of the mental faculties. Congestive headaches (Bell.).
Splitting, throbbing, bursting, piercing pains. Headaches at 10 a.m. Headache causes him to close eyes.
Headaches, worse by least movement of head, light, noise, stooping.
Lungs - Constrictive feeling in chest with difficult breathing, cough with tickling in throat. Expectoration thick,
yellow.
Modalities - Better closing eyes. Worse by touch, motion. Worse moving head, beginning to move after sitting.
Worse walking (inclines to left), misstep. Worse swallowing. Worse morning on waking, light. Worse bright
sunshine (eyes).
Nose - Acute coryza, profuse, watery discharge from right nostril, left stopped up with chilly sensation,
alternating with heat.
Sensations - Brain as if swimming. As if things moving in a circle, when stooping. As if brain shaking about in
skull, on moving head. As if head would split. As from a blow on forehead. As if sand in eyes. As if splinter in
right tonsil. Tongue as if scalded. Pains come and go suddenly. Symptoms extend upward. Right upper, left
lower. Alternate coldness and heat.
Sleep - Night terrors.
Temperature - Alternation of coldness and heat. Scarlet fever, eruption in spots, large and vivid.
Vertigo - Vertigo with a terrible headache and complete cessation of the mental faculties. The vertigo is worse
on moving the head. Sensation as if the bed was being rapidly turned in a circle. Inclines to left on walking.
COMMENTS - The provings and symptoms of poisoning cases are unusually distinctive. Tendency to
blackness of the skin. Painful swelling, it enlarges, becomes shiny, hard and deep red and in several places,
quite black.
Marked dilatation of the pupils (Bell.). Dryness of mouth and throat. Spasms, convulsions and tetanic rigidity
of the whole body. “In the midst of these convulsions the children frequently stretch out their little hands, then
carry them eagerly to their mouths and go through the motions of chewing and swallowing.”
A patient of Cooper’s, after one dose of the tincture, patches of psoriasis on the knees, elbows and forehead,
scaly with red irritating spots at roots of hair disappeared. The day after taking a single dose of tincture, another
patient of Cooper’s had, “Head feels full across forehead, eyes heavy and forehead burns, could not apply
himself to work.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bell. (2) Sol- m. - pain in left hip joint. (3) Sol-t. - cramps in calves and contraction
of fingers, spitting through closed teeth. (4) Sol-v. recommended in facial paralysis. (5) Sol-a. - threatening
paralysis of the lungs in the course of bronchitis in the aged and children must cough a long time before able
to raise expectoration. (6) Sol-ps. - acute pains in lower abdomen, Sol-t. (7) Aegrotans - diseased potato. (8)
Sol-t. Potato berries - cramps in the calves of the legs and fingers.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Solanum Oleraceum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-o. Solanum oleraceum. Juquerioba. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of flowers. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Breast-milk, profuse. Breasts, swelling. Catarrh. Glands, swelling. Herpes Leucorrhea. Pustules.
Sleep excessive. Styes. Urticaria.
HOMEOPATHIC - Mure reported that this plant is herbaceous, stem somewhat woody, the upper branches
being covered with short and crooked thorns. It grows on the shores around Rio Janeiro in damp and shady
places.
The most remarkable symptom of the proving was “swelling of the breasts with profuse effusion of milk”
occurring in a woman of 60. “Pain and swelling of face and throat with inflammation.” “Cold feeling in left chest
after drinking.” Drowsiness with headache. The generally deranged sleep of the other Solanaceae.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Solanum Tuberosum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-t. Solanum tuberosum. Potato. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of the berries. Tincture of green
potatoes. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Colic. Cramps. Diarrhea. Faintness. Headache. Iritis, rheumatic. Stammering.
Trismus. Tumors. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The poisonous properties of the berries and leaves of the potato plant are well known, and
the tubers are popularly believed to have anti-scorbutic properties when eaten as food. Under some conditions
 the tubers have been known to contain poisonous quantities of Solanin.
The symptoms are the result of eating new potatoes, green potatoes, an extract and the berries. The last
proved fatal in a number of instances. Sickness and diarrhea with tenesmus, giddiness, dilated pupils and
indistinct vision. Tossing to and fro in bed. A paralytic condition of the tongue, cramps and tetanic spasms.
General rigidity. Patient is exceedingly weak. Faintness.
MIND - Almost lost consciousness.
Abdomen - Violent colic and vomiting. Pain in bowels. Tumors.
Eyes - Eyes deep in sockets. Pupils dilated. Staring look. Vision indistinct.
Face - Hippocratic face. Anxious expression.
Female - Tumors around cervix, uterus.
Limbs - Cramps, especially in calves with spasmodic contractions of fingers and thumbs.
Lungs - Difficult breathing. Respiration is hurried, irregular, at times suppressed, usually short and incomplete,
only seldom slow and sighing.
Mouth - Constantly spitting through the closed teeth, viscid, frothy phlegm. Tongue covered with brown, moist
fur. Tongue is heavy and difficult to move, hardly able to articulate. Speech thick. Speechless.
Pulse - Pulse small, rapid, scarcely perceptible.
Rectum - Diarrhea with tenesmus. Tends to relax bowels.
Skin - Skin livid.
Stomach - Epigastric region sensitive to pressure. Felt sick, a darkness over her eyes, skin cold, cramped all
over. Violent retching followed by vomiting and diarrhea.
Temperature - Skin cold. Face, chest and limbs cold. Skin beaded with cold, clammy sweat.
Vertigo - Vertigo, headache, stupor.
COMMENTS - Cooper relieved with a single dose of Sol-t. tincture a case of rheumatic iritis.
Burnett cured a case of tumors feeling like masses of potatoes in the abdomen with Sol-t. It also assisted him
in the cure of a case of tumors all around the cervix uterus. Urt-u. finished this cure.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Solin. (2) In paralysis of tongue, Caust., Dulc. (3) Iritis, Bell. (4) Stammering
speech, Merc., Stram.
REFERENCES
 Clarke.

name: Solanum Tuberosum Aegrotans
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-t-ae. Solanum tuberosum aegrotans. Rotten potato. Diseased potato due to several fungi.
Tincture of the affected tubers. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Anal, prolapse. Breasts, painful. Constipation. Nosebleed. Headache. Ileus. Menses interrupted.
Noma. Pruritus vulva. Rectal, prolapse. Scalp, painful. Sciatica. Scurvy. Tenesmus. Tongue cracked.
Vertebra, pain, pulsation.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to the Treasury of Botany, the “potato murrain” is characterized by “the rapid
putrescence of the leaves and haulm, which is first indicated by the presence of a little mold, Peronospora
infestans, which preys upon the tissues, spreading rapidly in every direction. The tubers also exhibit brown
spots on their surface and within their tissues and according to circumstances decay with greater or less
rapidity.”
In 1846, the sudden inroad of this disease led to the famine in Ireland, resulting in the death of thousands.
Mure made the first proving of Sol-t-ae., using a potato “in an entire state of decomposition without, however,
being completely rotten.” Effects of eating diseased potatoes, some of them fatal, have been observed and
these have been added to Mure’s.
Dark skin. Breath and odor of body are offensive. Excruciating muscular pains. Cold water causes shock. The
urine has an oily pellicle. Prolapse of the rectum and anus. Tumors of rectum look like decayed potato.
Dreams of pools of blood. Irritability.
MIND - Quarrelsome, irritable mood. Bad temper. Dread of work. Hypochondriac mood. Fancies she is
miserable, and dwells much on the future. Wants to enjoy achange of scenery. Crowd of ideas. Attention is
easily disturbed by other things. Confusion of mind.
Abdomen - Painfulness of abdomen to contact along the median line. Belly hard, swollen, dropsical. Pain after
eating, spasmodic pains, as though the bowels became twisted together, rumbling. Pain, as if sprained, in right
groin. Stitch in right groin near inguinal ring. Flatulence.
Back - Violent beating in spine, early, when lying. Prickling sensation in spine. Stinging pain. Sensation of
weariness in whole back. Stiffness in muscles of back. Tingling in sacrum. Prickling in psoas muscles. Pain in
 lumbar vertebra, impeding walking. Swelling of muscles of neck.
Breasts - Breasts are painful, especially when raising arm.
Chest - Oppression in chest. Congestions to chest. Tearing in chest. Prickling as from a thousand pins on the
inner surface of sternum. Violent stitching pain above right breast. Acute pain in the sides like a stitch.
Ears - Ringing in the left ear.
Eyes - Congestion of the conjunctiva. Prickling and burning in eyes. Profuse lachrymation, on waking. Burning
in lids. Prickling about the lids, the surface of which is red. Spasmodic contraction and twitching of left upper
lid.
Face - Face pale, bloodless. Swollen, especially about eyelids, nearly closing them. Face hot and red. Red
pimples on cheeks. Desquamation of face. Bluish-black, fetid ulcer of left cheek. Upper lip is bleeding, cracked.
Female - Suppression of the menses. Menstrual blood rose-colored. Menses smelling of foul fish. Small
pimples and intolerable itching of labia. Burning and itching in vagina. Flatulence presses on uterus.
Spasmodic pains in uterus. Twisting pains through uterus. Feeling of dislocation in hip joint with pain in womb
after a slight exertion.
Food - Canine hunger. Salt taste. Taste of raw potatoes. Food tastes as bitter as gall. Great desire for spirits
and oranges. Burning thirst.
Head - Heat in head, evening. Heaviness of head. Catarrhal dullness. Lancinations, as if brain would burst
open. Headache at noon, worse by the smell of spirits. Sensation of water splashing in head. Painful
sensitiveness of scalp and roots of hair, cannot bear combing.
Heart - Weight and pain in heart region. Lancinations in heart. Palpitations of heart. Pulse is irregular,
sometimes weak, hard and tense.
Kidneys - Region of bladder distended. Difficult urination. Urine reddish, mingled with mucus. Urine is very
thick, soapy, turbid, of a dingy yellow with copious white sediment. Constant urination while at stool. Heat and
pain in urethra after urinating.
Limbs - Sense of weariness in all the limbs. Inclination to stretch. Joints swollen and very painful. Acute pains
in hip joint caused by least motion. Feeling of dislocation of hip joint. Legs edematous. Shuddering in right leg.
Heat in hands.
Lungs - Constriction and difficulty breathing. Constant involuntary sighing. In trachea, tearing, prickling with
cough. Cough with expectoration of yellow mucus, at night. Dry cough, day and night. Expectoration of lumps
of black blood, early in the morning. After eating choking and difficult breathing caused by dryness of mouth.
Hoarseness on walking.
Male - Weight in right testicle all day.
Modalities - Worse by touch, pressure, walking. Worse from smell of alcohol. Worse at 5 p.m., sleeping.
Headache is worse on waking, from working.
Mouth - Dry mouth. Breath horribly fetid. Tongue pale, coated white or yellowish white. Tongue yellowish along
the median line. Tongue swollen, cracked, early in the morning. Prickling in right half of tongue.
Nose - Repeated sneezing, followed by feeble cough. Pressure at root of nose. Nosebleeds. Smell of blood.
Rectum - Alternate protrusion and retraction of rectum during stool. Contraction of anal sphincter. Prolapsed
rectum and anus. Acute pain in anus. Great heat in anus. Frequent urging to stool. Has to strain until tears
come. Hard, large, lumpy stool, with violent burning in anus and rectum. Constipation. Copious greenish-yellow
diarrhea. Violent colic previous to stool.
Sensations - Of water splashing on head, as if brain were leaping in skull (on stooping). As of something
sticking in throat. As if there were a fleshy growth in throat. As if a spring unrolled in left hypochondrium. As if
a hollow body were turning rapidly in chest. Of stoppage in trachea. Of something becoming detached from
sacrum.
Skin - Skin is tender. Rose-colored patches appear and as suddenly vanish. Small red pimples cause violent
itching.
Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness. Sleepless. Restless sleep. Starting from sleep, as in a fright. Amorous dreams.
Dreams about men who become transformed to talking animals. Confused dreams, about fires, revolution,
corpses, thieves.
Stomach - Pain in stomach, with red face, after breakfast. Spasmodic pains, griping- tearing at night. Acidity,
bitterness, and gulping-up, after eating. Belchings followed by rumbling in stomach. Sour belchings causing a
cough.
Teeth - Teeth covered with white mucus. Swelling of mucus membrane of the inner margin of the two incisors.
Teeth loose and very painful. Gums, especially lower, spongy, oozing blood.
Temperature - Chilliness and sensation of internal coldness. Alternate burning heat and chilliness, at night.
Sweat all over, early is morning, in bed, cold nightsweat. The sweat makes the bed smell of potatoes. Heat all
 over with sweat. Fever, afterwards dropsical appearance. Violent paroxysms of heat.
Throat - Feeling as of a fleshy growth in throat. Feeling as if something sticking in throat. Mucus accumulates
in throat. Fauces and mouth inflamed, ulcerated in patches. Inflamed fauces, unable to swallow saliva.
COMMENTS - The symptoms of the Sol-tae. proving were severe, and one of the most important, prolapse of
the rectum, has been confirmed by the poisoning cases.
A man and three children ate boiled diseased potatoes and among their symptoms were “Pain of an acute
character was referred to the region of the anus, which on examination was found perfectly patulous and
exquisitely tender to the touch.
Two of the four patients had prolapsed anus, which was probably caused by the violent and ineffectual efforts
to discharge the contents of the rectum.
There had not been an evacuation of the bowels, nor had they passed water, except in drops and with extreme
suffering, for six days. On introducing the finger into the rectum, which caused acute pain, it was found that
the intestine was completely
filled to within an inch of the orifice with a solid substance.”
The foul odor of the diseased potato is reproduced in the breath and body odor of the patients. Lips cracked
and raw, gums bleeding tongue coated, thick, cracked, throat inflamed and ulcerated with sensation of
something sticking in it or a fleshy growth.
In one poisoning case a condition of noma of left cheek was induced.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bry., Ars., Plb., Nux-v., Sep., Stron., Viol-t., Squil., Puls., Graph., Alum., Merc.,
Nat-m., Ign., Calc. (2) Sensation of machinery inside, Nit-ac. (3) Constipation, black balls, Op. (4) Prolapsus
anus, Podo., Ruta. (5) Patulous anus, Apis., Phos.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Solanum Xanthocarpus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sol-x. Solanum xanthocarpus. Kantikari. N. O. Solanaceae. Root, bark, fruit and flower.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Abscesses. Asthma. Boils. Bronchitis. Buboes. Cough. Cystitis. Dropsy. Dysuria. Hemorrhoids.
Hoarseness. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, stones. Lung, disorders. Ophthalmia. Pneumonia. Smallpox. Teeth,
decay. Urinary, stricture. Vomiting.
HERBAL - Ayurvedic physicians prized Sol-x. as an excellent remedy for cough, respiratory troubles, cough
associated with hoarseness, ophthalmia, stone or calculus, stricture, and retention or suppression of urine.
Sol-x. is an aperient, carminative, expectorant, and diuretic. It is given in asthma, cough, catarrhal affections
of the lungs, fever, flatulent and pain in the chest. As a diuretic, the decoction is given in dysuria, cystitis, calculi
and dropsy, also given in costiveness.
A paste of the seeds is locally applied to promote suppuration of boils, buboes, and other indolent chronic
abscesses. Fumigation of the fruit is largely used by natives
as sialogogue and applied for the relief of pain in carious teeth.
Charaka recommended Sol-x. in hemorrhoids, cough, delirium tremens, urinary difficulties, stone and calculus.
Shushruta found it efficacious in ophthalmia, respiratory troubles, cough, urinary difficulties and troubles and
stricture.
Chakradatta said that Sol-x. is useful in cough, stricture, and urinary troubles. Bangasena has recommended
it in the cough of children.
Sol-x. is used by them separately or as a principal ingredient in their compound medicines for the above
mentioned complaints.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hoarseness (Caust., Phos., Sei.), associated with cough. Bronchitis, pneumonia, or bronco-
pneumonia associated with voice loss. Asthma.
Fevers associated with thirst, vomiting, aversion to food, burning sensation felt over the body and pains felt
over the collective body of the ribs. Stricture, suppression or retention of urine and kidney stone.
Preventive against smallpox. The Ayurvedic physicians also used it against smallpox, dose being 1/8 tola of
its root (white variety) to be given in the morning in empty stomach.
RELATIONS - Compare: In the cure of kidney maladies it can be compared with Berb., Canth., Sars. and Lyc.
REFERENCES - Ghose.

name: Solidago Virgaurea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - solid. Solidago virgaurea. Goldenrod. N. O. Compositae, Tribe, Corymbifere. Tincture of whole
 fresh plant. Tincture of flowers. The fresh blossoms are macerated in twice their weight of alcohol. Infusion of
dry leaves and flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies. Asthma. Backache. Bright’s disease. Bronchitis. Calculus. Colds.
Conjunctivitis. Coughs. Croup. Cystitis. Deafness. Dysentery. Dysuria. Eczema. Edema. Eruptions. Gangrene.
Gout. Hay fever. Hemorrhages. Kidney, disorders. Leucorrhea. Nephritis. Ophthalmia, scrofulous.
Phosphaturia. Prostate, enlarged. Prostate, weak. Rheumatic fever. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Scrofula.
Tuberculosis. Urine, suppressed
HERBAL - The common golden rod is the only British species of Solidago. It is common in woods and healthy
thickets. “This herb,” said Rademacher, “is a very old and good kidney medicine. It is a specific for kidneys
and brings the patients back to the normal condition.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Solid, has helped diseases arising from or complicated with defective functions of kidneys.
It affects the digestive tract, lower limbs and blood. Hemorrhages. Feeling of weakness, chilliness alternating
with heat.
Homeopathic replacement for the catheter. Pain in region of kidneys with dysuria. Kidneys sensitive to
pressure. Bright’s disease. Chronic nephritis. Uremic asthma. “Clear, stinking urine” is an indication of
Cooper’s.
Hay fever when golden rod is the exciting cause. Takes cold easily. Inhalation of the pollen has caused
hemorrhage from the lungs in tuberculosis. Repeated colds of tuberculosis. Naso-pharyngeal catarrh,
burning in throat, pains in limbs and thoracic oppression.
Abdomen - Costiveness, sensation of pain in the abdomen on both sides of the navel, upon deep pressure,
gas. Severe pricking in both hypochondria to the region of the kidneys, reaching to the lower limbs.
Back - Backache. Lumbar ache, makes her sick all over.
Bladder - Cystitis. Catarrh of the bladder. Obstructed flow of urine. Scanty urine. Nightly dysuria. Catheterizing
of bladder.
Chest - Rheumatism of the inter-costal muscles.
Constitutions - Especially suited to scrofulous subjects.
Ears - Sudden deafness with ringing in the ears and albuminous urine.
Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Scrofulous, herpetic inflammation. Red with enlarged prostate gland.
Female - Uterine enlargement organ pressed down upon the bladder. Fibroid tumors. Hemorrhage. Chronic
leucorrhea in connection with copious, watery urine and sediments of mucus particles and uriniferous tubules,
epithelium.
Kidneys - Kidneys, sore and tender, ache, feel distended. Pain in kidneys extends forward to abdomen,
bladder, down the thighs. Chronic nephritis. Urine, voided with difficulty.
Limbs - Chronic pains in the loins. Rheumatic pains in the leg. Pains in the thighs, the leg can be moved
horizontally. When limbs are moved perpendicularly they feel lame. Limping, dragging gait.
Lungs - Oppressed breathing. Continuous dyspnea. Allergies. Asthma. Periodical asthma with nightly dysuria.
Bronchitis. Chronic catarrh of the lungs. Cough with much purulent expectoration blood- streaked. Heavy
expectoration in coughing, croup and diminished urine.
Male - Enlarged prostate gland, obstructing flow of urine or inflammation. Weak prostate gland.
Modalities - Better from profuse urination. Worse from pressure, at night.
Mouth - Continuous bitter taste. Tongue heavily coated, clears when urine becomes normal. Flat ulcers in the
mouth and throat.
Nose - Allergies and hay fever. Dry, inner surface of the nose covered with blood crust, scalding and very
scanty urine. Paroxysms of sneezing with abundant mucus discharge.
Rectum - Chronic catarrh of the bowels. Dysentery, diarrhea. Profuse involuntary mucus stools.
Skin - Petechiae, on lower limbs with edema and itching, Gangrene, diabetic. Eczema worse from suppressed
urine. Scrofulous rash, little blotches on hands and feet. Very obstinate, itching exanthemas. Exanthema of
the lower limbs without swelling of the inguinal glands, but with disturbance in urinating.
Sleep - Insomnia.
Temperature - Rheumatic fever, very frequent pulse, high fever.
Urine - Dark urine, especially at night with very scanty brown and sour urine. Scalding and very scanty urine.
Urine, dark and scanty or clear, stinking. Urine, voided with difficulty. Urine, albuminous, mucous, phosphatic.
COMMENTS - Anshutz wrote, “A lady, by administering, morning and evening, an infusion of the dry leaves
and flowers of Golden Rod (Solidago virgaurea) tells me that she cured her husband of an affection of the
bladder which had compelled him to use a catheter for a year or more.
“A friend of homeopathy desired to test the energetics of this plant. He had the first dilution of its tincture to be
taken three times a day by seven patients. From forty-two to seventy-fours years of age. They had been obliged
 to catheterize themselves for weeks, months and years.
“Homeopathy cured them so thoroughly that they had no relapses. Surgeons who spend much time in
catheterizing such patients for months and years could often cure them much more rapidly by prescribing for
them the remedy just mentioned.”
Gallavardin told of a woman who cured her husband, who had been compelled to use the catheter for more
than a year, by administering an infusion of the dried leaves and flowers of Solid, morning and evening.
Dr. White said “I have used it in several other cases where it seemed indicated by the tenderness in kidney
region and the inability to control the water from whatever cause, always the perfect satisfaction to patient and
myself.”
Gucken confirmed Rademacher’s clinical observations and quoted further confirmations and cures by Dr. Buck
of Wurtemburg.
The grand keynote of this remedy lies in the condition and the action of the kidneys and the quality of their
secretions. Diseases arising from or complicated with defective action of the kidneys are very likely to be
benefited by Solid.
Pain and tenderness in kidney region, pains extending from kidneys to abdomen, bladder and down limbs,
urine dark, red-
brown, scanty, thick, voided with difficulty, albuminous, mucus and phosphatic urine. Affections of any other
parts or organs complicated with these symptoms will probably find their remedy in Solid.
Buck mentioned scrofulous inflammation of the eyes. Clarke saw very sharp attack of conjunctivitis produced
in a patient who was taking Solid. Also for prostatic troubles.
Buck noted several cases, including that of a boy, age 8, who had severe membranous diphtheria with scarlet
rash, which was removed by Merc-cy. and Bell., but a fever of the typhoid type remained. The urine was
albuminous and scanty, pulse weak and intermittent, feet swollen. Kali-ar. 4c was given, but the symptoms
grew worse.
A thorough examination of the patient showed great sensitiveness of the kidneys to pressure in spite of the
otherwise apathetic condition. Solid. 3x was given and in one day the urine became more profuse with
corresponding improvement in the general condition. The body peeled and recovered completely.
A clerk, 45, had sleeplessness and pain in the back. He casually mentioned that it took him a long time to
urinate for want of the necessary pressure. This he attributed to gonorrhea, which he had years before. No
sleep until 3 a.m. when he got some sleep, which was not refreshing.
On rising, tired, especially upper part of thighs, then would begin the pain in the back, which extended to the
loins and lasted until bedtime. Nux-v. did not relieve. The urine was found dark, slimy, reddish, slightly acid,
not albuminous. Kidneys sensitive to pressure.
Solid. 3x, taken steadily for three months, cured. A year afterwards there was a relapse, but this time it took
the form of sciatica and Solid, again proved to be the remedy.
Mrs. F., 53, wife of a farmer, stout, freshlooking, had her present trouble twenty-six years. After her
confinement, which was difficult and followed by prolapse uterus, still existing. Her legs began to swell and an
itching rash broke out by degrees.
Menstruation had always come on at
the proper time, but suddenly stopped six months before Buck saw her. Since then the itching had been almost
intolerable, the legs more swollen and always cold.
Appetite very poor, constant bitter taste in mouth tongue thickly coated, at the same time a rising from the
stomach as if she would suffocate and at the least exertion she lost her breath. Urinated very little and mostly
at night.
No pains in the back, but the kidneys were sensitive to pressure. “The appearance of the lower limbs of this
patient,” said Buck, “frightened me. From knee to heel they formed a bluish-red mass in the shape of a stove-
pipe and were covered with little blotches and crusts.”
The prolonged use of Solid. 3x, though it did not effect a cure, produced a mitigation of the whole body, so that
the woman induced her eldest son to consult the doctor.
This man had also trouble in his lower limbs not unlike his mother’s. A year before he had some severe throat
trouble after which his lower limbs began to swell and itch. They were also tinted blue-red and covered with
vesicles, his urine was scanty and his kidneys sensitive to pressure. Solid. 3x cured him in a few months.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In prostatic and urinary affections, Sabal., Santa., Hydrang., Tritic. (2) Kidney-
ache, Santa. (3) Gonorrhea and its effects, sciatica, Med.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - solid. Solidago virgaurea. Goldenrod. N. O. Compositae, Tribe, Corymbifere. Tincture of whole
 fresh plant. Tincture of flowers. The fresh blossoms are macerated in twice their weight of alcohol. Infusion of
dry leaves and flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies. Asthma. Backache. Bright’s disease. Bronchitis. Calculus. Colds.
Conjunctivitis. Coughs. Croup. Cystitis. Deafness. Dysentery. Dysuria. Eczema. Edema. Eruptions. Gangrene.
Gout.

name: Sphingurus Martini
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sphing. Sphingurus martini. Porcupine tree. Spiggurus martini. Hystrix prehensis. N. O.
Sphingurinae. Trituration of prickles taken from one of the sides. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Hair, loss. Jaw, pains. Stammering. Zygoma, pain.
HOMEOPATHIC - The old world porcupines have the name Histricinae, those of the new world, Sphingurinae.
Mure proved the 3x trituration of the prickles.
The most noteworthy symptoms were falling out of the hair, especially of whiskers. Itching of the pubes after
taking tea. Pain in the jaw-joint and right zygoma. Embarrassed speech. Nausea at sight of food.
Modalities - Better walking on open air. after dinner. Worse lying down, after tea.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Spigelia Anthelmintica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - spig. Spigelia anthelmintica. Pinkroot. Demerara. N. O. Loganiacae. Middle and South America.
Tincture of dried herb. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenoids. Amaurosis. Angina pectoris. Anorexia. Anxiety. Ascarides. Bulimia. Ciliary,
neuralgia. Colds. Colic. Concussions. Constipation. Depression. Diaphragm, stitches. Dyspnea. Exophthal-
mic, goiter. Eyes, pains. Face, pains. Gastric, catarrh. Glaucoma. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hernia,
inguinal. Iritis. Jaw, pain. Migraines. Nausea. Neuralgias. Otalgia. Palpitations. Pericarditis. Photophobia.
Post-nasal, catarrh. Prosopalgia. Prostatorrhea. Pterygium. Rectum, cancer. Rheumatism. Scarlatina.
Sigmoid flexure, cancer. Stammering, speech. Strabismus. Tinnitus. Tobacco habit. Toothache. Vertigo.
Worms.
HERBAL - Spigelia anthelmia is a common weed in South America. Spigelia Mary- landica, ‘‘Pink-root’’ or
“Worm-grass,” is a native of the southern states of North America. Spig. was known in Europe in
Hahnemann’s time as an anthelmintic, the drug properties were learned from the natives of the Antilles.
HOMEOPATHIC - Spig. markedly affects the nerves, trifacial, heart, eyes, teeth, fibrous tissue and left side.
Useful for pericarditis and other diseases of the heart. Heart disorders and neuralgias. It produces combined
heart and eye symptoms, or the latter as an accompaniment.
Affected by the sun. Headache beginning at sunrise, at its height at noon, declining to sunset. Pains of
neuralgias and headaches increases and declines with sun. Sun pains.
Neuralgia of the fifth nerve. Stabbing pains. Pains are violent, burning like hot needles or wires, jerking,
tearing, stitching, radiating to other parts. Very sensitive to touch. Parts feel chilly, send shudder through
frame. Body feels light while walking, heavy and sore when rising from a seat. Moves very carefully.
A remedy for stitches due to the presence of worms. Child refers to the navel as the most painful part
(Gran., Nux-v., Plb., Mosch.).
MIND - Mental exertion difficult. Weakness of memory. Absence of ideas. Difficulty of thinking. Unfit for
intellectual labor. Confusion on stooping. Sadness and discouragement. Stammering, repeats first syllable
three or four times. Sits as if lost in thought, stares at a single object.
Agitation and anxiety, with restlessness. Anxiety about future. Restless and anxious. So nervous he can’t
control himself, feels as if he must run. Anxiety on seeing any one move quickly, on breathing deeply. Afraid
ofsharp, pointed things, pins, needles (Sil., Apis.). Delusions about pins. Excitement after sadness.
Irritability during chill.
Mental irritability. Easily offended. Very restless and anxious. Cannot tolerate thinking of pain. Can become
suicidal because the pain is too severe. Gloomy, suicidal mood. Desires death during chill. Great dejection in
evening, he could have killed himself. Timidity.
Abdomen - Abdomen hard and painfully tight. Contact and pressure of clothes is unbearable. Colic with
pinching pains in the umbilical region. Expulsion of fetid flatus.
Back - Neck stiff, pains into right temple or pain from left shoulder to neck. Cutting about the left scapula.
Causations - Concussions. Worms, ascarides and lumbrici. Sunlight. Tobacco.
Chest - Aching at the chest with painful oppression. Angina pectoris. Contraction of chest with anguish and
obstructed respiration. Stitches in diaphragm with dyspnea. Craving for hot water which
Spigelia anthelmintica relieves chest pain.
Constitutions - Adapted to anemic, debilitated, rheumatic and scrofulous subjects. Suited to persons with
light hair, pale, thin, bloated, weak with wrinkled, yellow, earthy skin. Children afflicted with worms, ascarides
and lumbrici.
Ears - Roaring, buzzing and pulsation in ears. Stoppage of ears. Periodical deafness, ears feel as if stuffed.
Eyes - Pupils dilated. Rheumatic ophthalmia. Feel too large, pressive pain on turning the eyes. Severe pain
 in and around the eyes, extending deep into socket, worse thinking of them. Ciliary neuralgia, neuritis. As
if needles were thrust in. Profuse lachrymation, from affected side, tears acrid. Eyes, red, sore, drawing ache.
Yellow rings about the eyes. Difficulty in raising the eyelids with painful sensation of stiffness. Evertedeyelids.
Inclination to wink. Difficult to fit glasses, no settled focus, no fixed vision, latent errors of vision. Pricking in
lids. Squints with worms. Photophobia.
Face - Prosopalgia involving eye, zygoma, cheek, teeth, temples. Worse from touch, stooping, from morning
until sunset, drinking tea, suddenly going and coming.
Food - Ravenous hunger. Anorexia with violent thirst. Bulimia, sometimes with nausea and thirst. Putrid, fetid
taste. Aversion to coffee, tobacco smoke and snuff. Craving for hot water which relieves chest pain.
Head - Feels too large. Migraines. Awn from beneath frontal eminence and temples, extending to eyes
(Onos.). Semi-lateral involving left eye, pain violent, throbbing, worse making afalse step. Pain as if a band
around head (Carb-ac., Cact., Gels.). Pain from left occiput to over left eye, worse stooping, making a false
step, opening mouth. Supra-orbital neuralgia.
Heart - Violent sticking or compressive pains, radiating to throat, arms, scapula, worse least motion or
bending double. Soreness, purring, cracking in the region of heart. Angina pectoris. Neuralgia extending to
arm or both arms. Craving for hot water which relieves. Violent palpitations, audible, attending other
symptoms. Frequent attacks of palpitations, especially with foul odor from mouth. Throbbing of carotids and
subclavian arteries. Precordial pain and great aggravation from movement. Pericarditis. Rheumatic carditis,
trembling pulse, whole left side sore. Pulse intermittent with palpitations, weak tremulous irregular.
Kidneys - Frequent want to urinate with profuse emission, even at night. Sudden and involuntary dribbling of
urine with burning sensation in anterior part of urethra. Urine with whitish sediment.
Limbs - Fatigue. Drawing, tearing, twitching pains in limbs and joints. Left arm numb. Pulsation in patellae.
The limbs are affected mostly when walking.
Lungs - Dyspnea, must lie on right side with head high, worse moving in bed, raising arms. Hydrothorax.
Trembling in chest. Stitches in chest worse least motion or when breathing.
Male - Discharge of prostatic fluid from the urethra.
Modalities - Better from rest, lying on right side with head high. Better inspiring, steady pressure, warmth.
Pressure helps the neuralgia, cold application helps temporarily. Better while eating, worse immediately after.
Worse light touch but better firm pressure. Worse motion, jar. Worse turning, rising, raising arms, stooping.
bending forward. Worse from sex. Worse slightest draft, cold, damp, rainy, stormy weather, cold air, cold
washing. Worse with the sun (Nat-m.). Worse morning, on waking. Worse blowing nose, expiration, tobacco.
Worse noise. Worse thinking of problems.
Mouth - Foul odor from mouth. Offensive taste. Tongue, coated yellow or white, cracked, with burning or
stitching pain. Tongue fissured, painful. Opening mouth aggravates headache.
Nose - Tickling and itching of nose. Forepart of nose always dry. Chronic catarrh with post-nasal drip of bland
mucus. Discharge through posterior sinuses. Flow of water during prosopalgia.
Rectum - Constipation and diarrhea. Frequent, ineffectual urging to stool. Faints at stool. Stools of large lumps
of mucous. Itching, tickling and crawling in anus and rectum. Worms, ascarides.
Sensations - As if he would fall. As if intoxicated. As if head would burst. As of a band around head, as if head
tightly bound. As if electric sparks in temples. Brain as if loose. As if eye would be pushed out of head. As if
hairs or feathers on lashes. Face feels as if it had been scorched. As if heart compressed or squeezed with a
hand. As if everything in chest were too short, loose and wobbling about. As if something tearing in chest.
Skin - Pale, wrinkled skin of body. Painful sensibility when touched. Painful glandular swellings. Red pimples
with pain when touched, as from excoriation.
Stomach - Pressure in stomach. Accumulation of mucus in the stomach. Sour risings. Nausea with sensation
of a worm rising in throat. Nausea when fasting.
Teeth - Tearing pains, worse after eating, cold, and when thinking of it. Toothache with facial pain, better by
warmth or the warmth of the bed. Nerve toothache. Toothache, worse cold drinks (Mag-p., better warm drinks.),
better by smoking tobacco.
Temperature - Chilliness on the slightest motion. Cold, offensive sweat on upper part of the body, on hands.
Heat, flushes at night in back.
Throat - Sore throat with lancinations and swelling in palate. Discharge of mucus from fauces all day, most
from posterior sinuses. Swollen cervical glands.
Vertigo - Vertigo on stooping with heat of head. Vertigo as if they are drunk. Vertigo, the feet as if higher than
head. Vertigo worse looking down, must look straight ahead, worse standing, walking. Vertigo, hearing exalted.
COMMENTS - Hahnemann said Spig. has the peculiarity that the primary action of a single unrepeated dose
usually increases somewhat daily during the first seven to ten days. Experiments should be conducted with
 caution, seeing that 60, 80 to 100 drops of
the tincture produce violent effects even in robust persons.
Keynote violence. More left-sided than right, but by no means exclusively leftsided. Primarily affects the head,
eyes, face, teeth and heart. Sensitivity to cold, wet and stormy weather.
Produces intense pains in all parts. Hypersensitive to all pain. Burning, jerking, tearing, pressing and stitching
pains, radiate and extend to other parts. Pains are largely out-pressing and proceed from within outward and
below upward. Pains are worse by noise, jar, movement, change of weather, especially stormy weather. The
pains were worse night and morning and in damp weather. Sensitive to pain remedies (Cham., Nux-v., Ign.,
Hep.).
Darting and aching pains in head, nose and eyes and similar pains about the heart with slow, irregular action,
but no murmur. Sudden pains at bottom of back. The body is painfully sensitive to touch. Pain feels like shiver
in the body, eye or face. The part touched feels chilly. Touch sends a shudder through the whole frame. Pain
radiates from a spot, not in a straight line. Darting pain. Pain will transfix (Bry.).
Neuralgia, especially facial neuralgias. Pains over the left eye or the left side of the face, trigeminal neuralgias.
Neuralgias with burning sensations or electric-like sensations. Intercostal neuralgias (Ran-b.). Often with
neuralgia, their whole left face consists of tearing pain as if someone is cutting their face or tearing the skin off
their face.
Neuralgias and inflammation of the eye, amaurotic conditions, and glaucoma. Exophthalmic goiter. Intolerable
pressive pains, worse on motion. Stabbing pains through eye backwards into brain. Uveitis. Ciliary neuralgia
or affection to the optic nerve with cutting, stabbing pain, the eye becomes inflamed and watery. Sensation as
if eye would burst. Deep pain in eye socket.
Dilated pupils, can see sparks and rays of light. Severe photophobia, especially with headache, they want to
be in the dark with a hand covering their left side and making no noise and staying from noise.
Migraine, from occiput, settling in or over left eye (Sang, starts at the occiput and settles in the right eye; Sil.
and Gels, are from occiput to forehead.). Occiput feels numb and stiff.
Heart attack, aching pain. Acute heart attacks with sharp, stabbing, burning pains down the left arm (Lat-m.),
or it feels as if a hot, red, burning knife is stuck into the heart and turned. The heart feels as if squeezed or
compressed, sense of suffocation. Palpitation as if the whole chest will shake. Violent palpitation, can hear or
see the heart beating. Irregular heartbeat. Left-sided angina.
Suffocative attacks, can become anguished, think they are going to die. Chest pain, worse during deep
breathing (Bry.). The movement of the rib cage aggravates. Stitching pains synchronous with the pulse. Heart
disorders from rheumatism. Rheumatism.
Abdominal ailments with worms. Masses of lumbrici have been expelled and also threadworms. Itching of anus
and nose, colic and borborygmus. Fetid breath and fetid flatus.
In one prover, the accustomed evening smoke caused violent toothache. Clarke cured a case of cardiac
neuralgia caused by tobacco. He saw cardiac murmurs appearing in acute rheumatism disappear under Spig.
Hochecker related the case of Miss O., 27, who was blonde, tall, and robust, and had neuralgia for several
weeks without traceable cause. Pains came suddenly, twitching and tearing of left side of face, now in ear,
then in lower jaw, particularly worse by mastication. Whenever the pains were about to commence a diarrhea
set in. A single powder of Spig. 6c cured.
Hochecker also cured with Spig. 3c, 6c, 10c and 20c a case of tic douloureux of the right side that had lasted
fifteen months. In this case, each lower potency, after first relieving, caused an aggravation. So the potencies
were successively raised. Spig. 20c completed the cure. This patient had dark hair and dark complexion. She
attributed her trouble to taking cold in a draft when heated by dancing.
A patient Clarke successfully treated for a serious heart affection with Spig. 3c said that under the treatment
he had lost a pain in the right knee that he had for eighteen months and which he had not mentioned at first.
The pain was as if dislocated, unable to rise from kneeling, could not find an easy position often for hours at
night.
Clarke found it especially useful in heart cases where constipation has been a troublesome complication.
Hering gave this case, “Helminthiasis: dilated pupils, strabismus, putrid smell from mouth, itching of nose,
griping pain in belly, throat inflamed, swallows often, pale redness in throat and swelling of mucus membrane,
palpitation.”
Meninger had a severe case of nausea during pregnancy that he cured with Spig. The only leading symptom
in the case was that she was afraid of pointed things and asked her husband to take away a fork, crochet-
needle, etc. Sil. has a somewhat similar symptom, but the Sil. patient hunts for pins although afraid of them.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Aur. (restlessness in limbs), Cocc., Puls. Antidote to: Merc., Colch.
(heart). Compare: (1) Spig-m., Nux-v., Ign., Cur. (2) Aeon., Cact., - Cimic., (3) Arn., Spig. is a chronic Arn. (4)
 Cinnb. - supra-orbital pain. (5) Naja, Spong.
- heart. (6) Sabad., Teucr., Cina - worm symptoms. (7) Pains, left eye, Aeon. (8) Neuralgia in left eye, Ther.
(9) Headaches, coming and going with sun, Nat-m., Sang., Tab. (10) Eye pains, Bell., Ciliary neuralgia, Cedr.,
Mez. (11) Heart pains, white stools, Dig. (12) Stitches in heart. Hep., Nat-m., Kali-c., Ars., Caust. (13)
Headache begins occiput and goes to left eye, (Sang, to right, Sil. to both). (14) Tic douloureux, Thuj., Cocci-
s. (15) Neuralgia with pallor (with redness, Bell.). (16) Worms, Sabad., Cina, Teucr., Scirr. (17) Worse tight
clothing, Lach., sensitiveness to touch, Kali-c. Compatible: Aeon, (endocarditis), Ars., Dig., Kali-c., Zinc,
(heart), Iris (prosopalgia), Arn. (Carbuncle).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Spigelia Marylandica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY -spig-m. Spigelia marylandica. Worm grass. N. O. Loganiaceae. Tincture of dried root. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Mania. Strabismus. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms of Spig- m. are mainly from overdosing. A state of mania was induced in a
boy from large and frequent doses of a decoction of the root. Strabismus of right eye was noted in one case.
On attempting to assume erect position, seized with general tremor lasting a few seconds and leaving her
exhausted.
Maniacal excitement, paroxysmal laughing and crying, loud, disconnected talking, vertigo, dilated pupils,
congestions. On attempting to assume erect position, seized with general tremor lasting a few seconds and
leaving her exhausted.
MIND - Suddenly affected with complete mental derangement(Stram.).Countenancedistorted, running and
skipping. Fits of laughing and crying. Wild and incoherent talking.
Eyes - Pupils greatly dilated. Irregular movement of adductors and abductors of eyes. Strabismus of right eye.
Pain in and about the eyes. Sensation of stiffness of eyelids.
Face - Wild, staring, ludicrous expression. Swelling of face and about eyes. Face flushed.
Heart - Pulse is accelerated, irregular. Mouth - Tongue pointed and tremulous. Skin - Hot and dry.
Sleep - Drowsiness.
Vertigo - Dizziness.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Spilanthes Acmella
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - spil. Spilanthes acmella. Toothache plant. Paracress. N. O. Aster- aceae. Paraguay cress.
Brazil. Tincture of fteshleaves, root and flower heads.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Bacteria, infections. Candida. Colds. Dysentery. Fungal, infections. Glands, swollen.
Gum, disease. Herpes. Influenza. Lyme disease. Malaria. Parasites. Ringworm. Salivation. Sore throats.
Toothaches. Viral, infections. Wounds.
HERBAL - Also known as “Toothache Plant” or “Paracress,” Spilanthes acmella is a flowering herb in the
Asteraceae family. Its leaves and flower heads contain an analgesic agent that may be used to numb
toothaches. It is native to the tropics of Brazil, though it is grown as an ornamental (and occasionally as a
medicinal) in various parts of the world.
Chewing on one of the flower buds will numb your mouth and make you salivate. The leaves may be used
topically to treat bacterial and fungal skin diseases such as ringworm. Leaf decoction is used as diuretic and
lithotriptic. Root decoction is used as purgative. The whole plant is used in treatment of dysentery.
Useful for enhancing the immune sy stem’s resistance to infections. It stimulates wound healing, protects the
individual from colds and flu. Decreases allergic symptoms. Antibacterial. Inhibits the yeast/fungal organism
Candida albicans.
Indicated for swollen glands, gum disease and all manner of acute bacterial, viral and fungal infections. Herpes.
Sore throats. Useful against blood parasites, particularly malarial spirochetes, either as a prophylactic or as a
treatment for malarial paroxysms. Lyme disease.
Because of their high isobutylamide content, both Spilanthes and Prickly Ash have similar stimulating and
therapeutic actions.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

***SPIRAEA ULMARIA (Meadow-sweet) PHARMACY - spirae. Spiraea ulmaria. Meadow-sweet. Hardback.
 Queen of the Meadows. N. O. Rosacea. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bites. Conscientiousness, morbid. Convulsions. Eclampsia. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture.
Eyelids, disorders. Gleet. Hydrophobia. Prostatorrhea. Ptosis. Rabies. Urine, deposits.
HOMEOPATHIC - Bojanus proved Spiraea ulmaria, taking substantial doses. A leading symptom was the
production of general and local heat. Heat in throat in esophagus, under sternum, under ensiform cartilage.
Bojanus was seized with remorse, a kind of morbid conscientiousness. Fullness and heaviness of head.
Washing with cold water was very unpleasant and caused a feeling as if the head were too large.
A scurfy condition of eyelids and heaviness of lids after afternoon sleep were noted. The urine was turbid as if
mixed with clay and deposited red sand, had an oily film on the surface.
The burning in esophagus was better by eating and drinking but not by empty swallowing. Burning and
pressure in esophagus, feels contracted but not made worse by swallowing.
Relieves irritation of the urinary passages influences the prostate gland. Checks gleet and prostatorrhea. Bites
of mad animals. Heat in various parts.
Hansen mentioned that Spirae. was recommended in hydrophobia, epilepsy and eclampsia.
MIND - Restlessness, obliged to rise and walk about. Morbid conscientiousness. Remorse over a long-past
slight indiscretion. Fearful qualms of conscience. Loathing of himself. Hydrophobia.
Abdomen - Sensation of heaviness in the lowerpart of the abdomen. Very offensive flatus. Odorless flatus.
Bladder - Burning in the urethra while urinating.
Eyes - Sclera is bright red. Sensation as if something hot in the eyes. Eyes filled with mucus. Lachrymation
with smarting and increased sensation of warmth. Indistinct vision, as through a mist, relieved by blinking and
rubbing the eyes. Heaviness of the eyelids with headache.
Face - Redness of the face. Sensation of heat in the face and eyes.
Head - Headache on shaking the head. Pulsations. Dullness and heaviness in the head. Pain as if a ring were
tightened about the head. Sensation as if the brain wobbled to and fro.
Food - Hunger disappeared. No relish for smoking.
Limbs - Heaviness in all the limbs.
Lungs - Dry cough. Cold feeling in lungs on inspiration.
Male - In the morning, in bed, violent erections, with great sexual desire.
Modalities - Better moving about. Better in open air. Worse leftside. Worse indoors. Worse moving head,
sneezing.
Mouth - Drawing pain. Toothache in back teeth.
Rectum - Sensation as if drawn rectum inward. Sensation as if the anus would not open sufficiently. Prickling
constrictive sensation in the anus. Crawling and prickling in the rectum. Frequent desire for stool, that suddenly
disappeared. Hard stool. Feces lumpy, like balls of rabbit’s dung, without being hard.
Sleep - Overpowering sleepiness. Restless sleep, frequent waking and tossing about. Sleep full of vivid
dreams. Lascivious dreams and emission.
Stomach - Cold sensation in the esophagus. Burning pressure in the esophagus, better belching. Heartburn.
Frequent eructations of odorless gas.
Throat - Sensation of increased warmth in the pharynx.
Urine - Urine turbid. Bright lemon yellow urine, almost straw-colored. Cloudy urine with an iridescent film.
Looks like red sand, brick-dust powder.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Salicylic acid is in Spirae. (2) Bell.
REFERENCES - Allen. Boericke. Clarke.

Brazil. Tincture of fteshleaves, root and flower heads.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Bacteria, infections. Candida. Colds. Dysentery. Fungal, infections. Glands, swollen.
Gum, disease. Herpes. Influenza. Lyme disease. Malaria. Parasites. Ringworm. Salivation. Sore throats.
Toothaches. Viral, infections. Wounds.
