name: Spiranthes Autumnalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - spira. Spiranthes autumnalis. Lady’s tresses. N. O. Orchidaceae. Tincture of the root. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acidity. Belching. Breasts, painful. Breath, putrid. Bums. Colic. Coryza. Dyspareunia. Eczema.
Hysteria. Jaundice. Kidneys, pain. Lumbago. Milk, excessive. Nausea. Nosebleed. Rash. Rheumatism. Skin,
disorders. Toothache. Vision, dimness. Vomiting.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany reported that the genus to which this orchid belongs received its name
from the spiral arrangement of flowers. Spiranthes is an anti-phlogistic remedy akin to Aeon. Its symptoms
showing congestion and inflammation. The tuberous roots of Spira, were formerly esteemed as an aphrodisiac.
HOMEOPATHIC - Spira, has been used for milk-flow in nursing women, lumbago and rheumatism. Pulsations
in arteries over whole body. Acidity and burning in esophagus with eructation. Colic with drowsiness and
spasmodic yawning. Appears intoxicated. Lies on left side rather than right.
 MIND - Melancholy. Complaining and sobbing. Ill-humor. Confusion of ideas. Indolence and boredom. Worse
from mental effort. The least emotion or excitement causes palpitations.
Abdomen - Intermittent pressure in umbilical region. Pain, weakness, tympanites after a meal. Borbory gmi.
Desire to tighten clothes. Piercing, sharp insupportable pain in colon, on becoming erect. Laughing heat in
lower abdomen. Eruption in groin.
Back - Cramp-like pain in neck at night compelling change of position. Lumbago preventing walking. Pain in
center of scapula. Pain in scapula, when standing, worse walking.
Bladder - Bladder, pain on urinating, pain and burning after waking. Urine, abundant, scanty, decomposes
rapidly. Urine, deposits a gelatinous red sediment.
Breasts - Pain in breast on raising it. Burning on tips of breasts, especially the left. Milk abundant, more in left
breast.
Chest - Sensation of weakness of lungs. Sensation of dilatation of left lung. Pleuritic and intercostal pains,
worse left side.
Ears - Pain in left auditory canal. Itching in ear, externally and internally.
Eyes - Eyes brilliant, fixed. Pain in eyes on looking up. Burning in eyes with lachrymation. Eyes hot inflamed.
Vision dim, obscured with sleepiness instantaneously lost, objects at a distance seem to move, on closing lids,
sees wheels of fire. Lids swollen. Heaviness of brows.
Face - Swollen, red and hot, black, pale. Fixed, meditative expression. Burning in upper lip. Chin is red with
pain. Burning itching in left cheek near mouth.
Female - Pressing pain in uterus. Dryness of vagina. Itching, red vulva and burning in vagina. Burning pain in
vagina during sex. Bloody discharge from vagina. Yellowish leucorrhea.
Food - Loss of appetite. Desire for acid, sour foods. Constant thirst.
Head - Brain troubles, worse bending or raising arm. Heaviness and heat in brain. Sensation of band tied
about head. Weight on forehead. Pain in forehead and nasal bone. Pain in roots of hair. Hair falls out.
Heart - Pain in heart. Palpitations with difficult respiration from least emotional excitement. Pulse full and hard
at beginning of proving afterwards small and quiet.
Kidneys - Cramp-like pain at night in kidneys, obliging change of position. Burning pain preventing stooping,
worse going up stairs, better lying on back, coldness and heat.
Limbs - Trembling in limbs, weakness. Sciatic pain, especially right side. Pain in shoulders. Swelling of veins
of hands. Pain in all articulation of hands. Coldness of feet and toes.
Liver - Pain in liver and spleen, on pressure.
Lungs - Breathing difficult, short, panting on walking. Hacking cough, caused by tickling in larynx. Dry cough
at night with
burning in throat.
Male - Constant erections, on waking. Great desire for or repugnance to sex. Pricking pain in cords.
Modalities - Better lying on left side, on back. Worse by touch, stooping. Worse bending or raising arm, raising
breast. Rheumatism of shoulders worse when bending over. Laughing causes heat in lower abdomen.
Mouth - Putrid odor from mouth. Taste acid, sweetish like nitre, bitter in morning. Salivation with dryness of
mouth. Irritation of sublingual glands. Numerous small excresences on palate, which was bloody. Gums red
and burning. Sensation of coldness in teeth. Pain and elongation of teeth. Toothache only at night.
Nose - Pain in right nasal bones. Burning, itching at root of nose. Itching of right nostril. Dry coryza. Dripping
of water from nose. Nosebleed in clots. Smell very acute.
Rectum - Burning and itching in anus, worse during evacuation. Stool preceded and followed by prickling and
itching in anus. Diarrhea or constipation, stools sour in children.
Sensations - Sensation of a band tied around head. Sensation of a foreign body in throat. Coldness of teeth.
Coldness of the affected part. Pulsation in arteries over whole body. Preference for lying on left side or else
on back. Pain followed by numbness.
Skin - Dryness of skin. Jaundice. Yellow spots. Whole skin red, red in spots. Miliary rash. Eruption of red points
on buttocks with itching and heat. Blisters as from a burn with purulent secretion. Pricking over whole body.
Itching in axilla in pubes, scrotum, forearms at night, backs of hands.
Sleep - Incomplete yawning. Sleeping during day. Late falling to sleep in evening. Sleeplessness in infants.
Starting up during sleep. Lascivious dreams with emissions.
Stomach - Epigastrium distended, intolerant of touch, painful after a meal, the pain corresponding to the pain
in loins. Heat rising from stomach to head. Regurgitations. Belchings preceded by heat in lower abdomen and
lancinations in colon, acid, bitter, difficult, empty. Nausea after eating. Vomiting of food right after eating.
Temperature - Alternations of cold and heat. Hands alternately hot and cold. Coldness, evening, especially of
hands. Affected part colder than rest of body. Coldness of feet and toes. Heat of whole skin, flushes of heat in
 head, followed by sensation of cold. Flushes of heat. Fever, followed by thirst. Fever at night, sweat in morning.
Hands very hot. Sweat of palms.
Throat - Globus rising from lower abdomen to esophagus. Burning in larynx. Sensation of foreign body in
throat. Incessant desire to clear throat, caused by a thick mucus. Burning in pit of throat. Irritation of tonsils.
Tickling in throat, provoking cough. Sensation of acidity and burning in esophagus. Incarceration of air in
esophagus. Pain on swallowing.
Vertigo - Vertigo, obliged to lean head against wall, on rising from bed, worse sitting or lying.
COMMENTS - The tincture of the root was proved by Dr. Patti Chagon, Duc de Sorentino, who said of it, “The
action of this drug begins with decided symptoms of inflammation of the eyes, chin, chest, which become red
and hot, the whole skin is dry and hot, the hands are burning, the limbs of the feet are cold most of the time,
there is a sensation of oppression and heat with palpitation and a desire to uncover.
“This condition lasted two hours and gave place to others including desire to meditate and complain, vertigo,
pains in shoulders, boredom, loss of appetite.
“The last symptoms to appear are: pains in scalp, on vertex, distress in kidneys and intestinal troubles after
eating. The secretions of urine and milk were first diminished afterwards increased.
“The aphrodisiac property of Spira, was shown in some of the symptoms of the proving and this bears on the
increased secretion of milk. A number of symptoms appear in the lower abdomen. The globus hystericus rises
from thence to esophagus.
Heat in lower abdomen, preceding belchings, caused by laughing.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cypr. (2) Skin and mucus membranes, Arum-t. (3) Desire for tight clothing,
dryness of vagina, Nat-m. (4) Pain followed by numbness, Gnaph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Spongia Tosta
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - spong. Spongiatosta. Roasted sponge. Common Sponge. Porifera. Radiata. N. O.
Coelenterata. Tincture of the powdered sponge after toasting. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Aneurysm. Angina, pectoris. Asthma. Bronchitis. Catalepsy. Chin, disorders.
Clumsiness. Colds. Constipation. Coughs. Croup. Diphtheria. Diplopia. Dyspnea. Endocarditis. Epididymitis.
Exhaustion. Exophthalmos. Fainting. Gland, disorders. Goiter, exophthalmic. Headache. Heart,
hypertrophy. Hernia. Hyperthyroid. Jaw joint, pain. Laryngismus. Laryngitis. Lung, disorders. Myopia.
Orchitis. Rheumatic, fever. Rheumatism. Somnambulism. Testicles, disorders. Thyroid, disorders.
Tuberculosis. Varicose, veins. Whooping cough. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Hahnemann, toasted sponge was first mentioned as a specific for goiter by
the alchemist Arnold Von Villanova in the thirteenth century, but it was generally given mixed with other
substances and had fallen into disuse when Hahnemann proved it.
The virtues of Spong, have been attributed to the iodine contained in it and partially liberated by the presence
of roasting. But Spong, contains many other elements besides iodine and has a distinctive action of its own.
Affects the heart valves, larynx, trachea and glands, especially ductless. Useful for the symptoms of the
respiratory organs, cough, croup, heart disorders and tubercular diathesis.
Keynote dryness of mucus membranes, of tongue, pharynx, larynx, and trachea. Cough is caused by
dryness, hacking, crowing, “dry as a bone,” sounding like a saw being driven through a pine board. Cough is
excited by talking, by dry, cold winds, better by eating or drinking, swallowing, especially from warm food.
Dry, chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart disease. Anxiety with pain in the region of heart or
dyspnea. Hypertrophy of the heart. The right heart is affected, with asthmatic symptoms.
Anxiety and difficult breathing, terrible sinking sensation. Dry asthma. In laryngismus, croup and asthma
the patient rouses up generally after midnight with fear of suffocation and death. Contraction of larynx as if
suddenly grasped. The larynx is sensitive, but has not the hyperesthesia of Lach. The sputa cannot be raised,
must be swallowed, swallowing relieves.
Exhaustion and heaviness of the body with slight exertion, he must lie down with orgasms of blood to chest,
face etc. Feels stuffed up. Hard swelling of glands, thyroid. As if everything were shaking and moving about in
goiter.
Clothes feel uncomfortable. Numbness of lower half of the body. Stiff without ability to move. Faint, when losing
her breath, on raising hands above head. Worse after sleep (Lach.). Rises up in sleep as if in a great fright.
MIND - Timidity. Anxiety and difficult breathing. Fear of future. Terror. Anxiety with pain in the region of
heart or dyspnea. Aggravated from excitement and thinking of symptoms. Every excitement increases the
cough. Starting from sleep. Starting from trifles.
 Fear of death from suffocation (Puls., Aeon, Phos., Stram.), wakes frightened and anxious. Fear of dying.
Anxiety about his heart, fear of heart disease. Attacks of anguish and pain with fear. Anxiety during flushes of
heat.
Obstinate and improper behavior. Abusive. Quarrelsome. Tired of life. Despair during fever. Apprehension of
a fatal termination of his disease. Inconsolable.
Despondent about loss of sexual power. Suicidal disposition during perspiration. Weeps with dreams,
whooping cough, fever, sweat.
Ill humor, crying, indifference to everything, during croup. Taciturn and discontented mood, not disposed to
talk. Indifference to everything. Cheerful alternating with aversion to work. Irresistible desire to sing with
excessive mirth, followed by sadness. Singing alternating with distraction.
Abdomen - Violent action of abdominal muscles during inspiration. Viscera drawn up against diaphragm. Pain
in abdomen instead of menses.
Back - Neck as if a cord about. Pain in sacrum instead of menses. Cramps in the muscles of neck. Coldness
in back, not better by warmth of stove.
Chest - Oppression and heat of chest with sudden weakness. Chest weak, can scarcely talk, choking on falling
to sleep. Fullness and obstruction in chest. A fixed, sharp and pressive pain. Spasmodic, constrictive pains.
Shootings in chest. Burning, rawness, soreness in chest.
Constitutions - Suited to blue-eyed, fair-haired patients (lod. acts best on brunettes). Children with a fair
complexion, lax fiber, swollen glands. Suited to scrofulous disorders.
Cough - Dry, barking, croupy cough, larynx sensitive to touch. Deep, resonating coughs. Foghorn coughs.
Croup, worse during inspiration and before midnight. Asthmatic cough. Cough abates after eating or
drinking, especially warm drinks. Irrepressible cough from a spot deep in chest, as if raw and sore. Dry,
chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart disease. Cough is caused by dryness, hacking, crowing, “dry
as a bone,” sounding like a saw being driven through a pine board. Cough is excited by talking. Cough worse
by dry, cold winds, better by eating or drinking, swallowing, especially from warm food. Whooping cough.
Ears - Otalgia with contractive pain. Ulceration of external ear. Boils on left ear painful to touch. Inflamed
nodule in left concha. Heat, pressure in ears. Hard of hearing. Dull ringing in ears.
Eyes - Protrude, staring. Red with lachrymation and burning. Watering, gummy or mucus discharge. Diplopia,
better lying down.
Face - Terrified, anxious expression. Blue lips. Pale from exercise instead of ruddy glow. Cold sweat on chin.
Chin numb.
Female - Hunger and palpitations of heart before menses. Pain in sacrum before menses or instead of menses.
Awakes with suffocative spells during menses (Cupr., lod., Lach.). Amenorrhea with asthma (Puls.).
Food - Excessive úúist. great hunger. Desire for dainties, sweets aggravate.
Glands - Glands painful on pressure. Swelling and induration of glands. Cervical glands swollen with
tensive pain on turning head. Thyroid disorders. Hyperthyroid. Thyroid gland swollen, even with the chin.
Exophthalmic goiter. Goiter with suffocative spells, worse touching neck or pressure or pains with heart.
Head - Rush of blood, bursting headache, worse forehead. Throbbing, pulsation, heaviness and fullness of
head. Headache with lachrymation. Pressing headache. Sensation as if hair were standing on end, on vertex.
Violent itching in scalp.
Heart - Angina pectoris, faintness and anxious sweat. Surging of heart into chest, as if it would force out
upward. Blood surging up to neck, head and face with closure of eyelids and tears. Hypertrophy of heart,
especially right, with asthmatic symptoms. Valvular insufficiency. Aneurysm of the aorta. Rheumatic
endocarditis. Pulse frequent, hard, full or feeble. Rapid and violent palpitations with dyspnea, cannot lie down,
feels best resting in horizontal position. Awakened suddenly after midnight with pain and suffocation,
flushed, hot and frightened to death (Aeon.). Dry, chronic sympathetic cough of organic heart disease (Naja.).
Limbs - Fingers numb. Numbness of lower half of the body. Thighs, numb and cold. Pain in the knees, when
rising from kneeling. Thickening of joints after rheumatic fever.
Lungs - Great dryness of all air-passages. Noisy, whistling inspiration on falling to sleep. Suffocation, as
from a plug, valve or leaf. Anxious, gasping breathing. As if breathing through a dry sponge. Respiration short,
panting, difficult. Asthma, must throw head back, worse full moon. Croup, worse during inspiration and
before midnight. Bronchial catarrh with wheezing, asthmatic cough, worse cold air with profuse expectoration
and suffocation.
Male - Screwing, squeezing or stitches up into cord and testes. Orchitis. Testes hard and swollen. Swelling
of spermatic cord and testicles with pain and tenderness. Epididymitis. Fistulous opening in scrotum with
little, thick, white discharge. Genitals hot.
Modalities - Better descending. Better lying with head low, resting in horizontal position. Better eating or
 drinking warm food or drink. Frosty weather helps the cough. Worse from dry, cold, wind. Worse warm room.
Worse from sweets. Worse from exertion, motion, walking, stooping, rising, raising arms, ascending. Worse
talking, singing. Worse touch, pressure. Worse lying on the right side. Worse at night, before midnight, full
moon, after sleep.
Mouth - Sweetish taste. Salivation. Tongue dry and brown. Mouth and edge of tongue covered with vesicles.
Burning pain. Speech difficult.
Nose - Nose pinched, cold. Chronic dryness. Dry, nasal catarrh. Dry coryza, nose feels stuffed up. Fluent
coryza, alternating with stoppage. Nostrils wide open, fan like motion.
Rectum - Hard and retarded evacuations. Loose, whitish evacuations. Tenesmus in the anus during the
evacuation. Itching, smarting and pain as from excoriation in anus. Passage of ascarides from rectum and
tingling in rectum. Diarrhea with ascarides.
Sensations - As if head would fall to one side. As if tipsy. As if skull would burst. As if hair were standing on
end. Eyes as if twisted around. As if a battery of guns were discharged in ears. Stitches as if passing through
tympanum. As if skin of neck were compressed between fingers. As if air were passing up and down thyroid
and cervical glands.
Skin - Sensitive to touch. Biting, itching of the whole body. Red, itching blotches. Herpes. Ringworm. Ulcers
with scanty discharge. Erysipelas, erythema. Pricking, itching during fever. Measles. Itching in swollen glands.
Sleep - Sleeplessness with fantastic dreams and delirium on going to sleep. Generally worse after sleep or
sleeps into an aggravation (Lach.). Awakes in a fright andfeels as if suffocating with terror and fear.
Starting from sleep. Sad, anxious, frightful dreams. Somnambulism.
Stomach - Cannot bear tight clothing. Stomach feels flaccid as if standing open. Chill in pit of stomach. Sour
regurgitations. Frequent hiccough. Nausea with acidity in mouth. Vomiting after having partaken of milk.
Temperature -Attacks of heat with anxiety. Heat, redness of face, perspiration. Heat in flushes with anxiety,
cardiac pain, would rather die, with cold moist thighs, worse thinking of it. Heat and sudden weakness after
walking in open air, must lie down.
Throat - Burning and stinging. Stitches and dryness. Bitter taste. Sensation as if plug in larynx. Diphtheria.
Larynx, painful, dry, constricted worse touch, singing, talking or swallowing, he grasps it. Laryngeal
tuberculosis. Sore throat, worse eating sweet things. Clears throat constantly. Throat symptoms better lying
on back. Swallows water in small quantity and with difficulty. Numb externally. Hoarseness with many
complaints, cough, coryza. Voice gives way when singing or talking.
Vertigo - Vertigo with giddiness to such an extent as to fall. Vertigo with a sensation as if head were about to
fall on one side. Vertigo with nausea, on waking at night.
COMMENTS - The action of Spong, on the respiratory organs is closely connected with its action on the
glandular system,
Spongia tosta the lymphatics. The thyroid and testes are indurated. The blood, heart and veins are also
involved and, with the protruding eyes, a perfect picture of exophthalmic goiter is produced.
Tuberculosis of the larynx. Tuberculosis of apices, with commencing solidification, tubercles spreading
downwards. Tuberculosis of the lungs with weakness of the voice and a chronic, dry, hacking cough.
Congestion of chest coming on when the patient is moving about, with sudden weakness as if he would fall.
Croup (Aeon., Hep., Samb., Brom., and lod.), of the larynx. Croupy deposits on the valves of the heart.
Chronic bronchitis with a deep, resonating cough, especially in the elderly, worse excitement or exertion, with
constant dryness, hacking. Must sit up and lean forward. Respiratory symptoms in excited children. Dry asthma
with asthmatic cough, wheezing and whistling. Laryngitis with change of voice, the throat feels plugged up, like
the larynx was grabbed.
Rapid and suffocative breathing with a deep, resonating cough. Slow and deep breathing. Paralyzed with
dryness and constriction, must breathe slowly. Sensation of a sponge in the throat, as though they had to
breathe through a sponge. Wakes up at night suffocating (Aeon., Lach.), with dryness. Fear of suffocation.
General dryness of the mucus membranes (Bry., Alum., Nux-m.). Suffocating, constricting dryness. Dry nasal
passages with dry cough, worse in acold, dry wind (Aeon.). Chronic sore throat, especially with swollen glands
and cough. Dry, hacking coughs (Bry., Rumx.). Deep, resonating coughs. Foghorn coughs with a shrill at the
end, peaks at the end. Burning and rawness in the chest with the coughing. As though the chest would burst
because of all the coughing.
Cough is worse in cold, dry weather, wind, warm and stuffy rooms. Cough worse from exertion. Tobacco
aggravates the cough. Worse lying down and with head lowered. Talking aggravates, can’t talk during attacks.
Desires warm fluids.
Hypertrophy of the heart with asthma. Sensation as though the heart will burst. In a heart attack the heart feels
bigger and bigger (Cact. feels smaller and smaller.). Constriction of the chest and the heart (Cact.). Stinging,
 pressing pain in the heart with violent gasping.
Excitement of the nerves, tendency to start, twitching of muscles with fever. Stiff, without ability to move.
“Conscious but unable to act on her limbs” as in a cataleptic state. Clumsiness of the body. Faint when losing
breath. Feeling of numbness of lower half of body.
Thyroid problems (Calc-i., Fuc., Sep., Nat-m., Thyr.). Hyperthyroid. Goiter. Exophthalmic goiter, protruding
eyes, staring, headaches and enlarged thyroid. Keynote sensation of something alive in the goiter, as if
something moving there. Swollen and hard glands, causes difficulty in breathing, suffocative dryness. There
may be tingling or shooting pain in the thyroid.
Testicular problems. Metastasis of mumps to the testes (Puls., Carb-v.), orto the breast. Hard, swollen,
indurated testicles. Pressing, squeezing or sharp pains in the testicles. The testicles are swollen and very
painful (Clem., Aur., and Puls.). Orchitis, with heaviness and screw-like squeezing pain in cord and testicles.
Orchitis from suppressed gonorrhea (Thuj.).
Chill usually commences across the back, cannot be warmed. Chill, followed by heat, extendiung over the
whole body except the thighs, which remain numb and chilly. Frequent flashes of heat. Skin is hot and dry.
Etiology of exposure to cold, dry wind (Aeon.), but takes a day or so to come out.
Worse after sleep, or sleeps into the aggravation (Lach.). Worse when thinking of the symptoms (Ox-ac.).
Aversion to tobacco and aggravated from it. Problems may start on the right and go to the left.
Kent gave the indication “Rheumatic fever after having been over-heated with arising heart complications.”
Nash gave the keynote of Spong, in valvular diseases^ “Awakes out of sleep from a sense of suffocation with
violent, loud cough, great alarm, agitation, anxiety and difficult respiration.” Nash said it is better
than Lach., and relieves the “dry, chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart disease” more frequently and
more permanently than Naja. Psor. also meets thickening of joints after rheumatic fever.
Boenninghausen’s croup powders consisted of a sequence of Aeon., Spong., and Hep., given in that order.
Spong, is dry. Hep. rattling, Spong, worse before midnight, Hep. worse after midnight.
RELATIONS - Anlidoied by: Camph. Compare: (1) Aeon., Hep., Brom. (2) lod. - goiter. Hep. (3) Lach., Merc.,
Prot. (4) Laryngitis, Samb., Lach. (5) Cough better by eating, Anae. (6) Dry tongue, Nux-m. (7) Better warm
drinks, Ars., Alum., Lyc., Nux-v. (8) Heart, Naja, Sep., Kalm., Lach. (9) Orchitis, Gels., Puls., Ham. (10) Jawjoint
as if dislocated, Rhus-t. (11) Worse thinking of symptoms, Ox-ac., Pip-m. (12) Tubercular diathesis, Bac., Tub.,
Dros. Follows well: Aeon., Hep. Followed well by: Brom., Carb-v.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Squilla Maritima
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - squil. Squilla maritima. Sea onion. Squill. N. O. Liliaceae. Red variety. Hyacinthaceae. Tincture
of fresh bulb. His- iorical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina, pectoris. Ascites. Asthma. Bright’s, disease. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia.
Conjunctivitis, phlyctenular. Coryza. Cough, caiarrhaL Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy, splenic. Dyspnea. Eyes,
disorders. Fidgets. Heart, palpitations. Hydrothorax. Lungs, disorders. Measles. Pleurisy. Pneumonia.
Spleen, disorders. Toothaches. Urine, excessive. Whooping cough. Worms.
HERBAL - Squilla maritima grows on the shores of the Mediterranean Sea and has had a place in medicine
from the most ancient time. The genus Squillais distinguished from Allium by having the flowers inserted one
above the other on the scape, and from Ornithogalum by having the petals deciduous. Green’s Herbal noted
that Squil. promotes expectoration and urine in large doses, vomiting and purging. “Its cardiac action is exactly
the same as that of Digitalis.” An old rule runs “Put squills in every coughmixture.”
Mile recorded “Diuretic, expectorant, emetic, cathartic and a narcotic-acrid poison in large doses it produces
inflammation of the alimentary and urinary canals and a dose of 24 grains has proved fatal.”
According to Hamilton, Avicenna employed Squil. “in complaints of the gums in inveterate coughs in diseases
of the spleen in dropsy and jaundice and forbids its use in ulceration of the viscera,” the last caution also being
mentioned by Celsus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Cooper noted that Squil., if much handled, irritates the skin, and in large doses excites
nausea, strangury, bloody urine and hemorrhoids. Fatal inflammation, gangrene of stomach and bowels in
small doses. The continuous use of squills seems to cause teeth and gums to ache.
The reputation of Squil. as a splenic was revived by Rademacher, whom Burnett quoted, “I have found it
quickly and surely helpful in painful spleen diseases disorders painful and beyond any doubt in and of the
spleen. In those dull pains on the border of the left hypochondriac and epigastric regions, there being no signs
of any liver affection, I have used Squil. as a remedy with advantage.”
Rademacher also mentioned as cured by Squil. those so-called “stomachpains” that are made much better
 by lying on the left side and probably in reality splenic, one case of asthma from a splenic affection with
nocturnal exacerbation, and possibly splenic dropsy.
Burnett improved on Rademacher’s teachings and applied Squil. successfully in cases of spleen-cough.
Hahnemann’s proving brought out many symptoms, apparently arising from the spleen, notably stitches under
the free'ribs of the left side.
Squil. affects the serous and mucus membranes of the respiratory and digestive tract and acts also on the
kidneys, heart and
Squilla marítima spleen. Slow acting, useful for those condition which require several days to reach their
maximum. Persistent, dull, rheumatic pains throughout the body.
A spleen remedy, stitches under left free ribs. Heart and kidney ailments. Bronchopneumonia. Valuable in
chronic bronchitis of old people with mucus rales, dyspnea and scanty urine.
Exudations and profuse secretions. Dropsy with profuse urine. Gurglings. Cardio-urinary effects. Action is like
Dig.; follows Dig. when it fails to relieve dropsical conditions.
MIND - Great anxiety of the mind. Angry about trifles. Malicious. Haughty. Aversion to mental and bodily labor.
Inclination to sit, aversion to bed. Confusion after sleeping, on walking. Delirium after hemorrhage. Fear of
death.
Abdomen - Painful diseases of the spleen. Aching in hypochondria. Cutting pain in abdomen. Rumbling and
gurgling in paroxysms above pubic region, better eating. Bubbling sensation in muscles of right side. Frequent
discharge of fetid flatulence. Ascites with scanty urine.
Back - Stiffness of nape of neck. Bubbling beneath scapula. Painful jerking above left scapula. Drawing in left
scapula.
Chest - Stitches in chest. Perspiration in armpit.
Ears - Tearing behind left ear. Tearing pains in both ears.
Eyes - Left eye looks much smaller than right. Child rubs eyes and face much, as if to relieve itching in brain
affectations, measles. As if swimming in cold water. Tears with cough. Staring look, eyes wide open.
Face - Changeable expression and color of face. Distorted countenance. Child rubs the face with fist during
cough. Lips twitch and are covered with yellow crusts. Humid, spreading eruption on upper lip. Black, cracked
lips and black teeth.
Female - Atony of the cervix, uterus. Hemorrhage from uterus.
Food - Insatiable appetite. Longing for acids. The food tastes bitter, especially bread. Tastes sweet, especially
soup and meat. Tastelessness of tobacco when smoked. Thirst for cold drinks. Drinks in sips during dyspnea.
Head - Stinging headache. Headache in morning on waking, with pressing pains. Painful sensitiveness of
vertex every morning. Pulsation in head when raising it.
Heart - A cardiac stimulant affecting the peripheral vessels and coronary arteries. Pulse small and slow, slightly
hard.
Kidneys - Great urging, much watery urine, involuntary spurting of urine when coughing (Caust., Puls.).
Frequent calls to urinate at night, passing large quantities (Ph-ac.). Bloody urine. Feces escape when urinating.
Limbs - Hands and feet cold, body hot (Meny.). Feet get sore from standing. Nails become brittle and split.
Lungs - Wheezing. Splenic asthma. Dyspnea and stitches in chest and painful contraction of abdominal
muscles. Sneezing, throat irritated, short, dry cough, must take a deep breath. Pleurisy. Bronchopneumonia.
Fluent coryza, margins of nostrils feel sore. Sneezing with coughing. Cough, stubborn, dry, rattling, disturbs
sleep. Child rubs face with fist during cough (Caust., Puls.). Violent, exhausting cough with much mucus,
v,ilh involuntary spurting of urine and sneezing. Expectoration, easy, heavy, difficult in small round balls
of sweetish taste, white or reddish offensive. Profuse, salty, and a slimy expectoration. Cough provoked by
taking a deep breath or cold drinks from exertion. Cough changes from warm to cold air. Cough of measles.
Male - Erotic pollutions. Dull stitches in glans causing anxiety. Compressive pain in testicles.
Modalities - Better from rest, lying down in bed, sitting up, wrapping warmly. Better expectoration even a small
quantity. Worse early morning. Worse motion, exertion, ascending. Worse inspiration, coughing, cold air,
uncovering. Drinking cold water causes cough.
Mouth - Taste, sweet of food, especially soup and meat. Bitter taste to bread. In-
Squilla maritima creased saliva. Open, dry mouth. Scraping, burning on palate. Vesicles on tongue. Black
spots on teeth.
Nose - Violent sneezing with fluent acrid coryza. Sneezing during cough. Copious running worse in morning.
Coryza with ulcerated nostrils. Humid eruptions under nose with itching.
Rectum - Stitches in anus when walking. Itching in anus. Painless constipation. Stools dark, brown, frothy,
very offensive. Diarrhea, stool very offensive, watery. Passes thread worms and white tissues with tenesmus.
Sensations - Prominent stitches, in teeth, in chest, in head. Eyes as if swimming in cold water. Nostrils as if
 sore. As if chest too tight. Tickling creeping in chest. As if intestines would burst through abdomen. As if
diarrhea would set in.
Skin - Handling the fresh squills caused blisters. Eruptions like itch, with burningitching. Small red spots all
over the body with pricking pain. Soreness in the bends of the joints. Hard swellings. Gangrene.
Sleep - Frequent yawning without sleepiness. Restless sleep, with much tossing about. Dreamed that his body
was excessively swollen.
Stomach - Pressure in stomach as from a stone. Stomach pains are better lying on left side. Constant nausea
in pit of stomach. Nausea during the morning cough.
Temperature - Chill internally at night with external heat. Heat with aversion to uncover. Heat, dry, burning,
internally predominates. Whenever he uncovers himself during the fever he suffers from chilliness and pain.
Perspiration wanting, even during the violent burning heat.
Throat - Dryness in throat. Burning in mouth and throat. Irritation in throat causing constant cough. Pain in
submaxillary glands.
Vertigo - Vertigo in the morning with nausea. Vertigo as if he would fall sideways on rising from bed. Cloudy
dizziness.
COMMENTS - Burnett used the Acetum Squil. and Clarke gave this (five drops of in water three times a day)
with excellent effect in the case of an elderly woman, very gouty, who had a distressing paroxysmal cough
with a pain extending from splenic region into the throat. The cough caused sneezing, flow of tears, spurting
of urine and even involuntary stools.
The kidneys are acted on by Squil. and many of the traditional uses of the drug have been with the idea of
eliminating dropsical effusions by reproducing a great flow of urine. Hahnemann pointed out that the excessive
flow of urine accompanying dropsy and other complaints was one of the best indications for its use.
Boger added the heart to the organs primarily affected by Squil. He gave three cases. Mr. B. suffered from
angina pectoris, forcible cardiac contractions, profuse urine, much loose mucus in throat and trachea, heart
pain indefinite but very severe. Squil. 30c relieved in a few hours and kept him free from an attack for three
months.
Miss L., pleuro-pneumonia, pulse 132, temperature 103 F, respiration 30, must sit erect in bed. Stitching pains
in left chest, constant hacking cough. Frequent, hot, scanty urine, great weakness and anorexia. Squil.
100,000c cured.
A boy, 7, hay fever for third year in succession. Teeth show black marks, constantly rubs eyes and sneezes,
bloated about eyes and face, loose cough. Under Squil. there was complete relief in two days and no further
trouble that season.
Boger mentioned that Lippe noted “black teeth” as a symptom of Squil. Boger added that the nails become
brittle and split and that veterinarians use Squil. for cracked hoof in horses.
The use of Squil. as an “expectorant” depends on its power of producing free secretion from the respiratory
mucus membranes; in homeopathy this free secretion is one of the leading indications.
Hering said Squil. is suited to the pleurisy and pneumonia that follow blood-letting.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1/Headache, worse motion, chest symptoms, Bry. (2) Bry.
cough is worse change to warm, Squil. cough worse change to cold air. (3) Stitches, swollen upper eyelids,
Kali-c.
(4) Cold drink causes or worse cough, Lyc., Sil. (better by cough, Caust.). (5) Expectoration sweetish and
offensive, Calc., Stann. (6) Spurting of urine when coughing, Caust., Alum., Con., Nat-m., Puls. (7) Dig.,
Stroph., Apoc., Bry., Kali-c. Compatible after: Bry. Squil. follows Dig., if this fails to relieve water-logged cases.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Stachys Betonica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stach. Stacnys betónica. Wood betony. N. O. Labiate. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Belching. Colds. Diaphragm, paralysis. Headaches. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Berridge published the proving of Stach. made by Croker and himself with some others.
Pains in various parts, dizziness, fullness in head and eyes with disposition to take cold.
Tired, especially in legs. Great sensitiveness to take cold. A feeling of oppressed breathing as from paralysis
of diaphragm. Stach. has been used in eye-waters and as a remedy for headaches.
MIND - Inability to concentrate mind. Distracted easily. Mental dullness.
Abdomen - Pains in abdomen, hepatic region and of transverse colon, also in gallbladder and right inguinal
region and spermatic cords.
 Ears - Slight earache.
Eyes - Heavy, sleepy feeling in eyes. Pain in eyeballs as if too tense, worse looking at light, reading, thinking,
bending head down.
Head - Stitches in right temple. Fullness over and in eyes as if they would burst. Dull, heavy action in frontal
region better walking about in room.
Kidneys - Woke with desire to urinate in night. Urine high-colored, ammoniacal.
Limbs - Shooting pain in back of both wrist joints. Wrist drops. Pain in right popliteal space down leg, which
feels paralyzed.
Liver - Pains in hepatic region and gallbladder.
Lungs - Breathing oppressed as from paralysis of diaphragm, constriction just behind ensiform cartilage, on
walking up hill must keep mouth open.
Nose - Frequent sneezing, increased nasal mucus on going indoors from open air.
Stomach - Warmth in stomach increasing to sharp cutting pain. Weight in stomach with feeling of sickness.
Belchings, tasting of drug.
Temperature - Free perspiration. In night profuse sweat, limited to head, neck and chest.
Vertigo - Dizziness better open air, worse closing eyes or moving head.
RELATIONS - Compare: (6) Lycps. and the Labiate.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Stannum Iodatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stann-i. Stannum iodatum. Tin iodide. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Coughs. Lung, disorders. Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Stann-i. is valuable in chronic chest diseases characterized by tissue changes, with
persistent inclination to cough. It is indicated in cases that ‘hang fire’ and need an alternative.
Stann-i. has been used in preference to Stann. in some tubercular cases in which the general features of
Stann. were present.
Persistent inclination to cough, excited by tickling dry spot in the throat, apparently at root of tongue. Dryness
of throat. Tracheal and bronchial irritation of smokers. Pulmonary symptoms, cough, loud, hollow, ending with
expectoration (Phel.). Purulent infiltration.
Stonham noted that in advanced tuberculosis when Stann-i. has not taken effect, an additional dose of iodine
in milk caused the drug to have its usual beneficial effect.
Chest - Feeling of dryness, weakness in chest and throat and increased oppression.
Lungs - Persistent cough, excited by tickling, dry spot in the throat. Cough beginning with a weak sounding
cough with short breath, soon gathers strength and sound. Coughs up a copious, pale yellowish expectoration.
Consolidation in middle of right lung.
COMMENTS - O. S. Haines considered Stann-i. especially indicated where the patient “has a clear complexion
and long eyelashes and where the progress of the disease is rapid.” He used the 2x trituration.
M. D. Youngman found it a deeply acting drug, chiefly of value in chronic chest diseases characterized by
plastic tissue changes. Stann-i. is indicated in cases that “hang fire” and need an “alterative.”
Youngman gave the keynote, “A persistent inclination to cough. Cough excited by a tickling dry spot in the
throat, sometimes in one place, sometimes in another often apparently at root of tongue.”
This cough, which begins as a weak- sounding cough, accompanied by shortness of breath. The cough soon
gathers strength and sound and induces raising of a free, copious, pale yellowish expectoration, which at first
aggravates. Buf is soon followed by a feeling of dryness, weakness in throat and chest and increased
oppression.
An inveterate smoker, who had a cough of this kind, said it came from his throat and ascribed it to his smoking.
Youngman found consolidation areas in the middle of the right lung. There was weak feeling in chest after
coughing.
Stann-i. 3x trituration, greatly relieved. The man was sent to a high altitude, where he enjoyed perfect health
and was freed from his smoking habit.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Stannum Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stann. Stannum metallicum. Tin metal. (Sn, At. Wt. 118.102). Trituration of the pure metal.
Historical dose: All potencies.
 CLINICAL - Anemia. Asthma. Bronchitis. Chest, weakness. Chilblains. Colic. Convulsions. Cramps.
Debility. Dentition. Diaphragm, pains. Dyspepsia. Ears, ulceration. Epilepsy. Gastralgia. Hematemesis.
Hemoptysis. Headaches. Hectic, fever. Hemiplegia. Hypochondriasis. Hysteria. Lachrymal fistula. Lungs,
weak. Milk, altered, Nails, splitting. Neuralgias. Neurasthenia. Nosebleeds. Opisthotonos. Paralysis. Ptosis.
Sleeplessness. Sore, throat. Styes. Tapeworms. Trachitis. Tuberculosis. Uterus, prolapsed. Vagina,
prolapse. Voice, weak. Weakness. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Stannum is the Jupiter of the alchemists. “The ancients have recorded wonderful cures of
the most serious diseases with Tin,” said Hahnemann, but in his day, until he proved it, its main use was as a
vermifuge. The chief action centers on the nervous system, respiratory organs, and liver.
Marked debility. Debility in chronic bronchial and pulmonary conditions, characterized by profuse muco-
purulent discharges upon tuberculosis basis. Talking causes a very weak feeling in the throat and chest.
Extreme weakness in the chest, throat, stomach, upper arms and thighs. The patient is unable even to talk,
drops into a chair instead of sitting down, trembles on moving. Weakness is felt much more on going downstairs
than going up. Paralytic heaviness or weakness. Paralysis from worms after spasms, emotions, onanism.
Hemiplegia, part constantly moist.
Pains increase gradually and gradually subside. Pressive drawing pains. Spasms with pain in abdomen
and diaphragm. Epileptic spasms with tossing of limbs, clenching of thumbs, opisthotonos, unconsciousness
and sexual complications.
Cramps, hysteria. Neuralgia, diaphragmatic, suppressed.
Affections of mucus membranes produces yellow, muco-purulent secretions. Bland secretions. Emaciation.
Girdle sensation with yawning. Trembling more from slow motion or exercise. Child wants to be carried across
shoulders.
MIND - Depressed and hopeless with lung problems. Low spirited, despondent and without hope, feels like
crying all the time, but crying aggravates. Anxious, nervous, sad, worse before menses. Miserable. Sad and
discouraged.
Discontented with everything. Uneasy, knows not what to do with himself. Forgetful and absent-minded.
Forgetful on waking in morning. Thinking makes her feel wretched. Cannot get rid of an idea once fixed in her
mind.
Taciturn and dislike to society. Dread of seeing people. Fear in a crowd. Fear of men, during pregnancy.
Suspicious. Aversion to certain persons (Nat-c.). Child wants to be carried across shoulders. Very sensitive as
to what others say about her. Changeable mood. Sudden fits of passion. Can’t answer questions from
weakness.
Abdomen - Abdomen painfully distended and sensitive to touch. Incarceration of flatus. Cutting, pinching,
cramp-like colic, around navel. Colic with hunger, diarrhea and a feeling of emptiness, exhausting, relieved
by hard pressure. Colic in children, better by carrying them on shoulder. Spasmodic pain in abdomen,
hysterical.
Back - Stitches in back, small of back, and into limbs. Opisthotonos. Weakness of the muscles of the nape of
the neck.
Breasts - A child leaves the breast of its mother and will not nurse (Sil.).
Causations - Ill effects of emotions, fright, masturbation, dentition, using voice.
Chest - Oppression of chest when coughing, with emptiness in pit of stomach. Oppression as if chest were
internally constricted. Tension across upper part of chest with emptiness in lower. Weak, empty sensation in
chest, is constantly obliged to stop and take a breath. Chest feels weak, can hardly talk. Chest feels raw or
hollow. Aching in chest from reading aloud. Diaphragmatic neuralgia, hysterical. Soreness. Stitches in left side
of chest, when breathing or lying on that side. Knife-like pains, below left axilla. Itching, tickling in chest. Sharp
pains in chest and sides hinder respiration. Sharp, cutting stitches in left side of chest, worse stooping.
Gnawing pain at middle of sternum.
Constitutions - Tubercular constitutions.
Cough - Cannot walk, cannot do anything without coughing. Short breath from every effort, must loosen
clothes. Hemoptysis with copious expectoration. Concussive, in paroxysms of three coughs. Violent, dry cough
in evening until midnight. Cough excited by laughing, singing, talking. Cough worse lying on right side.
Influenza cough from noon to midnight with scanty expectoration. Hoarse, mucus expelled by forcible cough.
Cough during day, with copious green, sweetish expectoration, most profuse in morning. Retching with
coughing.
Ears - Cracking, shrieking noise in ear when blowing nose. Tinkling, ringing in ears, particularly the left.
Earache with drawing tearings. Ulceration of holes pierced for earrings.
Eyes - Sunken, dull, clouded eyes. Pupils contracted. Eyes sore. Itching, smarting and burning sensation in
 eyes. Great sensitiveness to light during headache. Jerking and quivering of eyes. Burning lancinations in lids.
Agglutination of eyelids at night. Pustular swelling of left inner canthus. Blenorrhea. Ptosis. Styes.
Face - Face pale, sickly-looking, flushing easily on exertion. One cheek hot and red. Painful swelling of
submaxillary glands. Swelling of cheeks and upper jaw. Spasm in jaw. Prosopalgia, pains increase and de-
crease gradually. Drawing pains in malar bones. Malar neuralgia, at menses.
Female - Strong body odor during menses. Menses early andprofuse. Bearing-down sensation. Gushing
leucorrhea, yellowwhite or transparent mucus, with much debility. Prolapse uterus and vagina, worse stools.
Prolapse with weak, sink
ing feeling in stomach (Sep.). Uterine symptoms with a weak, drawn sensation in the chest. Pain in vagina
upward and back to spine. Scratching of distant parts (of arms) produce an intolerable sensation of pleasure
in genital organs producing orgasm. Increased sexual desire, early orgasm.
Food - Increased hunger, which cannot be satisfied. Increased thirst. Bitter taste of all food. Bitter, herbaceous
taste of beer. Smell of cooking causes vomiting. Excessive weakness of digestion. Nausea and vomiting
after a meal.
Head - Severe, painful constriction in forehead and temples. Pressi ve and stupefying headache. Migraine of
cerebral origin, better by vomiting. Aching in temples and forehead. Pains worse motion, gradually increasing
and decreasing. Violent, glowing, beating pains, as if the head would burst with inward blows. Jarring of
walking resounds painfully in head. Drawing pains in malar bones and orbits. Ulceration of hole in lobe of ear.
Obstinate acute coryza and influenza with cough.
Heart - Pain in precordial region and hiccough. Pulse frequent and small.
Kidneys - Dull stitches inward in kidney region. Insensibility of the bladder, only the sense of fullness indicates
the necessity to urinate. Atony of bladder. Retention of urine. Blister on margin of meatus.
Limbs - Paralytic weakness, drops things. Limbs suddenly give out when attempting to sit down. Tremulous
knees. Swelling of the hands and ankles. Spasmodic twitching of muscles of forearm and hand. Cramps in
hands, cannot let go the broom. Fingers jerk when holding pen. Typist’s paralysis. Contraction of fingers,
retraction of thumbs. Neuritis. Aching in deltoid from reading.
Liver - Pressure and burning sensation in hepatic region. Weak liver, poor digestion. Bitter and sour taste.
Lungs - Asthma. Emphysema. Pneumonia. Bronchiectasis. Takes deep breaths. Shortness of breath on
exertion. Short, oppressive respiration, stitches in left side when breathing and lying on same side. Lungs
feels weak, can hardly talk. Sharp pains in lungs which hinder respiration. Much mucus in trachea. Copious
green, sweetish expectoration. Easy expectoration, quantities of sweet, salty, sour, putrid or bright yellow pus
or ball of mucus. Catarrhal tuberculosis. Last-stage tuberculosis remedy, used for tuberculosis epidemics.
Last stages of respiratory illnesses heading toward lung failure.
Male - Increased sexual desire. Voluptuous feeling in genitals ending in emission, which exhausts. Frequent
pollutions with excessive prostration.
Modalities - Pains are better walking, but must soon rest. Better by pressure, lying across something hard,
bending double. Better rapid motion. Better coughing, expectorating and open air. Worse using voice,
laughing, talking, singing. Worse going down stairs, ascending. Worse lying, gentle motion, touch. Worse from
weakness of chest. Worse from cold, warm drinks. Worse during stool. Worse at 10 a.m.
Mouth - Sweet, sour, bitter taste, for all food except water. Fetid exhalation from mouth. Flow of acid saliva.
Tickling at the root of the tongue. Tongue coated with a yellowish mucus. Tongue red or yellow. Difficult, weak
speech, occasioned by weakness.
Nose - Oversensitive to smells. Heaviness and sensation of obstruction. Stuffed feeling and heaviness high
up in nostrils. Burning sensation in nose. Dry coryza on one side only. Obstinate coryza and influenza with
cough. Nosebleed on moving, on rising from bed.
Perspiration - Heat in evening, exhausting night sweats, towards the morning. Perspiration at 4 a.m.
Debilitating perspiration, principally on forehead and nape of neck. Sweat smelling musty or offensive.
Rectum - Burning in anus, constant itching. Constipation. Monday constipation, occurring after working days.
Frequent ineffectual want to evacuate. Hard, dry, knotty feces or else scanty and greenish. Stools are green,
curdy with colic. Passes worms.
Sensations - As if all objects were too far off. As if she would faint. As if forehead were shattered. As if forehead
would be pressed inward. Tickling as from soreness in trachea. Inclination to hawk as if mucus were in chest.
Chest, as if eviscerated, as if internally constricted. As of a heavy load in affected arm and side of chest.
Epigastric region as if beaten. As if limbs beaten. As if sweat would break out.
Skin - Itching, burning, shootings over skin of whole body. Itching pimples on face, sore to touch or on washing.
Chilblains. Flaws in nails. Painful hangnails.
Sleep - Nocturnal agitation and many vivid dreams, anxious or lascivious. Moaning, weeping and plaintive
 lamentations while sleeping. Sleeps with one leg drawn up, the other stretched out.
Stomach - Pain better pressure, but sore to touch. Sensation of emptiness in stomach. Uneasy feeling.
Smell of cooking causes nausea and vomiting. Bitter taste. Vomiting, violent of blood of bile, early in the
morning with odor of ingesta.
Teeth - Sensation of elongation and looseness in teeth. Toothache after a meal with jerking pain and heat in
the face. Ulcer on gums with swelling of cheeks.
Temperature - Chill 10 a.m. with numb fingertips. Hectic fever. Burning palms and soles. Heat in evening,
exhausting night sweats, towards the morning.
Throat - Throat dry and stings. Sore throat, as from an internal swelling. Rawness in larynx. Cutting in pharynx
and esophagus on swallowing. Nausea in throat. Adhesive mucus, difficult to detach, efforts to detach cause
nausea. Voice deep, hollow, hoarse, better hawking mucus. Hoarseness with weakness of voice. Laryngitis.
Vertigo - Dizziness and weakness when descending. Vertigo, all objects seem too far off. Vertigo on sitting
down, with loss of ideas.
COMMENTS - Hahnemann’s Stann. proving appears in his Materia Medica Pura and in his Chronic Diseases.
A number of worm symptoms appeared, including a sinking, empty, all-gone feeling, and diaphragmatic and
abdominal pains. Tendency to exces-
sive mucus secretions. Pale, sunken, sickly countenance with dark rings around the eyes. Convulsions. Hectic
fever.
Compressive and cramp-like pains. Cramps and spasms. Opisthotonic convulsions, thumbs are drawn in,
particularly in teething children, in children who masturbate, or who have worms.
Pains associated with the hypochondriac or hysterical mental state. Pains begin lightly, increase gradually to
the highest point and then gradually decline, particularly in headaches, facial and dental neuralgias, abdominal
and other pains. Diaphragmatic neuralgia.
Characteristic weakness, exhaustion of mind and body. Nervous weakness with trembling. Neurasthenia.
Depressed and hopeless with lung problems. Low spirited, despondent and without hope. Trembling of arms
and legs, limbs as heavy as lead. Palpitations and anxiety occur from slightest exertion.
The chest is so weak as to make talking impossible. Weakness in the throat in singers and speakers.
Weakness and aching of the deltoid and arm, felt when using the voice. The patient will drop into a chair
instead of sitting down. Must sit down several times to rest while dressing in the morning. Weakness felt more
going down stairs than on going up. Weak, empty, sinking sensation felt at the epigastrium.
Characteristic respiratory or lung weakness. Last-stage tuberculosis remedy, used historically tuberculosis
epidemics. Last stages of respiratory illnesses heading toward lung failure. Emphysema. Pneumonia.
Hoarseness, laryngitis, hollow voice.
Keynote weakness in the lungs and breathing. Patient talks extremely weakly, must put ear to patient’s mouth
to hear. Weak, empty feeling in the chest, in tubercular conditions. Stitches in the chest. Shortness of breath
on exertion.
Deep, hollow, shattering cough (Spong.). Deep, husky, hollow voice, better by hawking or expectorating
mucus. Profuse expectoration, like an egg white (Nairn.), sweetish, salty, sour, putrid, musty, yellow-green
pus. Thick globs of green
sputum. Coughs up green pus and globs of green mucus (Kali-b.). Yellow secretions, including sputa,
leucorrhea and coating on the tongue.
Dyspepsia, with nausea and vomiting from the smell of cooking. Stomach pain compels the patient to walk
about for relief, yet the weakness is so great that he is soon compelled to rest. Colic, better by hard pressure,
as by laying the child with its abdomen across the knee or on the point of the shoulder.
Menses are early and profuse. Uterine and vaginal prolapse, worse during stool, especially during pressure.
Labor pains are spasmodic and put the patient out of breath. The milk of nursing woman is changed and the
child rejects it.
Sexual excitement in both sexes. Emissions with excessive prostration. Orgasm is easily produced,
“Scratching arm produces an intolerable sensation of pleasure in genital organs which extends to uterus and
produces orgasm.”
Clinique quoted a typical case of a neuralgia cured by Stann. A man, 30, suffered for eight years off and on
and for some months continuously with neuralgic headache. Pain centered over one or the other eye (usually
the right) and extended over whole or part of head and was at limes unbearable.
It began in the early morning (4 to 5 a.m.), increased gradually to noon, when it gradually declined to sunset,
reappearing again the following morning. Two doses of Stann. cured in a fortnight.
Hering gave as cured by Stann. “Monday constipation,” that is, constipation occurring on days following rest-
days. Stann. has marked periodicity.
 T. H. Urquhart cured an affection of the nails characterized by breaking and splitting, and a sequel of scurvy,
with an application of Stannum oleate on a narrow flannel bandage. All symptoms were cured in two months.
Alston obtained indirectly from “a woman of Leith in Scotland” this prescription of which he had witnessed the
efficacy in a case of tapeworm: “Take an ounce and a half of Tin, (pewter metal) and grind it small to powder,
mix it with sugar syrup and take, on a Friday before the change of the moon, one-half of it, the following day
the half of the remainder and the Sunday following the rest, but on the Monday a purgative.”
Alston also noted in his Materia Medica that he had seen hematemesis cured by this remedy.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Puls., Phos. Compare: (1) Stann-i., Phos.,Caust., Calc., Sil., Tub., Bac., Melon.
(2)Myrt-ch. - chronic bronchitis, cough of tuberculosis, emphysema with gastric catarrh and thick, yellow
difficult sputum. Old persons with weakened power of expectoration. (3) Sour sensation in stomach, Chel.,
Phos., Sep. (4) Weeps all the time, but crying aggravates. (5) Worse descending, can go up well enough, Bor.
(6) Pain increases and decreases gradually, Plat., Stront. (7) Nausea from smell of cooking food, Ars., Colch.
(8) Weak from talking, Cocc., Verat., Sulph., Calc. (9) Catarrhal tuberculosis, Sil. ( 10) Paralysis by emotions,
Staph., Nat-m. Complementary: Puls. Follows well: Caust., Cina. Followed well by: Calc., Phos., Sei.,
Sulph., Bac.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Staphylococcinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - staphycoc. Staphy lococcinum. Staphylococcusbacteria. Nosodes. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Acne. Adenitis. Allergies. Anthrax. Aortitis. Blepharitis. Boils. Carbuncle. Cellulitis.
Conjunctivitis. Dacrocystitis. Edema. Endocarditis. Empyema. Fever. Folliculitis. Furuncle. Impetigo. Kidney,
disorders. Lymphadenitis. Mastitis. Mastoiditis. Meibomian cysts. Meningitis. Myelitis. Osteomyelitis.
Parotiditis. Pemphigus. Phlebitis. Prostatitis. Pyelonephritis. Pyemia. Radiculitis. Septicemia. Staphylococcal,
infections. Styes. Sycosis. Thrombophlebitis. Whitlow.
HOMEOPATHIC - Staphycoc. is used for diseases where the staphylococcus bacteria is the chief bacterial
factor, such as acne, abscess, furuncle, empyema, impetigo, and endocarditis. Morbid conditions where the
staphylococcus pyogenes aureus or albus or citreus is notably symbiotic or is the direct and chief bacterial
factor.
Julian wrote that the main indications for Staphycoc. are chronic illnesses in which staphylococci are present,
e.g. in boils, impetigo, blepharitis, styes, Meibomian cysts, osteomyelitis, whitlow, but possibly also in
perinephritic abscess, malignant staphylococcal infections of the face, acne vulgaris, cystic acne,
thrombophlebitis, and possibly also in anthrax.
Psoric and sycotic. Allergic conditions. Pre-diabetic conditions. Syndrome of acute septicemia. Oscillating
fever with great chill, general condition is weakened, an enlarged spleen. Radiculitis. Myelitis. Meningitis.
Abscess of the brain.
Heart - Endorcarditis. Pericarditis.
Kidneys - Pyelonephritis. Prostatitis. Acute prostatic abscess.
Limbs - Spondylitis. Osteitis. Ostemy- elitis.
Lungs - Pulmonary abscesses.
Skin - Abscess. Purpura vesicles, pustular. Follicular pustule. Follicultis of the integument. Sycosis of the
mustache. Adenitis of the armpits. Anthrax. Ecthyma. Panaris. Onyxis. Perionyxis.
COMMENTS - Dr. P. W. Shedd of New York noted that Staphycoc. is made from the Staph, alb. aur. citreus,
a species whose variations in color are dependent upon what the plant gets as nourishment.
The attenuations of this nosode are prepared from the washings of cultures of staphylococci. While preparing
this particular remedy, the maker was compelled to get out of the room several times because of a decided,
though indefinite, malaise.
The odor, aroma or effluvium was ambrosia compared to the atmosphere of the dissecting room with its lumps
of putrefaction, but it had much greater expulsive power, not nauseating, but sickening and chemically probably
due to some of the fatty acids.
Anshutz wrote, “In the human economy the staphylococcus does best where weakness of the protective
mechanism or debility due to other than bacterial agencies, e.g., overwork, worry, lack of proper food, heredity,
excess, etc., is prominent.”
Staphycoc. may be of value in conditions due to damage from staphylococcal toxins. Auto-immune diseases
of all kinds, in which staphylococci were involved. Myocardial lesions, nephritis, hepatic lesions, connective
tissue lesions and thyroid illnesses.
 RELATIONS - Compare: Strept., Ars., Bapt., Sil., Pyrog.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.
