name: Strontium Carbonicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stront-c. Strontium carbonicum. Strontium carbonate. Strontianite. Trituration. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Ankle, sprains. Anus, burning. Arteriosclerosis. Bedwetting. Bones, diseases.
Cardialgía. Constipation. Cramp. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Feet, cold. Femur, decay. Headaches. Heart,
disorders. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Hoarseness. Leucorrhea. Menses, disorders. Neuritis. Phlebitis.
Photophobia. Sciatica. Shock. Sprains. Sternum, pains. Strokes. Sycotic, eruptions. Varicose, veins. Vision
disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - Strontianite was first discovered in the lead mines of Strontain in Argyllshire, from which it
received its name. It occurs in massive, fibrous, stellated, rarely ortho-rhombic, crystals. The metal stronlium
is dark yellow. Strontium carbonate varies in color from white to yellow and pale green.
Stront-c. was proved by Nenning, Schreter, Seidel, Trincks and Woost. It affects the circulation, causing a
 congestive feeling of tension. The heart, kidneys, marrow, ankles and right side are also affected.
Rheumatic pains, chronic sprains and stenosis of esophagus. Pains make patient faint or sick all over. Pain
and itching alternate. Pains are fleeting, can hardly tell where they are, seemingly felt in marrow of bones.
Pains increase and decrease gradually or make the patient faint and sick all over. Burning, gnawing. Right
side most affected.
For the shock after surgical operations. Chronic sequelae of hemorrhages, after operations with much
oozing of blood and coldness and prostration.
Arteriosclerosis. High blood pressure, with flushed face pulsating arteries, threatened strokes. Edema,
especially about the ankles as a concomitant. Numbness. Soreness. Restlessness at night, smothering feeling.
Affections of bones, especially femur.
Violent involuntary starts. Immobility of one side. Sense of paralytic weakness.
Formication in limbs. Neuritis, worse cold. Coldness in spots, on calves. Pressure in stomach is better by
eating and worse after a meal. Emaciation.
MIND - Depression of spirits. Excessive forgetfulness. Inquietude and anguish. Apprehension as from bad
conscience. Irritable, suddenly becomes angry, beats anything that comes in his way. Peevishness with
tendency to fly into a rage.
Abdomen - Sticking in the abdominal ring. Uncomfortable fullness and swelling of abdomen. Colic in umbilical
region.
Back - Pain, as of a fracture in loins and back. Drawing pain in back and lumbar region.
Causations - Hemorrhages, chronic sequelae. Injuries, sprains. Shock. Surgical shock after blood loss.
Great exhaustion after surgery.
Chest - Pressure at chest in sternum. Constriction, pressive pain, worse walking. Drawing pain in muscles of
chest. Angina pectoris.
Constitutions - Suited to bone disorders of scrofulous children when associated with diarrhea.
Ears - Tearing in front of right ear as if in the bone. Sticking in front of left ear in frequent paroxysms. Humming
in the ears.
Eyes - Burning and redness of eyes. Pain and lachrymation on using eyes, with dancing and alternation of
colors of objects looked at. Photophobia, remaining after operation, especially when objects appear covered
with blood. Green spots before the eyes in the dark.
Face - Flushed face, worse from exertion. Violent, pulsating flushes in face. Red with burning heat or very
pale, every time the patient walks. Red face, burns, itches.
Female - Flushes of heat, worse during menopause. Profuse perspiration at night, menopausal.
Food - Loss of appetite, food tasteless. Craving for bread, beer. Aversion to meat.
Head - Aches into upper jaw with vertigo and nausea. Headaches from nape of neck, spreading upwards,
better wrapping head up warmly (Sil.). Distensive pressure on head. Aching eyebrows. Supra-orbital neuralgia,
pains increase and decrease slowly (Stann.).
Heart - Heart feels smothered. Heart block. Dull, intermitting pressure in precordial region. Violent beating of
arteries and of heart.
Kidneys - Pale urine with strong smell of ammonia. Increased secretion of a yellow, deep-colored urine.
Diminished secretion of urine. Nocturnal emission of urine.
Limbs - Rheumatic pain, in joints, in right shoulder. Rheumatism with diarrhea. Sciatica with edema of ankle.
Immobility of the limbs of one side only, like paralysis. Gnawing as if in marrow of the bones. Chronic sprained
joints. Ankles sprained or swollen. Swelling of ankle remaining after a sprain. Weakness of ankles. Chronic
spasms, especially of ankle joints. Cramps in calves and soles. Icy-cold feet. Veins of hands engorged. Hands
numb.
Lungs - Pressure, as of a load on chest. Pain in the left breast, with oppression, worse after meals. Dry cough,
excited by irritation in trachea, worse at night. Dyspnea, when walking with heat and redness of face.
Modalities - Aversion to darkness. Better from light, heat, and sun. Better immersing in hot water. Better
wraps, hot bath, covering, warm stove. Worse change of weather. Worse cold, uncovering, drafts. Worse
evening, night and early morning. Worse 2 a.m. or 3 a.m., from being quiet. Worse when beginning to move,
walking, stooping Worse sprains, bleeding. Worse touch, rubbing, scratching.
Mouth - Feels numb and dry on waking. Bad odor from mouth. Teeth as screwed together.
Nose - Itching, redness and burning of nose. Bloody crusts in nose. Blowing of dark scabs from nose. Quivering
on one side of nose. Twitching of left side of nose.
Rectum - Exhausting di arrhea with constant urging of yellow water with gripping, worse at night, better
towards morning. Periodical diarrhea. Burning in anus lasts a long time after stool (Rat.). Hard, knotty
Strontium carbonicum stools, evacuated slowly with much effort, then burning in anus lasting for a long time.
 Sensations - As if head were expanded from within. As if scalp were too tight. As if tendons of neck were
drawn up. As if a load on chest. As if all power had left right arm. As ifbruised in back and sacrum. Gnawing
as if in marrow of bones. Symptoms as if in marrow of bones. Symptoms like phantoms, difficult to locate.
Skin - Sprains of ankle joint with edema.
Moist, itching, burning eruption, better in open air, especially warm sunshine. Violent perspiration at night.
Sleep - Retarded sleep. Jerking in body and starts when sleeping. Frequent waking at night, principally caused
by a dry cough. Many fantastic dreams.
Stomach - Pressure in stomach during digestion. Heartburn. Belchings after eating. Violent hiccough causes
chest pains, cardialgía. Nausea, with burning heat in face.
Temperature - Flushes of heat in face, with aversion to uncovering. Profuse perspiration at night, menopausal.
Throat - Hoarseness and roughness in throat, which excites a cough.
Vertigo - Vertigo with headache and nausea.
COMMENTS - Congested state. Flushing in the face and violent pulsation of the arteries, congestion to heart,
lungs and head. Symptoms better by warmth and wrapping up and worse by cold. All complaints are worse
walking, particularly headache, leucorrhea, dyspnea and pressure in the sternum.
Headaches are boring, pressive and tensive. Tension from vertex to upper jaw, as if head were expanded from
within and as if scalp were too tight, worse in evening, when lying with head low, slowly increasing and
decreasing, better from heat. Tension in the nape, as if the tendons were drawn up. Tensive drawing in dorsal
and lumbar muscles. External soreness, numbness.
Venous tension in the arms. “The veins of the arms and hands are injected and tense with great prostration
and ill-humor." Phlebitis, varicose veins. Angina pectoris.
Predisposition toward strokes and high blood pressure. Surgical shock after blood loss. Great exhaustion after
surgery.
Pressure in the stomach, better by eating and worse by walking. Pressure after eating. Diarrhea and
constipation. Stools are accompanied and followed by burning in the rectum. Diarrhea is worse at night, urgent,
with yellow stools. Emaciation.
Calcification, osteoporosis. Weak and brittle bones that break easily. Bony growths and enlargements. Bone
pains, especially the femur, the thighbone. Bone disorders, particularly the femur. Bone disorders in scrofulous
children when associated with diarrhea.
Characteristic weak ankles (Nat-c.). Chronic sprains of the ankle with edema. Sciatica associated with weak
ankles. Ice cold feet. Leg and foot cramps (Calc.).
C. M. Boger cured a sciatica accompanied by edema of left ankle with Stront-c. after other remedies had failed.
A. P. Bowie cured a case occurring after a tedious labor. The stools were large and hard, expelled with great
effort, followed by great pain in anus, burning, lasting a long time and compelling patient to lie down. Anus
violently contracted after stool. Complained of coldness in spots on calves of legs. Stront-c. 6c entirely relieved.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1) Arn., Ruta, Sil., Bar-c., Chin. (2) Stront-br., Stront-n.,
Stront-i. - Arteriosclerosis.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

PHARMACY - stront-c. Strontium carbonicum. Strontium carbonate. Strontianite. Trituration. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Ankle, sprains. Anus, burning. Arteriosclerosis. Bedwetting. Bones, diseases.
Cardialgía. Constipation. Cramp. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Feet, cold. Femur, decay. Headaches. Heart,
disorders. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Hoarseness. Leucorrhea. Menses, disorders. Neuritis. Phlebitis.
Photophobia. Sciatica. Shock. Sprains. Sternum, pains. Strokes. Sycotic,

name: Strontium Nitricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stront-n. Strontium nitricum. Strontium nitrate. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - C. M. Boger had a case in a menopausal woman of passive congestion of the kidneys
completely relieved by Stront-n. The menses, which were usually exceedingly scanty, became profuse.
Morbid cravings. Eczema behind ears.
Headaches. Kidney congestion. Menses scanty. ,
COMMENTS - Boger recorded the following caseofMissD., 18,brunette, who haddull pains over eyes worse
by sunlight, motion, loss of sleep, sewing, reading. Pains were better after stool, with headache, swelling of
upper lids, worse in morning. Bad taste in mouth.
Menses irregular, profuse, dark. Felt tired and weak. Addicted to eating cloves. In hot weather, sweats
profusely and easily about head and chest, staining yellow. Very susceptible to cold. Cough provoked by op-
pression of breathing and talking.
Formerly had catarrh, followed by rightsided deafness. She had typhoid fever two years before and during the
fever was allowed unlimited quantities of ice. Preceding the fever she had a post auricular eczema suppressed
by salves, now is anemic and bloated. Urine contained epithelium, excess of chlorides, calcium oxalate and a
trace of albumen (due probably to the clove habit).
Glon. helped the case, but for a time only. Stront-n. was chosen because Stront. irritates the kidneys and Nit-
 ac. corresponds to the vasomotor disturbance besides having cravings for odd things.
Stront-n. 6x was given and in a few days the headache vanished. At the end of a month the post-auricular
eruption had reappeared. Five months later there had been no return of headache or palpebral edema, the
craving for cloves had gone, the patient had taken on good flesh and color. The eruption had not all gone.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Strophanthus Hispidus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stroph. Strophanthus hispidus. Kombe seed. Strophanthus gratus. Inee. Onaye. Onage. Poison
of Pahonias. N. O. Apocynaceae. Tincture of the seeds.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Alcoholism. Anasarca. Anemia. Arteriosclerosis. Colitis. Cough. Cystitis. Diplopia. Dropsy,
cardiac. Edema. Exophthalmia goiter. Faintness. Heart, disorders. Hemoptysis. Hives. Levitation. Nausea,
obesity. Pneumonia. Urticaria.
HOMEOPATHIC - Strophantus is an ornamental, evergreen and a climbing shrub, native of tropical Africa and
Asia. The mother tincture comes from the seeds of the plant. It is used as an arrow-poison by natives of Africa.
Among the alkaloids is strophanthin.
Stroph. occasions no gastric distress, diuretic. It has no cumulative action, safe for corpulent, aged persons
with rigid arteries, as it does not affect the vaso-motors. Restores tone to a weak tissue, especially of the
heart muscle and valves.
Stroph. increases the contractile power of all striped muscles, especially the heart, increasing the systole and
diminishing the rapidity. Acts on the heart increasing the systole and diminishes the rapidity. Tones the
heart and run off dropsical effusions.
Especially useful in failing compensation dependent upon fatty heart. After the long use of stimulants.
Arteriosclerosis, rigid arteries of aged. Precordial anxiety. Retrosternal pain. Functional disturbances of heart
from alcohol, tobacco, tea.
In small doses for weak heart, that feels enlarged. In mitral regurgitation, where edema and dropsy have
supervened (Dig.). Severe prostration from hemorrhage after operations and acute diseases.
Anemia with palpitations and loss of breath. Faintness. Pneumonia. Rapid alternations of symptoms with slow
pulse. Undulating sensation in whole body. Throbbings. Stitching pains. Twitchings of the muscles.
Obesity. Increased secretions. Nausea with special disgust for alcohol. Alcoholism, with drop doses of Stroph-
h. tincture. Hives. Exophthalmia goiter.
MIND - Worse from strong emotions. Irritable. Anxiety and fear. Fear of ordeals. Feels lifted up during sleep.
Precociously talkative children.
Abdomen - Abdomen distended, painful, especially in the umbilical and inguinal regions. Rumbling and
pinching at navel. Shooting pains in right hypochondrium. Stitches in region of sigmoid flexure.
Acute entero-colitis. Colic.
Back - Joint and muscular pains in the limbs, back and lumbar region with stiffness, muscular weakness,
coldness at the limbs.
Causations - Alcohol, tea, tobacco.
Chest - Pressive pain in middle of right third rib on anterior half, worse by pressure. Thoracic pain on left side.
Constrictive, cramping pain behind the sternum, crushed, gnawing, needle-like sensation.
Eyes - Pupils quivering, dilating and contracting alternately. Eyes brilliant. Glimmering in vision. Impaired sight
of left eye with nausea and faintness. Double vision.
Face - Flushed, red spots. Lips scarlet.
Female - Uterine hemorrhage. Uterus heavily congested.
Food - Craving for alcohol, tea, coffee, stimulants. Nausea with special disgust for alcohol. Loss of appetite.
Loathing of food, followed by choking and vomiting after eating.
Head - Temporal pains with double vision, impaired sight, brilliant eyes, flushed face. Violent, pulsating
headache, aggravated by movement.
Heart - Weak heart with aching or anguish. Heart’s action weak, rapid, irregular, due to muscular debility and
insufficiency. Cardiac pain and dyspnea. Chronic, nervous palpitations and arrest of breathing. Violent
palpitations, worse by emotion and exercise. Sense of lively action. Mitral regurgitation. Stitches and twitches
at apex beat. Pulse, rapid, alternating with slow, weak, small irregular.
Kidneys - Kidneys become hyperemic. Cystitis. Urinary tract infections. No urine passed for hours. Frequent
urination. Urine increased secretion or scanty albuminous. Urine strong, odor is fruity or like horse urine, pale.
Limbs - Swollen, dropsical. Anasarca. Swelling of legs. Itching and stitching in both feet. Dorsum of foot painful
and tense. Muscular and joint pains with stiffness and coldness of the limbs. The pains are aggravated by
 movement. Heaviness and
pain in forearms and the fingers.
Liver - Pressure in liver region.
Lungs - Edema of lungs. Bronchial and cardiac asthma. Breathing deep, difficult, thirsty for air, feeling of
dryness in the mucus membranes, aggravated by movement. Cough worse by lying down. Expectoration of
bright red blood.
Modalities - Better from rest, lying down. Worse from exertion, exercise, standing. Worse tobacco, tea,
alcohol. Worse from emotions.
Mouth - Dryness of tongue and fauces.
Rectum - Stool with burning and tenesmus in anus. Diarrhea with burning and tenesmus in anus. Frequent
diarrhea with violent colic but good appetite. Infectious or toxic diarrhea.
Skin - Hives, chronic, receding. Urticaria, especially more chronic forms.
Stomach - Bulky feeling in the stomach. Twitching in stomach. Burning in esophagus and stomach with loss
of appetite and extreme gastric distress. Cramping, acrid stomachache with belching and nausea. Eructation
and hiccough. Nausea with special disgust for alcohol.
Temperature - Coldness of limbs. Temperature raised, skin dry. Profuse sweat.
Throat - Seems dry, constricted. Burning in throat and esophagus to stomach, compelling empty swallowing.
Vertigo - Vertigo with swimming vision. Senile vertigo. Undulations in head.
COMMENTS-The homeopathic proving was conducted by Templeton on five provers, using 2x, 3x, 6c, 12c,
30c and by O’ Hanlon on twelve provers, using 6c, 12c and 30c.
Piedvache proved the tincture, but only with reference to the pulse. Gise vius proved Stroph-h. tincture,
beginning with 5 drops increasing to 80 drops during the five days of his proving. Matthes proved Stroph-h.
tincture in 10 drops doses.
Some well-marked symptoms were produced on two chemists from preparing the tincture. Other effects
curative and pathogenetic have been observed on patients taking the drug. Stroph-h. disorders the digestion,
causes burning in the esophagus and stomach, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
A. P. Skworzow gave an infusion of Stroph. to an alcoholic, 63, for weak heart and intermittent pulse, 7 drop
doses three times a day. The first dose caused nausea and a repugnance to alcohol which proved to be
permanent. The man entirely discontinued the habit.
On this hint, Stroph. was given to two other alcoholics with the same result of abolishing the taste for alcohol.
It caused nausea and profuse sweating and the sudden withdrawal of alcohol was not attended with delirium.
A case of Clarke’s illustrates the gastric and cardiac action of the remedy. W. G., 16, a delicate-looking boy,
was admitted to a hospital. He had rheumatic pains for three months and an attack of rheumatic fever two
years previously. He had been laid up a month before admission and a week before was taken with cough,
shivering and occasional vomiting.
When admitted, he had a frequent, short, dry cough, worse lying down, had to be propped up in bed, had
edema of feet, especially left. Tongue white, unable to retain any food for three days, no pain after food, but
much flatulence, belchings giving much relief.
Heart greatly dilated, pulsation diffused, double mitral bruit. Dullness at bases of both lungs, moist rales,
halfway up right lung. Expectoration of bright blood for seven days.
Stroph. tincture, one drop every four hours, was given. Improvement in all the symptoms was immediate,
sickness, cough, hemoptysis and dropsy all disappeared and the heart sounds had cleared up to a large extent
when the boy went home, less than three weeks after admission.
Hamer mentioned that Stroph. cured “functional disturbance of the heart from alcohol tobacco and tea.” This
agrees with the relation of Stroph. to alcoholism and symptoms of indigestion.
A writer gave his experience with Stroph. : a woman had constant outbursts of urticarial rash dating from
exposure to an offensive effluvium from a dead whale cast on the sands. The attacks would recur after drinking
a glass of table beer. Stroph-h. cured.
Any accompanying cardiac weakness would be an additional indication. The same writer considered Stroph.
of great service in the anemia of young girls when palpitation and breathlessness are marked features.
An accidental proving on a girl of five was made through the mother giving twenty drops of the tincture by
mistake. Some half an hour later her face was flushed, lips scarlet, eyes brilliant, temperature raised, skin dry,
tongue normal. Pupils quivering, dilating and contracting every few seconds. Pulse 140, arteries distended.
Heart sounds vigorous, slight regurgitant mitral murmur. Intellect clear, precociously loquacious during the five
hours the poisonous symptoms lasted. An ipecac emetic was administered. No urine passed for ten hours
after the dose.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Heart dropsy, Apoc. (2) Heart, Dig. is cumulative, Stroph-h. is not. (3) Crat.,
 Phase., Cact. (4) Anemia, Fenr. (5) Alcoholism, Chin., Nux-v., Aven., Querc. (6) Kali-c. - heart weakness,
fatigue, chill, acute stinging pains, aggravated by the cold and at 2 a.m. (7) Aeon. - Sharp intolerable pains,
much more agitated with fear of death. (8) Lach. - worse left-side, aggravated on waking, hyperesthesia of the
skin, tendency to hemorrhage. (9) Sarcol-ac.- Pains and muscular weakness, extreme asthenia, aggravated
by the slightest movement. (10) movement, feeling of fullness in the epigastrium, constipation. Compatible:
Ferr. in anemia.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Strychnia Phosphoricum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stry-p. Strychnia phosphoricum. Strychnine phosphate. Alkaloid obtained from several species
of Strychnos. Solution. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Atelectasis. Heart, disorders. Headache. Paralysis. Pulse, irregular. Spinal cord, disorders.
Tachycardia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Stry-p. is useful in chorea, hysteria, acute asthenia after acute fevers. Hands and axilla
covered with clammy perspiration. Cold and clammy feet. Better rest and in open air, worse from motion.
Acts through the cerebro-spinal system upon muscles, causing twitching, stiffness, weakness and loss of
power. Anemia of spinal cord, paralysis, burning, aching and weakness of spine, pain extends to front of chest,
tenderness on pressure in mid-dorsal region.
Atelectasis and break in the compensation of a hypertrophied heart, the beginning of fatty degeneration of the
heart muscle. Tachycardia. Irregular pulse. Rapid and weak pulse.
MIND - Affects upon the mind, producing lack of control, uncontrollable desire to laugh and disinclination to
use the brain.
COMMENTS - A woman to whom Clarke gave Stry-p. 3x in five-drop doses twenty minutes before meals, felt
at once constriction of the throat and after each meal violent headache in forehead over the eyes. The choking
sensations were a constant feature in provings and poisonings.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Royal.

of Strychnos. Solution. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Atelectasis. Heart, disorders. Headache. Paralysis. Pulse, irregular. Spinal cord, disorders.
Tachycardia.
HOMEOPATHIC - Stry-p. is useful in chorea, hysteria, acute asthenia after acute fevers. Hands and axilla

name: Strychninum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - stry. Strychninum. Strychnine. Alkaloid obtained from several species of Nux vomica,
Loganiaceae. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Aorta, pain. Aphonia. Asthma. Athetosis. Bedwetting. Bladder, paralysis, pains.
Breasts, pains. Coughs. Cramps. Diaphragm, spasms. Emphysema. Exophthalmos. Eye, disorders.
Headaches. Hemiplegia. Influenza. Joints, stiffness. Laryngeal, crises. Locomotor, ataxia. Malar, bones, pains.
Neurasthenia. Night-blindness. Paraplegia. Proctalgia. Rheumatism. Scrotum, abscess. Spinal irritation.
Tetanus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Liquor Strychnie is responsible for many of the poisonings, the powdered crystals, either
pure or mixed in pills or rat-poison, for others. Strychnia itself
is very sparingly soluble in cold water (1 in 5760). A homeopathic proving of Stry. was made by Henry Robinson
on two provers, a man and a woman.
The man took 900 drops in twenty-three days, the woman 445 drops in fifty-three days. These have furnished
the most distinctive symptoms. Extreme nervous excitability. Visions of an ugly face. Fits of laughing with light.
Idiotic-like chuckle. Confusion of ideas, stupor and weariness were some of the mental symptoms. Swimming
sensation in the head and giddiness involuntary.
Stimulates the motor centers and the reflex action of the spinal cord. Stimulates the central nervous system,
mental activities, special senses rendered more acute. All reflexes are made more active.
Spasmodic rigidity. Spasms of muscles, cramps from an undue reflex excitability of the cord, spasms of the
bladder, etc. Stiffness in muscles and face and neck. Athetosis. Tetanus with violent jerking, twitching and
trembling.
Tetanic convulsions with opisthotonos. The muscles relax between paroxysms, worse slightest touch, sound,
odor. Influences more directly the spinal cord and is less appropriate in visceral derangements than Nux-v.
Explosive nervousness. The pains and sensations come suddenly and return at intervals. Darting, pinching
lancinating, fulgurating, electric pains. Spine is cold. Gushing sweat from head and chest.
Drowsiness, with headache. Frontal headaches, momentary dartings like electric shocks. Respiration
increased. Inability to take deep breath, fixation of chest walls. Sudden palpitations.
The direct “tonic” action of Stry. was shown in one of Robinson’s provers, who had “unusually good appetite,
 she enjoys her food amazingly.”
Stry. is an antidote to chloral, used in asphyxia from gas and chloroform and early stages of opium poisoning.
Abdomen - Sharp pain in abdominal muscles, griping pain in bowels.
Back - Rigidity of cervical muscles. Sharp pain in nape and down spine. Back stiff, violent jerks in spinal
column. Icy sensation down spine.
Ears - Hearing very acute, burning, itching and roaring in ears.
Eyes - Hot, painful, protruding, staring. Pupils dilated. Spasmodic contraction of ocular muscles, twitching and
trembling of lids. Sparks before eyes.
Face - Pale, anxious, livid. Jaws stiffened, lower jaw spasmodically closed.
Female - Desire for sex increased (Plat.). Any touch on body excites a voluptuous sensation.
Head - Over irritability. Restless. Full and bursting headache with heat in eyes. Vertigo with roaring in ears.
Jerking of head forwards. Scalp sore. Itching of scalp and nape.
Limbs - Cramp-like pains. Rheumatism with stiff joints. Limbs stiff. Violent jerking, twitching and
trembling. Tetanic convulsions and opisthotonos, spasms provoked by slightest touch and attempt to move.
Shocks in the muscles.
Lungs - Spasm of muscles about larynx. Sharp, contractive pains in muscles of chest. Excessive dyspnea.
Persistent cough, recurring after influenza.
Modalities - Better from lying on back. Worse morning, after meals. Worse touch, noise, motion, exertion,
walking.
Rectum - Very obstinate constipation. Feces discharged involuntarily during spasms.
Sensations - Feeling as if head and face were enlarged, after affects of debauches (Nux-v.). As if an iron cap
were on head. Paralyzed feeling in left half of head and face. Scalp sore, as if hair had been pulled. As if
nerves suddenly pulled out of teeth. As of a lump in throat. As if water dripped off right elbow, at intervals and
off right shoulder. As if chopped in half at waist, at night.
Skin - Itching of whole body, especially nose. Icy sensation down the spine.
Stomach - Constant retching. Violent vomiting. Nausea of pregnancy.
Temperature - Cold chills down spine. Perspiration in a stream down head and chest. Lower limbs cold.
Throat - Dry, contracted, feeling of a lump. Swallowing impossible. Burning along and spasms of esophagus.
Violent itching in roof of mouth.
COMMENTS - Innumerable poisonings with strychnine are on record, the symptoms being convulsions of a
tetanic nature, in the fatal cases ending in asphyxia. The spasms are intermittent and the least touch or
movement is sufficient to induce an attack. Lying on the back is the only tolerable position.
“Lying on her back, body rigid, jaws set, arms and hands flexed, the thumbs nearly touching across the chest
and the whole muscular system convulsed with shortjerky spasms. Which would continue for about a minute
and then remit, the muscles remaining contracted and as hard as wood during the intervals between the
paroxysms.”
The convulsions generally take the form of opisthotonos, cries, terror, hippocratic countenance and frothing at
the mouth are common occurrences.
Meyhoffer experimented with Stry. on himself and two other persons, one of whom was a woman of lymphatic
temperament.
“It always brought on electric shocks, occurring whenever the prover was touched or whenever any one lightly
shook the bed on which he or she was lying. This happened to all, only the woman (lymphatic and feeble)
needed a stronger dose.” Any touch on any part of the body caused a voluptuous sensation.
Gamper of St. Petersburg experimented with Stry-n. on healthy young hospital assistants and found that it
increased the amount of gastric juice secreted, the general acidity and the quantity of free acid in the secretion.
It hastened the absorption from the stomach and strengthened mechanical movements. The effects continued
some time after the administration was stopped.
Marked action on the rectum and genitourinary organs (Ign. and Nux-v.). The male prover had his left testicle
and cord swollen and an abscess of the scrotum developed and discharged.
“Gurgling noise in rectum with electric darts” is a symptom of one prover. Many pains center about the lips and
eyes. Pains and chills occur in the occiput and nape and run down whole length of spine. Stiffness is a leading
note of Stry. and Cooper gave “rheumatism with stiff joints” as an indication.
Itching of the whole body and “violent itching in roof of mouth.” Jerkings, twitch- ings and shocks in all parts.
Increased activity of the spinal senses. Dread of touch, shrinks from drafts.
Clarke found Cooper’s suggestion that many cases of persistent cough recurring after influenza are met by
Stry. to be correct. The influenza cough has in it a strong spasmodic and asthmatic element, whether dry or
not, and this seems to give one point of correspondence.
 C. W. Lawson related the case of a medical man who took continuously for two years, Stry. hydrochlor., 5 to
10 minims, thrice daily with a little sal volatile. He was at first benefited, but afterwards experienced a desire
to take deep insoirations. “He felt that to do so would overcome the inhibitory power over the lung, probably
the action of the diaphragm.”
One morning after a dose of Stry., he was taking such an inspiration and from that moment experienced the
sensations complained of an inability to take a deep breath. Fixation of chest walls compelled him to stoop,
weakness on exertion, great confusion of thought and memory, occasional clay-colored feces, usually greater
in amount than ordinary.
After six months, the apex beat descended to the 6th interspace and headache and drowsiness became
marked. He traveled for six months without benefit. All attempts to act on the heart with drugs increased the
headache. Lawson then found the heart dilated, wide sub-costal angle, chest emphysematous, moving en
mass.
After a full year of treatment with Hyos. tincture at bedtime, which proved strikingly beneficial, drowsiness
ceased entirely and improvement in all other respects followed.
Hale mentioned the following uses of Stry. and its salts as observed by him and others. Stry. 6c. in the tetanic
spasms of cerebrospinal meningitis. Amaurosis from atony of retina. Diplopia and night-blindness. Stry-s., and
in one case when all other Stry. preparations had failed, Stry-val. cured facial neuralgia and neuralgic
headache.
Spasms of esophagus in an hysterical woman. Stry-val. 2x. cured brain exhaustion of women in whom high
nervous weakness exists. Stry. 12c or 30c for chorea, when the convulsions do not cease during sleep.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Eucal. - neutralizes ill effects of strychnine. (2) Cic., Arn. (tetanus). (3) Stry. ars.
- Paresis in the aged, relaxed musculature. Prostration. Psoriasis, chronic diarrhea with paralytic symptoms.
Compensatory hypertrophy of heart with beginning fatty degeneration. Stry-ar. - Marked dyspnea when lying
down, edema of lower limbs, urine scanty, high specific gravity, heavily loaded with glucose. Diabetes, use the
6x trituration. (4) Stry-f-c. - chlorotic and paralytic conditions, dyspepsia with vomiting of ingesta, 2x and 3x
trituration. (5) Stry-n. - 2x and3x. Saidtoremovecravingforalcohol. Use for two weeks. (6) Stry-s. - Gastric atony.
(7) Stry-val. - exhaustion of brain-power, women of high nervous weakness, 2x trituration.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Strychnos Gaultheriana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - strych-g. Strychnos gaultheri- ana. Hoang nan. Tropical Bind-weed. N. O. Loganiacee. Tincture
of dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Boils. Cancer. Carbuncles. Colic. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Eczema. Fatigue.
Hydrophobia. Leprosy. Paralysis. Prurigo. Pustules. Rabies. Snakebites. Syphilis. Ulcers. Vertigo.
HERBAL - The Strych-g. plant is indigenous to Tonquin, where it has a great reputation as aremedy for leprosy,
hydrophobia, snakebites and diseases of the skin. The red dust of the bark contains the most active properties.
HOMEOPATHIC - The native method of
Strychnos gaultheriana preparing the medicine is by moistening the mixture of the three powders with a little
vinegar and forming the paste into pills of about a centimeter in diameter.
When taken by a healthy person these pills cause fatigue, general indisposition, vertigo, tingling of the hands
and feet involuntary movements of jaw. When a person is bitten by a poisonous animal, a dose of three or four
grams is administered in vinegar.
If none of these symptoms appear it is understood that the medicine is antagonized and the dose is increased
until some of the symptoms manifest themselves, when the poison is considered to be destroyed. The use of
alcohol is forbidden while a patient is taking this medicine. Vinegar appears to modify its virulence.
In animals poisoned with it, tetanic convulsions always begin in the hind legs and spread all over the body.
Brain, liver, kidneys and lungs were found congested post mortem.
Generally improves nutrition, especially in constitutional syphilis. Exhaustion with vertigo, numbness and
tingling in hands and feet involuntary action of lower jaw. Tetanic convulsions beginning in legs and spreading
over body.
Eczema, prurigo. Pustules and boils. Old ulcers. Leprosy. Snakebites. Tertiary syphilis and paralysis.
Glandular disorders. Cancer of glandular structures. Removes fetor and hemorrhage in cancer, revives the
healing process.
MIND - Apathy. Lassitude, indisposition to make mental effort.
Abdomen - Colic and diarrhea.
Head - Vertigo, headache.
 Kidneys - Albuminuria. Mucus casts.
Skin - Malignant ulcers, pustular eczema, boils, carbuncles, leprosy.
COMMENTS - In 1883 a proving of Strych-g. was made by seven people, producing a few symptoms.
According to Hansen, there is prurigo, pustular eczemain parts well supplied with sebaceous glands (face,
neck, genitals).
General malnutrition. Glandular cancer. Boils, carbuncles, constitutional syphilis. The dose of which is 5 to 30
drops of the tincture three times a day.
RELATIONS - Compare: Nux-v„ Cur., Ang., Bruc., Hydre. Follows well after Ars.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Succinum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - succ-ac.Succinum acidum. Succinic acid. Amber oil. A mineralized fossil resin not to be
confounded with Ambergris, Ambra. Trituration. Solution of the non-recti- fied oil prepared by dry distillation of
Amber. Solution of Succinic acid. Historical dose: All potencies. Drop doses of the oil.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Fears. Globus. Hay fever. Hiccough. Hysteria. Leucocythemia splenica. Spleen
disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Morris Weiner tested Succ-ac„ which he prepared himself from amber by dry distillation.
The fumes of the crude acid, he said, are inflammable and produce asthma, cough, sneezing, weeping,
dropping of watery mucus from nostrils, pain in chest and headache.
On this indication, he treated thirty people suffering from hay fever and cured them all, saving them the
necessity of making an annual exodus. He gave one or two grains of the 3x trituration of Succ. diluted in twelve
teaspoonfuls of water, a teaspoonful every two hours.
Burnett wrote in Diseases of Spleen, that the non-rectified oil is used as an organ remedy in spleen affections,
especially when accompanied by nervous and hysterical phenomena. The crude oil is a thick brown liquid
having a strong empyreumatic odor. It is a powerful local irritant and has been used with success as such in
lumbago, rheumatism and sciatica.
Succ-ac. enters into the composition of “Roche’s Embrocation,” and “Haarlem Oil,” and has a popular
reputation as a remedy for whooping cough, the directions being for it to be rubbed into the spine night and
morning.
Succ-ac. produces many nervous and hysterical symptoms. Asthma. Fear of trains and closed places.
Affections of spleen.
Burnett noted it for hysterical convulsions in women.
MIND - Fear of trains and closed places.
Eyes - Lachrymation.
Head - Headaches.
Lungs - Pains in chest. Asthma. Incipient tuberculosis. Chronic bronchitis. Whooping cough.
Nose - Sneezing, dropping of watery mucus from nostrils.
Stomach - Persistent hiccough. Violent vomiting.
Throat - Globus.
COMMENTS - A tablespoonful dose, said Murrell, has caused persistent vomiting, diarrhea and symptoms of
collapse and the patient aborted. He gave the oil, six ounces of acorn-water added half a scruple of the oil.
They do not mix chemically, but by shaking each time a dose is taken the required division and potency is
attained.
Burnett’s keynote was “Painful spleen disorders where there are convulsive attacks such as the hysterical and
hypochondriacal often have.”
Burnett related in his book a most remarkable case of “chronic enlargement of the spleen with hyperesthesia,
head pain, Dyspnea orthopnea, convulsions” in a young woman “towards the end of her teens.”
After years of treatment, Burnett concluded from Rademacher’s account of Succ-ac. that it might provide the
remedy. It was given in five-drop doses three times a day. In forty-eight hours the convulsive attacks ceased
and all the phenomena slowly disappeared.
A keynote of Burnett’s is “Fear of trains and close places.” His dose is five drops of the oil three times a day.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Amber gemstone. Succinum purum. (2) Ars-i. - Hay fever. Paroxysmal sneezing,
dropping of watery mucus from nostrils, asthma. Inflammation throughrespiratory tract, causing asthma, chest
pains, etc., itching of eyelids and canthi and nose worse drafts. (3) Arund., Wye., Sabad, Sinapis nigra.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
 ***SULFANILAMIDE
PHARMACY - sulfa. Sulfanilamide. Para- amino-phenylsulfamide. Allopathie drug. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. Anemia. Audio-visual, disorders. Boils. Cataract. Coma. Cyanosis. Delirium.
Dermatitis. Goiter. Hypoglycemia. Jaundice. Ménière’ sdisease. Muscular, atrophy. Myxedema. Nephritis.
Schizophrenia. Thyroid, deficiency.
HOMEOPATHIC - In medicine, Sulfanilamide is known in one form as Exoseptoplix. It was the active part in
the decomposition ofprontosil which was used in experiments by Domagk in 1935. The homeopathic proving
of sulfanilamide was conducted by Sutherland, who used the 3x. 6x and the 200th potency.
Sulfa, has a slowing down of all physical and mental functions. Halt in development and puberty comes late in
the child. Myxedema. Fatigue, general weariness. Indefinable discomfort with giddiness or vertigo, with apathy.
Febrile condition with rash, aching, conjunctivitis, which may be accompanied by fever with shivering, pain in
the joints increase in leucocytes with granulocytosis. Paresis and muscular atrophy of the feet and hands.
Cramping pains in the hypogastric region. Oliguria and kidney colic. Hypoglycemic conditions.
Heart rhythmic anomaly, cyanosis and comatose condition. Cyanosis with violet or livid coloring of the lips,
nose, ears, fingertips. Vesicular eruptions. Goiter. Thyroid deficiency and congestion of the thyroid gland.
MIND - Mental backwardness. Clouded mental state. Idea association complaints. Concentration complaints.
Difficulty in determining contrasts and shapes. Loss of memory for graphic movements and for sounds and
words. Loss of memory with diminution in auditory acuity. Physical and mental apraxia.
Alternating psychological condition. Cyclical moods. At times happy, joyful, then sad and dejected. Indolence,
apathy, state of confusion. Attacks of delirium.
Schizophrenia.
Abdomen - Sensation of fullness. Pain in the hypogastric region. Cramping abdominal pains. Congestion of
the liver with alternate constipation and diarrhea. Gastric and duodenal ulcer. Jaundice.
Blood - Anemia. Aplastic anemia. Hemolytic anemia. Chronic leukemia. Thrombopenia. Acetone elimination
in the urine or excessive nitrogen in the blood. Agranulocytosis syndrome with fever, leucopenia, necrotic
angina and light hemorrhaging of the skin and mucus membranes.
Chest - Pain and heat in the chest.
Ears - Pustules and papules on the outer ear. Buzzing in the ears, as if produced by a bell. Bilateral diminution
in auditory acuity. Deafness through atrophy of the auditory nerve. Ménière’s disease. Boils in the auditory
canal.
Eyes - Chemosis of the left eye. Cloudiness of the crystalline lens or capsule. Cataract. Hemorrhaging of the
retina. Optic neuritis. Stye on the lower left eyelid. Eruption of yellow pustules on the edge of the eyelids.
Face - Acne of the chin.
Food - Hypoglycemic syndrome with condition of weakness, sweating, hunger pangs and tendency to faint
with or without convulsions. Loss of appetite.
Head - Frontal or occipital headache increasing towards evening.
Heart - Rhythmic anomaly, especially in elderly people.
Kidneys - Chronic interstitial nephritis. Kidney colic. Kidney stones. Paresis of the bladder with retention of
urine. Slow urination, urinary stream weak. Urine cloudy. Oliguria. Presence of porphyrin in the urine.
Hematuria. Uremia.
Limbs - Severe muscular pains. Acute rheumatism. Sciatica. Neuritic, especially sciatic pains. Progressive
symmetrical muscular atrophy, beginning in the hands. Paresis or paralysis of the feet with muscular atrophy
and absence of the Achilles' reflex. Acrocyanosis with formication and numbing of the limbs of the legs. Pain
in the right leg. Pain and weakness in the
small muscles of the feet and hands.
Lungs - Dyspnea, difficulty in breathing deeply. Bronchial asthma.
Male - Inhibition of the production of spermatozoa. Sterility.
Modalities - Better from hot compresses, discharges.
Nose - Pustules in the left nasal fold. Sneezing. Boils.
Rectum - Alternate constipation and diarrhea.
Skin - Burns. Acne of the chin. Burning papular and pustular eruptions. Dermatitis. Sycosis of the beard.
Chronic eczema. Pityriasis rubra. Erythema. Pigmentation disorders of the skin. Vesicular eruptions on
uncovered areas exposed to the sun. Dermatitis from photosensitization. Measles-type, urticarial eruptions.
Eruptions ameliorated by hot compresses and by discharges.
Stomach - Nausea, vomiting.
Temperature - Basal metabolism reduced.
 Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea, ameliorated in the open air and by leaning forwards.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars. - Anxiety and agitation, especially between 1 a.m. and 3 a.m. Burning pains.
Edema of the lower eyelids. Thirsty for small amounts of iced water. V omiting and diarrhea with severe
prostration. Oppression. Scaly, burning eruptions and itching, worse between 1 a.m. and 3 a.m. (2) Cresol. -
Asthenia with euphoria. Loquacious mood, talks non-stop. Paresis of the lower legs with ataxia. Hypertrophy
of the muscles in the hands. Hypertension and oliguria. Hardening of the cartilages. Thickening and hardening
of the skin. Itching, pigmented erythema of the skin. (3) Cic. - Convulsions, contraction of the muscles of the
entire body. Pupils dilated. Pustular eruptions with thick, yellow scabs.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Sulfonalum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sulfon. Sulfonalum. Sulfonal. Diethylsulphone dimethyl methane. Coal tar product. Trituration.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Chorea. Constipation. Cramps. Cyanosis. Diarrhea. Epilepsy. Headaches. Heart
failure. Hematoporphyri- nuria. Insomnia. Locomotor ataxia. Nausea. Paralysis, ascending. Ptosis. Reflexes,
abolished. Tinnitus. Twitching. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sulfonal was at first regarded as one of the safest of hypnotics, but many cases of poisoning
by medicinal doses have occurred and the schema is made up of reported effects produced on patients.
Sulfon. is a coal tar product which produces ataxic symptoms, staggering gait, anesthesia of legs with absence
of knee jerks. Chorea. Cerebellar disease. V ertigo of cerebral origin. The symptoms disappear slowly.
Reflexes abolished. Epilepsy, with overexcitability of the cortical substance. Twitching of muscles, especially
of face and flexors, worse by voluntary movement, but always present in sleep. Muscular incoordination.
Paralysis of body, better by cold water, and cold douches. Great prostration. Paralysis progressive sometimes
with hyperesthesia and abnormal sensation, affecting first legs, then arms.
Profound weakness, faint feeling and despondency. Fainted and vomited. Loss of control of sphincter. Livid,
especially the face. Cyanosis. Death by respiratory failure preceded by unconsciousness.
MIND - Mental confusion, incoherence, illusions, apathetic. Alternation of happy, hopeful states with
depression and weakness. Extreme irritability. Stupidity. Unconscious with dilated and fixed pupils, profuse
sweat.
Abdomen - Spleen enlarged, hyperemic. Back - Chronic leptomeningitis.
Ears - Tinnitus.
Eyes - Pupils dilated and fixed. Eyes bloodshot and restless. Ptosis, heavy look about eyes. Double vision.
Face - Livid.
Head - Headache and tinnitus aurium. Pain on attempting to raise head.
Heart - Heart failure and edema of lungs. Heart’s action feeble, occasionally intermittent.
Kidneys - Constant desire to urinate. Retention of urine, had to be drawn off, darkcolored. Urine very scanty,
albuminous, almost solid when cooled, with casts. Pink color. Urine cherry-color, later like dark port wine.
Hematoporphyrinuria, urine oscillated between deep claret and light claret color. Dark brown urine.
Limbs - Restlessness, muscular twitchings. Ataxic movements, staggering gait, cold, weak, trembling, legs
seem too heavy. Knee-jerks. Plantar reflex deficient. Cramps of legs and single muscles. Stiffness and
paralysis of both legs. Anesthesia of legs.
lutings - Congestion of lungs, stertorous breathing. Sighing dyspnea. Edema of lungs. Signs of
bronchopneumonia.
Male - Erythema on prepuce.
Mouth - Breath smells of onions. Tongue as if paralyzed.
Rectum - Diarrhea and vomiting. Great constipation.
Skin - Itching, bluish purpura. Discolored patches like purpura on skin. Erythematous measles-like eruption.
Sleep - Insomnia. Fidgety, wakeful, drowsy. Sleepiness and weariness with unsteady gait. Stupor. Heaviness
and drowsiness.
Stomach - Constant retching, vomiting and sorenessoverepigastrium. Vomiting, diarrhea and violent chills.
Great disturbance of digestion with scanty urine.
Temperature - Violent chills.
Throat - Aphasia, dysphagia, difficult speech.
Vertigo - Vertigo of cerebral origin, unable to rise from seat.
COMMENTS - Ataxic gait and diminished or abolished reflexes. Locomotor ataxia. Ascending paralysis.
Stupor. Headache with noises in ears. Rashes on the skin, purpura, erythematous, etc. Vomiting and diarrhea.
 Urine retained or secretion arrested, claretcolored, containing albumen, porphyrin. Weak
Sulfonalum heart, fainting occurs and death takes place by heart failure.
One man observed uniform skin effects every time he took Sulfon., more intense the larger the dose. This
occurred from 5 grains: patches of erythema appeared first on inner side of first phalanx of right little finger,
next over proximal ends of metacarpal bones of left thumb and index, on posterior surface of left forearm a
little below elbow, fourth on prepuce. The symptoms were better by cold douches.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Trion. - insomnia associated with physical excitement, vertigo, loss of
equilibrium, ataxia, nausea, vomiting. Diarrhea, stertorous breathing, cyanosis, tinnitus, hallucination.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.
