name: Sulphur
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sulph. Sulphur. Brimstone. Sulphur lotum. Sulphur sublimatum. Sul- phur(At. Wt. 31.98).
Trituration of Flowers of Sulphur. A saturated solution of Sulphur in absolute alcohol constitutes the tincture.
A trituration of amorphous Sulphur has also been used. Sulphur prepared by precipitation from a solution of
Calc-s. with hydrochloric acid, are included. Historical dose; All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Adenoids. Alcoholism. Allergies. Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Anus, prolapsed.
Asthma. Atelectasis. Backache. Bedsore. Belching. Biliousness. Boils. Brain, congestion. Bright's disease.
Bronchitis. Cataract. Catarrh. Chancre. Chest, pains. Chilblains. Chloasma. Colds. Constipation. Corns.
Cough. Crusta, serpiginosa. Dental fistula. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Eczema. Epilepsy. Eruptions. Esophagus,
constriction. Eyes, disorders. Faintness. Feet, burning. Fever. Freckles. Ganglion. Glands, disorders. Gleet.
Globus hystericus. Gonorrhea. Gout. Headache. Head, congestion. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Hydrocele.
Hydrocephalus. Hydrothorax. Hypochondriasis. Impotence. Influenza. Intermittents. Irritation. Itching.
Jaundice. Keloids. Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Lichen.
Liver, disorders. Lumbago. Lungs disorders. Mania. Masturbation. Measles. Memory, weak. Meningitis.
Menstruation, disorders. Miscarriage. Molluscum. Nettle rash. Neuralgia. Nipples, sore. Nosebleed.
Ophthalmia. Phimosis. Phlegmasia dolens. Peritonitis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Pregnancy, disorders.
Prostatorrhea. Psoriasis. Rectaidisorders. Rheumatic fever. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Scabies. Sciatica.
Senile, dementia. Skin, disorders. Sleep, disorders. Smell, illusions. Spinal curvature. Spleen, pain.
Stomatitis. Taste, illusions. Tenesmus. Tonsillitis. Toothache. Trachea. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Urticaria.
Uterus, prolapsed. Vaccination. Varicocele. Varicose veins. Vertigo. Warts. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sulphur is an elementary substance, occurring in nature as a brittle crystalline solid, burning
in the air with a blue flame, being oxidized to Sulphur dioxide (Sulphurous acid).
Sulphur is a product of volcanic eruptions, found free in nature and was used from ancient times to remove
skin disorders. The reputation of Sulphur as a remedy is perhaps as old as medicine. “As early as 2,000 years
ago,” said Hahnemann, “Sulph. had been used as the most powerful specific against the scabies.
“The itch with which the workers in wool are so much affected, causes an intolerably agreeable, tingling, itching,
gnawing as of vermin. Some designate it as an intolerably voluptuous titillating itching, ceasing as soon as the
parts are scratched and commencing to burn, which burning continues after the scratching.
“Sulph. frequently produces in healthy persons burning-itching pimples and vesicles resembling the itch
vesicles and especially itching in the joints and in the night.”
The domestic use of Sulph. as a “Spring medicine” is based on its anti-psoric properties. “It is one of the most
popular diaphoretics of the day,” said Milne, “few old women failing to use it when any eruption is supposed to
be struggling through the skin.”
The specific power of Sulph. to cure itch can be abused if applied externally as baths and ointments. Instead
of being cured, the skin affection can be repelled and a host of secondary disorders will appear in its place.
Sulph. is a major anti-psoric. A great reabsorbent and is frequently needed after acute illnesses which do not
entirely clear up. Complaints that relapse. When carefully selected remedies fail to act, especially in
acute diseases. It is often of great use in beginning the treatment of chronic diseases and in finishing acute
ones or when the reaction is deficient.
Irregular distribution of circulation, causing local burning, throbbing or congestion, flushes of heat, rush of
blood to head, chest, heart. Its action is centrifugal from within outward. Ascending effects.
Affinity for the skin, where it produces heat and burning with itching, made worse by heat of the bed. Dry,
unhealthy hair and skin. Very red lips and face, flushing easily. Redness of orifices or of single parts is
another prominent feature due to irregular circulation, lips, ears, nose, eyelids, anus, vulva.
Weak faint spells, frequently during the day after nursing or night watching with great sleepiness. Empty,
sinking feeling, in stomach. Sensation of fullness, roughness or numbness. Inertia and relaxation of fiber,
 characteristic feebleness of tone.
Chorea, chronic after suppressed eruptions. Epilepsy with a feeling that mouse is running up arms to back,
before the fit. Child jumps, starts and screams fearfully. As if swinging or standing on wavering ground.
Nutrition is affected on account of defective assimilation in spite of voracious appetite, the patient emaciates
(especially children). Thin and weak, even with good appetite. Hungry and always tired. Cat-nap sleep.
Glandular swelling indurated and suppurating. Mucus discharges and exhalations are acrid, blood streaked
offensive and cause itching. Serous effusions or deposits are absorbed slowly.
General offensive character of discharge and exhalations. Body offensive in spite of washing. Aversion
to being washed, always worse after the bath. Aversion to water.
Child looks dried, a little old man, big head, big belly with emaciated limbs. Dirty, filthy people, prone to skin
disorders. Patient is unable to walk erect, stoop shouldered, unwashed, tall and lean, untidy. Coal miner’s
disorders. Ragged philosopher.
MIND - Absent-minded. Dullness of mind. Brain fatigue. Difficult thinking. Very forgetful. Weak memory,
especially for names. Misplaces things, words, cannot find proper words when talking or writing. Scatter-
brained, burntout brains (Sil., Ph-ac., Med., Cann.). Repeats everything said to him on account of difficult
comprehension.
Awkwardness at his work. Aversion to do mental or physical work. Bored easily. Lazy, cannot arouse himself.
Lazy, hungry and always tired. Averse to business, or busy all the time. Workaholics, ambitious, aggressive
(Nux-v.).
Often irritable, depressed. Irritated greatly by least advice. Dislikes having anyone near him. Quarrelsome and
impatient nothing pleases. Impatience about trifles. Censorious, critical. Despises literary people and
education. Anger over his mistakes. Alcoholism.
Melancholy. Sadness from injuries of head. Sadness during labor. Tired of life. Strong impulsive tendency to
suicide by drowning or leaping from a window. Imagines giving wrong things to people, causing their death.
Worried by trifles. Anxiety about others, imagination leads them to worry. Anxiety from pressure on chest.
Anxiety about friends at home. Fear of failure, or poverty, of starving. Fear of ghosts at night, of robbers.
Childish peevishness in adults. Moaning and complaining day and night, with wringing of hands.
Anxiety with an overactive mind, preventing sleep. Restlessness at night. Persistent thoughts, expressions
and words heard recur to his mind. Absorbed in thoughts in evening. Obsessive, curious. Intellectuals.
Haughty. Egotistical and obstinate. Very selfish, no regard for others. Indifference to the welfare of others.
Megalomania. Delusions of grandeur. Foolish happiness and pride. Imagines himself a great person. Fear
of not being recognized. Insecurity, poor self-confidence. Indifference to personal appearance.
Monomania. Strong tendency to philosophical or religious reveries with fixed ideas. Makes many plans and
theories. Philosophical mania, wants to know who made this or that and how. Racks his brain about
metaphysical subtleties. Ragged philosophers. Religious melancholy. Religious aversion to opposite sex.
Indisposition to play in children. Religious affections in children.
Laughing over serious matters. Thinks himself in possession of beautiful things, everything looks pretty.
Senility. Senile dementia.
Abdomen - Sore, very sensitive to pressure, internal feeling of rawness and soreness. Abdomen heavy, as of
a lump. Movements as of something alive (Croc., Thuj.), as of the fist of a child. Stitches in region of spleen,
worse coughing or deep inspiration. Intestines feel as if strung in knots, worse bending forward. Bearing down
against rectum. Colic after eating or drinking, obliging one to bend double, worse sweet things. Colic after
drinking. Colicky babies. Big belly, emaciated limbs in children. Eczema about navel.
Baek - Curvature of spine. Drawing pain between shoulders. Neck stiff. Muscles of neck weak, child cannot
hold head. Boils on neck. Sensation as if the vertebrae glide over each other or crack on bending backwards.
Aching between scapulae. Lumbar pains to stomach, walks bent from pain in the back, can only straighten up
after moving. Supports weight on hands when sitting. Coccyx pains during stools. Aching in small of back,
worse when urinating.
Breasts - Sharp burning in breasts. Nipples, cracked, around the base, smart, burn, bleed after nursing, pain
extends to back. Cancer of breast or uterus. Breast and
uterus develops imperfectly.
Causations - Suppressions. Alcohol. Sun. Chills. Sprains, over-exertion, reaching high. Falls, blows.
Bedsores.
Chest - Burning sensation in chest. Oppression, as of a load on chest. Shooting pains in chest extending to
back worse coughing, lying on back and deep breathing. Pain backward from left nipple. As of a band or load
on chest. Red, brown spots all over chest. Heat, throughout chest. Sensation of burning or coldness in chest,
extending to face. Feeling of weakness in chest, while talking.
 Constitutions - Suited to lean, stoopshouldered persons, who walk and sit stooped, standing is the most
uncomfortable position. Persons of psoric temperament, nervous, quick-motioned, quick-tempered, plethoric,
skin excessively sensitive to atmospheric changes. Dirty, filthy people with greasy skin and long, straight,
matted hair, prone to skin disorders. Children who cannot bear to be washed or bathed, emaciated, big-bellied,
restless, hot, kick off clothes at night, have worms. Persons of scrofulous diathesis, subject to congestions,
especially of portal system. Lymphatic temperaments, nervous constitutions disposed to hemorrhoids with
constipation or morning diarrhea, diseases caused especially by suppressed eruptions. Emaciated children,
old-looking faces, big bellies, dry, flabby skin. Full-blooded persons with great irritability, restlessness and
hastiness. Old people. People with hot, sweaty hands. “Ragged philosophers,” dirty-looking persons who
are always speculating on religious or philosophical subjects.
Ears - Purulent, offensive otorrhea, catarrhal discharge even on the eighth day. Bad effects from the
suppression of an otorrhea. Very red ears in children. Sensation as if sounds do not come through the ear but
through forehead. Whizzing in ears. Swashing as of water. Deafness preceded by exceedingly sensitive
hearing, catarrhal deafness.
Eyes - Painful inflammation of eye from presence of foreign body. Cutting as from sand. Heat and burning in
eyes (Ars., Bell.). Bursting pain in eyeballs. Trembling of eyes, quivering of eyelids. Chronic ophthalmia with
much burning and itching. First stage of ulceration of cornea. Photophobia. Parenchymatous keratitis. Keratitis,
cornea like ground glass. Retinitis caused by overuse of eyes. Oily tears. Burning ulceration of margin of lids.
Agglutination of lids. Styes and tarsal tumors. Eczema of lids. Trachoma. Opacities of vitreous. Obscuration of
vision like black gauze or motes before eyes. Halo around lamplight. Objects seem more distant than they are.
Face - Pale, sickly and old looking. Circumscribed redness of cheeks. Lips, bright red, swollen (upper), dry,
rough, cracked, burning, twitching or trembling. Freckled, spotted. Acne. Mumps. Swollen veins on forehead.
Female - Amenorrhea. Suppression of men - ses from excitement. Menses preceded by headache. Menses
too late, short, scanty and difficult, thick, black, acrid, making parts sore. Leucorrhea of yellow mucous,
burning, excoriating. Weak feeling in genitals. Offensive genitals with offensive sweat on thighs. Pudenda
itches. Vagina and vulva burn, itch and sore, worse sitting is scarcely able to keep still. Sore feeling in vagina
during sex. Bearing down in pelvis towards genitals, worse standing. Puerperal sepsis with high fever, profuse
sweat of whole body, tenderness of abdomen and drowsiness. Prolapse of uterus from reaching high. Cancer
of uterus. Uterus develops imperfectly.
Food - Complete loss of appetite or ravenous appetite. Feels hungry, but when comes to the table, he loathes
the food, turns away from it. Eats anything and everything. Headache or feels tired if he does not eat often.
Food tastes too salty. Aversion to meat. Desire for sweets (Arg-n.), for raw food. Sweets, milk disagrees.
Water fills the patient up. Drinks much, eats little.
Head - Hot head with cold feet. Constant heat on top of head (Cupr., Graph.). Hot,
 throbbing, heavy, sore vertex. Heaviness and fullness, pressure in temples. As of a band about or pain deep
in brain. Beating headache, worse stooping and with vertigo. Sick headaches recurring periodically, on every
Sunday, preceded by photopsia. Head bent forward when walking. Fontanelles remain open too long.
Hydrocephalus with convulsions, red face and pupils dilated. Tinea capitis, dry form. Itching, scratching
causes burning. Scalp dry. Sweaty scalp. Hair, dry, cold, hard, falling off, worse washing.
Heart - Heart feels too large. Pericarditis with effusion. Sharp pains go through chest to between shoulders.
Palpitations, worse lying at night in bed, going up an ascent. Pulse more rapid in morning than in evening.
Kidneys - Painful, ineffectual efforts to urinate, retention. Itching, burning in urethra during urination, lasting
long after. Parts sore over which it passes. Thin stream, intermits. Great quantities of colorless urine,
greasy particles, mucus and pus in it. Sudden call to urinate, must hurry. Urination involuntary while passing
flatus or on coughing. Frequent urination, especially atnight. Bedwetting, especially in scrofulous, untidy
children. Every cold settles in the bladder.
Limbs - Heaviness, paretic feeling in limbs. Jerks one limb on dropping to sleep. Rheumatic gout with itching.
Swelling of the joints with hydro-arthrosis. Joints stiff, especially knees and ankles. Tense hamstring (left).
Cramp in calf (left). Soles, burn, wants them uncovered, at night, cold in bed, dry. Poplitiae tight on stooping.
Tuberculosis of the knee and hip joints. Unsteady gait. Ganglion. Cannot walk erect, stoop-shouldered.
Heavy shoulders. Rheumatic pain in left shoulder. Left arm numb, worse lying. Numb fingers. Tremulous
sensation in hands, when writing. Palms, dry, bum, crack, peel, eczema on, warts on. Ulcers around the nails.
Whitlow with rapid swelling of the finger, redness, stiffness and excessive burning stitching. Involuntary
contraction of hands as if about to grasp something.
Hot, sweaty hands. Sweat in armpits, smelling like garlic.
Liver - Pain and soreness of liver. Stitches in region of liver. Gallbladder colic and çhronic jaundice. Relapsing
jaundice.
 Lungs - Difficult respiration, wants windows open, nightly suffocative air hunger. Dyspnea in middle of
night, relieved by sitting up. Irregular breathing. Asthma preceded by colds. Loose cough, worse from talking,
morning, greenish, purulent, sweetish expectoration. Much rattling of mucus and heat in chest, worse 11
a.m. Pleuritic exudations. Cough, violent in two or three incomplete bouts, tickling as from down in larynx.
Greenish, sweetish and purulent expectoration. Violent cough with headache worse lying on back. As of rivet
through upper third of left lung. Neglected pneumonia.
Male - Hydrocele. Testes hang low. Induration of testes. Discharge of prostatic fluid after urination and stool.
Stitches in penis. Penis cold. Prepuce stiff, hard like leather with copious smegma, causes itches. Fetid sweat
on genitals. Itching of genitals when going to bed. Organs cold, relaxed and powerless. Involuntary elaissions.
Seminal emission on touching a woman. Seminal emission with burning in urethra. Semen, odorless, watery.
Sexual power weak, impotence. Exhaustion in the morning after seminal emission. Backache and weakness
of the limbs after sex, with sadness and irritability.
Modalities - Better dry, warm weather, dry heat. Better open air, motion. Better sweating, walking. Better
lying on right side, drawing up affected limbs. Standing is the most uncomfortable position. Worse at rest,
stooping, reaching high. Worse talking, looking down. Worse crossing . running water, washing, bathing.
Worse in morning, 11 a.m., at night. Worse full moon, atmospheric changes. Worse from alcoholic stimulants.
Worse periodically. Worse from suppressions, milk, sweets. Worse warmth, over-exertion in bed. Worse
woolens. Worse vaccinations. Worse suppressed hemorrhoids. Worse menopause.
Mouth - Bitter taste in morning. Sour, sweetish, foul taste. Food tastes like straw or too salty. Profuse saliva,
with nauseous taste. Nursing sore mouth. Aphthae, thrush. Tongue white with red tip and borders. Dry,
tremulous tongue. Sensitive, tender teeth. Jerking, shooting, throbbing pains in teeth. Grinding of the teeth.
Gums bleeding. Swelling of gums, throbbing pain. Lips dry, bright red, burning.
Nose-Pale, red and scabby. Fluent burning coryza, worse outdoors, stopped indoors. Frequent sneezing.
Obstructed on alternate sides. Chronic dry catarrh, dry scabs and readily bleeding. Nosebleeds, worse at
night, on lying on right side. Polyps and adenoids. Herpes across the nose. Freckles and black pores on nose.
Tip of nose or alae nasi red, swollen, worse cold. Sensitive to smell. Imaginary odors.
Rectum - Redness around the anus with itching. Pain, urging and burning in rectum. Involuntary stools on
sneezing or laughing with emission of flatus. Morning diarrhea, drives out of bed with prolapsed rectum.
Painless diarrhea, changing, mushy, foul, painless, watery, grayish, frothy worse milk. Stools flat and thin.
Diarrhea of infants with profuse sweating, drowsiness, suppression of urine and the child wakes up screaming.
Children afraid, hold stools back on account of pain. Diarrhea alternating with constipation. Habitual
constipation. Frequent, unsuccessful desire, hard, knotty, insufficient. Odor of stool follows him as if he had
soiled himself. Hemorrhoids, oozing and belching. External and internal hemorrhoids, great bunches that are
sore, tender, raw, burn, bleed and smart. Hemorrhoids during pregnancy.
Sensations - As if a band were tied tightly around forehead or cranium. Vertigo as if swinging. As if one stood
on wavering ground. As if hair on vertex stood on end. As if hernia would form. As if lungs came in contact
with back. Heart as if enlarged. Like a weight on shoulder. Asif something heavy hanging on upper arm. Arms
as if beaten. As of a mouse running up arms and back. Thigh as if broken. As if too
short in popliteal space. As if bed were not large enough to hold him.
Skin - Skin as if denuded and sore. Unhealthy skin, breaks out, dry, scaly. Skin festers and would not heal,
every little injury suppurates. Excoriation, especially in folds (Lyc.). Voluptuous, violent itching, worse at
night, heat of bed, scratching and washing. Burning when scratched, painfully sensitive to air, wind, washing.
Itching, especially from warmth in evening, often recurs in spring, in damp weather. Pimply eruption,
pustules, cracks, hangnails. Freckles. Crops of boils. Scabies. Cracks. Eczema. Ulcers. Creeping erysipelas.
Suppuration with air bubbles. Varicóse veins, ulcerate, rupture and bleed. Eruptions, can alternate with other
complaints, asthma etc. Skin disorders after local medication. Feeling of a band around bones.
Sleep - Drowsy, then migraine. Sleeps in catnaps, slightest noise awakens. Drowsy by day, wakeful at night.
Heavy, unrefreshing. Talks, jerks and twitches during sleep. Awakes with starts or screams. Sings during sleep
or wakes up singing. Vivid dreams, remain impressed on the memory. Wakes frequently and becomes wide
awake suddenly. Cannot sleep between 2 and 5 a.m.
Stomach - Burning, painful, weight-like pressure. Heaviness in stomach. Very weak and faint about 11 a.m.,
must have something to eat. Great acidity, sour eructation. Belchings on pressing on stomach. Putrid
belchings tasting like bad eggs, worse eating or at night. Milk causes sourtaste andsour belchings. Vpmitingof
undigested food or sour vomiting. Nausea during pregnancy.
Temperature - Dry skin and great thirst. Chill spreading up back. Flushes of heat. Feels too hot. Frequent
flashes of heat, violent ebullitions of heat throughout entire body. Heat with general throbbing, between
scapulae. Sweat on single parts in axilla, hands and feet. Profuse sweat at night with sulphur odor. Night
 sweat, on nape and occiput. Sweat without relief. Sweat may occur on one side of the body only or on neck
only. Remittent fever. Septic, puerperal fever.
Throat - Burning, redness and dryness. External redness. Sensation, as of a lump, hair or splinter or as of a
vapor rising in. Ball seems to rise and close the pharynx. As if swollen. Dry, exciting cough. Deep, hoarse
voice. Aphonia.
Vertigo - Vertigo in forehead, worse when crossing a river, stooping with headache.
COMMENTS - Sulph. is used in various countries for allaying pain in a variety of forms. A piece of stick Sulph.
carried in the pocket is commonly used in England to ward off rheumatism. Natives of South America apply
Sulph. in solid form to painful parts and allow it to act for an hour before result is effected. For lumbago and
chronic rheumatic pains a bag filled with Flowers of Sulphur, heated and applied to the part, immediately
relieves the pain.
An experienced sea captain testified to the extreme frequency of rheumatism among his sailors, but, he added,
when carrying cargoes of Sulph., he had never had a case of acute rheumatism on board.
Dr. Laugardiere of Toulouse, reported to the Academy of Medicine that he had discovered a cure for croup: a
tablespoonful of Flowers of Sulphur dissolved in a tumbler of water. After three days of this treatment his
patients were rescued from imminent death and fully recovered. Many practitioners spoke highly of a local
application of Sulph. to the fauces in the treatment of croup and diphtheria.
Nettle rash is often relieved by a little Flowers of Sulphur, water and Sulph. mixed with sea sand and rubbed
over itch vesicles destroys the acarus at once. In the early days of vaccination it was found that the action of
Sulph. was adverse to the receptivity of vaccine. According to Dr. Tierney, Dr. Jenner failed in vaccinating
thirty soldiers, all under treatment by Sulph.
Cooper noted that operatives in sulphur mines enjoy an immunity against ague when prevalent in surrounding
districts, and that, before going on hunting expeditions in malarious districts, men in Ethiopia sub-
Sulphur mit themselves to fumigations with Sulph. and find it an efficient prevention of ague. Cooper thought
there was a great probability of Sulph. having a power of destroying the organisms in the blood of ague
patients.
Hahnemann found in Sulph. the homeopathic counterpart of the peculiar constitutional weakness which tends
to manifest in itch-like eruptions and which he named Psora. Sulph. is the chief of the anti-psoric remedies. It
is this property of Sulph. to divert to the surface constitutional irritants which renders it the chief of
Hahnemann’s anti-psorics.
Sulph. has also an anti-psoric action independently of its power of “bringing out” rashes. The psoric poison
may be present and active in a case of disease and “apparently well-indicated remedies may fail to act” in
consequence.
In such cases, one or two doses of Sulph. will frequently antidote the psora and either clear up the case or
open the way for the action of other remedies. In such cases there will almost certainly be some Sulph.
indications present.
Sulph. is a potent antiseptic and is one of the most certain destroyers of scabies. The exact relation of acarus
itch to psora and other itching eruptions need not be considered, but as Sulph. has the power of repressing
constitutional eruptions when locally applied, as well as the power of destroying the acarus, it is best to use
other means (e.g., oil of lavender) for the latter purpose and give Sulph. or other indicated remedies internally.
The symptoms of latent psora are detailed in Hahnemann’s Chronic Diseases. They are. for the most part,
almost exact reproductions of the symptoms of Sulph. But while Sulph. is the chief of anti-psorics, it is only
one of many and Sulph. is in no way limited in its uses to cases of latent or declared psora.
When well-selected remedies fail to act or act too short a time because of the patient’s feeble reactive powers,
Sulph. will often build up the vital powers of the patient to effect the cure. It will clear the way by removing the
psoric miasm to permit other similar remedies on their indications to cure the patient.
Useful for complaints that are always relapsing (menses, leucorrhea, etc.), patient seems to get almost well
when the disease returns again and again.
Irregular distribution of the circulation, flushes of heat, rush of blood to the head, chest, and heart. Plethora
from suddenly suppressed eruptions, hemorrhoids, discharges. Heat and burning sensation of all parts or
coldness, and sweating of many parts.
Hot flushes during the day with weak, faint spells, passing off with a little moisture. Sensation of burning on
vertex, of vesicles in mouth, and dryness of throat. Smarting in eyes, cutting, stabbing pain in right eye.
Congestions to single parts, eye, nose, chest, abdomen, ovaries, arms, legs or any organ of the body, marking
the onset of tumors or malignant growths, at menopause.
First right, then left in stomach, in rectum, in anus and itching. Heat in chest rising to face and skin, with hot
flushes in spots below scapulae. Burning soles, must find a cool place for them at night. Hot head with cold
 feet. Lutze found that Sulph. 1,000c will make feet that have been cold for years comfortably warm.
Irregularities may go on to actual inflammation with effusions and to fever of intermittent or other types. Will
cause absorption of effusions from pleuritis, hydrocephalus or synovial.
Periodical headaches, headaches occurring every week, every month. Sick headaches. Headaches are
accompanied by red face and hot head, are better in warm room, at rest, worse in open air, worse from
stooping. Headache on coughing. Clarke cured a severe occipital headache worse on coughing with Sulph.
30c.
Stopped catarrh, nose obstructed indoors, better outdoors. Nasal catarrh where the nose is stopped indoors
and free out of doors. White, frothy expectoration. Asthma. Alternation between skin irritation and asthma.
Tuberculosis with marasmus, with hunger at 11 a.m., sore, red orifices, flushes of heat. Tuberculosis of the
lungs when the “body feels too hot.” Must have windows open.
Rheumatism and sciatica, better morning and worse at night in bed. Rheumatism, begins below and spreads
upwards.
Unhealthy skin, tendencies to eczema, psoriasis. Burning and heat. Voluptuous itching, worse scratching,
scratching causes burning, worse from heat of bed, soreness infolds. Red blotches. Sores that don’t heal well.
Boils, coming in crops in various parts or a single boil is succeeded by another as soon as the first is healed.
Offensive odor of body despite frequent washing. Aversion to bathing. Aggravated by water (Petrol.), with
itching and burning. Poor hygiene or poverty (Psor.). Unkempt appearance. Allergic to wool. Skin disorders
that have been treated by medicated soaps or creams, hemorrhoids that have been treated by ointments.
Redness of orifices and parts near orifices. Red ears, eyelids and borders around eyelids. Brilliant red lips,
bright red anus in children, red meatus of urethra, red vulva. Red nose, worse by cold, the colder the redder.
Orifices are red, congested, sore and hypersensitive. The passage of all discharges or excretions is painful.
Feeling of emptiness. “Faint, sinking, allgone sensation at 11 a.m.” Empty sensation in head, heart, stomach,
abdomen. “Must have something between breakfast and dinner-time.” Low blood sugar. Ravenous hunger.
Defective assimilation, hungry yet emaciated. Poor breakfast eaters.
Poor dietary habits. Toxicity. Ulcers and burning in the stomach. Dyspepsia from suppressed eruptions, from
farinaceous food. After eating, dyspeptic patients feel puffed up, heavy, sluggish, and low-spirited.
Cannot take milk, vomits it at once. Sour vomit with undigested food. Crave sweets, fats, spicy foods, wine,
beer and marijuana. Alcoholism (Nux-v.). They crave beer, and marijuana. Aversion to eggs.
Dyspepsia of alcoholics. Craving for alcohol. Chronic alcoholism, dropsy and other ailments in alcoholics, they
reform but are continually relapsing. Gallavardin cured many apparently hopeless alcoholics with Sulph.
1,000c.
Scalding urine like fire. Portal congestion. Constipation with ineffectual urging, constipation alternating with
diarrhea. Stools are hard, dry, knotty, as if burnt, large, painful.
Child is afraid to have stool on account of pain, or pain compels child to desist on first effort, alternating with
diarrhea. Diarrhea, after midnight, painless, driving out of bed early in morning, as if bowels were too weak to
contain their contents. Hemorrhoids with burning and itching.
Drowsy in afternoon, after sunset, wakeful the whole night. Chronic insomnia from an overactive mind. Nightly
suffocative attacks, wants doors and windows open. Becomes suddenly wide awake at night. Happy dreams,
wakes up singing. Cramp in calves and soles at night. Will stick their feet out from the covers to cool down the
body at night in bed.
“Worse by heat,” by warmth of the bed, humidity. Worse at night, 11 a.m. Aversion to being washed, always
worse after a bath. Not well since vaccinations, especially skin problems. Ailments from the abuse of metals.
Taken altogether there are more symptoms on the left side than the right. It acts strongly on the left side of the
chest. “Sharp stitching pains through left lung to back, worse lying on back, worse by least motion.”
The child looks dried up, a little old man, skin hanging in folds, yellowish, wrinkled, flabby. Head large in
proportion to body. Lymphatic glands enlarged.
Clarke frequently cured ganglion of the wrist with Sulph. given on general indications. Sulph. 30c rescued a
patient from a condition that seemed desperate in a case of left pleuro-pneumonia following a violent
hemoptysis.
Lippe cured a case of menorrhagia with “a single dose of Sulph. at new moon,” the patient had not been well
since her last miscarriage.
Skinner gave a single dose of Sulph. 100,000c with instructions to take it on a certain date (when the moon
was full) to a man who had paresis of the lower limbs.
The man recovered suddenly.
Cooper used it to keep his regiment of sepoys in India healthy when many others were in the hospital with
fever.
 One writer treated nine cases with the pilules and arrested the fever in twenty-four hours. One of the cases
was a particularly obstinate one and had been pronounced by the doctors to be complicated with liver affection.
Quinine had been tried before to Sulph. cured.
Cooper, in a case of “Charges fever” of West Indies, which had lasted three months, ordered a Sulphur bath
as well as the Sulph. pilules. That single bath seemed to alter the whole condition and the patient, an unhealthy,
anemic, bilious-looking man, rapidly became the picture of health.
RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Aeon., Camph., Cham., Chin., Merc., Puls., Rhus, Sep., Thuj. Antidote to: Aeon.,
Aloe., Chi., lod., Merc., Nit-ac., Olean., Rhus, Sep., Thu., ailments from abuse of metals generally. Compare:
(1) Aeon., Ars. - Sulph. often follows in acute diseases. (2) Merc, and Calc., Lyc., Sep., Sars., Puls. (3) Tann-
ac. - nasal hemorrhage, elongated uvula, gargle, constipation. (4) Pyrar. - a fish caught in the Amazon, clinically
used for various skin affections, leprosy, tuberculosis, syphilis, varicosities, etc. (5) Meningitis, Apis. (6) Early-
morning diarrhea, Bry. (as soon as he moves), Nat-s. (with much flatus), Podo, (stools changeable, go on all
day, though worse at noon, Sul. raw, sore anus), (7) Defective reaction, Psor., Op., Care. (8) Hot flashes at
menopause, Lach., Sul-ac., Amyl-n., Kali-bi. (9) Intermittent fever and neuralgia, Chin., Ars., Bapt. (10)
Ravenous hunger with heat at vertex, Calc., Phos. (11) Tuberculosis, Bac., Calc., Tub., Phos. (12) Itch, Merc.,
Sep., Caust. (13) Dyspepsia, Lyc., Nux-v., Sep. (14) Pneumonia, restoration imperfect, Sang.
Complementary: Aloe, Psor., Aeon., Ars. Nux-v., Lyc., Sars., Sep., Puls., Thuj. Follows well: Merc-s.
complements Rhus-t. in paralysis.

Trituration of Flowers of Sulphur. A saturated solution of Sulphur in absolute alcohol constitutes the tincture.
A trituration of amorphous Sulphur has also been used. Sulphur prepared by precipitation from a solution of
Calc-s. with hydrochloric acid, are included. Historical dose; All potencies.

name: Sulphur Hydrogenisatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sul-h. Sulphur hydrogenisatum. Sulfuretted hydrogen. Solution of the gas. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Asphyxia. Asthma. Blood, poisoning. Convulsions. Delirium. Fever. Headache. Mania.
Prostration. Tetanus. Typhoid fever.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sul-h. is a colorless inflammable gas, having a sweetish taste and an exceedingly fetid
smell resembling rotten eggs. It is extremely poisonous when inhaled. It is evolved when animal or vegetable
tissues containing sulphur decay. It also occurs in mineral springs, being liberated by the reduction of gypsum
or other sulphates through the action of a microbe.
Sulph-h. is one of the remedies which help “blood poisoning” especially when bad smells are encountered.
Asphyxia, tetanus, delirium, low continued fever have been observed as resulting from the gas.
COMMENTS - J. Wiglesworth recorded two cases of insanity, one certainly and both probably, due to inhaling
the gas. The first concerned R. H., 32, an engine man at chemical works, who had been kept at home with an
attack of bronchitis for ten days. A few days after his return to work he became “gassed” (i.e., accidentally
inhaled Sul-h.).
This caused headache, stupor, prostration, compelling him to stay at home for a few days, when he became
wildly delirious. He passed into a very excited state, shouting and gesticulating, said he was Jesus Christ.
He tried to bury his head in the floor and to raise his feet above his head. Three days later he was admitted to
Rainhill Asylum and there was still very violent and excited, gesticulating and talking incoherently, chiefly on
religious subjects. At the end of a month there was some improvement and he was discharged, he recovered
five months after admission.
In the other case, that of a laborer at chemical works, Wiglesworth is not quite certain that Sul-h. was the
poison inhaled. This patient was greatly excited, threw his arms about, shouted and laughed by turns,
was excited and talkative. He remained permanently insane.

name: Sulphur Iodatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sul-i. Sulphur iodatum. Sulphur iodide. Trituration. Historicaldose: All potencies, third
trituration.
CLINICAL - Acne. Allergies. Asthma. Barber’s itch. Coryza. Ears, noises. Eczema, weeping. Gonorrhea. Hay
fever. Influenza. Kidneys, pain. Lichen planus. Lips, eruption. Parotid glands, hypertrophy, prostate disorders.
Scalp, soreness. Spine, weakness. Stricture, urethral. Tongue, thickening. Tonsils, chronic hypertrophy.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sul-i. was proved by Kelsall on himself and some others. Hale used it in “obstinate skin
diseases, notably barber’s itch, for which it is almost a specific.” The provings indicate this in “pustular eruption
on upper lip” and “erythema on chin.”
 Hale also noted it for large and painful suppurating acne. Weeping eczema. He used the 3x trituration, internally
and applied a cerate of one or two grains of Sul-i. to an ounce of Cosmoline.
Useful for psoric, allergic constitutions. Obstinate skin affections. Suppuration. Acrid discharges. Painless
enlargement of glands and infiltration of tissues with thickening and induration after inflammation.
Weakness, as from the influenza. Prostration, sensitive to everything. Faint and sick. Raw burning heat
internally with external coldness. Single parts, fingers etc. turn white and insensible.
MIND - Doubtful. Dread of exertion. Incapacity for business. Feverish excitement. Hurried, impatient, sad.
Restlessness at night. Starting, frightened on waking.
Abdomen - Mesenteric disease.
Eyes - Zigzag before vision.
Face - Acne. Suppurating pimples. Parotid hypertrophy after mumps.
Female - Irregular menses. Copious thick, burning, leucorrhea worse before and after menses.
Food - Anorexia. Appetite increased in marasmus of children. Desire for acids.
Head - Headache better sundown. Hair seems erect.
Kidneys - Urine, scanty, purulent, with brown sand. Urine smells like raspberries. Stricture after gonorrhea,
painful urination, stream twisted. Burning at the end of penis, dull pain in prostate.
Limbs - Aching soreness below knees. Soles of feet ache, bum and sore, when standing.
Lungs - Chest constricted, dropsy of pleura and eruptions on chest. Breathing asthmatic, irregular, rattling and
suffocative. Cough worse a.m., spasmodic. Expectoration greenish, purulent, copious, viscid and yellow.
Male - Testes soft. Prepuce cracked. Hydrocele of small boys. Deficient erections.
Modalities - Better by expectoration. Better from cool air, winter. Better standing. Worse from exertion, even
slight. Worse lying on right side, leaning forward, stooping, ascending stairs, rising. Worse before storms.
Worse night, in morning.
Mouth - Raw, dry, wants to moisten it. Cold sores on lips. Tongue is glazed, thickened after inflammation.
Teeth feel soft. Parotid hypertrophied.
Rectum - Stubborn constipation. Bright yellow stools. Foul anal discharge.
Sensations - Hair feels as if erect. As if a band across forehead. As if heat in heart.
Skin - Moist eczema. Suppurating acne. Barber’s itch. Lichen planus. Papular eruption on face. Itching.
Ulcers. Itching on ears, nose and in urethra. Arms covered with itching rash. Boils on neck. Hair feels as if
erect.
Stomach - Tremors in epigastrium on exertion.
Throat - Raw, dry, painful in swallowing. Uvula and tonsils enlarged and red. Swollen.
Vertigo - Vertigo worse stooping, binding of the hair, fasting, before and during menses.
COMMENTS - Dr. Berlin treated with Sul-i. two cases of “weeping eczema” associated
with varicose veins of the leg and pronounced itching. Also a child with eczema of arms. The keynote was
“dark red, swollen and sweeping eczematous surface which itches terribly.” Sul-i. 3x trituration, was given.
Hansen mentioned, among the therapeutic uses of Sul-i., thickness of tongue remaining after glossitis.
Hypertrophy of parotids after parotiditis. Chronic hypertrophy of tonsils. Lichen planus, chronic and simple.
Bradford reported a case of burning at the end of penis, dull pain in prostatic region, weakness across kidneys.
Frequent desire to urinate with slight flow, eats very little, does not go out of doors is much discouraged about
himself. Sul-i. 3x cured.
Violent attack of pain in kidney region with shootings down ureters, pain and weakness about kidneys, constant
desire to urinate, urine thick and whitish with creamy sediment. Sul-i. 3x and 6x cured.
Stricture after gonorrhea, chordee, very painful urination, twisted stream. Yellow discharge. Sul-i. cured.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Band across forehead, Mane. (2) Difficult expectoration, Kali-bi. (3) Heat in heart,
Lachn., Rhod. (4) Sleepy by day, restless at night, Staph. (5) Acne, Bell-p., Kali-br.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

***SULPHUR TEREBINTHINATUM (Terebinthinated Sulphur) PHARMACY - sul-ter. Sulphur terebinthina-
tum. Terebinthinated sulphur. One part of purified Sulphur is dissolved by heating in one hundred parts of
Turpentine. Dilutions. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Chorea. Rheumatoid, arthritis. St. Vitus’s dance.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sul-ter. is referred to in the Hon. Robert Boyle’s works. A Sul-ter. lx dilution cured a most
obstinate case of St. Vitus’s dance and has often relieved pain in chronic rheumatic arthritis.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Cooper.

name: Sulphuricum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sul-ac. Sulphuricum acidum. Sulphuric acid. Vitriol. Dilution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acidity. Alcoholism. Alopecia. Aphthae. Backaches. Back. pain. Bedsores. Brain, concussions.
Breath, offensive. Bruises. Burns. Cachexia. Cancer. Can- crum, oris. Chafing. Chilblains. Constipation.
Corns. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dyspepsia. Erythema nodosum. Esophagitis. Gangrene.
Gastritis. Glossitis. Hair, ioss. Heartburn. Hemorrhoids. Hernia, inguinal. Hiccoughs. Hot, flushes. Impo-
tence. Infertility. Injuries. Intermittent fever. Irritation. Lead, poisoning. Liver disorders. Menopausal.
Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Myopia. Nephritis. Nightmares. Paralysis. Perspiration, great. Pneumonia.
Pregnancy, sickness. Purpura hemorrhagica. Pyorrhea. Rheumatism. Scurvy. Spleen, disorders. Thrush.
Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Uterus, prolapse. Vagina, prolapsed. Varicose, veins. Warts. Weakness. Wounds.
Writer’s cramp.
HOMEOPATHIC - Known as vitriol to the Alchemists., Sul-ac. was a favorite remedy of the Middle Ages. It
was used extensively in dilution for scrofulous, phagedenic, cancerous and venereal ulcers, as a gargle and
mouthwash for aphthae, ulceration of the gums and diphtheria. It was given as “Mineral Lemonade” in cases
of lead poisoning. Clarke verified this last use by giving water acidulated with the 3x.
The “Acid Soap” of Achard was prescribed as a dissolvent in scirrhous of the breast and nephritis, obstinate
intermittent fevers, visceral obstructions, dropsy jaundice, cachexia and “certain tumors of the feet.”
Elixir of vitriol is a mixture of the sulphuric acid, alcohol and water. It was a popular remedy for nervous
weakness in women. Dippel, Haller and others each had an “Elixir,” differing only in the proportions of the chief
ingredients.
The elixirs were used in intermittent, putrid, malignant, contagious, comatose
Sulphuricum acidum and petechial fevers, scarlatina, confluent and malignant variola, dysentery, plague,
leprosy, itch and other skin diseases, nocturnal emissions, suppression of menses and hemorrhoids, nephritis
and gout, tuberculosis, and chorea.
Grimmer stated that patients needing this remedy are weak and exhausted, yet mentally impatient and hurried.
Prone to suffer from ulcerations, both externally and internally, that readily tend to become gangrenous or
cancerous. Ulcers become red, blue and painful. Gangrene following mechanical injuries. Profuse, acrid or
stringy discharges.
Hemorrhages of dark blood, from lungs, stomach, uterus and rectum. Violent hemorrhages of thin, black blood
from all the orifices. Veins (of feet) distended. Purpura hemorrhagia. Removes long lasting black and blue
spots with soreness and stiffness of the part after trauma (follows Arn.).
Weakness or debility, especially in the digestive tract, giving a very relaxed feeling in the stomach. Tremor
and weakness, everything must be done in a hurry. Trembling internal, wants to be held. Weakness is out
of proportion to the disease, from some deep seated dyscrasia. Hot flushes, followed by perspiration with
trembling.
Stomach pain and hypochlorhydria. Sour stomach. Craving for alcoholic stimulants. Inflammatory
ulcerations and malignancy of the stomach occur in those who are chronic users of alcohol to excess.
Parts feel stiff and tight. Pains increase gradually and end abruptly. As of a blunt plug being driven in. Great
painfulness. Pains felt during sleep. Disappear on waking. Gnawing pains. Burning, darting pains. Shocks as
from pain. Writer’s cramp. Lead poisoning.
MIND - Irritable, impatience about trifles. Fretful, impatient. Hurried feeling. Must do everything in great hurry.
Hurried while walking, movements, eating, in writing, occupation. Sullen, impatient, angry because things
move so slowly. Nervous fatigue and tendency to take fright.
Changeable mood during perspiration. Vacillating and morose. Disheartened. Constant crying or weeping.
Unwilling to answer questions, says yes or no with difficulty. Speech monosyllabic. Extreme mental dejection,
unfit for work, would sit and weep whole day long.
Abdomen - Colic with sensation as if hernia would protrude, especially left side. Spleen enlarged, hard,
painful, on coughing. Sinking sense in abdomen after stools.
Back - Weak feeling with dragging into the hips and small of back. Weakness of spine, cannot sit or stand.
Large abscess on right side of neck.
Causations - Burns. Mechanical injuries. Falls, bruises, concussion of brain. Chafing. Surgical operations.
Sprains, wounds.
Chest - Great weakness in the chest with difficult speech.
Constitutions - Suited to topers, old persons, especially women in menopausal years, weak children with no
other complaint. Light-haired people. Sour babies. When some deep-seated dyscrasia prevails. Cases where
the weakness is out of proportion to the disease.
Ears - Feeling as of a leaf lying before the ear. Tearing and shaking in right ear. Violent tickling. Rhythmical
 roaring in ears. Ringing of bells before ears. Humming in ears in evening.
Eyes - Intra-ocular hemorrhage, following trauma. Great chemosis of conjunctiva with aching and sharp pain.
Eyes, smart, burn and lachrymation, while reading. Feeling as of a lump in outer canthi, moves to inner canthi
on closing eye and returns to outer on opening. Eyelids difficult to open.
Face - Deathly pale or wrinkled. Feels as if the white of an egg had dried on it.
Female - Distressing nightmares before menses or after menses. Menses too early and too profuse. Acrid,
burning leucorrhea often of bloody mucus. Prolapse of vagina and uterus from weakness. Gangrene of vagina
after prolapse. Erosion of cervix in the aged, easily bleeding. Hot flushes.
Flushes of heat, followed by sweat and a feeling of tremors all over the body during menopausal.
Food - Averse to smell of coffee. Craves alcohol, brandy. Desires fruits, fresh food. Wine aggravates. Worse
drinking cold water. Sweats after eating, especially warm food.
Head - Concussion of brain where skin is cold, body bathed in cold sweat. Sensation as if brain was loose in
forehead and falling from side to side (Bell., Rhus-t.). Compressive pai n in occiput, better by holding the
hand near head. Electric like shocks in forehead, temples. Right-sided neuralgia, painful shocks, skin feels
pinched. Thrust in right temple as if plug were pressed in. Pain of outer parts, as if there were subcutaneous
ulceration, painful to touch. Hair falls out, turns gray.
Kidneys - Pain in the bladder if urging for urinating is not attended to. Diminished secretion of urine. Slimy
sediment in the urine. Hematuria. Diabetes with lassitude, debility, despondency.
Limbs - Cramp-like paralytic contraction in arms, hands. Jerking of the tendons. Fingers jerk while writing,
sleeping. Writers’ cramp. Knees, ankles weak, cannot walk.
Lungs - Rapid respiration. Bronchitis in children with short, teasing cough. Cough, then belchings or vomiting.
Larynx moves up and down violently, rapid motion of alae nasi during dyspnea, better hanging down legs.
Bloody expectoration during menopause.
Modalities - Better from warmth, moderate temperature, hot drinks. Better lying on affected side, hands near
head, rest. Worse from excessive heat, open air. Worse cold, drinking cold water. Worse alcohol, odor of
coffee. Worse towards evening. Worse from touch, pressure. Worse lifting arms. Worse injuries, sprains,
surgical operations. Worse concussion of brain. Worse during menopausal period.
Mouth - Offensive breath. Bloody saliva from mouth. Aphthae during protracted disease, especially in children
with marasmus. Ulcers spread rapidly. Gums bleed
easily. Pyorrhea. Destruction of teeth in diabetes mellitus.
Nose - Dry coryza with loss of smell and taste. Coryza with thin, lemon-colored discharge. Flow of water from
nose. Nosebleed in evening. Oozing of dark, thin blood, worse odor of coffee, of old people. Pimples on side
of nose
Rectum - Diarrhea with sour odor of body and empty, faint feeling in abdomen. Diarrhea, very foul, green,
black or of hacked stools orange yellow, from unripe fruit and oysters, from least indigestion. Hemorrhoids,
with oozing moisture. Hemorrhoids prevent stools. Rectum feels as if it has a big ball.
Sensations - As if brain were loose and falling from side to side. As if one side of head filled with smoke. As
if a plug were thrust quickly into head. As from subcutaneous ulceration in scalp. As if white of egg had dried
on face. As if skin of cheek and chin were pinched. As of want of elasticity of vocal organs. As if there were a
lump in throat. As if rectum were torn to pieces during stool. As if hernia would protrude. As if menses would
come on.
Skin - Bad effects from mechanical injuries, - with bruises and livid skin. Petechia. Livid, red, itching blotches.
Purpura hemorrhagica. Hemorrhage of black blood from all outlets. Ecchymosis. Nodular urticaria.
Carbuncles, boils and other staphylococcic and streptococcic infections. Itching all over the body. Scars turn
red and blue, become painful. Chilblains with gangrenous tendency. Bed sores, abscesses.
Sleep - Sleeplessness from mental excitement. Sleepiness. Retarded sleep and early waking. Jerkings during
sleep. Anxious dreams, nightmares before menses.
Stomach - Weak, relaxed feeling at stomach, worse after stools. Coldness of stomach relieved by applied
heat. Heartburn, sourbelchings, sets teeth on edge (Rob.). Drinks chill the stomach and rejected unless
mixed with liquor. Nausea with chilliness. Sour vomiting, hiccough of alcoholics, nausea with shivering.
Vomits mucus instead of food. Coughs before vomiting during pregnancy.
Temperature - Hotflushes, then trembling or cold sweat, worse after warm ingesta, worse upper parts, better
motion. Drenching sweats. Disproportionate weakness during fevers like typhoid.
Throat - Sore. Liquids regurgitate, on swallowing. Larynx moves up and down violently. Throat looks
whitewashed. Stringy lemon-yellow mucus hangs from posterior sinuses in diphtheria.
Vertigo - Vertigo when sitting down, disappearing in the open air. Vertigo in room, better open air. Vertigo,
must lie down, as soon as he raises himself dizziness returns.
 COMMENTS - Hahnemann noted that Sul- ac. is useful for disorders characterized by “tension in the eyelids
in the morning, shortsightedness, hardness of hearing inguinal hernia, chronic looseness of the bowels,
roughness in the throat, asthma, profuse menses, metrorrhagia, swelling of the feet, coldness of the feet.”
Hahnemann’s proving with homeopathic experience confirmed many of the ancient uses of Sul-ac.
Characteristic weakness and prostration. Suited to cases where the weakness is out of proportion to the
disease. Weakness that seems to come from deep-seated dyscrasia. General internal trembling, as if trembling
from head to foot, but without visible trembling.
Symptoms often appear on right side, but the left cheek and left parotid are most affected. Pain travels from
left to right around hypochondria. Pains felt during sleep and disappearing on waking. Jerking on falling asleep.
Neuralgic pains increase gradually and end abruptly. Dull pain, pressure as of a plug thrust in. External
soreness and sensitiveness. Severe pain over the whole left side of the head, face and neck, coming on from
exposure to draft.
Agues and periodic neuralgias. Concussion, with cold sweats and great fatigue after the head injury. Easy
sweating, mostly on upper body. Sour body odor, cannot be washed off, particularly in children. Severe hot
flashes with profuse perspiration.
Trauma. Hemorrhage. Keynote of black blood (Croc.). Easily bleeding ulcers. Easily bruised. Extensive
bruising (Arn., Ham.), when bruises turn black or very dark blue. Purpura hemorrhagica. Bruises of soft parts
(Arn.), glands (Con.), and bones (Ruta.). Bruising pains. Long-lasting black and blue spots with soreness and
stiffness of the parts. Scars turn black or dark blue. Gangrene after injury. Boils, bedsores. Blotches.
Menses are too early, too profuse, may cause infertility. Menses with oozing of dark thin blood. Prolapse of
vagina and uterus, weakness. Flushing, with sweat, particularly during menopause. Cervicitis where the cervix
has been eroding and bleeding. Cervix bleeds when touched, friable.
Bloody saliva. Throat is filled with ulcers. Aphthous ulcer with pinpoint bleeding. Thrush in nursing infants.
Heartburn, burning in the stomach, with sour belchings that set the teeth on edge. “Vomiting in morning, acidity
in stomach, burning is esophagus and stomach, sour, acrid or foul belchings.”
Pain in bladder unless call to pass water is immediately attended to. Cholera, diarrhea. Diarrhea in emaciated
children. External heiuorrhoids, sensitive to touch, accompanied by itching.
Thirsty, but water is not tolerated. Water chills the stomach unless qualified with alcohol. Uncontrollable craving
for alcohol (Lach.). Cirrhosis of the liver in alcoholics. Vomiting after alcohol.
For inebriates who are “on their last legs,” long after Nux-v. had ceased to help. Hering said the craving for
liquor has been subdued by taking for two or four weeks, thrice daily, ten to fifteen drops of a mixture of one
part of Sul-ac. with three parts of alcohol.
Cooper contended that many ague cases, supposed to have been cured with Chin-s., were really cured by the
sulphuric acid used in dissolving it. “Moreover.” said Cooper, “in all epidemic diseases influenza, cholera,
small-pox, etc.”
With Sul-ac. 30c, a dose every night, Clarke gave great help to a delicate woman who had nightmare, waking
in a fright,
Sulphuricum acidum before each menstrual period.
A chemist in Covent Garden used a lotion of Sulphuric acid, well diluted, for all the cases of itch that came
before him.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Puls. Antidote to: Lead poisoning. Compare: (1) Arn., Calen., Led., Sep., Calc.
Complementary: Puls. Follows well: In injuries, Arn., Con., Ruta.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Alcoholism. Alopecia. Aphthae. Backaches. Back. pain. Bedsores. Brain, concussions.
Breath, offensive. Bruises. Burns. Cachexia. Cancer. Can- crum, oris. Chafing. Chilblains. Constipation.
Corns. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dyspepsia. Erythema nodosum. Esophagitis. Gangrene.

name: Sulphurosum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sulo-ac. Sulphurosum acidum. Sulphur dioxide. Sulphurous acid. Sulphurous anhydride. The
remedy is obtained by dissolving sulphur dioxide in water. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne rosacea. Allergies. Colds. Constipation. Croup. Diphtheria. Eczema. Epidemics. Favus.
Hands, chapped. Heartburn. Infections. Influenza. Nipples, sore. Pityriasis versicolor. Stomatitis, ulcerative.
Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sulo-ac. is soluble in water, it produces an acid solution containing sulphurous acid. In this
way, relatively weak solutions are obtained.
Gutman carried out a clinical study, and taking as a base the results obtained, he drew up aclinical
symptomatology in 1968. Julian completed Gutman’s description with reference to the symptom data which
resulted from acute and chronic poisoning cases.
Sulo-ac. irritates any mucus membrane with which it comes into contact and by becoming oxidized, it is
 transformed into sulphurous acid and then into sulfuric acid. Acting on the upper respiratory tract, it is known
even to create retro-sternal constriction and phenomena such as anoxia ischemia and myocarditis.
Predisposition to pulmonary tuberculosis. Chronic, purulent hyper secretion of bronchial mucus in the young
without dilatation of the bronchi. Need for fresh air, vertigo. Irritation of the nose, pharynx and larynx.
Dyspnea, wheezing, coughing and retrosternal constriction. Pulmonary tumors. Cold in the head, influenza.
Asthma, bronchitis, croup. Chronic tuberculosis. Clergyman’s sore throat.
Dyspepsia with ptyalism and gastric acidity. Keratitis and conjunctivitis. Chilblains, chapped hands. Diphtheria.
Scarlatina malign. Typhoid fever. Sensitivity to infections.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Constriction behind the sternum.
Eyes - Irritation of both conjunctivae and cornea. Tension of the artery of the retina. Change in the reaction of
the pupil. Conjunctivitis. Superficial epidemic spotted keratitis. Herpes of the cornea. Chronic glaucoma.
Choroiditis. Dacryocystitis. Blepharitis. Edema of the eyelids.
Heart - Rapid pulse, cold sweating. Accentuation of the second pulmonary sound. Systolic pulsation in the pit
of the stomach. Inflammation of the coronary arteries.
Limbs - Chilliness at the limbs.
Lungs - Feeling of suffocation and cyanosed face. Wheezing and rhonchi widespread in the chest.
Bronchiectasis. Emphysema, asthma. Chronic pulmonary tuberculosis. Chronic bronchitis. Oppression,
sneezing and spasmodic coughing. Expectoration of dirty-gray or bloodstained mucous.
Mouth - Brownish stains on the teeth, especially on the incisors. Dental caries. Ptyalism, gingivitis. Ptyalism
in pregnant women.
Nose - Burning sensation in the nose and discharge of a viscous liquid. Mucopurulent rhinitis. Nasal polyps.
Skin - Eruption of vesicles and edema. Brownish coloring of the skin. Eczematic eruption, very sensitive.
Leucoderma. Urticaria.
Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Dyspepsia and hyperchlorhydria.
Temperature - Septic fevers of all kinds. Epidemic influenza. Typhoid fever. Tuberculosis. Smallpox. Plague.
Throat - Burning sensation in the throat. Feeling of tightness around the throat. Lingering huskiness of voice.
Scratching in the throat and chest.
COMMENTS - Some forty years ago, when the germ theory of disease in its present form was in its infancy,
Dewar of Fite, conceived the idea that sulphurous acid was an innocent and at the same time universal germ
destroyer and consequently universal remedy. His views met with cordial acceptance and
inhalationsofsulphurous acid given off from burning sulphur became the fashion.
Dewar’s method was simple. A few red cinders were put in a kitchen shovel, this was placed in the center of a
room and flowers of sulphur sprinkled thereon. In a very short time every person in the room was sneezing
violently, coughing and wheezing and running at the eyes and nose.
Dewar also used the ordinary solution and a spray. Wounds, sore nipples, bruises were also amenable to its
local use. For erysipelas, a local application of equal parts of the acid and glycerine.
Sulo-ac. doubtless shares the anti-septic properties of Sulph. The symptoms' are from observations of the
effects on workmen in mines from air contaminated with Sulo-ac.
Milne summed up its virtues, “Anti-septic, disinfectant, a powerful deoxidizer and destroyer of vegetable life.”
As a gargle it is used in the strength of one to six. In parasitic skin disorders the B. P. solution is used and is
effective.
Ringer said that ten to fifteen minims taken ten minutes before each meal will remedy heartburn in most
instances. It prevents flatulence and fermentations and that “the solution, either strong or diluted in varying
proportions, speedily removes thrush.” In potencies, it has cured ulcerative inflammation of the mouth.
Headache, better by vomiting.
C. Wootton tasted the acid with this result it at once stopped the mucus secretion of the bowels. The
constipation was so severe that he was in misery for nine months, until he took Hydr., which cured. The use
of Sulo- ac. as a hair-wash at a later time produced the same result.
RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Hydr. (constipation). Compare: (1) Sulph. in ulcerated sore mouth, Nat-m.,
Caps., Sul-ac. (2) The effects on the back recorded by Hahnemann as from the fumes of burning Sulph. were
antidoted by electricity. (3) Brom. - Persistent, excoriating cold in the head, huskiness worse in the evening.
dry cough and attacks of suffocation. (4) Kali-i. - Streaming, burning, excoriating, cold in the head, with violent
cough and soapy, salty, greenish expectoration. (5) Tub. - Emaciation, varying pains, chronic swelling of the
tonsils, palpitations, perspiration, very sensitive to the cold, coughing hoarseness.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

name: Sumbulus Moschatus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sumb. Sumbulus moschatus. Musk root. Sumbul. Ferula sumbul. N. O. Umbelliferae. Tincture
of the powdered root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Ascarides. Asthma. Breasts, pains. Chorea. Diarrhea. Epilepsy. Fainting. Heart, disorders.
Pneumonia. Hysteria. Insomnia. Neuralgias. Numbness. Palpitations. Spermatorrhea. Throat, catarrh.
Throat, spasms. Typhoid fever. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sumbul, as its name, “Musk-root,” implies, has an odor resembling that of musk. The
resemblance is so close that Sumbul is used to adulterate musk. Sumb. was proved by Lembke, Cattell and
others.
The symptoms are as like to those of Mosch, as the physical resemblance would imply. Hysterical and nervous
disorders. Easy fainting, nervous palpitations. Nervous, irritable and sleepless.
Anomalous, functional, cardiac disorders. Sclerosed arteries. Menopausal flushings. Asthma. Yellow tenacious
discharges. The left side was more affected than the right.
Neuralgia. Chorea, constant jerking of the head and limbs with protrusion of the tongue. Numbness on
becoming cold, on left side. Insomnia of delirium tremens (fifteen drops of tincture). Sensation as if water
dropped down spine. As of a hot water flowing through part. Early senility.
MIND - Emotional and fidgety. Mistakes in writing and adding. Weeps and laughs by turns. Fear of becoming
insane. Faintness from hearing music.
Abdomen - Abdomen full, distended and painful.
Back - Trickling along spine.
Breasts - Pulling like a string in right breast. Neuralgia around left breast and left hypochondriac region.
Face - Neuralgia. As of a hair or cobweb on face. Idiotic expression.
Female - Ovarian neuralgia. Screwing pain in left side of uterus. Sexual excitability. Menopausal flushes.
Head - Dull in morning, clear in evening.
Heart - Nervous palpitations in hysterical subjects or at menopause, worse least exertion and thinking of it.
As if heart beating in water. Neuralgia around left breast simulating angina pectoris. High blood pressure due
to arteriosclerosis. Cardiac asthma. Aching in left arm, heavy, numb and weary. Pulse irregular.
Kidneys - Oily pellicle on surface of urine.
Limbs - Left arm aching, heavy, numb, weary.
Lungs - Asthma, cardiac, hysterical. Oppressed tightness in left chest, as if clogged. Loses breath on any
exertion.
Modalities - Better from gentle motion, warmth. Worse from cold, inspiration. Worse menopausal. Worse
motion, active exercise. Worse left side, after sitting. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse in morning. Music
causes faintness.
Mouth - Tongue feels rough as if scraped.
Nose - Comedones. Tenacious yellow mucus from nose.
Sensations - Tongue as if scraped. Clogged sensation in left chest. As if heart beating in water. Like a string
pulling in right breast. Corkscrew pains in (left) uterus and appendages.
Skin - Pale, cold. Internal itching.
Sleep - Dreams of falling, of sex, followed by profuse, sudden emission.
Stomach - Burning water brash. Belching of gas from stomach.
Throat - Choking constriction, with con-
stant swallowing. Hysterical. Spasm of pharyngeal muscles. Tenacious mucus in throat.
COMMENTS - Hale gave indications for Sumb. including nasal and pharyngeal catarrh with nervousness,
sleeplessness and tendency to spasms (especially in children), discharge of tenacious, yellow mucus.
Catarrhal, spasmodic or cardiac asthma. Ascarides with bloated, drum-like abdomen and constipation, picking
nose cured with Sumb. 15c. Oily pellicle in urine. Pain in left uterine region. Menopausal flushings.
Neuralgia, facial or ovarian in women of quick and lively nervous constitutions. Neuralgia of the left
hypochondrium, simulating angina pectoris with palpitation in nervous women. Insomnia of chronic alcoholism.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Asaf., Mosch. (2) Mosch., Asaf., Melit., Med., Mez. (3) Oily pellicle on urine,
Sulph., Puls., Petr. (4) Tenacious, yellow mucus, Hydr. (5) Infra-breast pain, Cimic., Puls., Lil-t. (6) Worse
thinking of symptoms, Ox-ac., Pip-m.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Sweet Chestnut
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - sw-ch-b. Sweet chestnut. Castanea sativa. Flowering sprigs with both male and female flowers
 are boiled for half an hour. The water is strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from
the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or
weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or
juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sw-ch-b. belongs to Bach’s groupofDespondency andDespair withCrb- a-b., Oak-b., Will-
b., Star-b-b., Elm-b., Pine-b. and Lar-b. States of apathy and anguish.
Severe and prolonged physical suffering, leading to anguish. Suffering seems to be unbearable. Physical side
effects of deep depression. Morbid preoccupation and depression (Must-b.). Existential doubt, despair.
Suicidal.
MIND- Anguish. Apathy, faithlessness, nihilism and despair. Religious despair with loss of faith. The “dark
night of the soul.” Depressive disorders (Must-b.), especially when suicide is threatened with deep-seated
despair Morbid preoccupation with death.
Void of emotional life. Despair and despondent. Sense of meaninglessness of life may lead to carelessness
of attitude. Lack of aspirations and meaningful purpose.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Swertia Chirata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - swer-ch. Swertia chirata. N. O. Gentianaceae. Tincture from the flowers and leaves. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acidity. Bilious. Boils. Cough. Dropsy. Dyspepsia. Fevers. Flatulence. Indigestion. Intermittent
fever. Leprosy. Malaria. Typhoid fever. Worms.
HERBAL - Charaka recommended Swertia in hematemesis and dropsy. Habita found it efficacious in vomiting
of pregnancy.
Ayurvedic physicians extolled its therapeutic virtues in typhoid and intermittent fevers, malarial fever,
respiratory troubles, bilious troubles, impurities of blood, burning, cough, dropsy, thirst, leprosy, boils and
worms.
Swertia is a well-known and well-tried febrifuge among these practitioners and they very often use it in all sorts
of fevers. It has been in constant demand among the Kavirajas of India.
Like cinchona and other bitter tonics, it is bitter, stomachiec, laxative, anthelmintic and febrifuge. It excites the
appetite, strengthens digestion, but does not constipate. It diminishes flatulence and hyperacidity. Removes
biliousness in atonic dyspepsia, liver troubles. Removes acidity of the stomach and flatulence, gout,
intermittent and other fevers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Kali Kumar Bhat- tacharjea, of Gouripore, Assam, made a short proving of Swer-ch. An
account of the proving and the symptoms developed therein were published in the Hahnemann of Falgoon.
Dr. Bhattacharjea prepared a tincture from the flowers and leaves of the plant.
MIND - Dullness of mind, laziness, desire to lie down always.
Abdomen - Accumulation of wind in the abdomen.
Ears - Hissing sound in the ears.
Eyes - Severe burning sensation in the eyes.
Food - Desire for bitter substances and meat.
Head - Dull pain over both the temples, gradually extending to the whole of the head. Coldness is felt over the
head.
Kidneys - Dull pain in the kidney, especially on the right side. Urine is of high redcolor. Burning while urinating.
Limbs - Aching pains in the hands and feet. Weakness of the legs, difficulty in walking.
Liver - Enlargement of both liver and spleen associated with pain.
Lungs - Hurried respiration during fever. Dry mucus, dry hacking cough. Dry cough in the bronchial region.
Male - Weakness of the male sexual organ, slight discharge of semen.
Mouth - Bad taste in the morning, offensive odor.
Nose - Flushes of heat come out of the nostrils.
Temperature - Stage of coldness lasts long, but there is no desire for drinking. Cold with nausea, bilious
vomiting. Desire for hot water. Hot stage generally lasts for three hours, and afterwards sweating stage
appears. Sweat only on chest, axilla and thighs. Slight thirst with heat. No fixity of the appearance of fever.
Burning sensation in the eyes during fever.
Throat - In the morning and evening, pain is felt in the throat, not relieved by hot drinks.
Tongue - The middle of the tongue is enveloped with a thick yellowish coating. Heaviness of the tongue.
Difficult speech.
COMMENTS - A noted febrifuge. Acute and chronic malarial fevers. Chronic fevers. Liver troubles after fever
 has stopped. Debility after fevers. Long-lasting malarial
fever, turns into Kala-azar associated with enlarged spleen and liver.
The fever may come on at any time of the day and night; in chronic cases the fever appears usually in the
afternoon. In the morning attacks, cold stage lasts for a long time, there is no appreciable thirst in this stage
and if there be any, it is generally relieved by hot drinks.
Before the appearance of hot stage, nausea and bilious vomiting trouble the patient. The hot stage lasts for 3
to 4 hours and there is slight thirst. Severe burning sensation in the eyes, continues as long as the fever is
present.
Indigestion, atonic dyspepsia. Flatulence. Loss of appetite. Troubles arising out of worms. Catarrhs, leprosy
and some skin diseases.
RELATIONS - Compare: Chin., Ars.
REFERENCES - Ghose.
