name: Sycotic Co. Bacillus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - syc-co. Sycotic co. bacillus. Sycotic bacillus. Bowel nosode. Bacillus streptococcus faecalis.
Sycotic co. from non-lactose fermenting cocci ofintestinal tract. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies, food. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Arthritis. Asthma. Backaches.
Bedwetting. Conjunctivitis. Cough. Cystitis. Deafness. Dysmenorrhea. Enteroptosis. Fibrositis. Food,
poisoning. Gastroenteritis. Headaches. Indigestion. Leucorrhea. Lumbosacral pain. Menorrhagia.
Metrorrhagia. Neuritis. Otorrhea. Photophobia. Polyps. Rheumatism. Sebaceous, cysts. Vaginitis. Warts.
HOMEOPATHIC - Characteristic irritation, particularly in relation to the mucus membranes. Catarrhal states
of the respiratory tract, the bladder and the vagina. Asthma, sinusitis. Cough about 2 a.m., worse from change
of atmosphere.
Irritation of synovial linings in rheumatism. Enlarged lymphoid tissue of tonsils and adenoids, glands.
Meningeal irritation. Convulsions. Cold and sensitive to dampness. Warty growths. Ailments from vaccinations.
Vulvo-vaginitis, leucorrhea. Gastroenteritis. Bedwetting, cystitis. Albuminuria. Stools are excoriating, loose and
offensive with urgent call to stool on rising.
MIND - Nervous and tense. Ailments from anticipation. Bites the fingernails. Nervous irritability. Cross,
irritable and restless. Quick tempered, outbursts of temper from resentment. Oversensitive. Shy, sensitive
and fussy. Exhausted. Timidity. Weepy and depressed. Fears of dark, of being left alone, of animals and dogs.
Abdomen - Distended abdomen, colon.
Enteroptosis. Chronic irritation of whole digestive tract. Acute or chronic gastroenteritis in the child.
Back - Severe backache. Pain in morning on rising. Backache from damp weather. Stiff Mover. Fibrositis,
myositis. Neuritis of head and neck. Sebaceous cyst back. Lumbosacral pain. Pain in sacral-iliac joints. Hips
stiff.
Blood - Anemia and hydremia.
Chest - Pleurisy. Pleurodynia. Fibrositis of chest wall. Sudden pain at the base of right lung. Intercostal
neuralgia. Pain in left shoulder blade.
Constitutions - Pale, sallow, flabby and soft with long eyelashes (Tub.), and sweat of the head.
Ears - Otorrhea. Excessive formation of wax. Deafness. Itching of meatus. Cracks under ears.
Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Vitreous opacities. Pain in eyeballs. Photophobia, hemiopia. Blinking. Tarsal cysts.
Cystic tumors on eyelids. Swelling of upper eyelids.
Face - Puffy in morning, especially under eyes. Acne rosacea. Eruptions, herpes about mouth. Erythema.
Vesicular eruption on cheeks. Malignant growth on right cheek. Hair on face and upper lip. Facial neuralgia.
Twitching facial muscles.
Female - Amenorrhea. Pain left ovary at menstrual period. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Dysmenorrhea.
Leucorrhea acrid, excoriating. Leucorrhea copious, yellow. Leucorrhea profuse, bland. Vaginal discharge,
offensive, fishy. Pruritus vulvae,
vulvo-vaginitis, balanitis. Tumors, ovarian cysts. Uterine polyps. Genital warts, herpes.
Food - Desires butter, fat, cheese. Desires sweets, milk and salt. Averse to breakfast. Aversion to egg, fat,
cheese, milk, milk pudding, cream. Aversion to salt, vinegar, sugar, tea. Aversion to bread, potato, tomato,
vegetables, meat. Aggravated by egg, causing nausea, vomiting, bilious attack and hay fever. Worse from fat,
eggs, onion and oranges.
Head - Irritation of meninges, sub-acute or chronic. Headache from infection of sinuses. Aching pain deep in
brain. Headache on left side. Frontal congestive headache which lasts for many days. Sick headache, worse
at menstrual period. Throbbing, better heat and rest, worse noise. Sweating of head at night. Painful dry scaly
 spots. Premature gray hair. Alopecia. Baldness.
Kidneys - Irritation of mucus membranes from kidney to urethra. Kidney pain. Nephritis, pyelitis, nephrosis,
cystitis. Frequency and urgency. Urine corrosive. Albuminuria. Urinary tantrums.
Limbs - Fibrositis, shoulders. Muscular rheumatismof arms. Arthritis fingers, pain generally better dry day and
hot water. Fingers deformed, nodules on fingers. Fingertips cracked. Fingers go dead, numb, with spasm of
the fingers. Prickly feeling in hands. Nails brittle. Feet and legs painful when walking as if walking on loose
cobble stones. Feet and legs painful at night. Pesplanus. Rheumatism of knees. Ankles swollen and stiff. Feet
swollen at night. Fidgety feet at night in bed. Soles of feet painful. Big toe joint painful.
Lungs - Dyspnea in morning on waking. Asthma and bronchitis, worse with damp and frost and better at the
sea side. Frequent bronchial colds. Bronchitis in winter. Tracheitis. Wheeze and coughing at 2 to 3 a.m. Irritable
cough of croupy nature at night, wakes from sleep. Coughs until sick. Chronic spasmodic persisting cough.
Cough with tough sputum.
Male - Impotency. Genital warts and herpes.
Modalities - Wofse from change of atmosphere, damp.
Mouth - Salivation increased. Bad taste, sense of taste lost. Pins and needle sensation on tongue. Pain like a
splinter in tongue. Tongue sore, scalded, dry, fissured, furred. Tongue dry, sticks to roof of mouth. Warts on
tongue. Deep ulcers on tongue. Ulcers in mouth. Lips dry and cracked. Cracks in angles of mouth. Herpes of
mouth.
Neck - Fibrositis in neck, shoulders and back.
Nose - Nasal, post nasal catarrh. Catarrh extending to frontal sinuses. Turbinates congested, sinus infection.
Vasomotor rhinorrhea. Hay fever. Coryza after eating eggs. Polyps. Nose dry, crusting and burning. Cracks at
corners of nostrils. Nosebleed. Sense of smell lost.
Perspiration - Profuse perspiration at night during sleep.
Rectum - Condylomata around anus. Anal warts. Splinter pain. Distended feeling in rectum. Prolapse.
Constipation or looseness. Stool pale, crumbly, bad odor. Loose, offensive stool, excoriating (Med.). Diarrhea
from excitement of emotions. Diarrhea after eating, fatty food. Liquid motion after every meal. Urgent call to
stool as soon as rising out of bed.
Skin - Sallow and oily skin. Impetigo. Warts large, flat and rugged. Herpes on face, neck and chest. Herpes
groin. Váricellar eruption of limbs since immunization. Intertrigo breasts. Eczema of face in infants. Eczema
on back of hands. Palmar dermatitis. Cracks on fingertips. Paronychia. Nails and toenails brittle and painful.
Cracks on heals. Varicóse eczema of ankles. Chilblains on feet.
Sleep - Insomnia. Restless sleep. Perspiration of head and body during sleep. Wheeze or cough. Can’t sleep
until 3 a.m. Wakes 2 to 3 a.m. Night terrors. Nightmares, of dead bodies.
Stomach - Anorexia. Burning pain in stomach. Pain and distention in the epigastrium. Flatulence. Acidosis
attacks. Eructation acid, bilious attacks. Nausea from the smell of cooking. Nausea or sickness after
eating eggs (Ferr.). Nocturnal vomiting, must empty stomach.
Throat - Fibrositis of neck and throat. Goiter. Glands enlarged. Enlargement of tonsils and adenoids. Tonsillitis,
cheesy masses from tonsil. Quinsy. Throat feels raw, scorched, dry. Profuse mucus from throat in morning.
Swallowing difficult, chokes easily.
COMMENTS - This organism of the intestinal tract is related morphologically and clinically to the gonococcus
bacteria. Hahnemann related what he called “the Sycotic Miasm” to the disease, gonorrhea, but this disease
is only one form of catarrhal infection of the mucus membrane of the urinary tract.
There are many non gonorrheal organisms associated with the symptom picture of “Catarrh” and according to
Dr. John Paterson the miasm “Sycosis” may be considered synonymous with “Catarrh.” Gonorrhea is an
infection of mucus membrane, but catarrhal manifestations (sycotic) are not at all due to gonorrheal infection.
Characteristic warty growths. Exanthema of chickenpox. Chronic and recurring cystitis, often treated several
times with antibiotics. Usually additional remedies are required, particularly a constitutional prescription, but
intercurrent doses of Syc- co. can be of great help.
Griggs noted it for human “flu,” cat “flu,” foul pest, foot and mouth disease and canine distemper are all the
signs of Syc-co. Convulsions, meningitis or epileptic forms of seizures are to be found in the clinical picture
and also chorea, though less frequently than in Dysentery Co.
Syc-co. 200c in nosebleeds of long standing in a girl without any apparent reasons, cured completely with a
few doses at long intervals.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The related sycotic remedies are Thuj, Nit-ac., Nat-s. and Bac. (2) Vesicular type
of rash related to Ant-t., Rhus-t., Bac., and Thuj. Complementary: Lyc., is often complementary to this nosode.
REFERENCES - Bach. Paterson.
 ***SYMPHORICARPUS RACEMOSUS
(Snowberry)
PHARMACY - sym-r. Symphoricarpus racemosus. Snowberry. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of fresh ripe
berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Constipation. Hematemesis. Indigestion. Morning sickness. Nausea. Vomiting. Water brash.
HOMEOPATHIC - Prof. S. Burdick investigated the medicinal properties of many plants hitherto unused by
the profession, including Symphoricarpus racemosa.
Useful for persistent vomiting of pregnancy. Nausea during menstruation. Nausea, worse from any motion.
Averse to all food, better when lying on the back. Gastric disturbances, fickle appetite, nausea, water brash,
bitter taste. Smell and thought of food repugnant. Constipation.
COMMENTS - When Burdick gave some of the Sym-r. to the first prover, a woman, she felt the marked nausea,
and exclaimed, as soon as it was produced, “Doctor, this is precisely like the morning sickness I always
experienced during pregnancy.”
Dr. Burdick became more interested, repeated the experiment with other provers, and obtained almost uniform
results, viz., a feeling varying from qualmishness to intense vomiting. It was given to female provers only and
merely tested far enough to verify that symptom.
Upon this clue, Dr. Burdick gave Sym-r. in the higher potencies to patients suffering from the vomiting of
pregnancy with the most satisfactory results. After a trial of many years, he found it so far superior to other
remedies that he relied on it altogether with rarely any but entirely satisfactory results.
Burdick mentioned the drug in his course of lectures, so Moaffat bore it in mind waiting for a test case. Soon
that came in the person of a young woman three months advanced in her first pregnancy.
She was suffering from a deathly nausea with vomiting and retching so prolonged and violent as to produce
hematemesis. The smell or thought of food was repugnant in the extreme.
An examination disclosed no malposition or apparent cause for the trouble, so he procured some Sym-r. 200c
from Dr. Burdick and gave her one dose in the midst of a violent paroxysm.
In a few minutes she stopped vomiting and said she felt soothed and quieted all over. In half an hour the
nausea began again, but a few pellets checked it promptly and she fell asleep. Once during the night she
awoke distressed and took a dose, but slept again quite soon.
For a month or so she felt very well until after over-exerting herself she became nauseated once more, but it
was promptly checked, nor did it return during her pregnancy. The indications have been observed in cases
of pregnancy with a feeling of qualmishness, with indifference to food.
In more severe cases, there is a deathly nausea, the vomiting is continuous, violent retching. Sym-r. does not
seem to be confined to any particular morning aggravation, a prominent symptom is the disgust at the sight, smell or
thought of food.
In one case, the patient was comparatively comfortable while lying on the back, but would be nauseated by
the slightest motion of the arms, particularly raising them. The case was completely relieved by a few doses
of Sym-r.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Phatak
keynote:
PHARMACY - syc-co. Sycotic co. bacillus. Sycotic bacillus. Bowel nosode. Bacillus streptococcus faecalis.
Sycotic co. from non-lactose fermenting cocci ofintestinal tract. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Allergies, food. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Arthritis. Asthma. Backaches.
Bedwetting. Conjunctivitis. Cough. Cystitis. Deafness. Dysmenorrhea. Enteroptosis. Fibrositis. Food,

name: Symphytum Officinale
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - symph. Symphytum officinale. Comfrey. Knit-bone. Healing herb. N. O. Boraginaceae. Tincture
of fresh root-stock collected before flowering and in autumn. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies. Tincture, externally as a dressing for sores and ulcers and itching of anus.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Amputation. Backache. Bone, cancer. Bone, fractures. Bone, injuries. Breasts, sore.
Eyes, injuries. Fractures. Gingivitis. Glands, enlarged. Gunshot wounds. Hernia. Menses, suppressed.
Osteoporosis. Periosteum, painful. Periostitis. Psoas, abscess. Sexual excess. Sprains. Stump, pain. Tennis
elbow. Wounds.
HERBAL - Symphytum is also called consolida, and the word comfrey is derived from confirnare. The common
name, knit-bone or bone-set, gives the indication for this remedy. The root contains a crystalline solid that
stimulates the growth of bone cells and epithelium on ulcerated surfaces.
The glutinous juice of the root seems, according to Gerarde, to have given the key to its action as a vulnerary.
Symphytum may be considered the orthopedic specific of herbal medicine.
HOMEOPATHIC - Symph. is abone remedy. It may be administered internally in the treatment of gastric and
duodenal ulcers, and in stomach pain, and externally for anal itching. External application disposes the
swelling, due to injury or other growths.
Wounds penetrating to perineum and bones. Injuries to bones, cartilages, ligaments, joints, tendons and the
 periosteum, with excessive pain. Pricking pain and soreness of periosteum. Pricking, sticking, jagging pains.
Fractures, broken bones. Painful bone at point of fracture. Pricking, stitching pains, remaining after wound
is healed, worse touch. Non-union of fractures. Painful, irritable stump after amputation. Painful old injuries.
Bruises, sprains and inflammation of bones, diseased spinous processes. Deficient callus. Acts on joints
generally. Neuralgia or arthralgia of the knee. Sore breasts. Psoas abscess. Sarcoma.
Abdomen - Pain about navel, worse sitting.
Pains across epigastrium from one side to the other, when sitting. Griping pain.
Back - Backaches from excessive sexual indulgence, or from violent motion. Low back pain from injury,
overexertion, or excess sexual activity. Spinal injury. Pain in back from a fall. Pott’s disease from a fall. Decay
of vertebrae. Caries of spinal and other bones.
Breasts - Sore breasts.
Causations - Broken bones. Injures to eye, bone, periosteum. Falls. Blows from blunt instruments. Sexual
excess.
Ears - Cannot hear well, feels as if ears were stopped up. Inflamed ears.
Eyes - Injuries to the eyes from blunt instruments, blows, knocks, to the eyeball, eye socket, or sclera. Black
eyes (Arn., Led.). Bleeding inside the eye after injury. Retinal bleeding. Traumatic conjunctivitis. Long-lasting
pain or soreness in the eye after injury. Eyelids spasmodically closed.
Face - Facial injuries. Inflammation of inferior maxillary bone, hard, red swelling. Cancer, tumor of antrum.
Cancer of jaw bone.
Female - Menses stopped. Leucorrhea.
Head - Headache in occiput, in top of head, in forehead, changing places. Pain comes down bone of nose.
Inflammation of inferior maxillary bone, hard, red, swelling. Skull fracture or head injury (Hyper., Nat-s.).
Kidneys - Stricture of urethra.
Limbs - Bone fractures. Comminuted fracture. Non-union of bones. Accelerates the formation of callus.
Reduces healing. Prickling, stitching pains. Bruises. Injuries from blunt instruments. Pain in area of bony
protuberances, elbow, epicondyles, ankles. Injury to periosteum. Injury to hard tissue, shins. Bone
inflammation, periostitis with pain and soreness. Osteoporosis. Brittle bones. Knee arthralgia. Tennis elbow.
Psoas abscess. Bone cancers. Pain at the site of old wounds or fractures, past injury to cartilage or bone.
Post-surgical pain at the site of amputation or bone puncture.
Male - Testicles become painful and tender, prevent walking. Backache from excessive sexual indulgence,
with spermatorrhea.
Modalities - Better gentle motion, warmth. Worse frominjuries. Worse sexual excess. Worse touch, motion,
pressure. Stooping causes weight in forehead. Sitting causes pain about navel. Walking causes pain opposite
spleen.
Nose - Pain comes down bone of nose and sometimes down both sides of nose.
Rectum - Dysentery. Inflamed and bleeding hemorrhoids.
Sensations - As if upper lid passed over an elevation on closing eye. As if ears were stopped up.
Skin - Cold.
Stomach - Ulcers of the stomach.
Teeth - Periodontal disease. Toothache after injury. Jaw swollen and painful after dental work. Pain worse
after tooth extraction.
COMMENTS - Grimmer noted that, though the proving was meager, there was a rich clinical history.
According to Gerarde, “The roots of Comfrey stamped and the juice drunk with wine, help those that spit blood
and heal all inward wounds and bursting. The same bruised and laid to in manner of a plaster, do heal all fresh
and green wounds and are so glutinous, that it will solder and glue together meat that is chopped in pieces,
seething in a pot and make it in one lump.”
Gerarde added that it eases pains in the back from violent motion such as wrestling or from excessive sexual
indulgence (Arn.), even when spermatorrhea has been induced thereby.
Peter Squire gave, as the medicinal properties of Symph., “Astringent, mucilaginous, glutinous, useful to form
cases for injured limbs. The black rind of the root is scraped off and the mucilaginous root is then scraped
carefully into a nice even pulp. This spread upon cambric or old muslin in wrapped round the limb and
bandaged over, it shortly stiffens and forms a casing superior to starch, giving support and strength to the
part.”
Squire knew a bonesetter who rendered himself famous for setting compound fractures with this root, which
he kept secret. He never removed the bandage after the first dressing until the limb was well.
Sir Wm. Thomson of Dublin related a case of malignant tumor of the face that had extended to the nose.
Microscopic examination proved it to be round-celled sarcoma. The patient, a man, refused advice at the time,
 and was examined by Felix Semon, who saw the man later. After still further delay, Thomson performed the
operation in the month of May, 1896.
A month later the growth began to show again, increased rapidly, closed the right eye, was blue, tense, firm,
lobulated, but did not break. Thomson declined to operate again. Early in October, the man walked into Thom-
son’s study well. “The tumor had completely disappeared from the face and I could not identify any trace of it
in the mouth.” The man had applied poultices of comfrey root and the swelling disappeared.
Comfrey ' s therapeutic history is rich with clinical cures of round-cell sarcoma of the antrum and many cases
of bone cancer. It seems to have special curative action on the periosteum and bony structures, facilitating the
formation of callus in fractures, bringing about union, even in compound fractures, and in cases of slow or
delayed union.
Curative in injuries to the eyeball by blows etc. It follows Arn. in such cases, as well as in injuries to and bruising
of the testicles. Backaches after strains and from sexual excesses. Pott’s disease, psoriasis and abscesses
from a fall. One case of inguinal hernia has been cured with the topical application of the tincture of the root.
H. C. Allen referred to the following indications for Symph. given by Lippe: when the bone or periosteum has
been injured and the soft parts have recovered from the bruised soreness under Arn., the remaining pain and
soreness of periosteum may be promptly relieved by Symph.
Symph. was the only remedy Lippe had seen which was efficient in traumatic injuries of bone or periosteum.
He cured many cases after others had used Arn. and failed.
H. C. Allen gave the following cure, reported by Fowler. Mrs. J. stepped on the edge of a scantling, which
rolled and she turned her ankle. In a few minutes the ankle began to swell and become painful, pain increased
rapidly, so that in hour or two the patient was in great agony.
She declared that her leg was broken, she “could feel the rough ends of the broken bones jagging into the
flesh.” She could not bear any one to approach her for fear of be- wgbMNedsi;^ promptly relieved, so that she
went about her usual duties in forty-eight hours.
Allen regarded pricking pain as a guiding symptom. He noted its usefulness, next to bone injuries, for injuries
to the eyeball. “I have long since ceased to use Arn. in injuries of the globe of the eye, Symph. having given
such prompt and permanent relief.”
Croserio was one of the first to use Symph. in the potencies for fractures. “Injuries of the bones are healed
most promptly with Symph. 30c internally, once a day.”
Wells gave cases of his own, including the case of a boy, 14, who broke the bone of his forearm at the junction
of middle and lower thirds, two years before. He had twice repeated the fracture by slight falls. The ends were
now slightly movable on each other, and the arm was of little use. Three doses of Symph. 30c made a perfect
cure and the boy became robust and much better in health than he had ever been before.
Wells also recorded the case of a boy, 8, with a fractured humerus near the junction of condyles and shaft.
Arn. 30c immediately arrested the spasmodic jerks of muscles of the injured arm. Arn. was continued three
days, by which time all traumatic fever had subsided. Symph. 3c was given, one drop in half a tumbler of water,
a teaspoonful morning and evening. The splints were removed the ninth day and the bone was found to be
consolidated. The cure was entirely without pain.
F. H. Brett cured himself of inguinal rupture by rubbing the part with tincture of the root. On another occasion,
a blow on the lower part of the back from a fall resulted in a secondary affection of the spine in the mid-dorsal
region, a protuberance as if from a light dislocation appearing at the spot. Again Symph. was applied. The
tenderness at the point subsided after three applications, and in a few days the protuberance disappeared.
Brett mentioned a case he had heard of a diseased arm that had begun to mortify. It was dressed with a
poultice of comfrey root and this “drew off the mortified substance. The arm became sound again.”
Cooper noted that one patient, just before her marriage, had a dangerous attack of scarlatina, leaving
abscesses on both sides
of the neck and great internal swelling, so that she could swallow only liquids and those with great difficulty.
The external swelling extended from ear to chin and was hard and very painful. Poultices of comfrey root were
applied. The pain was immediately relieved and her abscesses decreased rapidly until they were entirely
absorbed without external opening so far as the patient could remark.
For bone tumors, osteomyelitis, bone ulcers. Sarcomas. Bone cancers of the jaw or bones (Hecla.). Bone
cancer, even if there is no bone injury (Calc-p., Hecla.). Non-union of fractures. Broken bones that don’theal
well. Acutely for osteoporosis, or osteogenesis imperfecta (Calc., or Calc-p. chronically). Stump pain after
amputation of a limb (Hyper., All-c., Coff., Calen.), strong aching pains.
Spinal diseases after trauma and injury. Injuries that result in a lump or tumor. For swellings, nodules and
tumors in bones and limbs after an injury (Bell-p. and Con. after injury to soft tissue). Tailbone injuries (Arn.,
Hyper.), with an aching pains.
 Blows to the eyes (Led., Arn.). Corneal abrasions. Hernias (Nux-v., Calc., Lyc.). As a compress for mastitis. In
tincture for stomach ulcers.
RELATIONS - Antidote to: Canth. Compare: (1) Arn., Bry., Calc-p. - fractures. (2) injuries, Arn., soft parts,
Symph., hard, Arn., sore, bruised lame, Symph., pricking, stitching jagging pains. (3) Calen., Fl-ac., Hep., Sil.,
Staph., Led., Rhus-t., Hyper. (4) Effects of sexual excess, Am. (5) Calc., Calc-f. Follows well: Am. - for pricking
pains and after the bmising of the soft parts is healed.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Syphilinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - syph. Syphilinum. Syphilis nosode. Luesinum. Lueticum. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Alcoholism. Anus, fissures. Aphasia. Asthma. Baldness. Bone, disorders. Breasts,
sensitive. Bubo. Cachexia. Cancer, Chancres. Constipation. Deafness. Debility. Deltoid rheumatism.
Dentition. Diplopia. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy. Hair, loss. Headache, syphilitic. Hoarseness. Hodgkin’s
disease. Insomnia. Iritis. Leucorrhea. Mouth, ulcers. Myopia. Nerve, disorders. Neuralgia. Night-sweats.
Ophthalmia. Otorrhea. Ovaries, disorders. Ozaena. Pains, severe. Paralysis. Pemphigus. Prostration.
Psoas, abscess. Ptosis. Rectum, stricture. Rheumatism. Sciatic pain. Sleeplessness. Spine, decay.
Strabismus. Strictures. Sunstroke. Syphilis. Teeth, decay. Throat, ulcerated. Tibia, pains. Tongue, cracked.
Tongue, ulcerated. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Whitlow.
HOMEOPATHIC - The syphilis nosode is mainly used on the general symptomatology with the family and
personal history of the patient. Its nightly aggravation of complaints, with extreme mental and physical
restlessness, together with its intense irritability, are striking indications for its use.
It’s frequently used to great advantage as an intercurrent remedy in the course of treatment in chronic disease,
prior to or following the apparently indicated remedy when the patient’s response to that remedy is feebly or
nil.
Syph. has been used in cancer, tuberculosis, severe types of neuro-arthritis, mental disturbances or various
forms of paralysis. Syphilitic disorders. Especially useful when there is hereditary tendency to alcoholism or
a syphilitic miasm.
Affects the nerves, mucus membranes and bones. Utter prostration and debility in the morning. Great
weakness with very few symptoms.
Shifting rheumatic pains. Chronic eruptions and rheumatism. Persistent pains in
Syphilinum any part of the body. Cold pains. Pains from darkness to daylight, decrease and increase
gradually. Violent or linear pains. Knots in muscles. Pains in bones. Bones, sore, decay, curvature. Exostoses.
Ulceration of mouth, nose, genitals, skin. Stubborn ulcerations. Succession of abscesses. Fetid
discharges, foul or green pus. Foul odor of the body. Ichthyosis Slowly advancing hemiplegia. Glands enlarged.
Hodgkin's disease. Epilepsy, worse after menses. As of hot water in blood vessels.
Crying infants, who begin crying immediately after birth. Dwarfed, shriveled up, old looking babies and
children, bald head, pouting lips and big belly.
MIND - Loss of memory, but remembers everything previous to his disease. Difficulty in making arithmetical
calculations.
Apathetic. Severe insomnia and suicidal depression (Aur.), especially during extreme attacks of pain. Sad and
lamenting. Antisocial, aversion to company. Cross, irritable, peevish. Does not want to be soothed.
Anxiety about health. Great restlessness and paces the floor at night. Hopelessness. Despair of recovery.
Fear of suffering and pains. Desperate, can’t take the pain or suffering anymore. Fear of dying. Fears the
night. Fears from exhaustion.
Very nervous. Fastidious. Fear of germs, of catching an infection. Always washing or wringing the hands.
Causeless weeping. Laughs or weeps without cause. Nightly delirium. Senile dementia. Feels as if going
insane or being paralyzed. Insanity, syphilitic insanity.
Abdomen - Pain or distress deep in abdomen as if in omentum. Feeling of heat internally in hypogastric region.
Pain in right groin followed by swelling of glands. Large, painless bubo in right groin, opened and discharged
freely.
Back - Neck feels short. Pain at coccyx with sensation as if it is swollen, worse sitting. Pain in the back in the
region of kidney, worse after urinating.
Breasts - Sensitive to touch, feel sore during menses and other times.
Causations - Sun. Syphilis. Damp weather, thunderstorms.
Chest - Soreness of chest. Rattling in chest and throat. Oppression of chest to such an extent as almost to
arrest breathing. Sensation of pressure under upper part of sternum.
 Constitutions - Syphilitic.
Ears - Deafness without any obvious cause, nervous with cachexia. Abscess of the middle ear. Calcareous
deposit on tympanum. Decay of ossicles in ear, of syphilitic origin.
Eyes - Ophthalmia, neonatorum. Tubercular iritis. Amaurosis, atrophy of optic nerve. Spots on cornea.
Chronic, recurrent, inflammation of cornea. Successive crops ofphyctenules and abrasions of epithelial
layer of cornea. Intense pain at night. Feeling of cold air blowing on eye (Fl-ac.). Photophobia and profuse
lachrymation. Glimmering vision. Diplopia. Vertical diplopia. Squints. Ptosis. Lids swollen, especially upper
eyelids. Eyelids glued together.
Face - Pale, wrinkled, old looking. Pain over eyes (right) worse protruding tongue. Paralysis of one side with
difficult speech, mastication and twitching of eyes, lids. Twitching of muscles.
Female - Menses, with putrid meat-like odor. Leucorrhea profuse, thin, watery, acrid with sharp, knife-like
pain in ovaries. Yellow, offensive, acrid leucorrhea, so profuse it soaks through napkins and runs to the heels,
with itching of the genitals. Ulcers on labia. Ulcers on the vulva with ovarian pain, sensitive to touch. Cutting
pain in ovary during sex, at the moment of orgasm. Habitual abortion.
Food - Capricious appetite. No food agrees or satisfies him. Total loss of appetite for months. Craves
alcoholic drinks. Aversion to meat.
Head - Stupefying headaches. Pain in bones of head. Deep, crushing headpains across the base of
temples. Linear pains from temples across, or from eyes backward, cause sleeplessness and delirium at night.
Beats head against the wall. Feels pulled back. Top of head feels as if coming off. Cerebral softening. Falling
of the hair. Tubercles all over the scalp.
Heart - Large, soft pulse. Valvular disease of heart. Sharp pains in heart from base to apex (Med. has reverse),
at night. As if hot water flowing in the veins.
Kidneys - Urine frothy, scanty, yellow. Urinates only once a day, but profuse. Passes urine better while
standing. Nocturnal bedwetting.
Limbs - Muscles contracted in hard knots. Indolent ulcers. Sciatica, worse at night, better about daybreak.
Bones pain as if sawed. Bilateral exostoses sore and painful. Osteo-sarcoma in center of tibia. Cold pain in
legs. Shin bones painful, better pouring cold water on them. Soles painful with feeling of contraction, worse
standing on them. Cannot sit on low chair or squat. Redness and rawness between toes (Sil.). Rheumatism of
shoulder j oint, at insertion of deltoid, worse from raising arm laterally or in front. Itching eruptions about elbows.
Affections of middle fingers. Always washing the hands.
Lungs - Asthma with wheezing and rattling (Ant-t.). Chronic asthma, worse in summer, during thunderstorms,
at night, humid weather. Dry cough, worse lying on right side, worse at night, windpipe sensitive to touch
(Lach.). Sharp pains from base of heart to apex at night.
Male - Nodular formation in testes, spermatic cord and scrotum. Chancres. Aching of genitals, cannot sit still.
Modalities - Better inland, mountains, high altitude. Better during day, from applied heat. Better continued or
slow motion. Better changing positions. Worse at night, from sundown to sunrise. Worse full moon. Worse
damp, thunderstorms. Worse extreme heat or cold, winter, summer. Worse at the seashore. Worse in any
position, squatting. Worse motion, raising arms laterally. Worse protruding tongue.
Mouth - Excessive flow of saliva, it runs out of mouth when sleeping. Putrid taste, before epileptic fit.
Ulcers, smart and burn. Tongue, coated, indented, deep longitudinal cracks along center. Paralysis of tongue.
Aphasia.
Nose - Decay of nasal bones, hard palate and septum with perforation. Ozaena offensive, thick yellow-green
discharge. Attacks of fluent coryza. Snuffles. Green lumps from posterior sinuses. Sinuses, painful, from
inhaled air. Saddle across the bridge of the nose (Sep.). Itching nostrils.
Perspiration - Perspires at night, with exhaustion. Sweats at night, most marked between scapulae and down
to waist. Peculiar disagreeable odor from body.
Rectum - Fissures in anus and rectum, prolapsed. Feels tied up with strictures. Obstinate constipation.
Diarrhea, bilious, painless worse seashore, drives her out of bed about 5 a.m. Water from enema escapes,
with pain.
Sensations - A seething feeling as if hot water or hot oil running through all veins of the body, all night long.
A far-away feeling with apathy. As if going insane or about to be paralyzed. As if top of head were coming off.
As if teeth were loose. Tongue feels as if paralyzed. Fluttering as of something alive in teeth. As if throat tearing
to pieces. As of a nervous chill commencing in anus and running down legs. Palms and soles as if pricked by
needles. As if bitten by bugs.
Skin - Extreme emaciation. Reddish-brown eruption with a disagreeable odor. Swollen and blotched. Biting as
from bugs. Wandering erysipelas. Conical crusts. Bullae. White or pockmark scars. Coppery spots. Distorted
nails.
 Sleep - Sleeplessness. Great restlessness at night, impossible to keep leg in one position. Wakes soon after
midnight and cannot sleep again until 6 a.m.
Stomach - Nausea. Vomiting for weeks or months due to erosion from superficial ulceration of lining of viscous.
Heartburn with pain and rawness from stomach to throat pit, often with cough.
Temperature - Chilly. Nervous chills preceded by pains in head. Fever dry, hot, shortly after going to bed,
parted lips, great thirst. Sweats at night with exhaustion.
Throat - Aphonia before the menses. Continuous pain in the larynx, worse touch. Sore, right to left, worse cold
drinks. Chronic hypertrophy of tonsils with
syphilitic taint.
Teeth - Teeth feel sticky, as of a worm in. Feeling as if teeth had all got out of place. Teeth decay at the edge
of gums. Toothache better pressing them together, worse hot or cold things. Teeth cupped in children.
Vertigo - Vertigo on looking up, seems to be caused by heat.
COMMENTS - Syph. is useful for ailments since syphilis, or a history of syphilis in the family. Pains get worse
or better gradually, are shifting and require frequent change of position. Unbearable pains (Aur.). Linear pain.
Ulcers and bone pains (Merc.).
Characteristic aggravated by night, pains from darkness to daylight, begin with twilight and end with daylight.
All symptoms are worse at night. Terrible dread of night, because of mental and physical exhaustion on waking.
Neuralgia and headache, asthma, coughs worse from sunset to sunrise, whether syphilitic or not.
Sleeplessness (Sulph.).
Epilepsy. Parkinson’s disease. Facial paralysis. Hemiplegia, “persistent pains in any part of the body.” Neurotic
behavior, especially wringing and washing of the hands. AIDS, dementia, sleeplessness, anxiety, fear of
infection, and neurotic behavior.
Ulceration, affecting the mouth, nose, genitals or skin. Ulcers have grayish bases. Abscesses with foul
secretions. Fetid pus formations. Succession of abscesses. Eruptions with copper-colored spots. Pemphigus.
Ozaena with discharge of fetid clinkers. Catarrhal and nerve deafness. Itching of nostrils. Fetid discharges
from the ear. Alopecia universalis. Dark purple lines between alae nasi and cheeks. Itching, scabby eruptions
on face or breast, singly or in clusters, looking like herpes. Pain and pressure behind sternum.
Ophthalmia neonatorum, the lids adhere during sleep, pains worse 2 to 5 a.m., profuse pus, better cold bathing.
Iritis, syphilitic or rheumatic. Diplopia, one image seen below the other. Ptosis, sleepy look from drooping lids.
Teeth decay at the edge of the gums and break off. Cupped teeth, serrated edges, dwarfed in size and
converge at their tips. Deformities of the teeth. The teeth come in rotten and deformed (Calc-f., Kreos.).
Paralysis of tongue. Aphasia.
Craving for alcohol in any form. Hereditary tendency to alcoholism. Impaired nutrition, emaciation. Burnett
recorded many instances of Syph. helping stunted children. Progeria. Babies that never stop crying and
screaming ever since they were born (Jal., Aeon.).
Leucorrhea, profuse, soaking through napkins and running to heels. Rectal pain. “Obstinate constipation for
years, rectum seems tied up with strictures, when enema was used the agony of passage was like labor.”
H. C. Allen said “Syphilitics or patients who have had chancre treated by local means and as a result have
suffered from throat and skin troubles for years, are nearly benefited by this remedy at commencement of
treatment unless some other remedy is clearly indicated.”
; Thomas Wildes noted that, in his experience with Syph., the chancre increases for the first two weeks and
then gradually fades away, not being followed by secondaries.
Wildes cured a bookkeeper who, for many months, had a piercing, pressing, excruciating headache over his
right eye extending deep into his brain. It was so severe, he was losing continuity of thought and memory.
Under Syph. 1,000c every night, the headache disappeared entirely in ten days and his mental faculties were
fully restored. But in six weeks the whole eyebrow on that side broke out into a sickly, yellow, syphilitic eczema
with a red, angry and oozing base extending under the arch to the lid, from canthus to canthus, up into forehead
and down the side of the nose.
The cure of this was tedious; Wildes attributed it to his change of remedy instead of continuing with Syph. This
man had syphilis a few years before.
In 1879 a woman, 26, extremely bright and intelligent, came to Wildes with a dreadful
Syphilinum ozaena. She also had a spinal curvature and congestion of right ovary. She had always been
delicate.
Syph. cured the ozaena and improved her health, but it “drove out a saddle to which the Sepia saddle is but a
shadow.” A furious inflammatory mass of syphilitic sores, scabs and eczema, red and angry with a fiery base
extending from one malar prominence to the other, across nose up to eyes and forehead. This took eighteen
months to cure. The ozaena never returned.
 A boy, age 4, had an obstinate rash, a combination of prurigo and herpes, on his chin, lips, cheekbone,
forehead and hairy scalp, on arms, chest, back, bends of joints and on the joints and on fingers and hands,
nowhere profuse. In spite of authorities to the contrary, Wildes maintained that syphilitic rashes may itch and
that prurigo is infectious and is one of the initial stages of leprosy.
This boy had a spot of eruption on the left thigh the size of the top joint of a man’s thumb. This was distinctly
a leper spot. Syph. 1,000c caused the rash to come out strongly all over the body in patches, the face was
one-third covered with a thick, yellow, scabby eruption. The remedy was continued and the boy got well,
wonderfully improved in health, was no longer nervous, grew well, slept well, with good appetite.
A girl, 16, had measles a year before which did not come out properly. A year and a half prior she was subject
to neuralgic headaches. She had been ailing about two years, very despondent, wanted to die, headaches
growing more violent.
During the headaches, the temple veins stood out, had pains all over the body, was very irritable, restless,
walked about much of the time, did not wish to be soothed, violent on being opposed, had tremors and seemed
on the verge of convulsions, dazed, absentminded and almost insane. Always washed her hands. She was
formerly constipated, but now subject to “a kind of diarrhea.”
Menses never came on properly and for the past year had been very irregular, much delayed, scanty and
always extremely painful. Often feverish. Anxious sleep, distressed and often wakeful and violently restless.
The symptoms indicated Syph. and under this she steadily recovered.
A young woman contracted “leprosysyphilis” from vaccination. She had ablood- boil on her arm that would not
heal. Face broken out with a fiery rash. With Syph. 1,000c at bedtime she recovered rapidly. The arm healed
quickly and her face became free from eruption.
A boy, 3, had a cluster of yellow blotches on his fingers and roots of nails, distorting the nails. The boy ’ s father
was epileptic. The boy was helped with Fl-ac. and cured with Syph., the nails became straight.
G.    H. Carr related the case of an old man who had been troubled for two or three winters with an intense
cold pain in both legs. It came on every night on lying down and lasted all night, the only relief was from getting
up and walking.
Magnetic leggings had given the most relief. Syph. 1,000c, one dose daily, was given. He lost the pain for six
weeks, when it returned in milder form. Syph. 100,000C was given and he had no more pains all the winter.
The medicine, he said “made his genitals ache so that he couldn’t sit still.” This lasted over a month.
Syph. 100,000c cured a woman of “asthma” that she had for twenty-five years, the attack coming on only at
night after lying down or during a thunderstorm.
Swan said he gave crying infants one dose of Syph. 100,000c, when they developed the propensity
immediately after birth and did not cease, and it was difficult to make them cry after that.
Yingling reported the case of Rev. D., 30, who was dark and free from venereal disease. Haggard look. He
had a constant dull, heavy ache above inner angle of right eye, very distressing with an occasional thrust as
of an iron rod from the same spot through to lower part of occiput. This thrust was excruciating.
He was due to preach the next day, but the pain quite incapacitated him, which led him to appeal for help.
Syph. 100,000c, one dose,
was given. He was free from pain before he reached home, and was perfectly well the next morning.
RELATIONS-Compare: (l)Merc„ Kali-hp., Nit-ac., Aur., Alum.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Syzygium Aromaticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - eug-c. Syzygium aromaticum. Clove oil. Eugeniacaryophallata. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Asthma. Bronchitis. Rheumatism. Sprains. Strains. Toothache.
HERBAL - The clove plant originated in the lowlands, valleys, and hillsides of the southern Philippine islands.
The essential clove oil, the most popular clove product, is extracted from the flower of the clove.
 Clove oil constituents include eugenol, eugenyl acetate, caryophyllene and iocaryophyllene.
Clove oil is used in connection with respiratory ailments such as asthma and bronchitis, muscle aches, sprains
and strains, arthritis and rheumatism. Many individuals use clove oil for its analgesic effects for body pain.
Clove oil is considered by many to be an effective antibiotic, antiseptic, antiviral, analgesic, antioxidant,
carminative, expectorant, antifungal, anti-parasitic, spasmodic, and stimulant.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Syzygium Jambolanum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - syzyg. Syzygiumjambolanum. Jambol seeds. Syzygium cumini. Eugenia jambolana. Jumbul.
N. O. Myrtacae. India. Trituration of the seeds. Tincture of the powdered fruit-stones. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Diabetes. Glycosuria. Pimples. Prickly heat. Ulcers.
HERBAL - Syzygiumjambolanum is a native of India. It has an edible fruit, the powdered stones of which have
a popular use in India as a remedy for diabetes. Syzyg. has an immediate effect of increasing the blood sugar,
glycosuriaresults. The dose is five to ten grains of the powdered stones three times a day, also, the tincture.
HOMEOPATHIC - Syzyg. is a most useful remedy in diabetes mellitus. Dudgeon used Syzyg. in the lower
homeopathic potencies with marked success, which has been repeated by many others.
Diminution and disappearance of sugar in the urine. Great thirst, weakness, emaciation. Very large
amounts of urine, specific gravity high. Prickly heat in upper part of the body, small red pimples itch violently.
Hansen mentioned “old ulcers of skin, probably of a diabetic foundation” as having been cured with Syzyg.
COMMENTS - Dudgeon related the case of a scientific man, 56, who complained of “prickly heat” all over
upper part of body and arms. The skin was covered with small, red papules, which itched so intensely he could
get no rest.
There was much thirst and great flow of urine, which he was obliged to pass every two hours, night and day,
mouth very dry. Urine 1036, very saccharine.
Syzyg. tincture, mixed with three times the quantity of alcohol, was given of this two drops every three hours.
The specific gravity of the urine steadily declined, sugar disappeared and all the symptoms passed off. This in
spite of the fact that the dietetic rules were relaxed.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Insulin. - an aqueous solution of an active principle from pancreas which affects
sugar metabolism. If administered at suitable intervals in diabetes mellitus, the blood sugar is maintained at a
normal level and the urine remains free of sugar. Overdosage is followed by weakness and fatigue and
tremulousness and profuse sweating.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Tabacum Fumus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tab-fum. Tabacum fumus. Tobacco smoke. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Asthma. Bronchitis. Coughs. Lung, disorders. Tobacco, addiction.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tab-fiim. is made by blowing cigarette smoke into a bottle of water, which is then mixed
and potentized. A homeopathic proving of Tab-fum. was done by Chachanidze. It has been used to reduce
the cravings for smoking of cigarettes. Allergies to cigarette smoke, headaches and irritability from smell of
tobacco. Asthma in cigarette smokers.
MIND - Concentration difficult during study. Anxiety, which comes from the heart. Anticipation as if something
bad will happen. Irritability in the crowd, desire to escape. Dullness. Indifference to habitual deeds. Sensation
as if one has a disease of throat (fixed idea).
Eyes - Burning, itching and lachrymation, worse in the right eye.
Face - Aching of the left upper jaw-bone in the morning after awaking, as if it is toothache. It is extending to
the left eye- socket and left side of the nose bone, lasts whole day. Pain goes to the forehead and nose in the
evening.
Head - Sensation of emptiness in the right half of the head with the nausea. Dull pain in the head. Headache,
aggravation from the sun. Heaviness in the occiput, more in the left side, began in the morning awaking after.
Heaviness of the whole head. Sensation as if head is bursting. As if all bones of the scull are aching, especially
along the sutures. Nausea and emptiness in the head. Amelioration from the stool.
Lungs - Shortness of breath even after slight physical exertion, worse ascending stairs. Hoarseness, burning
of throat and weakness of voice. Dry cough, as if would choke.
Mouth - Tickling. Heat in the mouth, as if hot air go out from mouth. Sensation that mouth is dirty. Desire to
 clean teeth. Sensation of loosening of teeth with bitter saliva. Salivation. Pressure of parotid glands as if after
sour lemon. Desire to make massage with tongue of gums. As if toothache in upper incisors. Ache in the root
of the tooth of upper jaw-bone. Sensation as if teeth are unnecessary. Desire to rub gums and teeth. Pain like
from little nail. Stretching pain in the right submaxillary region. Sensation of swelling of the inner cheek. Little
white ulcer on inner cheek.
Nose - Sensation of smell of smoke. Stuffed-up nose, amelioration in open air. Discharge of mucus to the
postnasal region.
Sensations - Sensation as if faint, as if body is like cotton wool.
Sleep - Drowsy from 7 to 8 p.m. Dreams of heavy shower, rain, flood, dirty water. Dreams of being dirty, desire
to take a shower.
Stomach - Hunger, burning in stomach as if hot water is pouring, in the morning. Increased appetite with
impatience. Hunger after eating. Desire chocolate.
Tongue - Sensation of coating at the root of the tongue. Tickling and itching of tongue. Pricking in tip of tongue.
As if beating of electricity to the tip op of tongue. Dryness, burning of tongue. Shooting pain in the root of
tongue extending to the right Eustachian tube and to the right ear.
Throat - Sensation of coating at the throat and at the postnasal region. Numbness of posterior part of gullet
and of throat and hoarseness. Sensation feel like tissues are hanging from the gullet. Sensation as if ulcers
on gullet.
Vertigo - Sensation of vertigo, as if falling to the right. Vertigo with palpitations during walking.
REFERENCES - Chachanidze. Murphy.

name: Tabacum Nicotiana
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tab. Tabacum nicotiana. Tobacco. Nicotiana tabacum. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of the fresh
leaves collected before the flowers are developed. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Anemia. Angina, pectoris. Anus, prolapse. Asthma. Backaches. Brain, anemia. Brain-
fag. Catalepsy. Cholera. Cholera, infantum. Color-blindness. Constipation. Diarrhea. Epilepsy. Esophagus,
stricture. Fainting. Freckles. Giddiness. Glands, enlarged. Heartbeats, disorders. Heartburn. Hernia.
Hiccough. Idiocy. Itching. Legjerking. Lip, cancer. Lung, disorders. Masturbation, effects. Ménière’s disease.
Morning sickness. Motion, sickness. Nausea. Optic, neuritis. Pregnancy, disorders. Prostatorrhea. Rectum,
paralysis. Seasickness. Speech, disorders. Strabismus. Strokes. Tetanus. Toothache. Varicocele. Vertigo.
Vomiting.
HERBAL - When Columbus and his followers landed in Cuba in 1492, the practice of smoking tobacco was in
common use among the natives throughout the island and also throughout the continent of America. On their
return to Spain, the practice rapidly spread throughout the Peninsula.
Nicotiana tabacum received its specific name from Jean Nicot, the French ambassador to Portugal, who was
the means of introducing the tobacco plant into France about 1560.
Sir Walter Raleigh and his companions introduced the practice into England in 1586. From that time, the
cultivation, manufacture and use of tobacco, either by smoking, snuffing or chewing, rapidly became popular.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tab. has nausea, giddiness, deathly sinking, vomiting, icy coldness and sweat, with
intermittent pulse. Complete prostration of the entire muscular system. Collapse. Seasickness.
Marked anti-septic qualities, antidotal to cholera germs. Cholera infantum, cold, but wants abdomen
uncovered. Vigorous peristaltic activity. Diarrhea.
Produces high tension and arteriosclerosis of the coronary arteries. Angina pectoris with coronary sclerosis
and high tension. Constriction of throat, chest, bladder and rectum. Pallor, breathlessness, hard cord-like
pulse. Vagus, sympathetic, cerebro-spinal nerves and heart are prominently affected.
Complete prostration and relaxation of the entire muscular system with free secretions, vomiting, profuse
sweat, lachrymation, salivation etc. Constriction of the muscles of hollow organs, throat, bladder, rectum, chest
etc. Cramps, then paralysis of bowels, heart etc. Convulsions, head firmly drawn back. Jerking throughout the
body. Trembling.
Pains are worse from heat. Excessive emaciation, especially of the muscles of back and cheeks. Gait slow
and shuffling, unsteady, difficulty in ascending stairs. Faintness. Tetanus. Paralysis of sphincters. Slides in
bed. Coughing causes hiccough, stitches in pit of stomach. Symptoms come in paroxysms, are periodical.
Gastralgia, enteralgia.
MIND - Mental confusion and fatigue. Confusion from motion. Brain fag. Idiotic, epileptic idiocy. Slow
perception. Forgetful. Indifferent. Desire for company in evening and at night.
Morose, sensation of extreme wretchedness. Feels wretched during menopause period and menses. Feels
 very despondent. Discontented. Apathetic, indifferent. Sadness is better after complaining. Sadness with
impeded respiration. Weeping ameliorates symptoms. Suicidal disposition but lacks courage.
Nervous and restlessness. Anguish when walking in open air. Sudden anxiety, with angina pectoris or
oppression of chest, driving him from place to place. Anxiety from thinking about it. Anxiety better after crying.
Anxiety at night. Fear after eating food. Fear from noises.
Cheerful, merry and talkative. Sings all day. Silly talk. Talks nonsense. Talks to himself. Delusions, preventing
sleep. Feels as if someone were coming to arrest him or murder him. Doesn’ t recognize his relatives.
Unconsciousness, as in a trance, better when
cold water poured over head.
Abdomen - Coldness in abdomen. Wants abdomen uncovered, it lessens the nausea and vomiting. Sinking
feeling in epigastrium with dreadful faint sense. Retraction of navel, abdominal muscles contracted. Violent
burning in abdomen, extorting cries. Painful distentions. Intestinal obstruction. Incarcerated hernia.
Strangulated hernia. Gurgling in bowels. Horrible colic, must shriek, with weakness. Colic during stool.
Back - Emaciation of the muscles of back. Pain in the small of back worse lying, better while walking. Heat
down spine. Throbbing in sacral region. Red eruption on back. Pustules on nape and upper limbs. Violent pain,
in lumbar region. Neck stiff. Neuralgia of neck, with tightness of throat. Head drawn back in convulsions.
Causations - Effects of sunstroke. Bee-sings and mosquito bites.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Tightness of chest, better inspiration. Violent constriction of chest. Oppression of the
chest with anguish. Pain radiates from the center of sternum. Sticking under sternum with inability to take a
deep breath. Nocturnal attacks of tightness across chest. Tuberculosis is said to make less rapid progress
among tobacco workers.
Cough - Cough dry, teasing, must take a swallow of cold water (Caust., Phos.). Cough followed by hiccough.
Cough and hiccough at the same time. Suffocative cough from irritation in throat and larynx, worse at night.
Dry cough, cardiac in origin. Coughing causes stitches in pit of stomach.
Ears - Burning heat and redness of the ears. Hyperesthesia to music and loud talking. Hearing music causes
pain in the ears. Ménière’s disease with feeling of seasickness. Sensation as if ears were closed. Nerve
deafness.
Eyes - Sunken eyes, blue around them. Heat and burning in eyes. Pupils dilated. Retina retains the image too
long. Eyeballs injected, cornea covered with mucus, must wipe it off. Contraction of eyelids. Strabismus.
Face - Emaciation of face. Deathly pale, blue, pinched, sunken, collapsed, covered with cold sweat (Ars.,
Verat.). One cheek hot and glowing, other pale. Freckles. Miliary rash on cheeks. Violent tearing in facial bones
and teeth, worse evening. Pain in maxillary joint, worse laughing. Spasms of the lower jaw.
Female - Retarded and profuse menses. Leucorrhea of serous fluid, worse after menses. During menopause
and menses, subjective coldness, epigastric sinking, palpitation, slight diarrhea, muscular relaxation.
Excessive sense of wretchedness during menopausal period and menses. Morning sickness of pregnancy,
nausea and vomiting, patient dreads least movement. Severe itching of the whole body during pregnancy.
Food -. Thirstlessness. Great thirst, worse at night, in cholera infantum. Complete loss of appetite. Constant
hunger, nausea if stomach is not satisfied. Incessant nausea, worse smell of tobacco smoke. Desires sweets,
ice cream, salt. Immoderate smoking of cigars causes vertigo.
Head - Head drawn back in convulsions. Sick headache with deathly nausea. Periodical headache from
fatigue or excitement. Headache better in the open air. Headache with nausea and vertigo. Tight feeling as
from a band. Heaviness sensation with heat of head, better open air. Sensation as if head would burst, or as
if brain were being bored out. Sudden pain as if struck by a hammer, worse while passing urine. Hair falls out.
Secretion from eyes, nose and mouth increased.
Heart - Angina pectoris, pain in precordial region. Angina pectoris with nausea, cold sweat and collapse.
Shooting pain from heart down left arm or up into neck. Pain radiates from center of sternum. Bradycardia.
Tachycardia. Acute dilatation of heart caused by shock or violent physical exertion. Twisting about the heart.
Unsteady heartbeat. Precordial oppression with palpitations and pain between shoulders. Violent beating of
heart and carotids. Violent palpitations, worse lying on left side (Phos.). Palpitations due to tobacco. Pulse
rapid and small. Pulse thready, intermittent, hard, cord like, imperceptible.
Kidneys - Kidney pain with cold sweat, deathly nausea. Kidney colic, violent pain along ureter, left side. Renal
region sensitive to pressure. Paralysis of sphincters, urine dribbles. Enuresis. Urine increased, or scanty high-
colored urine. Urine yellowish-red with increased secretion. Inflammation of the orifice of the urethra.
Bedwetting.
Limbs - Formication. Feebleness of arms. Fingertips fuzzy. Cramps in single fingers, worse washing. Legs
and hands icy cold, limbs tremble. Paralysis following a stroke (Plb.). Cramps in legs. Gait shuffling, unsteady.
Can’t walk with angina pectoris. Tremor and disabling weakness of feet.
 Liver - Stitches in liver. Pressure in liver region as from a heavy body. Hepatic region sensitive to pressure.
Lungs - Difficult, violent constriction of chest. Dyspnea with tingling down left arm when lying on left side.
Difficult breathing, worse ascending, with distress in heart and palpitations. Paroxysms of suffocation. Hurried,
anxious, irregular breathing. Inability to take a deep breath, from sticking under sternum. Periodical attacks of
asthma, sits up in bed, suffering with extreme dyspnea. Asthma with blueness of face and swelling of jugular
veins.
Male - Frequent erections. Nocturnal emissions. Impotency. Genital organs flabby, no erections or little sexual
desire. Masturbation and its consequences. Discharge of prostatic fluid. Hyperesthesia and neuralgia of penis.
Varicocele.
Modalities - Better when uncovering abdomen. Better cold, open fresh air, cold applications. Better walking.
Better weeping, vomiting. Worse from motion of boat, riding in cars. Worse extremes of heat and cold, being
indoors. Worse stimulants. Worse motion, pressure. Worse in evening, rising up, opening eyes. Worse lying
on left side, causes palpitations. Music causes pains in ears.
Mouth - Profuse salivation. Salivation with burning in mouth and throat, tickling, dryness, rawness. Spits much
with other complaints. Frothing from the mouth. Mouth full of white tenacious mucus. Dryness of the mouth
and tongue with violent thirst. Tongue feels swollen. Swelling of glands under tongue. Drawling, monotonous
style of reading. Lips retracted. Lips cracked, swollen, covered with a brown crust. Speech difficult. Weak,
interrupted speech.
Nose - Burning sensation and tingling in the nose. Paroxysms of sneezing. Secretion increased. Dryness and
obstruction of nose. Nasal catarrh with crawling sensation in nostrils. Naso-pharyngitis and tracheitis.
Perspiration - Cold sweats. Sudden cold sweats with chill, angina pectoris, kidney colic etc. Perspiration at
night. Cold, clammy sweats at night on hands, forehead and face.
Rectum - Habitual constipation. Constipation with rectum paralyzed, prolapsed. Rectal tenesmus. Involuntary
stool, watery or thick curdled stools like sour milk. Sudden diarrhea, watery with nausea and vomiting,
prostration and cold sweat. Cholera infantum, warmth of body with icy-cold hands. Watery diarrhea, urgent,
painless in morning. Evacuations like cholera, with deathly faintness, cold skin, irregular pulse. Sudden,
papescent, yellow-green or greenish, slimy stools.
Sensations - As if struck by a hammer on right side of head. As if a band around head. As if brains were being
bored out. As if black dots filled visual field. As if ears were closed. As of a plug in esophagus. As if throat
influenced by a hand. As if chest too tight. As if a crowbar were twisted around the heart. As if seasick. As if
stomach were relaxed.
Skin - Skin swollen, yellow, hot and dry. Itching over the whole body, as from flea or insect bites. Eruption of
itching pimples or vesicles with yellow serum and red areola. Red spots on face and on right shoulder, burning
when touched. Violent itching of whole surface. Dark, color of
skin. Vesicles containing yellow serum and surrounded by red areola. Cold skin in cholera, livid, with angina
pectoris. Jaundice.
Sleep - Drowsiness, better in open air. Urgent inclination to sleep, especially after a meal and towards evening
with frequent yawn- ings. Insomnia with dilated heart with cold, clammy skin and anxiety. Disturbed sleep at
night with fright. Nightmares. Stupefying sleep at night.
Smell - Diminished power of smell. Sensitive to smell of wine. Smell of tobacco, aggravates (Ign.). Patient
tormented by smell of tobacco.
Stomach - Coldness in stomach, with nausea. Shocks in stomach, at night while sleeping. Gastralgia, pain
from cardiac end extending to left arm. Frequent fluttering sensation in pit, with heartburn. Acidity. Burning in
stomach. Eructations, sour, hot, of small amounts of food, loud, noisy. Sense of relaxation of stomach with
nausea (Ip.). Terrible faint, sinking feeling in pit of stomach. Incessant nausea, worse smell of tobacco
smoke (Phos.). Deathly nausea and violent vomiting, worse least motion, better uncovering abdomen.
Seasickness, motion sickness. Morning sickness. Nausea during pregnancy, with much spitting.
Retching. Vomiting of fecal matter.
Temperature - Icy cold skin. Chills with cold sweat. Coldness and shivering, sometimes with chattering of
teeth. Chilliness after eating and drinking. Heat down spine, of one cheek, internal. Body warm, with icy
coldness of hands and legs.
Throat - Throat dry, can hardly swallow. Much viscid mucus in throat. Nasopharyngitis and tracheitis.
Hemming cough. Morning cough, sometimes with vomiting. Hoarseness of public speakers. Violent
constriction of throat in angina pectoris. Swallowing difficult on account of spasms of pharynx. Scraping in
larynx causes frequent hawking and coughing. Laryngismus stridulus.
Vertigo - Vertigo with seasickness. Excessive vertigo, with copious cold sweat, worse opening eyes. Vertigo
on open
 ing eyes, in sick headache with deathly nausea, periodical. Vertigo on rising or looking upward. Vertigo
with nausea, worse indoors, better open air. Vertigo and fainting, loss of consciousness. Vertigo followed
by vomiting of food and tremulous weakness. Ménière’s disease with feeling of seasickness.
Vision - Amaurosis. Muscae volitantes. Central scotoma. Retina retains image too long. Diplopia. Dim and
confused, as if black dots filled visual field. Sudden loss of vision without lesion, followed by atrophy of optic
nerve. Loss of sight on looking steadily at any white object. Strabismus. COMMENTS - M. E. Douglass, in the
Homeopathic News of 1897, wrote about the “medicinal uses” of tobacco and it seems that it was regarded as
a perfect panacea by the Virginians for diseases of men and cattle.
Douglass mentioned its palliative use for bee stings and mosquito bites. A portion of a leaf was moistened with
vinegar and applied to the part. Ip., one of the antidotes of Tab., has a similar reputation. Strong tobaccojuice
is the most effectual destroyer of the burrowing-flea, Chigoe.
Leaves of tobacco are moistened with vinegar or camphor solution and applied to the forehead and nape for
headaches. The pain is allayed and sleep induced. The local application over the pit of the stomach relieves
nausea.
Douglass used small doses of vinegar for the acute symptoms of nicotine poisoning, either chewing or
smoking, with excellent results. Nothing, he said, relieves the sensation of constriction of the esophagus as
quickly as vinegar. There is violent rectal tenesmus, paralysis, and prolapsed anus. The bladder sphincter is
paralyzed, debility of urine, and bedwetting. Cholera.
The power of Tab. to paralyze sphincters and morbid constrictions accounts for its traditional use in cases of
strangulated herriia and obstruction of the bowels. Kidney colic comes under the same heading. Impotency in
males, prostate discharges (Calad.), and constant dribbling of the urine.
The same pair of opposites, relaxation and constriction are seen in the weakness, paralysis, and convulsions.
All shades of nervous tremors, faintings, cramps, jerk- ings and restlessness. Tab. holds its place in society
by its power of antidoting such conditions. Intermittent heartbeats and arrhythmias, especially in elderly people.
Central nervous action that can lead to degeneration of nerve tissue, as seen in tobacco blindness. Amaurosis,
optic nerve degeneration following blindness (Phos.). Tab. also produces a condition like brainfag, an inability
to concentrate thoughts that may even go on to a state of idiocy. Silly talking in boys.
Profoundly influences nutrition, retards growth in children. Characteristic deathly, sinking nausea. It is no doubt
by virtue of this, acting homeopathically, that Tab. enables persons who cannot have proper meals endure
starvation better than they otherwise would.
Terrible faint, sinking feeling at pit of stomach. Pallor, coldness, icy cold surface, covered with cold sweat.
Motion sickness (Cocc.). Morning sickness with cold sweats, sinking nausea and dizziness. Violent vomiting,
as soon as he began to move, better on deck and in fresh air.
Keynote better by uncovering abdomen. Child wants abdomen uncovered, it helps the nausea and vomiting.
There may be a coldness of the abdomen at the same time. Skin affections with itching.
Teste cured with it several cases of freckles, he repeated the remedy and gave it for weeks at a time : “A
country girl had her face and hands covered with freckles, two-thirds of which disappeared completely [under
Tab.] in summer, the season in which they are most frequent and obstinate.”
Terry cured a case of seasickness, with heat along the spine from the nape down, cold sweat, then vomit. He
also cured a case of Meniere’s disease with a feeling as if seasick.
Boger cured, with Tab. 100,000c, a persistent backache, worse lying down, better walking, with a history of
anginalike attacks.
Burnett noted that an infusion of tobacco is a popular German remedy for scrofulous glands. Cooper gives as
an indication, “intermittent heart in old people.”
C. W. was troubled with spasm of lower jaw, worse outdoors. No remedy worked until he remained one evening
with two friends who were smoking and saturated himself with the smoke. That cured him. Slight subsequent
returns were always removed by Tab.
J. W. Scott observed a case of epileptiform convulsions brought on by tobacco. For five months the patient
had two attacks weekly and they grew worse in spite of treatment until the tobacco habit was discontinued.
RELATIONS - Antidote: Vinegar, sour apples. Camphor in the physiological antagonist. Compare: (1) Calad.,
Daph., Lob. and Plan. - cause aversion to tobacco. (2) Nicot. (3) Ars. - chewing tobacco. (4) Ign. - aversion to
tobacco smoke. (5) Sep. - neuralgia and dyspepsia), Lyc. impotency. (6) Nux-v. - bad taste due to tobacco. (7)
Phos. - tobacco heart, sexual weakness. (8) Hydrobr-ac., Camph., Verat., Ars.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Tabernanthe Iboga
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tab-ib. Tabernanthe iboga. Iboga bark. Black bugbane. Bitter grass. N. O. Apocynacae. Bark
and root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Addictions. Alcoholism. Delirium tremens. Drug, abuse. Fatigue. Heroin, habit. Tobacco, habit.
HERBAL - Tabernanthe iboga, also known as black bugbane, is a perennial rainforest shrub and hallucinogen,
native to western Africa. Iboga stimulates the central nervous system when taken in small doses and induces
visions in larger doses.
Ibogaine is the active chemical in the African root. It is a strong, long-lasting psychedelic used traditionally in
a coming of age ritual, but also known for its modern use in treating heroin addiction.
Tabernanthe iboga
The drug’s story as an anti-addictive began in 1962, when college dropout and heroin addict Howard Lotsof
obtained a dose from a chemist friend. Iboga relieved him of all cravings for heroin.
In 1986, Lotsof began to supply ibogaine to a clinic for addicts in Holland. The clinic found that ibogaine works
in three stages. First the addict has about four hours of waking dreams in which he seems to confront inner
demons.
This is followed by an eight- to 10-hour “cognitive evaluation period," during which the user analyzes the waking
dream. Then comes a sleepless day or two, which Lotsof calls the “residual stimulation phase.”
Lotsof said ibogaine allows addicts, especially heroin users, to put aside their fears of withdrawal and begin
the process of detoxification.
One methadone patient said that in just four days he reached a state that normally would have taken him three
months, but without the agony.
The heroin addiction therapy may last several days and upon completion the subject is generally no longer
physically dependent. Research suggests that ibogaine may also help to treat addictions to alcohol and
nicotine.
Ibogaine breaks down in the liver into a metabolite called nor-ibogaine. This metabolite has been shown in
clinical research to prevent cravings for several weeks after a single dose in some individuals.
Others have observed Iboga having some undesirable side effects regarding blood pressure and heartbeat.
COMMENTS - The Iboga was brought back from Gabon in 1864 by Dr. Griffon du Bel- lay, a navy surgeon.
He wrote, “The root of this plant is the part that the Gabonese eat. They say that it is inebriating, aphrodisiac,
and, with it, they claim that they feel no need for sleep.”
However, as early as 1885, Father Henri Neu had written in a manuscript entitled “Le Gabon” (Neu 1885),
“The natives use an infusion of iboga root scrapings as a potent philter that enables one to discover hidden
Tabernanthe iboga things and to tell the future. The one who drinks it falls into a deep sleep during which he
is obsessed by uninterrupted dreams which, until the time that he awakens, he takes to be actual events.”
REFERENCES - Lotsof. Murphy.

name: Tamarindus Indica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tama. Tamarindus indica. Tamarind. N.O. Leguminosae. Tamari- caceae. Africa. India. Tincture
of the fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acidity. Asthma. Boils. Constipation. Rheumatism. Spleen, disorders. Tobacco, habit.
HERBAL - People in India use tamarind as a souring agent like vinegar. It is used in common preparations
like chutneys. It is also eaten as a fruit by those who have a craving for sour things. Tamarind flavored
beverages are popular in Italy and Latin America.
Patients suffering from rheumatic problems are said to be aggravated from tamarind.
MIND - Indifference, apathy. Indolence. Lethargy, no desire to work, even if it is important and requires
immediate attention. Mental dullness, sluggishness. Difficulty thinking and comprehending. Forgetfulness.
Restlessness, nervousness. Starting easily. Fear of his own shadow. Fear of passing stool, on account of pain.
Irritability from trifles. Tolerance in persons normally easily annoyed and irritated. Quiet disposition. Involuntary
sighing. Weeping, tearful mood. Dreams of talking to deceased grandfather.
Back - Pain in one spot under right scapula, worse lying on back.
Eyes - Lachrymation, especially in left eye.
Food - Increase thirst. Desires ice-cold water, cold drinks, ice cream, tamarind, sour foods, spicy foods.
Craves tobacco. Worse from spicy foods and tobacco.
Head - Heaviness of head.
Modalities - Better drinking cold water, worse from spicy foods and tobacco. Worse morning. Worse from the
sun. Mouth - Dryness of mouth, lips and throat.
Stringy salvia.
 Nose - Obstruction of nose.
Rectum - Ineffectual urging with unsatisfactory stools. Constipation. Rectal pain worse passing stools, walking,
sitting, squatting.
COMMENTS - Vakil stated, “People consuming tobacco in any form, chewing or smoking, are especially
affected. Tamarindus may be useful to give up the habit of tobacco chewing or smoking. Provers addicted to
tobacco developed some unbearable symptoms of tobacco, e.g. vertigo. One prover who had stopped smoking
one year back, developed increased desire for smoking again and now he is not able to give it up.”
Joseph Miller, in Potter’s Cyclopedia, wrote about Tamarindus, “They are accounted specific for all disorders
of the Spleen, as being believed to lessen it much; nay they used to drink out of cups made of this wood to
cure those illnesses.”
RELATIONS - Compare: Phos., Ph-ac., Mangi, Sulph.
REFERENCES - Murphy. Vakil.
