name: Tamus Communis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tarn. Tamus communis. Ladies seal. Black bryony. Black bryonia. Blackeye root. Tamus crética.
N. O. Dioscoreaceae. Tincture of fresh root. Tincture of the berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Broken, bones. Bruises. Chilblains. Splinters.
HERBAL - The Greeks used the young suckers like asparagus, which they resemble.
Tamus is a popular remedy for removing discoloration caused by bruises. The fresh root is scraped and the
pulp rubbed into parts affected by gout, rheumatism, or paralysis. It is also reputed as a diuretic. The fruits
steeped in gin are a popular remedy for chilblains. The tincture also has a reputation for curing chilblains when
applied externally.
The root-plaster of Tamus has been used to removed scars and deformities and it softens harden tissues
(Thiosin.). It draws forth splinters and heals broken bones, dissolves congealed blood. If laid on hip or knuckles
or any other part where there is great pain, it takes away the pain speedily.
COMMENTS - Gerarde reported, “The root is very great and thick oftentimes as big as a man’s leg, black
without and very clammy or slimy within, which having been scraped with a knife, it seems to be a matter fit to
be spread upon cloth or leather in manner of a plaster of sear-cloth.”
Dioscorides, according to Gerarde, said the fruit or berries take away sun-burns and other blemishes of the
skin, and Gerarde added that these, “very quickly waste and consume away black and blue marks that come
of bruises and dry beatings: which thing also the roots perform being laid upon them.”
Joseph Miller stated, “A cataplasm of the root with vinegar and cow-dung, helps the gout” and he added
significantly, “It is but rarely used.”
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
keynote:
PHARMACY - tarn. Tamus communis. Ladies seal. Black bryony. Black bryonia. Blackeye root. Tamus crética.
N. O. Dioscoreaceae. Tincture of fresh root. Tincture of the berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Broken, bones. Bruises. Chilblains. Splinters.
HERBAL - The Greeks used the young suckers like asparagus, which they resemble.
Tamus is a popular remedy for removing discoloration caused by bruises. The fresh root is scraped and the
pulp rubbed into parts affected by g

name: Tanacetum Vulgare
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tanac. Tanacetum vulgare. Tansy. Chrysanthemum vulgare. N. O. Com- positae. Tincture of
the fresh plant in flower. Potencies of the oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abortion. Abscess. Amenorrhea. Chorea. Convulsions. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Epilepsy.
Eyes, inflamed. Eyes, sclerotica. Hallucinations. Hydrophobia. Labia, abscess. Menorrhagia. Paralysis. Poison
ivy. Strabismus. Worms.
HERBAL - The word “tansy” is derived from immortality with its deep-yellow button-like flowers, a close
companion of the Ragwort (Senecio facobea). In olden times puddings were made containing tansy leaves
and these puddings were called “tansies” also.
Gerarde also said that the seeds kill and expel worms of every sort, the root is good in gout, and being drunk
with wine relieves pain in the bladder and dysuria when a man is only able to urinate by drops.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hale noted it for amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia, uterine cramps and metritis. In
one instance it caused a large abscess of the labia majora. Hale said acrystalline acid identical with Santonin
has been isolated from it.
Abnormal lassitude, a nervous and tired feeling. “Half dead, half alive feeling” all over. It is of use in chorea
and reflex spasms due to worms. Tanac. is said to be a specific against effects of poison ivy.
Tanac. induces all the cardinal features of rabies, including abundant salivation, excitability, tendency to bite.
Hoarse cry. Hallucinations. Diminished sensibility and mobility, momentary paralysis. Frothy, bloody mucus in
the air passages. Convulsions, without loss of consciousness. Opisthotonos. Spasms of pharynx, larynx and
 the thorax.
MIND - Mental fatigue, nausea and vertigo, worse in a closed room. Inability to think coherently. Confusion of
thought. Dullness of all the senses. Fatigue of the mind after the least exertion. Ambitious. Wants to stand on
his head, stretches and draws up his feet, and says, “it does me good.”
Sadness, with desire to be let entirely alone. Irritable, sensitive to noise. Irritable and lazy. Very nervous and
low spirited, annoyed by trifles; noise of the children almost unbearable. Extremely sensitive to noise. Coma
and violent convulsions.
Abdomen - Dull pains in the right hypochondrium, sharp in left. Sharp, sticking pains in whole umbilical region.
Back - Severe attack of lumbago. Constant dull ache in loins.
Ears - Stitches in internal ear. Ears seem to close up suddenly. Roaring, ringing in ears. Her own voice
sounds strange in her ears.
Eyes - Eyes open, very brilliant, pupils equal, widely dilated, immovable. Pupils contracted. Sclerotic
congested, dark purple, glassy-looking. Dull aching in eyeballs. Slight inward squint, right eye. Lids
agglutinated in morning.
Face - Features seemed fixed, giving an expression of deep solemnity. Face dusky, flushed, cheeks bright
red. Fullness of head and face.
Female - Menses suppressed, later, profuse. Dysmenorrhea with bearing-down pains, tenderness, drawing in
groins. Miscarriage in the early months of pregnancy.
Head - Weariness in head. Heavy, dull, confused. Dull, frontal headache with cutting in temples. Headache
with least exertion.
Heart - Feeble heart-action and all signs of impending dissolution. Pulse increased in force and frequency,
feeble.
Kidneys - Constant desire. First suppression, then profuse flow. Marked diuresis, must rise in night to urinate.
Urine is very fetid, high-colored increased. Urine caused slight scalding.
Limbs - Numbness and sensation as though arms and legs were suddenly swelling. Prickling, coming and
going, over limbs and along spine with flashes of heat. Cold numbness over limbs, going on to paralysis.
Lungs - Breathing laborious. Hurried, stertorous respiration. Frothy mucus obstructs the air-passages.
Modalities - Worse at night, at 4 a.m. Suddenness is a characteristic of a number of the symptoms.
Mouth - Flat insipid taste. Tongue white coated, feels rough. Mouth, blood-stained, frothy.
Nose - Profuse secretion of mucus in nose with fluent coryza. Dryness of nostrils.
Rectum - Pain in bowels, relieved by stool. Dysentery. Desire for stool immediately after eating.
Sensations - As if something closed the ears very suddenly. His own voice sounds strange in his ears.
Sensation like a thrill all through body. As though arms and legs suddenly swollen.
Stomach - Thirst. Drawing, cutting pains in epigastrium. Faint and sick at stomach. Constant belchings, tasting
of the oil. Belchings of sour air at night. Nausea and vomiting.
Temperature - Surface cool and moist.
Cold, clammy sweat. Feeling of warmth diffused over whole abdomen.
Throat - Roughness of throat. Feeling in throat as if one could cough all the time. Unable to swallow.
COMMENTS - Like Senec., Tanac. has an action on the female generative organs and a large proportion of
the observations with it have been on women who have taken it to procure abortion. Other effects are from its
use as a vermifuge, and in addition to these are provings by Burt and others.
In Russia, Tanac. has a reputation as a remedy for hydrophobia. M. Peyraud even used Tanac. as a substitute
for Pasteurian “vaccinations,” and reported success.
W. H. Pierson observed a woman who took two drachms of the oil to procure abortion. The attempt failed, but
throughout her pregnancy she suffered from mixed tonic and clonic convulsions. Frothing at the mouth,
clenched hands, thumbs turned in, followed by exhaustion and a short coma. Since then, Pierson treated every
case of epilepsy which came to him with drop doses of the fluid extract of Tanac. four times a day, with marked
success.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In uterine symptoms, Sabin., Tereb., Hedeo., Ruta. (2) In convulsions, Stram.,
Cic., Cupr. (3) Worm symptoms, convulsions, paralysis, Sant., Cina, Chen-a. (4) Abscess on labium majus,
Stry., abscess of scrotum. Follows well: Cimic., Cina, Absin., Nux-v.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale.

name: Tanghinia Venenifera
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tang. Tanghinia venenífera. N. O. Apocynaceae. Trituration of the seed. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Anxiety. Debility. Delirium. Numbness. Paralysis. Stupor. Vomiting. Weakness.
 HERBAL - Tanghinia, the Tanghin or Tanquen of Madagascar is the only representative of its genus of
Apocynaceae. The fruit of the tree is ellipsoid, between two and three inches long, having a smooth, purplish
skin tinged with green, containing a hard stone surrounded by
Tanghinia venenífera a thick fibrous flesh.
HOMEOPATHIC - Intense and distressing vomiting, accompanied by anxiety and weakness. Great debility
and anxiety with the vomiting. General weakness. Numbness, over whole body, especially of the hands.
Staggers if attempts to walk, is unable to support his own weight and falls down helpless and paralyzed.
Complete paralysis. Death, preceded by spasmodic movements of fingers and toes.
MIND - Anxiety, with the vomiting. Stupor. Lies as if asleep and when roused answers like a drowsy man and
then relapses into former condition. Delirium.
Limbs - Hands numb. Spasmodic movements of the fingers and toes.
Mouth - Numbness, tingling in mouth and fauces.
Rectum - Purging and urination.
Stomach - Vomiting intense, distressing and repeated, first of contents of stomach, then of bile and mucus.
Vertigo - Giddy, staggers.
COMMENTS - The seed has been used as an “ordeal” test for those thought to have committed a crime. The
seed is pounded and a small piece is swallowed by the person to be tried. Those in whom it causes vomiting
escape punishment. Those whose stomachs retain it are thought to have been proven guilty, and are quickly
killed.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Tannicum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tann-ac. Tannicum acidum. Tannic acid. Tanninum. There are two forms of tannic acid, Gallo-
tannic acid, derived from nut-galls. Also querc-tannic acid, derived from healthy leaves and bark of the oak.
The former is the most used. Trituration. Solution in rectified spirit. One-half percent solution. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Colic. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Hematuria. Ileus. Nosebleed. Ophthalmia. Palpitations.
Vomiting. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tannin, or tannic acid, of which gallic acid is a derivative, has produced effects on healthy
persons and on those taking it for diarrhea. Mostly used locally against excessive secretion of mucus
membranes to contract tissue and check hemorrhage.
Leathery dryness of mouth and intestinal canal, a condition like ileus and a very aggravated state of
constipation. Obstinate constipation. Typhoid fever and dysentery. Intestines can be felt like cylindrical en-
largements. Pain in abdomen, sensitive to pressure. Diabetes. Hematuria. Ulcerated tissues. Fetor of the
perspiration. Weakness. Chronic nervous coughs.
Abdomen - Abdomen is sensitive to pressure but not distended. Irritable bowel. Intestines could be felt like
cylindrical enlargements through walls of abdomen. Ileus. Colic. Ulceration of bowels. Hemorrhage.
Eyes - Acute and chronic conjunctivitis. Granular lids and vascular cornea. Chemosis and pannus. Ophthalmia.
Purulent ophthalmia of infants.
Female - Sore breasts and nipples. Uterine bleeding. Syphilitic ulceration of the cervix.
Food - Loss of appetite. Thirst.
Heart - Palpitations.
Kidneys - Dysuria. Urine scanty, darkcolored. Albuminuria. Hematuria.
Lungs - Tuberculosis. Bronchial catarrh. Nervous coughs. Whooping cough.
Mouth - Leathery dryness of mucus membrane of mouth and intestinal canal. Hemorrhage and sponginess of
the gums. Mercurial salivation. Toothache.
Nose - Nosebleeds. Chronic catarrh and coryza.
Rectum - Obstinate constipation. Chronic diarrhea. Painless and bloody discharge from bowels. Foul stools.
Prolapsed rectum. Hemorrhoids.
Skin - Ulcers with copious discharges.
Stomach - Painful sensation in epigastric region and abdomen. Violent pains in stomach. Dyspepsia.
Obstinate vomiting of bilious substances.
Tongue - Tongue white, dry.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Querc., Gall-ac., Op., Plb.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
 ***TARAXACUM OFFICINALE
(Dandelion)
PHARMACY - tarax. Taraxacum officinale. Dandelion. Leontodum taraxacum. Taraxacum dens-leonis. N. O.
Compositae. The tincture from the whole plant when in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ague. Bilious. Cancerous, conditions. Debility. Diabetes. Flatulence. Gallstones. Headaches.
Hepatitis. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Liver, weakness. Neuralgias. Night, sweats. Rheumatism. Tongue,
mapped. Typhoid fever.
HERBAL - Taraxacum’s chief traditional uses are as a remedy for jaundice, liver obstruction in dysentery,
involuntary emissions and in difficulties in passing water.
The young leaves of the dandelion are sometimes eaten in salads. They have a bitter chicory like taste, as
does the root. Children may eat the flowers, although they are supposed to cause bedwetting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The first provings were done by Hahnemann and his pupils. Hahnemann’s provings brought
out the leading symptoms “painless urging to urinate,” and “frequent urging to urinate with copious discharge
of urine.”
Hahnemann pointed out that the urging to urinate with thirst may indicate Tarax. in some cases of diabetes.
Hahnemann’s dosage was a single drop of the tincture.
Langhammer noted the “mapped tongue.” The tongue is coated white and clears off in patches, leaving dark
red, very sensitive spots.
Affinity for the liver and bladder. A bilious remedy. Pains in both splenic and liver regions. Heaviness in the
liver region. Gastric headaches, bilious attacks with mapped tongue and jaundiced skin. Jaundice with
enlarged, indurated liver. Disorders of the liver, sour taste, darting pains in outer parts. Hysterical tympanites.
Flatulence. Cancer of bladder.
Hands and nose cold at 8 p.m. Cold fingertips. Feeling of sickness and exhaustion, inclined to sit or lie down.
Muscular pains with shuddering and muscular prickling. Stitching pains. Affections in left upper side, right lower
side, back of foot, sole of foot. Almost all symptoms appear while the patient is seated and are dissipated by
walking.
MIND - Depressive, morose, sad condition. Memory weak. Apathy, lack of reactions. Dislike for labor, but after
beginning works well. Impatient and irritable. Anxiety while sitting. Restlessness on waking. Irresolution.
Constant muttering to himself. Inclined to talk, laugh and be merry. Loquacity during perspiration.
Unconsciousness.
Abdomen - Stinging abdominal pains. Sharp stitches in left side. Grumbling and movements in abdomen.
Sensation of bubbles bursting in bowels. Hysterical tympanites. Pinching in abdomen. Pressive shootings in
abdomen and sides of abdomen, in left side of the hypogastrium.
Back - Tearing pain from ear down to neck. Sternomastoid muscle very painful to touch. Pressive jerkings
and shootings in muscles of neck, throat and nape. Pressive and tensive shootings in back and loins, when
lying down with obstructed respiration. Pressing, stinging in spine and sacrum with dyspnea. Vibration and
quivering in right scapula.
Chest - Pressure at chest. Shootings in chest and sides of chest. Jerkings in muscles.
Ears - Shootings in ears. Drawing pain in external ear. Stinging, rending pains in the ears.
Eyes - Pain in eyes, as if a grain of sand were in internal canthus. Burning and stinging pains in the eyes.
Inflammation of eyes. Lachrymation and photophobia. Nocturnal agglutination of lids. Aversion to light.
Face - Hot and red face. Sensation of heat and redness in face. Shootings and pressure in cheeks. Upper ftp
cracked. Pusa/e in right corner of lips. Purulent pimples on face, cheeks, alae nasi and lips.
Female - Suppressed menses.
Food - Loss of appetite. Food tastes sour. Salt or acid taste of food. Butter and meat taste salty. Bitter taste
after eating. Tobacco smoke is very disagreeable, causes heartburn and interrupts respiration. Great
Taraxacum officinale chilliness after drinking creating. No thirst during fever. Thirst during sweat.
Head - Heavy and numbing headache. Stinging pains in the head and face. Neuralgic headaches. Headaches
due to liver disturbances. Headaches, as from contraction orexpansion of brain. Violent headache, felt only
when standing or walking. Sensation of great heat in vertex. Drawing pain in left temple while sitting, ceasing
when walking or standing. Tearing pain in occiput. Lancinations in forehead and temples. Tension of scalp.
Kidneys - Bladder weakness. Frequent desire to urinate with copious urine. Urination with painless urging.
Bedwetting during sleep.
Limbs - Muscular pains with shuddering and prickling in the muscles. Restless limbs. Limbs painful,
tenderness of all limbs when touched. Tearing pains in limbs. Dull, joint pains. Fingertips cold. Pressive pains
in loins. Heaviness of the legs, ameliorated by walking. Neuralgia of knee, better pressure. Jerking pain in
calf (right) better on touch. Toes burning.
 Liver - Pain in the region of liver and spleen. Liver enlarged and indurated. Sensation of heaviness in the liver
region. Deficiency of the liver. Liver weakness. Chronic cholecystitis. Gallstones. Jaundice. Hepatitis with
jaundice.
Lungs - Cough after eating.
Male - Pain in testes. Permanent erections. Frequent pollutions, on alternate nights.
Modalities - Better from touch. Better moving, walking, open air. Burning in throat is better by drinking. Worse
while lying down, resting, at night. Worse from fat food.
Mouth - Sour, bitter taste. Acid saliva in mouth. Salivation with sensation as if larynx was pressed shut
Biller laste, rising from pharynx into mouth. Smarting, burning and rawness in mouth and fauces.
Accumulation of sour water in mouth. Tough, ropy, sour-tasting saliva.
Nose - Cold nose. Nosebleeds.
Perspiration - Very debilitating perspiration, causing biting on the skin. Sweat on falling asleep. Profuse night
sweats, mostly before midnight, when just going to sleep.
Rectum - Stools white. Inefficient urging to go to stool. Evacuations often, but accomplished with difficulty,
even if stool is soft. Feces of the consistence of pap, followed by tenesmus. Bilious diarrhea. Constipation
following an abundant expulsion of feces. Voluptuous itching in perineum.
Sensations - As if brain was constricted. As if teeth were set on edge. As if larynx were compressed. As if
bubbles were forming and bursting in abdomen. As of rolling and gurgling in right scapula. As if limbs were
bound or powerless.
Skin - Stinging on skin. Unhealthy, pimply, sycotic skin. Eruptions over body and limbs, itching severely and
appears to be a mixture of lichen and urticaria. Profuse night sweats, biting in skin with sweat.
Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness after meals. Sleepiness in daytime and yawning while sitting. Sleepiness and
going to sleep while listening to a scientific discourse. Vivid, unremembered dreams, frequent waking and
tossing.
Stomach - Gastric bilious attacks. Bitter taste, risings, belchings and hiccough. Empty belching after drinking.
Nausea, as after an excess of greasy food. Nausea with inclination to vomit or vomiting from very fat food, with
anxiety and pressive headache, better in open air. Nausea, with headache, anxiety, after fat food.
Teeth - Toothache with drawing pain in carious teeth, extending to eyebrows. Pressive pains in teeth. Teeth
set on edge as from acids. Flow of acid blood from decayed teeth. Blunt teeth. Hawking up of sour mucus,
causing teeth to feel dull.
Temperature - Chill in open air. Chilliness after eating and drinking. Chilliness, shiverings, all over with
pressive headache. Fingertips cold. Heat at night on waking, especially on face and hands. Heat without
thirst, in face or toes.
Throat - Hawking up of acid mucus. Sore throat with pressive pain, as from internal swelling. Dryness,
shootings and bitter mucus in the throat. Burning in throat
from smoking, better drinking.
Tongue - Tongue, coated, mapped. Tongue covered with a white film. Tongue feels raw, comes off in
patches, leaving red. sensitive spots. Tongue dry, loaded with a brown coating on waking in morning.
Vertigo - Vertigo with giddiness and staggering when walking in the open air. Vertigo with unsteady gait, falls
to either side.
COMMENTS - The Treasury of Botany noted that “the bright-yellow flowers of Taraxacum open in the morning
between 5 a.m. and 6 a.m. and close in the evening between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. Hence this was one of the
plants selected by Linneus to form his floral clock.”
Cooper noted the case of an old Indian officer who, when in India, suffered from gallstones and was advised
to take dandelion infusion every day. He did so and soon the symptoms left him and he remained free from
them for over twenty years.
Gastric and bilious attacks, especially gastric headaches. The headaches art: generally pressive. Pains in both
splenic and liver regions. Jaundice with enlarged, indurated liver.
Pressure in lower occiput after lying down. Debility, loss of appetite, profuse night sweats, especially when
convalescing from bilious or typhoid fever. Restlessness of limbs in typhoid. Sweat between toes.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In gastric and bilious affections, Card-m.. Bry., Chel., Hydr., Lyc., Nux-v. (2)
Mapped tongue, Ars., Nat-m., Merc., Ran-s. (3) Restlessness of limbs with tearing pains, Rhus-t. (4) Chel.-
Tongue dry, yellowish with red edges, retains the imprint of the teeth. Epigastric pain, spreading to the lower
corner of the right shoulder blade. Pressing sensation in the hepatic region. (5) Bry. - Dryness of the mucus
membranes, acute, stinging pains, aggravated by movement. Intense thirst, stubborn constipation. (6) Nux-v.
- Impatient, sleepy after meals, sensation of a weight in the stomach, constipation with empty urging.
Compatible: Ars. - Night-sweats.
 REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

The former is the most used. Trituration. Solution in rectified spirit. One-half percent solution. Historical dose:
All potencies.

Vomiting. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tannin, or tannic a

name: Tarentula Cubensis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tarent-c. Tarentula cubensis. Cuban tarantula. Mygale cubensis. Aranea peluda. N. O.
Araneideae. Tincture of whole decomposed spider. Tincture of whole spider. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Atasses. Anthrax. Bites,insect. Boils. Bubonic plague. Carbuncles. Chills. Chorea. Convulsions.
Delirium. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Felon. Fever. Gangrene. Headaches. Intermittent, fever.Itching. Meningitis.
Paralysis. Pruritus, vulvae. Scirrhus. Senile, ulcers.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tarent-c. affects the cellular tissues. It is useful in septic conditions, when incubation is
slow, but further progress is rapid with alarming prostration, atrocious burning or sharp stinging pains, board
like hardness of affected part and copious sweat.
Intermittent septic chills. Severe types of inflammation and pain. Purplish hue and burning, stinging pains.
Itching, especially about genitals. Diphtheria with intense fever and numb aching pains.
Various forms of malignant suppuration. Gangrene. Bluish abscesses,painful. Felon. Carbuncles. Bubo.
Bubonic plague, as a curative and preventive remedy especially during the period of invasion.
Early and persistent prostration. Restless feet. Paralysis then convulsions. Tarent-c. is a remedy for the pain
of death, soothes the last agony.
MIND - Nervous restlessness. Sensitive to others. Anxiety. Excessive hyperesthesia. Hysteria. Lacks
emotional control. Delirium due to pains. Agony of pains, compels the patient to walk on the floor for nights
Keeps hands busy, picks fingers.
Back - Itches across kidney region. Female - Pruritus vulvae.
Head - Dull ache on top of head. Fullness in head. Headaches. Shooting pain through left eye across frontal
region. Meningitis.
Kidneys - Retention of urine. Urine hot, thick. Cannot hold urine on coughing.
Limbs - Hands tremble, turgid with blood. Fidgety feet. Unsteady gait.
Lungs - Spasmodic difficulty of breathing. Shattering cough, whooping cough.
Modalities - Better from tobacco smoking. Worse from cold drinks. Worse exertion. Worse at night.
Rectum - Diarrhea.
Skin - Feels puffed all over. Pungent burning, stinging pains. Red spots and pimples. Purple discoloration.
Carbuncles. Abscesses, where pain and inflammation predominate. “Senile ulcers.” Gangrene. Anthrax.
Scirrhous of breasts.
Sleep - Drowsiness. Sleep restless, prevented by harsh cough.
Stomach - Feels hard, sore. Loss of appetite, except for breakfast. Tendency to vomit.
Temperature - Pungent heat of surface.
Vertigo - Dizziness after heat and hot perspiration.
COMMENTS - Hering stated “The Mygale Cubensis, which may be called the Cuban Tarentula, also found in
South Carolina and Texas is a larger spider of a dark brown color, less poisonous and covered with more hairs
than the Tarentula Hispánica.”
Tarent-c. seems to be a toxemic remedy, acting directly on the blood, and is in this way an analogue of Crot-
h., Apis, Ars., etc.
The bite is painless. The person is not sensible of it until next day. Then an inflamed pimple is found surrounded
by a scarlet areola. From the pimple to some other part of the body a red erysipelatous line is seen, which
marks the line followed by the spider over the skin after biting.
The pimple swells, the inflamed areola spreads, chills and fever set in with copious sweat and retention of
urine, the pimple becomes a hard, large. Exceedingly painful abscess, ending by mortification of the tissues
over it and having several small openings.
Discharging a thick, bloody matter containing pieces of tissue, fascia and tendons. The openings grow, run
into one another, forming a large cavity. At this period the fever takes the intermittent type with evening
exacerbations.
In two cases in delicate children, the bite proved fatal, but the majority recover in from three to six weeks.
A case of chorea in a girl of twelve was reported cured with Tarent-c. 6c. The movements were confined to the
left side and occurred chiefly at night, when Tarent-c. was prescribed.
Dr. Burt related the case of Don M. B. Aet. 72, good constitution, with an abscess in the back of his neck,
whose burning, excruciating pain had completely banished sleep for six or seven nights.
Fever, with great thirst and prostration. On examination, it was found to be anthrax, with all the accompanying
train of symptoms. Burt gave Tarent-c., 6c one dose every two hours; after the second dose, the pain was
 greatly relieved, and that very night the patient was able to sleep through the whole night. Under the use of
this remedy, the patient recovered without using any other, except Sil. to aid cicatrization.
Carbuncle, even to sloughing with great prostration and diarrhea. Intermittent fever with evening exacerbation.
Atrocious pains.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars., Pyrog., Crot-h., Echi., Anthr., Bell., Apis. (2) in intermittents, Aran-d. (3)
Carbuncle, Anthr., Lach., Sil.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Tarentula Hispanica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tarent. Tarentula hispánica. Spanish tarantula. Wolf spider. Lycosa tarentula. Lycosa
fasciiventris. N. O. Araneideae. Italy and Spain. Tincture of the whole spiders. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina, pectoris. Bites, spider. Boils. Callosities. Cancer. Chorea.Coccyx, pain. Cornea, opacity.
Cystitis. Depression. Diabetes mellitus. Diphtheria. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspnea. Fibroids. Headaches. Hiccough.
Hysteria. Insanity. Intermittent fevers. Kleptomania. Leucorrhea. Levitation. Locomotor, ataxia. Mania.
Ménière’s disease. Migraine. Multiple sclerosis. Nervous, disorders. Noma. Nosebleeds.
Numbness. Onanism. Ovaries, enlarged. Parkinson’s disease. Photophobia. Phy- sometra. Proctalgia.
Pruritus, pudendi. Pruritus, vulvae. Quinsy. Septic, fever. Sexual, mania. Spinal, irritation. Spinal, sclerosis.
Suffocation. Tonsillitis. Tumors. Twitching. Uterus, cancer. Uterus, neuralgia. Vertebrae, tumors. Vertigo.
Violent, pains.
HOMEOPATHIC - The name tarantula covers a number of poisonous spiders, but in homeopathy, unless
distinguished, it refers to Tarentula hispánica. Nunez instigated the proving and collected much outside
information bearing on the action of the poison.
“Tarantella” is a dance named from the city of Tarentum. “Tarantism” is a dancing mania, set up in persons
bitten by the tarantula or in those who imagine themselves bitten. The cure is music and dancing. These
symptoms give a keynote indication to this remedy.
Affects the nerves, which are highly strung, producing remarkable nervous symptoms, hysteria with
chlorosis, chorea. often reflexive from generative sphere. The heart, spine, respiration and right side are also
prominently affected.
Extreme restlessness, fidgety, hurried, must keep in constant motion even though walking aggravates. Music
causes excitement. Rolls on ground from side to side or strikes vehemently with his feet or rolls the head and
rubs it to relieve her distress. Chorea with arm symptoms. Irregular movements. Can run better than walk.
Symptoms appear suddenly, with violence. Quivering, jerking, trembling, twitchings. Violent pains,
neuralgias, as if thousands of needles were pricking. Joint pains. Headache with pain in uterus, throat with eye
pains, face pain with stomach pain, pain in the ear with hiccough. Tickling, burning, scorching and numbness
with prickling. Palliates the death pains and agony of dying process.
Nervous phenomena, dysmenorrhea, spinal irritability. Bladder tenesmus. Constriction sensation. Deep
septic conditions, abscess, evacuates pus rapidly. Noma. Emaciation, as if the flesh fairly fell off the bones,
worse in the face. Cancer, fibrous tumors. Hysterical epilepsy.
Intense sexual excitement, causing pain. Formication. Diabetes mellitus with great prostration and pain as if
whole body were bruised.
MIND - Adroit. Crafty, sly, cunning. Instability of intelligence. Obstinacy. Selfish and demanding. Very
impatient and irritable with others. Hateful. Destructive impulses. Throws things away. Kleptomania. Desire
to strike herself or others. Angry with despair. Discontented. Melancholy.
Intolerant to any criticism. Averse to company, but wants someone present. Ungrateful. Conceited and
deceptive behavior. Feigns fainting, insensibility. When there are no observers, there is no hysteria, when
attention is directed to her. she begins to twitch.
Suddenly changing moods, fancies or strength. Lacks emotional control. Erratic. Impulsive. Fits of nervous
laughter then screaming. Moral depravity. Restlessness and compelled to walk. Tormenting and intense
behavior. Anxious and full of fears.
Erratic moods. Sometimes a sweet cheerfulness and gaiety, while at other times, anger, irritability.
Quarrelsome, excitable, exhilarated or sad. Self-indulgence. Hysterical emotions. Intense sexual excitements,
lasciviousness. Mania, very excitable.
Sensitive to music. Dances up and down. Laughs, mocks, runs, dances, makes gestures and jokes. Cries
and sings until hoarse or exhausted. Aversion to colors, black, red, yellow, green. Mental symptoms better in
evening after eating. Refuses to eat.
Delirium, mania, shrieking, singing, erotic mania. Stupefaction. Indisposed to talk. Sensation of being small
 (contrast to Aur., Plat., Stram.). Weeping, causeless, during sleep. Palliates the agony and pains of the dying
process.
Abdomen - Violent burning in abdomen.
Burning in hypogastrium with great weight, interferes with walking. Hepatic region painful to touch. Pain in
hepatic region, with nausea and vomiting, worse before paroxysm of malaria. Sharp pain in umbilical region.
Back - Painfully sensitive spine, touch excites pains in chest, heart etc. Coccy-
Tarentula hispánica godynia, better standing, worse slightest movement, touch. Tumors around vertebral
column. Painfully sensitive spine.
Bladder - Bladder seems swollen and hard, during cystitis. Pains in region of bladder. Very painful, frequent
urination, worse at night. Incontinence when coughing, laughing, or making any effort whatever. Urine foul,
with sandy sediment.
Causations - Ill effects of unrequited love, bad news, scolding, punishment, falls, sepsis.
Chest - Panting with oppression of the chest. Sensations of oppression of chest when raising arms or lying on
left side. Rheumatic pains in chest. Angina pectoris.
Constitutions - Suited to nervous, hysterical patients subject to chorea disorders; to persons of foxy,
mischievous and destructive tendency. Suited to chorea disorders when whole body or right arm and left leg
are involved.
Ears - Snapping, cracking in ears (right), with pain and hiccough. Noises, ringing as of bells, worse on waking
in the morning. Singing, like a tea-kettle, in left ear.
Eyes - Itching of the eyes with thick tears. Stitching in eyes as sand or thorn. One pupil dilated, other
contracted. Eyes are wide open spasmodically and staring. Photophobia. Squinting of eyes which remain open
during epileptic attack.
Face - Acne in face since menopause. Fiery red, bloated. Expression of terror. Wrinkled. Pains in angles of
lower jaw.
Female - Menses early. Profuse menstruation with frequent erotic spasms. Dysmenorrhea with very sensitive
ovaries. Dysmenorrhea better during warm weather, when outdoors, worse during cold weather. Pruritus
vulvae after menses. Leucorrhea alternating with bloody discharge. Leucorrhea of clear acrid, sticky lumps.
Dry, hot raw, itching vulva and vagina, worse scratching. Great sexual desire. Violent nymphomania, worse
sex. Sensation of motion in uterus like a fetus. Sensation of burning. Expulsion of gas from vagina. Strong
bearing-down pelvic pains. Displacement of uterus. Neuralgia of uterus, with sadness and despair. Violent
tearing pains in uterus. Fibroid tumors of uterus with bearingdown pains. Ovaries, sensitive to pressure. Cancer
of cervix.
Food - Loss of appetite. Refuses to eat. Food tastes sour. Mental symptoms better evening, after eating.
Craving for sand or raw food. Craving for raw food during pregnancy. Desires highly seasoned food, salty
things. Desires ashes, cuttlefish, smoking. Aversion to meat, bread. Thirst for cold water. Thirst often and for
large quantities.
Head - Intense pain, as if thousands of needles were pricking into brain. Heavy pain in temples, extending to
face and neck with nausea and impatience. Violent crushing headaches. Migraine, can’topen eyes, with
tendency of head to incline backward. Fullness in head with throbbing carotids, better nosebleed. Burning heat
in occiput with pricking and itching over whole body. Neuralgia in temples. Meningitis. Wants hair, brushed,
pulledor head rubbed. As if cold water were poured on head and body.
Heart - Diseases of heart, worse by wetting hands in cold water. Angina pectoris. Palpitations, precordial
anguish. Trembling and thumping of heart as from bad news or fright. Sensations as if heart twisted and turned
around. Heart takes sudden jumps. Pulse, hard infrequent, irregular. Heart suddenly ceases to beat, patient
fears to die. Heart as if squeezed or compressed.
Kidneys - Foul urine with sandy sediment. Incontinence on laughing, coughing etc. Diabetes mellitus. Polyuria
with violent pains in lumbar region and paralysis of lower limbs.
Limbs - Multiple sclerosis with trembling. Chorea movements. Twitching and jerking. Extraordinary
contractions and movements. Legs restless, impulse to walk. Can run better than walk. Numbness of legs.
Weak legs, cannot plant them firmly, do not obey. Y awning with uneasiness of legs, must move them
constantly. Festination. Kneeling difficult. Soles itching. Cold, moist feet and hands. Restless arms, keeps
hands busy, picks fingers.
Lungs - Attacks of suffocation, with crying, screaming and restlessness, must have fresh air, worse
coughing. Panting with oppression of the chest. Cough when expectorating, gagging, fatiguing. Cough worse
after sex, noise, better smoking.
Male - Sensitive genitals. Extreme sexual excitement. Lasciviousness almost to insanity, worse sex.
Prostatic ailments after masturbation. Seminal emission hot, bloody. Indolent tumors of testicles.
 Modalities - Better open air, sun. Better bright colors. Better from music. Better pressure, rubbing affected
parts. Better relaxation. Better warm water, sweating, smoking. Better riding in a carriage. Motion improves
headache but aggravates uterine pains and pains in coccyx. Worse from rest, touch, contact, motion. Worse
noises. Worse seeing others in trouble. Worse damp, cold, washing head or putting hands in cold water. Worse
after menses. Worse at night, evening. Worse periodically, yearly, at the same hour. Worse after sex:
sadness, difficult respiration, cough, and general weakness specifically increased by sexual excitement.
Mouth - Dry mouth and teeth. Tongue drawn backward, preventing speech. Pain in lower jaw, as if teeth would
fall out. Grinding of teeth.
Nose - Catarrh, dryness, burning, sneezing and bleeding, worse right side. Nosebleed better throbbing carotids
and fullness in head.
Perspiration - Profuse excoriating sweat. Copious perspiration, worse after excitement.
Rectum - Weakness of anal sphincter. Violent burning in abdomen and rectum. Burning pain with profuse,
dark, fetid, bloody stools and violent urging. Severe constipation, not relieved by purgatives or enema.
Constipation with involuntary passing of urine on coughing or any effort.
Sensations - As if thousands of needles were pricking into brain. As of needles sticking into muscle of neck
when touched. As of insects creeping and crawling. As if occiput were struck with a hammer. As of a hair in
eye. As if lower teeth were going to fall out. As if heart turned and twisted around.
Skin - Purplish skin. Ecchymosed spots. Cold spots or as of a cold matter flowing or dropping on part. Boils,
burning and painful. Carbuncle. Deep abscesses. Helps evacuation of pus. Dry eczema (Ars., Sulph.). Miliary
eruptions and furuncles, with diabetes. Itching, as of insects creeping and crawling.
Sleep - Sleepless before midnight from excitement. Sad dreams, with weeping.
Stomach - Gastric symptoms, worse at onset of fever. Gastric disturbances, accompanied by pains in head,
face, teeth etc. Bitter belchings, hysterical. Vomits all food eaten. Vomiting during pregnancy.
Stools - Stools oily, black offensive, worse by washing head. Very dark, fetid, partly formed stools, containing
much mucus, expelled with difficulty. Stools followed by smarting and burning in anus, but no tenesmus.
Temperature - Alternate chill and heat. General heat with cold feet. Septic fever. Sweat profuse, excoriating.
Intense chill all over before convulsions.
Throat - Tonsils greatly swollen, with offensive odor. Diphtheria both tonsils covered by a firm membrane,
color of pearl.
Vertigo - Vertigo after breakfast, with bad taste in mouth. Vertigo when fixing sight on any object. Vertigo at
night, when descending stairs. Vertigo before or following epileptic attack. Vertigo, worse carrying burden on
head, then spasms.
Vision - Sees ghosts, faces, flashes. As if a cloud before left eye, before epileptiform fits.
COMMENTS - Clarke recorded two cases of poisoning. The first was the case of a girl, three months old, who
was bitten by a tarantula. She appeared at first uneasy, then exhibited dyspnea and complained. Showed
signs of suffocation, vomited. She was agitated and convulsed. Music was played, movements of the limbs
were set up, resulting in a profuse sweat, followed by sleep and complete recovery.
Clarke also noted the case of Francis Mustek a peasant, who was bitten by a tarantula on the left hand about
the middle of July as he was gathering corn. He went home with his companions but on the way fell as if struck
by a stroke. Dyspnea followed and his face, hands and feet became dark. Knowing the remedy, his
companions fetched musicians.
When the patient heard their playing he began to revive, to sigh, to move first his feet, then his hands and then
the whole body. At last getting on his feet he took to dancing violently with sighing so labored that the
bystanders were almost frightened.
At times he rolled himself on the ground and struck it vehemently with his feet. Two hours after the music
began the blackness of his face and hands went off, he perspired freely and regained perfect health.
Every succeeding year at the same season the pain and attending symptoms returned, but less violently and
they could always be averted by music. But if the imminent paroxysm was not averted in time, he was found
by his friends struck down as at first and was restored in the same way.
Hysterical hyperesthesia. The least excitement irritates, followed by languid sadness. Great excitability of
nerve endings. Fingertips are extremely sensitive. Sore and bruised feeling all over, worse moving about.
Spinal irritation, slightest touch along spine causes spasmodic pain in chest and heart regions. Hypersensitive
to the least touch.
Neuralgias, particularly in the head, “as if thousands of needles were pricking to the brain.” Worse by noise
touch, strong light. Better by rubbing head against pillow. Keynote better by rubbing. “Ends of nerves become
so irritated. That some kind of friction is necessary in order to obtain relief.”
Chorea (Ign., Staph.), most marked on right side. Characteristic unceasing movements, twitching, jerking, and
 dancing. Restlessness, particularly in the lower limbs, with desire to cry. Must keep moving about though all
symptoms are worse walking.
Farrington noted that “When there are no observers there is no hysteria, when attention is directed to her she
begins to twitch,” and “cunning attempts to feign paroxysms of wild dancing."
Mental symptoms in connection with sexual disorders. Sighing, yawning, laughing and crying. Joking and
profound melancholy. Insanity. Better by music. Music at first excites then it subsequently relieves.
Dark red or purplish coloration and swelling of skin and tissue. Septic boils that turn really blue and painful.
Spider bites in general (Hyper., Led.). Periodicity, deep action returning annually on the date of the bite.
Diphtheria tonsillitis, threatening suffocation. Apparent imminent choking. Cystitis. Septic and intermittent
fevers. Constrictive headache with pain in uterus.
P. C. Majumdar reported the case of a woman, 18, who had oppression of the chest, with a suffocating
sensation. She had continuous jerking and movement of her hands. Foam at mouth. Complete insensibility.
Profuse and delaying menses. Very sleepy. Hysterical epilepsy was diagnosed. Ign. 30c did nothing. Tarent.,
200c, brought her out of the fit and restored her completely in a few minutes.
C. M. Boger cured a case of irritative cough with Tarent. 30c. Mr. B.. 41, was sore all over, throat felt dry.
Coughed when lying down at night and in morning after rising. Dry with tearing pain in chest. Excited by
pressure of phlegm in chest. Felt short of breath for at least an hour after each coughing attack. Only better
from smoking. Bad taste in the evening. Three doses cured.
In Med. Ad., a case of hyperesthesia of the fingertips was mentioned. The patient, a woman, 33, could not
dress herself without gloves. The irritation caused a sensation in the teeth as if set on edge by a strong acid.
The pain was not in the fingers. Tarent, gave relief after Asar., Gels, and Sul-ac. had failed.
Farrington related a case of typhoid in a child cured by Tarent. The child rolled its head and bit its nightgown.
Apis, and Agn. improved. Tarent, slightly aggravated at first, then rapidly improved.
RELATIONS - Tarent.’s action is similar to Ars. in many symptoms, therefore when Ars. seems indicated but
fails, it is better to give Tarent. Antidote to: Lach. Antidotes: Puls., Mag-c., Mosch., Cupr., Chel., Gels., Bov.,
Carb-v. Compare: (1) Agar., Ars., Cupr., Mag. phos. (2) Kali-br. - Irritation of periphery of nerves better
exercising and rubbing. (3) Chorea, Mygal.. Cimic., Agar., Stram. (4) Desire to jump, Stram., Croc., Nat-m.,
Stict., Asar., Agar., Hyos.. Cic. (5) Bores head in pillow, Bell. (Tarent, is more rubbing). (6) Croc. (7) As if
occiput struck with a hammer, Naja. (8) Deep-in headache, Bac. (9) Extreme joy, Coff. (10) Unfortunate love,
Ph-ac. (11) Ménière’s disease, ague, Chin-s. (12) Sees faces, Sulph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Tartaricum Acidum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tart-ac. Tartaricum acidum. Tartaric acid. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Debility. Gastritis. Heels, pain. Paralysis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Found in grapes, pineapple, sorrel and other fruits. Tart-ac. is an anti-scor- butic anti-septic,
stimulating the mucus and salivary secretions.
Extreme weakness. In evening feels very tired, can scarcely drag himself along. General bruised sensation,
especially of lower limbs. Convulsions just before death.
Abdomen - Pain around umbilicus and region of loins. Pinching below navel with emission of flatulence, cold
feeling in abdomen.
Face - Face instantly became red as fire and having exclaimed that he was poisoned, became speechless,
died on tenth day (drank 2 oz. in solution). Lips, turn brown and black on their inner edges. Constant dryness
of lips, must moisten them continually. Burning of lips.
Food - Excessive, very urgent thirst.
Heart - Very weak action of the heart. Feeble pulse.
Limbs - Sharp pain in region of loins. Paralysis of thighs and legs. Tearing pains at soles, near the heel, which
prevents him setting his foot on the ground after luncheon.
Lungs - Breathing accelerated, then laborious and slow.
Modalities - Better in open air. Pasty taste is better after eating.
Mouth - Teeth set on edge. Brown and dry tongue. Taste, pasty in morning, ceases on eating.
Rectum - Many stools during night. Stools like color of coffee grounds.
Sleep - Frequent yawning and stretching.
Stomach - Dyspepsia with copious secretion of mucus. Belchings. Nausea. Vomiting is repeated and almost
continuous. Continued vomiting with burning in throat and stomach. Vomited deep green matter.
Temperature - General cold feeling, evening in bed.
 Throat - Hoarseness and scraping in larynx. Burning sensation in throat and stomach as if on fire.
Vertigo - Confusion in head, dizziness.
COMMENTS - A proving by Nenning and some poisonings have furnished the pathogenesis of Tart-ac. One
of the most marked symptoms was intense burning in throat and stomach, feeling “as if on fire.” Tongue brown
and dry. Almost constant vomiting, vomited matter of deep green color. Feces coffee-ground color.
Dullness andlassitude. Paralytic debility. “Weakness in the evening, can scarcely drag himself along.” Difficult
respiration. Great weakness with diarrhea with dry and brown tongue. “Tearing pain on the soles of the feet,
near the heel, which prevents him putting his foot on the ground after luncheon” (Phyt.).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Taxol
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - taxol. Taxol. Alkaloid of Pacific Yew Tree, (Taxus brevifolia). Taxol is an anti-cancer
chemotherapy drug. N. O. Taxaceae. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Allergic reactions. Anemia. Arthritis. Breast, cancer. Cancer. Chemotherapy, effects. Chills.
Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Edema. Fatigue. Fever. Hair loss. Hypersensitivity. Hypotension. Hives. Kaposi’s
sarcoma. Liver problems. Lung, cancer. Lung, disorders. Mouth, sores. Nail, discoloration. Nausea. Ovarian,
cancer. Peripheral neuropathy. Radiation, effects. Rheumatism. Stomach, disorders. Skin, disorders.
Tumors. Ulcers. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weight, gain.
HERBAL - The Taxol compound belongs to a family of compounds called Taxanes that are unique to the Yew
species. During the Taxol studies, several yew taxanes in addition to the Taxol tanane were found to exert
anti-cancer properties. Other Pacific Yew taxanes (also called diterpenes) are known by various names such
as baccatin 111, brevitaxin, brevifoliol andcephalomannine, as well as variations of taxol compounds. Taxol is
only one of hundreds of organic compounds in Taxus brevifolia.
Taxol was originally approved for use as a treatment for ovarian cancer, ongoing research was showing its
efficacy in other arenas such as cancers of the lung, breast, bladder, prostate, testes, esophagus, head and
neck, cervix, and endometrium. Also used to treat Kaposi’s sarcoma and melanoma.
HOMEOPATHIC - The homeopathic indications for prescribing Taxol can be determined from the side effects
of Taxol cancer therapy. Homeopathic potencies of Taxol maybe given to lessen the toxic side effects of the
treatment.
The following Taxol side effects are common for patients taking Taxol: Low blood counts. White and red blood
cells and platelets may become decreased. Hair loss. Pain in the joints and muscles. Peripheral neuropathy,
numbness and tingling of the hands and feet. Nausea and vomiting. Diar-
rhea. Mouth sores. Hypersensitivity reaction with fever, facial flushing, chills, shortness of breath, or hives after
Taxol is given.
The following are less common side effects for patients receiving Taxol: Swelling of the feet or ankles (edema)
.Liver problems. Low blood pressure. Darkening of the skin where previous radiation treatment has been given.
Nail changes, discoloration of nail beds.
Fever, chills. Shortness of breath, wheezing, difficulty breathing, closing up of the throat, swelling of facial
features, hives. Allergic reaction. Redness or pain at the site of injection. Nausea. Vomiting. Diarrhea. Unusual
bleeding or bruising. Black or tarry stools. Blood in stools or urine
Extreme fatigue. Mouth sores, painful redness, swelling or ulcers. Yellowing of the skin or eyes. Swelling of
the feet or ankles. Sudden weight gain. Signs of infection such as redness or swelling, pain on swallowing,
coughing up mucus, or painful urination.
RELATIONS - Compare: Taxus brevifolia (Pacific Yew) belongs to the botanical family Taxaceae, which is a
small family with one main genus - Taxus. Species include Taxus baccata (European Yew), Taxus cuspidate
(Japanese Yew), Taxus globosa (Mexican Yew) and Taxus canadensis (Canadian Yew).
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Taxus Baccata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tax. Taxus baccata. Yew bark. N. O. Coniferae. Tincture of the fresh young shoots. Tincture of
the bemes.Historicaldose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Cancer. Chemotherapy, effects. Ciliary, neuralgia. Collapse. Convulsions. Cystitis.
Delirium. Digestion, quick. Dysuria. Ear, polyps. Eruptions. Fainting. Gout. Hair, loss. Headaches. Heart,
disorders. Kidneys, disorders. Knees, abscess. Lachrymation. Nose, eruptions. Rheumatism. Purpura.
Spermatorrhea. Strangury. Stupor. Trembling. Uterine, tumors. Vision, dim.
 HERBAL - The poisonous properties of the
yew have been recognized and disputed from ancient times. Gerarde said that in his school days he and his
companions ate their fill of yew berries and slept not only under its shade, but on its branches without any ill
effect, but there is plenty of evidence on the other side.
In the Med. Press, May 29, 1901, a patient of Mullingar Asylum died suddenly from eating the leaves. Some
years ago a correspondence in the Times brought to light instances of the lethal effects of yew leaves on cattle.
One correspondent, Mr. James Simmons of Haslemere, mentioned an observation made by himself and
others, that yew leaves are more poisonous some time after they have been cut than when fresh.
“Yew cropped green from the tree has no fatal effect,” and animals do not eat it fresh, they prefer grass, but if
Yew has been cut and allowed to wither cattle will eat it in large quantities and in that state it is deadly poison.”
“My people,” said Mr. Simmons, “once buried some Yew cuttings deep in the dung of a farmyard, a number of
large hogs dug it up, ate it and all died.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Tax. is for pustular diseases of skin and night-sweats. Gout and chronic rheumatism. Pains
in the knees, elbows and back. Slight tremor over whole frame. Trembling. Convulsions. Fainting and collapse.
Relaxation of muscles. Cancer, chemotherapy effects.
MIND - Impatience, which unfits the patient for mental application. Delirium. Stupor.
Abdomen - Tension in abdomen, as if the stomach were overloaded. Squeezing and tension across abdomen.
Aching in umbilical region. Borborygmi.
Back - Drawing pain in muscles of neck (left). Constant pain in back. Sacral pains, which allow no rest either
in a standing or sitting posture and which compel the patient to remain in bed. Incisive pain in sacrum. Pain in
shoulder blade, which subsequently removes to loins.
Chest - Oppression, when stomach is either too full or too empty or else with pain below xiphoid cartilage.
Sharp pain in left side. Chest full and hot. Lungs engorged.
Ears - Polyps in the ears.
Eyes - Pupils widely dilated. Drawing with lachrymation and pressure. Lachrymation of left eye. Itching of
external angle of left eye. Burning itching in eyelids. Vision dim.
Head - Supra-orbital and temporal pain on right side with lachrymation.
Heart - Irregular action of heart. Pulse rapid, slow, feeble, small, wiry, almost imperceptible.
Face - Puffy and pale. Looks ill. Face livid, convulsed. Lips are purplish, livid, black brown, especially upper.
Frothing at mouth.
Female - Uterine cancer and tumors.
Food - Violent hunger. Frequent want to eat with activity of digestive functions.
Kidneys - Cutting pain at base of kidneys which allows him neither to sit still nor stand up and even prevents
turning in bed. Urinary tenesmus. Frequent want to urinate with difficult emission in a fine stream. Strangury,
urine red.
Limbs - Numbness of limbs and paralysis after several sweats. Sharp, transient, wandering pains. Contusive
and incisive pain, which hinders walking. Abscess at right knee. Violent pinching in left calf. Tingling crawling
sensation in whole left foot. Lancinations in hand. Burning dryness of palms of hands. Dull pain in joints of
fingers. Rheumatic pain in fingers.
Lungs - Violent and fatiguing cough. Short cough after every meal, excited by full inspirations with oppression.
Male - Flow of semen without erection or sexual pleasure for several successive nights. Great excitement
during sex. After sex, weakness and great oppression.
Modalities - Worse by pressure, by application of liquids. Worse before and after each meal. Worse after sex.
Coughing causes headache. Deep breathing causes cough. Rubbing improves the itching of eyelids.
Mouth - Sensation of coldness in teeth. Mouth dry. Burning pricking on tongue. Tongue excoriated, moist,
tremulous. Saliva hot, acrid. Saliva increased, extremely viscid, acrid. Bitter taste like that
Taxus baccata of Cinchona.
Nose - A round spot of a reddish-brown color, on the end of the nose with desquamation of skin.
Rectum - Hard, difficult, dry evacuations. Occasionally a stool which is soft or of a natural consistence.
Diarrhea with insupportable tenesmus and burning at every evacuation.
Skin - Large, flat, itching pustules. Badly smelling and offensive night-sweats. Peculiarly offensive sweat with
eruption of vesicles. Podagra. Erysipelas. All hairy parts become denuded. Black jaundice. Skin red. Body
covered with pustules. Miliary eruption. Eruption of large pimples. Dry tetter causing much itching.
Sleep - Sleeplessness during whole night, yawning without inclination to sleep.
Stomach - Feeling of emptiness, must eat frequently. Violent hunger, soon after breakfast with general
uneasiness and weakness in region of stomach. Aching, burning and pinching in region of stomach. Pain in
pit of stomach and region of navel. After eating, cough. Feeling of pins and needles at pit of stomach. Nausea
 with accumulation of saliva. Retching. Vomiting ending in death. Vomit, tenacious, containing bile.
Temperature - Perspiration from least exertion with great prostration of strength. Profuse night-sweats.
Commencing with shivering followed by dry heat of hands and feet. Offensive viscid sweats with itching and
redness.
COMMENTS - The symptoms of the Tax. pathogenesis are made up of poisonings by leaves and berries and
also of provings by Gastier. Fainting is a very prominent feature with Tax. And, in the fatal cases there are
convulsions, collapse and syncope.
Death from yew poisoning, said Cooper, is remarkably painless. “Empty feeling” in the stomach was prominent
and it was noted that the digestion was very rapid. “Must eat frequently.” Gastric catarrh is set up with vomiting
of tenacious mucus. Increased saliva, viscid. Pustular skin affection. Large, flat, strongly itching pustules.
Viscid sweat. Shooting pains in the toes. Gout. Irritation in the kidneys and bladder. Disturbed heart. Tax. has
been recommended as a substitute for Dig., being considered superior to the latter in having no cumulative
effect.
On the suggestion of Cooper, Clarke once gave a single dose of Tax. tincture in a case of ear polyps (bright
red) with catarrh in a youth with the result that the polyps shriveled up to one-third of its former size.
RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Staph - prostration with oppression after an embrace. Compare: (1) Ars., Bell.,
Nux-v., Colch., Dulc., Kali phos., Lyc. (2) The Coniferae. (3) Load at stomach, Abies-n. (4) Rapid digestion,
Sulph. (5) Podagra, Urt-u.
RÉFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Tela Araneae
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tela. Tela araneae. Cobweb. Araneae tela. Spider’s web. Aranearum tela. N. O. Arachnida. The
cobweb of the black spider found in barns, cellars, dark places. Tincture or trituration. Historical dose: Tinc-
ture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphthae. Asthma. Chills. Chorea. Coryza. Coughs. Delirium. Eczema. Fatigue. Headaches. Hectic
fevers. Hiccoughs. Hydrothorax. Insomnia. Intermittent fever. Leucorrhea. Nervous, weakness. Numbness.
Sleeplessness. Tuberculosis. Urticaria.
HOMEOPATHIC - The spider’s web has been used as a remedy since ancient times. Tela, has been
experimented with on healthy persons; t very rapidly lowers the frequency of the pulse rate.
In some it produced “a calm and delightful state of feeling, followed by a disposition to sleep. The most delicious
tranquility, resembling the action of opium and followed by no bad effects.”
Twenty grains given to an old and infirm asthmatic produced “slight but pleasant delirium.” Muscular energy is
increased, could not be kept in bed, but danced and jumped about the room all night.
In cases of febrile depression, deficient animation or indifference to surrounding objects, the exhibition of eight
or ten grains of cobwebs was often followed by exhilaration, the eyes sparkled.
The countenance assumed a temporary life and, though the course of the disease might not be changed or
the danger averted, more respite was obtained than is gotten from wine, opium or anything else within my
knowledge.
“In spasmodic disorders of various kinds in asthma in periodic headaches in general restlessness and
muscular irritability, its good effects are often signal. The cobweb gives sleep, but not by narcotic power,
tranquility and sleep here appear to be the simple consequence of release from pain and irritation.”
Tela, acts on arterial system. The pulse is full, strong, and compressible. Lowers pulse rate frequency. Cardiac
sleeplessness increased muscular energy. Excitement and nervous agitation in febrile states.
Dry asthma, harassing coughs, periodic headaches with extreme nervous weakness. Obstinate intermittents.
Masked periodical diseases, hectic, broken down patients. Symptoms come on suddenly with cool, clammy
skin. Numbness of hands and legs when at rest. Continued chilliness.
MIND- Absent-mindedness. Mental dullness, brain as if enveloped in a fog. Makes mistakes in spelling, time.
Disoriented feeling. Spaced-out feeling. Thoughts, disconnected. Prostration of mind. Tranquility and a sense
of well-being.
Sadness, despondency, depression with heaviness of body. Pities herself. Sighing. Offended easily by jokes.
Censorious, critical. Cursing. Irritability. Aversion to being touched. Kleptomania. Anxiety with chest
constriction. Anxiety about health. Fear of disease. Fear of being bitten. Bites himself.
Abdomen - Distension. Sensation of full
ness, heaviness. Abdomen sensitive to clothing. Stabbing pain in left hypochondria. Spasms and twisting in
the bowels
Back - Heat flushes. Heaviness sensation. Pain in dorsal region, left scapulae. Stabbing, sensation of a knife
 in the back. Pulling sensation. Burning pain in cervical region. Stiffness in cervical region. Stiffness of spine.
Desire to stretch, neck region. Sensation as if stretched backwards.
Chest - Anxiety with chest constriction. Heaviness feeling. Stabbing pain. Stinging pain in sternum. Wave
sensation, behind sternum. Pain in axilla. Perspiration in right axilla. Hydrothorax.
Ears - Boring pains. Heaviness sensation in ears. Heat sensation. Noises while eating. Sounds seem far away.
Eyes - Dryness of eyes. Heaviness sensation. Aching pain, better cold application. Eye inflammation, better
from cold. Discharges are green. Pains, burning and sore. Injected, inner canthus. Lachrymation, in the wind.
Face - Fullness, heat sensations. Numbness, heaviness of jaw. Heat flushes. Aphthae on lips. Twitching of
lips. Facial paralysis.
Female - Leucorrhea, offensive smell. Sexual desire decreased or increased.
Food - Appetite increased. Desires beets, chocolate, ginger, ice, warm soup. Fruit aggravates.
Head - Headaches with flushes of heat. Boring and pressing pains. Tingling pains in scalp.
Heart - Anxiety with constriction. Cardiac sleeplessness. Piercing pain, heart, region. Pulsation in heart region.
Pulse is full, strong, and compressible. Lowers pulse rate frequency.
Kidneys - Pain at close of urination.
Limbs - Awkwardness. Chilliness. Heaviness sensation in limbs, hip. Numbness. Aching pains. Stitching pain
in knee, patella. Eczema in the hollow of the knee. Urticaria on the leg, calf. Heat with alternating cold in feet.
Weakness of legs during stool. Sharp pain in shoulders. Trembling of hand, right.
Lungs - Difficult breathing with palpitations, stabbing pains. Dry, irritating coughs.
Male - Stitching pains in penis.
Modalities - Aversion to air, drafts. Cold, better applications. Better when it rains.
Mouth - Metallic taste. Aphthae on the tongue. Biting sensation on tongue. Itching inside cheek. Mucus on
teeth.
Nose - Coryza, as if about to get a cold or flu, with anxiety. Coryza with fever. Nosebleed during exercise.
Twitching of nose.
Perspiration - Clammy, offensive sweat. Perspiration of hands, feet. Perspiration with fever.
Sleep - Sleeplessness with heat in feet. Cardiac sleeplessness.
Skin - Clammy skin. Eczema. Urticaria.
Stomach - Appetite increased. Indigestion.
Hiccoughs. Vomiting, with spasms and twisting.
Temperature - Fever alternating with chills.
Obstinate intermittents. Perspiration with fever, shivering, at night. Hectic fevers.
Throat - Constriction of throat. Dryness, sore pain, on waking. Congested. Sensation of a lump. Unsteady
speech and voice.
Vertigo - Vertigo after exertion, exercising.
Vision - Focusing difficult. Vision is blurred, worse after eating chocolate.
COMMENTS - Dr. Chapman wrote of Tela., “I have cured some obstinate intermittents, suspended the
paroxysm of hectic fevers. Overcome morbid vigilance from excessive nervous mobility and quieted irritation
of the system from other causes and particularly as connected with protracted coughs and other chronic
pectoral disorders.”
Dr. Gillespie of Edinburgh reported, “I cured an obstinate intermittent with cobweb after other means had
failed.”
Dr. Jackson wrote, “I think I may venture to say that it prevents the recurrence of febrile paroxysms more
abruptly and more effectively, than quinine bark or arsenic or any other remedy employed for that purpose with
which I am acquainted: that like all other remedies of the kind, it is only effectual as applied under a certain
conditions of habit, but that the condition of susceptibility for cobweb is at the same time of more latitude than
for any other of
the known remedies.”
“If the cobweb,” said Dr. Jackson, “was given in the time of perfect intermission, the return of paroxysm was
prevented, if given under the first symptoms of a commencing paroxysm, the symptoms were suppressed and
the course of the paroxysm was so much interrupted that the di sease, for the most part, lost its characteristic
symptoms.
“If it was not given until the paroxysm was advanced in progress the symptoms of irritation, viz., tremors,
startings spasms and delirium, if such existed as forms of febrile action, were usually reduced in violence,
sometimes entirely removed. In this case sleep, calm and refreshing, usually followed the sudden and perfect
removal of pain and irritation.
“Vomiting, spasms and twisting in the bowels, appearing as modes of febrile irritation, were also usually allayed
 by it, there was no effect from it where the vomiting or pain was connected with real inflammation.”
Jackson noted particular changes induced on the existing state of the system, and characterized it as
powerfully stimulant base on its affects.
Where the pulses of the arteries were quick, irregular and irritated, they became calm, regular and slow after
the cobweb had passed into the stomach. The effect was accompanied, for the most part, with perspiration
and perfect relaxation of the surface.
When the pulses were slow, regular and nearly natural, they usually became frequent small, irregular,
sometimes intermitting.
Languor and depression characterize the disease, sensation of warmth and comfort are diffused about the
stomach and increased animation is conspicuous in the appearance of the eye and countenance.
Dr. Jackson likewise effected perfect cures with it in some troublesome spasmodic disorders and gave it with
the most marked benefit in dry, irritating coughs, usually termed nervous. In the advanced stage of tuberculosis
it procured a respite beyond his expectation.
He also found it useful in restraining a troublesome hiccough. Remembering the fame of Mygale avicularia in
chorea, this other spider to be of use “in some troublesome spasmodic affections.”
Dr. Thatcher cited the following case from apaperofDr. Jackson’s: “W. Sands has been afflicted for many years
a distressing asthma, which has proved fatal to his father and two sisters. The complaint being hereditary and
aggravated by malformation of the thorax, no remedy gave any permanent relief, nor did change of climate
procure any alleviation of symptoms.
“For a considerable time back he has never been able to lie down in bed on account of a sense of suffocation,
but is obliged to be supported half sitting by pillows and is seldom able to sleep.
“He swallowed nearly a scruple of the spider’s web, he swallowed it at bed time and to his utter astonishment
enjoyed sound and uninterrupted sleep all night, a blessing to which he had been an entire stranger above six
years.
“Since he began with the cobweb thinks his health is improved, the cough has entirely abated, but whenever
the remedy is omitted the complaint returns.”
Dr. Oliver found that by the use of this remedy a patient laboring under organic disease of the heart and
hydrothorax obtained great relief and refreshing sleep, who had not before slept for three nights.
Another, under similar affection, experienced uncommon relief from the same prescription. To one suffering
much pain from cancer, it afforded ease and comfortable sleep.
A patient in tuberculosis pulmonalis being affected with distressing agitation of mind and nervous irritation, it
answered like a charm and soon induced great sleep like a moderate dose of opium.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.
