name: Tellurium Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tell. Tellurium metallicum. Tellurium metal. An element (Te, At. Wt. 125). Trituration of the
precipitated element. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Axilla, sweat. Backache. Barber’s itch. Boils. Cataract. Cholecystitis. Conjunctivitis. Coryza.
Coughs. Eczema. Entropion. Eruptions. Eye, inflammation. Deafness. Emphysema. Foot, sweat. Gastritis.
Gleet. Gonorrhea. Heartburn. Hepatitis. Herniated, disks. Herpes. Hoarseness. Injuries. Insomnia.
Levitation. Mastoiditis. Migraines. Numbness. Offensive, sweat. Otitis. Pityriasis, versicolor. Post-nasal,
catarrh. Psoriasis. Ringworm. Scarlet fever. Sacro-iliac, pain. Sciatica. Spinal, irritation. Threadworms.
Vertigo. Worms. Yawning.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tellurium occurs in the native state and in combination with gold, silver, lead and antimony.
It resembles sulphur and selenium in its chemical reactions. Tellurium is an element situated between antimony
and iodine; it was discovered in a gold mineral by the Austrian Muller in 1782.
The proving was conducted by Hering in about 1850 on fourteen provers, using the low potencies. A new
proving was established by Raeside in London. He conducted a proving on seventeen provers, eleven women
and six men. The provers took the remedy night and morning for fourteen days. The potencies 6x and 6c
produced the maximum symptoms.
The most notable feature of the provings was the irritation of the skin, including the skin of the eyelids and
ears, of the spinal column and of some nerves. Dryness of the skin and mucus membranes. Herpes circi-
natus, ringworm, especially of the face and body. Vesicular, burning, itching eruptions. Itching, urticarial or
macular eruption.
Offensive discharges. Chronic fetid suppuration from the ear. Persistent fetid body odor. Heavy perspiration
from the feet, extremely foul-smelling.
 Restlessness and pains all over body. Very sensitive back. Pain in the cervical, right lumbar and sciatic
regions. Sacral and sciatic pains. Slight amnesia with frontal headache. Lassitude. Afraid, cannot bear to be
touched on sensitive areas. Slow development of symptoms (Rad-br.).
MIND - Rough and angular disposition. Excitable, disposed to fly into a passion. Afraid of any movement and
of anyone approaching them. Fear of being touched in sensitive places.
Lassitude. Quiet disposition. Absentminded. Neglectful and forgetful, when engaged in doing one thing,
forgets and neglects others. Incapable of mental activity. Amnesia, inability to fix the memory on immediate
events. Depressed. Depressive psychosis. Serene and cheerful, then impatient and irritable.
Abdomen - Fullness and oppression in hypogastrium, clothing must be loosened. Pressing first left, then right
side, as from wind. When lying on left side, throbbing under right ribs, and vice versa. Pinching in abdomen.
Frequent spasmodic pains in bowels as from incarcerated wind, mostly from 5 to 9 p.m.
Back - Weak feeling in back. Vertebral pain from last cervical to fifth dorsal vertebra, very sensitive to
pressure and touch (Chin-s., Phos.). Herniated disks (Aesc, Agar.). Sensitive spinal column with coughing,
straining. Pressing ache in scapula. Numbness in nape and occiput. Pain in sacrum. Neck pain, spreading to
the shoulder and between the scapulae. Lumbar pain spreading to the right thigh, ameliorated by walking.
Afraid of any movement and of anyone approaching.
Breasts - Cutting around and in left nipple, through to scapula. Eruption about nipple.
Causations - Falls, injuries. Eating rice causes vomiting. Eating and drinking improves sore throat.
Chest - Pain in the sternum, aggravated by deep breaths and by bending. Pressure in middle of chest under
sternum, better in open air. Shooting in left chest, fifth rib. Feeling as if some fluid is pressing downward in,
from right lung.
Ears - Catarrh of middle ear. Chronic suppurating otitis. Otitis after scarlet fever. Fetid, irritating discharge,
smells of brine from the ear, especially the left ear. Chronic mastoiditis. Itching, swelling, throbbing in meatus.
Dull, throbbing pain in ears, day and night, thin, watery, excoriating discharge. Ache in the left ear. Vesicular
eruption on the eardrum, suppurating and perforating. Eczema behind ears with formation of thick crusts.
Deafness. Buzzing, ringing in the ears.
Eyes - Pustular conjunctivitis, with eczema on lids and much purulent discharge from eyes. Deposit of chalky-
looking white mass on anterior surface of lens. Cataract, following ocular lesions. Aids the absorption of
infiltrations in iris and choroid. Herpes conjunctivae, phlyctenules near edge of cornea, worse from crying. The
eyelids are thickened and inflamed, with pustules, pale red, edematous and oozing. Feeling as if lashes of
lower lid were turned in.
Face - Heat in face. Sudden flushes of redness over face. Distortion and twitching in left facial muscles, left
corner of mouth drawn up when talking. Ringworm on face. Barber’s itch. Pimples on face. Burning in lips.
Female - Shooting deep in pelvis across to left. Premenstrual colic in lower abdomen. Menses painful and
late. Menses too early in menopausal years. Long intervals between menses.
Food - Craving for apples, fatty bacon, salt, bread during the evening, cold drinks, beer. Hungry at night. After
meals, great drowsiness. Vomits after eating rice.
Head - Feeling of heat in the head. Heaviness and fullness of head in morning. Pain in left side of head and in
forehead above left eye. Periodic headaches. Migraines. Sudden rush of blood to head. Congestion to head
and nape of neck, followed by weakness and faintness in stomach. Brain feels as if beaten on slightest
movement. Violent linear pain in small spot over left eye. Itching of scalp, red spots. Numbness of nape and
occiput.
Heart - Dull pain in region of heart when lying on left side, better lying on back. Heart irregular when lying on
the back or right side. Palpitations with throbbing through whole body and full pulse, folio wed by sweat.
Palpitation with sensation of thoracic constriction and pain. Rapid pulse rate.
Kidneys - Painful soreness in kidneys, extending downward like a weight, worse morning, making her irritable.
Increased, high-colored, acid urine.
Limbs - Aching all over, mostly in limbs, worse right side and in walking. Sciatica, right side, worse lying on
affected side. Sciatica with sensitiveness of vertebral column. Weakness of the legs in the morning. Bruised
pain in hip joints after walking. Contraction of tendons in bends of knees. Sharp, quick pains in elbows,
ankles and other parts. Fetid sweat on feet, mostly on toes. Fingertips feel dead on stretching hand.
Rheumatism of right little finger, worse moving it.
Liver - Hepatitis and gastritis. Chronic cholecystitis.
Lungs - Coughing on laughing, worse aching in small of back. Wakened by cough. Cough towards morning,
looser after a few days. Wheezing, scraping cough with mucus. Emphysema.
Male - Herpes on scrotum and perineum. Secondary gonorrhea. A drop of viscid fluid in meatus. Increased
sexual desire, followed by long-lasting indifference. Erections all night.
 Modalities - Better lying on back. Worse while at rest, at night, lying on painful side. Worse in morning, on
waking. Worse cold weather. Worse coughing, laughter. Worse from touch, friction. Spine sensitive to touch.
Eating causes drowsiness.
Mouth - Dryness of the lips and mouth with raw, irritated areas. Ulcerations on the gums tongue, mouth, palate.
Gums bleed easily and profusely. Tongue somewhat swollen, furred white, shows print of teeth. Breath has
odor of garlic. Copious saliva. Tenacious mucus runs from mouth. Taste earthy, metallic. Coldness of mouth
and pharynx on drawing in air.
Nose - Hawks dried yellowish-red phlegm from posterior sinuses, salty tasting, in mornings. Coryza,
lachrymation and hoarseness, better in open air (All-c.). Nose obstructed, must breathe through mouth. Head
cold with running of a blood- streaked liquid accompanied by tears and hoarseness, ameliorated in the open
air. Nostrils itch. Boils.
Perspiration - Offensivefoot-sweat. Heavy perspiration from the feet, extremely foul-smelling. Offensive
sweat of armpits, smelling of garlic. Sweat on face, on spots.
Rectum - Very offensive flatus. Spasmodic pains with urging to stool. Stools soft at first, then hard. Copious
stool with feeling of flatulence in bowels. Costive. Itching anus, rectum and perineum after stool. Tetter on
perineum, itching. Passes many threadworms with stool.
Sensations - As if in air on going to sleep. Brain as if beaten. As if lashes were turned in. As if air whistled
through left Eustachian tube. As if strapped together in epigastric region. As if fluid wanted to discharge in lobe
of right lung.
Skin - Skin dry, hot. Stinging in skin. Barber’s itch. Herpetic spots, ringworm (Tub.), worse lower limbs, on
single parts. Ring-shape lesions. Circular patches of eczema. Small red pimples, very bright red and very
sharply defined with minute vesicles upon them. Psoriasis. Scrofulous eczematous eruption. Eczema, back of
ears and occiput. Itching of hands and feet. Itching worse in cool air. Offensive odors from affected parts. Fetid
exhalations (Sulph.).
Sleep - Drowsy after a meal. Yawning and belching. Insomnia with unpleasant dreams. Sleepless, restless
turning from weariness and bruised feeling. At night, pains all over. On going to sleep, feels as if in air, quick
drawing towards feet wakens him. Wakes with a start during the night.
Stomach - Empty and weak feeling. Sensation of weakness, like faintness in the stomach after local
congestion of blood to head and nape, also with chest symptoms.
Heartburn with warmth in stomach as from alcohol. Belching with taste of food eaten. Fullness in pit of stomach,
must lie down after dinner. Constrictive feeling in stomach as if strapped together.
Temperature - Inner shivering and fever, fetid, repulsive sweating, forcing him to be alone. Chilly with pains.
Sweat on face, on spots, with increased itching of these places, often throbbing through whole body, generally
warm, while sitting in a cool breeze. Skin hot and dry, sensation as if overstrained, as if bruised, as if he had
taken cold after severe exertion.
Throat - Hoarseness in morning with fluent coryza, a rough, pressing, tickling sensation in larynx. In morning,
hawks pieces of salty, yellowish-reddish phlegm. Painful dryness of fauces. Rough, scratching sensation in
throat, worse towards evening. Throat feels sore with a prickly, rough sensation evening and morning. Throat
sore on swallowing, better after eating or drinking. Pain in throat extends into ear.
Vertigo - Vertigo, when going to sleep, morning after rising. Vertigo worse walking, sitting up or turning head.
Vertigo better lying perfectly quiet and still.
COMMENTS - Ringworm, herpes. Offensive, garlic-like odor of the body and sweat. Fishy odors and
discharges (Hep., Sanie). Offensive foot sweats (Sil.). Vesicating effect on the skin, hair-roots, breasts,
perineum and anus. Acrid discharge, blisters any part of the skin it touches.
Otorrhea. Discharge of the ear smells of fish brine. Nash cured several cases of postscarlatina otorrhea using
Tell. 6c, higher potencies had failed. Eyelids are inflamed. Phlyctenular conjunctivitis. Itching in the rectum
after stool. Threadworms.
Great sensitiveness to touch. Neuralgic hypersensitive state of the spine. Painful spots along the spinal cord
(Agar.). Injuries to the spine and pelvic bones. Radiating pain down both thighs from an injury to the sacroiliac
area. Pains are sharp and radiating, or electric-like. Contractures. Pressing pain in the scapula. Neuralgic
symptoms, especially on the right side.
Sciatica. Sciatic pain deep in the leg, behind the knee. Herniated disks (Aesc, Agar.). Sacro-iliac problems
with radiating pains (Aesc, Hyper.). Worse lying on the affected part, from touch, worse in C7 to T5 and in the
Sacro-iliac joint.
Many of the pains and symptoms come and go suddenly. The ears are suddenly stopped. Sudden rushes of
blood to the head. Drowsiness. Yawning after retching, drowsy after eating.
Clarke once gave Tell, to a child for an eruption and cured it incidentally of constant yawning with which it had
 been troubled. The eruption improved at the same time.
Clarke also cured with Tell, an Indian officer home on furlough whose body was covered over with a ringworm-
like eruption.
Kent had a case in which a boy, 4, slid down banisters and struck his head on a tiled floor. He became
unconscious and a surgeon was summoned, who found him unconscious with a clear, watery discharge from
the ear, which the surgeon pronounced to be cerebrospinal fluid.
This condition lasted three days and the case had been pronounced hopeless when Kent first saw the boy.
Kent noticed that the discharge was acrid and reddened whatever part it came in contact with. One dose of
Tell, was given. In two hours the child vomited, a sign of reaction, and in two weeks was well.
Shelton related three cases using Tell. The first concerned a widow, 50, who had pain and soreness in the
upper part of her back for a long time. She shrank from the slightest touch on the part. The sensitiveness was
so acute that, when touched, the pain extended into the occiput and all over the upper region of the back. Tell.
6c cured in eighteen days.
The second case concerned Miss X., 45, who had a fall, striking a severe blow on the sacrum. She suffered
for some weeks from concussion with one point of great soreness in the sacral region, just above the spot
where the blow was received. She was kept in bed for some weeks and improved generally, but the painful
spot remained and sensitiveness
appeared over the back, especially its upper third. Tell. 6c cured all completely.
The third case concerned Miss Y., 29, who had severe spinal meningitis ten years before, and consulted
Shelton for a burning, pressing pain at base of brain. He diagnosed the condition as meningitis. The patient
grew worse and gradually ptosis, and then right and then left hemiplegia set in.
Finally hyperesthesia of the back became so distressing that it was a question of finding any support that did
not intensify the pain. She could not bear the slightest touch, complaining that it not only hurt her at the point
of contact, but that she felt it in the head and in remote parts of the body. Tell, cleared up the case.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Nux-v. (epigastric oppression). Compare: (1) Rad-br., Berb., Hyper., Sei. (2)
Tet. - coccygodynia, ulceration of nails, pains in hands in small spots, ankles, heels and Achilles tendon, (3)
Sep., Ars., Rhus-t. (4) Restlessness, garlicky odor, Ars. (5) Coryza, All-c. (6) Otitis, Puls., Bell., Ter. (7)
Ringworm, Bac., Sep., Nairn. (8) Ringworm in clusters Sep., Calc. (9) Threadworms. Teucr. (10) Pains come
and go suddenly, Bell., Lyc. ( 11) Worse laughing, Phos. (12) Worse straining at stool ind. (13) Cough and
skin, Osm.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

CLINICAL - Axilla, sweat. Backache. Barber’s itch. Boils. Cataract. Cholecystitis. Conjunctivitis. Coryza.
Coughs. Eczema. Entropion. Eruptions. Eye, inflammation. Deafness. Emphysema. Foot, sweat. Gastritis.
Gleet. Gonorrhea. Heartburn. Hepatitis. Herniated, disks. Herpes. Hoarseness. Injuries. Insomnia.
Levitation. Mastoiditis. Migraines

name: Teplitz Aqua
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tep. Teplitz aqua. Teplitz Mineral Springs of Teplitz in Bohemia. Teplitz aqua, contains:
Natrumcarbonicum, Natrum muriaticum, Natrum fluorica, Natrum sili- cata, Kali sulphuricum. Kali muriaticum,
Calcarea carbónica, Silica, etc. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Bones disorders. Breast, tumors. Eruptions. Erysipelas. Flatulence. Gout.
Hemorrhoids. Irritability. Leucorrhea. Metrorrhagia. Nosebleed. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Scurvy.
Speech, difficult. Spine, pains. Tongue, paralysis. Toothache. Ulcers. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - The waters of Teplitz are chiefly in repute for the treatment of gouty patients, especially
those suffering from atonic gout. The springs are alkaline and hot, and the temperature forms a leading feature
in their action.
The symptoms of Tep. are from Perutz, who experimented on himself and several healthy individuals, together
with symptoms by Hromada. Symptoms of Nat-c. and Nat-m. appear throughout. Tearfulness, low spirits and
irritability were noted and giddiness of much intensity. “Giddiness, when she walks all the houses seem to
move too.”
Modalities - Better by friction. Better drinking cold water. The symptoms are worse at night, especially bone
pains. Worse from motion.
COMMENTS - On moving head it seems as if something fell from one side to the other. Cold feelings in upper
arm in foot. Increased sensitiveness to cold. Paralysis of tongue of limbs.
Vesicles in mouth and on tongue. Vesicular erysipelas. Burning sensation in many parts. Burning in stomach,
better drinking cold water. Hemorrhage, nosebleed, hemorrhoids with stool, metrorrhagia. Better from
hemorrhoid bleeding.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-c., Nat-m., Kali-s., Mang., Lith., Sil., Alum.
REFERENCES - Clarke.
 ***TEREBINTHINIAE OLEUM
(Oil of Turpentine)
PHARMACY - ter. Terebinthiniae oleum. Oil of Turpentine. Turpentine. Oleum terebinthine. Pinaceae. The oil
distilled from the oleo-resin (turpentine) obtained from various species of Pinus, purified by repeated
rectification with water. Solution in rectified spirit. Ozonized oil of Turpentine (prepared by exposure of the
common oil to sun and air in a half-filled bottle and shaking from time to time'). Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amblyopia. Ascites. Asthma. Backache. Bladder, irritable. Brachial neuralgia.
Bronchitis. Chilblains. Chordee. Chorea. Ciliary neu
ralgia. Coma. Cystitis. Dentition. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Enteric, fever. Epilepsy. Erysipelas.
Erythema. Fibroma. Gallstone, colic. Glands, swelling. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Hematuria. Hem-
orrhage. Hemorrhoids. Hernia. Herpes. Hypochondriasis. Injuries. Insanity. Intestines, ulceration. Iritis.
Jaundice. Kidneys, disorders. Lumbago. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Ovaries, dropsy. Ovaries, pains. Peritonitis.
Pityriasis. Purpura hemorrhagica. Rabies. Scabies. Scarlatina. Sciatica. Spermatorrhea. Strangury. Stricture.
Tetanus. Tympanites. Uremia. Urethritis. Urine, retention. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - Ter. was introduced to homeopathy by Hartlaub. The symptoms have been added to from
poisonings and overdosings in allopathic practice. According to Dr. Taylor, children are particularly sensitive
to its action. Illness caused by sleeping in newly painted rooms is due in great part to the turpentine.
Milnes noted that Ter., as an internal remedy, is “A stimulant and tonic to the mucus membranes, especially
of the bladder and urethra: it proves useful in leucorrhea and gleet.”
Selective affinity for the mucus membranes of kidneys, bladder, respiration, bronchi, heart and blood.
Bleeding mucus surfaces, oozing hemorrhage of a passive, black offensive fluid. Purpura hemorrhagica.
Marked tympanites and urinary symptoms. Inflammation of kidneys with dark, passive, fetid hemorrhages.
Affections of kidneys with rheumatism. Goullon indicated it for Bright’s disease preceded by dropsy.
Aching, soreness and stiffness of the muscles. Even minor bumps cause bruises. Unbroken chilblains.
Burning in various parts, tip of tongue, epigastrium, small of back, kidney, uterus etc. Exhausted, sensitive and
tired. Disturbed sense of equilibrium. Drowsiness and strangury. Coma.
MIND - Anxiety on going to bed. Confusion of mind, better when urinating freely. Tired and difficult
concentration of thoughts. Intense irritability, children fly into tern-
per during dentition. Muttering delirium. Hydrophobia.
Despondent during nervous headache. Fear of apoplexy during fullness and pressure in head. Loathing of life.
Suicidal disposition, by hanging. Comatose, can be roused only by shaking out of apparent stupor, but falls
immediately into it again. Unconsciousness after stool.
Abdomen - Bruised soreness. Dropsy, pelvic peritonitis. Enormous distention. Tympanites. Ascites.
Flatulence. Enterocolitis, hemorrhage and ulceration of bowels. Bowels were drawn towards spine. Bleeding
ulcers in the intestine.
Back - Backache and soreness in kidney disorders. Burning pain in region of kidneys. Drawing in right
kidney, extending to hip.
Causations - Ill effects of alcohol, falls, strains, tooth extraction, damp cellars.
Chest - Burning and tightness across chest.
Constitutions - Suited to children, dentition, nosebleed, worms. Complaints of elderly people, people of
sedentary habits. Chronic rheumatism and gouty complaints. Bleeders. Nervous women with headaches,
amenorrhea and dysmenorrhea. Hydrogenoid.
Ears - Disturbed sense of equilibrium. Own voice sounds unnatural, humming as of a seashell. Loud talking is
very painful. Otalgia. Sensation in ears as of striking of a clock.
Eyes - Opens eyes when swallowing in coma. Eyes dark red, face red on affected side. Intense pain in eye
and side of head. Ciliary neuralgia over right eye. Amblyopia from alcohol.
Face - Pale, earthly, sunken. Hot flushes followed by sweat.
Female - Intense burning in uterine region.
Metritis and puerperal peritonitis. Metrorrhagia with burning in uterus. Uterine diseases after wearing
pessaries.
Food - Hunger and thirst with debility. Diminished appetite, loss of appetite, great thirst. Desire to eat more
after a satisfying meal. Aversion to animal food.
Head - Dull pain like from a band around the head (Carb-ac.).
Heart - Warmth in heart while sitting in evening, obliged to yawn a great deal. Frightful oppression in precordial
region. Palpitations. Rapid, small, thready, intermittent pulse.
Kidneys - Nephritis after exanthemata with violent bronchitis. Burning, drawing pain in region of kidney, along
ureters. Cystitis. Urethritis with painful excretions (Canth.). Bleeding bladder. Constant tenesmus. Strangury
 with bloody urine. Scanty, suppressed urine, odor of violets. Urine, smoky with coffee grounds or thick,
yellow, slimy, muddy sediment. Pains alternate between navel and bladder, better walking.
Limbs - Brachial or sub-scapular neuralgia. Intense pain along the larger nerves, worse damp weather. Stiff
muscles. Hands feel swollen. Cramps in knees. Stands with feet apart, has no power of balancing the body.
As if pitched forward while walking. Walks bent like an old man.
Lungs - Dyspnea. Difficult breathing, the lungs feel distended, hemoptysis. Bronchitis of children with
drowsiness and retention of urine. Bronchial asthma or catarrh with profuse expectoration. Bloody
expectoration.
Modalities - Better from motion, stooping. Better belching and passing flatus. Loose stool better nausea.
Burning in anus better cold water. Worse from dampness, cold. Worse at night, 1 a.m. to 3 a.m. Worse walking
in open air. Worse lying, sitting. Worse pressure, touch. Worse by pressure in region of bladder it causes
convulsions. Worse lying on left side, better turning to right. Pain in crest of ilium worse from motion and least
jar. Damp dwellings aggravates. Damp cellar causes diarrhea. Damp weather causes neuralgia in legs.
Mouth - Foul, cold breath. Dry, red, sore, shining, smooth and glossy tongue, burning in tips with prominent
papillae (Arg-n., Bell., Kali-b„ Nux-m.). Choking sensation in throat; Aphthae from mouth to anus. Dentition.
Nose - Discharge of serum without coryza. Cold in head with sore nostrils, with disposition to bleed. Passive
nosebleed in children.
Perspiration - Suddenly checked sweat causes neuralgia. Suppressed foot sweat causes rheumatic iritis.
Cold sweat on legs. Cold, clammy, all over with prostration. Profuse sweat on legs in evenings in bed.
Rectum - Pain before flatus with and relief after stool. Fainting after every stool. Diarrhea with watery, greenish,
fetid stool. Diarrhea with tetanic spasms. Bloody stools. Hemorrhage from bowels. Worms, lumbrici.
Sensations - As of a band around head. As if sand thrown violently in eye. As of a seashell sounding in left
ear. Sound in ear as of a clock striking. As from hasty swallowing in epigastrium. As if he had swallowed a
bullet, which had lodged in stomach. As if he would pitch forward on walking.
Skin - General sensibility increased. Acne. Erythema, itching pustular, vesicular eruption, urticaria. Purpura
hemorrhagica, advancing. Ecchymosis, dropsies. Scarlatina. Chilblains with excessive itching and pulsative
pains. Aching soreness of the muscles.
Sleep - Drowsiness with urine retention. Lethargy. Retarded sleep. Agitated sleep at night with tossing and
frequent waking. Many dreams, nightmares. Wakes frightened at night, looks ghastly and shrieks.
Stomach - Rancid, flatulent, acrid belchings. Burning in epigastric region. Nausea and vomiting with intense
burning. Nausea, better loose stool. Aversion to meat.
Temperature - Heat under the skin. Heat with violent thirst, dry tongue, profuse cold, clammy sweat. Cold
sweat on legs. Typhoid fever with tympanites, hemorrhages, stupor, delirium. Prostration.
Vertigo - Vertigo with vanishing of vision, nausea. Disturbed sense of equilibrium. Vertigo as if intoxicated, as
if he would fall forward, when walking.
COMMENTS - Brunton noted that Ter., when
applied to the skin, acts as an irritant and rubefacient, causing vesicles and a sensation of burning if applied
for any length of time. Inhaled, it causes sneezing, tightness across the eyes and dyspnea.
Given internally, it causes burning in the mouth and salivation in stomach, sensation of heat or cold, gastro-
enteritis with vomiting and diarrhea, and ulceration of the intestines. The pulse is sometimes slowed,
sometimes quickened.
Respiration is quickened and spasmodic, the chemical is partly excreted by the lungs and acts on the mucus
membrane, lessening its secretion. The temperature sometimes rises, or falls. Voluntary movement is dimin-
ished, reflex action lowered, blood pressure lowered and vessels dilated.
Acute and chronic nephritis. Kidney infections. Protein or blood in the urine. Albuminuria and hematuria after
scarlatina and also to the consequent dropsy. Effects of chemical inhalation of exposure, particularly if there
is kidney damage.
Diminished quantity of urine. Urine has an odor of violets. Lumbar pain, burning in urethra, painful urination.
Hematuria with smoky, turbid urine depositing a sediment like coffee-grounds. Dull pain or burning pain in
region of kidneys. Burning during urination.
Brunton mentioned its usefulness in treating gallstone colic, given in ether in the proportion of one part of the
oil of turpentine to three of ether. Homeopaths have confirmed the value of this treatment.
Characteristic burning. Burning in gums, tongue, tip of tongue, mouth, throat, stomach, rectum and anus,
kidneys, bladder and urethra, uterus, air passages, and chest. Burning in the sternum, particularly after warm
drinks, the pain running along the sternum with the drink and spreading in the chest. Burning extends from
kidneys along ureters.
“Burning in uterus.” Peritonitis, metritis, metrorrhagia with burning. Passive, dark and fetid hemorrhages.
 Hemorrhages from any orifice. Purpura hemorrhagica with fresh ecchymoses in great numbers from day to
day. Smooth, glossy, red tongue, as
Terebinthiniae oleum if deprived of papillae.
Drowsiness. Drowsiness with capillary bronchitis, in child. Stupor and great weakness, particularly in cases of
typhus, typhoid, and uremic poisoning. “Drowsy with retention of urine.”
Excessive tympanites, with extreme sensitiveness to touch. Sensitivity of the hypogastrium and pains in
symphysis pubis with cystitis. Urogenital and rectal troubles. Pains go from left to right across bowels and then
shoot upward.
Sense of anxiety and utter prostration about epigastrium. Umbilical region feels as if covered with a round,
cold plate. Sprained pains, contusive pains and rheumatic pains appear, notably pressure and drawing pains.
Irritation of the meninges and often ascarides or other intestinal worms. Maniacal fury. Cooper found Ter.
indicated in children (especially teething children) when they fly into passions.
Lippe observed that this irritability manifests itself in some cases of spasms and convulsions. He had a case
of a woman who had made her feet sore by walking and applied turpentine to them. This was followed by a
state like hydrophobia, she had spasms whenever she saw water, heard it poured, or saw a bright object and
also whenever she attempted to urinate.
Cooper noted the case of a woman, 35, who, from being exposed to the odor of turpentine, got pain as from
pinchings in the throat with lifeless feeling in the tongue and dryness of the mouth, followed by pain in her right
eyeball, which extended back to the same side of occiput.
S. H. Roberts maintained that Ter. had a specific effect in tonsillitis when applied externally.
Marc Jousset gave Ter. lx with marked benefit in two cases of bronchial asthma. He was led to give it in the
first case by coincident hematuria, but this was not present in the second.
A young man who was badly poisoned by a low potency of Phos. got more relief from Ter. 3x than from any
other remedy.
Brunton argued that it is only ozonized Ter. that is effective in such cases. Dr. Hering says the ozonized oil is
recommended as a prophylactic in malarial and African fevers, a few drops being given daily on a lump of
sugar.
George Royal gave three cases illustrating the action of Ter. The first concerned a man, 24, with typhoid in the
third week. He had extreme distention, with a rapid, small and compressible pulse. Cold sweat in lower limbs.
Ter. 6x was given, two drops in water every half-hour. Oil of Ter. was applied locally to the abdomen, mixed
with lard. Later in the evening, when there was already slight improvement, an injection containing turpentine
was administrated. This relieved the patient of a large quantity of flatus and he began to recover the next
morning.
The second case concerned pyemia after miscarriage at the third month, brought on by the patient herself.
Enormous distention, lower limbs covered with cold sweat, lochia thin, scanty offensive.
Ter. given in another case brought about slow improvement for three days, when Chin. 30c was indicated and
finished the cure.
The third case from Royal concerned a teamster, 36, who had severe nephritis after being out in cold rain. He
had a constant desire to urinate, severe pain in back, down ureter to bladder, urine scanty, very high-colored.
Temperature 102. Pulse weak, 130. Ter. 6x was given every half-hour and hot fomentations on kidneys greatly
relieved. After three days he was able to leave his bed.
Royal considered cold sweat of lower limbs and rapid pulse with the distention, as leading indications. A
keynote of Burnett’s forTer. is “Pains in the bowels which causes frequent urination.”
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Phos. Antidote to: Phos., Merc. Compare: ( 1 ) Alumn., Sec., Canth., Nit-ac. (2)
Terebe. lx - chronic bronchitis and winter coughs, sub-acute stages of inflammation of respiratory tract.
Loosens secretion, relieves tightened feel- ing, makes expectoration easy. Neurotic coughs. Huskiness of
public speakers and singers. (3) Cystitis when urine is alkaline and offensive. (4) Onon. - Diuretic. Chronic
nephritis, diuretic effects like Juniper, calculus, nosebleed, worse washing face. Followed well by: Merc-c.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

name: Terminalia Arjuna
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - term-a. Terminaba arjuna. N. O. Combretaceae. Bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Boils. Contusions. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Ecchymosis. Fractures. Gonorrhea.
Heart, diseases. Hemorrhages. Palpitations. Spermatorrhea. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Wounds.
HERBAL - Terminaba arjuna is a large, deciduous tree measuring a height of 60 to 80 feet. Sanskrit writers
found the bark to be a cardiac tonic. Bagbhata was the first to prescribe the bark in heart diseases.
 The ayurvedic physicians of India have been using this herb independently or as one of the ingredients in all
sorts of heart diseases with marked success for a long time. They use it in both functional and organic diseases
of the heart. Angina pectoris, palpitations of the heart, pain in the heart, weakness of the heart.
Fractures. Pains all over the body owing to a fall. Ecchymosis. Hemorrhages. Spermatorrhea and gonorrhea.
Charaka used it in hematemesis. He prescribed equal quantities of the bark, pulverized red sandalwood, sugar
and rice water. Its leaves are also used for boils.
Sushruta used a decoction of the bark with equal quantity of white sandalwood in spermatorrhea. Harita found
it useful in gonorrhea.
Bangasena has recommended it in chronic diarrhea and dysentery. Bagbhata recommended its decoction for
suppression and retention of urine. He also recommended an ointment prepared of the bark and honey in
acne.
Chakradatta found it useful in bloody
Terminalia arjuna dysentery and in cardiac affections. He also recommended it in fractures. Bhavaprakasha
recommended it for tuberculosis of the lungs and for suppression and retention of urine.
COMMENTS - R. N. Khory in his Materia Medica of India, vol. II, wrote, “Astringent ad tonic given in heart
disease. Locally used as a wash for wounds, ulcers, contusions and specially used in promoting union of
fractures and dispersion of ecchymosis. Internally, largely used by the natives in hemorrhagic and other fluxes
and as a lithontriptic.”
REFERENCES – Ghose

name: Terminalia Chebula
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - term-c. Terminalia chebula. Myrobalans. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Catarrh. Colds. Colic. Constipation. Cough. Delirium tremens. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery.
Elephantiasis. Glands, enlarged. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Jaundice. Rheumatism. Salivation.
Scorpion, sting. Spleen, enlarged. Stomach, disorders. Typhoid fever. Vomiting. Whitlow.
HERBAL - R. N. Khory. Materia Medica of India, vol. II, p. 260, said, “Purgative, astringent and alternative.
The ripe fruits are generally purgative and the unripe ones astringent and aperient.”
Lt. Col. R. N. Chopra, I. M.S., wrote in his book Indigenous Drugs of India, p. 532, “It is astringent, laxative,
alternative; used in scorpion sting.”
Charaka found it useful in bleeding piles, diseases of the stomach, chronic dysentery, jaundice due to cough,
cold and catarrhs, and vomiting.
Sushruta recommended it in rheumatism, blind piles, elephantiasis, chronic enlargement of the spleen and
glandular enlargement of the abdomen and hiccough.
Bagbhata prized it is an excellent remedy for piles, stone and calculus and throat affections ad as a tonic.
Harita recommended it in hemorrhages of the stomach and lungs.and delirium tremens.
Chakradatta found it useful in rheumatism, dropsy and in several affections of the eye. Bhavaprakasha
recommended it in typhoid fever, chronic diarrhea and dysentery and biliary colic.
Bangasena said that it is an excellent remedy in diarrhea associated with colicky pains and also in whitlow.
HOMEOPATHIC - Term-c. is an indigenous remedy, very much used in ayurvedic medicine. The symptoms
for homeopathic use are ineffectual desire, hard stools, distended abdomen, and bleeding hemorrhoids.
Therapeutic action to clear the bowels. Constipation, chronic dysentery, dropsy, chronic diarrhea. Frequent in
effectual desire to pass stools, but the patient passes only small quantity of feces with great force. Sweat
breaks out during stool. For piles, some skin diseases.
Vertigo, relieved by cold bathing. Profuse salivation with great thirst which accompanies all affections.
Offensive odor comes out of the mouth. Tongue is flabby, dry, and covered with a brown coating on tip of the
tongue.
MIND - Mind indifferent. Single mindedness. Easily indisposed to yawn, constant yawning.
Abdomen - Rumbling and gurgling sounds in abdomen. Flatulence. Pain in right lower abdomen.
Back - Intense pain in back (right lumbar region and lower spinal column). Sitting is painful due to pain, often
at intervals. Pain increased while sitting straight, and decreased altogether while lying on bed and during sleep.
Pain in back of neck.
Chest - Intense pressive pain in right chest.
Food - Thirst for drinking cold water.
Head - Headache in occiput and right cranium with intense vertigo. Stitching pain in right temporal region and
occipital suture.
Heart - Pressive pain in region of heart. Pulse is accelerated and quick in motion, irregular. Pulse for some
 moments is rapid, hard and for some moments is
weak simultaneously. Some heartbeats are feeble or of low sound, some normal and some of loud sound,
everything in successive order.
Limbs - Muscular pain in right upper hand. Pain in the region of deltoid muscle. Itching pains relieved by
scratching.
Liver - Slight pain in the region of liver (large lobe). Pain better temporarily by external pressure.
Lungs - Hot deep breathing.
Modalities - Every complaint is better by cold bathing. Better dry, cold air. Better while eating. Better closing
the eyes, sleeping, evening. Better during complete rest of mind and body.
Mouth - Fetid odor in mouth. Profuse salivation with intense thirst. Sensation of dryness in upper jaw. Gums
of teeth swollen and hard.
Rectum - Sweats while passing stool. Pressive itching and full sensation in rectum. Constipation, stool hard,
of small quantity, and slightly yellowish. Diarrhea, stools is liquid, and small in quantity. Feces mixed with some
mucus, flatulence associated with burning sensation in the stomach.
Stomach - Sensation of fullness in stomach. Distension of stomach. Downward pain in stomach and
epigastrium. Rumbling and gurgling sounds in stomach. Fetid eructation. In the morning constant acid, empty
eructation.
Stool - Frequent ineffectual desire for passing stool, but passes very small quantity of feces with great force
or sometimes with ineffectual action to pass stool. After much trying a little quantity of feces comes out with
great force.
Tongue - Flabby, dry, tongue. Brown coating on tip of tongue. Sore and raw tongue.
Urine - Quantity of urine is slightly diminished. Frequency of urination is increased at night.
Vertigo - Vertigo remains all the day and night for hours. Vertigo is worse by hot sun’s rays, hard pressure
and motion. Vertigo is better by cold bathing, evening dry cold air and during sleep and eating. Intense vertigo
begins in occiput and spreads to the whole right side of the head (right temporal region to right frontal region).
RELATIONS - Compare: Chin., Nux-v., Lyc.
REFERENCES - Ghose.

name: Testosterone
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - test. Testosterone. Male hormone. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Baldness. Bleeding. Cancer. Emaciation. Fatigue. Hepatitis. Im- potency. Jaundice.
Menstrual, disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - Low levels of Testosterone can cause symptoms of fatigue, malaise, loss of sex drive, and
loss of muscle tissue.
Anabolic steroids are compounds related to testosterone. The most common side effects of using Testosterone
in both men and women include increased facial and body hair, oily skin or acne, male pattern baldness, water
retention joint stiffness, and soreness at the injection site. Lab tests may show increased levels of liver
enzymes.
A deepened or hoarsened voice, growth of the clitoris, and menstrual irregularities have been reported in
women. The masculinizing side effects may be irreversible in women, even with short term use.
At higher doses over longer periods, increased or decreased sex drive, mood swings, aggressive behavior,
persistent painful erections, shrinking testicles, and breast growth have been reported in men. Long term use
of high dose anabolics can damage the liver, causing jaundice, hepatitis, bleeding, or, possibly, cancer.
RELATIONS - Compare: Orch., Sep.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Tetracycline
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tetra. Tetracycline. Antibiotic. The attenuations are prepared from the antibiotic, Tetracycline
hydrochloride. Potentized allopathic drug. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Agranulocytosis. Allergies.
Tetracycline Anemia. Blood, disorders. Convalescence. Diarrhea. Dystonia. Headache. Hives. Nausea.
Photophobia. Rash. Skin, disorders. Sores. Tinnitus. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Protracted convalescence. Post-infectious anemia. Agranulocytosis. Blood disorders.
Dizziness, light headed- ness. Headache, bulging soft spot on head (in infants). Blurred vision. Ringing in the
ears. Muscle weakness.
Extreme allergic reactions. Rash. Skin peeling. Skin eruptions. Inflammation of the tongue, of the upper
 digestive tract. Hives, inflammation of large bowel. Genital or anal sores or rash. Inflammation of the penis.
Sore throat and inflammation. Sore mouth and perineal itching due to overgrowth of yeasts. Difficult or painful
swallowing. Indigestion. Irritation of the gastrointestinal mucosa. Autonomic dystonia. Diarrhea or loose stools.
Cramps or burning of the stomach. Abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. Loss of appetite.
Bone deformation. Discoloration of teeth. Swelling due to fluid accumulation. Liver poisoning. Photosensitivity.
Prone to sunburns. Exaggerated sunburn.
RELATIONS - Compare: Ars., Fl-ac., Nit- ac.
REFERENCES - Murphy. Reckeweg.

Photophobia. Rash. Skin, disorders. Sores. Tinnitus. Vomiting.

name: Tetradymitum
author: Murphy
full:

contain about 60 parts of bismuth, 33 of tellurium, 6 of sulphur and traces of selenium and iron. Triturations.
Historical dose: All potencies.

from eating shell-fish. Pains in ankles, heels and Achilles tendons were also severe, worse rising from a seat.

name: Teucrium Marum Verum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-teucr.Teucriummarumverum. Cat-thyme. Marum verum. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of whole fresh
plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Locally for polyps, dry powder.
CLINICAL - Anorexia. Anus, itching. Ascarides. Cachexia. Colic. Concussion. Eyelids, tumor. Fibroma.
Hiccoughs. Ingrown, toenail. Nasal, catarrh. Otalgia. Ozaena. Polyps. Psoriasis. Rheumatism.
Threadworms. Urethra, excrescences. Uterine, fibroids. Worms.
HERBAL - The Germander group of the Labiatae, to which the Teucriums belong, had an important place in
old herbal medicine, and homeopathy has placed Teucr. on a firm foundation. Stapf and others proved it.
HOMEOPATHIC - Worm infestations, irritation of anus and nose. Threadworms. Worms and polyps suggest
a tubercular taint and Clarke has used both Teucr. and Teucr. scorod. in tubercular cases.
Nasal polyps. Guernsey noted “Polyps with stoppage of nose on side lain on. large red pimples under right
nostril near septum, sore and smarting to touch.”
Chronic nasal catarrh with atrophy, large offensive crusts and clinkers. Ozaena. Loss of sense of smell.
Fibrous tumor of the eyelid.
Affections of children. Suitable after too much medicine has been taken. Over sensitiveness. Desire to
stretch. Urethral granulations following gonorrhea and also uterine fibroids.
Abdomen - Pressure in abdomen. Expulsion of much flatus, having the smell of rotten eggs. Incarceration of
flatus. Colic with tearing drawings. Cutting pain after drinking beer or water.
Back - Burning in left scapula. Rheumatic drawing and tension in back.
Causations - Concussion (brain). Injuries likely to set up tetanus.
Chest - Chest loaded, with sensation of dryness in trachea. Squeezing pressure in lower part of chest, with
anxious uneasi
ness, without affecting the breathing.
Constitutions - Suited to elderly persons and children. When too much medicine has produced an over-
sensitive condition and remedies fail to act.
Ears - Otalgia. Shootings and tearings in ears. Hissing and ringing.
Eyes - Eyes red, inflamed. Smarting in canthi, lids red and puffy, tarsal tumor (Staph.).
Female - Smooth pedunculate, pear-shaped polypus of vagina, protruding three inches beyond hymen.
Food - Hunger in morning and evening. Appetite increased. Sensation of hunger, as if the food were
unsatisfying and which hinders sleep. Bitter taste in gullet after dinner. Cuttings or nausea with inclination to
vomit after drinking water.
Head - Excited, tremulous feeling. Frontal pain, worse stooping. Strengthens brain after delirium tremens.
Limbs - Tearing pains in arms and legs. Affection of fingertips and joints of toes. Pain in toenails, as if they
had grown into flesh.
Lungs - Dry cough, excited by a tickling in trachea, as if dust had been inspired, worse by coughing. Moldy
taste in throat when hawking up mucus, expectoration profuse.
 Male - Sexual desire decreased. Drawing pain behind left side of root of penis, extending to left side of scrotum,
became sore to touch. Pressive, drawing sensation from abdomen into cords and testes. Burning, pressing,
biting in fore part of urethra when not urinating. Excrescences in urethra following gonorrhea.
Modalities - Desires exercise in open air, which does not fatigue. Moving improves. Worse by touch. Worse
sitting, stooping, on side lain on. Disinclined for exertion. Worse warmth, warmth of bed, wet weather. Worse
evening and at night.
Mouth - Foul breath. Mouth clammy. Much mucus in mouth. Smarting as from pepper, first on left, later also
on right side. Smarting in root of the tongue.
Nose - Catarrhal condition of both anterior and posterior nostrils. Mucus polyps. Chronic catarrh, Discharge
of large, irregular clinkers. Crawling in nostrils with lachrymation and sneezing. Coryza with stoppage of
nostrils.
Rectum - Itching of anus and constant irritation in the evening in bed. Crawling in the rectum after stool.
Ascarides with nightly restlessness. Swelling, itching, and creeping at anus as from ascarides. Frequent
itching and tingling in anus, often after the evacuations. Copious fetid evacuations of the consistence of pap.
Sensations - As if air forced through mucus in ear. As if right nostril were partly stopped. Chill as from
abdomen. Sensation as from flea bites. As if nail had grown into flesh of right great toe.
Skin - Very dry skin. Itching causes tossing about all night. Suppurating grooves in the nails.
Sleep - Sleep retarded in evening. Restless with twitching, choking and starting up frightened. Unrefreshing
sleep and difficulty in waking in morning. Agitated sleep at night, from excessive excitement. Vivid dreams and
frequent starts.
Stomach - Vomiting of large quantities of dark-green masses. Constant hiccough, attended with pain in back.
Hiccough on eating after nursing.
Temperature - Shivering and shaking, often with icy coldness in hands, and frequent yawning. Chilliness after
eating, and when talking about unpleasant things. Heat worse in evening, with exaltation and great loquacity.
Frequent feeling of flushing in face, without external redness.
Throat - Sore throat with shooting pain and impeded deglutition. Pressure or drawing and tearing in throat.
Frequent necessity to hawk. Hawking up of much mucus of a moldy taste.
COMMENTS - Clarke gave Teucr. tincture in five-drop doses three times a day to a man of 44 who had
tuberculosis affecting the right lung with severe recurrent hemorrhages. Teucr. helped him, and with other
remedies he got quite well. While taking Teucr. he noticed that he passed a large quantity of threadworms to
which he was not at all subject.
C. M. Boger related a case of cough in which his patient had with the cough a moldy taste in the throat when
hawking up mucus. Expectoration profuse. Rapid loss of weight and strength. Anorexia. A brother had died of
tuberculosis four years before with very similar symptoms. Teucr. 3x helped and 20x finished the cure.
Teucr. has the craving hunger of the anti- psorics and worm remedies, it prevents sleep at night. Nervous,
irritable, sensitive. Rheumatic and gouty symptoms and scapular pains, both in the bones and joints. Limbs go
to sleep with tingling when sitting.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1) Teucr-s. (2) Cina, Ign., Sang., Sil. Compatible: Chin.,
Puls., Sil.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Teucrium Scorodonia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - teucr-s. Teucrium scorodonia. Wood sage. Wood germander. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of whole
fresh plant. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Asthma. Bronchorrhea. Catarrhs. Coryza. Coughs. Epidymitis. Nasal, catarrh. Testicle,
tuberculosis. Tuberculosis.
HERBAL - Teucrium scorodonia is an extremely bitter plant with the smell and taste of hops, for which it has
been substituted. Some have observed an alliaceous smell and Cazin said that it gives agarlicky taste to the
milk of cows, goats and sheep which eat it.
HOMEOPATHIC - Teucr-s. has been used in tuberculosis with muco-purulent expectoration. Dropsy orchitis
and tuberculous epidymitis, especially in young, thin individuals with tuberculosis of lungs, glands, bones
and uro-genitals.
It is used as an adjuvant in severe afflictions of the lungs. Remarkable results have been observed in chronic
catarrhs of the lungs and bronchi, in nasal catarrhs, coryza, cough and asthma bronchiale.
COMMENTS - Dr. Criquelion told how Dr. Martiny one day in the Ardennes, had occasion to examine a man
of thirty who was apparently in the last stage of consumption and had a cavity in one apex. Martiny gave his
 opinion that he had not long to live.
A year later, being in the same district, he called at the house and inquired of a man whom he saw there,
apparently in perfect health, what had become of the in valid. “I am he,” was the reply. It was the fact, though
it took some time to convince Martiny of it.
An old woman had recommended him to make a tisane of the wood germander which grew abundantly about
there. He had taken it daily and got well. “A similar case,” said Cooper, “was told me by a distinguished scientist.
Martiny introduced Teucr-s. into his practice and used a tisane of it with much success in bronchorrhea and
consumptive disorders with tuberculous elements and muco-purulent expectoration. Clarke confirmed this,
using the tincture in five or ten-drop doses two or three times a day.
Criquelion pointed out that Teucrine has been used as a subcutaneous injection in tubercular cases as a
substitute for Koch’s Tub. Criquelion had a patient, a farmer of scrofulous habit, high color, thick neck, who
had for ten years an enlarged testicle the size of a quince, which he diagnosed to be tuberculous.
Teucr-s. 6c was given, one drop in four spoonfuls of water, a spoonful three-quarters of an hour before each
meal. After three months the testicle was softer in six months it had almost returned to its proper size.
RELATIONS - Teucr-s. is allied to Marrubium vulgare (Common or White Horehound), a well-known cough
remedy. Also to Nepeta glechoma (Ground Ivy), which was formerly muchused with snail-jellyforchest
affections.” Compare: (1) Bac., Tub., Teucr., Helix.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Thalamus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - thala. Thalamus. Gray nuclei around the encephalon. Nerve-hormonal tissue from brain.
Sarcode. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Catatonia. Contractures. Cyanosis. Hebephrenia. Hyperthyroidism. Menopausal,
complaints.
Neuralgias. Pains. Parkinson’s disease. Raynaud’s syndrome. Sciatica. Vasomotor, complaints.
HOMEOPATHIC - Thala. belongs to the group of gray nuclei around the encephalon. It is a large ganglion,
even and symmetrical. Situated in front of and outside the quadrigeminal bodies inside the striped bodies.
Laterally bordering the third ventricle, surrounded on its convexity by the caudate nucleus. It is egg-shaped
and the distal end is large.
Hardy conducted a clinical proving, but there is no homeopathic proving. Complaints of the psychological
system, including spasmodic laughter and cry ing, consciousness disorders inner sensitivity disorders. Patient
misinterprets his illnesses.
Pseudo-bulbar paralysis. Neuralgias, cervical and brachial, sciatica. Tabes. Painful stumps. Vasomotor
disorders. Parkinson’s disease. Pre-cancerous conditions, predominantly painful.
Paresthesia in the female during the menopause. Formication, painful numbness situated particularly in the
arms and which keeps the patient awake. Tingling, which is always distal and which appears with no apparent
cause. Neuralgia of the left cervical region and arm with formication.
Pains accompanied by phenomena of anguish, ill-defined feeling of uneasiness, painful discomfort.
Spontaneous pains, appear suddenly and then immediately reach their peak intensity. The painful sensation
is much greater than the stimulus. Exaggerated pain. Violent attacks of paroxysm. Pains reside in one half of
the body, predominantly of the limbs. Pain accompanied by sweating.
MIND - Catatonic conditions. State of inertia, desire for solitude and peace, loss of initiative. The patient does
not want to do anything. He sits in a comer, immobile. Condition of psychological strain, which causes the
feeling of being ill at ease in his body. Hebephrenia.
Spasmodic laughing and crying without any real cause, expressed by involuntary, automatic contracture of the
muscles in the face and by mimicry, which is either ill-times or irrelevant or exaggerated.
Abdomen - Epigastric pain in a continuous transverse bar, not changed by eating, but aggravated by emotion.
Pain is diffuse, badly localized. Accompanied by discomfort. Abdominal meteorism ameliorated by emission of
wind. Abdominal pains with emission of soft stools.
Chest - He feels as though his thoracic cage were trapped inside an iron corset.
Constitutions - Psoric, syphilitic or tubercular disposition. Nervous, biliary and lymphatic temperament.
Ears - Hallucinations of hearing with feeling of strangeness and fright. Buzzing in the ears, sound of a bell in
the fog or of a foghorn. Noises in the ears. Feeling of confusion in the ears.
Eyes - Sight becomes weaker on one side of the field of vision. Objects seem lost in a halo of light. Diminution
of sight on one half of the field of vision.
Female - Frigidity. Libido disturbed, impotence, frigidity, sexual asthenia. Menopausal complaints with hot
flashes, aggravated at night. Hyperthyroidism during the menopause with swelling at the base of the neck.
 Head - Occipital headaches, worse on the left side, spreading to the entire left side of the body.
Heart - Vasomotor complaints. Vascular disorders, accompanied by pain. Pain in the left side of the thorax,
which may spread to the arm, aggravated by physical exercise and capable of stimulating an attack of angina
pectoris.
Limbs - Raynaud’s syndrome. Cyanosis of the limbs with tingling and burning sensation. Movements badly
coordinated for the upper as well as the lower limbs. Often drops things. Hands in a contracted state without
total paralysis. Numbness of the hands with cyanosis and trembling. Numbness of the feet with cyanosis,
formication, swelling and edema of the ankles. Copious perspiration from the feet. Spastic gait.
Lungs - Asthmatic dyspnea, the patient has difficulty in exhaling.
Male - Impotence with dwindling or libido and lack of orgasm. Sex painful with premature ejaculation.
Modalities - Better by fresh air and movement. The pains are better at night. Worse by the cold, heat. Worse
from emotions, especially unhappy emotions.
Nose - Ozaena. Reduction in the olfactory sensitivity. Sensation of evil-smelling, unpleasant whiffs like sulphur.
Smells are badly tolerated.
Skin - Dermographia. Burning sensation on the skin, aggravated by heat and cold. Excessive sweating,
predominantly on one half of the body. Lesion caused by parasites, on the nails. Deformity of the nails, which
are concave, ridged, breaking. Nails extremely fragile. Inflammation beneath the nails.
Stomach - Pains with nausea, worse after ingestion of food. Cramping stomachache, accompanied by nausea
and meteorism.
Temperature - Vascular complaints, the skin is either very red or very pale, but always cold. Cyanosis and
edema at the limbs, accompanied either by an increase in the local heat or, the opposite, by decrease in the
heat.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Agar., Op., Hyos., (2) Hypoth., Pitu-gl.
REFERENCES - Julian.

name: Thallium Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - thal. Thallium metallicum. Thallium metal. Thallium aceticum. A Rare Metal. Trituration. Solution
of the Sulphate. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Atherosclerosis. Baldness. Cachexia. Conjunctivitis. Cyanosis.
Dysuria. Emaciation. Emphysema. Folliculitis. Glomerulonephritis. Hair, loss. Hematuria. Hyperthyroidism.
Insomnia. Locomotor ataxia. Malaria. Muscular, atrophy. Myelitis. Neuritis. Night-sweats. Paraplegia.
Paralysis. Pleurisy. Pneumoconiosis. Polyneuritis. Rheumatism. Sciatic pains. Trembling. Tremors.
Tuberculosis.
HOMEOPATHIC - Thallium is a rare metal discovered by Crookes in 1861. He found it in the residue left from
the distillation of selenium and named it thallium (a green shoot) from the green it gives in the spectrum.
Thallium and its derivatives are toxic.Thallium has been experimented with by Lamy and Marme. The
symptoms picture of Thallium were established in 1965-66 by Panos, Rogers and Stephenson, on seven male
and nine female provers.
Combermale of Lille, used Thal, with success in the night-sweats of tuberculosis, but this treatment had the
effect of causing profuse falling of the hair, so serious as to contraindicate its use. Huchard had patients
become quite bald in several days. Hansen said Thal, relieves the violent pains of tabes dorsalis.
Horrible, neuralgic, spasmodic shooting pains. Pains like electric shocks. Muscular atrophy. Tremors.
Trembling. Chorea-like movements. Locomotor ataxia with pain. Paralysis of lower limbs. Paraplegia. Poly-
neuritis. Neuritis. Trigeminal neuralgia. Spinal neurasthenia. Pseudo-bulbar paralysis. Intermittent paralysis.
Muscular pains. Muscular atrophy. Numbness or formication starting in the fingers and toes, extending up to
lower limbs and down to feet and involving lower abdomen and perineum. General emaciation with a lack of
strength.
Hyperemia, swelling and excessive secretion. Night-sweats of tuberculosis. Dermatrophic lesions. Alopecia,
hair loss following acute, exhausting diseases. Loss of body hair and hair of the head.
Influences the endocrine glands, especially the thyroid and adrenalin. Hyperthyroidism symptoms. Emaciation,
hypotonia, chilliness.
Pains in the legs, aggravated when lying on the affected side. Unable to find a position in the bed which eases
the pain. Pain in the right knee on bending or stretching it. Pain in the sciatic nerve.
Discomforts are of a periodic nature, recurring in strength, at the same hour and then disappearing again.
Permanent state of jangled nerves. Trophic conditions of the nails.
MIND - Growing impatience. Extreme irritability and violence, uneasiness with insomnia. Extreme anxiety for
 no reason.
Hysterical symptoms with hyperesthesia and then hypoesthesia.
State of jangled nerves of excitability and bewailing with weeping and shouting. Attacks of weeping,
excitement. Bursts into tears for the least thing, only to blow up soon after. Stubborn. Indifferent resignation.
Apathy. Depression.
Abdomen - Retraction or depression of abdomen. Distention of the abdomen. Heavy flatulence, even after a
light meal. Spasmodic pain in the stomach and intestines with abdominal pains. Pain in intestinal canal.
Back - Formication on the back. Lumbar aching.
Blood - Attacks of hypertension with hyperthyroid phenomena. Bleeding from the capillary vessels.
Atherosclerosis. Cyanosis. Increase of carbon dioxide in the blood plasma.
Chest - Painful, heavy feeling on the sternum. Retro-sternal pain in the esophagus. Neuralgia after herpes
zoster.
Eyes - Dacryocystitis. Iritis. Blepharitis. Purulent conjunctivitis. Frequent conjunctivitis with abundant
production of mucus. Muco-purulent discharge from the right eye, worse in the morning. Glittering spots in
front of the eyes with formication on the face. Visual complaints with feeling of heaviness behind the eye.
Scotoma. Eyebrows fall out.
Face - Facial neuralgia. Hair loss from beard.
Female - Menses prolonged with black blood. Amenorrhea. Loss of pubic hair.
Food - Thirst. Voracious appetite. Loss of appetite.
Head - Headaches. Pain in occiput in morning. Alopecia. Hair falls off with great rapidity. Falling out of hair
after diseases. Hair falls off in handfuls. Hair loss in spots
Heart - Diminished frequency of pulse. Pulse rapid with precordial constriction.
Kidneys - Involuntary passing of urine. Casts in urine. Acute glomerulonephritis. Dysuria. Proteinuria.
Hematuria.
Limbs - Sharp pains like electric shocks. Very tired. Disorders of movement coordination. Chorea-like
movements and rapid movements like convulsions. Exaggerated reflexes and muscular atrophy. Trembling.
Paralytic feeling. Chronic myelitis. Numbness in fingers and toes with extension up lower limbs involving
lower abdomen and perineum. Paralysis of lower limbs. Cyanosis of limbs. Formication, beginning in fingers
and extending through pelvis. Emaciation of fingertips. Deformed nails.
Liver - Gallbladder distended. Coating of liver white and granular-looking.
Lungs - Slow and difficult breathing. Dyspnea. Respiration difficult with pain all over the thoracic cage.
Emphysema. Pleurisy. Pneumoconiosis. Cyanosis.
Male - Impotence. Loss of pubic hair.
Modalities - Better from walking. Worse at night. Worse from contact, pressure.
Mouth - Lips dry with thirsty feeling. Bad breath, irritation of the mucus membranes in the mouth with excessive
salivation. Stomatitis. Aphthae. Gingivitis. Dental caries. Toothache. Numbness.
Rectum - Spasmodic, stubborn constipation, alternating with attacks of diarrhea and anal and rectal pains.
Diarrhea, bloody stools.
Skin - Dryness of the skin. Red stripes after scratching. Acne. Folliculitis. Skin pigmentation disorders. Loss
of hair on the body (axillary and pubic). Skin sensitive in particular areas, especially on the soles of the feet.
Pustular formations. Trophic complaints of the nails, which are deformed. Inflammation beneath the nails.
Deformed nails.
Sleep - Sleep is light, wakes often. Great difficulty in falling asleep again.
Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Bitterbelchings and bitter taste in the mouth. Feels nauseated but cannot vomit.
Nausea and vomiting. Pain in stomach and bowels, terribly severe lancinations, following each other with the
rapidity of electric shocks.
Temperature - Profuse sweating in cases of severe illness. Night-sweats of tuberculosis.
Throat - Goiter. Swollen thyroid gland.
RELATIONS - Thal, belongs to the Lead
group of metals and approaches Plb. closest in its symptoms. Compare: (1) Thal-s. Plb., Lath., Caust., Arg-n.
(2) Baldness, Jab., Pilo., Petr. (3) Baldness and tuberculosis, Phos. (4) Aran. - Feeling of constant coldness.
Periodic return of symptoms. Severe pain in the heels.(5) Cedr. - Periodicity of symptoms, supra-orbital
neuralgia, periodic migraines. (6) Aran-ix.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian. Phatak.

name: Thea Sinensis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - thea. Thea sinensis. Chinese tea. Camellia thea. N. O. Temstromiaceae, Theaceae. Tincture
or infusion of dried leaves and flowers. Trituration of Theine. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Delirium, tremens. Mania. Homicidal. Insanity. Insomnia. Kidney, disorders. Mania. Megrim.
Nervousness. Neuralgias. Paralysis. Sleeplessness. Suicidal.
HERBAL - Tea contains an alkaloid, Thein, which is considered by some identical with caffeine, and both tea
and coffee are used to stimulate the jaded faculties. The stimulation will enable persons to endure fatigue and
get more enjoyment out of themselves than they could obtain by mere food.
Coffee and tea are different in their effects though they may be alike in their chemistry. The after-effect of all
stimulation is reaction, unless it is kept off by a repetition of the stimulant as the effect of the last dose wears
off.
The sign that the first dose of tea is wearing off is a nervous, restless, depressed, ill- tempered state, which is
visible in persons who rely on tea, at about 5 p.m.
HOMEOPATHIC - Neuralgia and insomnia. All-gone, sinking sensation at the epigastrium. Nervous
sleeplessness, heart troubles, palpitations and dyspepsia of old tea-drinkers. Sensitive kidneys. Sick head-
aches. Allen noted it was antidotal to Tab.
MIND - Nervousness and want of confidence. Great nervous excitability with exaltation of intellectual faculties.
Ill-humored. Peevish. Disposition to quarrel at the most harmless speech.
Nocturnal fright, suicidal thoughts. Temporary mental exaltation. Delirium with ecstasy, laughed incessantly,
talked in rhyme. Delirium tremens. Mania. Suicidal and homicidal. Impulses to kill. Impulse to jump out of the
window.
Abdomen - Borborygmi. After lunch, stitch below ribs in paroxysms. Intestines relaxed. Liability to hernia.
Chest - Oppressed and constricted. Fluttering in left side and feeling of suffocation.
Ears - Neuralgic pains in cartilage of ears. Roaring in ears. Hallucinations of hearing.
Eyes - Eyes are unusually bright. Dilated pupils. Neuralgia of eyes. Sight is dim, dark before eyes, fiery lines,
sparks.
Face - Wild, distressed expression. Face is pale, with congested redness, flushed.
Female - Soreness and tenderness in ovaries. Menses delayed, scanty with severe cramp-like pains. Uterine
bearing down from beginning to end of period.
Food - Very hungry, but little satisfies. Thirst, but every mouthful of cold water affects the head like a shock.
Craves acids, lemons.
Head - Rush of blood to head. Sick headache radiating from one point. Sleepless and restless. Hallucinations
of hearing. Cold damp feeling at back of head. Scalp tender can scarcely comb hair.
Heart - Anxious oppression. Precordial distress. Palpitation, unable to lie on left side. Fluttering. Pulse rapid,
irregular
Thea sinensis intermittent.
Kidneys - Very marked increase of urine. Must pass water immediately after drinking tea.
Limbs - Paralyzed numbness of limbs. Joints of hands and feet tender. Nervous excitability in wrists, hands,
and feet. Hand trembled violently. Restlessness of feet. Neuralgic pains in outer hamstrings. Sensation as if
the weight of a sheet even would crush toes.
Lungs - Edema of respiratory tract. Breathing increased in frequency and amplitude. Breathlessness on least
exertion. Paroxysm of asphyxia. Cough is dry, severe and bloody expectoration.
Male - Erections. Unnatural excitement.
Modalities - Better warmth, warm bath, applying hand or warm clothes to occiput. Worse at night, from cold
water, walking in open air. Worse after meals.
Mouth - Bitter taste in mouth. Much viscid saliva. Whole mouth cavity dry and sensitive. Tongue clean and
pale. Tongue red, blistered, painful as if scalded. Teeth frequently decayed.
Nose - Dryness, soreness of nose. Sensation at root of nose as if nosebleed would occur. Nosebleed before
menses.
 Rectum - Swelling of lower end of rectum, with slight itching. Chronic relaxed bowels. worse by beer, better
by port wine. Constipation.
Sensations - As if on the verge of fainting. As if a foreign body in throat. As if the stomach hung down relaxed
in the body like an empty bag. As if the weight of a sheet on the feet would crush the toes. Cold sensations
are prominent, cold, damp feeling at back of head with pain spreading thence to eyes, also dryness and
swelling of mucus membrane.
Skin - Skin dry as if pores obstructed. Skin of fingertips peels from excessive dryness. Eruption of red, indolent
pimples. Itching, crawling, prickling in different parts.
Sleep - Sleepy in daytime, sleepiness at night with vascular excitement and restlessness and dry skin. Horrible
dreams cause no horror.
Stomach - A sinking sensation at the epigastrium. Faint, gone feeling (Sep., Hydr., Olean.). Weakness about
stomach. Sudden production of wind in large quantities. Nausea, and vomiting after eating. Vomits bile, when
pain at its height.
Temperature - Intense coldness passing over whole head. Lowered temperature. Hands and face cold as
marble. Beaded with chilly moisture. Excessive internal heat with flushes of heat on the surface, coming and
going quickly. Disposition to perspire.
Throat - Scraping in larynx. Hoarseness. Diphtheria sore throat. Painless swelling of mucus membrane.
Uneasy feeling in pharynx, as if obstructed by a foreign body.
Vertigo - Vertigo with darkness before eyes, sudden in open air.
COMMENTS - The symptoms are made up of observed effects of overdosing and some direct provings. A
woman who was addicted to dri nking tea showed very pronounced delirium tremens indistinguishable from
that caused by alcohol, though there was no alcoholism in the case.
Another woman, who kept a pot of tea boiling on the stove and drank several bowls every day, developed both
suicidal and homicidal mania, impulse tojump out of the window, to cut her baby’s throat or throw it downstairs.
Thea 100,000c, Fincke, cured.
A man who had been many years in the East and was used to one-story houses, on his return to the West had
a curious impulse tojump out of the window, which he traced to tea-drinking and which disappeared when he
left it off.
Teste noted that the homicidal impulse appeared in the dreams of one prover, who was so far from being
horrified by his dreammurders that he even took pleasure in them after awaking. The talkativeness of Thea, is
one of its chief allurements.
Among tea-tasters, who do not drink the tea they taste, but only hold it in the mouth a short time, yet long
enough for the mouth to absorb some, there is sometimes developed what is known as tea-tasters’ paralysis,
affecting mostly the lower limbs with loss of
sensation of both upper and lower.
A man, after drinking tea, had pain in his epigastrium going through to his back with a feeling as if he wanted
to be sick and could not, better sitting down and stretching out. Thuj. 30c cured.
Guernsey gave these as indications for Thea, “Nervous sleeplessness, heart troubles, of old tea-drinkers,
palpitations of the heart, can’t lie down.”
RELATIONS -Antidote: Thuj., Ferr., Kali-hp. - Material dosesfortea-taster’scoughAnridoted by: Beer.
Compare: (1) Gone, faint feeling, sick-headache radiating from one point and pain in left ovary, Sep. (2) Averse
to work, especially writing, Hydr. (3) Relaxed feeling in stomach. Ip. (4) Desire for acids, Verat., Sulph., Ant-c.,
Phos., Sabin.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

or infusion of dried leaves and flowers. Trituration of Theine. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Delirium, tremens. Mania. Homicidal. Insanity. Insomnia. Kidney, disorders. Mania. Megrim.

HERBAL - Tea contains an alkaloid, Thein, which is considered by some identical with caffeine, and both tea
