name: Thyroidinum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - thyr. Thyroidinum. Thyroid gland extract. Thyreoidinum. Thyroidea. Glándula thyreoidea.
Thyroidin. A sarcode. Trituration of the fresh or dried thyroid gland of sheep or calf. Potencies of a liquid extract
of the gland. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Acromegaly. Albuminuria. Amblyopia. Amenorrhea. Anemia, pernicious. Angina
pectoris. Backache. Bedwetting. Breast, tumors. Chilblains. Constipation. Convulsions, puerperal. Cre-
tinism. Cysts. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Diuresis. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Ear, disorders. Eczema. Edema.
Epilepsy. Fainting. Fibroma. Fractures. Goiter, exophthalmic. Hair, loss. Heart, disorders. Hysteria.
Ichthyosis. Idiocy. Leprosy. Malnutrition. Mania. Milk, deficiency. Myxedema. Neurasthenia. Obesity. Optic
neuritis. Paralysis, hands and arms. Paraplegia. Pityriasis rubra. Psoriasis. Puerperal fever. Rupia.
Scleroderma. Syphilis. Tetanus. Tachycardia. Thyroid, disorders. Tuberculosis. Uterine, fibroids.
 Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Thyroidinum, also known as Thyroidea, is an organopathic. The sarcode is prepared from
the dried thyroid gland taken from a sheep, ox or calf. The thyroid is closely connected with the heart and it
exercises a general regulating influence on growth and development.
The homeopathic proving was established by M. Panos, R. Rogers, and J. Stephenson in 1963-64, using a
double-blind method. The potencies 12x, 30x, 200c and 1000c were used. The symptomatology completes
the work of Ghosh of Calcutta, which dates from 1963. Thyr. symptoms are made up of the toxicological and
clinical sources as well as the proving symptoms.
Thyr. affects the central nervous system, skin and left side. Metabolic disorders. Goiter. Myxedema with hair
loss and cretinism. Diuretic action in myxedema and various types of edema.
Anemia, emaciation. Infantile wasting. Rickets. Arrested development of children. Acromegaly, delayed union
of fractures. A state of puffiness and obesity. Excessive obesity. Great weakness and hunger, yet loses flesh.
Craving for large quantities of sugar.
Rheumatoid arthritis. Nervous tremor of face and limbs. Tingling sensations. Paralysis. Hystero-epilepsy.
Tetany, worse cold. Muscular weakness. Sensation of faintness after acute diseases, weakness. Easy fatigue,
weak pulse with a tendency to fainting, palpitations.
Increased heart rate. Dilates arterioles. Tachycardia. Low blood pressure. Cold hands and feet, chilliness and
sensitive to cold. As of a cold wind blowing on the body. Sweating, headache. Exophthalmus and dilatation of
pupils. Amblyopia. Weak memory. Cretinism. Psoriasis. Nocturnal bedwetting.
Breast tumors. Cystic tumors of the breast (2x trituration). Lack of breastmilk. Vomiting of pregnancy.
Uterine fibroids. Saidto be effective in undescended testicles in boys when given in half-grain doses twice
a day over a considerable period.
Feels tired and sick, easy fatigue, wants to lie down. Fainting fits, tremors, nervous of face and limbs. Stabbing,
splitting, clutching sensation. Choking. Convulsion in the nursing children, related to a febrile cutting of teeth.
MIND - Stupor, alternating with restless melancholy. Marked irritability of temper. Irritable, worse least
opposition, goes into a rage over trifles. Grumbling, all the time. Irritable before menses.
Difficult concentration. Absent-minded. Nervous and apprehensive. Depression on waking. Depressed,
inclined to cry. Weeps when undressing. Morose and sulky, wants
Thyroidinum to be left alone.
Euphoria. Laughing in a way peculiar to herself. Argues with family. Suspicious. Paranoia that they are being
pursued or persecuted. Psychosis from anguish. Homicidal tendency. Insanity, puerperal insanity with fever.
Nightmares.
Abdomen - Bearing and aching down through pelvis into anterior thigh. Acute cramping pains with cold
sweating. Pain after eating. Pain midway between umbilicus and either anterior superior iliac spine. Sharp,
cutting, colicky pains with fullness, worse on pressure and walking, better bending forward and after passage
of flatus. Large quantities of flatus passed from bowels often smelling of hydrogen sulphate. Rolling flatulence
with gurgling, then loose, gassy stool.
Back - Backache.
Breasts - Breasts tumors and cysts. Deficient in breast milk.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Anxiety about chest. Chest feels as if constricted.
Constitutions - Suited to the phosphoric or carbonic types, generally hyperthyroids. Nervous temperament.
Psoric, tubercular and sycotic range of dispositions.
Ears - Sclerosis of ossicles. Difficult hearing. Pain on the right side. Pain in the left ear lobe.
Eyes - Progressive loss of sight with central scotoma (Carbn-s.). Conjunctivitis and chemosis, itching with
weeping. Stinging pain in the right eye. Eyeballs prominent. Exophthalmic goiter. Irritation of the eyelids.
Face - Flushed. Dry, red lips, burn with free desquamation. Eruption of acne, worse on the right cheek.
Sensation of something heavy, which falls from the cheeks.
Female - Amenorrhea in young girls. Pelvic congestion ameliorated by menses. Amelioration of premenstrual
discomforts by the menses. Menses often too early. Metrorrhagia. Endometriosis. Gnawing in the uterus.
Uterine fibroids. Vomiting of pregnancy. Puerperal, convulsions insanity. Tendency tomiscarriage or
premature birth. Puerperal psychosis. Uterine atony after giving birth. Sterility.
Food - Insatiable appetite, always wants something more interesting to eat. Desire for sweets and thirst for
cold water. Aversion to greasy foods.
Head - Feeling of lightness in brain. Fullness and heat. Persistent frontal headache, heaviness over eyes.
Headaches ameliorated after menses. Heavy throbbing headache worse in the frontal region, worse from
concentrating the mind, better out of doors, worse using the eyes. Fullness in the head with throbbing of the
temporal arteries, worse morning and afternoon, from motion, physical or mental, from heat or indoors, better
 in cool fresh air, often better from external pressure. Falling of hair.
Heart - Ready excitability of heart. Heart’s action weak with numbness of fingers. Tachycardia (Naja.).
Palpitations, worse least exertion, hammering, beats felt in ear. Heart pains radiate into axilla. Clutching,
constricting pains, worse lying down, causing short breath. Severe heart pains. Angina pectoris. Hypertrophy
after hard labor. As if blood were rushing downwards, through the body. Jumping sensation at heart. Large
veins on arms and hands. Valvular diseases of heart (Naja). Weak, frequentpulse with inability to lie down.
Kidneys - Pressing urge to urinate. Frequent urination during the day. Burning along urethra, increase of uric
acid. Increased flow of urine, polyuria, some albumen and sugar. Urine smells of violets. Bedwetting in weakly
children who are nervous and irritable. Diabetes mellitus.
Limbs - Rheumatic arthritis with tendency to obesity, coldness and cramps of limbs. Aching pains. Trembling
of limbs and entire body. Edema of legs. Numbness, left fingers then right leg. Itching without eruption, worse
night. Peeling of skin of lower limbs. Cold limbs. Cold, clammy hands. Left hand icy cold. Abnormal growth of
limbs due to excessive exertion.
Liver - Cutting pain in liver, worse deep breathing. Jaundice with itching, in the newborn child, accompanied
by vomiting.
Lungs - Breathlessness better lying in recumbent position. Dry, painful cough with scanty, difficult
expectoration and burning in pharynx. Cough on entering a warm room from cool air. Asthma. Allergies.
Modalities - Better after or during menses. Better evening, rest, lying on abdomen or reclining position. Worse
in women, before and during menses. Worse least exertion, stooping. Worse cold. Heart worse lying down.
Mouth - Dryness of mouth. Bad taste, metallic, bitter and sour. Tongue, metallic taste at tip. Tongue coated
grayish white in center with red edges or tip. Papillae enlarged and prominent. Tongue thickly coated. Swelling
of the upper lip.
Nose - Dry mucus membrane indoors, fluent coryza, profuse, watery and bland outdoors. Dryness and sticking
pain in posterior nares, worse on swallowing. Rhinitis with sneezing and edema of the nasal mucus
membranes. Pain in the sinuses. Tickling sensation with headaches and dry throat.
Perspiration - Drenching sweats. Oily, musty sweat.
Rectum - Stools dark, fragmented with cadaverous or sulphurous smell. Stools soft, watery.
Skin - Eczema. Psoriasis associated with obesity. Very dry skin. Itching without eruption, worse night. Brown
swellings. Swelling of glands of stony hardness. Symmetrical serpiginous eruptions. Jaundice with itching, in
the newborn child, accompanied by vomiting. Urticaria. Ichthyosis. Lupus. Peeling skin of lower limbs.
Scleroderma.
Sleep - Insomnia. Difficulty in falling asleep. Nightmares. Wakes for no reason.
Stomach - Increased appetite. Thirst for cold water. Pains, tenderness, aggravated by eating, ameliorated in
the evening. Dyspepsia before menses. Flatulence, much flatus in abdomen. Nausea, worse riding in a car,
better in cool air. Vomiting of pregnancy.
Temperature - Hot flushes, then chills or drenching sweats.
Throat - Dry larynx, congested, raw, burning, worse on left side. As of a splinter stuck across the throat.
Pharynx congested, red and dry, with rawness and burning.
Vertigo - Vertigo, in the morning on rising, on leaning forwards.
COMMENTS - Thyr. has a profound action on the heart. Fatal syncope occurred in a number of cases under
“thyroid feeding.” Cyanosis was produced in many cases. Burnett gave a patient 3x, producing severe angina
pectoris. The connection between the heart and the thyroid gland is very close, as seen in cases of
exophthalmic goiter, of which many cases have been cured.
In a case of valvular heart disease following rheumatism in a man, 24, Thyr. 3x, thrice daily, quickly relieved a
squeezing pain at the heart with inability to lie down, and hastened the patient’s recovery.
Dr. F.C. Skinner cured a case of dysmenorrhea in a goiter subject with Thyr. 1,000c.
In myxedema, cachexia, cretinism and similar conditions, the thyroid gland is absent or defective and the idea
is to supply a physiological want. As such, a state of puffiness and obesity may be regarded as a keynote
indication for Thyr.
Clarke gave Thyr. 3x to a living skeleton of a child, 5, who looked not older than 2. He had been kept in a box
in a cellar all his life until brought into the hospital, when he weighted only 14.25 pounds. Under Bac. 200c and
careful feeding he gained .25 pounds per week. When Clarke commenced Thyr. he put on weekly .75 pound
and gained the use of his legs, being able to stand by holding on to a chair.
In a case of universal and very aggravated psoriasis in a schoolboy, fair, very chilly, cold, clammy hands and
feet, Thyr. 3x and later 30c completely cured after a prolonged course.
An obese lady, age 60, developed diabetes. Clarke cured her completely with Thyr. 3x and 30c. She then
could take any kind of food.
 H. O. Nicholson related a case of toxemia of pregnancy in a woman, 32, during her third pregnancy. She had
a fit on October
3. Thyroid feeding was begun the next day. Marked improvement followed. Edema of face and body
diminished. On October 23, the patient was about her usual duties. On November 6, she was delivered of a
healthy boy without any untoward symptoms.
Pityriasis rubra, intense redness and scales of legs, and also with intense itching. Ichthyosis, syphilitic
eruptions and scleroderma. Acromegaly. Myxedema with hair loss.
Increases the flow of milk in nursing women when the flow has been deficient. Insanity, puerperal insanity with
fever. Paranoia that they are being pursued or persecuted. Nightmares.
Optic neuritis and accommodative asthenopia. Exophthalmic goiter, with bulging eyes. Weak heart, valvular
problems, shortness of breath. Tachycardia. Operative and idiopathic tetany, worse from spasms by cold.
Stitching, aching or heavy pains. Tingling sensations.
Thyr. has poor nutritional development in children. Low thyroid function, with skin problems. It can stimulate
function of thyroid gland, or decrease the need for thyroid medications. Thyroid treatment nearly always raises
the body heat.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Spong., Calc., Fuc., Lycps. (2) Thyri. (3) Thym-gl. extract - arthritis deformans,
metabolic osteoarthritis, 5 grain tablets 3 times daily. High potencies very effective cases of exophthalmic
goiter.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

***THYROIODINUM (lodothyrinum) PHARMACY - thyri. Thyroiodinum. lodothyrinum. The iodine exists in
organic combination and Thyr. contains 0.003 parts of iodine to every gram. Trituration. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Emaciation. Dyspnea. Glycosuria. Goiter. Hoarseness. Obesity. Thyroid, disorders. Thyroid,
nodules. Urine, increased. Weight, loss.
HOMEOPATHIC - Thyroiodine is now more generally named lodothyrine, but Clarke retained the former as
more convenient.
Hoenigschmied said of it that it is present in only small quantities in the thyroid of sheep. It is completely free
from albuminous substances, stable and directly assimilated. The general effects of the drug are increased
secretion of urine and corresponding loss of flesh.
Thyri. is the active principle isolated form thyroid gland, a substance rich in Iodine and nitrogen, affects
metabolism, reducing weight, may produce glycosuria. It should be used cautiously in obesity, for a fatty heart
may not be able to maintain the accelerated metabolic rhythm. Milk contains the internal secretion of the
thyroid.
COMMENTS - Hoenigschmied gave some cases, including that of a laborer, 42, for several years had
enlargement and induration of all lobes of thyroid, the enlargement caused compression of the structures of
the neck, dyspnea, whistling respiration, hoarseness, short, dry cough, vertigo.
Thyri. was given, 5-grain tablets, one every evening, at the end of a week twice daily. After using twenty-five
tablets, the gland was smaller and softer, the previously hard and resistant nodules were elastic after two more
weeks only remnants of the goiter remained.
Another case, that of a man, 60, thyroid enlarged in all its lobes with a glandular cystic swelling in the right
one, dyspnea, loud whistling breathing. Two, three and at last four tablets were given daily for two months, by
which time the goiter had vanished, but the cyst was not changed.
A man, 45, medium height, sedentary, suffered from obesity, vertigo, dyspnea, weariness. Pulse feeble, 76,
functions normal, appetite and sleep good, weight 230 pounds.
With increasing doses of Thyri., up to ten tablets daily the weight steadily went down to 160 pounds, activity
increasing in proportion. When the dose had reached four tablets daily the urine became very abundant, but
was free from albumen. The daily dose was
Thyroiodinum increased one tablet every four days.
REFERENCES – Clarke
keynote:
PHARMACY - thyr. Thyroidinum. Thyroid gland extract. Thyreoidinum. Thyroidea. Glándula thyreoidea.
Thyroidin. A sarcode. Trituration of the fresh or dried thyroid gland of sheep or calf. Potencies of a liquid extract
of the gland. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Acromegaly. Albuminuria. Amblyopia. Amenorrhea. Anemia, pernicious. Angina
pectoris. Backache. Bedwetting. Breast, tumors. Chilblains. Constipation. Convulsions, puerperal. Cre-
tinism. Cysts. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Di

name: Tilia Europea
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - til. Tilia europea. Common Lime. Linden. Tilia cordata. Tilia sylvestris. N. O. Tiliacae. Tincture
of fresh blossoms. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bedwetting. Dentition. Hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Neuralgias. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis.
Puerperal, metritis. Rheumatism. Toothache. Urticaria. Uterus, prolapsed.
 HERBAL - The sap of the linden contains sugar, and the flowers an abundance of honey, which makes the
tree particularly attractive to bees.
HOMEOPATHIC - A tincture of the fresh blossoms was proved by the Austrian Society. The most striking
characteristic is “an intense sore feeling about the abdomen and profuse warm sweat which gives no relief.”
This led to its successful use in cases of peritonitis.
In addition to this are marked bearingdown symptoms in the whole genito-urinary and rectal regions, especially
in the uterus and these combined with the others have indicated Til. in puerperal metritis and other disorders
of the female generative sphere.
Til. is of value in muscular weakness of the eye. Hemorrhages of thin, pale blood. Puerperal metritis. Disease
of the antrum (Hydr., Chel.). Intense soreness of the abdomen, uterus. Bearing or dragging down pains in
genito-urinary and rectal region. Bed feels too hard. Edema. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. The more he sweats
the greater the pain.
MIND - Love-sick. Dread of society. Melancholy, disposed to weep. Irritable. Disinclined to work.
Abdomen - Bloated abdomen, pains as from incarcerated flatulence, repeated noisy discharges of it, which
aggravates. Peritonitis. Soreness with warm sweat which gives no relief.
Back - Tearing from nape to top of shoulder. Stitching, drawing, and heat in right back between liver and
kidneys. Heaviness in sacral and dorsal region.
Chest - Oppression. Whole chest weak, acute pressure and pinching under sternum. Throbs as from a dull
stitch from thorax to back. Bruised pain and swelling. Tearing from left pectoralis major to axilla.
Ears - Stinging in ears.
Eyes - Binocular vision imperfect. Sensation as of gauze or a veil before eyes (Calc., Caust., Nat-m.). As if a
piece of cold iron pressed through right eye causing burning.
Face - Face pale, or flushed, frequent alternations. Cutting pains. Sensation of something alive under skin of
face. Quivering of lips. Sprained pain in left jaw-point.
Female-Intense sorefeeling about uterus. Bearing-down pains with hot sweat, but without relief. Soreness
and redness of external genitals (Thuj., Sulph.). Pelvic inflammation, tympanites, abdominal tenderness and
hot sweat which does not relieve. Much slimy leucorrhea when walking (Bov., Carb-an., Graph.). Puerperal
metritis.
Head - Neuralgias, first right, then left side, with veil before eyes. Confusion with dimness of vision. Much
sneezing with fluent coryza. Bleeding from nose.
Kidneys - Heavy dragging pain in urethra. Constant painful pressure on bladder and urethra. Frequent,
copious urination. Scanty urine.
Limbs - Trembling, weariness, bruised feeling in limbs. Paralytic heaviness of arms, especially upper arm.
Heaviness and painful lameness in left shoulder. Drawing in small spot left hip while sitting. Cramp in left sole.
Ulcerative pain in ball of left great toe.
Lungs - Cough from tickling in throat. Tickling, scraping, irritating, provoking slight cough, especially in left
side of larynx. Fine stitches in larynx, worse talking. Hoarseness. Frequent sighing.
Modalities - Better in cool room. Better from motion, walking about in open air. Better closing eyes. Better
from coffee. Worse talking, walking, stooping, sneezing. Worse in afternoon and evening. Worse
cold water, drafts. Worse from sweating, warm room, heat of bed, after sleep. Skin symptoms worse heat of
bed.
Mouth - Much mucus in mouth, causing fuzzy feeling, affecting speech. Taste bitter, bitter-slimy, pasty.
Stinging pain in all the teeth, worse by cold water. Drawing pains in gums.
Nose - Tickling of nose. Much sneezing with fluent coryza. Nosebleeds, blood thin and pale, but coagulates
quickly.
Perspiration - Sweat warm and profuse soon after falling asleep. Sweat increases as rheumatic pains
increase.
Sensations - As if a piece of cold iron pierced through right eye, causing burning. Burning as if a piece of ice
were drawn over ear and face. As if something living were under skin of face. Tearing in anterior muscles of
thigh, as if they were too short.
Skin - Urticaria. Eruption of small, red itching pimples. Violent itching and burning like fire after scratching.
Sleep - Yawning, sleepy, exhausted, worse during pain. Sleeplessness with restlessness, Bed seems too
hard. Vivid frightful dreams, bathed in perspiration. Sudden wakings.
Temperature - Profuse warm sweat, soon after falling asleep without relief.
Throat - Burning in throat. Sensation of swelling of the palate, with desire to swallow, and hoarse voice. Tickling
in palate causing cough.
Vertigo - Vertigo, with staggering, and like gauze before the eyes. Intoxication.
 COMMENTS - An intense facial neuralgia was developed in the proving and also a very aggravated condition
of skin irritation with pimples of the lichen order. Pains above the root of the nose, nosebleed of thin, pale blood
which coagulated quickly. The left side was most affected. Great sensitiveness to draft of air was induced.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lil-t., Bell. (2) Puerperal metritis, Bell. (3) Uterine bearing down, Lil-t. (4) Sweat
without improvement. Merc.
REFERENCES - Buericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Tillandsia Usneoides
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - till-u. Tillandsia usneoides. Spanish moss. Tree hair. Old mans beard. Florida moss. N. O.
Bromeliaceae (Brome- liad or Pineapple family). Historical dose: Tincmre and all potencies potencies.
CLINICAL - Blood, sugar. Breast, milk. Childbirth. Diabetes. Epilepsy. Hemorrhages. Rheumatism.
HERBAL - Tillandsia is usually an epiphytic plant with reduced to absent stems. Found mostly in tropical to
temperate Americas. Hangs in the trees and swamps of the southeast coastal plains.
Many Native American tribes used the moss while cooking to absorb unwanted liquids, for bedding, for tanning
hides, and to rub on newborn babies heads for curly hair. It is also used as fodder for animals.
Colonial pickers harvested moss with long poles during the winter. The harvest hung for several months to
cure in a moss yard. Curing loosened the outer gray scales making it ready for commercial ginning.
Medicinal use of Spanish moss has a long history. Extracts from it have been used in the treatment of diabetes
and it has been used to help control blood sugar levels. Spanish moss was taken, while green, and brewed
into tea for expectant mothers, supposedly to aid the flow of breast milk and make the delivery easier. Tea
from the plant was also used as a folk remedy for rheumatism.
In Mexico, it has been used to treat infantile epilepsy. In the early 1950s. it was used as an estrogen substitute
and scientists have found the plant exhibits anti-bacterial properties. In the West Indies it has been used to
make a styptic ointment for the purpose of stopping bleeding.
COMMENTS - Dr. C. W Mayo reported that, in the Feb. 9, 1944 “Staff Meetings of the Mayo Clinic,” the
absorptive qualities of Spanish Moss for use in surgical dressings had been investigated with interesting
results.
“The dried moss will retain its absorptive power better than a substance like cotton, as
the liquid taken up is stored chiefly inside the leaves and cells, instead of merely being held between adjoining
strands. Spanish moss will take up from six to ten times its dry weight of water.”
REFERENCES - Buttimer. Murphy.

name: Tinospora Cordifolia
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tinos. Tinospora cordifolia. Gulancha. N. O. Menispermaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bilious. Cough. Dysuria. Elephantiasis. Fever. Flatulence. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhoids. Impetigo.
Intermittent, fever. Jaundice. Malaria. Palpitations. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Syphilis. Urticaria.
Vomiting. Worms.
HERBAL - The stem and root are used medicinally; they possess a bitter taste. The root and stem contain
starchy extract, bitter principle and a trace of berbomic. Fresh stem is more efficacious than the dry one and
is a good substitute for Calumbu.
The Ayurvedic physicians used it as a febrifuge and named it “Indian quinine.” They have found it to be bitter
tonic and strength giving. It destroys wind, bile and phlegm. It is good for thirst, burning sensation, gonorrhea,
cough.
Useful in enlarged spleen. Secondary syphilis, rheumatism, leprosy, skin diseases such as impetigo. Jaundice,
torpidity of the liver, splenic affections. Leprosy, rheumatism. Acute and chronic fevers. Worms, vomiting,
hemorrhoids, dysuria, flatulence and palpitations of the heart.
As a diuretic and demulcent it is given in dysuria, in scanty, high-colored urine due to catarrh of the bladder. It
is stomachic, bitter, tonic, alternative, aphrodisiac, anti-periodic, and demulcent. It is given in dyspepsia and in
debility caused by repeated attacks of fever.
HOMEOPATHIC - No proving of Tinos, has been made, but many Indian homeopaths have been using it
clinically with excellent results.
Debility. Rheumatism. Skin diseases, leprosy, secondary syphilis. Jaundice, torpidity of the liver. Splenic
affections. Acidity of urine, urinary diseases such as gonorrhea and dysuria.
Intermittent fevers. Acute and chronic malarial fevers, the temperature generally rises in the afternoon with
 chilliness or shaking chill. Fevers with bilious vomiting associated with thirst and headache.
Chronic slow fevers, especially where there is a history of gonorrhea and weakness due to seminal emissions.
Fever due to an excessive use or maladministration of quinine. Fever with burning sensation is felt in face,
hands and feet, and enlargement of the liver and spleen, jaundice with yellow color of the eyes, no desire for
food, and headache.
Vomiting, specially bilious vomiting. Decreased quantity of urine, passes it frequently, burning while urinating?
The urine is mixed with pus-like discharges. Gonorrhea. Rheumatism, leprosy and skin diseases. Secondary
syphilis.
Tonic, widely used as a stimulant remedy where the patient has become extremely weak owing to repeated
attacks of fever and also to exhausting seminal emissions.
COMMENTS - R. N. Khory noted, in the Materia Medica of India, vol. II., that the juice of the Tinospora stem
combined with Pakanbhed and honey is given in gonorrhea. The starchy extract is nutritious, largely used in
native practice in cold fevers and seminal weakness, also in urinary affections.
W. Dymock, in the Pharmacographia Indica, vol. 1. noted that it is favorably spoken of by those who have tried
it as a tonic, anti-periodic and diuretic. Charaka recommended it in chronic fevers, jaundice, bilious vomiting
and some other diseases. He found it useful to purify the breast-milk after delivery.
Baghbhata spoke highly of it as an excellent tonic, and noted that it is generally used in chronic fevers and
jaundice. Chakradatta reported that Tinospora is an excellent remedy in urticaria, fevers, leprosy, and
elephantiasis.
Tinospora cordifolia
Bangasena recommended it in vomiting and flatulence associated with extreme palpitations of the heart. “It is
useful in general and seminal debility, fever, jaundice, torpidity of the liver, skin diseases, secondary syphilis,
rheumatism, acidity of urine and urinary diseases, some forms of dyspepsia, splenic affections, chronic
gonorrhea, leucorrhea, etc.”
Nadkarni wrote “In malaria Tinospora is sometimes more efficacious than quinine.” R. N. Chopra, in the
Indigenous Drugs of India, wrote “An infusion is prepared from the stem and root which is a valuable tonic in
debilitating diseases, intermittent fever and dyspepsia.”
RELATIONS - Compare: Chin., Chin-ars.
REFERENCES - Ghose.

name: Titanium Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - titan. Titanium metallicum. Titanium metal. Trituration of the copper-red crystals obtained from
the slag at the bottom of a blast iron furnace. Consisting of Titan, cyanide and Titan, nitride. Titanium is found
in the bones and muscles. Apples contain 0.11 percent of Titan. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Bright’s disease. Eczema. Hemiopia. Lupus. Nasal, catarrh. Premature, ejaculation. Rhinitis.
Sexual, weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Titanium stands midway between silicon and tin in some of its relations and in other respects
it is closely related to iron, chromium and aluminium.
The crystals were proved by Sharp who took 2 grains of the first trituration, daily for a week. It was believed to
be the pure metal, but was proved later to be the cyanonitrid.
Titan, has been used in lupus and tuberculosis processes externally, also in skin diseases, nasal catarrh, etc.
Giddiness with verticalhemiopia. Bright’s disease. Eczema, lupus and rhinitis.
“Imperfect vision, the peculiarity being that half an object only could be seen. ” Another symptom, which
Burnett has turned to good account in cases of sexual
Titanium metallicum
weakness is “Too early ejaculation of semen during sex.”
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Half-sight, Nat-c., Lyc., Aur., Lith.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Tongo
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tong. Tongo. Coumarouna seeds. Dipterix odorata. Tonca. Tonka. Tonquin bean. N. O.
Leguminosae. Papil- ionoideae. A tree in Guiana. Tincture of the dried beans. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Hip, pain. Migraines. Neuralgias, face. Toothache. Whooping cough.
HERBAL - The fragrant seeds of Tongo is used by perfumers. Dipteryx odorata. which yields it, is a native of
 Cayenne. The fruit is something like that of the almond tree.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tong, was proved by Nenning. In the proving Tong, produced “Risings with taste of bitter
almonds.” The chief uses have been in migraine and neuralgic disorders. Whooping cough.
Eyes - Trembling in right upper lid.
Head - Tearing pain in supra-orbital nerve with heat and throbbing pain in head.
Limbs - Tearing pains in hip joints, femur and knee, especially left side.
Modalities - Better by movement, pressure. Worse by rest, when seated.
Nose - Coryza, nose stopped, must breathe through mouth.
Vertigo - Confused, especially in the occiput with somnolence and a sort of intoxication.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Vinegar. Meli. Compare: (1) Hay fever, Trif-p., Napht., Sabad. (2) Antho., Asper.
and Tong, contain Coumarin, the active principle.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Topaz
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - top. Topaz. Gemstone. A12SiO4(F,OH)2 + Cr. Hydroxy-fluoro- aluminum silicate. Historical
dose: All
CLINICAL - Anxiety. Asthma. Blood, sugar. Depression. Diabetes. Exhaustion. Hemorrhages. Indigestion.
Insomnia. Liver, disorders. Nightmares. Restlessness. Sexual, dysfunction. Sleepwalking. Tumors.
HOMEOPATHIC - Topaz has been said to cure insomnia, asthma, and hemorrhages. Depression, exhaustion,
said to increase stamina. Mood swings, worries, fears, anxiety, stress. It was thought to cure cowardice.
Insomnia, sleepwalking, nightmares. Restlessness.
Stomach, liver and pancreas disorders. Disturbed blood sugar. Indigestion. Diabetes. Tumors. Weak eyesight.
Strengthens weak tissue and backbone. Said to be a powerful aphrodisiac and was often used to treat sexual
dysfunction.
COMMENTS - Topaz occurs not only in the transparent yellow, yellow brown, orangey brown, and pinky brown
colors most popularly associated with it, but also in a very light to medium red. In the past, almost any yellow
stone was called topaz.
Yellow topaz is used for protective purposes, specifically against envy, jealousy, intrigue, disease, death,
negativity and lunacy. Mounting in gold is said to enhance these properties; rings, wrist bracelets and
necklaces with the stone next to the heart are thought to be the most projective.
Topaz was also said to change color in the presence of poisoned food or drink. Its curative powers waxed and
waned with the phases of the moon. Supposedly helped to break up stagnation of energy within the body, and
elimination of toxins.
Powdered and mixed with rosewater, topaz prevented bleeding. Nosebleeds could be stopped by pressing a
stone against the side of the nose. It was believed that madness could be cured by a dose of topaz and wine.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

Rectum - Constipation.
 Skin - Boils, recurrent. Itching eczema around ankles. Tinea versicolor.

name: Toxicophis Pugnax
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - toxi. Toxicophis pugnax. Moccasin snake. N. O. Ophidia. Trituration. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Edema. Fever. Periodic neuralgia. Skin, dry. Snake, bites.
Toxicophis pugnax
HOMEOPATHIC - Some effects of bites with this snake have been recorded. A peculiar feature of the cases
was that the symptoms of pain and fever recurred annually at exactly the same period for many years with
decreasing intensity each year.
In one case, the pains spread to other parts after some years. The right leg became painful and swollen rapidly.
For several years the pain was confined to the knee of the bitten limb, in a few years it left the knee and seized
the hip and finally attacked the shoulder. Skin rather dry.
Pain and fever recur annually after a bite from this snake (Cedr., Lach.), but without swelling, decreasing in
intensity each year. Pains will sometimes change location with disappearance of first symptoms. Unusual
dryness of the skin. Edematous swellings and periodical neuralgia.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Vertigo - Dizzy.

***TRIBULUS TERRESTRIS (Ikshugandha)
PHARMACY - trib. Tribulus terrestris. Ikshugandha. Hygrophila spinosa. N. O. Acanthaceae. India. Tincture
of root leaves and seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Apathy. Dropsy. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Impotency. Incontinence. Insomnia. Kidney, stone.
Leucorrhea. Malaria. Mas
turbation. Pimples. Prostatitis. Rheumatism. Sexual, weakness. Spermatorrhea. Strangury. Urticaria.
HERBAL - Ikshugandha is an East Indian remedy useful in urinary affections, especially dysuria, and in
debilitated states of the sexual organs, as expressed in seminal weakness, early emissions and infertile
semen.
The root is demulcent, diuretic, and given in dropsy, gonorrhea, hepatic obstruction, and in urinary affections.
A paste of the seeds is applied to rheumatic joints. The seeds are used as an aphrodisiac.
HOMEOPATHIC -The Tribulus plant is full of thorns, which cause intolerable burning, swelling and redness. It
produces small red pimples and eruptions which look like meals and eruptions due to prickly heat.
Malarial attacks associated with urticaria. Fevers appear in the morning, no chill or thirst, urticaria-like eruptions
come on along with the rise of temperature, intense itching which is relieved by cold applications.
Sexual neurasthenia. Impotency. Ailments from masturbation, prostate emissions and spermatorrhea.
Impotence caused by overindulgence of advancing age or when accompanied by urinary symptoms incon-
tinence, painful urination, etc. Prostatitis. Leucorrhea. Gonorrhea.
Dropsy. Urinary affections. Urinary calculus. Kidney stones. Hepatic obstruction. Skin diseases, worse from
heat and better from cold. Ulcers due to impurities of blood. Rheumatism. Insomnia.
COMMENTS - Charaka found it useful in stone, gravel and calculus in the bladder, and strangury. Sushruta
recommended it as a great sexual tonic. Bagbhata recommended it for all skin diseases due to impurities of
blood. Chakradatta thought that it could be effectively used in dropsy.
Bangasena acknowledged its efficacy in effecting safe delivery. Harita recommended it for sleeplessness. He
also said that it can produce sound sleep if the root is placed on the head.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Ghose.

name: Trichosanthes Dioica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - trich-d. Trichosanthes dioica. Wild snakegourd. N. O. Cucurbitaceae. Roots and leaves.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anasarca. Bilious. Catarrh. Chickenpox. Cholera. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Fever. Headache.
Hemoptysis. Jaundice. Kala-azar. Nausea. Rheumatism. Smallpox. Synovitis. Vomiting. Water brash.
HERBAL - The leaves of Trichosanthes dioica are tonic, febrifuge. Fruits of the bitter variety are used in
scorpion stings. The fruit is described by Sanskrit writers as febrifuge, laxative and anti-bilious.
Ayurvedic physicians of India found this drug to be of great use in multifarious complaints. Charaka found it to
be a sovereign remedy in cases of dropsy, anasarca, bilious and catarrhal fevers, slow chronic fevers
associated with hemoptysis and also in synovitis.
Chakradatta recommended it in bilious and catarrhal fevers and rheumatism. Su- shruta found it efficacious in
hemoptysis and bilious fevers.
Bhavaprakasha recommended its use in smallpox with predominance of bilious symptoms. In the opinion of
some Ayurvedic physicians, it is an excellent remedy in smallpox and chickenpox.
HOMEOPATHIC - The root-bark of Trichosanthes dioica possesses highly purgative properties. It causes
purging to such a great extent that a little overdose may cause death.
At first the stool appears to be loose, gradually the patient passes bilious and mucous stools, and finally bloody
stools and vomiting of blood appear producing the stage of collapse.
Useful for diarrhea, dysentery, cholera and cholerine. Copious loose stools, of green or yellow color, may be
mixed with bile and mucus. Prolapsed rectum. Burning in anus. Smarting after stool. Passage of involuntary
and bloody stool.
Bloody stools appear without cessation and cause profound prostration and exhaustion. The stools may be
mixed with particles of mucus. Frothy stool, during its passage no pain or uneasiness is felt, after stool, urging
and straining continue for a long time.
Cholera where there are copious stools and vomiting associated with restlessness, thirst, burning, sweat,
extreme weakness, coldness of extremities, pulselessness and other symptoms.
Pain and gurgling in stomach. Gurgling with copious yellow stools. Nausea before vomiting, water brash and
 rumbling in abdomen. Nausea after drinking water. Constant water brash. Vomiting, copious stringy mucus
which may be streaked with blood. Vomiting of bile.
Jaundice. Yellow eyes, with dropsy. Chronic fevers, with enlargement of the liver and spleen. Fevers with
bilious symptoms, with headache, water brash, nausea, and especially bilious diarrhea.
Acute, chronic and malarial fevers and also in kala-azar. The fever comes on at 11 a.m. or 12 noon with
chilliness, and thirst and headache exist. After this stage headache continues, but it increases with the rise of
temperature. The fever may be of short duration one day and of longer duration the next day. Fever with
vomiting (Ip.).
Trichosanthes bears a close resemblance to Podo, and it may be safely used in those cases where Podo, is
indicated or where Podo, fails to do any good.
RELATIONS - Compare: Trich-d. may be a grand substitute for Ip. and Podo, or it may be employed where
these two medicines fail to do any good.
REFERENCES - Ghose.

name: Trifolium Pratense
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - trif-p. Trifolium pratense. Red clover. N. O. Papilionoideae. Tincture of flower heads. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Blood, disorders. Cancer. Cough. Crusta, lactea. Diabetes.
Dysentery. Fainting. Fibroids, bleeding. Hemorrhages. Hoarseness. Menopause. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia.
Tumors. Whooping cough. Writer’s cramp.
HERBAL - Red clover is an herbal blood tonic and puriher. It has a reputation among herbalists in whooping
cough and the coughs of measles and tuberculosis. Felter gave red clover to persons disposed to cancer. He
found it retarded the progress of cancerous tumors and improves the general condition of the patient.
HOMEOPATHIC - T. C. Duncan and others proved it and elicited some very decided respiratory symptoms,
dry, tickling cough, oppressed breathing with fever. One peculiar symptom was a cough followed by hiccough.
Marked salivation. Feeling of fullness with congestion of salivary glands, followed by increased flow of saliva.
Crusta lactea, dry, scaly crusts. Stiff neck. Feeling as if mumps were coming on. Preventive for mumps and
cancer. Retards progress of cancerous tumors before ulceration has taken place. Cancerous diathesis.
MIND - Mental breakdown. Confusion of ideas, morning. Loss of memory.
Abdomen - Griping pains in abdomen and headache. Colicky pains all day.
Back - Neck stiff, cramp in sterno-cleido muscles, relieved by heat and irritation.
Constitutions - Cancer diathesis.
Head - Confusion and headaches on awaking. Dullness in anterior brain.
Limbs - Hands and feet cold. Tingling in palms. Tibial ulcers.
Lungs - Sensation in lungs as if breathing hot air. Air feels as if full of impurities.
Mouth - Increased flow of saliva (Merc., Syph.).
Lungs - Hay fever. Coryza like that which precedes hay fever, thin mucus with much irritation. Hoarse and
choking, chills with cough at night. Cough on coming into the open air. Spasmodic cough. Whooping
cough, paroxysms, worse at night.
Throat - Sore throat with hoarseness.
COMMENTS - Trif-p. has many symptoms of congestion. Dull, stupid feeling generally.
The head and lungs feel full of blood. Sensation in lungs as if breathing hot air, as if air full of impurities.
Persistent headache on waking. Unreffeshing sleep. Weak and intermittent pulse, later full and bounding.
Irritation of the pharynx and trachea. “Sharp pain through uvula causing tears to start.” Dryness of trachea
causing him to clear throat of some foreign substance. Secretion of urine increased.
Farrington noted “Hoarseness and choking spells at night with cough, the neck is stiff, cramps in sternomastoid
muscle better by heat and friction.”
Cooper said of Trif-p. that it causes salivation in horses and diarrhea if they eat much of it and that it cures
mumps and disorders of the pancreas and salivary glands. Hale said it causes “heaves” in horses.
Felter noted “scaly and ulcerated conditions of the tibial region of the old.” The symptoms are worse in close
room, better in open air. “When I became very warm with the fever my breathing stopped, lungs felt as if
breathing hot air.” Worse after sleep.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Trif-r. Complementary: Calc-p. - menstrual andhemorrhagic affections.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Trigonella Foenum Graecum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - trig-f-g. Trigonella foenum graecum. Fenugreek. Foenumgraecum officinale. North Africa, India.
N. O. Fabaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses. Baldness. Beriberi. Boils. Bronchitis. Burns. Cancer. Carbuncles. Cataracts. Cellulitis.
Colic. Constipation. Convalescence. Cough. Cysts. Dermatitis. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Eczema. Gout. Hernia.
High blood pressure. Hives. Hyperthyroidism. Hypoglycemia. Impotence. Indigestion. Infections. Leg, edema.
Leukemia. Lice. Liver disease. Lymphadenitis. Menopausal symptoms. Muscle aches. Peptic ulcer. Rickets.
Sores. Spleen, enlargement. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Vaginal, dryness. Wounds.
HERBAL - Fenugreek is native to southern Europe, the Mediterranean region, and Western Asia. The words
foenum - graecum mean Greek hay and arise because of the appearance of the plant which has long slender
stems. Fenugreek seeds contain a high percentage of mucilage, a natural gummy substance present in the
coatings of many seeds. Although it does not dissolve in water, mucilage forms a thick, gooey mass when
exposed to fluids.
The resulting soft mass is not absorbed by the body, but instead passes through the intestines and also triggers
intestinal muscle contractions. Both actions promote the emptying of intestinal contents. Therefore, fenugreek
is a mild but effective laxative.
In addition, fenugreek seeds contain chemicals that slow down the time that food takes to go through the
intestinal tract. As one result, sugars are absorbed from foods more slowly and blood sugar levels may not
rise as high or fluctuate as much as
usual. Fenugreek may further affect blood sugar levels by decreasing the activity of an enzyme that is involved
in releasing stored sugar from the liver into the blood.
Some evidence suggests that fenugreek may also have other medical uses. Fenugreek lowers cholesterol
levels as well as blood sugar levels. It may reduce the amounts of calcium oxalate in the kidneys. Calcium
oxalate often contributes to kidney stones.
Fenugreek also appeared to lessen the chance of developing colon cancer. It may have some ability to protect
the liver against damage from alcohol and other chemicals. Fenugreek is a skin softener and is often an
ingredient of soothing facial masks.
Fenugreek is also used for hair care as it prevents hair fall, cures dandruff, and promotes hair growth. A paste
of fenugreek seeds is usually applied to the scalp at least 40 minutes before washing hair to help get rid of
dandruff, and act as a remedy for hair loss.
The use of shampoo to wash hair can be skipped if fenugreek seed paste is applied on the scalp as the paste
helps to remove oil and dirt from the hair and also makes the hair soft. The paste of fresh fenugreek leaves is
also used to get rid of dandruff, increase the length of hair, soften the hair, and help preserve its natural color.
Paste of the fresh leaves of fenugreek, applied on the face every night before going to bed and washed with
warm water, prevents pimples, blackheads, dryness of the face, and early appearance of wrinkles. It improves
complexion and leads to younger looking skin. Fenugreek paste made by grinding fenugreek seeds when used
as a mask has a granular texture that helps remove blackheads.
The topical application of the gelatinous texture of fenugreek seed may also have some benefit for soothing
skin that is irritated by eczema or other conditions. Fenugreek helps to remove excess oil from the skin. It has
also been applied as a warm poultice to relieve muscle aches and gout pain.
A poultice of the leaves can be used for boils, cysts, burns, ulcers, hives, eczema, abscesses, carbuncles, etc.
It is also used to treat cuts and sores. Excessive topical use of fenugreek on the same areas may cause itching,
 redness, rash, or other reactions. Individuals who have allergies to peanuts or soybeans may also be allergic
to fenugreek.
RELATIONS - Compare: Alf., Avena.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Trillium Pendulum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tril. Trillium pendulum. Lamb’s quarter. White bethroot.Trillium erectum. Purple trillium.
Bethroot. Birthroot. Rattlesnake root. Wake Robin. Three-leaved nightshade. N. O. Smilaceae orTrilliaceae of
the Liliaceae. Tincture of the fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Menopause. Diabetes. Dysentery. Fainting. Fibroids, bleeding. Headache.
Hemorrhages. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Nosebleeds. Writer’s cramp.
HERBAL - The chief uses of Trillium pendulum come to us from herbalists, who learned some of them from
the Native Americans. The popular name Birth-root sufficiently ' indicates one part of its reputation.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tril. is a great hemorrhagic medicine. Hemorrhage with great faintness and dizziness.
Hemorrhages of all kinds with pregnancy. Hemorrhages after childbirth, menopause, from fibroid tumors,
gushing, bright red. Uterine hemorrhage.
Threatened miscarriage. Cramp-like pains. Relaxation of pelvic region. Chronic diarrhea of bloody mucus.
Tuberculosis with purulent and copious expectoration and spitting of blood.
MIND - Irritable .Anguish, agitation and tossing about, impossible to keep still. Repugnance to conversation.
Melancholy with sadness.
Abdomen - Swelling of abdomen as in ascites. Much flatulence and grumbling.
Constitutions - Suited to women who bleed after every labor pain, flabby subjects.
Eyes - Feel too large and as if would fall out from their sockets. Vision blurred,
Trillium pendulum everything looks bluish.
Female - Leucorrhea is copious, yellow, and stringy (Hydr., Kali-bi., Sabin.). Menses every two weeks. Uterine
hemorrhages with sensation as though hips and back were falling to pieces, better tight bandages.
Gushing of bright blood on least movement. Hemorrhage from fibroids (Calc., Thal., Spig., Phos., Ust.).
Prolapsed uterus with great bearing-down. Metrorrhagia at menopausal. Lochia suddenly becomes bloody.
Profuse long-lasting bloody lochia. Varicose veins of pregnancy. Dribbling of urine after labor.
Head - Dull pain, worse noise, walking, coughing, better bending forward. Pain in forehead, worse noise.
Headache worse by least noise, walking, coughing. Confused, eyeballs feel too large.
Heart - Palpitations with great anxiety.
Limbs - Cramping pains in muscles of arms and calves.
Lungs - Suffocative attack of irregular breathing with sneezing. Shooting pains through chest. Aching at end
of sternum. Cough with spitting of blood. Copious and purulent expectoration. Hemoptysis.
Modalities - Better by exercise in open air. Better from a tight bandage, bending forward. Worse from motion,
sitting erect. Worse menopause. Worse after eating. Motion aggravates the hemorrhages. Standing or walking
causes bearing down in pelvis.
Mouth - Very offensive taste, especially on rising in morning. Greasy feeling on tongue and gums. Bleeding
from gums. Bleeding after tooth extraction.
Nose - Profuse nosebleed (Mill., Meli.).
Rectum - Chronic diarrhea with bloody discharge. Dysentery with passing of almost pure blood. Diarrhea thin,
watery, tinged with blood, painless. Constipation succeeded by thin, watery, very offensive diarrhea.
Sensations - As if eyes too large. As if a crumb were in larynx. As if the chest was tightly bound and could not
be expanded. As if hips and small of back were falling to pieces. As if sacroiliac joint were falling apart, wants
to be bound tightly. As if bones were broken. Left side most affected.
Skin - Skin hot and dry, with itching and burning, worse by scratching.
Stomach - Sickness, excessive pain, cramp of stomach. Faintness and sinking at stomach, with heat. Heat
and burning stomach rising up in esophagus. Hematemesis.
Temperature - Feverish during pain in abdomen, on the subsidence of which a profuse perspiration broke out.
Vertigo - Vertigo on rising in morning.
COMMENTS - Millspaugh considered Tril. erectum as the proper source of the homeopathic tincture.
According to Millspaugh, Tril. pendulum is the white variety of Tril. erectum. The Treasury of Botany gave the
names as synonymous. The symptoms of H. Minton, the original prover, were given in Allen under Tril.
cernuum.
Minton’s proving ofTril. cernuumbrought out the hemorrhagic property in the blood tinged diarrhea.
 Copious hemorrhages, either active or passive, usually bright red and profuse. Hemorrhage, ante-partum and
menopausal, fibroid tumors. Hemorrhage, with faintness and sinking at the stomach, also cold limbs and rapid,
feeble pulse. “Flooding with fainting.”
Hemorrhages with restlessness and exhaustion. Blue vision, craving for ice water. Tendency to putrescence
of fluids. Tril. has been used as a local hemostatic in nosebleed and for bleeding after tooth extraction.
Minton’s proving brought out “Sensation of emptiness in abdomen.” He also noted extreme debility, palpitation
and anxiety. Restless tossing agitation, fear of being sick, and great anguish were experienced by Minton.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Tril-c. - eye symptoms, everything looks bluish, greasy feeling in mouth. (2) Fic.
- hemorrhages, menorrhagia, hematuria, nosebleed, hematemesis, bleeding hemorrhoids. (3) Hir., Leech -
hemorrhages, bleeding from anus. (4) Ip., Sabin., Lach., Ham. Complementary: Calc-p. (menstrual and
hemorrhagic affections).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Menopause. Diabetes. Dysentery. Fainting. Fibroids, bleeding. Headache.

name: Trinitrotoluenum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - trinit. Trinitrotoluenum. T.N.T. Trotyl. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Cramps. Cyanosis. Depression. Dermatitis. Dyspnea. Faintness. Fatigue. Heart,
disorders. Hemorrhages. Insomnia. Jaundice. Palpitations. Vertigo. Vesicles.
HOMEOPATHIC - TNT is a high explosive, obtained by nitrating toluene, a product of coal tar distillation. When
the skin or hair is exposed to TNT by contact a characteristic yellow or tawny-orange stain is produced, which
lasts for some weeks. Indicated in graver forms of anemia (pernicious) and jaundice. Produces fatal toxic
jaundice.
Symptoms were noted in ammunition workers handling TNT who inhale and ingest it, and also absorb some
through the skin. They were compiled by Dr. C. Wesselhoeft and published in the December, 1926 issue of
the Journal of the American Institute of Homeopathy.
The destructive action of Trinit. on the red blood corpuscles is responsible for the anemia and the jaundice
with their secondary symptoms. The hemoglobin is changed so it cannot act satisfactorily as an oxygen carrier
and as a result there is breathlessness, dizziness. Headaches, faintness, and palpitations. Undue fatigue,
muscle cramps and cyanosis, also drowsiness, depression and insomnia.
Later stages of the poisoning produce toxic jaundice and aplastic anemia. The jaundice is the result of cellular
destruction in contrast to obstructive jaundice. Faintness, dizziness, mental sluggishness, delirium, convulsion,
coma. Face very dark.
MIND - Depression. Apathetic and cries easily. Aversion to company. Mental sluggishness, delirium.
Food - Aversion to tea. Alcohol aggravates.
Head - Frontal headache and depression.
Heart - Palpitations, tachycardia and bradycardia. Intermittent pulse.
Kidneys - Sudden desire, incontinence and retention. High colored urine, burning on urination.
Lungs - Nose dry with stuffed sensation. Burning of trachea, choking weight on chest, dry, convulsive cough,
raising mucus plugs.
Modalities - Worse alcohol, falls after one or two drinks of whisky.
Nose - Sneezing, coryza.
Skin - Tendency to hemorrhage under the skin and from the nose. Hands stained yellow. Dermatitis, nodular
erythema, vesicles, itching and burning, puffiness. Tired pain in back of knees.
Stomach - Bitter taste, much thirst, sour regurgitation, dull burning behind the ensiform, nausea, vomiting,
constipation followed by diarrhea with cramps.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Zinc., Phos., Cina, Ars., Plum.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Triosteum Perfoliatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - trio. Triosteum perfoliatum. Fever-wort. Fever root. Wild coffee. Horsegentian. N. O.
Caprifliaceae, Tribe, Lonicereae. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Adenoma. Angina pectoris. Arteritis. Asthma. Backaches. Biliousness. Blepharitis. Breast pain.
Conjunctivitis. Coughs. Cystitis. Dyspepsia. Encephalitis. Erysipelas. Erythema. Fevers. Headache, bilious.
Herpes zoster. Infections. Influenza. Joints, stiff. Measles. Menorrhagia. Numbness. Otitis. Ozaena.
Pyelonephritis. Rheumatism. Scarlet, fever. Typhoid, fever. Typhus, fever. Urticaria. Vomiting.
HERBAL - The name “fever-wort” tells its traditional reputation. Hale said it is one of the ingredients of the
 “fever powder” of the herbalists.
HOMEOPATHIC - Trio, is an energetically acting drug and has been proved by Williamson, Neidhard, Gatchell
and other experienced provers. The symptoms were established by Raeside on fifteen provers (eight men and
seven women) in 1959-60. Raeside used the 8c potency, at the rate of
one dose every morning until the symptoms appeared.
Trio, is traditionally prescribed as a febrifuge. Above all, it causes vomiting, gastric pains, generalized pains,
fever with agitation and insomnia. Talmadge, one of the provers, found it of great value in typhoid and gastric
fevers. It produced acute rheumatic symptoms and an intense urticaria.
Biliousness. Gallbladder colic. Diarrhea attended with colicky pains and nausea. Numbness of lower limbs
after stool. Increased flow of urine.
Dryness of the mucus membranes of the lips, mouth and throat. Dry cough. Influenza with aching pains all
over with heat in the limbs. Acute encephalitis in infancy, especially after diphtheria, measles, whooping cough.
Sudden weariness around 2 a.m. and4 p.m. Sensation of sleeping standing up. Sensation of needles all over
the body when hot. Generalized pain in the upper and lower limbs. Nervous symptoms (Coff., Hyos.).
Generalized itching, especially on the scalp and limbs of the upper and lower limbs. Erythema, eruption of flat,
hard nodules, brown or purple in color, on the joints in the limbs.
MIND - Irritated by noise and in the evening. Irritability, difficulty in controlling himself. In the evening, feels in
a rage, difficult to control himself. Tends to quarrel bitterly, argumentative.
Nervous and sleepy, cannot concentrate. Mental exhaustion. All mental activity requires a great effort.
Euphoria, followed by a state of depression. Feels isolated, better when alone.
Abdomen - Distended and full of gas. Pain in the coccyx. Sharp pain in the left side of the groin. Epigastric
pain spreading to the thorax and throat. Enterocolitis. Colic, especially in the right iliac fossa and the
hypogastrium. Flatulence, after drinking milk.
Back - Painful stiffness of the back.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Pressing pain in the precordial region when lying on the left side. Dull ache all over
the thorax, predominately in the retro-sternal region with thoracic constriction. Swollen glands in right axilla.
Ears - Otitis. Constant earache in the left ear and discharge. Itching around the ears. Buzzing noises, worse
when lying down.
Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Smarting and hot, painful, especially when closed. Left eye swollen, red and hot. Eyes
water, difficult to focus. Blepharitis. Eyelids irritated, especially the right side. Twitching of right eyelid in the
evening.
Female - Irregular cycle, either late or early menses. Menses long and late. Menses painful, scanty.
Menorrhagia.
Food - Loathing of food. Painful hungry feeling, aggravated around 11 a.m. and in the evening. Worse after
drinking milk.
Head - Occipital pain with nausea on rising, followed by vomiting. Frontal headache. Dull pain, pulsating or
pressing, located at the forehead, occiput or temples. Pressing headache at the left temple and occiput and
on the right side of the forehead. Stinging, needle-like pain in the left orbital region. Painful tenderness of the
scalp and hair when touched.
Heart - Angina pectoris. Arteritis of the coronary arteries. Pulse slow and weak.
Kidneys - Pyelonephritis. Cystitis. Frequent urination. Smell of ammonia in the urine. Adenoma of the prostate
gland.
Limbs - Generalized pains in the upper and lower limbs. Stiffness of all joints, calves numbs, aching in the
bones. Rheumatic pain in back. Pains in limbs. Numbness of the lower limbs after going to stool. Burning,
pulsating pains in the right axilla, where the glands are swollen. Cramping pain in the left shoulder and arm in
the two lower limbs and in the fingers of the right hand.
Lungs - Sensation of choking, has to grope for breath. Asthma. Bronchitis. Dry cough, caused by irritation of
the larynx after eating. Cough, especially in the evening, aggravated in a warm room.
Modalities - Better from rest, solitude. Better fresh air, cold drinks. Worse early morning, 3 a.m. to 7 a.m.
Worse in the
Triosteum perfoliatum evening, at night, lying, turning in bed, after sleep, rising from bed, waking. Worse
sitting up, movement. Worse from heat, drinking cold water.
Mouth - Dry mouth and lips. Mouth like parchment, hot with paresthesia of the lips. Fissure on the lower lip,
painful ulcerated areas on the mouth, palate and lips. Sensation of a bitter taste, upper teeth painful. Tongue
white and seems swollen.
Nose - Spots on the nose. Dryness of the nose and ears. Dull, continual aching behind the root of the nose.
Painful rightsided sinusitis and hyperesthesia of the left side of the face. Rhinitis. Ozaena. Sinusitis, spasmodic
 coryza. Coryza with running nose, thick, green discharge with sneezing. Nosebleed and smell of blood in the
nose.
Rectum - Proctitis. Constipated, great effort to pass stools, which produces small, hard stools. Stools followed
by diarrhea and nauseating wind. Stools watery, frothy. Rectal pains, stabbing, aggravated by pushing to
evacuate, worse after passing stools. Rectal burning with anal itching, especially at night. Hemorrhoids.
Skin - Erysipelas. Eczema. Itching welts. Urticaria from gastric derangement. Itching of the whole body.
Itching, especially of the feet, scalp, palms of hands, where there isadry eruption. Erythematous eruption on
the calves, back, scrotum and on the inside of the thighs. Soles of feet itchy in the evening and in bed. Itching
eruption on the shoulders and between the scapulae. Patches of brown on the skin. Peeling of the skin on the
abdomen. Hyperesthesia of the skin, profuse perspiration, worse at night and from exercise.
Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Loathing of food, nausea on rising, followed by vomiting and cramps. Nausea,
worse after meals, thirsty for cold drinks, which soothe.
Throat - Painful, irritated, especially at night and on waking. Pharynx red, causing a sensation of constriction.
Tickling feeling causes coughing, the left tonsil is painful. Better by drinking cold drinks, even though
swallowing is painful. Hoarseness, aggravated when speaking and in fresh air. Tickling feeling at the back of
the throat with constriction, stifling feeling, causing a dry cough.
COMMENTS - Talmadge said of the effect on himself, ‘Trios, acted promptly and emphatically, causing aching
pains in nearly every part of the body, especially of lower limbs and head.”
The right side of the head was more affected than the left. The stomach was very much disordered. Severe
vomiting and pain in the stomach. Itching at the anus, exudation of mucus.
A peculiar concomitant of the evacuations was numbness of the lower limbs after stool. Many symptoms came
on in the early morning hours. One prover, though sleepy, could not sleep after midnight.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bapt. - Gastric fever. Digestive complaints, putrid excreta, exhaustion, muscle
pain. (2) Rheumatism, Bry., Rhus-t. (3) Load at epigastrium, Abies-n. (4) Sleepy but cannot sleep, Bell. Bell. -
Fever, heat, restlessness, thirst. (5) Aeon. - Skin dry, anxiety, extreme restlessness. (6) Ars. - Anxiety,
restlessness, burning pains ameliorated by the heat. (7) Coff. - Palpitations insomnia, restlessness. (8) Lach.
- Congestive rush of blood, pharyngeal constriction, worse on waking. (9) Lat-m. - Pre-stemal pains resembling
angina. ( 10) Lyc. - Distention aggravated after 4 p.m. (11) Sulph. - Itching and heat on the feet, alternating
with coldness.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Triticum Repens
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tritic. Triticum repens. Couch grass. Agropyrum repens. Cooch-grass. Cutch-grass. Quitch
grass. N. O. Gramineae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, disorders. Cystitis. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Incontinence. Prostate, enlarged. Pyelitis.
Strangury.
HERBAL - Burnett told how he learned from an herbalist the use of Tritic.; the herbalist cured a patient of
Burnett’s with it, the man suffered from dysuria. Burnett found it no less valuable for women than for men.
“Frequently in dysuria from an inflamed state of the urethra, Tritic., ten drops in a little water, frequently
repeated of prompt effect often giving complete relief in a few hours and if the ailment is primarily in the urethra
the relief is an abiding cure, if from a tugging of the heavy womb, it is only relief.”
HOMEOPATHIC - Excessive, chronic irritability of the bladder. Dysuria, cystitis and gonorrhea. Strangury,
pyelitis. Enlarged prostate. Incontinence, constant desire.
Dysuria, frequent, difficult and painful urination (Pop.). Catarrhal and purulent discharges (Pareir.). Urine
is filled with gravel and sediment which causes irritation of the mucus surfaces. Always blowing nose.
COMMENTS - Burnett gave the case of a widow who was suffering from a complete procidentia uterus and
very bad hemorrhoidal bleeding. She wrote that she was driven almost mad with painful urination, the burning
and straining were truly awful.
Tritic., as above, was ordered and brought a most grateful letter from the patient. She kept a supply always at
hand.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chim., Senec., Pop., Buchu, Uva., Trad. (2) Polytr. - Ground Moss - Painful
urination of old people, dropsy, urinary obstruction and suppression).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Trombidium Muscae Domesticae
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - from. Trombidium muscae domesticae. Acarus. Red acarus of the fly. N. O. Acarudea, class,
Arachnida. Tincture of the animals. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, prolapsed. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Hip joint, pain. Liver, pain. Nose, catarrh. Sciatica. Tibia,
pain. Toothache.
HOMEOPATHIC - Trom. is a parasite found singly or in groups upon the common house-fly of a bright red
color, nearly circular in shape. The alcoholic tincture, a brilliant orange in color was prepared from specimens,
about 115 in number, collected in Frankfort, Philadelphia in 1864.
The provings, under the supervision of Hering, were made with the 3x, 6x, 9c, 18c. and 30c potencies. Trom.
has cured dysentery with brown, thin, bloody stools and tenesmus. Dysentery, worse by food and drink.
Brown, thin, bloody stools, much pain before and after stools. Stools only after eating.
Mucus discharge from nose while eating dinner. Weakness. Felt better in evening, better in open air. Rising
up causes fainting. Reading aloud causes toothache. Rheumatic pains in left shoulder, arm, knee, and region
of heart. Inability to keep quiet.
MIND - Talkative during day. Disposed to be contrary. Constant disposition to gape. Inability to collect ideas.
Absence of ideas. Loss of memory.
Abdomen - Congestion of the liver. Griping in hypochondrium in morning. Much pain in abdomen before and
after stool.
Chest - Cutting to right of lower part of sternum. Sharp pain in lower part of chest. Throbbing all over chest
from 9 to 11 a.m.
Ears - Shooting in ears in afternoon, worse swallowing or blowing nose. Itching in ears after rising. Burning in
ears in evening.
Eyes - Redness of internal part of conjunctiva, similar to a pterygium. Lachrymation in open air. Itching at right
inner canthus.
Food - Appetite lost.
Head - Oppressive headache. Dullness of head in forenoon. Head heavy, sometimes sharp pains in temples.
Lungs - Hoarseness. Hacking cough from irritation in throat.
Modalities - Warm drink improves toothache. Open air improves coryza. Worse from anyfood ordrink, after
stool. Worse by touch, pressure. Worse shaking head, moving. Cold air aggravates toothache. Cold bath
aggravates pain in abdomen.
Mouth - Tongue coated white.
Nose - Nose obstructed on rising. Fluent coryza in open air and on eating. Mucus discharge from nose, worse
during dinner. Dryness of nose in evening, with scabs.
Nosebleed in morning, afternoon.
Rectum - Burning in anus. Sharp pain in left side, shooting downward during stool. Urgent, loose, stools on
rising. Stool only after eating. Brown, thin, bloody stools with tenesmus.
Sensations - As if there were no weight in ear, lightness. As from incarcerated flatus in abdomen. As if
excoriated after tenesmus. As if everything were coming out of anus. As if hot air blowing over lower abdomen
and thigh. As if abdomen needed support. As if three toes on left foot would be twisted off. As if her breath
were leaving her.
Skin - Pimples on nape in evening. Itching in spots on chin and among whiskers, in evening, and about neck.
Sleep - Constant inclination to gape through day, in afternoon. Sleepiness. Restless sleep. Lewd dreams.
Wakefulness after 4 a.m., with restlessness.
Stomach - Griping in pit of stomach, worse after dinner. Belching after meals, tasting of ingesta. Vomiting after
breakfast, thought it was from drinking coffee.
Teeth - Toothache, better warm drinks. Aching in left decayed tooth, worse lying down, eating, talking, and
cold air.
Temperature - Chilliness at night, worse morning on waking. Fever in afternoon, with pulsation in arteries of
head and aching on occiput and small of back.
Throat - Throat sore on right side.
Vertigo - Lightness of head. Dizziness, on every attempt to rise from bed, with faintness.
COMMENTS - The grand keynote of Trom. is “worse by eating or drinking,” in the nose, teeth or tonsils. On
this indication, Clarke cured some of the worst cases of diarrhea and intestinal pains coming on when the
patient eat or drinks.
“Much pain before and after stool, stool only after eating.” Congested liver with urgent, loose stools on rising
from bed. During stool, sharp pain in left side, shooting downward.
Skin symptoms, especially itching of scalp and in whiskers. Restlessness, inability to keep quiet. Fainting on
rising up.
 RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Staph, (toothache), Merc-c. (diarrhea), Compare: ( 1 ) Rheumatism, Led. (2)
Diarrhea. Sulph. (3) Worse blowing nose. Cube, Thuj. (4) Stitches up anus, Ign., Nit-ac., Sul-ac. with prolapse,
Podo.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Tropaeolum Majus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - trop. Tropaeolum majus. Indian cress. Garden Nasturtium. N. O. Tro- paeolaceae. Tincture of
fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
HERBAL - Tropaeolum is a native of Peru. The taste of the leaves were considered like the taste of cress, and
they have been used like cress in salads. The seeds make pickles and are used as a substitute for capers.
A patient to whom Cooper gave Trop, noted that it made the urine extremely fetid in smell. On this keynote,
Cooper relieved several cases of urinary difficulty, giving single doses of the tincture.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Tuberculinum Aviaire
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - tub-a. Tuberculinum aviaire. Chicken tuberculosis. Tuberculinum avis. Nosodes. A preparation
of chicken tuberculosis. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Chronic fatigue. Colds. Coughs. Debility. Emaciation.
Influenza. Lung, disorders. Measles. Pneumonia. Prostration. Tuberculosis. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Tub-a. is prepared from the infected liver of chickens. Dr. Cartier gave an account of this
nosode in his paper read at the International Homeopathic Congress, 1896. The bacillus of avian tuberculosis
has been identified with that of human tuberculosis. But the clinical properties of the two nosodes are not
identical.
Tub-a. acts most prominently on the apices of the lungs and it corresponds most closely to the bronchitis
ofinfluenza, which simulates tuberculosis, having cured several hopeless-looking cases. It has also done
Tuberculinum aviaire excellently in some cases of bronchitis following measles. H. D. Baker noted “Tub.
aviare has served me better than any remedy in the long lasting prostration after the influenza."
Dr. Francois Cartier of France found it useful in broncho-pneumonia of children and persistent cough after
influenza and measles.
Symptoms similar to tuberculosis, relieves the debility, diminishes the cough, improves the appetite and braces
up the whole organism. Acute broncho-pulmonary diseases of children. Itching of palms and ears. Coughs
are irritating, incessant and tickling, loss of strength and appetite. Emaciation (Hydr. to fatten patients after
tuberculosis).
Acts on the mind, spinal nerves and branches, muscles, joints, bronchi and mucus membranes. Influenza and
its sequelae. Chronic fatigue. Muscular or nerve pains are better by motion, but the patient tires easily. Pains
and mental symptoms are better in the open air.
Relaxed, degraded conditions of tissues and secretion. Dingy, unhealthy, doughy or aged appearance and
feeling of the skin and soft tissues and an old catarrhal aspect of mucus excretions. In acute conditions the
rapidity of the emaciation is notable.
MIND - Depressed. Easily frightened. Mentally changeable in feeling and purpose. Desires change.
Dissatisfied with present conditions and surroundings. Desperate, wicked feelings. Lack of moral sense. Rest-
lessness, the desire for change is physical as well as mental.
COMMENTS - Anshutz related a case of a woman who entered the hospital suffering from influenza and who,
a few days after a slight amelioration of her symptoms, was attacked with a pulmonary congestion, clearly
localized in the top of the left lung and accompanied by all the clinical symptoms of tuberculosis.
Rales and moist crepitation, dullness, exaggeration of the thoracic vibration, expectoration, fever, perspiration,
spitting of blood. Examination of the sputa showed distinctly the presence of Koch’s bacilli.
Anshutz gave her Tub-a. and in three weeks all the symptoms had left. That woman left the hospital completely
cured and a year later her health was still perfect. Anshutz noted ten cases of influenzal bronchitis with
incessant coughs, fever and expectoration, rapidly cured by Tub-a.
It seems that Tub-a. does not act in diminishing the cough like an anodyne, but braces up the whole organism.
The relief of debility and the return of appetite are the phenomena which was observed in conjunction with the
diminution of the cough.
In contrast with Bac., Tub-a. has considerable cough and little dyspnea. It has an acute, irritating cough, such
as one meets with in acute diseases or sub-acute disorders in young people. A cough which fatigues and
 which leads to enfeeblement and loss of appetite, a suspicious cough.
Dr. R.E.S. Hayes made the following statement: “My experience has led me to select the Tub. Bovinum for
patients presenting more pronounced localizations in the meninges, abdomen, skin, glands or joints. But the
Tub. Aviare for patients who were affected by a more evident depreciation of quality in the entire person at the
same time, such as occurs after influenza or similar crises. This observation is purely clinical.
“Recurrent influenza with long continued cough. Long continued, annoying, teasing cough remaining after the
active symptoms of bronchitis or influenza, in a good many instances Tuberculinum aviare put an immediate
end to this cough any related discomforts. Aviare has the usual characteristics of Tuberculinum plus its affinity
to influenza and to nerve elements, both sympathetic and cerebro-spinal.”
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bac., Bac-ts., Tub., Ars-i.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke
