name: Veratrum Viride
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - verat-v. Veratrum viride. American hellebore. Veratrum helonias viridis. Indian Poke. N. O.
Melanthacae of the Liliaceae. Tincture of fresh root gathered in autumn. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Bunions. Carphology. Cecum. Chilblains. Chorea. Colds.
Convulsions. Delirium. Diplopia. Diaphragmitis. Dysmenorrhea. Eclampsia. Esophagitis. Esophagus,
spasms. Erysipelas. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hiccoughs. Hyperpyrexia. Influenza. Malarial fever.
Measles. Meningitis. Menses, suppressed. Muscle, pains. Orchitis. Pneumonia. Proctalgia. Puerperal,
convulsions. Puerperal mania. Pupils, dilated. Sleep, dream filled. Spinal, congestion. Spleen, congested.
Strokes. Sunstroke. Typhoid fever. Uremia. Uterus, congestion.
 HERBAL - Growing side by side, Verat and Verat-v. are scarcely distinguishable when not in flower.
Millspaugh, however, said that though much like Verat. in its minor points, Verat-v. is strikingly different in
general appearance.
Verat-v. having a much more pointed leaf, panicles looser and more compound, the racemes of Verat. being
more compact and as a whole cylindrical, those of Verat- v. scattered, compound and craggy. Verat. flourishes
in mountain meadows, Verat-v. grows in swamps and wet meadows and along mountain creeks from Canada
to the Carolinas.
Through this confusion, an accidental proving of the latter has been included in the pathogenesis of Verat-v.
The plants belong to different orders, though it must be admitted there is a close resemblance in their effects.
The root of Verat-v. contains Veratrine and the other alkaloids found in the root of Verat., but in different
proportions.
HOMEOPATHIC - Burt proved Squibb’s liquid extract of Verat-v, and said he found no other preparation
satisfactory.
Hinsdale noted that it is known clinically that such diseases as Tiegel’s contracture, Thompson’s disease,
athetosis and muscular paralysis present a symptomatology quite like that produced by Verat-v. upon muscular
tissue.
Verat-v. produces violent congestive conditions, base of brain, medulla, lungs with nausea and vomiting and
weakness. Stomach, heart and capillaries are also affected. Congestions, especially to lungs, base of brain
with nausea and vomiting. Congestive stage and early manifestations of hepatization in pneumonia.
Twitchings and convulsions, here and there during sleep, jerking and trembling, threatened with convulsions.
Chorea, twitching, contortions, unaffected by sleep, froth about the lips. Lies with head low.
Continuous jerking of the head, sexual excitement. Spasms with violent shrieks, opisthotonos, before and after
menses. Children tremble as if frightened and on verge of spasm. Furious delirium.
Muscular prostration, pseudo-hypertrophic muscular paralysis. Great prostration. Sudden effects. Sudden
fainting, prostration, nausea. Fainting, nausea. Erratic motion, staggering. Lowers blood-pressure.
Numbness. Uneasy sensation in the whole body. Effects of sunstroke. Burn-
Veratrum viride ing in different places tongue, pharynx, gullet of skin which is cold with prickling. Zigzag of
temperature. As if damp clothing on arms and legs or clothes would not fit him, seemed as if they were
scratching him somewhere.
Especially adapted to full-blooded and plethoric persons. Bloated, lividface. Rheumatism of heart. Paroxysms
of auricular fibrillation. Induces fall of both systolic and diastolic blood pressure. General pulsations. Eclampsia.
Verat-v. has a pronounced action on the esophagus, it causes a sort of ruminating action or reversed
peristalsis. The least food causes vomiting. Red streak down the center of the tongue. Farrington noted it
for esophagitis. Uremia.
MIND - Loquacity with exaltation of ideas. Suspiciousnature.Fearofseeingherphysician, of being poisoned.
Quarrelsome. Delirium, furious, screams, howls, strikes incessant muttering. Mania, puerperal. Carphology.
Abdomen - Pain above pelvis with soreness. Cutting at navel to groin. Pain in bowels runs into scrotum.
Enteritis with high fever.
Back - Aching pain in back of neck and shoulders. Cannot hold the head up. Opisthotonos.
Causations - Sunstroke. Suppressed menses, lochia.
Chest - Burning in chest.
Constitutions - Suited to full-blooded plethoric persons.
Ears - Deafness from moving quickly with faintness. Cold and pale.
Eyes - Wild, staring during delirium. Blood shot. Pupils dilated. Vision of red spots, purple, on closing eyes,
unsteady. Double vision.
Face - Face flushed, livid turgid, but becomes faint on sitting up. Convulsive twitching of facial muscles
(Agar.). Tension across malar bones. Chewing motions of the jaw.
Female - Menstrual colic before the appearance of the discharge with strangury. Suppressed menstruation
with congestion to head (Bell.). Rigid os (Bell., Gels.). Puerperal fever, convulsions with mania or mania
continues after convulsions
have ceased.
Food - Very thirsty, drinks little, which ameliorates for a short time.
Head - Head retracted. Pain from nape of neck, cannot hold head up. Congestion intense, almost apoplectic.
Hot head, bloodshot eyes. Bloated, livid face. Hippocratic face. Sunstroke, head full, throbbing arteries (Bell.,
Glon., Usn.). Aching on vertex and between eyes. Strokes. Pain up occiput with dim vision and dilated pupils.
Constant jerking or nodding of the head (chorea), throbs on raising up. Meningitis, basilar.
Heart - Constant, dull, burning pain in region of heart. Valvular disease. Beating of pulses throughout body,
 especially in right thigh. Pulse slow, soft, weak, irregular intermittent. Rapid pulse, low tension (Tab., Dig.).
Kidneys - Cystitis with fever. Urine scanty with cloudy sediment.
Limbs -Acute rheumatism. Severe pain in joints and muscles. Violent electric-like shocks in limbs. Cramps
in legs, feet, soles, fingers toes. Convulsive twitching. Pain about the condyles. Pulsation felt in thighs. Restless
hands during delirium. Vesicles on hands.
Lungs - Dyspnea. Difficult breathing. Slow and heavy breathing, as of a load on chest. Congestion of lungs.
Pneumonia, with faint feeling in stomach and violent congestion. Croup. Violent cough from very start.
Modalities - Better from rubbing, lying with head low. Better eating. Pain in head better by pressure. Closing
eyes and resting head helps vertigo. Worse from raising up, lying on back. Worse cold, sunstroke, going
from warm to cold. Worse morning, on waking, evening. Worse after confinement. Motion aggravates, sudden
motion causes faintness and blindness. Walking causes blindness. Lying down aggravates headache,
breathing.
Mouth - Taste like musty odor. Odor from mouth like chloroform or ether. Foul. Increased saliva. Mouth feels
as if scalded. Drawn at one corner.
Nose - Pinched and blue. Rapid and con
tinued sneezing with warm biting feeling in mouth.
Rectum - Tenesmus and burning in rectum, better during and after stools.
Sensations - Confused feeling in head as if head would burst. Tongue as if scalded. As if a ball rising into
esophagus. As if stomach tightly drawn against spine. As of a load on chest. As of galvanic shocks in limbs.
As if damp clothing on arms and legs. As if boiling water poured over parts. As if ankles distorted.
Skin - Hot sweating. Tingling and prickling in skin. Cold, clammy, bluish. Erysipelas with brain symptoms.
Erythema. Itching in different parts better rubbing.
Sleep - Sleeplessness. Dreams of drowning of being on water. Coma.
Stomach - Gastritis. Burning in stomach and esophagus. Stomach seems to press against the spine.
Constrictive pain increased by warm drinks. Hiccoughs, excessive and painful withspasmsofesophagus.
Nausea and vomiting. Vomiting, violent without nausea. Smallest quantity of food or drink immediately rejected.
Temperature - Hyperpyrexia or rapidly oscillating temperature with sweat. Cold clammy or hot sweat.
Cerebrospinal, suppurative, acute rheumatic, fever. Fever high in the evening, below normal in the morning.
Suppurative fevers with great variation of temperature.
Throat - Burning in gullet, esophagitis. As if as ball rising in.
Tongue - Tongue, white as if bleached. Tongue dry with red streak down center.
Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea and sudden prostration, better closing eyes and resting head.
COMMENTS - Hale was instrumental in introducing Verat-v. to homeopathy, using it in fevers and particularly
in pneumonia.
Burt made a heroic proving of the liquid extract and his infant daughter (twenty-one months) very nearly died
from taking a few drops of the tincture from a phial.
In two minutes she began vomiting. Coffee and camphor were given as antidotes. In five minutes her jaws
were rigid, pupils widely dilated, face blue, hands and feet cold, no pulse at wrist.
Her abdomen and back were rubbed with camphor, when she went into spasms with violent shrieks. These
spasms were frequently repeated, a hot path being most effective in relaxing the muscles.
Vomiting ropy mucus kept up for three hours. Pulseless, hands and feet shriveled. After three and a half hours
she slept quietly and soundly and next morning was well but a little weak.
The congestive symptoms and also of nausea and vomiting, form one of the leading indications of Verat-v. in
a great variety of cases. Sensations of fullness. “Head feels full and heavy, rush of blood to the head, face
flushed, buzzing in the ears, chest constricted or oppressed as from a heavy load,” point to the congestive
tendency.
Congestion at the base of brain, chest, spine, stomach. Slowing of the heart’s action is a leading effect of the
provings (from its action on the heart muscle and cardiac ganglia Dig. on the pneumogastric). Violent pains
attending inflammation. Head full, throbbing of arteries, sensitive to sound, double or partial vision.
Chorea, “twitchings during sleep.” “Constant jerking or nodding of the head, jerking and trembling. Threatened
with convulsions,” are other leading symptoms. Puerperal convulsions, Verat-v. has only succeeded when
nauseating doses have been given.
Used locally and internally in muscular and joint rheumatism, and in chorea an application to the spine of the
tincture, diluted with spirit, has proved a serviceable adjunct.
Verat-v. has been used to “knock down” fever in the same way as Aeon. Nash pointed out that there is some
risk in this. When Ve- rat-v. was first introduced he used it largely and successfully in a number of cases, but
in one case which appeared to be going on favorably, the patient died suddenly. This he attributed to the Verat-
 v.
D.     McLellan was sent for in the middle of the night to see an old woman Whom he
found sitting up in bed gasping for breath and blue. Rapid congestion of the lungs had occurred. The attack
had come on suddenly. Verat-v. quickly rescued the patient from a condition of imminent peril.
Clarke with the 30c, cured a man, 56 of dim sight as if scales over it, numbness, pain in head as if a tight band
were around it, rush of blood to head, sleeplessness. Dreaming about water is a characteristic which he has
confirmed.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Hot coffee. Antidote to: Strychnine, use fluid extract, 20-40 drops. Compare:
(1) Puerperal convulsions, Gels, has dull, drowsy state of mind. (2) Verat-v., apoplectic condition between the
fits, face red, eyes congested, violent convulsive twitches. (3) Congestions, Ferr-p., Bell. (4) Plethora, Aeon.
(5) Chorea, Hyos. (6) Pneumonia with engorgement, Sang. (Verat-v. more marked arterial tension). (7)
Scalded tongue, Sang. (8) Tetanus, Nux-v., Hyper. (9) Rheumatic fever,Bry., Sal-ac. (lO)Sunstroke, double or
partial vision. Glon., Gels.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
keynote:
PHARMACY - verat-v. Veratrum viride. American hellebore. Veratrum helonias viridis. Indian Poke. N. O.
Melanthacae of the Liliaceae. Tincture of fresh root gathered in autumn. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Bunions. Carphology. Cecum. Chilblains. Chorea. Colds.
Convulsions. Delirium. Diplopia. Diaphragmitis. Dysmenorrhea. Eclampsia. Esophagitis. Esophagus,
spasms. Erysipelas. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hiccoughs. Hyperpyrexia. Influenza. Malarial feve

name: Verbascum Thapsus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - verb. Verbascumthapsus. Mullein oil. Verbascumthapsiforme. Oleum mullein. Great Mullein. N.
O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of fresh plant at the commencement of flowering. To prepare mullein oil, fill a
bottle with the blossoms from the Verbascum thapsus, cork it tight and hang in the sun for four or five weeks.
By that time there will be an oily liquid distilled. Mix with ten percent of alcohol. Tincture of the whole plant
beginning to flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, itching. Bedwetting. Colic. Constipation. Cough. Deafness. Ear, pain. Hemorrhoids.
Hoarseness. Neuralgia. Prosopalgia. Tumors. Urinary, incontinence.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany said, “The thick woolly leaves of Verbascum thapsus, the Great Mullein,
have a mucilaginous, bitter taste and a decoction of them is employed in domestic practice in catarrhs and
diarrhea.
“The leaves are also used as emollient
applications to hard tumors and in pulmonary complaints in cattle hence one of its popular names is Bullock’s
Lung-wort. It is also called Adam’s flannel from its flannellike leaves.”
Among its traditional uses Gerarde mentioned it as a remedy for hemorrhoids and as applications for itching
hemorrhoids or anal itching. An ointment is made of the tincture. Gerarde said that the oil of the yellow flowers
is also curative in hemorrhoids.
The flowers contain, according to Millspaugh, “A yellow volatile oil and fatty acid, free malic and phosphoric
acids and their ate salts of lime, a yellow resinous coloring matter and the general plant constituents including
an uncrystallisable sugar.” An oil prepared from the flowers has been found useful locally in cases of deafness
or earache.
HOMEOPATHIC - Verb, has a pronounced action on the inferior maxillary branch of the fifth pair of the cranial
nerves, on the ear and respiratory tract and bladder.
Catarrhs and colds with periodical prosopalgia, spasmodic effects, neuralgias. Nervous and bronchial
coughs. Urinary irritation. Tearing, stitching, cramping squeezing, crushing, paralyzing pains. Intermittent
pains.
Abdomen - As of a lump or twisting around navel. Incessant gurgling and rumbling beneath left ribs. Inflation
of the abdomen, violent and painful pressure on navel. Pinchings and gripings in abdomen.
Back - Lancinations in the back and shoulder blades. Sharp intermittent stitches in left scapula. Backache
worse from pressure.
Chest - Shooting in chest, sometimes with oppression and obstructed respiration. Stitch :s in the chest. Red
nodosity near xiphoid cartilage, painful when pressed upon.
Ears-Earache. Numbness in left ear. Otalgia with a sense of obstruction. Deafness from getting water in, as
in swimming or as if stopped by a valve. Dry, scaly condition of meatus (locally).
Eyes - Pains in eyes, as from contraction of the sockets with burning in eyes. Sight confused, as if directed
through a veil.
Face - Neuralgia affecting zygoma, temporo-maxillary joint and ear (Meny.), particularly of left side with
lachrymation, coryza and sensation as if parts were crushed with tongs. Talking, sneezing and change of
temperature aggravate the pains, also, pressing teeth together. Pains seem to come in flashes, excited by
least movement, occurring periodically at same hour in morning and afternoon each day.
Food - Mawkish taste with fetid breath. Hunger without relish for food. Insatiable thirst.
 Kidneys - Increased urine with pressure in bladder. Burning urination. Constant dribbling. Bedwetting, at
night, worse coughing.
Limbs - Stitching in the limbs. Stiffness and soreness ofjoints of lower limbs. Lower limbs feel heavy.
Cramp-like pain in soles, right foot and knee. Neuralgic pain in left ankle. Thumb feels numb.
Lungs - Asthma. Catarrh with hoarseness and stuffed chest. Frequent attacks of deep, hollow cough with
sound like a trumpet, better deep breathing. Soreness in pharynx, cough during sleep. Dry, hoarse cough
worse at night. Cough, nervous without waking.
Male - Pollutions without lewd dreams.
Modalities - Better from taking deep inspirations. Worse touch, pressure. Worse cold, drafts, change of
temperature. Worse from stooping, walking, talking. Worse sneezing, biting hard (inferior dental nerve). Worse
9 a.m. to 4 p.m., twice a day, at same hour.
Mouth - Copious accumulation of salty saliva in the mouth. Root of tongue brown. Tongue of abrownish
yellow color, loaded with viscid mucus in morning and after dinner.
Nose - Profuse coryza from frontal sinuses with hot, burning, profuse lachrymation. Sensation of stoppage of
larynx and ears.
Rectum - Many bowel movements a day with twisting about navel. Feces hard like sheep-dung and expelled
with effort. Fearful diarrhea. Hemorrhoids, obstructing stools, itching and inflamed. Inflamed and painful
hemorrhoids. Pain extends deep down, causing contraction of anal sphincter.
Sensations - As if everything would press out at forehead. As if temples were pinched and crushed. As if ears
were stopped up. As if something had fallen before ear. As if left ramus of jaw were pressed against upper
jaw. As if nose and larynx were stopped up. As if intestines were adherent to wall of abdomen and were being
torn away. As of a twist around navel. As if cold water were poured over side of body from shoulder to thigh.
Sleep - Strong disposition to sleep after a meal. Disturbed sleep, at night with tossing. Short sleep at night,
lasting only until 4 a.m. with anxious, frightful dreams of wars and dead bodies.
Stomach - Aching of stomach. Sensation of emptiness at pit of stomach, which disappears with a rumbling
below left ribs. Frequent hiccough. Regurgitation of insipid serum. Empty or else bitter risings with nausea.
Temperature - Internal coldness of whole body of hands and feet, perceptible also externally. Shuddering,
especially on one side of body, as if it were bathed in cold water.
Throat - Very severe pain in throat on swallowing. Hoarseness, voice deep, harsh, sounds like a trumpet,
“bassoprofundo.’’ Sensation of obstruction in the larynx.
Vertigo - Vertigo when pressing one cheek while supporting the head. Vertigo sudden, as from pressure on
whole head.
COMMENTS - Mullein oil is used, locally, for earache and dry, scaly condition of meatus. Also for teasing
cough at night or lying down. Bedwetting, five-drop doses night and morning
Cushing introduced this now rather well- known remedy to the medical profession in 1884. He wrote “My
father’s house was the home for all poor tramps, as well as ministers, etc. He fell into the river, got water in his
ears and was quite deaf for months.
“A blind man had called, heard loud conversation, asked the cause, etc., then said for kindness received he
would tell us how
Verbascum thapsus to make something that would surely cure him and it was worth a thousand dollars in
New York City.
“We made the oil, put it in his ears at night and he was well in the morning. For years we kept a bottle of it and
it traveled all around the towns and did wonders. That was when I was a youngster.”
Hering, in “Hearing and Ears,” noticed “In Germany flowers of Verbascum thapsus put in a dark-colored bottle,
hung up in the sunlight, give in two or three weeks an oily fluid which has cured many old people and children.”
Hahnemann proved Verb, and his proving confirmed many of the old uses. It produced neuralgic pains of very
great intensity, pressing and sharp and especially in the facial bones, navel and limbs and a peculiar cough.
Chronic dermatitis of the external meatus and drumhead or exfoliation after furuncle. Catarrhal inflammation
of the tympanum Suppurative disease of the tympanum. Accumulations of debris in the case of perforation,
scarred eardrum. Chronic inflammation of the eyes. Chilblains. Burns.
Nash described a “Cough, deep, hollow, hoarse in sound like a trumpet.” He cured many cases and always
used it low. It is more especially a night cough. It occurs in children during their sleep.
Mullein was used as a popular specific for tuberculosis, the leaves being boiled in milk, which was then strained
and given warm.
W. B. McCoy gave several illustrations. According to him Verb, (i.e., the “oil”) has a “soothing effect on the
entire nervous system in many cases acting as a soporific.”
In summer diarrhea he gave one to four drops in two ounces of warm water, a teaspoonful every hour. In
 bedwetting or dribbling of urine one-drop doses in warm water three or four times a day.
Among his cases were those of two boys who had become deaf from getting water in their ears when
swimming. They were cured by having three drops of the oil instilled “in each ear alternately night and morning.”
O. S. Laws cured a youth of 16 of bed-wetting with fifteen drops of the oils three times a day.
The oil plainly acts on the indications of the proving and may be regarded as an alternative preparation to the
official tincture. It might be called Verbasci oleum.
Mr. Kemmis spent a large amount of money treating with various physicians for what they pronounced a rose
cancer and without any relief. An Indian woman told him to use mullein oil. He distilled it (by sun exposure)
and for a short time bathed the cancer with the oil.
The growth of cancer was permanently checked, but it was not healed. Mr. K. lived, perhaps, forty years after
the treatment was used and the cancer never again bothered him.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-a., Caust., Plat., Sphing. - pain in zygoma. (2) in neuralgia. Plat. - pressure,
Stann. - gradually increasing and decreasing. (3) Deep cough, Cor-r., Dros., Spong., Sulph. (4)Sheep-dung
stools, Mag-m. (5) Cough from tickling in chest, Verat.
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Verbena Hastata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - verbe-h. Verbena hastata. Blue Vervain. Ironweed. Vervain.Tincture of entire fresh plant. N. O.
Verbenaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Depression. Epilepsy. Insomnia. Intermittent, fever. Mental, exhaustion. Poison oak.
HERBAL - Verbena, in the form of a tea as a diuretic drink, is used by Vannier to aid elimination in tuberculosis
cases. In epilepsy it must be continued for a long time.
HOMEOPATHIC - Verbe-h. affects the skin and nervous system. Nervous depression, weakness and
irritation and spasms. Promotes the absorption of blood and allays pain in bruises. Passive congestion.
Epilepsy, insomnia, mental exhaustion. In epilepsy, it brightens up the patient’s mental powers and helps
the constipation. Intermittent fever. Poison-oak. Vesicular
erysipelas.
COMMENTS - Anshutz reported “An extract from a paper by Dr. J. N. White, Queen City, Texas, detailing at
length the case of a five- year old boy, who after six weeks of whooping cough, developed epileptic symptoms,
having as high as twelve spasms in twenty-four hours.
“After two months of treatment with such remedies as Sol-c., Sulfonal, Hyos., Cann- i., Calomel, Zinc., etc.
with no results, the cases was given Verbena.
“Another doctor was in consultation and we quote: I told my friend (the Doctor) that when he became satisfied
with the zinc treatment, I wanted to try another eclectic remedy. (The Doctor was an allopath). He was perfectly
willing and I put him on Verbena hastata tincture, twelve drops, every four hours, skipping the dose at midnight.
“After we both took the case we decided, as there were no curative properties in the sulfonal, we would drop
it and not use anything to control the paroxysms. Consequently the boy seemed to get worse to the parents,
as now he would have several falling spells a day.
“From the first dose of the Verbena hastata the boy began to improve. He would have contractions of the
muscles of the arms and legs and look wild for a minute or more for the first week, but after that he never had
another symptom. We kept him on the medicine, as above, for six weeks and now he takes twelve drops three
times a day.
“He has not had any symptom in over two months and all that wild vacant look is gone and he plays, eats,
sleeps, etc., as if he had never been troubled with epilepsy.”
REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

name: Veronal
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - veronal. Veronal. A dangerous drug made by the action of alcohol upon urea and contains the
same radical that alcohol does. Historical dose: All potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - Confluent, reddish spots, dermatitis. Itching of glans and prepuce. Circumscribed dermatitis
patch on first metacarpal phalangeal joint. Dr. V arney noted staggering, cannot stand up. Veronal makes a
man just as drunk as pure alcohol.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chlol.
REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Veronica Officinalis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY- vero-o. Veronica officinalis. Common speedwell. N.O. Scrophulariaceae. Historical dose: All
potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - Perspiration at night. Perspiration followed by chills and cold sweats after uncovering.
Sleepless at night and desire for naps during the day. Desire to sleep on the right side. Worse right side. Sense
of fatigue and lethargy. Weakness, worse missing a meal.
Skin eruptions, red and itching violently. Worse evening, exposure to dampness. Tingling sensation throughout
body. Sensation of heat. Dramatic increase in energy, increased clarity of thinking.
Dryness. Sensation of cotton in mouth. Numb sensation in gums, as if having received anesthesia. Burning
pain in stomach as from heartburn. Worse beginning to eat. Increased or lost appetite. Increased thirst. Better
eructations.
MIND-Great mental anxiety. Mental confusion and a sense of being overwhelmed, alternates with clarity of
thinking. Irritability, particularly with alternating moods. Desire for husband. Homesickness. Detached feeling.
Delusion that people are distant, that the body is vibrating. Delusion of having smoked marijuana.
Abdomen - Abdomen pain, better rubbing.
Back - Stiffness in lumbar region, worse standing. Pain in cervical region, worse cold.
Cough - Persistent bronchial cough with little or no mucus production.
Ears - Hears popping noises, ringing.
Eyes - Heaviness of eyelids. Pain in right eye, worse touch.
Female - Dark brown, mucus-like discharge during ovulation. Sexual desire decreased or increased.
Food - Desires sweets.
Veronica officinalis Limbs - Sharp pain in hips. Perspiration of palms of hands.
Modalities - Worse afternoon, 4 p.m. to 7 p.m.
Nose - Tingling in sinuses.
Rectum - Urging followed by loose stool. Stool, odor of rotten eggs or sulphur.
Sleep - Dreams of smoking cigarettes. Dreams of riding horses, of snakes.
Throat - Sensation of pinpricks, extending to whole throat. Sore throat. Skin in external throat around thyroid
sensitive to pressure. Fleeting prickling sensation in trachea.
REFERENCES - Riley.

name: Vervain
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - verv-b. Vervain. Verbena officinalis. Bach Flower Essence. The flowering branches are put in
a bowl of sunlit water and left to the sun’s action for several hours. Subsequently, the water is strained and
used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add
brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops
straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Verv-b. belongs to Bach’s group of Over-Care for Other’s Welfare, along with Rck-w-b.,
Beech-b., Vine-b. and Chic-b. Verv-b treats states of over-enthusiasm which lead to exaggerated attempts to
convert others to one’s own views. Escalating tension and excessive drive of willpower. Gradual depletion of
reserves. Manic and catatonic states (Cher- p-b., Imp-b.). Hyperthyroidism.
MIND - Enthusiastic, fixed ideas. Fervency and fanaticism. Excitability, impressionability and quickly aroused
motivation and fondness for others. Excessive joy, exaggerated, unbalanced emotions of love and friendship.
Extreme disgust and rejection. Hysterical mood swings. Political fanaticism and outbursts of violence. Self-
righteous.
Manic states within mental illness. Bipolar disorders and problems with impulse control (Cher-p-b., Holly, Imp-
b.). Obsessive-compulsive disorders. Delusions and psychoses with excessive fervency, ecstasy (Clem-b.)
and mania.
REFERENCES Bach.

name: Vesicaria Communis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vesi. Vesicaria communis. N. O. Cruciferae. Alyssineae. Tincture of whole fresh plant.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bladder, pain. Cystitis. Dropsy. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Gravel. Hematuria. Kidney, pain.
Prostatitis.
HERBAL - According to the Treasury of Botany, Vesicaria is a genus of Cruciferae, natives of the Northern
Hemisphere, distinguished by the globose or oboid inflated pouch with hemispherical valves and numerous
 seeds (generally four to six) in each cell. They are herbs, sometimes shrubby at the base with oblong or linear
entire or ripened leaves and terminal racemes of yellow flowers.
The Vesicaria communis tincture is prepared from the whole plant collected fresh. It has been an old home
remedy in various parts of Germany for various forms of urinary troubles attendant on gonorrhea, gravel,
cystitis, nephralgia, prostatitis etc.
HOMEOPATHIC - George R. Shafter found nephralgia, acute cystitis, irritable bladder, following acute cystitis,
and chronic cystitis. particularly amenable to Vesi. Its main indication is a great burning and smarting in urethra
with a frequent desire to pass urine. Marked strangury (Thlaspi., Berb., Sars., Chim. and Canth.).
COMMENTS - Shafter recorded many cases, including that of T. S., age 67, who suffered from kidney pain,
for which he had received morphine injections in former attacks. Vesi. in 15 drop doses every fifteen minutes,
gave marked relief in two hours, which in six hours was complete.
S. B., age 57, had cystitis from cold, high fever, eating, burning pain on voiding urine, which was drop by drop.
Vesi. tincture in 10 drop doses, cured in two days.
A woman, age 39, had pain in her back,
brick-dust sediment in urine, hands and feet swelling so she could hardly close her hands or walk. Vesi. tincture
cured.
Man, age 65, with an irritable bladder, had to rise twenty to thirty times in the night. Vesi. tincture in 20-drop
doses, relieved quickly and cured in six weeks.
C. M., 89, chronic cystitis, passing large quantities of mucus, pus. The bladder was at first washed out with
boric acid solution, then Vesi. tincture 20 drops every two hours, were given. Improvement followed and in two
hours the boric acid washing was stopped and Vesic. given every four hours. This finally cured.
Gonorrhea with smarting and burning on urination and thick creamy discharge. Vesi. tincture a drachm every
four hours, soon cured. Gonorrhea, female after being treated for two weeks with injections, was cured in
seven days with Vesi. tincture in drachm doses.
Cowperthwaite succeeded in causing albumen to disappear from the urine even in cases of actual Bright’s
disease. He added that “it is necessary to use only the imported [i.e., European] tincture, 15 drops every four
hours” (There are several Vesicarias native to North America).
A. L. Davison treated Mrs. P. for general dropsy of a year’s standing, was in uremic spasms when first seen,
the kidneys having ceased to secrete urine. Vesi. tincture was prescribed, 15 drops in a teaspoonful of water
every hour until urine was freely secreted, then three times a day. The second day the kidneys were pouring
out urine and watery stools were passed. In a week all dropsy had disappeared.
Bancroft treated Mrs. T. for irritable kidneys and bladder with polyuria. After a time the urine became bloody
with occasional thin clots. Previously there had been for some months a thick, yellow sediment. Vesi. tincture,
6 drops four times a day and later 15 drops three times a day, taken persistently, effected a cure.
Halbert reported the case of Mr. H., a young man whose occupation involved much outdoor exercise and who
contracted a chill and had lumbago in consequence. Under an “orificial” surgeon his rectum was operated on
and the sphincter stretched.
Thereafter he had fever, rigors and acute prostatitis. Urination was painful and difficult and soon hematuria
ensued. The pain and nervous exhaustion were so extreme that he was put into hospital and for a time only
relieved by injections of morphine. The urine contained albumen, blood-clots, much pus. Urine was only
passed by means of the catheter and defecation was extremely painful.
Vesi. lx was given hourly and great relief followed. The painful tenesmus was alleviated and he was soon able
to pass urine without the catheter. In three weeks he was able to go home.
Shafer gave Cact. and Thlaspi. in a case of dropsy from heart disease in a woman, age 48. These gave little
relief. He then gave Vesi. in combination with the others. There was marked relief in twenty-four hours and in
ten days the dropsy had disappeared.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Thlaspi, Berb., Sars., Chim. and Canth. (2) In Gravel, Coc- c., Urt-u., Thlaspi. (3)
Hematuria, Chin-s., Fic., Phos. (4) Prostatic affections, Hydrang., Solid., Sabal. (5) Cystitis, Chim.
Compatible: Cact., Thlaspi.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Vespa Crabro
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vesp. Vespa crabro. Wasp. Vespa maculata. Vespa vulgaris. European hornet. Giant hornet.
Yellow-jacket. American hornet. N. O. Hymenoptera, Sub-order Vespidae. Tincture of the insects. Historical
dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscesses, multiple. Alopecia. Bee stings. Bedwetting. Boils. Cervix, ulcerated. Chemosis.
 Edema. Erythema. Fainting. Flushing. Glottis, spasm. Indigestion. Ophthalmia. Ovary, pain. Quinsy. Tongue,
swelling. Uterus, ulcerated. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms are mostly the results of stings although Berridge proved Vesp. 30c on three
persons. The symptoms included low spirits, pain in right ear, nausea
Vespa crabro with faint feeling and trembling, pain in left side of the neck on waking.
Stinging, burning pains, as if pierced with red hot needles. Stinging piercing deeply, as if a hook were pulled
out. Sudden stinging and burning in cheek. Burning of the part, then swelling, red with burning pain. Sudden
tearing. Indurated feeling.
Cutting like electric shocks through all joints. Arm, head and face swollen. Eyes red and twitching. Red lines
along absorbents. Itching over whole body. Insensibility. Vasomotor symptoms of skin and mucus membranes.
Nerve and muscular excitement. Trembling, quaking with chattering of teeth. Convulsions, loss of
consciousness, does not answer when spoken to, looks into space, has no recollection of the attack.
Dizzy, better lying on back. Faintness, all day with trembling and nausea. Numbness and blindness. Pulse
slow, heart’s action scarcely perceptible. Feeling as if dying at night. Heat especially overpowers him. Feet
were cold except in summer, when they burned uncomfortably. Perspiration on parts laid on with itching.
Axillary glands swollen with soreness of upper arms.
Nausea and vomiting, followed by creeping chills from feet upward. Cramping pain in bowels. Frequent
urination. Weakness with bedwetting. Pain in sacrum extending up back. Disorders of left ovary with
tenderness.
MIND - Terrible anxiety. Low-spirited. Insensibility. Unconsciousness with inability to move.
Abdomen - Uneasiness in abdomen.
Back - Pain in left side of neck, waking her at night, preventing her from turning it to left side, felt least when
lying on back, best on right side. Pain in scapula with soreness.
Ears - Sticking deep in right ear. Purulent catarrh of middle ears.
Eyes - Injection of right conjunctiva. Chemosis of conjunctiva. Inflammation of right eye with baggy swelling
of conjunctiva. Itching of right lid in evening with swelling afterwards pain in lid and ball. Erysipelatous
inflammation of lid, whole side of face painful and swollen.
Face - Pain in cheek as if pierced with red- hot needles, suddenly awakening him from sleep and recurring
periodically. Painfill and swollen. Erysipelatous inflammation of lids. Swelling of mouth and throat with violent
burning pains. Face livid. Face smooth, dark red, bloated. Anxious look.
Female - Menstruation, preceded by pain, pressure, depression and constipation. Menses intermittent,
sometimes brown, accompanied by pain and flatulence, preceded by mental depression, pain, pressure and
constipation. Left ovary markedly affected with frequent burning, urination, sacral pains extending up
back. Erosion around external os. Pain in left ovarian region. An irritable ulcer surrounded os tincae. Irritation,
worse in groin, passing into pudenda.
Head - Fainting and loss of consciousness. A violent heat came over him, felt sick, then turned giddy and spun
around and around like a top until he fell, staggered to the house, got into a chair in a moment, fell out of it,
almost fainting, dashed water into his face, at length was able to lie down on his bed. Headache. Face and
head swollen and inflamed. Alopecia.
Heart - Aching in heart. Slow beating of heart, almost imperceptible. Pulse rapid and small, feeble, with violent
beating of carotids.
Kidneys - Marked tenderness to deep pressure in kidney region. Remittent dysuria with backache. Burning
pain with urination, also itching. Burning urination in women. Hematuria. Incessant bedwetting.
Limbs - Pain in shoulder, axillary glands swollen. Sprained pain in left shoulder joint on moving it, worse lifting
arm or twisting it. Aching in hand and arm.
Lungs - Dyspnea. Respiration hurried. Hoarseness. Voice lost. Spasm of glottis (after application of diluted
ammonia to tongue), face pale, drops of sweat on forehead, arms thrown out to gasp for air, he got out of bed,
sank back on bed, face livid, breath and pulse stopped.
Male - Swelling of scrotum and penis.
Modalities - Better from cold washing of hands. Cold water first relieves then aggravates. Skin better by
bathing with vinegar. Worse from hot stove, in a closed room. Worse after sleep, after eating. Worse by motion.
Open air aggravates lachrymation.
Mouth - Tongue swollen and tense, swelling below chin, between that and hyoid bone, pain in a point in middle
line of tongue, swollen, red, rounded, filled the mouth, immovable, could not speak, only mumbled, swallowing
was painful and difficult. Swelling of palate with inflammation. Peculiar taste, as when a nest of wasps is
disturbed, worse heat.
Sensations - As if a harpoon were sticking deep in and were drawn on. As if pierced with red-hot needles. As
 if a cutting instrument were piercing all joints like an electric shock. Cold, chilly sensation around sting. As if
left shoulder joint were sprained. As if about to suffocate. As if dying.
Skin - Erythema intense itching, burning. Boils, stinging and soreness, relieved by bathing with vinegar.
Wheals, macules and swellings with burning, stinging and soreness. Erythema multiforme.
Sleep - Night restless. Sleepless all night.
Stomach - Cold feeling in stomach. Heat in stomach. Indigestion with flushing. Belchings. Nausea in evening
after coming indoors with weight in stomach with faint feeling and trembling. Vomiting with swelling of head.
Throat - Swelling of throat, soreness, heat of throat. Hypertrophied tonsils which secreted a cheesy matter.
Pharyngeal varicosis.
Vertigo - Fainting, loss of consciousness. COMMENTS - W. Rowbotham was stung on the right cheek. The
next day, about 4 a.m., he was suddenly awakened by burning, stinging pain in cheek, “as if pierced with red-
hot needles” and soreness and smarting along the lymphatics. After bathing the face he got to sleep and was
again suddenly awakened by the pain two hours later, which recurred periodically in paroxysm, throughout the
day.
Burnett observed a case of a sting on the tongue in a woman. The tongue entirely filled the buccal cavity. The
patient’s appearance was exactly like one suffering from severe synanche. The swelling was diffuse and deep-
seated. There was not much redness.
Berridge demonstrated that the poison of the hornet and the wasp may answer to each other’s indications. He
cured with Vesp. 100,000c. (Fincke) a symptom produced by Vespa vulgaris, namely, chemosis of the right
eye.
Mr. X. age 66, had his right eye inflamed for six days. When seen there was redness of right lower lid, baggy
swelling of conjunctiva partly covering the cornea when pressed upward, lachrymation of right eye worse in
open air, right lids adhere in morning. Vesp. three times daily cured in a few days.
E.       T. Blake cured with Vesp. face swollen and puffy, skin transparent and blanched, scalding urine
followed by itching, itching of right arm.
Blake also related the case of Miss C. J., who at the age of thirty-one was stung on the left thumb, through
some calico and . was never well after, dying at the age of thirty-eight. She was prone to constipation all her
life and at twenty-three had “congestion of the left lung.” Most of the abdominal, urinary, ovarian and uterine
symptoms were hers. Among the latter was an irritable ulcer.
RELATIONS - Antidote: Semp., locally. Antidoted by: Apis, Led., Camph., salt water, vinegar. Compare:
(1) Scorp. - sahvation, strabismus, tetanus, Apis. (2) pains as if pierced with red-hot needles, Ars., Apis. (3)
Ulcers around os uterus, Mitch., Eup-pur., Apis., Hydre. Incompatible: Arg-n.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:

pectoris. Arthritis. Asthma. Blindness. Cataracts. Chest, pain. Chills. Circulation, disorders. Coughs.
Depression. Diarrhea. Diplopia. Edema. Erectile, dysfunction. Eye, disorders. Facial, flushing. Fainting.

disorders. Sinusitis. Strokes. Thrombosis. Tremors. Ulcers. Vision, disorders. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC - Viagra, used for male impotence, works by dilating blood vessels in the penis, allowing the
inflow of blood needed for an erection. Viagra causes erections only during sexual excitement. It does not work
in the absence of arousal.
Heart attack, stroke, heart irregularities, dangerous surges in blood pressure, and sudden death have all been
reported after use of Viagra, usually in men with existing cardiac risk factors, and typically during or shortly
after sex.
Allergic reactions. Chills. Dizziness. Drowsiness. Fainting, falling. Muscle ache. Joint disease. Bone pain.
Numbness. Coordination problems. Slow reflexes. Tremors. Seizures. Strokes. Flushing. Thrombosis.
Insomnia. Gout. Diabetes. Sinus and throat inflammation.
MIND - Emotional and mental disturbances. Anxiety. Depression. Abnormal dreams.
Abdomen - Abdominal pain. Colitis. Intestinal inflammation. Gastroenteritis.
Bladder - Cystitis. Urinary tract infection. Loss of bladder control. Urinary incontinence. Increased night-time
urination.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Breast enlargement.
 Ears - Tinnitus. Ringing in the ears. Deafness. Ear pain.
Eyes - Dry eyes. Bloodshot eyes. Increased pressure in the eyes. Eye inflammation and pain. Retinal
bleeding. Cataracts. Dilated pupils. Photophobia. Sensitivity to light. Floaters.
Face - Facial flushing. Edema.
Female - Vaginal dryness. Anorgasmia. Head - Headaches. Migraine headaches. Cerebral thrombosis.
Heart - Angina pectoris. Heart problems. Cardiomyopathy. Heart failure. Hypotension. Low blood pressure.
Rapid or throbbing heartbeats. Tachycardia, palpitation. Myocardial ischemia.
Lungs - Dyspnea. Breathing difficulty. Asthma. Coughs. Lung inflammation. Bronchitis, sputum increased.
Male - Genital problems. Erectile dysfunction. Painful erection. Prolonged erections. Abnormal ejaculation.
Anorgasmia. Impotency.
Mouth - Dry mouth. Difficulty swallowing. Gum inflammation. Stomatitis.
Nerves - Ataxia. Hypertonia. Neuralgias. Paresthesia. Tremors, reflexes increased. Hypesthesia.
Nose - Nasal congestion. Sinusitis. Nosebleeds.
Rectum - Diarrhea. Rectal bleeding.
Skin - Raised skin patches. Itchy skin. Contact dermatitis. Rashes. Ulcers. Urticaria. Herpes simplex.
Sweating.
Sleep - Insomnia. Abnormal dreams. Somnolence.
Stomach - Thirst. Stomach inflammation. Dyspepsia. Acid indigestion. Nausea, vomiting.
Throat - Laryngitis, pharyngitis.
Vertigo - Dizziness and fainting.
Vision - Abnormal vision. Double vision. Blue color tinge in vision. Blurred vision. Color perception changes.
Light perception changes. Light sensitivity. Blindness.

name: Viburnum Opulus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vib. Viburnum opulus. Cramp bark. High cranberry. Bush cramp. Bark water elder. N. O.
Caprifliaceae. Great Britain. The Gueldres Rose or Snowball-tree is the cultivated and sterile variety. Tincture
of the fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - After-pains. Cough, pregnancy. Cramps. Dysmenorrhea. Ears, painful. Epididymitis. Headaches.
Hysteria. Labor,
Viburnum opulus false. Labor, pains. Lumbago. Menstruation, painful. Miscarriages. Ovaries, pain.
Paralysis. Uterus, pain.
HOMEOPATHIC - Viburnum opulus, a native of Great Britain, is widely distributed over the northern parts of
the continent and America. According to Hale, in America the wild species is called “Cramp bark” and the
knowledge of its curative virtues in painful spasmodic diseases, like dysmenorrhea, is derived from the Native
Americans. The tincture has a strong odor of Valerianic acid (as also has that of Vib. tinus).
Hale derived his knowledge from herbal sources. In spasmodic dysmenorrhea he gave a few drops of tincture
to 3x thrice daily for a week before the period, every hour when the pains set in or every fifteen minutes if the
pains are severe.
Cramps in abdomen and legs of pregnant women. To prevent miscarriage when the pains are spasmodic or
threatening. False pains preceding labor. After-pains, a dose after each pain.
HOMEOPATHIC - Vib. is a remedy for general cramps. Colicky pains in pelvic organs. Conscious of internal
sexual organs. Prevents miscarriage. False labor-pains. Spasmodic and congestive affections, dependent
upon ovarian or uterine origin.
Paralytic conditions after convulsions. Violent, spasmodic, nervous effects, especially in females, dependent
upon the ovarian or uterine origin. Pains make her so nervous, she cannot keep still. Sick feeling all over in
pelvic complaints. Hemorrhages. Left sided symptoms.
MIND - Very nervous and irritable.
Abdomen - Excruciating crampy colicky pain. Heavy aching, hypogastrium, better menses. Sudden cramps
and colic pains. Tender, worse pressure about umbilicus.
Back - Bruised feeling in back as after severe exertion. Tired backache, better pressure. Lumbago, better
walking with a cane pressed, arms across the back. Pains in the back end in a cramp in uterus or go down the
thighs.
Chest - Feeling of oppression over whole chest. Sensation as if muscles of chest failed to act, causing
dyspnea. Shooting over left sixth rib near sternum.
Constitutions - Suited to tall, slender, dark or fair haired hysterical subjects.
 Ears - Stabbing in ears. Pains in bone waking at night. External ear sore as if bruised.
Eyes - Sclerotica streaked with blood. Sensation of sand in eyes. Pain in right eye with congestion. Burning
and lachrymation. Sore feeling in eyeballs. Sore feeling on closing lids. Heaviness of eyes.
Face - Flushed and hot. Face swollen and congested. Swelling about right eye with induration. Face and lips
pale, dark circles under eyes. Lips dry.
Female - Heavy aching feeling or excruciating cramps in pelvis, better from menses. Bearing-down pains
before menses. Menses too late, scanty, lasting a few hours, offensive in odor with crampy pains, cramps
extend down thighs (Bell.). Spasmodic and membranous dysmenorrhea (Bor.). Leucorrhea, thick, white,
blood streaked worse during stools. Leucorrhea, excoriating. Smarting and itching of genitals. Consciousness
of internal sexual organs. Pelvic organs turning upside down. Aching in sacrum and pubes with pain in anterior
muscles of thighs (Xanth.). Pains from back to loins and womb worse early morning. Uterine pains extend
around the pelvis often extending down the thighs. Ovarian region feels heavy and congested. Uterine
hemorrhage. Frequent and very early miscarriage, causing seeming infertility. False labor pains. Violent
persistent after-pains. Faint on attempting to sit up.
Food - No appetite. No desire to eat, stomach feels full. Indigestion, food lies heavy.
Head - Head dull and sluggish. Throbbing in head. Terrible crushing pain worse left parietal region with a
sensation as if head opening and shutting. Severe pain in temporal region. Head hurt by every cough.
Kidneys - Frequent urging. Frequent, profuse urination during headache, menses, hemorrhages etc. Dysuria,
spasmodic. Copious, pale, light-colored urine. Cannot hold water on coughing or walking.
Limbs - Stiff, sore feeling in nape of neck. Feels as if back would break. Sacral backache. Lower limbs weak
and heavy. Cramps in calves, before menses.
Lungs - Suffocative spells at night, worse cold, damp. Infantile asthma. Cough during pregnancy.
Modalities - Better by pressure, resting. Better in open air. Worse from motion, sudden jar, lying on left side,
lying on affected side. Worse evening and night. Worse in close room, warm room. Worse cold, snow, air.
Worse from fright. Worse before menses. Straining at stool aggravates headache. Stooping causes dizziness.
Rising causes fainting, nausea and dizziness.
Rectum - Stools large and hard with cutting in rectum and soreness of anus.
Sensations - As if she could not tell where she was or what to do on awaking. As if she could not live, sick
feeling at stomach. Emptiness, as if stomach hollow. As if body from waist to lower pelvis would collapse. As
if urine continued to flow after urinating. As if menses coming on. As if pelvic organs were turning upside down.
As if parts would be forced through vulva and she must support the part. Left side as if strained or bruised by
over-lifting.
Skin - Tettery spots on cheeks, arms etc. Sleep - Very restless sleep, felt sick all over.
When asleep, sensation of falling and awakened frequently with a start.
Stomach - Constant nausea, relieved by eating.
Vertigo - Vertigo, feels as if falling forward, worse descending stairs. Feels faint on sitting up.
COMMENTS - The first Vib. provings were by H. C. Allen, assisted by eleven provers, male and female with
the tincture and first and 30c dilutions. Dr. Susan Fenton of Oakland, proved Vib. on six provers.
One of the six took the tincture up to drachm doses without obtaining a single symptom. One pro ver was cured
of a number of symptoms, but developed no new ones. All took potencies at first witfiout eliciting any
symptoms.
Taking the tincture all had these symptoms with variations: severe backache going
through to the front or around the abdomen to uterus. Cramping pelvic pain. Temporal headache. Three had
nausea with pains. All had “sick feeling all over.” One had omission of a period, two had menses early.
One case was cured; Miss F., 25, a housekeeper, medium height, rather slender, blonde, sanguine, was strong
until she had severe pelvic congestion and was fifteen months under treatment and most of the time in bed.
In June, 1892, a double oophorectomy was performed with great relief, but attacks of pelvic congestion with
severe pain still persisted, at first every two to four weeks, later less frequently, causing impairment of general
health and strength.
Symptoms included excruciating pains through lower abdomen with bearing-down sensation and a feeling as
if the body from the waist to lower part of pelvis would collapse, an indescribable sick feeling all over with
severe aching in rectum, great depression of spirits, symptoms better when lying down.
Vib. tincture was taken in three-drop doses thrice daily. After taking it for three days she lost all her symptoms
and felt “perfectly well for the first time in over four years.” It is evident that “sick feeling all over” in connection
with pelvic complaints and “worse from movement, better by rest” are keynotes of Vib.
RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Aeon, (epididymitis), Verat. (Diarrhea). Compare: (1) Vib-p. Cimic., Caul., Sabin.,
Sep., Thlaspi., Xanth.
 REFERENCES - Clarke. Hale.

name: Viburnum Prunifolium
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - Vib-p. Viburnum prunifolium. Black haw. An American species. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of
fresh bark gathered in October and November from trees grown in open situations. Phares. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - After-pains. Dysmenorrhea. Infertility. Menorrhagia. Menstrual disorders. Miscarriage. Morning
sickness. Tetanus. Tongue, cancer. Uterine, disorders.
HERBAL - Hale quoted his experiences showing a close resemblance between Vib-p. and Vib. with some
additional uses of Vib-p.
Viburnum prunifolium is a uterine tonic. Useful for habitual miscarriage. After-pains. Menstrual irregularities
of infertile females with uterine displacements. Morning sickness. Cancer of the tongue, obstinate hiccough.
Phares said of it, “Vib-p. is particularly valuable in preventing abortion and miscarriage, whether habitual or
otherwise, whether threatened from accidental causes or criminal drugging.”
COMMENTS - Phares noted the case of Mrs. W. had never gone to full term, had several children at eight
months, all of them dying one month after birth. Frequent pregnancies and hemorrhages had seriously
impaired her health.
When next pregnant Vib-p. was ordered and at the eighth month when pains set in vigorously with copious
bloody discharge, Vib-p. was given freely and she went to term, giving birth to a healthy boy, who survived.
He also recorded the case of Mrs. L., married eighteen months, had miscarried and suffered long and much
in consequence. Being again pregnant, Phares gave her Vib-p. tincture, a teaspoonful thrice daily. At the third
month, she was severely injured by a fall from her carriage.
Strong uterine contractions ensued, but were arrested by Vib-p., which had to be given freely for several days,
the dose being gradually diminished. For nearly a week, miscarriage was threatened whenever Vib-p. was too
long suspended. The patient went to term and gave birth to a large boy.
Hale used the tincture in threatened miscarriage, dysmenorrhea and spasmodic uterine pains. It entirely
antidotes the effect of Goss., which is much used for procuring abortion in some of the States, one pint of a
strong decoction of the cotton-root being sufficient. Vib-p. when taken regularly completely neutralizes this.
E. P. Fowler cured two cases of cancer of the tongue with the decoction of Vib-p. bark, used topically. Phares
thinks it perhaps “the best remedy in the world for tetanus.”
RELATIONS - Antidote to: Goss.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Hale.

name: Vichy Aqua
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vichy-g. Vichy aqua. Vichymin- eral springs. Grande grille. Springs at Vichy, France. Vichy
springs containing carbonicum acidum, muriaticum acidum, sulphuricum acidum, silica, phosphoric acidum,
arseni- cum acidum, ferrum oxidatum, natrum, kalium, calcium and magnesium. Arsenicums. Oxygenums.
Silicas. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Constipation. Diabetes. Gallstones. Gout. Gravel. Heartbum. Indigestion.
Intermittent, fevers. Liver, disorders. Neck, stiff. Rheumatism. Salivation. Skin, disorders. Uterus, disorders.
HOMEOPATHIC - The springs of Vichy are alkaline, both hot and cold. Croserio proved Vichy, taking the water
 and triturations of the salt and dilutions.
Constantin James noted that the springs are used in a large number of maladies, especially diseases of the
digestive tract, diseases of the liver with or without stones. Abdominal engorgements consequent on paludal
fevers, chronic engorgements of the uterus, catarrh of the bladder, gravel, gout and rheumatism, diabetes
mellitus, skin diseases.
Among the most prominent symptoms were stitches below mastoid in chest in right loin and in heart. Across
the chest there was a sensation as of a bar impeding breathing. Sinking sensation and sensation as if about
to be sick. Burning flatulence. In the nose there were illusions of smell, corpse-like odor, odor of cucumbers.
After sex there was excessive weakness as if from hunger. Modalities - Worse from cold, drafts of air. Worse
when seated. Worse after sex. Worse after eating, when eating. Uneasiness is better by dinner.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Nat-m. (2) Stitching pains, Kali-c. (3) Bar sensation, Haematox., Ars., Ox-ac.
(4) Worse from sex, Kali-c., Kali- bi., Staph. (5) Illusory smells, Anae.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Vinca Minor
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vine. Vinca minor. Lesser periwinkle. N. O. Apocynaceae. Grows in woods and shady places.
Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: All potencies, first to third potency.
CLINICAL - Acne. Alopecia. Diphtheria. Crusta lactea. Eczema. Favus. Hemorrhages. Neck, stiff. Nose,
redness. Plica polonica. Seborrhea. Throat, sore. Toothache. Uterus, bleeding.
HOMEOPATHIC - Vinca was proved by Rosenburg on four healthy persons, who took the tincture in 20 to 60
drop doses. It produced a deep impression on the organism and tissues. Weakness and prostration.
“Weakness as if he would die.” Inclination to stretch. Trembling and tendency to start, especially on exciting
the mind. Trembling in all the blood vessels. Uterine hemorrhages, followed by great debility. “Toothache better
from warmth of bed.” Diphtheria. Empty, all gone sensation in the stomach and chest. Distention of abdomen
after stool. Stool caused exhaustion. Skin affections, eczema. Plica polonica. Marked affects on the tissues.
The left side was most affected.
Abdomen - Abdomen full, tense but painless. Griping. Rumbling and gurgling with passage of much offensive
flatus. Distention after a stool.
Back - Painful tension and stiffness of cervical muscles with an illusive sensation as if a weight were lying on
them.
Causations - Anger. Mental exertion.
Chest - Pains in chest with sticking and dyspnea. Stitching in sternum. Pressure on sternum with feeling of
emptiness in chest.
Ears - Ringing and whistling in ears with feeling of cold wind, especially the left.
Eyes - Itching and burning of lids, which become red. Eye dry, on getting snuff into it there was so little secretion
he was obliged to wash it out. Foggy vision while reading, at times also while walking.
Face - Bloated face with pimples. Dry lips. Swelling of upper lip and corner of mouth. Tearing in malar bones.
Female - Menses, profuse, flowing like a stream without interruption with great weakness, at menopause.
Passive uterine hemorrhages (Ust., Trill., Sec.). Menorrhagia, continuous flow, at menopausal (Lach.).
Bleeding fibroids.
Food - Hunger alternating with loss of appetite before the hunger has been satisfied. Scarcely any thirst.
Head - Tearing pain in vertex, ringing and whistling in ears. Corrosive itching of scalp. Irresistible desire to
scratch. Spots on scalp, oozing moisture, matting hair together, plicapolonica. Bald spots covered with
short woolly hair. Hair falls out and is replaced by gray hair.
Kidneys - Diminished secretion of urine. Urine pale yellow.
Limbs - Inclination to stretch limbs. Tearing pains in limbs. Arthritic tearing in bones. Swelling and stiffness of
first joints of fingers with burning pain in the nails. Cramp-like drawing in feet and toes.
Lungs - Hoarseness. Tenacious mucus in trachea. Spasmodic cough with little tickling in larynx. Rapid
respiration.
Modalities - Worse after swallowing, walking, stooping, moving. Worse anger. Worse reading. Worse in open
air. Drinking aggravates, liquids (especially beer) causes belchings, coffee causes nausea.
Mouth - Increased secretion of saliva. Insipid taste in mouth to all food. Aphthae. Tearing in teeth better by
warmth of bed.
Nose - Becomes red on becoming the least angry. Tip gets red easily. Moist eruption on septum. Seborrhea
upper lip and base of nose. Stoppage of one nostril. Sores in nose. Frequent nose bleeding.
Rectum - Urging to stool. Stool first hard, then soft. Stool exhausting with burning in anus.
 Sensations - As if he would die from weakness. As if a hammer were beating from within outwards in vertex,
cold wind in ears. As if something sticking low down in esophagus. As if a weight lying on cervical muscles.
Skin - Eczema of head and face. Corrosive itching. Great sensitiveness of skin with redness and soreness
from slight rubbing. Pustules, itching, burning and offensive odor. Hair matted together. Weeping ec - zema
intermingled with foul, thick, crusts. Corrosive itching.
Sleep - Frequent yawning. Sleeplessness and restlessness at night. Lascivious dreams.
Stomach - Emptiness in stomach. Gastric disturbance. Empty belchings after drinking beer and generally
worse from taking liquid. Nausea after coffee. Violent, bitter, copious vomiting of yellowish-green liquid.
Throat - Cutting in lower esophagus, which provokes swallowing. Diphtheria. Ulcers. Frequent hawking.
Difficult swallowing.
Vertigo - Whirling vertigo with flickering before eyes.
COMMENTS - Vine, has a wide range in passive uterine hemorrhages. This case is related in Ind. H. R. (ix.
113): uterine hemorrhage, blood dark red, flow copious, uninterrupted with extreme debility. Chin, and Helon.
failed to relieved, Vine, lx effected a rapid and permanent cure.
Frequent nosebleed. The nose “becomes red from the slightest cause, when the least bit angry.” Scabby
eruptions about the nose and on the septum, which are part of the general skin effect of the remedy.
Corrosive itching of the skin provoking scratching, moist spots and burning in ulcers. The most characteristic
effect is on the scalp, where it produces a condition having many features of crusta lactea, favus and plica
polonica.
Clarke cured With Vine, “sore spots on the scalp” in a young woman. A number of symptoms were produced
in the throat and esophagus.
C. M. Bogerrecordedthecaseofawomen, 31, who had a cutting sensation in lower part of esophagus while
swallowing food and continuing after. Empty faintness in stomach better by eating. Stomach sore to touch or
pressure of clothing. Constipation from induration of feces. Hemorrhoids constantly sore, smarting after stool.
Vine. 41,000c (Fincke) cured.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Olnd., Staph. (2) peevishness with repentance, Croc. Crusta lactea, Med., Melit,
Mez., Jug-r., Olnd. (3) Viol-t. - with strong-smelling urine. (4) Lappa - glands swollen, axillary glands even
suppurate. (5) Staph. - sickly children, pale face, dark rings around eyes. (6) Ust. - filthy eruptions, part of hair
comes out, part matted. (7) Alopecia, Bac., Phos.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Vine
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vine-b. Vine. Vitis vinifera. Vinum. The flowering clusters, shortly after the stamens have grown
out, are put in a sunlit bowl of water and left to the sun’s action for several hours. Subsequently, the water is
strained and used as medicine. Only the wild vine is used. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock
bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This
is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Vine-b. belongs to Bach’ s group of Over-Carefor Others ’Welfare, with Rck-w-b.,Beech-
b., Verv-b. andChic-b. Vine- b treats the tendency to engage in dominant behavior.
Over-ambitiousness accompanied by envy, frustration and worry, leading to the formation of gastric and
duodenal ulcers, or coronary heart disease.
MIND - Assumes control over others. Dominance, preceded by overt attempts to fight back. Disregards
peoples’ opinions and wishes. Condescending.
Manipulations, schemes and tricks or flattery. Exploitive. Abusive behavior and stubbornness. Passive
aggressive personalities. Resistant to change. Very goal-oriented. Tendency to forget one’s needs.
Ruthless and violent. Haughty, egocentered and self-aggrandizing. Anger, impatient and exasperated.
Calculating. Reserved. Frustration, a sense of injustice, self-pity, rebelliousness and stubbornness.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Viola Odorata
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - viol-o. Viola odorata. Sweet- scented violet. Violet. N. O. Violaceae, an order most members of
which contain emetin, allied to Cinchonaceae. Tincture of fresh plant in flower. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cancer. Choroiditis. Cough, spasmodic. Deafness. Dyspnea. Headaches. Hoarseness. Hysteria.
Neuralgias, supra-orbital. Otorrhea, suppressed. Palpitations. Rheumatism. Seminal emissions. Styes.
 Whooping cough. Worms. Wrists, rheumatism.
HOMEOPATHIC - Viol-o. has a specific action on the ear. Affects especially darkhaired patients, supra-orbital
and orbital regions, rheumatism in upper parts of the body when on the right side.
Locally, for pain due to uterine fibroids. Marked affinity for the wrists, especially the right. Affects ears, eyes,
and skin. Combined eye, ear and kidney symptoms. Worm disorders in children (Teucr.). For snakebites,
bee-stings.
Produces great nervous debility. Nervous activity, then sudden exhaustion. Tension. “Tension of the occiput
and forehead,” “Tension of the scalp of occiput even when not moving, though worse bending head forward
and backward, painful, compelling him to wrinkle forehead, lasting several days.” Tension extends to upper
half of face and ears.
MIND - Inclined to weep without knowing why. Childish behavior, despondent, refuses eating, talks in low soft
voice. Aversion to music, especially the violin.
Abdomen - Distention of abdomen.
Back - Tension in muscles of the neck.
Jerking drawing in cervical muscles, near nape, extending down, worse lying on opposite side.
Causations - Suppressed discharges.
Chest - Oppression of chest, as of weight on chest.
Constitutions - Cooper considered it suited to “dark-complexioned people of the Ferr. pic. type.” Teste used
Viol-o. frequently, described the type as “a lymphatico- nervous temperament, a mild disposition, dry and cool
skin.” Many patients cured by him were tall and slender. Suited to tall, thin, nervous girls.
Ears - Affections with pain in eyeballs. Otorrhea, recurrent from birth. Deafness. Shooting in ears. Roaring and
tickling. Deep stitches beneath ears. Aversion to music.
Eyes - Cramp in eyes. Choroiditis. Pain from eyes (left) to vertex worse cough. Eyeball feels compressed. Lids
tend to close without physical sleepiness. Heaviness of lids. Flames before eyes. Myopia. Illusions of vision,
fiery, serpentine circles.
Female - Dyspnea during pregnancy.
Food - Craves meat.
Head - Heaviness of head with sensation of weakness in muscles of nape of neck. Scalp tense, must knit
the brows. Headache across the forehead, above the eyebrows. Tendency to pain immediately above
eyebrows. Burning in the forehead. Throbbing under eye and temple. Acts upon frontal sinuses. Hysterical
attacks in tuberculous patients.
Kidneys - Urine milky with strong smell. Bedwetting in nervous children.
Limbs - Trembling of limbs. Rheumatism of deltoid muscles and wrists (right) especially in females. Shoulders
cold. Pressing pain in bones of fingers. Pressing pain in right carpal and metacarpal joints (Ulm.).
Lungs - Difficult breathing, anxiety and palpitations. Dyspnea duringpregnancy. Dry, short, spasmodic cough
and dyspnea, worse in daytime. Long spells of cough during day time only with dyspnea. Whooping cough
with hoarseness.
Modalities - Bone pains, better after rising in morning. Worse from cloudy weather, cold air. Worse music.
Worse puberty, suppressed discharges. Worse bending head backward andforward. Cough worse by day.
Hoarseness worse in a cold room. Vision worse from dull, wet days.
Nose - Tip numb, as from a blow. Torpor in the end of nose, as from a blow.
Rectum - Itching at anus'. Worms.
Sensations - As if everything in head whirled around. As if eyeballs were compressed. As if nose had been
beaten and blood were pressing out. As if hard palate were dried up. As if a stone were lying on chest. Burning
like a small, transient flame in spots here and there.
Skin - Dry with moist palms.
Sleep - Yawning and stretching without sleepiness.
Vertigo - Vertigo, everything in head seems to whirl around.
COMMENTS - Viol-o. was introduced by Gross and proved by Hahnemann, Gross and Stapf. Gross said of
his symptoms that they recurred equally in all positions, were mild, yet more definitely than from other drugs.
Hahnemann had bruised pain in all the bones in the morning in bed after waking, better after rising. Stapf had
relaxation of all the muscles.
The mind was greatly excited and disturbed and Viol-o. found its first uses in hysterical cases. Aversion to
music, especially the violin is one of the peculiar symptoms.
Increased activity and rush of ideas, generally confused, “Can only grasp half an idea, puts it in its proper place
but cannot hold it.” Gross experienced the former and Stapf the latter of these.
Gross also noted, “Tension which at times extends to upper half of face, especially of nose, thence to forehead
 and temples, as far as ears, alternating with a similar sensation in occiput and cervical muscles.”
The cure of Lady Margaret Marsha, age 67 of an affection of the throat pronounced to be malignant (apparently
epithelia of tonsil) with an infusion of violet leaves is on record. Boiling water was poured on the fresh leaves
and allowed to stand twelve hours.
Compresses moistened with this were applied externally to the throat and covered with oil-silk. Relief of pain,
dysphagia and suffocative symptoms was immediate. The external swelling disappeared in a week, the growth
on the tonsil in a fortnight.
Viol-o. has cured a number of cases of rheumatism, chiefly right-sided. It has a marked affinity for the wrists,
especially the right. Ear disorders with pain about the eye orbits indicate Viol-o.
RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Camph. Compatible: in whooping cough, Cor-r. in worms, Cina. Compare: ( 1 )
Ulm. - formication in feet, numb, creeping pain in legs and feet, rheumatic pains above wrists, numbness,
tingling and full soreness where the gastrocnemius gives off its tendon. (2) Chen-a. (3) Aur., Puls.,
Sep., Ign., Cina. (4) Caul. - in rheumatism of small joints.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Viola Tricolor
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - viol-t. Viola tricolor. Pansy. Ja- cea. Hearts-ease. N. O. Violaceae. Tincture of fresh plant in
flower. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bedwetting. Crusta lactea. Dyspnea. Eczema. Flatulence. Gonorrhea. Gout Impetigo.
Leucorrhea. Ophthalmia. Orchitis. Plica polonica. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Seminal, emissions. Syphilis.
Throat, ulceration. Vaginitis.
HERBAL - It had an ancient reputation in asthma and epilepsy and especially in obstinate skin diseases. In
Russia a decoction of pansy is a popular remedy for scrofula, swollen glands. Schlegel, of Moscow, used it
with good effect in syphilitic affections, especially venereal ulcers.
HOMEOPATHIC - The pansy was proved by Hahnemann and his provers. Skin, scalp and urinary organs are
the chief centers of action of Viol-t. The principal uses of this remedy are for eczema in childhood and nocturnal
emission accompanied by very vivid dreams. Combined urinary symptoms and skin affection. Nervous
paroxysms after suppressed crusta lactea, eczema.
Eczema with urinary disturbances, too copious urination or sudden arrest of secretion. Tinea capitis with
frequent involuntary urination. Urine smelling like cat’s urine. The male sexual organs were much excited.
Emissions with vivid dreams occurred, swelling, itching and pains in prepuce and glans with erections.
Hot face and sweating after eating. Dyspnea after eating. Hands twitch and are clenched in sleep. Nervous
paroxysms followed suppressed milk-crust. The axillae and clavicular regions were noticeably affected and
stitches and burning stitches were prevailing pains. Lying causes anxiety about heart.
Abdomen - Stitches and cutting pain in abdomen with urging to stool, fol- lowed by discharge of lumps of
mucus and flatulence. Pressing, stinging in the diaphragm.
Back - Swelling of glands of neck. Spasmodic pain and contraction with pinching between shoulder blades
(with cutting, tingling and crawling in the skin).
Causations - Suppressed milk-crust (nervous paroxysms).
Chest - Syphilitic ulcers on clavicles. Shooting in chest. Stitches in the chest, on the ribs, sternum and
intercostal muscles.
Eyes - Pain in eyes, as if a hard body were between upper eyelid and eyeball. Smarting and incisive and
itching shootings in eye. Contraction and closing of eyelids. Myopia.
Face - Hot and sweating after eating. Thickness and hardness of skin of face. Scabs on face with burning
itching.
Female - Stitch in region of mons veneris, right side. Painful pustules on labia. Leucorrhea with stitching pain
in children in syphilis. Chancroid ulcers about breasts.
Head - Cracked, gummy crusts on scalp, exuding profuse tenacious yellow fluid, matting the hair together with
swelling of cervical glands. Eczema of scalp with swollen glands. Milk crusts. Heavy, pressing-outward pain.
Kidneys - Copious, disagreeable odor. Urine offensive, smelling like cat’s urine. Bedwetting.
Limbs - Joint rheumatism. Itching like eruptions around the joints.
Lungs - Stitches in left side of chest, worse during inspiration and expiration.
Male - Seminal emissions with vivid dreams. Involuntary, seminal emissions at stool. Swelling of prepuce,
burning in glans. Itching.
Modalities - Open air helps headache, but causes chilliness. Aversion to open air. Worse in winter, when
walking in cold air. Worse 11 a.m. Worse by pressure on side opposite to painful side, lying on non-painful
 side. Walking causes vertigo, stitches through chest and abdomen. Sitting causes stitches in abdomen and
groin, standing relieves.
Mouth - Accumulation of saliva in the mouth with sensation of dryness. Tongue loaded with whitish mucus of
a bitter taste.
Rectum - Chopped soft stools. Stool with mucus and much flatus.
Skin - Eczema of childhood. Large boils all over the body in scrofulous children. Impetigo. Intolerable itching.
Eruptions, particularly over face and head with burning, itching, worse at night. Thick scabs, which crack and
exude a tenacious yellow pus. Sycosis.
Sleep - Inclination to sleep in afternoon. Disturbed sleep with frequent waking. Awakens frequently without
cause. Sleep retarded by a concourse of ideas with difficulty in waking in morning. Vivid and amorous dreams.
Temperature - Chill or chilliness in forenoon and in open air. Dry, anxious heat at night in bed with red face.
General heat, especially in face with anxiety, dyspnea immediately after eating. Night-sweats.
Throat - Sore throat in evening. Swallowing difficult and very painful. Syphilis. Swelling of cervical glands.
Much phlegm, causing hawking, worse in the air. Chancroid ulcers.
Vertigo - Vertigo and dizziness when walking. Head bewildered and perplexed.
COMMENTS - Teste put Viol-t. in two groups, whose types are Lyc. and Cham. Homeopathy has brought out
some characteristics of Viol-t. which single out its cases.
Teste quoted from old observers the following as cured by Viol-t.: Milk-crust in children at the breast, or recently
weaned. Milk-crust with violent cough and excessive oppression.
Impetigo of hairy scalp and face in children and adult females. Favus and serpiginous crusts in children and
adults with swelling and induration of cervical glands. Large boils all over body in a scrofulous child. Pustules
and ichorous exanthema of feet. Squamous spots on skin.
Rheumatism and gout, joint rheumatism with itch-like eruption around the joints. Impetigo-like exanthema on
forehead. Ichorous ulcers with violent itching.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Merc., Puls., Rhus-t. Compare: ( 1 )Tension of tissues of face and
forehead, Viol-o. (2) Crusta lactea, Vine. (Viol-t. has urinary concomitants). (3) Eruptions, ulcers, Cham.,
Graph., Hep., Merc., Olnd., Petr., Staph. (4) Stitches, Kali-c. (5) Viol-o. (6) Lyc. Rhus-t., Calc., Sep. Compat-
ible: Puls., Rhus-t., Sep., Staph.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Vipera Aspis
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vip-a. Vipera aspis. Aspis adder. N. O. Viperidae. Historical dose: All potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - Proved in 1970 by Boffa and Dupin on 14 subjects, 7 men, and 7 women. The heart, blood
and blood vessels were chiefly affected. Sleepiness during daytime. Chilly. Worse left side.
Nerves. Throbbing pains. Throbbing headache. Heavy sensation in eyes. Dazzling when raising eyes. Dryness
of mouth, with pasty tongue, on waking in morning. Dry mouth before menses. Menses with small, very dark
clots or with big red clots.
MIND - Pessimism. Nervousness. Irritability. Disposition to contradict. Impatience. Anxiety. Dreams of death..
Food - Intense thirst for cold drinks.
Heart - Palpitations of heart at night, worse lying on left side.
Limbs - Spontaneous ecchymoses on arms.
Painful heaviness in legs, worse walking, better raising legs. Veins of thighs distended. Marbled, mottled
appearance of thighs.
Modalities - Better during menses. Better gentle motion. Worse warm, damp weather, warm room, heat.
Worse left side, pressure. Worse evening. Worse before menses.
RELATIONS - Compare: Vip., Lach., Naja., Aran-ix., Buth-aust.
REFERENCES-Julian.
