name: Vipera Berus
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vip. Vipera berus. German viper. Vipera torva. Pelias berus. Adder. Vipera communis. Common
Viper. European Viper with other varieties, especially the Red Italian Viper. N. O. Ophidia, family, Viperidae.
Dilutions of the venom. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Bites. Goiter. Hemorrhages. Jaundice. Liver, enlargement. Menopause. Multiple neuritis.
Nosebleeds. Paralysis. Paraplegia. Phlebitis. Poliomyelitis. Senility, premature. Tongue, swelling. Varicose
veins.
 HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of bites by the common viper and related species have been collected and have
furnished the data for homeopathic prescribing. The venom of common German Vipera torva affects the blood
and blood vessels, leading to hemorrhage and inflammation of the vessels.
Allen related the case of a gold beater who found the veins of his right arm become exceedingly swollen and
painful, so that he could no longer work or let his hand hang down. Vip. cured immediately.
A case quoted from Med. Adv. of varicose veins of the popliteal space with the sensation as though the leg
would burst and a nervous, fidgety condition of the feet which kept them in constant motion, was cured with
Vip. 30c. The bursting feeling appears to be at the root of this characteristic.
A keynote for Vip. in cases of phlebitis and varicose veins is “Worse on letting the limb affected hang down,”
as if it would burst with fullness. The region of the vessel affected is inflamed and sensitive.
Swan said Vip. was a remedy for all forms of nosebleed.
Vip. affects veins, causing inflammation and ahemorrhagic tendency. Inflammation of veins with great
swelling. Cardiac dropsy. Bursting sensation, enlargement of liver. Special action on kidneys and induces
hematuria. Edema of glottis. Goiter. Ailments of menopause.
Paralysis, ascending, paraplegia of foot. Multiple neuritis. Poliomyelitis. Temporary
increase in reflexes, paresis supervenes, a paraplegia of the lower limbs extending upwards. Resembles acute
ascending paralysis of Landry. Vip. has a chronic and periodic action, the symptoms return annually for years.
Abdomen - Excruciating pain in the epigastrium, worse pressure. Violent pain in enlarged liver extends to
shoulder and hip, jaundice with fever.
Back - Sticking in kidneys. Pain in loins.
Chest - Oppression with anxiety with violent efforts to breathe and swallow. Veins of chest and abdomen thick
and hard. Swelling of chest as far as umbilicus after bite on face.
Eyes - Eyes are dark yellow, red, inflamed and watery, staring, sunken. Pupils are dilated or left dilated, right
contracted. Paralysis of lids, dropped over eyes. Vision is dim, dim in left eye, lost in right.
Face - Excessively swollen. Lips and the tongue swollen, livid, protruding. Tongue dry, brown, black. Speech
difficult.
Food - Appetite lost. Thirst with moist tongue, for cold drinks.
Female - Menopausal hemorrhage, flow red with dark clots, not profuse but continuous with prostration and
faintness from nursing the child.
Kidneys - Strangury. Involuntary urination. Urine is increased, suppressed, dark yellow, as in jaundice.
Hematuria. Ineffectual desire.
Limbs - Patient is obliged to keep the limbs elevated. When limbs are allowed to hang down, it seems as
if they would burst and the pain is unbearable. Shuffling gait caused by paralysis of foot. Varicose veins
and acute phlebitis. Veins swollen, sensitive, bursting pain. Blue lower limbs. Severe cramps in lower limbs.
Liver - Violent pain in enlarged liver with jaundice and fever, extends to shoulder and hip.
Modalities - Worse from letting limbs hang down. Worse by pressure. Worse change of weather, from cold
touch. Worse yearly.
Mouth - Scorbutic line on gums. Tongue swollen, brownish-black, protruding. Lips, blue, swollen. Speech
difficult.
Nose - Nosebleed with vertigo, while nursing the child.
Skin - Livid. Boils, carbuncles with bursting sensation, relieved by elevating parts. Ulcers. Gangrene. Skin
peels in large plates. Lymphangioma.
Stomach - Digestion slow. Pain in epigastrium, worse pressure. Nausea with shuddering with attack of
faintness. Retching with suffocative sensation. Vomiting after milk of all food and drink.
Sleep - Disposed to yawn. Sleepiness and heaviness with inability to sleep and also almost constant necessity
to change the position. Sleeplessness from pain. Restless at night.
Temperature - Temperature is diminished, resists cold badly. Chilliness with cold sweat, with rigidity and
clammy sweat, then fever. Fever of irregular type intermittent fever. Sweat after vomiting.
Throat - Swelling like goiter. Edema of glottis. Closure of throat so that she could swallow only water and milk.
COMMENTS - Vip. patients resist the cold badly. The parts may be paralyzed and ulcers and gangrene follow.
Worse from letting limb or part hang down. Sensation as if something ran up the thigh occurred in the bitten
limb in one case. In one case there was sweat over the whole body except the bitten limb.
Leonard gave Vip. to a woman suffering from menopausal hemorrhage, flow red with dark clots, excessive to
prostration and faintness. She had a small uterine fibroid. A few doses relieved and the excessive hemorrhage
did not return.
He also noted the case of a woman nursing a child a year old who was much prostrated by hemorrhage lasting
several weeks, not profuse, but continuous: Nosebleed nearly every day, weaning brought no relief. Chin. 200c
 did no good. Vip. 100,000c cured in three doses.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Hemorrhage of fluid blood, Sanguis. (2) Worse hanging down limbs, Calc.,
Alumn., Am-c., Sabin., Thuj. (3) Pelius berus. Adder. - Prostration and fainting, faltering pulse, skin yellow,
pain about navel. Swelling of arm. tongue, right eye with giddiness, nervousness, faintness,
and sickness. Compression of chest, could not breathe properly or take a deep breath, aching and stiffness of
limbs, joints stiff, collapsed feeling, great thirst. (4) Ser-ang. - heart and kidney diseases. Failure of
compensation and impending asystole.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Viscum Album
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - vise. Viscum album. Mistletoe. N. O. Loranthaceae. Viscaceae. Tincture of ripe berries. Tincture
of bruised leaves. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Ankylosing spondylitis. Arteriosclerosis. Asthma. Aura epiléptica. Cancer. Chorea. Deafness.
Dupuytren’s disease. Dysphagia. Endometritis. Epilepsy. Hypertension. Labor pains, slow. Lumbago.
Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Migraine. Neuritis. Orchitis. Osteoporosis. Otorrhea. Ovaritis. Raynaud’s
syndrome. Retained placenta. Sciatica. Spasmodic paralysis. Spleen pain. Throat, sore. Whooping cough.
HERBAL - Viscum Album’s active principle is viscotoxin, a mixture of acetylcholine and choline. Viscum is a
chlorophyllous plant, which grown on various trees (apple, poplar) and forms large bunches. It is gathered in
August and September, before the fruit ripens. The leaves are then blanched and dried quickly in hot air and
stabilized.
In the middle ages, it was used as an anti-epileptic. Hypo-tensor and diuretic. Anti-tumors, by external use, as
for papilloma, due to the necrotizing properties of the viscotoxin.
Viscine is most abundant in the mistletoe of the apple-tree, Visco-resin in that of the oak and acacia, excites
the sexual appetite. The mistletoe of the hawthorn possesses like all the rest, but in a higher degree, the
contractile properties of Sec. on the uterus in uterine inertia. That of the oak has a remarkable anti-epileptic
power on horses.
According to Laville, all mistletoes are useful in epilepsy and rabies. A breeder had a very fine stock which
became epileptic at four or five years old. He cured them
with a tincture of the fresh leaves bruised in a mortar.
HOMEOPATHIC - The first homeopathic symptomatology was established by Proll, Stager, Schier and Black
during the second half of the 19th century, using the mother tincture and low potencies. Proell made a proving
of the tincture and the symptoms developed resembling an epileptic aura and petit mal, which had the
additional epileptic feature of recurrence they recurred frequently for two years.
Vise, affects the nerves and female sexual organs. Lowered blood pressure. Dilated blood vessels but does
not act on the centers in the medulla. Pulse is slow due to central irritation of the vagus. The symptoms point
to rheumatic and gouty complaints, neuralgia, especially sciatica.
Epilepsy, feels a glow that rises up from feet to head. Chorea and metrorrhagia. Chorea from fright. Symptoms
like epileptic aura and petit mal. General tremor as if all muscles are in fibrillary contraction. Neuralgia.
Paresthesia.
Rheumatism, tearing pains. Rheumatoid condition ameliorated in fresh air and by the movement. Gouty.
Sciatica with otorrhea. Spinal pains from uterine causes.
Feeling of lightness as if floating on air. The brain is swaying around the inside the skull. Congestion in the
head with headaches and vertigo. Blood would not clot and wounds would not heal. Bleeding of bright red
blood from the uterus. Valvular disease with disturbances in sexual sphere.
Rheumatic deafness. Asthma. Hypertensive albuminuria. Nausea at the sight of the bottle containing the
medicine to be taken. Pruritus. Burning cold under the right shoulder.
MIND - Apathy, sadness. Lack of optimism liveliness. Irritable, sad, morose. Restless, nervous, thoughtless,
shakes with impatience. Unable to carry out intellectual activities. Thoughts keep turning to past events, for
hours on end. Obsessive persistence of thoughts.
Sensation of strength, optimism, gaiety, desire to undertake anything, full of ideas for the future. Hallucinatory
psychosis. Extremely sensitive to noise. Fear of telephones.
Abdomen - Feels as if someone were dragging her down from the waist. Sore about waist. Violent rumbling
and painful distention of the supra-umbilical region, ameliorated by expelling wind and leaning backwards.
Colitis. Chronic pancreatitis.
Back - Lumbago from a chill, wants someone to press against the back. Stiffness and muscular pains in the
nape of the neck, thoracic cage and back. Torticollis. Sensation of a burning coal under the right shoulder.
 Causations - Chill, wetting. Fright. Suppression of menses.
Chest - Angina pectoris. Nervous dyspnea with feeling of constriction in the chest.
Ears - Deafness from cold. Buzzing and stopped-up feeling in ear. Hypersensitive to noise. Whistling, buzzing.
Hears heartbeat. Sclerosis of the ears.
Eyes - Blue rings around eyes. Ocular neuralgia. Conjunctivitis. Mydriasis, ocular neuralgia, conjunctival
irritation. Double vision. Bad focusing, eyes weep through fatigue.
Face - Facial muscles in constant agitation. Countenance suffused. Lips livid. Face hot and flushed.
Female - Menses too early, copious with bright red blood and very painful. Menorrhagia. Chronic endometritis.
Metrorrhagia. Atonic, post-partum hemorrhage. Hemorrhage with pain. Blood partly clots and bright red.
Menopausal complaints (Lach., Sulph.). Pain from sacrum into pelvis with tearing, shooting pains from above
downwards. Ovarian pain, especially left. Retained placenta (Sec.).
Food - Felt starving at supper-time. Appetite ravenous.
Head - Feeling as if whole vault of skull were lifted up. Sudden throbbing in vertex. Headache, especially at
the forehead, temples andparietalbone,can spread to the whole heat. Dull, heavy aching, numbing and
congestive, beating or hammering.
Heart - Hypertrophy with valvular insufficiency, pulse small and weak, unable to
rest in a reclining positions. Low blood pressure. Failing compensation, dyspnea worse lying on left side.
Weight and oppression of heart, as if a hand were squeezing it, ticking sensation about heart. Inflammation of
the coronary arteries. Feeling of tightness of heaviness. As if the heart is being squeezed by a hand. Heartbeat
irregular. Agitation and fibrillation. Pulse accelerated or slow with fear of death. Palpitations in the chest, throat
and upper part of the abdomen. Palpitations during sex.
Kidneys - Urinary tenesmus and copious urine. Bladder paralyzed. Involuntary passing of urine as a result of
an irritating cough. Urine is turbid and evil-smelling. Urine milky after standing. Bedwetting.
Limbs - Chorea-like movements of the arms and legs. A glow rises from the feet to the head, seems to be on
fire. General tremor, as if all muscles were in state of fibrillary contraction. Dropsy of limbs. Sciatica. Drawing,
tearing pains in the arm. Pains alternate in the knee and ankle with shoulder and elbow. Periodic pains from
sacrum into pelvis, worse in bed with pains into thighs and upper limbs. Tearing, shooting pains in both thighs
and upper limbs. Cannot keep legs still. Sensation of a spider crawling over back of hand and foot. Itching all
over. Compressing pain in feet. Raynaud’s syndrome. Walking, bending is painful. Burning sensation in the
feet.
Lungs - Dyspnea, feeling of suffocating when lying on leftside. Stertorous breathing. Asthma, if connected
with gout or rheumatism. Bronchial asthma, connected with gout or rheumatism. Glottal spasms and rattles in
the bronchi. Painful, frequent cough, scanty, gray or yellow sputum. Spasmodic cough.
Male - Libido increased or diminished. Disturbed libido. Violent, painful erection. Atonic discharge of seminal
fluid. Cramping pain in the prostate. Prostatitis.
Modalities - Better by counter-pressure, resting quietly, walking in the fresh air. Worse by slightest movement.
Worse winter, cold, stormy weather, becoming chilled while hot, heat. Worse in bed, lying on left side. Worse
suppression of menses. Worse mental effort. Worse tobacco.
Mouth - Lips cracked. Dryness of the mouth. Mouth suddenly fills with saliva. Unpleasant taste on waking
tongue coated to tip with ochre-yellow fur. Tongue sore. Buccal mucus membrane is as if tanned.
TeetWehattered.
Nose - Catarrh in the nose and pharynx. Catarrhal congestion of the mucus membranes with discharge of a
watery or purulent liquid. Purulent rhinitis. Polyps. Nosebleed.
Rectum - Feeling of constriction of the anus with empty urging. Feeling of not having emptied the intestine
completely after stool. Stools soft, watery or thick, frothy, stinking, explosive, bulky with nightly urging, forcing
him to get out of bed. Stools hard and dry. Pruritus and burning of the anus with splinter-line pain. Bleeding
hemorrhoids.
Skin - General itching and tingling with no apparent cause, ameliorated in the evening and by perspiration.
Formication along the arms. Pruritus, senile and vulvae.
Sleep - Falls asleep late, wakes early. Sleeps, despite exhaustion and after drinking coffee. Troubled dreams
of war, bombardment.
Stomach - Gastritis. Heavy sensation, feeling of a stone in the stomach. Squeamish before breakfast and
dinner. Heartburn, cutting pain in the stomach, ameliorated by eating and belching. Nausea ameliorated by
vomiting.
Temperature - General shivering followed by sudden hot flush towards the head and feeling of anguish.
Throat - Throat dry, burning with sticky discharge. Sensation of constriction around the neck. The feeling of a
lump in the throat disappeared in one female prover.
 Vertigo - Vertigo, persistent after epileptic attack. Sensation of lightness, as if floating on air. Severe attacks
of vertigo totters and has to hold on to the furniture. Vertigo occurs on rising from movement, by moving the
head quickly, tends to fall backwards. Vertigo never occurs when
lying down. Vertigo when looking out of a window.
COMMENTS - Two women took Vise, to procure abortion. Every muscle save those of the eyes became
paralyzed, as did also the intestinal tract. They could not swallow and died of starvation in consequence, the
bowels being obstinately constipated. The muscles of speech were also paralyzed.
A boy, 14, ate some berries, soon after began to feel giddy and then became insensible. He was found with
suffused countenance, lips livid, conjunctiva injected, pupils slightly dilated and fixed, pulse slow and full,
bounding, breathing slow, stertorous.
On pricking the soles the feet were quickly drawn up. Then, cold applications aroused him, when he began to
talk incoherently, had spectral illusions and was inclined to be violent.
In a pamphlet on “Viscum Album” Dr. George Black of Torquay put together most of the facts relating to this
plant including four new provings, by himself and three female provers.
Black removed with Vise. 3c lumbago from chill, tearing pain, wants something to press against it. Lumbago,
right, extending to right buttock, worse by slightest movement. Pain in sacral region, unable to turn either side,
worse slightest movement, “pain of a terrible clutching nature, as if her vitals were affected.”
Cooper gave great relief with Vise, in “old spinal irritation pains.” He also named “spinal symptoms due to
uterine causes” as indicating it. Rheumatism, “the weight of my body on the joint causes it to be very sore,”
excessive perspiration.
Sciatica associated with otorrhea. Burning pain from center of left buttock to inner ankle, heel as if red-hot coal
applied, leg feels heavy as lead. In addition a number of cases of catarrhal deafness with noises in the ears
were cured or greatly improved.
Belcher gave to a girl, 17, suffering from chorea, 5 drop doses of a tincture of leaves and berries. On the
second day he was called to see her and found her suffering as if under the influence of an opiate.
Black also quoted William Huber’s experiences with Vise., the first case was of retained placenta with
constitutional symptoms after miscarriage at sixth month. Expulsion rapidly effected by Vise. 3c.
A man, 22, robust, fair took a chill from traveling in ice-cold wind. Got a drawing, tearing pain in left lower jaw,
lasting some hours. Succeeded by loud buzzing and stopped-up feeling, ending in complete deafness of that
ear. Vise. 3c cured.
Metrorrhagia following suppression from working in water. Sciatica left side, cured with Vise. 3c. Rheumatism
from wading ill-shod through great tracts of snow, cured with Vise. 3c. Hydrothorax (right) from chill with
shooting in spleen, cured with Vise. 4c and 3c.
John Wilde made a tincture of the bruised leaves and gave 5 drop doses to a boy, 14, who had chorea affecting
face and limbs. There was improvement in two days and in a few weeks a complete cure.
A boy, nine, strumous with tendency to skin disease, was affected with chorea after a fright. He was completely
changed in expression, speech quite inarticulate, look idiotic.
The movements continued at night and the boy was worn out for want of sleep. Vise., 1 to 2 drop doses, did
no good. The dose was then increased to 15 drops. Improvement set in at once and a perfect cure was
effected, the doses being diminished after a time because soreness of the tongue and redness of the
conjunctiva were set up.
C. M. Boger related a case in which persistent vertigo after epileptic seizures, lasting a month at a time, was
cured with Vise. 100,000c.
Huber used the 3x and 6x. He considered it applicable to all kinds of rheumatism, acute and chronic, especially
when characterized by tearing pains in cases occurring in winter, the result of exposure to sharp winds and in
cases of rheumatic deafness.
RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Chin. Compare: (1) Sec., Conv., Bry., Puls., Rhod.
(2) Guipsine - active principle - exalts the hypotensive properties of Viscum. (3) Hed. -
Intercranial pressure. (4) Bry. - Vertigo in the morning on rising, prickling pains, aggravated by movement,
great thirst, dry constipation, menses copious with brown blood. (5) Bell. - Neuro-vascular congestion, fear of
imaginary things, hypersensitivity and hyper-exicitability of the senses, pulse strong, irregular, menses too
early with bright red, hot blood. (6) Aran-ix. Follows well: Aeon, (rheumatism).
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian.

The waters produced orgasm of blood, pressure and tension. The throat was sensitive to swallowing warm

name: Walnut
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - waln-b. Walnut. Juglans regia. Female flowers are collected and boiled for half an hour. The
female flower resembles a green bud with two fuzzy stigmas growing out of the top. After boiling, the water is
strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper
bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few
drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Waln-b. belongs to Bach’s group of Over sensitivity to Influences and Ideas with Agri-
b., Cent-b. and Holly-b. Waln-b. gives protection from heightened impressionability and sensitivity. Lack of
physical stability. Heightened impressionability, may create over-ambitiousness, envy and frustration. Gastric
and duodenal ulcers (Vine-b.). Allergies.
MIND - Overly influenced by impressions. Emotional disturbances from impressions. Heightened sensitivity.
Exaggerated attraction to sexual matters, even though it may just be mental preoccupation. Delusions when
one feels obsessed or influenced by forces beyond one’s control (Asp-b.).
REFERENCES Bach.

name: Wasabia Japonica
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - wasa. Wasabia japónica. Wasabi. Japanese horseradish. Wasabi pungens. Cochlearia wasabi.
The whole plant is used, leaves, stems and rhizomes. N. O. Brassicaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Blood, clots. Cancer. Cerebral, thrombosis. Colds. Coughs. Diarrhea. Food, poisoning. Sinusitis.
HERBAL - The wasabi plant is native to Japan, and is traditionally found growing in or by cold mountain
streams. The earliest cultivation of wasabi in Japan dates back to the 10th century.
The grated rhizome, or above-ground rootlike stem, has a fiery hot flavor that quickly dissipates in the mouth,
leaving a lingering sweet taste, with no burning sensation. The roots have a strong penetrating odor, which
can clear the head and bring tears to the eyes, when inhaled or ingested.
Wasabi is valuable medicinally for its antibacterial properties, and anti-inflammatory action. It has been used
for coughs, colds, sinusitis and diarrhea. It is a powerful digestive stimulant, and removes toxins from the body.
As a member of the cruciferous family, wasabi contains the same cancer-fighting isothiocynates as its cabbage
relations. Researchers believe that the substances in cruciferous vegetables help prevent cancer by helping
the body eliminate excess hormones such as estrogen, thus reducing the risk of hormone-related cancers
such as breast and prostate cancer.
Scientists have recently found that a component of the plant inhibits the formation of blood clots and cerebral
thrombosis. The plant has exhibited strong antioxidant properties. Research also found that wasabi contains
substances that suppress the growth of stomach cancer cells. It has also been used as an antidote to fish
poisoning.
RELATIONS - Compare: Ars.
 REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Water Violet
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - wat-v-b. Water violet. Hot- tonia palustris. Several flowers are picked by the stalk and left floating
in a bowl of sunlit water for several hours. The water is then strained and prepared as medicine. Historical
dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle
will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed
in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Wat-v-b. belongs to Bach’s group of Loneliness, with Imp-b and Heath-b. Wat-v-b. treats
states of aloofness and haughtiness. Lack of spontaneity and lively involvement. Internal retreating or raising
above others may be reflected in a posture of haughtiness and aloofness. Physical stiffness and rigidity.
MIND - Haughty. Feels special, eccentric. Grandiose delusions, narcissistic personality disorder. Reserved
dignity. Desire for attention and admiration. Alienates others.
Active engagement with others is avoided oreven considered disturbing to inner peace. Disinterest, lack of
spontaneity, or even apathy. Tendency to retreat and isolate oneself. Vulnerable and lonely. Insecure. Ailments
after severe offense or humiliation.
REFERENCES Bach.
WHITE CHESTNUT
(Bach Flower Essence)
PHARMACY - wh-ch-b. White chestnut. Aesculus hippocastanum. Individual flowers are picked and placed in
a bowl of water which is left to the sun’s action for several hours. The water is strained and used as medicine.
Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol,
if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth
or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Wh-ch-b. belongs to Bach’s group of Lack of Interest in Present Circumstances,
withClem-b.,Honey-b., Wld- r-b., Oliv-b., Must-b. and Ch-bd-b.
States of preoccupation and intense worry. Mental preoccupation’s and worries. Obsessive-compulsive
dwelling on an emotional experience. Insomnia from worry, mental preoccupation. Restlessness from worry.
Eyesight failure. Irritable colon, gastrointestinal symptoms. Hyper motility, pylorospasm and ulcers.
MIND - Preoccupied with worrisome, returning thoughts. Anxiety, despair. Obsessions, fixations and persistent
thought patterns. Delusions and chronic introspection. Automatic
responses and compulsive thinking (Cher- p-b., Crb-a-b., Pine-b.). Worried in a state of regret or self-reproach.
Disappointment and annoyance. Frustration and exhaustion. Diverted attention.
REFERENCES - Bach.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Angina pectoris. Body, odor of offensive. Constipation. Coms. Diarrhea. Earwax,
excessive. Glaucoma. Gout. Hair, rapid growth, loss, grows darker. Hemorrhage. Hemorrhoids. Hernia
inguinal, femoral. Indigestion. Miscarriages. Nosebleed. Rheumatism. Infertility. Vertigo. Whitlow.
HOMEOPATHIC - The hot, chlorinated saline springs of Wiesbaden contain 8.176 grams of solids to each
liter, and of these Nat-m. makes up more than seven grams. The baths, which constitute the chief part of the
treatment, are extremely stimulating.
The baths, combined with drinking the water, generally determine at the begining of the cure certain
phenomena of saturation which disappear on temporary suspension of the treatment. The most common of
these is a saburral state of the stomach and a feeling of fullness and tension in the whole abdomen.
Passive or atonic gout, these cases usually pass through a period of aggravation before improvement sets in.
Torpid and rheumatisms, the douche being employed as well as the bath. Paralysis, muscular and tendinous
contractions. Sprains in complete anchyloses. Stiffness from old fractures. Gunshot wounds which are slow to
heal. Modalities - Better by nosebleed, by hemor-
rhoid flux. Worse during menses. Frequent urination worse from coffee. V ertigo worse lying in bed.
COMMENTS - Constantin James noted, “Abdominal plethora and portal obstruction are relieved.” By the
 artificial congestion which they set up in the venous plexus of the rectum they have for a constant effect the
disengorge- mentof the viscera under the diaphragm and the prevention of stasis in their parenchyma.
Pelt observed the effects of drinking the water and excessive bathing.
Magdeburg observed the effects on eight very healthy persons. The stimulating, congestive and évacuant
effects mentioned by James appeared in the provings. Blood rushes to the face. Vertigo when lying in bed and
vertigo which causes falling. Hemorrhages occur from anus and nose which relieve other symptoms.
Fermentation occurs in the abdomen and there is great exhaustion after diarrhea. Hemorrhoid flow occurs with
better of abdominal plethora. In one case nosebleed occurred persistently for six weeks, at the end of which a
weakness of vision bordering on blindness was cured. During the menses there is great weakness, also
constipation.
A number of remarkable symptoms appeared in reference to the skin and nails. The hair grew rapidly and
became darker. Nails also grew rapidly. Corns and callosities dropped off.
Berridge cured with Wies. 200c a Miss B., 21 of a soft corn between the fourth and fifth toes of right foot. There
was burning and shooting pain. Itching with the sweat. The sweat on the diseased parts made a brown stain.
The urine stiffened linen.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-m. Corns, Ferr-pic. (2) Callosities, Ant-c. (3) Hair turns darker, Jab., Piloc.,
Wild.
REFERENCES - Clarice.

name: Wild Oat
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - wld-o-b. Wild oat. Bromus ramosus. The flowering ends are picked and placed in a bowl of
water which is left standing in bright sunlight for several hours. The water is strained and used as medicine.
Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol,
if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth
or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Wld-o-b. belongs to Bach’ s group of Uncertainty, with Cer-b., Scler- b., Gent-b., Gors-b.
and Hom-b. Wld-o-b. deals with lack of motivation and incentive. A depressive mood may permeate the mind
and body. Lethargy, a lack of appetite and mental dullness.
Organic mental disorders and mental retardation after head injuries (Horn-b., Must-b., Scler-b.). Obesity.
Peptic ulcer. Non-insulin dependent diabetes. Drug abuse.
MIND - Aimless, dissatisfied. Unmotivated. Absent-minded. Lack of motivation and incentive. Lack of
concentration. Boredom, lethargy and dissatisfaction.
COMMENTS - Emotions of frustration, joylessness, aversion, dissatisfaction, meaninglessness, boredom and
futility. Feelings of being not fully awakened or activated in one’s potential. In some forms of mental illness
with organic dysfunction and retardation, this remedy will give incentive within the physical limitations of the
disease (Horn-b., Must-b.).
RELATIONS - Cer-b., Scler-b., Gent-b., Gors- b. and Hom-b.
REFERENCES - Bach.

name: Wild Rose
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - wld-r-b. Wild rose. Rosa canina. Sprigs with leaves and flower heads are boiled for half an hour.
Subsequently, the water is strained and prepared as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the
stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks).
This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Wld-r-b. is part of Bach’ s group of Lack of Interest in Present Circumstances, with Clem-
b., Honey-b., Oliv-b., Wh-ch-b., Must-b. and Ch-b-d.
States of apathy and resignation. Lethargy, listlessness, lack of energy. Passivity. In sickness, when the
fighting spirit is gone and recuperation is not proceeding, or even when death is threatened due to resignation.
Schizophrenic states, developmental disorders, psychosis, schizoid personality disorders. Reduced social
contact, low emotional involvement.
MIND - Apathy and resignation. Helplessness and powerlessness. Anger or frustration. Disinterest in fighting
for health when sick. Retreat from involvement in unfavorable circumstances. Stifled capacity for joy,
disinterest in amusement and play, lack of hopes, wishes and dreams.
REFERENCES - Bach.
 ***WILDBAD AQUA
PHARMACY - wild. Wildbad aqua. The Springs at Wildbad in Wurtemburg. The water contains in 16 ounces,
Carbonic ac. grains 0.972, Nat-m. 1.808, Nat-c. 0.837, Nat-s. 0.291, Kali-s. 0.018, Calc. 0.738, Silicic acid
0.480, Mag-c. 0.079, Ferr-c. 0.002, Alum. 0.004 and traces of Mang. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bones, pains. Catarrh. Gout. Hair, disorders. Indigestion. Knees, creaking. Nails, soft. Paralysis,
spinal. Paraplegia. Rheumatism. Shoulder, rheumatism.
HOMEOPATHIC - In spite of its very slight mineralization, said Constantin James, the water produces very
distinct effects in a graduated series.
The first impression of the bath is delicious, this is succeeded by sensations more clear and distinct: a slight
degree of excitement, at times luminous sparks before the sight, a finer blood seems to flow to the brain(Puls.).
“One would like to remain in the bath, but something unusual and strange warns you that it is time to get out.”
Wildbad is chiefly for disorders of the spinal cord, more then half the patients being paraplegic. Sensation
as if the brain were over-filled. Gnawing, sinking, empty sensation. Pain as if sprained.
Sensation of looseness in the joints, ankles loose, knees loose, the bones seem as if they did not fit. Teeth
seem too long. In one pro ver the hair, which had been greasy, became dry and the beard became of a darker
color. Desire to stretch.
Modalities - Worse on waking, at night.
Throbbing and heat in occiput worse lying down. Pain in sciatic nerve, looseness of knees worse walking.
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Uric acid in urine.
(2) pain in right shoulder, Urt-u. Sang.
REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Willow
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - will-b. Willow. Salix vi- tellina. Twigs with male or female catkins are boiled for half an hour.
Subsequently, the water is strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock
bottle into J one ounce dropper bottle (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This
is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.
HOMEOPATHIC - Wifl. belongs to Bach’s group of Despondency and Despair, with Crb-a-b„ Oak-b., Star-
b-b., Sw-ch-b., Elm-b., Pine-b. and Lar-b. Will-b. deals with states of resentment and bitterness with one’s fate.
Physical rigidity and worn features may speak of internal bitterness and resentment. Bitter-
ness, disillusionment and depression.
Chronically engaged in repression of aggressive impulses, affecting the heart and intestinal region.
Suppressed anger, causing colicky pains, tension headaches, depression. Tachycardia, irregularities in heart
activity, hypertension. Hyperventilation. Chronic coughs and constipation (Chic- b., Must-b.) Skin lesions and
intermittent insomnia.
MIND - Burdened by an unfavorable and undeserved fate. Blames others for misfortunes. Unfounded
resentment, blame. Dissatisfaction and self-pity. Bitterness and dormant despair. Sadness and
disappointment. Anger at being mistreated. Outrage and sense of injustice. Self-righteousness, denial of
reality, envy and lack of sympathy and compassion.
Malingering (Chic-b.), passive aggressive personality, antisocial and in disruptive behaviors (Holly-b.). Fixed
ideas, delusions. Paranoia, as one feels persecuted and thwarted in one’s destiny due to the fault of others
(Beech-b.).
REFERENCES Bach.

name: Withania Somnifera
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - with-s. Withania somnífera. Ashwagandha. Physalis somnífera. Indian winter cherry. Indian
ginseng. Wintercheny. N. O. Solanaceae. Historical dose: Tincture to first potency.
CLINICAL-Alcoholism. AIDS. Alzheimer’s disease. Anemia. Arthritis. Asthma. Brain, fatigue. Breathing,
difficulty. Bronchitis. Cancer. Carbuncles. Convalescence. Coughs. Emaciation. Emphysema.Ex/iaus- tion.
Hyperglycemia. Immune, disorders. Impotency. Infertility. Insomnia. Lumbago. Memory, loss. Nerve,
weakness. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Sexual, debility. Spermatorrhea. Skin, disorders. Swollen, glands.
Tuberculosis. Tumors. Ulcers. Weakness.
HERBAL - Withania somnífera is an important herb used in Ayurveda, the traditional Indian medicine. A native
of India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, the name comes from the peculiar odor of this herb, smell akin to that of a
 sweaty horse.
It is an erect branched shrub with a greenish or lurid yellow flowers. In India, it is akin to ginseng in other parts
of the orient, both are touted for their longevity enhancing and sexually stimulating properties.
The shoots and seeds are also used as food and to thicken milk in India. It is said to work mainly on the
reproductive and nervous systems coupled with rejuvenating qualities. Tumors, inflammation (including
arthritis), and a wide range of infectious diseases.
Regulates blood sugar, which aids in suppressing sugar cravings. It is commonly used to increase vitality,
recover from chronic illnesses and pain management for arthritic conditions.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to B. Gan- gooly, M.D., from Calcutta, India, in the Homoeopathic Recorder, vol.
37, 1922, With-s. has been employed successfully in all cases of debility. Nervousness. Brain fatigue. Loss
of memory. Spermatorrhea. Problems resulting from masturbation. Speedy emissions, nocturnal emissions.
MIND - Confused. Cannot collect his thoughts. Loss of memory. Brain fatigue. Indifferent. Sadness, low spirits.
Back - Pain in back.
Ears - Whizzing noises.
Limbs - Great debility.
Eyes - Blue margins around eyes. Painful in the morning. Weak sight.
Face - Pale, flushes of heat.
Female - Infertility. Low sex drive.
Food - Desires sweets, sugar.
Head - Dull headache with buzzing in the head.
Heart - Palpitations.
Lungs - Respiratory disorders. Emphysema. Asthma. Bronchitis and coughs,
Male-Impotency. Low sex drive. Masturbation. Spermatorrhea. Emissions at night and at stool.
Sleep - Lascivious dreams with emissions.
Stomach - Pressure as from as load, with drowsiness, nausea, vomiting.
Urine - Frequent desire to urinate. Burning urination.
Vertigo - Vertigo on standing or walking.
COMMENTS - With-s. is specific for a wide range of conditions including arthritic inflammation. Respiratory
disorders including emphysema, asthma bronchitis and coughs, gynecological disorders, especially functional
female and male infertility and impotence. Low sexual libido.
Chronic neurological diseases especially anxiety, nervousness, depression and insomnia. Weak digestion,
fluid retention caused by lowered body metabolism.
Immuno-compromised diseases including tuberculosis and AIDS, chronic upper respiratory diseases,
degenerative symptoms attendant to aging, juvenile mal-develop- ment and growth.
RELATIONS - Compare: Phos.
REFERENCES - Gangooly. Murphy.

name: Wyethia Helenoides
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - wye. Wyethia helenoides. Poison weed. Alarconia helenioides. Melar- hiza inuloides. N. O.
Compositae. Tincture of the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, first to sixth potency.
CLINICAL - Allergies. Asthma. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Bronchitis. Constipation. Coryza. Coughs. Depression.
Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Epiglottis disorders. Fatigue. Fevers. Hay fever. Headache. Hemorrhoids.
Hiccoughs. Indigestion. Influenza. Itching. Leucorrhea. Nervousness, Ovaries, pain. Pharyngitis. Post-nasal
catarrh. Salivation. Sneezing. Throat, sore. Uvula disorders. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Wye. was introduced and proved with the fresh root or the tincture, on seven men and two
women, by Selfridge. The first proving gave Wye. a definite and important place in throat disorders. Those
symptoms make up the first pathogenesis.
Wye. has marked effects on the throat and has proven an excellent remedy in pharyngitis, especially the
follicular form. Irritable throats of singers and public speakers. Throat feels swollen, epiglottis dry and burning.
Constant desire to swallow saliva to relieve the dryness yet affording no comfort. Swallows with difficulty.
Hay fever symptoms, itching in posterior sinuses. Prickling, dry sensation in posterior sinuses, sensation
as if something were in nasal passages, an effort to clear them through the throat affords no relief. Burning
sensation in bronchial tubes. Dry, hacking cough, caused by tickling in epiglottis. Useful also in hemorrhoids.
MIND - Nervous, uneasy, apprehensive of calamity. Depressed. Incapacitated for mental work. Averse to
company. Impatient and quarrelsome.
Abdomen - Pain and bearing down in abdomen, right side. Pain below ribs of right side.
 Back - Swollen and sore glands on right side of neck.
Chest - Deep-seated sharp pain just below right ribs, followed by soreness.
Ears - Itching in right ear. Pain in left ear. Eyes - Itching in left inner canthus.
Female - Menses commenced with intense burning pain. Leucorrhea. Pain in left ovary, shooting down to
knee. Pain in uterus, can outline its contour.
Head - Rush of blood to head. Sharp pain in forehead. Severe headache.
Limbs - Pain in back, extends to end of spine. Pain right arm, stiffness of wrist and hand. Aching pains all
over.
Lungs - Dry asthma. Dry, hacking cough caused by tickling of the epiglottis. Burning sensation in bronchial
tubes.
Modalities - Worse afternoon, after eating.
Worse motion. Worse exercise, it causes perspiration.
Mouth - Feels as if scalded, sensation of heat down esophagus. Itching of the palate.
Nose - Hay fever symptoms. Sensation as if something in nasal passages.
Rectum - Loose, dark, at night. Constipation with hemorrhoids, not bleeding. Great constriction of rectum.
Itching of anus and rectum.
Sensations - Mouth as if scalded. Uvula as if elongated. Epiglottis feels dry and burning. Weight in stomach
as if something indigestible had been eaten. Uterus feels as if it enlarged in order to contain all the pain.
Sleep - Wakes frequently and too early.
Stomach - Belching of gas, alternating with hiccough. Nausea and vomiting. Sense of weight in stomach, as
if something indigestible had been eaten.
Temperature - Chill at 11 a.m. Thirst for ice water during chill. No thirst with heat. Profuse sweat all night.
Terrific headache during sweat.
Throat - Hot, dry throat. Constant clearing and hemming. Dry, posterior sinuses, no relief from clearing. Throat
feels swollen, epiglottis dry and burning. Difficult swallowing. Constant desire to swallow saliva. Uvula feels
elongated. Tendency to get hoarse talking or singing.
Vertigo - Dizzy.
COMMENTS - Nonspecific hay fever, characteristic itching of the upper palate. Hay asthma, allergic asthma.
A history of hay fever going to the lungs, or asthma caused by hay fever treatments or decongestants. Kent
used this as a prophylactic hay fever remedy.
Tough, ropy saliva. Belching alternating with hiccough. Pain over left ovary, shooting down to knee. In one
case, menses, which had been in abeyance since confinement a year before, remmed with much pain.
Hale noted several cases from Selfridge. The first concerned dry asthma in a woman who had several attacks
promptly relieved with Wye. The second case noted the effectiveness of Wye. in chronic follicular pharyngitis
with dryness of pharynx and burning in epiglottis. In the third case, Hale found Wye. to be successful in a case
of severe epidemic influenza.
Clarke had a case reported to him in which a boy had been kept awake many nights by a persistent, dry,
hacking, nervous cough. Wye. 30c cured in one dose.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Arum, Sang., Lach. (2) In throat affections, Arum-d., Caust., Hep., Stict., Rumx.,
Pen., Phos., Sulph. (3) Tough, ropy saliva and headache, Epip. (4) Sensation as if something indigestible
eaten, Abies-n. (5) Scalded mouth, Ran-s.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-

name: X-Ray
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - x-ray. X-ray. Dilutions made from absolute alcohol irritated with x-rays through a glass bottle.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Anemia. Anorexia. Burns. Cancer. Chronic fatigue. Debility. Dermatitis. Emaciation. Heart,
problems. Hemaphila. Hemorrhages. Infertility. Leukemia. Mastectomy, pains. Memory, weak. Ovaries,
atrophy. Psoriasis. Purpura. Radiation, dermatitis. Skin tumors. Sterility. Sun, exposure. Testes, atrophy.
Vitality, low. Warty growths. Weakness. X-ray, poisoning.
HOMEOPATHIC - Roentgen noted that repeated exposure to X-rays produced skin lesions often followed by
cancer. Changes take place in the blood lymphatics and bone marrow. Its homeopathic action is centrifugal
towards the periphery of the body. The stock comes from the potency lc of this irradiated alcohol.
The proving on X-ray was conducted by Fincke in 1897, on ten provers, using 6x. This was repeated by W. B.
Griggs on two male and one female provers, and published in the Homeopathic Recorder in 1952 using the
30c and 200c potencies.
X-rays have the property of stimulating cellular metabolism. Arouses the vitality, mentally and physically.
 Useful for syndromes of deficiency of certain elements present in the blood. Leukemia.
General debility. Chronic fatigue and a sick feeling. Unexplained weakness. Low vitality and anemia.
Discharges, gray, white withjelly-like lumps. Psoriasis. Corresponds to burns, that refuse to heal. Distressing
pain. Sexual glands are particularly affected. Atrophy of ovaries and testicles. Infertility.
X-rays brings to the surface suppressed symptoms, especially the psoric and sycotic due to mixed infections.
For cancer patients submitted to treatment by radiation. X-rays, cobalt. For patients submitted for therapy by
immuno-suppressors and all anti-tumor chemotherapy.
MIND - Sadness. Aversion to company. Memory, weak. Sleepy. Irritable, desire to kill, especially before and
during menses. Abdomen - Heaviness and fullness in lower abdomen, distended. Flatulence with ineffectual
desire for stool.
Back - Lame and stiff in back. Aching whole length of spine. Cramping pains in the back and lumbar region in
the morning, on walking. Soreness in small of back.
Blood - Decreased leucocytes and platelets. Leukemia. Hypochromic anemia. Hemorrhagic syndromes.
Hematoma, tendency to hemorrhage, purpura.
Breasts - Nerve pains after mastectomy.
Chest - Thorax painful, palpitations. Contraction of chest at night relieved by belching. Sensation of drops of
water trickling down on inside of chest.
Ears - Sensation of fullness, noises in the ear, buzzing. Sore pain in cartilage of left ear when pressing it, later
in right ear. Pressing outward in ears. Buzzing in right ear with pressure extending to temples. Intermittent
noise as of deep steam-whistle in left ear.
Eyes - Painful to the touch. Eyeballs sore. Sensation in right eye as if bulging. Bearing down of eyelids. Eyelids
heavy and sleepy.
Face - Red, smooth eruption on right side of face. Dull pain in right upper jaw. Paralytic feeling in right cheek.
Stinging pains in different parts of head and face.
Female - Menses profuse or lacking. Menses dark green one day. Pain darting upward in region of left ovary.
Flushes of heat, better afternoons and evenings.
Food - Anorexia, aversion to food. Can eat plenty but does not enjoy it. Desire for sweets.
Head - Sticking pains in different parts of head and face. Ringing in head. Sensation of fullness in the head.
Pain in the forehead, occiput, temples, extending to the neck. Better by hot compresses on the forehead.
Heart - Extra systole on coughing or crying. Pain in the precordial region. Noises from the heart prevent him
from sleeping on the left side.
Kidneys - Oliguria, tenesmus of the bladder. Retained urine. Kidney colic with vomiting. Clutching pain from
left kidney to bladder.
Limbs - Rheumatic pains. Trembling of the limbs. Generalized pains in the limbs, sciatic neuralgia. Sensation
of electric current at the limbs.
Lungs - Cough caused by palpitation, in evening. Cough in the morning with green sputum. Grayish
expectoration.
Male - Lewd dreams. Sexual desire lost. Sterility. Re-establishes suppressed gonorrhea.
Modalities - Better from hot applications. Worse from cold, open air. Worse movement. Worse afternoon,
evening and night, when in bed.
Mouth - Bad taste in the mouth. Tongue dry, rough, sore. Teeth discolored, graygreen color.
Neck - Painful stiffness of the neck, on lifting the head from the pillow. Sudden “cricks” attack first one side of
neck, then the other, worse on getting cold. Aching pains in left side of neck.
Nose - Nasal congestion, odor of sulphur vapor.
Rectum - Diarrhea, constipation and anal itching. Green stools.
Skin - Skin is discolored, pale, sclerous, cold. Skin dry, wrinkled. Hyperkeratosis of the skin. Warty growths.
Radiation dermatitis. Chronic itching eruptions. Papular, vesicular, itching eruptions. Dry, itching eczema.
Psoriasis. Palms rough and scaly. Erythema around roots of nails. Painful cracks. Nails thicken. Ingrown nails.
Sleep - Sleepy with headache. Sleepy all the time with chronic fatigue. Sleepy, but unable to sleep for some
hours after retiring.
Stomach - Nausea with a sick feeling. Nausea and vomiting with profuse sweat after immense stool. Sick
feeling in stomach.
Temperature - Chills as soon as beginning to sleep, running up back, preventing sleep. Chilly while undressing
in warm room. Chilliness on moving or from draft. Perspires easily. Profuse perspiration on
getting into bed, keeping him awake. Night sweats. Spells of fever, perspiration and weakness.
Throat - Throat painful on swallowing. The pharynx has gray-green mucus, discomfort and cramping pain on
swallowing. Sensation of narrowness in the throat.
 COMMENTS - Dr. John B. Campbell, one of Fincke’s original provers, discovered the great value of this
remedy in rousing the reactive vitality of the system, both mentally and physically. In doing so, it brings
suppressed symptoms to the surface in persons laboring under a combination of Hahnemann’s miasms. This
is particularly helpful in deep-seated constitutional ailments, sycotic in character, which often terminate in
malignant disease, especially cancer.
Useful for conditions lacking presenting symptoms. When well selected anti-psoric remedies (Calc., Med.,
Psor., Sep., Sulph., Syph., or Tub.) fail to relieve completely. When well-indicated remedies fail with a history
of exposure to radiation. Tends to bring out old suppressed eruptions or discharges (Sulph.).
Non-specific chronic fatigue and weakness. Sores that fail to heal. Neuralgias after mastectomy. Extreme thirst
and dryness of the mouth.
X-ray burns, whether of the bone or skin. History of exposure to x-rays. Radiation sickness. Weakness after
radiation treatments (Sol.).
Dr. King developed an x-ray burn on his left hand. Eighteen months later, seedy warts appeared. Caust. finally
helped, so he believed that Caust. may potentially be another antidote for x-rays.
RELATIONS - Antidotes: Nux-v., Sulph. and the dynamic potencies of the remedy. Compare: (1) Cadm-s.,
Care. - Cancer patients, weak immune system. (2) Electr. - Sugar of milk saturated with the current. Anxiety,
nervous tremors, restlessness, palpitation, headaches. Dreads approach of thunder-storms, heaviness of
limbs. (3) Magn-ambo. Magn-arct. Magn-aust. (4) Merc. - Desire to hurt, even those dear to him, agitated,
confused. Tongue covered with a yellowish coating and retaining the teeth imprints. (5) Phos. - Bleeding of
bright red blood, frightened, hypersensitive, afraid of the dark an of storms. (6) Sec. - The limbs are cold with
paresthesia, hemorrhaging of black blood, aggravated by the heat, ameliorated by the cold.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-
keynote:

CLINICAL -Anemia. Anorexia. Burns. Cancer. Chronic fatigue. Debility. Dermatitis. Emaciation. Heart,

Vitality, low. Warty growths. Weakness. X-ray, poiso

name: Xanthium Spinosum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - xanth. Xanthium spinosum. Spiny cocklebur. N. O. Compositae. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cystitis. Hydrophobia. Rabies.
HOMEOPATHIC-Xanth. is a wildflower that occurs throughout North America. Boericke stated that cockle is
known to be a specific for hydrophobia and is recommended for chronic cystitis in women.
Chronic cystitis, that responds to several remedies in the acute phase but keeps recurring. For chronic or
interstitial cystitis with a history of sexual abuse at a young age, especially those that include violence and
repeated torment. Strong fear of being attacked, especially at night.
RELATIONS - Compare: Staph., Lyss., Hyos., Lach., Stram., Care.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Klein.

name: Xanthoxylum Fraxineum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - xan. Xanthoxylum fraxineum. Prickly ash. Xanthoxylum americanum. Toothache tree. N. O.
Rutaceae. Tincture of fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - After-pains. Amenorrhea. Aphonia. Asthma. Cholera. Coccyx, pain. Colic. Dyspepsia. Dysentery.
Dysmenorrhea. Earache. Fibroids. Flatulence. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hoarseness. Hysteria. Injuries.
Insomnia. Jaw joint, pain. Levitation. Menstruation, painful. Nausea. Nerves, injured. Nervousness. Neuralgia.
 Neurasthenia. Ophthalmia. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Toothache. Ulcers.
HERBAL - Xan. belongs to the Rutaceae and has a vulnerary action (Ruta.). Xan. contains Piperin.
Rafinesque was the first to investigate Xan., which was known to him as “a great article in the Materia Medica
of the Indians,” who use the root bark in decoction for “colics, gonorrhea, syphilis inward pains toothache,
ulcers, etc. It is a great topical stimulant,” he continues, “changing the nature of malignant ulcers.”
T. C. Duncan, recounting reminiscences of his boyhood, said, “There was another remedy that set my youthful
mouth and stomach on fire and that was Prickly Ash. You wanted to open the mouth to let the cool air get in.”
This warmth is felt as a warm glow through the entire system with a sensation in the nerves as if gentle shocks
of electricity were passing through the body.
HOMEOPATHIC - Xan. exerts its influence on nerves, female sexual organs, respiration and left side. Its action
is on the nervous system and mucus membranes.
Injury to nerves. Neurasthenia. Pricking sensation, shocks as from electricity. Numbness of left side. Paralysis,
of single parts. Hemiplegia. Insomnia. Occipital headache. Neuralgic and rheumatic disorders, especially in
patients of spare habit and nervous, delicate organization.
Increases mucus secretion of mouth and stimulates the secretion from all glands with ducts opening in the
mouth. Poor assimilation, emaciation. Indigestion from over-eating or from too much fluid.
Painful hemorrhages, after-pains, dysmenorrhea. Sluggish capillary circulation. Mucus membranes smart as
from pepper. As if floor were soft like wool, on walking. Injury to nerves.
Grinding, shooting, radiating, sudden pains, neuralgia. Many pains are radiating, some are sudden, arouse
from sleep and cause the patient to catch her breath. Pains are excruciating, unbearable and are accompanied
with red, hot face, but the heart pains causes pallor.
MIND - Nervous, frightened feeling. Mental depression. Did not care if she lived or died. Abdomen - Some
pain in right side below ribs. Griping pain on waking in morning. Colic pain in right iliac region. Rumbling with
soreness on pressure. Flatulence.
Back - Very severe pain in cervical and upper sacral region. Back of neck numb. Dull pain from nape to right
scapula.
Causations - Injury to nerves. Wetting (getting feet wet). Suppression of menses.
Chest - Oppression of chest.
Constitutions - Suited to women of spare habit, nervous temperament and delicate nerves. Neurasthenic
patients who are thin, emaciated, poor assimilation with insomnia and occipital headache.
Ears - Ringing in ears. Loud noise in right ear, as of a valve constantly opening and shutting. Dull pain in right
ear. Darting pain under and back or right ear.
Eyes - Watering of eyes and nose. Lachrymation, pain in lid of right eye. Eyes bloodshot with red margins and
feel as if full of sand. Dull, heavy, grinding pain in left eye. Ophthalmia. Eyes twitched, pupils dilated. Vision
blurred, as if looking through blue lace. Objects seem a long way off.
Face - Hot flushes over face and head. Face much flushed. Pallor even to lips with heart pains. Neuralgia of
lower jaw. Pain in right jaw-socket.
Female - Menses too early and painful. Menses thick, almost black. Leucor- rhea at time of menses.
Leucorrhea with amenorrhea. Neuralgic dysmenorrhea with neuralgic headaches, pain in back and down
legs. Ovarian neuralgia with pain in loins and lower abdomen, worse leftside, extending down the thigh, along
genito-crural nerves. After pains (Arn., Cupr., Cham.).
Food - Very thirsty, drank much at a time. Unusually hungry. No appetite. Anorexia.
Head - Feels full. Weight and pain on vertex. Pain over eyes, throbbing pressure over nose, pressure in
forehead, head seems divided, ringing in ears. Occipital headache. Sick headache with dizziness and
flatulence. Throbbing headache, pain as if top of head would fly off. As if head is divided into two parts. As of
a tight band around.
Kidneys - Urine at night and next morning scanty and high-colored. Profuse, lightcolored urine, nervous
women.
Limbs - Numbness of left side, impairment of motion. Paralysis of left side following spinal disorders.
Hemiplegia. Left arm numb. Neuralgic shooting pain, as from electricity, all over limbs. Anterior neuralgia
(Staph.). Sciatica, worse hot weather. Pain in nape, extending down back.
Lungs - Shortness of breath. Constant desire to take a long breath, oppression of chest. Dry cough, day and
night. Cough, slight hacking in spells, only in open air.
Modalities - Better from drinking ice-water, vomiting. Better lying down. Headache is better by cold water and
in open air. Neck pain is better by pressure and by throwing head back. Worse from sleeping, in morning, 4
a.m. Worse dampness, getting feet wet. Worse suppressed menses. Worse by moving head suddenly.
Mouth - Peppery taste in mouth, fauces and throat. Burning and dry feeling in mouth and tongue. Ptyalism,
 tongue coated yellow. Tongue seemed to alternately expand and contract. Dryness of mouth and fauces.
Pharyngitis (Wye.).
Nose - Fluent coryza. Right nostril seems filled up, discharge of dry and bloody scales of mucus. Discharge of
mucus from nose with congested feeling, as if it were about to bleed. Slight nose-bleed. Dryness of both
nostrils. Numbness throughout left side of body, division felt in nose.
Rectum - Constipation in morning. Griping and diarrhea. Dysentery with tympanites, tenesmus, inodorous
discharges. Epidemic dysentery. Cholera collapse stage.
Sensations - As if top of head would be taken off by flashes of throb-like pain. As if bewildered with pain in
back of head. Feeling of looseness of brain. Eyes as if full of sand. As if walking on wool. As if sunk deep in
bed. As if body expanded.
Skin - Measles, dullness, bewilderment, drowsiness and want of sufficient development of the eruption. Old,
indolent ulcers.
Sleep - Continued gaping, drowsiness. Hard and unrefreshing, dreams of flying. Sleeplessness in
neurasthenics. A dream of suffocation woke her.
Stomach - Dyspepsia from excessive eating and drinking. Feeling of fullness of pressure in epigastrium,
fluttering. Intense burning and stinging in esophagus with slight nausea. Empty belchings with slight taste of
ingesta. Nausea with headache, with sense of oppression at stomach.
Temperature - Slight chill accompanied by death-like nausea. Frequent chills with pains in limbs, nausea.
Typhoid fever in stage of collapse. Sense of heat all over veins, flashes of heat from the head to foot.
Throat - Aphonia. Hoarseness with husky feeling in throat, obliged to clear throat frequently. Throat dry, very
difficult to talk. Peppery taste in mouth and throat.
Feels hollow. Pain and soreness in right side of throat. Throat felt as if in a vice.
COMMENTS - Xan. belongs to the Rutaceae and like Ruta, has a vulnerary action, as Clarke discovered in
the case of Miss X., 28, who injured her right ulnar nerve at the elbow by repeatedly striking it against the edge
of a bath while washing some articles.
For two months she had to keep the arm in a sling. A few weeks after that the arm was swollen. Some eight
months after the injury Clarke saw her. The pain centered in the ulnar nerve where it crosses the inner condyle
of the humerus, though there was pain above and below as well.
Clarke gave Ruta 30c, which gave some relief to the pain and relieved a frontal headache to which the patient
was subject. The arm becoming less well, Clarke gave Xan. 12c four times a day. This made a distinct
improvement in the arm and also relieved a dysmenorrhea to which Miss X. was subject. After treatment with
various potencies of Xan. the nerve lost its sensitiveness and the patient could use her arm freely.
In one of Cullis’ provers, Miss D. (there were six provers, three of them women, all took the tincture), the entire
left half of the body became numb, the left half of the head being sharply divided in sensation from the other
half. These symptoms with the many head pains and fullness in the head, give the correspondence in
hemiplegia in which Xan. has been given with success.
Two additional provings on women appear in C. D. P. In these provings 20 to 100 drop doses of the tincture
were taken and symptoms of great severity were produced. Both provers had severe dysmenorrhea pains with
increased and anticipating flow.
The symptoms in each case roused the prover from sleep with pain and suffocation, the pain being confined
to head, heart, throat and pelvis. Many of the pains were radiating from above right eye over head from right
ovary down thigh and in other directions. Left-sided numbness was present in one, who also had symptoms
of levitation and disordered sensation.
Cullis, who had success in cases of dysmenorrhea and amenorrhea, related several cases, including that of
Miss A., 25, brunette, who had menstrual irregularity since commencement, would go three, four or five months
and then her sufferings were excruciating. When she came under treatment had no menses for two months.
Xan. 1c was give, 5 drops thrice daily. Menses appeared in three days and were painless.
Miss B., fair, nervous, had menses suppressed by getting feet wet, being then a weekovertime.Xan.lx,5 drops
every three hours, brought on menses the next day.
P. C. Majumdar cured a case of uterine fibroid with Xan. 3x. An emaciated, feeble, wrinkled woman, 56, widow,
had been advised by allopaths to have an operation for tumor. Menstruation hadceasedfifteen years before. It
had been profuse and painful and preceded and followed by leucorrhea.
She had neuralgic pain in right ovarian region, a hard nodular tumor size of a small orange, painful on deep
pressure. Fetid, yellowish white discharge from vagina. Nervous, depressed, lazy and sleepy even in daytime.
Appetite poor, disgust for food.
Xan. 3x was given night and morning. In a week the pain was better and discharge less. In four weeks
Majumdar found the patient a changed person. The tumor was much softer and reduced by half. In six months
 the tumor had gone and the patient was quite well, Xan. having been taken intermittently all the time.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Gnaph., Cimic., Staph., Mez., Pise.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Xerophyllum Tenax
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - xero. Xerophyllum tenax. Basket grass flower. Tamalpais lily. N. O. Melanthiaceae. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Backache. Constipation. Dermatitis. Dyslexia. Eczema. Flatulence. Leucorrhea. Poison oak.
Typhoid.
HOMEOPATHIC - Xero. should prove curative in eczema conditions, poison oak and early
typhoid states, etc.
MIND - Dull, cannot concentrate. Forgets names. Dyslexia. Writes last letters of words first. Misspells
common words. Bewildered. Loss of consciousness.
Abdomen - Intestinal flatulence. In morning, rumbling with desire for stool.
Back - Feels hot from sacrum to scapulae. Heat deep in spine. Backache, extending down legs. Pain over
kidneys.
Eyes - Painful, as if sand, smarting, Hard to focus for close work. Eyes sore, burn.
Face - Bloated, morning. Puffy eyes.
Female - Bearing-down sensation. Vulva inflamed with furious itching. Increased sexual desire with ovarian
and uterine pains and leucorrhea.
Head - Feels full, stuffed up, pain across forehead and above eyes. Great pressure at root of nose. Pulsating
headache.
Kidneys - Difficulty retaining urine, dribbling when walking. Frequent urination.
Limbs - Limbs feel stiff (Rhus-t.). Muscular lameness, trembling. Inguinal glands and behind knees swollen.
Pain in knees.
Lungs - Posterior sinuses raw, discharge thick, yellow mucus. Sneezing. Trachea sore, lumps feel constricted.
Modalities - Better application of hot water. Better in morning. Better moving affected part. Worseapplication
of cold water. Worse in afternoon and evening.
Nose - Stuffed, tightness at bridge of nose, acute nasal catarrh.
Rectum - Constipation, stools hard, small lumps. Difficult, soft stools with much straining. Much flatus. Bearing-
down pain in rectum.
Skin - Skin rough and cracked, feels like leather. Dermatitis, especially around knees. Inflammation resembling
poison oak. Erythema with vesication and intense itching, stinging and burning. Blisters, little lumps.
Stomach - Feels full and heavy. Belchings sour offensive, an hour after luncheons and dinner. Vomiting at 2
p.m.
Throat - Stitching pain upon swallowing. RELATIONS - Compare: Rhus-t., Anae.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Yersin Serum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - yersin. Yersin serum. The yersin serum is derived from the anti-plague serum, supplied by
Institute Pasteur. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Abscess. Adenitis. Buboes. Colitis. Crohn’s disease. Encephalitis. Erythema. Gastroenteritis.
Influenza. Ileitis. Meningitis. Parkinson’s disease. Plague. Septicemia.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Fortier-Ber- noville, it is Barishac who proposed Yersin for the treatment of
grave or a typical forms of influenza. Severe form of influenza of pulmonary type with hyperthemia, respiratory
troubles, soft thick, rosy expectorations, presence of sub-crepitant rales in the base of lungs.
Mesenteric adenitis. Acute entero-colitis, gastro-enteritis with lesion of ilium. Acute enteritis of young children.
Crohn’s regional ileitis. Influenza of gastro-intestinal form. Pseudo-typho meningitis of milkmen. Meningitis
syndromes of influenzal origin. Encephalitis lethargica. Parkinson’s disease.
Severe toxic, infectious states, either cutaneous (bubo) or pulmonary. Septicemias accompanied with icterus
and hepatic abscess. Acute toxicosis of babies. Lymphoid terminal ileitis of Arnulf and Buffart. Nodulous
erythema.
RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Tub-a., Bapt., Pyrog. (2) Mimosa Púdica - thoracic pain, dry cough, irritation of
naso-pharyngeal and laryngeal mucus, frequent irritating stools with colic, better by not bath. (3) Amorpho-
phallus Ri vieri - general ill feeling with great weakness, gastro-intestinal troubles with weakening diarrhea,
 fetid stools.
REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

name: Yohimbinum Coryanthe
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY-yohim.Yohimbinumcoryanthe. Yohimbe bark. N. O. Rubiaceae. A crystalline alkaloid obtained
from the bark of the Y ohim- beha or Yumbehoa tree of the Cameroons. Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphrodisiac. Diuresis. Hyperemia. Impotence. Menorrhagia. Neurasthenia. Palpitations. Priapism.
Urethritis. Sexual, neurasthenia.
HERBAL - The natives of West Africa discovered a potent aphrodisiac in the bark of the Yohimbeha tree, and
from this an active principle. It is a powerful stimulant of the genital function in males.
Excites the sexual organs and acts on the central nervous system and respiratory center. An aphrodisiac, used
in physiological doses, but contraindicated in all acute and chronic inflammations of abdominal organs.
HOMEOPATHIC - Useful for priapism and congestive states of the sexual organs. Menorrhagia. Hyperemia
of the milk glands, stimulates breast-feeding. In animals Yohim. causes increased liveliness and cheerfulness,
hyperemia of the conjunctiva, heat and redness of the ears and of the nose also in dogs.
MIND - Intense agitation with trembling.
Abdomen - Flying heat sensations in abdomen.
Back - Flying heat sensations in back.
Face - Sensations of heat, heightening the color.
Food - Appetite almost completely disappeared.
Head - Agitation with flying sensations of heat in face.
Heart - Heart beats more intense and more frequent, pulse, normally 80, became 108. Flying sensation of
heat in heart.
Kidneys - Urine clean abundant, foamy, no trace of albumen, had to rise three times in the night. Urethritis.
Limbs - Hands trembled, could scarcely write, writing was illegible.
Male - Sexual neurasthenia with impotence. Priapism. Strong and lasting erections in the morning without
increase of desire. Enlargement of testicles and epididymis.
Mouth - Disagreeable, metallic taste. Copious salivation. Tongue covered with a yellow coat.
Rectum - Intestinal hemorrhage. Bleeding hemorrhoids. Stools frequent, liquid, black and bilious.
Sleep - No sleep all night. Sleeplessness. Thoughts of events of whole past life keep him awake.
Stomach - Nausea and eructation.
Temperature - Rigor intense heat, waves of heat and chilliness, tendency to sweat.
COMMENTS - Lambreghts related the case of a young man, 28, “thin, anemic, nervous and partially impotent,”
who took a 5 mg. tablet one morning, another in the evening and a third the following morning. The symptoms
were so severe that he discontinued the herb in spite of a certain amelioration of the sexual neurasthenia.
Yohim. set up symptoms of fever, disordered the digestion, caused agitation and tremors and increased the
action of the heart. Eulenburg used Yohim. in 10 drop doses of a 1 percent solution and “in cases of
neurasthenic impotence with excellent result.”
RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Erections - Canth., Pic-ac., Phos., Graph., Canth.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Yttrium Metallicum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - yttr. Yttrium metallicum. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Aphonia. Cancer. Colds. Eye problems. Headache. Hoarseness. Lung, problems. Voice,
problems.
HOMEOPATHIC - Headache in forehead, temples and vertex. Neck problems, stiffness. Eye inflammations,
visual disturbances. Colds with watery coryza. Hoarseness. Voice problems. Loss of voice. Stammering. Lung
problems. Irritation of lungs. Cancer. Pain in arms. Problems with genitalia, testes
and ovaries. Menses profuse.
Bruised pains. Itching. Weakness. Sleepy. Nervous trembling. Worse left side. Worse cold weather, cold feet,
cold, damp. Better being outside.
MIND - Irritability. Humiliation. Mood uncertain, crying. Anticipation. Fear of giving performance, speeches.
Fear of heights, ladders. Fear of narrow spaces. Dreams of heights, falling, ladders. Dreams of mountains,
volcano, water.
REFERENCES - Scholten.
 ***YUCCA FILAMENTOSA
(Bear Grass)
PHARMACY - yuc. Yucca filamentosa. Bear grass. Agavaceae. N. O. Melanthacae, Lili- aceae. Tincture of
root and leaves when not in flower. Tincture of flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Biliousness. Coryza. Diarrhea. Flatulence. Headache, temporal. Post-nasal catarrh. Throat,
granular.
HOMEOPATHIC-Yuc. was proved by Rowell and four others in the 30c. Farrington gave these Yuc.
indications: biliousness with pain going through upperpart of liver to back. Diarrhea which contains an excess
of bile. Much flatus passed by rectum. Frequent passage of flatus and of watery, yellowish-brown stools. Dull
ache in center of liver. Abdomen sensitive.
As with many liver disorders, there is chilliness, cannot bear to be away from the fire. Face sallow. Bilious
symptoms with headache. Frontal or temporal headache with frequent flushing of face. Bad taste in mouth.
Tongue coated yellow and taking imprint of teeth. The tongue is usually a bluish white.
MIND - Despondent and irritable. Irresolute. Disinclined to study. Mind wanders, uses wrong words. Unable to
remember anything read. When others talking to him, hears but doesn't seem to understand.
Abdomen - Deep pain in right side over liver, going through back. Abdomen bloated after dinner and feels
sore. Rumbling. Colic. Crampy pains in abdomen after breakfast. Throbbing, painless, right side about twelfth
rib. Much flatus emitted, odorless.
Back - Constriction of neck muscles, seems to draw head backward. Tight feeling around neck, evening, had
to take off collar. Severe pain in left scapula, at 9 p.m. Backache.
Chest - Constriction in whole chest and in heart. Pain in upper intercostal muscles.
Ears - Pain behind right ear, 6:30 p.m. Very sensitive to least noise.
Eyes - Dark rings under eyes. Eyes feel hot and inflamed. Itching and smarting left eye, left inner canthus. Dull
pain over left eye.
Face - Pale, flushed, burning, yellow. Momentary aching in zygoma, recurring several times. Pain in jaw joints.
Food - Appetite increased, food relished, lost.
Head - Headaches frontal, heavy, pressing, throbbing. Headaches as if top of head would fly off. Temporal
arteries throb. Sensation of cold air blowing on left side of scalp.
Heart - Constriction in heart. Momentary aching in heart region. Visible throbbing in arteries of hand. Pulse full
and heavy, a little irregular.
Kidneys - Circumscribed edematous red swelling, raw sensation around meatus. Irritable bladder, frequent
urination. Burning when urinating. Urine increased, high specific gravity.
Limbs - Crampy pains in knees. Sore, crampy pains in muscle of back of left leg, just above ankle, as if
sprained.
Lungs - Hard, rattling cough.
Male - Burning and swelling of the prepuce with redness of meatus. Gonorrhea (Cann-s.). Erections, all night
long but no emissions, cannot study, mind runs on sexual subjects.
Modalities - Griping pain is better bending forward. Worse by noise. Worse motion, pressure.
Mouth - Bad odor from mouth. Taste as of rotteneggs(Arn.). Back of mouth dry. Yellow tongue yellow, coated,
taking imprint of teeth (Merc., Podo., Rhus-t.).
Nose - Nose red. In evening, right side of nose constantly running, left dry. Profuse, bloody, watery discharge.
Coryza. Sensation as if something hung down from posterior sinuses, cannot get it up or down.
Rectum - Constant desire for stool. Sudden, violent tenesmus, followed by discharge of wind, which relieves
the pain. Diarrhea following pains in abdomen. Stools are watery, copious, thin, yellowish brown with smarting
at anus. Stool yellowish brown with bile. Tenesmus after stool.
Sensations - As of something hanging down from back of sinuses. As if cold air blowing on left side of scalp.
Skin - Erythematous redness.
Sleep - Very sleepy in the evening. Restless night. Lewd dreams.
Stomach - Aching and sharp pains in stomach. Region of stomach sore and sensitive.
Temperature - Coldness of scalp, left side, as if cold air blowing on it. Coldness, cannot bear to be away from
fire. Restless and feverish. Hot, feverish. Face sweats, evening.
Throat - Tonsils dark red, not sore. Pharynx seems covered with granules is dark red. Stringy, greasy-looking
mucus back of throat. Sensation as if something hanging down from posterior sinuses.
RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Cocc. Compare: ( 1 ) Constriction in heart, Lil-t. (2) Biliousness, Bry. (3) Tongue
imprinted with teeth, Merc., Podo. (4) Blue tongue, Gymn.
REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.
 ***ZEA ITALICA
(Corn-silk)
PHARMACY - zea-i. Zea itálica. Corn-silk. Gramineae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, tincture
in ten to fifty drop doses in water.
HOMEOPATHIC - Zea-i. has curative properties in skin diseases, particularly in psoriasis and eczema rubrum.
Appetite increased, voracious, alternating with disgust for food. Heartburn, nausea, vomiting, better from
drinking wine.
MIND - Easily angered. Mania for bathing. Impulse to suicide, particularly by drowning.
RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Cocc. Compare: (l)Stigm.
REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Zincum Aceticum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - zinc-acet. Zincum aceticum. Zinc acetate. Trituration of the metal. Histori cal dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Erysipelas. Gastritis. Night watching, effects. Toothache.
HOMEOPATHIC - Zinc-acet. was proved by Hahnemann and others. The only clinical uses of Zinc-acet. are
from Burnett. He used Rademacher’s solution of zinc in acetic acid and gave 5 drop doses three times a day
in water to nurses and others who were compelled to work on an insufficient amount of sleep. Clarke verified
the great value of this. Burnett also used it for erysipelas of elderly people.
The most peculiar Zinc-acet. symptoms were “Brain feels sore and as if sprinkled with salt.” “Throat seems too
tight and tongue too short.” Empty, hungry sensation. Shaking chill during and after vomiting. Pain and paralytic
condition of arms. In the provers it produced a pustular eruption on forehead and knee and the latter was
attended with voluptuous itching.
Modalities - Toothache is worse by touch.
Worse in evening. Worse by motion,
ZINCUM ARSENICOSUM
PHARMACY - zinc-ar. Zincum arsenicosum. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Anemia. Backaches. Chorea. Nervous, disorders. Night watching. Numbness. Prostration.
Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Zinc-ar. affects the lumbar region and lower limbs. Chorea. Numbness, right arm then left,
better when writing. Lumbar pain, worse from exertion, sitting, jarring or standing. Occipital pain. Blue vision.
Burning in bladder.
Anemia. Neurasthenia. Weakness, enervation, exhaustion, prostration, infirmity. Profound exhaustion on
slightexertion. Slight exertion aggravates. Soles ache when tired, better pressure.
Worse exertion, ascending stairs. Weakness, in acute diseases. Weakness and infirmity from nursing the sick.
Ailments from night watching. Desires to walk. Worse from 10 a.m. and 3 p.m.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Zincum Bromatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - zinc-br. Zincum bromatum. Zinc bromide. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Chorea. Cramps. Dentition. Hydrocephalus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hale used Zinc-br. on its double indications for teething children who suffer intensely from
pain in nerves of head and face. Pains which throw the children into a state of stupor alternating with
wakefulness. Hale used the 3c and 6c potencies.
REFERENCES Clarke.

name: Zincum Chromatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - zinc-chr. Zincum chromatum. Zinc chromate. Chrome. Trituration. Historical dose: All
potencies.
HOMEOPATHIC - Zinc-chr. acts upon the ears, nose, throat and left side. Aching, gnawing, grinding, pain or
wandering in shocks. Catching stitches that impede motion.
MIND - Aversion to work.
Abdomen - Cannot tolerate her hands on abdomen.
 Back - Gnawing and grinding below and above left scapula.
Ears - Throbbing behind the ears.
Eyes - Vision wavering.
Female - Dryness of vagina with sense of a coming sickness, 10 to 12 a.m.
Food - Indefinite craving, knows not for what. Aversion to even thinking of food.
Head - Inward pressure in spot on bregma. Throbbing temples.
Heart - Cutting at apex, at night.
Limbs - Feet sore. Cramps of gnawing, grinding pain in toes, at night.
Lungs - Cough from tickling in throat-pit. Expectoration, sweet, loose, but had to be swallowed or tough with
constant spitting spells.
Modalities - Worse from motion. Worse lying on the back. Worse washing the head.
Mouth - Metallic taste in mouth.
Nose - Bad odor within nose. Blowing of pus and blood and scabs.
Throat - Shooting pain from larynx (left side) up through tonsils into ear.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Zincum Cyanatum
author: Murphy
full:
PHARMACY - zinc-cy. Zincum cyanatum. Zinc cyanide. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Agitation. Chorea. Congestive Headaches. Constipation. Convulsions. Epilepsy. Hysteria.
Meningitis. Parkinson’s disease. Petit mal. Trembling.
HOMEOPATHIC - Kopp’s proving showed it produces the nervous and mental symptoms of Zinc met. with
great intensity. Useful for convulsions and paralytic conditions. Great physical agitation. General trembling.
Parkinson’s disease. Petit mal.
MIND - Great excitement. Great sensitiveness.
Bad temper.
Face - Face suddenly changes color.
Head - Congestion to head.
Rectum - Constipation.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

full:
